question: 14. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Brains are expensive in terms of energy. Twenty percent of the calories we consume are used to power the brain. So brains try to operate in the most energy-efficient way possible, and that means processing only the minimum amount of information from our senses that we need to navigate the world. Neuroscientists weren't the first to discover that fixing your gaze on something is no guarantee of seeing it. Magicians figured this out long ago. By directing your attention, they perform tricks with their hands in full view. Their actions should give away the game, but they can rest assured that your brain processes only small bits of the visual scene. This all helps to explain the prevalence of traffic accidents in which drivers hit pedestrians in plain view, or collide with cars directly in front of them. In many of these cases, the eyes are pointed in the right direction, but the brain isn't seeing what's really out there.
options: ① examples of optical illusions that deceive brains
② brain's capacity for processing sensory information
③ importance of paying full attention to avoid accidents
④ how brains' energy efficiency leads to selective vision
⑤ ways to increase brain energy efficiency for better performance
explanation: 이 글은 뇌가 많은 에너지를 소비하기 때문에 가장 효율적인 방식으로 작동하려고 노력하며, 그 결과 세상에 대응하는 데 필요한 최소한의 정보만을 처리한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 마술사의 속임수나 교통사고 사례를 통해 눈은 보고 있어도 뇌가 시각 정보를 선택적으로 처리하여 실재를 다 보지 못하는 현상을 설명하고 있으므로, 주제는 '뇌의 에너지 효율성이 어떻게 선택적 시각으로 이어지는가'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌를 속이는 착시 현상의 예시들
② 감각 정보를 처리하는 뇌의 용량
③ 사고를 피하기 위해 충분한 주의를 기울이는 것의 중요성
④ 뇌의 에너지 효율성이 어떻게 선택적 시각으로 이어지는가
⑤ 더 나은 성과를 위해 뇌 에너지 효율을 높이는 방법

question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The built-in capacity for smiling is proven by the remarkable observation that babies who are congenitally both deaf and blind, who have never seen a human face, also start to smile at around 2 months. However, smiling in blind babies eventually disappears if nothing is done to reinforce it. Without the right feedback, smiling dies out. But here's a fascinating fact: blind babies will continue to smile if they are cuddled, bounced, nudged, and tickled by an adult - anything to let them know that they are not alone and that someone cares about them. This social feedback encourages the baby to continue smiling. In this way, early experience operates with our biology (A)_______________________________. In fact, you don't need the cases of blind babies to make the point. Babies with sight smile more at you when you look at them or, better still, smile back at them.
options: ① suppress emotional expression
② independently affect all behavior
③ determine complex social abilities
④ ignore social behaviors completely
⑤ collaborate to shape social behaviors
explanation: 아기가 선천적으로 눈이 보이지 않고 귀가 들리지 않아도 미소를 짓는다는 것은 생물학적인 능력(biology)을 보여주지만, 타인의 반응이나 신체적 접촉과 같은 사회적 피드백(experience)이 있어야 미소가 유지된다는 내용을 통해, 생물학적 특성과 초기 경험이 상호작용하여 사회적 행동을 형성함을 알 수 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '사회적 행동을 형성하기 위해 협력한다'는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 감정 표현을 억제하기 위해
② 모든 행동에 독립적으로 영향을 주기 위해
③ 복잡한 사회적 능력을 결정하기 위해
④ 사회적 행동을 완전히 무시하기 위해
⑤ 사회적 행동을 형성하기 위해 협력한다

question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If we've invested in something that hasn't repaid us - be it money in a failing venture, or time in an unhappy relationship - we find it very difficult to walk away. This is the sunk cost fallacy. Our instinct is to continue investing money or time as we hope that our investment will prove to be worthwhile in the end. Giving up would mean acknowledging that we've wasted something we can't get back, and that thought is so painful that we prefer to avoid it if we can. The problem, of course, is that if something really is a bad bet, then staying with it simply increases the amount we lose. Rather than walk away from a bad five-year relationship, for example, we turn it into a bad 10-year relationship; rather than accept that we've lost a thousand dollars, we lay down another thousand and lose that too. In the end, by delaying the pain of admitting our problem, we only add to it. Sometimes we need to do is (A)<u>to cut our losses.</u>
options: ① to blame someone else for the failure
② to wait longer hoping for a better outcome
③ to give up investment without compensation
④ to analyze the reasons for the failure in detail
⑤ to continue doing the same thing but with less effort
explanation: 이 글은 매몰 비용의 오류(sunk cost fallacy)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 우리는 이미 투자한 것이 아까워(또는 실패를 인정하기 싫어) 손해를 보면서도 계속 투자하는 경향이 있는데, 이는 결국 더 큰 손실을 초래합니다. 밑줄 친 'to cut our losses'는 더 큰 손실을 막기 위해 손해를 감수하고라도 현재의 투자나 상황을 중단하는 것을 의미하므로, '보상 없이 투자를 포기하는 것'이 가장 적절한 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 실패에 대해 다른 사람을 비난하는 것
② 더 나은 결과를 희망하며 더 오래 기다리는 것
③ 보상 없이 투자를 포기하는 것
④ 실패의 원인을 상세히 분석하는 것
⑤ 같은 일을 계속하되 노력을 덜 들이는 것

question: 17. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: On our little world, light travels, for all practical purposes, instantaneously. If a lightbulb is glowing, then of course it's physically where we see it, shining away. We reach out our hand and touch it: It's there all right, and unpleasantly hot. If the filament fails, then the light goes out. We don't see it in the same place, glowing, illuminating the room years after the bulb breaks and it's removed from its socket. The very notion seems nonsensical. But if we're far enough away, an entire sun can go out and we'll continue to see it shining brightly; we won't learn of its death, it may be, for ages to come - in fact, for how long it takes light, which travels fast but not infinitely fast, to cross the intervening vastness. The immense distances to the stars and the galaxies mean that we see everything in space in the past.
options: ① The Star Is Dead, But Still It Shines
② Accidental Discovery of Cosmic Mysteries
③ The Speed Wars : Racing at the Limit of Light
④ How to Deal with When a Lightbulb Goes Out
⑤ A Brief History of the Invention of the Lightbulb
explanation: 이 글은 빛의 속도가 매우 빠르지만 무한하지 않다는 점과 우주의 거대한 거리 때문에, 우리가 우주에서 보는 별들이 실제로는 과거의 모습이라는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 죽은 별일지라도 그 빛이 지구에 도달하기까지 시간이 걸려 여전히 빛나는 것처럼 보인다는 ①번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 별은 죽었지만, 여전히 빛난다

③ 속도 전쟁 : 빛의 한계에서의 경주
④ 전구가 나갔을 때 대처하는 방법

question: 18. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We collect stamps, coins, vintage cars even when they serve no practical purpose. The post office doesn't accept the old stamps, the banks don't take old coins, and the vintage cars are no longer allowed on the road. These are all side issues; the attraction is that they are in short supply. In one study, students were asked to arrange ten posters in order of attractiveness - with the agreement that afterward they could keep one poster as a reward for their participation. Five minutes later, they were told that the poster with the third highest rating was no longer available. Then they were asked to judge all ten from scratch. The poster that was no longer available was suddenly classified as the most beautiful. In psychology, this phenomenon is called reactance: when we are deprived of an option, we suddenly deem it more attractive.
options: ① Letting Go Brings Peace
② The Value Lies in the Use
③ Out of Reach, Into Our Hearts
④ The More You See, The Less You Want
⑤ The Best Things Are Always In Front of You
explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 실용적이지 않은 물건을 수집하는 이유가 '공급의 부족' 때문이며, 심리학적으로 어떤 선택권이 박탈되었을 때 그것을 더 매력적으로 느끼는 '저항(reactance)' 현상에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. '손에 닿지 않는 것이 마음속으로 들어온다(더 매력적으로 느껴진다)'는 의미의 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 놓아주는 것이 평화를 가져온다
② 가치는 사용에 있다
③ 손이 닿지 않는 곳, 우리 마음속으로
④ 더 많이 볼수록, 더 적게 원한다
⑤ 최고의 것들은 항상 당신 앞에 있다

question: 19. 다음 글을 읽고 알 수 있는 내용이 아닌 것은?
passage: Many things spark envy: ownership, status, health, youth, talent, popularity, beauty. It is often confused with jealousy because the physical reactions are identical. The difference: the subject of envy is a thing (status, money, health etc.). The subject of jealousy is the behaviour of a third person. Envy needs two people. Jealousy, on the other hand, requires three: Peter is jealous of Sam because the beautiful girl next door rings him instead. Paradoxically, with envy we direct resentments toward those who are most similar to us in age, career and residence. We don't envy businesspeople from the century before last. We don't envy millionaires on the other side of the globe. As a writer, I don't envy musicians, managers or dentists, but other writers. As a CEO you envy other, bigger CEOs. As a supermodel you envy more successful supermodels. Aristotle knew this: 'Potters envy potters.'
options: ① Envy is frequently misidentified as jealousy, as both evoke the same bodily responses.
② Envy is a reaction between two individuals, whereas jealousy occurs in a triangular relationship.
③ When a retired engineer is impressed by a young athlete's physical strength and energy, what the engineer feels can be calle 'envy'.
④ When a new classmate talks more to Jack's best friend than Jack, what Jack feels can be called 'jealousy'.
⑤ Negative emotions triggered by envy are frequently aimed at people in comparable life situations
explanation: 지문에 따르면 질투(envy)는 나이, 직업, 거주지 등이 우리와 가장 유사한 사람들에게 향하는 경향이 있다고 설명하고 있습니다(Potters envy potters). ③번의 경우 은퇴한 엔지니어와 젊은 운동선수는 나이나 직업 면에서 유사성이 낮으므로, 지문의 논리에 따르면 질투의 대상으로 적절하지 않습니다.

passage: Shoppers confronted with the choice of thirty different varieties of gourmet chocolates are more likely to walk away without buying any, compared with when they are presented with only half a dozen choices. If employees are given a free trip to Paris, they are happy. If you give them a free trip to Hawaii, they are happy. But if you offer them the choice between the two destinations, they are less happy, no matter what they choose. Why might choice be so disruptive? The reason is that choice forces us to make comparisons and acknowledge relative disadvantages. People who choose Paris complain that it doesn't have the ocean and those who choose Hawaii regret that it doesn't have the museums. Psychologist Barry Schwartz calls this the 'tyranny of choice' because rather than providing freedom, it actually constrains our decision-making. He argues that greater choice increases unhappiness because we worry that we are going to make the wrong decision and so we get stressed about trying to process all the comparisons in an effort to get it right. This both increases our fear of making the wrong choice and raises expectations that we should be able to get the best choice. Having made the choice, we then start to regret, wondering whether it was the right one.

④ saving account

explanation: 이 글은 보상이 가면 갈수록 더 큰 가치림 부여하게 되는 '하이퍼볼릭 할인(hyperbolic discounting)' 현상에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 특히 '현재' 시점에서 보상이 가까울수록 심리적윴로 더 큰 이자율(감정적 이자율)을 부여하여 비일관적인 선택을 하게 된다는 내용이므로, 비칸에는 '감정적 이자율'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 감정적 이자율
밴상 비용
장기적 가격
저축 계제
하이퍼 인플레이션

question: 22. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Steve Jobs used analogy to get people to embrace the new technology. Before computers, people worked in a physical world. We used paper and pens and physical file folders and so on. The idea of working in a virtual world was radically different. Or at least seemed radically different. What Jobs understood was that a physical office was fundamentally similar to a virtual office. To win over the masses, Jobs drew strong analogies between the traditional workplace people knew well with the new, unfamiliar virtual workplace. In the pre-computer workplace, when ideas were written on paper it was called . . . a document. When those documents needed to be stored they were put in . . . a folder. And those folders were kept on . . . a desk. Documents, folders, and desktops are the terms we use in our virtual work because Steve Jobs understood that using familiar terms would make the new technology easier to understand. The parallels between the physical and virtual workplace now seem obvious.
options: ① The parallels between the physical and virtual workplace
② Steve Job's speech highlighting linguistic difference
③ Steve Job's attitude receiving continuos feedback
④ Office space arrangement focusing on efficiency
⑤ New technology prioritizing user preference
explanation: 스티브 잡스가 츨숙한 물리적 사무실 환경(문서, 폴더, 책상)을 가상 환경에 비유하여 사람들이 새로운 기술을 쉽게 이해하고 밑아들이게 했다는 내용입니다. 따노서 물리적 작업 개념감 가상 작업 개념 사이의 유사성(팘러랐)이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 물리적 작업 개념감 가상 작업 개념 사이의 유사성
언어적 차이림 강조하는 스티브 잡스의 연설
지섽적인 피드백을 수용하는 스티브 잡스의 태도
효율성에 초점을 둔 사무 갰간 배치
사용자 선호도림 우선시하는 새로운 기술

question: 1. 다음 글의 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Take a look at some of the most powerful, rich, and famous people in the world. Ignore the trappings of their success and what they're able to buy. Look instead at what they're forced to trade in return - look at what success has cost them. Mostly? Freedom. Their work demands they wear a suit. Their success depends on attending certain parties, kissing up to people they don't like. It will require ─ inevitably ─ realizing they are unable to say what they actually think. Worse, it demands that they become a different type of person or do bad things. Sure, it might pay well ─ but they haven't truly examined the transaction. As Seneca put it, "Slavery resides under marble and gold." Too many successful people are prisoners in jails of their own making. Is that what you want? Is that what you're working hard toward? Let's hope not.
options: ① 성공을 위해서 일정 수준의 희생은 감수할 가치가 있다.
② 성공의 이면에 숨겨진 대가를 깊이 생각해 보아야 한다.
③ 성공한 사람들의 공통점은 명확한 목표 설정과 시간 관리 능력이다.
④ 성공은 끊임없는 경쟁 속에서 살아남는 사람만이 누릴 수 있는 특권이다.
⑤ 성공이란 자신이 원하는 삶을 얻기 위해 외부의 요구에 적절히 순응하는 것이다.
explanation: 이 글은 세상의 권력자나 부유한 사람들이 성공의 대가로 자유를 희생하고, 원하지 않는 행동을 강요받으며, 스스로 만든 감옥에 갇힌 죄수처럼 살아가는 현실을 지적하고 있습니다. 필자는 세네카의 말을 인용하며 성공이라는 화려함 뒤에 숨겨진 '자유의 상실'이라는 거래(대가)를 제대로 검토해 보아야 한다고 주장합니다. 따라서 정답은 ②번입니다.

question: 2. 다음 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: On our little world, light travels, for all practical purposes, instantaneously. If a lightbulb is glowing, then of course it's physically where we see it, shining away. We reach out our hand and touch it: It's there all right, and unpleasantly hot. If the filament fails, then the light goes out. We don't see it in the same place, glowing, illuminating the room years after the bulb breaks and it's removed from its socket. The very notion seems nonsensical. But if we're far enough away, <u>an entire sun can go out and we'll continue to see it shining brightly</u>; we won't learn of its death, it may be, for ages to come -in fact, for how long it takes light, which travels fast but not infinitely fast, to cross the intervening vastness. The immense distances to the stars and the galaxies mean that we see everything in the past.
options: ① 우리가 보는 별과 은하의 빛은 현재가 아닌 과거의 것이다.
② 매우 빠른 빛은 속도로 별의 죽음이 우리에게 즉시 보인다.
③ 빛의 속도는 우주 공간의 먼 거리를 무의미하게 만든다.
④ 빛은 우주에서 항상 일정한 속도로 이동한다.
⑤ 우리는 항상 물체를 현재 상태로 본다.
explanation: 빛의 속도는 유한하기 때문에, 우주처럼 아주 먼 거리를 이동할 때는 시간이 걸립니다. 따라서 멀리 떨어진 별이 이미 사라졌더라도 그 빛이 우리에게 도달할 때까지는 계속 빛나는 것처럼 보이게 됩니다. 이는 결국 우리가 보는 별의 모습이 현재의 모습이 아니라 과거의 모습임을 의미합니다.

question: 3. 주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Most people resist the idea of a true selfestimate, probably because they fear it might mean downgrading some of their beliefs about who they are and what they're capable of. As Goethe's maxim goes, it is a great failing "to see yourself as more than you are." (A) How could you really be considered self-aware if you refuse to consider your weaknesses? (B) Don't fear self-assessment because you're worried you might have to admit some things about yourself. (C) The second half of Goethe's maxim is important too. (D) We underestimate our capabilities just as much and just as dangerously as we overestimate other abilities. (E) Cultivate the ability to judge yourself accurately and honestly. Look inward to discern what you're capable of and what it will take to unlock that potential.
insertion_sentence: He states that it is equally damaging to "value yourself at less than your true worth."
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장은 괴테의 격언의 나머지 절반을 언급하며, 스스로를 실제 가치보다 낮게 평가하는 것 역시 해롭다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (C) 뒤에서 '괴테 격언의 후반부 또한 중요하다'고 언급했으므로, 그 후반부의 구체적인 내용인 '실제 가치보다 낮게 평가하는 것'에 대한 설명이 이어지는 (D) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다. (D) 뒤의 문장인 '우리는 다른 능력을 과대평가하는 것만큼이나 위험하게 우리의 능력을 과소평가한다'는 내용과도 일맥상통합니다.

question: 4. 주어진 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Financial markets do more than just take capital from the rich and lend it to everyone else. They allow each of us to smooth consumption over our lifetimes ─ a fancy way of saying we don't have to spend income at the exact moment we earn it. (A) Shakespeare may have warned us to be neither borrowers nor lenders, but the reality is that most of us will be both at some point. (B) If we lived in an agrarian society, we would have to consume our crops soon after harvest or find a way to store them. (C) Financial markets, however, offer a more sophisticated way of managing our "harvest." (D) We can spend income now that we have not yet earned or we can earn income today and choose to spend it years later by saving for the future. (E) Being able to borrow, save, and invest means we can navigate life's financial demands with greater ease. In other words, financial markets play a crucial role in modern life by allowing individuals to separate the timing of earning and spending, providing flexibility to borrow or save based on their needs at different life stages.
insertion_sentence: This flexibility is reflected in student loans that make higher education accessible before we've accumulated wealth, credit cards that help manage short-term expenses, and retirement accounts that ensure we have resources long after we've stopped working.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'This flexibility(이러한 유연성)'는 앞 문장에서 설명된 '벌지 않은 소득을 미리 쓰거나 번 소득을 나중에 쓰기 위해 저축하는 행위'를 가리킵니다. (D) 위치 앞부분은 금융 시장을 통해 우리가 수입과 지출의 시점을 분리할 수 있다는 원론적인 내용을 설명하고, (D) 위치 뒤에서 학자금 대출, 신용카드, 퇴직 계좌 등 구체적인 사례를 통해 이러한 유연성이 어떻게 실현되는지 보여주고 있습니다. 또한 문장 삽입 후 이어지는 (E)의 'In other words(즉)' 결론 부분이 전체 내용을 요약하고 있어 흐름상 ④번이 적절합니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If we've invested in something that hasn't repaid us ─ be it money in a failing venture, or time in an unhappy relationship ─ we find it very difficult to walk away. This is the sunk cost fallacy. Our instinct is to continue investing money or time as we hope that our investment will prove to be worthwhile in the end. Giving up would mean acknowledging that we've wasted something we can't get back, and that thought is so painful that we prefer to avoid it if we can. The problem, of course, is that if something really is a bad bet, then staying with it simply increases the amount we lose. Rather than walk away from a bad five year relationship, for example, we turn it into a bad 10 year relationship; rather than accept that we've lost a thousand dollars, we lay down another thousand and lose that too. In the end, by delaying the pain of admitting our problem, we only add to it.
summary_sentence: The fear of acknowledging a poor decision often leads people to (A)__________, which ultimately (B)__________ their losses.
options: ① let it go ...... improves
② stick with it ...... worsens
③ reflect deeply ...... eliminates
④ follow their instincts ...... balances
⑤ deny the opportunity ...... reduces
explanation: 잘못된 결정을 인정하는 두려움 때문에 사람들은 그것을 계속 고수하게 되고(stick with it), 이는 결국 손실을 악화시킨다(worsens)는 내용이 적절합니다. 이는 매몰 비용 오류(sunk cost fallacy)에 대한 설명입니다.
options_translation: ① 그것을 놓아주다 ...... 개선하다
② 그것을 고수하다 ...... 악화시키다
③ 깊이 반성하다 ...... 제거하다
④ 본능을 따르다 ...... 균형을 맞추다
⑤ 기회를 부정하다 ...... 줄이다

question: 14. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We tend to break up time into units, such as weeks, months, and seasons; in a series of studies among farmers in India and students in North America, psychologists found if a deadline is on the other side of a "break" ─ such as in the New Year ─ we're more likely to see it as (A)___________, and, as a result, be less ready to jump into action. What you need to do in that situation is find another way to think about the time frame. For example, if it's November and the deadline is in January, it's better to tell yourself you have to get it done "this winter" rather than "next year." The best approach is to view deadlines as a challenge you have to meet within a period that's (B)___________. That way the stress is more manageable, and you have a better chance of starting ─ and therefore finishing ─ in good time.
options: ① far-off ... distant
② pressing ... upcoming
③ abstract ... postponed
④ impending ... obscure
⑤ physically detached ... close
explanation: 사람들은 시간을 단위(주, 월, 계절)로 나누는 경향이 있으며, 마감 기한이 새로운 해와 같은 '경계' 너머에 있을 때 그것을 더 멀게 느껴 일을 미루게 됩니다. 이를 해결하기 위해 마감 기한을 현재와 같은 기간(예: '올겨울') 내에 있는 것으로 재설정하면 더 관리하기 쉬워지고 제때 시작할 가능성이 높아진다는 내용입니다. (제시된 정답 ④에 따르면 A는 '임박한', B는 '모호한'으로 되어 있으나, 지문의 논리상으로는 ①이나 ⑤가 더 적절해 보입니다. 다만 제공된 정답지에 따라 정답을 확정합니다.)
options_translation: ① 멀리 떨어진 ... 먼
② 긴박한 ... 다가오는
③ 추상적인 ... 연기된
④ 임박한 ... 모호한
⑤ 물리적으로 분리된 ... 가까운

question: 15. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If a firm is going to be saved by the government, it might be easier to concentrate on lobbying the government for more money rather than taking the harder decision of restructuring the company to be able to be profitable and viable in the long term. This is an example of something known as moral hazard ─ when government support alters the decisions firms take. For example, if governments rescue banks who get into difficulty, as they did during the credit crisis of 2007-08, this could encourage banks to take greater risks in the future because they know there is a possibility that governments will intervene if they lose money. Although the government rescue may be well intended, it can negatively affect the behavior of banks, encouraging risky and poor decision making.
options: ① Successful Restructuring Strategies for Businesses
② The Importance of Supporting Struggling Companies
③ When Government Help Leads to Reckless Behavior
④ How Government Lobbying Drives Economic Growth
⑤ How Governments Protect National Economies in Crisis
explanation: 이 글은 도덕적 해이(moral hazard)에 대해 설명하며, 정부가 위기에 처한 기업이나 은행을 구제해 줄 때, 해당 기업들이 스스로 수익성을 개선하려는 노력 대신 로비에 집중하거나 더 큰 위험을 감수하게 되는 부작용을 경고하고 있습니다. 따라서 '정부의 도움이 무모한 행동으로 이어질 때'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 기업을 위한 성공적인 구조조정 전략
② 어려움을 겪는 기업을 지원하는 것의 중요성
③ 정부의 도움이 무모한 행동으로 이어질 때
④ 정부의 로비가 어떻게 경제 성장을 이끄는가
⑤ 정부가 위기 상황에서 국가 경제를 보호하는 방법

question: 16. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The Net differs from most of the mass media it replaces in an obvious and very important way: it's bidirectional. We can send messages through the network as well as receive them, which has made the system all the more useful. The ability to exchange information online, to upload as well as download, has turned the Net into a thoroughfare for business and commerce. With a few clicks, people can search virtual catalogues, place orders, track shipments, and update information in corporate databases. But the Net doesn't just connect us with businesses; it connects us with one another. It's a personal broadcasting medium as well as a commercial one. Millions of people use it to distribute their own digital creations, in the form of blogs, videos, photos, songs, and podcasts, as well as to critique, edit, or otherwise modify the creations of others.
options: ① Blog It, Vlog It, Sell It: The Rise of Digital Business
② Click, Share, Connect: What Makes the Internet Unique
③ The Harmony of Traditional Media in the Internet Age
④ Why Social Networking Sites Are Taking Over the World
⑤ Uploading the Future: How E-Commerce Changed the World
explanation: 이 글은 인터넷이 기존 매체와 달리 '양방향성(bidirectional)'을 가지고 있다는 점을 강조합니다. 정보를 주고받는 능력 덕분에 비즈니스뿐만 아니라 개인 간의 연결, 그리고 디지털 창작물의 배포 및 수정이 가능해졌다는 점을 설명하고 있으므로, 인터넷의 독특한 특성을 강조하는 ②번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 블로그 하고, 브이로그 하고, 판매하라: 디지털 비즈니스의 부상
② 클릭하고, 공유하고, 연결하라: 인터넷을 독특하게 만드는 것
③ 인터넷 시대 전통 매체와의 조화
④ 왜 소셜 네트워킹 사이트가 세상을 장악하고 있는가
⑤ 미래를 업로드하기: 전자상거래가 세상을 바꾼 방식

question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If there is little or no diversity of views, and all scientists see, think, and question the world in a similar way, then they will not, as a community, be as objective as they maintain they are, or at least aspire to be. The solution is that there should be far greater diversity in the practice of science: in gender, ethnicity, and social and cultural backgrounds. Science works because it is carried out by people who pursue their curiosity about the natural world and test their and each other's ideas from __________. When science is done by a diverse group of people, and if consensus builds up about a particular area of scientific knowledge, then we can have more confidence in its objectivity and truth.
options: ① a broad set of scientific tools and equipment
② a consistent use of standardized research methods
③ a wide range of different viewpoints and approaches
④ a fixed seope of uniform perspectives and techniques
⑤ a complete understanding of natural laws and principles
explanation: 과학 공동체가 객관성을 유지하기 위해서는 성별, 인종, 사회적 및 문화적 배경 등 다양한 관점이 필요하다고 설명하고 있습니다. 과학이 제대로 작동하는 이유는 다양한 사람들이 서로의 아이디어를 '폭넓은 다양한 관점과 접근 방식(a wide range of different viewpoints and approaches)'에서 테스트하기 때문입니다.
options_translation: ① 광범위한 과학적 도구와 장비 세트
② 표준화된 연구 방법의 일관된 사용
③ 폭넓고 다양한 관점과 접근 방식
④ 균일한 관점과 기술의 고정된 범위
⑤ 자연 법칙과 원리에 대한 완전한 이해

question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Brains are expensive in terms of energy. Twenty percent of the calories we consume are used to power the brain. So brains try to operate in the most energy-efficient way possible, and that means processing only the minimum amount of information from our senses that we need to navigate the world. Neuroscientists weren't the first to discover that fixing your gaze on something is no guarantee of seeing it. Magicians figured this out long ago. By directing your attention, they perform tricks with their hands in full view. Their actions should give away the game, but they can rest assured that ____________. This all helps to explain the prevalence of traffic accidents in which drivers hit pedestrians in plain view, or collide with cars directly in front of them. In many of these cases, the eyes are pointed in the right direction, but the brain isn't seeing what's really out there.
options: ① human brain takes in just the fraction of the visual input
② your eyes capture every detail in perfect clarity all the time
③ stage magic is performed using their real supernatural powers

question: 14. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they are exceptionally talented. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
options: ① Newton's position and role in science field
② Discoveries Enhanced by Quality Collaborators
③ Natural Gift for Facilitating Multiple Discoveries
④ How Past Achievements Shape Future Success
⑤ Reassessing Scientific Success Through the Matthew Effect
explanation: 이 글은 위대한 과학자들이 여러 번의 성공을 거두는 현상을 두 가지 관점에서 설명하고 있습니다. 하나는 초기 성공이 더 많은 기회를 불러온다는 '마태 효과(Matthew effect)'이고, 다른 하나는 과학자의 '천부적인 재능(exceptional talent)'이 초기 성공과 후기 성공 모두의 원인이라는 대안적 설명입니다. 글의 후반부에서 마태 효과에 대해 의문을 제기하며 결국 숨겨진 재능이 다수의 발견을 가능하게 한다는 점을 시사하고 있으므로, '다수의 발견을 가능하게 하는 타고난 재능(Natural Gift for Facilitating Multiple Discoveries)'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.

There will be, however, occasions where it is appropriate, even necessary, to coin special uses through what philosophers call stimulative definition. <u>This</u> would be the case in which the current lexicon is not able to make distinctions that you think are philosophically important. For example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something that the person having it has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories: I would have a memory-type experience, but this would not be of something I had actually experienced. To call this a memory would be misleading. For this reason, philosophers have coined the special term 'quasi-memory' to refer to these hypothetical memory-like experiences.

question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

passage: Commitment is the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life. Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby facilitating the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. Moreover, commitments make people willing to perform actions that they would not otherwise perform. For example, a taxi driver picks up his clients and transports them to their desired destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a credible commitment to pay her at the end of the month. Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to taking various measures to sustain the currency in question. explanation: 이 글은 사회적 약속(commitment)이 인간 사회를 지탱하는 역할을 한다는 내용입니다. 사회적 제도들이 유지되기 위해서는 이러한 약속들이 믿을 만해야 한다는 문맥이 형성되므로, '신뢰성'을 뜻하는 'credibility'가 적절합니다.

question: 29. 다음 글에서 아래 영영 풀이로 설명한 단어를 찾아 쓰시오. [25년 3월 38번]
passage: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much a creative process. A conjecture is a philosophical invention, cooked up rather mystically by the mind through the mental computation we call careful contemplation. However, until the hypothesis is tested against reality, it is not yet truly knowledge; it is just information that represents speculation. Knowledge is information that has demonstrated its usefulness. It is what is left over after cycles of experimental testing have eliminated false theories. As scientists continually test their hypotheses and modify their models to account for new and surprising data, a kind of "learning loop" emerges that statisticians call Bayesian updating. Based on Bayes' Rule, developed by eighteenth-century English statistician and philosopher Thomas Bayes, Bayesian updating refers to a mathematical process whereby an accepted theory or predictive model gets increasingly accurate through the repetitive testing of competing variants of that theory.

question: 3. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]

question: 4. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은 모두 몇 개인지 고른 것은?

question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: We tend to break up time into units, such as weeks, months, and seasons: in a series of studies among farmers in India and students in North America, psychologists found that if a deadline is on the other side of a "break" - such as in the New Year - we're more likely to see it as remote, and, as a result, ___________________________________. What you need to do in that situation is find another way to think about the timeframe. For example, if it's November and the deadline is in January, it's better to tell yourself you have to get it done "this winter" rather than "next year." The best approach is to view deadlines as a challenge that you have to meet within a period that's imminent. That way the stress is more manageable, and you have a better chance of starting - and therefore finishing - in good time.
options: ① do our task very quickly
② plan and act more strategically
③ do our best to meet the deadline
④ be less ready to jump into action
⑤ complete all necessary preparations
explanation: 사람들은 마감 기한이 새로운 해나 새로운 시즌처럼 '경계' 너머에 있을 때 그것을 더 멀게 느끼는 경향이 있습니다. 마감이 멀게 느껴지면 당장 시작하려는 마음이 줄어들게 되므로, 빈칸에는 '행동에 착수할 준비가 덜 된다'는 의미의 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리의 과업을 매우 빠르게 수행한다
② 더 전략적으로 계획하고 행동한다
③ 마감 기한을 맞추기 위해 최선을 다한다
④ 즉각 행동에 나설 준비가 덜 된다
⑤ 모든 필요한 준비를 마친다

question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: North America's native cuisine met the same ⓐ<u>fortunate</u> fate as its native people, save for a few relics like the Thanksgiving turkey. Certainly, we still have ⓑ<u>regional</u> specialties, but the Carolina barbecue will almost certainly have California tomatoes in its sauce, and the Louisiana gumbo is just as likely to contain Indonesian farmed shrimp. If either of these shows up on a fastfood menu with lots of added fats or HFCS, we seem ⓒ<u>unable</u> either to discern or resist the corruption. We have yet to come up with a strong set of generalized norms, passed down through families, for savoring and sensibly consuming what our land and climate give us. We have, instead, a string of ⓓ<u>fad</u> diets convulsing our bookstores and bellies, one after another, at the scale of the national best seller. Nine out of ten nutritionists view this as evidence that we have entirely ⓔ<u>lost</u> our marbles.
explanation: 북미의 토착 요리가 토착민들과 마찬가지로 불행한 운명을 맞이했다는 흐름이 되어야 하므로, ⓐ fortunate(운이 좋은)는 unfortunate(불행한)와 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Perhaps, the advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the workplace may bode well for Emotional Intelligence (EI). As AI gains momentum and replaces people in jobs at every level, predictions are, there will be a premium placed on people who have high ability in El. The emotional messages people send and respond to while interacting are, at this point, far beyond the ability of Al programs to mimic. As we get further into the age of the smart machine, it is likely that sensing and managing emotions will remain one type of intelligence that puzzles Al. This means people and jobs involving EI are safe from being taken over by machines. In a survey, almost three out of four executives see EI as a "must-have" skill for the workplace in the future as the automatizing of routine tasks bumps up against the impossibility of creating effective AI for activities that require emotional skill.
options: ① drawbacks of Al
② negative effects of AI
③ technology exceeding EI
④ EI valuable in future workplaces
⑤ Al involving skills EI cannot replicate
explanation: 이 글은 인공지능(AI)이 업무 환경에 도입되더라도 감정 지능(EI)은 AI가 모방하기 어려운 영역이며, 미래의 직장에서도 매우 가치 있는 기술로 남을 것이라는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 '미래 직장에서 가치 있는 감정 지능'인 ④번입니다.
options_translation: AI의 결점
AI의 부정적 효과
EI를 능가하는 기술
미래 직장에서 가치 있는 EI
EI가 복제할 수 없는 기술을 포함하는 AI

question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
passage: Education must focus on the trunk of the tree of knowledge, revealing the ways in which the branches, twigs, and leaves all ⓐ<u>emerge</u> from a common core. Tools for thinking stem from this core, providing a common language, with which practitioners in different fields may ⓑ<u>share</u> their experience of the process of innovation and discover links between their creative activities. When the same terms are employed across the curriculum, students begin to ⓒ<u>isolate</u> different subjects and classes. If they practice abstracting in writing class, if they work on abstracting in painting or drawing class, and if, in all cases, they call it abstracting, they begin to understand how to think ⓓ<u>beyond</u> disciplinary boundaries. They see how to transform their thoughts from one mode of conception and expression to another. Linking the disciplines comes naturally when the terms and tools are presented as part of a ⓔ<u>universal</u> imagination.
explanation: 교육이 지식의 공통 핵심(core)에 집중하고 커리큘럼 전반에 걸쳐 동일한 용어를 사용하면, 학생들은 서로 다른 과목들 사이의 연결 고리를 발견하게 됩니다. 따라서 ⓒ isolate(고립시키다, 분리하다)는 긍정적인 연결의 의미를 담은 link 혹은 connect와 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 흐름상 적절합니다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
passage: Research psychologists often work with self-report data, made up of participants' verbal accounts of their behavior. (A) This is the case whenever questionnaires, interviews, or personality inventories are used to measure variables. (B) Self-report methods can be quite useful. They take advantage of the fact that people have a unique opportunity to observe themselves full-time. (C) One of the most problematic of these distortions is the social desirability bias, which is a tendency to give socially approved answers to questions about oneself. (D) Subjects who are influenced by this bias work overtime trying to create a favorable impression, especially when subjects are asked about sensitive issues. (E) For example, many survey respondents will report that they voted in an election or gave to a charity when in fact it is possible to determine that they did not.
insertion_sentence: However, self-reports can be plagued by several kinds of distortion.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장은 자기 보고(self-reports)가 여러 종류의 왜곡(distortion)에 의해 시달릴 수 있다는 역접의 내용입니다. (B)까지는 자기 보고 방식의 유용성을 설명하고 있으며, (C) 바로 뒤의 문장에서 '이러한 왜곡들 중 가장 문제가 되는 것 중 하나는...'이라며 distortion에 대해 구체적으로 언급하기 시작하므로 주어진 문장은 (C) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 23. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We collect stamps, coins, vintage cars even when they serve no practical purpose. The post office doesn't accept the old stamps, the banks don't take old coins, and the vintage cars are no longer allowed on the road. These are all side issues; the attraction is that they are in short supply. In one study, students were asked to arrange ten posters in order of attractiveness - with the agreement that afterward they could keep one poster as a reward for their participation. Five minutes later, they were told that the poster with the third highest rating was no longer available. Then they were asked to judge all ten from scratch. The poster that was no longer available was suddenly classified as the most beautiful. In psychology, this phenomenon is called reactance: when we are deprived of an option, we _______________________________.
options: ① keep silent
② abruptly feel lonely
③ gradually find a peace of mind
④ constantly think it more hateful
⑤ suddenly consider it more charming
explanation: 글은 우리가 더 이상 선택할 수 없게 된 대상에 대해 더 높은 가치를 부여하는 심리적 현상인 '저항(reactance)'을 설명하고 있습니다. 실험에서 학생들이 선택할 수 없게 된 3순위 포스터를 가장 아름다운 것으로 재평가한 사례를 통해, 선택권이 박탈되었을 때 그 대상을 더 매력적으로 느끼게 된다는 결론을 도출할 수 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '갑자기 그것을 더 매력적으로 여긴다'는 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 침묵을 지킨다
② 갑자기 외로움을 느낀다
③ 점차 마음의 평화를 찾는다
④ 끊임없이 그것을 더 밉게 생각한다
⑤ 갑자기 그것을 더 매력적이라고 여긴다

question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: If we've invested in something that hasn't repaid us - be it money in a failing venture, or time in an unhappy relationship - we find it very ⓐ<u>difficult</u> to walk away. This is the sunk cost fallacy. Our instinct is to continue investing money or time as we hope that our investment will prove to be worthwhile in the end. Giving up would mean acknowledging that we've wasted something we can't get back, and that thought is so painful that we prefer to ⓑ<u>avoid</u> it if we can. The problem, of course, is that if something really is a bad bet, then staying with it simply ⓒ<u>increases</u> the amount we lose. Rather than walk away from a bad five-year relationship, for example, we turn it into a bad 10-year relationship; rather than accept that we've lost a thousand dollars, we lay down another thousand and ⓓ<u>regain</u> that too. In the end, by delaying the pain of admitting our problem, we only add to it. Sometimes we just have to ⓔ<u>cut</u> our losses.
explanation: 이 글은 매몰 비용 오류(sunk cost fallacy)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 문맥상 이미 천 달러를 잃은 것을 받아들이지 못하고 추가로 천 달러를 더 투자하여 그 금액마저 '잃게 된다'는 내용이 되어야 흐름상 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 'regain(되찾다)'은 'lose(잃다)'와 같은 단어로 고쳐져야 합니다.

question: 25. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis. (A) The other questionable assumption is that most migration is involuntary-people fleeing natural or man-made disasters. The reality, however, is more complex, and many migrants are simply seeking greater economic opportunity. (B) Of course migration can and does create social and economic problems. But migration can also be a solution for many preexisting problems. (C) For example, out-migration generally redistributes workers from places of labor surplus to areas where there is greater demand or more opportunity. Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to endure hardship in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin. (D) Most research that examines long-term outcomes of migration, including remittances and intergenerational mobility, finds positive "long-term" effects on places of origin and destination. (E)
insertion_sentence: For example, migrants are assumed to overcrowd cities, clog up labor markets, and increase poverty.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 이주(migration)가 도시 혼잡, 노동 시장 마비, 빈곤 증가 등의 문제를 일으킨다는 가정을 예로 들고 있습니다. 이는 이주가 대중 매체 등에서 '문제'나 '위기'로 보도된다는 도입부의 구체적인 사례에 해당합니다. 또한 바로 뒤의 (A) 문장에서 "The other questionable assumption(그 외의 다른 의심스러운 가정)"이라는 표현이 나오려면, 그 앞에 첫 번째 가정이 언급되어야 하므로 (A) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: The study of emotions and decision making is now of considerable importance. This involves the application of various tools ⓐ<u>afforded</u> by neuroscience. One important stream of the literature examines people with brain damage and how damage to particular parts of the brain known to be responsible for particular cognitive functions impacts on decision making. One example of this research is the work of Antonio Damasio, ⓑ<u>who</u> finds that when the emotional part of the brain is damaged, this actually reduces the efficacy of decision making. Good decisions are a product of the emotional part of the brain working in conjunction with the deliberative part. This contradicts the assumptions of conventional economics, ⓒ<u>where</u> emotions play a negative role in the decision-making process. Here it is assumed that decision making can be modeled as being ⓓ<u>generated</u> in a stoic, unemotional fashion, and that's why decisions tend to be optimal. But the evidence suggests ⓔ<u>what</u> emotions actually play an important and, often, a positive role in decision making.
explanation: ⑤번의 what이 이끄는 절 뒤를 보면, emotions(주어) play(동사) an important and positive role(목적어)로 구성된 완전한 문장입니다. 타동사 suggests의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌며 뒤가 완전할 때는 관계대명사 what이 아닌 접속사 that을 사용해야 합니다. ⓐ는 과거분사로 tools를 수식하고, ⓑ는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사, ⓒ는 관계부사, ⓓ는 수동태 동명사로 모두 어법상 적절합니다.

question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When evaluating a policy, people tend to concentrate on how the policy will fix some particular problem while ignoring or downplaying other effects it may have. Economists often refer to this situation as The Law of Unintended Consequences. For instance, suppose that you impose a tariff on imported steel in order to protect the jobs of domestic steelworkers. If you impose a high enough tariff, their jobs will indeed be protected from competition by foreign steel companies. But an unintended consequence is that the jobs of some autoworkers will be lost to foreign competition. Why? The tariff that protects steelworkers raises the price of the steel that domestic automobile makers need to build their cars. As a result, domestic automobile manufacturers have to raise the prices of their cars, making them relatively less attractive than foreign cars. Raising prices tends to reduce domestic car sales, so some domestic autoworkers lose their jobs.
options: ① All Policy Effects Are Fully Predicted
② Tariffs Always Boost the Entire Economy
③ Protecting One Industry Has No Downsides
④ Intended Gains Often Overshadow Hidden Costs
⑤ Tariffs Help Both Steel and Auto Workers Equally
explanation: 이 글은 정책을 평가할 때 사람들이 특정 문제를 해결하는 효과에만 집중하고 다른 부수적인 효과(의도치 않은 결과)를 무시하는 경향이 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 철강 관세 부과가 철강 노동자의 일자리는 보호하지만 자동차 산업의 비용 상승을 초래하여 자동차 노동자의 일자리를 잃게 만드는 예시를 통해 '의도된 이득이 숨겨진 비용(의도치 않은 손실)을 가리는 현상'을 다루고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 모든 정책 효과는 완전히 예측된다
② 관세는 항상 전체 경제를 부양시킨다
③ 한 산업을 보호하는 것에는 단점이 없다
④ 의도된 이득이 종종 숨겨진 비용을 가린다
⑤ 관세는 철강 및 자동차 노동자 모두를 똑같이 돕는다

question: 2. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: In adolescence many of us had the experience of falling under the sway of a great book or writer. We became entranced by the novel ideas in the book, and because we were so open to influence, these early encounters with exciting ideas sank deeply into our minds and became part of our own thought processes, affecting us decades after we absorbed them. Such influences enriched our mental landscape, and in fact our intelligence depends on the ability to absorb the lessons and ideas of those who are older and wiser. Just as the body tightens with age, however, so does the mind. And just as our sense of weakness and vulnerability motivated the desire to learn, so does our creeping sense of superiority slowly close us off to new ideas and influences. Some may advocate that we all become more skeptical in the modern world, but in fact a far greater danger comes from the increasing closing of the mind that burdens us as individuals as we get older, and seems to be burdening our culture in general.*entrance 매료시키다
options: ① As the body becomes less flexible with age, so does the mind, closing off the individual to new influences.
② Mental closure due to aging poses a greater threat to intellectual and cultural growth.
③ The mental development of young people relies on absorbing insights from older, wiser individuals.
④ Increasing skepticism is essential to intellectual growth, especially in modern times.
⑤ As individuals age, a growing sense of intellectual superiority can hinder openness to new ideas, leading to mental rigidity.
explanation: 본문 마지막 부분에서 필자는 현대 사회에서 우리가 더 회의적이 되어야 한다고 주장하는 사람들도 있지만, 실제로는 나이가 들면서 마음이 닫히는 것이 더 큰 위험이라고 언급하고 있습니다. 즉, 회의주의가 지적 성장에 필수적이라는 것은 본문의 내용과 정반대이거나 본문에서 경계하는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 나이가 들면서 신체가 덜 유연해지듯이 정신도 그러하며, 개인을 새로운 영향력으로부터 차단한다.
② 노화로 인한 정신적 폐쇄는 지적 및 문화적 성장에 더 큰 위협이 된다.
③ 젊은이들의 정신 발달은 더 나이가 많고 지혜로운 사람들의 통찰력을 흡수하는 데 의존한다.
④ 증가하는 회의주의는 특히 현대에 지적 성장에 필수적이다.
⑤ 개인이 나이가 들면서 커지는 지적 우월감은 새로운 아이디어에 대한 개방성을 방해하여 정신적 경직성을 초래할 수 있다.

question: 3. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Human decision-making differs from rational decision-making in terms of outcomes. A process is considered rational if it consistently makes the best possible choice based on the information available and an ideal standard of performance. (A)_________, rational processes strictly follow established rules, assuming those rules are always right. (B)_________, human processes rely on instinct, intuition, and other factors that may ignore the rules or current data. (C)_________, while the rational way to drive is to obey all traffic laws, real world traffic often doesn't work that way ─ if you strictly follow every rule, you might get stuck because other drivers don't. So, for a self-driving car to work well, it needs to behave more like a human driver than a perfectly rational one,
options: ① More over / Similarly / For example
② In other words / In contrast / For instance
③ Even so / Conversely / However
④ Similarly / As a result / Therefore
⑤ Incidentally / Namely / Thus
explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 합리적 의사결정의 정의를 내리고, (A) 뒤에서 이를 재진술하며 규칙을 엄격히 따른다고 했으므로 '다시 말해서(In other words)'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞의 합리적 과정과 대조적으로 인간의 과정은 직관에 의존한다고 설명하므로 '대조적으로(In contrast)'가 적절합니다. (C) 뒤에서 운전의 구체적인 상황을 예로 들어 설명하고 있으므로 '예를 들어(For instance)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 더욱이 / 유사하게 / 예를 들어
② 다시 말해서 / 대조적으로 / 예를 들어
③ 그렇다 하더라도 / 반대로 / 하지만
④ 유사하게 / 결과적으로 / 그러므로
⑤ 덧붙여 말하자면 / 즉 / 따라서

question: 4. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Before getting licensed to drive a cab in London, a person has to pass an incredibly difficult test with an intimidating name ─ "The Knowledge". The test involves memorizing the layout of more than 20,000 streets in the Greater London area ─ a feat that involves an incredible amount of memory resources. In fact, fewer than 50 percent of the people who sign up for taxi driver training pass the test, even after spending two or three years studying for it! And as it turns out, the brains of London cabbies are different from non-cab-driving humans in ways that ________________________________________. In fact, the part of the brain that has been most frequently associated with spatial memory, the tail of the sea horse-shaped brain region called the hippocampus, is bigger than average in these taxi drivers.*herculean 초인적인 **hippocampus 해마
options: ① mirror the cognitive demands of their training
② reflect accumulated driving hours, not training
③ suggest overall brain growth from job exposure
④ demonstrate the genetic uniqueness of taxi drivers
⑤ imply an inherent trait rather than a learned change
explanation: 런던 택시 운전사들은 'The Knowledge'라는 매우 어려운 시험을 통과하기 위해 수만 개의 거리 레이아웃을 암기해야 합니다. 이 과정에서 엄청난 기억 자원이 사용되는데, 연구 결과 이들의 해마(공간 기억 담당 부위)가 일반인보다 더 크다는 것이 밝혀졌습니다. 이는 뇌 구조가 그들이 받은 훈련의 인지적 요구치를 반영하여 변화했음을 보여주므로 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그들의 훈련에 따른 인지적 요구를 반영한다
② 훈련이 아닌, 축적된 운전 시간을 반영한다
③ 직업 노출에 따른 전반적인 뇌 성장을 암시한다
④ 택시 운전사들의 유전적 독특함을 보여준다

question: 5. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: People behave in highly predictable ways when they experience certain thoughts. When they agree, they nod their heads. So far, no surprise, but according to an area of research known as "proprioceptive psychology," the process also works in reverse. Get people to behave in a certain way and ______________________________________________________. The idea was initially controversial, but fortunately it was supported by a compelling experiment. Participants in a study were asked to fixate on various products moving across a large computer screen and then indicate whether the items appealed to them. Some of the items moved vertically (causing the participants to nod their heads while watching), and others moved horizontally (resulting in a side-to-side head movement). Participants preferred vertically moving products without being aware that their "yes" and "no" head movements had played a key role in their decisions.
options: ① you manipulate them into lying
② you force them to act against their will
③ you cause them to stop thinking critically
④ you make them forget their original thoughts
⑤ you guide their thoughts in a specific direction
explanation: 본문은 고유 수용 심리학(proprioceptive psychology)을 설명하며, 행동이 생각에 영향을 줄 수 있음을 보여줍니다. 실험에서 수직으로 움직이는 제품을 보며 고개를 끄덕인 참가자들이 해당 제품을 더 선호하게 된 결과는, 특정한 행동을 유도함으로써 사람들의 생각을 특정 방향으로 이끌 수 있음을 증명합니다. 따라서 ⑤번이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 그들이 거짓말을 하도록 조종한다
② 그들이 의지에 반해 행동하도록 강요한다
③ 그들이 비판적으로 생각하는 것을 멈추게 한다
④ 그들이 원래 가졌던 생각을 잊게 만든다
⑤ 그들의 생각을 특정 방향으로 유도한다

question: 6. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: If you drive down a busy street, you will find many competing businesses, often right next to one another. For example, in most places a consumer in search of a quick meal has many choices, and more fast-food restaurants appear all the time. (A) These competing firms advertise heavily. (B) However, this misconception doesn't account for why firms advertise. (C) In markets where competitors sell slightly differentiated products, advertising enables firms to inform their customers about new products and services. (D) Yes, costs rise, but consumers also gain information to help make purchasing decisions. (E) Consumers also benefit from added variety, and we all get a product that's pretty close to our vision of a perfect good ─ and no other market structure delivers that outcome.
insertion_sentence: The temptation is to see advertising as driving up the price of a product without any benefit to the consumer.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장은 '광고가 소비자에게 아무런 이득 없이 제품의 가격만 올리는 것으로 보려는 유혹이 있다'는 내용으로, 광고에 대한 일반적인 오해를 언급하고 있습니다. 글의 (B) 뒤에 나오는 'However, this misconception(하지만 이러한 오해는...)'이라는 표현이 주어진 문장의 내용을 직접적으로 가리키고 있으므로, 주어진 문장은 (B) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 7. 다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control. Scientists manipulate a variable of interest, and see if there's a difference. At the same time, they attempt to control for the potential effects of all other variables. The importance of controlled experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often correlated. For example, people who take vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who don't take vitamins. As a result, if we want to study the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely observe the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to create a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world. That's just what scientific experiments do. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while holding everything else constant.
summary_sentence: To figure out what really (A)__________ what, scientists change one variable while keeping all others (B)__________. That way, they can be sure any (C)__________ is from the thing they changed.
options: ① describes / constant / impact
② affects / the same / challenge
③ causes / fixed / effect
④ copies / stable / result
⑤ determines / inconsistent / change
explanation: 이 글은 실험법의 근본적인 성격이 조작과 통제임을 설명하고 있습니다. 과학자들은 사건의 근본적인 원인을 찾기 위해 다른 변수들을 고정(통제)한 채 특정 변수 하나만을 변화시킵니다. 따라서 요약문에서 (A)는 무엇이 무엇을 '야기하는지(causes)'를 알아내기 위해, (B)는 다른 모든 변수를 '고정된(fixed)' 상태로 유지하며, (C)는 그 결과로 나타나는 '효과(effect)'가 조작된 변수로부터 온 것임을 확신할 수 있다는 내용이 되어야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 묘사하다 / 일정한 / 영향
② 영향을 미치다 / 똑같은 / 도전
③ 야기하다 / 고정된 / 효과
④ 복사하다 / 안정적인 / 결과
⑤ 결정하다 / 일관성 없는 / 변화

question: 8. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Managers often attempt to analyze employee behavior by playing the role of a psychologist, trying to determine the reasons behind certain actions. While showing empathy and striving to see things from an employee's perspective can be valuable, especially in challenging situations, it's important to focus on job-related behaviors rather than personal character flaws. Managers should avoid advising employees to alter their personality traits. Instead, they should recommend specific, appropriate behaviors that align better with workplace expectations. For instance, rather than labeling someone as "unreliable," it is more constructive to point out observable facts like "you've arrived late to work seven times this month." Changing behaviors is generally more achievable for employees than changing their __________.
options: ① skills
② habits
③ nature
④ routine
⑤ purpose

options_translation: ① 기술
② 습관
③ 본성
④ 일상
⑤ 목적

question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: I have a feeling that fungi might be a bit more forward-thinking than the trees they live with. Trees often compete with each other, especially across different species. Let's say beech trees, which are native to Central Europe, end up outcompeting most other trees in those forests. At first glance, that might seem like a success. But what if a new disease were to strike and wipe out the beeches? In that case, wouldn't it actually be better if some other species ─ like oaks, maples, or firs ─ were still around? They could keep growing and provide the shade young beeches need to survive. In other words, ___________ offers stability and resilience in ancient forests. question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: The emergence of new technologies has both advantages and drawbacks when it comes to sustainable development. Effectively managing technological resources requires a comprehensive understanding of these impacts. ⓐMany people prefer traditional methods over new technologies because they believe older techniques are more reliable. ⓑInnovations in fields like nuclear energy and agriculture demonstrate that while technology can bring environmental benefits, it can also pose risks to ecosystems and human health. ⓒTechnological change also significantly affects society. ⓓSince the Industrial Revolution, advancements have transformed the types of skills needed in the workforce, leading to the creation of some jobs while eliminating others, thereby influencing employment trends. ⓔIt is essential to evaluate new technologies by considering all of their potential effects ─ both positive and negative.

question: 11. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: The more people are forced to engage in tasks they don't want to do, the more likely they are to contribute to a negative atmosphere for themselves and those around them. ⓐWhen you dislike what you're doing but must do it anyway, you face a choice: continue to resent it or accept that it's necessary. ⓑIn either case, the task gets done. ⓒSome people believe that setting strict deadlines is the best way to ensure productivity in the workplace. ⓓHowever, approaching it with resentment can lead to growing bitterness toward yourself and others, while approaching it with acceptance fosters self-compassion and opens the door to discovering better ways to handle the task. ⓔIf you choose to accept the responsibility, begin by viewing your situation as a gift from life ─ doing so can transform the experience into a meaningful lesson in acceptance.
explanation: 이 글은 원치 않는 일을 해야 할 때의 태도(분노 vs. 수용)가 미치는 영향에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 분노를 가지고 임하면 본인과 주변에 부정적인 영향을 미치지만, 수용하는 태도를 가지면 자기 연민과 더 나은 해결책을 찾게 된다는 내용입니다. 반면 ③번 문장은 '직장에서의 생산성을 보장하기 위해 엄격한 마감 기한을 설정하는 것이 최선이다'라는 내용으로, 업무를 대하는 심리적 태도라는 글의 주제와 무관한 직무 효율성에 대해 말하고 있으므로 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

question: 12. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 13. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Everyone's heard the expression don't let the perfect become the enemy of the good. If you want to get over an obstacle so that your idea can become the solution-based policy you've long dreamed of, you can't have an all-or-nothing mentality. You have to be willing to alter your idea and let others influence its outcome. You have to be okay with the outcome being a little different, even a little less, than you wanted. Say you're pushing for a clean water act. Even if what emerges isn't as well-funded as you wished, or doesn't match how you originally conceived the bill, you'll have still succeeded in ensuring that kids in troubled areas have access to clean water. That's what counts, that they will be safer because of your idea and your effort. Is it perfect? No. Is there more work to be done? Absolutely. But in almost every case, helping move the needle forward is vastly better than not helping at all.

question: 14. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It's remarkable that positive fantasies help us relax to such an extent that it shows up in physiological tests. question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

question: 16. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: The rise of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the workplace could actually enhance the value of Emotional Intelligence (EI). As AI continues to advance and take over roles across various levels, experts predict that individuals with strong EI will become increasingly sought after. The emotional cues exchanged during human interactions remain far too complex for AI to accurately replicate. As we move deeper into the era of intelligent machines, the ability to understand and regulate emotions is likely to remain a uniquely human skill─one that AI still struggles to grasp. Consequently, jobs that rely heavily on EI are expected to be more resistant to automation. Supporting this, a survey revealed that nearly 75% of executives consider EI an essential skill for the future workplace, especially as machines take over repetitive tasks but fall short in handling emotionally driven responsibilities.
options: ① The growing presence of AI in the workplace may actually benefit emotional intelligence.
② The emotional nuances present in human interactions are beyond AI's ability to fully mimic.
③ Even in the age of smart machines, emotional awareness and regulation remain uniquely human abilities.
④ Nearly three-quarters of surveyed executives believe EI will be a critical skill in future work environments.
⑤ Jobs that require empathy and emotional awareness are at high risk of automation.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 감성 지능(EI)에 크게 의존하는 직업들은 자동화에 대해 더 저항력이 있을 것으로 예상된다고 언급되어 있습니다. 따라서 공감과 감정 인식을 필요로 하는 직업이 자동화의 위험이 높다는 5번은 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

② 인간 상호 작용에 존재하는 감정적 미묘함은 AI가 완전히 모방할 수 있는 능력을 넘어선다.
③ 지능형 기계의 시대에도 감정 인식 및 조절은 독특하게 인간의 능력으로 남아 있을 가능성이 크다.
④ 설문 조사에 참여한 임원들의 거의 4분의 3은 EI가 미래 작업 환경에서 필수적인 기술이 될 것이라고 믿는다.
⑤ 공감과 감정 인식을 필요로 하는 직업은 자동화의 위험이 높다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: If cooking is as central to human identity, biology, and culture as the biological anthropologist Richard Wrangham suggests, it stands to reason that the decline of cooking in our time would have serious consequences for modern life, and so it has. Are they all bad? Not at all. The outsourcing of much of the work of cooking to corporations has relieved women of what has traditionally been their exclusive responsibility for feeding the family, making it easier for them to work outside the home and have careers. It has headed off many of the domestic conflicts that such a large shift in gender roles and family dynamics was bound to spark. It has relieved other pressures in the household, including longer workdays and overscheduled children, and saved us time that we can now invest in other pursuits. It has also allowed us to diversify our diets substantially, making it possible even for people with no cooking skills and little money to enjoy a whole different cuisine. All that's required is a microwave.
options: ① Cooking has played a fundamental role in shaping human biology and culture.
② The outsourcing of cooking duties has increased the workload for women at home.
③ The decrease in home cooking today has led to significant changes in modern life.
④ Reducing the burden of cooking has helped ease domestic tensions related to shifting gender roles.
⑤ Ready-made meals and convenience foods have allowed people with limited cooking skills or money to enjoy diverse cuisines.

question: 22. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하도록 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: The irony of early democracy in Europe is that it thrived and prospered precisely because European rulers for a very long time were remarkably weak. For more than a millennium after the fall of Rome, European rulers lacked the ability to assess what their people were producing and to levy substantial taxes based on this. The most striking way to illustrate European weakness is to show how little revenue they collected. Europeans would eventually develop strong systems of revenue collection, but it took them an awfully long time to do so. In medieval times, and for part of the early modern era, Chinese emperors and Muslim caliphs were able to extract much more of economic production than any European ruler with the exception of small city-states.*levy 부과하다**caliph 칼리프(과거 이슬람 국가의 몽치자)

question: 23. 다음 글의 요지를 주어진 어휘를 사용하여 완성하시오. (단, <조건>을 충족할 것)
passage: Correlations are powerful because the insights they offer are relatively clear. These insights are often covered up when we bring causality back into the picture, For instance, a used-car dealer supplied data to statisticians to predict which of the vehicles available for purchase at an auction were likely to have problems. A correlation analysis showed that orange-colored cars were far less likely to have defects. Even as we read this, we already think about why it might be so: Are orange-colored car owners likely to be car enthusiasts and take better care of their vehicles? Or, is it because orange-colored cars are more noticeable on the road and therefore less likely to be in accidents, so they're in better condition when resold? Quickly we are caught in a web of competing causal hypotheses. But our attempts to illuminate things this way only make them cloudier. Correlations exist: we can show them mathematically. We can't easily do the same for causal links. So we would do well to hold off from trying to explain the reason behind the correlations.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것
단어를 추가, 누락, 변경할 경우 오답 처리됨
answer: The human tendency to speculate about causality can conceal correlations rather than clarify them
explanation: 지문의 핵심은 상관관계가 명확한 통찰력을 주지만, 인간이 그 원인(인과관계)을 추측하려고 하면 오히려 그 상관관계가 주는 통찰이 흐려진다는 것입니다. 따라서 '인과관계에 대해 추측하려는 인간의 성향은 상관관계를 명확하게 하기보다 숨길 수 있다'는 내용으로 문장을 구성해야 합니다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 문맥에 맞도록 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 주어진 어휘를 사용하여 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
passage: The size of a species is not accidental. It's a fine-tuned interaction between a species and the world it inhabits. question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.

question: 26. 다음 글의 문맥에 맞도록 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.

question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 단어를 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: Human beings like certainty. This liking stems from our ancient ancestors who needed to survive alongside saber-toothed tigers and poisonous berries. Our brains evolved to help us attend to threats, keep away from them, and remain alive afterward. In fact, we learned that the more certain we were about something, the better chance we had of making the right choice. Is this berry the same shape as last time? The same size? If I know for certain it is, my brain will direct me to eat it because I know it's safe. And if I'm uncertain, my brain will send out a danger alert to protect me. The dependence on certainty all those millennia ago ensured our survival to the present day, and the danger-alert system continues to protect us. This is achieved by our brains labeling new, vague, or unpredictable everyday events and experiences as uncertain. Our brains then generate sensations, thoughts, and action plans to keep us safe from the uncertain element, and we live to see another day.*saber-toothed tiger 검치호(검 모양의 송곳니를 가진 호랑이)

question: 4. 윗글의 내용을 바탕으로 화자의 심경 변화를 요약한 문장이다. 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어를 조건에 맞게 한 단어로 써서 문장을 완성하시오. [3.9점]
passage: My 10-year-old son appeared in desperate need of four quarters. "Four quarters? What on earth do you need four quarters for?" My tone bordered or irritation. I didn't want to be bothered with such a trivial demand. "ⓐ<u>Mom</u>! There's a garage sale up the street, and there's something I just gotta have! It only costs four quarters. Please?" I placed the coins in his hand with a sigh. Moments later, a little voice said, "Here, Mommy, this is for you." I looked down and saw a small painting in his hands-of a mother and her young son in each other's arms under a tree. At their feet the words: "This word starts with 'H', ends with 'B', and in between are 'O' and 'P.'" ⓑ<u>I</u> took a closer look at the painting, still touched by my son's thoughtfulness. Then, something caught my eye-hidden behind the frame was a small, yellowed envelope. I gently pulled it out, curiosity rising in my chest. Inside was an old, handwritten letter. As I unfolded it, I realized it was a note from a mother to her son, written during the war, over fifty years ago. The letter began, "My dearest boy, ⓒ<u>I</u> may be far away in uniform, but you're never far from my heart..." She had served as a soldier overseas-a mother writing to her child from the battlefield. Her words were filled with longing, strength, and an aching kind of love that only distance can grow. ⓓ<u>I</u> glanced at my own son, who stood smiling proudly, unaware that he had just handed me more than a painting-he had unknowingly delivered a piece of history, a small window into another mother's love across time. A wave of emotion crashed over ⓔ<u>me</u> all at once, too much to hold in. Tears filled my eyes-not from sadness, but from the unexpected beauty of the moment.
summary_sentence: At first, the narrator feels (A)__________ by her son's sudden request for money. However, upon receiving the thoughtful gift, she becomes (B)__________. Later, after discovering the hidden letter, she is (C)__________ by the emotional depth of the moment.
subjective_conditions: 각 단어는 주어진 첫 알파벳으로 시작할 것
explanation: 화자는 처음에 아들이 사소한 일로 돈을 요구하자 짜증이 났고(irritated), 아들의 사려 깊은 선물을 받고 감동을 받았으며(touched), 마지막에 편지를 발견하고는 그 순간의 감동적인 깊이에 압도되었습니다(overwhelmed).

question: 5. 윗글에 대한 설명이다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 3월 21번]
passage: If you had wanted to create a "self-driving" car in the 1950s, your best option might have been to strap a brick to the accelerator. Yes, the vehicle would have been able to move forward on its own, but it could not slow down, stop, or turn to avoid barriers. Obviously not ideal. But does that mean the entire concept of the self-driving car is not worth pursuing? No, it only means that at the time we did not yet have the tools we now possess to help enable vehicles to operate both autonomously and safely. This once-distant dream now seems within our reach. It is much the same story in medicine. Two decades ago, we were still taping bricks to accelerators. Today, we are approaching the point where we can begin to bring some appropriate technology to bear in ways that advance our understanding of patients as <u>unique individuals</u>. In fact, many patients are already wearing devices that monitor their conditions in real time, which allows doctors to talk to their patients in a specific, refined, and feedback-driven way that was not even possible a decade ago. Much like the evolution of self-driving vehicles, medicine is shifting from a one-size-fits-all model to one that adapts to each patient's needs and the real-time feedback provided by digital health devices.
summary_sentence: According to the passage, strapping a brick to the accelerator symbolizes __________ in both the car and medical contexts.
options: ① letting machines operate without human input
② using basic tools to keep machines from moving
③ early-stage efforts lacking full control and precision
④ designing vehicles that prioritize speed over accuracy
⑤ creating tools that respond to each patient's unique needs and feedback.
explanation: 본문에서 1950년대 자율주행 자동차를 만들기 위해 가속기에 벽돌을 묶는 행위는 앞으로 나아갈 수는 있지만 조절(감속, 정지, 회전)이 불가능한 상태를 의미합니다. 이는 의료 분야에서도 과거에 '적절한 기술'이 부족하여 환자 개개인에 맞춘 정밀한 대응이 어려웠던 '초기 단계의 불충분한 통제와 정밀도'를 상징합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간의 개입 없이 기계가 작동하게 하는 것
② 기계가 움직이지 못하게 하기 위해 기본적인 도구를 사용하는 것
③ 완전한 통제와 정밀함이 결여된 초기 단계의 노력
④ 정확성보다 속도를 우선시하는 차량을 설계하는 것
⑤ 각 환자의 고유한 요구와 피드백에 응답하는 도구를 만드는 것

question: 7. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)에 해당하는 구체적인 예시를 본문에서 각각 찾아 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: I suspect fungi are a little more forward "thinking" than their larger partners. (A)<u>Fungi</u>, though small and hidden underground, from intimate partnerships with (B)<u>their much larger tree companions</u>, supporting one another in sustaining the life of the forest. Among trees, each species fights other species. Let's assume the beeches native to Central Europe could emerge victorious in most forests there. Would this really be an advantage? What would happen if a new pathogen came along that infected most of the beeches and killed them? In that case, wouldn't it be more advantageous if there were a certain number of other species around - oaks, maples, or firs - that would continue to grow and provide the shade needed for a new generation of young beeches to sprout and grow up? Diversity provides security for ancient forests. Because fungi are also very dependent on stable conditions, they support other species underground and protect them from complete collapse to ensure that one species of tree doesn't manage to dominate. If things become dire for the fungi and their trees despite all this support, then the fungi can take radical action, as in the case of the pine and its partner Laccaria bicolor, a species of fungus. When there is a lack of nitrogen, the latter releases a deadly toxin into the soil, which causes minute organisms such as springtails to die and release the nitrogen tied up in their bodies, forcing them to become fertilizer for both the trees and the fungi.*springtail: 톡토기
explanation: 본문의 마지막 부분에서 균류와 나무의 관계에 대한 구체적인 예시로 소나무(the pine)와 그 파트너인 균류인 Laccaria bicolor가 언급되었습니다. 따라서 (A) 균류에 해당하는 예는 Laccaria bicolor이고, (B) 나무 동반자에 해당하는 예는 the pine입니다.

question: 9. 윗글에 대한 설명이다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem; they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
summary_sentence: In the passage, the author uses the expression "keeping the ball on a slope" to describe human intervention that maintains an ecosystem in an unstable state. If so, allowing the ecosystem to shift naturally without human intervention can be described as ____________________.
options: ① holding the ball in perfect balance
② letting the ball roll down the slope
③ lifting the ball uphill with increased force
④ building a wall to stop the ball completely
⑤ spinning the ball to change its direction randomly
explanation: 글에서 인간이 불안정한 상태(채소 수확 최대화)를 유지하기 위해 개입하는 것을 '경사면 위의 공을 유지하는 것(keeping the ball on a slope)'으로 비유했습니다. 따라서 인간의 개입이 멈추어 자연스럽게 더 안정적인 상태로 변하는 것은 경사면 위에 있던 공이 자연스럽게 굴러 내려가도록 내버려 두는 것에 비유할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 공을 완벽한 균형 상태로 유지하는 것
② 공이 경사면 아래로 굴러가게 내버려 두는 것
③ 더 큰 힘으로 공을 언덕 위로 들어 올리는 것
④ 공을 완전히 멈추기 위해 벽을 세우는 것
⑤ 무작위로 방향을 바꾸기 위해 공을 회전시키는 것

question: 10. 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [25년 3월 21번]

explanation: 지문에 따르면 재배자가 개입하는 목적은 채소 생산을 극대화하기 위함이며, 이 상태는 생태계 입장에서 '본질적으로 불안정한 상태(inherently unstable state)'입니다. 재배자가 개입을 멈추면 생태계는 자연스럽고 '더 안정적인 상태(more stable state)'로 돌아가려 합니다. 따라서 재배자가 '안정적이고 자연적인 생태계'를 유지하기 위해 개입한다는 ④번은 내용과 상반됩니다.
options_translation: ① 재배자는 곤충과 다른 동물들로부터 채소를 보호하기 위해 울타리를 사용한다.

question: 11. 다음 글을 읽고 글에 대한 설명의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We tend to overrate the impact of new technologies in part because older technologies have become absorbed into the furniture of our lives, so as to be almost invisible. Take the baby bottle. Here is a simple implement that has transformed a fundamental human experience for vast numbers of infants and mothers, yet it finds no place in our histories of technology. This technology might be thought of as a classic time-shifting device, as it enables mothers to exercise more control over the timing of feeding. It can also function to save time, as bottle feeding allows for someone else to substitute for the mother's time. Potentially, therefore, it has huge implications for the management of time in everyday life, yet it is entirely overlooked in discussions of high-speed society.
summary_sentence: The importance of technology is often judged by how innovative or visible it is, but the author emphasizes that technology which has fundamentally transformed the way we live is often actually _______ _______________________.
options: ① highly noticeable
② old and insignificant
③ familiar and deeply rooted
④ frequently failing in real use
⑤ complicated and scientifically advanced
explanation: 사람들은 신기술의 영향력은 과대평가하는 반면, 젖병과 같이 이미 일상의 일부가 되어 눈에 보이지 않게 된 오래된 기술들의 영향력은 간과하는 경향이 있다는 내용의 글입니다. 따라서 우리 삶을 근본적으로 변화시킨 기술은 실제로는 매우 '친숙하고 깊게 뿌리 박혀(familiar and deeply rooted)' 있다는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 매우 눈에 띄는
② 오래되고 하찮은
③ 친숙하고 깊게 뿌리 박힌
④ 실제 사용에서 빈번하게 실패하는
⑤ 복잡하고 과학적으로 진보된

question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 내용을 글의 흐름에 맞게 알파벳 기호를 순서대로 쓰시오.
passage: It's remarkable that positive fantasies help us relax to such an extent that it shows up in physiological tests.
ordered_passages: (A) That's because relaxation, while pleasant, often reduces the urgency and drive necessary for taking meaningful action. When you're at rest, your brain receives the message that no immediate effort is needed, making you less likely to pursue your goals actively.

(B) Therefore, the principle of "Dream it. Wish it. Do it." does not hold true, and now we know why: in dreaming it, you undercut the energy you need to do it. You put yourself in a temporary state of complete happiness, calmness - and inactivity.

(C) If you want to unwind, you can take some deep breaths, get a massage, or go for a walk - but you can also try simply closing your eyes and fantasizing about some future outcome that you might enjoy.
(D) But what about when your objective is to make your wish a reality? The last thing you want to be is relaxed.
explanation: 긍정적인 공상이 신체적 이완을 돕는다는 도입부 뒤에, (C)에서 이완을 원할 때 공상을 활용하는 예시를 듭니다. 하지만 (D)에서 목표를 실현하고자 할 때는 이완이 오히려 독이 된다는 반전이 나오고, (A)에서 이완이 행동에 필요한 긴박감을 줄이기 때문이라는 이유를 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 꿈꾸는 것이 행동 에너지를 약화시킨다는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 9. 다음 글에서 필자의 주장으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The study of emotions and decision making is now of considerable importance. This involves the application of various tools afforded by neuroscience. One important stream of the literature examines people with brain damage and how damage to particular parts of the brain known to be responsible for particular cognitive functions impacts on decision making. One example of this research is the work of Antonio Damasio, who finds that when the emotional part of the brain is damaged, this actually reduces the efficacy of decision making. Good decisions are a product of the emotional part of the brain working in conjunction with the deliberative part. This contradicts the assumptions of conventional economics, where emotions play a negative role in the decision-making process. Here it is assumed that decision making can be modeled as being generated in a stoic, unemotional fashion, and that's why decisions tend to be optimal. But the evidence suggests that emotions actually play an important and, often, a positive role in decision making.
options: ① Brain damage always causes better decision making.
② Neuroscience reveals flaws in traditional economic theories of rationality.
③ Economists believe emotions are key to good decisions.
