question: 10. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Steve Jobs used analogy to get people to embrace the new technology. Before computers, people worked in a physical world. We used paper and pens and physical file folders and so on. The idea of working in a virtual world was radically different. Or at least seemed radically different. What Jobs understood was that a physical office was fundamentally similar to a virtual office. To win over the masses, Jobs drew strong analogies between the traditional workplace people knew well with the new, unfamiliar virtual workplace. In the pre-computer workplace, when ideas were written on paper it was called . . . a document. When those documents needed to be stored they were put in . . . a folder. And those folders were kept on . . . a desk. Documents, folders, and desktops are the terms we use in our virtual work because Steve Jobs understood that using familiar terms would make the new technology easier to understand. The parallels between the physical and virtual workplace now seem obvious.
options: ① why Steve Jobs liked offices

explanation: 스티브 잡스는 사람들이 생소한 가상 세계(컴퓨터)에 적응하도록 돕기 위해 기존 물리적 사무실에서 쓰던 용어(문서, 폴더, 데스크톱)를 비유로 가져와 사용했다는 내용입니다. 즉, 익숙한 예전의 도구 개념이 새로운 것을 배우는 데 도움을 주었다는 것이 주제입니다.

question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?

question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Of central importance for understanding the development of handedness is the answer to the question of when in development it is actually determined whether a child will be left-handed or right-handed. It was long thought that handedness could only be reliably determined in elementary school, when a child learns to write.
ordered_passages: (A) In such studies, the hand and arm movements of unborn children in the womb are recorded using ultrasound images. Using this technique, it was shown that a clear preference for the movement of the right arm exists as early as 10 weeks after fertilization.

(B) However, this assumption is incorrect. In fact, scientific studies show that left-handedness is established in many children long before elementary school ─ interestingly, even before birth in most people.

(C) In this study, ultrasound images of 72 unborn children 10 weeks after fertilization were evaluated and 85% showed more movements of the right arm than the left. This number is already very close to the approximately 89.4% right-handers among adults.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 손잡이가 초등학교 때 결정된다는 통념을 제시한 뒤, (B)에서 'However'를 통해 이 가설이 틀렸으며 출생 전 결정된다는 연구 결과를 반박으로 제시합니다. (A)에서 그 구체적인 연구 방법(초음파)과 10주 차의 오른팔 선호 현상을 설명하고, (C)에서 'In this study'로 (A)의 연구 결과를 구체적인 수치(85%)와 함께 성인 통계와 비교하며 마무리하는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the ⓐ<u>scarcity</u> of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and ⓑ<u>weighty</u> to transport. Wood suffers from splitting and is ⓒ<u>susceptible</u> to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is limited. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex ─ or, as we call it now, the book ─ that the material reached its full ⓓ<u>potential</u>. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a ⓔ<u>subordinate</u> form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, won out as the guardian of the written word is a remarkable materials story.
explanation: 지식 전달 수단으로서 종이가 오늘날에도 여전히 지배적인(dominant) 형태임을 설명하는 문맥이므로, '부수적인, 하위의'라는 뜻의 subordinate는 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 20. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is difficult, if not impossible, to define the limits which reason should impose on the desire for wealth; for there is no absolute or definite amount of wealth which will satisfy a man. The amount is always relative, that is to say, just so much as will maintain the proportion between what he wants and what he gets; for to measure a man's happiness only by what he gets, and not also by what he expects to get, is as pointless as to try and express a fraction which shall have a numerator but no denominator. A man never feels the loss of things which it never occurs to him to ask for; he is just as happy without them; whilst another, who may have a hundred times as much, feels miserable because he has not got the one thing he wants. In fact, every man has a horizon of his own, and he will expect as much as he thinks it is possible for him to get.
options: ① The Importance of Saving Money

question: 23. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In art, there are a number of ways to use perspective to obtain the illusion of depth, including using colors and graduated values of black and white, and accurately drawing the subject by applying the rules of the geometric system of perspective. question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis. question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Would you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month? Most people will opt for the larger sum in thirteen months ─ where else will you find a monthly interest rate of 10 percent. A wise choice, since the interest will compensate you generously for any risks you face by waiting the extra few weeks. Second question: Would you prefer $1,000 today cash on the table or $1,100 in a month? If you think like most people, you'll take the $1,000 right away. This is amazing. In both cases, if you hold out for just a month longer, you get $100 more. In the first case, it's simple enough. You figure: "I've already waited twelve months; what's one more?" Not in the second case. The introduction of "now" causes us to make inconsistent decisions. Science calls this phenomenon hyperbolic discounting. ___________________________, the higher our "emotional interest rate" rises and the more we are willing to give up in exchange for it.
options: ① the closer a reward is
② the larger a reward is
③ the more uncertain the reward is
④ the longer we wait for a reward
⑤ the more valuable the reward is
explanation: 이 글은 '쌍곡선 할인(hyperbolic discounting)' 현상을 설명하고 있습니다. 먼 미래의 보상 사이에서는 이성적인 선택을 하지만, 보상 중 하나가 '현재(now)'와 가까워지면 즉각적인 만족을 위해 더 큰 미래의 보상을 포기하는 경향이 있다는 것입니다. 따라서 보상이 가까워질수록 정서적 이자율이 높아져 더 많은 것을 기꺼이 포기하게 된다는 1번이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.

② 보상이 더 클수록

④ 보상을 위해 더 오래 기다릴수록
⑤ 보상이 더 가치 있을수록

question: 20. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The writer and zoologist Desmond Morris observed that our feet communicate exactly what we think and feel more honestly than any other part of our bodies. Why are the feet and legs such accurate reflectors of our sentiments? For millions of years, long before humans spoke, our legs and feet reacted to environmental threats (e.g., hot sand, ill-tempered lions) instantaneously, without the need for conscious thought. Our limbic brains made sure that our feet and legs reacted as needed by either ceasing motion, running away, or kicking at a potential threat. This survival regimen, retained from our ancestral heritage, has served us well and continues to do so today. In fact, these age-old reactions are still so hardwired in us that when we are presented with something dangerous or even disagreeable, our feet and legs still react as they did in prehistoric times.*limbic: (대뇌) 변연계(邊綠系)의 **regimen: 양생법(養생法)

question: 21. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 23. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]

question: 25. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
passage: We might forget an anecdote about a stranger because it makes few connections with our existing associations, but we won't forget a piece of gossip about our cousin. (In fact, there were entire years during junior high when we weren't capable of thinking about much else.) (B) It hits even closer to home than our actual home - we can take a vacation away from our home, but not from ourselves. (C) The most effective communicators find ways to make the abstract personal. (B) 바로 뒤의 문장은 '그것(자기 자신과의 연관성)은 실제 집보다 더 가깝게 느껴진다'는 내용을 이어가며, 주어진 문장의 결과(정보 처리의 용이함)가 (B) 위치에 들어감으로써 앞서 설명한 '자기 자신'이라는 네트워크의 강력함에 대한 결론적 진술을 형성합니다. 뒤이어 (C)부터는 이러한 원리를 이용하는 효과적인 전달자들에 대한 예시가 이어지므로 (B)가 가장 적절한 위치입니다.

question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The big problem with money created by the government is that those who run the government always face the temptation to create more money and spend it. Whether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, leading to inflation and the many economic and social problems that follow from inflation. For this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that is inherently limited in supply, as money. It is a way of depriving governments of the power to expand the money supply to inflationary levels. Gold has long been considered ideal for this purpose, since the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased rapidly. When paper money is convertible into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money is said to be "backed up" by gold. This expression is misleading only if we imagine that the value of the gold is somehow transferred to the paper money, when in fact the real point is that the gold simply limits the amount of paper money that can be issued.
summary_sentence: Governments tend to (A)__________ too much money, which causes inflation, so many countries (B)__________ gold to keep the value of money stable.
options: ① collect --- trade
② issue --- ignore
③ print --- adopt
④ borrow --- reject
⑤ save --- preserve
explanation: 본문은 정부가 화폐를 과도하게 발행하여 인플레이션을 초래하는 문제를 지적하며, 이를 방지하기 위해 공급이 제한적인 금을 화폐 시스템에 도입(채택)하는 것을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 화폐를 찍어낸다는 의미의 'print'가, (B)에는 금 본위제 등을 선택한다는 의미의 'adopt'가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 28. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: Shoppers confronted with the choice of thirty different varieties of gourmet chocolates are more likely to walk away without buying any, compared with when they are presented with only half a dozen choices. If employees are given a free trip to Paris, they are happy. If you give them a free trip to Hawaii, they are happy. But if you offer them the choice between the two destinations, they are less happy, no matter what they choose. Why might choice be so disruptive? The reason is that choice forces us to make comparisons and acknowledge relative disadvantages. People who choose Paris complain that it doesn't have the ocean and those who choose Hawaii regret that it doesn't have the museums. Psychologist Barry Schwartz calls this the 'tyranny of choice' because rather than providing freedom, it actually constrains our decision making. He argues that wider choice increases unhappiness because we worry that we are going to make the wrong decision and so we get stressed about trying to process all the comparisons in an effort to get it right. This both increases our fear of making the wrong choice and raises expectations that we should be able to get the best choice. Having made the choice, we then start to regret, wondering whether it was the right one.
summary_sentence: Having too many options can (A)____________ people and lead to regret, even when all the choices are appealing. People become less happy with their decisions because (B)____________ choice increases doubt and stress.
options: ① overwhelm --- excessive
② encourage --- abundant
③ confuse --- moderate
④ encourage --- unlimited
⑤ overwhelm --- balanced
explanation: 본문은 선택지가 너무 많을 때 사람들이 결정을 내리기 어려워하고 결과에 대해 더 많은 후회와 스트레스를 느끼는 '선택의 폭정'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 너무 많은 옵션은 사람들을 압도(overwhelm)할 수 있으며, 과도한(excessive) 선택은 의심과 스트레스를 증가시키기 때문에 (A)에는 overwhelm, (B)에는 excessive가 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 압도하다 --- 과도한
② 격려하다 --- 풍부한
③ 혼란스럽게 하다 --- 적당한
④ 격려하다 --- 무제한의
⑤ 압도하다 --- 균형 잡힌

question: 30. 다음 글을 읽고, 주제가 드러날 수 있도록 마지막 문장을 조건에 맞게 완성하시오. [4.0점]
passage: The study of emotions and decision making is now of considerable importance. This involves the application of various tools afforded by neuroscience. One important stream of the literature examines people with brain damage and how damage to particular parts of the brain known to be responsible for particular cognitive functions impacts on decision making. One example of this research is the work of Antonio Damasio, who finds that when the emotional part of the brain is damaged, this actually reduces the efficacy of decision making. Good decisions are a product of the emotional part of the brain working in conjunction with the deliberative part. This contradicts the assumptions of conventional economics, where emotions play a negative role in the decision-making process. Here it is assumed that decision making can be modeled as being generated in a stoic, unemotional fashion, and that's why decisions tend to be optimal. But the evidence suggests that _________________________________ ___________________________________________________________.

answer: emotions actually play an important and, often, a positive role in decision making
explanation: 이 글은 감정이 의사결정 과정에서 중요한 역할을 하며, 감정이 배제된 이성적인 판단만이 최적은 아니라는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 마지막 문장은 감정이 의사결정에 긍정적이고 중요한 역할을 한다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: Most mice in the wild are eaten or die before their life span of two years is over. They die from external causes, such as disease, starvation, or predators, not due to internal causes, such as aging. That is why nature has made mice live, on average, for no longer than two years. Now we have arrived at an important point: The average life span of an animal species, or the rate at which it ages, is determined by the average time that this animal species can survive in the wild. That explains why a bat can live to be 30 years old. In contrast to mice, bats can fly, which is why they can escape from danger much faster. Thanks to their wings, bats can also cover longer distances and are better able to find food. Every genetic change in the past that made it possible for a bat to live longer was useful, because bats are much better able than mice to flee from danger, find food, and survive.

question: 12. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The writer and zoologist Desmond Morris observed that our feet communicate exactly what we think and feel more honestly than any other part of our bodies. Why are the feet and legs such accurate reflectors of our sentiments? For millions of years, long before humans spoke, our legs and feet reacted to environmental threats (e.g., hot sand, ill-tempered lions) instantaneously, without the need for conscious thought. Our limbic brains made sure that our feet and legs reacted as needed by either ceasing motion, running away, or kicking at a potential threat. This survival regimen, retained from our ancestral heritage, has served us well and continues to do so today. That is, these age-old reactions are still hardwired in us. As a result, when we are presented with something dangerous or even disagreeable, our feet and legs still react as they did in prehistoric times.
options: ① evolutionary processes of our bodily structures
② strategies for wisely dealing with uncomfortable situations
③ universal emotions rooted in prehistoric human experience
④ primitive survival responses expressed through feet and legs
⑤ differences in the survival responses between ancient and modern humans
explanation: 이 글은 동물학자 데즈먼드 모리스의 관찰을 바탕으로, 우리의 발과 다리가 인간의 감정을 가장 정직하게 반영한다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 수백만 년 전부터 인류가 환경적 위협에 대응하기 위해 무의식적으로 반응해 온 생존 방식이 현대인에게도 여전히 내재되어 있기 때문입니다. 따라서 주제로는 '발과 다리를 통해 표현되는 원시적인 생존 반응'이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Information encountered after an event can influence subsequent remembering. External information can easily ⓐ<u>integrate</u> into a witness's memory, especially if the event was poorly encoded or the memory is from a distant event, in which case time and forgetting have degraded the original memory. With reduced information available in memory with which to confirm the validity of post-event misinformation, it is less likely that this new information will be ⓑ<u>dismissed</u>. Instead, especially when it fits the witness's current thinking and can be used to create a story that makes sense to him or her, it may merge into part of the ⓒ<u>original</u> experience. This process can be explicit (i.e. the witness knows it is happening), but it often happens ⓓ<u>consciously</u>. That is, the witness might find himself or herself, thinking about the event differently without awareness. Over time, the witness may not even know the source of information that led to the (new) memory. Sources of ⓔ<u>misinformation</u> in forensic contexts can be encountered anywhere, from. discussions with other witnesses to social media searches to multiple interviews with investigators or other legal professionals, and even in court.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 지문에서 목격자가 새로운 정보를 받아들여 기억이 변하는 과정은 명시적일 수도 있지만, 주로 '인식하지 못한 채(without awareness)' 일어난다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 'consciously(의식적으로)'는 문맥상 'unconsciously(무의식적으로)'로 고쳐야 적절합니다.

question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A reason for a conclusion is very unlikely to consist in a single claim. No matter how we might state it in shorthand, it is, analytically, a/an ___________________ among many ideas and implications, which is quite complicated. The reason must be broken down into a chain of more precise premises. For example, the claim that 'university education should be free for all Australians' might be supported by the reason that 'the economy benefits from a well-educated Australian population'. But is our analysis of the situation clearly expressed in just one statement? Hardly. The conclusion is about universities and free education, while the reason introduces some new ideas: economic benefit and a well-educated population. While the link between these two ideas and the conclusion might seem obvious, the purpose of reasoning is to avoid assuming the 'obvious' by carefully working through the connections between the various ideas in the initial statement of our reason.
options: ① linear process
② exceptional case
③ refined reasoning
④ mutual relationship
⑤ logical contradiction
explanation: 결론에 대한 이유는 단 하나의 주장으로 구성되지 않으며, 분석적으로 보면 많은 아이디어와 함의들 사이의 '상호 관계(mutual relationship)'입니다. 본문에서는 대학 교육 무상화라는 예시를 통해 결론(무상 교육)과 이유(경제적 혜택) 사이에 여러 아이디어가 얽혀 복잡한 사슬을 이루고 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 이러한 여러 요소 간의 연결성을 뜻하는 'mutual relationship'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 선형적 과정
② 예외적인 경우
③ 정제된 추론
④ 상호 관계
⑤ 논리적 모순

question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Steve Jobs used analogy to get people to embrace the new technology. Before computers, people worked in a physical world. We used paper and pens and physical file folders and so on. The idea of working in a virtual world was radically different. Or at least seemed radically different. What Jobs understood was that ___________________________________. To win over the masses, Jobs drew strong analogies between the traditional workplace people knew well with the new, unfamiliar virtual workplace. In the pre-computer workplace, when ideas were written on paper it was called ... a document. When those documents needed to be stored they were put in ... a folder. And those folders were kept on ... a desk. Documents, folders, and desktops are the terms we use in our virtual work because Steve Jobs understood that using familiar terms would make the new technology easier to understand. The parallels between the physical and virtual workplace now seem obvious.
options: ① a physical office would be replaced by a virtual one
② a virtual office replicated the basic structure of a physical one
③ new words should be devised to explain the unfamiliar situations
④ there would be a significant discrepancy between a reality and a virtual life
⑤ problems brought about by the rise of new technologies can be addressed by using familiar methods
explanation: 스티브 잡스는 대중이 생소한 가상 환경의 컴퓨터 기술을 쉽게 받아들일 수 있도록 기존 물리적 업무 환경의 구조와 용어(문서, 폴더, 데스크탑)를 가상 세계에 그대로 적용했습니다. 즉, 가상 사무실이 물리적 사무실의 기본 구조를 복제(replicated)했다는 점을 활용한 것이므로 ②번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 물리적 사무실이 가상 사무실로 대체될 것이다
② 가상 사무실이 물리적 사무실의 기본 구조를 복제했다
③ 익숙하지 않은 상황을 설명하기 위해 새로운 단어들이 고안되어야 한다

question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Would you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month? Most people will opt for the larger sum in thirteen months - where else will you find a monthly interest rate of 10 percent. A wise choice, since the interest will compensate you generously for any risks you face by waiting the extra few weeks. Second question: Would you prefer $1,000 today cash on the table or $1,100 in a month? If you think like most people, you'll take the $1,000 right away. This is amazing. In both cases, if you hold out for just a month longer, you get $100 more. In the first case, it's simple enough. You figure: "I've already waited twelve months; what's one more?" Not in the second case. The introduction of "now" causes us to make inconsistent decisions. Science calls this phenomenon hyperbolic discounting. The nearer a reward is in time, the more intensely we value it emotionally, making us more likely to ______________ future benefits to get it immediately.
options: ① appreciate
② sacrifice
③ protect
④ retain
⑤ value
explanation: 사람들은 보상이 시간적으로 가까울수록(지금 당장일수록) 감정적으로 더 높은 가치를 부여합니다. 이로 인해 당장의 만족을 위해 더 큰 나중의 혜택을 포기하게 되는데, 이를 '쌍곡선 할인(hyperbolic discounting)'이라고 합니다. 따라서 즉각적인 보상을 얻기 위해 미래의 혜택을 '희생(sacrifice)'하게 만든다는 흐름이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 높게 평가하다
② 희생시키다
③ 보호하다
④ 유지하다
⑤ 가치 있게 여기다

question: 22. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The brain is not ______________________________. To put it simply, sensory organs are the only channels through which the brain communicates with its external environment. For instance, an exposed brain would neither sense light shining on it nor feel something touching it. In fact, patients are often kept awake during brain surgery, which can help a surgeon isolate specific regions of the brain. The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle recognized this characteristic of the brain over 2,000 years ago when he said, "Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses." This concept can be seen clearly when volunteers are blind-folded and placed in the warm water of a sensory deprivation tank. They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as incoherent thought patterns. From these experiments and others, it is apparent that we need constant input from our senses to carry out functions that give us personality and intellect.
options: ① clearly separated from personality
② influenced by external sensory organs
③ equipped to sense things independently
④ shaped to process complex sensory inputs
⑤ connected to sources of sensory stimulation
explanation: 지문은 뇌가 외부 환경과 소통하기 위해 오직 감각 기관이라는 통로를 필요로 한다고 설명합니다. 뇌 자체는 빛이나 촉감을 직접 느끼지 못하며, 감각 차단 실험을 통해 감각 입력이 없을 때 뇌의 기능이 비정상적으로 변함을 보여줍니다. 따라서 뇌는 '독립적으로 사물을 감지할 수 있는 능력을 갖추고 있지 않다'는 의미인 ③번이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인격과 명확하게 분리되어 있지 않다
② 외부 감각 기관에 의해 영향을 받지 않는다
③ 독립적으로 사물을 감지할 수 있는 능력을 갖추고 있지 않다
④ 복잡한 감각 입력을 처리하도록 형성되어 있지 않다
⑤ 감각 자극의 원천에 연결되어 있지 않다

question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: The study of emotions and decision making is now of considerable importance. This involves the application of various tools afforded by neuroscience. (A) One important stream of the literature examines people with brain damage and how damage to particular parts of the brain known to be responsible for particular cognitive functions impacts on decision making. (B) One example of this research is the work of Antonio Damasio, who finds that when the emotional part of the brain. is damaged, this actually reduces the efficacy of decision making. (C) Good decisions are a product of the emotional part of the brain working in conjunction with the deliberative part. (D) Here it is assumed that decision making can be modeled as being generated in a stoic, unemotional fashion, and that's why decisions tend to be optimal. (E) But the evidence suggests that emotions actually play an important and, often, a positive role in decision making.
insertion_sentence: This contradicts the assumptions of conventional economics, where emotions play a negative role in the decision-making process.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장은 '이것이 감정이 의사결정 과정에서 부정적인 역할을 한다고 보는 전통 경제학의 가정과 모순된다'는 내용입니다. (D) 앞 문장까지는 감정이 의사결정에 긍정적이고 필수적인 역할을 한다는 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '이것(감정의 긍정적 역할)'이 전통 경제학의 가정과 상충됨을 언급하는 주어진 문장은 (D) 자리에 들어가야 하며, (D) 이후의 내용은 전통 경제학의 관점(냉정하고 감정이 없는 방식의 최적의 결정)을 부연 설명한 뒤 (E)에서 다시 실제 증거(감정의 중요성)로 돌아오는 구조가 자연스럽습니다.

question: 25. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. (A) Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. (B) Wood suffers from splitting and is susceptible to decay, while wall paintings are static and space is limited. (C) But it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex - a stack of papers bound to a single spine and sandwiched between covers - that the material reached its full potential. (D) The genius of the new format allowed for text on both sides of the paper and provided a continuous reading experience. (E) The advantage of the codex, with its individual pages, was that many scribes could work on different sections of the same book simultaneously, and after the invention of the printing press it allowed many copies to be created at once.
insertion_sentence: The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these problems.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: (A)와 (B)에서는 기존 기록 매체(돌, 점토판, 나무, 벽화)들이 가졌던 문제점들(깨지기 쉬움, 무거움, 부식 등)을 나열하고 있습니다. 주어진 문장은 '종이의 발명이 이러한 문제들(these problems)을 해결했다'는 내용이므로, 문제점 나열이 끝난 직후이자 종이로 만든 책의 형태(codex)를 설명하기 시작하는 (C)에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 26. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Of central importance for understanding the development of handedness is the answer to the question of when in development it is actually determined whether a child will be left-handed or right-handed.
ordered_passages: (A) It was assumed that handedness could only be reliably determined in elementary school, when a child learns to write. However, this assumption needs qualification. In fact, scientific studies show that left-handedness is established in many children long before elementary school - interestingly, even before birth in most people.

(B) Ultrasound images of 72 unborn children 10 weeks after fertilization were evaluated and 85% showed more movements of the right arm than the left. This number is already very close to the approximately 89.4% right-handers among adults.

(C) In such studies, the hand and arm movements of unborn children in the womb are recorded using ultrasound images. Using this technique, it was shown that a clear preference for the movement of the right arm exists as early as 10 weeks after fertilization.
explanation: 주어진 글은 왼손잡이/오른손잡이가 결정되는 시기에 대한 질문을 던집니다. (A)에서 초등학교 때 결정된다는 기존 통념과 이를 반박하며 태어나기 전부터 결정된다는 과학적 연구를 언급합니다. (C)에서 (A)의 마지막에 언급된 '태아 대상 연구'가 어떻게 이루어지는지(초음파 영상 기법) 구체적으로 설명하며 10주 차의 선호도를 언급합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 해당 연구의 구체적인 수치(72명 중 85%)를 제시하며 성인 비율과 유사함을 설명하며 마무리되는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 27. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The big problem with money created by the government is that those who run the government always face the temptation to create more money and spend it. Whether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, leading to inflation and the many economic and social problems that follow from inflation. For this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that is inherently limited in supply, as money. It is a way of depriving governments of the power to expand the money supply to inflationary levels. Gold has long been considered ideal for this purpose, since the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased rapidly. When paper money is convertible into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money is said to be "backed up" by gold. This expression, however, deserves a cautious look as it might be misleading if people assume that the value of gold is transferred to the paper money, when in fact the real point is that _____________________________________.
options: ① gold serves as an ideal alternative to money
② the true value of money is supported by the various usages of gold
③ paper money loses its significance as the value of gold becomes inflated
④ paper money and gold circulate together to maintain economic balance
⑤ gold places a constraint on the volume of paper currency that can be issued
explanation: 정부가 발행하는 화폐의 문제점인 과도한 발행에 따른 인플레이션을 막기 위해 공급이 제한적인 '금'을 사용하게 되었다는 내용입니다. 지폐가 금으로 뒷받침된다는 표현은 금의 가치가 지폐로 전이된다는 뜻이라기보다는, 금이 발행될 수 있는 지폐의 양에 제한을 가한다는 것이 핵심입니다. 따라서 ⑤번 '금은 발행될 수 있는 지폐의 양에 제한을 둔다'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 금은 돈에 대한 이상적인 대안 역할을 한다
② 돈의 진정한 가치는 금의 다양한 용도에 의해 뒷받침된다
③ 금의 가치가 팽창함에 따라 지폐는 그 중요성을 잃는다
④ 경제적 균형을 유지하기 위해 지폐와 금이 함께 순환한다
⑤ 금은 발행될 수 있는 지폐의 양에 제한을 가한다

question: 28. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
passage: It is difficult, if not impossible, to define the limits which reason should impose on the desire for wealth; for there is no absolute or definite amount of wealth which will satisfy a man. The amount is always ⓐ<u>relative</u>, that is to say, just so much as will maintain the proportion between what he wants and what he gets; for to estimate a man's satisfaction only by what he gets, and not also by what he expects to get, is as ⓑ<u>rational</u> as to try and express a fraction which shall have a numerator but no denominator. A man never feels the ⓒ<u>loss</u> of things which it never occurs to him to ask for; he is just as happy without them; whilst another, who may have a hundred times as much, feels ⓓ<u>downhearted</u> because he has not got the one thing he wants. In fact, the extent of what one desires varies ⓔ<u>considerably</u> from person to person.
explanation: 인간의 부에 대한 욕망은 상대적이며, 만족감은 단순히 얻은 것뿐만 아니라 기대하는 것(분모)과의 비율로 결정된다는 내용입니다. 따라서 얻은 것만으로 만족도를 측정하고 기대치를 고려하지 않는 것은 '분모 없는 분수'를 표현하려는 것만큼이나 '불합리하다(irrational)'는 맥락이 되어야 하므로 ②번 'rational(합리적인)'은 잘못된 쓰임입니다.

question: 29. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis. For example, migrants are assumed to overcrowd cities, ⓐ<u>conjest</u> labor markets, and increase poverty. The other questionable assumption is that most migration is ⓑ<u>involuntary</u> - people fleeing natural or man-made disasters. The reality, however, is more complex, and many migrants are simply seeking greater economic opportunity. Of course migration can and does create social and economic problems. But migration can also be a solution for many preexisting problems. For example, out-migration generally ⓒ<u>redistributes</u> workers from places of labor surplus to areas where there is greater demand or more opportunity. Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to ⓓ<u>endure</u> hardship in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin. Most research that examines long-term outcomes of migration, including remittances and intergenerational mobility, finds ⓔ<u>hostile</u> "long-term" effects on places of origin and destination.
explanation: 이 글은 이주를 단순히 문제나 위기로만 보는 시각에 반박하며, 이주가 노동력 재배치 등 기존 문제의 해결책이 될 수 있고 장기적으로 긍정적인 효과를 가져온다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 장기적인 결과에 관한 연구가 '적대적인(hostile)' 효과를 발견했다는 것은 문맥상 어색하며, '긍정적인(positive/beneficial)' 효과가 적절합니다.

question: 30. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: All of the restaurants are using carefully chosen words to evoke vivid mental images of delicious food and rich desserts in order to draw the potential customer to their particular establishment. Just like the restaurants, nature has its own dining establishments. In a fashion similar to the restaurants' financial dependence upon drawing in many customers, the restaurateurs of the natural world (i.e., flowers) must also attract potential diners to sample their offerings. In the natural world, there are no neon signs or flashy words in which to market a potential meal to hungry animals. These restaurants that I am referring to are the world's flowers, and the potential guests are the host of organisms that visit flowers to obtain nectar and other valuable resources. Instead of using a written language or neon sign, they advertise their offerings just as effectively using the language of smell.
summary_sentence: Just like restaurants, flowers in nature are trying to (A)____________ animals not with signs or words but through the powerful use of (B)____________ to offer nectar and other resources.
options: ① lure / scent
② distract / bait
③ expel / noise
④ fascinate / touch
⑤ attract / flash
explanation: 이 글은 식당이 화려한 문구로 고객을 유혹하듯, 자연 속의 꽃도 동물을 유인하기 위해 '냄새'라는 도구를 사용한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 동물들을 유인한다는 의미가 들어가야 하므로 lure(유혹하다)가 적절하며, (B)는 글의 마지막 부분에 언급된 'language of smell'을 대체할 수 있는 scent(향기)가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 유인하다 / 향기
산만하게 하다 / 미끼
쫓아내다 / 소음
매료시키다 / 촉각
끌어들이다 / 번쩍임

question: 13. 다음 ⓐ~ⓗ 중 쓰임이 같은 것끼리 올바르게 짝지어진 것은?
passage: If we've invested in something ⓐ<u>that</u> hasn't repaid us - be it money in a failing venture, or time in an unhappy relationship - we find it very difficult to walk away. This is the sunk cost fallacy. Our instinct is to continue investing money or time as we hope ⓑ<u>that</u> our investment will prove to be worthwhile in the end. Giving up would mean acknowledging ⓒ<u>that</u> we've wasted something we can't get back, and ⓓ<u>that</u> thought is so painful ⓔ<u>that</u> we prefer to avoid it if we can. The problem, of course, is ⓕ<u>that</u> if something really is a bad bet, then staying with it simply increases the amount we lose. Rather than walk away from a bad five-year relationship, for example, we turn it into a bad 10-year relationship; rather than accept ⓖ<u>that</u> we've lost a thousand dollars, we lay down another thousand and lose ⓗ<u>that</u> too. In the end, by delaying the pain of admitting our problem, we only add to it. Sometimes we just have to cut our losses.
explanation: ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓖ는 모두 뒤에 완전한 절이 오는 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 'that'으로 쓰였습니다. 반면, ⓐ는 주격 관계대명사, ⓓ는 지시형용사("그" 생각), ⓔ는 so...that 구문의 접속사, ⓕ는 보어 역할을 하는 명사절 접속사(다른 명사절과 성격은 같으나 ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓖ가 동사의 목적어절인 것과 차이가 있을 수 있음 - 그러나 가장 명확한 그룹은 ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓖ임), ⓗ는 지시대명사("그것" 또한)입니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: The Net differs from most of the mass media it replaces in an obvious and very important way: it's ⓐ<u>bidirectional</u>. We can send messages through the network as well as receive them, which has made the system all the more useful. The ability to ⓑ<u>exchange</u> information online, to upload as well as download, has turned the Net into a thoroughfare for business and commerce. But the Net doesn't just connect us with businesses; it connects us with one another. It's a personal broadcasting medium as well as a ⓓ<u>individual</u> one. Millions of people use it to distribute their own digital creations, in the form of blogs, videos, photos, songs, and podcasts, as well as to critique, edit, or otherwise ⓔ<u>modify</u> the creations of others.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 인터넷은 비즈니스뿐만 아니라 사람과 사람 사이를 연결하며, 개인적인 방송 매체인 동시에 공동의(communal) 매체라는 문맥이 적절합니다. 따라서 'individual'은 문맥상 어울리지 않습니다.

question: 15. 다음 글을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, <보기>에 주어진 단어만을 모두 한 번씩만 사용하여 빈칸을 완성하시오. (어형 변형 가능)
passage: Many things spark envy : ownership, status, health youth, talent, popularity, beauty. It is often confused with jealousy because the physical reactions are identical. The difference: the subject of envy is a thing (status, money, health etc.). The subject of jealousy is the behaviour of a third person. Envy needs two people. Jealousy, on the other hand, requires three: Peter is jealous of Sam because the beautiful girl next door rings him instead. Paradoxically, with envy we direct resentments toward those who are most similar to us in age, career and residence. We don't envy businesspeople from the century before last. We don't envy millionaires on the other side of the globe. As a writer, I don't envy musicians, managers or dentists, but other writers. As a CEO you envy other, bigger CEOs. As a supermodel you envy more successful supermodels. Aristotle knew this: 'Potters envy potters.'
summary_sentence: Jealousy involves three parties, focusing on the actions of a third person, _____________________________, with one person resenting the other.
answer: whereas envy involves two individuals whose personal circumstances are most alike
explanation: 질투(jealousy)는 세 명 사이에서 발생하고 제3자의 행동에 초점을 두는 반면(whereas), 부러움(envy)은 개인적 상황이 가장 유사한(whose personal circumstances are most alike) 두 사람(two individuals) 사이에서 한 사람이 다른 사람을 원망하며 발생한다는 내용이 되도록 주어진 단어를 배열해야 합니다. be는 주어인 circumstances에 맞춰 are로 변형합니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Research psychologists often work with self-report data, made up of participants' verbal accounts of their behavior. This is the case whenever questionnaires interviews, or personality inventories are used to measure variables. Self-report methods can be quite useful. They take advantage of the fact that people have a unique opportunity to observe themselves full-time. However, self-reports can be plagued by several kinds of distortion. One of the most problematic of these distortions is the social desirability bias, which is a tendency to give socially approved answers to questions about oneself. Subjects who are influenced by this bias work overtime trying to create a favorable impression, especially when subjects are asked about sensitive issues. For example, many survey respondents will report that they voted in an election or gave to a charity when in fact it is possible to determine that they did not.
options: ① People always give honest answers in self-report surveys.
② Psychologists prefer interviews over questionnaires for collecting data.
③ Social desirability bias exists because self-report methods are unreliable.
④ Voting and charity are the most common topics in psychological research.
⑤ Self-report methods are useful but can be affected by social desirability bias.
explanation: 자기 보고 방식은 유용성이 있지만 사회적 바람직성 편향으로 인해 데이터의 왜곡이 발생할 수 있다는 것이 글의 핵심 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들은 자기 보고 설문 조사에서 항상 정직한 답변을 한다.

④ 투표와 자선은 심리학 연구에서 가장 흔한 주제이다.

question: 17. 다음 글을 읽고, 주어진 질문에 대한 가장 적절한 답을 고른 것은?
passage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control. Scientists manipulate a variable of interest, and see if there's a difference. At the same time, they attempt to control for the potential effects of all other variables. The importance of controlled experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often correlated. For example, people who take vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who don't take vitamins. As a result, if we want to study the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely observe the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to create a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world. That's just what scientific experiments do. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while holding everything else constant.
options: ① To explain how vitamins affect health
② To promote the benefits of regular exercise
③ To criticize people's reliance on supplements
④ To show the limitations of observational studies
⑤ To emphasize the importance of a balanced diet

question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: We collect stamps, coins, vintage cars even when they serve no practical purpose. The post office doesn't accept the old stamps, the banks don't take old coins, and the vintage cars are no longer allowed on the road. (A) These are all side issues; the attraction is that they are in short supply. (B) In one study, students were asked to arrange ten posters in order of attractiveness - with the agreement that afterward they could keep one poster as a reward for their participation. (C) Five minutes later, they were told that the poster with the third highest rating was no longer available. (D) Then they were asked to judge all ten from scratch. (E) In psychology, this phenomenon is called reactance: when we are deprived of an option, we suddenly deem it more attractive.
insertion_sentence: The poster that was no longer available was suddenly classified as the most beautiful.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 '더 이상 구할 수 없게 된 포스터가 갑자기 가장 아름다운 것으로 분류되었다'는 내용입니다. 이는 (D)에서 학생들이 다시 모든 포스터를 처음부터 평가한 결과에 해당하며, (E)에서 설명하는 심리학적 현상인 '리액턴스(반발 심리)'에 대한 구체적인 실험 결과입니다. 따라서 실험 과정을 거쳐 결과가 도출되고 그 현상을 정의하는 (E) 자리가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 The Law of Unintended Consequences의 예시로 볼 수 없는 것은?
passage: When evaluating a policy, people tend to concentrate on how the policy will fix some particular problem while ignoring or downplaying other effects it may have. Economists often refer to this situation as The Law of Unintended Consequences. For instance, suppose that you impose a tariff on imported steel in order to protect the jobs of domestic steelworkers. If you impose a high enough tariff, their jobs will indeed be protected from competition by foreign steel companies. But an unintended consequence is that the jobs of some autoworkers will be lost to foreign competition. Why? The tariff that protects steelworkers raises the price of the steel that domestic automobile makers need to build their cars. As a result, domestic automobile manufacturers have to raise the prices of their cars, making them relatively less attractive than foreign cars. Raising prices tends to reduce domestic car sales, so some domestic autoworkers lose their jobs.
options: ① The country banned alcohol to reduce crime but it unexpectedly fueled illegal drinking.
② Installing bright streetlights to reduce crime ended up disrupting local wildlife's natural behaviors.
③ Raising the minimum wage helped some workers earn more, but also caused small businesses to cut staff or reduce hours.
④ The government enforced car emissions regulations, so car companies responded by designing more fuel-efficient vehicles.
⑤ Banning plastic to protect the environment led to more paper bag use, resulting in more trees being cut down.
explanation: 본문에 설명된 '의도치 않은 결과의 법칙(The Law of Unintended Consequences)'은 어떤 정책이 특정 문제를 해결하려다가 예상치 못한 부정적인 부작용을 낳는 현상을 말합니다. ④번은 정부의 배출가스 규제에 대응하여 기업이 연비가 좋은 차량을 설계한 것으로, 이는 정책의 의도에 부합하는 긍정적이고 예상된 결과이므로 부작용 사례인 '의도치 않은 결과'에 해당하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 범죄를 줄이기 위해 술을 금지했으나 예상치 못하게 불법 음주를 부추겼다.
② 범죄 감소를 위해 밝은 가로등을 설치했으나 결국 지역 야생 동물의 자연스러운 행동을 방해하게 되었다.
③ 최저 임금을 인상하여 일부 노동자들이 더 많은 돈을 벌게 도왔으나, 소규모 사업체들이 직원을 감축하거나 근무 시간을 줄이는 결과를 초래했다.
④ 정부가 자동차 배출가스 규제를 강화하자 자동차 회사들이 더 효율적인 연료의 차량을 설계함으로써 대응했다.
⑤ 환경 보호를 위해 플라스틱을 금지했으나 종이봉투 사용이 늘어났고, 결과적으로 더 많은 나무가 베어지게 되었다.

question: 20. 다음 글을 읽고, <조건>에 맞게 주제문을 완성하시오.
passage: Because people tend to adapt, interrupting positive things with negative ones can actually increase enjoyment. Take commercials. Most people hate them, so removing them should make shows or other entertainment more enjoyable. But the opposite is true. Shows are actually more enjoyable when they're broken up by annoying commercials. Because these less enjoyable moments break up adaptation to the positive experience of the show. Think about eating chocolate chips. The first chip is delicious: sweet, melt-in-your-mouth goodness. The second chip is also pretty good. But by the fourth, fifth, or tenth chip in a row, the goodness is no longer as pleasurable. We adapt. Interspersing positive experiences with less positive ones, however, can slow down adaptation. Eating a Brussels sprout between chocolate chips or viewing commercials between parts of TV shows disrupts the process. The less positive moment makes the following positive one new again and thus more enjoyable.
subjective_conditions: Putting으로 시작하는 완전한 문장을 완성할 것
<보기>의 단어만을 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것
필요시 단어의 형태를 바꾸어 사용할 것
answer: Putting unpleasant moments between positive ones can make the latter more enjoyable by slowing down adaptation
explanation: 사람들은 자극에 쉽게 적응하기 때문에, 긍정적인 경험 사이에 부정적이거나 덜 유쾌한 순간을 끼워 넣음으로써 적응 속도를 늦추고 결과적으로 긍정적인 경험을 더 즐겁게 만들 수 있다는 내용의 글입니다. 주어진 단어들을 활용하여, '부정적인 순간을 긍정적인 순간 사이에 두는 것은 적응을 늦춤으로써 후자를 더 즐겁게 만들 수 있다'는 주제문을 완성합니다. 이때 'slow down'을 전치사 'by' 뒤의 동명사 형태인 'slowing down'으로 변형해야 합니다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Imagine that seven out of ten working Americans got fired tomorrow. What would they all do? It's hard to believe you'd have an economy at all if you gave pink slips to more than half the labor force. But that is what the industrial revolution did to the workforce of the early 19th century. Two hundred years ago, 70 percent of American workers lived on the farm. Today automation has eliminated all but 1 percent of their jobs, replacing them with machines. But the displaced workers did not sit idle. Instead, automation created hundreds of millions of jobs in entirely new fields. Those who once farmed were now manning the factories that manufactured farm equipment, cars, and other industrial products. Since then, wave upon wave of new occupations have arrived - appliance repair person, food chemist, photographer, web designer - each building on previous automation. Today, the vast majority of us are doing jobs that no farmer from the 1800s could have imagined.
summary_sentence: The Industrial Revolution drastically reduced farm work through (A)____________, shifting the economy away from agriculture. This major change sparked (B)____________ and led to entirely new industries and careers. Today, most people work in fields that would have been unimaginable before industrialization.
options: ① modernization ... renovation
② automation ... innovation
③ digitization ... revolution
④ cultivation ... exploration
⑤ transportation ... regulation
explanation: 산업 혁명 당시 기계가 농업 일자리를 대체한 과정은 (A) 'automation(자동화)'에 해당하며, 이러한 변화가 새로운 산업과 일자리를 창출한 과정은 (B) 'innovation(혁신)'으로 요약할 수 있습니다. 지문에서 자동화가 일자리를 없앴지만 동시에 수억 개의 새로운 일자리를 창출했다고 설명하고 있으므로 2번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 현대화 ... 개조
자동화 ... 혁신
디지털화 ... 혁명
경작 ... 탐험
운송 ... 규제

question: 22. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: In the course of his research on business strategy and the environment, Michael Porter noticed a peculiar pattern: Businesses seemed to be profiting from regulation. He also discovered that the stricter regulations were prompting more innovation than the weaker ones. The Dutch flower industry provides an illustration. For many years, the companies producing Holland's world-renowned tulips and other cut flowers were also contaminating the country's water and soil with fertilizers and pesticides. In 1991, the Dutch government adopted a policy designed to cut pesticide use in half by 2000 - a goal they ultimately achieved. Facing increasingly strict regulation, greenhouse growers realized they had to develop new methods if they were going to maintain product quality with fewer pesticides. In response, they shifted to a cultivation method that circulates water in closed-loop systems and grows flowers in a rock wool substrate. The new system not only reduced the pollution released into the environment; it also increased profits by giving companies greater control over growing conditions.
options: ① 지나친 정부의 규제는 경제 전반에 악영향을 미친다.
② 엄격한 규제가 기업의 혁신과 수익성 향상으로 이어진다.
③ 지속 가능한 성장을 위해서는 기업의 자발적인 윤리 경영이 필요하다.
④ 규제 완화는 기업의 창의성과 자유로운 시장 활동을 극대화하는 데 필수적이다.
⑤ 기술 혁신은 주로 시장 경쟁에서의 생존을 위한 기업 내부 동기에 의해 촉발된다.
explanation: Michael Porter의 연구에 따르면 엄격한 환경 규제가 오히려 기업의 혁신을 촉진하고 수익성을 향상시키는 경향이 있다고 설명합니다. 네덜란드 화훼 산업의 사례를 통해 살충제 규제가 새로운 친환경 재배 방식을 도입하게 만들었고, 결과적으로 오염 감소와 수익 증대라는 두 마리 토끼를 잡았다는 내용을 전달하고 있습니다. 따라서 '엄격한 규제가 기업의 혁신과 수익성 향상으로 이어진다'는 ②번이 가장 적절한 요지입니다.

question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is difficult, if not impossible, to define the limits which reason should impose on the desire for wealth; for there is no absolute or definite amount of wealth which will satisfy a man. The amount is always __________, that is to say, just so much as will maintain the proportion between what he wants and what he gets; for to measure a man's happiness only by what he gets, and not also by what he expects to get, is as pointless as to try and express a fraction which shall have a numerator but no denominator. A man never feels the loss of things which it never occurs to him to ask for; he is just as happy without them; whilst another, who may have a hundred times as much, feels miserable because he has not got the one thing he wants. In fact, every man has a horizon of his own, and he will expect as much as he thinks it is possible for him to get.
options: ① fixed
② relative
③ imaginary
④ objective
⑤ meaningless
explanation: 부의 만족감은 절대적인 양이 정해져 있지 않고, 자신이 원하는 것과 얻는 것 사이의 비율에 달려 있다는 내용입니다. 즉, 개인이 기대하는 바에 따라 부의 만족도가 달라진다는 것이므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말은 '상대적인(relative)'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고정된
② 상대적인
③ 가상의
④ 객관적인

question: 18. 다음 글의 전개 방식으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The big problem with money created by the government is that those who run the government always face the temptation to create more money and spend it. Whether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, leading to inflation and the many economic and social problems that follow from inflation. For this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that is inherently limited in supply, as money. It is a way of depriving governments of the power to expand the money supply to inflationary levels. Gold has long been considered ideal for this purpose, since the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased rapidly. When paper money is convertible into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money is said to be "backed up" by gold. This expression is misleading only if we imagine that the value of the gold is somehow transferred to the paper money, when in fact the real point is that the gold simply limits the amount of paper money that can be issued.
options: ① Presenting a historical pattern of inflation → Explaining the rationale behind gold-backed money → Emphasizing gold's function as a monetary limiter
② Identifying misconceptions about gold's value → Clarifying the true economic role of gold → Contrasting gold with government-issued currency
③ Explaining what causes inflation → Illustrating monetary abuse across time → Highlighting the practical necessity of limitless currency in supply
④ Outlining the risks of unrestricted money creation → Introducing the paper money as a control mechanism → Correcting a misleading interpretation of gold convertibility
⑤ Discussing symbolic uses of currency → Tracing philosophical views on money → Arguing for the emotional appeal of the gold-backed system
explanation: 이 글은 정부가 발행하는 화폐가 초래하는 인플레이션의 역사적 반복(Ancient kings, modern politicians)을 먼저 제시합니다. 그에 대한 해결책으로 공급이 제한된 금본위제 화폐의 근거(rationale)를 설명하며, 마지막 부분에서 금의 진정한 역할이 지폐 발행량을 제한(limits the amount of paper money)하는 데 있음을 강조하며 마무리됩니다.
options_translation: ① 인플레이션의 역사적 패턴 제시 → 금본위제 화폐의 이면의 근거 설명 → 통화 제한 장치로서의 금의 기능 강조
② 금의 가치에 대한 오해 확인 → 금의 진정한 경제적 역할 명확화 → 금과 정부 발행 통화의 대조
③ 인플레이션의 원인 설명 → 시대에 따른 통화 남용 설명 → 무제한 통화 공급의 실질적 필요성 강조
④ 제한 없는 화폐 생성의 위험 개괄 → 통제 기제로서의 지폐 도입 → 금 태환에 대한 잘못된 해석 수정
⑤ 통화의 상징적 용도 논의 → 돈에 대한 철학적 관점 추적 → 금본위제 시스템의 정서적 호소력 주장

question: 19. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Would you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month? Most people will opt for the larger sum in thirteen months - where else will you find a monthly interest rate of 10 percent. A wise choice, since the interest will compensate you generously for any risks you face by waiting the extra few weeks. Second question: Would you prefer $1,000 today cash on the table or $1,100 in a month? If you think like most people, you'll take the $1,000 right away. This is amazing. In both cases, if you hold out for just a month longer, you get $100 more. In the first case, it's simple enough. You figure: "I've already waited twelve months; what's one more?" Not in the second case. The introduction of "now" causes us to make inconsistent decisions. Science calls this phenomenon hyperbolic discounting. The closer a reward is, the higher our "emotional interest rate" rises and the more we are willing to give up in exchange for it.
options: ① Immediate rewards tend to weaken consistent decision-making.
② The value of a reward remains stable regardless of when it is received.
③ Short-term options are generally preferred due to higher associated risks.
④ Those who calculate interest properly tend to avoid irrational financial behavior.
⑤ Financial self-discipline increases as rewards become emotionally appealing.
explanation: 이 글은 '쌍곡선 할인(hyperbolic discounting)' 개념을 설명하며, 보상이 현재와 가까울수록 감정적 이율이 높아져서 더 큰 보상을 기다리지 못하고 즉각적인 보상을 선택하는 '일관되지 않은 결정(inconsistent decisions)'을 내리게 된다는 점을 지적하고 있습니다. 따라서 즉각적인 보상이 일관된 의사결정을 방해한다는 내용인 1번이 요지로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 즉각적인 보상은 일관된 의사결정을 약화시키는 경향이 있다.
② 보상의 가치는 그것을 언제 받느냐에 상관없이 안정적으로 유지된다.
③ 단기적인 선택지는 일반적으로 더 높은 관련 위험 때문에 선호된다.
④ 이자를 적절하게 계산하는 사람들은 비합리적인 금융 행위를 피하는 경향이 있다.
⑤ 보상이 정서적으로 매력적일수록 금융적 자제력이 증가한다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Turtle hatchlings have, it seems, ⓐ<u>adapted</u> to move toward the brightest direction. For millions of years this was a highly rational and effective strategy because the illumination on a dark beach ⓑ<u>indicated</u> the reflection of celestial bodies on the sea's surface. Following the glow led baby turtles safely to the ocean. Problems began when humans started building seaside houses and glittering resorts on the landward side of beaches. Now, after emerging from their nests, turtles moving toward the most intense lights were being ⓒ<u>directed</u> straight into urban roads. Are self-destructive creatures inherently ⓓ<u>pragmatic</u>? Yes, in the modern world. But there's a deeper truth. Turtles are relying on simple environmental cues that were completely ⓔ<u>appropriate</u> for their evolutionary ancestors. These days, however, their evolved decision-making mechanisms are being blinded by the buildings' lights.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 바다거북 새끼들이 인공 조명을 따라가 도로로 나가는 행동은 스스로를 죽음으로 몰아넣는 비합리적인 행동이므로, '실용적인(pragmatic)'이라는 단어는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다. '비합리적인(irrational)' 등의 단어가 적절합니다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고른 것은?
passage: The study of emotions and decision making ⓐ<u>is now of considerable importance</u>. This involves the application of various tools afforded by neuroscience. One important stream of the literature examines people with brain damage and how damage to particular parts of the brain known to be responsible for particular cognitive functions ⓑ<u>impacts on decision making</u>. One example of this research is the work of ⓒ<u>Antonio Damasio, who finds that when the emotional part of the brain are damaged</u>, this actually reduces the efficacy of decision making. Good decisions are a product of the emotional part of the brain working in conjunction with the deliberative part. This contradicts the assumptions of ⓓ<u>conventional economics, which emotions play a negative role in the decision-making process</u>. Here it is assumed that ⓔ<u>decision making can be modeled as being generated in a stoic, unemotional fashion</u>, and that's why decisions tend to be optimal. But the evidence suggests that emotions actually play an important and, often, a positive role in decision making.
options: ① ⓐ
explanation: ⓑ: 'impact'는 타동사로 주로 쓰여 'impacts decision making'으로 쓰거나 명사형으로 'has an impact on'으로 쓰는 것이 자연스럽습니다.ⓒ: 'the emotional part(단수 주어)'이므로 'are damaged'를 'is damaged'로 고쳐야 합니다.ⓓ: 뒷문장이 완전하므로 관계대명사 'which' 대신 관계부사 'where' 또는 'in which'가 필요합니다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Shoppers confronted with the choice of thirty different varieties of gourmet chocolates are more likely to walk away without buying any, ⓐ<u>compared with when they are presented with only half a dozen choices</u>. If employees are given a free trip to Paris, they are happy. If you give them a free trip to Hawaii, they are happy. But if you offer them the choice between the two destinations, they are less happy, no matter what they choose. Why might choice be so disruptive? The reason is that choice forces us ⓑ<u>making comparisons and to acknowledge relative disadvantages</u>. People who choose Paris complain that it doesn't have the ocean and those who choose Hawaii regret that it doesn't have the museums. Psychologist Barry Schwartz calls this the 'tyranny of choice' because ⓒ<u>rather than providing freedom</u>, it actually constrains our decision-making. He argues that wider choice increases unhappiness because we worry that we are going to make the wrong decision and so we get stressed about trying to process all the comparisons in an effort to get it right. This both increases our fear of making the wrong choice and raises expectations ⓓ<u>that we should be able to get the best choice</u>. ⓔ<u>Having made the choice</u>, we then start to regret, wondering whether it was the right one.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓑ: 'force + 목적어 + to 부정사' 구문이 사용되어야 하며, 뒤의 'and to acknowledge'와 병렬 구조를 이루어야 하므로 'making'을 'to make'로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Low oil prices are a good thing, because it means lower energy costs of production for the majority of industries, not least the automobile and the logistics industries. Firms directly benefit from the decrease in their costs of production and provision of services. This has the effect of stimulating the aggregate supply and provides a stimulus for growth. Conversely, a sudden rise in oil prices due to a shrink in oil production is never good news, even though it definitely gives a big boost to the energy sector. A look through the history of oil price fluctuations confirms this notion, as this has been the subject of much economic research. Following an oil price jump of 10 per cent due to a contraction in supply, an economy (as typified by the US economy) typically sees its output (GDP) slowed by close to 1 percentage point. For a $15 trillion economy, that is a loss of $150 billion in potential wealth or economic growth. Conversely, there has never been much concern with oil price __________ following an excess in its supply.
options: ① drop
② increase
③ correction
④ stabilization
⑤ normalization
explanation: 글의 전반부에서 저유가는 경제 성장을 자극하는 좋은 것이라고 언급하고 있으며, 반대로 유가 급등은 경제 성장을 둔화시키는 부정적인 영향을 미친다고 설명하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서는 공급 과잉에 따른 유가의 상황을 언급하고 있는데, 글의 맥락상 공급 과잉은 유가 하락으로 이어지며 이는 경제에 우려할 만한 상황이 아니라는 흐름이 되어야 하므로 빈칸에는 '하락(drop)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 하락

question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A reason for a conclusion is very unlikely to consist in a single claim. No matter how we might state it in short-hand, it is, analytically, a complex interaction of many ideas and implications. The reason must be broken down into a chain of more precise premises. For example, the claim that 'university education should be free for all Australians' might be supported by the reason that 'the economy benefits from a well-educated Australian population'. But is our analysis of the situation clearly expressed in just one statement? Hardly. The conclusion is about universities and free education, while the reason introduces some new ideas: economic benefit and a well-educated population. While the link between these two ideas and the conclusion might seem obvious, the purpose of reasoning is to avoid assuming the 'obvious' by carefully working through the connections between the various ideas in the initial statement of our reason. In short, forming a solid argument involves not just proposing a reason but also _________________________________.
options: ① acknowledging personal bias and intuition
② replacing abstract ideas with emotional appeal
③ relying on concise and intuitive generalizations
④ prioritizing simplicity over analytical complexity
⑤ examining the interrelations among diverse ideas
explanation: 이 글은 결론에 대한 근거가 단일한 주장이 아니라 여러 아이디어와 함축적 의미들의 복합적인 상호작용임을 강조하고 있습니다. 추론의 목적은 '명백해 보이는 것'을 당연하게 여기지 않고, 초기 진술에 포함된 다양한 아이디어들 사이의 연결 고리를 면밀히 검토하는 것이라고 설명합니다. 따라서 견고한 논거를 형성한다는 것은 단순히 이유를 제시하는 것뿐만 아니라, 그 안에 담긴 다양한 아이디어들 간의 상호 관계를 조사하는 것을 포함합니다.
options_translation: ① 개인적인 편견과 직관을 인정하는 것
② 추상적인 아이디어를 감정적 호소로 대체하는 것
③ 간결하고 직관적인 일반화에 의존하는 것
④ 분석적 복잡성보다 단순함을 우선시하는 것

question: 25. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world. Simply put, the brain is not designed to sense on its own. For instance, an exposed brain would neither sense light shining on it nor feel something touching it. In fact, patients are often kept awake during brain surgery, which can help a surgeon isolate specific regions of the brain. The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle (A)[recognized / overlooked] this characteristic of the brain over 2,000 years ago when he said, "Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses." This concept can be seen clearly when volunteers are blind-folded and placed in the warm water of a sensory (B)[demonstration / deprivation] tank. They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as (C)[coherent / incoherent] thought patterns. From these experiments and others, it is apparent that we need constant input from our senses to carry out functions that give us personality and intellect.
options: ① recognized, demonstration, coherent
② recognized, deprivation, incoherent
③ recognized, deprivation, coherent
④ overlooked, deprivation, incoherent
⑤ overlooked, demonstration, incoherent
explanation: (A) 뒤에 이어지는 인용문 "감각을 통하지 않고는 마음속에 아무것도 존재하지 않는다"는 뇌가 스스로 감각할 수 없다는 특성을 설명하므로 Aristotle은 이를 '인식했다(recognized)'가 적절합니다. (B) 눈을 가리고 탱크에 들어가는 실험은 외부 감각을 차단하는 것이므로 '감각 차단(deprivation)' 탱크가 맞습니다. (C) 감각이 차단된 상태에서 환각을 경험하고 사고가 흐트러지는 현상을 설명하므로 '비일관적인(incoherent)' 사고 패턴이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인식했다, 입증, 일관된
② 인식했다, 차단, 비일관적인
③ 인식했다, 차단, 일관된

question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Of central importance for understanding the development of handedness is the answer to the question of when in development it is actually determined whether a child will be left-handed or right-handed. It was long thought that handedness could only be reliably determined in elementary school, when a child learns to write. However, this assumption is incorrect. In fact, scientific studies show that left-handedness is established in many children long before elementary school - interestingly, even before birth in most people. In such studies, the hand and arm movements of unborn children in the womb are recorded using ultrasound images. Using this technique, it was shown that a clear preference for the movement of the right arm exists as early as 10 weeks after fertilization. In this study, ultrasound images of 72 unborn children 10 weeks after fertilization were evaluated and 85% showed more movements of the right arm than the left. This number is already very close to the approximately 89.4% right-handers among adults. These findings call into question the long-held belief that handedness is a product of after-birth development and instead support the view that ________________________________________.
options: ① one hand dominance arises from early motor training and reinforcement
② cognitive control develops primarily through writing activities in school
③ dominant hand usage is primarily the result of cultural conditioning
④ handedness emerges unpredictably during early childhood experiences
⑤ individual hand preference is established before birth, as shown by the early movement of the unborn children
explanation: 글의 중반부 이후에서 태아의 초음파 영상을 통해 수정 후 10주라는 아주 이른 시기(출생 전)에 이미 오른팔 운동에 대한 선호가 나타나며, 이 비율이 성인의 오른손잡이 비율과 비슷하다는 연구 결과를 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 기존의 '출생 후 발달의 산물'이라는 믿음을 반박하고, 손잡이 성향이 출생 전에 이미 결정된다는 내용인 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 한 손의 우세함은 초기 운동 훈련과 강화에서 비롯된다
② 인지 조절은 주로 학교에서의 쓰기 활동을 통해 발달한다
③ 우세한 손 사용은 주로 문화적 조건 형성의 결과이다
④ 손잡이 성향은 어린 시절의 경험 동안 예측 불가능하게 나타난다
⑤ 태아의 초기 움직임에서 보여지듯이, 개인의 손 선호도는 출생 전에 확립된다

question: 27. 다음 글의 핵심 내용을 효과적으로 반영하지 못한 사례는?
passage: We might forget an anecdote about a stranger because it makes few connections with our existing associations, but we won't forget a piece of gossip about our cousin. There's one complex network that is larger and quicker to access than all others - the self. We've been thinking about ourselves in our whole lives. (In fact, there were entire years during junior high when we weren't capable of thinking about much else.) So if a new piece of information has something to do with us, it will be more easily and thoroughly processed. It hits even closer to home than our actual home - we can take a vacation away from our home, but not from ourselves. The most effective communicators find ways to make the abstract personal. Consider the warning that law schools give to motivate first-year law students concerning the rigors of their program. Hearing that "the first-year dropout rate is 33%" is an abstract statistic. "Look to your left, look to your right. One of the three of you won't be joining us next fall" wakes up the self.
options: ① In a biology class, the teacher asks students to relate the process of digestion to what they ate for lunch that day.
② In a chemistry class, students write down a list of chemical reactions on their notes, which they struggle to memorize.
③ In an ethics class, students are asked to write about a personal dilemma they've faced and how it relates to moral theories.
④ In an English conversation class, students participate in interviews for their dream jobs, using vocabulary and expressions learned in class.
⑤ In a geography class, the teacher asks students to map out their daily route to school and analyze the geographical features or urban structures they encounter.
explanation: 지문의 핵심 내용은 '새로운 정보가 자기 자신(the self)과 관련될 때 더 쉽게 처리되고 기억된다'는 것과 '추상적인 것을 개인적인 것으로 만드는 것'이 효과적이라는 점입니다. ①, ③, ④, ⑤는 모두 학습 내용을 학생 개인의 경험, 생활, 목표와 연결시키는 사례입니다. 반면 ②는 단순히 화학 반응 목록을 개인적 연관성 없이 적고 암기하려고 애쓰는 모습이므로, '자기 참조 효과(self-reference effect)'를 활용하지 못한 사례에 해당합니다.
options_translation: ① 생물 수업에서, 선생님이 학생들에게 그날 점심으로 먹은 것과 소화 과정을 연관 지어 보라고 요청한다.
② 화학 수업에서, 학생들이 노트에 화학 반응 목록을 적고 이를 암기하느라 애를 먹는다.
③ 윤리 수업에서, 학생들은 자신이 직면했던 개인적인 딜레마와 그것이 도덕 이론과 어떻게 연관되는지에 대해 써 보라는 요청을 받는다.
④ 영어 회화 수업에서, 학생들은 수업 시간에 배운 어휘와 표현을 사용하여 자신의 꿈의 직업을 위한 인터뷰에 참여한다.
⑤ 지리 수업에서, 선생님은 학생들에게 학교까지 가는 매일의 경로를 지도로 그리고 그들이 마주치는 지리적 특징이나 도시 구조를 분석해 보라고 요청한다.

question: 28. 다음 글을 읽고 나눈 아래의 대화에서 글의 내용을 제대로 이해하지 못한 사람을 두 명 고르면?
passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. Wood suffers from splitting and is susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is limited. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex - or, as we call it now, the book - that the material reached its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a dominant form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, won out as the guardian of the written word is a remarkable materials story.
options: ① Amy: Cultural transmission in oral societies was highly dependent on memory and interpersonal interaction.
② Noze: The codex allowed paper to be used more effectively by solving the problems of earlier writing formats.
③ Ibuki: The history of writing materials shows how the codex became and has remained the dominant form of the written word.
④ Uwa: The fact that paper is softer than other materials such as stone or wood played a major role in hindering paper from serving as the guardian of the written word.
⑤ Marlee: It seems that paper still requires further innovation before it can reach the pinnacle of its potential as a medium.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 종이는 돌이나 나무보다 훨씬 부드러운 재료임에도 불구하고 기록된 단어의 수호자로서 승리했다고(won out) 설명되어 있으므로, 부드러움이 방해가 되었다는 Uwa의 말은 틀렸습니다. 또한, 로마 시대에 코덱스(책)의 형태로 발전하면서 종이가 잠재력에 도달했다고 했으며 현재까지도 지배적인 형태라고 언급되었으므로, 여전히 혁신이 더 필요하다는 Marlee의 의견도 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① Amy: 구전 사회에서의 문화적 전수는 기억과 대인 상호작용에 크게 의존했다.
② Noze: 코덱스는 초기 기록 포맷의 문제들을 해결함으로써 종이가 더 효과적으로 사용되도록 해주었다.
③ Ibuki: 필기 재료의 역사는 코덱스가 어떻게 기록된 단어의 지배적인 형태가 되었고 유지되어 왔는지를 보여준다.
④ Uwa: 종이가 돌이나 나무 같은 다른 재료들보다 부드럽다는 사실이 종이가 기록된 단어의 수호자 역할을 하는 것을 방해하는 주요한 역할을 했다.
⑤ Marlee: 종이가 매체로서의 잠재력의 정점에 도달하기 위해서는 여전히 추가적인 혁신이 필요한 것처럼 보인다.

question: 29. 다음 글을 읽고 나눈 아래의 대화에서 글의 내용을 제대로 이해하지 못한 사람을 두 명 고르면?
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis. For example, migrants are assumed to overcrowd cities, clog up labor markets, and increase poverty. The other questionable assumption is that most migration is involuntary - people fleeing natural or man-made disasters. The reality, however, is more complex, and many migrants are simply seeking greater economic opportunity. Of course migration can and does create social and economic problems. But migration can also be a solution for many preexisting problems. For example, out-migration generally redistributes workers from places of labor surplus to areas where there is greater demand or more opportunity. Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to endure hardship in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin. Most research that examines long-term outcomes of migration, including remittances and intergenerational mobility, finds positive "long-term" effects on places of origin and destination.
options: ① Aaliyah: Migration is often portrayed as an involuntary response to crises, but the passage shows that many migrants move in search of better opportunities.
② Kyoka: Migration mainly creates economic and social problems, and the text denies any significant positive effects.
③ Jay: Migration mostly involves people who are older and in poor health, struggling to adapt to new environments.
④ Kaeya: Migration contributes to both origin and destination areas in the long term by expanding opportunities for economic prosperity and social mobility.
⑤ Tasha: Migration helps shift workers from places with surplus labor to regions with greater demand.
explanation: 지문은 이주가 긍정적인 장기적 효과를 가진다고 언급하며 단순한 문제 이상의 복잡한 현실을 설명하므로, 긍정적 효과를 부정한다는 Kyoka의 말은 틀렸습니다. 또한 이주는 대개 더 젊고 건강하며 유연한 사람들을 선택한다고 했으므로, 주로 나이가 많고 건강이 좋지 않은 사람들이 이주한다는 Jay의 말도 지문과 정반대되는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① Aaliyah: 이주는 종종 위기에 대한 비자발적 반응으로 묘사되지만, 이 글은 많은 이주자가 더 나은 기회를 찾아 이동한다는 것을 보여준다.

question: 30. 다음 글을 바탕으로 추론할 때 Steve Jobs가 새로운 기술을 소개할 때 사용한 언어 전략에 대한 설명으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Steve Jobs used analogy to get people to embrace the new technology. Before computers, people worked in a physical world. We used paper and pens and physical file folders and so on. The idea of working in a virtual world was radically different. Or at least seemed radically different. What Jobs understood was that a physical office was fundamentally similar to a virtual office. To win over the masses, Jobs drew strong analogies between the traditional workplace people knew well with the new, unfamiliar virtual workplace. In the pre-computer workplace, when ideas were written on paper it was called ... a document. When those documents needed to be stored they were put in ... a folder. And those folders were kept on ... a desk. Documents, folders, and desktops are the terms we use in our virtual work because Steve Jobs understood that using familiar terms would make the new technology easier to understand. The parallels between the physical and virtual workplace now seem obvious.
options: ① He regarded literal naming as essential for users to fully grasp innovation.
② He prioritized technical precision over linguistic familiarity in his terminology.
③ He avoided comparisons to prevent misconceptions about digital environments.
④ He assumed users would naturally adapt to the logic of computing without support.
⑤ He believed that adopting metaphorical language would reduce users' resistance to change.
explanation: 이 글은 스티브 잡스가 컴퓨터라는 새로운 기술을 대중에게 소개할 때, 사람들이 이미 익숙한 물리적 세계의 개념(문서, 폴더, 데스크톱 등)을 비유(analogy)로 활용하여 생소한 가상 세계에 대한 이해를 돕고 거부감을 줄였다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 잡스는 익숙한 용어(familiar terms)를 사용하는 것이 새로운 기술을 더 쉽게 이해하도록 만든다는 점을 파악했습니다. 따라서 5번 '그는 비유적인 언어를 채택하는 것이 변화에 대한 사용자의 저항을 줄여줄 것이라고 믿었다'는 설명이 글의 내용과 가장 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 그는 사용자들이 혁신을 완전히 이해하기 위해 문자 그대로의 이름을 붙이는 것이 필수적이라고 여겼다.
② 그는 용어 선택에 있어 언어적 친숙함보다 기술적 정확성을 우선시했다.
③ 그는 디지털 환경에 대한 오해를 방지하기 위해 비교를 피했다.
④ 그는 사용자들이 지원 없이도 자연스럽게 컴퓨팅 논리에 적응할 것이라고 가정했다.
⑤ 그는 은유적인 언어를 채택하는 것이 변화에 대한 사용자의 저항을 줄여줄 것이라고 믿었다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
