When I first saw an elite diver do four and a half somersaults. I asked how he managed to spin so fast. His answer: "Just go up in a ball." Experts often have an ⓓ<u>intuitive</u> understanding of a route, but they find it ⓔ<u>difficult</u> to clearly express all the steps to take. (B)<u>Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage.</u>
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 전문가가 초보자에게 가르치는 것을 힘들어하는 이유(지식의 저주, 암묵적 지식 등)를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 첫 문장의 내용은 전문가가 종종 최고의 안내자가 '아님'을 의미해야 하므로, ⓐ 'best'는 'worst'나 'not the best' 등 부정적이거나 회의적인 맥락의 단어로 바뀌어야 합니다.

question: 23. 윗글에서 밑줄 친 (B)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It’s often said that those who can’t do, teach. It would be more accurate to say that those who can do, can’t teach the basics. A great deal of expert knowledge is implicit, not explicit. The further you progress toward mastery, the less conscious awareness you often have of the fundamentals. Experiments show that skilled golfers and wine aficionados have a hard time describing their putting and tasting techniques ? even asking them to explain their approaches is enough to interfere with their performance, so they often stay on autopilot. When I first saw an elite diver do four and a half somersaults, I asked how he managed to spin so fast. His answer: “Just go up in a ball.” Experts often have an intuitive understanding of a route, but they struggle to clearly express all the steps to take. Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage.
options: ① Experts' explanations can be a confusing mix of insight and unfiltered thoughts.
② Experts lose interest in basic concepts after reaching a high level of mastery.
③ Experts deliberately give misleading or incorrect information to challenge beginners' understanding.
④ Experts provide explicit explanation of complex processes to make their expertise more accessible to beginners.
⑤ Experts often overwhelm learners with too many technical details because they want to show off their expertise.
explanation: 전문가들이 쏟아내는 정보(brain dump)의 일부는 '쓸데없는 것(garbage)'으로 채워져 있다는 것은 전문가의 설명이 요점을 명확히 전달하기보다 불필요하거나 정제되지 않은 생각들이 얽혀 초보자를 혼란스럽게 할 수 있다는 뜻이다.
options_translation: ① 전문가들의 설명은 통찰력과 여과되지 않은 생각들의 혼란스러운 혼합물일 수 있다.
② 전문가들은 고도의 숙련도에 이른 후에는 기본 개념에 흥미를 잃는다.
③ 전문가들은 초보자의 이해에 도전하기 위해 일부러 오도하거나 잘못된 정보를 제공한다.
④ 전문가들은 초보자가 자신들의 전문 지식에 더 쉽게 접근할 수 있게 하려고 복잡한 과정에 대한 분명한 설명을 제공한다.
⑤ 전문가들은 자신들의 전문 지식을 과시하고 싶어서 종종 너무 많은 기술적인 세부 사항으로 학습자를 압도한다.

question: 27. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: The well-known American ethnologist Alfred Louis Kroeber made a rich and in-depth study of women's evening dress in the West, stretching back about three centuries and using reproductions of engravings. Having adjusted the dimensions of these plates due to their diverse origins, he was able to analyse the constant elements in fashion features and to come up with a study that was neither intuitive nor approximate, but precise, mathematical and statistical. He reduced women's clothing to a certain number of features: length and size of the skirt, size and depth of the neckline, height of the waistline. He demonstrated unambiguously that fashion is a profoundly regular phenomenon which is not located at the level of annual variations but on the scale of history. For practically 300 years, women's dress was subject to a very precise periodic cycle: forms reach the furthest point in their variations every fifty years. If, at any one moment, skirts are at their longest. fifty years later they will be at their shortest.
options: ① Kroeber는 약 300년 간의 서양 여성 이브닝드레스 변화를 분석했다.
② Kroeber는 다양한 출처의 판화를 조정하여 패션 특징의 일관된 요소를 분석했다.
③ Kroeber는 여성 의복의 특징을 수치화하고 통계적으로 분석했다.
④ Kroeber는 패션은 매년 변하는 규칙적인 현상이라고 결론 내렸다.
⑤ Kroeber의 연구 결과에 따르면 치마 길이는 약 50년 주기로 가장 길거나 가장 짧은 형태에 도달한다.
explanation: 지문에서 Kroeber는 패션이 '매년의 변화 수준에 있는 것이 아니라 역사의 척도에 있는 매우 규칙적인 현상(not located at the level of annual variations but on the scale of history)'이라고 명시했으므로, 매년 변하는 규칙적인 현상이라는 설명은 틀린 것입니다.

question: 31. 다음 글을 읽고, 아래 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 적절한 말을 <보기>의 표현을 모두 사용하여 각각 7단어 이하로 완성하시오. (어형 변화 불가능, 단어 추가 가능)
passage: Merely convincing your children that worry is senseless and that they would be more content if they didn't worry isn't going to stop them from worrying. For some reason, young people seem to believe that worry is a fact of life over which they have little or no control. Consequently, they don't even try to stop. Therefore, you need to convince them that worry, like guilt and fear, is merely an emotion, and like all emotions. it can be regulated through the strength of their own will. Tell them that they can eliminate worry from their lives by simply refusing to attend to it. Explain to them that if they refuse to act worried regardless of how they feel, they will eventually stop feeling worried and will begin to experience the contentment that accompanies a worry-free life.
summary_sentence: → The main idea of the text is that worry is (A)__________________, and young people need to be taught that worry is (B)__________________.
subjective_conditions: 각각 7단어 이하로 완성
어형 변화 불가능
단어 추가 가능
answer: (A) nothing more than an emotion(B) subject to the power of the will
explanation: 이 글은 걱정이 조절 불가능한 삶의 사실이 아니라, 죄책감이나 공포처럼 의지력을 통해 충분히 조절할 수 있는 '감정'에 불과하다는 사실을 아이들에게 가르쳐야 한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 걱정이 단지 감정일 뿐이라는 의미인 'nothing more than an emotion'이 적절하며, (B)에는 걱정이 의지력의 지배를 받는다는 의미인 'subject to the power of the will'이 들어가는 것이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: All of the restaurants are using carefully chosen words to evoke ⓐ<u>vivid</u> mental images of delicious food and rich desserts in order to draw the potential customer to their particular establishment. Just like the restaurants, nature has its own dining establishments. In a fashion similar to the restaurants' ⓑ<u>financial</u> dependence upon drawing in many customers, the restaurateurs of the natural world (i.e., flowers) must also attract potential diners to sample their offerings. In the natural world, there are no neon signs or ⓒ<u>flashy</u> words in which to market a potential meal to hungry animals. These restaurants that I am referring to are the world's flowers, and the potential guests are the host of organisms that visit flowers to obtain nectar and other ⓓ<u>valueless</u> resources. Instead of using a written language or neon sign, they advertise their offerings just as ⓔ<u>effectively</u> using the language of smell.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 꽃은 꿀(nectar)과 같은 보상을 제공하여 유기체들을 유인합니다. 따라서 이러한 자원은 '가치 없는(valueless)' 것이 아니라 '가치 있는(valuable)' 것이어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
passage: It is difficult, if not impossible, to define the limits which reason should impose on the desire for wealth; for there is no absolute or definite amount of wealth which will satisfy a man. The amount is always relative, that is to say, just so much as will maintain the proportion between what he wants and what he gets; for to measure a man's happiness only by what he gets, and not also by what he expects to get, is as pointless as to try and express a fraction which shall have a numerator but no denominator. A man never feels the loss of things which it never occurs to him to ask for; he is just as happy without them; whilst another, who may have a hundred times as much, feels miserable because he has not got the one thing he wants. In fact, every man has a horizon of his own, and he will expect as much as he thinks it is possible for him to get.
options: ① Happiness is determined by how other perceive our success.
② Each person has a unique standard of desire and happiness.
③ People who expect less always end up wealthier in the long run.
④ True happiness lies in appreciating what others have achieved.
⑤ The more wealth a person has, the more likely they are to feel satisfied.
explanation: 글의 내용은 부에 대한 갈망과 만족이 절대적인 수치가 아니라 개인이 기대하는 바와 얻는 것 사이의 상대적인 관계에 달려 있으며, 사람마다 자신만의 지평(기준)을 가지고 있다는 것이 핵심입니다.
options_translation: ① 행복은 타인이 우리의 성공을 어떻게 인식하느냐에 의해 결정된다.
② 개개인은 욕망과 행복에 대한 고유한 기준을 가지고 있다.
③ 적게 기대하는 사람들이 결국 장기적으로 더 부유해진다.
④ 진정한 행복은 타인이 성취한 것을 인정하는 데 있다.
⑤ 사람이 더 많은 부를 가질수록, 만족감을 느낄 가능성이 더 높다.

question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
passage: Would you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month? Most people will opt for the larger sum in thirteen months ─ where else will you find a monthly interest rate of 10 percent. (A) A wise choice, since the interest will compensate you generously for any risks you face by waiting the extra few weeks. (B) Second question: Would you prefer $1,000 today cash on the table or $1,100 in a month? (C) If you think like most people, you'll take the $1,000 right away. This is amazing. In both cases, if you hold out for just a month longer, you get $100 more. In the first case, it's simple enough. (D) You figure: "I've already waited twelve months; what's one more?" Not in the second case. The introduction of "now" causes us to make inconsistent decisions. (E) The closer a reward is, the higher our "emotional interest rate" rises and the more we are willing to give up in exchange for it.
insertion_sentence: Science calls this phenomenon hyperbolic discounting.
explanation: 제시된 문장의 'this phenomenon(이 현상)'은 앞 문장에서 설명한 '보상이 가까울수록 감정적 이율이 올라가 당장의 보상을 위해 더 큰 미래 보상을 포기하는 비일관적인 결정'을 가리킵니다. 따라서 이 현상에 대한 학술적 명칭인 'hyperbolic discounting'을 소개하는 문장은 글의 결론 부분인 (E) 자리에 오는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.6점]
passage: Of central importance for understanding the development of handedness is the answer to the question of when in development it is actually determined whether a child will be left-handed or right-handed. It was long thought that handedness could only be reliably determined in elementary school, when a child learns to write. However, this assumption is incorrect. In fact, scientific studies show that left-handedness is established in many children long before elementary school ─ interestingly, even before birth in most people. In such studies, the hand and arm movements of unborn children in the womb are recorded using ultrasound images. Using this technique, it was shown that a clear preference for the movement of the right arm exists as early as 10 weeks after fertilization. In this study, ultrasound images of 72 unborn children 10 weeks after fertilization were evaluated and 85% showed more movements of the right arm than the left. This number is already very close to the approximately 89.4% right-handers among adults.
options: ① 과거에는 아이가 글을 쓰는 것을 배우는 시점에서 손잡이를 알 수 있다고 여겼다.
② 연구에 따르면 많은 아이들의 손잡이는 태어나기 전에 결정된다.
③ 수정 후 10주 된 태아의 팔 움직임은 초음파 영상으로 분석되었다.
④ 오른팔을 더 많이 사용하는 태아는 약 85%로 보고되었다.
⑤ 성인의 오른손잡이 비율은 태아기 팔 움직임 결과와 크게 다르다.
explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 태아의 오른팔 움직임 비율(85%)이 성인의 오른손잡이 비율(약 89.4%)과 '이미 매우 가깝다(very close to)'고 했으므로, 크게 다르다는 설명은 일치하지 않습니다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
passage: We might forget an anecdote about a stranger because it makes few connections with our existing associations, but we won't forget a piece of gossip about our cousin. There's one complex network that is larger and quicker to access than all others ─ the self. We've been thinking about ourselves in our whole lives. (In fact, there were entire years during junior high when we weren't capable of thinking about much else.) So if a new piece of information has something to do with us, it will be more easily and thoroughly processed. It hits even closer to home than our actual home ─ we can take a vacation away from our home, but not from ourselves. The most effective communicators find ways to make the abstract personal. Consider the warning that law schools give to motivate first-year law students concerning the rigors of their program. Hearing that "the first-year dropout rate is 33%" is an abstract statistic. "Look to your left, look to your right. One of the three of you won't be joining us next fall" wakes up the self.
options: ① Why We Lie to Strangers
② Why We Remember What's About Us
③ What Makes a Statistic True or False
④ The Secrets of Logical Communication
⑤ The Reason We Ignore Stories About Strangers
explanation: 이 글은 새로운 정보가 우리 자신과 관련이 있을 때 더 쉽고 철저하게 처리된다는 점을 설명하며, 자기 자신이라는 네트워크가 정보 기억과 처리에 강력한 역할을 한다는 것을 강조합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리가 낯선 사람에게 거짓말을 하는 이유
② 우리 자신에 관한 것을 더 잘 기억하는 이유

question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Steve Jobs used ____________ to get people to embrace the new technology. Before computers, people worked in a physical world. We used paper and pens and physical file folders and so on. The idea of working in a virtual world was radically different. Or at least seemed radically different. What Jobs understood was that a physical office was fundamentally similar to a virtual office. To win over the masses, Jobs drew strong analogies between the traditional workplace people knew well with the new, unfamiliar virtual workplace. In the pre-computer workplace, when ideas were written on paper it was called . . . a document. When those documents needed to be stored they were put in . . . a folder. And those folders were kept on . . . a desk. Documents, folders, and desktops are the terms we use in our virtual work because Steve Jobs understood that using familiar terms would make the new technology easier to understand. The parallels between the physical and virtual workplace now seem obvious.
options: ① analogy
② emotion
③ definition
④ prediction
⑤ translation
explanation: 스티브 잡스가 가상 세계의 개념을 익숙한 물리적 세계의 개념(문서, 폴더, 데스크탑)과 연결하여 설명했다는 내용이므로, '비유(analogy)'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 비유
② 감정
③ 정의
④ 예측

question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.0점]
passage: Turtle hatchlings have, it seems, evolved to crawl toward the light. For millions of years this was a highly rational and effective strategy because the light on a dark beach represented the reflection of the moon and stars on the water's surface. (A) Following the lights led baby turtles back home to the sea. (B) Now after hatching, turtles heading for the brightest nearby lights were being guided straight into traffic. (C) Are self-destructive sea turtles naturally irrational? (D) Yes, in the modern world. But there's a deeper truth. (E) Turtles are basing their decisions on simple cues that were perfectly rational for their ancestors; these days, however, their evolved decision-making mechanisms are being blinded by modern lights.
insertion_sentence: The problems started when humans began building beachfront homes and sparkling hotels on the other side of the beach.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 '문제가 시작되었다'는 내용과 그 원인(해변가 건물들의 불빛)을 설명하고 있습니다. (A)까지는 거북이가 빛을 따라가는 조상들의 합리적인 생존 방식이 설명되고, (B)부터는 현대의 불빛 때문에 교통 체증 속으로 뛰어드는 '문제'가 발생하므로 (B) 자리가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis. For example, migrants are assumed to ⓐ<u>overcrowd</u> cities, clog up labor markets, and increase poverty. The other questionable assumption is that most migration is ⓑ<u>involuntary</u> ─ people fleeing natural or man-made disasters. The reality, however, is more complex, and many migrants are simply seeking greater economic opportunity. Of course migration can and does create social and economic problems. But migration can also be a ⓒ<u>solution</u> for many preexisting problems. For example, out-migration generally redistributes workers from places of labor surplus to areas where there is greater ⓓ<u>surplus.</u> Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to ⓔ<u>endure</u> hardship in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin. Most research that examines long-term outcomes of migration, including remittances and intergenerational mobility, finds positive "long-term" effects on places of origin and destination. *clog: 막히게 하다 **remittance: 송금
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이주가 노동력을 재배치하는 역할을 한다고 했으므로, 노동력이 '잉여(surplus)'인 곳에서 노동력이 '부족(shortage/need)'한 곳으로 이동해야 문맥상 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 surplus는 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
passage: The writer and zoologist Desmond Morris observed that our feet communicate exactly what we think and feel more honestly than any other part of our bodies. Why are the feet and legs such accurate reflectors of our sentiments? For millions of years, long before humans spoke, our legs and feet reacted to environmental threats (e.g., hot sand, illtempered lions) instantaneously, without the need for conscious thought. Our limbic brains made sure that our feet and legs reacted as needed by either ceasing motion, running away, or kicking at a potential threat. This survival regimen, retained from our ancestral heritage, has served us well and continues to do so today. In fact, these age-old reactions are still so hardwired in us that when we are presented with something dangerous or even disagreeable, our feet and legs still react as they did in prehistoric times.
summary_sentence: Our feet and legs reflect our true emotions because they are influenced by (A)_____________ that were originally developed for responding to (B)_____________.
options: ① (A) instinctive reactions - (B) threats
② (A) emotion expressions - (B) people
③ (A) social behaviors - (B) danger
④ (A) hardwired behaviors - (B) emotion
⑤ (A) conscious decisions - (B) physical pain

question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The big problem with money created by the government is that those who run the government always face the temptation to create more money and spend it. Whether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, leading to inflation and the many economic and social problems that follow from inflation. For this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that is inherently limited in supply, as money. It is a way of depriving governments of the power to expand the money supply to inflationary levels. Gold has long been considered ideal for this purpose, since the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased rapidly. When paper money is convertible into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money is said to be "backed up" by gold. This expression is misleading only if we imagine that the value of the gold is somehow transferred to the paper money, when in fact the real point is that the gold simply limits the amount of paper money that can be issued.

passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. Wood suffers from splitting and is susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is limited. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex ─ or, as we call it now, the book ─ that the material reached its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a dominant form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, won out as the guardian of the written word is a remarkable materials story.

question: 24. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: The study of emotions and decision making is now of considerable importance. This involves the application of various tools afforded by neuroscience. One important stream of the literature examines people with brain damage and how damage to particular parts of the brain known to be responsible for particular cognitive functions impacts on decision making. One example of this research is the work of Antonio Damasio, who finds that when the emotional part of the brain is damaged, this actually reduces the efficacy of decision making. Good decisions are a product of the emotional part of the brain working in conjunction with the deliberative part. This contradicts the assumptions of conventional economics, where emotions play a negative role in the decision-making process. Here it is assumed that decision making can be modeled as being generated in a stoic, unemotional fashion, and that's why decisions tend to be optimal. But the evidence suggests that emotions actually play an important and, often, a positive role in decision making.
options: ① 다마지오는 뇌의 특정 영역의 손상이 인지 및 정서에 미치는 영향을 연구했다.
② 다마지오의 연구에 따르면, 감정 관련 뇌 부위가 손상되면 의사결정 능력이 저하된다.
③ 감정가 이성적 사고는 함께 작용하여 좋은 결정을 내리게 한다.
④ 전통적인 경제학은 감정을 의사결정에 부정적인 요소로 본다.
⑤ 감정은 의사결정에 긍정적인 역할을 할 수 있다.
explanation: 본문에서 안토니오 다마지오의 연구는 뇌의 특정 부위(특히 감정 관련 부위)의 손상이 '인지 및 정서 자체'에 미치는 영향이라기보다, 그것이 '의사결정(decision making)'에 어떤 영향을 미치는지를 연구한 것입니다. 1번 선택지는 연구의 궁극적인 초점인 '의사결정에 미치는 영향'이 누락되어 있어 지문의 핵심 내용과 가장 거리가 멉니다. 반면 2, 3, 4, 5번은 지문의 내용과 정확히 일치합니다.

question: 9. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world. Simply put, the brain is not designed to sense on its own. They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as incoherent thought patterns. question: 26. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Shoppers confronted with the choice of thirty different varieties of gourmet chocolates are more likely to walk away without buying any, compared with when they are presented with only half a dozen choices. If employees are given a free trip to Paris, they are happy. If you give them a free trip to Hawaii, they are happy. But if you offer them the choice between the two destinations, they are less happy, no matter what they choose. Why might choice be so disruptive? The reason is that choice forces us to make comparisons and acknowledge relative disadvantages. People who choose Paris complain that it doesn't have the ocean and those who choose Hawaii regret that it doesn't have the museums. Psychologist Barry Schwartz calls this the 'tyranny of choice' because rather than providing freedom, it actually constrains our decision-making. He argues that broader choice increases unhappiness because we worry that we are going to make the wrong decision and so we get stressed about trying to process all the comparisons in an effort to get it right. This both increases our fear of making the wrong choice and raises expectations that we should be able to get the best choice. Having made the choice, we then start to regret, wondering whether it was the right one.
options: ① Ways to Secure Your Own Happiness

③ Tyranny: What Makes Us Feel Stressed Out

question: 32. 다음 글을 읽고, <보기>의 단어를 배열하여 제시된 요약문의 (A), (B)를 완성하시오.
passage: Would you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month? Most people will opt for the larger sum in thirteen months - where else will you find a monthly interest rate of 10 percent. A wise choice, since the interest will compensate you generously for any risks you face by waiting the extra few weeks. Second question: Would you prefer $1,000 today cash on the table or $1,100 in a month? If you think like most people, you'll take the $1,000 right away. This is amazing. In both cases, if you hold out for just a month longer, you get $100 more. In the first case, it's simple enough. You figure: "I've already waited twelve months; what's one more?" Not in the second case. The introduction of "now" causes us to make inconsistent decisions. Science calls this phenomenon hyperbolic discounting. Hyperbolic discounting is our inclination to choose immediate rewards over rewards that come later in the future, even when these immediate rewards are smaller.

question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Steve Jobs used analogy to get people to embrace the new technology. Before computers, people worked in a physical world. We used paper and pens and physical file folders and so on. The idea of working in a virtual world was radically different. Or at least seemed radically different. What Jobs understood was that a physical office was fundamentally similar to a virtual office. To win over the masses, Jobs drew strong analogies between the traditional workplace people knew well with the new, unfamiliar virtual workplace. In the pre-computer workplace, when ideas were written on paper it was called ... a document. When those documents needed to be stored they were put in ... a folder. And those folders were kept on ... a desk. Documents, folders, and desktops are the terms we use in our virtual work because Steve Jobs understood that using familiar terms would make the new technology easier to understand. The parallels between the physical and virtual workplace now seem obvious.
options: ① Innovative Use of Analogies
② The History of Computer Terms
③ The Evolution of Physical Workplaces
④ Challenges in Developing Virtual Offices
⑤ Differences Between Physical and Virtual Workplaces
explanation: 이 글은 스티브 잡스가 사람들이 낯선 가상 세계(컴퓨터)의 개념을 쉽게 받아들일 수 있도록 '문서', '폴더', '데스크톱'과 같이 기존 사무실에서 사용하던 익숙한 용어들을 비유(analogy)로 사용했다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 가장 적절한 제목은 '비유의 혁신적인 사용'입니다. (원문의 정답 표시인 ②번은 '컴퓨터 용어의 역사'인데, 지문의 핵심인 '비유를 통한 신기술 수용'을 담기엔 ①번이 더 적절하나, 시험지의 정답 표기에 따라 ②로 기재하되 해설상으로는 비유의 활용이 핵심입니다.)

question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Would you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month? Most people will opt for the larger sum in thirteen months - where else will you find a monthly interest rate of 10 percent. (A) A wise choice, since the interest will compensate you generously for any risks you face by waiting the extra few weeks. Second question: Would you prefer $1,000 today cash on the table or $1,100 in a month? (B) If you think like most people, you'll take the $1,000 right away. (C) This is amazing. In both cases, if you hold out for just a month longer, you get $100 more. In the first case, it's simple enough. You figure: "I've already waited twelve months; what's one more?" Not in the second case. (D) Science calls this phenomenon hyperbolic discounting. (E) The closer a reward is, the higher our "emotional interest rate" rises and the more we are willing to give up in exchange for it.
insertion_sentence: The introduction of "now" causes us to make inconsistent decisions.
explanation: 지문은 먼 미래의 보상에 대해서는 이성적으로 기다리지만, '지금 당장'의 보상이 개입될 때는 일관성 없는 선택을 하는 인간의 특성을 설명하고 있습니다. (C) 이후의 문장에서 두 사례(1년 뒤 vs 오늘)의 차이를 설명하며 두 번째 사례에서는 기다리지 못한다는 점을 지적합니다. 따라서 '현재(now)'의 도입이 일관성 없는 결정을 내리게 한다는 주어진 문장은 이 현상을 '하이퍼볼릭 디스카운팅'이라 부른다는 과학적 정의(D) 바로 앞에 위치하는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Of central importance for understanding the development of handedness is the answer to the question of when in development it is actually determined whether a child will be left-handed or right-handed.
ordered_passages: (A) In such studies, the hand and arm movements of unborn children in the womb are recorded using ultrasound images. Using this technique, it was shown that a clear preference for the movement of the right arm exists as early as 10 weeks after fertilization.

(B) It was long thought that handedness could only be reliably determined in elementary school, when a child learns to write. However, this assumption is incorrect. In fact, scientific studies show that left-handedness is established in many children long before elementary school-interestingly, even before birth in most people.

(C) In this study, ultrasound images of 72 unborn children 10 weeks after fertilization were evaluated and 85% showed more movements of the right arm than the left. This number is already very close to the approximately 89.4% right-handers among adults.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 주주리 손잡이 결정 시기에 대한 질문을 제기합단다. (B)에서 기존의 통념(초등학교 때 결정)이 틀렸음을 밝히고, 태아 시기에 결정된다는 과학적 연구를 언급합니다. (A)는 (B)에서 말한 '괴연구(such studies)'의 구체적인 방박(초음파)을 설명하며, (C)는 괴 연구의 구체적인 통계 치(85%)를 제시하며 결론을 내립니다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 개수는? [25년 6월 29번]
passage: In art, there are a number of ways to use perspective to obtain the illusion of depth, ⓐ<u>included</u> using colors and graduated values of black and white, and ⓑ<u>accurately</u> drawing the subject by applying the rules of the geometric system of perspective. In order to achieve perspective, you must make a number of observations. The forms or objects that you draw on a flat surface actually ⓒ<u>has</u> depth and dimension in real life. As you view them and place their shapes and forms on a drawing surface, ⓓ<u>trying</u> to represent that depth to make the objects ⓔ<u>appear</u> realistic and three-dimensional. Objects appear differently when ⓕ<u>viewing</u> from various positions. Because of this, it's important to establish the viewpoint, and stick with ⓖ<u>it</u>. When observing a subject, you see depth and three dimensions. When you draw this subject onto a flat surface as it appears to the eye, you are ⓗ<u>drawn</u> in perspective.
options: ① 3개
② 4개
③ 5개
④ 6개
⑤ 7개
explanation: 어법상 어색한 부분은 총 5개입니다.ⓐ included → including: '~를 포함하여'라는 의미의 능동 분사구문이 적절합니다.ⓒ has → have: 주어가 복수인 'The forms or objects'이므로 복수 동사가 필요합니다.ⓓ trying → try: 'As you view...'로 시작하는 절 뒤에 이어지는 주절이므로 명령문 형태인 동사원형이 필요합니다.ⓕ viewing → viewed: 물체(Objects)가 '보여지는' 수동의 관계이므로 과거분사가 적절합니다.ⓗ drawn → drawing: '당신이 ~을 그리고 있는 중이다'라는 의미의 능동형 진행형이 필요합니다.옳은 것: ⓑ accurately (부사로 drawing 수식), ⓔ appear (사역동사 make의 목적격 보어로 원형부정사), ⓖ it (단수인 viewpoint를 지칭)

question: 21. 다음 주어진 글에 있는 문법적인 오류 세 곳을 찾아 바르게 고치고 그 이유를 설명하시오.
passage: Filippo Brunelleschi is considered to be the founding father of Renaissance architecture. He was born in Florence in 1377. Filippo was artistically talented, and trained as a goldsmith and a clockmaker before becoming an architect. When he was around 25, he traveled to Rome with his friend, the sculptor Donatello, which he studied the remains of ancient Roman buildings. His first architectural commission was the Ospedale degli Innocenti, that is one of the great Renaissance buildings. A number of other fine works, including chapels in Florentine churches, strengthened his reputation. And the stunning dome of Il Duomo is his masterpiece. He also designed machinery to produce special effects in theatrical productions. He died in Florence and buried in Il Duomo.
answer:
(1) which → where / 수정 이유: 선행사 'Rome'을 수식하는 관계사절이 완전한 문장이므로 관계부사 where가 적절합니다.
(2) , that → , which / 수정 이유: 관계대명사 that은 계속적 용법(콤마 뒤)으로 사용할 수 없으므로 which로 고쳐야 합니다.
(3) buried → was buried / 수정 이유: 주어인 Brunelleschi가 '안치된(묻힌)' 수동의 관계이므로 수동태인 was buried가 적절합니다.
explanation:
지문에서 어법상 어색한 세 부분을 찾아 수정하는 문제입니다. 
(1) Rome을 장소의 선행사로 하며 뒤에 완전한 문장이 이어지므로 관계부사 where가 적절합니다. 
(2) 관계대명사의 계속적 용법에서는 'that'을 사용할 수 없으므로 'which'로 수정해야 합니다.
(3) 문맥상 주인공이 '안치된' 것이므로 수동태 형식이 필요하며, 앞의 died와 병렬 구조를 이루어 was buried가 되어야 합니다.

question: 16. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 23. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 'A wave of doubt washed over her'가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It was the championship race. Emma was the final runner on her relay team. She anxiously waited in her spot for her teammate to pass her the baton. question: 24. 다음 글과 관련된 속담으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We collect stamps, coins, vintage cars even when they serve no practical purpose. The post office doesn't accept the old stamps, the banks don't take old coins, and the vintage cars are no longer allowed on the road. These are all side issues; the attraction is that they are in short supply. In one study, students were asked to arrange ten posters in order of attractiveness - with the agreement that afterward they could keep one poster as a reward for their participation. Five minutes later, they were told that the poster with the third highest rating was no longer available. Then they were asked to judge all ten from scratch. The poster that was no longer available was suddenly classified as the most beautiful. In psychology, this phenomenon is called reactance: when we are deprived of an option, we suddenly deem it more attractive.
options: ① Don't cry over spilt milk.
② Out of sight, out of mind.
③ Forbidden fruit is the sweetest.
④ Many hand makes light works.
⑤ Saying is one thing, doing is another.

options_translation: ① 엎질러진 물을 두고 울지 마라. (이미 일어난 일은 후회해도 소용없다.)
② 눈에서 멀어지면 마음에서도 멀어진다.
③ 금지된 열매가 가장 달콤하다.
④ 백지장도 맞들면 낫다.
⑤ 말하는 것과 행동하는 것은 별개다.

question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 가장 적절한 답을 고르면?Q. Suppose a young professional is offered a high-paying job that requires giving up his moral values and personal free time. Based on the passage, what advice would the author most likely give him.
passage: Take a look at some of the most powerful, rich, and famous people in the world. Ignore the trappings of their success and what they're able to buy. Look instead at what they're forced to trade in return - look at what success has cost them. Mostly? Freedom. Their work demands they wear a suit. Their success depends on attending certain parties, kissing up to people they don't like. It will require - inevitably - realizing they are unable to say what they actually think. Worse, it demands that they become a different type of person or do bad things. Sure, it might pay well - but they haven't truly examined the transaction. As Seneca put it, "Slavery resides under marble and gold." Too many successful people are prisoners in jails of their own making. Is that what you want? Is that what you're working hard toward? Let's hope not.
options: ① Carefully consider what personal freedoms might be sacrificed before making a decision.
② Accept the job for its financial benefits and prioritize earning a higher salary above all else.
③ Seek social approval at all costs, even if it means sacrificing your own values and beliefs.
④ Ignore any feelings of discomfort and proceed with the job regardless of your personal concerns.
⑤ Focus solely on climbing the corporate ladder and dedicate all your efforts to career advancement.
explanation: 필자는 성공한 사람들이 그 대가로 자유를 희생하고 자신의 생각과 다르게 행동하거나 나쁜 일을 하게 되는 등 '자신이 만든 감옥'에 갇히게 된다고 경고하고 있습니다. 따라서 고소득 직장이 도덕적 가치와 자유 시간을 희생하라고 요구한다면, 결정을 내리기 전에 희생될 개인적 자유에 대해 신중히 고려하라고 조언할 것입니다.
options_translation: ① 결정을 내리기 전에 어떤 개인적 자유가 희생될 수 있는지 신중하게 고려하라.
② 경제적 이득을 위해 일자리를 수락하고 다른 무엇보다 높은 급여를 받는 것을 우선시하라.
③ 자신의 가치관과 신념을 희생하더라도 수단과 방법을 가리지 말고 사회적 승인을 구하라.
④ 불편한 기분은 무시하고 개인적인 우려와 상관없이 일을 진행하라.
⑤ 오로지 기업 내 승진에만 집중하고 경력 발전에 모든 노력을 바쳐라.

question: 29. 윗글의 밑줄 친 This가 의미하는 것은?
passage: Brains are expensive in terms of energy. Twenty percent of the calories we consume are used to power the brain. So brains try to operate in the most energy-efficient way possible, and that means processing only the minimum amount of information from our senses that we need to navigate the world. Neuroscientists weren't the first to discover that fixing your gaze on something is no guarantee of seeing it. Magicians figured this out long ago. By directing your attention, they perform tricks with their hands in full view. Their actions should give away the game, but they can rest assured that your brain process only small bits of the visual scene. <u>This</u> all helps to explain the prevalence of traffic accidents in which drivers hit pedestrians in plain view, or collide with cars directly in front of them. In many of these cases, the eyes are pointed in the right direction, but the brain isn't seeing what's really out there.
options: ① the brain's habit of saving energy by filtering sensory input
② the increase in accidents involving distracted or careless drivers
③ the brain's focus on what is directly in the center of your vision
④ the illusions magicians create by shifting attention from key actions
⑤ the human ability to maintain focus on objects directly in their sight
explanation: 밑줄 친 'This'는 앞 문장에서 설명한 내용, 즉 뇌가 에너지 효율을 위해 시각적 장면의 아주 작은 부분만을 처리한다는 특성을 의미합니다. 이러한 뇌의 정보 필터링 습관 때문에 눈앞에 있는 보행자나 차량을 보지 못해 사고가 발생하는 현상을 설명할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 감각 입력을 필터링하여 에너지를 절약하는 뇌의 습관
② 주의가 산만하거나 부주의한 운전자와 관련된 사고의 증가
③ 시야의 바로 중앙에 있는 것에 대한 뇌의 집중
④ 핵심 동작에서 주의를 돌려 마술사들이 만들어내는 환상
⑤ 시야에 직접적으로 들어오는 물체에 계속 집중하는 인간의 능력

passage: Brains are expensive in terms of energy. Twenty percent of the calories we consume are used to power the brain. By directing your attention, they perform tricks with their hands in full view. subjective_conditions: 주어와 서술어로 구성된 문장으로 작성할 것

question: 31. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 아래 <보기>의 단어 중 알맞은 것을 골라 주어진 요약문을 완성하시오.
passage: We tend to break up time into units, such as weeks, months, and seasons; in a series of studies among farmers in India and students in North America, psychologists found that if a deadline is on the other side of a "break" - such as in the New Year - we're more likely to see it as remote, and, as a result, be less ready to jump into action. What you need to do in that situation is find another way to think about the timeframe. For example, if it's November and the deadline is in January, it's better to tell yourself you have to get it done "this winter" rather than "next year." The best approach is to view deadlines as a challenge that you have to meet within a period that's imminent. That way the stress is more manageable, and you have a better chance of starting - and therefore finishing - in good time.
summary_sentence: To act faster on a deadline, _________________________.
subjective_conditions: 한 문장으로 작성할 것
보기에서 필요한 단어를 한 번만 사용할 것
어형 변화 가능
vocabulary_box: need to / near / finish / overcome / think / it / suffer / is / create / we / ignore
answer: we need to think it is near
explanation: 지문의 핵심 내용은 마감 기한을 멀게 느끼면 행동이 늦어지므로, 마감 기한이 임박한(imminent) 기간 내에 있다고 생각해야 한다는 것입니다. 따라서 '마감 기한에 더 빨리 대처하기 위해서는, 그것이 가깝다고 생각할 필요가 있다'는 의미가 되도록 보기의 단어를 조합하여 'we need to think it is near'를 완성합니다.

question: 3. 다음 밑줄 친 a piece of gossip about our cousin이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We might forget an anecdote about a stranger because it makes few connections with our existing associations, but we won't forget <u>a piece of gossip about our cousin</u>. There's one complex network that is larger and quicker to access than all others ─ the self. We've been thinking about ourselves in our whole lives. (In fact, there were entire years during junior high when we weren't capable of thinking about much else.) So if a new piece of information has something to do with us, it will be more easily and thoroughly processed. It hits even closer to home than our actual home ─ we can take a vacation away from our home, but not from ourselves. The most effective communicators find ways to make the abstract personal. Consider the warning that law schools give to motivate first-year law students concerning the rigors of their program. Hearing that "the first-year dropout rate is 33%" is an abstract statistic. "Look to your left, look to your right. One of the three of you won't be joining us next fall" wakes up the self.*rigor: 엄격함
options: ① knowledge gained from past experiences
② information that lacks personal relevance
③ rumors that are groundless and invade privacy
④ information that concerns the listener personally
⑤ information that has been more thoroughly processed
explanation: 글의 주제는 정보가 자기 자신(the self)과 관련이 있을 때 더 잘 기억되고 처리된다는 '자기 참조 효과'입니다. '사촌에 관한 가십'은 모르는 타인의 이야기보다 자신과 더 밀접한 관련이 있는 정보를 의미하므로, 듣는 사람과 개인적으로 관련이 있는 정보를 뜻하는 4번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 과거의 경험으로부터 얻은 지식
② 개인적 관련성이 부족한 정보
③ 근거가 없고 사생활을 침해하는 소문
④ 듣는 사람과 개인적으로 관련된 정보
⑤ 더 철저하게 처리된 정보

question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis. For example, migrants are assumed to overcrowd cities, clog up labor markets, and increase poverty. The other questionable assumption is that most migration is involuntary ─ people fleeing natural or man-made disasters. The reality, however, is more complex, and many migrants are simply seeking greater economic opportunity. Of course migration can and does create social and economic problems. But migration can also be a solution for many preexisting problems. For example, out-migration generally redistributes workers from places of labor surplus to areas where there is greater demand or more opportunity. Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to endure hardship in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin. Most research indicates that migration has lasting positive effects on both origin and destination regions, including through remittances and intergenerational mobility.*clog: 막히게 하다 **remittance: 송금
options: ① 세계적인 대규모 이주의 주된 원인은 자연재해이다.
② 도시는 이주로 인해 인구 밀집과 빈곤이 심화되고 있다.
③ 이주는 문제로만 인식되지만 양 지역에 긍정적 영향을 가져온다.
④ 경제적 약자의 생활 수준은 이주로 인해 점차 낮아지고 있다.
⑤ 출신지의 경제 기반은 이주로 인해 장기적으로 약화되고 있다.
explanation: 이주(migration)가 흔히 문제나 위기로 묘사되지만, 실제로는 노동력 재배치 등 기존 문제의 해결책이 될 수 있으며, 출발지와 목적지 양쪽 모두에 지속적인 긍정적 영향(lasting positive effects on both origin and destination regions)을 미친다는 내용의 글입니다.

question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Shoppers confronted with the choice of thirty different varieties of gourmet chocolates are more likely to walk away without buying any, compared with when they are presented with only half a dozen choices. If employees are given a free trip to Paris, they are happy. If you give them a free trip to Hawaii, they are happy. But if you offer them the choice between the two destinations, they are less happy, no matter what they choose. Why might choice be so disruptive? The reason is that choice forces us to make comparisons and acknowledge relative disadvantages. People who choose Paris complain that it doesn't have the ocean and those who choose Hawaii regret that it doesn't have the museums. Psychologist Barry Schwartz calls this the 'tyranny of choice' because rather than providing freedom, it actually constrains our decision-making. He argues that wider choice increases unhappiness because we worry that we are going to make the wrong decision and so we get stressed about trying to process all the comparisons in an effort to get it right. This both increases our fear of making the wrong choice and raises expectations that we should be able to get the best choice. Having made the choice, we then start to regret, wondering whether it was the right one.
options: ① the influence of product variety on marketing success
② how too many options restrain our decision-making
③ cultural preferences in vacation decision-making
④ the psychological benefits of consumer freedom
⑤ how incentives increase workplace motivation
explanation: 선택지가 너무 많을 때 사람들은 오히려 결정을 내리지 못하거나, 결정을 내린 후에도 후회와 스트레스를 느끼게 된다는 '선택의 폭정(tyranny of choice)'에 관한 글입니다. 너무 많은 옵션이 의사 결정을 제한하고 불행하게 만든다는 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 제품 다양성이 마케팅 성공에 미치는 영향
② 너무 많은 선택지가 우리의 의사 결정을 제한하는 방식
③ 휴가 의사 결정에서의 문화적 선호도
④ 소비자 자유의 심리학적 이점
⑤ 인센티브가 직장 동기 부여를 증가시키는 방법

question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The big problem with money created by the government is that those who run the government always face the temptation to _______________________. Whether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, leading to inflation and the many economic and social problems that follow from inflation. For this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that is inherently limited in supply, as money. It is a way of depriving governments of the power to expand the money supply to inflationary levels. Gold has long been considered ideal for this purpose, since the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased rapidly. When paper money is convertible into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money is said to be "backed up" by gold. This expression is misleading only if we imagine that the value of the gold is somehow transferred to the paper money, when in fact the real point is that the gold simply limits the amount of paper money that can be issued.
options: ① reduce spending and balance the budget
② create more money and spend it
③ create more jobs through public employment
④ print less money to avoid inflation
⑤ invest in gold and other stable assets
explanation: 정부가 발행하는 화폐의 문제점은 정부 운영자들이 돈을 더 많이 찍어내어 지출하려는 유혹을 받는다는 것입니다. 이러한 화폐 공급의 팽창은 인플레이션을 유발하기 때문에, 이를 방지하기 위해 공급이 제한적인 '금'을 화폐의 기준으로 삼아 지폐 발행량을 제한하려 한다는 논리입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 정부의 유혹인 '더 많은 돈을 만들어 지출하는 것'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 지출을 줄이고 예산 균형을 맞추려는
② 더 많은 돈을 만들어 지출하려는
③ 공공 고용을 통해 더 많은 일자리를 창출하려는
④ 인플레이션을 피하기 위해 돈을 덜 찍어내려는
⑤ 금과 다른 안정적인 자산에 투자하려는

question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Turtle hatchlings have, it seems, evolved to crawl toward the light.
ordered_passages: (A) The problems started when humans began building beachfront homes and sparkling hotels on the other side of the beach. Now after hatching, turtles heading for the brightest nearby lights were being guided straight into traffic. Are self-destructive sea turtles naturally irrational?(B) For millions of years this was a highly rational and effective strategy because the light on a dark beach represented the reflection of the moon and stars on the water's surface. Following the lights led baby turtles back home to the sea.(C) Yes, in the modern world. But there's a deeper truth. Turtles are basing their decisions on simple cues that were perfectly rational for their ancestors; these days, however, their evolved decision-making mechanisms are being blinded by modern lights.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 바다거북 부화마가 빛을 향해 기어가는 본능을 가졌다는 내용입니다. (B)에서 수백만 년 동안 이것이 왜 합리적이었는지(달빛의 반사를 따라 바다로 유도) 설명합니다. (A)에서 현대 인공 조명으로 인해 이 전략이 문제가 되어 거북이들이 도로로 향하게 된다는 상황을 제시하고 질문을 던집니다. (C)에서 그 질문에 답하며 현대의 빛이 진화된 메커니즘을 방해하고 있다는 결론으로 마무리됩니다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]
passage: Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world. Simply put, the brain is not designed to sense on its own. (A) For instance, an exposed brain would neither sense light shining on it nor feel something touching it. (B) In fact, patients are often kept awake during brain surgery, which can help a surgeon isolate specific regions of the brain. (C) The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle recognized this characteristic of the brain over 2,000 years ago when he said, "Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses." (D) This concept can be seen clearly when volunteers are blind-folded and placed in the warm water of a sensory deprivation tank. (E) From these experiments and others, it is apparent that we need constant input from our senses to carry out functions that give us personality and intellect.
insertion_sentence: They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as incoherent thought patterns.
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'They'는 (D) 문장에 언급된 감각 박탈 탱크에 들어간 자원봉사자들을 지칭합니다. 탱크 속에서 감각이 차단된 자원봉사자들이 환각과 사고 장애를 겪는다는 내용이 실험의 결과로 제시되어야 하며, (E) 문장의 'From these experiments'를 통해 이러한 실험 결과로부터 얻은 결론(감각 입력의 필요성)으로 이어지는 것이 논리적으로 적절합니다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Would you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month? Most people will opt for the larger sum in thirteen months ─ where else will you find a monthly interest rate of 10 percent. A wise choice, since the interest will compensate you generously for any risks you face by waiting the extra few weeks. Second question: Would you prefer $1,000 today cash on the table or $1,100 in a month? If you think like most people, you'll take the $1,000 right away. This is amazing. In both cases, if you hold out for just a month longer, you get $100 more. In the first case, it's simple enough. You figure: "I've already waited twelve months; what's one more?" Not in the second case. The introduction of "now" causes us to make inconsistent decisions. Science calls this phenomenon hyperbolic discounting. The closer a reward is, the higher our "emotional interest rate" rises and the more we are willing to give up in exchange for it.
summary_sentence: People tend to choose (A)__________ rewards when they are (B)__________ while they wouldn't make the same choice if both options were in the future.
options: ① smaller imminent
② smaller delayed
③ smaller distant
④ bigger reserved
⑤ bigger immediate
explanation: 사람들은 보상이 주어지는 시점이 아주 가까울 때(imminent), 이성적으로는 더 큰 보상을 기다리는 것이 유리함에도 불구하고 감정적 이율이 상승하여 당장의 더 작은(smaller) 보상을 선택하는 경향이 있다는 '쌍곡선 할인' 현상을 설명하는 글입니다.
options_translation: ① 더 작은 - 임박한
② 더 작은 - 지연된
③ 더 작은 - 먼
④ 더 큰 - 보류된
⑤ 더 큰 - 즉각적인

question: 16. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: It is difficult, if not impossible, to define the limits which reason should impose on the desire for wealth: for there is no absolute or definite amount of wealth which will satisfy a man. The amount is always relative, that is to say, just so much as will maintain the proportion between what he wants and what he gets: for to measure a man's happiness only by what he gets, and not also by what he expects to get, is as pointless as to try and express a fraction which shall have a numerator but no denominator. A man never feels the loss of things which it never occurs to him to ask for: he is just as happy without them: whilst another, who may have a hundred times as much, feels miserable because he has not got the one thing he wants. passage: A reason for a conclusion is very unlikely to consist in a single claim. No matter how we might state it in short-hand, it is, analytically, a complex interaction of many ideas and implications. The reason must be broken down into a chain of more precise premises. For example, the claim that 'university education should be free for all Australians' might be supported by the reason that 'the economy benefits from a well-educated Australian population'. But is our analysis of the situation clearly expressed in just one statement? Hardly. The conclusion is about universities and free education, while the reason introduces some new ideas: economic-benefit and a well-educated population. While the link between these two ideas and the conclusion might seem obvious, the purpose of reasoning is to avoid assuming the 'obvious' by carefully working through the connections between the various ideas in the initial statement of our reason.

passage: We are the only species that seasons its food, deliberately altering it with the highly flavored plant parts we call herbs and spices. In contrast, the most lightly spiced cuisines - those of Scandinavia and northern Europe - are from cooler climates. question: 34. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 36. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 it doesn't가 의미하는 것을 찾아 영어로 구체적으로 쓰시오.
passage: It's untrue that teens can focus on two things at once - what they're doing is shifting their attention from one task to another. In this digital age, teens wire their brains to make these shifts very quickly, but they are still, like everyone else, paying attention to one thing at a time, sequentially. Common sense tells us multitasking should increase brain activity, but Carnegie Mellon University scientists using the latest brain imaging technology find <u>it doesn't</u>. As a matter of fact, they discovered that multitasking actually decreases brain activity. Neither task is done as well as if each were performed individually. Fractions of a second are lost every time we make a switch, and a person's interrupted task can take 50 percent longer to finish, with 50 percent more errors. Turns out the latest brain research supports the old advice "one thing at a time." It's not that kids can't do some tasks simultaneously. But if two tasks are performed at once, one of them has to be familiar. Our brains perform a familiar task on "automatic pilot" while really paying attention to the other one. That's why insurance companies consider talking on a cell phone and driving to be as dangerous as driving while drunk - it's the driving that goes on "automatic pilot" while the conversation really holds our attention. Our kids may be living in the Information Age but our brains have not been redesigned yet.
explanation: 지문에서 'Common sense tells us multitasking should increase brain activity, but... find it doesn't.'라고 언급되어 있습니다. 여기서 'it doesn't'는 앞 문장의 'multitasking should increase brain activity'를 부정하며 실제로는 그렇지 않다는 것을 의미하므로, '멀티태스킹이 뇌 활동을 증가시키지 않는다'는 의미인 'multitasking doesn't increase brain activity'가 정답입니다.

explanation: ⑤의 which는 타동사 seeing의 목적어 역할을 해야 하며, 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 문장이 오고 있습니다. 그런데 which는 선행사가 필요하지만 여기서는 수식을 받을 선행사가 없습니다. 따라서 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사인 what으로 고쳐야 '거기 정말로 있는 것'이라는 의미가 되어 자연스럽습니다.① that: consume의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 문장을 이끄는 목적격 관계대명사로 적절합니다.② means: 앞 문장 전체를 선행사로 하는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which의 동사로, 단수 취급하여 -s가 붙은 형태가 적절합니다.③ fixed: gaze(시선)가 무언가에 고정된(수동) 상태를 나타내므로 과거분사가 적절합니다.④ where: traffic accidents를 수식하며 뒤에 완전한 문장이 이어지므로 관계부사로 적절합니다.

question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We collect stamps, coins, vintage cars even when they serve no practical purpose. The post office doesn't accept the old stamps, the banks don't take old coins, and the vintage cars are no longer allowed on the road. These are all side issues; the attraction is that they are in short supply. In one study, students were asked to arrange ten posters in order of attractiveness - with the agreement that afterward they could keep one poster as a reward for their participation. Five minutes later, they were told that the poster with the third highest rating was no longer available. Then they were asked to judge all ten from scratch. The poster that was no longer available was suddenly classified as the most beautiful. In psychology, this phenomenon is called reactance: when we are deprived of an option, we suddenly deem it more attractive.
options: ① The Role of Rewards in Student Motivation
② The Psychology of First Impressions in Experiments
③ The Reason We Should Limit Options in Experiments
④ How Limited-Edition Collectibles Gain Educational Value
⑤ The Reason behind the Attractiveness of the Unavailable
explanation: 이 글은 심리학의 '저항(reactance)' 현상을 설명하고 있습니다. 실용적인 목적이 없더라도 공급이 부족하거나(short supply), 선택권이 박탈되었을 때(deprived of an option) 그것을 더 매력적으로 느낀다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로는 '이용 불가능한 것의 매력 뒤에 숨겨진 이유'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 학생 동기 부여에서 보상의 역할
② 실험에서 첫인상의 심리학
③ 실험에서 선택지를 제한해야 하는 이유
④ 한정판 수집품이 교육적 가치를 얻는 방법
⑤ 이용 불가능한 것의 매력 뒤에 숨겨진 이유

question: 5. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: As the old joke goes: "Software, free. User manual, $10,000." But it's no joke. A couple of highprofile companies make their living selling instruction and paid support for free software. The copy of code, being mere bits, is free. The lines of free code become valuable to you only through support and guidance. A lot of medical and genetic information will go this route in the coming decades. Right now getting a full copy of all your DNA is very expensive ($10,000), but soon it won't be. The price is dropping so fast, it will be $100 soon, and then the next year insurance companies will offer to sequence you for free. When a copy of your sequence costs nothing, the interpretation of what it means, what you can do about it, and how to use it - the manual for your genes - will be expensive.
summary_sentence: As with software, the value of genetic data will (A)___________ not on access but on interpretation; sequencing may be cheap, but (B)___________ its implications will be costly.
options: ① (A) depend --- (B) decoding
② (A) intrude --- (B) comprehending
③ (A) dwell --- (B) limiting
④ (A) concentrate --- (B) challenging
⑤ (A) rely --- (B) criticizing
explanation: 글의 요지는 소프트웨어나 유전자 데이터 자체(복사본, 접근)는 무료가 되지만, 그것을 해석하고 활용하는 방법(매뉴얼, 지침)이 가치를 지니게 된다는 것입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 가치가 해석에 '달려 있다(depend)'가 적절하고, (B)에는 그것의 의미를 '해독하는 것(decoding)'이 비싸질 것이라는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 달려 있다 --- (B) 해독하는 것
② (A) 침범하다 --- (B) 이해하는 것
③ (A) 거주하다 --- (B) 제한하는 것
④ (A) 집중하다 --- (B) 도전하는 것
⑤ (A) 의존하다 --- (B) 비판하는 것

question: 6. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Imagine that seven out of ten working Americans got fired tomorrow. What would they all do? It's hard to believe you'd have an economy at all if you gave pink slips to more than half the labor force.
ordered_passages: (A) But that is what the industrial revolution did to the workforce of the early 19th century. Two hundred years ago, 70 percent of American workers lived on the farm. Today automation has eliminated all but 1 percent of their jobs, replacing them with machines.

(B) Since then, wave upon wave of new occupations have arrived - appliance repair person, food chemist, photographer, web designer - each building on previous automation. Today, the vast majority of us are doing jobs that no farmer from the 1800s could have imagined.

(C) However, the displaced workers did not sit idle. Instead, automation created hundreds of millions of jobs in entirely new fields. Those who once farmed were now manning the factories that manufactured farm equipment, cars, and other industrial products.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 미국 노동자의 70%가 해고되는 상황을 가정합니다. (A)에서 이것이 바로 산업혁명이 19세기에 했던 일이라며 과거의 실업(농업 자동화)을 언급합니다. (C)에서 '하지만(However)'을 통해 그들이 빈둥거리지 않고 자동화가 만든 새로운 분야(공장 등)에서 일하게 되었음을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 '그 이후로(Since then)'를 통해 더 현대적인 새로운 직업들이 생겨났음을 순차적으로 제시합니다.

question: 7. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Take a look at some of the most powerful, rich, and famous people in the world. Ignore the trappings of their success and what they're able to buy.
ordered_passages: (A) Therefore, it will require - inevitably - realizing they are unable to say what they actually think. Worse, it demands that they become a different type of person or do bad things. Sure, it might pay well - but they haven't truly examined the transaction.

(B) Look instead at what they're forced to trade in return - look at what success has cost them. Mostly? Freedom. Their work demands they wear a suit. Their success depends on attending certain parties, kissing up to people they don't like.

(C) As Seneca put it, "Slavery resides under marble and gold." Too many successful people are prisoners in jails of their own making. Is that what you want? Is that what you're working hard toward? Let's hope not.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 성공한 사람들의 겉모습(장식)을 무시하라고 합니다. (B)에서 '그 대신(instead)' 그들이 성공을 위해 지불한 비용(자유의 상실)을 보라고 하며 구체적인 예시(양복 착용, 아부)를 듭니다. (A)에서 '그러므로(Therefore)' 그들은 자신의 생각을 말하지 못하고 다른 사람이 되어야 함을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 세네카의 말을 인용하며 성공한 사람들이 스스로 만든 감옥의 수인이라는 결론을 내립니다.

question: 8. 다음 글을 읽고 이해한 내용으로 옳은 것은?
passage: We tend to break up time into units, such as weeks, months, and seasons. In a series of studies among farmers in India and students in North America, psychologists found that if a deadline is on the other side of a "break" - such as in the New Year - we're more likely to see it as remote. As a result, we're likely to be less ready to jump into action. What you need to do in that situation is find another way to think about the timeframe. For example, if it's November and the deadline is in January, it's better to tell yourself you have to get it done "this winter" rather than "next year." The best approach is to view deadlines as a challenge that you have to meet within a period that's imminent. That way the stress is more manageable, and you have a better chance of starting - and therefore finishing - in good time.*imminent: 임박한
options: ① Deadlines that come after a "break" "can be considered to be closer than they actually are.
② We are encouraged to jump into action when a deadline seems remote.
③ When it's November, thinking of a January deadline as "this winter" can be less motivating than "next year."
④ The likelihood that we finish our task on time increases when we see our deadline as fast-approaching.
⑤ Viewing deadlines as distant challenges helps to improve productivity.
explanation: 글의 후반부에서 마감 기한을 임박한(imminent) 것으로 바라보는 것이 스트레스를 관리하기 쉽게 하고, 제때 시작하여 끝낼 가능성을 높여준다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 마감 기한이 빠르게 다가오고 있다고 생각할 때 일을 제시간에 마칠 가능성이 높아진다는 4번이 글의 내용과 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① '휴식기' 이후에 오는 마감 기한은 실제보다 더 가깝게 여겨질 수 있다.
② 마감 기한이 멀게 느껴질 때 우리는 즉각 행동에 나서도록 장려된다.
③ 11월일 때, 1월 마감 기한을 '내년'보다 '이번 겨울'로 생각하는 것이 동기 부여가 덜 될 수 있다.
④ 마감 기한이 빠르게 다가오고 있다고 볼 때 우리가 업무를 제때 마칠 가능성이 증가한다.
⑤ 마감 기한을 먼 도전으로 보는 것이 생산성 향상에 도움이 된다.

question: 9. 다음 A~E 중에서 글에 대해 올바르게 이해하고 있는 사람은?
passage: On our little world, light travels, for all practical purposes, instantaneously. If a lightbulb is glowing, then of course it's physically where we see it, shining away. We reach out our hand and touch it: It's there all right, and unpleasantly hot. If the filament fails, then the light goes out. We don't see it in the same place, glowing, illuminating the room years after the bulb breaks and it's removed from its socket. The very notion seems nonsensical. But if we're far enough away, an entire sun can go out and we'll continue to see it shining brightly; we won't learn of its death, it may be, for ages to come - in fact, for how long it takes light, which travels fast but not infinitely fast, to cross the intervening vastness. The immense distances to the stars and the galaxies mean that we see everything in space in the past.*instantaneously: 순간적으로 **intervene: 사이에 들다
options: ① A: The speed of light eliminates any delay between the event in the universe and its observation.
② B: As light travels infinitely fast, any star that dies is immediately removed from our view, regardless of its distance from Earth.
③ C: Since light from distant galaxies reaches us instantly, just like lightbulb, we can observe the universe in their present state.
④ D: The vast expanses between the Earth and the galaxies ensure that our view of the universe is essentially a look into the distant past.
⑤ E: Once a light source which is close enough to us, such as a lightbulb, goes out, the human eye continues to perceive its glow for a substantial amount of time due to light's speed.
explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장에서 별과 은하까지의 거대한 거리는 우리가 우주의 모든 것을 과거의 모습으로 본다는 것을 의미한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 지구와 은하 사이의 광활한 공간 때문에 우주를 보는 것이 본질적으로 먼 과거를 들여다보는 것과 같다는 D의 설명이 옳습니다.
options_translation: ① A: 빛의 속도는 우주에서의 사건과 그 관찰 사이의 어떠한 지연도 없앤다.
② B: 빛은 무한히 빠르게 이동하므로, 죽은 별은 지구와의 거리와 상관없이 즉시 우리 시야에서 사라진다.
③ C: 먼 은하로부터의 빛은 전구처럼 즉각 우리에게 도달하므로, 우리는 우주의 현재 상태를 관찰할 수 있다.
④ D: 지구와 은하 사이의 광활한 구역은 우리가 우주를 보는 것이 본질적으로 먼 과거를 보는 것임을 보장한다.
⑤ E: 전구와 같이 충분히 가까운 광원이 꺼지면, 빛의 속도 때문에 인간의 눈은 상당한 시간 동안 그 잔광을 계속 감지한다.

question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Buying a television is current consumption. It makes us happy today but does nothing to make us richer tomorrow. Yes, money spent on a television keeps workers employed at the television factory. But if the same money were invested, it would create jobs somewhere else, say for scientists in a laboratory or workers on a construction site, while _________________ __________________________. Think about college as an example. Sending students to college creates jobs for professors. Using the same money to buy fancy sports cars for high school graduates would create jobs for auto workers. The crucial difference between these scenarios is that a college education makes a young person more productive for the rest of his or her life; a sports car does not. Thus, college tuition is an investment; buying a sports car is consumption.
options: ① promoting students' applications for a scholarship in college
② increasing a person's long-term productivity and wealth
③ resolving instructor shortage problems in the educational industry
④ contributing to assessing the nation's overall level of education
⑤ facilitating subordinate values in life, such as how much people spend money
explanation: 이 글은 텔레비전이나 스포츠카 구매와 같은 '소비'와 대학 교육과 같은 '투자'의 차이를 대조하고 있습니다. 소비는 현재의 즐거움을 주지만 미래를 더 부유하게 만들지는 못하는 반면, 투자는 일자리 창출뿐만 아니라 사람을 장기적으로 더 생산적으로 만듭니다. 빈칸은 투자(대학 교육 예시와 연결됨)의 결과로 생기는 긍정적 효과가 들어가야 하므로, 장기적인 생산성과 부를 늘려준다는 내용의 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 대학에서의 장학금 신청 장려
② 개인의 장기적인 생산성과 부의 증대
③ 교육계의 강사 부족 문제 해결
④ 국가의 전반적인 교육 수준 평가에 기여
⑤ 사람들이 돈을 얼마나 쓰는지와 같은 삶의 부수적인 가치 촉진

question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Most people ________________________________, probably because they fear it might mean downgrading some of their beliefs about who they are and what they're capable of. As Goethe's maxim goes, it is a great failing "to see yourself as more than you are." How could you really be considered self aware if you refuse to consider your weaknesses? Don't fear self assessment because you're worried you might have to admit some things about yourself. The second half of Goethe's maxim is important too. He states that it is equally damaging to "value yourself at less than your true worth." We underestimate our capabilities just as much and just as dangerously as we overestimate other abilities. Cultivate the ability to judge yourself accurately and honestly. Look inward to discern what you're capable of and what it will take to unlock that potential.*maxim: 격언
options: ① acknowledge their true self
② overlook the idea of mutual respect
③ avoid judging themselves objectively
④ accept that they have inappropriate self-concept
⑤ tend to develop the abilities they've already found before
explanation: 글 전체에서 자신에 대해 정확하고 정직하게 판단할 수 있는 능력을 기르는 것의 중요성을 강조하고 있습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 내용은 사람들이 자신의 신념을 하향 조정해야 할까 봐 두려워한다는 이유를 설명하므로, 사람들이 '스스로를 객관적으로 판단하는 것을 피한다'는 내용의 ③번이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 자신의 진정한 자아를 인정한다
② 상호 존중의 개념을 간과한다
③ 자신을 객관적으로 판단하는 것을 피한다
④ 자신이 부적절한 자아 개념을 가지고 있음을 받아들인다
⑤ 이전에 이미 발견한 능력을 개발하는 경향이 있다

question: 13. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Many things spark envy: ownership, status, health, youth, talent, popularity, beauty. It is often confused with jealousy because the physical reactions are identical. (A)____________, the subject of each notion is different : envy deals with a thing (status, money, health), and the subject of jealousy is the behaviour of a third person. Envy needs two people. Jealousy, on the other hand, requires three: Peter is jealous of Sam because the beautiful girl next door rings him instead. Paradoxically, with envy we direct resentments toward those who are most similar to us in age, career and residence. (B)____________, We don't envy businesspeople from the century before last. We don't envy millionaires on the other side of the globe. As a writer, I don't envy musicians, managers or dentists, but other writers. As a CEO you envy other, bigger CEOs. As a supermodel you envy more successful supermodels. Aristotle knew this: 'Potters envy potters.'
options: ① In other words ... Surprisingly
② However ... For instance
③ For example ... Whereas
④ Moreover ... Certainly
⑤ Nevertheless ... Meanwhile
explanation: (A)의 앞부분에서는 부러움과 질투가 물리적 반응이 같아 혼동된다고 했지만, 뒷부분에서는 각 개념의 대상이 다르다고 설명하고 있으므로 역접의 'However'가 적절합니다. (B)의 앞부분에서는 우리가 자신과 비슷한 사람들에게 원망(부러움)을 느낀다는 원칙을 제시했고, 뒷부분에서는 시대가 다르거나 먼 곳에 있는 사람이 아닌, 같은 직업군(작가, CEO 등)의 사람을 부러워한다는 구체적인 예시를 들고 있으므로 'For instance'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다시 말해서 ... 놀랍게도
② 그러나 ... 예를 들어
③ 예를 들어 ... 반면에
④ 게다가 ... 확실히
⑤ 그럼에도 불구하고 ... 한편

question: 15. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Imagine that there is little or no diversity of views, and all scientists see, think, and question the world in a similar way. ⓐThen they will not, as a community, be as objective as they maintain they are, or at least aspire to be. ⓑThe solution is that there should be far greater diversity in the practice of science: in gender, ethnicity, and social and cultural backgrounds. ⓒThe political neutrality of scientists is easily overlooked because of their social status and expertise. ⓓScience works because it is carried out by people who pursue their curiosity about the natural world and test their and each other's ideas from as many varied perspectives and angles as possible. ⓔWhen science is done by a diverse group of people, and if consensus builds up about a particular area of scientific knowledge, then we can have more confidence in its objectivity and truth.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 과학에서 다양성(성별, 민족, 배경 등)이 확보되어야 과학적 객관성을 가질 수 있다는 내용입니다. ③번 문장은 과학자의 '정치적 중립성'에 대해 언급하고 있으나, 이는 글의 전체 주제인 '다양성을 통한 객관성 확보'와는 거리가 멉니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: If a firm is going to be saved by the government, it might be easier to concentrate on lobbying the government for more money rather than taking the harder decision of restructuring the company to be able to be profitable and viable in the long term. (A) This is an example of something known as moral hazard - when government support alters the decisions firms take. question: 19. 윗글을 읽고 이해한 내용으로 옳은 것은?

② One-way interaction has turned the Internet into a hub for commerce.
③ A few clicks are not enough to carry out most shopping-related tasks.
④ The Net makes the connection only between individuals and commercial entities.
⑤ Many people use the Internet to both distribute their own digital works and interact with others.
explanation: 이 글은 인터넷이 기존의 대중 매체와 달리 양방향(bidirectional) 성격을 띠고 있어 정보의 송수신이 자유롭고, 상업적 통로뿐만 아니라 개인적인 방송 매체의 역할도 수행하며 타인의 창작물에 대한 피드백도 가능하게 함을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 5번 '많은 사람들이 자신의 디지털 작품을 유포하고 타인과 상호작용하기 위해 인터넷을 사용한다'는 내용이 정답입니다.

③ 몇 번의 클릭으로는 대부분의 쇼핑 관련 업무를 수행하기에 충분하지 않다.
④ 인터넷은 개인과 상업적 실체 사이에서만 연결을 만든다.

question: 21. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: If we've invested in something that hasn't ⓐ<u>repaid</u> us - be it money in a failing venture, or time in an unhappy relationship - we find it very difficult to walk away. This is the sunk cost fallacy. Our instinct is ⓑ<u>to continue</u> investing money or time as we hope that our investment will prove to be worthwhile in the end. Giving up would mean acknowledging that we've ⓒ<u>been wasted</u> something we can't get back, and that thought is so painful that we prefer to avoid it if we can. The problem, of course, is that if something really is a bad bet, then staying with it simply ⓓ<u>increases</u> the amount we lose. Rather than walk away from a bad five-year relationship, for example, we turn it into a bad 10-year relationship; rather than accept that we've lost a thousand dollars, we lay down another thousand and ⓔ<u>lose</u> that too. In the end, by delaying the pain of admitting our problem, we only add to it. Sometimes we just have to cut our losses.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓒ 'been wasted'는 현재완료 수동태(have been p.p.) 형식이나, 뒤에 'something'이라는 목적어가 뒤따르고 있으므로 수동태가 아닌 능동태인 'wasted' (현재완료 have wasted)가 쓰여야 문법적으로 옳습니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
passage: A reason for a conclusion is very unlikely to consist in a single claim. No matter how we might state it in short-hand, it is, analytically, a complex interaction of many ideas and implications. The reason must be broken down into a chain of more precise premises. For example, the claim that 'university education should be free for all Australians' might be supported by the reason that 'the economy benefits from a well-educated Australian population'. But is our analysis of the situation clearly expressed in just one statement? Hardly. The conclusion is about universities and free education, while the reason introduces some new ideas: economic benefit and a well-educated population. While the link between these two ideas and the conclusion might seem obvious, the purpose of reasoning is to avoid assuming the 'obvious' by carefully working through the connections between the various ideas in the initial statement of our reason.
options: ① Complex arguments should be simplified into one clear sentence to be better understood.
② Conclusions about public policy, such as free university education, do not require logical analysis.
③ Identifying errors in reasoning is more important than understanding how conclusions are supported.
④ A valid reason for a conclusion requires analyzing a set of related ideas, not relying on a single obvious statement.
⑤ The most persuasive conclusions are presented in a single clear and concise statement.
explanation: 이 글은 결론에 대한 근거가 단 하나의 주장으로 이루어질 가능성은 낮으며, 분석적으로 볼 때 여러 아이디어와 함축된 의미들의 복잡한 상호작용으로 구성된다고 설명합니다. 따라서 근거는 더 정밀한 전제들의 연쇄로 분해되어야 하며, 단순히 '당연한 것'으로 가정하지 말고 연결 고리를 면밀히 살펴야 한다는 것이 핵심입니다. 이를 가장 잘 요약한 것은 ④번입니다.
options_translation: ① 복잡한 주장은 더 잘 이해되기 위해 하나의 명확한 문장으로 단순화되어야 한다.
② 대학 무상 교육과 같은 공공 정책에 대한 결론은 논리적 분석을 필요로 하지 않는다.
③ 추론에서 오류를 식별하는 것이 결론이 어떻게 뒷받침되는지 이해하는 것보다 더 중요하다.
④ 결론에 대한 유효한 근거는 단 하나의 명백한 진술에 의존하는 것이 아니라, 연관된 아이디어들의 집합을 분석하는 것을 필요로 한다.
⑤ 가장 설득력 있는 결론은 하나의 명확하고 간결한 진술로 제시된다.

question: 33. Which of the following statements does not agree with the passage?
passage: It is difficult, if not impossible, to define the limits which reason should impose on the desire for wealth; for there is no absolute or definite amount of wealth which will satisfy a man. The amount is always relative, that is to say, just so much as will maintain the proportion between what he wants and what he gets; for to measure a man's happiness only by what he gets, and not also by what he expects to get, is as pointless as to try and express a fraction which shall have a numerator but no denominator. A man never feels the loss of things which it never occurs to him to ask for; he is just as happy without them; whilst another, who may have a hundred times as much, feels miserable because he has not got the one thing he wants. In fact, every man has a horizon of his own, and he will expect as much as he thinks it is possible for him to get.*fraction: 분수 **numerator: 분자 ***denominator: 분모

question: 9. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.8점]

question: 11. 다음 글의 내용을 바탕으로 migration의 부정적인 면과 긍정적인 면을 아래와 같이 분류할 때 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.3점]
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis. For example, migrants are assumed to overcrowd cities, clog up labor markets, and increase poverty. The other questionable assumption is that most migration is involuntary - people fleeing natural or man-made disasters. The reality, however, is more complex, and many migrants are simply seeking greater economic opportunity. Of course migration can and does create social and economic problems. But migration can also be a solution for many preexisting problems. For example, out-migration generally redistributes workers from places of labor surplus to areas where there is greater demand or more opportunity. Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to endure hardship in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin. Most research that examines long-term outcomes of migration, including remittances and inter-generational mobility, finds positive "long-term" effects on places of origin and destination.negative aspect (부정적인 면)ⓐoversupplying the workforce in labor marketsⓑincreasing poverty and cities undergoing overcrowdingpositive aspect (긍정적인 면)ⓒredistribution of labor surplusⓓyounger persons' willingness to endure hardship back in their home countriesⓔremittances and inter-generational mobility as long-term outcomes
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 지문에서 이주민들은 더 나은 삶을 희망하며 고난을 견딜 의지가 있는 사람들이라고 설명하지만, 이는 자신의 고국(home countries)에서 견디는 것이 아니라 더 나은 기회가 있는 곳으로 이동하는 맥락입니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 'back in their home countries'는 글의 내용과 흐름상 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 17. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The study of emotions and decision making is now of considerable importance. This involves the application of various tools afforded by neuroscience. One important stream of the literature examines people with brain damage and how damage to particular parts of the brain known to be responsible for particular cognitive functions impacts on decision making. One example of this research is the work of Antonio Damasio, who finds that when the emotional part of the brain is damaged, this actually reduces the efficacy of decision making. Good decisions are a product of the emotional part of the brain working in conjunction with the deliberative part. This contradicts the assumptions of conventional economics, where emotions play a negative role in the decision-making process. Here it is assumed that decision making can be modeled as being generated in a stoic, unemotional fashion, and that's why decisions tend to be optimal. But the evidence suggests that emotions actually play an important and, often, a positive role in decision making. to make a long story short, the brain's emotional part working in relation with its deliberative part enhances the effectiveness of decision making, which counters the ideas about emotions in the decision-making process of traditional economics.
options: ① Conventional economic theories deny Antonio Damasio's finding that decision making can happen in an unemotional way.
② Effective decision making occurs when the deliberative and emotional parts of the brain work in cooperation.
③ The traditional economic assumptions see emotions as useful factors in rational decision making.
④ Scientific tools are essential to examine how brain damage of cognitive parts influences decision making.
⑤ There are significant differences in researching methods between conventional and modern neuroscience.
explanation: 이 글은 뇌의 감정적인 부분과 숙고하는 부분이 서로 협력하여 작동할 때 의사 결정의 효율성이 높아진다는 신경과학의 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 감정을 의사 결정의 부정적인 요인으로 보았던 전통적인 경제학의 가설과 대조되는 내용입니다. 따라서 주제로는 감정과 숙고 부위의 협력을 통한 효과적인 의사 결정을 언급한 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 전통적인 경제 이론은 의사 결정이 감정이 없는 방식으로 일어날 수 있다는 Antonio Damasio의 발견을 부정한다.
② 효율적인 의사 결정은 뇌의 숙고하는 부분과 감정적인 부분이 협력하여 작동할 때 발생한다.

④ 인지 부위의 뇌 손상이 의사 결정에 어떻게 영향을 미치는지 조사하기 위해 과학적 도구는 필수적이다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
passage: Would. you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month? A wise choice, since the interest will ⓑ<u>compensate</u> you generously for any risks you face by waiting the extra few weeks. Second question: Would you prefer $1,000 today cash on the table or $1,100 in a month? If you think like most people, you'll take $1,000 right away. This is amazing. question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: Financial markets do more than take capital from the rich and lend it to everyone else. They enable each of us to smooth consumption over our lifetimes, which is a fancy way of saying that we don't have to spend income at the same time we earn it. Shakespeare may have admonished us to be neither borrowers nor lenders; the fact is that most of us will be both at some point. If we lived in an agrarian society, we would have to eat our crops reasonably soon after the harvest or find some way to store them. Financial markets are a more sophisticated way of managing the harvest. We can spend income now that we have not yet earned - as by borrowing for college or a home or we can earn income now and spend it later, as by saving for retirement. The important point is that earning income has been divorced from spending it, allowing us much more flexibility in life.
options: ① problems with borrowing practice
② risks of relying on financial markets
③ inequality caused by financial systems
④ separation of earning and spending income
⑤ criticism of consumer culture and materialism
