question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Many people look for safety and security in popular thinking. They figure that if a lot of people are doing something, then it must be right. It must be a good idea. If most people accept it, then it probably represents fairness, equality, compassion, and sensitivity, right? Not necessarily. Popular thinking said the earth was the center of the universe, yet Copernicus studied the stars and planets and proved mathematically that the earth and the other planets in our solar system revolved around the sun. Popular thinking said surgery didn't require clean instruments, yet Joseph Lister studied the high death rates in hospitals and introduced antiseptic practices that immediately saved lives. Popular thinking said that women shouldn't have the right to vote, yet people like Emmeline Pankhurst and Susan B. Anthony fought for and won that right. We must always remember there is a huge difference between acceptance and intelligence. People may say that there's safety in numbers, but that's not always true.
options: ① What We Believe: Universal Truths
② The Easy Path: Following the Majority
③ The Power of the Crowd: Safety in Numbers
④ Great Discoveries in History: Celebrating Human Ingenuity
⑤ The Fallacy of Popular Thinking: Why the Majority Isn't Always Right
explanation: 이 글은 대중적인 사고(popular thinking)가 항상 옳은 것은 아니라는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 지문에서는 지구가 우주의 중심이라는 믿음, 수술 시 청결이 불필요하다는 믿음, 여성의 투표권 불허 등 과거의 잘못된 대중적 통념을 사례로 들며, 수용(acceptance)과 지능(intelligence) 사이에는 큰 차이가 있음을 설명합니다. 따라서 제목으로는 '대중적 사고의 오류: 왜 다수가 항상 옳은 것은 아닌가'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리가 믿는 것: 보편적 진리
② 쉬운 길: 다수를 따르기
③ 군중의 힘: 머릿수에서의 안전
④ 역사 속 위대한 발견들: 인간의 창의성을 기리며
⑤ 대중적 사고의 오류: 왜 다수가 항상 옳은 것은 아닌가

question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: If we've invested in something that hasn't repaid us - be it money in a failing venture, or time in an unhappy relationship - we find it very difficult to walk away. This is the sunk cost fallacy. Our instinct is to continue investing money or time as we hope that our investment will prove to be ⓐ<u>worthwhile</u> in the end. Giving up would mean acknowledging that we've wasted something we can't get back, and that thought is so painful that we prefer to ⓑ<u>avoid</u> it if we can. The problem, of course, is that if something really is a bad bet, then ⓒ<u>staying</u> with it simply increases the amount we lose. Rather than walk away from a bad five-year relationship, for example, we turn it into a bad 10-year relationship; rather than accept that we've lost a thousand dollars, we lay down another thousand and ⓓ<u>lose</u> that too. In the end, by delaying the pain of admitting our problem, we only ⓔ<u>decrease</u> it. Sometimes we just have to cut our losses.
explanation: 이 글은 '매몰 비용 오류(sunk cost fallacy)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 실패가 확실한 상황에서도 이미 투입한 비용(시간, 돈 등)이 아까워 그 상황에서 벗어나지 못하는 심리를 다룹니다. 마지막 문장에서 문제를 인정하는 고통을 미룸으로써 결과적으로 그 고통이나 손실을 줄이는(decrease) 것이 아니라 '늘리게(increase)' 된다는 문맥이 되어야 하므로 ⓔ가 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: In the course of his research on business strategy and the environment, Michael Porter noticed a peculiar pattern: Businesses seemed to be profiting from ⓐ<u>regulation</u>. He also discovered that the stricter regulations were ⓑ<u>prompting</u> more innovation than the weaker ones. The Dutch flower industry provides an illustration. For many years, the companies producing Holland's world-renowned tulips and other cut flowers were also contaminating the country's water and soil with fertilizers and pesticides. In 1991, the Dutch government ⓒ<u>adopted</u> a policy designed to cut pesticide use in half by 2000 - a goal they ultimately achieved. Facing increasingly strict regulation, greenhouse growers realized they had to develop new methods if they were going to maintain product quality with ⓓ<u>fewer</u> pesticides. In response, they shifted to a cultivation method that circulates water in closed-loop systems and grows flowers in a rock wool substrate. The new system not only reduced the pollution released into the environment; it also ⓔ<u>decreased</u> profits by giving companies greater control over growing conditions.
explanation: 이 지문은 엄격한 환경 규제가 오히려 기업의 혁신을 유도하여 이익을 증가시킬 수 있다는 마이클 포터의 발견(포터 가설)을 설명합니다. 네덜란드 화훼 산업의 사례에서, 새로운 시스템은 오염을 줄였을 뿐만 아니라 재배 조건을 더 잘 통제하게 함으로써 이익을 감소시킨(decreased) 것이 아니라 '증가시켰다(increased)'는 흐름이 되어야 하므로 ⓔ가 잘못된 표현입니다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If there is little or no diversity of views, and all scientists see, think, and question the world in a similar way, then they will not, as a community, be as objective as they maintain they are, or at least aspire to be. When science is done by a diverse group of people, and if consensus builds up about a particular area of scientific knowledge, then we can have more confidence in its objectivity and truth.

explanation: 이 글은 과학계에서 관점의 다양성이 결여될 경우 발생할 수 있는 객관성의 결여를 지적하며, 그 해결책으로 과학 실천에 있어 성별, 민족, 사회 문화적 배경 등 다양한 측면의 다양성이 필요함을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에 가장 적절한 표현은 'far greater diversity(훨씬 더 큰 다양성)'입니다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Research psychologists often work with self-report data, made up of participants' verbal accounts of their behavior. This is the case whenever questionnaires, interviews, or personality inventories are used to measure variables. Self-report methods can be quite useful. question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Imagine that seven out of ten working Americans got fired tomorrow. What would they all do? It's hard to believe you'd have an economy at all if you gave pink slips to more than half the labor force. But that is what the industrial revolution did to the workforce of the early 19th century. Two hundred years ago, 70 percent of American workers lived on the farm. Today automation has eliminated all but 1 percent of their jobs, replacing them with machines. But the displaced workers did not sit idle. Instead, automation created hundreds of millions of jobs in entirely new fields. Those who once farmed were now manning the factories that manufactured farm equipment, cars, and other industrial products. Since then, wave upon wave of new occupations have arrived - appliance repair person, food chemist, photographer, web designer - each building on previous automation. Today, the vast majority of us are doing jobs that ________________________________________.

question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: We tend to break up time into units, such as weeks, months, and seasons; in a series of studies among farmers in India and students in North America, psychologists found that if a deadline is on the other side of a -break- - such as in the New Year - we're more likely to see it as remote, and, as a result, be less ready to jump into action. ␖What you need to do in that situation is find another way to think about the timeframe. ␗For example, if it's November and the deadline is in January, it's better to tell yourself you have to get it done -this winter- rather than -next year.- ␘The best approach is to view deadlines as a challenge that you have to meet within a period that's imminent. ␙This is why many people think deadlines should be set later, not earlier. ␚That way the stress is more manageable, and you have a better chance of starting - and therefore finishing - in good time.
explanation: ␙는 많은 사람들이 마감 기한을 더 이르게 잡아야 한다고 생각한다는 내용으로, 기한을 멀게 느끼지 않도록 시간 프레윤을 재구성해야 한다는 전체 흠름과 무관합니다.

question: 13. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Perhaps, the advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the workplace may bode well for Emotional Intelligence (EI). As AI gains momentum and replaces people in jobs at every level, predictions are, there will be a premium placed on people who have high ability in EI. ␖The emotional messages people send and respond to while interacting are, at this point, far beyond the ability of AI programs to mimic. ␗As we get further into the age of the smart machine, it is likely that sensing and managing emotions will remain one type of intelligence that puzzles AI. ␘As technology continues to advance, AI is becoming increasingly capable of sensing and managing human emotions with precision. ␙This means people and jobs involving EI are safe from being taken over by machines. ␚In a survey, almost three out of four executives see EI as a -must−have- skill for the workplace in the future as the automatizing of routine tasks bumps up against the impossibility of creating effective AI for activities that require emotional skill.
explanation: 이 글은 AI가 감성 지능(EI)을 모방하기 어렵기 때문에 EI의 가측가 더 높아질 갓이띀 내용입니다. ␘는 AI가 감정을 정밀하게 감지하고 관리할 수 있게 된다는 내용이므로 전체 흠름과 반대됩니다.

question: 14. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Most people resist the idea of a true selfestimate, probably because they fear it might mean downgrading some of their beliefs about who they are and what they're capable of. As Goethe's maxim goes, it is a great failing -to see yourself as more than you are.- How could you really be considered selfaware if you refuse to consider your weaknesses? Don't fear selfassessment because you're worried you might have to admit some things about yourself. The second half of Goethe's maxim is important too. ␖He states that it is equally damaging to -value yourself at less than your true worth.- ␗His statement makes us eager for education systems devoted to enhancing students' self-esteem. ␘We underestimate our capabilities just as much and just as dangerously as we overestimate other abilities. ␙Cultivate the ability to judge yourself accurately and honestly. ␚Look inward to discern what you're capable of and what it will take to unlock that potential.
explanation: 이 글은 자신을 과대평가하거나 과소평가하지 않고 정확하게 평가하는 것이 중요하다는 내용입니다. ␗은 자아존중감 향상을 은한 교육 시스템에 대한 내용으로, 객관적인 자기 평가띀 주제와 거리가 있습니다.

question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 서절한 것은?
passage: Because people tend to adapt, interrupting positive things with negative ones can actually increase enjoyment. Take commercials. Most people hate them, so removing them should make shows or other entertainment more enjoyable.
ordered_passages: (A) Interspersing positive experiences with less positive ones, however, can delay adaptation. Eating a Brussels sprout between chocolate chips or viewing commercials between parts of TV shows disrupts the process. The less positive moment makes the following positive one new again and thus more enjoyable.

(B) But the opposite is true. Shows are actually more enjoyable when they're broken up by annoying commercials. Because these less enjoyable moments break up adaptation to the positive experience of the show.

(C) Think about eating chocolate chips. The first chip is delicious: sweet, melt-in-your-mouth goodness. The second chip is also pretty good. But by the fourth, fifth, or tenth chip in a row, the goodness is no longer as pleasurable. We adapt.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 광고를 없애면 프로그램을 더 즐기게 될 것이라고 생각하지만, (B)에서 그 반대가 사실임을 밝힙니다. (C)는 적응에 대한 예시로 초콜릿 칩을 들고 있으며, (A)는 이러한 적응을 나쁜 경험으로 방해함으로써 즐거움을 준다는 결론을 내립니다.

question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Education must focus on the trunk of the tree of knowledge, revealing the ways in which the branches, twigs, and leaves all emerge from a common core.
ordered_passages: (A) When the same terms are employed across the curriculum, students begin to link different subjects and classes. If they practice abstracting in writing class, if they work on abstracting in painting or drawing class, and if, in all cases, they call it abstracting, they begin to understand how to think beyond disciplinary boundaries.

(B) They see how to transform their thoughts from one mode of conception and expression to another. Linking the disciplines comes naturally when the terms and tools are presented as part of a universal imagination.

(C) Tools for thinking stem from this core, providing a common language with which practitioners in different fields may share their experience of the process of innovation and discover links between their creative activities.
explanation: 교육은 지식의 뿌리가 공통된 핵심으로부터 나온다는 것을 보여주는 데 집중해야 한다는 내용이 언급된다. (C)에서는 공통된 핵심으로부터 사고 도구가 나오고, 서로 다른 분야의 전문가들이 혁신의 과정을 공유하고 창의적 활동 사이의 연결고리를 발견하는 공통 언어를 제공한다는 내용이다. (A)에서는 공통된 언어(용어)가 교육과정 전반에서 사용되면서 학생들이 학문 간 경계를 넘어 사고하는 방법을 깨닫고 터득하게 된다는 내용이다. (B)에서는 학생들이 생각과 표현의 양식을 다른 방식으로 전환하는 법을 배우게 되고, 학문 간 연결이 자연스럽게 나타난다고 설명한다.

question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: People behave in highly predictable ways when they experience certain thoughts. When they agree, they nod their heads. So far, no surprise, but according to an area of research known as 'proprioceptive psychology,' the process also works in reverse.
ordered_passages: (A) Participants in a study were asked to fixate on various products moving across a large computer screen and then indicate whether the items appealed to them. Some of the items moved vertically (causing the participants to nod their heads while watching), and others moved horizontally (resulting in a sidetoside head movement).
(B) Get people to behave in a certain way and you cause them to have certain thoughts. The idea was initially controversial, but fortunately it was supported by a compelling experiment.
(C) Participants preferred vertically moving products without being aware that their 'yes' and 'no' head movements had played a key role in their decisions.
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 사람들의 사고 방식과 행동이 연결된다는 점과 그 반대 과정도 가능하다는 '고유 수용성 심리학'을 소개하고 있다. (B)에서는 행동이 생각을 유발한다는 역방향의 아이디어와 이를 뒷받침하는 실험을 도입한다. (A)에서는 실험 참가자들이 화면상의 제품들이 상하(vertical) 또는 좌우(horizontal)로 움직이는 것을 보며 고개를 움직이는 구체적인 실험 과정을 설명한다. (C)에서는 고개를 끄덕이게 되는 상하 움직임 제품을 더 선호했다는 실험 결과를 통해 결론을 제시하고 있으므로 순서는 (B)-(A)-(C)가 가장 적절하다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Brains are expensive in terms of energy. Twenty percent of the calories we consume are used to power the brain. So brains try to operate in the most energy-efficient way possible, and that means processing only the minimum amount of information from our senses that we need to navigate the world. (A) Neuroscientists weren't the first to discover that fixing your gaze on something is no guarantee of seeing it. (B) Magicians figured this out long ago. (C) By directing your attention, they perform tricks with their hands in full view. (D) Their actions should give away the game, but they can rest assured that your brain processes only small bits of the visual scene. (E) In many of these cases, the eyes are pointed in the right direction, but the brain isn't seeing what's really out there.
insertion_sentence: This all helps to explain the prevalence of traffic accidents in which drivers hit pedestrians in plain view, or collide with cars directly in front of them.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'This all'은 앞서 언급된 내용들, 즉 뇌가 에너지 효율을 위해 필요한 최소한의 정보만 처리하며 눈이 향하더라도 뇌가 보지 못할 수 있다는 사실을 가리킨다. (E) 문장에서 눈은 올바른 방향을 향하고 있지만 뇌가 거기 있는 것을 보지 못하는 경우를 설명하며 지문의 핵심 논리를 마무리하고 있으며, 주어진 문장은 이러한 현상이 실제 생활에서 뻔히 보이는 보행자를 치거나 앞차와 충돌하는 교통사고의 원인이 됨을 설명하는 구체적인 예시에 해당한다. 따라서 주어진 문장은 (E) 뒤에 위치하는 것이 가장 적절하다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: In adolescence many of us had the experience of falling under the sway of a great book or writer. (A) We became entranced by the novel ideas in the book, and because we were so open to influence, these early encounters with exciting ideas sank deeply into our minds and became part of our own thought processes, affecting us decades after we absorbed them. (B) Just as the body tightens with age, however, so does the mind. (C) And just as our sense of weakness and vulnerability motivated the desire to learn, so does our creeping sense of superiority slowly close us off to new ideas and influences. (D) Some may advocate that we all become more skeptical in the modern world. (E) But in fact a far greater danger comes from the increasing closing of the mind that burdens us as individuals as we get older, and seems to be burdening our culture in general.
insertion_sentence: Such influences enriched our mental landscape, and in fact our intelligence depends on the ability to absorb the lessons and ideas of those who are older and wiser.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'Such influences'는 (A) 문장에서 설명한 청소년기의 책이나 작가에 의한 '초기 경험(early encounters)'과 영향력을 의미한다. 따라서 해당 경험이 우리의 생각의 과정이 되었다는 (A) 문장 바로 뒤인 (B)에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절하다. (B) 이후부터는 'however'를 기점으로 나이가 들면서 사고가 경직되는 현상을 설명하고 있으므로 (B)가 정답이다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The Net differs from most of the mass media it replaces in an obvious and very important way: it's bidirectional. We can send messages through the network as well as receive them, which has made the system all the more useful. The ability to exchange information online, to upload as well as download, has turned the Net into a thoroughfare for business and commerce. With a few clicks, people can search virtual catalogues, place orders, track shipments, and update information in corporate databases. But the Net doesn't just connect us with businesses; it connects us with one another. It's a personal broadcasting medium as well as a commercial one. Millions of people use it to distribute their own digital creations, in the form of blogs, videos, photos, songs, and podcasts, as well as to critique, edit, or otherwise modify the creations of others.
summary_sentence: The Net is a bidirectional medium that (A)__________ users to both share and receive information, (B)__________ commerce, personal communication, and the widespread distribution and modification of digital content like blogs, videos, and podcasts.
options: ① enables / facilitating
② enables / hindering
③ forbids / approving
④ forbids / blocking
⑤ causes / clearing
explanation: 인터넷은 정보를 주고받을 수 있는 양방향 매체이며, 이는 상업 및 개인 간 소통, 디지털 콘텐츠의 배포 및 수정을 가능하게 하거나 촉진한다는 내용의 글입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '가능하게 하다(enables)', (B)에는 '촉진하다(facilitating)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: 가능하게 하다 / 촉진하는
가능하게 하다 / 방해하는
금지하다 / 승인하는
금지하다 / 차단하는
야기하다 / 치우는

question: 21. 다음 글의 주제를 완성하려고 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 적절한 말을 주어진 철자로 시작하여 각각 1단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: We collect stamps, coins, vintage cars even when they serve no practical purpose. The post office doesn't accept the old stamps, the banks don't take old coins, and the vintage cars are no longer allowed on the road. These are all side issues; the attraction is that they are in a short supply. In one study, students were asked to arrange ten posters in order of attractiveness - with the agreement that afterward they could keep one poster as a reward for their participation. Five minutes later, they were told that the poster with the third highest rating was no longer available. Then they were asked to judge all ten from scratch. The poster that was no longer available was suddenly classified as the most beautiful. In psychology, this phenomenon is called reactance: when we are deprived of an option, we suddenly deem it more attractive.
summary_sentence: (A)____________ and the (B)____________ of choice make things seem more valuable.
explanation: 이 글은 대상이 부족하거나(short supply) 선택권이 박탈되었을 때(deprived of an option) 그것을 더 매력적으로 느끼는 현상인 '심리적 저항(reactance)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 부족을 뜻하는 'scarcity', (B)에는 선택권의 제거를 뜻하는 'removal'이 적절합니다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 적절한 말을 주어진 철자로 시작하여 각각 1단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: The built-in capacity for smiling is proven by the remarkable observation that babies who are congenitally both deaf and blind, who have never seen a human face, also start to smile at around 2 months. However, smiling in blind babies eventually disappears if nothing is done to reinforce it. Without the right feedback, smiling dies out. But here's a fascinating fact: blind babies will continue to smile if they are cuddled, bounced, nudged, and tickled by an adult - anything to let them know that they are not alone and that someone cares about them. This social feedback encourages the baby to continue smiling. In this way, early experience operates with our biology to establish social behaviors. In fact, you don't need the cases of blind babies to make the point. Babies with sight smile more at you when you look at them or, better still, smile back at them.
summary_sentence: Smiling is an (A)__________ human ability, but it can (B)__________ away without proper social feedback.
explanation: 미소 짓는 능력은 타고난(built-in) 것이지만, 사회적 피드백(강화)이 없으면 사라질 수 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 선천적인을 의미하는 'inborn', (B)에는 서서히 사라지다를 의미하는 'fade'가 적절합니다.

question: 23. 다음 밑줄 친 this could encourage banks to take greater risks in the future 문장이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 단어를 주어진 철자로 시작하여 1단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: If a firm is going to be saved by the government, it might be easier to concentrate on lobbying the government for more money rather than taking the harder decision of restructuring the company to be able to be profitable and viable in the long term. This is an example of something known as moral hazard - when government support alters the decisions firms take. For example, if governments rescue banks who get into difficulty, as they did during the credit crisis of 2007-08, <u>this could encourage banks to take greater risks in the future</u> because they know there is a possibility that governments will intervene if they lose money. Although the government rescue may be well intended, it can negatively affect the behavior of banks, encouraging risky and poor decision making.
summary_sentence: Government (A)___________ can lead to (B)___________ behavior in firms and banks.
explanation: 정부의 지원이 기업이나 은행의 도덕적 해이를 유발하여 더 위험한 결정을 내리게 한다는 내용입니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 '정부의 지원(support)', (B)는 그로 인한 '위험한(risky)' 행동을 의미합니다.

question: 24. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절한 것을 3단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: Before getting licensed to drive a cab in London, a person has to pass an incredibly difficult test with an intimidating name - "The Knowledge." The test involves memorizing the layout of more than 20,000 streets in the Greater London area - a feat that involves an incredible amount of memory resources. In fact, fewer than 50 percent of the people who sign up for taxi driver training pass the test, even after spending two or three years studying for it! And as it turns out, the brains of London cabbies are different from noncabdriving humans in ways that reflect their herculean memory efforts. In fact, the part of the brain that has been most frequently associated with spatial memory, the tail of the sea horseshaped brain region called the hippocampus, ______________________ average in these taxi drivers.
explanation: 런던 택시 기사들의 뇌를 연구한 결과, 엄청난 양의 지리 정보를 외우는 과정에서 공간 기억과 관련된 해마 부위가 일반인보다 더 커졌다는 내용이 글의 핵심입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '평균보다 크다'는 의미인 'is bigger than'이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 적절한 말을 주어진 철자로 시작하여 각각 1단어의 영어로 쓰시오. (본문에 있는 단어를 쓰면 오답 처리)
passage: Events or experiences that are out of ordinary tend to be remembered better because there is nothing competing with them when your brain tries to access them from its storehouse of remembered events. In other words, the reason it can be difficult to remember what you ate for breakfast two Thursdays ago is that there was probably nothing special about that Thursday or that particular breakfast - consequently, all your breakfast memories combine together into a sort of generic impression of a breakfast. Your memory merges similar events not only because it's more efficient to do so, but also because this is fundamental to how we learn things - our brains extract abstract rules that tie experiences together. This is especially true for things that are routine. If your breakfast is always the same - cereal with milk, a glass of orange juice, and a cup of coffee for instance - there is no easy way for your brain to extract the details from one particular breakfast. Ironically, then, for behaviors that are routinized, you can remember the generic content of the behavior (such as the things you ate, since you always eat the same thing), but particulars to that one instance can be very difficult to call up (such as the sound of a garbage truck going by or a bird that passed by your window) unless they were especially distinctive. On the other hand, if you did something unique that broke your routine - perhaps you had leftover pizza for breakfast and spilled tomato sauce on your dress shirt - you are more likely to remember it.
summary_sentence: (A)____________ experiences are remembered better than routine ones because our brains merge similar events into genetic memories, making specific details harder to (B)____________ unless something distinctive breaks the routine and stands out.
subjective_conditions: 본문에 있는 단어를 쓰면 오답 처리
explanation: 일상적이지 않은 경험은 기억에서 경쟁하는 요소가 없어 더 잘 기억되는 반면, 일상적인 일들은 뇌가 하나로 뭉뚱그려 저장하기 때문에 세부 사항을 떠올리기 어렵다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '일상적이지 않은'의 의미인 'Extraordinary', (B)에는 '떠올리다/상기하다'의 의미인 'recall'이 적절합니다. 본문의 distinctive나 call up을 피해서 써야 합니다.

question: 26. 다음 밑줄 친 what scientific experiments do이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 주어진 철자로 시작하여 각각 1단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control. Scientists manipulate a variable of interest, and see if there's a difference. At the same time, they attempt to control for the potential effects of all other variables. The importance of controlled experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the realuncontrolledworld, variables are often correlated. For example, people who take vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who don't take vitamins. As a result, if we want to study the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely observe the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to create a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world. That's just <u>what scientific experiments do</u>. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while holding everything else constant.
summary_sentence: that scientific experiments create artificial situations to (A)___________ one variable by manipulating it while keeping all others constant to (B)___________ true cause-and-effect relationships.
explanation: 과학적 실험의 핵심은 변인 통제를 통해 특정 변인을 분리하고 인과관계를 밝혀내는 것입니다. 따라서 인위적인 상황을 만들어 하나의 변인을 '고립/분리(isolate)'시키고, 진정한 인과관계를 '결정/확인(determine)'한다는 내용이 적절합니다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition. But it's important to understand the limits of dictionary definitions. More often than not, a definition in a dictionary requires readers to have a fairly robust understanding of the language already at their disposal. In other words, a dictionary functions in many cases as a cross-reference or translator between words one knows and words that one doesn't yet know. Even the most obscure words in a dictionary, say, for example, "pulchritudinous" or "kalokagathia," must be defined using words that the reader already knows and understands. Otherwise, the dictionary isn't very helpful.
options: ① Dictionaries rely on a reader's existing knowledge of language to be effective.
② Vocabulary plays a important role in understanding a language.
③ The usefulness of a dictionary depends on how often the user uses it.
④ A dictionary is the best tool for satisfying a learner's linguistic curiosity.
⑤ To understand the meaning of an ambiguous word, one should consult multiple dictionaries.
explanation: 글의 중반부 이후에 언급된 것처럼, 사전은 독자가 이미 알고 있는 단어를 사용하여 모르는 단어를 정의하기 때문에, 사전이 효과적으로 기능하려면 독자의 기존 언어 지식이 필요하다는 것이 핵심 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 사전이 효과적이기 위해서는 독자의 기존 언어 지식에 의존한다.
② 어휘는 언어를 이해하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다.
③ 사전의 유용성은 사용자가 얼마나 자주 사용하는지에 달려 있다.
④ 사전은 학습자의 언어적 호기심을 충족시키는 최고의 도구이다.
⑤ 모호한 단어의 의미를 이해하려면 여러 사전들을 참고해야 한다.

question: 28. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [25년 3월 36번]
passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of ⓐ<u>insuring</u> that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food ⓑ<u>self-sufficiency</u>, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly ⓒ<u>sensitive</u> to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on ⓓ<u>exports</u> for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both ⓔ<u>domestic</u> production and imports.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 미국은 커피, 차, 바나나와 같은 열대 산물을 자국 내에서 공급하기 위해 수입에 의존해야 합니다. 따라서 '수출(exports)'이 아니라 '수입(imports)'으로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
passage: As the old joke goes: "Software, free. User manual, $10,000." But it's no joke. A couple of high-profile companies make their living selling instruction and paid support for free software. The copy of code, being mere bits, is free. The lines of free code become ⓐ<u>valueless</u> to you only through support and guidance. A lot of medical and genetic information will go this route in the coming decades. Right now getting a full copy of all your DNA is very ⓑ<u>expensive</u> ($10,000), but soon it won't be. The price is ⓒ<u>dropping</u> so fast, it will be $100 soon, and then the next year insurance companies will offer to ⓓ<u>sequence</u> you for free. When a copy of your sequence costs nothing, the ⓔ<u>interpretation</u> of what it means, what you can do about it, and how to use it - the manual for your genes - will be expensive.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 글의 맥락상 소프트웨어 코드 자체는 무료이지만, 그것을 이해하고 활용할 수 있게 해주는 지원과 지침이 있어야 비로소 사용자에게 가치가 있게 된다는 내용입니다. 따라서 'valueless'(가치 없는)는 문맥에 어긋나며 'valuable'(가치 있는)로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A), (B)가 가리키는 바를 본문에서 찾아 영어로 쓰시오. [4.0점]
passage: Brains are expensive in terms of energy. Twenty percent of the calories we consume are used to power the brain. So brains try to operate in the most energy-efficient way possible, and that means processing only the minimum amount of information from our senses that we need to navigate the world. Neuroscientists weren't the first to discover that fixing your gaze on something is no guarantee of seeing it. Magicians figured this out long ago. By directing your attention, (A)<u>they</u> perform tricks with their hands in full view. Their actions should give away the game, but they can rest assured that your brain processes only small bits of the visual scene. (B)<u>This</u> all helps to explain the prevalence of traffic accidents in which drivers hit pedestrians in plain view, or collide with cars directly in front of them. In many of these cases, the eyes are pointed in the right direction, but the brain isn't seeing what's really out there.
answer: (A) magicians(B) your brain processes only small bits of the visual scene
explanation: (A) 'they'는 문맥상 사람들의 주의를 돌려 눈앞에서 마술을 부리는 주체인 'Magicians'를 가리킵니다. (B) 'This'는 뇌가 시각적 장면의 아주 작은 일부분만 처리한다는 앞 문장의 내용('your brain processes only small bits of the visual scene')을 가리키며, 이것이 운전자가 눈앞의 장애물을 보지 못해 발생하는 사고의 원인이 됨을 설명합니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은? [3.2점]
passage: On our little world, light travels, for all practical purposes, instantaneously. If ⓐ<u>a lightbulb</u> is glowing, then of course ⓑ<u>it</u>'s physically where we see it, shining away. We reach out our hand and touch ⓒ<u>it</u>: It's there all right, and unpleasantly hot. If the filament fails, then the light goes out. We don't see it in the same place, glowing, illuminating the room years after the bulb breaks and ⓓ<u>it</u>'s removed from its socket. The very notion seems nonsensical. But if we're far enough away, an entire sun can go out and we'll continue to see ⓔ<u>it</u> shining brightly; we won't learn of its death, it may be, for ages to come - in fact, for how long it takes light, which travels fast but not infinitely fast, to cross the intervening vastness. The immense distances to the stars and the galaxies mean that we see everything in space in the past.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ는 모두 일상적인 환경에서의 '전구(lightbulb)'를 가리킵니다. 반면 ⓔ는 멀리 떨어져 있어 빛이 도달하는 데 시간이 걸리는 대상인 '태양/항성(an entire sun)'을 가리킵니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Imagine that seven out of ten working Americans got (A)[hired / fired] tomorrow. What would they all do? It's hard to believe you'd have an economy at all if you gave pink slips to more than half the labor force. But that is what the industrial revolution did to the workforce of the early 19th century. Two hundred years ago, 70 percent of American workers lived on the farm. Today automation has (B)[eliminated / supplemented] all but 1 percent of their jobs, replacing them with machines. But the displaced workers did not sit idle. Instead, automation created hundreds of millions of jobs in entirely new fields. Those who once farmed were now manning the factories that manufactured farm equipment, cars, and other industrial products. Since then, wave upon wave of new (C)[unemployment / occupations] have arrived ─ appliance repair person, food chemist, photographer, web designer ─ each building on previous automation. Today, the vast majority of us are doing jobs that no farmer from the 1800s could have imagined.
options: ① hired - supplemented - unemployment
② hired - supplemented - occupations
③ fired - eliminated - occupations
④ fired - eliminated - unemployment
⑤ hired - eliminated - occupations
explanation:
이 글은 과거 산업 혁명이 농장 일자리를 기계로 대체(자동화)했지만, 동시에 수많은 새로운 직업군을 창출했음을 설명하고 있습니다.

(A) 'pink slips(해고 통지서)'를 준다는 뒷문장의 내용을 통해 10명 중 7명이 '해고된다(fired)'는 가정을 하고 있음을 알 수 있습니다.
(B) 오늘날 자동화가 농장 일자리의 1%를 제외한 나머지를 '제거했다(eliminated)'는 내용이 기계로 대체되었다는 문맥과 자연스럽게 어울립니다.

② 고용된 - 보충된 - 직업

question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We have biases that support our biases!. If we're partial to one option ― perhaps because it's more memorable, or framed to minimize loss, or seemingly consistent with a promising pattern ― we tend to search for information that will justify choosing that option.
ordered_passages: (A) For example, nearly all companies include classic "tell me about yourself" job interviews as part of the hiring process, and many rely on these interviews alone to evaluate applicants.
(B) But it turns out that traditional interviews are actually one of the least useful tools for predicting an employee's future success.

(C) On the one hand, it's sensible to make choices that we can defend with data and a list of reasons. On the other hand, if we're not careful, we're likely to conduct an imbalanced analysis, falling prey to a cluster of errors collectively known as "confirmation biases."

(D) This is because interviewers often subconsciously make up their minds about interviewees based on their first few moments of interaction and spend the rest of the interview cherry-picking evidence and phrasing their questions to confirm that initial impression.
explanation:
주어진 글은 자신의 편향을 정당화하려는 성향에 대해 소개하고 있습니다. 
(C)에서는 이러한 성향이 불균형한 분석으로 이어져 결국 '확증 편향'이라는 오류에 빠지게 된다는 일반적인 원리를 먼저 설명합니다. 
(A)에서는 그 구체적인 예시(For example)로 전통적인 기업 면접을 제시하고, 
(B)에서는 반전의 접속사 'But'을 통해 이러한 면접이 실제 채용 성공을 예측하는 데 효과적이지 않음을 지적합니다. 
마지막으로 (D)에서 그 구체적인 원인(This is because)으로 면접관들이 초기에 형성한 인상을 확인하기 위해 질문을 유도하거나 증거를 선택적으로 수집(cherry-picking)한다는 점을 언급하며 마무리하는 것이 가장 논리적입니다. 따라서 정답은 (C)-(A)-(B)-(D) 순인 ④번입니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The first human beings probably evolved in tropical regions where survival was possible without clothing. It is likely that they had very dark skin because light skin would have given little protection against the burning rays of the sun. There is a debate about whether these people spread into other parts of the world or, instead, whether people developed independently in various parts of the world. Whichever the case, it is believed that in time they became capable of spreading out from Africa, eventually to most of the world. This was probably because their physical characteristics changed. For instance, early hominids probably did not walk upright, but when they developed that ability, they could travel more efficiently. More important, perhaps, was their development of tool making. With tools, they could hunt other animals, so they could consume more protein and fat than their lowenergy vegetarian diet would have provided. Not only their bodies but also their brains would have been changed with more energy. The brain needs lots of energy to grow. As their diet expanded, hominids could physically and intellectually expand their territory.
options: ① The Impact of Diet on Brain Growth
② The Invention of Tools in Human Prehistory
③ How Early Humans May Have Spread from Africa
④ The Important Role of Clothing in Skin Color Evolution
⑤ The Benefits of Vegetarianism Among Early Human Ancestors

question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When we get an unfavorable outcome, in some ways the last thing we want to hear is that the process was fair. As outraging as the combination of an unfavorable outcome and an unfair process is, this combination also brings with it a consolation prize: the possibility of attributing the bad outcome to something other than ourselves. We may reassure ourselves by believing that our bad outcome had little to do with us and everything to do with the unfair process. If the process is fair, however, we cannot nearly as easily externalize the outcome; we got what we got "fair and square." When the process is fair we believe that our outcome is deserved, which is another way of saying that ____________________________________________________.
options: ① we are simply unlucky and victims of the system
② we are the ones responsible for what happened
③ we should question the fairness of the entire situation
④ bad outcome had little to do with us and the unfair process
⑤ there must have been something outside ourselves that caused the outcome
explanation: 이 글은 결과가 좋지 않을 때 과정이 불공정했다면 그 결과를 외부 탓(과정 탓)으로 돌릴 수 있어 위안이 되지만, 과정이 공정했다면 그 결과가 본인 탓이라는 것을 받아들여야 한다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸은 과정이 공정할 때 우리가 느끼는 점을 기술하고 있으므로, 우리가 일어난 일에 대해 책임을 져야 한다는 의미인 ②번이 정답입니다.

우리가 일어난 일에 대해 책임을 져야 하는 사람이다.
우리는 전체 상황의 공정성에 의문을 제기해야 한다.
나쁜 결과는 우리나 불공정한 과정과 거의 관련이 없었다.

question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The well-known American ethnologist Alfred Louis Kroeber made a rich and in-depth study of women's evening dress in the West, stretching back about three centuries and using reproductions of engravings. Having adjusted the dimensions of these plates due to their diverse origins, he was able to analyse the constant elements in fashion features and to come up with a study that was neither intuitive nor approximate, but precise, mathematical and statistical. He reduced women's clothing to a certain number of features: length and size of the skirt, size and depth of the neckline, height of the waistline. He demonstrated unambiguously that fashion _____________________________________________.For practically 300 years, women's dress was subject to a very precise periodic cycle: forms reach the furthest point in their variations every fifty years. If, at any one moment, skirts are at their longest, fifty years later they will be at their shortest; thus skirts become long again fifty years after being short and a hundred years after being long.
options: ① follows a regular historical cycle instead of yearly shifts
② changes are driven solely by individual designers' creative decisions
③ reflects immediate cultural shifts rather than following long-term trends
④ is which is not located on the scale of history but at the level of annual variations
⑤ is completely random and cannot be understood through measurable patterns

완전히 무작위적이며 측정 가능한 패턴을 통해 이해될 수 없다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Over the last few centuries, humanity's collective prosperity has skyrocketed, as technological progress has made us ⓐ<u>much</u> wealthier than ever before. To share out those ⓑ<u>riches</u>, almost all societies have settled upon the market mechanism, rewarding people in various ways for the work that they do and the things that they own. But ⓒ<u>increasing</u> inequality, itself often driven by technology, has started to put that mechanism under strain. Today, markets already provide immense rewards to some people but leave many others with very little. And now, technological unemployment threatens to become a more radical version of the ⓓ<u>same</u> story, taking place in the particular market we rely upon the most: the labor market. As that market begins to break down, more and more people will be in danger of ⓔ<u>receiving</u> a share of society's prosperity.
explanation: 이 글은 기술 발전이 부를 창출했지만 동시에 불평등과 기술적 실업을 초래하여 시장 경제 메커니즘을 압박하고 있다는 내용입니다. 노동 시장이 붕괴됨에 따라 더 많은 사람들이 사회적 번영의 몫을 '받지 못할' 위험에 처하는 것이 문맥상 자연스러우므로 ⓔ의 receiving은 failing to receive 등으로 바뀌어야 합니다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: It's often said that those who can't do, teach. It would be more accurate to say that those who can do, can't teach the basics. A great deal of expert knowledge is implicit, not explicit. The further you progress toward mastery the less conscious awareness you often have of the fundamentals. Experiments show that skilled golfers and wine aficionados have a hard time describing their putting and tasting techniques - even asking them to explain their approaches is enough to interfere with their performance, so they often stay on autopilot. When I first saw an elite diver do four and a half somersaults, l asked how he managed to spin so fast. His answer: "Just go up in a ball." Experts often have an intuitive understanding of a route, but they struggle to clearly express all the steps to take. Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage.
options: ① 초보자는 전문가보다 기본에 대해 더 깊이 이해하고 있다.
② 전문가들은 자신의 기술을 설명할수록 수행 능력이 향상된다.
③ 기술을 잘 가르치기 위해서는 명시적인 지식만 있으면 된다.
④ 전문가는 자신이 하는 일을 오랜 시간 반복하여 숙달된 만큼, 초보자보다 더 효과적으로 지식을 전달할 수 있다.
⑤ 전문가들의 전문 지식은 암시적이기 때문에 기초를 가르치는 데 어려움을 겪는다.
explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 전문가들의 지식이 명시적이기보다는 암시적(implicit)이기 때문에, 숙달될수록 오히려 기초적인 부분을 설명하거나 가르치는 데 어려움을 겪는다는 내용이다. 마지막 문장의 'struggle to clearly express all the steps'가 이를 뒷받침한다.

question: 21. John is a kindergartener and Mary is a high school student. If both see a child in distress while with a friend, who is less likely to help?
passage: The concern about how we appear to others can be seen in children, though work by the psychologist Ervin Staub suggests that the effect may vary with age. In a study where children heard another child in distress, young children (kindergarten through second grade) were more likely to help the child in distress when with another child than when alone. But for older children - in fourth and sixth grade - the effect reversed: they were less likely to help a child in distress when they were with a peer than when they were alone. Staub suggested that younger children might feel more comfortable acting when they have the company of a peer, whereas older children might feel more concern about being judged by their peers and fear feeling embarrassed by overreacting. Staub noted that "older children seemed to discuss the distress sounds less and to react to them less openly than younger children." In other words, the older children were deliberately putting on a poker face in front of their peers.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 나이가 많은 아이들(older children)은 혼자 있을 때보다 또래와 함께 있을 때 곤경에 처한 아이를 돕는 경향이 적어진다(less likely to help). 고등학생인 Mary는 지문의 older children에 해당하므로 유치원생인 John보다 친구와 함께 있을 때 돕지 않을 가능성이 더 높다.

question: 23. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman - and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison. (D) If this were true, we might like people more if they reveal some evidence of fallibility. insertion_sentence: However, the research evidence is paradoxical.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장은 연구 증거가 역설적(paradoxical)이라는 전환을 나타낸다. (B) 앞부분까지는 유능한 사람을 좋아한다는 일반적인 기대를 설명하고 있고, (B) 뒷부분부터는 유능한 사람이 가장 인기 있는 사람이 아닐 수 있다는 역설적인 현상을 설명하므로 (B)에 들어가는 것이 적절하다.

question: 24. 윗글의 내용을 요약한 것이다. <조건>에 알맞게 (가)~(다)를 영작하시오.

subjective_conditions: 1. 다음 단어를 모두 사용할 것. (중복 사용 가능) [more / less / small flaws / approachable / although / competent / like ]

question: 25. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Sleep is clearly about more than just resting. One curious fact is that animals that are hibernating also have periods of sleep. It comes as a surprise to most of us, but hibernation and sleep are not the same thing at all, at least not from a neurological and metabolic perspective. Hibernating is more like being anesthetized: the subject is unconscious but not actually asleep. So a hibernating animal needs to get a few hours of conventional sleep each day within the larger unconsciousness. A further surprise to most of us is that bears, the most famous of wintry sleepers, don't actually hibernate. By this definition, bears hibernate, because their body temperature stays near normal and they are easily awakened. Their winter sleeps are more accurately called a state of torpor.
options: ① negative factors of hibernation
② various causes of bear torpor in winter
③ diverse interpretations of energy conservation
④ differences between sleep and hibernation
⑤ discussion of body temperature regulation in wintering animals
explanation: 이 글은 동물의 동면(hibernation)과 수면(sleep)이 신경학적 및 대사적 관점에서 서로 다른 상태임을 설명하고 있습니다. 동면 중에도 실제 수면 시간이 필요하며, 곰의 사례를 통해 일반적인 정의와 실제 동면/휴면 상태의 차이를 논하며 수면과 동면의 차이점을 주제로 다루고 있습니다.

question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There are deep similarities between viral contagion and behavioral contagion. For example, people in close or extended proximity to others infected by a virus are themselves more likely to become infected, just as people are more likely to drink excessively when they spend more time in the company of heavy drinkers. But there are also important differences between the two types of contagion. One is that visibility promotes behavioral contagion but inhibits the spread of infectious diseases. Solar panels that are visible from the street, for instance, are more likely to stimulate neighboring installations. In contrast, we try to avoid others who are visibly ill. Another important difference is that whereas viral contagion is almost always a bad thing, behavioral contagion is sometimes negative - as in the case of smoking - but sometimes positive, as in the case of solar installations.
summary_sentence: While viral and behavioral contagion are similar in how they spread through (A)___________, they differ in that visibility encourages behavioral spread but (B)___________ viral spread, and behavioral contagion can have both positive and negative effects.
options: ① timeinhibits
② peoplestimulates
③ infectionpromotes
④ diseasesblocks
⑤ proximitydiscourages
explanation: 글의 내용에 따르면 바이러스 전염과 행동 전염은 물리적 근접성(proximity)을 통해 퍼진다는 점에서 유사합니다. 그러나 가시성(visibility)의 경우, 행동 전염을 촉진하지만 질병의 전염은 피하게 만들기 때문에 저해(discourages/inhibits)한다는 차이점이 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 proximity, (B)에는 discourages가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world. Simply put, the brain is not designed to sense on its own. For instance, an exposed brain would neither sense light shining on it nor feel something touching it. In fact, patients are often kept awake during brain surgery, which can help a surgeon isolate specific regions of the brain. The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle recognized this characteristic of the brain over 2,000 years ago when he said, "Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses." This concept can be seen clearly when volunteers are blind-folded and placed in the warm water of a sensory deprivation tank. They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as incoherent thought patterns. From these experiments and others, it is apparent that we need constant input from our senses to carry out functions that give us personality and intellect.

question: 7. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: The big problem with money created by the government is that those who run the government always face the temptation to create more money and spend it. Whether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, leading to inflation and the many economic and social problems that follow from inflation. ⓐ<u>But low inflation and a "stable economy have softened demand for gold, sending its price tumbling.</u> ⓑ<u>For this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that is inherently limited in supply, as money.</u> ⓒ<u>It is a way of depriving governments of the power to expand the money supply to inflationary levels.</u> ⓓ<u>Gold has long been considered ideal for this purpose, since the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased rapidly.</u> ⓔ<u>When paper money is convertible into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money is said to be "backed up" by gold.</u> This expression is misleading only if we imagine that the value of the gold is somehow transferred to the paper money, when in fact the real point is that the gold simply limits the amount of paper money that can be issued.
explanation: 이 글은 정부가 무분별하게 화폐를 발행하여 인플레이션을 일으키는 문제를 막기 위해, 공급이 한정된 '금'이나 '은' 등을 화폐로 사용하는 시스템(금 본위제 등)의 필요성과 원리를 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓐ는 낮은 인플레이션과 안정된 경제 상황에서 금에 대한 수요가 줄어 가격이 하락했다는 시장 현상을 설명하고 있어, 화폐 가치를 제한하는 수단으로서의 금의 역할이라는 전체 맥락에서 벗어납니다.

question: 13. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The writer and zoologist Desmond Morris observed that our feet communicate exactly what we think and feel more honestly than any other part of our bodies.
ordered_passages: (A) In fact, these age-old reactions are still so hardwired in us that when we are presented with something dangerous or even disagreeable, our feet and legs still react as they did in prehistoric times.

(B) Our limbic brains made sure that our feet and legs reacted as needed by either ceasing motion, running away, or kicking at a potential threat. This survival regimen, retained from our ancestral heritage, has served us well and continues to do so today.

(C) Why are the feet and legs such accurate reflectors of our sentiments? For millions of years, long before humans spoke, our legs and feet reacted to environmental threats (e.g., hot sand, illtempered lions) instantaneously, without the need for conscious thought.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 발이 우리 감정을 가장 정직하게 전달한다는 관찰을 제시했습니다. (C)에서 왜 발과 다리가 정확한 반사체인지에 대한 질문을 던지며 진화론적 배경(위협에 즉각 반응)을 설명합니다. (B)에서 이러한 반응을 변연계 뇌가 담당하며 조상으로부터 물려받은 생존 방식임을 구체화합니다. (A)에서 이러한 오래된 반응이 여전히 우리 안에 내재(hardwired)되어 현대에도 나타난다는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 14. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis.
ordered_passages: (A) Of course migration can and does create social and economic problems. But migration can also be a solution for many preexisting problems. For example, out-migration generally redistributes workers from places of labor surplus to areas where there is greater demand or more opportunity.

(B) Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to endure hardship in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin. Most research that examines long-term outcomes of migration, including remittances and intergenerational mobility, finds positive "long-term" effects on places of origin and destination.

(C) For example, migrants are assumed to overcrowd cities, clog up labor markets, and increase poverty. The other questionable assumption is that most migration is involuntary ─ people fleeing natural or man-made disasters. The reality, however, is more complex, and many migrants are simply seeking greater economic opportunity.
explanation: 주어진 글은 '이주'가 문제나 위기로 보도되는 경향을 언급합니다. (C)에서 'For example'을 통해 도시 과밀화, 빈곤 증가 등 문제로 인식되는 사례들을 나열하고, 이주가 비자발적이라는 통념과 달리 실제로는 경제적 기회를 찾는 복잡한 현실이 있음을 지적합니다. (A)에서 이러한 사회경제적 문제를 인정하면서도, 'But'을 통해 이주가 기존 문제의 해결책(노동력 재배치)이 될 수 있음을 제시합니다. (B)에서 이주민의 특성(젊고 유연함)과 이주가 미치는 긍정적인 장기적 효과를 설명하며 논의를 확장합니다.

And today, ⓑ<u>가상 근무 환경이 사람들에게 더 필수적이었던 적은 없었다</u>.
subjective_conditions: 1. 총 10개의 단어로 구성할 것
2. 다음의 단어를 반드시 포함시키되 필요한 경우 단어의 형태는 변형시킬 수 있음: the, to, virtual, essential, be, workplace
3. 도치된 문장으로 쓰시오.
answer: Never has the virtual workplace been more essential to people
explanation: 부정어 도치를 사용하여 '가장 필수적이다'라는 최상급의 의미를 강조해야 합니다. 'Never(부정어) + has(조동사) + the virtual workplace(주어) + been more essential(비교급) to people'의 구조로 영작합니다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Turtle hatchlings have, it seems, evolved to crawl toward the light. For millions of years this was a highly rational and effective strategy because the light on a dark beach represented the reflection of the moon and stars on the water's surface. Following the lights led baby turtles back home to the sea. The problems started when humans began building beachfront homes and sparkling hotels on the other side of the beach. Now after hatching, turtles heading for the brightest nearby lights were being guided straight into traffic. Are self destructive sea turtles naturally irrational? Yes, in the modern world. But there's a deeper truth. Turtles are basing their decisions on simple cues that were perfectly rational for their ancestors; these days, however, their evolved decision-making mechanisms are being blinded by modern lights.
options: ① The detailed process of turtles' decision-making mechanisms
② The positive aspects of the modern environments for turtles
③ Why did humans start to build hotels near the beach?
④ Why turtles follow the lights when they hatching?
⑤ Modernization makes turtles' survive strategy useless
explanation: 거북이 부화마들이 빛을 따라 바다로 향하는 진화적 전략이 현대 사회의 인공 조명(건물, 호텔 등)으로 인해 오히려 생존에 위협이 되는 상황으로 변했음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 현대화가 거북이의 생존 전략을 무용지물로 만든다는 내용의 ⑤번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 거북이의 의사결정 메커니즘의 상세 과정
② 거북이에게 있어 현대 환경의 긍정적인 측면
③ 왜 인간은 해변 근처에 호텔을 짓기 시작했는가?
④ 거북이는 부화할 때 왜 빛을 따르는가?
⑤ 현대화는 거북이의 생존 전략을 쓸모없게 만든다

question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The built-in capacity for smiling is proven by the remarkable observation that babies who are congenitally both deaf and blind, who have never seen a human face, also start to smile at around 2 months. However, smiling in blind babies eventually disappears if nothing is done to reinforce it. Without the right feedback, smiling dies out. But here's a fascinating fact: blind babies will continue to smile if they are cuddled, bounced, nudged, and tickled by an adult - anything to let them know that they are not alone and that someone cares about them. This social feedback encourages the baby to continue smiling. In this way, early experience operates with our biology to establish social behaviors. In fact, you don't need the cases of blind babies to make the point. Babies with sight smile more at you when you look at them or, better still, smile back at them.
options: ① The Rise of Innate Responses Over Time
② How Language Development Affects Infant Vision
③ The Cultural Origins of Nonverbal Social Behavior
④ Learning to Read Faces: The First Step in Social Life
⑤ The Developmental Interplay of Innate Smiling and Social Feedback
explanation: 이 글은 타고난 미소 짓기 능력(innate capacity)이 사회적 피드백(social feedback)과 결합하여 어떻게 사회적 행동으로 정착되는지를 설명하고 있습니다. 선천적 시청각 장애 아기도 미소를 짓지만, 성인의 보살핌과 같은 사회적 피드백이 있어야 그 행동이 유지된다는 내용을 통해 생물학적 요인과 초기 경험의 상호작용을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '타고난 미소와 사회적 피드백의 발달적 상호작용'을 의미하는 ⑤번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 시간이 지남에 따른 선천적 반응의 증가
② 언어 발달이 유아의 시력에 미치는 영향
③ 비언어적 사회적 행동의 문화적 기원
④ 얼굴 읽기 배우기: 사회 생활의 첫 단계
⑤ 선천적 미소와 사회적 피드백의 발달적 상호작용

question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Imagine that seven out of ten working Americans got fired tomorrow. What would they all do? It's hard to believe you'd have an economy at all if you gave pink slips to more than half the labor force. But that is what the industrial revolution did to the workforce of the early 19th century. Two hundred years ago, 70 percent of American workers lived on the farm. Today automation has eliminated all but 1 percent of their jobs, replacing them with machines. But the displaced workers did not sit idle. Instead, automation created hundreds of millions of jobs in entirely new fields. Those who once farmed were now manning the factories that manufactured farm equipment, cars, and other industrial products. Since then, wave upon wave of new occupations have arrived - appliance repair person, food chemist, photographer, web designer - each building on previous automation. Today, the vast majority of us are doing jobs that no farmer from the 1800s could have imagined.
options: ① Why Does Industrial Innovation Lead to the Collapse of Employment Structure?
② The Structural Transformation of Occupational Landscapes in the Age of Automation
③ Negative Implications of Imbalance between Technological Advancement and Labor System
④ The Paradox of Economic Recession: Why Employment Instability Accelerates Automation
⑤ The Secret Behind the History of Automation: Effect of Bold Industrial Restructuring Policy
explanation: 이 글은 산업 혁명과 자동화가 과거의 직업(농업 등)을 없앴지만, 동시에 완전히 새로운 분야에서 수백만 개의 일자리를 창출하며 직업 구조를 변화시켜 왔음을 설명합니다. 따라서 자동화 시대의 '직업 지형의 구조적 변화'를 언급한 ②번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 왜 산업 혁신이 고용 구조의 붕괴를 초래하는가?
② 자동화 시대의 직업 지형의 구조적 변화
③ 기술 진보와 노동 시스템 간의 불균형의 부정적 영향
④ 경기 침체의 역설: 왜 고용 불안정이 자동화를 가속화하는가?
⑤ 자동화 역사의 비밀: 대담한 산업 구조조정 정책의 효과

question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Financial markets do more than take capital from the rich and lend it to everyone else. They enable each of us to smooth consumption over our lifetimes, which is a fancy way of saying that we don't have to spend income at the same time we earn it. Shakespeare may have admonished us to be neither borrowers nor lenders; the fact is that most of us will be both at some point. If we lived in an agrarian society, we would have to eat our crops reasonably soon after the harvest or find some way to store them. Financial markets are a more sophisticated way of managing the harvest. We can spend income now that we have not yet earned - as by borrowing for college or a home - or we can earn income now and spend it later, as by saving for retirement. The important point is that earning income has been divorced from spending it, allowing us much more flexibility in life.
options: ① The Role of Financial Markets to Shift Traditional Structure of Supply and Demand
② Borrow Now, Repay Whenever You Want: The Common Myth of Credit Transaction
③ The Principle of Financial Management: Spend Based on Future Value, Not Current Income
④ How Financial Markets Facilitate Dynamic and Adaptive Management of Personal Economic Life
⑤ Why Securing Economic Flexibility Is Essential to Improving Efficiency in the Financial Market System
explanation: 이 글은 금융 시장이 소득을 얻는 시점과 소비하는 시점을 분리(divorce)시켜줌으로써, 개인이 전 생애에 걸쳐 소비를 조절하고 유연한 경제 생활을 영위할 수 있게 해준다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 금융 시장이 개인의 경제적 삶의 역동적이고 적응적인 관리를 어떻게 돕는지를 다룬 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 공급과 수요의 전통적 구조를 변화시키는 금융 시장의 역할
② 지금 빌리고 원할 때 갚아라: 신용 거래의 흔한 신화
③ 재무 관리의 원칙: 현재 소득이 아닌 미래 가치에 기반하여 소비하라
④ 금융 시장이 개인 경제 생활의 역동적이고 적응적인 관리를 용이하게 하는 방법
⑤ 경제적 유연성 확보가 금융 시장 시스템의 효율성 향상에 필수적인 이유

question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In the course of his research on business strategy and the environment, Michael Porter noticed a peculiar pattern: Businesses seemed to be profiting from regulation. He also discovered that the stricter regulations were prompting more innovation than the weaker ones. The Dutch flower industry provides an illustration. For many years, the companies producing Holland's world-renowned tulips and other cut flowers were also contaminating the country's water and soil with fertilizers and pesticides. In 1991, the Dutch government adopted a policy designed to cut pesticide use in half by 2000 - a goal they ultimately achieved. Facing increasingly strict regulation, greenhouse growers realized they had to develop new methods if they were going to maintain product quality with fewer pesticides. In response, they shifted to a cultivation method that circulates water in closed-loop systems and grows flowers in a rock wool substrate. The new system not only reduced the pollution released into the environment; it also increased profits by giving companies greater control over growing conditions.
options: ① Transition of traditional farming methods to sustainable systems
② Challenges of balancing environmental sustainability with product quality
③ Economic consequences of government intervention in agricultural markets
④ Influence of global environmental standards on export-oriented industries
⑤ Paradoxical impact of strict regulations on business innovation and profitability
explanation: 이 글은 마이클 포터의 연구 결과를 바탕으로, 엄격한 환경 규제가 오히려 기업의 혁신을 자극하고 생산성을 높여 수익성을 향상시킨다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 네덜란드 화훼 산업의 사례를 통해, 살충제 규제가 수경 재배와 같은 혁신적인 시스템 도입을 이끌어 환경 오염 감소와 수익 증대라는 두 마리 토끼를 잡았음을 설명하고 있으므로 ⑤번 '기업 혁신과 수익성에 미치는 엄격한 규제의 역설적인 영향'이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 전통적인 농법의 지속 가능한 시스템으로의 전환
② 환경적 지속 가능성과 제품 품질 사이의 균형을 맞추는 도전 과제
③ 농산물 시장에 대한 정부 개입의 경제적 결과
④ 수출 지향 산업에 대한 글로벌 환경 표준의 영향
⑤ 기업 혁신과 수익성에 미치는 엄격한 규제의 역설적인 영향

question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Take a look at some of the most powerful, rich, and famous people in the world. Ignore the trappings of their success and what they're able to buy. Look instead at what they're forced to trade in return - look at what success has cost them. Mostly? Freedom. Their work demands they wear a suit. Their success depends on attending certain parties, kissing up to people they don't like. It will require - inevitably - realizing they are unable to say what they actually think. Worse, it demands that they become a different type of person or do bad things. Sure, it might pay well - but they haven't truly examined the transaction. As Seneca put it, "Slavery resides under marble and gold." Too many successful people are prisoners in jails of their own making. Is that what you want? Is that what you're working hard toward? Let's hope not.
options: ① how to balance public image with personal values
② the loss of personal freedom in exchange for success
③ habits that lead to fame and wealth in modern society
④ financial success that can help people gain social influence
⑤ the importance of attending elite events for career advancement
explanation: 이 글은 성공한 사람들이 누리는 외적인 화려함 뒤에 숨겨진 대가, 즉 '자유의 상실'에 대해 이야기하고 있습니다. 성공을 유지하기 위해 원치 않는 복장을 갖추고, 싫어하는 사람에게 비위를 맞추며, 자신의 생각을 솔직하게 말하지 못하는 상황을 '스스로 만든 감옥'이나 '대리석과 황금 아래의 노예 상태'로 비유하며 경고하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 ②번 '성공의 대가로 지불하는 개인적 자유의 상실'입니다.
options_translation: ① 대중적 이미지와 개인적 가치 사이의 균형을 맞추는 방법
② 성공의 대가로 교환되는 개인적 자유의 상실
③ 현대 사회에서 명성과 부로 이끄는 습관들
④ 사람들이 사회적 영향력을 얻도록 도와줄 수 있는 재정적 성공
⑤ 경력 발전을 위해 엘리트 행사에 참석하는 것의 중요성

question: 6. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: New words and expressions emerge continually in response to new situations, ideas and feelings. The Oxford English Dictionary publishes supplements of new words and expressions that have entered the language. Some people deplore this kind of thing and see it as a drift from correct English. But it was only in the eighteenth century that any attempt was made to formalize spelling and punctuation of English at all. The language we speak in the twenty-first century would be virtually unintelligible to Shakespeare, and so would his way of speaking to us. Alvin Toffler estimated that Shakespeare would probably only understand about 250,000 of the 450,000 words in general use in the English language now. In other words, so to speak, if Shakespeare were to materialize in London today he would understand, on average, only five out of every nine words in our vocabulary.
options: ① Excessive linguistic change leads to confusion and social division.
② Efforts to preserve linguistic tradition help protect cultural identity.
③ Language should resist external influences to preserve historical consistency.
④ Language evolves naturally in response to social, cultural, and communicative needs.
⑤ The emergence of new words is a threat to the clarity and tradition of the English language.
explanation: 이 글은 언어가 고정된 것이 아니라 새로운 상황과 필요에 따라 지속적으로 변화하고 진화한다는 점을 설명합니다. 셰익스피어 시대의 언어와 현대 영어를 비교하여, 언어의 변화가 자연스러운 현상임을 강조하고 있습니다. 언어의 표준화 시도는 비교적 최근의 일일 뿐이며, 언어는 끊임없이 새로워진다는 것이 핵심 내용이므로 ④번 '언어는 사회적, 문화적, 소통적 필요에 따라 자연스럽게 진화한다'가 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 과도한 언어 변화는 혼란과 사회적 분열을 초래한다.
② 언어적 전통을 보존하려는 노력은 문화적 정체성을 보호하는 데 도움이 된다.
③ 언어는 역사적 일관성을 유지하기 위해 외부의 영향을 거부해야 한다.
④ 언어는 사회적, 문화적, 소통적 필요에 부응하여 자연스럽게 진화한다.
⑤ 새로운 단어의 출현은 영어의 명확성과 전통에 대한 위협이다.

question: 7. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: People behave in highly predictable ways when they experience certain thoughts. When they agree, they nod their heads. So far, no surprise, but according to an area of research known as "proprioceptive psychology," the process also works in reverse. Get people to behave in a certain way and you cause them to have certain thoughts. The idea was initially controversial, but fortunately it was supported by a compelling experiment. Participants in a study were asked to fixate on various products moving across a large computer screen and then indicate whether the items appealed to them. Some of the items moved vertically (causing the participants to nod their heads while watching), and others moved horizontally (resulting in a side-to-side head movement). Participants preferred vertically moving products without being aware that their "yes" and "no" head movements had played a key role in their decisions.
options: ① People tend to nod their heads when they agree with something.
② The idea that behavior can influence thoughts was controversial at first.
③ Participants were instructed to nod or shake their heads as they evaluated products.
④ Vertically moving products were preferred by participants.
⑤ Participants weren't aware that their head movements had played a significant role in their decision making.
explanation: 실험 참가자들은 직접 고개를 끄덕이거나 가로저으라는 지시를 받은 것이 아니라, 화면에서 수직 혹은 수평으로 움직이는 제품들을 바라보게 함으로써 자연스럽게 고개가 움직이도록 유도되었습니다. 따라서 ③번은 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들은 무언가에 동의할 때 고개를 끄덕이는 경향이 있다.
② 행동이 사고에 영향을 미칠 수 있다는 생각은 처음에는 논란의 여지가 있었다.
③ 참가자들은 제품을 평가할 때 고개를 끄덕이거나 가로저으라는 지시를 받았다.
④ 수직으로 움직이는 제품들이 참가자들에 의해 선호되었다.
⑤ 참가자들은 자신의 머리 움직임이 의사 결정에 중요한 역할을 했다는 것을 인식하지 못했다.

question: 8. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 a telescope is a true time machine이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: On our little world light travels, for all practical purposes, instantaneously. If a lightbulb is glowing, then of course it's physically where we see it, shining away. We reach out our hand and touch it: It's there all right, and unpleasantly hot. If the filament fails, then the light goes out. We don't see it in the same place, glowing, illuminating the room years after the bulb breaks and it's removed from its socket. The very notion seems nonsensical. But if we're far enough away, an entire sun can go out and we'll continue to see it shining brightly; we won't learn of its death, it may be, for ages to come - in fact, for how long it takes light, which travels fast but not infinitely fast, to cross the intervening vastness. Indeed, the immense distances to the stars and the galaxies mean that we see everything in space in the past - some as they were before the Earth came to be. In this regard, <u>a telescope is a true time machine</u>. Billions of years ago, when an early galaxy began to pour light out into the surrounding darkness, no witness could have known that thinking beings would evolve who would one day capture a little of that galactic light, and try to figure out what had sent it on its way.
options: ① it allows us to precisely predict the future of celestial bodies by comparing their developments over time
② it reveals the bygone states of the universe by observing light that has traveled vast distances across space
③ it captures light from various moments in time simultaneously, enabling us to see into the past without any distortion
④ it challenges prevailing myths about the intrinsic relationship between time and space through the observation of light
⑤ it helps us to intuitively understand the relativity of light speed by clearly demonstrating complex physical phenomena
explanation: 빛의 속도는 유한하기 때문에 우주의 먼 곳에서 오는 빛은 우리에게 도달하는 데 오랜 시간이 걸립니다. 따라서 망원경을 통해 먼 별이나 은하를 관찰하는 것은 과거의 상태를 보는 것과 같다는 의미입니다. 그러므로 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그것은 천체의 시간에 따른 발달을 비교함으로써 미래를 정확하게 예측하게 해준다.
② 그것은 우주의 광대한 거리를 가로질러 온 빛을 관찰함으로써 우주의 과거 상태를 드러낸다.
③ 그것은 다양한 시점의 빛을 동시에 포착하여 왜곡 없이 과거를 볼 수 있게 해준다.
④ 그것은 빛의 관찰을 통해 시간과 공간 사이의 본질적 관계에 대한 널리 퍼진 신화에 도전한다.
⑤ 그것은 복잡한 물리적 현상을 명확하게 보여줌으로써 빛의 속도의 상대성을 직관적으로 이해하도록 돕는다.

question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Some of us jump right in when there's a deadline, but many of us tend do put things off and only begin to feel the ⓐ<u>pressure</u> when time is almost up. This is related to what psychologists call an "implemental" mindset - that is, an attitude of getting down to action rather than planning and evaluating. To meet a deadline, we need to put into action whatever plans we have. According to psychologists, one obstacle is, how we ⓑ<u>categorize</u> time. We tend to break up time into units, such as weeks, months, and seasons; in a series of studies among farmers in India and students in North America, psychologists found that if a deadline is on the other side of a "break" - such as in the New Year - we're more likely to see it as remote, and, as a result, be ⓒ<u>more</u> ready to jump into action. What you need to do in that situation is find another way to think about the timeframe. For example, if it's November and the deadline is in January, it's better to tell yourself you have to get it done "this winter" rather than "next year." The best approach is to view deadlines as a challenge that you have to meet within a period that's ⓓ<u>imminent</u>. That way the stress is more manageable, and you have a ⓔ<u>better</u> chance of starting - and therefore finishing - in good time.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 심리학자들의 연구에 따르면, 마감 기한이 새해와 같은 '경계(break)' 너머에 있으면 이를 멀게 느끼게 되어 즉시 행동을 개시할 준비가 '더 덜(less)' 된다는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다. 따라서 ⓒmore를 less로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: The core characteristic of the experimental method lies in its emphasis on manipulation and control. Researchers deliberately change one variable they are interested in and ⓐ<u>observe</u> whether this leads to a difference. At the same time, they attempt to control for the potential effects of all other variables. Controlled experiments play an essential part in determining the underlying causes of events, and ⓑ<u>their</u> significance cannot be exaggerated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often correlated. For instance, people who take vitamin supplements may also follow healthier diets and engage in more physical activity than those who don't. Because of this, simply observing real-life situations isn't enough ⓒ<u>to study</u> the health effects of vitamins - any of the related factors (like diet, exercise, or the supplements themselves) could influence the results. Rather, we have to create a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world. That's exactly ⓓ<u>what</u> scientific experiments do. They attempt to isolate naturally occurring relationships by manipulating one variable at a time with all other factors held ⓔ<u>constantly</u>.
explanation: ⓔ의 'hold'는 목적어와 목적격 보어를 취하는 5형식 구조로 쓰였습니다. 'with + 목적어(all other factors) + 목적격 보어' 구문에서 보어 자리에는 부사가 아닌 형용사가 와야 하므로 constantly를 constant로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Consider a family faced with a choice with a spare $1,000: buying a big-screen television or investing the money in public offering fund. Buying a television is current consumption. It makes us happy today but does nothing for tomorrow. Yes, money spent on a television keeps workers ⓐ<u>employed</u> at the television factory. But if the same money were invested, it would create jobs somewhere else, say for scientists in a laboratory or workers on a construction site, while also ⓑ<u>making</u> us richer in the long run. Think about college as an example. Sending students to college creates jobs for professors. The money used to buy fancy sports cars for high school graduates ⓒ<u>creates</u> jobs for auto workers. The crucial difference between these scenarios is ⓓ<u>what</u> a college education makes a young person more productive for the rest of his or her life; a sports car does not. Though the expenditure involved in both choices may be identical, it is evident that the effects, ⓔ<u>which</u> each choice has on the economy, differ profoundly. Thus, college tuition is an investment; buying a sports car is consumption.
explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 is 뒤의 절은 '대학 교육이 한 젊은이를 생산적으로 만든다'는 완전한 문장입니다. 따라서 관계대명사 what이 아닌 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 that이 와야 합니다.

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: While eyaluating a given policy, individuals tend to direct their attention primarily toward the extent to which it addresses a specific issue, often neglecting to consider, or ⓐ<u>deliberately</u> minimizing, the broader range of unintended consequences that such a policy might entail. Economists often refer to this situation as The Law of Unintended Consequences. For instance, suppose that you impose a tariff on ⓑ<u>importing</u> steel in order to protect the jobs of domestic steelworkers. If you impose a high enough tariff, their jobs will indeed be protected from competition by foreign steel companies. But an unintended consequence is that the jobs of some autoworkers will be lost to foreign competition. Why? The tariff that protects steelworkers raises the price of the steel ⓒ<u>which</u> domestic automobile makers need to build their cars. As a result, domestic automobile manufacturers have to raise the prices of their cars, making ⓓ<u>them</u> relatively less attractive than foreign cars. ⓔ<u>Raising</u> prices tends to reduce domestic car sales, so some domestic autoworkers lose their jobs.
explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 '관세(tariff)'는 '수입된 강철(imported steel)'에 부과되는 것이 문맥상 자연스럽습니다. steel은 '수입되는' 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 'imported'로 수식하는 것이 적절합니다. ① 'deliberately'는 동명사 'minimizing'을 수식하는 부사로 적절합니다. ③ 'which'는 목적격 관계대명사로 'the steel'을 수식하며 뒤에 'need'의 목적어가 빠져있으므로 적절합니다. ④ 'them'은 'domestic automobile makers'가 만드는 'their cars'를 지칭하는 대명사로 적절합니다. ⑤ 'Raising'은 문장의 주어 역할을 하는 동명사로 쓰여 단수 동사 'tends'와 호응하므로 적절합니다.

question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It's hard to pay more for the speedy but highly skilled person, simply because there's less effort being observed. They found that people would pay a little more for a greater quantity of rescued data, but what they were most sensitive to was the number of hours the technician worked. When the data recovery took only a few minutes, willingness to pay was low, but when it took more than a week to recover the same amount of data, people were willing to pay much more. question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Why do people in the Mediterranean live longer and have a lower incidence of disease? Some people say it's because of what they eat. question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Because people tend to adapt, interrupting positive things with negative ones can actually increase enjoyment. Take commercials. question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In 2003, British Airways announced that they would stop operating the London to New York Concorde flight as it had proven uneconomical. What happened the very next day? Sales for the route soared sharply, while there had been no changes like discounted airfare or improved cabin service.
ordered_passages: (A) Such promotional strategies, even if implemented, would likely have had only a marginal effect; the real appeal lay in passengers' recognition that the route was in short supply. This scarcity bias might seem incomprehensible at first glance, yet it could count quite significantly in shaping human judgment and perception.

(B) Interestingly, when they were asked to judge all ten from scratch, the item that had just become cut of reach was suddenly rated as the most beautiful. This kind of response had been consistently observed in similar experiments involving participants with diverse attributes. In psychology, these phenomena are known as reactance: when we are deprived of an option, we suddenly deem it more desirable.

(C) Professor Stephen Worchel, intrigued by this kind of irony, designed an experiment to establish its underlying mechanism. He asked students to arrange ten posters in order of attractiveness - with the agreement that afterward they could keep one as a reward for their effort. Five minutes later, however, they were informed that the poster they had appraised as the third highest was no longer available.
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 콩코드 항공편 중단 발표 후 오히려 판매가 급증했다는 사례를 제시합니다. (A)에서는 이러한 현상이 희소성 편향(scarcity bias) 때문임을 설명합니다. (C)에서는 이러한 심리적 기제를 확인하기 위한 Stephen Worchel 교수의 포스터 선호도 실험을 소개하고, (B)에서는 실험 결과 선택할 수 없게 된 항목을 더 아름답다고 평가하는 '심리적 저항(reactance)' 현상을 설명하며 마무리합니다. 따라서 (A)-(C)-(B) 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 21. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: If a firm is going to be saved by the government, it might be easier to concentrate on lobbying the government for more money rather than taking the harder decision of restructuring the company to be able to be profitable and viable in the long term. For example, if governments rescue banks who get into difficulty, as they did during the credit crisis of 2007-08, this could encourage banks to take greater risks in the future. ⓐThis is because they know there is a possibility that governments will intervene if they lose money. ⓑAlthough the government rescue may be well intended, it can negatively affect the behavior of banks, encouraging risky and poor decision making. ⓒBanks offer a wide range of financial services including savings accounts, loans, and investment advice. ⓓIn the long run, such interventions may undermine the overall stability of the financial system. ⓔTherefore, it is crucial for governments to carefully weigh the long-term consequences of their support and consider mechanisms that reduce the likelihood of moral hazard.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

question: 22. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
