explanation: 식당이 광고를 통해 손님을 끌어들이듯, 자연계의 꽃들도 동물(손님)을 유혹하기 위해 광고를 하는데, 글의 마지막 문장에서 언급하듯 꽃들은 '냄새의 언어'를 사용하여 이를 효과적으로 수행한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '향기: 자연의 광고 방식'이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 밝은 색상은 큰 영향을 미친다.
② 향기: 자연의 광고 방식
③ 식당이 손님을 유혹하는 방법
④ 꽃 요리: 식당의 식용 꽃
⑤ 향기로운 초대: 식당의 마케팅 전략

question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: The big problem with money created by the government is that those who run the government always ␖<u>face</u> the temptation to create more money and spend it. Whether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, ␗<u>leading</u> to inflation and the many economic and social problems that follow from inflation. For this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that inherently ␘<u>limited</u> in supply, as money. It is a way of depriving governments of the power to expand the money supply to inflationary levels. Gold has long been considered ␙<u>ideal</u> for this purpose, since the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased rapidly. When paper money is convertible into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money is said to be "backed up" by gold. This expression is misleading only if we imagine that the value of the gold is somehow transferred to the paper money, when in fact the real point is ␚<u>that</u> the gold simply limits the amount of paper money that can be issued.
options: ① ␖
② ␗
③ ␘
④ ␙
⑤ ␚
explanation: ␘번 문장에서 'that inherently limited in supply'는 선행사 'some other material'을 수식하는 관계절입니다. 관계대명사 that 뒤에 동사가 필요한데, limited는 과거분사로 쓰여 동사 역할을 할 수 없습니다. 따라서 '공급이 내재적으로 제한되는'이라는 수동의 의미를 갖는 동사구가 되어야 하므로 'is limited' 또는 'was limited'로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis. For example, migrants are ⓐ <u>assumed</u> to overcrowd cities, clog up labor markets, and increase poverty. The other questionable assumption is that most migration is involuntary - people fleeing natural or man-made disasters. The reality, however, is more complex, and many migrants are simply seeking greater economic opportunity. Of course migration can and ⓑ<u>do</u> create social and economic problems. But migration can also be a solution for many preexisting problems. For example, out-migration generally redistributes workers from places of labor surplus to areas ⓒ<u>where</u> there is greater demand or more opportunity. Migration is ⓓ<u>generally</u> selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to endure hardship in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin. Most research that examines long-term outcomes of migration, including remittances and intergenerational mobility, ⓔ<u>finds</u> positive "long-term" effects on places of origin and destination.
explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'migration'으로 3인칭 단수입니다. 따라서 조동사 'can'과 병렬 구조를 이루며 뒤따르는 일반 동사의 강조형 조동사는 'do'가 아니라 'does'가 되어야 적절합니다. (migration can and does create...)

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: It is difficult, if not impossible, to define the limits which reason should impose on the desire for wealth; for there is no ⓐ<u>fixed</u> amount of wealth which will satisfy a man. The amount is always ⓑ<u>constant</u>, that is to say, just so much as will maintain the proportion between what he wants and what he gets; for to measure a man's happiness only by what he gets, and not also by what he expects to get, is as ⓒ<u>meaningless</u> as to try and express a fraction which shall have a numerator but no denominator. A man never feels the loss of things which it never occurs to him to ask for; he is just as happy without them; whilst another, who have a hundred times as much, feels ⓓ<u>discontented</u> because he has not got the one thing he wants. In fact, every man has a ⓔ<u>boundary</u> of his own, and he will expect as much as he thinks it is possible for him to get.
explanation: 부의 만족감은 절대적인 양에 의해 결정되는 것이 아니라, 개인이 갈망하는 것과 실제로 얻는 것 사이의 비율에 따라 달라진다는 맥락입니다. 따라서 만족스러운 부의 양은 'constant(일정한/변함없는)'한 것이 아니라 상대적이라는 의미의 'relative' 등이 오는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Low oil prices are a good thing, because it means lower energy costs of production for the majority of industries, not least the automobile and the logistics industries. Firms directly benefit from the ⓐ<u>reduction</u> in their costs of production and provision of services. This has the effect of ⓑ<u>encouraging</u> the aggregate supply and provides a stimulus for growth. Conversely, a sudden rise in oil prices due to a shrink in oil production is ⓒ<u>bad</u> news, even though it definitely gives a big boost to the energy sector. A look through the history of oil price fluctuations ⓓ<u>proves</u> this notion, as this has been the subject of much economic research. Following an oil price jump of 10 per cent due to a contraction in supply, an economy (as typified by the US economy) typically sees its output (GDP) ⓔ<u>stimulated</u> by close to 1 percentage point. For a $15 trillion economy, that is a loss of $150 billion in potential wealth or economic growth. Conversely, there has never been much concern with oil price decreases following an excess in its supply.
explanation: 유가 급등(oil price jump)이 발생하면 경제에 악영향을 미치며, 뒤이은 문장에서 1,500억 달러의 잠재적 부나 경제 성장의 '손실(loss)'이라고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 GDP가 'stimulated(자극받은/활성화된)' 되는 것이 아니라 'reduced(감소된)' 혹은 'depressed(위축된)' 되어야 문맥이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If we've invested in something that hasn't repaid us - be it money in a failing venture, or time in an unhappy relationship - we find it very difficult to walk away. This is the sunk cost fallacy. Our instinct is to continue investing money or time as we hope that our investment will prove to be worthwhile in the end. Giving up would mean acknowledging that we've wasted something we can't get back, and that thought is so painful that we prefer to avoid it if we can. The problem, of course, is that if something really is a bad bet, then staying with it simply increases the amount we lose. Rather than walk away from a bad five-year relationship, for example, we turn it into a bad 10-year relationship; rather than accept that we've lost a thousand dollars, we lay down another thousand and lose that too. In the end, by _______________________________________, we only add to it. Sometimes we just have to cut our losses.
options: ① sticking to the previous plan
② accepting the wrong decision
③ holding on hope for a bright future
④ postponing the pain of admitting our problem
⑤ distracting ourselves with temporary pleasure
explanation: 매몰 비용 오류(sunk cost fallacy)에 관한 글로, 사람들은 이미 투자한 것이 아까워 실패한 투자를 포기하지 못하는 경향이 있다는 내용입니다. 포기하는 것은 우리가 되돌릴 수 없는 무언가를 낭비했다는 것을 인정하는 고통스러운 일이기 때문에, 빈칸에는 이러한 '문제를 인정하는 고통을 미룸(postponing the pain of admitting our problem)'으로써 결국 손해만 더 늘리게 된다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 이전의 계획을 고수함으로써
② 잘못된 결정을 수용함으로써
③ 밝은 미래에 대한 희망을 가짐으로써
④ 우리의 문제를 인정하는 고통을 미룸으로써
⑤ 일시적인 즐거움으로 주의를 돌림으로써

question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Of central importance for understanding the development of handedness is the answer to the question of when in development it is actually determined whether a child will be left-handed or right-handed. It was long thought that handedness could only be reliably determined in elementary school, when a child learns to write. However, this assumption is incorrect. ⓐIn fact, scientific studies show that left-handedness is established in many children long before elementary school - interestingly, even before birth in most people. ⓑIn such studies, the hand and arm movements of unborn children in the womb are recorded using ultrasound images. ⓒThese ultrasound images can be used to estimate the baby's size and weight. ⓓUsing this technique, it was shown that a clear preference for the movement of the right arm exists as early as 10 weeks after fertilization. ⓔIn this study, ultrasound images of 72 unborn children 10 weeks after fertilization were evaluated and 85% showed more movements of the right arm than the left. This number is already very close to the approximately 89.4% right-handers among adults.
explanation: 이 글은 주로 사용하는 손(handedness)이 언제 결정되는지에 대한 연구를 다루고 있습니다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 태아기 때부터 이미 오른손잡이인지 왼손잡이인지가 결정된다는 연구 결과와 그 측정 방법에 관한 설명입니다. 반면 ⓒ '초음파 영상은 아기의 크기와 무게를 추정하는 데 사용될 수 있다'는 내용은 손잡이의 결정 시기라는 전체 주제와 무관한 일반적인 사실입니다.

question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
passage: If there is little or no diversity of views, and all scientists see, think, and question the world in a similar way, then they will not, as a community, be as objective as they maintain they are, or at least aspire to be. ①The solution is that there should be far greater diversity in the practice of science: in gender, ethnicity, and social and cultural backgrounds. ②Science often relies on substantial funding and institutional support to achieve significant advances. ③Science works because it is carried out by people who pursue their curiosity about the natural world. ④These people test their and each other's ideas from as many varied perspectives and angles as possible. ⑤When science is done by a diverse group of people, and if consensus builds up about a particular area of scientific knowledge, then we can have more confidence in its objectivity and truth.
explanation: 이 글은 과학의 객관성감과 진리를 확보하기 위해 과학 실행에 있어서의 '다요성(성별, 인준, 사회문•화적 배경 등)'이 필요함을 강조하고 있습니다. ②번 문장은 과학적 발전을 위한 '자금 및 제도적 지원'에 대해 언급하고 있으뭀로, ' 다요성을 통한 객관성 확보'라는 전체 흐ℹ과 관계가 없습니다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 흐ℹ으로 밴아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 설정한 곳은? [2.9점]
passage: The built-in capacity for smiling is proven by the remarkable observation that babies who are congenitally both deaf and blind, who have never seen a human face, also start to smile at around 2 months. (A) Without the right feedback, smiling dies out. (B) But here's a fascinating fact: blind babies will continue to smile if they are cuddled, bounced, nudged, and tickled by an adult - anything to let them know that they are not alone and that someone cares about them. (C) This social feedback encourages the baby to continue smiling. (D) In this way, early experience operates with our biology to establish social behaviors. (E) In fact, you don't need the cases of blind babies to make the point. Babies with sight smile more at you when you look at them or, better still, smile back at them.
insertion_sentence: However, smiling in blind babies eventually disappears if nothing is done to reinforce it.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장은 '시각 장애를 가진 아기들의 미소는 강화하기 위한 조치가 없으뭴 서서히 사라지게 된다'는 내용입니다. (A) 됤의 문장 'Without the right feedback, smiling dies out(적절한 피드백이 없으뭴 미소가 사라진다)'와 내용이 일치하며, 선찜적으로 미소 지을 수 있다는 앑 내용과 대조를 이루기 알맞은 위치는 (A)입니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 흐ℹ으로 밴아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 설정한 곳은? [3.2점]
passage: Brains are expensive in terms of energy. Twenty percent of the calories we consume are used to power the brain. So brains try to operate in the most energy-efficient way possible, and that means processing only the minimum amount of information from our senses that we need to navigate the world. (A) Magicians figured this out long ago. (B) By directing your attention, they perform tricks with their hands in full view. (C) Their actions should give away the game, but they can rest assured that your brain processes only small bits of the visual scene. (D) This all helps to explain the prevalence of traffic accidents in which drivers hit pedestrians in plain view, or collide with cars directly in front of them. (E) In many of these cases, the eyes are pointed in the right direction, but the brain isn't seeing what's really out there.
insertion_sentence: Neuroscientists weren't the first to discover that fixing your gaze on something is no guarantee of seeing it.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장은 '시선을 고정하는 것이 보는 것을 방증하지 않다는 것을 뇌과학자들이 처음으로 발견한 것은 아니다'라고 합니다. 이는 (A) 다음에 나오는 마술사들이 이를 오래전에 알았다는 내용과 자연스럽게 연결됩니다. 뇌과학자들이 알아내기 전에 이미 마술사들이 이를 활용하고 있었다는 놼리적 흐ℹ에 따라 (A)가 적절합니다.

question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 ℹ서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: We tend to break up time into units, such as weeks, months, and seasons; in a series of studies among farmers in India and students in North America, psychologists found the fascinating fact.
ordered_passages: (A) The best approach is to view deadlines as a challenge that you have to meet within a period that's imminent. That way the stress is more manageable, and you have a better chance of starting - and therefore finishing - in good time.(B) If a deadline is on the other side of a "break" - such as in the New Year - we're more likely to see it as remote, and, as a result, be less ready to jump into action.(C) What you need to do in that situation is find another way to think about the timeframe. For example, if it's November and the deadline is in January, it's better to tell yourself you have to get it done "this winter" rather than "next year."
explanation: 주어진 글에서 시간을 단위로 나누는 경향과 관련된 흥미로운 사실을 발견했다고 언급합니다. (B)에서 괴 구체적인 현상(마감기한이 '경계' 너머에 있을 때 멀게 냌기는 것)을 설먱하고, (C)에서 괴 사황(괴 문제)에 대한 해결책으로쏌 시간 프러임을 다리 생각하는 방법(내년 대신 이번 겨울)을 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이를 최선의 접근법으로 정리하며 마무리하는 (B)-(C)-(A)가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The Net differs from most of the mass media it replaces in an obvious and very important way: it's bidirectional.
ordered_passages: (A) It's a personal broadcasting medium as well as a commercial one. Millions of people use it to distribute their own digital creations, in the form of blogs, videos, photos, songs, and podcasts, as well as to critique, edit, or otherwise modify the creations of others.(B) With a few clicks, people can search virtual catalogues, place orders, track shipments, and update information in corporate databases. But the Net doesn't just connect us with businesses; it connects us with one another.(C) We can send messages through the network as well as receive them, which has made the system all the more useful. The ability to exchange information online, to upload as well as download, has turned the Net into a thoroughfare for business and commerce.
explanation: 주어진 문장에서 인터넷이 양방향성(bidirectional)이라는 특징을 언급합니다. (C)에서 이 양방향성을 메시지를 보내고 받는 능력으로 구체화하며 비즈니스 통로가 되었음을 설명합니다. (B)에서는 비즈니스적 측면(주문, 배송 추적 등)을 구체화한 뒤, 비즈니스뿐 아니라 '우리 서로'를 연결한다고 전환합니다. (A)에서 우리 서로를 연결하는 개인적 방송 매체로서의 성격(블로그, 포드캐스트 등)을 상술하며 마무리되는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 (C)-(B)-(A) 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 22. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 we won't forget a piece of gossip about our cousin이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: We might forget an anecdote about a stranger because it makes few connections with our existing associations, but <u>we won't forget a piece of gossip about our cousin</u>. There's one complex network that is larger and quicker to access than all others - the self. We've been thinking about ourselves in our whole lives. (In fact, there were entire years during junior high when we weren't capable of thinking about much else.) So if a new piece of information has something to do with us, it will be more easily and thoroughly processed. It hits even closer to home than our actual home - we can take a vacation away from our home, but not from ourselves. The most effective communicators find ways to make the abstract personal. Consider the warning that law schools give to motivate first-year law students concerning the rigors of their program. Hearing that "the first-year dropout rate is 33%" is an abstract statistic. "Look to your left, look to your right. One of the three of you won't be joining us next fall" wakes up the self.
options: ① We are reluctant to talk about ourselves to strangers.
② Gossip captures people's attention more than anything else.
③ The way we process information involves cognitive reasoning.
④ Information with personal relevance is remembered more easily.
⑤ The more intense an experience is, the less likely we are to forget it.
explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 정보가 '자기 자신(the self)'과 관련이 있을 때 더 쉽고 철저하게 처리된다는 것입니다. 사촌에 대한 가십을 잊지 않는다는 것은 낯선 사람의 일화보다 친척(나와 관련된 인물)의 이야기가 나에게 더 개인적인 의미가 있어 잘 기억된다는 비유입니다. 따라서 '개인적 관련성이 있는 정보가 더 쉽게 기억된다'는 4번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 우리는 낯선 사람에게 우리 자신에 대해 말하기를 꺼린다.
② 가십은 다른 어떤 것보다 사람들의 주의를 끈다.
③ 우리가 정보를 처리하는 방식은 인지적 추론을 포함한다.
④ 개인적 관련성이 있는 정보는 더 쉽게 기억된다.
⑤ 경험이 강렬할수록, 우리는 그것을 잊어버릴 가능성이 낮다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: Turtle hatchlings have, it seems, evolved to crawl toward the light. For millions of years this was a highly rational and effective strategy because the light on a dark beach represented the reflection of the moon and stars on the water's surface. Following the lights led baby turtles back home to the sea. The problems started when humans began building beachfront homes and sparkling hotels on the other side of the beach. Now after hatching, turtles heading for the brightest nearby lights were being guided straight into traffic. Are self-destructive sea turtles naturally irrational? Yes, in the modern world. But there's a deeper truth. Turtles are basing their decisions on simple cues that were perfectly rational for their ancestors; these days, however, their evolved decision-making mechanisms are being blinded by modern lights.
summary_sentence: Once (A)____________ instincts guided hatchlings safely on dark beaches, but now (B)____________ them into deadly traps.
subjective_answer_format: (A)   (B)① primitive  warn② irraitonal  steer③ innate  rescue④ inherited  protect⑤ evolved  mislead
options: ① primitive ... warn
② irraitonal ... steer
③ innate ... rescue
④ inherited ... protect
⑤ evolved ... mislead
explanation: 지문에 따르면 바다거북은 빛을 따라가는 방식이 진화(evolved)하여 과거에는 이것이 합리적이고 안전하게 바다로 인도했습니다. 하지만 현대의 인공적인 빛은 이러한 진화된 메커니즘을 눈멀게 하여 거북이들을 잘못된 길(traffic 등)로 인도(mislead)하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 진화된(evolved), (B)에는 잘못 인도하다(mislead)가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 원시적인 ... 경고하다
② 비이성적인 ... 조종하다
③ 타고난 ... 구조하다
④ 물려받은 ... 보호하다
⑤ 진화된 ... 잘못 인도하다

question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Because people tend to adapt, interrupting positive things with negative ones can actually increase enjoyment. Take commercials. Most people hate them, so removing them should make shows or other entertainment more enjoyable. But the opposite is true. Shows are actually more enjoyable when they're broken up by annoying commercials. Because these less enjoyable moments break up adaptation to the positive experience of the show. Think about eating chocolate chips. The first chip is delicious: sweet, melt-in-your-mouth goodness. The second chip is also pretty good. But by the fourth, fifth, or tenth chip in a row, the goodness is no longer as pleasurable. We adapt. Interspersing positive experiences with less positive ones, however, can slow down adaptation. Eating a Brussels sprout between chocolate chips or viewing commercials between parts of TV shows disrupts the process.
summary_sentence: The (A)____________ moment makes the following positive one more enjoyable by (B)____________ adaptation to positive experience.
options: ① less positive ...... accelerating
② positive ...... slowing down
③ enjoyable ...... controlling
④ less negative ...... making speedy
⑤ negative ...... decelerating
explanation: 이 글은 사람들이 긍정적인 경험에 적응하기 때문에, 그 사이에 부정적이거나 덜 즐거운 순간(예: TV 광고)을 끼워 넣으면 적응 속도가 늦춰져서 이후의 긍정적인 경험을 더 즐겁게 느낀다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 요약문의 (A)에는 'negative'(부정적인) 또는 'less positive'가 들어갈 수 있고, (B)에는 적응을 늦춘다는 의미의 'decelerating'(속도를 줄이는)이 가장 적절합니다. ①번의 accelerating(가속하는)은 반대 의미이므로 ⑤번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 덜 긍정적인 ••• 가속화함으로써
② 긍정적인 ••• 늦춤으로써
③ 즐거운 ••• 통제함으로써
④ 덜 부정적인 ••• 빠르게 만듦으로써
⑤ 부정적인 ••• 감속함으로써(늦춤으로써)

question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고, 흐름에 어울리는 문장이 되도록 <조건>에 맞게 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: The writer and zoologist Desmond Morris observed that our feet communicate exactly what we think and feel more honestly than any other part of our bodies. Why are the feet and legs such accurate reflectors of our sentiments? For millions of years, long before humans spoke, our legs and feet reacted to environmental threats (e.g., hot sand, ill-tempered lions) instantaneously, without the need for conscious thought. Our limbic brains made sure that our feet and legs reacted as needed by either ceasing motion, running away, or kicking at a potential threat. This survival regimen, retained from our ancestral heritage, has served us well and continues to do so today. In fact, these age-old reactions are still so hardwired in us that ____________ _________________________________________ as they did in prehistoric times.
subjective_conditions: 1. 14~16개의 단어를 사용하여 작성하시오.
2. 주어와 동사가 들어간 완전한 문장으로 서술하시오.
3. disagreeable, feet and legs, or, our, we, when, with를 반드시 사용하시오.  (중복사용 불가능, 어형 변형 불가능)
answer: when we are presented with something dangerous or (even) disagreeable, our feet and legs (still) react
explanation: 글의 맥락상 선사 시대부터 이어져 온 생존 본능으로 인해, 우리가 위험하거나 불쾌한 것을 접할 때 발과 다리가 여전히 즉각적으로 반응한다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 조건에 주어진 단어들을 활용하여 '위험하거나 불쾌한 것이 제시될 때, 우리의 발과 다리는 (여전히) 반응한다'는 의미의 문장을 구성합니다. 'when we are presented with something dangerous or disagreeable, our feet and legs react'를 기본으로 하며, 단어 수 조건(14~16단어)을 맞추기 위해 부사 등을 조절할 수 있습니다. 예시 답안은 14~15단어 수준입니다.

question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고, 흐름에 어울리는 문장이 되도록 <조건>에 맞게 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: Financial markets do more than take capital from the rich and lend it to everyone else. They enable each of us to smooth consumption over our lifetimes, which is a fancy way of saying that ____________________________________________. Shakespeare may have admonished us to be neither borrowers nor lenders; the fact is that most of us will be both at some point. If we lived in an agrarian society, we would have to eat our crops reasonably soon after the harvest or find some way to store them. Financial markets are a more sophisticated way of managing the harvest. We can spend income now that we have not yet earned - as by borrowing for college or a home - or we can earn income now and spend it later, as by saving for retirement. The important point is that earning income has been divorced from spending it, allowing us much more flexibility in life.
subjective_conditions: 1. 10~15개의 단어를 사용하여 작성하시오.
2. 주어와 동사가 들어간 완전한 문장으로 서술하시오.
3. earn, income, same, we를 반드시 사용하시오.  (중복사용 가능, 어형 변형 불가능)
answer: we don't have to spend income at the same time we earn it
explanation: 금융 시장이 소비를 평탄하게 해준다는 것은 수입을 얻는 시점과 소비하는 시점을 일치시킬 필요가 없다는 의미입니다. 글 하단에 'earning income has been divorced from spending it(소득을 얻는 것이 그것을 소비하는 것과 분리되었다)'라는 핵심 내용이 있으므로, 이를 바탕으로 '우리가 수입을 얻는 것과 동시에 그 수입을 소비할 필요는 없다'는 문장을 작성합니다. 'we don't have to spend income at the same time we earn it'은 13단어로 조건에 부합합니다.

question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고, 알맞은 요지를 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: On Saturday morning, Todd and his 5-year-old daughter Ava walked out of the store with the groceries they had just purchased. As they pushed their grocery cart through the parking lot, they saw a red car pulling into the space next to their pick-up truck. A young man named Greg was driving. "That's a cool car," Ava said to her dad. He agreed and looked at Greg, who finished parking and opened his door. As Todd finished loading his groceries, Greg's door remained open. Todd noticed Greg didn't get out of his car. But he was pulling something from his car. He put a metal frame on the ground beside his door. Remaining in the driver's seat, he then reached back into his car to grab something else. Todd realized what he was doing and considered whether he should try to help him. After a moment, he decided to approach Greg. By this time, Greg had already pulled one thin wheel out of his car and attached it to the frame. He was now pulling a second wheel out when he looked up and saw Todd standing near him. Todd said, "Hi there! Have a great weekend!" Greg seemed a bit surprised, but replied by wishing him a great weekend too. Then Greg added, "Thanks for letting me have my independence." "Of course," Todd said. After Todd and Ava climbed into their truck, Ava became curious. So she asked why he didn't offer to help the man with his wheelchair. Todd said, "Why do you insist on brushing your teeth without my help?" She answered, "Because I know how to!" He said, "And the man knows how to put together his wheelchair."
subjective_conditions: 1. 10~15개의 단어를 사용하여 작성하시오.
2. 주어와 동사가 들어간 완전한 문장으로 서술하시오.
3. allow, best, do, help, others, way를 반드시 사용하시오. (중복 사용 가능, 필요시 형태 변형 가능)
answer: The best way to help others is to allow them to do things themselves.
explanation: 이 지문은 타인이 스스로 할 수 있는 능력을 인정하고 그들의 독립성을 존중해 주는 것이 진정한 도움이라는 교훈을 담고 있습니다. 휠체어를 스스로 조립하는 남성을 지켜보며 도움을 주는 대신 그의 독립성을 지켜준 토드의 행동을 통해, ‘타인을 돕는 가장 좋은 방법은 그들이 스스로 할 수 있도록 해주는 것이다’라는 요지를 도출할 수 있습니다. 조건에 주어진 단어들을 모두 활용하여 'The best way to help others is to allow them to do things themselves.'라는 완전한 문장(총 14단어)으로 작성할 수 있습니다.

question: 3. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 "Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses."가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world. Simply put, the brain is not designed to sense on its own. For instance, an exposed brain would neither sense light shining on it nor feel something touching it. In fact, patients are often kept awake during brain surgery, which can help a surgeon isolate specific regions of the brain. The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle recognized this characteristic of the brain over 2,000 years ago when he said, <u>"Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses."</u> This concept can be seen clearly when volunteers are blind-folded and placed in the warm water of a sensory deprivation tank. They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as incoherent thought patterns. From these experiments and others, it is apparent that we need constant input from our senses to carry out functions that give us personality and intellect.
options: ① A certain part of the brain can sense on its own.
② What we perceive may not always come through our senses.
③ The brain is an independent organ that monitors outside world.
④ Sensory organs may hallucinate humans by providing inconsistent inputs.
⑤ Everything we perceive comes through sensory organs before reaching our brain.
explanation: 이 글은 뇌가 스스로 감각할 수 없으며, 오직 감각 기관을 통해서만 외부 세계와 소통한다는 점을 강조합니다. 아리스토텔레스의 말은 감각을 통하지 않고서는 마음(정신)에 도달하는 것이 없다는 뜻이므로, 우리가 인지하는 모든 것은 뇌에 도달하기 전 감각 기관을 거친다는 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌의 특정 부분은 스스로 감각할 수 있다.
② 우리가 지각하는 것이 항상 감각을 통해 오는 것은 아닐 수도 있다.
③ 뇌는 외부 세계를 감시하는 독립적인 기관이다.
④ 감각 기관은 일관되지 않은 입력을 제공하여 인간에게 환각을 일으킬 수 있다.
⑤ 우리가 지각하는 모든 것은 우리 뇌에 도달하기 전에 감각 기관을 통해 들어온다.

question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Imagine that seven out of ten working Americans got fired tomorrow. What would they all do? It's hard to believe you'd have an economy at all if you gave pink slips to more than half the labor force. But that is what the industrial revolution did to the workforce of the early 19th century. Two hundred years ago, 70 percent of American workers lived on the farm. Today automation has eliminated all but 1 percent of their jobs, replacing them with machines. But the displaced workers did not sit idle. Instead, automation created hundreds of millions of jobs in entirely new fields. Those who once farmed were now manning the factories that manufactured farm equipment, cars, and other industrial products. Since then, wave upon wave of new occupations have arrived - appliance repair person, food chemist, photographer, web designer - each building on previous automation. Today, the vast majority of us are doing jobs that no farmer from the 1800s could have imagined.
options: ① concerns about technology displacing human workers
② the creation of new jobs through the progress of automation
③ worker's emotional and behavioral responses to layoff notices
④ economic declines caused by the reduction of farming-related jobs
⑤ negative impacts of technology on traditional employment opportunities
explanation: 이 글은 산업 혁명과 자동화가 과거의 직업(예: 농업)을 없앴지만, 그 과정에서 수많은 새로운 분야의 직업들을 창출해냈다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 자동화가 인간의 일자리를 뺏는 것에 그치지 않고 새로운 기회를 만들어냈다는 내용이 핵심이므로 ②번이 주제로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기술이 인간 노동자를 대체하는 것에 대한 우려
② 자동화의 진보를 통한 새로운 일자리 창출
③ 해고 통지에 대한 노동자들의 감정적 및 행동적 반응
④ 농업 관련 일자리 감소로 인한 경제적 쇠퇴
⑤ 전통적인 고용 기회에 미치는 기술의 부정적 영향

question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Our brains are complex webs of associations, and we can access a piece of information in many different ways. The more a new fact connects with the existing network of associations in our brains, the more likely we are to remember it. We might forget an anecdote about a stranger because it makes few connections with our existing associations, but we won't forget a piece of gossip about our cousin. There's one complex network that is larger and quicker to access than all others - the self. We've been thinking about ourselves our whole lives. (In fact, there were entire years during junior high when we weren't capable of thinking about much else.) So if a new piece of information has something to do with us, it will be more easily and thoroughly processed. It hits even closer to home than our actual home - we can take a vacation away from our home, but not from ourselves. The most effective communicators find ways to make the abstract personal. Consider the warning that law schools give to motivate first-year law students concerning the rigors of their program. Hearing that "the first-year dropout rate is 33%" is an abstract statistic. "Look to your left, look to your right. One of the three of you won't be joining us next fall" wakes up the self. We feel something.
options: ① Speak Numbers, Win Minds
② Make It Personal: "This Is About You"
③ Speak to the General You, and That'll Be Heard
④ The Magic of Turning Statistics into the Abstract
explanation: 이 글은 뇌의 기억 방식이 '자기 자신(the self)'과 관련될 때 가장 강력하게 작용한다는 점을 설명합니다. 추상적인 정보라도 개인적인 일로 만들면 훨씬 더 잘 기억되고 영향을 미친다는 사례(법대 중도 탈락률 통계 vs 주변 동료 중 한 명이라는 표현)를 통해, 효과적인 전달을 위해서는 정보를 개인적인 것으로 만들어야 함을 주장하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 숫자로 말하라, 마음을 얻으라
② 개인적인 것으로 만들어라: "이것은 당신에 관한 것이다"
③ 일반적인 당신에게 말하라, 그러면 들릴 것이다
④ 통계를 추상적인 것으로 바꾸는 마법

question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The built-in capacity for smiling is proven by the remarkable observation that babies who are congenitally both deaf and blind, who have never seen a human face, also start to smile at around 2 months. However, smiling in blind babies eventually disappears if nothing is done to reinforce it. Without the right feedback, smiling dies out. But here's a fascinating fact: blind babies will continue to smile if they are cuddled, bounced, nudged, and tickled by an adult - anything to let them know that they are not alone and that someone cares about them. This social feedback encourages the baby to continue smiling. In this way, early experience operates with our biology to establish social behaviors. In fact, you don't need the cases of blind babies to make the point. Babies with sight smile more at you when you look at them or, better still, smile back at them.
options: ① The Disappearance of Smiling in Adulthood
② How Social Factors Influence a Baby's Smile
③ Why Do Babies Smile While They Are Sleeping?
④ How Smiling Affects Brain Development in Infants
⑤ Various Types of Smiles Displayed by 2-Month-Old Infants
explanation: 이 글은 아기들이 선천적으로 미소를 짓는 능력을 가지고 태어나지만, 시각 장애가 있는 아기들의 사례를 통해 타인의 관심과 반응(사회적 피드백)이 있어야 미소가 지속되고 사회적 행동으로 자리 잡게 된다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '사회적 요인이 아기의 미소에 미치는 영향'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 성인기 미소의 사라짐
② 사회적 요인이 아기의 미소에 미치는 영향
③ 아기들이 자는 동안 왜 미소를 짓는가?
④ 미소가 영유아의 뇌 발달에 미치는 영향
⑤ 2개월 된 영유아들이 보여주는 다양한 미소의 유형

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: If we've invested in something that hasn't repaid us - be it money in a failing venture, or time in an unhappy relationship - we find it very difficult to walk away. This is the sunk cost fallacy. Our instinct is to continue investing money or time as we hope that our investment will prove to be ⓐ<u>worthwhile</u> in the end. Giving up would mean acknowledging that we've wasted something we can't get back, and that thought is so painful that we prefer to ⓑ<u>avoid</u> it if we can. The problem, of course, is that if something really is a bad bet, then staying with it simply ⓒ<u>decreases</u> the amount we lose. Rather than walk away from a bad five year relationship, for example, we turn it into a bad 10 year relationship; rather than accept that we've lost a thousand dollars, we lay down another thousand and ⓓ<u>lose</u> that too. In the end, by delaying the pain of ⓔ<u>admitting</u> our problem, we only add to it. Sometimes we just have to cut our losses.
explanation: 이미 가망이 없는 일(bad bet)에 계속 머물러 있는 것은 우리가 잃는 양을 줄이는 것(decreases)이 아니라 오히려 '늘리는(increases)' 결과를 초래합니다. 이어지는 문장에서 5년의 나쁜 관계가 10년이 되고, 천 달러의 손실이 이천 달러가 된다는 예시를 통해 손실이 늘어남을 알 수 있습니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Imagine you have the best tea in the world and you put it into a bag that's impermeable. It won't work. You just won't be able to make a cup of tea. For the teabag to work, it needs to be ① <u>penetrable</u>. You need the tea and the water to come in ② <u>touch</u> with each other. In our lives too, we cannot survive and thrive in ③ <u>community</u>. Leaders need to be careful not to build walls around themselves that prevent people from reaching out to them. As a leader, you need to be able to ④ <u>connect</u> with other people. The tea was meant to mix with the water. Similarly all of us were designed to live in ⑤ <u>company</u> with other people, with teams, and with society at large.
options: ① penetrable
② touch
③ community
④ connect
⑤ company
explanation: 이 글은 찻잎이 물과 섞여야 차가 우러나듯이, 살아가는 데 있어 타인과의 '결합'과 '소통'이 필수적임을 티백의 비유를 통해 설명하고 있습니다. 문맥상 우리는 '고립된 상태'에서는 생존하거나 번창할 수 없다는 내용이 되어야 하므로, ③번의 'community(공동체)'는 'isolation(고립)'이나 'loneliness(고독)'와 같은 단어로 고쳐야 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 통과할 수 있는 (투과 가능한)
② 접촉

question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A reason Yor a conclusion is ________________________. No matter how we might state it in short-hand, it is, analytically, a complex interaction of many ideas and implications. For example, the claim that 'university education should be free for all Australians' might be supported by the reason that 'the economy benefits from a well-educated Australian population'. But is our analysis of the situation clearly expressed in just one statement? Hardly. The conclusion is about universities and free education, while the reason introduces some new ideas: economic benefit and a well-educated population. While the link between these two ideas and the conclusion might seem obvious, the purpose of reasoning is to avoid assuming the 'obvious' by carefully working through the connections between the various ideas in the initial statement of our reason.
options: ① very unlikely to consist in a single claim

question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis. The reality, however, is more complex, and many migrants are simply seeking greater economic opportunity. Of course migration can and does create social and economic problems. For example, out-migration generally redistributes workers from places of labor surplus to areas where there is greater demand or more opportunity. Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to endure hardship in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin. question: 23. 윗글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Have you heard the Korean tale of the green frog that never listened to its mother? In Korea, people often call someone ⓐ<u>rebellious</u> a "green frog." In psychology, this is known as the reactance effect - a response that occurs when people feel their freedom is threatened. The greater the restriction, the ⓑ<u>greater</u> the urge to resist. A classic literary example is found in Romeo and Juliet by William Shakespeare. Their parents didn't allow them to be together, which made the two want each other even more. Just like the green frog, they did the opposite of what they were told. The more the lovers' parents opposed their relationship, ____________________________. This shows how people often want something more when it's ⓒ<u>forbidden</u>. Psychologists suggest that if their parents had stayed out of it, the relationship might have ⓓ<u>strengthened</u> on its own. Reactance is often used in marketing. Ads with phrases like "limited time only" or "almost sold out" create urgency by threatening freedom of choice. Some ads even use reverse psychology - like "Don't click this!" - which ironically leads to higher click rates. A chewing gum commercial targeting teens became a hit by telling them not to buy the product, sparking ⓔ<u>huge</u> demand.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 지문의 문맥상 심리적 반발(리액턴스 효과)에 대해 설명하고 있다. 지문의 논리에 따르면, 부모의 간섭이 자유를 향한 갈망을 부추겨 로미오와 줄리엣의 관계를 더 돈독하게 만들었다는 것이다. 따라서 만약 부모가 개입하지(관여하지) 않았더라면 그들의 관계는 저절로 '약화되었을(faded 또는 weakened)' 것이라는 추론이 가능해야 하므로, ⓓ의 'strengthened(강화되다)'는 문맥상 반대되는 의미가 되어 어색하다.

question: 28. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. <조건>에 맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오.
passage: Brains are expensive in terms of energy. Twenty percent of the calories we consume are used to power the brain. So brains try to operate in the most energy efficient way possible, and that means processing only the minimum amount of information from our senses that we need to navigate the world. Neuro scientists weren't the first to discover that fixing your gaze on something is no guarantee of seeing it. Magicians figured this out long ago. By directing your attention, they perform tricks with their hands in full view. Their actions should give away the game, but they can rest assured that your brain processes only small bits of the visual scene. This all helps to explain the prevalence of traffic accidents in which drivers hit pedestrians in plain view, or collide with cars directly in front of them. In many of these cases, the eyes are pointed in the right direction, but the brain isn't seeing what's really out there.
summary_sentence: Although our eyes may be looking directly at something, the brain often fails to process it fully because it ___________________________________________.

단어 수 제한 없음 (*꼭 필요한 말만 쓸 것)
위 지문에 있는 단어를 사용할 수 있음
철자 및 어법 오류당 1점 감점 (단, 의미 전달에 오류가 없을 시 한함)
위 조건 1, 2를 어길 시 0점 처리함
answer: processes only the minimum amount of information
explanation: 뇌는 에너지 효율성을 극대화하기 위해 감각 기관으로부터 전달되는 방대한 데이터 중 생존에 필수적인 최소한의 정보만을 선별적으로 처리합니다. 이러한 기제 때문에 마술사의 속임수에 속거나 전방을 주시하면서도 보행자를 발견하지 못하는 교통사고가 발생하게 됩니다. 따라서 요약문은 뇌가 최소한의 정보만을 처리하기 때문이라는 내용이 되어야 하며, 지문의 'processing only the minimum amount of information' 부분을 문맥에 맞게 변형하여 완성할 수 있습니다.

passage: The study of emotions and decision making is now of considerable importance. This involves the application of various tools afforded by neuroscience. question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Would you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month? Most people will opt for the larger sum in thirteen months - where else will you find a monthly interest rate of 10 percent. A wise choice, since the interest will compensate you generously for any risks you face by waiting the extra few weeks. Second question: Would you prefer $1,000 today cash on the table or $1,100 in a month? If you think like most people, you'll take the $1,000 right away. This is amazing. In both cases, if you hold out for just a month longer, you get $100 more. In the first case, it's simple enough. You figure: "I've already waited twelve months; what's one more?" Not in the second case. The introduction of "now" causes us to make inconsistent decisions. Science calls this phenomenon hyperbolic discounting. The closer a reward is, the higher our "emotional interest rate" rises and the more we are willing to give up in exchange for it.

② How to Resist Temptation and Delay Gratification
③ Understanding Interest Rates for Better Investments
④ Hyperbolic Discounting: A Path to Financial Success

question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Financial markets do more than take capital from the rich and lend it to everyone else. They enable each of us to smooth consumption over our lifetimes, which is a fancy way of saying that we don't have to spend income at the same time we earn it. Shakespeare may have admonished us to be neither borrowers nor lenders; the fact is that most of us will be both at some point. If we lived in an agrarian society, we would have to eat our crops reasonably soon after the harvest or find some way to store them. Financial markets are a more sophisticated way of managing the harvest. We can spend income now that we have not yet earned - as by borrowing for college or a home - or we can earn income now and spend it later, as by saving for retirement. The important point is that earning income has been divorced from spending it, allowing us much more flexibility in life.
options: ① The Risks of Borrowing Without Planning

③ Limits of Using Loans for Education and Housing
④ Financial Markets: Enabling Consumption Flexibility

explanation: 이 글의 핵심은 금융 시장이 소득을 얻는 시점과 소비하는 시점을 분리(divorced)할 수 있게 해준다는 것입니다. 이를 통해 대학 등록금을 위해 미리 빌려 쓰고 나중에 갚거나, 은퇴를 위해 지금 벌어 나중에 쓰는 등 생애 주기에 맞춰 소비를 유연하게 조절할 수 있게 해준다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ④가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Steve Jobs used analogy to get people ⓐ<u>embrace</u> the new technology. Before computers, people worked in a physical world. We used paper and pens and physical file folders and so on. The idea of working in a virtual world was radically different. Or at least seemed radically different. What Jobs understood was ⓑ<u>that</u> a physical office was fundamentally similar to a virtual office. To win over the masses, Jobs drew strong analogies between the traditional workplace ⓒ<u>which</u> people knew well with the new, unfamiliar virtual workplace. In the pre-computer workplace, when ideas were written on paper it was called ... a document. When those documents needed to be stored they were put in ... a folder. And those folders were kept on ... a desk. Documents, folders, and desktops are the terms we use in our virtual work because Steve Jobs understood that using familiar terms would make the new technology ⓓ<u>easier</u> to understand. The parallels between the physical and virtual workplace now ⓔ<u>seem</u> obvious.
explanation: ⓐ의 'get'은 준사역동사로 사용될 때 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취합니다. 따라서 'embrace'는 'to embrace'로 수정되어야 어법상 적절합니다. ⓑ 'that'은 명사절을 이끄는 접속사로 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오며 문장에서 보어 역할을 합니다. ⓒ 'between A and B'의 구문 안에서 'the traditional workplace'를 수식하는 관계대명사절 'which people knew well'이 적절히 쓰였으며, between의 짝인 with(여기서는 and 대신 쓰임)가 뒤에 연결됩니다. ⓓ 'make' 동사의 목적격 보어로 형용사 'easier'가 적절합니다. ⓔ 문장의 주어가 복수인 'The parallels'이므로 복수형 동사 'seem'이 올바르게 쓰였습니다.

question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: The transition from an oral culture, ⓐ<u>in which</u> knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy ⓑ<u>to transport</u>. Wood suffers from splitting and is susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is ⓒ<u>limited</u>. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex - or, as we call it now, the book - ⓓ<u>which</u> the material reached its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and ⓔ<u>it</u> is still a dominant form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, won out as the guardian of the written word is a remarkable materials story.
explanation: 이 문장은 'it is ~ that ...' 강조 구문의 부정형인 'it wasn't until ... that ...' 구문을 사용하고 있습니다. 따라서 관계대명사 ⓓwhich를 접속사 that으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다. 로마인들이 두루마리를 코덱스(책)로 교체하고 나서야 비로소 그 재료가 잠재력을 완전히 발휘하게 되었다는 의미입니다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: The built-in capacity for smiling is proven by the remarkable observation that babies who are congenitally both deaf and blind, who have never seen a human face, also start to smile at around 2 months. However, smiling in blind babies eventually disappears if nothing is done to ⓐ<u>reinforce</u> it. Without the right feedback, smiling ⓑ<u>dies out</u>. But here's a fascinating fact: blind babies will ⓒ<u>continue</u> to smile if they are cuddled, bounced, nudged, and tickled by an adult - anything to let them know that they are not alone and that someone cares about them. This social feedback ⓓ<u>encourages</u> the baby to continue smiling. In this way, early experience operates with our biology to ⓔ<u>establish</u> social behaviors. In fact, you don't need the cases of blind babies to make the point. Babies with sight smile more at you when you look at them or, better still, smile back at them.
explanation: 해당 지문의 맥락상 시각과 청각 장애를 가진 아기들의 미소는 적절한 강화(ⓐreinforce)나 피드백이 없으면 사라지게 됩니다. ⓑ'dies out'은 '사라지다, 자취를 감추다'라는 의미로 문맥상 'disappears'와 일치하여 적절해 보일 수 있으나, 제공된 정답지에 따르면 이 부분이 문맥상 어색한 표현으로 지적되었습니다. (일반적으로 이 유형에서는 반의어가 정답이 되므로, 원래 문맥에 맞는 'disappears/dies out' 대신 강화된다는 식의 잘못된 단어가 쓰여야 하나, 여기서는 ⓑ가 정답으로 제시됨)

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: We might forget an anecdote about a stranger because it makes ⓐ<u>few</u> connections with our existing associations, but we won't forget a piece of gossip about our cousin. There's one complex network that is larger and quicker to access than all others - the self. We've been thinking about ourselves in our whole lives. (In fact, there were entire years during junior high when we weren't capable of thinking about much else.) So if a new piece of information has something to do with ⓑ<u>us</u>, it will be more easily and thoroughly processed. It hits even closer to home than our actual home - we can take a vacation away from our home, but not from ourselves. The most effective communicators find ways to make the abstract ⓒ<u>personal</u>. Consider the warning that law schools give to motivate first-year law students concerning the rigors of their program. Hearing that "the first-year dropout rate is 33%" is an ⓓ<u>abstract</u> statistic. "Look to your left, look to your right. One of the three of you won't be joining us next fall" ⓔ<u>inactivate</u> the self.
explanation: 글의 맥락상 정보를 자신과 연관 지을 때 더 잘 기억되고 처리된다는 '자기 참조 효과'를 설명하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 구체적인 예를 들어 학생들에게 직접적으로 '당신들 중 한 명'이라고 지칭하는 것은 자아를 '비활성화(inactivate)'하는 것이 아니라 '활성화(activate)'하여 정보를 더 강하게 받아들이게 하는 것이므로 ⓔ가 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Imagine that seven out of ten working Americans got fired tomorrow. What would they all do? question: 15. 다음 글의 맥락에 맞게 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Because people tend to adapt, interrupting positive things with negative ones can actually increase enjoyment. Take commercials. Most people hate them, so removing them should make shows or other entertainment more enjoyable.
ordered_passages: (A) Think about eating chocolate chips. The first chip is delicious: sweet, melt-in-your-mouth goodness. The second chip is also pretty good. But by the fourth, fifth, or tenth chip in a row, the goodness is no longer as pleasurable. We adapt.

question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Low oil prices are a good thing, because it means lower energy costs of production for the majority of industries, not least the automobile and the logistics industries. Firms directly benefit from the decrease in their costs of production and provision of services. This has the effect of stimulating the aggregate supply and provides a stimulus for growth. Conversely, a sudden rise in oil prices due to a shrink in oil production is never good news, even though it definitely gives a big boost to the energy sector. A look through the history of oil price fluctuations confirms this notion, as this has been the subject of much economic research. Following an oil price jump of 10 per cent due to a contraction in supply, an economy (as typified by the US economy) typically sees its output (GDP) slowed by close to 1 percentage point. For a $15 trillion economy, that is a loss of $150 billion in potential wealth or economic growth. Conversely, there has never been much concern with oil price decreases following an excess in its supply.
summary_sentence: A decline in oil prices encourages economic expansion by (A)____________________, whereas a sharp increase in oil cost which is driven by (B)_____________ tends to undermine output(GDP).
options: ① (A) boosting oil exports - (B) a contraction in supply
② (A) reducing input costs - (B) rising consumer demand

explanation: 지문은 낮은 유가가 생산 비용을 낮추어 경제 성장을 자극하는 반면, 공급 축소로 인한 유가 상승은 생산량(GDP)을 둔화시킨다고 설명하고 있습니다. 요약문의 (A)에는 낮은 유가가 가져오는 효과인 '운영 비용(생산 비용) 절감(lowering operational expenses)'이, (B)에는 유가 상승의 원인인 '석유 생산 감소(a reduction in oil production)'가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다. ①과 ⑤의 (A)도 맥락상 가능해 보일 수 있으나, (B)에서 '공급의 수축'을 의미하는 ④의 표현이 지문의 'shrink in oil production'과 가장 잘 부합합니다.
options_translation: ① 석유 수출을 증대시킴으로써 - 공급의 수축
② 투입 비용을 줄임으로써 - 증가하는 소비자 수요
③ 세계적인 인플레이션을 일으킴으로써 - 증가된 산업 활동
④ 운영 비용을 낮춤으로써 - 석유 생산의 감소
⑤ 총공급을 자극함으로써 - 국제 무역 장벽

question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
passage: All of the restaurants are using carefully chosen words to evoke vivid mental images of delicious food and rich desserts in order to draw the potential customer to their particular establishment. question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸에 들어갈 내용을 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
passage: We have biases that support our biases! If we're partial to one option - perhaps because it's more memorable, or framed to minimize loss, or seemingly consistent with a promising pattern - we tend to search for information that will justify choosing that option. On the one hand, it's sensible to make choices that we can defend with data and a list of reasons. On the other hand, if we're not careful, we're likely to conduct an imbalanced analysis, falling prey to a cluster of errors collectively known as "confirmation biases."For example, nearly all companies include classic "tell me about yourself" job interviews as part of the hiring process, and many rely on these interviews alone to evaluate applicants. But it turns out that traditional interviews are actually one of the least useful tools for predicting an employee's future success. This is because interviewers often subconsciously make up their minds about interviewees based on their first few moments of interaction and spend the rest of the interview cherry-picking evidence and phrasing their questions to confirm that initial impression: "I see here you left a good position at your previous job. You must be pretty ambitious, right?" versus "You must not have been very committed, huh?" This means that interviewers can be prone to _________________________. More structured approaches, like obtaining samples of a candidate's work or asking how he would respond to difficult hypothetical situations, are dramatically better at assessing future success, with a nearly threefold advantage over traditional interviews.
subjective_conditions: 1. 13~18단어로 작성할 것
2. 다음에 제시된 어휘와 어구를 모두 활용하되, 필요시 어형을 변형할 것
answer: overlooking significant information that would clearly indicate whether this candidate was(is) actually the best person to hire
explanation: 확증 편향으로 인해 면접관들이 첫인상을 강화하는 정보만을 수집하고, 해당 지원자가 실제로 적임자인지를 나타내는 중요한 정보를 간과하기 쉽다는 내용이 빈칸에 적절합니다. 조건에 따라 주어진 단어들을 활용하여 문장을 완성합니다.

question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Because people tend to adapt, interrupting positive things with negative ones can actually increase enjoyment. Take commercials. Most people hate them, so removing them should make shows or other entertainment more enjoyable. But the opposite is true. Shows are actually more enjoyable when they're broken up by annoying commercials. Because these less enjoyable moments break up adaptation to the positive experience of the show. Think about eating chocolate chips. The first chip is delicious: sweet, melt-in-your-mouth goodness. The second chip is also pretty good. But by the fourth, fifth, or tenth chip in a row, the goodness is no longer as pleasurable. We adapt. Interspersing positive experiences with less positive ones, however, can decelerate adaptation. Eating a Brussels sprout between chocolate chips or viewing commercials between parts of TV shows disrupts the process. The less positive moment makes the following positive one new again and thus more enjoyable.
options: ① 부정적 요소가 적응을 막아 긍정적 경험의 즐거움을 높인다.

question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: A reason for a conclusion is very unlikely to consist in a single claim. ⓐ<u>However</u> briefly we might state it, it is, analytically, a complex interaction of many ideas and implications. The reason must ⓑ<u>be broken</u> down into a chain of more precise premises. For example, the claim ⓒ<u>which</u> university education should be free for all Australians might be supported by the reason that 'the economy benefits from a well-educated Australian population. But is our analysis of the situation explicitly expressed in just one statement? Hardly. The conclusion is about universities and free education, while the reason introduces some new ideas: economic benefit and a well-educated population. The link between the conclusion and these two ideas ⓓ<u>seems</u> obvious. The purpose of reasoning, however, is to avoid ⓔ<u>assuming</u> the 'obvious' by carefully working through the connections between the various ideas in the initial statement of our reason.

question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In art, there are a number of ways to use perspective to obtain the illusion of depth, including using colors and graduated values of black and white, and accurately drawing the subject by applying the rules of the geometric system of perspective. In order to achieve perspective, you must make a number of observations. The forms or objects that you draw on a flat surface actually have depth and dimension in real life. As you view them and place their shapes and forms on a drawing surface, try to represent that depth to make the objects appear realistic and three-dimensional. Objects appear differently when viewed from various positions. Because of this, it's important to establish the viewpoint, and stick with it. When observing a subject, you see depth and three dimensions. When you draw this subject onto a flat surface as it appears to the eye, you are drawing in perspective.

question: 9. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world. Simply put, the brain is not designed to sense on its own. For instance, an exposed brain would neither sense light shining on it nor feel something touching it. In fact, patients are often kept awake during brain surgery, which can help a surgeon isolate specific regions of the brain. The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle recognized this characteristic of the brain over 2,000 years ago when he said, "Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses." This concept can be seen clearly when volunteers are blind-folded and placed in the warm water of a sensory deprivation tank. They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as incoherent thought patterns. From these experiments and others, it is apparent that we need constant input from our senses to carry out functions that give us personality and intellect.

② Discovering New Senses Through Isolation

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Imagine that seven out of ten working Americans got fired tomorrow. What would they all do? question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The writer and zoologist Desmond Morris observed that our feet communicate exactly what we think and feel more honestly than any other part of our bodies. Why are the feet and legs such accurate reflectors of our sentiments? For millions of years, long before humans spoke, our legs and feet reacted to environmental threats (e.g., hot sand, ill-tempered lions) instantaneously, without the need for conscious thought. Our limbic brains made sure that our feet and legs reacted as needed by either ceasing motion, running away, or kicking at a potential threat. This survival regimen, retained from our ancestral heritage, has served us well and continues to do so today. In fact, ____________________________________ that when we are presented with something dangerous or even disagreeable, our feet and legs still react as they did in prehistoric times.
options: ① muscles react so quickly and unconsciously
② the legs and feet are such active parts of the body
③ muscles and brains are so closely connected through nerves
④ such primitive reactions are still so deeply embedded within us
⑤ the senses in our legs and feet are so sensitive to any stimulation
explanation: 이 글은 인간의 발과 다리가 감정의 정직한 지표임을 설명하고 있습니다. 그 이유는 수백만 년 전 인류가 말을 하기 전부터 위협에 즉각적으로 반응하도록 진화했기 때문입니다. 이러한 조상으로부터 물려받은 생존 방식은 오늘날에도 여전히 유효하여, 위험하거나 불쾌한 상황에서 발과 다리는 선사 시대와 똑같이 반응합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '그러한 원시적인 반응들이 여전히 우리 안에 깊숙이 박혀 있다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 근육이 매우 빠르고 무의식적으로 반응한다
② 다리와 발은 신체의 매우 활동적인 부분이다
③ 근육과 뇌는 신경을 통해 매우 밀접하게 연결되어 있다
④ 그러한 원시적인 반응은 여전히 우리 안에 깊숙이 박혀 있다
⑤ 우리 다리와 발의 감각은 어떤 자극에도 매우 민감하다

question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We tend to break up time into units, such as weeks, months, and seasons; in a series of studies among farmers in India and students in North America, psychologists found that if a deadline is on the other side of a "break" - such as in the New Year - we're more likely to see it as remote, and, as a result, be less ready to jump into action. What you need to do in that situation is find another way to think about the timeframe. For example, if it's November and the deadline is in January, it's better to tell yourself you have to get it done "this winter" rather than "next year." The best approach is to consider deadlines as _________________________________. That way the stress is more manageable, and you have a better chance of starting - and therefore finishing - in good time.
options: ① commitments that require thoughtful planning
② tasks that may be addressed when time allows
③ obligations that are due in the immediate future
④ goals that should be pursued over an extended period
⑤ priorities recognized as valuable but not time-sensitive
explanation: 사람들은 시간의 경계(예: 새해)를 넘어서는 마감 기한을 멀게 느끼는 경향이 있어 일을 미루게 됩니다. 이를 해결하기 위해 시간 프레임을 다르게 생각해야 하는데, 예를 들어 '내년' 대신 '이번 겨울'로 인식하는 것입니다. 따라서 마감 기한을 '가까운 미래에 해야 할 의무'로 여기는 것이 스트레스를 관리하고 제때 시작하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
options_translation: ① 사려 깊은 계획을 필요로 하는 약속
② 시간이 허락할 때 처리될 수 있는 과업
③ 가까운 미래에 마감되는 의무
④ 장기간에 걸쳐 추구되어야 할 목표
⑤ 가치 있지만 시간에 민감하지 않은 것으로 인식되는 우선순위

question: 16. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We might forget an anecdote about a stranger because it makes few connections with our existing associations, but we won't forget a piece of gossip about our cousin. There's one complex network that is larger and quicker to access than all others ─ the self. We've been thinking about ourselves in our whole lives. (In fact, there were entire years during junior high when we weren't capable of thinking about much else.) So if a new piece of information has something to do with us, it will be more easily and thoroughly processed. It hits even closer to home than our actual home ─ we can take a vacation away from our home, but not from ourselves. The most effective communicators find ways to make the abstract personal. Consider the warning that law schools give to motivate first-year law students concerning the rigors of their program. Hearing that "the first-year dropout rate is 33%" is an abstract statistic. "Look to your left, look to your right. One of the three of you won't be joining us next fall" wakes up the self.
options: ① devices that help memories last longer
② changing trends of law school dropouts
③ enhanced memory retention through personal relevance
④ the link between adolescent self-concept development and egocentrism
⑤ the sequence of information storage, processing, and retrieval in the brain
explanation: 이 글은 정보가 '자기 자신'과 관련이 있을 때 훨씬 더 쉽고 철저하게 처리되어 잘 기억된다는 '자기 참조 효과'를 설명하고 있습니다. 타인보다 사촌에 대한 소문을 더 잘 기억하고, 추상적인 통계보다 자신에게 직접 적용되는 이야기가 더 효과적인 동기부여가 된다는 사례를 통해 개인적 관련성이 기억 유지에 미치는 긍정적인 영향을 강조하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 기억이 더 오래 지속되도록 돕는 장치들
② 법학 전문 대학원 중퇴자의 변화하는 추세
③ 개인적 관련성을 통한 향상된 기억 유지
④ 청소년기 자아 개념 발달과 자기중심성 사이의 연결고리
⑤ 뇌에서의 정보 저장, 처리, 그리고 인출의 순서

question: 17. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Take a look at some of the most powerful, rich, and famous people in the world. Ignore the trappings of their success and what they're able to buy. Look instead at what they're forced to trade in return - look at what success has cost them. Mostly? Freedom. Their work demands they wear a suit. Their success depends on attending certain parties, kissing up to people they don't like. It will require - inevitably - realizing they are unable to say what they actually think. Worse, it demands that they become a different type of person or do bad things. Sure, it might pay well - but they haven't truly examined the transaction. As Seneca put it, "Slavery resides under marble and gold." Too many successful people are prisoners in jails of their own making. Is that what you want? Is that what you're working hard toward? Let's hope not.
options: ① how the spoils of success set you free
② what you have to let go of for worldly success
③ the impact of success on your status and privileges
④ the social manners of people with high social status
⑤ the process by which class is determined in modern society
explanation: 이 글은 세상에서 성공한 사람들이 누리는 겉모습(부, 지위) 대신 그 성공을 위해 그들이 치러야 하는 대가, 즉 자유의 상실과 자기다움의 포기에 대해 이야기하고 있습니다. 세네카의 말을 인용하며 성공이 때로는 스스로 만든 감옥이 될 수 있음을 경고하므로, '세속적인 성공을 위해 포기해야 하는 것'이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 성공의 전리품이 당신을 자유롭게 하는 방법
② 세속적인 성공을 위해 당신이 놓아주어야 하는(포기해야 하는) 것
③ 성공이 당신의 지위와 특권에 미치는 영향
④ 높은 사회적 지위를 가진 사람들의 사회적 매너
⑤ 현대 사회에서 계급이 결정되는 과정

question: 18. 다음 밑줄 친 the guardian of the written word가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. Wood suffers from splitting and is susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is limited. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex ─ or, as we call it now, the book ─ that the material reached its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a dominant form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, won out as <u>the guardian of the written word</u> is a remarkable materials story.
options: ① a means to guarantee freedom of expression
② a medium preserving written knowledge over time
③ a tool for blocking spoken stories in oral cultures
④ a material that protects visual art like wall paintings
⑤ an invention that helped illiterate people avoid writing
explanation: 이 글은 지식을 전달하는 매체가 구비 문화에서 문자 문화로 전환될 때, 종이와 책(코덱스)의 발명이 기존의 돌, 점토, 나무 등이 가진 한계를 극복하고 문자화된 지식을 보존하는 지배적인 형태가 되었음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '문자 언어의 수호자'는 오랜 시간 동안 기록된 지식을 보존하는 매체를 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 표현의 자유를 보장하는 수단
② 시간이 지나도 기록된 지식을 보존하는 매체
③ 구비 문화에서 구전 이야기를 차단하는 도구
④ 벽화와 같은 시각 예술을 보호하는 재료
⑤ 문맹인들이 글쓰기를 피하도록 도운 발명품

question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: As the old joke goes: "Software, free. User manual, $10,000." But it's no joke.
ordered_passages: (A) A few prominent companies make their living selling instruction and paid support for free software. The copy of code, being mere bits, is free. The lines of free code become valuable to you only through support and guidance.(B) As soon as your genetic information is easily accessible, the interpretation of what it means, what you can do about it, and how to use it - the manual for your genes - will be expensive.(C) Many types of medical and genetic information will go this route in the coming decades. Right now getting a full copy of all your DNA is very expensive ($10,000), but soon it won't be. The price is dropping so fast, it will be $100 soon, and then the next year insurance companies will offer to sequence you for free.

(A) A few prominent companies make their living selling instruction and paid support for free software. The copy of code, being mere bits, is free. The lines of free code become valuable to you only through support and guidance.
(B) As soon as your genetic information is easily accessible, the interpretation of what it means, what you can do about it, and how to use it - the manual for your genes - will be expensive.

(C) Many types of medical and genetic information will go this route in the coming decades. Right now getting a full copy of all your DNA is very expensive ($10,000), but soon it won't be. The price is dropping so fast, it will be $100 soon, and then the next year insurance companies will offer to sequence you for free.
explanation: 주어진 문장에서 소프트웨어는 공짜지만 매뉴얼은 비싸다는 농담이 실제 상황임을 언급합니다. (A)에서 실제 소프트웨어 업계에서 코드는 공짜지만 지원과 안내(매뉴얼 역할)가 유료로 판매되는 사례를 구체적으로 설명합니다. (C)에서 이러한 경로가 의료 및 유전자 정보로 확장될 것임을 예고하며 DNA 복제 비용이 급격히 낮아질 것을 언급하고, (B)에서 유전자 정보가 공짜에 가까워졌을 때 그 해석(유전자 매뉴얼)이 비싸질 것이라는 결론으로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Of central importance for understanding the development of handedness is the answer to the question of when in development it is actually determined whether a child will be left-handed or right-handed. It was long thought that handedness could only be reliably determined in elementary school, when a child learns to write.
ordered_passages: (A) In this study, ultrasound images of 72 unborn children 10 weeks after fertilization were evaluated and 85% showed more movements of the right arm than the left. This number is already very close to the approximately 89.4% right-handers among adults.

(B) Nonetheless, this commonly held belief has been proven inaccurate. In fact, scientific studies show that left-handedness is established in many children long before elementary school ─ interestingly, even before birth in most people.

(C) In such studies, the hand and arm movements of unborn children in the womb are recorded using ultrasound images. Using this technique, it was shown that a clear preference for the movement of the right arm exists as early as 10 weeks after fertilization.
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 왼손잡이와 오른손잡이가 결정되는 시기에 대한 질문을 던지며, 과거에는 초등학교 입학 시기에 결정된다고 여겨졌음을 언급합니다. (B)에서는 이러한 통념이 부정확하며 태어나기 전부터 결정된다는 연구 결과를 소개합니다. (C)에서는 태아의 움직임을 초음파로 기록하는 연구 방식을 설명하며 10주 차에 이미 오른팔 선호가 나타남을 보여줍니다. (A)에서는 해당 연구의 구체적 수치(72명의 태아 중 85%)를 제시하며 이것이 성인 오른손잡이 비율과 유사함을 강조하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Turtle hatchlings have, it seems, evolved to crawl toward the light. For millions of years this was a highly rational and effective strategy because the light on a dark beach represented the reflection of the moon and stars on the water's surface. Following the lights led baby turtles back home to the sea. The problems started when humans began building beachfront homes and sparkling hotels on the other side of the beach. Now after hatching, turtles heading for the brightest nearby lights were being guided straight into traffic. Are self-destructive sea turtles naturally irrational? Yes, in the modern world. But there's a deeper truth. Turtles are basing their decisions on simple cues that were perfectly rational for their ancestors; these days, however, their evolved decision-making mechanisms are being blinded by modern lights.
summary_sentence: Turtle hatchlings, once guided safely to the sea by natural light, are led into (A)___________ by artificial lights, demonstrating how evolutionary (B)___________ can fail in modern settings.
options: ① danger ...... intuition
② home ...... sequence
③ danger ...... stage
④ home ...... instinct
⑤ trouble ...... trait
explanation: 바다거북 새끼들은 본래 달빛과 별빛을 따라 바다로 향하도록 진화했지만, 현대의 인공 조명 때문에 도로와 같은 위험한 곳으로 유인되고 있습니다. 이는 조상들에게는 합리적이었던 진화적 본능이나 직관이 현대 환경에서는 잘못 작동할 수 있음을 보여줍니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '위험(danger)', (B)에는 '직관(intuition)' 혹은 본능적 메커니즘을 뜻하는 단어가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 위험 ...... 직관
② 집 ...... 순서
③ 위험 ...... 단계
④ 집 ...... 본능
⑤ 문제 ...... 특성

question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
passage: Brains are expensive in terms of energy. Twenty percent of the calories we consume are used to power the brain. So brains try to operate in the most energy-efficient way possible, and that means processing only the minimum amount of information from our senses that we need to navigate the world. (A) Neuroscientists weren't the first to discover that fixing your gaze on something is no guarantee of seeing it. (B) Magicians figured this out long ago. (C) By directing your attention, they perform tricks with their hands in full view. (D) Their actions should give away the game, but they can rest assured that your brain processes only small bits of the visual scene. (E) In many of these cases, the eyes are pointed in the right direction, but the brain isn't seeing what's really out there.
insertion_sentence: Such limitations in our brain's processing capacity shed light on the prevalence of traffic accidents in which drivers hit pedestrians in plain view, or collide with cars directly in front of them.
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'Such limitations(그러한 한계)'는 앞선 문장에서 언급된 뇌가 정보의 극히 일부만을 처리한다는 내용을 가리킵니다. 또한 운전자가 바로 앞의 보행자나 차량을 보지 못하고 사고를 내는 구체적인 예시는, 눈은 올바른 방향을 향하고 있어도 뇌가 실제로 보고 있지 않다는 내용의 (E) 위치에 들어가는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 문맥상 마술의 예시를 통해 뇌의 처리 한계를 설명한 뒤, 이를 실제 교통사고라는 현실적 상황에 적용하여 설명하는 흐름이 적절합니다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: All of the restaurants are using carefully chosen words to evoke vivid mental images of delicious food and rich desserts in order to draw the potential customer to their particular establishment. Just like the restaurants, nature has its own dining establishments. In a fashion similar to the restaurants' financial dependence upon drawing in many customers, the restaurateurs of the natural world (i.e., flowers) must also attract potential diners to sample their offerings. In the natural world, there are no neon signs or flashy words in which to market a potential meal to hungry animals. These restaurants that I am referring to are the world's flowers, and the potential guests are the host of organisms that visit flowers to obtain nectar and other valuable resources. Instead of using a written language or neon sign, they advertise their offerings just as effectively using the language of smell.
summary_sentence: Just as restaurants use (A)_____________________, flowers serve as nature's restaurants, (B)_____________________.
subjective_conditions: (A)는 attract, language, appealing, to, diners를 한 번씩 모두 사용하여 배열할 것
(B)는 with, signs, animals, lure, smell, instead of를 한 번씩 모두 사용하여 배열할 것
(A), (B) 모두 형태 변형 가능, 단어 추가 불가
answer: (A) appealing language to attract diners(B) luring animals with smell instead of signs
explanation: 이 글은 식당이 잠재적인 고객을 끌어들이기 위해 화려한 언어를 사용하는 것처럼, 자연의 꽃들 또한 냄새라는 언어를 사용하여 동물을 유인한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 식당이 사용하는 수단인 '식객을 유혹하기 위한 매력적인 언어'가 들어가야 하며, (B)는 꽃들이 하는 행동인 '표지판 대신 냄새로 동물들을 유혹하는 것'이 들어가야 합니다. 조건에 맞춰 분사 형태(luring) 등을 활용하여 완성합니다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: It is difficult, if not impossible, to define the limits which reason should impose on the desire for wealth; for there is no absolute or definite amount of wealth which will satisfy a man. The amount is always relative, that is to say, just so much as will maintain the proportion between what he wants and what he gets; for to measure a man's happiness only by what he gets, and not also by what he expects to get, is as pointless as to try and express a fraction which shall have a numerator but no denominator. A man never feels the loss of things which it never occurs to him to ask for; he is just as happy without them; whilst another, who may have a hundred times as much, feels miserable because he has not got the one thing he wants. In fact, every man has a horizon of his own, and he will expect as much as he thinks it is possible for him to get.
summary_sentence: The sense of one's happiness is (A)__________, as it depends on the ratio between his (B)__________ and his (C)__________ rather than on (D)___________________.
subjective_conditions: (A)~(C): 한 단어로 답하시오.

question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: Steve Jobs used analogy to get people to embrace the new technology. Before computers, people worked in a physical world. We used paper and pens and physical file folders and so on. The idea of working in a virtual world was radically different. Or at least seemed radically different. What Jobs understood was that a physical office was fundamentally similar to a virtual office. To win over the masses, Jobs drew strong analogies between the traditional workplace people knew well with the new, unfamiliar virtual workplace. In the pre-computer workplace, when ideas were written on paper it was called . . . a document. When those documents needed to be stored they were put in . . . a folder. And those folders were kept on . . . a desk. Documents, folders, and desktops are the terms we use in our virtual work because Steve Jobs understood that using familiar terms would make the new technology easier to understand. The parallels between the physical and virtual workplace now seem obvious.
summary_sentence: Steve Jobs bridged the gap between (A)______________________ by using analogies. By adopting everyday terms like document, folder, and desktop from the physical workplace, the new technology (B)______________________.
subjective_conditions: (A)는 unfamiliar, physical을 포함하여 9단어 이내로 쓸 것.
(B)는 make, for, easier, to를 포함하여 8단어 이내로 쓸 것. (형태 변형 가능)
(B)는 수동태를 포함할 것.
answer: (A) the familiar physical world and the unfamiliar virtual world(B) was made easier for users to understand

question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It's hard to pay more for the speedy but highly skilled person, simply because there's less effort being observed. Two researchers once did a study in which they asked people how much they would pay for data recovery. They found that people would pay a little more for a greater quantity of rescued data, but what they were most sensitive to was the number of hours the technician worked. When the data recovery took only a few minutes, willingness to pay was low, but when it took more than a week to recover the same amount of data, people were willing to pay much more. Think about it: They were willing to pay more for the slower service with the same outcome. Fundamentally, when we value effort over outcome, we're paying for incompetence. Although it is actually irrational, we feel more rational, and more comfortable, paying for incompetence.

question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control, Scientists manipulate a variable of interest, and see if there's a difference. At the same time, they attempt to control for the potential effects of all other variables. The importance of controlled experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often correlated. For example, people who take vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who don't take vitamins. As a result, if we want to study the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely observe the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to create a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world. That's just what scientific experiments do. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while holding everything else constant.
options: ① differences between a controlled world and an uncontrolled world
② importance of accepting various aspects of variables
③ understanding the natural concept under causal relations
④ preference for real-world experiments over controlled experiments
⑤ significance of controlled environments when it comes to scientific experiments

passage: In adolescence many of us had the experience of falling under the sway of a great book or writer. We became entranced by the novel ideas in the book, and because we were so open to influence, these early encounters with exciting ideas sank deeply into our minds and became part of our own thought processes, affecting us decades after we absorbed them. Such influences enriched our mental landscape, and in fact our intelligence depends on the ability to absorb the lessons and ideas of those who are older and wiser. Just as the body tightens with age, however, so does the mind. And just as our sense of weakness and vulnerability motivated the desire to learn, so does our creeping sense of superiority slowly close us off to new ideas and influences. Some may advocate that we all become more skeptical in the modern world, but in fact a far greater danger comes from the increasing closing of the mind that burdens us as individuals as we get older, and seems to be burdening our culture in general.*entrance: 매료시키다
