question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: The transition from an oral culture, ⓐ<u>in which</u> knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. Wood suffers from splitting and ⓑ<u>is</u> susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is limited. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, ⓒ<u>solving</u> these problems. But it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex - or, as we call it now, the book - ⓓ<u>that</u> the material reached its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a dominant form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, ⓔ<u>won out</u> as the guardian of the written word is a remarkable materials story.
explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장의 구조를 보면 'The invention of paper'가 주어이며, 'said to be ~ Chinese'는 삽입된 분사구입니다. 따라서 ⓒ는 문장의 본동사 자리가 되어야 하므로 현재분사인 solving을 과거동사인 solved로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.[오답 분석]① ⓐ: '전치사+관계대명사(in which)' 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어지고 있으므로 적절합니다.② ⓑ: 문장의 주어 Wood에 연결되는 두 번째 동사로, 단수 동사 is는 적절합니다.④ ⓓ: 'It was ~ that' 강조 구문에서 시간 부사절인 'until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex'를 강조하고 있으므로 적절합니다.⑤ ⓔ: 'That paper ~ wood'가 이끄는 명사절 내의 동사로, '이겼다'라는 의미의 과거형 won out은 적절합니다.

question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: We might forget an anecdote about a stranger because it makes few connections with our existing associations, but we won't forget a piece of gossip about our cousin. There's one complex network ⓐ<u>which</u> is larger and quicker to access than all others - the self. We've been thinking about ourselves in our whole lives. In fact, there were entire years during junior high ⓑ<u>where</u> we weren't capable of thinking about much else. So if a new piece of information has something to do with us, it will be more easily and thoroughly ⓒ<u>processed</u>. It hits even closer to home than our actual home - we can take a vacation away from our home, but not from ourselves. The most effective communicators find ways to make the abstract ⓓ<u>individual</u>. Consider the warning that law schools give to motivate first-year law students concerning the rigors of their program. Hearing that "the first-ear dropout rate is 33%" ⓔ<u>is</u> an abstract statistic. "Look to your left, look to your right. One of the three of you won't be joining us next fall" wakes up the self.
explanation: ⓑ가 수식하는 선행사는 'entire years'로 시간적 개념을 나타냅니다. 관계부사 뒤에 완전한 문장('we weren't capable of thinking about much else')이 오고 있으므로 장소를 나타내는 where보다는 시간을 나타내는 관계부사 when을 쓰는 것이 문법적으로 더 적절합니다.[오답 분석]① ⓐ: 주어가 빠진 불완전한 절을 이끄는 주격 관계대명사로, 선행사 'one complex network'를 적절히 수식합니다.③ ⓒ: 주어인 'a new piece of information'이 처리되는 대상이므로 수동태(be processed) 표현이 적절합니다.④ ⓓ: 'make + 목적어 + 목적격 보어' 구조에서 형용사인 individual이 보어로 쓰여 '추상적인 것을 개인적인 것으로 만들다'라는 의미를 형성하므로 적절합니다.⑤ ⓔ: 동명사구 'Hearing that ~ 33%'가 문장의 주어이므로 단수 동사 is가 오는 것은 적절합니다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: The big problem with money created by the government is that those who run the government always confront the ⓐ<u>urge</u> to create more money and spend it. Whether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, leading to inflation and the many economic and social problems that follow from inflation. For this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that is inherently ⓑ<u>restricted</u> in supply, as money. It is a way of depriving governments of the power to ⓒ<u>enlarge</u> the money supply to inflationary levels. Gold has long been considered ideal for this purpose, since the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased swiftly. When paper money is ⓓ<u>inconvertible</u> into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money is said to be "backed up" by gold. This expression is ⓔ<u>deceptive</u> only if we imagine that the value of the gold is somehow transferred to the paper money, when in fact the real point is that the gold simply limits the amount of paper money that can be issued.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 정부가 돈을 마음대로 발행하여 발생하는 인플레이션을 막기 위해 금본위제를 사용하는 이유를 설명하고 있습니다. 'the money is said to be "backed up" by gold(그 돈은 금에 의해 뒷받침된다고 말해진다)'라는 표현이 성립하려면 지폐를 언제든 금으로 바꿀 수 있어야 합니다. 따라서 '태환 불가능한(inconvertible)'이 아니라 '태환 가능한(convertible)'이 문맥상 적절합니다.[오답 분석]① ⓐ urge: 정부 운영자들이 돈을 더 찍어내고 싶어 하는 '충동'을 느낀다는 의미로 적절합니다.② ⓑ restricted: 금이나 은은 공급이 본질적으로 '제한되어' 있어 화폐로 선호된다는 의미로 적절합니다.③ ⓒ enlarge: 정부가 통화 공급을 인플레이션 수준으로 '확대하는' 권한을 박탈한다는 의미로 적절합니다.⑤ ⓔ deceptive: 금의 가치가 지폐로 전이된다고 생각하면 '기만적인(오해의 소지가 있는)' 표현일 수 있다는 의미로 적절합니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage:

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: When evaluating a policy, people tend to concentrate on how the policy will fix some particular problem while ignoring or downplaying other effects it may have. Economists often refer to this situation as The Law of Unintended Consequences. For instance, suppose that you impose a tariff on ①<u>imported</u> steel in order to protect the jobs of domestic steelworkers. If you impose a ②<u>high</u> enough tariff, their jobs will indeed be protected from competition by foreign steel companies. But an unintended consequence is that the jobs of some autoworkers will be ③<u>lost</u> to foreign competition. Why? The tariff that protects steelworkers ④<u>raises</u> the price of the steel that domestic automobile makers need to build their cars. As a result, domestic automobile manufacturers have to raise the prices of their cars, making them relatively less attractive than foreign cars. Raising prices tends to ⑤<u>increase</u> domestic car sales, so some domestic autoworkers lose their jobs.
explanation: 자동차 제작에 필요한 철강 가격이 오르면 국산 자동차의 가격도 인상되어 소비자들에게 매력이 떨어지게 됩니다. 국산차 가격 인상은 판매량의 감소(decrease/lower)를 초래하여 자동차 산업의 일자리가 줄어드는 '의도치 않은 결과'로 이어지므로, ⑤의 increase는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: People behave in highly predictable ways when they experience certain thoughts. When they agree, they nod their heads. So far, no surprise, but according to an area of research known as "proprioceptive psychology," the process also works in __________. Get people to behave in a certain way and you cause them to have certain thoughts. The idea was initially controversial, but fortunately it was supported by a compelling experiment. Participants in a study were asked to fixate on various products moving across a large computer screen and then indicate whether the items appealed to them. Some of the items moved vertically (causing the participants to nod their heads while watching), and others moved horizontally (resulting in a side-to-side head movement). Participants preferred vertically moving products without being aware that their "yes" and "no" head movements had played a key role in their decisions.
options: ① context
② reverse
③ balance
④ sequence
⑤ repetition
explanation: 생각이 행동으로 이어지는 것과 마찬가지로, 특정한 행동을 하게 함으로써 그에 따른 생각을 유도하는 현상을 다루고 있습니다. 즉, 인과관계가 '거꾸로(반대로)' 작용한다는 의미이므로 빈칸에는 ② reverse가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 맥락
② 반대
③ 균형
④ 순서
⑤ 반복

question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Species that are found in only one area are called endemic species and are especially vulnerable to extinction. They exist on islands and in other unique small areas, especially in tropical rain forests where most species are highly specialized. One example is the brilliantly colored golden toad once found only in a small area of lush rain forests in Costa Rica's mountainous region. Despite living in the country's well-protected Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve, by 1989, the golden toad had apparently become extinct. Much of the moisture that supported its rain forest habitat came in the form of moisture-laden clouds blowing in from the Caribbean Sea. But warmer air from global climate change caused these clouds to rise, depriving the forests of moisture, and the habitat for the golden toad and many other species dried up. The golden toad appears to be one of the first __________ of climate change caused largely by global warming.
options: ① victims
② pioneers
③ survivors
④ winners
⑤ participants
explanation: 기후 변화로 인해 서식지가 마르고 결국 멸종하게 된 금개구리(golden toad)는 지구 온난화로 인한 기후 변화의 첫 번째 '희생자(victims)'가 된 것이므로 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 희생자들
② 개척자들
③ 생존자들
④ 승리자들
⑤ 참여자들

question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Education must focus on the trunk of the tree of knowledge, revealing the ways in which the branches, twigs, and leaves all emerge from a common core. Tools for thinking stem from this core, providing a common language with which practitioners in different fields may share their experience of the process of innovation and discover links between their creative activities. When the same terms are employed across the curriculum, students begin to link different subjects and classes. If they practice abstracting in writing class, if they work on abstracting in painting or drawing class, and if, in all cases, they call it abstracting, they begin to understand how to think beyond disciplinary boundaries. They see how to transform their thoughts from one mode of conception and expression to another. Linking the disciplines comes naturally when the terms and tools are presented as part of a(n) ___________________________.
options: ① separated understanding
② individualized identity
③ specialized usage
④ specified category
⑤ universal imagination
explanation: 이 글은 교육이 지식의 나무의 줄기, 즉 공통의 핵심(common core)에 집중해야 함을 강조하고 있습니다. 서로 다른 학문 분야에서 동일한 용어(추상화 등)를 사용함으로써 학생들이 학문의 경계를 넘어 생각하는 법을 배울 수 있다고 설명합니다. 따라서 학문 간의 연결은 이러한 도구들이 '보편적 상상력(universal imagination)'의 일부로 제시될 때 자연스럽게 이루어진다는 결론이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 분리된 이해
개별화된 정체성
전문화된 사용
명시된 범주
보편적 상상력

question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Why do people in the Mediterranean live longer and have a lower incidence of disease? Some people say it's because of what they eat. Their diet is full of fresh fruits, fish, vegetables, whole grains, and nuts. Individuals in these cultures drink red wine and use great amounts of olive oil. Why is that food pattern healthy? One-reason is that. __________________ ________________. More and more research is surfacing that shows us the benefits of the thousands of colorful "phytochemicals" (phyto=plant) that exist in foods. These healthful, non-nutritive compounds in plants provide color and function to the plant and add to the health of the human body. Each color connects to a particular compound that serves a specific function in the body. For example, if you don't eat purple foods, you are probably missing out on anthocyanins, important brain protection compounds. Similarly, if you avoid green-colored foods, you may be lacking chlorophyll, a plant antioxidant that guards your cells from damage.
options: ① they are eating a palette of colors
② they try to eat a particular amount of food
③ they avoid consuming any plant-based antioxidants
④ they restrict their intake to only a single type of nutrient
⑤ they rely exclusively on supplements for health benefits
explanation: 지중해 식단이 건강한 이유로 본문은 '파이토케미컬(phytochemicals)'의 중요성을 언급하며, 이것이 식물에 색과 기능을 제공한다고 설명합니다. 각 색깔이 신체의 특정 기능과 연결되어 있다는 예시(보라색-안토시아닌, 초록색-엽록소)를 통해, 지중해 사람들이 건강한 이유가 '다양한 색깔의 식단(a palette of colors)을 섭취하기 때문'임을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: 그들은 다채로운 색깔의 식단을 먹고 있다
그들은 특정한 양의 음식을 먹으려 노력한다
그들은 식물 기반 항산화제 섭취를 피한다
그들은 섭취를 단 한 종류의 영양소로 제한한다
그들은 건강상의 이점을 위해 오로지 보충제에만 의존한다

question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A reason for a conclusion is very unlikely to consist in a single claim. No matter how we might state it in shorthand, it is, analytically, ________________________. But is our analysis of the situation clearly expressed in just one statement? Hardly. The conclusion is about universities and free education, while the reason introduces some new ideas: economic benefit and a well-educated population. The reason must be broken down into a chain of more precise premises. For example, the claim that 'university education should be free for all Australians' might be supported by the reason that 'the economy benefits from a well-educated Australian population'. While the link between these two ideas and the conclusion might seem obvious, the purpose of reasoning is to avoid assuming the 'obvious' by carefully working through the connections between the various ideas in the initial statement of our reason.
options: ① the conclusion drawn from only one statement
② a complex interaction of many ideas and implications
③ the fruit of unknown knowledge and unclear reasoning
④ a well-researched, unique argument based on a single idea
⑤ a misjudgment made up of many supporting details in different areas
explanation: 결론에 대한 근거가 단 하나의 주장으로 구성되기 어렵다는 것이 글의 핵심입니다. 아무리 짧게 말하더라도 분석적으로는 '많은 아이디어와 함축적 의미들의 복합적인 상호작용'이라는 설명이 뒤따르는 대학 무상 교육 예시와 일맥상통합니다. 글 후반부에서 근거는 더 정확한 전제들의 사슬로 분해되어야 한다고 강조하므로 복합적 상호작용이 정답입니다.
options_translation: 오직 하나의 문장에서 도출된 결론
많은 아이디어와 함축적 의미의 복합적인 상호작용
미지의 지식과 불분명한 추론의 결과물
단일 아이디어에 기반한 잘 연구된 독특한 주장
다양한 분야의 많은 세부 지원 내용으로 구성된 오판

question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Low oil prices are a good thing, because it means lower energy costs of production for the majority of industries, not least the automobile and the logistics industries. Firms directly benefit from the decrease in their costs of production and provision of services.
ordered_passages: (A) For a $15 trillion economy, that is a loss of $150 billion in potential wealth or economic growth. Conversely, there has never been much concern with oil price decreases following an excess in its supply.

(B) A look through the history of oil price fluctuations proves this notion, as this has been the subject of much economic research. Following an oil price jump of 10 per cent due to a contraction in supply, an economy (as typified by the US economy) typically sees its output (GDP) slowed by close to 1 percentage point.

(C) This has the effect of stimulating the aggregate supply and provides a stimulus for growth. Conversely, a sudden rise in oil prices due to a shrink in oil production is never good news, even though it definitely gives a big boost to the energy sector.
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 낮은 유가로 인한 생산 비용 절감과 기업의 혜택에 대해 언급하고 있습니다. (C)에서 이러한 효과가 총공급을 자극하여 성장의 촉진제가 됨을 설명하고, 반대로 유가 급등은 좋지 않은 소식임을 도입합니다. (B)에서 유가 급등이 경제 성장(GDP)을 둔화시킨다는 구체적인 연구 결과와 수치를 제시하며, (A)에서 그 구체적인 경제적 손실액($150 billion)을 언급하며 내용을 마무리하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: North America's native cuisine met the same unfortunate fate as its native people, save for a few relics like the Thanksgiving turkey.
ordered_passages: (A) Certainly, we still have regional specialties, but the Carolina barbecue will almost certainly have California tomatoes in its sauce, and the Louisiana gumbo is just as likely to contain Indonesian farmed shrimp.

(B) We have, instead, a string of fad diets convulsing our bookstores and bellies, one after another, at the scale of the national best seller. Nine out of ten nutritionists view this as evidence that we have entirely lost our marbles.

(C) If either of these shows up on a fast-food menu with lots of added fats or HFCS, we seem unable either to discern or resist the corruption. We have yet to come up with a strong set of generalized norms, passed down through families, for savoring and sensibly consuming what our land and climate give us.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 북미 토착 요리가 사라졌음을 언급합니다. (A)에서 지역 특색 요리들이 여전히 존재하지만 타 지역이나 외국 식재료가 혼합되어 본래의 색을 잃었음을 설명합니다. (C)에서는 이러한 음식이 패스트푸드로 변질될 때 저항하지 못하며, 전통적인 식문화 규범이 없음을 지적합니다. (B)에서 그 대신 유행하는 다이어트 식단에 의존하게 된 현실을 비판하며 마무리됩니다.

question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: New words and expressions emerge continually in response to new situations, ideas and feelings. The Oxford English Dictionary publishes supplements of new words and expressions that have entered the language.
ordered_passages: (A) Some people deplore this kind of thing and see it as a drift from correct English. But it was only in the eighteenth century that any attempt was made to formalize spelling and punctuation of English at all.
(B) In other words, so to speak, if Shakespeare were to materialize in London today he would understand, on average, only five out of every nine words in our vocabulary.

(C) The language we speak in the twenty-first century would be virtually unintelligible to Shakespeare, and so would his way of speaking to us. Alvin Toffler estimated that Shakespeare would probably only understand about 250,000 of the 450,000 words in general use in the English language now.
explanation: 새로운 어휘의 등장을 언급한 도입부에 이어, (A)에서 이러한 변화에 대한 부정적인 시각과 역사적 배경(18세기의 표준화 노력)을 제시합니다. (C)에서 언어 변화의 결과로 21세기의 영어가 셰익스피어에게는 이해 불가능할 것이라는 예측치를 제시하고, (B)에서 'In other words'를 사용하여 그 수치를 다시 한번 명확하게 요약하여 설명하는 구조입니다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Research psychologists often work with self-report data, made up of participants' verbal accounts of their behavior. This is the case whenever questionnaires, interviews, or personality inventories are used to measure variables. (A) Self-report methods can be quite useful. (B) They take advantage of the fact that people have a unique opportunity to observe themselves full-time. (C) One of the most problematic of these distortions is the social desirability bias, which is a tendency to give socially approved answers to questions about oneself. (D) Subjects who are influenced by this bias work overtime trying to create a favorable impression, especially when subjects were asked about sensitive issues. (E) For example, many survey respondents will report that they voted in an election or gave to a charity when in fact it is possible to determine that they did not.
insertion_sentence: However, self-reports can be plagued by several kinds of distortion.
explanation: 자기 보고(self-report) 데이터의 유용성을 설명한 글의 전반부 이후, 삽입 문장은 '그러나(However)'를 사용하여 자기 보고 방식이 여러 종류의 '왜곡(distortion)'에 시달릴 수 있음을 언급합니다. (C) 뒤에 나오는 문장에서 '이러한 왜곡들 중 가장 문제가 되는 것 중 하나(One of the most problematic of these distortions)'라고 언급하며 구체적인 예시인 '사회적 바람직성 편향'을 소개하고 있으므로, 삽입 문장은 (C) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: All of the restaurants are using carefully chosen words to evoke vivid mental images of delicious food and rich desserts in order to draw the potential customer to their particular establishment. (A) Just like the restaurants, nature has its own dining establishments. (B) In a fashion similar to the restaurants' financial dependence upon drawing in many customers, the restaurateurs of the natural world (i.e., flowers) must also attract potential diners to sample their offerings. (C) These restaurants that I am referring to are flowers, which reside in a world without such things. (D) Their potential guests are the host of organisms that visit flowers to obtain nectar and other valuable resources. (E) Instead of using a written language or neon sign to attract these guests, they advertise their offerings just as effectively using the language of smell.
insertion_sentence: In the natural world, there are no neon signs or flashy words in which to market a potential meal to hungry animals.
explanation: 이 글은 인간 사회의 식당과 자연계의 꽃을 비유하여 설명하고 있습니다. (A)와 (B)에서 식당과 꽃의 유사성을 언급한 후, 삽입 문장은 자연계에는 네온사인이나 화려한 문구가 없다는 사실을 제시합니다. (C) 위치 뒤에 오는 문장에서 꽃이 '그러한 것들(such things)이 없는 세상'에 살고 있다고 말하는데, 여기서 '그러한 것들'이 가리키는 대상이 바로 삽입 문장의 네온사인과 화려한 문구이므로 문장 삽입 위치로 (C)가 적절합니다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Over the past several decades, there have been some agreements to reduce the debt of poor nations, but other economic challenges (like trade barriers) remain. Nontariff trade measures, such as quotas, subsidies, and restrictions on exports, are increasingly prevalent and may be enacted for policy reasons having nothing to do with trade. However, they have a discriminatory effect on exports from countries that lack the resources to comply with requirements of nontariff measures imposed by rich nations. For example, the huge subsidies that rich nations give to their farmers make it very difficult for farmers in the rest of the world to compete with them. Another example would be domestic health or safety regulations, which, though not specifically targeting imports, could impose significant costs on foreign manufacturers seeking to conform to the importer's market. Industries in developing markets may have more difficulty absorbing these additional costs.
summary_sentence: There have been supportive efforts to help developing countries, but due to measures to (A)__________ domestic industries and public health, unexpected consequences have made it (B)__________ for poor countries to compete with rich nations.
options: ① protect ... difficult
② strengthen ... effortless
③ support ... manageable
④ suppress ... impossible
⑤ control ... advantageous
explanation: 가난한 나라들의 부채를 줄이려는 노력이 있었음에도 불구하고, 부유한 국가들이 자국 산업을 보호(protect)하기 위해 사용하는 보조금이나 보건 규정 같은 비관세 조치들이 개발도상국에게 과도한 비용을 지게 하여 경쟁을 어렵게(difficult) 만든다는 것이 글의 핵심입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 protect, (B)에는 difficult가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 보호하다 ... 어려운
② 강화하다 ... 노력이 필요 없는
③ 지원하다 ... 관리 가능한
④ 억제하다 ... 불가능한
⑤ 통제하다 ... 유리한

question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis. For example, migrants are assumed to overcrowd cities, clog up labor markets, and increase poverty. The other questionable assumption is that most migration is involuntary - people fleeing natural or man-made disasters. The reality, however, is more complex, and many migrants are simply seeking greater economic opportunity. Of course migration can and does create social and economic problems. But migration can also be a solution for many preexisting problems. For example, out-migration generally redistributes workers from places of labor surplus to areas where there is greater demand or more opportunity. Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to endure hardship in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin. Most research that examines long-term outcomes of migration, including remittances and intergenerational mobility, finds positive "long-term" effects on places of origin and destination.*clog: 막히게 하다 **remittance: 송금
summary_sentence: While migration can produce (A)___________, it can likewise solve current issues by (B)___________ workers to areas with demand.
options: ① challengesreassigning
② benefitsdismissing
③ difficultiesdiminishing
④ efficiencyredistributing
⑤ flexibilityreducing
explanation: 본문은 이주(migration)가 미디어에서 흔히 문제나 위기로 보도되지만, 실제로는 노동력 과잉 지역에서 수요가 있는 지역으로 노동자를 재배치함으로써 기존의 사회적, 경제적 문제들을 해결하는 역할을 하기도 한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 부정적인 측면인 'challenges(어려움)'가, (B)에는 노동자를 다시 배치한다는 의미인 'reassigning(재배치하기)'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 어려움 - 재배치함으로써
② 이점 - 해고함으로써
③ 어려움 - 감소시킴으로써
④ 효율성 - 재분배함으로써
⑤ 유연성 - 줄임으로써

question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: In the course of his research on business strategy and the environment, Michael Porter noticed a peculiar pattern: ________________________________________. He also discovered that the stricter regulations were prompting more innovation than the weaker ones. The Dutch flower industry provides an illustration. For many years, the companies producing Holland's world-renowned tulips and other cut flowers were also contaminating the country's water and soil with fertilizers and pesticides. In 1991, the Dutch government adopted a policy designed to cut pesticide use in half by 2000 - a goal they ultimately achieved. Facing increasingly strict regulation, greenhouse growers realized they had to develop new methods if they were going to maintain product quality with fewer pesticides. In response, they shifted to a cultivation method that circulates water in closed-loop systems and grows flowers in a rock wool substrate. The new system not only reduced the pollution released into the environment; it also increased profits by giving companies greater control over growing conditions.

question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.

question: 13. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 <조건>를 지켜 빈칸을 완성하시오.
passage: We might forget an anecdote about a stranger because it makes few connections with our existing associations, but we won't forget a piece of gossip about our cousin. question: 17. 윗글에 드러난 Linda의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: As the train pulled into a quiet countryside station, the gentle chatter of passengers filled the air. Linda was excited to finally visit her grandparents after two years. She watched people getting onto the train and hurriedly finding their seats. A moment later, an elderly woman struggled with a heavy bag, trying to sit down next to her. The bag seemed almost too big for her small body. Linda hesitated, unsure if the elderly woman would want her help. But soon, she chose to assist the woman. "Let me help you with your bag," she said. Before she could reach the bag, the elderly woman suddenly lost her balance and fell down. She lay on her back, and her face was pale. Linda froze for a moment, feeling the urgency of the situation. She quickly knelt down beside the fallen woman, as a few people rushed over. Linda carefully tapped the elderly woman's shoulder to check if she was alright. The woman groaned softly, trying to gather her strength. Linda moved closer, sliding a hand under the woman's back. As the woman's eyes slowly opened, she reassured her softly, "It's okay, just relax for a moment." Linda helped the woman sit up slowly, then guided her back to her seat. As the situation settled, people around went back to their seats. As the elderly woman finally calmed down, she looked at Linda with a smile. "I'm so sorry," she said. "I have low blood pressure, and the sudden movement of the train must have made me feel dizzy. Thank you so much for helping me." Linda nodded gently in response, then turned her gaze back to the peaceful countryside scene. She thought that <u>no matter how unsure she might feel, even the smallest act of help is much better for someone in need than doing nothing</u>.*groan: 끙 소리를 내다
options: ① hesitant → relieved
② angry → regretful
③ jealous → frightened
④ indifferent → confident
⑤ confused → disappointed
explanation: Linda는 처음에 할머니를 도와드려야 할지 주저하며 망설였지만(hesitant), 할머니를 도와드리고 할머니가 안정을 찾고 감사의 인사를 전하자 안도하며(relieved) 평화로운 풍경을 바라보았습니다. 따라서 정답은 ①번입니다.

② 화난 → 후회하는
③ 질투하는 → 겁에 질린

⑤ 혼란스러운 → 실망한

question: 19. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A reason for a conclusion is very unlikely to consist in a single claim. No matter how we might state it in short-handit is, analytically, a complex interaction of many ideas and implications. The reason must be broken down into a chain of more precise premises. For example, the claim that 'university education should be free for all Australians' might be supported by the reason that 'the economy benefits from a well-educated Australian population'. But is our analysis of the situation clearly expressed in just one statement? Hardly. The conclusion is about universities and free education, while the reason introduces some new ideas: economic benefit and a well-educated population. While the link between these two ideas and the conclusion might seem obvious, the purpose of reasoning is to avoid assuming the 'obvious' by carefully working through the connections between the various ideas in the initial statement of our reason.
options: ① 결론과 이유 사이의 명백해 보이는 연결도 논리적으로 검토되어야 한다.

question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis. Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to endure hardship in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin. Most research that examines long-term outcomes of migration, including remittances and intergenerational mobility, finds positive "long-term" effects on places of origin and destination.*clog: 막히게 하다 **remittance: 송금
options: ① migration is often driven by promises of immediate prosperity and guaranteed success in destination areas

② 이주자들은 대안이 없는 구조적 어려움으로 인해 강제로 이주하게 된다

question: 21. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]

question: 25. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 be "backed up" by gold가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?"
passage: The big problem with money created by the government is that those who run the government always face the temptation to create more money and spend it. Whether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, leading to inflation and the many economic and social problems that follow from inflation. For this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that is inherently limited in supply, as money. It is a way of depriving governments of the power to expand the money supply to inflationary levels. Gold has long been considered ideal for this purpose, since the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased rapidly. When paper money is convertible into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money is said to <u>be "backed up" by gold</u>. This expression is misleading only if we imagine that the value of the gold is somehow transferred to the paper money, when in fact the real point is that the gold simply limits the amount of paper money that can be issued.
options: ① control the price of gold
② represent the actual value of gold
③ be exchanged for goods instead of gold
④ reflect the government's financial policy
⑤ be limited in amount by the supply of gold
explanation: 지문은 정부가 화폐를 무분별하게 발행하여 발생하는 인플레이션을 막기 위해 금본위제와 같은 시스템을 선호한다고 설명합니다. 금은 공급량이 한정되어 있기 때문에, 지폐가 금으로 '뒷받침된다(be backed up by gold)'는 것은 발행할 수 있는 지폐의 양이 보유한 금의 공급량에 의해 제한된다는 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 금의 가격을 조절하다
② 금의 실제 가치를 나타내다
③ 금 대신 상품으로 교환되다
④ 정부의 금융 정책을 반영하다
⑤ 금의 공급량에 의해 그 양이 제한되다

question: 26. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Stewe Jobs used analogy to get people to embrace the new technology. Before computers, people worked in a physical world.
ordered_passages: (A) To win over the masses, Jobs drew strong analogies between the traditional workplace people knew well with the new, unfamiliar virtual workplace. In the pre-computer workplace, when ideas were written on paper it was called ... a document. When those documents needed to be stored they were put in ... a folder. And those folders were kept on ... a desk.

(B) Documents, folders, and desktops are the terms we use in our virtual work because Steve Jobs understood that using familiar terms would make the new technology easier to understand. The parallels between the physical and virtual workplace now seem obvious.

(C) We used paper and pens and physical file folders and so on. The idea of working in a virtual world was radically different. Or at least seemed radically different. What Jobs understood was that a physical office was fundamentally similar to a virtual office.
explanation: 주어진 문장에서 컴퓨터 이전의 물리적 세계에서의 업무 방식을 언급했으므로, 구체적인 물리적 도구(종이, 펜 등)를 나열하며 가상 세계와의 유사성을 인식한 Jobs의 통찰을 보여주는 (C)가 가장 먼저 옵니다. 그 후 Jobs가 대중을 설득하기 위해 구체적인 유추(document, folder, desk)를 사용했음을 설명하는 (A)가 이어지고, 마지막으로 이러한 용어들이 현재 우리 가상 업무의 표준이 되었음을 정리하는 (B)로 마무리되는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 5. 다음 빈칸에 들어가는 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Most people resist the idea of a true self-estimate, probably because they fear it might mean downgrading some of their beliefs about who they are and what they're capable of. question: 6. 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 8. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?

question: 9. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 (A)negative ones에 해당하지 않는 것은?

⑤ ⓔ

question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 The very notion의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: On our little world, light travels, for all practical purposes, instantaneously. If a lightbulb is glowing, then of course it's physically where we see it, shining away. We reach out our hand and touch it: It's there all right, and unpleasantly hot. If the filament fails, then the light goes out. We don't see it in the same place, glowing, illuminating the room years after the bulb breaks and it's removed from itssocket. <u>The very notion</u> seems nonsensical. But if we're far enough away, an entire sun can go out and we'll continue to see it shining brightly; we won't learn of its death, it may be, for ages to come - in fact, for how long it takes light, which travels fast but not infinitely fast, to cross the intervening vastness. The immense distances to the stars and the galaxies mean that we see everything in space in the past.
options: ① The fact that light travels very fast from its source
② The idea that light lasts although its source fails
③ The fact that the sun's light can remain invisible long after it dies
④ The point that it takes a long time for light to travel through space
⑤ The phenomenon that light produces heat when it touches objects
explanation: 필라멘트가 끊어지면 전구가 즉시 꺼지는 우리 주변의 상황과 달리, 우주에서는 광원(별)이 사라진 후에도 그 빛이 우리에게 도달하기까지 광대한 거리를 이동해야 하므로 아주 먼 미래까지 여전히 빛나고 있는 것처럼 보일 수 있습니다. 'The very notion'은 앞에서 언급한 '전구가 꺼지고 소켓에서 제거된 지 몇 년 후에 같은 장소에서 빛나며 방을 밝히는 것을 본다는 생각'을 가리키며, 이는 지구상의 상식으로는 터무니없는 일입니다. 따라서 정답은 광원이 사라졌음에도 빛은 지속된다는 아이디어를 나타내는 ②번입니다.

광원이 사라졌음에도 빛은 지속된다는 생각
태양빛이 죽은 뒤에도 오랫동안 보이지 않는 상태로 남아 있을 수 있다는 사실
빛이 우주를 통과하여 여행하는 데 오랜 시간이 걸린다는 점

question: 20. 다음 'Financial market'에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Financial markets do more than take capital from the rich and lend it to everyone else. They enable each of us to smooth consumption over our lifetimes, which is a fancy way of saying that we don't have to spend income at the same time we earn it. Shakespeare may have admonished us to be neither borrowers nor lenders; the fact is that most of us will be both at some point. If we lived in an agrarian society, we would have to eat our crops reasonably soon after the harvest or find some way to store them. Financial markets are a more sophisticated way of managing the harvest. We can spend income now that we have not yet earned - as by borrowing for college or a home - or we can earn income now and spend it later, as by saving for retirement. The important point is that earning income has been divorced from spending it, allowing us much more flexibility in life.
options: ① Financial markets do more than simply move capital from wealthy individuals to others.
② People can smooth their consumption over time thanks to financial markets.
③ Shakespeare believed that everyone should borrow money early in life and lend it later.
④ In an agrarian society, people had to consume or store their crops shortly after harvesting.
⑤ Financial markets allow people to use income they haven't yet earned or to save for future use.
explanation: 본문에서 셰익스피어는 빌리지도 빌려주지도 말라고 권고(Shakespeare may have admonished us to be neither borrowers nor lenders)했다고 언급되어 있을 뿐, 인생 초반에 빌리고 나중에 빌려줘야 한다고 믿었다는 내용은 나오지 않습니다. 오히려 현실에서는 우리 대부분이 두 가지 모두를 하게 된다는 사실을 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: 금융 시장은 부유한 개인들로부터 다른 사람들에게 자본을 단순히 옮기는 것 이상의 일을 한다.
금융 시장 덕분에 사람들은 시간에 걸쳐 소비를 고르게 할 수 있다.
셰익스피어는 모든 사람이 인생 초반에 돈을 빌리고 나중에 빌려주어야 한다고 믿었다.
농경 사회에서 사람들은 수확 직후에 작물을 소비하거나 저장해야 했다.
금융 시장은 사람들이 아직 벌지 못한 수입을 사용하거나 미래를 위해 저축할 수 있게 해준다.

question: 21. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Brains are expensive in terms of energy. Twenty percent of the calories we consume ⓐ<u>is used</u> to power the brain. So brains try to operate in the most ⓑ<u>efficient</u> way possible, and that means processing only the minimum amount of information from our senses that we need to navigate the world. Neuroscientists weren't the first to discover that those ⓒ<u>who</u> fix their gaze on something may still fail to see it. Magicians figured this out long ago. By directing your attention, they perform tricks with their hands in full view. Their actions should give away the game, but they can rest assured ⓓ<u>that</u> your brain processes only small bits of the visual scene, filtering, ignoring, and ⓔ<u>simplifying</u> the flood of information.
explanation: ⓐ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'Twenty percent of the calories we consume'입니다. '분수/퍼센트 + of + 명사' 구문이 주어로 쓰일 때 수 일치는 of 뒤의 명사에 시킵니다. 여기서 'the calories'가 복수이므로 동사도 복수형인 'are used'가 되어야 합니다.

question: 22. 윗글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Brains are expensive in terms of energy. Twenty percent of the calories we consume ⓐ<u>is used</u> to power the brain. So brains try to operate in the most ⓑ<u>efficient</u> way possible, and that means processing only the minimum amount of information from our senses that we need to navigate the world. Neuroscientists weren't the first to discover that those ⓒ<u>who</u> fix their gaze on something may still fail to see it. Magicians figured this out long ago. By directing your attention, they perform tricks with their hands in full view. Their actions should give away the game, but they can rest assured ⓓ<u>that</u> your brain processes only small bits of the visual scene, filtering, ignoring, and ⓔ<u>simplifying</u> the flood of information.
options: ① People always believe what they see with their own eyes.
② Brains use more energy when we focus hard on a complex task.
③ Traffic accidents happen mostly because drivers are not careful.
④ Magicians can trick people by moving their hands quickly and silently.
⑤ The brain saves energy by processing limited information, causing us to miss things in plain sight.
explanation: 뇌는 에너지를 많이 소모하기 때문에 가장 효율적인 방식으로 작동하려고 노력하며, 이는 생존에 필요한 최소한의 정보만을 처리한다는 것을 의미합니다. 마술사들은 이러한 뇌의 특성(시각적 정보의 여과, 무시, 단순화)을 이용하여 관객의 눈앞에서 속임수를 성공시킨다는 것이 글의 요지입니다.
options_translation: 사람들은 항상 자신의 눈으로 보는 것을 믿는다.
복잡한 업무에 집중할 때 뇌는 더 많은 에너지를 사용한다.
교통사고는 주로 운전자들이 주의 깊지 않기 때문에 발생한다.
마술사들은 손을 빠르고 조용하게 움직여서 사람들을 속일 수 있다.
뇌는 제한된 정보만 처리함으로써 에너지를 절약하며, 이로 인해 우리는 눈앞에 있는 것을 놓치게 된다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 적절한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (다음 조건을 충족할 것)
passage: Buying a television is current consumption. It makes us happy today but does nothing to make us richer tomorrow. Yes, money spent on a television keeps workers employed at the television factory. But if the same money were invested, it would increase job opportunities somewhere else, say for scientists in a laboratory or workers on a construction site, while also contributing to our long-term wealth. Think about college as an example. Sending students to college creates jobs for professors. Using the same money to buy fancy sports cars for high school graduates would create jobs for auto workers. The crucial difference between these scenarios is that a college education makes a young person more productive for the rest of his or her life; a sports car does not. Thus, college tuition is an investment; buying a sports car is consumption.
summary_sentence: Spending money on televisions is consumption that brings short-term happiness but no lasting benefits, while (A)___________ in college education ___________ lifelong ___________ and ___________; therefore, college tuition represents investment, unlike sports cars.
subjective_conditions: 답안 작성 시, 밑줄 친 (A)부분 전체를 옮겨 쓸 것.
필요시 어형 변화 가능.
빈칸에는 하나의 단어만 적을 것.
조건 미충족 시 부분 점수 없음.
answer: investing in college education increases lifelong productivity and wealth
explanation: 본문은 TV와 같은 소비재 구매와 대학교육과 같은 투자의 차이점을 설명하고 있습니다. 대학교육은 개인의 생산성을 높이고 장기적인 부에 기여하는 '투자'입니다. 따라서 요약문 (A) 부분에는 '대학 교육에 투자하는 것(investing)은 평생의 생산성(productivity)과 부(wealth)를 증가시킨다(increases)'는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 주어인 동명사구 investing in college education에 맞춰 동사는 단수형인 increases로 변형해야 합니다.

question: 26. 다음 글의 사례를 바탕으로 moral hazard를 설명할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 적절한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 그대로 쓰시오. (답안 작성 시, 밑줄 친 (A) 부분 전체를 옮겨 쓸 것)
passage: If a firm is going to be saved by the government, it might be easier to concentrate on lobbying the government for more money rather than taking the harder decision of restructuring the company to be able to be profitable and viable in the long term. This is an example of something known as moral hazard - when government support alters the decisions firms take. For example, if governments rescue banks who get into difficulty, as they did during the credit crisis of 2007-08, this could encourage banks to take greater risks in the future because they know there is a possibility that governments will intervene if they lose money. Although the government rescue may be well intended, it can negatively affect the behavior of banks, encouraging risky and poor decision making.
summary_sentence: The moral hazard described in the passage shows (A) how __________ take greater __________ because they expect __________ to __________ them if things go wrong.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 그대로 쓸 것
밑줄 친 (A) 부분 전체를 옮겨 쓸 것
answer: how firms(또는 banks) take greater risks because they expect governments to rescue them
explanation: 이 글은 정부의 구제 정책이 기업이나 은행의 의사 결정에 부정적인 영향을 미치는 '도덕적 해이(moral hazard)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 정부가 손실을 보전해 줄 것이라는 기대가 있으면 기업이나 은행은 구조조정이나 건전한 경영 활동보다는 더 큰 위험을 감수하는 경향이 있다는 점을 바탕으로 요약문을 완성할 수 있습니다. 본문에서 firms(혹은 banks), risks, governments, rescue 등의 핵심어를 찾아 빈칸을 채울 수 있습니다.

question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A reason for a conclusion is very unlikely to consist in a single claim. No matter how we might state it in short-hand, it is, analytically, a complex interaction of many ideas and implications. The reason must be broken down into a chain of more precise premises. For example, the claim that 'university education should be free for all Australians' might be supported by the reason that 'the economy benefits from a well-educated Australian population'. But is our analysis of the situation clearly expressed in just one statement? Hardly. The conclusion is about universities and free education, while the reason introduces some new ideas: economic benefit and a well-educated population. While the link between these two ideas and the conclusion might seem obvious, the purpose of reasoning is to avoid assuming the 'obvious' by carefully working through the connections between the various ideas in the initial statement of our reason.
options: ① Connecting ideas: The Structure Behind Logical Claims
② Why Higher Education is Crucial for National Growth
③ When Premises Are Too Complicated to Be Effective
④ A Reason: The More Obvious It Seems, the Better
⑤ Economic: Benefits From Free University Education
explanation: 이 글은 결론에 대한 근거가 단일한 주장이 아니라 여러 아이디어와 함촡의 볼잡한 상호작용이며, 이를 더 정밀한 전제들로 분해하여 그 연결 고리를 명확히 해야 한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 논리적 주장 이면에 있는 구조와 아이디어의 연결을 언급한 1번이 가장 적절합다.
options_translation: ① 아이디어 연결하기: 논리적 주장 이면의 구조
② 고등 교육이 국가 성장에 중요한 이유
③ 전제가 효과적이기에 놈 볼잡할 때
④ 근거: 더 명확해 밴일수록 더 좋다
⑤ 경제: 뭄료 대학 교육으로부터의 혜택

question: 2. 다음 글을 읽고 추론할 수 있는 비유적 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There is no absolute or definite amount of wealth which will satisfy a man. So, it is difficult, if not impossible, to define the limits which reason should impose on the desire for wealth. The amount is always relative, that is to say, just so much as will maintain the proportion between what he wants and what he gets; for to measure a man's happiness only by what he gets, and not also by what he expects to get, is as pointless as to try and express a fraction which shall have a numerator but no denominator. A man never feels the loss of things which it never occurs to him to ask for; he is just as happy without them; whilst another, who may have a hundred times as much, feels miserable because he has not got the one thing he wants. In fact, every man has a horizon of his own, and he will expect as much as he thinks it is possible for him to get.
options: ① "Money won't create success, the freedom to make it will." - Nelson Mandela
② "Happiness is not something ready made. It comes from your own actions." - Dalai Lama
③ "Don't compare your life to others. You have no idea what their journey is all about." - Regina Brett
④ "If what you have seems insufficient to you, then though you possess the world, you will yet be miserable." - Seneca
⑤ "Don't tell me where your priorities are. Show me where you spend your money and I'll tell you what they are." - James W. Frick
explanation: 이 글은 부에 대한 만접은 상대적이며, 자신이 갖고 싶어하는 값걠와 가지고 있는 값걠 사이의 비율에 의해 행복이 결정된다는 점을 강조합다. ④번은 가지고 있는 갓이 불충분하다고 느낀다면 세상 모든 갓을 가졌더라도 불행할 갓이라는 내용으로 밴문의 요지와 가장 일치합다.
options_translation: ① "돈은 성공을 만들지 묻한다, 그갓을 만들 자유가 그렇가 할 갓이다." - 넬싨 만데라
② "행복은 이미 만들어진 갓이 아니다. 그갓은 당신의 행동에서 온다." - 달라이 라마
③ "당신의 삶을 다른 사람과 비교하준 률라. 그들의 여정이 어떤지 당신은 전혀 모른다." - 레지나 브렛
④ "당신이 가진 갓이 불충분해 밴인다면, 세상을 소유했더라도 당신은 여전히 불행할 갓이다." - 세네카
⑤ "당신의 우선순을 말하준 률라. 당신이 돈을 어딴에 쓰는지 보여주면 그갓이 무엇인지 말해주겠다." - 제임스 W. 프릭

question: 3. 다음 중 밑줄 친 문장의 예시에 해당하지 않는 것은?
passage: Education must focus on the trunk of the tree of knowledge, revealing the ways in which the branches, twigs, and leaves all emerge from a common core. Tools for thinking stem from this core, providing a common language with which practitioners in different fields may share their experience of the process of innovation and discover links between their creative activities. When the same terms are employed across the curriculum, students begin to link different subjects and classes. If they practice abstracting in writing class, if they work on abstracting in painting or drawing class, and if, in all cases, they call it abstracting, they begin to understand how to think beyond disciplinary boundaries. They see how to transform their thoughts from one mode of conception and expression to another. <u>Linking the disciplines comes naturally when the terms and tools are presented as part of a universal imagination</u>.
options: ① Teachers encourage students to discern patterns in historical events and scientific processes, fostering analytical thinking that transcends disciplines.
② Across subjects, students are taught to identify underlying principles, whether they're analyzing texts or conducting experiments.
③ Math and science each use their own specific terms, and students are expected to memorize them without reference to the other.
④ By using the universal term "core idea" in both literature and social studies, students begin to connect different kinds of texts.
⑤ In math and economics, students transform real-life problems into models, reinforcing shared methods of problem-solving.
explanation: 밑줄 친 문장은 공통된 용어와 도구를 통해 학문 간의 연결이 자연스럽갌 이루어진다는 내용입니다. ③번은 수학과 과학이 각자의 고유한 용어를 사용하며 타 과목과의 참고 없이 암기한다는 내용이므로, 학문 간의 연결을 부정하는 예시입니다.
options_translation: ① 교사는 학생들이 역사적 사건과 과학적 과정에서 패턴을 파악하도록 독려하여, 학문을 초월하는 분석적 사고를 기리다.
② 여러 과목에 걸쳐, 학생들은 텍스트를 분석하든 실험을 하든 근밸적인 원리를 식별하도록 배운다.
③ 수학과 과학은 각자 고유한 용어를 사용하며, 학생들은 다른 과목에 대한 참고 없이 그갓들을 암기할 갓으로 기대된다.
④ 문학과 사회 모됐에서 "핵심 아이디어"라는 밴통 용어를 사용함으로써, 학생들은 서로 다른 종류의 텍스트를 연결하기 시작한다.
⑤ 수학과 경제학에서 학생들은 실제 삶의 문제를 모델로 변환하여 공유된 문제 해결 방법을 강화한다.

question: 4. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
passage: Turtle hatchlings have, it seems, evolved to crawl toward the light. For millions of years this was a highly rational and effective strategy because the light on a dark beach represented the reflection of the moon and stars on the water's surface. ⓐFollowing the lights led baby turtles back home to the sea which served as a reliable navigation strategy throughout evolutionary history. ⓑThe problems started when humans began building beachfront homes and sparkling hotels on the other side of the beach. ⓒHowever, contrary to our concerns, some beachfront developments near turtle hatching sites have boosted tourism and revitalized local economics. ⓓToday, newly hatched turtles often crawl toward the brightest lights, leading them into oncoming traffic, making their once-effective behavior appear self-destructive and even naturally irrational in the modern world. ⓔBut the deeper truth is that turtles are relying on simple cues that made perfect sense to their ancestors, but in today's world, their evolved decision-making mechanisms are being misled by modern lights.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 거북이 부화마가 진화적으로 빛을 따라 바다로 나아가는 전략을 가졌으나, 현대의 인공 조명 때문에 길을 잃고 죽음에 이르게 된다는 내용입니다. ③번 문장은 해변 개발이 관광과 지역 경제를 활성화했다는 내용으로, 거북이의 생존 전략과 인공 조명으로 인한 피해라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

question: 5. 다음 글의 내용을 옳게 이해하지 못한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: In the course of his research on business strategy and the environment, Michael Porter noticed a peculiar pattern: Businesses seemed to be profiting from regulation. He also discovered that the stricter regulations were prompting more innovation than the weaker ones. The Dutch flower industry provides an illustration. For many years, the companies producing Holland's world-renowned tulips and other cut flowers were also contaminating the country's water and soil with fertilizers and pesticides. In 1991, the Dutch government adopted a policy designed to cut pesticide use in half by 2000 - a goal they ultimately achieved. Facing increasingly strict regulation, greenhouse growers realized they had to develop new methods if they were going to maintain product quality with fewer pesticides. In response, they shifted to a cultivation method that circulates water in closed-loop systems and grows flowers in a rock wool substrate. The new system not only reduced the pollution released into the environment; it also increased profits by giving companies greater control over growing conditions.
options: ① Michael Porter identified a peculiar pattern while stsudying environment and corporate tactics.
② It was found that the more severe the restrictions became, the more they sparked innovation among businesses.
③ Dutch flower producers, once polluting the environment with fertilizers and pesticides, responded to new environmental rulees by reducing their production to avoid the need for innovation.
④ Confronted with tighter environmental controls, greenhouse growers developed methods to preserve product quality while using fewer agricultural chemicals.
⑤ The new system not only limited contamination but also allowed businesses to earn more by enhancing environmental control.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 네덜란드 꽃 재배자들은 혁신을 피하기 위해 생산량을 줄인 것이 아니라, 엄격한 규제에 대응하여 제품의 품질을 유지하면서 살충제를 적게 사용하는 새로운 재배 방식(폐쇄 루프 시스템, 암면 배지 재배)을 개발하여 혁신을 이루어냈습니다.
options_translation: ① 마이클 포터는 환경과 기업 전략을 연구하는 동안 독특한 패턴을 확인했다.
② 제한이 더 엄격해질수록 기업들 사이에서 더 많은 혁신을 촉발한다는 사실이 밝혀졌다.
③ 한때 비료와 살충제로 환경을 오염시켰던 네덜란드 꽃 생산자들은 혁신의 필요성을 피하기 위해 생산량을 줄임으로써 새로운 환경 규칙에 대응했다.
④ 더 엄격한 환경 통제에 직면하여, 온실 재배자들은 더 적은 농약을 사용하면서도 제품 품질을 보존하는 방법들을 개발했다.
⑤ 새로운 시스템은 오염을 제한했을 뿐만 아니라 기업들이 환경 통제를 강화함으로써 더 많은 수익을 올릴 수 있게 해주었다.

question: 6. 다음 밑줄 친 <u>It hits even closer to home than our actual home</u>이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: We might forget an anecdote about a stranger because it makes few connections with our existing associations, but we won't forget a piece of gossip about our cousin. There's one complex network that is larger and quicker to access than all others ─ the self. We've been thinking about ourselves in our whole lives. (In fact, there were entire years during junior high when we weren't capable of thinking about much else.) So if a new piece of information has something to do with us, it will be more easily and thoroughly processed. <u>It hits even closer to home than our actual home</u> ─ we can take a vacation away from our home, but not from ourselves. The most effective communicators find ways to make the abstract personal. Consider the warning that law schools give to motivate first-year law students concerning the rigors of their program.Hearing that "the first-year dropout rate is 33%" is an abstract statistic. "Look to your left, look to your right. One of the three of you won't be joining us next fall" wakes up the self.

② It becomes activated far more positively than expected.
③ It makes us feel indescribably comfortable and relaxed.
④ It relates to something spiritual rather than physical.
⑤ It motivates us through immediacy and impact.
explanation: 이 글은 정보가 '자기 자신'과 관련이 있을 때 더 쉽고 철저하게 처리된다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 밑줄 친 부분은 우리가 우리 자신으로부터는 결코 떠날 수 없기 때문에 어떤 정보가 우리 자신과 관련될 때 그 무엇보다 더 절실하게 다가온다는 의미입니다. 따라서 '우리가 아는 그 어떤 것보다 더 관련이 있다고 느껴진다'는 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 그것은 우리가 아는 그 어떤 것보다 훨씬 더 관련이 깊게 느껴진다.
② 그것은 예상보다 훨씬 더 긍정적으로 활성화된다.
③ 그것은 우리를 필설로 다할 수 없이 편안하고 느긋하게 만든다.
④ 그것은 물리적인 것보다는 영적인 것과 관련이 있다.
⑤ 그것은 즉각성과 충격을 통해 우리에게 동기를 부여한다.

question: 7. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Species that are found in only one area are called endemic species and are especially vulnerable to extinction. They exist on islands and in other unique small areas, especially in tropical rain forests where most species are highly specialized. One example is the brilliantly colored golden toad once found only in a small area of lush rain forests in Costa Rica's mountainous region. Despite living in the country's well-protected Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve, by 1989, the golden toad had apparently become extinct. Much of the moisture that supported its rain forest habitat came in the form of moisture-laden clouds blowing in from the Caribbean Sea. But warmer air from global climate change caused these clouds to rise, depriving the forests of moisture, and the habitat for the golden toad and many other species dried up. The golden toad appears to be one of the first victims of climate change caused largely by global warming.
options: ① necessity of species population control on an ecological reserve
② the inadequacy of preservation initiatives across tropical regions
③ attempts to reverse the trend of extinction among endemic species
④ the crucial role of tropical rain forests in global climate regulation
⑤ vulnerability of an endemic species to climate-driven habitat change

options_translation: ① 생태 보존 구역에서의 종 개체수 조절의 필요성
② 열대 지역 전반의 보존 계획의 불충분함
③ 고유종의 멸종 추세를 되돌리려는 시도들
④ 지구 기후 조절에서 열대 우림의 결정적인 역할
⑤ 기후로 인한 서식지 변화에 대한 고유종의 취약성

question: 8. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Research psychologists often work with self-report data, made up of participants' verbal accounts of their behavior. This is the case whenever questionnaires, interviews, or personality inventories are used to measure variables. Self-report methods can be quite useful. They take advantage of the fact that people have a unique opportunity to observe themselves full-time. However, self-reports can be plagued by several kinds of distortion. One of the most problematic of these distortions is the social desirability bias, which is a tendency to give socially approved answers to questions about oneself. Subjects who are influenced by this bias work overtime trying to create a favorable impression, especially when subjects are asked about sensitive issues. For example, many survey respondents will report that they voted in an election or gave to a charity when in fact it is possible to determine that they did not.

options_translation: ① 심리학에서 주관적 보고의 유용성
② 민감한 주제에 대해 신뢰성 문제를 제기하는 자기 보고
③ 심리학에서 사회적 바람직성 편향을 다루는 것에서 오는 불이익
④ 자기 관련 질문에 답할 때 인상을 관리하려는 경향
⑤ 설문 조사의 목적을 훼손하는 오도하는 질문의 문제

question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Before getting licensed to drive a cab in London, a person has to pass an incredibly difficult test with an intimidating name ─ "The Knowledge."

(C)에서는 이러한 고된 준비 과정의 결과(As a result)로 택시 기사들의 뇌 구조가 일반인과 달라졌음을 시사하고, 마지막으로 (A)에서 뇌의 해마(hippocampus) 부위가 평균보다 크다는 구체적인 신체적 변화를 제시하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적으로 가장 적절합니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
passage: In art, there are a number of ways to use perspective to obtain the illusion of depth, including using colors and graduated values of black and white, and accurately drawing the subject by applying the rules of the geometric system of perspective. ① In order to achieve perspective, you must make a number of observations. ② The forms or objects that you draw on a flat surface actually have depth and dimension in real life. ③ As you view them and place their shapes and forms on a drawing surface, try to represent that depth to make the objects appear realistic and three-dimensional. ④ Objects appear differently when viewed from various positions. ⑤ When observing a subject, you see depth and three dimensions. question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
passage: North America's native cuisine met the same unfortunate fate as its native people, save for a few relics like the Thanksgiving turkey. question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis. For example, migrants are assumed to overcrowd cities, clog up labor markets, and increase poverty. The other questionable assumption is that most migration is ⓐ<u>forced</u> ─ people fleeing natural or man-made disasters. The reality, however, is more complex, and many migrants are simply seeking greater economic opportunity. Of course migration can and does create social and economic ⓑ<u>challenges</u>. But migration can also be a solution for many preexisting problems. For example, out-migration generally ⓒ<u>reallocates</u> workers from places of labor surplus to areas where there is greater demand or more opportunity. Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more ⓓ<u>inclined</u> to endure hardship in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin. Most research that examines long-term outcomes of migration, including remittances and intergenerational mobility, finds ⓔ<u>unfavorable</u> "long-term" effects on places of origin and destination.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 이주(migration)가 흔히 위기나 문제로 묘사되지만, 실제로는 경제적 기회를 찾는 복합적인 과정이며 긍정적인 측면이 많다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 송금(remittances)과 세대 간 이동성(intergenerational mobility)을 포함한 이주의 장기적 결과를 조사한 연구들은 대체로 긍정적인 효과를 발견한다는 맥락이 되어야 하므로, '불리한, 비호의적인'이라는 뜻의 unfavorable은 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다. 이를 favorable(유리한, 호의적인)과 같은 단어로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The writer and zoologist Desmond Morris observed that our feet communicate exactly what we think and feel more honestly than any other part of our bodies. Why are the feet and legs such accurate ⓐ<u>indicators</u> of our sentiments? For millions of years, long before humans spoke, our legs and feet reacted to environmental threats (e.g., hot sand, ill-tempered lions) ⓑ<u>immediately</u>, without the need for conscious thought. Our limbic brains made sure that our feet and legs reacted as needed by either ceasing motion, running away, or kicking at a potential threat. This survival regimen, ⓒ<u>preserved</u> from our ancestral legacy, has served us well and continues to do so today. In fact, these age-old reactions are still ⓓ<u>hardwired</u> in us. Therefore, when we are presented with something dangerous or ⓔ<u>agreeable</u>, our feet and legs still react as they did in prehistoric times.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control. Scientists manipulate a variable of interest, and see ⓐ<u>whether</u> there's a difference. At the same time, they attempt to control for the potential effects of all other variables. The importance of controlled experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often correlated. For example, people who take vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who ⓑ<u>don't</u>. As a result, ⓒ<u>wanting</u> to study the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely observe the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to create a situation ⓓ<u>where</u> the real world does not allow. That's just what scientific experiments do. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable ⓔ<u>manipulated</u> at a time, while holding everything else constant.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 'the real world does not allow'는 allow의 목적어가 빠져 있는 불완전한 절입니다. 따라서 관계부사인 where가 올 수 없으며, 앞의 선행사 a situation을 수식하면서 목적어 역할을 겸하는 관계대명사 which나 that이 와야 합니다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When evaluating a policy, people tend to concentrate on how the policy will fix some particular problem while ignoring or downplaying other effects it may have. (A)____________, suppose that you impose a tariff on imported steel in order to protect the jobs of domestic steelworkers. If you impose a high enough tariff, their jobs will indeed be protected from competition by foreign steel companies. (B)____________, an unintended consequence is that the jobs of some autoworkers will be lost to foreign competition. Why? options: ① (A) For example - (B) On the other hand - (C) Accordingly
② (A) Meanwhile - (B) Hence - (C) Consequently
③ (A) For instance - (B) However - (C) Nonetheless
④ (A) Besides - (B) After all - (C) In contrast
⑤ (A) Still - (B) In contrast - (C) Instead
explanation: 이 글은 정책 평가 시 발생하는 '의도하지 않은 결과의 법칙(The Law of Unintended Consequences)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. (A) 앞 문장에서 언급한 일반적인 상황에 대한 구체적인 예시로 철강 관세 부과를 들고 있으므로 'For example'이 적절합니다. (B) 철강 근로자의 일자리는 보호되지만, 반대로 자동차 근로자의 일자리는 줄어든다는 상반된 결과를 설명하므로 'On the other hand'가 적절합니다. (C) 앞선 원인(관세로 인한 철강 가격 상승)으로 인해 결과적으로 자동차 제조사가 가격을 올려야 하므로 인과관계를 나타내는 'Accordingly'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 예를 들어 - (B) 반면에 - (C) 따라서
② (A) 한편 - (B) 그러므로 - (C) 결과적으로
③ (A) 예를 들어 - (B) 그러나 - (C) 그럼에도 불구하고
④ (A) 게다가 - (B) 결국 - (C) 대조적으로
⑤ (A) 여전히 - (B) 대조적으로 - (C) 대신에

question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Would you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month? Second question: Would you prefer $1,000 today cash on the table or $1,100 in a month? If you think like most people, you'll take the $1,000 right away. This is amazing. ② The temptation of immediacy
③ A comparison of the two cases
④ An offer promising high returns
⑤ The emergence of an alternative
explanation: 사람들은 보상이 먼 미래에 있을 때는 합리적인 선택(더 큰 금액)을 하지만, 당장 보상을 받을 수 있는 상황이 되면 즉각적인 보상을 선택하는 경향이 있다는 내용입니다. 이를 '쌍곡선 할인(hyperbolic discounting)'이라 부르며, 보상이 가까울수록 감정적 이율이 높아진다고 설명합니다. 따라서 일관성 없는 결정을 내리게 하는 원인은 '즉각성의 유혹'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 투자 확률
② 즉각성의 유혹

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. Wood suffers from splitting and is susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is limited. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex ─ or, as we call it now, the book ─ that the material reached its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a dominant form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, won out as the guardian of the written word is a remarkable materials story.
summary_sentence: The shift from oral to written tradition was greatly delayed by (A)___________ writing materials until the invention of paper and the codex (B)___________ the preservation and portability of written texts.
options: ① fragileenabled
② adequaterevolutionized
③ abundantbalanced
④ impracticaltransformed
⑤ insufficientcompromised
explanation: ① fragile (깨지기 쉬운), enabled (가능하게 하다): (A)는 문맥상 '비실용적인'이 더 적절합니다. ② adequate (적절한), revolutionized (혁명적으로 변화시키다): (A)에 적절한 단어가 아닙니다. ③ abundant (풍부한), balanced (균형을 잡은): (A), (B) 모두 부적절합니다. ④ impractical (비실용적인), transformed (변형시키다/바꾸다): 구전 문화에서 문자 문화로의 전환이 '비실용적인' 기록 매체(돌, 점토판 등)로 인해 지체되었다가, 종이와 코덱스의 발명이 보존성과 휴대성을 '변화시켰다'는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다. ⑤ insufficient (불충분한), compromised (타협하다/손상시키다): (B)가 부적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 깨지기 쉬운 - 가능하게 했다
② 적절한 - 혁명적으로 변화시켰다
③ 풍부한 - 균형을 맞췄다

question: 23. 다음 글의 ①~⑥ 중 어법상 어색한 곳이 포함된 문장 2개를 찾아 문장의 기호를 각각 쓰고, 어색한 표현을 올바른 표현으로 고치시오.
passage: ①Over the past several decades, there have been some agreements to reduce the debt of poor nations, but other economic challenges (like trade barriers) remain. ②Nontariff trade measures, such as quotas, subsidies, and restrictions on exports, are increasingly prevalent and may be enacted for policy reasons having nothing to do with trade. ③However, they have a discriminatory effect on exports from countries that lack the resources to comply with requirements of nontariff measures imposed by rich nations. ④For example, the huge subsidies that wealthy nations give to their farmers making it very difficult for farmers in the rest of the world to compete with them. ⑤Another example would be domestic health or safety regulations, which, though not specifically targeting imports, could impose significant costs on foreign manufacturers sought to conform to the importer's market. ⑥Industries in developing markets may have more difficulty absorbing these additional costs.
subjective_conditions: • 문장의 기호를 반드시 쓸 것
• 어색한 표현은 한 단어로 찾아 쓸 것
• 올바른 표현은 한 단어로 고쳐 쓸 것
answer:
(1) ④ : making → make
(2) ⑤ : sought → seeking
explanation:
(1) ④: 문장의 주어인 'the huge subsidies'(that절의 수식을 받음)에 연결되는 본동사가 없으므로, 분사 형태인 'making'을 본동사인 'make'로 고쳐야 합니다.
(2) ⑤: 'foreign manufacturers'를 수식하는 분사구로, '순응하려고 노력하는'이라는 능동의 의미를 나타내야 하므로 과거분사 'sought'를 현재분사 'seeking'으로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 24. 다음 <보기>의 단어들을 조건에 맞게 사용하여 요약문을 완성하시오.
passage: Low oil prices are a good thing, because it means lower energy costs of production for the majority of industries, not least the automobile and the logistics industries. Firms directly benefit from the decrease in their costs of production and provision of services. This has the effect of stimulating the aggregate supply and provides a stimulus for growth. Conversely, a sudden rise in oil prices due to a shrink in oil production is never good news, even though it definitely gives a big boost to the energy sector. A look through the history of oil price fluctuations confirms this notion, as this has been the subject of much economic research. Following an oil price jump of 10 per cent due to a contraction in supply, an economy (as typified by the US economy) typically sees its output (GDP) slowed by close to 1 percentage point. For a $15 trillion economy, that is a loss of $150 billion in potential wealth or economic growth. Conversely, there has never been much concern with oil price decreases following an excess in its supply.
subjective_conditions: <보기>에 제시된 모든 단어를 사용하되, 한 번씩만 사용할 것
필요시 어형을 변화시킬 것
<보기>에 제시된 단어 이외의 단어는 추가하지 말 것
vocabulary_box: high prices / with / slower growth / boost / economic activity / low prices / and / lead to
answer: with low prices boosting economic activity and high prices leading to slower growth (또는 with high prices leading to slower growth and low prices boosting economic activity)
explanation: 이 글은 유가의 변동이 경제에 미치는 영향을 설명하고 있습니다. 저유가는 생산 비용을 낮추어 경제 활동을 촉진(boost)하고 성장을 자극하는 반면, 고유가는 생산 비용을 높이고 GDP 성장을 둔화(slower growth)시킨다는 내용입니다. <보기>의 단어를 활용하여 '저유가가 경제 활동을 촉진하고 고유가가 성장의 둔화로 이어지면서'라는 의미의 부대 상황 구문(with + 목적어 + 분사)을 완성해야 합니다. boost를 boosting으로, lead를 leading으로 변형하여 작성합니다.

question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고, 아래 learning log의 (A)와 (B)에 알맞은 표현을 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: In adolescence many of us had the experience of falling under the sway of a great book or writer. We became entranced by the novel ideas in the book, and because we were so open to influence, these early encounters with exciting ideas sank deeply into our minds and became part of our own thought processes, affecting us decades after we absorbed them. Such influences enriched our mental landscape, and in fact our intelligence depends on the ability to absorb the lessons and ideas of those who are older and wiser. Just as the body tightens with age, however, so does the mind. And just as our sense of weakness and vulnerability motivated the desire to learn, so does our creeping sense of superiority slowly close us off to new ideas and influences. Some may advocate that we all become more skeptical in the modern world, but in fact a far greater danger comes from the increasing closing of the mind that burdens us as individuals as we get older, and seems to be burdening our culture in general.
subjective_conditions: 문맥상 (A)에 알맞은 표현을 쓰시오.
문맥상 (B)에 알맞은 표현을 'know'를 사용하여 5단어 이하로 쓰시오.
subjective_answer_format: Learning LogTopic: the development of the human mind over timeReflect & Learn: The passage emphasizes how our openness to new ideas in youth often tends (A)__________ as we grow older. One line that stuck with me was the suggestion that vulnerability is the source of flexibility. At first, this seemed counter-intuitive, but I realized how true it is when we admit that (B)_________________, we're more willing to learn. However, when we grow confident in our knowledge or experience, we become less open to new ideas, perspective, and change.(A): _____________________________________________________(B): _____________________________________________________
answer: (A) to diminish (또는 to decline / to lessen / to decrease / to close) (B) we don't know everything (또는 we don't know enough / we don't know much / we know little)
explanation: (A) 본문은 나이가 들수록 마음이 닫히고 새로운 아이디어에 덜 개방적이게 된다는 점을 강조합니다. 따라서 젊은 시절의 개방성이 나이가 들면서 '줄어들거나 사라지는' 경향이 있다는 의미의 동사(diminish, decline 등)가 적절합니다.(B) 문맥상 취약함(vulnerability)이 배움의 동기가 된다는 것은, 우리가 모든 것을 알지 못한다는 사실을 인정할 때 더 기꺼이 배우려 한다는 의미입니다. 조건에 따라 'know'를 포함하여 5단어 이하로 구성하면 "we don't know everything" 등이 적절합니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The big problem with money created by the government is that those who run the government always face the temptation to create more money and spend it. Whether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, leading to inflation and the many economic and social problems that follow from inflation. For this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that is inherently limited in supply, as money, which is a way of depriving governments of the power to expand the money supply to inflationary levels. Gold has long been considered ideal for this purpose, since the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased rapidly. When paper money is convertible into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money is said to be "backed up" by gold. This expression is misleading only if we imagine that the value of the gold is somehow transferred to the paper money, when in fact the real point is that the gold simply limits the amount of paper money that can be issued.
options: ① The Economic Value of Gold Changes Over Time
② What Tempts Those in Power to Create More Money?
③ What Do Different Countries Prefer? Paper Money vs. Gold
④ Gold: A Check on the Excessive Issue of Paper Money
⑤ Arguments For and Against the Use of Gold as Money
explanation: 이 글은 정부가 화폐를 과도하게 발행하려는 유혹에 빠져 인플레이션을 유발하는 문제를 막기 위해, 공급이 제한적인 '금'을 화폐의 기준으로 사용하는 경제적 장치에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 즉, 금본위제와 같이 금이 지폐의 과도한 발행을 억제하는 체크 포인트(제한 장치) 역할을 한다는 내용이 핵심입니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis. For example, migrants are assumed to overcrowd cities, clog up labor markets, and increase poverty. The other questionable assumption is that most migration is involuntary - people fleeing natural or man-made disasters. The reality, however, is more complex, and many migrants are simply seeking greater economic opportunity. Of course migration can and does create social and economic problems. But migration can also be a solution for many preexisting problems. For example, out-migration generally redistributes workers from places of labor surplus to areas where there is greater demand or more opportunity. Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to endure hardship in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin. Most research that examines long-term outcomes of migration, including remittances and intergenerational mobility, finds positive "long-term" effects on places of origin and destination.*clog: 막히게 하다 **remittance: 송금
summary_sentence: Though often (A)__________(e)d as undesirable, migration is a complex process that can produce long-term (B)__________ for the societies and economies of both origin and destination regions.
options: ① favor - asset
② portray - value
③ conceal - benefit
④ regard - problems

explanation: 이 글은 이주(migration)가 흔히 위기나 문제로 보도되지만, 실제로는 노동력 재분배와 송금, 세대 간 이동성 등 긍정적인 장기적 효과를 가져온다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '묘사되다(portrayed)', (B)에는 '가치/이점(value)'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Would you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month? Most people will opt for the larger sum in thirteen months - where else will you find a monthly interest rate of 10 percent. A wise choice, since the interest will compensate you generously for any risks you face by waiting the extra few weeks. Second question: Would you prefer $1,000 today cash on the table or $1,100 in a month? If you think like most people, you'll take the $1,000 right away. This is amazing. In both cases, if you hold out for just a month longer, you get $100 more. In the first case, it's simple enough. You figure: "I've already waited twelve months; what's one more?" Not in the second case. The introduction of "now" causes us to make inconsistent decisions.
summary_sentence: The temporal proximity of a reward (A)__________ our emotional response, (B)__________ the likelihood that we will trade long-term advantages for immediate gratification.
options: ① (A) amplifies - (B) augmenting
② (A) descends - (B) increasing
③ (A) ascends - (B) diminishing
④ (A) descends - (B) converging
⑤ (A) amplifies - (B) eliminating
explanation: 본문은 보상을 받는 시점이 '현재(now)'와 가까울 때 사람들이 비논리적인 선택을 한다는 점을 지적합니다. 1년 뒤와 1년 1개월 뒤의 차이는 기꺼이 기다리지만, 당장 오늘과 한 달 뒤의 차이에서는 당장의 이익을 선택합니다. 즉, 보상의 시간적 근접성이 우리의 감정적 반응을 '증폭(amplify)'시키며, 이로 인해 장기적 이득보다 즉각적인 만족을 선택할 가능성을 '증가(augmenting)'시킵니다.
options_translation: ① 증폭시킨다 - 증가시키면서
② 하강시킨다 - 증가시키면서
③ 상승시킨다 - 감소시키면서
④ 하강시킨다 - 수렴하면서

question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Shoppers ⓐ<u>facing</u> the choice of thirty different varieties of gourmet chocolates are more likely to walk away without buying any, compared with when they are presented with only half a dozen choices. If employees are given a free trip to Paris, they are happy. If you give them a free trip to Hawaii, they are happy. But if you offer them the choice between the two destinations, they are less happy, ⓑ<u>whatever</u> they choose. Why might choice be so disruptive? The reason is that choice forces us to make comparisons and ⓒ<u>acknowledge</u> relative disadvantages. People who choose Paris complain that it doesn't have the ocean and those who choose Hawaii regret that it doesn't have the museums. Psychologist Barry Schwartz calls this the 'tyranny of choice' because rather than providing freedom, it actually constrains our decision-making. He argues that wider choice increases unhappiness because we worry that we are going to make the wrong decision and so we get ⓓ<u>stressed</u> about trying to process all the comparisons in an effort to get it right. This both increases our fear of making the wrong choice and raises expectations that we should be able to get the best choice. ⓔ<u>Having made</u> the choice, we then start to regret, wondering whether it was the right one.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 acknowledge는 force의 목적격 보어인 to make와 병렬 구조를 이루거나, 혹은 that절 내에서 choice forces us to (1) make ... and (2) acknowledge ... 의 구조를 가져야 합니다. 원문상 '선택이 우리로 하여금 비교하게 하고 상대적 단점을 인정하게 강요한다'는 의미이므로 to가 생략된 원형 부정사 acknowledge는 어법상 적절합니다. 다만, 원문이나 문제 의도상 병렬 구조의 확인을 묻는 것이나, 문맥상 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 가장 명확한 오류를 찾는다면 본래 지문의 원형인 'acknowledge'는 정답이 아닐 확률이 높으나 제시된 정답 3번에 따르면 acknowledge를 다른 형태(예: acknowledging 등)로 오인하게 유도했을 수 있습니다. 하지만 엄밀히 따지면 ⓒ는 force A to B and C 구조로 적절합니다. 만약 3번이 정답이라면 문맥상 동사 acknowledge가 주어 choice에 연결되는 본동사로 쓰여야 하는 상황인지 확인이 필요하나 여기서는 목적격 보어 병렬이 맞습니다. (제공된 정답 3번에 따라 분석함)

question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The train pulled into a quiet countryside station. Linda watched people getting onto the train and hurriedly finding their seats. A moment later, an elderly woman struggled with a heavy bag, trying to sit down next to her. The bag seemed almost too big for her small body. Linda hesitated, unsure if the elderly woman would want her help. But soon, she chose to assist the woman. "Let me help you with your bag," she said. Before she could reach the bag, the elderly woman suddenly lost her balance and fell down. She lay on her back, and her face was pale. Linda froze for a moment, feeling the urgency of the situation. But, she quickly knelt down beside the fallen woman and carefully tapped the elderly woman's shoulder to check if she was alright. The woman groaned softly, trying to gather her strength. As the woman's eyes slowly opened, she reassured her softly, "It's okay, just relax for a moment." Linda helped the woman sit up slowly, then guided her back to her seat. As the elderly woman finally calmed down, she looked at Linda with a smile. "I'm so sorry," she said. "I have low blood pressure, and the sudden movement of the train must have made me feel dizzy. Thank you so much for helping me." Linda nodded gently in response and then thought. "_______________________________."

question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Low oil prices are a good thing, because it means lower energy costs of production for the majority of industries, not least the automobile and the logistics industries.
