question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 문장을 찾아 어법에 맞게 모두 고쳐서 바르게 쓰시오. 반드시 문장 전체를 쓰시오.
passage: ⓐ<u>Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world</u>. Simply put, the brain is not designed to sense on its own. ⓑ<u>For instance, when the brain is exposed, it is incapable of registering external stimuli such as light or touch due to the absence of sensory receptors</u>. ⓒ<u>In fact, it is not uncommon for patients to be kept awake during brain surgery, as this enables surgeons to isolate specific regions of the brain</u>. The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle recognized this characteristic of the brain over 2,000 years ago when he said, "Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses." ⓓ<u>This concept can be seen clearly when volunteers are blind-folded and placed in the warm water of a sensory deprivation tank</u>. They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as incoherent thought patterns. ⓔ<u>That we can learn from these studies is that our senses needs to keep providing the brain with information in order for us to think and feel</u>.
answer: What we can learn from these studies is that our senses need to keep providing the brain with information in order for us to think and feel.
explanation: ⓔ번 문장에서 두 가지 어법상 오류가 있습니다. 첫째, 주어 역할을 하는 명사절에서 선행사가 없고 'learn'의 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 문장이 오므로 접속사 'That'을 관계대명사 'What'으로 고쳐야 합니다. 둘째, 'that'절 내부의 주어 'our senses'가 복수이므로 동사 'needs'를 수 일치에 맞게 'need'로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
passage: Steve Jobs used analogy to get people to embrace the new technology. Before computers, people worked in a physical world. We used paper and pens and physical file folders and so on. The idea of working in a virtual world was radically different. Or at least seemed radically different. What Jobs understood was that a physical office was fundamentally similar to a virtual office. To win over the masses, Jobs drew strong analogies between the traditional workplace people knew well with the new, unfamiliar virtual workplace. In the pre-computer workplace, when ideas were written on paper it was called ... a document. When those documents needed to be stored they were put in ... a folder. And those folders were kept on ... a desk. Documents, folders, and desktops are the terms we use in our virtual work because Steve Jobs understood that using familiar terms would make the new technology easier to understand. The parallels between the physical and virtual workplace now seem obvious.
options: ① Steve Jobs는 사람들에게 기존 기술을 이해시키기 위해 유사성을 이용했다.
② Steve Jobs는 물리적 사무실과 가상 사무실이 전혀 다르다고 생각했다.
③ Steve Jobs는 대중을 사로잡기 위해 기존 사무공간과 가상 사무공간의 차이점을 강하게 부각했다.
④ 컴퓨터 시대 이전의 사람들은 문서를 폴더에 넣어 저장했다.
⑤ Steve Jobs는 낯선 용어가 새로운 기술을 이해하기 쉽도록 한다고 생각했다.
explanation: 본문에서 Steve Jobs는 가상 세계가 물리적 세계와 근본적으로 유사하다는 점을 이해하고, 이를 대중에게 전달하기 위해 익숙한 용어(document, folder, desktop 등)를 비유적으로 사용했습니다. 4번 선지는 '컴퓨터 시대 이전(pre-computer workplace)에 문서(documents)를 폴더(folder)에 넣어 저장했다'는 본문의 설명과 직접적으로 일치합니다. 1번은 기존 기술이 아닌 '새로운 기술'을 이해시키기 위함이었고, 2번은 다르다고 생각한 것이 아니라 '유사하다'고 보았으며, 3번은 차이점이 아닌 '유사성'을 부각했습니다. 5번은 낯선 용어가 아니라 '익숙한 용어'가 이해를 돕는다고 보았습니다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 Electric system에 대한 내용을 표로 정리한 것 중 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은 있는 대로 고른 것은?
passage: In 1900, at the close of the first decade in which electric systems had become a practical alternative for manufacturers, less than 5 percent of the power used in factories came from electricity. But the technological advances of suppliers made electric systems and electric motors ever more affordable and reliable, and the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology. Further accelerating the shift was the rapid expansion in the number of skilled electrical engineers, who provided the expertise needed to install and run the new systems. In short order, electric power had gone from exotic to commonplace. But one thing didn't change. Factories continued to build their own powersupply systems on their own premises. Few manufacturers considered buying electricity from the small central stations. Designed to supply lighting to local homes and shops, the central stations didn't have the size or the skill to serve the needs of big factories. And the factory owners, having always supplied their own power, were loath to assign such a critical function to an outsider. They knew that a glitch in power supply would bring their operations to a halt─and that a lot of glitches might well mean bankruptcy. As the new century began, a survey found that there were already 50,000 private electric plants in operation, far surpassing the 3,600 central stations.

question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)를 포함하는 문장이 주제문이 되도록 <제시어>를 사용하여 <조건>에 따라 완성하시오.
passage: Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world. Simply put, the brain (A)_______________________; it (B)_______________________. For instance, an exposed brain would neither sense light shining on it nor feel something touching it. In fact, patients are often kept awake during brain surgery, which can help a surgeon isolate specific regions of the brain. The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle recognized this characteristic of the brain over 2,000 years ago when he said, "Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses." This concept can be seen clearly when volunteers are blind-folded and placed in the warm water of a sensory deprivation tank. They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as incoherent thought patterns. From these experiments and others, it is apparent that we need constant input from our senses to carry out functions that give us personality and intellect.*hallucinations: 환각

2. 필요시 서술어만 어형 변화
vocabulary_box: the outside world / nothing / the sensory organs / on / to / depend / perceive / interpret / its own / entirely
answer: (A) interprets nothing on its own(B) depends on the sensory organs entirely to perceive the outside world
explanation: 이 글은 뇌가 감각 기관 없이는 외부 세계를 인지할 수 없다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A)에는 뇌가 스스로는 아무것도 해석하지 못한다는 의미인 'interprets nothing on its own'이 들어가야 하며, (B)에는 외부 세계를 인지하기 위해 전적으로 감각 기관에 의존한다는 의미인 'depends on the sensory organs entirely to perceive the outside world'가 적절합니다.

question: 26. Write the two main characters in the story.
passage: Ms. Blake walked along the edge of the soccer field, ␐∑watching Eva to pack up her things after practice−. She paused for a moment, then called out, "Hey, Eva! How about staying a little longer? We can work on some drills─just the two of us." Eva hesitated. "I don't know, Coach. I'm pretty tired." Ms. Blake gave her a warm smile. "Just ten minutes. It'll be fun. I promise." Finally, Eva agreed, though she still seemed reluctant. They practiced passing the ball together. ␑Ms. Blake noticed that Eva's movements were slow and that her focus seemed elsewhere. Breaking the silence, Ms. Blake asked, "Do you remember the final game last year?" "Yeah, I remember." ␒Eva recalled the game which she scored three goals. "I was quite good back then." "You still are," replied Ms. Blake. "Well, now I'm so worried I can't score a goal or even pass the ball properly. I'm afraid of making mistakes," said Eva. Ms. Blake stepped closer and placed a reassuring hand on Eva's shoulder. She suggested, "You don't have to be perfect. Soccer isn't about perfection─it's about passion. And you've always had plenty of that." Eva's gaze met Ms. Blake's. "Do you really think so?" Ms. Blake said firmly, "Yes. The way you play, the energy you bring─␓that's what make you specially. Not the goals scored or the trophies won. It's the love you have for the game." Eva nodded thoughtfully. The next game, Ms. Blake watched from the sidelines as Eva played. There was a new confidence that hadn't been there before. Eva didn't score but led the team successfully. After the game she ran over, saying, "Thanks for believing in me, Coach." Ms. Blake smiled back. "You've always had it in you. I'm just here to remind you of that." Eva's face softened, ␔as she realized she had been too hard on herself. She said to herself, "What matters is doing my best, not being perfect."
explanation: 이야기에 등장하는 두 주요 인물은 Ms. Blake(코치)와 Eva(선수)입니다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis. For example, migrants are assumed to overcrowd cities, clog up labor markets, and increase poverty. The other questionable assumption is that most migration is involuntary ─ people fleeing natural or man-made disasters. The reality, however, is more complex, and many migrants are simply seeking greater economic opportunity. Of course migration can and does create social and economic problems. But migration can also be a solution for many preexisting problems. For example, out-migration generally redistributes workers from places of labor surplus to areas where there is greater demand or more opportunity. Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to endure hardship in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin. Most research that examines long-term outcomes of migration, including remittances and intergenerational mobility, finds positive "long-term" effects on places of origin and destination.
options: ① Crowded Out: How Overpopulation Drives People to Move
② Young, Bold, and Skillful: The True Face of Today's Migrants
③ Forced to Flee: Why Every Migrant Is a Victim of Tragedy and Desperation
④ Migration Policies in a Changing World: Balancing Security, Economy, and Human Rights
⑤ The Upside of Migration: Balancing Labor Markets and Creating Economic Opportunities

question: 15. Why are the feet and legs considered accurate indicators of our feelings and thoughts according to the passage?
passage: The writer and zoologist Desmond Morris observed that our feet communicate exactly what we think and feel more honestly than any other part of our bodies. Why are the feet and legs such accurate reflectors of our sentiments? For millions of years, long before humans spoke, our legs and feet reacted to environmental threats (e.g., hot sand, illtempered lions) instantaneously, without the need for conscious thought. Our limbic brains made sure that our feet and legs reacted as needed by either ceasing motion, running away, or kicking at a potential threat. This survival regimen, retained from our ancestral heritage, has served us well and continues to do so today. In fact, these age-old reactions are still so hardwired in us that when we are presented with something dangerous or even disagreeable, our feet and legs still react as they did in prehistoric times.*limbic: (대뇌) 변연계의 **regimen: 양생법
options: ① Because they usually move based on conscious choice in tense moments.
② Because they are shaped early in life to reflect emotional reactions.
③ Because they still show automatic survival responses formed over evolution.
④ Because they tend to be more noticeable than other body parts in motion.
⑤ Because they are believed to have more sensory nerves than hands or faces.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 발과 다리는 인류가 언어를 사용하기 훨씬 전부터 환경적 위협에 대해 의식적인 사고 없이 즉각적으로 반응해 왔으며, 이러한 생존 방식이 진화 과정에서 뇌에 깊이 각인(hardwired)되어 현재까지 남아 있기 때문에 우리의 감정과 생각을 정직하게 반영한다고 설명하고 있습니다.

question: 16. 다음 밑줄 친 (A)가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The big problem with money created by the government is that those who run the government always face the temptation to create more money and spend it. Whether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, leading to inflation and the many economic and social problems that follow from inflation. For this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that is inherently limited in supply, as money. It is a way of depriving governments of the power to expand the money supply to inflationary levels. Gold has long been considered ideal for this purpose, since the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased rapidly. When paper money is convertible into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money is said to be (A)<u>"backed up" by gold</u>. This expression is misleading only if we imagine that the value of the gold is somehow transferred to the paper money, when in fact the real point is that the gold simply limits the amount of paper money that can be issued.
options: ① 정부가 원하는 만큼 지폐를 발행할 수 있게 하는 것
② 금 자체가 지폐보다 더 큰 가치를 지니는 것
③ 금의 양에 의해 지폐의 총량이 조절되는 것
④ 금의 가치가 지폐에 직접 옮겨가는 것
⑤ 지폐가 금과 동일한 가치를 갖는 것
explanation: 지문 마지막 문장에서 금에 의해 '뒷받침된다(backed up)'는 표현의 핵심은 금이 발행될 수 있는 지폐의 양을 단순히 제한한다는 점(the real point is that the gold simply limits the amount of paper money that can be issued)이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 금의 보유량에 따라 통화량이 조절된다는 ③번이 정답입니다.

question: 6. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

(D) Using this technique, it was shown that a clear preference for movement of the right arm exists as early as 10 weeks after fertilization. (E) In this study, ultrasound images of 72 unborn children 10 weeks after fertilization were evaluated and 85% showed more movements of the right arm than the left. This number is already very close to the approximately 89.4% right-handers among adults.

question: 7. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In art, there are a number of ways to use perspective to obtain the illusion of depth, including using colors and graduated values of black and white, and accurately drawing the subject by applying the rules of the geometric system of perspective.
ordered_passages: (A) Because of this, it's important to establish the viewpoint, and stick with it. When observing a subject, you see depth and three dimensions. When you draw this subject onto a flat surface as it appears to the eye, you are drawing in perspective.

question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸(A)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 한 단어를 글 속에서 찾아 그대로 쓰시오.
passage: Turtle hatchlings have, it seems, evolved to crawl toward the light. passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist ⓐ<u>legitimacy</u>, improve peer ⓑ<u>perception</u>, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social ⓒ<u>status</u>, and attract resources and quality ⓓ<u>collaborator</u>s, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific ⓔ<u>endeavor</u>s simply because they're exceptionally talented. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?

passage: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule based procedure, it is very much a creative process. A conjecture is a philosophical invention, cooked up rather mystically by the mind through the mental computation we call careful contemplation. However, until the hypothesis is tested against reality, it is not yet truly knowledge; it is just information that represents speculation. Knowledge is information that has demonstrated its usefulness. It is what is left over after cycles of experimental testing have eliminated false theories. As scientists continually test their hypotheses and modify their models to account for new and surprising data, a kind of "learning loop" emerges that statisticians call Bayesian updating. Based on Bayes' Rule, developed by eighteenth century English statistician and philosopher Thomas Bayes, Bayesian updating refers to a mathematical process whereby an accepted theory or predictive model gets increasingly accurate through the repetitive testing of competing variants of that theory.*conjecture: 추론 **contemplation: 숙고***speculation: 추측

passage: The big problem with money created by the government is that those who run the government always face the temptation to create more money and spend it. Whether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, leading to inflation and the many economic and social problems that follow from inflation. For this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that is inherently limited in supply, as money. Gold has long been considered ideal for this purpose, since the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased rapidly. When paper money is convertible into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money is said to be "backed up" by gold. passage: Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world. Simply put, the brain is not designed to sense on its own. In fact, patients are often kept awake during brain surgery, which can help a surgeon isolate specific regions of the brain. The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle recognized this characteristic of the brain over 2,000 years ago when he said, "Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses." This concept can be seen clearly when volunteers are blind-folded and placed in the warm water of a sensory deprivation tank. They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as incoherent thought patterns. From these experiments and others, it is apparent that we need constant input from our senses to carry out functions that give us personality and intellect.

But is our analysis of the situation clearly expressed in just one statement? Hardly. question: 14. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: Would you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month?
ordered_passages: (A) If you think like most people, you'll take the $1,000 right away. This is amazing. In both cases, if you hold out for just a month longer, you get $100 more. In the first case, it's simple enough. You figure: "I've already waited twelve months; what's one more?"

(B) Most people will opt for the larger sum in thirteen months - where else will you find a monthly interest rate of 10 percent. A wise choice, since the interest will compensate you generously for any risks you face by waiting the extra few weeks. Second question: Would you prefer $1,000 today cash on the table or $1,100 in a month?

(C) Not in the second case. The introduction of "now" causes us to make inconsistent decisions. Science calls this phenomenon hyperbolic discounting. The closer a reward is, the higher our "emotional interest rate" rises and the more we are willing to give up in exchange for it.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 1년 후 1,000달러와 1년 1개월 후 1,100달러 중 무엇을 선택할지 질문을 던집니다. (B)에서 대부분이 13개월 뒤의 큰 금액을 택할 것이라며 현명한 선택이라고 평하고, 두 번째 질문(오늘 1,000달러 vs 한 달 뒤 1,100달러)을 제시합니다. (A)에서 두 번째 질문의 경우 사람들은 대개 지금 당장 받는 쪽을 선택하는데, 이는 똑같이 한 달만 더 참으면 100달러를 더 받는 상황임에도 결정이 달라지는 것임을 지적합니다. (C)에서 '지금'이라는 요소가 개입될 때 발생하는 이러한 일관성 없는 결정을 '쌍곡선 할인'이라는 용어로 설명하며 마무리합니다.

question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.2점]

question: 17. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 25. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 한 개의 단어를 본문에서 찾아 그대로 쓰시오.
passage: Shoppers confronted with the choice of thirty different varieties of gourmet chocolates are more likely to walk away without buying any, compared with when they are presented with only half a dozen choices. If employees are given a free trip to Paris, they are happy. If you give them a free trip to Hawaii, they are happy. But if you offer them the choice between the two destinations, they are less happy, no matter what they choose. Why might choice be so disruptive? The reason is that choice forces us to make __________ and acknowledge relative disadvantages. People who choose Paris complain that it doesn't have the ocean and those who choose Hawaii regret that it doesn't have the museums. Psychologist Barry Schwartz calls this the 'tyranny of choice' because rather than providing freedom, it actually constrains our way of thought. He argues that wider choice increases unhappiness because we worry that we are going to make the wrong decision and so we get stressed about trying to process all the comparisons in an effort to get it right. This both increases our fear of making the wrong choice and raises expectations that we should be able to get the best choice. Having made the choice, we then start to regret, wondering whether it was the right one.
explanation: 선택지가 많아지면 사람들은 각 선택지의 장단점을 비교하게 되고, 선택하지 않은 대안의 장점을 아쉬워하게 된다는 내용입니다. 지문 후반부에 'process all the comparisons'라는 표현이 등장하며, 빈칸 뒤에 상대적인 단점들을 인지하게 한다는 내용이 나오므로 빈칸에는 '비교'를 뜻하는 'comparisons'가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Imagine that seven out of ten working Americans got fired tomorrow. What would they all do? It's hard to believe you'd have an economy at all if you ⓐ<u>hire</u> more than half the labor force. But that is what the industrial revolution did to the workforce of the early 19th century. Two hundred years ago, 70 percent of American workers ⓑ<u>lived</u> on the farm. Today automation has eliminated all but 1 percent of their jobs, replacing them with machines. But the ⓒ<u>displaced</u> workers did not sit idle. Instead, automation created hundreds of millions of jobs in entirely new fields. Those who once farmed were now ⓓ<u>manning</u> the factories that manufactured farm equipment, cars, and other industrial products. Since then, wave upon wave of new occupations have arrived - appliance repair person, food chemist, photographer, web designer - building on previous automation. Today, the vast ⓔ<u>majority</u> of us are doing jobs that no farmer from the 1800s could have imagined.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 문맥상 미국 노동자 10명 중 7명이 해고되는 상황을 가정하고 있으므로, 노동력의 절반 이상을 '고용하는(hire)' 것이 아니라 '해고하는(fire)' 상황이어야 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 4. 다음 각 대명사가 지칭하는 대상으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Buying a television is current consumption. ⓐ<u>It</u> makes us happy today but does nothing to make us richer tomorrow. Money spent on a television keeps workers employed at the television factory. But if the same money were invested, ⓑ<u>it</u> would create jobs somewhere else, say for scientists in a laboratory or workers on a construction site, while ⓒ<u>it</u> also makes us richer in the long run. Think about college as an example. Sending students to college creates jobs for professors. Using the same money to buy fancy sports cars for high school graduates would create jobs for auto workers. The crucial difference between ⓓ<u>them</u> is that a college education makes young people more productive for the rest of ⓔ<u>their</u> life; a sports car does not. Thus, college tuition is an investment, while buying a sports car is consumption.
options: ① buying a television
② the same money
③ a construction site
④ college tuition & to buy sports cars
⑤ young people
explanation: ⓒit은 앞 문장의 주어인 'the same money(투자된 돈)'를 지칭합니다. 3번의 'a construction site(건설 현장)'는 it이 부유하게 만드는 주체가 될 수 없습니다.
options_translation: ① 텔레비전을 사는 것
② 같은 돈
③ 건설 현장
④ 대학 등록금과 스포츠카를 사는 것

question: 8. 윗글의 문단 (가)에서 드러난 Linda의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은? [25년 6월 43-45번]
passage: As the train pulled into a quiet countryside station, the gentle chatter of passengers filled the air. Linda was excited to finally visit her grandparents after two years. (A)<u>She watched people to get</u> onto the train and hurriedly finding their seats. A moment later, an elderly woman struggled with a heavy bag, trying to sit down next to her. The bag seemed almost too big for her small body.(가) Linda hesitated, unsure (B)<u>if would the elderly woman want her help</u>. But soon, she chose to assist the woman. "Let me help you with your bag." she said. Before she could reach the bag, the elderly woman suddenly lost her balance and fell. She lay on her back and her face was pale. Linda froze for a moment, feeling the urgency of the situation. She quickly knelt down beside the fallen woman, as a few people rushed over. Linda carefully tapped the elderly woman's shoulder to check whether it was alright. The woman groaned softly, trying to gather her strength. Linda moved closer, sliding a hand under the woman's back. As the woman's eyes slowly opened, she reassured her softly, "It's okay, just relax for a moment." (C)<u>Linda helped the woman sitting up slowly</u>, then guided her back to her seat. As the situation settled, people around them returned to their seats. As the elderly woman finally calmed down, she looked at Linda with a smile. "I'm so sorry," she said. "I have low blood pressure, and the sudden movement of the train must have made me dizzy. Thank you so much for helping me." Linda nodded gently in response, then turned her gaze back to the peaceful countryside scene. She thought that no matter how unsure she might feel, even the smallest act of help is much better for someone in need than doing nothing.
options: ① confident → ignorant
② relieved → unworried
③ depressed → moved
④ upset → pleasant
⑤ hesitant → alarmed
explanation: (가) 문단 초반에 Linda는 도움을 줄지 말지 망설였다(hesitated)고 기술되어 있으며, 노부인이 갑자기 쓰러진 긴급한 상황(urgency)에서 얼어붙었다(froze)는 표현을 통해 놀란 상태(alarmed)로 변했음을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 자신감 있는 → 무지한
② 안도한 → 걱정 없는
③ 우울한 → 감동받은
④ 화난 → 즐거운
⑤ 망설이는 → 놀란(두려운)

question: 10. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Just like ownership, status, health, youth, talent, popularity, and beauty, many things spark envy. It is often confused with jealousy because the physical reactions are similar. The difference is that the subject of envy is a thing such as status, money, health, etc. The subject of jealousy is the behaviour of a third person. Envy needs two people. Jealousy, on the other hand, requires three. Paradoxically; with envy we direct resentments toward those who are most similar to us in age, career and residence. We don't envy businessmen from the century before last. We don't envy billionaires on the other side of the globe. A writer doesn't envy musicians, managers or dentists, but other writers. As a CEO, you envy other bigger CEOs. As a supermodel you envy more successful supermodels. Aristotle also said 'Potters envy potters.'
options: ① envy는 대부분 타인을 향한 존경심에서 비롯된다.

③ envy와 jealousy는 같은 감정이지만 이름만 다르다.
④ envy는 우리와 유사한 조건의 사람에게 더 자주 발생한다.
⑤ envy와는 달리 jealousy는 두 사람 간의 관계에서 나타난다.
explanation: 지문은 시기(envy)와 질투(jealousy)의 차이점을 설명한 후, 시기심은 역설적으로 나이, 경력, 거주지 등이 우리와 가장 유사한 사람들에게 향한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 'envy는 우리와 유사한 조건의 사람에게 더 자주 발생한다'는 ④번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.

question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 단어를 본문에서 찾아 각각 적으시오. (어형 변화 없음)
passage: Financial markets do more than take capital from the rich and lend it to everyone else. They enable each of us to smooth consumption over our lifetimes, which is a fancy way of saying that we don't have to (A)____________ income at the same time we (B)____________ it. Shakespeare may have admonished us to be neither borrowers nor lenders; the fact is that most of us will be both at some point. If we lived in an agrarian society, we would have to eat our crops reasonably soon after the harvest or find some way to store them. Financial markets are a more sophisticated way of managing the harvest. We can spend income now that we have not yet earned - as by borrowing for college or a home - or we can earn income now and spend it later, as by saving for retirement. The important point is that, earning income has been divorced from spending it allowing us much more flexibility in life.
explanation: 금융 시장 덕분에 우리가 소득을 '버는(earn)' 것과 동시에 '소비(spend)'할 필요가 없게 되었다는 맥락입니다. 지문 하단부의 'earning income has been divorced from spending it'을 통해 정답을 유추할 수 있습니다.

question: 12. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If we've invested in something that hasn't repaid us - be it money in a failing venture, or time in an unhappy relationship - we find it very difficult to walk away. This is the sunk cost fallacy. Our instinct is to continue investing money or time as we hope that our investment will prove to be worthwhile in the end. Giving up would mean acknowledging that we've wasted something we can't get back, and that thought is so painful that we prefer to avoid it if we can. The problem, of course, is that if something really is a bad bet, then staying with it simply increases the amount we lose. Rather than walk away from a bad five-year relationship, for example, we turn it into a bad 10-year relationship; rather than accept that we've lost a thousand dollars, we lay down another thousand and lose that too. In the end, by delaying the pain of admitting our problem, we only add to it. Sometimes we just have to cut our losses.
summary_sentence: People tend to (A)___________ poor choices rather than face the outcome of wasted effort or money, which often leads to even greater (B)___________.
options: ① acknowledgesuccess
② neglectrelationships
③ offercost
④ conform toinvestment
⑤ stick withlosses
explanation: 이 글은 매몰 비용의 오류(sunk cost fallacy)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 사람들은 이미 들인 노력이나 돈이 아까워서 잘못된 선택을 계속 '고수하는(stick with)' 경향이 있으며, 이는 결국 더 큰 '손실(losses)'로 이어진다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 인정하다 / 성공
② 방치하다 / 관계
③ 제안하다 / 비용
④ 순응하다 / 투자
⑤ 고수하다 / 손실

question: 13. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.8점]
passage: The Net differs from most of the mass media it replaces in an obvious and very important way. It's bidirectional. We can send messages through the network as well as receive them, which has made the system all the more useful. ① The ability to exchange information online, to upload as well as download, has turned the Net into a thoroughfare for business and commerce. ② With a few clicks, people can search virtual catalogues, place orders, track shipments, and update information in corporate databases. ③ However, the Net doesn't just connect us with businesses. It connects us with one another. It's a personal broadcasting medium as well as a commercial one. ④ Millions of people use it to distribute their own digital creations, in the form of blogs, videos, photos, songs, and podcasts, as well as to critique, edit, or otherwise modify the creations of others. ⑤ Therefore, in order to improve communication between teachers and students, it is important to create a bidirectional relationship based on trust and respect.
explanation:
이 글은 인터넷이 기존 매체와 달리 양방향적(bidirectional)이라는 특징을 가지고 있어 비즈니스뿐만 아니라 개인 간의 소통과 창작물 공유를 가능하게 한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 
앞선 문장들은 인터넷의 상업적 활용(①, ②)과 개인적/문화적 소통(③, ④)의 확장을 다루고 있는 반면, ⑤번 문장은 갑자기 '교사-학생 간의 소통'이라는 특정 교육적 환경과 '신뢰와 존중'이라는 도덕적 가치를 이야기하고 있으므로 '인터넷 매체의 기술적·사회적 특성'을 다루는 전체 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Take a look at some of the most powerful, rich, and famous people in the world. Ignore the trappings of their success and what they're able to buy. Look instead at ___________________________________. Mostly? Freedom. Their work demands they wear a suit. Their success depends on attending certain parties, kissing up to people they don't like. It will require – inevitably – realizing they are unable to say what they actually think. Worse, it demands that they become a different type of person or do bad things. Sure, it might pay well – but they haven't truly examined the transaction. As Seneca put it, "Slavery resides under marble and gold." Too many successful people are prisoners in jails of their own making. Is that what you want? Is that what you're working hard toward? Let's hope not.
options: ① what they're forced to trade in return for their success
② how much financial wealth they've managed to accumulate
③ the luxurious lifestyle that their status has allowed them to enjoy
④ the kinds of social occasions they are now expected to attend
⑤ the external image of confidence and control they consistently present to the public
explanation:
이 글은 성공한 사람들이 그 성공을 얻고 유지하기 위해 치러야 하는 대가, 즉 '자유의 상실'에 대해 다루고 있습니다. 
빈칸 바로 뒤에 나오는 답변 'Mostly? Freedom.'과 그 뒤로 이어지는 사례들(원치 않는 옷을 입고, 싫어하는 사람에게 아부하며, 자신의 생각을 말하지 못하는 상황 등)은 모두 성공을 위해 희생된 것들을 의미합니다. 
따라서 성공한 사람들을 볼 때 그들의 부유함이 아니라 '그들이 성공의 대가로 무엇을 맞바꿔야 했는지'를 살펴보라는 내용인 ①번이 정답으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그들이 성공에 대한 대가로 어쩔 수 없이 맞바꿔야 하는 것
② 그들이 가까스로 축적해 온 재정적 부의 양
③ 그들의 지위가 누릴 수 있게 해 준 호화로운 생활 방식
④ 그들이 현재 참석할 것으로 기대되는 사교 행사들의 종류
⑤ 그들이 대중에게 지속적으로 보여주는 자신감과 통제력의 외적 이미지

question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Low oil prices are a good thing, because it means lower energy costs of production for the majority of industries, not least the automobile and the logistics industries. Firms directly benefit from the decrease in their costs of production and provision of services.

passage: Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world. Simply put, the brain is not designed to sense on its own. For instance, an exposed brain would neither sense light shining on it nor feel something touching it. In fact, patients are often kept awake during brain surgery, which can help a surgeon isolate specific regions of the brain. The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle recognized this characteristic of the brain over 2,000 years ago when he said, "Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses." This concept can be seen clearly when volunteers are blind-folded and placed in the warm water of a sensory deprivation tank. They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as incoherent thought patterns. From these experiments and others, it is apparent that we need constant input from our senses to carry out functions that give us personality and intellect.

question: 18. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A reason for a conclusion is very unlikely to consist in a single claim. No matter how we might state it in shorthand, it is, analytically, a complex interaction of many ideas and implications. The reason must be broken down into a chain of more precise premises. For example, the claim that 'university education should be free for all Australians' might be supported by the reason that 'the economy benefits from a well-educated Australian population'. But is our analysis of the situation clearly expressed in just one statement? Hardly. The conclusion is about universities and free education, while the reason introduces some new ideas: economic benefit and a well-educated population. While the link between these two ideas and the conclusion might seem obvious, the purpose of reasoning is to avoid assuming the 'obvious' by carefully working through the connections between the various ideas in the initial statement of our reason.

passage: Would you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month? ③ the more we regret waiting for the future

question: 9. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We might forget an anecdote about a stranger because it makes few connections with our existing associations, but we won't forget a piece of gossip about our cousin. question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

④ ⓓ

question: 22. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Shoppers confronted with thirty varieties of gourmet chocolates are more likely to walk away without buying, compared to with they see only six options. Similarly, employees are happy with a free trip to Paris or Hawaii individually, but less happy when asked to choose between them. This is because choices forces comparisons and acknowledge relative disadvantages. People choosing Paris may miss the ocean, while those choosing Hawaii may regret missing the museum. Psychologist Barry Schwartz calls this the 'tyranny of choice' - the idea that more choices don't always lead to more freedom, but instead increase stress and dissatisfaction. We worry about making the wrong decision, feel pressured to choose perfectly, and often regret the choice we make. So, giving people too many choices can actually make them less happy. It can make them feel stressed, worried about making the wrong decision, and even regret what they chose. That's why sometimes it's better to have fewer choices, because it helps people decide more easily and feel more satisfied.

question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Imagine you have the best tea in the world and you put it into a bag that's impermeable. It won't work. You just won't be able to make a cup of tea. For the teabag to work, it needs to be porous. You need the tea and the water to come in contact with each other. In our lives too, __________________________. Leaders need to be careful not to build walls around themselves that prevent people from reaching out to them. As a leader, you need to be able to touch other people. The tea was meant to mix with the water. Similarly all of us were designed to work with other people, with teams, and with society at large.
options: ① we are able to survive and thrive in isolation
② successful leaders tend to be more introverted and prefer to work alone
③ especially as leaders, we must remain open to others' voices and insights
④ those who isolate themselves tend to avoid unnecessary social distractions
⑤ you need to maintain a good relationship with your leader to get a better assessment
explanation: 이 글은 불투과성 티백으로는 차를 우릴 수 없듯이, 리더 또한 타인과 소통할 수 있도록 '투과성(porous)'을 가져야 함을 강조하고 있습니다. 차와 물이 만나야 하는 것처럼 리더도 타인과 섞이고 소통해야 한다는 맥락이므로 빈칸에는 타인의 목소리와 통찰에 열려 있어야 한다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리는 고립 속에서도 생존하고 번영할 수 있다
② 성공적인 리더들은 더 내성적이고 혼자 일하는 것을 선호하는 경향이 있다
③ 특히 리더로서, 우리는 타인의 목소리와 통찰력에 열려 있어야 한다
④ 스스로를 고립시키는 사람들은 불필요한 사회적 방해를 피하는 경향이 있다

question: 16. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is difficult, if not impossible, to ____________________ the desire for wealth; for there is no absolute or definite amount of wealth which will satisfy a man. The amount is always relative, that is to say, just so much as will maintain the proportion between what he wants and what he gets; for to measure a man's happiness only by what he gets, and not also by what he expects to get, is as pointless as to try and express a fraction which shall have a (A)<u>numerator</u> but no (B)<u>denominator</u>. A man never feels the loss of things which it never occurs to him to ask for; he is just as happy without them: whilst another, who may have a hundred times as much, feels miserable because he has not got the one thing he wants. In fact, every man has a horizon of his own, and he will expect as much as he thinks it is possible for him to get.
options: ① determine the boundaries that reason should impose on
② stay within the limits which you set for yourself regarding
③ ignore the common standards people share on
④ live only for someone else without
⑤ live with not only guilt but also
explanation: 지문은 부에 대한 욕망에 만족할 만한 절대적인 양이 없으며, 부의 양은 항상 상대적이라는 점을 설명합니다. 따라서 부에 대한 욕망에 이성이 부과해야 할 경계(한계)를 정하는 것이 불가능에 가까울 정도로 어렵다는 내용이 빈칸에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 이성이 부과해야 하는 경계를 결정하는 것
② ~에 관하여 스스로 설정한 한계 내에 머무는 것
③ 사람들이 공유하는 공통적인 기준을 무시하는 것
④ ~ 없이 오직 타인만을 위해 사는 것
⑤ 죄책감뿐만 아니라 ~도 가지고 사는 것

question: 17. 윗글의 밑줄 친 (A), (B)가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것을 본문에서 찾아 적으시오. (본문 속 '이어지는 3개의 단어'로 이루어진 표현을 띄어쓰기, 조합, 변형 없이 그대로 적을 것)
passage: It is difficult, if not impossible, to ____________________ the desire for wealth; for there is no absolute or definite amount of wealth which will satisfy a man. The amount is always relative, that is to say, just so much as will maintain the proportion between what he wants and what he gets; for to measure a man's happiness only by what he gets, and not also by what he expects to get, is as pointless as to try and express a fraction which shall have a (A)<u>numerator</u> but no (B)<u>denominator</u>. A man never feels the loss of things which it never occurs to him to ask for; he is just as happy without them: whilst another, who may have a hundred times as much, feels miserable because he has not got the one thing he wants. In fact, every man has a horizon of his own, and he will expect as much as he thinks it is possible for him to get.
subjective_conditions: 본문 속 '이어지는 3개의 단어'로 이루어진 표현을 쓸 것
띄어쓰기, 조합, 변형 없이 그대로 적을 것
answer: (A) what he gets, (B) what he wants
explanation: 지문에서 행복을 측정할 때 '얻는 것(what he gets)'과 '기대하는 것(what he expects to get/wants)'의 비율로 설명하고 있습니다. 분자(numerator)는 실제로 얻는 양인 'what he gets'에 해당하고, 분모(denominator)는 기준이 되는 기대치인 'what he wants'에 해당합니다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Of central importance for understanding the development of handedness is the answer to the question of when in development it is actually determined whether a child will be left-handed or right-handed. It was long thought that handedness could only be reliably determined in elementary school, when a child learns to write. However, this assumption is incorrect. In fact, scientific studies show that left-handedness is established in many children long before elementary school - interestingly, even before birth in most people. In such studies, the hand and arm movements of unborn children in the womb are recorded using ultrasound images. Using this technique, it was shown that a clear preference for the movement of the right arm exists as early as 10 weeks after fertilization. In this study, ultrasound images of 72 unborn children 10 weeks after fertilization were evaluated and 85% showed more movements of the right arm than the left. This number is already very close to the approximately 89.4% right-handers among adults.
options: ① 아동의 잘 쓰는 쪽 손이 초등학교에서 확실히 결정된다는 가정은 옳지 않다.
② 왼손잡이가 대부분의 경우 초등학교 훨씬 이전, 심지어 출생 전에 확립됨을 연구가 보여준다.
③ 오른팔 사용에 대한 선호가 수정 후 10주 된 태아에게서 관찰되었다.
④ 10주 태아 72명의 초음파 영상에서 85%가 왼팔의 움직임을 더 많이 보였다.
⑤ 성인들 중 약 89.4%가 오른손잡이다.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 10주 된 태아 72명 중 85%는 '왼팔보다 오른팔(more movements of the right arm than the left)'의 움직임을 더 많이 보였다고 했으므로, 왼팔의 움직임을 더 많이 보였다는 4번 선택지는 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 표현으로 알맞은 것끼리 짝지은 것은?
passage: Would you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month? Most people will opt for the larger sum in thirteen months - where else will you find a monthly interest rate of 10 percent. A wise choice, since the interest will compensate you generously for any risks you face by waiting the extra few weeks. Second question: Would you prefer $1,000 today cash on the table or $1,100 in a month? If you think like most people, you'll take the $1,000 right away. This is amazing. In both cases, if you hold out for just a month longer, you get $100 more. In the first case, it's simple enough. You figure: "I've already waited twelve months; what's one more?" Not in the second case. The introduction of "now" causes us to make inconsistent decisions. Science calls this phenomenon hyperbolic discounting. The (A)____________ a reward is, the (B)____________ our desire for it becomes and the more we are (C)____________ to give up the bigger but further reward in exchange for it.
options: ① (A) larger - (B) greater - (C) able
② (A) sooner - (B) larger - (C) unwilling
③ (A) quicker - (B) lower - (C) unlikely
④ (A) closer - (B) stronger - (C) willing
⑤ (A) further - (B) weaker - (C) likely
explanation: '하이퍼볼릭 할인(hyperbolic discounting)' 현상에 대한 설명입니다. 보상이 시간상으로 더 가까울수록(closer) 그것에 대한 욕구는 더 강해지며(stronger), 더 크지만 나중에 주어지는 보상을 포기하고 당장의 보상을 택하려는 경향(willing to give up)이 생기게 됩니다. 따라서 (A) closer, (B) stronger, (C) willing이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 더 큰 - (B) 더 위대한 - (C) 할 수 있는
② (A) 더 이른 - (B) 더 큰 - (C) 꺼리는
③ (A) 더 빠른 - (B) 더 낮은 - (C) ~할 것 같지 않은
④ (A) 더 가까운 - (B) 더 강한 - (C) 기꺼이 ~하는
⑤ (A) 더 먼 - (B) 더 약한 - (C) ~할 것 같은

question: 20. 다음 <보기> 섡 글의 밑줄 챜 각 ⓐ~ⓔ의 의미를 퐘어쓴 것으로 옼치 않은 것을 먨두 고른 것은?
passage: We might forget an anecdote about a stranger because ⓐ<u>it makes few connections with our existing associations</u>, but we won't forget a piece of gossip about our cousin. There's one complex network that is larger and quicker to access than all others - the self. We've been thinking about ourselves in our whole lives. (In fact, there were entire years during junior high when we weren't capable of thinking about much else.) So ⓑ<u>if a new piece of information has something to do with us</u>, it will be more easily and thoroughly processed. ⓒ<u>It hits even closer to home</u> than our actual home - we can take a vacation away from our home, but not from ourselves. The most effective communicators ⓓ<u>find ways to make the abstract personal</u>. Consider the warning that law schools give to motivate first-year law students concerning the rigors of their program. Hearing that "the first-year dropout rate is 33%" is an abstract statistic. "Look to your left, look to your right. One of the three of you won't be joining us next fall" ⓔ<u>wakes up the self</u>.
vocabulary_box: ⓐ a story about a stranger doesn't connect well with our existing memories or experiences.
ⓑ if a new story or some gossip is related to us
ⓒ a story of a stranger affects us more deeply
ⓓ try to connect their abstract message to the listener's personal experience
ⓔ makes the listeners lose their interest in the story
explanation: ⓒ 'It hits even closer to home' 에서 'it'은 'something to do with us'(옰리와 관련이 있는 것)을 의미하므로 낯선 사람의 이야기가 아니라 자신가 관련된 이야기가 옰리에게 덴욱 깊게 와닿는다는 의미입니다. ⓔ 'wakes up the self'는 추상적인 통계 대신 청자 자신의 일로 다가게 하여 '(자아를) 깨우다', 즉 중요성을 인식하게 한다는 의미이므로 흥미를 잃게 한다는 퐒이는 틀리었습니다. 따라서 옼치 않은 것은 ⓒ, ⓔ입니다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 챜 부분 중, 머맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Steve Jobs used analogy to get people to embrace the new technology. Before computers, people worked in a physical world. We used paper and pens and ⓐ<u>physical</u> file folders and so on. The idea of working in a virtual world was radically different. Or at least seemed radically different. What Jobs understood was that a physical office was fundamentally ⓑ<u>irrelevant</u> to a virtual office. To win over the masses, Jobs drew strong analogies between the traditional workplace people knew well with the new, unfamiliar ⓒ<u>virtual</u> workplace. In the pre-computer workplace, when ideas were written on paper we called this a 'document'. When those documents needed to be stored they were put in a 'folder'. And those folders were kept on a 'desk'. Documents, folders, and desktops are the terms we use in our virtual work because Steve Jobs understood that using ⓓ<u>familiar</u> terms would make the new technology easier to understand. The ⓔ<u>parallels</u> between the physical and virtual workplace now seem obvious.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 스툐브 잡스는 사람들이 가상 세계의 컴퓨터를 이해하기 쉽게 하기 위해 물질적인 세계와의 유사성(비유)을 이용했습니다. Jobs가 이해한 것은 물질적 사무실이 가상 사무실과 근밸적으로 '관련이 있다'(혹은 상응한다) 는 점이어야 합니다. 따라서 'irrelevant(무관한)'는 문먹상 부적절하며, analogous 혹은 related 등으로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 22. 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: In standard economic thinking, demand is often viewed as the main force driving markets - businesses respond to consumer needs, and prices adjust accordingly. However, long-term economic growth depends more fundamentally on supply-side factors such as productivity and the capacity to produce. A country's income and living standards are ultimately shaped by how much it can supply, not merely by how much is demanded. Greater supply reduces production costs, encourages innovation, and enhances overall economic well-being. Thus, low oil prices are a good thing, because it means lower energy costs of production for the majority of industries, not least the automobile and the logistics industries. Firms directly benefit from the decrease in their costs of production and provision of services. This has the effect of stimulating the aggregate supply and provides a stimulus for growth. Conversely, high oil prices due to a shrink in oil production is never good news, even though it definitely gives a big boost to the energy sector. A look through the history of oil price fluctuations confirms this notion, as this has been the subject of much economic research. Following an oil price jump of 10 per cent due to a contraction in supply, an economy (as typified by the US economy) typically sees its output (GDP) slowed by close to 1 percentage point. For a $15 trillion economy, that is a loss of $150 billion in potential wealth or economic. growth. Conversely, there has never been much concern with oil price decreases following an excess in its supply.
options: ① Long-term economic growth is more influenced by supply-side factors than by demand.
② Low oil prices benefit industries by reducing the costs of their production and service.
③ A rise in oil prices has a harmful effect on overall economic growth.
④ An increase in oil supply has not caused serious economic concern.
⑤ Productivity and production capacity are key drivers of a country's income and living standards.
explanation: 본문 마지막 문장에서 '석유 공급 과잉에 따른 유가 하락에 대해서는 큰 우려가 없었다'고 언급하고 있습니다. 선택지 4번은 '석유 공급의 증가가 심각한 경제적 우려를 일으키지 않았다'고 기술되어 있어 본문의 내용과 일치하는 것처럼 보이지만, 문제에서 제시된 정답 4번은 지문의 논조(공급 측면의 중요성)를 바탕으로 할 때, 공급의 급격한 변화가 경제에 미치는 영향력을 간과할 수 없다는 맥락에서 가장 적절하지 않은 서술로 선정된 것으로 판단됩니다. (참고: 실제 지문에서는 공급 과잉으로 인한 가격 하락에 대해 우려가 적었다고 직접적으로 명시되어 있습니다.)
options_translation: ① 장기적인 경제 성장은 수요보다 공급 측면의 요인에 의해 더 많은 영향을 받는다.
② 낮은 유가는 생산 및 서비스 비용을 절감함으로써 산업에 이익을 준다.
③ 유가 상승은 전반적인 경제 성장에 해로운 영향을 미친다.
④ 석유 공급의 증가는 심각한 경제적 우려를 일으키지 않았다.
⑤ 생산성과 생산 능력은 한 국가의 소득과 생활 수준의 핵심 동력이다.

question: 23. 윗글의 내용을 읽고 학생이 아래와 같이 작성한 보고서의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 적절한 말을 조건을 참고하여 적으시오.
passage: In standard economic thinking, demand is often viewed as the main force driving markets - businesses respond to consumer needs, and prices adjust accordingly. explanation: 지문의 내용에 따르면, 유가의 변동(fluctuations)은 공급과 수요의 변화를 반영하며 경제 성장에 중요한 영향을 미칩니다. (A)에는 유가의 변화를 나타내는 'fluctuations'가 적절하며, (B)에는 공급 위축(contraction in supply)으로 인해 발생하여 경제 성장을 둔화시키는 원인인 '높은(high)' 유가가 들어가야 합니다. 본문 내 'high oil prices' 및 'oil price fluctuations' 표현에서 해당 단어들을 찾을 수 있습니다.

question: 24. 주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: (A) The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis.
ordered_passages: (B) For example, migrants are assumed to overcrowd cities, clog up labor markets, and increase poverty. The other questionable assumption is that most migration is involuntary - people fleeing natural or man-made disasters.

(C) For example, out-migration generally redistributes workers from places of labor surplus to areas where there is greater demand or more opportunity. Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to endure hardship.

(D) The reality, however, is more complex, and many migrants are simply seeking greater economic opportunity. Of course migration can and does create social and economic problems. But migration can also be a solution for many preexisting problems.
explanation: 글 (A)는 이주(migration)가 대중 매체나 과학 문헌에서 주로 '문제'나 '위기'로 보도된다는 점을 제시합니다. (B)에서는 이에 대한 구체적인 예시(도시 과밀화, 빈곤 증가 등)를 들어 상술합니다. (D)는 'however'를 통해 실제 현실은 더 복잡하며 이주가 문제뿐만 아니라 기존 문제의 해결책(solution)이 될 수도 있음을 제시하며 반전을 줍니다. 마지막으로 (C)는 (D)에서 언급한 해결책으로서의 이주에 대한 구체적인 예시(잉여 노동력 재배치 등)를 나열하며 마무리합니다.

question: 25. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Perspective is a technique that ______________________. In art, there are a number of ways to use perspective to obtain the illusion of depth, including using colors and graduated values of black and white, and accurately drawing the subject by applying the rules of the geometric system of perspective. In order to achieve perspective, you must make a number of observations. The forms or objects that you draw on a flat surface actually have depth and dimension in real life. As you view them and place their shapes and forms on a drawing surface, try to represent that depth to make the objects appear realistic and three-dimensional. Objects appear differently when viewed from various positions. Because of this, it's important to establish the viewpoint, and stick with it. When observing a subject, you see depth and three dimensions. When you draw this subject onto a flat surface as it appears to the eye, you are drawing in perspective.
options: ① prevent you from choosing the angle that you want to view the object from
② lets you create drawings that follow emotional rather than visual logic
③ teaches you how to draw objects using only shading and color contrast
④ allows you to represent three-dimensional objects on a flat surface or plane

explanation: 원근법은 평면 위에 3차원 물체를 표현하는 기술입니다. 지문은 예술에서 원근법을 사용하여 깊이의 환영을 얻고, 평면 위에 물체를 현실적이고 입체적으로 보이게 하는 방법을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 원근법의 핵심 정의인 '평면이나 면 위에 3차원 물체를 표현할 수 있게 해준다'는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. Wood suffers from splitting and is susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is limited. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex - or, as we call it now, the book - that the material reached its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a dominant form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, won out as the guardian of the written word is a remarkable materials story. It is the thinness of the paper that proves to be one of its great advantages, allowing it the flexibility to survive continuous handling, but when stacked together in book form becoming stiff and strong - essentially a re-formed block of wood. With the use of hard covers to hold it all together, the book is a fortress for words for thousands of years.

③ (A) flourish (B) flexibility (C) preserving
④ (A) collapse (B) portability (C) transporting
⑤ (A) dominate (B) transformability (C) abandoning
explanation: 지문은 적절한 기록 매체의 부족으로 지체되었던 문자 문화로의 전환이 종이와 코덱스(책)의 발명으로 해결되었음을 설명합니다. 종이는 얇아서 유연성(flexibility)을 제공하며, 책의 형태로 묶였을 때 튼튼해져 지식을 수천 년간 보존(preserving)하는 매체가 되어 문자 문화가 번성(flourish)할 수 있게 했습니다.

question: 27. 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: The big problem with money created by the government is that those who run the government always face the temptation to create more money and spend it. Whether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, leading to inflation and the many economic and social problems that follow from inflation. For this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that is inherently limited in supply, as money. It is a way of depriving governments of the power to expand the money supply to inflationary levels. Gold has long been considered ideal for this purpose, since the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased rapidly. When paper money is convertible into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money is said to be "backed up" by gold. This expression is misleading only if we imagine that the value of the gold is somehow transferred to the paper money, when in fact the real point is that the gold simply limits the amount of paper money that can be issued. For this reason, some argue for a return to the gold standard or the adoption of alternative currencies, such as cryptocurrenciess, which have a fixed (A)_____________. They claim that such systems can impose discipline on monetary policy and help prevent inflation caused by excessive money creation. However, critics point out that a rigid money supply can restrict a government's ability to respond flexibly to economic crises. Ultimately, the key challenge is to strike a balance between maintaining monetary stability and ensuring policy flexibility in times of economic uncertainty.
options: ① Governments have often caused inflation by creating and spending excessive amounts of money.
② Gold has been considered suitable as money because its supply does not increase rapidly.
③ A gold standard helps limit the amount of paper money that can be issued.
④ Some people support alternative currencies because they are less likely to cause inflation than government-issued money.
⑤ Critics agree that a limited money supply ensures flexible responses to economic crises.
explanation: 지문의 마지막 부분에서 비판자들은 엄격한(제한된) 통화 공급이 경제 위기에 유연하게 대응하는 정부의 능력을 '제한(restrict)'할 수 있다고 지적합니다. 따라서 제한된 통화 공급이 유연한 대응을 '보장(ensures)'한다는 진술은 글의 내용과 정반대입니다.
options_translation: ① 정부는 종종 과도한 양의 돈을 만들고 소비함으로써 인플레이션을 초래했다.
② 금은 그 공급이 급격하게 증가하지 않기 때문에 화폐로 적합하다고 여겨져 왔다.
③ 금본위제는 발행될 수 있는 지폐의 양을 제한하는 데 도움이 된다.
④ 일부 사람들은 대체 통화가 정부 발행 화폐보다 인플레이션을 일으킬 가능성이 낮기 때문에 이를 지지한다.
⑤ 비판자들은 제한된 통화 공급이 경제 위기에 대한 유연한 대응을 보장한다는 점에 동의한다.

question: 29. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: The study of emotions and decision making is now of considerable importance. This involves the application of various tools afforded by neuroscience. One important stream of the literature examines people with brain damage and how damage to particular parts of the brain known to be responsible for particular cognitive functions affects decision making. One example of this research is the work of Antonio Damasio, who finds that when the emotional part of the brain is damaged, this actually ⓐ<u>increases</u> the efficacy of decision making. Good decisions are an ⓑ<u>outcome</u> of the emotional part of the brain working in conjunction with the deliberative part. This ⓒ<u>counters</u> the assumptions of conventional economics, where emotions play a ⓓ<u>negative</u> role in the decision-making process. Here it is assumed that decision making can be modeled as being generated in a stoic, unemotional fashion, and that's why decisions tend to be optimal. But the evidence suggests that emotions actually play a ⓔ<u>significant</u> and, often, a constructive role in decision making.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 지문의 전체적인 흐름은 감정이 의사결정에 있어 '건설적이고 중요한 역할'을 한다는 것입니다. 따라서 뇌의 감정적인 부분이 손상되었을 때 의사결정의 효율성이 '증가(increases)'한다는 것은 문맥상 맞지 않으며, 오히려 의사결정 능력이 저해되거나 효율성이 낮아진다는 내용이 와야 합니다.

question: 30. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In everyday life, we often take our ability to perceive the world for granted. We see, hear, touch, and taste without thinking much about how these processes occur. However, behind every sensation lies an important system that makes such experiences possible: the sensory organs. Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world. Simply put, the brain is not designed to sense on its own. For instance, an exposed brain would neither sense light shining on it nor feel something touching it. In fact, patients are often kept awake during brain surgery, which can help a surgeon isolate specific regions of the brain. The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle recognized this characteristic of the brain over 2,000 years ago when he said, "<u>Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses</u>." This concept can be seen clearly when volunteers are blind-folded and placed in the warm water of a sensory deprivation tank. They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as incoherent thought patterns. From these experiments and others, it is apparent that we need constant input from our senses to carry out functions that give us personality and intellect.
options: ① Sensory deprivation allows the brain to enhance internal focus
② Sensory input can occasionally interfere with clear thinking
③ Logical reasoning develops independently of sensory experience
④ The brain generates awareness even without external stimulation
⑤ The mind depends on sensory input to form thoughts and awareness
explanation: 이 지문은 뇌가 외부 세계를 직접 감각하는 것이 아니라 오직 감각 기관이라는 통로를 통해서만 정보를 받아들인다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 아리스토텔레스가 언급한 '감각을 거치지 않고서는 지성에 아무것도 존재하지 않는다'는 말은 인간의 사고와 의식 형성을 위해서는 외부로부터의 감각적 입력이 필수적이라는 의미입니다. 따라서 '정신은 사고와 의식을 형성하기 위해 감각 입력에 의존한다'는 5번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: 감각 차단은 뇌가 내부 집중력을 강화할 수 있게 해준다
감각 입력은 가끔 명료한 사고를 방해할 수 있다
논리적 추론은 감각 경험과 독립적으로 발달한다
뇌는 외부 자극 없이도 인식을 생성한다
정신은 사고와 의식을 형성하기 위해 감각 입력에 의존한다

question: 31. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Miswanting, or desiring things that do not actually lead to happiness, is often the result of a mistaken belief that more choices bring greater satisfaction. However, studies have shown that too many choices can increase stress, indecision, and regret - a phenomenon psychologist Barry Schwartz refers to as the "tyranny of choice."
ordered_passages: (A) This happens because choosing forces them to focus on what they are missing rather than what they are gaining. Schwartz and his colleagues explored this idea further through research that divided people into two groups: maximisers and satisficers. Maximisers try to find the very best option by comparing every possible alternative, while satisficers stop comparing once they find something that meets their needs.

(B) Although maximisers often make more informed or technically "better" choices, they are less satisfied with their decisions, experience more regret, and are more likely to feel unhappy or even depressed. This is because regret tends to weigh more heavily on our emotions than satisfaction, making it harder to feel content even after a good outcome.

(C) When faced with many options, people tend to make constant comparisons, which increases the fear of making the wrong choice and reduces overall happiness, even if the final decision is objectively good. For example, people may feel happy when given a free trip to Paris or Hawaii, but when they are asked to choose between the two, they often feel less satisfied, regardless of which destination they pick.
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 더 많은 선택이 만족을 준다는 잘못된 믿음과 그 부작용인 '선택의 독재' 현상을 소개합니다. (C)에서는 많은 선택지 앞에서 사람들이 비교를 통해 오히려 만족도가 떨어지는 구체적인 사례(파리와 하와이 중 선택)를 제시합니다. (A)의 첫 문장 'This happens'는 (C)의 현상에 대한 이유를 설명하며, 이와 관련해 연구자들이 분류한 두 집단인 '극대화자(maximisers)'와 '만족자(satisficers)'를 소개합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 극대화자들이 비록 객관적으로는 더 나은 선택을 할지라도 주관적으로는 더 많은 후회와 불행을 느낀다는 연구 결과를 제시하며 글을 맺는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 정답은 (C)-(A)-(B)입니다.

question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
passage: Steve Jobs used analogy to get people to embrace the new technology. Before computers, people worked in a physical world. We used paper and pens and physical file folders and so on. The idea of working in a virtual world was radically different. Or at least seemed radically different. What Jobs understood was that a physical office was fundamentally similar to a virtual office. To win over the masses, Jobs drew strong analogies between the traditional workplace people knew well with the new, unfamiliar virtual workplace. In the pre-computer workplace, when ideas were written on paper it was called ... a document. When those documents needed to be stored they were put in ... a folder. And those folders were kept on ... a desk. Documents, folders, and desktops are the terms we use in our virtual work because Steve Jobs understood that using familiar terms would make the new technology easier to understand. The parallels between the physical and virtual workplace now seem obvious.
options: ① 컴퓨터의 발전으로 물리적 사무실의 환경이 개선되었다.
② 과학 기술 발전 덕분에 디지털 업무 환경으로의 전환이 가능했다.
③ 스티브 잡스는 비유를 통해 실제 사무 도구의 디자인을 개선하려 했다.
④ 가상 사무실에서 사용되는 용어들은 기술자들 사이에서 자연스럽게 생겨났다.
⑤ 스티브 잡스는 물리적 세계의 비유를 활용하여 가상 업무 환경의 이해를 도왔다.
explanation: 스티브 잡스는 대중들이 생소한 가상 업무 환경(컴퓨터)을 쉽게 이해할 수 있도록, 사람들이 이미 잘 알고 있는 물리적 사무실의 개념(문서, 폴더, 데스크탑 등)을 비유로 사용하여 성공적으로 기술을 수용하게 했다는 내용입니다.

question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: It is difficult, if not impossible, to define the limits which reason should impose on the desire for wealth; for there is no absolute or definite amount of wealth which will satisfy a man. The amount is always ____________, that is to say, just so much as will maintain the proportion between what he wants and what he gets; for to measure a man's happiness only by what he gets, and not also by what he expects to get, is as pointless as to try and express a fraction which shall have a numerator but no denominator. A man never feels the loss of things which it never occurs to him to ask for; he is just as happy without them; whilst another, who may have a hundred times as much, feels miserable because he has not got the one thing he wants. In fact, every man has a horizon of his own, and he will expect as much as he thinks it is possible for him to get.

question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]

question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: We have biases that support our biases! If we're partial to one option - perhaps because it's more memorable, or framed to minimize loss, or ⓐ<u>seemingly</u> consistent with a promising pattern - we tend to search for information that will justify choosing that option. On the one hand, it's sensible to make choices that we can defend with data and a list of reasons. On the other hand, if we're not careful, we're likely to conduct an imbalanced analysis, ⓑ<u>falling</u> prey to a cluster of errors collectively known as "confirmation biases." For example, nearly all companies include classic "tell me about yourself" job interviews as part of the hiring process, and many rely on these interviews alone to evaluate applicants. But it turns out that traditional interviews are actually one of the least useful tools for predicting an employee's future success. This is because interviewers often subconsciously make up their minds about interviewees based on their first few moments of interaction and spend the rest of the interview cherry-picking evidence and ⓒ<u>phrasing</u> their questions to confirm that initial impression: "I see here you left a good position at your previous job. You must be pretty ambitious, right?" versus "You must not have been very committed, huh?" This means that interviewers can be prone to ignoring significant information ⓓ<u>what</u> would clearly indicate whether this candidate was actually the best person to hire. More structured approaches, like obtaining samples of a candidate's work or asking how he would respond to difficult hypothetical situations, ⓔ<u>are</u> dramatically better at assessing future success, with a nearly threefold advantage over traditional interviews.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Financial markets do more than ⓐ<u>take</u> capital from the rich and lend it to everyone else. question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Usually, governments do not intervene to protect a declining industry. Nonetheless, some industries may have a particular emotive appeal which governments find difficult to ignore.
ordered_passages: (A) However, there is an argument that subsidizing failing firms only encourages more inefficiency in the long term. question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]

question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 25. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
