question: 26. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.7점]
passage: For much of history, gold has been used as money by many countries. Sometimes the gold has been used directly in coins or (for large purchases) in nuggets, gold bars or other forms. Even more convenient for carrying around were pieces of paper money printed by the government that were redeemable in gold whenever you wanted it redeemable. ⓐIt was not only more convenient to carry around paper money, but it was also safer than carrying large sums of money as mental that jingled in your pockets or was conspicuous in bags, attracting the attention of criminals. ⓑWithout paper money, it would be virtually impossible for criminals and corrupt officials to profit from illegal activities. ⓒThe big problem with money created by the government is that those who run the government always face the temptation to create more money and spend it. ⓓWhether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, leading to inflation and the many economic and social problems that flow from inflation. ⓔFor this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some material that is inherently limited in supply, as money.
explanation: 이 글은 과거부터 금이 화폐로 사용된 역사와 지폐의 편리함, 그리고 정부가 화폐를 과도하게 발행하면서 발생하는 인플레이션 문제로 인해 공급이 제한된 금이나 은과 같은 재료를 선호하게 된 배경을 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓑ번 문장은 지폐가 없으면 범죄자들이 불법 활동으로 이익을 얻는 것이 불가능해질 것이라는 내용으로, 화폐의 역사적 형태와 인플레이션 문제라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어나 지폐의 부작용(범죄 활용)을 언급하고 있으므로 부적절합니다.

question: 27. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [3.1점]
passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was handed down through stories, songs and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. Wood suffers from splitting and is susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is limited. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex - or, as we call it now, the book - that the material reached its full potential. ⓐThat was two thousand years ago, and it is still a dominant form of the written word. ⓑThat paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, won out as the guardian of the written word is a remarkable materials story. ⓒIt is the thinness of paper that proves to be one of its great advantages, allowing it the flexibility to survive continuous handling, but when stacked together in book form becoming stiff and strong - essentially a reformed block of wood. ⓓThis creates variations in the density of the paper fibers, resulting in an image that appears lighter or darker when viewed through light. ⓔWith the use of hard covers to hold it all together, the book is a fortress for words for thousands of years.
explanation: 이 글은 지식 전달 수단이 구비 문화에서 기록 문화로 전환되는 과정에서 종이와 책(코덱스)의 발명이 어떤 역할을 했는지, 그리고 종이라는 재료가 가진 물리적 장점(유연함과 견고함)을 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓓ번 문장은 종이 섬유의 밀도 차이로 인해 빛을 비추었을 때 이미지가 밝거나 어둡게 보인다는 내용으로, 종이의 제조 공정이나 워터마크와 관련된 기술적 특성을 언급하고 있어 기록 수단으로서의 종이의 역사와 장점을 다루는 전체 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Brands that fail to grow and develop lose their relevance. Think about the person you knew who was once on the fast track at your company, who is either no longer with the firm or, worse yet, appears to have hit a plateau in his or her career. Assuming he or she did not make an ambitious move, more often than not, this individual is a victim of having failed to stay relevant and embrace the advances in his or her industry. Think about the impact personal computing technology had on the first wave of executive leadership exposed to the technology. Those who embraced the technology were able to integrate it into their work styles and excel. Those who were resistant many times found few opportunities to advance their careers and in many cases were ultimately let go through early retirement for failure to stay relevant and update their skills.*hit a plateau 정체기에 들다
options: ① Staying Relevant: The Key to Career and Brand Growth
② How to Recover from a Career Plateau
③ The Danger of Technology Replacing Workers Completely
④ The Benefits of Avoiding Technological Change
⑤ Why Early Retirement Is Becoming More Common
explanation: 이 글은 브랜드나 개인이 시대의 흐름과 변화(적합성, relevance)를 유지하지 못하면 도태된다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 특히 신기술을 수용하지 못한 경영진의 사례를 통해, 커리어와 브랜드의 성장을 위해서는 끊임없이 변화를 수용하고 흐름에 발맞추는 것이 핵심임을 설명합니다. 따라서 ①번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 적합성을 유지하기: 커리어와 브랜드 성장의 핵심
② 커리어 정체기에서 회복하는 방법
③ 기술이 노동자를 완전히 대체할 위험성
④ 기술적 변화를 피하는 것의 이점
⑤ 조기 퇴직이 점점 흔해지는 이유

question: 8. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Perhaps, the advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the workplace may bode well for Emotional Intelligence (EI). As AI gains momentum and replaces people in jobs at every level, predictions are, there will be a premium placed on people who have high ability in EI. The emotional messages people send and respond to while interacting are, at this point, far beyond the ability of AI programs to mimic. As we get further into the age of the smart machine, it is likely that sensing and managing emotions will remain one type of intelligence that puzzles AI. This means people and jobs involving EI are safe from being taken over by machines. In a survey, almost three out of four executives see EI as a "must-have" skill for the workplace in the future as the automatizing of routine tasks bumps up against the impossibility of creating effective AI for activities that require emotional skill.*bode ~의 징조가 되다 ** momentum 추진력
options: ① The passage claims that AI will soon surpass EI abilities.
② Emotional Intelligence is difficult for AI to replicate.
③ Most executives believe EI is essential for the future workplace.
④ AI is expected to replace people in many jobs.
⑤ Emotional Intelligence is likely to remain a human advantage.
explanation: 지문에서는 AI가 감정을 감지하고 관리하는 능력(EI)을 모방하기는 매우 어렵다고 설명하며, EI가 필요한 직업은 AI에 의해 대체되기 어렵다고 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 AI가 곧 EI 능력을 능가할 것이라는 ①번 선택지는 본문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 이 글은 AI가 곧 EI 능력을 능가할 것이라고 주장한다.
② 감성 지능은 AI가 복제하기 어렵다.
③ 대부분의 경영진은 EI가 미래 직장에 필수적이라고 믿는다.
④ AI는 많은 직업에서 사람들을 대체할 것으로 예상된다.
⑤ 감성 지능은 인간의 장점으로 남을 가능성이 높다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 imperfect or bad proxies의 사례에 해당하지 않은 것은?
passage: Technologists are always on the lookout for quantifiable metrics. Measurable inputs to a model are their lifeblood, and like a social scientist, a technologist needs to identify concrete measures, or "proxies," for assessing progress. This need for quantifiable proxies produces a bias toward measuring things that are easy to quantify. But simple metrics can take us further away from the important goals we really care about, which may require complicated metrics or be extremely difficult, or perhaps impossible, to reduce to any measure. And when we have <u>imperfect or bad proxies</u>, we can easily fall under the illusion that we are solving for a good end without actually making genuine progress toward a worthy solution. The problem of proxies results in technologists frequently substituting what is measurable for what is meaningful. As the saying goes, "Not everything that counts can be counted, and not everything that can be counted counts."
options: ① A company evaluates employee performance by tracking how many hours each employee spends logged into their work system.
② A hospital evaluates the quality of its doctors by tracking how many patients they see per day.
③ A nonprofit selects grant recipients by combining financial need, interview performance, and peer recommendations.
④ A startup assesses team collaboration by reviewing how often employees send messages on the company's internal chat system.
⑤ A university ranks its departments for research quality by counting the number of published research papers each faculty member has produced.
explanation: 본문에서 'imperfect or bad proxies'는 측정하기 쉽다는 이유만으로 본질적 가치(의미 있는 것)를 대신하여 사용되는 단순하고 수량화된 지표를 의미합니다. ① 로그인 시간, ② 환자 수, ④ 메시지 빈도, ⑤ 논문 편수는 모두 단순 수치에 의존하는 불완전한 대용물입니다. 반면 ③번은 재정적 필요, 인터뷰 성과, 동료 추천 등 다각적이고 질적인 요소를 결합하여 평가하므로, 단순히 수량화하기 쉬운 것만 측정하는 '나쁜 대용물'의 사례로 보기 어렵습니다.
options_translation: ① 회사가 각 직원이 업무 시스템에 로그인한 시간을 추적하여 직원 성과를 평가한다.
② 병원이 의사들이 하루에 진찰하는 환자 수를 추적하여 의사의 자질을 평가한다.
③ 비영리 단체가 재정적 필요, 인터뷰 성과, 동료 추천을 결합하여 보조금 수혜자를 선정한다.
④ 스타트업이 직원들이 사내 채팅 시스템에서 메시지를 얼마나 자주 보내는지 검토하여 팀 협업을 평가한다.
⑤ 대학교가 각 교수진이 생산한 출판된 연구 논문의 수를 세어 연구 품질에 따른 학과 순위를 매긴다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: If a firm is going to ⓐ<u>be saved</u> by the government, it might be easier to concentrate on lobbying the government for more money rather than taking the harder decision of restructuring the company to be able to be profitable and viable in the long term. This is an example of something ⓑ<u>known</u> as moral hazard - when government support alters the decisions firm stake. For example, if governments rescue banks who get into difficulty, as they ⓒ<u>did</u> during the credit crisis of 2007-08, this could encourage banks to take greater risks in the future because they know ⓓ<u>it</u> is a possibility that governments will intervene if they lose money. Although the government rescue may be well intended, it can negatively affect the behavior of banks, ⓔ<u>encouraging</u> risky and poor decision making.*viable 성장할 수 있는
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ④번의 it은 가주어로 보기에 어색한 문장 구조입니다. '...라는 가능성이 있다'는 의미의 동격절을 이끄는 문장에서는 유도부사 there를 사용하여 'there is a possibility that...'의 형태로 표현하는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 it을 there로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: For years, many psychologists have held strongly to the belief that the key to addressing negative health habits is to change behavior. This, more than values and attitudes, is the part of ⓐ<u>personality</u> that is easiest to change. Behaviors like smoking, drinking, and different eating habits are the most frequent health issues people try to ⓑ<u>modify</u>. Process- addiction behaviors (workaholism, shopaholism, and the like) fall into this category as well. Mental imagery combined with power of ⓒ<u>suggestion</u> was taken up as the premise of behavioral medicine to help people change negative health behaviors into positive ones. Effective behavioral changes for some people have resulted from applying this technique together with other tactics for modifying behavior and strategies for coping, since the technique alone is ⓓ<u>effective</u>. What mental imagery does is reinforce a new desired behavior. Repeated use of images reinforces the ⓔ<u>desired</u> behavior more strongly over time.*premise 전제
explanation: 지문에서 심상 기법(mental imagery)이 효과적이긴 하지만, 기법 단독으로는 효과가 제한적이기 때문에 다른 전략들과 함께 사용할 때 효과적인 행동 변화가 나타난다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '기법 단독으로는 효과적이기 때문에'라는 맥락은 어색하며, effective를 ineffective(효과가 없는) 혹은 insufficient(불충분한)와 같은 단어로 바꾸어야 흐름상 적절합니다.

question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We tend to overrate the impact of new technologies in part because older technologies have become absorbed into the furniture of our lives, so as to be almost invisible. Take the baby bottle. Here is a simple implement that has transformed a fundamental human experience for vast numbers of infants and mothers, yet it finds no place in our histories of technology. This technology might be thought of as a classic time-shifting device, as it enables mothers to exercise more control over the timing of feeding. It can also function to save time, as bottle feeding allows for someone else to substitute for the mother's time. Potentially, therefore, it has huge implications for the management of time in everyday life, yet it is entirely overlooked in discussions of high-speed society.
summary_sentence: → This passage suggests that some technologies, despite their significant impact, are often ____________ ________________________.
options: ① overemphasized due to their complexity
② misunderstood as harmful inventions
③ neglected because of their simplicity and familiarity
④ rejected for disrupting traditional values
⑤ recognized only in scientific communities
explanation: 이 글은 젖병과 같은 오래된 기술들이 우리 삶에 너무 깊숙이 스며들어 일상의 가구처럼 친숙해졌기 때문에, 그 영향력이 상당함에도 불구하고 기술의 역사나 논의에서 종종 무시되거나 보이지 않게 된다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 기술이 '단순함과 친숙함 때문에 무시된다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 복잡함 때문에 과하게 강조된다
② 해로운 발명품으로 오해받는다
③ 단순함과 친숙함 때문에 무시된다
④ 전통적 가치를 파괴하여 거부된다
⑤ 오직 과학계에서만 인정받는다

question: 24. 다음 글을 읽고 추론할 수 없는 것은?
passage: There is little doubt that we are driven by the sell-by date. Once an item is past that date it goes into the waste stream, further increasing its carbon footprint. Remember those items have already travelled hundreds of miles to reach the shelves and once they go into waste they start a new carbon mile journey. But we all make our own judgement about sell-by dates; those brought up during the Second World War are often scornful of the terrible waste they believe such caution encourages. The manufacturer of the food has a view when making or growing something that by the time the product reaches the shelves it has already been travelling for so many days and possibly many miles. The manufacturer then decides that a product can reasonably be consumed within say 90 days and 90 days minus so many days for travelling gives the sell-by date. But whether it becomes toxic is something each individual can decide. It would seem to make sense not to buy large packs of perishable goods but nonperishable items may become cost-effective.*sell-by date 판매 유효 기한 **scornful 경멸하는
options: ① Products are transported hundreds of miles to stores and end up being wasted after their sell-by dates.
② Individual judgment regarding sell-by dates affects the amount of food waste generated.
③ Disposing of food past its sell-by date prevents environmental problems by increasing the carbon footprint.
④ It may be irrational to buy perishable goods in large quantities.
⑤ There may be a gap between the manufacturer's method of setting sell-by dates and the consumer's judgment of actual edibility.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 판매 유효 기한이 지난 품목이 폐기물 흐름으로 들어가면 탄소 발자국을 더욱 증가시킨다고 되어 있습니다. 따라서 환경 문제를 예방한다(prevents environmental problems)는 설명은 본문의 내용(탄소 발자국 증가)과 정반대이므로 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 제품은 상점까지 수백 마일을 운송되며 판매 유효 기한이 지나면 결국 낭비된다.
② 판매 유효 기한에 관한 개인의 판단은 발생하는 음식물 쓰레기의 양에 영향을 미친다.
③ 판매 유효 기한이 지난 음식을 처분하는 것은 탄소 발자국을 늘림으로써 환경 문제를 예방한다.
④ 상하기 쉬운 상품을 대량으로 구매하는 것은 비합리적일 수 있다.
⑤ 제조업체의 판매 유효 기한 설정 방식과 소비자의 실제 식용 가능성에 대한 판단 사이에는 간극이 있을 수 있다.

question: 25. 다음 본문과 연계하여 'Consumption Smoothing'이라는 주제로 글을 쓰려고 할 때, 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage:
Financial markets do more than take capital from the rich and lend it to everyone else. They enable each of us to smooth consumption over our lifetimes, which is a fancy way of saying that we don't have to spend income at the same time we earn it. Shakespeare may have admonished us to be neither borrowers nor lenders; the fact is that most of us will be both at some point. If we lived in an agrarian society, we would have to eat our crops reasonably soon after the harvest or find some way to store them. Financial markets are a more sophisticated way of managing the harvest. We can spend income now that we have not yet earned - as by borrowing for college or a home - or we can earn income now and spend it later, as by saving for retirement. The important point is that earning income has been divorced from spending it, allowing us much more flexibility in life.
*admonish 훈계하다 **agrarian 농경의(농민의)
options: ① Consumption smoothing is the idea that people try to keep their spending level relatively stable throughout their lives, even though their income changes.
② Financial markets enable consumption smoothing, offering the ability to borrow during periods of low income and save during periods of high income.
③ Consumption smoothing is like planning your finances so you can keep a stable lifestyle across your whole life.
④ Consumption smoothing allows you to spend more than you earn now by borrowing or save what you earn now to spend later by saving.
⑤ Consumption smoothing means that some individuals or groups have way more money than others, creating a noticeable gap in earnings.
explanation: 본문은 금융 시장이 소득을 얻는 시점과 지출하는 시점을 분리하여 평생에 걸쳐 소비를 고르게 유지(Consumption Smoothing)할 수 있게 도와준다는 내용입니다. ⑤번은 특정인이나 집단이 더 많은 돈을 소유하여 소득 격차를 만든다는 내용으로, 개인의 생애 주기별 소비 조절이라는 제품의 본질적인 주제와는 거리가 멀기 때문에 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 소비 평탄화는 사람들이 소득이 변하더라도 평생 동안 지출 수준을 비교적 안정적으로 유지하려 한다는 개념이다.
② 금융 시장은 소득이 낮은 기간에는 빌리고 소득이 높은 기간에는 저축하는 능력을 제공함으로써 소비 평탄화를 가능하게 한다.
③ 소비 평탄화는 평생 동안 안정적인 생활 방식을 유지할 수 있도록 재정을 계획하는 것과 같다.
④ 소비 평탄화는 대출을 통해 현재 소득보다 더 많이 지출하거나, 나중에 쓰기 위해 현재 소득을 저축하는 것을 허용한다.
⑤ 소비 평탄화는 일부 개인이나 집단이 다른 사람들보다 훨씬 많은 돈을 가지고 있어 눈에 띄는 소득 격차를 만든다는 것을 의미한다.

question: 26. 위 글의 (A)~(C)의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage:
(A) Lectins are large proteins that serve as a crucial weapon that plants use to defend themselves. The lectins in most plants bind to carbohydrates as we consume the plant. They also bind to sugar molecules found in the gut, in the brain, between nerve endings, in joints and in all bodily fluids. According to Dr. Steven Gundry, these sticky proteins can interrupt messaging between cells and cause toxic and inflammatory reactions. Brain fog is just one result of lectins interrupting communication between nerves. An upset stomach is another common symptom of lectin overload.
(B) It is important to remember that eating foods with a high amount of active lectins is rare. One reason is that lectins are most potent in their raw state, and foods containing them are not typically eaten raw. Cooking, especially with wet high-heat methods like boiling or stewing, or soaking in water for several hours, can inactivate most lectins. Lectins are water-soluble and typically found on the outer surface of a food, so exposure to water removes them.
(C) There are different types of lectins in different foods, and the reactions people have to them vary widely. It is possible that one who has an underlying digestive sensitivity, such as irritable bowel syndrome, may be more likely to experience negative symptoms from eating lectins and other anti-nutrients. ④ Reactions to lectins vary among individuals and types of food, and people with digestive sensitivities might be more prone to adverse symptoms from them.

question: 30. 다음 글 <B>의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <A>에서 골라 주어진 조건에 맞게 순서대로 쓰시오.
passage: <A>Correlations are powerful because the insights they offer are relatively clear. These insights are often covered up when we bring causality back into the picture. For instance, a used-car dealer supplied data to statisticians to predict which of the vehicles available for purchase at an auction were likely to have problems. A correlation analysis showed that orange-colored cars were far less likely to have defects. Even as we read this, we already think about why it might be so: Are orange-colored car owners likely to be car enthusiasts and take better care of their vehicles? Or, is it because orange-colored cars are more noticeable on the road and therefore less likely to be in accidents, so they're in better condition when resold? Quickly we are caught in a web of competing hypotheses - alternative explanations that often act like confounding factors. Our desire to explain a simple correlation can lead us to introduce other variables that blur rather than clarify the picture.<B>Observational studies of humans cannot be properly controlled. Humans live different lifestyles and in different environments. Thus, they are insufficiently homogeneous to be suitable experimental subjects. These are (A)_____________ variables (known or unknown) that make it difficult for epidemiologists to isolate the effects of the specific variable being studied. For example, Taubes argued that since many people who drink also smoke, researchers have difficulty determining the link between alcohol consumption and cancer. Similarly, researchers in the famous Framingham study identified a significant (B)_____________ between coffee drinking and coronary heart disease. However, most of this disappeared once researchers corrected for the fact that many coffee drinkers also smoke. If these variables are known, it is often possible to correct for them. However, if they are unknown, they will undermine our ability to establish (C)_____________ from epidemiological surveys.
subjective_conditions: 지문에 있는 단어만을 사용하되 변형하지 말 것.

question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Would you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month? Most people will opt for the larger sum in thirteen months - where else will you find a monthly interest rate of 10 percent.
ordered_passages: (A) This is amazing. In both cases, if you hold out for just a month longer, you get $100 more. In the first case, it's simple enough. You figure: "I've already waited twelve months; what's one more?"

(B) A wise choice, since the interest will compensate you generously for any risks you face by waiting the extra few weeks. Second question: Would you prefer $1,000 today cash on the table or $1,100 in a month? If you think like most people, you'll take the $1,000 right away.

(C) Not in the second case. The introduction of "now" causes us to make inconsistent decisions. Science calls this phenomenon hyperbolic discounting. The closer a reward is, the higher our "emotional interest rate" rises and the more we are willing to give up in exchange for it.
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 1년 뒤의 1,000달러와 1년 1개월 뒤의 1,100달러 중 후자를 선택하는 합리적인 경향을 설명합니다. (B)에서는 이에 대한 '현명한 선택'이라는 코멘트와 함께 새로운 질문(오늘 1,000달러 vs 한 달 뒤 1,100달러)을 던지며, 이때는 사람들이 당장 1,000달러를 택한다는 점을 언급합니다. (A)는 두 경우 모두 한 달을 더 기다리면 100달러를 더 받는다는 공통점을 분석하며 첫 번째 사례의 심리를 설명합니다. (C)는 두 번째 사례가 다른 이유를 '지금'이라는 단어의 도입과 '쌍곡형 할인(hyperbolic discounting)' 개념으로 설명하며 결론을 맺습니다. 따라서 적절한 순서는 (B)-(A)-(C)입니다.

question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Steve Jobs used analogy to get people to embrace the new technology. Before computers, people worked in a physical world.
ordered_passages: (A) To bridge this gap, Jobs drew strong analogies between the traditional workplace people knew well with the new, unfamiliar virtual workplace. In the pre-computer workplace, when ideas were written on paper it was called ... a document. When those documents needed to be stored they were put in ... a folder. And those folders were kept on ... a desk.

question: 21. 다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 괄호 안의 단어를 조건에 맞게 바르게 배열하여 요약문을 완성하시오.
passage: We might forget an anecdote about a stranger because it makes few connections with our existing associations, but we won't forget a piece of gossip about our cousin. There's one complex network that is larger and quicker to access than all others - the self. We've been thinking about ourselves in our whole lives. So if a new piece of information has something to do with us, it will be more easily and thoroughly processed. It hits even closer to home than our actual home - we can take a vacation away from our home, but not from ourselves. The most effective communicators find ways to make the abstract personal. Consider the warning that law schools give to motivate first-year law students concerning the rigors of their program. Hearing that "the first-year dropout rate is 33%" is an abstract statistic. "Look to your left, look to your right. One of the three of you won't be joining us next fall" wakes up the self.
summary_sentence: Information ( it / memorable / becomes / when / feels / rather than / more ) because it connects to our own experiences and emotions.
subjective_conditions: 1. '정보는 추상적일 때보다 개인적으로 느껴질 때 더 잘 기억된다.'는 의미가 되도록 작성할 것
2. 주어진 어구를 변형하지 말고 모두 한 번씩만 사용하되, 단어 2개를 본문에서 찾아 추가할 것
3. 어법과 맥락상 올바른 문장이 되도록 작성할 것
answer: becomes more memorable when it feels more personal rather than abstract
explanation: 이 글은 정보가 우리 자신(자기)과 연관될 때 더 잘 기억된다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 요약문은 정보가 추상적인 것보다 개인적으로 느껴질 때 더 기억에 남게 된다는 내용을 담아야 합니다. 본문에서 'personal'과 'abstract'라는 단어를 찾아 추가하여 문장을 완성할 수 있습니다.

question: 9. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The study of emotions and decision making is now of considerable importance. This involves the application of various tools afforded by neuroscience.
ordered_passages: (A) Antonio Damasio's research illustrates that damage to the brain's emotional centers diminishes decision-making effectiveness. question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: Understanding how hand preference, or handedness, develops in humans involves examining both genetic and environmental influences. For many years, it was believed that handedness could only be reliably determined when children· learned to write in elementary school. However, research has shown that hand preference is established much earlier, often before birth. Ultrasound studies have revealed that fetuses as early as 10 weeks after conception display a preference for moving one arm over the other, with about 85% favoring their right arm. This percentage closely matches the proportion of right-handed adults. Genetic factors play a role in handedness, with studies suggesting that genes contribute to brain asymmetries and motor control. However, genetics alone do not fully explain hand preference. Twin and family studies indicate that environmental factors are also significant. Prenatal conditions, such as fetal position, birthweight, and whether the baby is part of a multiple birth, can influence handedness. Some research has explored the impact of maternal behaviors during pregnancy, but findings are mixed며. After birth, cultural and social influences, as well as early experiences like how a baby is cradled or encouraged to use one hand, may further shape hand preference. Overall, handedness results from _______________________________. This helps explain why most people are right-handed, but a minority of people develop a preference for their left hand.
options: ① a complex interplay between genetic predispositions and environmental factors
② acquired behaviors that emerge during early childhood
③ external influences that override biological tendencies
④ temporary adaptations based on cultural practices
⑤ a fixed genetic code determined at conception

explanation: 글의 전반부에서 정부가 발행하는 화폐의 문제점은 공급량을 무제한으로 늘려 인플레이션을 유발할 수 있다는 점이라고 설명합니다. 이에 대한 해결책으로 공급이 제한적인 금을 화폐로 사용하는 것인데, 금이 이 목적에 이상적인 이유는 그 공급량이 자연적으로 제한되어 있어 급격하게 늘릴 수 없기 때문입니다. 따라서 5번이 정답입니다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸서 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is difficult, if not impossible, to define the limits which reason should impose on the desire for wealth; for the amount of wealth which will satisfy a man is not definite. To measure a man's happiness only by what he gets, and not also by what he expects to get, is as pointless as to try and express a fraction which shall have a numerator but no denominator. A man never feels the loss of things which it never occurs to him to ask for; he is just as happy without them; whilst another, who may have a hundred times as much, feels miserable because he has not got the one thing he wants. question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [25년 6월 38번]

question: 2. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world. Simply put, the brain is not designed to sense on its own. From these experiments and others, it is apparent that we need constant input from our senses to carry out functions that give us personality and intellect.

explanation: 이 글은 뇌가 스스로 감각하도록 설계되지 않았으며, 감각 기관을 통해서만 외부 세계와 소통한다는 점을 강조합니다. 감각 박탈 실험 등을 통해 우리의 인격과 지적 기능을 수행하기 위해서는 지속적인 감각 입력이 필요하다는 결론을 내리고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 '정상적인 뇌 기능을 위한 감각 입력의 중요성'입니다.

question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]

question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 15. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: For years, many psychologists have held strongly to the belief that the key to addressing negative health habits is to change behavior. This, more than values and attitudes, is the part of personality that is easiest to change. Ingestive habits such as smoking, drinking and various eating behaviors are the most common health concerns targeted for behavioral changes. Process-addiction behaviors (workaholism, shopaholism, and the like) fall into this category as well. Mental imagery combined with power of suggestion was taken up as the premise of behavioral medicine to help people change negative health behaviors into positive ones. Although this technique alone will not produce changes, when used alongside other behavior modification tactics and coping strategies, behavioral changes have proved effective for some people. What mental imagery does is reinforce a new desired behavior. Repeated use of images reinforces the desired behavior more strongly over time.
options: ① The Biological Roots of Negative Health Habits
② Why Behaviors Is Harder to Change Than Beliefs
③ Overcoming Addiction Through Medication and Therapy
④ The Role of Attitudes and Values in Health Psychology
⑤ Changing Health Behaviors Through Mental Imagery and Suggestion

question: 18. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
options: ① the idea that social status drives scientific achievement
② the belief that early education ensures scientific success
③ the view that the Matthew effect fully explains scientific success
④ the notion that practice and knowledge accumulation lead to repeated success
⑤ the debate over whether scientific success stems from prior achievements or innate talent

question: 19. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 The considerable crossover가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We must explore the relationship between children's film production and consumption habits. question: 20. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 this conventional wisdom이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food is taking a back seat. According to <u>this conventional wisdom</u>, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, do not depend on the quality of sensations provided by the food. question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: It is a common assumption that most vagrant birds are ultimately doomed, aside from the rare cases ⓐ<u>where</u> individuals are able to reorientate and return to their normal ranges. In turn, it is also commonly assumed that vagrancy itself is a ⓑ<u>relatively</u> unimportant biological phenomenon. This is undoubtedly true for the majority of cases, as the most likely outcome of any given vagrancy event is that the individual will fail to find enough resources, and/or ⓒ<u>exposed</u> to inhospitable environmental conditions, and perish. However, there are many lines of evidence to suggest ⓓ<u>that</u> vagrancy can, on rare occasions, dramatically alter the fate of populations, species or even whole ecosystems. question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: The explosion of popular music in the second half of the twentieth century as well as the global circulation and dissemination of music by the creative industries propelled a new understanding of accessibility in relation to music. question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 24. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 25. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking.
ordered_passages: (A) The specific sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and this appears to be true.(B) Without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Moreover, commitments make people willing to perform actions that they would not otherwise perform. For example, a taxi driver picks up his clients and transports them to their desired destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a credible commitment to pay her at the end of the month. Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because the central bank is committed to taking various measures to sustain the currency in question. Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money and government depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.
options: ① 상훈
② 강록
③ 영현
④ 상훈, 강록
⑤ 강록, 영현

question: 31. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: If you had wanted to create a "self-driving" car in the 1950s, your best option might have been to strap a brick to the accelerator. Yes, the vehicle would have been able to move forward on its own, but it could not slow down, stop, or turn to avoid barriers. Obviously not ideal. But does that mean the entire concept of the self-driving car is not worth pursuing? No, it only means that at the time we did not yet have the tools we now possess to help enable vehicles to operate both autonomously and safely. This once-distant dream now seems within our reach. It is much the same story in medicine. Two decades ago, we were still taping bricks to accelerators. Today, we are approaching the point where we can begin to bring some appropriate technology to bear in ways that advance our understanding of patients as unique individuals. In fact, many patients are already wearing devices that monitor their conditions in real time, which allows doctors to talk to their patients in a specific, refined, and feedback-driven way that was not even possible a decade ago.
options: ① In the 1950s, creating a self-driving car was unrealistic due to a lack of proper technology, even though basic movement could be achieved in a simple way.
② The limitations of past technology did not deny the idea of self-driving cars but highlighted the need for better tools.
③ Advances in technology have transformed what was once an unrealistic dream of autonomous vehicles into a possible reality.
④ Similarly, medicine has evolved from using basic, rough methods to incorporating sophisticated, personalized technology.
⑤ Today, despite technological progress, doctors still rely entirely on traditional methods and have only access to face-to-face contact with patients.
explanation: 지문 후반부에 따르면, 환자들은 실시간 상태를 모니터링하는 장치를 착용하고 있으며 이를 통해 의사들이 이전에는 불가능했던 방식으로 구체적이고 피드백 중심적인 대화를 나눌 수 있다고 했으므로, '의사가 여전히 전통적인 방식에만 의존하며 대면 접촉만 가능하다'는 ⑤번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 1950년대에는 적절한 기술 부족으로 자율주행차 제작이 비현실적이었으나, 단순한 방식으로 기본적 이동은 가능했다.
② 과거 기술의 한계가 자율주행차 개념 자체를 부정한 것은 아니며, 더 나은 도구의 필요성을 강조했을 뿐이다.
③ 기술의 발전은 한때 비현실적인 꿈이었던 자율주행차를 가능한 현실로 바꾸어 놓았다.
④ 마찬가지로, 의학도 기초적이고 거친 방식을 사용하는 것에서 정교하고 개인화된 기술을 통합하는 방향으로 진화해 왔다.
⑤ 오늘날 기술적 진보에도 불구하고, 의사들은 여전히 전적으로 전통적 방식에 의존하며 환자와 대면 접촉만 가능하다.

question: 32. 다음 글의 내용을 요약한 문장으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: Emotion socialization - learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them - starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may intrude on adolescents' autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.
options: ① Parental emotion socialization plays a significant role in emotion regulation development, and must adapt to support adolescents' increasing autonomy.
② Parental emotion socialization is crucial for children's emotion regulation, but it should remain the same throughout childhood and adolescence.
③ Adolescents' emotion regulation develops mainly through external influences, such as peers or media, rather than through parental involvement.
④ Parents should always provide direct guidance in emotion regulation, regardless of the child's age or emotional stage.
⑤ Parents need to strictly control their children's emotional responses to help them regulate emotions in adolescence.
explanation: 이 글은 부모의 정서 사회화가 자녀의 정서 조절 발달에 미치는 영향에 대해 다루고 있습니다. 아동기에는 직접적인 위로와 지도가 효과적이지만, 청소년기에는 자율성을 추구하는 특성에 맞춰 부모의 방식이 간접적인 지원과 수용의 형태로 조절되어야 한다는 내용이 핵심입니다. 따라서 '부모의 정서 사회화는 정서 조절 발달에 중요한 역할을 하며, 청소년의 증가하는 자율성을 지원하기 위해 적응되어야 한다'는 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 부모의 정서 사회화는 정서 조절 발달에 중요한 역할을 하며, 청소년의 증가하는 자율성을 지원하기 위해 변화해야 한다.
② 부모의 정서 사회화는 자녀의 정서 조절에 중요하지만, 아동기와 청소년기 내내 동일하게 유지되어야 한다.
③ 청소년의 정서 조절은 부모의 개입보다는 주로 또래나 미디어와 같은 외부의 영향을 통해 발달한다.
④ 부모는 자녀의 나이나 정서적 단계에 상관없이 항상 정서 조절에 있어 직접적인 지도를 제공해야 한다.
⑤ 부모는 청소년기 자녀가 정서를 조절하는 것을 돕기 위해 자녀의 정서적 반응을 엄격하게 통제해야 한다.

question: 33. 다음 글의 ecosystem states를 <그림>과 같이 표현하였다. 다음 글에 근거하여 <그림>을 바르게 이해하지 않은 사람을 <보기>에서 있는 대로 고른 것은? [3.3점]
passage: The concept of <u>ecosystem states</u> should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem; they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state, like the ball rolls down the slope. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
vocabulary_box: 강혁: 정원의 상태가 A 지점에 있을 때 정원이 가장 안정적이구나.
장미: 만약 재배자가 살충제와 울타리를 계속 사용하면 정원은 계속 B 상태에 머물겠구나.
유림: 재배자의 개입이 사라지면, 정원에는 채소뿐 아니라 다른 식물과 야생동물로 가득하게 되어 B 상태에서 C 상태로 향할 거야.
options: ① 강혁
② 장미
③ 유림
④ 강혁, 유림
⑤ 강혁, 장미, 유림
explanation: 글의 내용에 따르면, 재배자가 의도적으로 유지하려는 상태(최대 생산)는 '본질적으로 불안정한 상태'이며 이를 경사면 위의 공으로 비유하고 있습니다. 반면, 개입을 멈췄을 때 도달하는 자연스러운 상태가 '안정적인 상태'입니다. <보기>의 내용을 분석하면:- 강혁: A 지점은 공이 경사면 위에 있는 불안정한 상태이므로 틀렸습니다. (안정적인 상태는 경사면 아래인 C임)- 장미: 재배자의 지속적인 개입(살충제, 울타리 등)은 공을 경사면에 머물게 하는 것이므로, B 상태가 아닌 가장 높은 A 상태에 머물게 하는 것입니다. 따라서 틀렸습니다.- 유림: 개입이 사라지면 공은 경사면을 따라 아래로 내려가므로 B에서 C로 향하는 것은 맞으나, '안정적인 상태'로 가는 것이지 식물과 야생동물로 가득 차는 과정 전체를 B에서 C로만 한정 짓거나 설명하는 방식에서 논리적 오류가 있을 수 있으나, 문제의 의도상 세 사람 모두 본문의 비유를 잘못 이해한 것으로 파악됩니다. (특히 지문에 근거할 때 재배자가 유지하는 상태는 A, 자연으로 돌아가는 과정이 B, 안정된 상태가 C라고 볼 때 모든 설명이 비유의 핵심과 어긋납니다.) 정답은 ⑤입니다.

question: 34. 다음 글 (A)를 읽고 (B)의 각 빈칸 ⓐ~ⓓ에 들어갈 가장 적절한 한 단어를 (A)에서 찾아 쓰시오. (단, 필요시 변형 가능)
passage: (A) In order to bring the ever-increasing costs of home care for elderly and needy persons under control, managers of home care providers have introduced management systems. These systems specify tasks of home care workers and the time and budget available to perform these tasks. Electronic reporting systems require home care workers to report on their activities and the time spent, thus making the distribution of time and money visible and, in the perception of managers, controllable. This, in the view of managers, has contributed to elimination of inefficiencies in their organization. The home care workers, on the other hand, may perceive their work not as a set of separate tasks to be performed as efficiently as possible, but as a service to be provided to a client with whom they may have developed a relationship. This includes having conversations with clients, having discussions about the client's needs and enquiring about the person's own well-being and wishes. Restricted time and the requirement to report may be perceived as obstacles that make it impossible to deliver the service that is needed. If the management systems are too rigid, this may result in home care workers becoming overloaded and demotivated.
subjective_answer_format: (B)<Pros and Cons: Management Systems in Home Care> Manager's Advantage: By using management systems, managers can clearly monitor how time and budget are allocated, making the care process more ⓐ__________ and, in their view, more controllable. This helps them address rising costs and improve organizational ⓑ__________.  Home Care Workers' Disadvantage: For home care workers, however, these systems may seem to be restrictive. Limited time and strict reporting requirements may prevent them from building meaningful relationships with clients and delivering ⓒ__________ care, leading to stress and ⓓ__________. ⓐ: _____________________ⓑ: _____________________ⓒ: _____________________ⓓ: _____________________
explanation: (A)의 내용을 요약한 (B)를 완성하는 것입니다. 관리자 입장에서는 시간/예산 분배가 '가시적(visible)'이게 되어 '효율성(efficiency)'을 높이고, 노동자 입장에서는 '개별화된(personalized - relationship 및 well-being 관련)' 돌봄 제공이 어려워져 '의욕 상실(demotivation)'로 이어질 수 있다는 내용입니다.

question: 35. 윗글 (A), (B)에 근거하여 다음을 완성하고자 한다. 밑줄 친 우리말 표현과 같은 의미가 되도록 <보기>의 표현을 배열하시오. (단, 주어진 표현만 한 번씩 사용하며, 필요시 어형 변형 가능)
passage: (A) Empathy is frequently listed as one of the most desired skills in an employer or employee, although without specifying exactly what is meant by empathy. Some businesses stress cognitive empathy, emphasizing the need for leaders to understand the perspective of employees and customers when negotiating deals and making decisions. Others stress <u>affective empathy</u> and empathic concern, emphasizing the ability of leaders to gain trust from employees and customers by treating them with real concern and compassion. When some consultants argue that successful companies foster empathy, what that translates to is that companies should conduct good market research. In other words, an "empathic" company understands the needs and wants of its customers and seeks to fulfill those needs and wants. When some people speak of design with empathy, what that translates to is that companies should take into account the specific needs of different populations - the blind, the deaf, the elderly, non-English speakers, the color-blind, and so on - when designing products.(B)(The following is a conversation between students talking after class.)S2: Hey... I heard about your dog. I'm really sorry. That must be so hard.S1: Thanks. Yeah, it's been rough. I've had him since I was a kid.S2: I can't even imagine how that feels. Losing a pet is like losing family. When my cat died, I cried for days. If you need someone to talk to or just hang out, I'm totally here for you, okay?S1: Thanks. I can tell you really get it. It honestly helps. 필요시 어형 변형 가능
subjective_answer_format: <Two students' views on empathy> S1 shows cognitive empathy by understanding the situation from a rational perspective and acknowledging the emotional impact of losing a pet without necessarily sharing the same feelings. 반면, S2는 ⓐ<u>상황에 감정적으로 연결하고</u>, ⓑ<u>연민을 표현하고</u>, ⓒ<u>유사한 개인적 경험을 통해 관계를 맺음으로써</u> 정서적 공감을 드러낸다.In contrast, S2 demonstrates affective empathy by ⓐ____________________, ⓑ____________________ and ⓒ_____________________.ⓐ: ______________________________________________________ⓑ: ______________________________________________________ⓒ: ______________________________________________________

question: 37. 다음 글 (A)를 읽고 (B)의 각 빈칸 ⓐ~ⓓ에 들어갈 가장 적절한 한 단어를 (A)에서 찾아 쓰시오. (단, 필요시 변형 가능)
passage: (A) Intuition can be great, but it ought to be hard-earned. Experts, for example, are able to think on their feet because they've invested thousands of hours in learning and practice: their intuition has become data-driven. Only then are they able to act quickly in accordance with their internalized expertise and evidence-based experience. Yet most people are not experts, though they often think they are. Most of us, especially when we interact with others on social media, act with conviction, offering a wide range of opinions on global crises, without the substance of knowledge that supports it. And thanks to AI, which ensures that our messages are delivered to an audience more inclined to believing it, our delusions of expertise can be reinforced by our personal filter bubble. We have an interesting tendency to find people more open-minded, rational, and sensible when they think just like us.
subjective_answer_format: (B)(The following is a conversation between students about the last class.)S1: I always thought intuition was just some natural instinct, but it turns out real intuition has to be ⓐ________ through years of experience.S2: Right! I mean, they talk with so much ⓑ________, but their arguments lack any real substance. S2: Totally. It's like people confuse confidence with competence. And then people are becoming subject to the ⓒ________ belief that reading just a few headlines makes them an authority on global crises.S1: What makes it worse is how social media works. We're all stuck in our own bubbles, where we only see opinions that match ours. The algorithm acts as a(n) ⓓ________, blocking out everything else.S2: Couldn't agree more. Intuition is powerful, but only when it's based on something real.ⓐ: _____________________ⓑ: _____________________ⓒ: _____________________ⓓ: _____________________
explanation: (A)의 핵심 개념을 대화문 (B)에 채워 넣는 문제입니다. 전문가의 직관은 '내면화된(internalized)' 지식에서 오지만, 비전문가들은 근거 없는 '확신(conviction)'으로 말하며, 소셜 미디어의 '필터(filter)' 버블 때문에 스스로 전문가라는 '망상적(delusional)' 믿음을 갖게 된다는 내용입니다. ⓐ의 경우 문맥상 'internalized'가 적절합니다.

question: 1. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that <u>our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do</u>, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
options: ① Gestures can anticipate our speech before we are fully aware of it ourselves.
② Our hands move only after we have fully formed our thoughts.
③ Hand movements are always a random part of body language with no connection to thinking.
④ Gesture follows speech and only helps to emphasize what has already been said.
⑤ The brain controls speech and gestures separately with no interaction between them.
explanation: 이 글은 제스처(몸짓)가 단순한 말의 보조 수단이 아니라 사고의 최첨단을 나타낸다고 설명합니다. 특히 우리가 말하기 수백 밀리초 전에 제스처를 멈추거나, 제스처가 단어를 정신적으로 준비시킨다는 내용은 제스처가 의식적인 사고보다 앞서 우리가 할 말을 미리 '알고' 있음을 시사합니다. 따라서 정답은 ①번 '제스처는 우리가 스스로 완전히 인식하기 전에 우리의 말을 예상할 수 있다'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 제스처는 우리가 스스로 완전히 인식하기 전에 우리의 말을 예상할 수 있다.
② 우리의 손은 우리가 생각을 완전히 형성한 후에만 움직인다.
③ 손동작은 사고와 관련이 없는 보디빌딩의 항상 무작위적인 부분이다.
④ 제스처는 말을 따르며 이미 말해진 것을 강조하는 데에만 도움을 준다.
⑤ 뇌는 상호작용 없이 언어와 제스처를 별개로 제어한다.

question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain. A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol "on" instead of "off," which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.
options: ① Chronic stress helps the brain grow stronger in hard situations.
② Long-term stress harms the brain and disrupts stress control.
③ Only the hippocampus is affected by chronic stress, but it heals easily.
④ Long-term stress affects the body more than the brain.
⑤ Chronic stress makes people smarter by changing their brains.
explanation: 이 글은 스트레스가 뇌의 구조, 특히 해마(hippocampus)에 미치는 부정적인 영향에 대해 다루고 있습니다. 만성적인 스트레스는 해마를 작게 만들고, 스트레스 조절 시스템(코르티솔 신호 전달 등)을 교란시켜 건강한 반응을 방해한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 ②번 '장기적인 스트레스는 뇌에 해를 끼치고 스트레스 조절을 방해한다'입니다.
options_translation: ① 만성 스트레스는 어려운 상황에서 뇌가 더 강해지도록 돕는다.
② 장기적인 스트레스는 뇌에 해를 끼치고 스트레스 조절을 방해한다.
③ 오직 해마만이 만성 스트레스의 영향을 받지만 쉽게 치유된다.
④ 장기적인 스트레스는 뇌보다 신체에 더 많은 영향을 미친다.
⑤ 만성 스트레스는 뇌를 변화시켜 사람들을 더 똑똑하게 만든다.

question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food is taking a back seat. I suspect that most people view flavor as of secondary importance in social settings where food is served. Although our social gatherings coalesce around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, do not depend on the quality of sensations provided by the food. To focus excessively on flavor is to miss the larger significance of these social relations.
options: ① The Roles That food's Flavor Plays
② Why We Often Overlook Flavor in Social Gatherings
③ The Social Significance of Food Beyond Its Flavor

⑤ How Food Connects People Through Shared Experiences
explanation: 이 글은 음식과 관련된 글쓰기나 사회적 모임에서 음식의 '맛(풍미)' 자체보다는 그 음식을 둘러싼 '사회적 차원'이나 '관계'가 더 중요하게 여겨진다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 맛은 단지 배를 채우는 용도이거나 사회적 상호작용의 배경일 뿐이며, 음식 모임의 진정한 의미는 사회적 관계에 있다고 말합니다. 따라서 제목으로는 '풍미를 넘어선 음식의 사회적 의미'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 음식의 풍미가 수행하는 역할들

question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. ⓐ<u>In spite of</u> professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. All experts are not the same, nor ⓑ<u>do</u> they submit their work to the same scrutiny. Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims. For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, ⓒ<u>leading</u> the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were funded in part by the sugar industry. The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, ⓓ<u>where</u> their influential article appeared. Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have fostered higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. Stories such as this one fuel suspicion - but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. Funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since ⓔ<u>made</u> compulsory.

question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Quite often the interaction between groups is socially unequal, and this is reflected in the fact that in many cases borrowing of words or constructions goes mostly or entirely in one direction, from the more powerful or prestigious group to the less favored one. The languages of socially subordinated groups may from quite an early period of contact provide terminology for objects or practices with which speakers of the more powerful group were previously unfamiliar, but the effects of contact in that direction may not progress any further than this. In some cases, as with the Dharug language of Sydney, Australia, the source of some of the earliest loans from Indigenous Australian languages into English, the fate of the language system is extinction after the obliteration of many of its speakers. The remainder shifted to varieties of English, the language of the people who had suppressed them. This shows that linguistic exchange under unequal social conditions often leads to _______________________.
options: ① the dominance of the more powerful group's language and the decline of the other.
② a preservation of minority languages despite external pressure.
③ a mutual enrichment of both languages involved.
④ the revival of indigenous languages through borrowing.
⑤ the cultural independence of subordinated groups in terms of language.
explanation: 글의 내용은 사회적으로 불평등한 집단 간의 언어적 교류가 일방향(더 강력한 집단에서 덜 우세한 집단으로)으로 일어나며, 종국에는 소수 집단의 언어가 사라지고 지배적인 언어로 대체된다는 사례(호주 다루그어의 멸종 및 영어로의 전환)를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 불평등한 조건에서의 언어 교류는 '강력한 집단 언어의 지배와 다른 언어의 쇠퇴'로 이어진다는 결론이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 더 강력한 집단 언어의 지배와 다른 언어의 쇠퇴.
② 외부의 압력에도 불구하고 소수 언어의 보존.

question: 13. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Commitment is the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life. Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby facilitating the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. ⓐMoreover, commitments make people willing to perform actions that they would not otherwise perform. ⓑFor example, a taxi driver picks up his clients and transports them to their desired destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a credible commitment to pay her at the end of the month. ⓒIndeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to taking various measures to sustain the currency in question. ⓓBeyond merely printing money, these measures include managing interest rates, controlling exchange rates and inflation and maintaining trust in the currency. ⓔThus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글의 주제는 사회적 삶을 유지하는 데 있어 '약속(Commitment)'의 역할과 중요성입니다. 돈(화폐) 역시 약속의 망에 의해 가치를 지닌다는 예시를 들고 있으나, ⓓ 문장은 통화 가치를 유지하기 위한 구체적인 기술적 조치(금리 관리, 환율 통제 등)를 설명하고 있어, '약속의 사회적 기능'이라는 전체 맥락에서 벗어납니다.

question: 14. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition.
ordered_passages: (A) In other words, a dictionary functions in many cases as a cross-reference or translator between words one knows and words that one doesn't yet know. Dictionaries thus can't fully explain concepts to someone who doesn't already possess some linguistic knowledge.

(B) Even the most obscure words in a dictionary, say, for example, "pulchritudinous" or "kalokagathia," must be defined using words that the reader already knows and understands. Otherwise, the dictionary isn't very helpful.

(C) But it's important to understand the limits of dictionary definitions. More often than not, a definition in a dictionary requires readers to have a fairly robust understanding of the language already at their disposal.
explanation: 사전 정의의 한계에 대해 설명하는 글입니다. 주어진 글에서 사전적 정의(lexical definition)의 개념을 소개한 뒤, (C)에서 하지만 사전 정의에는 한계가 있으며 독자가 이미 언어에 대한 상당한 이해를 갖추고 있어야 함을 언급합니다. (A)에서는 이를 'In other words'로 연결하여 사전이 아는 단어와 모르는 단어 사이의 가교 역할을 할 뿐 언어 지식이 없는 사람에게 개념을 완전히 설명할 수는 없다고 부연합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 아주 생소한 단어라도 독자가 이미 아는 단어로 정의되어야 유용하다는 구체적 사례와 결론을 제시하는 (C)-(A)-(B) 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more acceptable than previously. Often a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. They were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage acceptance of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
summary_sentence: Since the early 1950s, U.S. sitcoms have used humour to (A)__________ social challenges and (B)__________ the acceptance of more progressive values associated with a pluralistic and tolerant society.
options: ① deal with     reject
② tackle     promote
③ resist     foster
④ overlook     facilitate
⑤ address     hinder
explanation: 이 글은 1950년대 초반부터 미국 시트콤이 인권, 여성 권리 등 다양한 사회적 갈등을 유머로 다루며 진보적인 가치를 수용하게 만드는 역할을 했다는 내용입니다. 따라서 시트콤은 사회적 도전 과제들을 '다루고(tackle)', 다원적이고 관용적인 사회와 관련된 진보적 가치의 수용을 '촉진(promote)'했다는 요약이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 다루다 - 거부하다
해결하다(다루다) - 촉진하다
저항하다 - 육성하다
간과하다 - 용이하게 하다
다루다 - 방해하다

question: 3. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
passage: Development of the human body from a single cell provides many examples of the structural richness that is possible when the repeated production of random variation is combined with nonrandom selection. All phases of body development from embryo to adult exhibit random activities at the cellular level, and body formation depends on the new possibilities generated by these activities coupled with selection of those outcomes that satisfy previously built-in criteria. Always new structure is based on old structure, and at every stage selection favors some cells and eliminates others. The survivors serve to produce new cells that undergo further rounds of selection. Except in the immune system, cells and extensions of cells are not genetically selected during development, but rather, are positionally selected. Those in the right place that make the right connections are stimulated, and those that don't are eliminated. This process is much like sculpting. A natural consequence of the strategy is great variability from individual to individual at the cell and molecular levels, even though large-scale structures are quite similar.
options: ① In human body development, structure is formed through purely random cellular activities without any selective process.
② Body structures are always formed on entirely new foundations and undergo developmental processes independent of previous structures.
③ In human development, all cells are genetically selected to form the final structure.
④ Cells that are positioned correctly and form the right connections are activated, while those that do not are eliminated.
⑤ All humans have identical structures at the cellular and molecular levels.
explanation: 지문 중반 이후의 'Those in the right place that make the right connections are stimulated, and those that don't are eliminated.'라는 문장과 ④번 선지의 내용이 정확히 일치합니다. 세포들은 유전적이 아니라 위치적으로 선택된다는 것이 핵심입니다.
options_translation: ① 인체 발달에서 구조는 선택 과정 없이 순전히 무작위적인 세포 활동을 통해 형성된다.
② 신체 구조는 항상 완전히 새로운 토대 위에 형성되며 이전 구조와는 독립적인 발달 과정을 거친다.
③ 인간의 발달에서 모든 세포는 최종 구조를 형성하기 위해 유전적으로 선택된다.
④ 올바른 위치에 자리 잡고 올바른 연결을 형성하는 세포는 자극을 받고(활성화되고), 그렇지 못한 세포는 제거된다.

question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We must explore the relationship between children's film production and consumption habits. question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 7. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: For years, many psychologists have held strongly to the belief that the key to addressing negative health habits is to change behavior. This, more than values and attitudes, is the part of personality that is easiest to change. Ingestive habits such as smoking, drinking and various eating behaviors are the most common health concerns targeted for behavioral changes. Process-addiction behaviors (workaholism, shopaholism, and the like) fall into this category as well. Mental imagery combined with power of suggestion was taken up as the premise of behavioral medicine to help people change negative health behaviors into positive ones. Although this technique alone will not produce changes, when used alongside other behavior modification tactics and coping strategies, behavioral changes have proved effective for some people. What mental imagery does is reinforce a new desired behavior. Repeated use of images reinforces the desired behavior more strongly over time.

question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중에서 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?

This, in the view of managers, has contributed to the resolution of the problem. The home care workers, on the other hand, may ⓒ<u>perceive their work not as a set of separate tasks to be performed as efficient as possible</u>, but as a service to be provided to a client with whom they may have developed a relationship. ⓓ<u>This includes having conversations with clients and enquiring about the person's well-being</u>. Restricted time and the requirement to report may be perceived as obstacles ⓔ<u>that make it impossible to deliver the service that is needed</u>. If the management systems are too rigid, ⓕ<u>this may result in home care workers becoming overloaded and demotivated</u>.
options: ① 1개
② 2개
③ 3개
④ 4개
⑤ 5개

question: 11. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Emotion socialization─learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them─starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents.
ordered_passages: (A) Therefore, more suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.(B) For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. explanation: 제시문에서 부모가 감정 사회화의 주요 대리인임을 언급한 뒤, (B)에서 그 구체적인 예시(롤모델 역할 및 부모의 관행)를 설명합니다. (C)에서는 어린 아이들과 달리 청소년기에는 부모의 직접적인 통제가 자율성을 침해할 수 있음을 대조적으로 설명하며, (A)에서 따라서 청소년기에는 간접적인 지지가 더 적절하다는 결론을 도출하는 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is a common assumption that most vagrant birds are ultimately doomed, aside from the rare cases where individuals are able to reorientate and return to their normal ranges. In turn, it is also commonly assumed that vagrancy itself is a relatively unimportant biological phenomenon.
ordered_passages: (A) The most profound consequences of vagrancy relate to the establishment of new breeding sites, new migration routes and wintering locations. Each of these can occur through different mechanisms, and at different frequencies, and they each have their own unique importance.

(B) However, there are many lines of evidence to suggest that vagrancy can, on rare occasions, dramatically alter the fate of populations, species or even whole ecosystems. Despite being infrequent, these events can be extremely important when viewed at the timescales over which ecological and evolutionary processes unfold.

(C) This is undoubtedly true for the majority of cases, as the most likely outcome of any given vagrancy event is that the individual will fail to find enough resources, and/or be exposed to inhospitable environmental conditions, and perish.
explanation:
주어진 글은 길을 잃은 새(vagrant birds)들이 대개 생존하지 못하며, 이러한 현상이 생물학적으로 중요하지 않다는 통념을 제시합니다.
(C)에서는 'This is undoubtedly true'라는 표현을 사용해 제시문의 가정이 대다수의 경우 사실임을 인정하고 보충 설명합니다.
(B)에서는 반전의 연결어 'However'를 통해 이러한 드문 사건이 생태학적·진화적 관점에서는 매우 중요할 수 있음을 언급하며 분위기를 전환합니다.
(A)는 (B)에서 언급한 '심오한 결과(profound consequences)'의 구체적인 예시들(새로운 번식지, 이주 경로 등)을 서술하며 논의를 구체화합니다.
따라서 가장 자연스러운 흐름은 (C)-(B)-(A)인 ⑤번입니다.

question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: If you had wanted to create a "self-driving" car in the 1950s, your best option might have been to strap a brick to the accelerator. But does that mean the entire concept of the self-driving car is not worth pursuing? No, it only means that at the time we did not yet have the tools we now ②retain to help enable vehicles to operate both autonomously and safely. This once-distant dream now seems within our reach. It is much the same story in medicine. Two decades ago, lack of advanced tools ③<u>resolved</u> a challenge in understanding patients. Today, we approaching the point where we can begin to bring some appropriate technology to bear in ways that advance our understanding of patients as ④<u>particular</u> individuals. 20년 전에는 첨단 도구의 부족(lack of advanced tools)으로 인해 환자를 이해하는 데 어려움이 여전히 남아 있었거나(remained) 어려움을 야기했다(presented/posed)는 내용이 와야 자연스럽습니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Intuition can be great, but it ought to be ⓐ<u>hard-earned</u>. And thanks to AI, which ensures that our messages are delivered to an audience more inclined to believing it, our delusions of expertise can be ⓓ<u>strengthened</u> by our personal filter bubble. explanation: 이 글은 전문가의 직관은 수천 시간의 학습과 연습을 통해 얻어진 데이터 기반의 것임을 강조합니다. 문맥상 전문가들은 '피상적인(superficial)' 전문지식이 아니라 '깊이 있는' 또는 '실질적인' 전문지식에 따라 행동해야 합니다. 따라서 ⓑ의 superficial은 deep 혹은 substantial과 같은 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The most prevalent problem kids report is that they feel like they need to be accessible at all times. Because technology allows for it, they feel an obligation. For a teen or tween who's still learning the ins and outs of social interactions, it's even worse. Here's how this behavior plays out sometimes: Your child texts one of his friends, and the friend doesn't text back right away. Now it's easy for your child to think, "This person doesn't want to be my friend anymore!" So he texts again, and again, and again ─ "blowing up their phone." question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Technologists are always on the lookout for quantifiable metrics. Measurable inputs to a model are their lifeblood, and like a social scientist, a technologist needs to identify concrete measures, or "proxies," for assessing progress. This need for quantifiable proxies produces a bias toward measuring things that are easy to quantify. But simple metrics can take us further away from the important goals we really care about, which may require complicated metrics or be extremely difficult, or perhaps impossible, to reduce to any measure. And when we have imperfect or bad proxies, we can easily fall under the illusion that we are solving for a good end without actually making genuine progress toward a worthy solution. The problem of proxies results in technologists frequently substituting what is measurable for what is meaningful. As the saying goes, "Not everything that counts can be counted, and not everything that can be counted counts."
summary_sentence: Technologists tend to (A)____________ measurable metrics, but this can often lead them to (B)____________ what truly matters.
options: ① rely on overlook
② extinguish overlook
③ utilize notice
④ monitor notice
⑤ improve emphasize

question: 21. 다음 글의 요지를 <조건>에 맞게 한 문장으로 쓰시오.
passage: We tend to overrate the impact of new technologies in part because older technologies have become absorbed into the furniture of our lives, so as to be almost invisible. Take the baby bottle. Here is a simple implement that has transformed a fundamental human experience for vast numbers of infants and mothers, yet it finds no place in our histories of technology. This technology might be thought of as a classic time-shifting device, as it enables mothers to exercise more control over the timing of feeding. It can also function to save time, as bottle feeding allows for someone else to substitute for the mother's time. Potentially, therefore, it has huge implications for the management of time in everyday life, yet it is entirely overlooked in discussions of high-speed society.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 어휘를 모두 사용할 것
단어 추가 시, 윗글에 나오는 단어만을 사용할 것
필요시 단어의 형태를 변형하여 사용할 것
answer: The influence of existing technologies is underestimated compared to emerging ones.
explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 우리가 신기술의 영향력은 과대평가하는 반면, 이미 일상에 스며든 기존 기술(예: 젖병)의 영향력은 과소평가한다는 것입니다. <보기>의 단어들을 활용하여 '기존 기술의 영향력은 신흥 기술들에 비해 과소평가된다'는 문장을 완성해야 합니다. compare를 compared to로 변형하고, 수동태(is underestimated)를 활용하는 것이 핵심입니다.

question: 23. 윗글을 읽고, 글의 흐름상 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 내용을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
passage: Beethoven's drive to create something novel is a reflection of his state of curiosity. Our brains experience a sense of reward when we create something new in the process of exploring something uncertain, such as a musical phrase that we've never played or heard before. When our curiosity leads to something novel, the resulting reward brings us a sense of pleasure. A number of investigators have modeled how curiosity influences musical composition. In the case of Beethoven, computer modeling focused on the thirty-two piano sonatas written after age thirteen revealed that the musical patterns found in all of Beethoven's music (A)______________________________, while novel patterns, including patterns that (B)______________________________, increased. In other words, Beethoven's music became less predictable over time as his curiosity drove the exploration of new musical ideas. Curiosity is a powerful driver of human (C)___________.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 표현을 모두 한 번씩 사용할 것 ( be / a particular / sonata / decrease / later sonatas / unique to / in )
필요시 단어를 변형하되, 단어를 추가하지 말 것

passage: Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested, that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. Revolutionaries have always looked to the past to frame their future cause, as is amply illustrated by examples from nationalism to communism. The future has often been seen as variously a recovery of a lost time, as a replication of what is established, or as a model bequeathed by a heroic age long gone. The writing of history is based on understanding or explaining future outcomes that were not known to contemporaries, since the historian has the benefit of hindsight and the past is nothing more than the accumulation of futures that are now our past. So, rather than see the hand of the past always shaping the future, perhaps it can be seen in reverse, with the past - in the sense of our understanding of it - being shaped by our orientation to the future.

question: 18. 다음 Gesture에 관한 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information and we solve problems less well. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.

question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: As a general rule, it's better if your definition corresponds as closely as possible to the way in which the term is ordinarily used in the kinds of debates to which your claims are pertinent.
ordered_passages: (A) For example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something the person having it has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories: I would have a memory-type experience, but this would not be of something that I had actually experienced.(B) There will be, however, occasions where it is appropriate, even necessary, to coin special uses through what philosophers call stipulative definition. This would be the case where the current lexicon is not able to make distinctions that you think are philosophically important.(C) To call this a memory would be misleading. question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other? This is because the brain has something of a two-tier memory system at work when it comes to retrieving memories, and this gives rise to a common yet infuriating sensation: recognising someone, but not being able to remember how or why, or what their name is. This happens because the brain differentiates between familiarity and recall. To clarify, familiarity (or recognition) is when you encounter someone or something and you know you've done so before. But beyond that, you've got nothing; all you can say is this person/thing is already in your memories. Recall is when you can access the original memory of how and why you know this person; recognition is just flagging up the fact that the memory exists.
summary_sentence: Recognition and recall are (A)____________: Recognition means knowing we have encountered someone before, while recall allows us to (B)____________ the details of how and why we know them.
options: ① distinct ... retrieve
② related ... erase
③ identical ... construct
④ opposite ... block
⑤ similar ... guess

This approach led to the punk movement, whose musicians even made it a condition for their music to be non-virtuosic and accessible to all in the 1970s. question: 7. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition. But it's important to understand the limits of dictionary definitions. More often than not, a definition in a dictionary requires readers to have a fairly robust understanding of the language already at their disposal. In other words, a dictionary functions in many cases as a cross-reference or translator between words one knows and words that one doesn't yet know. Even the most obscure words in a dictionary, say, for example, "pulchritudinous" or "kalokagathia," must be defined using words that the reader already knows and understands. Otherwise, the dictionary isn't very helpful.

question: 14. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: In most cases, it's best to define a term in a way that matches how people usually use it in real conversations or debates. However, sometimes there is no good word in everyday language to describe something exactly. In these cases, philosophers often make up new words or give special meanings to existing words. This is called a stipulative definition. This would be the case where the current lexicon is not able to make distinctions that you think are philosophically important. For example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something the person having it has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories: I would have a memory-type experience, but this would not be of something that I had actually experienced. To call this a memory would be misleading. For this reason, philosophers have coined the special term "quasi-memory," which refers to an experience that feels like a memory but isn't actually one.
summary_sentence: The passage explains that when ordinary language (A)___________ a term to describe a concept, philosophers create new words through stipulative definition, such as the term "quasi-memory," which refers to (B)___________ memory-like experiences.
options: ① (A) requires / (B) irrational
② (A) lacks / (B) hypothetical
③ (A) manipulates / (B) theoretical
④ (A) holds / (B) fictional
⑤ (A) possesses / (B) logical
explanation: 글의 내용에 따라 일상적인 어휘가 부족할 경우(lacks), 해당 개념을 설명하기 위해 가상의(hypothetical) 혹은 새로운 어휘를 만든다는 내용이므로 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고 <보기>의 단어들을 알맞게 배열하여, 본문의 흐름에 맞게 빈칸을 완성하시오. (필요한 경우 어형변화 시킬 것)
passage: Stress doesn't just harm your body - __________________________________________________, making you feel even more mentally tired. question: 26. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 단어를 <보기>에서 골라 쓰시오. (필요한 경우 어형변화 시킬 것)
