For example, forcing the turnout beyond one's hip flexibility to achieve a more dramatic look can result in (B)___________ pain that may shorten a dancer's career. Instead, dancers should focus on refining their own natural movement within safe boundaries. By understanding their physical strengths and weaknesses, dancers can adapt movements to fit their bodies and make (C)___________ progress without risking harm. Ultimately, self-awareness isn't just helpful - It's a vital part of a dancer's journey toward achieving a virtuosic level and longevity in the field.*pirouette :팽이처럼 도는 동작

explanation: (A) 문맥상 이러한 신체적 차이를 '인식하는 것'이 중요하므로 recognize를 동명사 주어 형태인 recognizing으로 변형합니다. (B) 무리한 동작으로 인해 무용수의 수명을 단축시킬 수 있는 '만성적인' 통증이 발생할 수 있으므로 chronic이 적절합니다. (C) 신체적 한계를 이해함으로써 부상 없이 '지속적인' 발전을 이룰 수 있으므로 continue를 형용사인 continuous로 변형합니다.

question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared. Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have fostered higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. question: 2. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

question: 4. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

question: 16. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 지문에서 찾아 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오.

question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much a creative process. question: 22. 다음 글을 읽고 주제를 가장 적절하게 작성하시오. [4.0점]
passage: Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested, that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. Revolutionaries have always looked to the past to frame their future cause, as is amply illustrated by examples from nationalism to communism. The writing of history is based on understanding or explaining future outcomes that were not known to contemporaries, since the historian has the benefit of hindsight and the past is nothing more than the accumulation of futures that are now our past. So, rather than see the hand of the past always shaping the future, perhaps it can be seen in reverse, with the past ─ in the sense of our understanding of it ─ being shaped by our orientation to the future.

passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?*posit: 상정하다

question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. passage: As a general rule, it's better if your definition corresponds as closely as possible to the way in which the term is ordinarily used in the kinds of debates to which your claims are pertinent. This would be the case where the current lexicon is not able to make distinctions that you think are philosophically important. ⓐFor example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something the person having it has experienced. ⓑSuch a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories; I would have a memory-type experience. ⓒIt's a way of acknowledging that we may not always remember every detail of our past, but we still have a sense of psychological continuity that connects us to our past and future selves. ⓓTo call this a memory would be misleading. ⓔFor this reason, philosophers have coined the special term 'quasi-memory' to refer to these hypothetical memory-like experiences.

question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were funded in part by the sugar industry. The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared. Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have fostered higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. Stories such as this one fuel suspicion - but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. Funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since been made compulsory.

For example, people who take vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who don't take vitamins. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while holding everything else constant.

question: 4. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: People behave in highly predictable ways when they experience certain thoughts. When they agree, they nod their heads. So far, no surprise, but according to an area of research known as "proprioceptive psychology," the process also works in reverse. Get people to behave in a certain way and you cause them to have certain thoughts. The idea was initially controversial, but fortunately it was supported by a compelling experiment. Participants in a study were asked to fixate on various products moving across a large computer screen. After that, they were also asked to indicate whether the items appealed to them. Some of the items moved vertically (causing the participants to nod their heads while watching), and others moved horizontally (resulting in a side-to-side head movement). Participants preferred vertically moving products without being aware that their "yes" and "no" head movements had played a key role in their decisions. This phenomenon highlights how we can shape our decisions by simply altering our behavior.

subjective_conditions: 1. (A)에는 본문에서 한 단어를 찾아 변형하여 주어진 철자로 시작하는 총 12철자의 한 단어를 쓰시오.
2. (B)에는 주어진 철자로 시작하며, [영영사전] 뜻풀이에 해당하는 총 9철자의 한 단어를 쓰시오.
3. 문맥과 어법에 맞춰 쓰시오.
(*답안지에는 주어진 철자를 포함하여 쓰시오.)
vocabulary_box: u______________: 1. done or experienced by everyone, existing or available for everyone2. existing or true at all times or in all places
explanation: 이 글은 교육이 지식의 공통된 핵심(뿌리)에 집중해야 함을 강조하며, 여러 학문을 연결하는 공통 언어의 필요성을 설명합니다. (A) 글의 맥락상 학생들이 서로 다른 과목과 수업을 연결하기 시작하면 '학문적(disciplinary)' 경계를 넘어 생각하는 법을 배우게 됩니다. 본문의 'disciplines'를 형용사형인 'disciplinary'(12철자)로 변형하여 사용할 수 있습니다. (B) 여러 학문을 연결하는 상상력은 모든 분야에 적용 가능한 성격이어야 하므로, 영영사전 정의인 '모든 이에게 존재하거나 이용 가능한(universal)'이라는 의미의 단어 'universal'(9철자)이 적합합니다.

question: 28. 다음 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: When evaluating a policy, people tend to concentrate on how the policy will fix some particular problem while ignoring or downplaying other effects it may have. Economists often refer to this situation as The Law of Unintended Consequences. For instance, suppose that you impose a tariff on imported steel in order to protect the jobs of domestic steelworkers. If you impose a high enough tariff, their jobs will indeed be protected from competition by foreign steel companies. But an unintended consequence is that the jobs of some autoworkers will be lost to foreign competition. Why? The tariff that protects steelworkers raises the price of the steel that domestic automobile makers need to build their cars. As a result, domestic automobile manufacturers have to raise the prices of their cars, making them relatively less attractive than foreign cars. Raising prices tends to reduce domestic car sales, so some domestic autoworkers lose their jobs. This, in turn, can lead to a decline in overall domestic automobile production, affecting not just autoworkers but also suppliers of auto parts and related industries. Over time, the policy that was meant to support one sector of the economy (A)_____________________________, highlighting the complex trade-offs involved in economic decision-making.
subjective_conditions: 1. <보기>의 어구들은 필요시 변형하여 모두 한 번씩 포함시키시오.
2. 주어진 철자로 시작하며 [영영사전] 뜻풀이에 해당하는 명사 1개를 추가하여 쓰시오.
2-1. 명사는 복수형으로 표기할 것.
2-2. [영영사전] 뜻풀이에 나오는 단어는 사용할 수 없음.
3. 문맥과 어법에 맞춰 총 6단어로 쓰시오.
vocabulary_box: [영영사전] d_____________: 1. disturbance or problems which interrupt an event, activity, or process 2. radical change to an existing industry or market due to technological innovation
answer: ends up creating disruptions in others
explanation: 해당 지문은 경제 정책을 평가할 때 흔히 발생하는 '의도치 않은 결과의 법칙(The Law of Unintended Consequences)'에 대해 다루고 있습니다. 철강 노동자를 보호하기 위해 부과한 관세가 결과적으로 자동차 산업의 비용 상승과 판매 감소를 불러와 자동차 노동자들의 일자리를 잃게 만드는 사례를 보여줍니다. 빈칸 (A)에는 한 분야를 도우려던 정책이 '결국 다른 분야에서 혼란(문제)을 야기하게 된다'는 내용이 들어가야 합니다. 주어 'the policy'에 맞춰 'end'를 'ends'로 수 일치 시키고, '결국 ~하게 되다'라는 표현인 'end up -ing' 구문을 사용하여 'ends up creating'을 구성합니다. 영영사전 정의에 부합하는 단어 'disruptions'를 목적어로 사용하고 'in others'를 덧붙여 총 6단어의 문장을 완성할 수 있습니다.

question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Free play is nature's means of teaching children that they are not helpless. In play, away from adults, children really do have control and can practice asserting it. In free play, children learn to make their own decisions, solve their own problems, create and follow rules, and get along with others as equals rather than as obedient or rebellious subordinates. In active outdoor play, children deliberately dose themselves with moderate amounts of fear and they thereby learn how to control not only their bodies, but also their fear. In social play children learn how to negotiate with others, how to please others, and how to manage and overcome the anger that can arise from conflicts. None of these lessons can be taught through verbal means; they can be learned only through experience, which free play provides.
options: ① 부모는 자유 놀이를 통해 아이들과 애착 관계를 강화할 수 있다.
② 아이들은 자유 놀이를 통해 삶의 중요한 기술을 터득한다.
③ 아이의 정서 안정을 위해 또래 갈등을 최소화해야 한다.
④ 말로 가르치는 교육이 경험 중심의 학습보다 효과적이다.
⑤ 부모의 개입은 아이의 자율성과 독립성을 높여준다.
explanation: 자유놀이가 아이들에게 무기력하지 않음을 가르치고 통제력, 결정력, 문제해결 능력 등 삶의 기술을 터득하게 해 준다는 내용이므로 2번이 요지로 적절하다.

question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A common but incorrect assumption is that we are creatures of reason when, in fact, we are creatures of both reason and emotion. We cannot get by on reason alone since any reason always eventually leads to a feeling. Should I get a wholegrain cereal or a chocolate cereal? I can list all the reasons I want, but the reasons have to be based on something. For example, if my goal is to eat healthy, I can choose the wholegrain cereal, but what is my reason for wanting to be healthy? I can list more and more reasons such as wanting to live longer, spending more quality time with loved ones, etc., but what are the reasons for those reasons? You should be able to see by now that reasons are ultimately based on non-reason such as values, feelings, or emotions. These deep-seated values, feelings, and emotions we have are rarely a result of reasoning, but can certainly be influenced by reasoning. We have values, feelings, and emotions before we begin to reason and long before we begin to reason effectively.
options: ① logical structure behind setting personal goals
② need to control emotional impulses through discipline
③ how people make healthier choices through rational thinking
④ emotional foundation of decision-making and human reasoning
⑤ why logical reasoning should always guide our everyday decisions
explanation: 이 글은 인간이 이성적인 존재일 뿐만 아니라 감정적인 존재임을 강조하며, 모든 이성적 추론과 결정의 근저에는 결국 가치, 느낌, 감정과 같은 비이성적인 요소가 자리 잡고 있다는 것을 설명하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 개인적인 목표 설정 뒤에 숨겨진 논리적 구조
② 훈련을 통해 감정적 충동을 통제할 필요성
③ 사람들이 합리적 사고를 통해 더 건강한 선택을 하는 방법
④ 의사 결정과 인간 추론의 감정적 토대
⑤ 왜 논리적 추론이 항상 우리의 일상적 결정을 안내해야 하는가

question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Winning turns on a self-conscious awareness that others are watching. It's a lot easier to move under the radar when no one knows you and no one is paying attention. You can mess up and be rough and get dirty because no one even knows you're there. But as soon as you start to win, and others start to notice, you're suddenly ⓐ<u>aware</u> that you're being observed. You're being judged. You worry that others will ⓑ<u>discover</u> your flaws and weaknesses. And you also start ⓒ<u>revealing</u> them, so you can be a good role model and good citizen and a leader that others can respect. There is nothing wrong with that. But if you do it at the expense of being who you really are, making decisions that ⓓ<u>satisfy</u> others instead of pleasing yourself, you're not going to be in that position very long. When you start apologizing for who you are, you stop growing and you stop ⓔ<u>winning</u>. Permanently.
explanation: 글의 맥락상 승리하게 되어 타인의 시선을 의식하게 되면, 사람들은 자신의 결점과 약점을 드러내기보다는 남들에게 존경받는 좋은 롤모델이 되기 위해 그것들을 감추려고 노력하게 됩니다. 따라서 '드러내는(revealing)' 것이 아니라 '숨기는(hiding)' 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Creativity can have an effect on productivity. Creativity leads some individuals to recognize problems that others do not see, but which may be very difficult. Charles Darwin's approach to the speciation problem is a good example of this; he chose a very ⓐ<u>challenging</u> problem, speciation, which led him into a long period of data collection and deliberation. This choice of problem did not allow for a quick attack or a simple experiment. In such cases creativity may actually ⓑ<u>increase</u> productivity (as measured by publication counts) because effort is focused on difficult problems. For others, whose creativity is more focused on methods and technique, creativity may lead to solutions that ⓒ<u>eliminate</u> unnecessary steps in solving a problem. We can see an example in the development of the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) which enables us to amplify small pieces of DNA in a short time. This type of creativity might reduce the number of steps or replace unreliable ones with steps that are more likely to ⓓ<u>succeed</u>. This, in turn, leads to ⓔ<u>improved</u> productivity.
explanation: 다윈의 사례처럼 매우 어렵고 도전적인 문제를 선택하여 창의성을 발휘할 경우, 오랜 시간 동안 데이터 수집과 숙고를 거쳐야 하므로 짧은 기간 동안의 출판물 수 등으로 측정되는 생산성은 '증가(increase)'하는 것이 아니라 오히려 '감소(decrease)'하게 됩니다.

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Human beings like certainty. This liking stems from our ancient ancestors who needed to survive alongside saber-toothed tigers and poisonous berries. Our brains evolved to help us attend to threats, keep away from them, and remain ⓐ<u>alive</u> afterward. In fact, we learned that the more certain we were about something, ⓑ<u>the better</u> chance we had of making the right choice. Is this berry the same shape as last time? The same size? If I know for certain it is, my brain will direct me to eat it because I know it's ⓒ<u>safe</u>. And if I'm uncertain, my brain will send out a danger alert to protect me. The dependence on certainty all those millennia ago ensured our survival to the present day, and the danger-alert system continues to ⓓ<u>protect</u> us. This is achieved by our brains labeling new, vague, or unpredictable everyday events and experiences as ⓔ<u>certain</u>. Our brains then generate sensations, thoughts, and action plans to keep us safe from the uncertain element, and we live to see another day.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 뇌가 새롭고 모호하거나 예측할 수 없는 사건을 불확실한 것으로 꼬리표를 붙임으로써 우리를 안전하게 지킬 수 있다는 맥락이므로 ⓔ는 certain이 아니라 uncertain이 되어야 한다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: What consequences of eating too many grapes and other sweet fruit could there possibly be for our brains? A few large studies have helped to shed some light. In one, higher fruit intake in older, cognitively healthy adults was linked with less volume in the hippocampus. This finding was unusual, since people who eat more fruit usually display the benefits associated with a healthy diet. In this study, however, the researchers isolated various components of the subjects' diets and found that fruit didn't seem to __________________________________. Another study from the Mayo Clinic saw a similar inverse relationship between fruit intake and volume of the cortex, the large outer layer of the brain. Researchers in the latter study noted that excessive consumption of high-sugar fruit (such as mangoes, bananas, and pineapples) may cause metabolic and cognitive problems as much as processed carbs do.
options: ① support people in following their diet plans
② be beneficial for their cognitive abilities
③ disrupt healthy brain development
④ be a risk factor for brain damage
⑤ help people overcome diabetes
explanation: 과일이 평소에는 건강식단에 긍정적이나, 당이 높은 과일을 많이 섭취한 연구(해마 및 피질 부피 감소) 등에서 과일이 그들의 인지능력에 도움을 주는 것(beneficial for their cognitive abilities) 같지는 않았다는 내용이므로 적절한 정답은 ②이다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: It seems natural to describe certain environmental conditions as 'extreme', 'harsh', 'benign' or 'stressful'. (A) It may seem obvious when conditions are 'extreme': the midday heat of a desert, the cold of an Antarctic winter, the salinity of the Great Salt Lake. (B) But this only means that these conditions are extreme for us, given our particular physiological characteristics and tolerances. (C) To a cactus there is nothing extreme about the desert conditions in which cacti have evolved; nor are the icy lands of Antarctica an extreme environment for penguins. (D) It is lazy and dangerous for the ecologist to assume that all other organisms sense the environment in the way we do. (E) Emotive words like harsh and benign, even relativities such as hot and cold, should be used by ecologists only with care.
insertion_sentence: Rather, the ecologist should try to gain a worm's-eye or plant's-eye view of the environment: to see the world as others see it.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 'Rather(대신에)'로 시작하며, 생태학자가 인간의 관점이 아닌 다른 생명체(벌레나 식물)의 관점에서 환경을 보아야 한다고 제안합니다. 이는 생태학자가 인간 중심적으로 환경을 판단하는 것이 위험하다고 비판하는 (D) 문장 뒤에 오는 것이 논리적으로 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 ⑤번에 위치하여 대안을 제시하고 그 뒤의 결론(E)으로 이어지는 것이 적절합니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [23년 3월 40번]
passage: A young child may be puzzled when asked to distinguish between the directions of right and left. (A) But that same child may have no difficulty in determining the directions of up and down or back and front. (B) Scientists propose that this occurs because, although we experience three dimensions, only two had a strong influence on our evolution: the vertical dimension as defined by gravity and, in mobile species, the front/back dimension as defined by the positioning of sensory and feeding mechanisms. (C) These influence our perception of vertical versus horizontal, far versus close, and the search for dangers from above (such as an eagle) or below (such as a snake). (D) A bear is equally dangerous from its left or the right side, but not if it is upside down. options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장은 '좌우 축은 자연에서 그만큼 중요하지 않다'는 내용입니다. (D) 앞부분까지는 수직 축(중력)과 앞뒤 축(감각기관 위치)이 진화에 큰 영향을 미쳤음을 설명하고 있습니다. (D) 뒤의 문장은 곰이 좌우 어디서 나타나든 똑같이 위험하지만 거꾸로 있을 때는 그렇지 않다는 구체적인 예시를 통해 좌우 축의 상대적 무관함(또는 대칭성)을 뒷받침하고 있으므로 (D)가 가장 적절한 위치입니다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오. [23년 3월 35번]
passage: Human processes differ from rational processes in their outcome. A process is rational if it always does the right thing based on the current information, given an ideal performance measure. In short, rational processes go by the book and assume that the book is actually correct. Human processes involve instinct, intuition, and other variables that don't necessarily reflect the book and may not even consider the existing data. As an example, the rational way to drive a car is to always follow the laws. However, traffic isn't rational; if you follow the laws precisely, you end up stuck somewhere because other drivers aren't following the laws precisely. To be successful, a self-driving car should reflect (A)__________ behavior, not assuming that all drivers are (B)__________.
subjective_conditions: (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 각각 한 단어로 작성할 것
본문에 있는 단어만을 변형 없이 그대로 사용할 것
조건을 미충족한 경우나 어법 또는 철자 오류가 있는 경우 감점 있음
explanation: 이 글은 인간의 과정과 이성적인 과정의 차이에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 자율 주행 자동차가 성공하기 위해서는 모든 운전자가 이성적(rational)이라고 가정해서는 안 되며, 실제 도로 상황인 인간의(human) 행동을 반영해야 합니다.

question: 9. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Development of the human body from a single cell provides many examples of the structural richness that is possible when the repeated production of random variation is combined with nonrandom selection. All phases of body development from embryo to adult exhibit random activities at the cellular level, and body formation depends on the new possibilities generated by these activities coupled with selection of those outcomes that satisfy previously built-in criteria. Always new structure is based on old structure, and at every stage selection favors some cells and eliminates others. The survivors serve to produce new cells that undergo further rounds of selection. Except in the immune system, cells and extensions of cells are not genetically selected during development, but rather, are positionally selected. Those in the right place that make the right connections are stimulated, and those that don't are eliminated. This process is much like sculpting. A natural consequence of the strategy is great variability from individual to individual at the cell and molecular levels, even though large-scale structures are quite similar.
options: ① The selection process in body formation follows previously established criteria.
② Body development is a continuous process in which old structures serve as the foundation for new ones.
③ Cells that fail to make the right connections are eliminated during development.
④ Cells are selected based on rules that are genetically determined.
⑤ In the process of human body development, variability can be seen at the cellular and molecular levels.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 면역 체계를 제외하고, 발달 과정 중 세포와 세포의 확장은 유전적으로 선택되는 것이 아니라 '위치적으로(positionally)' 선택된다고 설명되어 있습니다. 따라서 유전적으로 결정된 규칙에 따라 세포가 선택된다는 4번 선지는 본문의 내용과 정반대이므로 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 신체 형성의 선택 과정은 이전에 확립된 기준을 따른다.
② 신체 발달은 오래된 구조가 새로운 구조의 기초 역할을 하는 연속적인 과정이다.
③ 발달 과정 중 적절한 연결을 하지 못한 세포는 제거된다.
④ 세포는 유전적으로 결정된 규칙에 근거하여 선택된다.
⑤ 인체 발달 과정에서 세포 및 분자 수준의 가변성을 볼 수 있다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Beethoven's drive to create something novel is a reflection of his state of curiosity. Our brains experience a sense of reward when we create something new in the process of exploring something uncertain, such as a musical phrase that we've never played or heard before. When our curiosity leads to something novel, the resulting reward brings us a sense of pleasure. A number of investigators have modeled how curiosity influences musical composition. In the case of Beethoven, computer modeling focused on the thirty-two piano sonatas written after age thirteen revealed that the musical patterns found in all of Beethoven's music decreased in later sonatas, while novel patterns, including patterns that were unique to a particular sonata, increased. In other words, Beethoven's music became less predictable over time as his curiosity drove the exploration of new musical ideas. Curiosity is a powerful driver of human creativity.
options: ① The Life and Struggles of Beethoven
② The Decline of Beethoven's Music in His Later Years
③ The Curious Composer: Painting Sound with New Colors
④ The Great Composer of Perfectly Predictable Symphony
⑤ Curiosity vs. Creativity, What's More Important in Composition?
explanation: 이 글은 베토벤의 음악적 창의성의 원동력이 '호기심'이었음을 설명하며, 시간이 흐름에 따라 그의 음악이 정형화된 패턴에서 벗어나 더 새롭고 예측 불가능한 형태로 발전했음을 보여줍니다. 따라서 '호기심 많은 작곡가: 새로운 색채로 소리를 그리다'가 글의 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 베토벤의 삶과 투쟁
② 베토벤 말년 음악의 쇠퇴
③ 호기심 많은 작곡가: 새로운 색채로 소리를 그리다
④ 완벽하게 예측 가능한 교향곡의 위대한 작곡가
⑤ 호기심 대 창의성, 작곡에서 무엇이 더 중요한가?

question: 11. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Dancers often push themselves to the limits of their physical capabilities. But that push is misguided if it is directed toward accomplishing something physically impossible. For instance, a tall dancer with long feet may wish to perform repetitive vertical jumps to fast music, pointing his feet while in the air and lowering his heels to the floor between jumps. That may be impossible no matter how strong the dancer is. But a short-footed dancer may have no trouble! Another dancer may be struggling to complete a half-turn in the air. Understanding the connection between a rapid turn rate and the alignment of the body close to the rotation axis tells her how to accomplish her turn successfully. In both of these cases, understanding and working within the constraints imposed by nature and described by physical laws allows dancers to work efficiently, minimizing potential risk of injury.
options: ① Jumping Higher: The Secret to Becoming a Tall Dancer
② Mastering Dance by Disregarding All Physical Limitations
③ The Power of Belief: Why Dancers Should Push Beyond Their Limits
④ The Importance of Pushing Beyond Natural Constraints in Dance
⑤ Optimizing Dance Performance by Acknowledging Physical Realities
explanation: 이 글은 무용수가 신체적 조건과 물리적 법칙과 같은 자연적 제약(physical realities)을 이해하고 그 안에서 연습할 때 효율적으로 기량을 발휘하고 부상을 방지할 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '신체적 현실을 인정함으로써 무용 공연을 최적화하기'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 더 높이 점프하기: 키가 큰 무용수가 되는 비결
② 모든 신체적 한계를 무시함으로써 무용 마스터하기
③ 믿음의 힘: 왜 무용수는 자신의 한계를 넘어서야 하는가
④ 무용에서 자연적 제약을 넘어서는 것의 중요성
⑤ 신체적 현실을 인정함으로써 무용 공연을 최적화하기

question: 12. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In order to bring the ever-increasing costs of home care for elderly and needy persons under control, managers of home care providers have introduced management systems. These systems specify tasks of home care workers and the time and budget available to perform these tasks. Electronic reporting systems require home care workers to report on their activities and the time spent, thus making the distribution of time and money visible and, in the perception of managers, controllable. This, in the view of managers, has contributed to the resolution of the problem. However, while these systems aim to enhance efficiency, home care workers often perceive their work not merely as a set of separate tasks to be performed as efficiently as possible, but as a vital service to be provided to clients with whom they have developed meaningful relationships. This includes having conversations with clients and enquiring about the person's well-being. Restricted time and the requirement to report may be perceived as obstacles that make it impossible to deliver the service that is needed. If the management systems are too rigid, this may result in home care workers becoming overloaded and demotivated.
options: ① strategies for reducing costs in home care facilities
② benefits of technology in improving home care services
③ exploring the impact of social media on home care awareness
④ challenges faced by home care workers with newly introduced systems
⑤ how to enhance communication between home care workers and clients
explanation: 이 글은 노인 및 취약 계층을 위한 홈케어 비용을 통제하기 위해 도입된 관리 시스템이 홈케어 노동자들에게 어떤 영향을 미치는지 설명하고 있습니다. 관리자들은 시스템을 통해 효율성과 가시성을 높이려 하지만, 노동자들은 고객과의 정서적 유대와 관계를 중요하게 여기기 때문에 이러한 시스템을 서비스 제공의 장애물로 인식하며, 결과적으로 과부하와 의욕 저하를 겪게 된다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 ④ '새로 도입된 시스템으로 인해 홈케어 노동자들이 직면한 어려움'입니다.
options_translation: ① 재가 복지 시설의 비용 절감 전략
② 재가 복지 서비스 향상에 있어 기술의 이점
③ 재가 복지에 대한 인식에 소셜 미디어가 미치는 영향 탐색
④ 새로 도입된 시스템으로 인해 재가 복지 노동자들이 겪는 어려움
⑤ 재가 복지 노동자와 고객 간의 의사소통 강화 방법

question: 14. 다음 밑줄 친 it finds no place in our histories of technology가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We tend to overrate the impact of new technologies in part because older technologies have become absorbed into the furniture of our lives, so as to be almost invisible. Take the baby bottle. Here is a simple implement that has transformed a fundamental human experience for vast numbers of infants and mothers, yet <u>it finds no place in our histories of technology</u>. This technology might be thought of as a classic timeshifting device, as it enables mothers to exercise more control over the timing of feeding. It can also function to save time, as bottle feeding allows for someone else to substitute for the mother's time. Potentially, therefore, it has huge implications for the management of time in everyday life, yet it is entirely overlooked in discussions of high-speed society.
options: ① It is only relevant in discussions about infant care, not technology
② It is a recent invention that hasn't been recognized in historical accounts
③ It has become so familiar in everyday life that its importance is taken for granted
④ It has a minimal impact on society, so it is excluded from the history of technology
⑤ It does not contribute to technological advancement, becoming historically insignificant
explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 우리가 새로운 기술의 영향력은 과대평가하는 반면, 오래된 기술은 일상 속에 너무 깊이 스며들어 거의 보이지 않게 된다는 것입니다. '젖병'은 인간의 근본적인 경험을 변화시킨 중요한 도구임에도 불구하고, 일상의 가구처럼 너무나 익숙해졌기 때문에 기술사에서 언급되지 않거나 당연하게 여겨진다는 의미입니다. 따라서 ③번 '일상생활에서 매우 친숙해져서 그 중요성이 당연하게 여겨진다'가 가장 적절한 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 그것은 기술이 아닌 유아 보육에 관한 논의에만 관련이 있다
② 그것은 역사적 기록에서 인정받지 못한 최근의 발명품이다
③ 그것은 일상생활에서 매우 친숙해져서 그 중요성이 당연하게 여겨진다
④ 그것은 사회에 미치는 영향이 미미하여 기술사에서 제외된다
⑤ 그것은 기술적 발전에 기여하지 않아 역사적으로 중요하지 않게 된다

question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: The most prevalent problem kids report is that they feel like they need to be accessible at all times. Because technology allows for it, they feel an obligation. It's easy for most of us to ⓐempathize ─ you probably feel the same pressure in your own life! It is really challenging to deal with the fact that we're human and can't always respond ⓑinstantly. For a teen or tween who's still learning the ins and outs of social interactions, it's more ⓒproblematic. Here's how this behavior plays out sometimes: Your child texts one of his friends, and the friend doesn't text back right away. Now it's not ⓓdifficult for your child to think, "This person doesn't want to be my friend anymore!" So he texts again, and again, and again ─ "blowing up their phone." This can be stress-inducing and even read as ⓔconsiderate. But you can see how easily this could happen.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 계속해서 문자하는 이 행동이 배려하는(considerate) 것으로 읽힐 리 만무하다. 이것은 공격적이거나 스트레스를 유발하는 것으로 읽힐 수 있다. ⓔ가 부적절하다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Empathy is frequently listed as one of the most desired skills in an employer or employee, although without specifying exactly what is meant by empathy. Some businesses stress cognitive empathy, emphasizing the need for leaders to understand the perspective of employees and customers when negotiating deals and making decisions. Others stress affective empathy and empathic concern, emphasizing the ability of leaders to gain trust from employees and customers by treating them with real concern and compassion. When some consultants argue that ________________________________, what that translates to is that companies should conduct good market research. In other words, an "empathic" company understands the needs and wants of its customers and seeks to fulfill those needs and wants. When some people speak of design with empathy, what that translates to is that companies should take into account the specific needs of different populations ─ the blind, the deaf, the elderly, non-English speakers, the colorblind, and so on ─ when designing products.
options: ① thriving companies strategically nurture practical empathy
② companies need reliable sources to provide market information
③ employees find customers for their business and foster analytical skills
④ empathic leaders make critical business decisions and execute them successfully
⑤ successful companies blend consumer behavior and economic trends to confirm and improve their business idea
explanation: 좋은 시장조사를 해야 한다는 것과 제품 디자인 시 공감을 활용하라는 것은 결국 번창하는 회사들이 전략적으로 '실용적인 공감'을 육성해야 함을 가리킨다. 따라서 1번이 알맞다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We are the only species that seasons its food, deliberately altering it with the highly flavored plant parts we call herbs and spices. It's quite possible that our taste for spices has an evolutionary root. Many spices have antibacterial properties ─ in fact, common seasonings such as garlic, onion, and oregano inhibit the growth of almost every bacterium tested. And the cultures that make the heaviest use of spices ─ think of the garlic and black pepper of Thai food, the ginger and coriander of India, the chili peppers of Mexico ─ come from warmer climates, where _______________________________. In contrast, the most lightly spiced cuisines ─ those of Scandinavia and northern Europe ─ are from cooler climates. Our uniquely human attention to flavor, in this case the flavor of spices, turns out to have arisen as a matter of life and death.
options: ① using fewer spices is a bigger issue for the food preferences
② changing eating habits to improve your health tends to be common
③ the geographical characteristics of the region are taken into account
④ the prevalence of bacterial contamination poses a more significant challenge
⑤ individuals often exhibit a marked preference for dishes enriched with diverse seasonings
explanation: 따뜻한 기후에서는 세균 오염의 확산이 더 중대한 문제가 되기 때문에 항균 성분이 있는 향신료를 더 많이 사용한다는 내용이 문맥상 자연스럽다. 따라서 4번이 적절하다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is a common assumption that most vagrant birds are ultimately doomed, aside from the rare cases where individuals are able to reorientate and return to their normal ranges. In turn, it is also commonly assumed that ___________________________________________. This is undoubtedly true for the majority of cases, as the most likely outcome of any given vagrancy event is that the individual will fail to find enough resources, and/or be exposed to inhospitable environmental conditions, and perish. However, there are many lines of evidence to suggest that vagrancy can, on rare occasions, dramatically alter the fate of populations, species or even whole ecosystems. Despite being infrequent, these events can be extremely important when viewed at the timescales over which ecological and evolutionary processes unfold. The most profound consequences of vagrancy relate to the establishment of new breeding sites, new migration routes and wintering locations. Each of these can occur through different mechanisms, and at different frequencies, and they each have their own unique importance.
options: ① the birds' sense of direction is not innate but acquired
② vagrancy is generally considered non-influential in the ecosystem
③ vagrancy is typically viewed as having significant impact on species diversity
④ the routes of the birds are being disrupted by radical environmental changes
⑤ a mutant bird has a relatively unimportant evolutionary force in large populations
explanation: 이 글은 길을 잃은 새(vagrant birds)가 생태계에 미치는 영향에 대해 다루고 있습니다. 대다수의 경우 길을 잃은 새는 자원을 찾지 못하거나 열악한 환경에 노출되어 죽게 된다는 일반적인 가정을 언급한 뒤, 이와 마찬가지로 길을 잃는 것(vagrancy)이 생태계 전반에 미미한 영향만을 준다는 가정이 일반적임을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 문장에서 '이것은 대다수의 경우 확실히 사실이다'라고 하며 길을 잃은 개체가 멸절하는 상황을 묘사하므로, 빈칸에는 길을 잃는 행위가 생태계에 별다른 영향을 주지 않는다는 내용인 ②가 가장 적절합니다. 이후 'However'를 통해 드문 경우지만 이것이 종이나 생태계의 운명을 바꿀 수 있다는 반전의 내용을 전개합니다.
options_translation: ① 새들의 방향 감각은 타고난 것이 아니라 습득된 것이다
② 길을 잃는 것은 일반적으로 생태계에서 영향력이 없는 것으로 간주된다
③ 길을 잃는 것은 보통 종 다양성에 상당한 영향을 미치는 것으로 여겨진다
④ 새들의 경로가 급격한 환경 변화에 의해 방해받고 있다
⑤ 돌연변이 새는 큰 개체군에서 상대적으로 중요하지 않은 진화적 힘을 가진다

question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Intuition can be great, but it ought to be hard-earned. Experts, for example, are able to think on their feet because they've invested thousands of hours in learning and practice: their intuition has become data-driven. Only then are they able to act quickly in accordance with their internalized expertise and evidence-based experience. Yet most people are not experts, though they often think they are. Most of us, especially when we interact with others on social media, act with expert-like speed and conviction, offering a wide range of opinions on global crises, without the substance of knowledge that supports it. And thanks to AI, which ensures that our messages are delivered to an audience more inclined to believing it, our delusions of expertise can be reinforced by a situation _______________________________________. We have an interesting tendency to find people more open-minded, rational, and sensible when they think just like us.
options: ① where we accumulated hard-earned knowledge through years of hard work
② of relying entirely on data-driven approaches to interact with content on the web
③ in which intuition becomes the primary method for offering opinions on global issues
④ that came up between the evidence-based experience and the substance of knowledge
⑤ where we are exposed only to opinions and information that conform to our existing beliefs
explanation: 이 글은 전문가와 비전문가의 직관의 차이와, 소셜 미디어 및 AI로 인해 강화되는 가짜 전문성(delusions of expertise)에 대해 설명합니다. 전문가의 직관은 수천 시간의 학습과 실천으로 만들어진 것이지만, 일반인들은 근거 없는 의견을 전문가처럼 확신하며 내뱉습니다. 특히 AI는 사용자의 기존 믿음에 부합하는 정보를 더 많이 제공함으로써 이러한 착각을 강화시킵니다. 빈칸 뒤에서 우리와 똑같이 생각하는 사람을 더 합리적이라고 느끼는 경향을 언급하므로, 빈칸에는 기존의 믿음에 일치하는 정보에만 노출되는 상황을 뜻하는 ⑤가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 수년간의 노력을 통해 힘들게 얻은 지식을 축적한 곳
② 웹의 콘텐츠와 상호작용하기 위해 전적으로 데이터 기반 접근 방식에 의존하는 것
③ 직관이 글로벌 문제에 대한 의견을 제공하는 주요 방법이 되는 것
④ 증거 기반의 경험과 지식의 실체 사이에서 나타난 것
⑤ 우리의 기존 믿음에 부합하는 의견과 정보에만 노출되는 곳

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Emotion socialization ─ learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them ─ starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may intrude on adolescents' autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.↓ Emotion socialization starts early, with parents having a(n) (A)____________ influence on the development of emotion management, but as children grow into adolescents, parents need to (B)____________ their approach to encourage autonomy while offering indirect emotional support.
options: ① crucial / sustain
② foremost / modify
③ marginal / advocate
④ unbiased / adjust
⑤ restrictive / formulate
explanation: 초기에는 관리 발달에 주된(foremost) 영향을 가지나 성숙함에 다라 접근법을 수정해야(modify) 함.

question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If you had wanted to create a "selfdriving" car in the 1950s, your best option might have been to strap a brick to the accelerator. Yes, the vehicle would have been able to move forward on its own, but it could not slow down, stop, or turn to avoid barriers. Obviously not ideal. But does that mean the entire concept of the self-driving car is not worth pursuing? No, it only means that at the time we did not yet have the tools we now possess to help enable vehicles to operate both autonomously and safely. This oncedistant dream now seems within our reach. It is much the same story in medicine. Two decades ago, we were still taping bricks to accelerators. Today, we are approaching the point where we can begin to bring some appropriate technology to bear in ways that advance our understanding of patients as unique individuals. In fact, many patients are already wearing devices that monitor their conditions in real time, which allows doctors to talk to their patients in a specific, refined, and feedback-driven way that was not even possible a decade ago.↓ Just as self-driving cars have evolved from crude concepts to (A)___________ technology, medicine has advanced to provide (B)___________ tracking and care for patients.
options: ① integrated / prompt
② outstanding / cost-effective
③ cutting-edge / long-distance
④ sophisticated / personalized
⑤ intermediate / long-term
explanation: 조잡한 개념에서 '정교한(sophisticated)' 기술로 나아갔고 의학도 '개인화된(personalized)' 추적, 관리로 진화했다는 게 요약문으로 적절하다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Technologists are always on the lookout for quantifiable metrics. Measurable inputs to a model are their lifeblood, and like a social scientist, a technologist needs to identify concrete measures, or "proxies," for assessing progress. This need for quantifiable proxies produces a bias toward measuring things that are easy to quantify. But simple metrics can take us further away from the important goals we really care about, which may require complicated metrics or be extremely difficult, or perhaps impossible, to reduce to any measure. And when we have imperfect or bad proxies, we can easily fall under the illusion that we are solving for a good end without actually making genuine progress toward a worthy solution. The problem of proxies results in technologists frequently substituting what is measurable for what is meaningful. As the saying goes, "Not everything that counts can be counted, and not everything that can be counted counts."↓ Although technologists (A)___________ measurable metrics, relying on simple indicators can lead them away from important goals, potentially (B)___________ meaningful progress.
options: ① prioritize / preventing
② ignore / attaining
③ prefer / ensuring
④ create / hindering
⑤ discard / achieving
explanation: 전문가들이 측정가능 지표를 우선시(prioritize)하지만, 중요 목표로부터 멀어지게 해서 진전을 가로막을(preventing/hindering) 수 있다는 요지이다.

question: 24. 윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 주어진 철자로 시작하는 한 단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: It's untrue that teens can focus on two things at once ─ what they're doing is shifting their attention from one task to another. In this digital age, teens wire their brains to make these shifts very quickly, but they are still, like everyone else, paying attention to one thing at a time, sequentially. Common sense tells us multitasking should (A)__________ brain activity, but Carnegie Mellon University scientists using the latest brain imaging technology find it doesn't. As a matter of fact, they discovered that multitasking actually (B)__________ brain activity. Neither task is done as well as if each were performed individually. Turns out the latest brain research supports the old advice "one thing at a time."It's not that kids can't do some tasks simultaneously. But if two tasks are performed at once, one of them has to be familiar. Our brains perform a familiar task on "automatic pilot" while really paying attention to the other one. That's why insurance companies consider talking on a cell phone and driving to be as dangerous as driving while drunk ─ it's the driving that goes on "automatic pilot" while the conversation really holds our attention. question: 1. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production.
ordered_passages: (A) This tendency becomes evident when the grower stops intervening, even briefly. The ecosystem begins to shift toward its natural, balanced state. Although vegetables may still grow, the yield typically declines, as competing plants take over and wildlife consumes more of the produce.

(B) To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem. This means that the grower typically removes unwanted plants that begin to grow, sprays insecticides, and fences off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables.

(C) This constant intervention is necessary because maximizing vegetable growth creates an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem. Without human interference, the ecosystem naturally tends toward a more balanced and stable condition, which would not favor high vegetable yields.
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 채소밭을 특정 상태(생산 극대화)로 유지하려는 생태계 개념을 소개합니다. (B)에서 이를 달성하기 위해 재배자가 하는 구체적인 개입(잡초 제거, 살충제 살포 등)이 먼저 나오고, (C)에서 이러한 지속적인 개입이 필요한 이유(채소 성장의 극대화는 불안정한 상태이기 때문)를 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 개입을 멈췄을 때 생태계가 자연스러운 균형 상태로 돌아가며 수확량이 줄어드는 결과를 보여주는 것이 논리적입니다.

question: 2. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]

question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: If the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other?
ordered_passages: (A) But beyond that, you've got nothing; all you can say is this person/thing is already in your memories. Recall is when you can access the original memory of how and why you know this person; recognition is just flagging up the fact that the memory exists.

(B) This is because the brain has something of a two-tier memory system at work when it comes to retrieving memories, and this gives rise to a common yet infuriating sensation: recognising someone, but not being able to remember how or why, or what their name is.

(C) This happens because the brain differentiates between familiarity and recall. To clarify, familiarity (or recognition) is when you encounter someone or something and you know you've done so before.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 왜 얼굴과 이름 중 하나만 기억나는지 질문합니다. (B)에서 이는 뇌의 '2단계 기억 시스템' 때문이라고 답하며 아는 사람 같은데 기억이 안 나는 일반적인 상황을 제시합니다. (C)에서 이를 구체화하여 '친숙함(Familiarity)'과 '회상(Recall)'을 구분하기 시작하며, (A)에서 그 차이점을 마무리 설명(recognition은 기억의 존재만 알리는 것, recall은 상세 정보에 접근하는 것)하는 순서가 적절합니다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much a creative process. A conjecture is a philosophical invention, cooked up rather mystically by the mind through the mental computation we call careful contemplation. However, until the hypothesis is tested against reality, it is not yet truly knowledge; it is just information that represents speculation. Knowledge is information that has demonstrated its usefulness. It is what is left over after cycles of experimental testing have eliminated false theories. As scientists continually test their hypotheses and modify their models to account for new and surprising data, a kind of "learning loop" emerges that statisticians call Bayesian updating. Based on Bayes' Rule, developed by eighteenth-century English statistician and philosopher Thomas Bayes, Bayesian updating refers to a mathematical process whereby an accepted theory or predictive model gets increasingly accurate through the repetitive testing of competing variants of that theory.

question: 22. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, do not depend on the quality of sensations provided by the food. question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. ⓐ<u>Despite</u> professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. question: 24. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
passage: Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition. But it's important to understand the limits of dictionary definitions. More often than not, a definition in a dictionary requires readers to have a fairly robust understanding of the language already at their disposal. ④ Dictionaries must use complex terminology to describe obscure or philosophical concepts.

question: 25. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]

(A) In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. question: 26. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 the historian has the benefit of hindsight가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested, that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. Revolutionaries have always looked to the past to frame their future cause, as is amply illustrated by examples from nationalism to communism. The future has often been seen as variously a recovery of a lost time, as a replication of what is established, or as a model bequeathed by a heroic age long gone. The writing of history is based on understanding or explaining future outcomes that were not known to contemporaries, since <u>the historian has the benefit of hindsight</u> and the past is nothing more than the accumulation of futures that are now our past. So, rather than see the hand of the past always shaping the future, perhaps it can be seen in reversal, with the past - in the sense of our understanding of it - being shaped by our orientation to the future.
options: ① historians always write about the past based only on documented facts
② historians can predict the future better than people who lived in the past
③ historians interpret past events with knowledge of the outcomes that followed
④ historians use their imagination to reconstruct forgotten historical periods
⑤ historians create new versions of history based on future possibilities
explanation: 이 글은 과거에 대한 우리의 이해가 미래에 대한 관점에 의해 영향을 받는다는 점을 설명합니다. 'the historian has the benefit of hindsight(역사가는 뒤늦게 깨닫는 이점을 가진다)'는 역사가는 당대 사람들은 알지 못했던 사건의 결과(미래의 결과)를 이미 알고 있는 상태에서 과거를 해석한다는 의미이므로, 정답은 ③번 '역사가들은 뒤따른 결과에 대한 지식을 가지고 과거의 사건들을 해석한다'가 됩니다.
options_translation: ① 역사가들은 항상 기록된 사실에만 근거하여 과거에 대해 글을 쓴다
② 역사가들은 과거에 살았던 사람들보다 미래를 더 잘 예측할 수 있다
③ 역사가들은 뒤따른 결과에 대한 지식을 가지고 과거의 사건들을 해석한다

question: 27. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: As a general rule, it's better if your definition corresponds as closely as possible to the way in which the term is ordinarily used in the kinds of debates to which your claims are pertinent.
ordered_passages: (A) To call this a memory would be misleading. So instead of calling it a memory, philosophers have coined the special term 'quasi-memory' to refer to these hypothetical memory-like experiences.(B) There will be, however, occasions where it is appropriate, even necessary, to coin special uses through what philosophers call stipulative definition. This would be the case where the current lexicon is not able to make distinctions that you think are philosophically important.(C) A case like this is one where we don't have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that isn't necessarily of something the person has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories: I would have a memory-type experience, but this would not be of something that I had actually experienced.
explanation: 주어진 글은 용어 정의가 일상적 용법과 일치하는 것이 좋다는 원칙을 제시합니다. (B)에서는 'however'를 통해 예외적으로 새로운 용어를 만드는(stipulative definition) 것이 필요한 경우를 소개합니다. (C)는 그러한 경우의 구체적인 예시(자신이 경험하지 않은 기억)를 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 이러한 예시를 '기억'이라고 부르는 것은 오해의 소지가 있으므로 철학자들이 '유사 기억(quasi-memory)'이라는 용어를 고안했음을 설명하며 마무리됩니다. 따라서 순서는 (B)-(C)-(A)가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Emotion socialization - learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them - starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may undermine adolescents' autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.
options: ① Parents' emotional socialization methods should be consistent.
② Direct emotional involvement by parents is effective for all ages.
③ Peers and media greatly influence emotional development for adolescents.
④ Parental emotional expression is directly related to their children's reactions.
⑤ Parents should support adolescents' autonomy in managing their emotional crises.

question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is a common assumption that most vagrant birds are ultimately doomed, aside from the rare cases where individuals are able to reorientate and return to their normal ranges.
ordered_passages: (A) However, there are many lines of evidence to suggest that vagrancy can, on rare occasions, dramatically alter the fate of populations, species or even whole ecosystems. question: 27. Why are large data repositories referred to as "data tombs."
passage: The fast-growing, tremendous amount of data, collected and stored in large and numerous data repositories, has far exceeded our human ability for understanding without powerful tools. As a result, data collected in large data repositories become "data tombs" - data archives that are hardly visited. Important decisions are often made based not on the information-rich data stored in data repositories but rather on a decision maker's instinct, simply because the decision maker does not have the tools to extract the valuable knowledge hidden in the vast amounts of data. Efforts have been made to develop expert system and knowledge-based technologies, which typically rely on users or domain experts to manually input knowledge into knowledge bases. However, this procedure is likely to cause biases and errors and is extremely costly and time consuming. The widening gap between data and information calls for the systematic development of tools that can turn data tombs into "golden nuggets" of knowledge.
subjective_conditions: - 주어진 어구로 시작하는 완전한 문장을 완성할 것
subjective_answer_format: → Large data repositories are called "data tombs" because ____________________________________________
answer: Large data repositories are called "data tombs" because data archives are hardly visited.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 방대한 양의 데이터가 저장소에 쌓이지만, 이를 이해할 도구가 부족하여 거의 방문되지 않는(hardly visited) 상태로 남게 되기 때문에 '데이터 무덤(data tombs)'이라 불립니다.

Efforts have been made to develop expert system and knowledge-based technologies, which typically rely on users or domain experts to manually input knowledge into knowledge bases. However, this procedure is likely to cause biases and errors and is extremely costly and time consuming. The widening gap between data and information calls for the systematic development of tools that can turn data tombs into "golden nuggets" of knowledge.

question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently: their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion. gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
options: ① Our consciousness is followed by our hands.
② People who gesture a lot are more intelligent.
③ Gesture plays a crucial role in speech and thought.
④ Thinking and speaking are completely separate processes.
⑤ Gesture is merely a secondary tool to complement speech.

question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested, that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. Revolutionaries have always looked to the past to frame their future cause, as is amply illustrated by examples from nationalism to communism. The future has often been seen as variously a recovery of a lost time, as a replication of what is established, or as a model bequeathed by a heroic age long gone. The writing of history is based on understanding or explaining future outcomes that were not known to contemporaries, since the historian has the benefit of hindsight and the past is nothing more than the accumulation of futures that are now our past. So, rather than see the hand of the past always shaping the future, perhaps it can be seen in reverse, with the past ─ in the sense of our understanding of it ─ being shaped by our orientation to the future.

question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: As a general rule, it's better if your definition corresponds as closely as possible to the way in which the term is ordinarily used in the kinds of debates to which your claims are pertinent. There will be, however, occasions where it is appropriate, even necessary, to coin special uses through what philosophers call stimulative definition. This would be the case where the current lexicon is not able to make distinctions that you think are philosophically important. For example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something the person having it has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories: I would have a memory-type experience, but this would not be of something that I had actually experienced. To call this a memory would be misleading. For this reason, philosophers have coined the special term 'quasi-memory' to refer to these hypothetical memory-like experiences.
options: ① The Power of Translation in Understanding Language
② Philosophical Language: Creating Terms for New Concepts
③ How Technology Shapes Language and Communication
④ Understanding Semantics: The Changing Meaning of Words
⑤ The Need for Specialized Definitions in Philosophical Debate

question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 13. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Commitment is the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life.
ordered_passages: (A) For example, a taxi driver transports clients while expecting payment afterward, and a construction worker works daily, trusting her employer will pay her at month's end. Both accept payment because a network of agents ensures the currency maintains its value.

(B) Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby facilitating the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. Moreover. commitments make people willing to perform actions that they would not otherwise perform.
(C) Social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage therefore depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.
explanation: 주어진 글은 약속(Commitment)이 사회 생활을 유지하는 접착제라고 정의합니다. (B)는 약속이 개인의 행동을 예측 가능하게 하여 공동 행동의 계획과 조정을 용이하게 한다는 일반적인 기능을 설명합니다. (A)는 (B)의 '평소라면 하지 않았을 행동'에 대한 구체적인 예시로 택시 운전사와 건설 노동자의 사례를 듭니다. (C)는 'therefore'를 사용하여 이러한 약속의 신뢰성 덕분에 직업, 돈, 정부와 같은 사회적 제도들이 존재하고 안정성을 유지한다는 결론을 내립니다.

question: 6. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization.
ordered_passages: (A) The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?

(B) Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent.

(C) In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 뉴턴의 사례를 통해 위대한 과학자들은 여러 번 성공한다는 점을 언급합니다. (C)에서 이러한 현상을 '마태 효과'로 설명하며 초기 성공이 가져다주는 이점들을 나열합니다. (B)에서 'Yet'과 함께 대안적인 설명인 '천부적 재능' 가설을 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 마태 효과의 정의를 다시 정리하며, 성공이 지위에 의한 것인지 내재된 재능에 의한 것인지에 대한 근본적인 의문을 제기하며 마무리하는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Commitment is the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life. Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby facilitating the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: ⓐ<u>Despite of</u> the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested, ⓑ<u>that</u> our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. question: 15. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products.

question: 17. 다음 글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
passage: Quite often the interaction between groups is socially unequal, and this is reflected in the fact that in many cases borrowing of words or constructions goes mostly or entirely in one direction, from the more powerful or prestigious group to the less favored one. question: 22. 다음 글의 (A), (B)에 해당하는 밭의 모습을 본문에서 찾아 우리말로 쓰시오. [4.0점]
passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고 요약한 문장의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. [25년 3월 23번]
passage: If the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other? This is because the brain has something of a two-tier memory system at work when it comes to retrieving memories, and this gives rise to a common yet infuriating sensation: recognising someone, but not being able to remember how or why, or what their name is. This happens because the brain differentiates between familiarity and recall. To clarify, familiarity (or recognition) is when you encounter someone or something and you know you've done so before. But beyond that, you've got nothing; all you can say is this person/thing is already in your memories. Recall is when you can access the original memory of how and why you know this person; recognition is just flagging up the fact that the memory exists.*retrieve: 꺼내다 **infuriating: 짜증 나는
summary_sentence: Among the brain's dual memory systems, familiarity is (A)___________ that memory exists, and recall is (B)___________ the the details of that memory.
explanation: 본문에서 친숙함(familiarity)은 기억이 존재한다는 사실을 단순히 알리는 것(recognition)으로 설명되며, 회상(recall)은 기억의 상세 내용을 꺼내오는(retrieving) 과정으로 설명되어 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 recognition, (B)에는 retrieving이 적절합니다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑧ 중 어휘 및 어법상 어색한 곳이 네 군데 있습니다. 찾아서 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오. [25년 3월 41-42번]
passage: In 1900, at the close of the first decade in ①<u>which</u> electric systems had become a practical alternative for manufacturers, ②<u>more</u> than 5 percent of the power used in factories came from electricity. In short order, electric power had gone from exotic to commonplace. But one thing didn't change. Factories continued to build their own power-supply systems on their own premises. ⑥<u>Little</u> manufacturers considered buying electricity from the small central stations. ⑦<u>Designed</u> to supply lighting to local homes and shops, the central stations had neither the size nor the skill to serve the needs of big factories. question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food _______________________________. question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We collect stamps, coins, vintage cars even when they serve no practical purpose. passage: We are the only species that seasons its food, deliberately altering it with the highly flavored plant parts we call herbs and spices. And the cultures that make the heaviest use of spices - think of the garlic and black pepper of Thai food, the ginger and coriander of India, the chili peppers of Mexico - come from warmer climates, where bacterial spoilage is a bigger issue. In contrast, the most lightly spiced cuisines - those of Scandinavia and northern Europe - are from cooler climates. ② the human taste that discerns the various seasonings
③ other uses of spices except bacterial growth inhibition

⑤ the high economic value of plants with antibacterial properties

question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: Empathy is frequently listed as one of the most desired skills in an employer or employee, although without specifying exactly what is meant by empathy. Some businesses stress cognitive empathy, emphasizing the need for leaders to understand the perspective of employees and customers when negotiating deals and making decisions. Others stress affective empathy and empathic concern, emphasizing the ability of leaders to gain trust from employees and customers by treating them with real concern and compassion. When some consultants argue that successful companies foster empathy, what that translates to is that companies should conduct good market research. In other words, an "empathic" company understands the needs and wants of its customers and seeks to fulfill those needs and wants. When some people speak of design with empathy, what that translates to is that _____________________________________________.*empathy: 공감, 공감 능력 **compassion: 동정심
options: ① companies devise ways to prioritize profits over meeting customer needs when designing products
② companies should act ethically and treat their staff well to enhance both profitability and productivity
③ products are created to appear approachable, using appealing designs and user-friendly interfaces
④ designers should keep pace with the trend of young consumers who are comfortable with technology
⑤ product design should meet diverse needs, especially for individuals with disabilities, to ensure inclusiveness
explanation: 이 글은 기업 환경에서 '공감'이 의미하는 바를 설명하고 있습니다. 인지적 공감, 정서적 공감 등을 언급한 뒤, '공감하는' 회사는 고객의 요구와 욕구를 이해하고 충족시키려 노력한다고 설명합니다. 이러한 맥락에서 '공감을 바탕으로 한 디자인'이란 다양한 요구를 충족시키는 것, 특히 장애인과 같은 소수자를 포함하여 포용성을 보장하는 디자인을 의미한다고 추론하는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기업은 제품을 디자인할 때 고객의 요구를 충족시키는 것보다 이윤을 우선시하는 방법을 고안한다
② 기업은 수익성과 생산성을 모두 높이기 위해 윤리적으로 행동하고 직원들을 잘 대우해야 한다
③ 매력적인 디자인과 사용자 친화적인 인터페이스를 사용하여 제품이 접근하기 쉬워 보이도록 만들어진다

⑤ 제품 디자인은 포용성을 보장하기 위해 다양한 요구, 특히 장애가 있는 개인들의 요구를 충족시켜야 한다

question: 16. 다음 글에서 답을 찾을 수 있는 질문이 아닌 것은?
passage: Emotion socialization - learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them - starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may intrude on adolescents' autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.
options: ① Who primarily act as the main socializing agents for emotion regulation throughout childhood and adolescence?
② In what way do parents' reactions to emotional situations set an example for their children's emotional responses?
③ What are the potential consequences for teenagers facing emotional crises without parental support?
④ How do parental approaches differ between younger children and adolescents when parents address emotional difficulties?
⑤ Why might adolescents tend to distance themselves from their parents during periods of emotional distress?
explanation: 이 글은 감정 사회화와 그 과정에서 부모의 역할에 대해 다루고 있습니다. ①번은 '부모'라고 언급되어 있고, ②번은 부모의 반응이 롤모델이 된다는 내용이 있으며, ④번은 어린아이에게는 직접적인 달래기가, 청소년에게는 간접적 지원이 적합하다는 차이점이 설명되어 있고, ⑤번은 부모의 관행이 조정되지 않으면 청소년의 자율성을 침해하여 멀어질 수 있다는 이유가 나와 있습니다. 하지만 ③번 '부모의 지지 없이 정서적 위기에 처한 십대들에게 나타날 수 있는 잠재적 결과'에 대해서는 구체적으로 언급되지 않았습니다. 지문은 '부모의 방식이 적절하지 않을 때' 부모로부터 멀어질 수 있다는 점을 언급할 뿐, '지지가 아예 없을 때의 결과'를 다루지는 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 아동기와 청소년기 내내 정서 조절을 위한 주요 사회화 주체로 주로 누가 활동하는가?

③ 부모의 지지 없이 정서적 위기에 처한 십대들에게 나타날 수 있는 잠재적 결과는 무엇인가?

question: 17. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
passage: If you had wanted to create a "self-driving" car in the 1950s, your best option might have been to strap a brick to the accelerator. Yes, the vehicle would have been able to move forward on its own, but it could not slow down, stop, or turn to avoid barriers. Obviously not ideal. But does that mean the entire concept of the self-driving car is not worth pursuing? No, it only means that at the time we did not yet have the tools we now possess to help enable vehicles to operate both autonomously and safely. This once-distant dream now seems within our reach. It is much the same story in medicine. Two decades ago, we were still taping bricks to accelerators. Today, we are approaching the point where we can begin to bring some appropriate technology to bear in ways that advance our understanding of patients as unique individuals. In fact, many patients are already wearing devices that monitor their conditions. in real time, which allows doctors to talk to their patients in a specific, refined, and feedback-driven way that was not even possible a decade ago.*strap: 끈으로 묶다 **autonomously: 자율적으로
options: ① In the 1950s, creating a self-driving car would have involved simply strapping a brick to the accelerator.
② By using a brick, the vehicle was able to move forward, slow down, stop, and turn.
③ The limitations of early self-driving concepts made the pursuit of autonomous vehicle technology invalid.
④ Advances in automated driving systems have made the dream of a new medicine era more attainable today.
⑤ Doctors monitored through wearable health devices can offer a more personalized feedback to their patients.
explanation: 지문의 첫 문장에서 1950년대에 자율 주행 자동차를 만들고 싶었다면 최선의 선택은 가속 페달에 벽돌을 묶는 것이었을 것이라고 언급하고 있으므로 ①번은 내용과 일치합니다. ②번은 벽돌을 사용하면 감속이나 정지가 불가능하다고 했으므로 틀렸고, ③번은 자율 주행 개념을 추구할 가치가 없다는 뜻이 아니라고 했으므로 틀렸습니다. ④번은 자동 주행 시스템의 발전이 아닌 '의료 기술(웨어러블 기기 등)의 발전'이 새로운 의료 시대를 가능하게 했다는 비유적 표현이므로 부적절하며, ⑤번은 의사가 모니터링되는 것이 아니라 환자가 장치를 착용하여 의사가 피드백을 주는 것이므로 주체가 잘못되었습니다.
options_translation: ① 1950년대에 자율 주행 자동차를 만드는 것은 단순히 가속 페달에 벽돌을 묶는 것을 포함했을 것이다.
② 벽돌을 사용함으로써 차량은 앞으로 가고, 속도를 줄이고, 멈추고, 회전할 수 있었다.
③ 초기 자율 주행 개념의 한계는 자율 주행 차량 기술의 추구를 무효하게 만들었다.
④ 자동 주행 시스템의 발전은 오늘날 새로운 의학 시대의 꿈을 더 달성 가능하게 만들었다.
⑤ 웨어러블 건강 기기를 통해 모니터링되는 의사들은 환자들에게 더 개인화된 피드백을 제공할 수 있다.

question: 18. 다음 글 (A)를 대화문 (B)로 바꾸었다. (B)의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 글 (A)를 제대로 이해하지 못한 것은? [25년 3월 33번]
passage: (A) When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.*startling: 놀라운 **deleterious: 해로운↓(B)A: Have you ever noticed how we use hand gestures when we're explaining something?B: Yeah, I've always assumed it was just a habit, but is there more to it than that?A: Exactly! Research shows that gestures actually help us mentally prepare the words we want to say. It's like ⓐ<u>our hands give our brain a little nudge to bring the right words to mind</u>.B: Wow, so our gestures are kind of like ⓑ<u>a preview of what we're thinking?</u>A: Precisely! And it's not just about helping us speak more fluently. ⓒ<u>When people can't gesture, they tend to talk less smoothly and remember less</u>.B: Really? So, our gestures are more than just extra movements then?A: Right. Instead of just tagging along with speech, gestures actually make our communication more effective. ⓓ<u>They serve as a subordinate accessory to talking</u>; they're a key part of how we think and communicate.B: That makes sense. I guess I've been using my hands to help me think all along!A: Exactly! Our gestures are like a key player for our thinking, ⓔ<u>playing a crucial role in shaping our ideas</u>.B: I never looked at it that way. I'll pay more attention to my own gestures from now on.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 글 (A)의 마지막 문장에서 몸짓은 말의 서투른 동반자로서 뒤따라가는 것이 아니라 사고의 최첨단(leading edge)을 나타낸다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 '말하기의 부수적인 장신구(subordinate accessory)'로서의 역할은 지문의 내용과 정반대되는 설명입니다.
options_translation: ⓐ 우리의 손이 적절한 단어를 떠올리도록 뇌를 살짝 자극함
