question: 35. What is one clear advantage of using extracts in the classroom, according to the passage? Write in one sentence in English.
passage: There is no doubt that the length of some literary works is overwhelming. Reading or translating a work in class, hour after hour, week after week, can be such a boring experience that many students never want to open a foreign language book again. Extracts provide one type of solution. The advantages are obvious: reading a series of passages from different works produces more variety in the classroom, so that the teacher has a greater chance of avoiding monotony, while still giving learners a taste at least of an author's special flavour. On the other hand, a student who is only exposed to 'bite-sized chunks' will never have the satisfaction of knowing the overall pattern of a book, which is after all the satisfaction most of us seek when we read something in our own language. Moreover, there are some literary features that cannot be adequately illustrated by a short excerpt: the development of plot or character, for instance, with the gradual involvement of the reader that this implies and so on.
answer: one clear advantage is that it produces more variety in the classroom, avoiding(preventing) monotony, while giving learners a taste at least of an author's special flavour.

question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If you had wanted to create a "self-driving" car in the 1950s, your best option might have been to strap a brick to the accelerator. Today, we are approaching the point where we can begin to bring some appropriate technology to bear in ways that advance our understanding of patients as unique individuals. In fact, many patients are already wearing devices that monitor their conditions in real time, which allows doctors to talk to their patients in a specific, refined, and feedback-driven way that was not even possible a decade ago.

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: Emotion socialization that involves learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them - begins at a very young age and ⓐ<u>plays</u> a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain ⓑ<u>primary</u> in their role as socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, ⓒ<u>increasing</u> the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also ⓓ<u>impact</u> emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may intrude on adolescents' autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in adolescents' emotional experiences, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of ⓔ<u>it</u>, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.1점]

Some businesses stress cognitive empathy, ⓒ<u>emphasizing</u> the need for leaders to understand the perspective of employees and customers when negotiating deals and making decisions. Others stress affective empathy and empathic concern. They emphasize that leaders must gain trust from employees and customers by treating them with real concern and compassion. When some consultants argue that successful companies foster empathy, what that translates to is that companies should conduct good market research. In other words, an "empathic" company understands the needs and wants of its customers and ⓓ<u>seek</u> to fulfill those needs and wants. When some people speak of design with empathy, what that translates to is that companies should take into account the specific needs of different populations - the blind, the deaf, the elderly, non-English speakers, the color-blind, and so on - when ⓔ<u>they</u> design products.

question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.0점]
passage: We are the only species that seasons its food, deliberately ⓐ<u>altering</u> it with the highly flavored plant parts we call herbs and spices. It's quite possible that our taste for spices has an evolutionary root. Many spices have antibacterial properties - in fact, common seasonings such as garlic, onion, and oregano ⓑ<u>stimulate</u> the growth of almost every bacterium tested. And the cultures that make the heaviest use of spices - think of the garlic and black pepper of Thai food, the ginger and coriander of India, the chili peppers of Mexico - come from warmer climates, where bacterial ⓒ<u>spoilage</u> is a bigger issue. In contrast, the most ⓓ<u>lightly</u> spiced cuisines - those of Scandinavia and northern Europe - are from cooler climates. Our uniquely human attention to flavor, in this case the flavor of spices, turns out to have arisen as a matter of ⓔ<u>survival</u>.

question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.2점]

question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Development of the human body from a single cell provides many examples of the structural richness that is possible when the repeated production of random variation is combined with nonrandom selection. Always new structure is based on old structure, and at every stage selection favors some cells and eliminates others. Except in the immune system, cells and extensions of cells are not genetically selected during development, but rather, are positionally selected. A natural consequence of the strategy is great variability from individual to individual at the cell and molecular levels, even though large-scale structures are quite similar.

② abundance ... genes

④ consistency ... positions
⑤ consistency ... genes

question: 9. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 10. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?

question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Commitment is the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life.

question: 13. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. question: 22. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition. explanation: 이 글은 사전이 단어의 의미를 찾기에 좋은 자원이지만, 사전을 효과적으로 활용하기 위해서는 독자가 이미 언어에 대해 어느 정도 탄탄한 이해를 갖추고 있어야 한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 사전의 정의 자체도 독자가 이미 알고 있는 단어들을 사용하여 기술되어야 하기 때문입니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 5번 '효과적인 사전 사용을 위해 필요한 독자의 언어적 준비성'입니다.
options_translation: ① 어휘적 정의를 심층적으로 분석하는 것의 이점
② 사전에 대한 신뢰할 수 있는 자원을 찾는 데 있어서의 한계
③ 익숙하지 않은 단어의 함축된 의미를 발견하려는 노력
④ 언어 학습에 있어 사전 사용의 긍정적 영향
⑤ 효과적인 사전 사용을 위해 필요한 독자의 언어적 준비성

question: 23. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 taking a back seat이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Most people view flavor as of secondary significance in social settings where food is served. Although our social gatherings coalesce around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, do not depend on the quality of sensations provided by the food. In short, the prominence of the social dimension of food may suggest that the flavor of food is <u>taking a back seat.</u>
options: ① becoming less important in social relations
② shaping our everyday experiences continuously
③ improving the relative status of profound flavors
④ facing unprecedented responsibility in social gatherings
⑤ turning conventional rituals into casual dining experiences
explanation: 지문은 음식이 제공되는 사회적 상황에서 음식의 '맛'은 부차적인 의미를 가지며, 사회적 모임의 의미는 맛보다는 사회적 역학 관계나 의례 등에 의해 결정된다고 설명합니다. 즉, 음식의 사회적 측면이 두드러지면서 맛의 중요성이 뒤로 밀려나게 되었다는 흐름이므로, 'taking a back seat'은 '사회적 관계에서 덜 중요해짐'을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 사회적 관계에서 덜 중요해지는 것
② 우리의 일상적인 경험을 지속적으로 형성하는 것
① 깊은 맛의 상대적인 지위를 향상시키는 것
④ 사회적 모임에서 전례 없는 책임에 직면하는 것
⑤ 관습적인 의례를 일상적인 식사 경험으로 바꾸는 것

question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always ⓐ<u>intervening</u> in the dynamics of the ecosystem. They ⓑ<u>remove</u> unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently ⓒ<u>unstable</u> state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower ⓓ<u>continues</u> stepping in, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be ⓔ<u>lower</u> as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
explanation: 텃밭 가꾸기는 채소 생산 극대화를 위해 생태계 역학에 개입하는 과정입니다. 채소 성장의 극대화는 생태계 입장에서 불안정한 상태이므로, 재배자가 '개입하는 것'을 멈추어야(stops) 생태계가 자연스럽게 더 안정적인 상태(잡초가 무성해지는 등)로 돌아가게 됩니다. 따라서 'continues(계속하다)'를 'stops(중단하다)' 정도로 바꾸어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

question: 25. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. (A) The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. (B) However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. (C) Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. (D) Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. (E) The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports.
insertion_sentence: Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장은 일부 정부가 식량 자급자족(모든 식량을 국내에서 생산하는 것)을 목표로 설정했다는 내용입니다. (B) 다음 문장에서 'However'를 사용하여 '하지만 식량 안보가 식량 자급자족을 요구하는 것은 아니다'라고 반박하며 수입의 필요성을 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 식량 자급자족에 대한 정의와 목표 설정을 설명한 주어진 문장은 (B) 자리에 들어가는 것이 흐름상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)

question: 26. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much a creative process. ⓐA conjecture is a philosophical invention, cooked up rather mystically by the mind through the mental computation we call careful contemplation. ⓑHowever, until the hypothesis is tested against reality, it is not yet truly knowledge; it is just information that represents speculation. ⓒKnowledge results from information that has stood the test of usefulness. ⓓA scientific breakthrough is often sparked not in laboratories, but during walks, daydreams where the subconscious mind connects seemingly unrelated ideas. ⓔIt is what is left over after cycles of experimental testing have eliminated false theories.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 과학적 과정이 가설 검증과 실험적 테스트 등 규칙에 기반한 유용성 테스트를 견뎌 지식이 된다는 내용이다. 반면 ⓓ는 무의식이 번뜩일 때 과학적 혁신이 일어날 가능성이 크다는 창의성에 무게를 두는 내용으로 다른 문장들이 말하는 '가설의 검증'과 결이 맞지 않는다. (Wait, let's re-read.) No, the original text for 38 was: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much a creative process... Wait! Actually the overall text in paragraph discusses how knowledge is what survives testing. ⓓ refers to daydreaming producing breakthroughs which disrupts the "tested against reality" and "elimination of false theories". Wait, option 4 is indeed correct.

question: 29. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Early twentieth, at the close of the first decade in which electric systems had become a practical alternative for manufacturers, less than 5 percent of the power used in factories came from electricity.
ordered_passages: (A) But one thing didn't change. Factories continued to build their own power-supply systems on their own premises. Few manufacturers considered buying electricity from the small central stations. Designed to supply lighting to local homes and shops, the central stations had neither the size nor the skill to serve the needs of big factories.

(B) But the technological advances of suppliers made electric systems and electric motors ever more affordable and reliable, and the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology. Further accelerating the shift was the rapid expansion in the number of skilled electrical engineers. In short order, electric power had gone from exotic to commonplace.

(C) And the factory owners, having always supplied their own power, were reluctant to assign such a critical function to an outsider. They knew that a glitch in power supply would bring their operations to a halt - and that a lot of glitches might well mean bankruptcy.
explanation: (B)에서 기술 발전으로 전기 시스템이 더 저렴하고 신용할 만해져 확산되었다는 내용, 그러나(But) (A)에서 공장들은 자체 전력 시스템을 유지하려 했다는 반전, 그 이유가 (C)에서 외부자에게 그처럼 중요한 기능을 맡기는 것을 꺼렸기 때문이라고 설명하는 것이 논리적인 흐름이다.

question: 1. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: For years, many psychologists have held strongly to the belief that the key to addressing negative health habits is to change behavior. This, more than values and attitudes, is the part of personality that is easiest to change. Ingestive habits such as smoking, drinking and various eating behaviors are the most common health concerns targeted for behavioral changes. ⓐProcess-addiction behaviors (workaholism, shopaholism, and the like) fall into this category as well. ⓑA workaholic might stay at the office until midnight every day, not because they have to, but because they don't know what to do with their free time. ⓒMental imagery combined with power of suggestion was taken up as the premise of behavioral medicine to help people change negative health behaviors into positive ones. ⓓAlthough this technique alone will not produce changes, when used alongside other behavior modification tactics and coping strategies, behavioral changes have proved effective for some people. ⓔWhat mental imagery does is reinforce a new desired behavior. Repeated use of images reinforces the desired behavior more strongly over time.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 부정적인 건강 습관을 바꾸기 위해 '정신적 이미지(mental imagery)'를 활용하는 행동 변화 기법에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 초반에는 행동 변화의 중요성과 중독적 행동을 언급하며 도입하고, ⓒ번부터 본격적으로 정신적 이미지와 제안의 힘이 행동 의학의 전제로 사용됨을 설명합니다. 반면 ⓑ번은 워커홀릭이 사무실에 늦게까지 남는 이유(자유 시간을 어떻게 보낼지 몰라서)를 구체적으로 설명하는 문장으로, 정신적 이미지를 통한 행동 교정이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

question: 2. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Dancers often push themselves to the limits of their physical capabilities. But that push is misguided if it is directed toward accomplishing something physically impossible.
ordered_passages: (A) For instance, a tall dancer with long feet may wish to perform repetitive vertical jumps to fast music, pointing his feet while in the air and lowering his heels to the floor between jumps. That may be impossible no matter how strong the dancer is. But a short-footed dancer may have no trouble!
(B) In both of these cases, understanding and working within the constraints imposed by nature and described by physical laws allows dancers to work efficiently, minimizing potential risk of injury.

(C) Another dancer may be struggling to complete a half-turn in the air. Understanding the connection between a rapid turn rate and the alignment of the body close to the rotation axis tells her how to accomplish her turn successfully.
explanation: 주어진 글은 무용수들이 신체적 한계에 도전하지만, 물리적으로 불가능한 것을 성취하려 한다면 잘못된 것이라고 언급합니다. (A)에서 'For instance'를 통해 키가 크고 발이 긴 무용수가 빠른 음악에 맞춰 점프하는 것이 물리적으로 불가능할 수 있다는 첫 번째 사례를 제시합니다. (C)에서 'Another dancer'를 통해 공중 회전을 시도하는 두 번째 사례를 제시하며 물리적 원리(회전축)의 이해를 언급합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 'In both of these cases'를 통해 앞선 두 사례를 모두 아우르며 자연의 제약과 물리 법칙 내에서 작업하는 것의 중요성을 결론짓습니다.

question: 3. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The built-in capacity for smiling is proven by the noteworthy observation that babies who are congenitally both deaf and blind, who have never seen a human face, also start to smile at around 2 months.
ordered_passages: (A) But here's an interesting fact: blind babies will continue to smile if they are cuddled, bounced and tickled by an adult - anything to let them know that they are not alone and that someone cares about them.
(B) However, smiling in blind babies eventually diminishes if nothing is done to reinforce it. Without the right feedback, smiling dies out.
(C) This social feedback encourages the baby to continue smiling. In this way, early experience operates with our biology to establish social behaviors.
(D) In fact, you don't need the cases of blind babies to make the point. Babies with sight smile more at you when you look at them or, better still, smile back at them.
explanation: 주어진 글은 시각과 청각 장애를 가진 아기도 생후 2개월경 웃기 시작한다는 생득적인 웃음 능력을 설명합니다. (B)에서 'However'를 통해 강화가 없으면 이 웃음이 사라진다는 문제점을 제기합니다. (A)에서 'But'을 통해 성인이 안아주거나 달래주는 등의 자극이 있으면 계속 웃는다는 반전된 사실을 제시합니다. (C)에서 (A)의 행위들을 'This social feedback'으로 지칭하며 이것이 사회적 행동을 확립한다고 정리합니다. (D)에서 시각 장애가 없는 아기의 사례를 덧붙이며 논지를 일반화합니다.

question: 4. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 fallen prey to impatience가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Too many times people, especially in today's generation, expect things to just happen overnight. When we have these false expectations, it tends to discourage us from continuing to move forward. Because this is a high tech society, everything we want has to be within the parameters of our comfort and convenience. If it doesn't happen fast enough, we're tempted to lose interest. So many people don't want to take the time it requires to be successful. Success is not a matter of mere desire; you should develop patience in order to achieve it. Have you <u>fallen prey to impatience</u>? Great things take time to build.
options: ① lost interest in technology
② worked too hard to reach your goal
③ misunderstood what success really is
④ set a goal that is too difficult to achieve
⑤ given up easily because results didn't come quickly
explanation: 이 글은 현대인들이 성공을 위해 필요한 인내심을 갖지 못하고 모든 일이 즉각적으로 일어나기를 기대하는 태도를 비판하고 있습니다. 따라서 '조급함의 희생양이 되다(fallen prey to impatience)'라는 말은 결과가 빨리 나오지 않는다는 이유로 쉽게 포기해버리는 성향을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 기술에 대한 흥미를 잃었다
② 목표에 도달하기 위해 너무 열심히 일했다
③ 성공이 진정 무엇인지 오해했다
④ 달성하기 너무 어려운 목표를 설정했다
⑤ 결과가 빨리 나오지 않아서 쉽게 포기했다

question: 5. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Empathy is frequently listed as one of the most desired skills in an employer or employee, although without specifying exactly what is meant by empathy. Some businesses stress cognitive empathy, emphasizing the need for leaders to understand the perspective of employees and customers when negotiating deals and making decisions. Others stress affective empathy and empathic concern, emphasizing the ability of leaders to gain trust from employees and customers by treating them with real concern and compassion. When some consultants argue that successful companies foster empathy, what that translates to is that companies should conduct good market research. Through it, an "empathic" company understands the needs and wants of its customers and seeks to fulfill those needs and wants. When some people speak of design with empathy, what that translates to is that companies should take into account the specific needs of different populations - the blind, the deaf, the elderly, non-English speakers, the color-blind, and so on - when designing products.
options: ① Some companies emphasize cognitive empathy in order to help leaders to understand others' perspectives.
② Affective empathy focuses on building trust through genuine concern and compassion.
③ Being an empathic company means having only emotionally sensitive employees.
④ Some consultants suggest good market research as a way to cultivate empathy for successful companies.
⑤ Designing with empathy means considering the needs of various groups, such as the elderly and the blind.
explanation: 글의 중반부에서 '공감하는' 기업이 된다는 것은 고객의 요구와 욕구를 이해하기 위해 훌륭한 시장 조사를 수행하고 이를 충족시키려 노력하는 것을 의미한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 단순히 '감정적으로 예민한 직원들만 보유하는 것'을 의미한다는 내용은 지문에 언급되지 않았으므로 ③번이 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 일부 기업들은 리더들이 타인의 관점을 이해하도록 돕기 위해 인지적 공감을 강조한다.
② 정서적 공감은 진정한 관심과 동정심을 통해 신뢰를 쌓는 데 초점을 맞춘다.
③ 공감하는 기업이 된다는 것은 오직 감정적으로 예민한 직원들만 보유한다는 것을 의미한다.
④ 일부 컨설턴트들은 성공적인 기업을 위해 공감을 기르는 방법으로 훌륭한 시장 조사를 제안한다.
⑤ 공감으로 디자인한다는 것은 노인이나 시각 장애인과 같은 다양한 집단의 요구를 고려하는 것을 의미한다.

question: 6. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: In order to bring the ever increasing costs of home care for elderly and needy persons under control, managers of home care providers have introduced management systems. These systems clearly describe tasks of home care workers and the time and budget available to perform these tasks. Electronic reporting systems require home care workers to report on their activities and the time spent, thus making the distribution of time and money visible and, in the perception of managers, easy to manage. This, in the view of managers, has contributed to the resolution of the problem. The home care workers, on the other hand, may perceive their work not as a set of separate tasks to be performed as efficiently as possible, but as a service to be provided to a client with whom they may have built a connection. This includes having conversations with clients and enquiring about the person's well-being. Restricted time and the requirement to report may be perceived as obstacles that make it impossible to deliver the service that is needed. If the management systems are too rigid, this may result in home care workers becoming overloaded and demotivated.
options: ① To address the rising expenses of home care services, managers have implemented management systems.
② Electronic reporting tools require workers to report on their activities and the duration of each task.
③ Managers argue that the emotional aspect of care should be prioritized over efficiency and cost control.
④ Home care workers may regard their role as offering relational service rather than merely performing individual duties.
⑤ If the systems are overly strict, home care workers might end up feeling overwhelmed and losing motivation.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 관리자들은 비용 통제와 효율성을 위해 관리 시스템을 도입하였으며, 시간과 돈의 분배를 가시화하고 관리하기 쉽게 만드는 것을 중시했습니다. 돌봄의 감정적 측면을 효율성보다 우선시해야 한다고 주장한 것은 관리자가 아니라, 업무를 관계적 서비스로 인식하는 가사 지원 노동자들의 관점에 가깝습니다.
options_translation: ① 가사 돌봄 서비스의 비용 상승 문제를 해결하기 위해, 관리자들은 관리 시스템을 시행했다.
② 전자 보고 도구는 노동자들이 자신의 활동과 각 업무의 소요 시간을 보고하도록 요구한다.
③ 관리자들은 돌봄의 감정적 측면이 효율성과 비용 통제보다 우선시되어야 한다고 주장한다.
④ 가사 지원 노동자들은 자신의 역할을 단순히 개별 업무를 수행하는 것이 아니라 관계적 서비스를 제공하는 것으로 간주할 수 있다.
⑤ 시스템이 지나치게 엄격하면 가사 지원 노동자들은 결국 압도당하고 동기를 잃게 될 수 있다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We must explore the relationship between children's film production and consumption habits. The term "children's film" implies ownership by children - their cinema - but films supposedly made for children have always been consumed by audiences of all ages, particularly in commercial cinemas. The considerable crossover in audience composition for children's films can be shown by the fact that, in 2007, eleven Danish children's and youth films attracted 59 percent of theatrical admissions, and in 2014, German children's films comprised seven out of the top twenty films at the national box office. This phenomenon corresponds with a broader, international embrace of what is seemingly children's culture among audiences of diverse ages. The old prejudice that children's film is some other realm, separate from (and forever subordinate to) a more legitimate cinema for adults is not supported by the realities of consumption: children's film is at the heart of contemporary popular culture.
options: ① A History of Children's Film Production
② Children's Films: A Genre for a Niche Audience
③ The Decline of Children's Cinema in Modern Times
④ The Superiority of Adult Cinema Over Children's Films
⑤ Children's Films in Pop Culture: More Than Just for Kids
explanation: 이 글은 아동용 영화가 단지 아이들만을 위한 것이 아니라 모든 연령대의 관객들에 의해 소비되고 있으며, 현대 대중문화의 핵심에 위치하고 있다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '대중문화 속의 아동 영화: 단지 아이들만을 위한 것 이상'이라는 ⑤번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 아동 영화 제작의 역사
② 아동 영화: 특정 소수 관객을 위한 장르
③ 현대 아동 영화의 쇠퇴
④ 성인 영화의 아동 영화에 대한 우월성
⑤ 대중문화 속의 아동 영화: 단지 아이들만을 위한 것 그 이상

question: 9. 다음 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is a common assumption that most vagrant birds are ultimately doomed, aside from the rare cases where individuals are able to reorientate and return to their normal ranges. In turn, vagrancy itself is commonly viewed as having relatively little biological (A)___________. This is undoubtedly true for the majority of cases, as the most likely outcome of any given vagrancy event is that the individual will fail to find enough resources, and/or be exposed to inhospitable environmental conditions, and perish. However, there are many lines of evidence to suggest that vagrancy can, on rare occasions, dramatically alter the fate of populations, species or even whole ecosystems. Although such events are (B)___________, they can be extremely important when viewed at the timescales over which ecological and evolutionary processes unfold. The most significant effects of vagrancy involve the (C)___________ of new breeding areas, altered migratory pathways, and different wintering grounds. Each of these can occur through different mechanisms, and at different frequencies, and they each have their own unique importance.
options: ① impact - typical - preference
② rhythm - infrequent - marketing
③ structure - controversial - development
④ importance - uncommon - emergence
⑤ significance - normal - popularity
explanation: (A) 미조(길을 잃은 새) 현상은 대부분 죽음으로 끝나기 때문에 생물학적 '중요성(importance/significance)'이 낮다고 여겨집니다. (B) 하지만 드물게 생태계를 바꿀 수 있는데, 이러한 사건들은 '흔치 않지만(uncommon/infrequent)' 중요합니다. (C) 미조 현상의 가장 큰 효과는 새로운 번식지의 '출현(emergence/development)'을 포함합니다. 따라서 이를 모두 만족하는 것은 ④번입니다.
options_translation: ① 영향 - 전형적인 - 선호
② 리듬 - 드문 - 마케팅
③ 구조 - 논란이 되는 - 발달
④ 중요성 - 흔치 않은 - 출현
⑤ 의의 - 정상적인 - 인기

question: 10. 다음 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Beethoven's drive to create something novel is a reflection of his state of curiosity. Our brains experience a sense of reward when we come up with something (A)___________ while exploring an idea we haven't encountered before, such as a musical phrase we've never played or heard. When our curiosity leads to a fresh discovery, we experience a sense of pleasure as a form of internal (B)___________. A number of investigators have modeled how curiosity influences musical composition. In the case of Beethoven, computer modeling focused on the thirty-two piano sonatas written after age thirteen revealed that the musical patterns found in all of Beethoven's music faded in later sonatas, while novel patterns, including patterns that were unique to a particular sonata, gained (C)___________. In other words, Beethoven's music became less predictable over time as his curiosity drove the exploration of new musical ideas.
options: ① original - reward - prominence
② creative - benefit - knowledge
③ rational - motivation - momentum
④ outdated - satisfaction - attention
⑤ unconventional - regret - importance
explanation: (A) 이전에 접해보지 못한 아이디어를 탐구할 때 '독창적인(original/creative)' 것을 생각해내면 뇌가 보상을 느낍니다. (B) 호기심이 새로운 발견으로 이어질 때 내면의 '보상(reward)'으로서 즐거움을 경험합니다. (C) 베토벤의 후기 소나타에서 새로운 패턴들이 '두드러짐(prominence)'을 얻었다는 내용이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 독창적인 - 보상 - 두드러짐
② 창의적인 - 이익 - 지식
③ 합리적인 - 동기 - 탄력(가속도)
④ 시대에 뒤떨어진 - 만족 - 주의
⑤ 인습에 얽매이지 않는 - 후회 - 중요성

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: The Net differs from most of the mass media it replaces in an obvious and very important way: it's ⓐ<u>bidirectional</u>. We can send messages through the network as well as receive them, which has made the system all the more ⓑ<u>helpful</u>. The ability to exchange information online, to upload as well as download, has turned the Net into a ⓒ<u>thoroughfare</u> for business and commerce. With a few clicks, people can search virtual catalogues, place orders, track shipments, and upload information in corporate databases. But the Net doesn't just ⓓ<u>entertain</u> us from businesses; it links us with one another. People can chat with friends anytime, even if they are far away. It's a ⓔ<u>personal</u> broadcasting medium as well as a commercial one. Millions of people use it to distribute their own digital creations, in the form of blogs, videos, photos, songs, and podcasts, as well as to critique, edit, or otherwise modify the creations of others.
explanation: 이 글은 인터넷(Net)의 쌍방향적 특성과 그로 인한 사회적, 상업적 변화를 설명하고 있습니다. ⓓ가 포함된 문장은 인터넷이 기업으로부터 우리를 단순히 '연결해주는(connect/link)' 역할을 하는 것이 아니라 우리 서로를 연결해준다는 문맥이어야 합니다. ⓓ의 'entertain(즐겁게 하다)'은 문맥상 어색하며, 비즈니스 측면에서 소비자에게 일방적으로 제품이나 서비스를 제공하는 것과 대비되어 우리 사이를 연결한다는 맥락을 표현하기에 적합하지 않습니다. 흐름상 'isolate(고립시키다)'나 단순히 비즈니스 기능만 수행하는 것을 넘어서 개인 간의 연결을 강조하는 표현이 와야 합니다. 원문상에서는 'disconnect' 혹은 비즈니스와의 단절이라기보다는 비즈니스로부터 우리를 연결하는 매개체로서의 의미를 담고 있습니다. 사실상 원문 문맥에서는 'connect us with businesses'와 대조되는 'link us with one another'를 설명하는 과정에서 '연결하다'라는 의미의 단어가 적절합니다.

question: 12. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: On our little world, light travels, for all practical purposes, immediately. If a lightbulb is glowing, then of course it's physically where we see it, shining away. We reach out our hand and touch it: It's there all right, and unpleasantly hot. If the filament fails, then the light goes out. We don't see it in the same place, glowing, illuminating the room years after the bulb breaks and it's removed from its socket. The very notion seems absurd. But if we're far enough away, an entire sun can go out and we'll continue to see it shining brightly; we won't learn of its death, it may be, for ages to come - in fact, for how long it takes light, which travels fast but not infinitely fast, to cross the intervening expanse. The immense distances to the stars and the galaxies mean that we see everything in space in the past. In other words, the night sky is not a reflection of the present, but a glowing archive of cosmic history.
summary_sentence: Because light appears to travel (A)____________ on Earth, we perceive objects as they are. In contrast, the vastness of space causes a delay in the arrival of light, so what we observe of stars reflects their condition in the (B)____________, not the present.
options: ① indirectly ...... memory
② gradually ...... illusion
③ periodically ...... history
④ chronologically ...... atmosphere
⑤ instantaneously ...... past
explanation: 지구상의 짧은 거리에서는 빛이 즉각적으로 이동하는 것처럼 보이기 때문에 사물을 있는 그대로 인지하지만, 광대한 우주에서는 빛의 이동 속도가 유한하여 도달하는 데 시간이 걸리므로 우리가 보는 별의 모습은 과거(past)의 상태를 반영한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '즉각적으로'를 의미하는 instantaneously가, (B)에는 '과거'를 의미하는 past가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 간접적으로 ...... 기억
② 점진적으로 ...... 환상
③ 주기적으로 ...... 역사
④ 연대순으로 ...... 대기
⑤ 즉각적으로 ...... 과거

question: 13. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We collect stamps, coins, vintage cars even when they serve no practical purpose. The post office doesn't accept the old stamps, the banks don't take old coins, and the vintage cars are no longer allowed on the road, These are all side issues; the attraction is that they are in short supply. In one study, students were asked to arrange ten posters in order of attractiveness - with the agreement that afterward they could keep one poster as a reward for their participation. Five minutes later, they were told that the poster with the third highest rating was no longer available. Then they were asked to judge all ten from scratch. The poster that was no longer available was suddenly classified as the most beautiful. In psychology, this phenomenon is called reactance: when we are deprived of an option, we suddenly deem it more attractive.
options: ① The rarer an object is, the more likely people are to avoid it.
② People tend to choose collectible items based on their practical value.
③ People are likely to follow others' preferences in order to gain popularity.
④ Instead of choosing for themselves, people often imitate what others like.
⑤ When something is hard to access, people often perceive it as more appealing.
explanation: 지문은 사람들이 실용적 목적이 없더라도 공급이 부족한(희귀한) 물건을 수집하며, 선택권이 박탈되었을 때(심리적 저항) 그 대상을 더 매력적으로 느끼게 된다는 점을 실험을 통해 설명하고 있습니다. 즉, 접근하기 어려울수록 사람들은 그것을 더 매력적으로 느낀다는 ⑤번이 글의 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 물건이 희귀할수록 사람들은 그것을 피할 가능성이 높다.
② 사람들은 실용적 가치에 기반하여 수집품을 선택하는 경향이 있다.
③ 사람들은 인기를 얻기 위해 다른 사람들의 선호를 따르는 경향이 있다.
④ 스스로 선택하는 대신 사람들은 종종 타인이 좋아하는 것을 모방한다.
⑤ 무언가에 접근하기 어려울 때, 사람들은 종종 그것을 더 매력적이라고 인지한다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If you had wanted to create a "self-driving" car in the 1950s, your best option might have been to strap a brick to the accelerator. Yes, the vehicle would have been able to move forward on its own, but it could not slow down, stop, or turn to avoid barriers. But does that mean the entire concept of the self-driving car is not worth pursuing? No, it simply means that we did not yet have the tools we now possess to help vehicles to operate both autonomously and safely. This once distant dream now seems within our reach. A similar story is unfolding in the field of medicine. Two decades ago, we were still taping bricks to accelerators. Doctors had limited tools, and treatments were often the same for everyone. There was little way to adjust care based on individual differences among patients. Today, we are reaching a point where we can begin applying appropriate technology in ways that deepen our understanding of patients as unique individuals. In fact, many patients now wear devices that monitor their conditions in real time, allowing doctors to communicate with them in a more specific, personalized, and responsive way - something that was unimaginable just ten years ago.
options: ① Medical technology is advancing more slowly than self-driving technology.
② Past failures show the dangers of self-driving and personalized healthcare.
③ Most people still prefer general medical treatments over personalized ones.
④ Both self-driving cars and personalized medicine remain impossible to achieve.
⑤ Technological progress is turning what was once a distant dream into reality.
explanation: 이 글은 1950년대의 자율주행 자동차 구상이 당시에는 기술적 한계로 인해 불완전했으나 오늘날에는 실현 가능한 영역에 들어왔음을 설명하며, 의료 분야에서도 이와 유사하게 과거의 획일적 치료에서 벗어나 기술 발전을 통해 개인 맞춤형 의료 서비스가 가능해지고 있다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '기술적 진보가 과거의 꿈을 현실로 바꾸고 있다'는 5번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 의료 기술은 자율주행 기술보다 느리게 발전하고 있다.
② 과거의 실패는 자율주행과 맞춤형 의료의 위험성을 보여준다.
③ 대부분의 사람들은 여전히 맞춤형 치료보다 일반적인 치료를 선호한다.
④ 자율주행 자동차와 개인 맞춤형 의료 서비스 모두 달성 불가능한 상태로 남아있다.
⑤ 기술적 진보가 한때 멀게 느껴졌던 꿈을 현실로 바꾸고 있다.

question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Buying a television is current consumption. It makes us happy today but does nothing to make us richer tomorrow. Yes, money spent on a television keeps workers employed at the television factory. But if the same money were invested, it would create jobs somewhere else, say for scientists in a laboratory or workers on a construction site, while also making us richer in the long run. Think about college as an example. Sending students to college creates jobs for professors. Using the same money to buy fancy sports cars for high school graduates would create jobs for auto workers. The crucial difference between these scenarios is that a college education makes a young person more ____________ for the rest of his or her life; a sports car does not. Thus, college tuition is an investment; buying a sports car is consumption.
options: ① honest
② productive
③ responsible
④ confident
⑤ open-minded
explanation: 지문은 단순 소비(텔레비전, 스포츠카 구매)와 투자(대학 교육)의 차이를 설명하고 있습니다. 대학 교육은 단순히 일자리를 창출하는 것을 넘어, 개인의 능력을 향상시켜 평생 동안 더 많은 가치를 창출할 수 있게 하므로 'productive(생산적인)'이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 정직한
② 생산적인
③ 책임감 있는
④ 자신감 있는
⑤ 개방적인

question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Because people tend to adapt, interrupting positive things with negative ones can actually increase enjoyment. Take commercials. Most people hate them, so removing them should make shows or other entertainment more enjoyable. But the opposite is true. Shows are actually more enjoyable when they're broken up by annoying commercials. That is because inserting less enjoyable moments can keep us from ______________________________________. Think about eating chocolate chips. The first chip is delicious: sweet, melt-in-your-mouth goodness. The second chip is also pretty good. But by the fourth, fifth, or tenth chip in a row, the goodness is no longer as pleasurable. We adapt. Interspersing positive experiences with less positive ones, however, can slow adaptation. Eating a Brussels sprout between chocolate chips or viewing commercials between parts of TV shows disrupts the process. The less positive moment makes the following positive one new again and thus more enjoyable.
options: ① skipping parts that seem less interesting
② forgetting which parts of the show are fun
③ noticing how enjoyable the show actually is
④ becoming desensitized to the pleasure due to its repetition
⑤ focusing not only on the boring scenes but also on the interesting ones
explanation: 사람은 반복되는 긍정적인 경험에 적응하여 즐거움을 덜 느끼게 되는데, 그 사이에 광고와 같은 덜 즐거운 요소를 삽입하면 이러한 '적응' 과정을 늦추어 즐거움을 다시 새롭게 느낄 수 있게 한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '반복으로 인해 쾌락에 무뎌지는 것'을 막아준다는 의미인 4번이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 덜 흥미로워 보이는 부분들을 건너뛰는 것
② 프로그램의 어떤 부분이 재미있는지 잊어버리는 것
③ 프로그램이 실제로 얼마나 즐거운지 알아차리는 것
④ 반복으로 인해 즐거움에 무뎌지게 되는 것
⑤ 지루한 장면뿐만 아니라 흥미로운 장면에도 집중하는 것

question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: We are the only species that seasons its food, deliberately ⓐ<u>altering</u> it with the highly flavored plant parts we call herbs and spices. It's quite possible ⓑ<u>that</u> our taste for spices has an evolutionary root. Many spices have antibacterial properties - in fact, common seasonings such as garlic, onion, and oregano ⓒ<u>inhibits</u> the growth of almost every bacterium tested. And the cultures that make the heaviest use of spices - think of the garlic and black pepper of Thai food, the ginger and coriander of India, the chili peppers of Mexico - come from warmer climates, ⓓ<u>where</u> bacterial spoilage is a bigger issue. In contrast, the most lightly spiced cuisines - those of Scandinavia and northern Europe - are from cooler climates. Our uniquely human attention to flavor, in this case the flavor of spices, turns out ⓔ<u>to have arisen</u> as a matter of life and death.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'common seasonings such as garlic, onion, and oregano'입니다. 핵심 주어는 복수 명사인 'common seasonings'이므로, 동사는 단수 형태인 inhibits가 아니라 복수 동사인 inhibit으로 써야 어법상 적절합니다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Emotion socialization - learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them - starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example, ⓐ<u>their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations</u>. ⓑ<u>Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development</u>. ⓒ<u>Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do is beneficial for younger children, they may intrude on adolescents' autonomy striving</u>. In consequence, ⓓ<u>adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted</u>. ⓔ<u>More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk</u>.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓒ 문장의 주어는 'direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do'입니다. A and B 형태의 주어가 서로 다른 두 가지 개념을 나타내므로 복수 취급을 하거나, 문맥상 '직접적인 달래기'와 '지시적 안내'라는 두 가지 행위를 뜻하므로 동사 is를 복수 동사인 are로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: We tend to overestimate the impact of new technologies in part because older technologies have become absorbed into the furniture of our lives, so as to be almost imperceptible. (A) This technology might be thought of as a classic time shifting device, as it enables mothers to exercise more control over the timing of feeding. (B) It can also function to save time, as bottle feeding allows for someone else to substitute for the mother's time. (C) For example, the baby bottle lets others, such as the father or an aunt, feed the baby anytime, anywhere. (D) This helps make daily routines more flexible and less stressful. (E) Potentially, therefore, it has huge implications for the management of time in everyday life, yet it is entirely overlooked in discussions of high speed society.
insertion_sentence: Take the baby bottle - a simple tool that has transformed a fundamental human experience for vast numbers of infants and mothers - but it finds no place in our histories of technology.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장은 젖병(baby bottle)을 예로 들며 기술의 역사에서 간과되고 있다는 점을 언급하고 있습니다. (A) 뒤의 문장에서 'This technology(이 기술)'가 가리키는 대상이 주어진 문장의 'baby bottle'이 되어야 논리적으로 연결됩니다. 따라서 (A) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 20. 다음 빈칸을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오. [24년 6월 32번]
passage: If we've invested in something that hasn't repaid us - be it money in a failing venture, or time in an unhappy relationship - we find it very difficult to walk away. This is the sunk cost fallacy. Our instinct is to (A)___________ investing money or time as we hope that our investment will prove to be worthwhile in the end. Giving up would mean (B)___________ that we've wasted something we can't get back, and that thought is so painful that we prefer to avoid it if we can. The problem, of course, is that if something really is a bad bet, then staying with it simply (C)___________ the amount we lose. Rather than walk away from a bad five year relationship, for example, we turn it into a bad 10 year relationship; rather than accept that we've lost a thousand dollars, we lay down another, thousand and lose that too. In the end, by delaying the pain of admitting our problem, we only add to it. Sometimes we just have to cut our losses.
subjective_conditions: (A), (B), (C) 각각 1단어로 쓸 것.
(A), (B), (C)에 각각 서로 다른 단어를 쓸 것.
<보기>에 주어진 단어 중 알맞은 것을 골라서 쓸 것.
<보기>에 주어진 단어를 필요시 어법에 맞게 변형할 것.
vocabulary_box: increase / relate / continue / cut / diminish / acknowledge / lose
explanation: 본 지문은 매몰 비용 오류(sunk cost fallacy)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. (A) 문맥상 이미 투자한 것이 아까워 투자를 '계속하려는(continue)' 본능이 있다는 내용이 적절합니다. to 뒤의 동사원형 자리입니다. (B) 포기하는 것은 우리가 되돌릴 수 없는 것을 낭비했다는 것을 '인정하는(acknowledging)' 것을 의미합니다. mean 뒤의 동명사 목적어 자리입니다. (C) 나쁜 상황에 머무르는 것은 잃는 양을 '증가시킨다(increases)'는 내용이 적절합니다. 주어가 staying(동명사구)이므로 단수 동사형태가 필요합니다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 바탕으로 구성한 아래 대화문의 빈칸 (A)와 (B)를 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오. [24년 6월 20번]
passage: Most people resist the idea of a true self-estimate, probably because they fear it might mean downgrading some of their beliefs about who they are and what they're capable of. As Goethe's maxim goes, it is a great failing "to see yourself as more than you are." How could you really be considered self-aware if you refuse to consider your weaknesses? Don't fear self-assessment because you're worried you might have to admit some things about yourself. The second half of Goethe's maxim is important too. He states that it is equally damaging to "value yourself at less than your true worth." We underestimate our capabilities just as much and just as dangerously as we overestimate other abilities. Cultivate the ability to judge yourself accurately and honestly. Look inward to discern what you're capable of and what it will take to unlock that potential.
subjective_conditions: (A)는 5단어, (B)는 6단어로 쓸 것.
<보기>에 주어진 단어를 변형하지 않고 그대로 쓸 것.
<보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것.
<보기> 이외의 단어를 추가하지 말 것.
vocabulary_box: they / clearly / self-doubt / like / what / see / without / exaggeration / ourselves / or / not /
answer: (A) not like what they see(B) ourselves clearly without exaggeration or self-doubt
explanation: 본 지문은 자신을 과대평가하거나 과소평가하지 말고 정직하고 정확하게 평가하라는 괴테의 격언을 인용하고 있습니다. (A) 사람들이 자신을 정직하게 보기를 두려워하는 이유는 '자신이 보는 것을 좋아하지 않을까봐(not like what they see)'입니다. (B) 마지막 문장에서 요약하는 목표는 과장이나 자기 의심 없이 우리 자신을 명확하게 보는 것입니다: 'see ourselves clearly without exaggeration or self-doubt'.

question: 23. 다음 글의 요약문을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
passage: Technologists are always on the lookout for quantifiable metrics. Measurable inputs to a model are their lifeblood, and like a social scientist, a technologist needs to identify concrete measures, or "proxies," for assessing progress. This need for quantifiable proxies produces a bias toward measuring things that are easy to quantify. But simple metrics can take us further away from the important goals we really care about, which may require complicated metrics or be extremely difficult, or perhaps impossible, to reduce to any measure. And when we have imperfect or bad proxies, we can easily fall under the illusion that we are solving for a good end without actually making genuine progress toward a worthy solution. The problem of proxies results in technologists frequently substituting what is measurable for what is meaningful. As the saying goes, "Not everything that counts can be counted, and not everything that can be counted counts."
summary_sentence: Technologists often rely on (A)_________________________ progress, but flawed proxies can create (B)___________ ______________________ meaningful solutions.
subjective_conditions: (A)는 4단어, (B)는 6단어로 쓸 것.
<보기>에 주어진 단어를 변형하지 않고 그대로 쓸 것.
<보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것.
<보기> 이외의 단어를 추가하지 말 것.
answer: (A) measurable proxies to assess(B) the illusion of achieving progress without
explanation: 이 지문은 기술자들이 측정 가능한 지표(proxies)에 의존하여 진행 상황을 평가하려 하지만, 이러한 지표들이 실제 중요한 목표와는 동떨어질 수 있다는 위험성을 경고하고 있습니다. (A)에는 기술자들이 진행 상황을 평가하기 위해 의존하는 '측정 가능한 대용치'라는 의미가 들어가야 하므로 'measurable proxies to assess'가 적절하며, (B)에는 결함이 있는 대용치가 진정한 진전 없이 목표를 달성하고 있다는 '착각'을 불러일으킬 수 있다는 내용이 들어가야 하므로 'the illusion of achieving progress without'이 적절합니다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 요약문을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
passage: The most prevalent problem kids report is that they feel like they need to be accessible at all times. Because technology allows for the access, they feel an obligation. It's easy for most of us to relate - you probably feel the same pressure in your own life! It is really challenging to deal with the fact that we're human and can't always respond instantly. For a teen or tween who's still learning the ins and outs of social interactions, it's even worse. Here's how this behavior plays out sometimes: Your child texts one of his friends, and the friend doesn't text back right away. Now it's easy for your child to think, "This person doesn't want to be my friend anymore!" So he texts again, and again, and again - "blowing up their phone." This leads to behaviors that may come across as aggressive. But you can see how easily this could happen.
summary_sentence: Technology allows constant (A)_____________, making kids feel obligated to be available at all times. When friends don't (B)_____________ immediately, teens who are still learning (C)_____________ may feel stressed and keep messaging them. This frustration can build up and lead to (D)_____________ actions, like throwing their own phone.
subjective_conditions: (A), (B), (D)는 각각 1단어, (C)는 2단어로 쓸 것.
(A), (B), (C), (D)에 각각 서로 다른 단어를 쓸 것.
본문에서 단어를 찾아 변형하지 말고 그대로 쓸 것.
본문 이외의 단어를 추가하지 말 것.
explanation: 이 지문은 기술이 언제나 접속 가능한 환경을 제공함으로써 아이들이 즉각 응답해야 한다는 의무감을 느끼고, 상대방이 즉시 답하지 않을 때 불안감을 느껴 공격적인 행동으로 이어질 수 있음을 설명합니다. 본문의 내용을 바탕으로 (A)는 기술이 허용하는 '접속(access)', (B)는 친구가 즉각 '응답(respond)'하지 않는 상황, (C)는 십대들이 배우고 있는 '사회적 상호작용(social interactions)', (D)는 과도한 메시지 보내기로 나타나는 '공격적인(aggressive)' 행동을 의미합니다.

question: 12. 다음 그랽의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We are the only species that seasons its food, deliberately altering it with the highly flavored plant parts we call herbs and spices. It's quite possible that our taste for spices has an evolutionary root. Many spices have antibacterial properties - in fact, common seasonings such as garlic, onion, and oregano inhibit the growth of almost every bacterium tested. And the cultures that make the heaviest use of spices - think of the garlic and black pepper of Thai food, the ginger and coriander of India, the chili peppers of Mexico - come from warmer climates, where bacterial spoilage is a bigger issue. In contrast, the most lightly spiced cuisines - those of Scandinavia and northern Europe - are from cooler climates. Our uniquely human attention to flavor, in this case the flavor of spices, turns out to have arisen as a matter of life and death.
options: ① The Spread of Spices Through History
② Cultural Differences in the Use of Spices
③ How Cooking Changed Human Evolution
④ Why Humans Are the Only Species That Cook
⑤ The Evolutionary Role of Spices in Human Diet
explanation: 이 글은 인간이 필수적으로 향신뇌를 사용하게 된 이유가 박테리아 성장 역제를 통한 생존, 즉 진화적 뿌리(생사의 문제)에 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 인간의 식단에서 향신뇌가 갖는 진화적 역할을 다례 ⑤번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 역사를 통한 향신뇌의 확산
② 향신뇌 사용의 문화적 차이
③ 요리가 인류의 진화를 어떻게 바그었나
④ 요 인간이 요리하는 유일한 종인 이유
⑤ 인간 식단에서 향신뇌의 진화적 역할

question: 13. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are (A)[crucial / dispensable]. In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. All experts are not the same, nor do they submit their work to the same scrutiny. Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims. For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were funded in part by the sugar industry. The authors did not (B)[conceal / disclose] their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared. Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have encouraged higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. Stories such as this one fuel suspicion - but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. Funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since been made not (C)[optional / compulsory].
options: ① crucial   disclosecompulsory
② crucial   discloseoptional
③ crucial   concealoptional
④ dispensable   disclosecompulsory
⑤ dispensable   concealcompulsory
explanation: (A) 과학이 완전히 신뢰받지 못하는 이유가 있으므로 비판적 사고는 '필수적(crucial)'입니다. (B) 뒤에 이어지는 문맥에서 설탕 산업으로부터 자금을 지원받았음에도 이를 밝히지 않아 문제가 되었으므로, 저자들이 자금원을 '공개(disclose)'하지 않았다는 흐름이 적절합니다. (원문은 did not disclose)(C) 과거에는 요구되지 않았으나 이후에는 '선택적인(optional)' 사항이 아니게 되었다(즉, 의무가 되었다)는 흐름입니다. (원문의 Not optional은 필수적이라는 뜻입니다.) *참고: 원문 출처(25년 3월 30번)에서는 마지막 문장이 'have since been made compulsory'로 되어 있으나, 이 문제의 선택지 구성을 보면 'not optional'의 구조를 의도한 것으로 보입니다. 정답표상 ②번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 필수적인 - 공개하다 - 의무적인
② 필수적인 - 공개하다 - 선택적인
③ 필수적인 - 숨기다 - 선택적인
④ 없어도 되는 - 공개하다 - 의무적인
⑤ 없어도 되는 - 숨기다 - 의무적인

question: 14. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.0점]
passage: For years, many psychologists have held strongly to the belief that the key to addressing negative health habits is to change behavior. This, more than values and attitudes, is the part of personality that is easiest to change. Ingestive habits such as smoking, drinking and various eating behaviors are the most common health concerns targeted for behavioral changes. Process-addiction behaviors (workaholism, shopaholism, and the like) fall into this category as well. Mental imagery combined with power of suggestion was taken up as the premise of behavioral medicine to help people change negative health behaviors into positive ones. Although this technique alone will not produce changes, when used alongside other behavior modification tactics and coping strategies, behavioral changes have proved effective for some people. What mental imagery does is reinforce a new desired behavior. Repeated use of images reinforces the desired behavior more strongly over time.
options: ① 행동 변화는 가치관과 태도의 변화 이후에 이루어진다.
② 정신적 이미지 기법은 반복적으로 사용할수록 효과가 더 크다.
③ 행동 수정 전략은 부정적인 감정을 줄이는 데에 사용될 수 있다.
④ 행동 중심 접근과 다른 행동 전략을 함께 사용하면 성격을 변화시킬 수 있다.
⑤ 건강한 습관 형성을 위해서는 행동 중심의 접근과 정신적 이미지 기법이 효과적이다.
explanation: 이 글은 부정적인 건강 습관을 교정하기 위해 행동 변화(behavioral changes)를 타겟으로 하며, 특히 '정신적 이미지(mental imagery)' 기법이 다른 행동 수정 전략과 함께 사용될 때 새로운 바람직한 행동을 강화하는 데 효과적임을 설명하고 있습니다.

question: 15. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: Commitmentis the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life. Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby facilitating the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. Moreover, commitments make people (A)[reluctant / willing] to perform actions that they would not otherwise perform. For example, a taxi driver picks up his clients and transports them to their desired destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a (B)[doubtful / reliable] commitment to pay her at the end of the month. Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to taking various measures to (C)[maintain / undermine] the currency in question. Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.
options: ① reluctant reliablemaintain
② reluctant doubtfulundermine
③ willing doubtfulmaintain
④ willing reliableundermine
⑤ willing reliablemaintain
explanation: (A) 약속(Commitment)은 사람들이 평소라면 하지 않았을 행동을 기꺼이 '하도록(willing)' 만듭니다. (B) 고용주가 월말에 임금을 지불하겠다는 '신뢰할 만한(reliable)' 약속을 했기 때문에 노동자는 일합니다. (C) 화폐 가치를 '유지하기(maintain)' 위해 중앙은행 등이 약속하고 노력하기 때문에 사람들은 돈을 대가로 받아들입니다.
options_translation: ① 꺼리는 - 신뢰할 만한 - 유지하다
② 꺼리는 - 의심스러운 - 훼손하다
③ 기꺼이 하는 - 의심스러운 - 유지하다
④ 기꺼이 하는 - 신뢰할 만한 - 훼손하다
⑤ 기꺼이 하는 - 신뢰할 만한 - 유지하다

question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면? [2.9점]
passage: Intuition can be great, but it ought to be hard-earned. Experts, for example, are able to think on their feet because they ⓐ<u>had</u> invested thousands of hours in learning and practice: their intuition has become data-driven. Only then are they able to act quickly in accordance with their ⓑ<u>internalized</u> expertise and evidence-based experience. Yet most people are not experts, though they often think they are. Most of us, especially when we interact with others on social media, ⓒ<u>acting</u> with expert-like speed and conviction, offering a wide range of opinions on global crises, without the substance of knowledge that supports it. And thanks to Al, which ensures that our messages are delivered to an audience more inclined to ⓓ<u>believe</u> it, our personal filter bubble can ⓔ<u>reinforce</u> our delusions of expertise. We have an interesting tendency to find people more open-minded, rational, and sensible when they think just like us.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓐ 'had invested'는 문맥상 과거 완료를 쓸 근거가 부족하며, 현재까지 영향을 미치는 현재 완료 'have invested'가 적절합니다. ⓒ 문장의 주어는 'Most of us'이고 이에 대응하는 본동사가 필요하므로 현재분사 'acting' 대신 'act'가 와야 합니다. ⓓ 'believe'의 목적어인 'it'은 복수 명사인 'our messages'를 지칭하므로 'them'으로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓑ 'internalized'는 '내면화된 전문 지식'으로 과거분사가 적절하게 쓰였으며, ⓔ 'reinforce'는 조동사 'can' 뒤의 동사원형으로 적절합니다.

question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, ___________________________________________.
options: ① gestures delay the flow of fluent speech
② speech always leads thought, and gesture mirrors it
③ gestures are not just a secondary addition to speech
④ gestures were once useful but are not mostly unnecessary
⑤ gestures reflect the speaker's thoughts more clearly than speech

question: 18. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: In order to bring the ever-increasing costs of home care for elderly and needy persons under control, managers of home care providers have introduced management systems. These systems specify tasks of home care workers and the time and budget available to perform these tasks. Electronic reporting systems require home care workers to report on their activities and the time spent, thus making the distribution of time and money visible and, in the perception of managers, controllable. This, in the view of managers, has contributed to the resolution of the problem. The home care workers, on the other hand, may perceive their work not as a set of separate tasks to be performed as efficiently as possible, but as a service to be provided to a client with whom they may have developed a relationship. This includes having conversations with clients and enquiring about the person's well-being. Restricted time and the requirement to report may be perceived as obstacles that make it impossible to deliver the service that is needed. If the management systems are too rigid, this may result in home care workers becoming overloaded and demotivated.
options: ① How Electronic Reporting Improves the Quality of Home Care
② The Harmful Effects of Budget Reduction on Elderly Care Services
③ Why Do Management Systems Make the Home Care Workers' Work Easier?
④ Management Systems: Conflicting Perspectives Between Managers and Workers
⑤ Conversation with Clients: A Commonly Neglected Aspect in Elderly Care Services

question: 19. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 모두 고르면?
passage: Quite often the interaction between groups is socially unequal, and this is reflected in the fact that in many cases borrowing of words or constructions goes mostly or entirely in one direction, from the more powerful or prestigious group to the less favored one. The languages of socially subordinated groups may from quite an early period of contact provide terminology for objects or practices with which speakers of the more powerful group were previously unfamiliar. However, the effects of contact in that direction may not progress any further than this. In some cases, as with the Dharug language of Sydney, Australia, the source of some of the earliest loans from Indigenous Australian languages into English, the fate of the language system is extinction after the obliteration of many of its speakers. The remainder shifted to varieties of English, the language of the people who had suppressed them.
options: ① Word borrowing between languages always occurs in one direction.
② Powerful groups tend to borrow more from less favored ones.
③ Subordinated languages sometimes provide terms unfamiliar to dominant groups.
④ English borrowed some Indigenous Australian words from the Dharug language.
⑤ Many former Dharug speakers adopted forms of English.
explanation: 이 글은 언어 간의 상호작용이 사회적으로 불평등할 때, 단어의 차용이 주로 더 강력한 집단에서 덜 우호적인 집단으로 흐른다고 설명합니다. ① 본문에서 차용이 '대부분 또는 전적으로(mostly or entirely)' 한 방향으로 흐른다고 했지, '항상(always)' 그렇다고 하지는 않았으므로 틀린 설명입니다.② 본문에 따르면 강력한 집단이 덜 우호적인 집단으로부터 용어를 빌려오기도 하지만, 전반적인 차용의 흐름은 더 강력한 집단에서 덜 우호적인 집단으로 향합니다. 따라서 강력한 집단이 더 많이 빌려오는 경향이 있다는 진술은 본문의 내용(강력한 집단에서 덜 강력한 집단으로의 흐름)과 반대되므로 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 언어 간의 단어 차용은 항상 한 방향으로 일어난다.

③ 종속된 언어는 때때로 지배적인 집단에게 생소한 용어를 제공한다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 요약문의 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오. (단, 어형 변형 없음)
passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem; they remove unwanted plants that begin to emerge and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the fruit and vegetable.
summary_sentence: A vegetable garden is a small-scale ecosystem that a grower tries to maintain in a productive state by regularly (A)___________ in its natural processes. This involves actions like removing weeds or blocking pests. However, as this desired state is far from being (B)___________, even a short break in management can cause the garden to (C)___________ less produce, as other plants and animals start to take over.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 쓸 것
각각 한 단어로 쓸 것
어형 변형 없음
explanation: 채소밭이라는 생태계를 생산적인 상태로 유지하기 위해 재배자는 자연적인 과정에 규칙적으로 '개입(intervening)'합니다. 본문에서 'intervening'을 찾을 수 있습니다. 또한, 이러한 생산 최대화 상태는 본질적으로 '불안정한(unstable)' 상태이므로, '안정적인(stable)' 상태와는 거리가 멉니다(far from being stable). 마지막으로, 관리를 멈추면 다른 식물과 동물이 차지하게 되어 농작물을 덜 '산출(yield)'하게 됩니다.

question: 21. 다음 <보기>에 주어진 표현들을 모두 사용하여, 주어진 질문에 대한 답을 본문의 내용에 근거하여 완전한 문장으로 완성하시오. (단, 필요시 같은 단어 중복 사용 가능, 어형 변형 가능)
passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
subjective_conditions: <보기>에 주어진 표현을 모두 사용할 것
본문의 내용에 근거할 것
완전한 문장으로 완성할 것
필요시 같은 단어 중복 사용 가능, 어형 변형 가능
answer: The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the likelihood of future success.
explanation: 본문 하단에 'The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success'라는 문장이 명시되어 있습니다. <보기>의 'the likelihood'를 사용하여 'probability'를 대체하거나 변형하여 완전한 문장을 작성하면 됩니다.

question: 22. 다음 글에서 어법상 어색한 부분을 총 3개 찾아 어색한 부분만을 각각 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오. (단, 답의 순서는 무관함)
passage: Stress not only affects physical disease but the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain. A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and those who had experienced long-lasting stress. Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you to remain resilient when you are in the face of stress and is involving in mood regulation. It also helps you monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turn signals for cortisol "on" instead of "off," that can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.
subjective_conditions: 답의 순서는 무관함
answer: (1) those who → people, (2) involving → involved, (3) turn → turning
explanation: 1) 문맥상 해마와 스트레스를 겪은 '사람들' 사이의 연관성을 나타내는데, 지문 원문에 따라 'those who'를 'people'로 수정하는 것이 적절합니다. 2) 'be involved in'은 '~에 관여하다, 연루되다'라는 의미의 수동태 표현으로 쓰여야 하므로 'involving'을 'involved'로 고쳐야 합니다. 3) 'lead to'에서 'to'는 전치사로 쓰여 뒤에 명사나 동명사가 와야 하므로, 동사원형 'turn'을 동명사 'turning'으로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 15. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The explosion of popular music in the second half of the twentieth century as well as the global circulation and dissemination of music by the creative industries propelled a new understanding of accessbility in relation to music. Suddenly, in the 1950s, anyone could pick up spoons, a couple of pans, a second-hand guitar and start a band. This led to specific genres such as skiffle, but also, more generally, reflected a much more relaxed and inclusive attitude to music making. While ordinary people had always sung and made music, the popular music movement was driven by a spirit of rebellion and freedom. This approach led to the punk movement, whose musicians even made it a condition for their music to be non-virtuosic and accessible to all in the 1970s. Groups who had been entirely excluded from music revelled in opportunities to create. This led to a sense of novelty and empowerment in and beyond the music sphere.

question: 16. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem; they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. question: 17. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol "on" instead of "off," which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.

question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: As a general rule, it's better if your definition corresponds as closely as possible to the way ⓐ<u>in which</u> the term is ordinarily used in the kinds of debates to which your claims are pertinent. There will be, however, occasions where it is appropriate, even necessary, to coin special uses ⓑ<u>through which</u> philosophers call stimulative definition. This would be the case where the current lexicon is not able to make distinctions ⓒ<u>that</u> you think are philosophically important. For example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something the person ⓓ<u>having</u> it has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories: I would have a memory-type experience, but this would not be ⓔ<u>of something</u> that I had actually experienced. To call this a memory would be misleading. For this reason, philosophers have coined the special term 'quasimemory' to refer to these hypothetical memory-like experiences.
explanation: ⓑ 'through which' 다음에는 완전한 문장이 와야 하는데, 뒤의 'call' 동사의 목적어 보어는 있지만 직접 목적어가 빠져 있는 불완전한 문장 구조입니다. 따라서 여기서는 'call A B' (A를 B라고 부르다) 구문에서 목적어 A 역할을 하는 관계대명사 'which' 또는 'that'이 쓰여야 적절합니다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the ⓐ<u>astonishing</u> notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally ⓑ<u>trigger</u> a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes ⓒ<u>disjointed</u> because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other ⓓ<u>commendable</u> effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy ⓔ<u>companion</u>, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.

question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition. But it's important to understand the limits of dictionary definitions. More often than not, a definition in a dictionary requires readers to have a fairly robust understanding of the language already at their disposal. In other words, a dictionary functions in many cases as a cross-reference or translator between words one knows and words that one doesn't yet know. However, there are words that may be defined not through other words but only by pointing to something in our experience. Even the most obscure words in a dictionary, say, for example, "pulchritudinous" or "kalokagathia," must be defined using words that the reader already knows and understands. Otherwise, the dictionary isn't very helpful: its utility depends largely on ____________________________.

question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a ⓐ<u>prime</u> example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. Indeed, a ⓑ<u>final</u> success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these ⓒ<u>payoffs</u> further increasing her odds of scoring another win. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're ⓓ<u>extraordinarily</u> talented. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply ⓔ<u>reflect</u> an underlying talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
explanation: 글의 흐름상 이전의 성공이 다음 성공의 확률을 높인다는 마태 효과(Matthew effect)를 설명하고 있으므로, '최종적인(final)' 성공이 아니라 '초기(early/initial)'의 성공이 과학자에게 정당성과 자원 등을 제공하여 후속 성공으로 이어진다는 맥락이 되어야 합니다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much a creative process. A conjecture is a philosophical invention, cooked up rather mystically by the mind through the mental computation we call careful contemplation. However, until the hypothesis is tested against reality, it is not yet truly knowledge; it is just information that represents speculation. Knowledge is information that has demonstrated its usefulness. It is what is left over after cycles of experimental testing have eliminated false theories. As scientists continually test their hypotheses and modify their models to account for new and surprising data, a kind of "learning loop" emerges that statisticians call Bayesian updating. Based on Bayes' Rule, developed by eighteenth-century English statistician and philosopher Thomas Bayes, Bayesian updating refers to a mathematical process whereby an accepted theory or predictive model gets increasingly accurate through the repetitive testing of competing variants of that theory.
summary_sentence: In other words, science progresses not only through logical reasoning but also through _______________________________.
options: ① blind tests to established theories
② strong reliance on unchanging facts
③ continuous revision based on evidence
④ emotional contemplation and personal beliefs
⑤ the rejection of creativity in forming conjectures

question: 24. 다음 글을 읽고 나눈 아래의 대화에서 글의 내용을 이해하지 못한 사람을 두 명 고르면?
passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports.
options: ① Olivia: Because agricultural output is highly dependent on natural conditions, it is not always possible for many nations to be entirely self-sufficient in food production.
② Ethan: The primary objective of food security is to maintain national pride through complete independence in agricultural production.

④ Noah: Imports can be a strategic support to domestic agriculture in achieving a stable and sufficient food supply.
⑤ Grace: A country importing certain food items cannot maintain its ability to achieve food security.

question: 27. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

passage: Financial markets do more than take capital from the rich and lend it to everyone else. They enable each of us to smooth consumption over our lifetimes, which is a fancy way of saying that we don't have to spend income at the same time we earn it. Shakespeare may have admonished us to be neither borrowers nor lenders; the fact is that most of us will be both at some point. If we lived in an agrarian society, we would have to eat our crops reasonably soon after the harvest or find some way to store them. Financial markets are a more sophisticated way of managing the harvest. We can spend income now that we have not yet earned─as by borrowing for college or a home─or we can earn income now and spend it later, as by saving for retirement. The important point is that earning income has been divorced from spending it, allowing us much more flexibility in life.

passage: Commitment is the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life. Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby facilitating the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. Moreover, commitments make people willing to perform actions that they would not otherwise perform. For example, a taxi driver picks up his clients and transports them to their desired destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a credible commitment to pay her at the end of the month. Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to taking various measures to sustain the currency in question. Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.*fluctuation: 동요
