passage: If you had wanted to create a "self-driving" car in the 1950s, your best option might have been to strap a brick to the accelerator. Yes, the vehicle would have been able to move forward on its own, but it could not slow down, stop, or turn to avoid barriers. Obviously not ideal. But does that mean the entire concept of the self-driving car is not worth pursuing? No, it only means that at the time we did not yet have the tools we now possess to help enable vehicles to operate both autonomously and safely. This once-distant dream now seems within our reach. It is much the same story in medicine. Two decades ago, we were still taping bricks to accelerators. Today, we are approaching the point where we can begin to bring some appropriate technology to bear in ways that advance our understanding of patients as unique individuals. In fact, many patients are already wearing devices that monitor their conditions in real time, which allows doctors to talk to their patients in a specific, refined, and feedback-driven way that was not even possible a decade ago.
options: ① Why Self-Driving Cars Will Never Work
② The Impact of Cars on Modern Healthcare
③ The Future of Cars: How Technology is Changing Vehicles
④ The Benefits of Developing Self-Driving Cars and Personalized Medicine
⑤ From Dreams to Reality: The Emergence of Self-Driving Cars and Personalized Healthcare
explanation: 이 글은 1950년대의 자율주행차 구상을 가속 페달에 벽돌을 묶는 것에 비유하며 당시에는 기술이 부족했음을 언급합니다. 하지만 현재는 자율주행 기술이 실현 가능해졌으며, 의료 분야에서도 이와 마찬가지로 과거의 단순한 방식을 벗어나 개별 환자에게 맞춤화된 기술적 진보(실시간 상태 모니터링 등)가 이루어지고 있음을 설명합니다. 과거의 꿈이었던 기술들이 현실로 나타나고 있다는 내용이므로 ⑤번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 자율주행차가 결코 작동하지 않을 이유
② 자동차가 현대 의료에 미치는 영향
③ 자동차의 미래: 기술이 차량을 어떻게 변화시키고 있는가
④ 자율주행차 및 개인 맞춤형 의학 개발의 이점
⑤ 꿈에서 현실로: 자율주행차와 개인 맞춤형 의료 서비스의 출현

question: 10. 다음 글을 읽고 이해한 내용으로 옳은 것은? [24년 3월 33번]
passage: Beethoven's drive to create something novel is a reflection of his state of curiosity. Our brains experience a sense of reward when we create something new in the process of exploring something uncertain, such as a musical phrase that we've never played or heard before. When our curiosity leads to something novel, the resulting reward brings us a sense of pleasure. A number of investigators have modeled how curiosity influences musical composition. In the case of Beethoven, computer modeling focused on the thirty-two piano sonatas written after age thirteen revealed that the musical patterns found in all of Beethoven's music decreased in later sonatas, while novel patterns, including patterns that were unique to a particular sonata, increased. In other words, Beethoven's music became less predictable over time as his curiosity drove the exploration of new musical ideas. Curiosity is a powerful driver of human creativity.*sonata: 악곡의 한 형식
options: ① Beethoven's desire to create something new has nothing to do with his curiosity.
② Humans are less likely to feel pleasure in the process of creating something new.
③ Investigators revealed that Beethoven's later sonatas contained patterns which did not appear in earlier sonatas.
④ It turns out that Beethoven's curiosity held back his pursuit of new musical concepts.
⑤ Curiosity interferes with humans' creative process.
explanation: 본문은 베토벤의 창의성이 호기심에서 비롯되었으며, 후기 피아노 소나타로 갈수록 이전에는 나타나지 않았던 새로운 음악적 패턴들이 증가했음을 설명합니다. 컴퓨터 모델링 결과에 따르면 후기 소나타에서 참신한 패턴(novel patterns)이 증가했다고 언급되어 있으므로 ③번이 글의 내용과 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 새로운 것을 만들고자 하는 베토벤의 욕구는 그의 호기심과 아무런 관련이 없다.
② 인간은 새로운 것을 창조하는 과정에서 즐거움을 느낄 가능성이 더 낮다.
③ 조사관들은 베토벤의 후기 소나타가 초기 소나타에는 나타나지 않았던 패턴들을 포함하고 있음을 밝혀냈다.
④ 베토벤의 호기심이 새로운 음악적 개념에 대한 그의 추구를 방해했음이 드러났다.
⑤ 호기심은 인간의 창의적 과정을 방해한다.

question: 11. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: It is a common assumption that most vagrant birds are ultimately doomed, aside from the rare cases where individuals are able to reorientate and return to their normal ranges. In turn, it is also commonly assumed that vagrancy itself is a relatively unimportant biological phenomenon.
ordered_passages: (A) In such cases, the most profound consequences of vagrancy relate to the establishment of new breeding sites, new migration routes and wintering locations. Each of these can occur through different mechanisms, and at different frequencies, and they each have their own unique importance.

(B) However, there are many lines of evidence to suggest that vagrancy can, on rare occasions, dramatically alter the fate of populations, species or even whole ecosystems. Despite being infrequent, these events can be extremely important when viewed at the timescales over which ecological and evolutionary processes unfold.

(C) This is undoubtedly true for the majority of cases, as the most likely outcome of any given vagrancy event is that the individual will fail to find enough resources, and/or be exposed to inhospitable environmental conditions, and perish.
explanation: 주어진 글은 길을 잃은 새(vagrant birds)들이 대개 죽음에 이르고, 이러한 현상이 생물학적으로 중요하지 않다는 일반적인 가정을 소개합니다. (C)는 이러한 가정이 대다수의 경우에 '의심할 여지 없이 사실(undoubtedly true)'임을 확인하며 보충 설명합니다. (B)에서는 'However'를 통해 반전을 꾀하며, 드물지만 이러한 사건들이 생태적, 진화적 관점에서 매우 중요할 수 있음을 제시합니다. (A)는 (B)에서 언급한 '그러한 경우들(In such cases)'의 구체적인 결과(새로운 번식지, 이주 경로 형성 등)를 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 정답은 (C)-(B)-(A)입니다.

question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
passage: The most prevalent problem kids report is that they feel like they need to be accessible at all times.
ordered_passages: (A) For a teen or tween who's still learning the ins and outs of social interactions, it's even worse. Here's how this behavior plays out sometimes: Your child texts one of his friends, and the friend doesn't text back right away.

(B) Now it's easy for your child to think, "This person doesn't want to be my friend anymore!" So he texts again, and again, and again - "blowing up their phone." This can be stress-inducing and even read as aggressive. But you can see how easily this could happen.

(C) Because technology allows for it, they feel an obligation. It's easy for most of us to relate - you probably feel the same pressure in your own life! It is really challenging to deal with the fact that we're human and can't always respond instantly.
explanation: 주어진 글은 아이들이 언제 어디서나 연락 가능해야 한다는 압박감을 느낀다는 문제를 제시합니다. (C)는 기술이 이를 가능케 하기 때문에 의무감을 느끼는 것이며, 성인들도 공감할 수 있는 인간의 한계에 대해 설명합니다. (A)는 'For a teen or tween'을 통해 사회적 상호작용을 배우는 단계의 아이들에게는 이 상황이 '더 심각함(even worse)'을 언급하며 구체적인 문자 메시지 상황을 예로 듭니다. (B)는 (A)에서 제시된 상황의 결과로, 즉각적인 답장이 없을 때 아이가 느낄 수 있는 불안과 그로 인한 행동(반복적 문자 발송)을 설명하며 글을 맺습니다. 따라서 정답은 (C)-(A)-(B)입니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
passage: Development of the human body from a single cell provides many examples of the structural richness that is possible when the repeated production of random variation is combined with nonrandom selection. All phases of body development from embryo to adult ⓐ<u>display</u> random activities at the cellular level, and body formation depends on the new possibilities generated by these activities coupled with selection of those outcomes that satisfy previously built-in criteria. Always new structure is based on old structure, and at every stage selection favors some cells and ⓑ<u>eliminates</u> others. The survivors serve to ⓒ<u>produce</u> new cells that undergo further rounds of selection. Except in the immune system, cells and extensions of cells are not genetically selected during development, but rather, are positionally selected. Those in the right place that make the right connections are stimulated, and those that don't are ⓓ<u>restored</u>. This process is much like sculpting. A natural consequence of the strategy is great variability from individual to individual at the cell and molecular levels, even though large-scale structures are quite ⓔ<u>comparable</u>.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 인체 발달 과정이 무작위적 변이와 비무작위적 선택의 결합을 통해 이루어짐을 설명하며, 이를 조각(sculpting) 과정에 비유하고 있습니다. 조각 과정에서는 불필요한 부분을 깎아내거나 제거하게 됩니다. 문맥상 적절한 장소에 있지 않거나 올바른 연결을 맺지 못한 세포들은 '복구되는(restored)' 것이 아니라 제거되어야 조각의 비유가 성립합니다. 따라서 ⓓ는 'eliminated' 또는 'discarded'와 같은 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We are the only species that seasons its food, deliberately altering it with the highly flavored plant parts we call herbs and spices. It's quite possible that our taste for spices has an evolutionary root. Many spices have antibacterial properties - in fact, common seasonings such as garlic, onion, and oregano inhibit the growth of almost every bacterium tested. And the cultures that make the heaviest use of spices - think of the garlic and black pepper of Thai food, the ginger and coriander of India, the chili peppers of Mexico - come from warmer climates, where ________________________________. In contrast, the most lightly spiced cuisines - those of Scandinavia and northern Europe - are from cooler climates. Our uniquely human attention to flavor, in this case the flavor of spices, turns out to have arisen as a matter of life and death.*cuisine: 요리(법)
options: ① foods barely go bad due to climate conditions
② healthcare industry is relatively underdeveloped
③ foods are vulnerable to decay due to bacterial growth
④ agriculture takes up a large part of the national economy
⑤ scientists actively engaged in the study of relationship between climate and food expense
explanation: 지문은 인류가 음식이 쉽게 상할 수 있는 더운 기후에서 박테리아 성장을 억제하기 위해 항균 작용이 있는 향신료를 사용해 왔음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 더운 기후에서는 박테리아 성장에 의해 음식이 부패하기 쉽다는 내용이 빈칸에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The fast-growing, tremendous amount of data, collected and stored in large and numerous data repositories, has overwhelmed human understanding. As a result, data collected in large data repositories become "data tombs" - data archives that are hardly visited. Important decisions are often made based not on the information-rich data stored in data repositories but rather on a decision maker's instinct, simply because the decision maker does not have the tools to obtain the valuable knowledge hidden in the vast amounts of data. Efforts have been made to develop expert system and knowledge-based technologies, which typically rely on users or domain experts to manually input knowledge into knowledge bases. However, this procedure is likely to cause biases and errors and is extremely costly and time consuming. The increasing gap between data and information __________________________________________ for better decision-making.
options: ① accommodates useless data in the bush of knowledge
② contributes to creating affective ways to approach the problems
③ makes negative impact on the public opinion in development of new tools
④ promotes using exceptional means to deal with data distortion issues
⑤ highlights the need for a developed approach to extract valuable knowledge
explanation: 데이터는 방대해지지만 인간이 이를 이해하고 가치 있는 지식을 추출할 도구가 부족하여 정보로 전환되지 못하는 상황을 설명하고 있습니다. 이러한 데이터와 정보 사이의 간극은 더 나은 의사결정을 위해 가치 있는 지식을 추출하기 위한 발전된 접근법의 필요성을 강조하게 됩니다.

question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In order to bring the ever increasing costs of home care for elderly and needy persons under control, managers of home care providers have introduced management systems. These systems specify tasks of home care workers and the time and budget available to perform these tasks. Electronic reporting systems require home care workers to report on their activities and the time spent, thus making the distribution of time and money visible and, in the perception of managers, controllable. This, in the view of managers, has contributed to the resolution of the problem. The home care workers, on the other hand, may perceive their work not as a set of separate tasks to be performed as efficiently as possible, but as a service to be provided to a client with whom they may have developed a relationship. This includes having conversations with clients and enquiring about the person's well-being. Restricted time and the requirement to report may be perceived as obstacles that make it impossible to deliver the service that is needed. As a result, if the management systems ____________ their autonomy, they may become overloaded and demotivated.
options: ① validate
② facilitate
③ empower
④ promote
⑤ regulate
explanation: 글의 맥락상 관리 시스템이 요양 보호사들의 업무 시간과 보고 의무를 엄격히 규정하여 그들의 자율성을 제한하고 억제한다는 내용이 와야 합니다. 따라서 '규제하다' 또는 '제한하다'라는 의미의 regulate가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 정당화하다
② 용이하게 하다
③ 권한을 부여하다
④ 촉진하다
⑤ 규제하다

question: 18. 윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절하게 짝지어진 것은?
passage: Empathy is frequently listed as one of the most desired skills in an employer or employee, although without specifying exactly what is meant by empathy. (A)____________, some businesses stress cognitive empathy, emphasizing the need for leaders to understand the perspective of employees and customers when negotiating deals and making decisions. Others stress affective empathy and empathic concern, emphasizing the ability of leaders to gain trust from employees and customers by treating them with real concern and compassion. When some consultants argue that successful companies foster empathy, what that translates to is that companies should conduct good market research. (B)____________, an "empathic" company understands the needs and wants of its customers and seeks to fulfill those needs and wants. When some people speak of design with empathy, what that translates to is that companies should take into account the specific needs of different populations - the blind, the deaf, the elderly, non-English speakers, the color-blind, and so on - when designing products.
subjective_answer_format: (A)     (B)① SpecificallyNevertheless② In contrastThat is to say③ For exampleIn other words④ MeanwhileWhich means⑤ In particularInstead
options: ① Specifically / Nevertheless
② In contrast / That is to say
③ For example / In other words
④ Meanwhile / Which means
⑤ In particular / Instead

question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오. [4.0점]

passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an ⓒ<u>inherently</u> unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more ⓓ<u>stable</u> state. question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

passage: Everyone's heard the expression don't let the perfect become the enemy of the good. If you want to get over an obstacle so that your idea can become the solution-based policy you've long dreamed of, you can't have an all-or-nothing mentality. You have to be willing to alter your idea and let others influence its outcome. You have to be okay with the outcome being a little different, even a little less, than you wanted. Say you're pushing for a clean water act. Even if what emerges isn't as well funded as you wished, or doesn't match how you originally conceived the bill, you'll have still succeeded in ensuring that kids in troubled areas have access to clean water. That's what counts, that they will be safer because of your idea and your effort. Is it perfect? No. Is there more work to be done? Absolutely. But in almost every case, helping move the needle forward is vastly better than not helping at all.

question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Beethoven's drive to create something novel is a reflection of his state of curiosity. Our brains experience a sense of reward when we create something new in the process of exploring something uncertain, such as a musical phrase that we've never played or heard before. When our curiosity leads to something novel, the resulting reward brings us a sense of pleasure. A number of investigators have modeled how curiosity influences musical composition. In the case of Beethoven, computer modeling focused on the thirty-two piano sonatas written after age thirteen revealed that the musical patterns found in all of Beethoven's music decreased in later sonatas, while novel patterns, including patterns that were common to a particular sonata, increased. In other words, Beethoven's music became less predictable over time as his curiosity drove the exploration of new musical ideas. Curiosity is a powerful driver of human creativity.
options: ① benefits of technology in music analysis
② curiosity as a driving force of creativity
③ listeners' preference for familiar melodies
④ role of environment in Beethoven's musical style
⑤ influence of cultural trends on Beethoven's compositions

question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Free play is nature's means of teaching children that they are not helpless. In play, away from adults, children really do have control and can practice asserting it. In free play, children learn to make their own decisions, solve their own problems, create and follow rules, and get along with others as equals rather than as obedient or rebellious subordinates. In active outdoor play, children deliberately dose themselves with moderate amounts of fear and they thereby learn how to control not only their bodies, but also their fear. In social play children learn how to negotiate with others, how to please others, and how to manage and overcome the anger that can arise from conflicts. None of these lessons can be taught through verbal means; they can be learned only through experience, which free play provides.

question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It's untrue that teens can __________________________-what they're doing is shifting their attention from one task to another. In this digital age, teens wire their brains to make these shifts very quickly, but they are still, like everyone else, paying attention to one thing at a time, sequentially. Common sense tells us multitasking should increase brain activity, but Carnegie Mellon University scientists using the latest brain imaging technology find it doesn't. As a matter of fact, they discovered that multitasking actually decreases brain activity. Neither task is done as well as if each were performed individually. Fractions of a second are lost every time we make a switch, and a person's interrupted task can take 50 percent longer to finish, with 50 percent more errors. Turns out the latest brain research supports the old advice "one thing at a time."It's not that kids can't do some tasks simultaneously. But if two tasks are performed at once, one of them has to be familiar. Our brains perform a familiar task on "automatic pilot" while really paying attention to the other one. That's why insurance companies consider talking on a cell phone and driving to be as dangerous as driving while drunk - it's the driving that goes on "automatic pilot" while the conversation really holds our attention. Our kids may be living in the Information Age but our brains have not been redesigned yet.
options: ① learn to manage their time
② focus on two things at once

④ use technology to avoid distraction
⑤ trust common sense to explain brain function

question: 13. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?

question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Brands that fail to grow and develop lose their relevance. Think about the person you knew who was once on the fast track at your company, who is either no longer with the firm or, worse yet, appears to have hit a plateau in his or her career.
ordered_passages: (A) Think about the impact personal computing technology had on the first wave of executive leadership exposed to the technology. Those who embraced the technology were able to integrate it into their work styles and excel.

(B) Those who were resistant many times found few opportunities to advance their careers and in many cases were ultimately let go through early retirement for failure to stay relevant and update their skills.
(C) Assuming he or she did not make an ambitious move, more often than not, this individual is a victim of having failed to stay relevant and embrace the advances in his or her industry.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 커리어 정체기에 빠진 인물을 예시로 든 후, (C)에서 그 이유가 업계의 발전을 받아들이지 못했기 때문이라고 진단합니다. 이어 (A)에서 개인용 컴퓨터 기술 도입이라는 구체적 사례를 통해 기술을 수용한 사람들의 성공을 언급하고, (B)에서 반대로 기술을 거부한 사람들이 겪은 부정적인 결과(도태)를 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Dancers often push themselves to the limits of their physical capabilities. But that push is misguided if it is directed toward accomplishing something physically impossible.
ordered_passages: (A) But a short-footed dancer may have no trouble! Another dancer may be struggling to complete a half-turn in the air. Understanding the connection between a rapid turn rate and the alignment of the body close to the rotation axis tells her how to accomplish her turn successfully.
(B) In both of these cases, understanding and working within the constraints imposed by nature and described by physical laws allows dancers to work efficiently, minimizing potential risk of injury.

(C) For instance, a tall dancer with long feet may wish to perform repetitive vertical jumps to fast music, pointing his feet while in the air and lowering his heels to the floor between jumps. That may be impossible no matter how strong the dancer is.
explanation: 물리적으로 불가능한 목표를 지향하는 것이 잘못되었다는 서두 뒤에, (C)에서 긴 발을 가진 무용수가 빠른 음악에 맞춰 점프하는 것이 불가능할 수 있다는 구체적 사례를 제시합니다. (A)에서 발이 짧은 무용수의 대조적 상황과 회전 기술의 물리 법칙을 언급한 뒤, (B)에서 이러한 자연적 제약과 물리 법칙을 이해하는 것이 효율적이고 안전하다는 결론을 내립니다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Robert Blattberg and Steven Hoch noted that, in a changing environment, it is not clear that consistency is always a virtue and that one of the advantages of human judgment is the ability to detect change. (A) Thus, in changing environments, it might be advantageous to combine human judgment and statistical models. (B) Blattberg and Hoch examined this possibility by having supermarket managers forecast demand for certain products. (C) As part of this examination, they created a composite forecast by averaging these judgments with the forecasts of statistical models based on past data. (D) The logic was that statistical models assume stable conditions and therefore cannot account for the effects on demand of novel events such as actions taken by competitors or the introduction of new products. (E) The composite─or average of human judgments and statistical models─proved to be more accurate than either the statistical models or the managers working alone.
insertion_sentence: Humans, however, can incorporate these novel factors in their judgments.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'these novel factors(이러한 새로운 요인들)'는 (D) 문장에 언급된 '경쟁자의 행동이나 신제품 도입과 같은 새로운 사건들'을 가리킵니다. 통계 모델은 이러한 요인을 반영하지 못하지만, '인간은 이를 판단에 통합할 수 있다'는 내용이 (D) 뒤에 오고, 그 결과인 (E) '종합적인 예측이 더 정확했다'는 결론으로 연결되는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 (E) 자리에 위치해야 합니다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The most prevalent problem kids report is that they feel like they need to be accessible at all times. Because technology allows for it, they feel an obligation. It's easy for most of us to relate-you probably feel the same pressure in your own life! It is really challenging to deal with the fact that we're human and can't always respond instantly. For a teen or tween who's still learning the ins and outs of social interactions, it's even worse. Here's how this behavior plays out sometimes: Your child texts one of his friends, and the friend doesn't text back right away. Now it's easy for your child to think, "This person doesn't want to be my friend anymore!" So he texts again, and again, and again-"blowing up their phone." This can be stressinducing and even read as aggressive. But you can see how easily this could happen.
summary_sentence: Due to the influence of (A)___________, many teens feel pressured to stay constantly connected and respond (B)___________ to messages, which can lead to stress and aggressive behavior.
options: ① education      instantly
② education      gradually
③ technology      instantly
④ technology      emotionally
⑤ behavior      aggressively
explanation: 기술(technology)의 발달로 언제나 연락 가능해지면서 십대들은 끊임없이 연결되어 있어야 하고 메시지에 즉각적으로(instantly) 응답해야 한다는 압박감을 느끼게 되며, 이것이 스트레스와 공격적인 행동으로 이어질 수 있다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 교육 ... 즉각적으로
② 교육 ... 점진적으로
③ 기술 ... 즉각적으로
④ 기술 ... 감정적으로
⑤ 행동 ... 공격적으로

question: 21. 다음 글의 주제에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 주어진 철자로 시작하여 각각 한 단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: Like positive habits, bad habits exist on a continuum of easy-to-change and hard-to-change. When you get toward the "hard" end of the spectrum, note the language you hear- breaking bad habits and battling addiction. It's as if an unwanted behavior is a nefarious villain to be aggressively defeated. But this kind of language (and the approaches it spawns) frames these challenges in a way that isn't helpful or effective. I specifically hope we will stop using this phrase: "break a habit." This language misguides people. The word "break" sets the wrong expectation for how you get rid of a bad habit. This word implies that if you input a lot of force in one moment, the habit will be gone. However, that rarely works, because you usually cannot get rid of an unwanted habit by applying force one time.
subjective_answer_format: → (A)___________ of misleading language like "break a habit" in (B)___________ bad habits
explanation: '습관을 깨부수다(break a habit)'와 같은 표현은 단 한 번의 강한 힘으로 습관을 없앨 수 있다는 잘못된 기대를 심어주어 비효율적(ineffectiveness)이며, 나쁜 습관을 변화시키는(changing) 데 도움이 되지 않는다는 주제입니다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 제목에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 한 단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: We must explore the relationship between children's film production and consumption habits. The term "children's film" implies ownership by children-their cinema-but films supposedly made for children have always been consumed by audiences of all ages, particularly in commercial cinemas. The considerable crossover in audience composition for children's films can be shown by the fact that, in 2007, eleven Danish children's and youth films attracted 59 per cent of theatrical admissions, and in 2014, German children's films comprised seven out of the top twenty films at the national box office. This phenomenon corresponds with a broader, international embrace of what is seemingly children's culture among audiences of diverse ages. The old prejudice that children's film is some other realm, separate from (and forever subordinate to) a more legitimate cinema for adults is not supported by the realities of consumption: children's film is at the heart of contemporary popular culture.
explanation: 어린이 영화는 단순히 아이들만을 위한 것이 아니라 모든 연령층에 의해 폭넓게 소비되고 있다는 점을 통해, 그것이 가진 보편적인(Universal) 매력과 대중 문화에서의 중심적 역할을 강조하고 있습니다.

question: 23. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 creativity may actually decrease productivity (as measured by publication counts)이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 주어진 철자로 시작하여 각각 한 단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: Creativity can have an effect on productivity. Creativity leads some individuals to recognize problems that others do not see, but which may be very difficult. Charles Darwin's approach to the speciation problem is a good example of this; he chose a very difficult and tangled problem, speciation, which led him into a long period of data collection and deliberation. This choice of problem did not allow for a quick attack or a simple experiment. In such cases <u>creativity may actually decrease productivity (as measured by publication counts)</u> because effort is focused on difficult problems. For others, whose creativity is more focused on methods and technique, creativity may lead to solutions that drastically reduce the work necessary to solve a problem. We can see an example in the development of the polymerase chain reaction (PCR) which enables us to amplify small pieces of DNA in a short time. This type of creativity might reduce the number of steps or substitute steps that are less likely to fail, thus increasing productivity.
subjective_answer_format: → Focusing on complex problems can (A)___________ output, resulting in (B)___________ publications despite high creative effort
explanation: 어떤 이들의 창의성은 매우 어렵고 복잡한 문제에 집중되는데, 이 경우 긴 연구 시간이 필요하여 단기적인 성과(출판물 수)는 오히려 줄어들 수 있다는 의미입니다. 즉, 산출량을 줄이고(reduce) 더 적은(fewer) 출판물로 이어질 수 있다는 것입니다.

question: 26. 다음 글에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 모두 찾아 쓰고, 바르게 고치시오. (오답 감점, 단어 첨가는 안 됨, 본문에 있는 단어로 고치면 틀린 것으로 처리)
passage: Creative people aren't all cut from the same cloth. They have varying levels of maturity and sensitivity. They have different approaches to work. And they're each motivated by different things. Managing people is about being aware of their common personalities. It's also about empathy and adaptability, and knowing how the things you do and say will be interpreted and adapting accordingly. Who you are and what you say may not be the same from one person to the next. For instance, if you're asking someone to work a second weekend in a row, or telling them they aren't getting that deserved promotion just yet, you need to bear in mind the individual. Vincent will have a very different reaction to the news than Emily, and they will each be more receptive to the news if it's bundled with different things. Perhaps that promotion news will land easier if Vincent is given a few extra vacation days for the holidays, while you can promise Emily a bigger promotion a year from now. Consider each person's complex positive and negative personality traits, their life circumstances, and their mindset in the moment when deciding what to say and how to say it. Personal connection, compassion, and a standardized management style are key to drawing consistent, rock star-level work out of everyone.
explanation: (1) 창의적인 사람들은 모두 다르기 때문에 공통적인 성격이 아니라 각자의 '독특한(unique/individual)' 성격을 파악해야 합니다. (2) 사람마다 대응 방식이 달라야 한다는 글의 요지에 따라 '표준화된(standardized)' 관리 방식이 아니라 '개별화된(individualized)' 관리 방식이 성과를 이끌어내는 열쇠입니다.

question: 27. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 주어진 철자로 시작하여 한 단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: We tend to overrate the impact of new technologies in part because older technologies have become absorbed into the furniture of our lives, so as to be almost invisible. Take the baby bottle. Here is a simple implement that has transformed a fundamental human experience for vast numbers of infants and mothers, yet it finds no place in our histories of technology. This technology might be thought of as a classic time-shifting device, as it enables mothers to exercise more control over the timing of feeding. It can also function to save time, as bottle feeding allows for someone else to substitute for the mother's time. Potentially, therefore, it has huge implications for the management of time in everyday life, yet it is entirely _____________ in discussions of high-speed society.
explanation: 젖병과 같은 오래된 기술은 우리 삶에 너무 깊이 녹아들어 거의 눈에 보이지 않게 되었기 때문에, 일상생활의 시간 관리에 큰 변화를 가져왔음에도 불구하고 사회적 논의에서 완전히 '간과된다(overlooked)'는 맥락이 적절합니다.

question: 29. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 적절한 말을 주어진 철자로 시작하여 각각 한 단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: Development of the human body from a single cell provides many examples of the structural richness that is possible when the repeated production of random variation is combined with nonrandom selection. All phases of body development from embryo to adult exhibit random activities at the cellular level, and body formation depends on the new possibilities generated by these activities coupled with selection of those outcomes that satisfy previously built-인 criteria. Always new structure is based on old structure, and at every stage selection favors some cells and eliminates others. The survivors serve to produce new cells that undergo further rounds of selection. Except in the immune system, cells and extensions of cells are not genetically selected during development, but rather, are positionally selected. Those in the right place that make the right connections are stimulated, and those that don't are eliminated. This process is much like sculpting. A natural consequence of the strategy is great variability from individual to individual at the cell and molecular levels, even though large-scale structures are quite similar.
subjective_answer_format: → Human body development arises from (A)___________ processes generating variation and is refined through selection mechanisms based on (B)___________, resulting in structural complexity and individual diversity
explanation: 인체 발달은 무작위적인(random) 활동을 통해 변이를 만들고, 올바른 위치(position)에 있는 세포들이 선택되는 과정을 통해 복잡한 구조와 개인적 다양성을 형성한다는 요약이 적절합니다.

question: 3. 다음 글에서 전체 흤름과 가계없는 문장은? [⌢년 6월 35번]
passage: Quite often the interaction between groups is socially unequal, and this is reflected in the fact that in many cases borrowing of words or constructions goes mostly or entirely in one direction, from the more powerful or prestigious group to the less favored one. ⓐThe languages of socially subordinated groups may from quite an early period of contact provide terminology for objects or practices with which speakers of the more powerful group were previously unfamiliar. ⓑThe effects of contact in that direction, however, may not progress any further than this. ⓒIn some cases, as with the Dharug language of Sydney, Australia, the source of some of the earliest loans from Indigenous Australian languages into English, the fate of the language system is extinction after the obliteration of many of its speakers. ⓓThis reflects how loanwords enrich both languages equally over time. ⓔThe remainder shifted to varieties of English, the language of the people who had suppressed them.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 집단 간의 불평등한 사회적 관계가 언어 차용(단어나 구문의 빌림)에 미치는 영향에 대한 것입니다. 강대한 집단이 약소 집단의 언어를 차용하는 것은 매우 제한적이며, 결국 약소 집단의 언어가 소멸하감을 설명합니다. ⓓ번 문장은 차용어가 양태 언어를 '동등하게' 퐒요롭게 한다는 내용으로, 글 전체의 주제인 불평등한 언어 관계 및 소멸과 상치됩니다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We collect stamps, coins, vintage cars even when they serve no practical purpose. The post office doesn't accept the old stamps, the banks don't take old coins, and the vintage cars are no longer allowed on the road. These are all side issues; the attraction is that they are in short supply. In one study, students were asked to arrange ten posters in order of attractiveness - with the agreement that afterward they could keep one poster as a reward for their participation. Five minutes later, they were told that the poster with the third highest rating was no longer available. Then they were asked to judge all ten from scratch. The poster that was no longer available was suddenly classified as the most beautiful.
summary_sentence: In psychology, this phenomenon is called reactance: when we are (A)__________ of an option, we suddenly deem it more (B)__________.
options: ① deprivedappealing
② acquiredfertile
③ capturedexotic
④ imposeddiverse
⑤ taken awayunattractive
explanation: 글의 내용은 선택지가 사라지거나 공급이 부족해질 때 그것을 더 매력적으로 느끼게 된다는 '리액턴스(reactance)' 현상을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '박탈당하다/제한되다'의 의미인 'deprived'가, (B)에는 '매력적인'의 의미인 'appealing'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 박탈당한 - 매력적인
획득한 - 비옥한
포착된 - 이국적인
부과된 - 다양한
치워진 - 매력 없는

question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 문장을 2개 골라 기호를 쓰고, 올바른 문장으로 고쳐 문장 전체를 쓰시오.
passage: If we've invested in something that hasn't repaid us - be it money in a failing venture, or time in an unhappy relationship - we find it very difficult to walk away. This is the sunk cost fallacy. Our instinct is to continue investing money or time as we hope that our investment will prove to be worthwhile in the end. Giving up would mean acknowledging that we've wasted something we can't get back, and ⓐ<u>that thought is so painfully that we prefer to avoid it if we can</u>. The problem, of course, is that if something really is a bad bet, then ⓑ<u>staying with it simply increase the amount we lose</u>. ⓒ<u>Rather than walk away from a bad five-year relationship, for example, we turn it into a bad 10-year relationship</u>; rather than accept that we've lost a thousand dollars, ⓓ<u>we lay down another thousand and lose that too</u>. In the end, ⓔ<u>by delaying the pain of admitting our problem, we only add to it</u>. Sometimes we just have to cut our losses.
answer: (1) ⓐ, that thought is so painful that we prefer to avoid it if we can.(2) ⓑ, staying with it simply increases the amount we lose.
explanation: ⓐ 'so ~ that' 구문에서 is의 보어 자리이므로 부사인 painfully를 형용사인 painful로 고쳐야 합니다.ⓑ 동명사 주어 'staying with it'은 3인칭 단수 취급하므로 동사 increase를 increases로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Quite often the interaction between groups is socially ⓐ<u>unequal</u>. options: ① ⓐ

explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 be unfamiliar 뒤에는 전치사 with가 필요합니다. objects or practices를 수식하는 관계대명사절에서 'speakers ... were unfamiliar with (them)'의 구조이므로, which를 with which 또는 that ... with로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food is taking a back seat. I suspect that most people view flavor as of secondary importance in social settings where food is served. Although our social gatherings coalesce around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, do not depend on the quality of sensations provided by the food. To focus excessively on flavor is to miss the larger significance of these social relations.
options: ① 소수에 의한 정보 독점은 음식의 대중화를 방해한다.
② 꾸준한 반복을 통해 올바른 식습관을 형성할 수Status.
③ 음식이 중심인 사교 행사에서 음식의 맛이 크게 중요하지 않다.
④ 사교 행사에서 제공되는 음식의 맛이 그 행사의 성공 여부를 좌우한다.
⑤ 음식의 종류와 그 맛이 사교 모임의 성격을 만들고 그 지속성을 결정한다.
explanation: 이 글은 사교적인 모임에서 음식이 제공되지만, 그 모임의 의미나 사회적 역동성은 음식의 맛(flavor)보다는 사회적 관계에 달려 있으며, 맛은 부차적인 요소로 여겨진다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다.

question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
options: ① An Acknowledged Scientist: One-hit Wonder or Multiple Discoveries?
② The Secret Behind Superiority: Previous Success or Talent?
③ The Phenomena Explained by the Matthew Effect
④ The Matthew Effect: The Key to Success
⑤ What Is the Matthew Effect?
explanation: 글의 후반부에서 과학자들의 지속적인 성공이 마태 효과(이전의 성공이 주는 이점) 때문인지, 아니면 애초에 뛰어난 재능 때문인지에 대한 의문을 던지고 있으므로, '월등함 뒤의 비밀: 이전의 성공인가 재능인가?'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 인정받는 과학자: 단발성 성공인가 다수의 발견인가?
② 우월함 뒤의 비밀: 이전의 성공인가 재능인가?
③ 마태 효과로 설명되는 현상들
④ 마태 효과: 성공의 열쇠
⑤ 마태 효과란 무엇인가?

question: 9. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower _______________________________; they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
options: ① is unwilling to spray pesticides to boost productivity
② seeks to promote the harmonious growth of plants
③ is gardening with objective observation in mind
④ gives more importance to quantity than quality
⑤ is altering the natural balance of the ecosystem
explanation: 채소밭 가꾸기는 특정 목적(생산량 최대화)을 위해 생태계를 인위적으로 불안정한 상태로 유지하는 행위입니다. 재배자가 잡초를 제거하고 살충제를 뿌리는 것은 자연스러운 생태계의 평형 상태(안정적인 상태)로 돌아가려는 경향을 막고 인위적으로 개입하는 과정이므로, '생태계의 자연스러운 균형을 변경하고 있다'는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 생산성을 높이기 위해 농약을 뿌리는 것을 꺼린다
② 식물의 조화로운 성장을 촉진하려고 노력한다
③ 객관적인 관찰을 염두에 두고 원예를 한다
④ 질보다 양에 더 중요성을 부여한다
⑤ 생태계의 자연스러운 균형을 변경하고 있다

question: 10. 다음 밑줄 친 a creative process가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much <u>a creative process</u>. A conjecture is a philosophical invention, cooked up rather mystically by the mind through the mental computation we call careful contemplation. However, until the hypothesis is tested against reality, it is not yet truly knowledge; it is just information that represents speculation. Knowledge is information that has demonstrated its usefulness. It is what is left over after cycles of experimental testing have eliminated false theories. As scientists continually test their hypotheses and modify their models to account for new and surprising data, a kind of "learning loop" emerges that statisticians call Bayesian updating. Based on Bayes' Rule, developed by eighteenth-century English statistician and philosopher Thomas Bayes, Bayesian updating refers to a mathematical process whereby an accepted theory or predictive model gets increasingly accurate through the repetitive testing of competing variants of that theory.
options: ① Through the learning loop, statisticians represent what science is.
② Bayesian updating involves modifying knowledge based on a rule-based process.
③ Knowledge is an information scientists have gathered in laboratory.
④ Knowledge developed through contemplation challenges the previous hypothesis.
⑤ A hypothesis turns into knowledge as scientists reconstruct the previous supposition.
explanation: 글의 맥락에서 '창의적인 과정(a creative process)'은 단순히 규칙을 따르는 것이 아니라, 마음속의 사색을 통해 가설을 세우고(추측), 이를 반복적인 실험과 테스트를 통해 수정하며 지식으로 발전시켜 나가는 과정을 의미합니다. 지식은 가설이 검증되어 유용함을 입증한 결과물이므로, 과학자들이 이전의 가정을 재구성함에 따라 가설이 지식으로 변한다는 ⑤번이 가장 적절한 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 학습 루프를 통해 통계학자들은 과학이 무엇인지를 나타낸다.
② 베이지안 업데이트는 규칙 기반 과정에 따라 지식을 수정하는 것을 포함한다.
③ 지식은 과학자들이 실험실에서 수집한 정보이다.
④ 사색을 통해 개발된 지식은 이전 가설에 도전한다.
⑤ 과학자들이 이전의 가정을 재구성함에 따라 가설은 지식으로 변한다.

question: 11. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking.
ordered_passages: (A) Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips.

(B) Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
(C) When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 우리가 실수를 바로잡기 위해 멈출 때, 말하기를 멈추기 수백 밀리초 전에 손동작을 멈춘다는 내용입니다. (A)에서는 이러한 순서(sequences)가 우리의 손이 의식적인 마음보다 먼저 말할 내용을 '안다'는 것을 시사한다고 설명하며, 손동작이 단어를 정신적으로 준비시킨다고 언급합니다. 이어서 (C)에서 손동작을 못 하게 하면 다음 단어를 공급받지 못해 유창성이 떨어진다는 구체적인 사례를 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 손동작이 없을 때의 추가적인 부정적인 효과(기억력 저하, 문제 해결 능력 저하 등)를 언급하며 손동작이 사고의 최첨단을 나타낸다는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. (A) The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. (B) Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. (C) In terms of agricultural products, they are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. (D) Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. (E) The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports.
insertion_sentence: Food security, however, does not depend on self-sufficiency, since nations can acquire food products that are difficult to produce domestically through imports.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장은 '하지만 식량 안보가 자급자족에만 달려 있는 것은 아니며, 수입을 통해 보충할 수 있다'는 내용입니다. (B)까지는 자급자족(self-sufficiency)에 대한 설명이 나오고, (C) 뒤에서는 농산물의 지리적/기후적 한계로 인해 완전 자급자족이 어렵다는 점을 설명하기 시작하므로, 자급자족의 한계를 지적하며 수입의 필요성을 언급하는 주어진 문장은 (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: As a general rule, it's better if your definition corresponds as closely as possible to the way in which the term is ordinarily used in the kinds of debates to which your claims are pertinent. There will be, however, occasions where it is appropriate, even necessary, to coin special uses through what philosophers call stimulative definition. This happens when the current lexicon ______________________________. For example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something the person having it has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories: I would have a memory-type experience, but this would not be of something that I had actually experienced. To call this a memory would be misleading. For this reason, philosophers have coined the special term 'quasi-memory' to refer to these hypothetical memory-like experiences.
options: ① prioritizes everyday convenience over abstract theoretic clarity
② lacks terms needed to express philosophically significant differences
③ becomes too artificial to be taken seriously in philosophical analysis
④ reflects cultural biases that hinder objective philosophical reasoning
⑤ offers a number of synonyms that make precise communication nearly impossible
explanation: 이 글은 정의를 내릴 때 일반적인 용어의 사용법을 따르는 것이 좋지만, 철학적으로 중요한 구분을 표현하기 위해 기존 어휘가 부족할 때는 '규정적 정의(stimulative definition)'를 통해 새로운 용어를 만드는 것이 필요하다는 내용입니다. 예시로 든 '유사 기억(quasi-memory)'은 자신이 직접 경험하지 않은 기억을 설명하기 위해 일반 언어에 없는 용어를 새로 만든 사례입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 현재의 어휘가 '철학적으로 중요한 차이를 표현하는 데 필요한 용어가 부족할 때'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 추상적인 이론적 명료함보다 일상적인 편의를 우선시한다
② 철학적으로 중요한 차이를 표현하는 데 필요한 용어가 부족하다
③ 철학적 분석에서 진지하게 받아들여지기에는 너무 인위적이게 된다
④ 객관적인 철학적 추론을 방해하는 문화적 편향을 반영한다
⑤ 정밀한 의사소통을 거의 불가능하게 만드는 다수의 유의어를 제공한다

question: 15. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.6점]
passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. ⓐEach of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more acceptable than previously. ⓑNevertheless, this humourous approach sometimes oversimplified the complexities of social issues, offering a more digestible but less detailed perspective. ⓒOften a character, usually someone marked as a bigot, resisted one or more of these developments and was then made to appear ridiculous. ⓓThey were cut down either through their own stupidity, a brief scolding from others, or both. ⓔIn this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage acceptance of a more pluralistic and tolerant society.
options: ① ⓐ

③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글의 전체적인 흐름은 미국의 시트콤이 유머를 통해 사회적 갈등을 다루고 진보적인 가치를 수용하도록 돕는 역할을 했다는 것입니다. ⓑ번 문장은 이러한 유머러스한 접근법이 사회 문제의 복잡성을 지나치게 단순화하여 상세한 관점을 제공하지 못했다는 부정적인 측면을 언급하고 있으므로, 시트콤의 긍정적인 사회적 역할을 설명하는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.7점]

options: ① ⓐ

question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested, that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. ⓐRevolutionaries have always looked to the past to frame their future cause, as is amply illustrated by examples from nationalism to communism. ⓑThe future has often been seen as variously a recovery of a lost time, as a replication of what is established, or as a model bequeathed by a heroic age long gone. ⓒThe writing of history is based on understanding or explaining future outcomes that were not known to contemporaries, since the historian has the benefit of hindsight and the past is nothing more than the accumulation of futures that are now our past. ⓓThere is no doubt that no one can deny that the past influences the future. ⓔSo, rather than see the hand of the past always shaping the future, perhaps it can be seen in reverse, with the past - in the sense of our understanding of it - being shaped by our orientation to the future.
explanation: 이 글의 핵심 주제는 '미래에 대한 우리의 관점이 과거에 대한 이해를 형성한다'는 것입니다. 즉, 과거가 미래를 결정하는 것이 아니라 미래에 대한 지향성이 과거를 재구성한다는 역발상을 다루고 있습니다. 그러나 ⓓ문장은 '과거가 미래에 영향을 미친다는 것은 부정할 수 없다'는 일반적인 통념을 언급하고 있어, 글의 전체적인 논조(미래가 과거를 규정함)와 정반대되는 내용이므로 흐름상 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In 1900, at the close of the first decade where electric systems had become a practical alternative for manufacturers, less than 5 percent of the power used in factories came from electricity.
ordered_passages: (A) And the factory owners, having always supplied their own power, were unwilling to assign such a critical function to an outsider. They knew that a glitch in power supply would bring their operations to a halt - and that a lot of glitches might well mean bankruptcy. As the new century began, a survey found that there were already 50,000 private electric plants in operation, far surpassing the 3,600 central stations.

(B) But one thing didn't change. Factories continued to build their own power-supply systems on their own premises. Few manufacturers considered buying electricity from the small central stations. Designed to supply lighting to local homes and shops, the central stations had neither the size nor the skill to serve the needs of big factories.

(C) But the technological advances of suppliers made electric systems and electric motors ever more affordable and reliable, and the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology. Further accelerating the shift was the rapid expansion in the number of skilled electrical engineers, who provided the expertise needed to install and run the new systems. In short order, electric power had gone from exotic to commonplace.
explanation: 1900−년 대 공강내 껀기 사굥 비개율이 나자다는 제시문 다으ᄆ에는, 그 이유로 공장들이 자체 발전 시스테믈 고수해다는 (B)가 오교, 요부 전려ᄀ에 대한 불신가 그 결괴로 사설 발전소가 그교나나다는 (A)가 이어지는 거시 저ᄀ절하ᄇ니다. 마지마ᄀ으로 기샐자들의 마케핑괘 기샐 발전, 저나문 기샐자들의 즈가로 껀기 사굥이 보편해다는 (C)로 걸론 지어지는 구조이므로 (B)-(A)-(C) 순서가 마즈나, 제시댠 저다ᄇ ⑤는 오타로 보이며, 지문의 노느리상 (B)-(A)-(C) 순서의 ②버니 가자다 저ᄀ절하나 안서지 기준 저다ᄇ ⑤로 표기하ᄆ니다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. (A) In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. (B) All experts are not the same, nor do they submit their work to the same scrutiny. (C) For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were funded in part by the sugar industry. (D) The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared and their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have encouraged higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. (E) Stories such as this one fuel suspicion - but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process and funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since been made compulsory.
insertion_sentence: Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims.

passage: If you had wanted to create a "self-driving" car in the 1950s, your best option might have been to strap a brick to the accelerator. question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: A young child may have no difficulty in determining the directions of up and down or back and front. But that same child may be ⓐ<u>puzzled</u> when asked to distinguish between the directions of right and left. Scientists propose that this occurs because, although we experience three dimensions, only two had a strong influence on our evolution: the ⓑ<u>vertical</u> dimension as defined by gravity and, in mobile species, the front/back dimension as defined by the positioning of sensory and feeding mechanisms. These influence our ⓒ<u>perception</u> of vertical versus horizontal, far versus close, and the search for dangers from above (such as an eagle) or below (such as a snake). However, the left right axis is less ⓓ<u>significant</u> in nature. A bear is equally dangerous from its left or the right side, but not if it is upside down. In fact, we usually only notice if left and right are flipped when we see ⓔ<u>natural</u> objects like cars or signs.

question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: We have a tendency to ⓐ<u>overestimate</u> the impact of recent technological advancements. This is partly because older technologies have become fully ⓑ<u>integrated</u> in our daily routines that they're practically unnoticed. Consider the baby bottle, for example. This seemingly basic tool has drastically altered a core human interaction for vast numbers of infants and mothers, yet its significance is ⓒ<u>overlooked</u> in our histories of technology. This technology might be thought of as a classic time-shifting device. It gives mothers greater ⓓ<u>constraint</u> in determining when feedings occur. Additionally, it can save time, since bottle feeding allows other individuals to take over the mother's feeding responsibilities. Consequently, the baby bottle potentially has significant consequences for how we organize our time in everyday life. However, it's completely ⓔ<u>disregarded</u> in discussions of high-speed society.

question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The fast-growing, tremendous amount of data, collected and stored in large and numerous data repositories, has far exceeded our human ability for understanding without powerful tools. As a result, data collected in large data repositories become "data tombs" - data archives that are hardly visited. Important decisions are often made based not on the information-rich data stored in data repositories but rather on a decision maker's instinct, simply because the decision maker does not have the tools to extract the valuable knowledge hidden in the vast amounts of data. Efforts have been made to develop expert system and knowledge-based technologies, which typically rely on users or domain experts to manually input knowledge into knowledge bases. However, this procedure is likely to cause biases and errors and is extremely costly and time consuming. The widening gap between data and information calls for the systematic development of tools that can turn data tombs into "golden nuggets" of knowledge.

③ Data-Driven Decisions: Overcoming the Limitations of Human Prediction
④ The Importance of Instinct in Decision-making When Data is Insufficient
⑤ A Historical Perspective on Data Utilization: Trends and Transformations

question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: A common but incorrect assumption is that we are creatures of reason when, in fact, we are creatures of both reason and emotion. We cannot get by on reason alone since any reason always eventually leads to a feeling. Should I get a wholegrain cereal or a chocolate cereal? I can list all the reasons I want, but the reasons have to be based on something. For example, if my goal is to eat healthy, I can choose the wholegrain cereal, but what is my reason for wanting to be healthy? I can list more and more reasons such as wanting to live longer, spending more quality time with loved ones, etc., but what are the reasons for those reasons? You should be able to see by now that reasons are ultimately based on non-reason such as values, feelings, or emotions. These deep seated values, feelings, and emotions we have are rarely a result of reasoning, but can certainly be influenced by reasoning. We have values, feelings, and emotions before we begin to reason and long before we begin to reason effectively.
options: ① We Think, Therefore We Feel
② Emotion: The Basis of Reason
③ Reason Must Always Control Emotion
④ Every Decision Can Be Fully Justified by Logic
⑤ True Rationality Means Ignoring Your Emotions

question: 7. 다음 글의 내용을 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]

question: 20. 다음 도표를 참고하여 글의 문맥에 맞도록 <보기>에 주어진 단어를 배열하여 빈칸 (A)를 완성하시오.
passage: How Often Do You Read a Book? (Germany 2022) The above graph shows the reading habits of German children and young adults in 2022 according to age groups. In all age groups, except for 12- to 13-year-olds, the largest percentage of individuals reported reading books once a month or less. Of the 12 to 13 year old group, 42% stated they read daily or several times a week, which was the highest share within that group. In the 14 to 15 year old group, the percentage of teenagers who read daily or several times a week was more than twice as high as those who never read a book in the same age group. question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
passage: Many early dot com investors focused almost entirely on revenue growth instead of net income. Many early dot com companies earned most of their revenue from selling advertising space on their Web sites. To boost reported revenue, some sites began exchanging ad space. Company A would put an ad for its Web site on company B's Web site, and company B would put an ad for its Web site on company A's Web site. No money ever changed hands, but each company recorded revenue (for the value of the space that it gave up on its site) and expense (for the value of its ad that it placed on the other company's site). This practice did little to boost net income and resulted in no additional cash inflow - but it did boost reported revenue. This practice was quickly put to an end because accountants felt that it did not meet the revenue recognition principle.
summary_sentence: Early dot-com companies boosted reported revenue by (A)_________________________ without cash flow, but this practice was ended for not meeting (B)____________________________.
subjective_conditions: - 윗글에서 찾아서 변형 없이 그대로 쓸 것
answer: (A) exchanging ad space, (B) the revenue recognition principle
explanation: 지문에 따르면 초기 닷컴 기업들은 현금 유입 없이 '광고 공간을 교환(exchanging ad space)'함으로써 보고된 수익을 부풀렸습니다. 그러나 회계사들은 이 관행이 '수익 인식 원칙(the revenue recognition principle)'을 충족하지 못한다고 판단하여 이를 중단시켰습니다. 지문 내의 표현을 조건에 맞게 추출하면 됩니다.

question: 6. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.*startling: 놀라운 **deleterious: 해로운

question: 7. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other?
ordered_passages: (A) But beyond that, you've got nothing; all you can say is this person/thing is already in your memories. Recall is when you can access the original memory of how and why you know this person; recognition is just flagging up the fact that the memory exists.

(B) This happens because the brain differentiates between familiarity and recall. To clarify, familiarity (or recognition) is when you encounter someone or something and you know you've done so before.

(C) This is because the brain has something of a two-tier memory system at work when it comes to retrieving memories, and this gives rise to a common yet infuriating sensation: recognising someone, but not being able to remember how or why, or what their name is.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 뇌가 얼굴과 이름 중 하나만 기억하는 이유에 대해 질문을 던집니다. (C)에서 '이것은 뇌의 이중 기억 시스템 때문이다'라며 질문에 대한 직접적인 이유를 설명하고, 누군가를 알아보지만(recognising) 구체적인 정보를 기억하지 못하는 현상을 언급합니다. (B)에서 이 현상이 발생하는 구체적인 이유로 '친숙함(familiarity)'과 '회상(recall)'의 구분을 제시합니다. (A)에서 '친숙함'은 단지 기억 속에 있다는 사실만을 알리는 '재인(recognition)'인 반면, '회상'은 구체적인 맥락에 접근하는 것임을 설명하며 마무리됩니다.

question: 15. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓑ가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [25년 3월 36번]
passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, is ⓐ<u>a productive nation</u> in agriculture, but still depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, to assure adequate food supplies, governments should be careful ⓑ<u>not to put all their eggs in one basket.</u>
options: ① to diversify the sources of food supplies
② to rely only on a single plan or course of action

options_translation: ① 식품 공급원을 다양화하는 것

question: 16. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ를 <조건>에 맞게 고쳐 쓰시오. [25년 3월 36번]
passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, is ⓐ<u>a productive nation</u> in agriculture, but still depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, to assure adequate food supplies, governments should be careful ⓑ<u>not to put all their eggs in one basket.</u>
subjective_conditions: '가장 ~한 것들 중 하나'라는 의미를 담을 것
ⓐ에 제시된 단어 'productive'와 'nation'을 반드시 활용할 것 (단, 필요한 경우, 의미와 문법에 맞게 어형을 변형할 것
총 6개의 단어로 작성할 것
answer: one of the most productive nations
explanation: '가장 ~한 것들 중 하나'는 'one of the 최상급 + 복수명사' 구문을 사용합니다. 'productive'의 최상급은 'the most productive'이고, 'nation'의 복수형은 'nations'입니다. 따라서 'one of the most productive nations' (총 6단어)가 정답입니다.

question: 17. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [25년 3월 22번]
passage: ⓐ<u>약속은 사회생활에서의 인간적 형태를 특징적으로 함께 결속하는 접착체이다</u>. Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby facilitating the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. Moreover, (A)_____________________________________. For example, a taxi driver picks up his clients and transports them to their desired destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a credible commitment to pay her at the end of the month. Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to taking various measures to sustain the currency in question. Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.

② social commitments are important to create diverse relationships.
③ by receiving pay from employer, people can do their work as a duty
④ predicting desires and interests is a critical part to sustain social relationships
⑤ commitments lead individuals to take actions that they would not normally perform
explanation: 빈칸 이후의 예시(택시 운전사, 건설 노동자)는 그들이 약속(지불 보장)이 없다면 하지 않았을 행동을 약속 때문에 수행하고 있음을 보여줍니다. 따라서 약속이 개인이 평소라면 하지 않았을 행동을 하게 만든다는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

A weak electric current is created also in ordinary muscle cells when they contract. In the electric organ the muscle cells are connected in larger chunks, which makes the total current intensity larger than in ordinary muscles. The fish varies the signals by changing the form of the electric field or the frequency of discharging. The system is only working over small distances, about one to two meters. question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Flavor recognition is one of humans' special skills. Our ancestors had to judge what they could eat and what they couldn't, and flavor is how they made that decision. Those skills are now part of our evolutionary heritage. Humans are unique in that we season our food, intentionally enhancing it with the highly flavored plant parts we call herbs and spices. Interestingly, our taste for spices may have an evolutionary basis. Many spices have antibacterial properties - in fact, common seasonings such as garlic, onion, and oregano inhibit the growth of almost every bacterium tested. And the cultures that make the heaviest use of spices - think of the garlic and black pepper of Thai food, the ginger and coriander of India, the chili peppers of Mexico - come from warmer climates, where bacterial spoilage is a bigger issue. In contrast, the most lightly spiced cuisines - those of Scandinavia and northern Europe - are from cooler climates. ④ has gradually disappeared in colder regions due to climate constraints
⑤ shows that taste is a weak factor in evolutionary development

question: 19. 다음 밑줄 친 an ancient compass still buried deep within our minds가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Human beings like certainty. This preference comes from our ancient ancestors, who had to survive in a world filled with dangers like saber-toothed tigers and poisonous berries. In such dangerous situations, they learned that the more certain they were about something, the better their chances of making the right decision. Our brains evolved to help us notice threats, avoid them, and stay alive. Was this berry the same shape as last time? The same size? If our ancestors felt uncertain, their brains sent out a danger alert to keep them safe. That desire for certainty helped humans survive for thousands of years - and even now, it continues to influence us. Although today's world is much safer - we no longer worry about being chased by a tiger or choosing between eating a poisonous berry and starving - <u>an ancient compass still buried deep within our minds</u> continues to guide our responses. Our brains label unfamiliar or unpredictable situations as dangerous. In response, they create emotions, thoughts, and actions to avoid the risk - helping us survive, just as we did long ago.
options: ① the emotional influence of cultural traditions passed down from our ancestors
② the set of logical decision-making skills we have learned in modern society
③ the instinctive way our brain reacts to uncertainty as a potential threat
④ the deep impact of scientific knowledge developed over a long period of time
⑤ the formation of a tendency to avoid uncertainty through recent experiences and learning
explanation: 이 글은 인간이 확실성을 선호하는 경향이 선사시대 조상들로부터 물려받은 생존 본능에서 기인했음을 설명하고 있습니다. 과거에는 불확실한 상황(본 적 없는 베리, 맹수의 출현 등)이 곧 죽음과 직결될 수 있었기에, 뇌는 불확실성을 위험으로 인식하도록 진화했습니다. 오늘날 세상은 훨씬 안전해졌지만, 여전히 우리 뇌는 예측 불가능한 상황을 위험으로 간주하여 회피 반응을 만듭니다. 따라서 밑줄 친 부분은 불확실성을 잠재적 위협으로 인식하고 반응하는 뇌의 본능적인 방식을 의미합니다.

question: 20. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: It seems natural to describe certain environmental conditions as 'extreme', 'harsh', 'benign' or 'stressful'. It may seem obvious when conditions are 'extreme': the midday heat of a desert, the cold of an Antarctic winter, the salinity of the Great Salt Lake. But this only means that these conditions are extreme for us, given our particular physiological characteristics and tolerances. ⓐTo a cactus there is nothing extreme about the desert conditions in which cacti have evolved; nor are the icy lands of Antarctica an extreme environment for penguins. ⓑSome animals face challenges in adapting when their environment changes too quickly, leading to population decline. ⓒIt is lazy and dangerous for the ecologist to assume that all other organisms sense the environment in the way we do. ⓓRather, the ecologist should try to gain a worm's-eye or plant's-eye view of the environment: to see the world as others see it. ⓔEmotive words like harsh and benign, even relativities such as hot and cold, should be used by ecologists only with care.
explanation: 이 글의 주제는 환경 조건의 '극심함'이나 '가혹함'은 해당 생명체의 생리적 특성에 따라 상대적으로 결정된다는 것입니다. 선인장에게 사막은 극단적인 곳이 아니며 펭귄에게 남극 또한 마찬가지입니다. 따라서 생태학자는 인간의 관점이 아닌 해당 생물의 관점에서 환경을 바라봐야 한다고 조언합니다. 반면, ⓑ번 문장은 환경 변화 속도에 따른 동물의 적응 실패와 개체 수 감소에 대해 설명하고 있어, 환경의 상대적 인식이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

question: 21. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Winning turns on a self-conscious awareness that others are watching. It's a lot easier to move under the radar when no one knows you and no one is paying attention. You can mess up and be rough and get dirty because no one even knows you're there. ⓐBut as soon as you start to win, and others start to notice, you're suddenly aware that you're being observed and being judged. ⓑYou worry that others will discover your flaws and weaknesses, and you start hiding your true personality, so you can be a good role model and good citizen and a leader that others can respect. ⓒThere is nothing wrong with that, but if you do it at the expense of being who you really are, making decisions that please others instead of pleasing yourself, you're not going to be in that position very long. ⓓYou are eager to do so because you know that accommodating the opposing opinions is the best option for making your whole group bring together. ⓔWhen you start apologizing for who you are, you stop growing and you stop winning permanently.
explanation: 이 글은 승리나 성공이 가져오는 '남들의 시선에 대한 의식'과 그로 인한 부작용을 다루고 있습니다. 성공하면 타인의 판단을 두려워해 자신의 본모습을 숨기고 완벽한 모습만 보이려 애쓰게 되는데, 이것이 본래의 자아를 희생시키면 결국 성장이 멈추고 성공을 유지할 수 없게 된다는 내용입니다. ⓓ번 문장은 집단의 화합을 위해 반대 의견을 수용하는 것이 최선이라는 내용으로, 성공 이후의 자아 의식 변화와 가식에 대한 글의 흐름과 무관합니다.

question: 28. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is a common assumption that most vagrant birds are ultimately doomed, aside from the rare cases where individuals are able to reorientate and return to their normal ranges. In turn, it is also commonly assumed that vagrancy itself is a relatively unimportant biological phenomenon. This is undoubtedly true for the majority of cases, as the most likely outcome of any given vagrancy event is that the individual will fail to find enough resources, and/or be exposed to inhospitable environmental conditions, and perish. However, there are many lines of evidence to suggest that vagrancy can, on rare occasions, dramatically alter the fate of populations, species or even whole ecosystems. Despite being infrequent, these events can be extremely important when viewed at the timescales over which ecological and evolutionary processes unfold. The most profound consequences of vagrancy relate to the establishment of new breeding sites, new migration routes and wintering locations. Each of these can occur through different mechanisms, and at different frequencies, and they each have their own unique importance.
summary_sentence: While birds that become vagrant usually face death due to exposure to (A)____________ environment, rare cases of vagrancy can significantly (B)____________ ecological and evolutionary transition in various aspects.
options: ① harsh - drive
② adverse - diminish
③ favorable - promote
④ distinctive - cause
⑤ appropriate - hinder
explanation: 이 글은 길을 잃고 본래 서식지를 벗어난 새(vagrant birds)들이 대부분 가혹한 환경 조건으로 인해 죽음에 이르지만, 드물게는 이러한 배회 현상이 새로운 번식지나 이주 경로를 개척함으로써 종이나 생태계의 운명을 바꾸고 진화적 과정에 중요한 영향을 미칠 수 있다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 요약문의 (A)에는 죽음의 원인이 되는 '가혹한(harsh)' 환경이, (B)에는 생태적, 진화적 전환을 '추동하다(drive)'라는 의미의 표현이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 가혹한 - 추진하다[이끌어내다]
② 불리한 - 감소시키다
③ 유리한 - 촉진하다
④ 독특한 - 야기하다
⑤ 적절한 - 방해하다

question: 12. What is the gist of the author's argument?
passage: If a firm is going to be saved by the government, it might be easier to concentrate on lobbying the government for more money rather than taking the harder decision of restructuring the company to be able to be profitable and viable in the long term. This is an example of something known as moral hazard - when government support alters the decisions firms take. For example, if governments rescue banks who get into difficulty, as they did during the credit crisis of 2007-08, this could encourage banks to take greater risks in the future because they know there is a possibility that governments will intervene if they lose money. Although the government rescue may be well intended, it can negatively affect the behavior of banks, encouraging risky and poor decision making.
options: ① Moral hazard should be encouraged and promoted by the government and the company alike.
② Banks losing money will not only be rescued by the government but will receive more support in the future.
③ In times of trouble, firms should take bold steps to take greater risks to increase the profitability in the long term.
④ The government should stay out of the affairs of private sectors however well-intended they may be.
⑤ Banks are too important to fail so they should receive the government support whenever they need it.
explanation: 정부의 기업 구제가 도덕적 해이(moral hazard)를 초래하여 기업이 스스로의 구조조정보다 로비에 집중하게 만들고, 위험한 의사결정을 하도록 부추긴다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 정부가 의도가 좋을지라도 민간 부문의 문제에 개입하지 말아야 한다는 ④번이 필자의 주장을 가장 잘 나타냅니다. (본문 문맥상 개입의 부작용을 경고하는 것)
options_translation: ① 도덕적 해이는 정부와 기업 모두에 의해 장려되고 촉진되어야 한다.
② 돈을 잃는 은행들은 정부에 의해 구제될 뿐만 아니라 미래에 더 많은 지원을 받을 것이다.
③ 어려울 때, 기업들은 장기적으로 수익성을 높이기 위해 더 큰 위험을 감수하는 대담한 조치를 취해야 한다.
④ 정부는 민간 부문의 일이 아무리 선의일지라도 그 일에서 손을 떼야 한다.
⑤ 은행은 실패하기에 너무 중요하므로 필요할 때마다 정부의 지원을 받아야 한다.

question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We tend to overrate the impact of new technologies in part because older technologies have become absorbed into the furniture of our lives, so as to be almost invisible. Take the baby bottle. Here is a simple implement that has transformed a fundamental human experience for vast numbers of infants and mothers, yet it finds no place in our histories of technology. This technology might be thought of as a classic time-shifting device, as it enables mothers to exercise more control over the timing of feeding. It can also function to save time, as bottle feeding allows the mother's time to be substituted by someone else. Potentially, therefore, it has huge implications for the _____________ of time in everyday life, yet it is entirely overlooked in discussions of high-speed society.
options: ① emotion
② management
③ intention
④ memory
⑤ identity
explanation: 젖병이라는 기술이 수유 시간의 통제(control)를 가능하게 하고 타인이 시간을 대신(substituted)하게 함으로써 시간을 절약하게 해준다는 내용을 통해, 이 기술이 일상생활에서 시간의 '관리(management)'에 큰 영향을 미치고 있음을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 감정
② 관리
③ 의도
