question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Many historians have pointed to the significance of ⓐ<u>accurate</u> time measurement to Western economic progress. The French historian Jacques Le Goff called the ⓑ<u>birth</u> of the public mechanical clock a turning point in Western society. Until the late Middle Ages, people had sun or water clocks, which did not play any ⓒ<u>meaningful</u> role in business activities. Market openings and activities started with the sunrise and typically ended at noon when the sun was at its peak. But when the first public mechanical clocks were introduced and spread across European cities, market times were set by the stroke of the hour. Public clocks thus greatly contributed to public life and work by providing a new concept of time that was ⓓ<u>easy</u> for everyone to understand. This, in turn, helped facilitate trade and commerce. Interactions and transactions between consumers, retailers, and wholesalers became ⓔ<u>irregular</u>. Important town meetings began to follow the pace of the clock, allowing people to better plan their time and allocate resources in a more efficient manner.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 기계식 시계의 보급으로 시장 시간과 활동이 시간 단위로 정해지게 되면서, 소비자, 소매업자, 도매업자 사이의 상호작용과 거래는 이전의 해와 달에 의존하던 모호한 시간대보다 더 '규칙적'이거나 '예측 가능'하게 되었습니다. 따라서 'irregular(불규칙한)'은 문맥상 적절하지 않으며 'regular'나 'predictable' 등이 적절합니다.

question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: In response to human-like care robots, critics might charge that human-robot interactions create moral ⓐ<u>risks</u> for dementia patients. Even if deception is sometimes allowed when it serves worthy goals, should it be ⓑ<u>permitted</u> for vulnerable users? Just as children on the autism spectrum with robot companions might be easily fooled into thinking of robots as friends, older adults with cognitive deficits might be. According to Alexis Elder, a professor at UMD, robots are ⓒ<u>genuine</u> friends, inferior to true friendship. Reasoning along similar lines, John Sullins, a professor at Sonoma State University, holds that robots should "remain iconic or cartoonish so that they are easily ⓓ<u>recognized</u> as synthetic even by unsophisticated users." At least then no one is fooled. Making robots clearly fake also avoids the so-called "uncanny valley," where robots are perceived as scary because they so closely ⓔ<u>mirror</u> us, but not quite. Other critics of robot deception argue that when care recipients are deceived into thinking that robots care, this crosses a line and violates human dignity.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 문맥상 로봇과의 관계는 진정한 우정(true friendship)보다 열등한(inferior) 것이며, 사용자들이 속아 넘어가는 가짜 우정이라는 맥락입니다. 따라서 로봇이 'genuine(진실한)' 친구라고 하는 것은 논리적으로 맞지 않으며, 'false' 또는 'pretend' 성격의 단어가 와야 합니다.

question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: New words and expressions emerge continually in response to new situations, ideas and feelings. The Oxford English Dictionary publishes supplements of new words and expressions that have entered the language. Some people deplore this kind of thing and see it as a drift from correct English. But it was only in the eighteenth century that any attempt was made to formalize spelling and punctuation of English at all. The language we speak in the twenty-first century would be virtually unintelligible to Shakespeare, and so would his way of speaking to us. Alvin Toffler estimated that Shakespeare would probably only understand about 250,000 of the 450,000 words in general use in the English language now. In other words, so to speak, if Shakespeare were to materialize in London today he would understand, on average, only five out of every nine words in our vocabulary. This suggests that language is not a fixed system but rather a(n) ________________________________________.*deplore 한탄하다
options: ① declining tool that loses precision over time
② deliberate invention created by dictionary publishers
③ evolving organism that adapts to the needs of its speakers
④ historical treasure that should be preserved in its purest form
⑤ regional phenomenon that varies only by geographical location
explanation: 글의 전반부에서 새로운 상황과 아이디어에 대응하여 계속해서 새로운 단어가 나타난다고 언급하고, 셰익스피어 시대와 현재의 언어적 차이를 예로 들어 언어가 고정되어 있지 않음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 언어는 고정된 시스템이 아니라 '사용자의 필요에 적응하는 진화하는 유기체'라는 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 시간이 지남에 따라 정밀도를 잃는 쇠퇴하는 도구
② 사전 출판업자에 의해 만들어진 의도적인 발명품
③ 말하는 사람의 필요에 적응하는 진화하는 유기체
④ 가장 순수한 형태로 보존되어야 할 역사적 보물
⑤ 지리적 위치에 따라서만 변하는 지역적 현상

question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Mental development consists of individuals increasingly mastering social codes and signals themselves, which they can master only in social situations with the support of more competent individuals, typically adults. (A) In Denmark, the age of criminal responsibility is 15 years, which means that we then say that people have developed sufficient mental maturity to be accountable for their actions at this point. (B) And at the age of 18 people are given the right to vote and are thereby formally included in the basic democratic process. (C) I do not know whether these age boundaries are optimal, but it is clear that mental development takes place at different rates for different individuals, and depends especially on the social and family environment they have been given. (D) Therefore, having formal limits for responsibility from a specific age that apply to everyone is a somewhat questionable practice. (E) But the question, of course, is whether it can be done any differently.*developmental trajectory 발달 과정
insertion_sentence: In this way, cognitive growth involves absorbing societal norms and gradually evolving into an accountable member of the community.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'In this way'는 앞 문장에서 설명한 사회적 코드와 신호를 숙달하는 과정을 지칭하며, 이것이 인지적 성장과 사회적 규범 흡수, 그리고 책임 있는 공동체 구성원으로의 진화로 이어진다고 요약하고 있습니다. (A) 뒤에 나오는 덴마크의 형사 책임 연령 사례는 '책임 있는 구성원'에 대한 법적 규정의 구체적인 예시이므로, 일반적인 진술인 주어진 문장이 (A) 위치에 오는 것이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.

question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: If cooking is as central to human identity, biology, and culture as the biological anthropologist Richard Wrangham suggests, it stands to reason that the decline of cooking in our time would have serious consequences for modern life, and so it has. Are they all bad? Not at all. ⓐThe outsourcing of much of the work of cooking to corporations has relieved women of what has traditionally been their exclusive responsibility for feeding the family, making it easier for them to work outside the home and have careers. ⓑIt has headed off many of the domestic conflicts that such a large shift in gender roles and family dynamics was bound to spark. ⓒSome nutritionists argue that home-cooked meals generally contain fewer calories, less fat, and less sodium than restaurant meals or processed foods. ⓓIt has relieved other pressures in the household, including longer workdays and overscheduled children, and saved us time that we can now invest in other pursuits. ⓔIt has also allowed us to diversify our diets substantially, making it possible even for people with no cooking skills and little money to enjoy a whole different cuisine. All that's required is a microwave.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 요리 활동의 기업 외주화(간편식 등)가 현대 사회에 가져온 긍정적인 측면(여성의 사회 진출 용이, 가사 갈등 해소, 시간 절약, 식단의 다양화)을 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓒ번 문장은 집밥과 외식/가공식품의 영양학적 비교(칼로리, 나트륨 등)를 언급하고 있어, 요리 외주화의 사회적 영향이라는 주제에서 벗어납니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Sylvan Goldman invented the shopping cart and introduced it in his stores in 1937. It was an excellent device that would make it easy for shoppers to buy as much as they wanted without getting tired or seeking others' help. But Goldman discovered that in spite of his repeated advertisements and explanations, he could not persuade his shoppers to use the wheeled carts. Men were reluctant because they thought they would appear weak if they pushed such carts instead of carrying their shopping. Women wouldn't touch them because the carts reminded them of baby carriages. It was only a few elderly shoppers who used them. That made the carts even less attractive to the majority of the shoppers. Then Goldman hit upon an idea. He hired several models, men and women, of different ages and asked them to wheel the carts in the store and shop. A young woman employee standing near the entrance told the regular shoppers, 'Look, everyone is using the carts. Why don't you?' That was the turning point. A few shills disguised as regular shoppers easily accomplished what logic, explanations, and advertisements failed to do. Within a few weeks shoppers readily accepted those carts.*shill 바람잡이
options: ① Goldman faced a problem when introducing shopping carts in 1937.
② The shopping carts were specifically designed to reduce shoppers' physical tiredness while purchasing more items.
③ Goldman's advertisements and explanations eventually convinced most shoppers to use the carts.
④ Men avoided using the carts because they were concerned about appearing physically weak.
⑤ Goldman employed models of various ages to pose as regular customers using the shopping carts.
explanation: 본문에 따르면 Goldman의 반복적인 광고와 설명에도 불구하고 고객들을 설득할 수 없었습니다("...in spite of his repeated advertisements and explanations, he could not persuade his shoppers..."). 사람들을 설득한 것은 논리나 광고가 아니라 카트를 사용하는 모델(바람잡이)들을 고용한 전략이었습니다. 따라서 ③번은 사실과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① Goldman은 1937년에 쇼핑 카트를 도입할 때 문제에 직면했다.
② 쇼핑 카트는 더 많은 품목을 구매하는 동안 쇼핑객의 육체적 피로를 줄이기 위해 특별히 설계되었다.
③ Goldman의 광고와 설명은 결국 대부분의 쇼핑객들이 카트를 사용하도록 설득했다.
④ 남성들은 카트를 밀면 신체적으로 약해 보일까 봐 사용을 피했다.
⑤ Goldman은 다양한 연령대의 모델을 고용하여 쇼핑 카트를 사용하는 일반 고객인 척하게 했다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 각각 찾아 그대로 쓰시오.
passage: People seem to recognize that the arts are cultural activities that draw on (or react against) certain cultural traditions, certain shared understanding, and certain values and ideas that are characteristic of the time and place in which the art is created. In the case of science, however, opinions differ. Some scientists, like the great biologist J. B. S. Haldane, see science in a similar light - as a historical activity that occurs in a particular time and place, and that needs to be understood within that context. Others, however, see science as a purely "objective" pursuit, uninfluenced by the cultural viewpoint and values of those who create it. In describing this view of science, philosopher Hugh Lacey speaks of the belief that there is an underlying order of the world which is simply there to be discovered - the world of pure "fact" stripped of any link with value. The aim of science according to this view is to represent this world of pure "fact", independently of any relationship it might bear contingently to human practices and experiences.

question: 15. 윗글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially ⓐ<u>explained</u> by the Matthew effect. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, and each of these payoffs further ⓑ<u>increase</u> her odds of scoring another win. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally ⓒ<u>talented</u>. Therefore, future success again goes to those who ⓓ<u>have had</u> success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, ⓔ<u>raised</u> the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
options: ① The Hidden Force Behind Scientific Success: Endeavor
② The Matthew Effect: Why Untalented Scientists Keep Winning
③ The Most Famous One-Hit Wonder Scientist: Issac Newton
④ Why Success Follows Great Scientists: Talent or Status?
⑤ No Causal Link Between Early and Later Scientific Success

question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 밑줄 친 "the effect of contact in that direction may not progress any further than this"가 뜻하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Quite often the interaction between groups is socially unequal, and this is reflected in the fact that in many cases borrowing of words or constructions goes mostly or entirely in one direction, from the more powerful or prestigious group to the less favored one. The languages of socially subordinated groups may from quite an early period of contact provide terminology for objects or practices with which speakers of the more powerful group were previously unfamiliar, but <u>the effects of contact in that direction may not progress any further than this</u>. In some cases, as with the Dharug language of Sydney, Australia, the source of some of the earliest loans from Indigenous Australian languages into English, the fate of the language system is extinction after the obliteration of many of its speakers. The remainder shifted to varieties of English, the language of the people who had suppressed them.
options: ① The subordinate group's language begins to gradually influence the core grammatical structure of the dominant language, introducing significant changes to grammar and structure beyond just vocabulary borrowing.

② Linguistic influence from the less powerful group to the more powerful one is typically confined to providing specific terminology for unfamiliar items or customs and rarely affects the deeper structure or broader vocabulary of the dominant language.
③ The limited vocabulary items borrowed by the dominant group from the subordinate group eventually fall out of use, causing their influence to disappear entirely.
④ Speakers of the subordinate group learn only specific varieties of the dominant language, thereby limiting the potential effects of bidirectional language contact.
⑤ There is a tendency for mutual vocabulary borrowing to decrease sharply in both languages after the initial stages of contact, regardless of power relations.
explanation: 본문은 사회적으로 불평등한 관계에 있는 두 집단의 언어 접촉 시, 주로 강한 집단에서 약한 집단으로 언어 차용이 이루어짐을 설명합니다. 밑줄 친 부분은 약한 집단에서 강한 집단으로 향하는 영향(in that direction)이 단순히 낯선 사물이나 관습에 대한 용어를 제공하는 수준(this)을 넘어서지 않는다는 의미이므로, 언어적 영향이 특정 용어에 국한된다는 내용의 2번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 하위 집단의 언어가 지배적인 언어의 핵심 문법 구조에 점차 영향을 미치기 시작하여, 단순한 어휘 차용을 넘어 문법과 구조에 중대한 변화를 가져온다.

question: 23. 다음 글이 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested, that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. Revolutionaries have always looked to the past to frame their future cause, as is amply illustrated by examples from nationalism to communism. The future has often been seen as variously a recovery of a lost time, as a replication of what is established, or as a model bequeathed by a heroic age long gone. The writing of history is based on understanding or explaining future outcomes that were not known to contemporaries, since the historian has the benefit of hindsight and the past is nothing more than the accumulation of futures that are now our past. So, rather than see the hand of the past always shaping the future, perhaps it can be seen in reverse, with the past ─ in the sense of our understanding of it ─ being shaped by our orientation to the future.
options: ① Contrary to conventional thinking, our contemporary understanding and representation of the past are actively shaped and influenced by our orientation towards, and conceptions of, the future.
② While the past inevitably shapes the future, our understanding and interpretation of past events remain static and unaffected by our projections or aspirations for the future.
③ The traditional view suggests that historical tracks are predetermined by past events, with future outcomes being merely passive consequences.
④ Historical analysis is objective only when it strictly excludes any consideration of future possibilities or outcomes, focusing solely on documented past events.
⑤ Revolutionaries utilize historical narratives primarily to legitimize present actions, but their vision of the future rarely involves reinterpreting or recovering aspects of the past.

question: 24. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem; they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
options: ① The challenge of achieving natural ecosystem stability in home gardens with minimal intervention
② Garden ecosystem dynamics that naturally favor vegetable production, requiring only occasional intervention
③ Home vegetable gardening as a constant effort against natural ecosystem stability, demanding continuous active management
④ The ecosystem state concept illustrating maximized vegetable yields as a temporary, easily achieved phase without significant yield loss after stopping intervention
⑤ Fundamental garden ecosystem stability maintaining relatively high vegetable yields through the resilience of cultivated plant species, even during pauses in intervention

question: 25. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much a creative process. A conjecture is a philosophical invention, cooked up rather mystically by the mind through the mental computation we call careful contemplation. However, until the hypothesis is tested against reality, it is not yet truly knowledge; it is just information that represents speculation. Knowledge is information that has demonstrated its usefulness. It is what is left over after cycles of experimental testing have eliminated false theories. As scientists continually test their hypotheses and modify their models to account for new and surprising data, a kind of "learning loop" emerges that statisticians call Bayesian updating. Based on Bayes' Rule, developed by eighteenth-century English statistician and philosopher Thomas Bayes, Bayesian updating refers to a mathematical process whereby an accepted theory or predictive model gets increasingly accurate through the repetitive testing of competing variants of that theory.
options: ① Scientific knowledge's reliability is mainly determined by the logical rigor and credibility of initial conjectures, with empirical testing as a secondary validation step.
② Science embodies a view where creative, intuitive hypothesis generation is less central than systematic experimental testing and Bayesian refinement.
③ An initial hypothesis lacks knowledge status and remains speculative until its usefulness and correspondence with reality are proven through repeated testing and processes like Bayesian updating.
④ Bayesian updating is presented as the necessary endpoint for hypotheses to become knowledge, suggesting knowledge cannot be established through simpler experimental falsification.

⑤ Once a conjecture passes initial testing and becomes knowledge, its core principles are established, with Bayesian updating only fine-tuning peripheral aspects without changing its fundamental theoretical status.

② 과학은 체계적인 실험 테스트와 베이즈적 개선보다 창의적이고 직관적인 가설 생성이 덜 중심적이라는 견해를 구현한다.
③ 초기 가설은 지식의 지위가 부족하며, 반복된 테스트와 베이즈 업데이트와 같은 과정을 통해 그 유용성과 현실과의 일치가 입증될 때까지 추측으로 남아 있다.
④ 베이즈 업데이트는 가설이 지식이 되기 위한 필수적인 종착점으로 제시되며, 더 단순한 실험적 반증을 통해서는 지식이 확립될 수 없음을 시사한다.

question: 26. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. All experts are not the same, nor do they submit their work to the same scrutiny. Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims. For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were funded in part by the sugar industry. The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared. Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have fostered higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. Stories such as this one fuel suspicion ─ but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. Funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since been made compulsory.
options: ① Navigating Scientific Claims: The Indispensable Role of Skepticism and Awareness of Bias
② Funding Disclosure: A Historical Overview of Scientific Ethics
③ Sugar vs. Fat: Deconstructing a Decades-Long Health Debate
④ The Unquestioned Objectivity of Modern Scientific Inquiry
⑤ Peer Review and Professional Standards: Guarantees of Scientific Trustworthiness

question: 27. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
passage: The explosion of popular music in the second half of the twentieth century as well as the global circulation and dissemination of music by the creative industries propelled a new understanding of accessibility in relation to music. Suddenly, in the 1950s, anyone could pick up spoons, a couple of pans, a second-hand guitar and start a band. This led to specific genres such as skiffle, but also, more generally, reflected a much more relaxed and inclusive attitude to music making. While ordinary people had always sung and made music, the popular music movement was driven by a spirit of rebellion and freedom. This approach led to the punk movement, whose musicians even made it a condition for their music to be non-virtuosic and accessible to all in the 1970s. Groups who had been entirely excluded from music revelled in opportunities to create. This led to a sense of novelty and empowerment in and beyond the music sphere.
options: ① The global circulation of music primarily benefited professionally trained musicians, reinforcing the exclusivity of music creation before the mid-twentieth century.
② The rise of popular music genres like skiffle and punk primarily resulted from technological advancements in recording, rather than a shift in cultural attitudes towards music making.
③ While ordinary people always participated in informal music making, the post-1950s era marked a decline in accessibility due to the commercialization and industrialization of music.

④ The crucial change in the latter half of the 20th century was a philosophical shift towards inclusivity and rebellion, empowering previously excluded groups and valuing accessibility, sometimes over technical virtuosity.
⑤ The punk movement, despite its rebellious spirit, ultimately aimed to restore high standards of musical virtuosity that had been lost in the preceding popular music trends.
explanation: 20세기 후반 대중음악의 폭발적 증가와 펑크 운동 등은 음악의 접근성에 대한 새로운 이해를 가져왔습니다. 특히 기술적 정교함(virtuosity)보다 포용성, 저항, 모든 이의 접근 가능성을 중시하며 소외되었던 집단에게 권한을 부여했다는 점이 글의 핵심 내용과 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 음악의 전 세계적 유통은 주로 전문 교육을 받은 음악가들에게 혜택을 주어, 20세기 중반 이전의 음악 창작의 독점성을 강화했다.
② 스키플과 펑크와 같은 대중음악 장르의 부상은 음악 제작에 대한 문화적 태도의 변화보다는 주로 녹음 기술의 발전에 기인했다.
③ 일반인들이 항상 비공식적인 음악 제작에 참여해 왔지만, 1950년대 이후 시대는 음악의 상업화와 산업화로 인해 접근성이 하락했다.
④ 20세기 후반의 결정적인 변화는 포용성과 저항을 향한 철학적 변화였으며, 이는 이전에 배제되었던 집단에 권한을 부여하고 때로는 기술적 정교함보다 접근성을 가치 있게 여겼다.
⑤ 펑크 운동은 저항 정신에도 불구하고, 궁극적으로 이전 대중음악 트렌드에서 상실되었던 높은 수준의 음악적 기교를 복원하는 것을 목표로 했다.

question: 28. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
options: ① Gestures function as primary cognitive tools that precede speech, with hand movements stopping milliseconds before verbal correction, demonstrating their role in influencing and leading thought processes.
② Gestures significantly impact core cognitive processes, playing a crucial role in memory retention, problem-solving capabilities, and speech fluency beyond mere social signaling functions.

③ Gesture acts as a crucial forerunner and facilitator for both thought formulation and fluent speech production, with its inhibition leading to demonstrable impairments in memory, problem- solving, and verbal explanation.

④ The link between gesture and thought is causal rather than merely correlational; when prevented from gesturing, speakers become less fluent, demonstrating how gestures actively shape the cognitive processes underlying speech.
⑤ Hand gestures primarily serve to prime emotional states associated with speech content, rather than directly facilitating the retrieval or organization of semantic information.
explanation: 글의 내용에 따르면 제스처는 말을 하기 전에 단어를 준비시키고(prime a word), 다음 단어를 공급하며, 기억과 문제 해결 등 인지 과정 전반을 돕는 역할을 합니다. 즉, 의미 정보를 인출하고 조직하는 것을 돕는 것이지, 단순히 감정 상태를 준비시키는 것에 국한되지 않습니다. 따라서 5번은 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 몸짓은 언어에 앞서는 일차적인 인지 도구로 기능하며, 손의 움직임이 언어적 수정보다 수 밀리초 전에 멈추는 것은 사고 과정을 자극하고 주도하는 역할을 보여준다.
② 몸짓은 단순한 사회적 신호 기능을 넘어 기억력 유지, 문제 해결 능력 및 언어 유창성에서 중요한 역할을 하며 핵심 인지 과정에 큰 영향을 미친다.
③ 몸짓은 사고의 형성과 유창한 언어 생산 모두를 위한 중요한 선구자이자 촉진제 역할을 하며, 몸짓의 억제는 기억력, 문제 해결 및 언어적 설명에 있어 입증 가능한 장애를 초래한다.
④ 몸짓과 사고의 연결은 단순한 상관관계가 아니라 인과관계이다. 몸짓을 못하게 할 때 화자가 덜 유창해지는 것은 몸짓이 언어의 기초가 되는 인지 과정을 능동적으로 형성함을 보여준다.
⑤ 손짓은 의미 정보의 인출이나 조직을 직접적으로 촉진하기보다는 주로 언어 내용과 관련된 감정 상태를 준비시키는 역할을 한다.

question: 29. 다음 글의 주장과 일치하는 것은?
passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food is taking a back seat. I suspect that most people view flavor as of secondary importance in social settings where food is served. Although our social gatherings coalesce around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, do not depend on the quality of sensations provided by the food. To focus excessively on flavor is to miss the larger significance of these social relations.
options: ① The intricate nuances of flavor are often the primary stimuli for initiating and sustaining meaningful social interactions during shared meals.
② While acknowledging flavor's role in satisfying hunger, its subjective and personal nature actively hinders, rather than facilitates, the collective social bonding rituals surrounding food.
③ A re-evaluation is needed, in which flavor appreciation is elevated to the same level of importance as social dynamics in fully understanding food-centric gatherings.
④ Conventional wisdom holds that the quality of flavor directly correlates with the success and memorability of social events where food is served, dictating the overall social atmosphere.
⑤ Prioritizing the analysis of flavor during social gatherings is often seen as a social misstep, taking away from the more culturally significant shared and relationship-based aspects of the event.
explanation: 이 글은 음식과 관련된 사회적 모임에서 '맛'은 개인적이고 주관적인 부차적 요소로 취급되며, 모임의 진정한 의미는 사회적 관계와 의례에 있다고 설명합니다. 따라서 맛에 지나치게 집중하는 것은 이러한 사회적 관계의 더 큰 의미를 놓치는 것이라는 주장을 담고 있습니다. 선택지 ⑤는 사교 모임에서 맛에 대한 분석을 우선시하는 것이 문화적으로 중요한 관계적 측면을 저해한다는 내용으로 글의 주장과 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 맛의 복잡한 뉘앙스는 종종 식사를 공유하는 동안 의미 있는 사회적 상호작용을 시작하고 유지하기 위한 일차적인 자극제가 된다.
② 맛이 배고픔을 충족시키는 역할을 한다는 점을 인정하면서도, 그 주관적이고 개인적인 성격은 음식을 둘러싼 집단적 사회적 결속 의례를 돕기보다는 오히려 방해한다.
③ 음식 중심의 모임을 완전히 이해하기 위해서는 맛에 대한 감상을 사회적 역동성과 동일한 수준의 중요성으로 높이는 재평가가 필요하다.
④ 통념에 따르면 맛의 품질은 음식이 제공되는 사교 행사의 성공 및 기억에 남는 정도와 직접적인 상관관계가 있으며, 전반적인 사교 분위기를 좌우한다.
⑤ 사교 모임 중에 맛에 대한 분석을 우선시하는 것은 종종 사회적 실수로 간주되며, 행사의 문화적으로 더 중요한 공유 및 관계 기반 측면을 손상시킨다.

question: 30. 다음 글에서 제기하는 핵심 질문으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success. Is there really a Matthew effect after all?
options: ① Does the complexity of scientific problems dictate whether a scientist achieves a single breakthrough or multiple ones?
② Is repeated scientific success mainly due to advantages from initial success, or does it merely reflect persistent, exceptional underlying talent?
③ Is the peer review process more generous towards scientists who have already achieved significant success?
④ Are scientific breakthroughs, such as Newton's, primarily the result of individual genius or collaborative efforts facilitated by social status?
⑤ To what extent do resource allocation and funding rather than intellectual merit, determine the progression of a scientist's career?

question: 31. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports.
summary_sentence: While governments prioritize national food security, achieving complete self-sufficiency is often unrealistic and unnecessary; the primary goal of (A)__________ is typically met through (B)__________, acknowledging the global variability in agricultural conditions and leveraging international markets.
options: ① maximizing exports ... import controls
② food sovereignty ... traditional farming
③ adequate supply ... indigenous & imported food
④ total independence ... domestic technology
⑤ global price stability ... relying on neighbors

question: 32. 다음 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 해마(hippocampus)가 스트레스 상황에서 수행하는 두 가지 주요 기능을 각각 30자 내외의 우리말로 서술하시오.
passage: Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain. A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol "on" instead of "off," which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.
subjective_conditions: 각각 30자 내외의 우리말로 서술할 것
answer: (1) 기능 1: 해마는 감정 반응을 조절함으로써 스트레스에 대한 회복력을 유지하는 데 도움을 준다. (2) 기능 2: 환경의 안전성을 모니터링하고 위험한 자극을 장기 기억에 저장하여 미래에 회피할 수 있게 한다.
explanation: 지문에서 해마의 기능으로 언급된 두 가지를 찾아 한국어로 요약해야 합니다. 첫째는 스트레스 상황에서의 회복력 유지 및 기분 조절 기능이고, 둘째는 환경 안전성 모니터링 및 위험 자극의 장기 기억 저장을 통한 미래 위험 회피 기능입니다.

question: 33. 다음 글에서 설명하는 '유사 기억(quasi-memory)'의 개념을 우리말 30자 내외로 정의하고, 이 용어가 왜 일반적인 '기억(memory)'과 구분되어야 하는지 그 철학적 필요성을 우리말 50자 내외로 서술하시오.
passage: As a general rule, it's better if your definition corresponds as closely as possible to the way in which the term is ordinarily used in the kinds of debates to which your claims are pertinent. There will be, however, occasions where it is appropriate, even necessary, to coin special uses through what philosophers call stimulative definition. This would be the case where the current lexicon is not able to make distinctions that you think are philosophically important. For example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something the person having it has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories: I would have a memory-type experience, but this would not be of something that I had actually experienced. To call this a memory would be misleading. For this reason, philosophers have coined the special term 'quasi-memory' to refer to these hypothetical memory-like experiences.
subjective_conditions: '유사 기억(quasi-memory)'의 개념을 우리말 30자 내외로 정의할 것
일반적인 '기억(memory)'과 구분되어야 하는 철학적 필요성을 우리말 50자 내외로 서술할 것
answer: (1) 경험자가 직접 체험하지 않았음에도 기억과 유사한 심적 경험을 갖는 현상을 말한다.(2) 실제 경험에 기반한 기억과 타인의 기억 공유처럼 실제 경험이 없는 기억적 경험을 명확히 구분하여 철학적 분석의 오해를 막고 정밀성을 높이기 위함이다.
explanation: 글에서는 '유사 기억'을 '반드시 그 사람이 직접 경험한 것이 아닐 수도 있는 기억'으로 정의하고 있습니다. 타인의 기억을 공유하는 경우와 같이 '실제 경험'이 결여된 기억적 경험을 일반적인 '기억'이라고 부르는 것은 오해의 소지가 있기 때문에, 철학적 논의의 정밀성을 위해 이 둘을 구분하는 새로운 용어가 필요하다는 것이 핵심입니다.

question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
passage: Beethoven's drive to create something novel is a reflection of his state of curiosity. Our brains experience a sense of reward when we create something new in the process of exploring something uncertain, such as a musical phrase that we've never played or heard before. When our curiosity leads to something novel, the resulting reward brings us a sense of pleasure. A number of investigators have modeled how curiosity influences musical composition. In the case of Beethoven, computer modeling focused on the thirty-two piano sonatas written after age thirteen revealed that the musical patterns found in all of Beethoven's music decreased in later sonatas, while novel patterns, including patterns that were unique to a particular sonata, increased. In other words, Beethoven's music became less predictable over time as his curiosity drove the exploration of new musical ideas. Curiosity is a powerful driver of human creativity.
options: ① Beethoven's Melodies: A Journey Back in Time

question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 알맞은 것은?

question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
passage: Development of the human body from a single cell provides many examples of the structural richness that is possible when the repeated production of random variation is combined with nonrandom selection. All phases of body development from embryo to adult exhibit random activities at the cellular level, and body formation depends on the new possibilities generated by these activities coupled with selection of those outcomes that satisfy previously built-in criteria. Always new structure is based on old structure, and at every stage selection favors some cells and eliminates others. The survivors serve to produce new cells that undergo further rounds of selection. Except in the immune system, cells and extensions of cells are not genetically selected during development, but rather, are positionally selected. question: 14. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.9점]

question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 3월 34번]

question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: As a general rule, it's better if your definition corresponds as ⓐ<u>closely</u> as possible to the way in which the term is ordinarily used in the kinds of debates to which your claims are pertinent. There will be, however, occasions ⓑ<u>where</u> it is appropriate, even necessary, to coin special uses through what philosophers call stimulative definition. This would be the case where the current lexicon is not able to make distinctions that you think ⓒ<u>is</u> philosophically important. For example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something the person ⓓ<u>having</u> it has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories: I would have a memorytype experience, but this would not be of something that I had actually experienced. To call this a memory would be ⓔ<u>misleading</u>. For this reason, philosophers have coined the special term 'quasi-memory' to refer to these hypothetical memory-like experiences.

question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much a creative process. A conjecture is a philosophical invention, cooked up rather mystically by the mind through the mental computation ⓐ<u>called</u> careful contemplation. However, until the hypothesis is tested against reality, it is not yet truly knowledge; it is just information ⓑ<u>that</u> represents speculation. Knowledge is information that has demonstrated its usefulness. It is ⓒ<u>what</u> is left over after cycles of experimental testing have eliminated false theories. As scientists continually test their hypotheses and modify their models to account for new and surprising data, a kind of "learning loop" ⓓ<u>emerging</u> that statisticians call Bayesian updating. Based on Bayes' Rule, developed by eighteenth-century English statistician and philosopher Thomas Bayes, Bayesian updating refers to a mathematical process ⓔ<u>whereby</u> an accepted theory or predictive model gets increasingly accurate through the repetitive testing of competing variants of that theory.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 As절이 끝난 후 주절의 주어는 a kind of "learning loop"입니다. 따라서 뒤에는 본동사가 와야 하는데, 현재분사인 emerging은 동사 역할을 할 수 없습니다. 시제와 수 일치를 고려하여 emerges로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓐ는 수동 의미의 과거분사, ⓑ는 주격 관계대명사, ⓒ는 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사, ⓔ는 '그 과정에 의해'라는 의미를 가진 관계부사로 모두 어법상 적절합니다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸을 <보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성하시오. (단, 철자 오류 시 오답 처리)

question: 1. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 5. 다음 밑줄 친 stimulative definition이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: As a general rule, it's better if your definition corresponds as closely as possible to the way in which the term is ordinarily used in the kinds of debates to which your claims are pertinent. There will be, however, occasions where it is appropriate, even necessary, to coin special uses through what philosophers call <u>stimulative definition</u>. This would be the case where the current lexicon is not able to make distinctions that you think are philosophically important. For example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something the person having it has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories: I would have a memory-type experience, but this would not be of something that I had actually experienced. To call this a memory would be misleading. For this reason, philosophers have coined the special term 'quasi-memory' to refer to these hypothetical memory-like experiences.
options: ① creating a term for a specific philosophical use
② rejecting the use of terms that can't be defined
③ providing intellectual stimulus for abstract thinking
④ relying on ordinary language in philosophical debates
⑤ applying a term more broadly than its original meaning
explanation: 지문은 일상적인 용어로 설명하기 어려운 철학적 구분을 위해 철학자들이 새로운 용어를 만들어내는 'stimulative definition(약정적 정의)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 예시로 든 'quasi-memory'는 기존 어휘로 표현할 수 없는 특정 현상을 지칭하기 위해 만들어진 용어이므로, 정답은 '특정 철학적 용도를 위해 용어를 만드는 것'인 ①번입니다.

question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Beethoven's drive to create something novel is a reflection of his state of curiosity. Our brains experience a sense of reward when we create something new in the process of exploring something uncertain, such as a musical phrase that we've never played or heard before. When our curiosity leads to something novel, the resulting reward brings us a sense of pleasure. A number of investigators have modeled how curiosity influences musical composition. In the case of Beethoven, computer modeling focused on the thirty-two piano sonatas written after age thirteen revealed that the musical patterns found in all of Beethoven's music decreased in later sonatas, while novel patterns, including patterns that were unique to a particular sonata, increased. In other words, Beethoven's music became less predictable over time as his curiosity drove the exploration of new musical ideas. Curiosity is a powerful driver of human creativity.

question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.0점]
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
options: ① Long Journey from Hands to Lips
② Hands Always Follow Our Thought
③ Gesture: Guiding the Flow of Thought
④ Why We Use Gestures for Communication
⑤ Nonverbal Language: Speech's Clumsy Companion

question: 8. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: For years, many psychologists have held strongly to the belief that the key to addressing negative health habits is to change behavior. This, more than values and attitudes, is the part of personality that is easiest to change. Ingestive habits such as smoking, drinking and various eating behaviors are the most common health concerns targeted for behavioral changes. Process-addiction behaviors (workaholism, shopaholism, and the like) fall into this category as well. Mental imagery combined with power of suggestion was taken up as the premise of behavioral medicine to help people change negative health behaviors into positive ones. Although this technique alone will not produce changes, when used alongside other behavior modification tactics and coping strategies, behavioral changes have proved effective for some people. What mental imagery does is reinforce a new desired behavior. Repeated use of images reinforces the desired behavior more strongly over time.
options: ① Mental imagery is essential for improving mental health.
② Psychological factors are irrelevant to the process of habit formation.
③ Changing values and attitudes is the easiest way to break bad habits.
④ It is more challenging to address process-addiction than ingestive habits.

explanation: 이 글은 부정적인 건강 습관을 교정하기 위해 행동을 변화시키는 것이 중요하며, 특히 정신적 심상(mental imagery)을 행동 수정 전략과 병행하여 사용할 때 새로운 행동을 강화하고 건강하지 못한 습관을 극복하는 데 효과적이라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '정신적 심상을 이용한 행동 수정은 건강하지 못한 습관을 극복하는 데 도움이 된다'는 5번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 정신적 심상은 정신 건강을 향상시키는 데 필수적이다.

question: 9. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Technologists are always on the lookout for quantifiable metrics. Measurable inputs to a model are their lifeblood, and like a social scientist, a technologist needs to identify concrete measures, or "proxies," for assessing progress. This need for quantifiable proxies produces a bias toward measuring things that are easy to quantify. But simple metrics can take us further away from the important goals we really care about, which may require complicated metrics or be extremely difficult, or perhaps impossible, to reduce to any measure. And when we have imperfect or bad proxies, we can easily fall under the illusion that we are solving for a good end without actually making genuine progress toward a worthy solution. The problem of proxies results in technologists frequently substituting what is measurable for what is meaningful. As the saying goes, "Not everything that counts can be counted, and not everything that can be counted counts."
options: ① 의미 있는 것들은 측정할 수 있어야 한다.
② 일의 진척 상황은 측정이 어려운 영역이다.
③ 측정 기준이 단순해야 측정 결과에 오류가 없다.
④ 기술자는 정량화할 수 있는 측정 기준을 찾아야 한다.
⑤ 정량화할 수 있는 측정 기준이 편향을 유발할 수도 있다.
explanation: 이 글은 기술자들이 정량화 가능한 지표(대리 지표)에 지나치게 의존함으로써, 측정하기 쉬운 것들만 측정하려는 편향이 생기고 결과적으로 진짜 중요한 의미 있는 목표로부터 멀어질 수 있다는 위험성을 경고하고 있습니다. 따라서 5번 '정량화할 수 있는 측정 기준이 편향을 유발할 수도 있다'가 요지로 가장 적절합니다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. All experts are not the same, nor do they submit their work to the same scrutiny. Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims. For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were funded in part by the sugar industry. The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared. Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have fostered higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. Stories such as this one fuel suspicion ─ but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. Funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since been made compulsory.

options: ① biased  accept

④ improved  evaluate
⑤ manipulated  overlook

question: 11. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition. But it's important to understand the limits of dictionary definitions. More often than not, a definition in a dictionary requires readers to have a fairly robust understanding of the language already at their disposal. In other words, a dictionary functions in many cases as a cross-reference or translator between words one knows and words that one doesn't yet know. Even the most obscure words in a dictionary, say, for example, "pulchritudinous" or "kalokagathia," must be defined using words that the reader already knows and understands. Otherwise, the dictionary isn't very helpful.
options: ① the challenges of lexical definitions
② the completeness of lexical resources
③ the circular nature of dictionary explanations
④ the effectiveness of isolated word definitions
⑤ the importance of expanding vocabulary through reading
explanation: 사전적 정의는 독자가 언어에 대해 이미 꽤 확고한 이해를 갖추고 있어야 하고, 그렇지 않으면 별 도움이 되지 않는다는 한계를 다루고 있으므로 1번이 주제로 적절하다.

question: 12. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Quite often the interaction between groups is socially unequal, and this is reflected in the fact that in many cases borrowing of words or constructions goes mostly or entirely in one direction, from the more powerful or prestigious group to the less favored one. The languages of socially subordinated groups may from quite an early period of contact provide terminology for objects or practices with which speakers of the more powerful group were previously unfamiliar, but the effects of contact in that direction may not progress any further than this. In some cases, as with the Dharug language of Sydney, Australia, the source of some of the earliest loans from Indigenous Australian languages into English, the fate of the language system is extinction after the obliteration of many of its speakers. The remainder shifted to varieties of English, the language of the people who had suppressed them.
options: ① social inequality in linguistic borrowing
② the natural evolution of language over time
③ benefits of multilingualism in global society
④ reasons for preserving endangered languages
⑤ dialects as a means of expressing cultural identity
explanation: 집단 간의 상호 작용은 종종 차별적이며, 이것이 언어의 차용(borrowing)이 한쪽(더 강력한 쪽에서 덜 강력한 쪽)으로 향한다는 점에서 반영된다는 글이므로 1번이 주제로 적절하다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Intuition can be great, but it ought to be hard-earned. question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We tend to overrate the impact of new technologies in part because older technologies have become absorbed into the furniture of our lives, so as to be almost invisible. question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially ⓐ<u>explained</u> by the Matthew effect. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further ⓑ<u>increase</u> her odds of scoring another win. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and ⓒ<u>consistently</u> succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented. Therefore, future success again goes to those ⓓ<u>who</u> have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits ⓔ<u>that</u> success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 절에서 'each of these payoffs'가 의미상 주어 역할을 하는 독립분사구문 자리입니다. 문맥상 주절 뒤에서 부가적인 상황을 설명하고 있으며, 접속사 없이 문장이 이어지고 있으므로 동사 increase를 현재분사인 increasing으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

question: 20. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?

question: 21. 다음 글의 흠름으로 밴아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 22. 다음 글의 흠름으로 밴아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 23. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Commitment is the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life. Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby facilitating the planning and coordination of joint actions. Moreover, commitments make people willing to perform actions that they would not otherwise perform.
ordered_passages: (A) Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.

(B) For example, a taxi driver transports his clients to their desired destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a credible commitment to pay her.

(C) More specifically, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents is committed to taking various measures to sustain the currency in question.
explanation: 주어진 글은 약셍(Commitment)이 사회 생활을 유지하게 한다는 제시문입니다. (B)에서 택시 기사와 건설 노동자의 구체적인 예시를 들고, (C)에서 'More specifically'를 통해 그들이 돈을 받는 이유(통화 유지에 대한 약셍)를 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 'Thus'를 통해 이러한 약셍의 신뢰성이 서회 제도의 기원이 됨을 결론 집니다.

question: 24. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is a common assumption that most vagrant birds are ultimately doomed, aside from the rare cases where individuals are able to reorientate and return to their normal ranges.
ordered_passages: (A) However, there are many lines of evidence to suggest that vagrancy can, on rare occasions, dramatically alter the fate of populations, species or even whole ecosystems. Despite being infrequent, these events can be extremely important when viewed at the timescales over which ecological and evolutionary processes unfold.(B) In turn, it is also commonly assumed that vagrancy itself is a relatively unimportant biological phenomenon. This is undoubtedly true for the majority of cases, as the most likely outcome of any given vagrancy event is that the individual will fail to find enough resources, and/or be exposed to inhospitable environmental conditions, and perish.(C) The most profound consequences of vagrancy relate to the establishment of new breeding sites, new migration routes and wintering locations. Each of these can occur through different mechanisms, and at different frequencies, and they each have their own unique importance.
explanation: 이 글은 길 잃은 새(vagrant birds)에 대한 일반적인 가설과 그 중요성을 다루고 있습니다. 주어진 문장에서 길 잃은 새들이 결국 죽게 된다는 일반적인 가정을 언급한 후, (B)에서 그 연장선으로 이러한 현상이 생물학적으로 중요하지 않다는 일반적인 가정을 덧붙입니다. 하지만 (A)에서 'However'를 사용하여 이러한 현상이 드물지만 인구, 종, 또는 생태계의 운명을 바꿀 수 있는 중요한 사건이 될 수 있음을 시사합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 이러한 중요성의 구체적인 예시(새로운 번식지, 이동 경로, 월동지 형성 등)를 설명하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 25. 다음 글의 흐름에 어울리는 문장이 되도록 <조건>에 맞게 빈칸을 영어로 서술하시오.
passage: Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested, that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. Revolutionaries have always looked to the past to frame their future cause, as is amply illustrated by examples from nationalism to communism. The future has often been seen as variously a recovery of a lost time, as a replication of what is established, or as a model bequeathed by a heroic age long gone. The writing of history is based on understanding or explaining future outcomes that were not known to contemporaries, since the historian has the benefit of hindsight and the past is nothing more than the accumulation of futures that are now our past. So, rather than see the hand of the past always shaping the future, _____________________________________ in the sense of our understanding of it.
subjective_conditions: 17~18개의 단어를 사용하여 주어와 동사가 들어간 완전한 문장으로 서술하시오.
it을 주어로 사용하시오.
being, by, can, our orientation to, seen, with, in reverse를 반드시 사용하시오.
(중복사용 불가능, 어형 변형 불가능)
answer: it can be seen in reverse with the past being shaped by our orientation to the future
explanation: 이 글은 과거가 미래를 결정한다는 통념과 달리, 우리의 미래에 대한 관점이나 지향점이 과거를 이해하고 재구성하는 방식에 영향을 미친다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 마지막 문장은 '과거가 미래를 형성하는 것이 아니라 그 반대 상황(미래에 대한 우리의 지향에 의해 과거가 형성되는 것)으로 보일 수 있다'는 결론을 도출해야 합니다. 조건에 따라 'it can be seen in reverse(그것은 거꾸로 보일 수 있다)'와 부대상황을 나타내는 'with + 목적어 + 분사' 구문인 'with the past being shaped by our orientation to the future(우리의 미래에 대한 지향에 의해 과거가 형성되면서)'를 조합하여 문장을 완성합니다.

question: 26. 다음 글의 요지를 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 서술하시오.
passage: Too many times people, especially in today's generation, expect things to just happen overnight. When we have these false expectations, it tends to discourage us from continuing to move forward. Because this is a high tech society, everything we want has to be within the parameters of our comfort and convenience. If it doesn't happen fast enough, we're tempted to lose interest. So many people don't want to take the time it requires to be successful. Success is not a matter of mere desire; you should develop patience in order to achieve it. Have you fallen prey to impatience? Great things take time to build.
subjective_conditions: 6~10개의 단어를 사용하여 주어와 동사가 들어간 완전한 문장으로 서술하시오.
We를 주어로 사용하시오.
success를 반드시 사용하시오.
(중복 사용 불가능, 어형 변형 가능)
answer: We should develop patience in order to achieve success.
explanation: 이 글은 현대인들이 빠른 결과만을 기대하며 성공에 필요한 시간을 견디지 못하는 경향을 비판하며, 진정한 성공을 위해서는 인내심을 길러야 한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 요지는 '성공을 거두기 위해 인내심을 가져야 한다'는 내용이 되어야 합니다. 조건에 맞춰 'We'를 주어로 하고 'success'를 포함하여 'We should develop patience to achieve success' 또는 'We need patience to achieve success'와 같은 문장으로 작성할 수 있습니다.

question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. question: 5. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법상 옳은 것은? [2.8점]
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
