question: 15. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden functions as a miniature ecosystem that the gardner strives to maintain in a particular condition, with the goal of maximizing the output of fruits and vegetables. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem; they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
options: ① The maximization of vegetable growth leads to ecological instability.
② Growers actively intervene by eliminating weeds and applying insecticides to protect their crops.
③ The grower must refrain from amy interference in the ecosystem, allowing the vegetables to grow even better.
④ Once the grower ceases intervention, the ecosystem of the small patch naturally transitions toward a more stable condition.
⑤ In the absence of the grower's intervention, weeds might take over the garden, and wildlife may feed on the crops, resulting in reduced harvests.
explanation: 3번은 '재배자가 환경 생태계 개입을 삼가면 야채가 훨씬 잘 자랄 수 있다'고 말하고 있으나, 본문 마지막 문장에서 수확량은 결국 낮아진다(yield will almost certainly be lower)고 하므로 일치하지 않는다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be scarcely considered ⓐ<u>biased</u>. All experts are not the same, nor do they submit their work to the same scrutiny. ⓑ<u>Perceiving</u> the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims. For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were in part under the ⓒ<u>patronage</u> of the sugar industry. The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared. Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have fostered higher use of sugar, now widely ⓓ<u>implicated</u> as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. Stories such as this one fuel suspicion ─ but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. Funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since been made ⓔ<u>prerequisite</u>.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 문맥상 과학적 연구가 완벽하게 객관적이지 않을 수 있음을 시사하는 내용이므로, 전문적 기준이나 동료 검토 과정에도 불구하고 과학의 수행이 '편향되지 않았다고(biased)' 간주될 수 '거의 없다(scarcely)'는 논리는 어색합니다. 문맥상 과학의 수행이 결코 '객관적(objective)'이라고만 볼 수는 없다는 의미가 되어야 하므로 ⓐ의 biased는 objective와 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 '거의 객관적이라고 볼 수 없다(scarcely considered objective)'는 흐름이 자연스러워집니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.3점]
passage: If the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other? (A) This is because the brain has something of a two-tier memory system at work when it comes to retrieving memories, and this gives rise to a common yet infuriating sensation: recognising someone, but not being able to remember how or why, or what their name is. (B) To clarify, familiarity (or recognition) is when you encounter someone or something and you know you've done so before. (C) But beyond that, you've got nothing; all you can say is this person/thing is already in your memories. (D) Recall is when you can access the original memory of how and why you know this person; recognition is just flagging up the fact that the memory exists. (E)
insertion_sentence: This happens because the brain differentiates between familiarity and recall.
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'This'는 앞 문장에서 언급한 '누군가를 알아보지만 이름이나 이유를 기억하지 못하는 현상'을 가리킵니다. (B) 위치에 이 문장이 들어가면, 뇌가 '친숙함(familiarity)'과 '회상(recall)'을 구분하기 때문에 이런 일이 발생한다고 원인을 설명하게 되고, 그 뒤인 (B) 이후 문장들에서 '친숙함'과 '회상'의 개념을 구체적으로 설명(To clarify)하는 구조가 되어 논리적 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Ms. Blake walked along the edge of the soccer field, watching Eva practicing alone She noticed that Eva's movements were slow and that her focus seemed elsewhere. Ms. Blake asked, "Do you remember the final game last year?" "Yeah, I remember. I was quite good back then." "You still are," replied Ms. Blake. "Well, now I'm so worried I can't score a goal or even pass the ball properly. I'm afraid of making mistakes," said Eva. Ms. Blake suggested, "You don't have to be perfect. Soccer isn't about perfection ─ ________________________. And you've always had plenty of that. The way you play, the energy you bring ─ that's what makes you special. Not the goals scored or the trophies won. It's the love you have for the game." Eva nodded thoughtfully and there was a new confidence in her mind that hadn't been there before.
options: ① teamwork is important
② what matters is your passion
③ it's about winning in the end
④ trophies are the driving force
⑤ it depends on creative strategies
explanation: 이 글은 축구 연습 중 자신감을 잃은 에바에게 블레이크 선생님이 완벽함이 중요한 것이 아니라 경기에 대한 열정과 사랑이 중요하다고 조언하는 내용입니다. 빈칸 바로 뒤 문장에서 "And you've always had plenty of that"(그리고 너는 항상 그것을 많이 가지고 있었다)라고 언급하며, 이어서 경기를 대하는 방식, 에너지, 경기에 대한 사랑을 강조하고 있으므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은 '열정이 중요하다'는 의미인 ②번입니다.
options_translation: ① 팀워크가 중요하다
② 중요한 것은 당신의 열정이다
③ 결국 승리하는 것에 관한 것이다
④ 트로피가 원동력이다
⑤ 그것은 창의적인 전략에 달려 있다

question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Fans who are inclined to spend a lot of time thinking about what athletes owe them as fans should also think about ________________________ that fans might have as fans. One who thinks only about what they are entitled to receive from their friends without ever giving a moment's thought to what they owe their friends is, to put it mildly, not a very good friend. Similarly, fans who only think about what athletes owe them without ever thinking about what they owe to athletes have failed to take the fan/athlete relationship all that seriously. As in nearly every other area of human life, whatever special rights fans may possess are limited by a corresponding set of obligations, and fans who never think about how they can be better fans even as they confidently opine about what athletes owe them are hardly fulfilling their end of the bargain.
options: ① the indispensable criticism
② the reciprocal obligations
③ the critical points of view
④ the corresponding rights
⑤ the correlative hostility
explanation: 이 글은 팬과 운동선수의 관계를 친구 관계에 비유하며, 팬들이 선수들에게 무언가를 기대할 권리(rights)만큼이나 선수들에게 가져야 할 상호적인 의무(obligations)도 중요하다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 빈칸은 팬들이 선수들에게 무엇을 빚지고 있는지, 즉 팬으로서 가져야 할 '상호적인 의무'를 생각해야 한다는 맥락이 되어야 하므로 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 없어서는 안 될 비판
② 상호적인 의무
③ 비판적인 관점
④ 상응하는 권리
⑤ 상관관계가 있는 적대감

question: 30. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Commitment is the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life. Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby facilitating the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. Moreover, commitments make people willing to perform actions that they would not otherwise perform. For example, a taxi driver picks up his clients and transports them to their desired destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a credible commitment to pay her at the end of the month. Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to taking various measures to sustain the currency in question. Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.↓Commitment is central to human social life, enabling (A)__________ in behavior and motivating individuals to act cooperatively and sustain social systems through shared (B)__________.
options: ① predictability / trust
② creativity / credibility
③ creativity / morality
④ efficacy / personality
⑤ efficacy / tradition
explanation: 약속은 인간의 사회 생활에서 개인의 행동을 예측 가능하게 만들고(predictable -> predictability), 약속의 신뢰성(credibility -> trust)을 바탕으로 সামাজিক 제도의 안정과 유지를 가능하게 한다.

question: 31. 다음 글은 'stress'에 관해 의사와 환자가 토론을 한 대화문이다. 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 완성하시오.
passage: Stress affects not only physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain. A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol "on" instead of "off," which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.Patient: I've heard stress is bad for your health, but can it actually change the brain?Doctor: Yes, especially chronic stress. It affects a part of the brain called the hippocampus.Patient: The hippocampus? What does that do?Doctor: It helps (A)________________________________Patient: Wow, it does a lot more than I expected.Doctor: Exactly. It also helps balance the autonomic nervous system, especially the sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves.
subjective_answer_format: It helps regulate your mood, builds stress resilience, decides whether the environment is safe, and stores threatening experiences as long-term memories.
answer: (It helps) regulate your mood, builds stress resilience, decides whether the environment is safe, and stores threatening experiences as long-term memories.
explanation: 해마의 역할을 본문에서 찾아 조건에 맞게 요약하는 서술형.

question: 3. 다음 밑줄 친 the flavor of food is taking a back seat이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that <u>the flavor of food is taking a back seat</u>. I suspect that most people view flavor as of secondary importance in social settings where food is served. Although our social gatherings coalesce around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, do not depend on the quality of sensations provided by the food. To focus excessively on flavor is to miss the larger significance of these social relations.
options: ① food testings play a major role in event planning because they help ensure a successful event
② the flavor provided by the food does not play a significant role in social relations
③ the flavor of food is not something we actually sense, but is created in our brain
④ the flavor of food is an important quality attribute driving consumers' choice
⑤ the role of food flavor includes bringing together communities and individuals
explanation: 글의 핵심 내용은 음식과 관련된 사교적 모임에서 '맛(flavor)' 자체보다는 그 모임의 '사회적 차원(social dimension)'이 더 중요하다는 것입니다. 밑줄 친 표현 'taking a back seat(뒷전으로 밀려나다)'은 맛이 사회적 관계나 모임의 의미 형성에 있어 부차적인 요소가 되었음을 의미합니다. 따라서 ②번 '음식에 의해 제공되는 맛은 사회적 관계에서 중요한 역할을 하지 않는다'가 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 음식 시식은 성공적인 행사를 보장하는 데 도움이 되기 때문에 행사 계획에서 중요한 역할을 한다
② 음식에 의해 제공되는 맛은 사회적 관계에서 중요한 역할을 하지 않는다
③ 음식의 맛은 우리가 실제로 느끼는 것이 아니라 뇌에서 만들어지는 것이다
④ 음식의 맛은 소비자의 선택을 이끄는 중요한 품질 속성이다
⑤ 음식 맛의 역할은 공동체와 개인을 하나로 묶는 것을 포함한다

question: 4. 다음 밑줄 친 Don't fall prey to impatience가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Too many times people, especially in today's generation, expect things to just happen overnight. When we have these false expectations, it tends to discourage us from continuing to move forward. Because this is a high tech society, everything we want has to be within the parameters of our comfort and convenience. If it doesn't happen fast enough, we're tempted to lose interest. So many people don't want to take the time it requires to be successful. Success is not a matter of mere desire; you should develop patience in order to achieve it. <u>Don't fall prey to impatience</u>.
options: ① Be patient and don't give up too soon.
② Let your impatience drive you toward success.
③ Achieve success through honesty and sincerity.
④ Keep your motivation strong, even when plans fall apart.
⑤ Recognize the crucial role of technology in achieving success.
explanation: 이 글은 오늘날의 사람들이 즉각적인 결과를 기대하지만, 성공을 위해서는 시간과 인내가 필수적임을 강조하고 있습니다. 밑줄 친 'Don't fall prey to impatience(조급함의 희생양이 되지 마라)'는 조급함 때문에 쉽게 포기하거나 흥미를 잃지 말고 인내심을 가져야 한다는 의미입니다. 따라서 ①번 '인내심을 갖고 너무 빨리 포기하지 마라'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인내심을 갖고 너무 빨리 포기하지 마라.
② 조급함이 당신을 성공으로 이끌게 하라.
③ 정직과 성실을 통해 성공을 달성하라.
④ 계획이 무너질 때도 동기부여를 강하게 유지하라.
⑤ 성공을 달성하는 데 있어 기술의 결정적인 역할을 인식하라.

question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Emotion socialization ─ learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them ─ starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may intrude on adolescents' autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.
options: ① significant gender differences in adolescent emotion regulation difficulties
② the parental influence on children's emotion regulation across development
③ the effect of nonjudgmental acceptance on children's moral development
④ underlying psychological causes of emotional crises during adolescence
⑤ the impact of children's emotional and behavioral changes on parenting styles
explanation: 발달 과정 전반에 걸쳐 자녀의 감정 조절에 미치는 부모의 역할 및 영향력에 관한 글이므로 2번이 주제로 적절하다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: For years, many psychologists have held strongly to the belief that the key to addressing negative health habits is to change behavior. This, more than values and attitudes, is the part of personality that is easiest to change. Ingestive habits such as smoking, drinking and various eating behaviors are the most common health concerns targeted for behavioral changes. Process-addiction behaviors (workaholism, shopaholism, and the like) fall into this category as well. Mental imagery combined with power of suggestion was taken up as the premise of behavioral medicine to help people change negative health behaviors into positive ones. Although this technique alone will not produce changes, when used alongside other behavior modification tactics and coping strategies, behavioral changes have proved effective for some people. What mental imagery does is reinforce a new desired behavior. Repeated use of images reinforces the desired behavior more strongly over time.
options: ① Emotional Interventions for Managing Compulsive Disorders
② Behavior Improvement through Strategies like Mental Imagery
③ Ingestive Habits vs. Process-addiction Behaviors: Which is Worse?
④ The Role of Social Pressure in Unhealthy Behavioral Choices
⑤ Understanding Psychological Triggers Behind Harmful Habits
explanation: 부정적인 건강 습관을 고치기 위해 심상(Mental Imagery) 같은 전략을 통한 행동 개선에 대해 설명하고 있으므로 2번이 제목으로 가장 적절하다.

question: 9. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
options: ① The Less You Move, The Better
② An Efficient Error Correcting Mechanism
③ The Importance of Thinking Before Acting
④ Thinking with Gesture: A Gesture Foreshadowing
⑤ How Gestures Hinder the Language Development of Late Talkers
explanation: 제스처가 생각보다 먼저 일어나고 뇌의 사고 과정을 돕는다는 내용이므로 생각의 전조(Foreshadowing) 역할을 한다는 4번이 알맞다.

question: 10. 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: The graph above illustrates the average daily amount of animal protein consumed per person in three countries - the U.S., Brazil, and Japan - in 2020, categorized into four types: Poultry, Meat, Eggs and Dairy, and Fish and Seafood. ⓐAmong the three countries, the U.S. recorded the highest daily consumption of animal protein per person, with a total of 74.8g. ⓑAll three countries showed a greater consumption of Poultry than Meat, indicating a shared tendency toward preferring Poultry over red meat. ⓒIn Brazil, Meat was the leading source of animal protein at 18.0g per person per day, slightly higher than both Eggs and Dairy. ⓓUnlike the U.S. and Brazil, Japan consumed significantly more Fish and Seafood than any other type of animal protein, making it the most consumed category in that country. ⓔMeanwhile, Japan had less than 50g of the total animal protein consumption per person, which was the smallest among the three countries.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 원본 도표를 보아야 정확히 알 수 있으나, 보통 '모든 세 국가가 육류보다 가금류 소비가 많다'가 틀리게 출제된다. 여기서는 ⓒ에서 '브라질은 고기(Meat)가 주요 공급원이었다'고 했으므로 ⓑ에서 모든 국가가 가금류를 더 많이 소비했다는 문장은 브라질의 경우에 모순되어 틀리다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: We are the only species that ①<u>seasons</u> its food, deliberately altering it with the highly flavored plant parts we call herbs and spices. It's quite possible ②<u>that</u> our taste for spices has an evolutionary root. Many spices have antibacterial properties ─ in fact, common seasonings such as garlic, onion, and oregano inhibit the growth of almost every bacterium ③<u>testing</u>. And the cultures that make the heaviest use of spices ─ think of the garlic and black pepper of Thai food, the ginger and coriander of India, the chili peppers of Mexico ─ come from warmer climates, ④<u>where</u> bacterial spoilage is a bigger issue. In contrast, the most lightly spiced cuisines ─ those of Scandinavia and northern Europe ─ are from cooler climates. Our ⑤<u>uniquely</u> human attention to flavor, in this case the flavor of spices, turns out to have arisen as a matter of life and death.
explanation: ③번이 포함된 문장에서 수식을 받는 명사인 'bacterium(박테리아)'은 스스로 무언가를 테스트하는 주체가 아니라, 실험 과정에서 테스트되는 '대상'이다. 따라서 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 'testing'을 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 'tested'로 고쳐야 한다. 분사구의 수식을 받는 'almost every bacterium (that was) tested(테스트된 거의 모든 박테리아)'의 구조가 되어야 문맥상 적절하다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the ①<u>maximization</u> of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always ②<u>intervening</u> in the dynamics of the ecosystem; they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently ③<u>balanced</u> state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower ④<u>stops</u> intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be ⑤<u>lower</u> as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
explanation: 채소의 성장을 극대화하려는 상태는 생태계에게 있어 본질적으로 '봨균형적인(unbalanced)' 상태입니다. 이를 유지하기 위해 경작자가 계속 개입해야 한다는 내용이 뒤에 따라오므로 balanced는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other? This is because the brain has something of a two-tier memory system at work when it comes to retrieving memories, and this gives rise to a common yet infuriating sensation: recognising someone, but not being able to remember how or why, or what their name is. This happens because ______________________________________. To clarify, familiarity (or recognition) is when you encounter someone or something and you know you've done so before. But beyond that, you've got nothing; all you can say is this person/thing is already in your memories. Recall is when you can access the original memory of how and why you know this person; recognition is just flagging up the fact that the memory exists.
options: ① the brain differentiates between familiarity and recall
② cues help retrieve information stored in different systems
③ we often mistake an unknown person for a familiar person
④ the brain is receiving confused signals from different senses
⑤ we expect that the wording is correct at the first occurrence
explanation: 글은 뇌가 친숙함(인식)겼 회상(기억 인출)을 구분하여 찘리한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 친숙함은 기억이 존재한다는 사실만을 알리고, 회상은 구체적인 내용에 접근하는 것이므로 뇌가 이 둀 가지를 구별한다는 ①이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌가 친숙함겼 회상을 구분하기 때문에

③ 우리가 종종 모르는 사람을 친숙한 사람으로 오해하기 때문에
④ 뇌가 서로 다른 감각으로부터 혼란수러운 신호를 받고 있기 때문에

question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested, that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. ⓐRevolutionaries have always looked to the past to frame their future cause, as is amply illustrated by examples from nationalism to communism. ⓑThe future has often been seen as variously a recovery of a lost time, as a replication of what is established, or as a model bequeathed by a heroic age long gone. ⓒThe writing of history is based on understanding or explaining future outcomes that were not known to contemporaries, since the historian has the benefit of hindsight and the past is nothing more than the accumulation of futures that are now our past. ⓓSince the past is already gone and the future is not yet here, there's only one moment for us to live, and that is the present moment. ⓔSo, rather than see the hand of the past always shaping the future, perhaps it can be seen in reverse, with the past ─ in the sense of our understanding of it ─ being shaped by our orientation to the future.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 전체 글의 흐름은 과거와 미래의 상호 영향력, 특히 우리가 미래를 바라보는 관점에 따라 과거에 대한 이해가 형성된다는 내용입니다. 하지만 ④번 문장(ⓓ)은 과거와 미래는 존재하지 않고 현재만이 살아가야 할 유일한 순간이라는 '현재의 중요성'을 역설하고 있으므로 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. (A) For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were funded in part by the sugar industry. (B) The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared. (C) Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have fostered higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. (D) Stories such as this one fuel suspicion ─ but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. (E) Funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since been made compulsory.
insertion_sentence: Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 제시된 문장은 과학적 주장을 평가할 때 '자금 지원의 출처'를 아는 것이 중요하다는 일반적 진술입니다. (A) 뒤의 내용은 하버드 연구원들이 설탕 산업계로부터 자금을 지원받아 설탕의 유해성을 은폐하고 지방에 책임을 전가했다는 구체적인 사례를 소개하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A) 자리에 일반적 원칙을 먼저 제시하는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In order to bring the ever-increasing costs of home care for elderly and needy persons under control, managers of home care providers have introduced management systems. These systems specify tasks of home care workers and the time and budget available to perform these tasks. Electronic reporting systems require home care workers to report on their activities and the time spent, thus making the distribution of time and money visible and, in the perception of managers, controllable. This, in the view of managers, has contributed to the resolution of the problem. The home care workers, on the other hand, may perceive their work not as a set of separate tasks to be performed as efficiently as possible, but as a service to be provided to a client with whom they may have developed a relationship. This includes having conversations with clients and enquiring about the person's well-being. Restricted time and the requirement to report may be perceived as obstacles that make it impossible to deliver the service that is needed. If the management systems are too rigid, this may result in home care workers becoming overloaded and demotivated.
summary_sentence: Despite their aim to enhance efficiency and manage expenses, inflexible management systems in home care services can actually (A)____________ care workers and (B)____________ the quality of service they give.
options: ① encourage ...... improve
② frustrate ...... reduce
③ motivate ...... enhance
④ restrict ...... standardize
⑤ replace ...... monitor

options_translation: ① 격려하다 ...... 개선하다

④ 제한하다 ...... 표준화하다

question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: For years, many psychologists have held strongly to the belief that the key to addressing negative health habits is to change behavior. This, more than values and attitudes, is the part of personality that is easiest to change. Ingestive habits such as smoking, drinking and various eating behaviors are the most common health concerns targeted for behavioral changes. Process-addiction behaviors (workaholism, shopaholism, and so forth) fall into this category as well. Mental' imagery combined with power of suggestion was taken up as the premise of behavioral medicine to help people change negative health behaviors into positive ones. Although this technique alone will not produce changes, when used alongside other behavior modification tactics and coping strategies, behavioral changes have proved effective for some people. What mental imagery does is reinforce a new desired behavior. Repeated use of images reinforces the desired behavior more strongly over time.
options: ① Healthy habits naturally develop through a proper diet and regular exercise.
② Mental imagery alone can fundamentally solve the root causes of health problems.
③ Repeating positive images can replace negative emotions and reduce stress.
④ Process addictions are difficult to treat, so prevention should be the main priority.
⑤ Behavior change, supported by mental imagery, improves negative health habits.

question: 2. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 the corresponding obligations가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Fans who are inclined to spend a lot of time thinking about what athletes owe them as fans should also think about <u>the corresponding obligations</u> that fans might have as fans. One who thinks only about what they are entitled to receive from their friends without ever giving a moment's thought to what they owe their friends is, to put it mildly, not a very good friend. Similarly, fans who only think about what athletes owe them without ever thinking about what they owe to athletes have failed to take the fan/athlete relationship all that seriously. As in nearly every other area of human life, whatever special rights fans may possess are limited by a corresponding set of obligations, and fans who never think about how they can be better fans even as they confidently opine about what athletes owe them are hardly fulfilling their end of the bargain.

question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports.
options: ① Closing Borders to Secure Our Plates
② How Climate Shapes Agricultural Trade
③ Achieving Food Security Through Production and Imports
④ Import Dependency : A Threat to National Control over Food
⑤ The Illusion of Food Self-Sufficiency in Developed Countries

question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested, that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In 1900, at the close of the first decade in which electric systems had become a practical alternative for manufacturers, less than 5 percent of the power used in factories came from electricity.(A) But one thing didn't change. Designed to supply lighting to local homes and shops, the central stations had neither the size nor the skill to serve the needs of big factories. And the factory owners, having always supplied their own power, were loath to assign such a critical function to an outsider.(B) But the technological advances of suppliers made electric systems and electric motors ever more affordable and reliable, and the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology. Further accelerating the shift was the rapid expansion in the number of skilled electrical engineers, who provided the expertise needed to install and run the new systems. In short order, electric power had gone from exotic to commonplace.(C) They knew that a glitch in power supply would bring their operations to a halt ─ and that a lot of glitches might well mean bankruptcy. As the new century began, a survey found that there were already 50,000 private electric plants in operation, far surpassing the 3,600 central stations.
explanation: 1900년에 처음에는 공장에서 전기 사용이 5% 미만이었다는 제시문에 이어, 공급자의 기술 발전과 마케팅 등으로 전기 채택 속도가 빨라져 전기가 흔해졌다는 (B)가 온다. 이어 (B)의 확산에도 불구하고 바뀌지 않은 하나(But one thing didn't change)로 공장들이 중앙 발전소가 아닌 자체 발전소를 짓기를 고집했다는 (A)가 오며, 마지막으로 공장주들(They)이 자체 발전소를 짓는 이유(정전 위협 등)와 그에 따른 프라이빗 발전소 통계 수치를 보여주는 (C)로 마무리 됨이 적절하다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It's untrue that teens can focus on two things at once ─ what they're doing is shifting their attention from one task to another. question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고, 주제를 완성하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 단어를 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오.
passage: Quite often the interaction between groups is socially unequal, and this is reflected in the fact that in many cases borrowing of words or constructions goes mostly or entirely in one direction, from the more powerful or prestigious group to the less favored one. In some cases, as with the Dharug language of Sydney, Australia, the source of some of the earliest loans from Indigenous Australian languages into English, the fate of the language system is extinction after the obliteration of many of its speakers. subjective_conditions: 1. (A), (B) 각각 한 단어로 작성할 것

explanation: 본문은 사회적으로 불평등한 집단 간의 상호작용에서 단어의 차용이 주로 더 강력한 집단에서 열세인 집단으로 한 방향으로 일어나며, 열세인 집단의 언어가 억압받거나 결국 소멸되는 현상을 다루고 있습니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 사회적 집단을 수식하므로 '지배적인(dominant)'이 적절하고, (B)는 소수 언어의 상태를 나타내므로 '사라짐/소멸(disappearance)'이 적절합니다. 제시된 단어 'dominate'와 'disappear'를 문맥에 맞게 어형 변화하여 작성합니다. (참고: (B)에 'extinction'의 의미로 'extinguishing' 등을 고려할 수 있으나 문맥상 'disappearance'가 가장 자연스럽습니다.)

question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오. [3.0점]
passage: Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition. subjective_conditions: 1. (A), (B) 각각 한 단어로 작성할 것

question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸에 들어갈 내용을 <조건>에 맞게 작성하시오. [4.0점]
passage: Since their start in the early 1950s U.S. television sitcoms have charted many of the social conflicts in U.S. society: civil rights, women's rights in the home and in the workplace, children's rights, immigration and multiculturalism, as well as evolving conceptions of the family. options: ① depicting everyday life with wit and meaning
② expanding support for the socially disadvantaged

⑤ offering emotional support to the elderly facing communication struggles

question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If you had wanted to create a "self-driving" car in the 1950s. your best option might have been to strap a brick to the accelerator. Yes, the vehicle would have been able to move forward on its own, but it could not slow down, stop, or turn to avoid barriers. Obviously not ideal.
ordered_passages: (A) Two decades ago, we were still taping bricks to accelerators. Today, we are approaching the point where we can begin to bring some appropriate technology to bear in ways that advance our understanding of patients as unique individuals.

(B) Does that mean self-driving cars weren't worth pursuing? Not at all ─ we just lacked the tools to make them safe and autonomous. This once-distant dream now seems within our reach. The same goes for medicine.

(C) In fact, many patients are already wearing devices that monitor their conditions in real time, which allows doctors to talk to their patients in a specific, refined, and feedback-driven way that was not even possible a decade ago.
explanation: 주어진 글은 1950년대 자율주행차 기술의 한계(가속기에 벽돌을 묶는 수준)를 설명합니다. (B)에서 그렇다고 자율주행차를 추구할 가치가 없었느냐는 질문과 함께, 과거엔 도구가 부족했을 뿐이며 이제는 의학 분야도 마찬가지 상황임을 언급하며 화제를 전환합니다. (A)에서 20년 전 의학계의 상황을 자동차 예시에 빗대어 설명하고 현재의 발전을 언급한 뒤, (C)에서 환자들이 실시간 모니터링 기기를 사용하는 구체적인 사례를 제시하며 마무리하는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization.
ordered_passages: (A) The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?

(B) Many renowned scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win.

(C) Another compelling explanation, however, suggests that great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent.
explanation: 주어진 글은 위대한 과학자들이 여러 업적을 남긴다는 점을 뉴턴의 사례로 제시합니다. (B)에서 이러한 현상을 '마태 효과'로 설명할 수 있다며, 초기 성공이 가져다주는 여러 이점들이 다음 성공 가능성을 높인다는 내용을 기술합니다. (C)에서는 '그러나(however)'를 통해 다른 설명, 즉 성공의 원인이 환경적 이점이 아니라 과학자의 타고난 재능 때문이라는 관점을 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서 마태 효과를 정의하며 성공이 단순히 지위 때문인지 아니면 내재적 재능을 반영하는 것인지에 대한 근본적인 질문을 던지며 글을 맺습니다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: We tend to overrate the impact of new technologies in part because older technologies have become absorbed into the furniture of our lives, so as to be almost invisible. (A) Let's take the baby bottle as an example. (B) However it finds no place in our histories of technology. (C) This technology might be thought of as a classic time-shifting device, as it enables mothers to exercise more control over the timing of feeding. (D) It can also function to save time, as bottle feeding allows for someone else to substitute for the mother's time. (E) Possibly, therefore, it has huge implications for the management of time in everyday life, yet it is entirely overlooked in discussions of high-speed society.

② (B)

question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem; they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
summary_sentence: A home vegetable garden, as a small ecosystem, remains productive only when the grower continuously (A)____________ its ecological balance; otherwise, it returns to a more stable but less (B)____________ state.
options: ① neglects      fruitful
② controls      natural
③ adjusts      yielding
④ observes      efficient
⑤ intervenes      sustainable
explanation: 가정 채소밭은 재배자가 생태계 역학에 지속적으로 개입하고 조절(adjusts/controls)해야 생산성이 유지됩니다. 개입을 멈추면 더 안정적이지만 수확량(yield)은 더 적은 상태로 돌아가게 됩니다. 따라서 (A)에는 개입/조절을 의미하는 단어가, (B)에는 수확과 관련된 yielding이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 방치한다 - 결실이 있는
② 통제한다 - 자연스러운
③ 조정한다 - 수확이 많이 나는
④ 관찰한다 - 효율적인
⑤ 개입한다 - 지속 가능한

question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Technologists are always on the lookout for quantifiable metrics Measurable inputs to a model are their lifeblood, and like a social scientist, a technologist needs to identify concrete measures, or "proxies," for assessing progress. This need for calculable proxies produces a bias toward measuring things that are easy to quantify. But simple metrics can take us further away from the important goals we really care about, which may require complicated metrics or be extremely difficult, or perhaps impossible, to reduce to any measure. And when we have imperfect or bad proxies, we can easily fall under the illusion that we are solving for a good end without actually making genuine progress toward a worthy solution. The problem of proxies results in technologists frequently substituting what is measurable for what is meaningful. As the saying goes, "Not everything that counts can be counted, and not everything that can be counted counts."
summary_sentence: Technologists often rely on (A)____________ proxies to assess progress, but this can blur the line between data and (B)____________.
options: ① quantifiable      actual value
② calculable      perfect metrics
③ perfect      accurate numbers
④ measurable      accurate numbers
⑤ meaningful      actual value
explanation: 기술자들이 수량화하기 쉬운 지표에 의존하다 보니, 실제 가치(의미 있는 것)보다는 측정 가능한 것만 중요하게 여기게 된다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '수량화할 수 있는(quantifiable)', (B)에는 '실제 가치(actual value)'가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 수량화할 수 있는 - 실제 가치
② 계산할 수 있는 - 완벽한 지표
③ 완벽한 - 정확한 숫자

question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: Emotion socialization─learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them-starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example. their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may intrude on adolescents' autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional  crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.
summary_sentence: Parents play a vital role in children's (A)____________ by teaching emotion regulation, transitioning from direct guidance in childhood to fostering (B)____________ in adolescence.
subjective_conditions: • (A)는 2단어, (B)는 1단어로 작성할 것
• 지문에 있는 단어를 변형 없이 사용할 것
explanation: 이 글은 아동기에서 청소년기로 넘어감에 따라 부모의 감정 사회화 역할이 직접적인 지도에서 자율성을 존중하는 방식으로 변해야 함을 강조합니다. (A)에는 부모가 아이들의 '감정 사회화(emotion socialization)'에 중요한 역할을 한다는 내용이, (B)에는 청소년기에 부모가 촉진해야 할 '자율성(autonomy)'이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

question: 26. 다음 글의 요지를 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food is taking a back seat. I suspect that most people view flavor as of secondary importance in social settings where food is served. Although our social gatherings coalesce around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. According to this conventional wisdom, the ceremonies and rituals around food, the social events that supply food with its meaning, do not depend on the quality of sensations provided by the food. To focus excessively on flavor is to miss the larger significance of these social relations.
subjective_conditions: • flavor, social gatherings, function을 사용할 것 (형태 변형 가능)
• with+명사+분사 형태를 사용할 것
• 15단어 이내의 문장으로 작성할 것
※ <조건> 위반, 철자 오류, 문법 오류 시 각각 1점 감점함.
answer: In social gathering, flavor of food functions secondarily, with food serving to support social relations. (혹은 Food functions to foster relations in social gatherings, with its flavor playing a secondary role.)
explanation: 이 글은 사회적 모임에서 음식의 맛은 부차적인 역할을 하며, 모임의 진정한 의미는 사회적 관계 형성에 있다는 요지를 담고 있습니다. 'with + 명사 + 분사' 구문을 사용하여 맛이 부차적인 역할을 하는 상황을 묘사하면서 요지를 작성합니다.

question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much a creative process. A conjecture is a philosophical invention, cooked up rather mystically by the mind through the mental computation we call careful contemplation. However, until the hypothesis is tested against reality, it is not yet truly knowledge; it is just information that represents speculation. Knowledge is information that has demonstrated its usefulness. It is what is left over after cycles of experimental testing have eliminated false theories. As scientists continually test their hypotheses and modify their models to account for new and surprising data, a kind of "learning loop" emerges that statisticians call Bayesian updating. Based on Bayes' Rule, developed by eighteenth-century English statistician and philosopher Thomas Bayes, Bayesian updating refers to a mathematical process whereby an accepted theory or predictive model gets increasingly accurate through the repetitive testing of competing variants of that theory.*conjecture: 추론 **contemplation: 숙고 ***speculation: 추측
options: ① Absolute Certainty of Scientific Knowledge
② Bayesian Logic: How Statistics Replace Scientific Theories
③ Scientific Discovery as an Immutable and Linear Evolution of Ideas
④ From Hypothesis to Certainty: The Role of Empirical Validation in Aesthetic Knowledge
⑤ Evolution of Knowledge: How Science Refines Truth Through Experimentation
explanation: 이 글은 과학이 단순한 규칙의 적용이 아니라 창의적인 추론과 가설 검증을 통해 지식을 정교화해 나가는 과정임을 설명합니다. 특히 '베이지안 업데이트'라는 개념을 통해 실험을 반복하며 이론이 점점 더 정확해지는 과정을 묘사하고 있으므로, 실험을 통해 진리를 정제해 나가는 지식의 진화를 다룬 5번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.

question: 2. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 조건을 지켜 빈칸을 완성하시오.
passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, ______________________________________ because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports.
subjective_conditions: 1. 글의 흐름에 맞게 영어로 작성할 것
2. 다음 어휘를 한 번씩 사용할 것 'food security' / 'food self-sufficiency'
answer: food security does not require food self-sufficiency
explanation: 글의 흐름상 국가들은 국내에서 생산하기 어려운 식품을 수입함으로써 식량 공급 문제를 해결할 수 있다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 식량 안보(food security)를 달성하는 것이 반드시 모든 식량을 자국 내에서 해결하는 식량 자급자족(food self-sufficiency)을 의미하지는 않는다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: In 1900, at the close of the first decade in which electric systems had become a practical alternative for manufacturers, less than 5 percent of the power used in factories came from electricity. But the technological advances of suppliers made electric systems and electric motors ever more affordable and reliable, and the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology. Further accelerating the shift was the rapid expansion in the number of skilled electrical engineers, who provided the expertise needed to install and run the new systems. In short order, electric power had gone from exotic to commonplace.But one thing didn't change. Factories continued to build their own power-supply systems on their own premises. Few manufacturers considered buying electricity from the small central stations. Designed to supply lighting to local homes and shops, the central stations had neither the size nor the skill to serve the needs of big factories. And the factory owners, having always supplied their own power, were loathe to assign such a critical function to an outsider. They knew that a glitch in power supply would bring their operations to a halt - and that a lot of glitches might well mean bankruptcy. As the new century began, a survey found that there were already 50,000 private electric plants in operation, far surpassing the 3,600 central stations.*premises: (공장) 부지 **glitch: (작은) 결함
summary_sentence: Despite the increasing affordability and (A)____________ of electric power enabled by technological progress and a growing pool of skilled engineers, most manufacturers remained (B)____________ to give up control over power generation to central stations, opting instead to maintain their own on-site systems.
options: ① (A) proliferation / (B) reluctant
② (A) surge / (B) eager
③ (A) scarcity / (B) unwilling
④ (A) reduction / (B) hesitant
⑤ (A) escalation / (B) enthusiastic
explanation: 이 글은 1900년대 초반 전력 시스템이 보편화되었음에도 불구하고, 공장주들이 외부 중앙 발전소로부터 전기를 구매하기보다는 자체 전력 공급 시스템을 유지하려 했던 경향을 설명하고 있습니다. 기술 발전과 숙련된 엔지니어의 증가로 전력이 저렴해지고 확산(proliferation)되었음에도 불구하고, 공장주들은 전력 공급의 작은 결함이 사업 중단이나 파산으로 이어질 것을 우려하여 외부인에게 그 통제권을 넘기기를 꺼려(reluctant)했다는 내용이 요약문에 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 확산 / (B) 꺼리는
② (A) 급증 / (B) 열망하는
③ (A) 희귀성 / (B) 내키지 않는
④ (A) 감소 / (B) 망설이는
⑤ (A) 확대 / (B) 열광적인

question: 16. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested, that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. Revolutionaries have always looked to the past to frame their future cause, as is amply illustrated by examples from nationalism to communism. The future has often been seen as variously a recovery of a lost time, as a replication of what is established, or as a model bequeathed by a heroic age long gone. The writing of history is based on understanding or explaining future outcomes that were not known to contemporaries, since the historian has the benefit of hindsight and the past is nothing more than the accumulation of futures that are now our past. So, rather than see the hand of the past always shaping the future, perhaps it can be seen in reverse, with the past - in the sense of our understanding of it - being shaped by our orientation to the future.
options: ① 역사는 동시대인의 시각에서 쓰일 때 가장 진실에 가깝다.

question: 24. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 5. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much a creative process. explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 절에서 주격 관계대명사 that 뒤의 동사는 문맥상 '건강한 식단과 연관된 이점'을 의미하므로 수동태인 'are associated'로 쓰이거나, 분사구문/형용사구 형태로 쓰여야 합니다. 여기서는 문장의 본동사 display 뒤에 연결되는 관계사절이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 be associated with 형태가 되어야 합니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Electric communication is mainly known in fish. The electric signals are produced in special electric organs. When the signal is discharged the electric organ will be negatively loaded compared to the head and an electric field is created around the fish. A weak electric current is created also in ordinary muscle cells when they contract. In the electric organ the muscle cells are connected in larger chunks, which makes the total current intensity larger than in ordinary muscles. The fish varies the signals by changing the form of the electric field or the frequency of discharging. The system is only working over small distances, about one to two meters. This is an advantage since the species using the signal system often live in large groups with several other species. If many fish send out signals at the same time, the short range decreases the risk of interference.
options: ① 특별한 전기 기관에서 방출된 전기 신호로 인해 전기 기관은 음전하를 띠게 되고 물고기 주위에 전기장을 형성한다.
② 일반적 근육 세포가 수축할 때 발생한 약한 전류는 이 근육 세포가 더 큰 덩어리로 연결되면서 그 강도가 증가한다.
③ 전기장의 형태 혹은 방출 주파수를 바꿈으로써 물고기는 전기 신호를 다양하게 한다.
④ 흔히 큰 무리를 지어 다른 여러 종과 함께 사는 종들에게 짧은 거리에서만 작동하는 전기 신호 체계는 이점이 된다.
⑤ 짧은 거리에서만 작동하는 전기 신의 범위는 동시에 방출되는 많은 물고기의 신호 간 간섭의 위험을 줄여준다.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 일반 근육 세포가 아닌, '전기 기관(electric organ)' 내에서 근육 세포들이 큰 덩어리로 연결되어 있을 때 전류 강도가 일반 근육보다 커진다고 설명하고 있습니다. ②번 선지는 일반적 근육 세포 자체가 연결되어 강도가 증가한다고 하였으므로 일치하지 않습니다.

question: 15. 다음 글의 내용을 읽고 옳게 이해한 것만을 <보기>에서 고른 것은?
passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. All experts are not the same, nor do they submit their work to the same scrutiny. Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims. question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: If the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other? This is because the brain has something of a two-tier memory system at work when it comes to retrieving memories, and this gives rise to a common yet infuriating sensation: recognising someone, but not being able to remember how or why, or what their name is. ①It is believed that people who are better at remembering names tend to form stronger emotional associations with new acquaintances. ②This happens because the brain differentiates between familiarity and recall. ③ To clarify, familiarity (or recognition) is when you encounter someone or something and you know you've done so before. ④But beyond that, you've got nothing; all you can say is this person/thing is already in your memories. ⑤Recall is when you can access the original memory of how and why you know this person; recognition is just flagging up the fact that the memory exists.
explanation: 이 글은 뇌가 친숙함(familiarity)과 회상(recall)을 구분하여 작동하는 이중 기억 체계에 대해 설명하고 은 글이다. 하지만 ①번 문장은 이름을 잘 기억하는 사람들이 감정적 유대감을 강하게 형성한다는 내용으로, 기억 체계의 작동 방식을 다련 전체 흠름과는 갑이 멀다.

question: 17. 주어질 글 │에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Human beings like certainty. This liking stems from our ancient ancestors who needed to survive alongside saber-toothed tigers and poisonous berries.
ordered_passages: (A) If I know for certain it is, my brain will direct me to eat it because I know it's safe. And if I'm uncertain, my brain will send out a danger alert to protect me. The dependence on certainty all those millennia ago ensured our survival to the present day, and the danger-alert system continues to protect us.

(B) This is achieved by our, brains labeling new, vague, or unpredictable everyday events and experiences as uncertain. Our brains then generate sensations, thoughts, and action plans to keep us safe from the uncertain element, and we live to see another day.

(C) Our brains evolved to help us attend to threats, keep away from them, and remain alive afterward. In fact, we learned that the more certain we were about something, the better chance we had of making the right choice. Is this berry the same shape as last time? The same size?
explanation: 주어진 문장에서 인간이 확실성을 선호한다는 점을 언급한 현, (C)에서 그 이유가 위협에 대비하기 위함임을 설명하며 베리의 예시림 들어 의문을 제기한다. (A)는 그 의문에 대한 답으로, 확실할 때 먹고 불확실할 때 피하는 생존 방식을 설명한다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 이랬한 생존 방식이 현대에서 뇌가 불확실한 것을 라벨링하여 우리림 보호하는 과정으로 이어지며 문맥이 완성된다.

question: 18. │다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 핀칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: As a general rule, it's better if your definition corresponds as closely as possible to the way in which the term is ordinarily used in the kinds of debates to which your claims are pertinent. There will be, however, occasions where it is appropriate, even necessary, to coin special uses through what philosophers call stimulative definition. This would be the case where the current lexicon is not able to make distinctions that you think are philosophically important. For example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something the person having it has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories: I would have a memory-type experience, but this would not be of something that I had actually experienced. To call this a memory would be misleading. For this reason, philosophers have coined the special term 'quasi-memory' to refer to these hypothetical memory-like experiences.
summary_sentence: (A)____________ is/are ideal, but philosophers create special terms when necessary for precision, as seen in an example of the term 'quasi-memory,' which is used to (B)____________ a hypothetical memory-like experience from a memory.

question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports.↓Governments worldwide prioritize food security by developing mechanisms to (A)__________ an adequate food supply, which does not (B)__________ self-sufficiency, as countries can bring in items not easily produced domestically. question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 22. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A)~(F)에 들어갈 말을 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오. (답안지에 (A), (B), (C), (D), (E), (F)를 쓰고 답안을 작성하시오.)
passage: Robert Blattberg and Steven Hoch noted that in dynamic environments, consistency might not always be ideal, highlighting that one of the strengths of human judgment lies in the ability to recognize changes. As such, in situations where conditions are evolving, combining human judgment with statistical models could be beneficial. To explore this, Blattberg and Hoch had supermarket managers forecast demand for specific products and then created a composite forecast by averaging these human judgments with predictions from statistical models based on past data. The rationale was that while statistical models rely on stable conditions and fail to explain novel events, such as competitors' actions or new product introductions, humans can incorporate these changes into their forecasts. The results showed that the composite forecast ─ blending human judgment with statistical predictions ─ was more accurate than either approach used independently.↓Experimental Journal by Robert Blattberg and Steven Hoch--------------------------------------------------------------┆ HypothesisIn changing environments, composite forecasts, which (A)__________ human judgment with statistical models, will be more accurate than forecasts generated using either human judgment or statistical models alone.┆ Experiment Method1) (B)_________ _________ were asked to forecast the demand for selected products.2) Statistical models were used to generate forecasts based on past data, assuming (C)_________ conditions.3) A composite forecast was created by averaging the managers' predictions with those from the statistical models.4) The accuracy of the composite forecast was compared to that of the human-only and statistical-model-only forecasts.┆ Experiment ResultsThe composite forecast, which blended human judgment and statistical predictions, outperformed either method used (D)s_________.┆ Analysis and InterpretationThis suggests that in dynamic environments, where conditions change and (E)_________ factors arise, statistical models alone cannot account for these changes, while humans are capable of (F)_________ these elements into their forecasts, thereby improving forecast accuracy.

3. (D)는 주어진 철자로 시작하는 한 단어로 쓰되, 본문에 없는 단어로 쓸 것

question: 23. 다음 굸의 요지를 <밴기>의 표현들을 주어진 <점건>에 맞게 사용하여 ※성하시오.

question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Eva, a soccer player, and her coach, Ms. Blake, practiced passing the ball together. Ms. Blake noticed that Eva's movements were slow and that her focus seemed elsewhere. Ms. Blake asked, "Do you remember the final game last year?" "Yeah, I remember." Eva recalled the game where she scored three goals. "I was quite good back then." "You still are," replied Ms. Blake. "Well, now I'm so worried I can't score a goal or even pass the ball properly. I'm afraid of making mistakes," said Eva. Ms. Blake placed a reassuring hand on Eva's shoulder. She suggested, "You don't have to be perfect. Soccer isn't about perfection - it's about passion. And you've always had plenty of that." She continued. "The way you play, the energy you bring - that's what makes you special. Not the goals scored or the trophies won. It's the love you have for the game." Eva nodded thoughtfully. In the next game, she played with a new confidence that hadn't been there before. Eva didn't score, but she led the team successfully. After the game she ran over, saying, "Thanks for believing in me, Coach." Ms. Blake smiled back. "You've always had it in you. I'm just here to remind you of that." Eva's face softened as she realized she had been too hard on herself. She said to herself, "What matters is _____________________."

② giving my best effort rather than being perfect

④ shaping my inborn nature into a desirable one

question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

question: 17. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 18. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 20. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.8점]

question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential.

question: 21. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition. But it's important to understand the limits of dictionary definitions. More often than not, a definition in a dictionary requires readers to have a fairly robust understanding of the language already at their disposal. In other words, a dictionary functions in many cases as a cross-reference or translator between words one knows and words that one doesn't yet know. Even the most obscure words in a dictionary, say, for example, "pulchritudinous" or "kalokagathia," must be defined using words that the reader already knows and understands. question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by relying on both domestic production and imports.

passage: Emotion socialization - learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them - starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may hinder adolescents' autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.

question: 5. 윗글에 대한 내용과 일치하는 것은?
passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in multiple discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally talented. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits that success alone increases the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
options: ① 뉴턴은 뉴턴 역학을 넘어 중력이론, 기하학, 운동 법칙 및 최적화를 발전시켰다.
② 매튜효과에 따르면, 최초의 성공은 과학자에게 정당성을 부여하지만, 과학자 자신에 대한 인식을 하락시킨다.
③ 매튜효과에 의하면, 최초의 성공으로 인한 보상들 각각은 과학자가 또 다른 성공을 거둘 가능성을 더욱 높여준다.
④ 위대한 과학자들이 여러 번의 성공 및 지속적으로 과학적 노력에서 성과를 이루는 이유는 그들의 노력 덕분이라는 대안 설명도 있다.
⑤ 매튜효과는 성공이란 하나의 성공이 아닌 여러 성공이 모여 미래의 성공 확률을 높인다고 상정한다.
explanation: 지문의 'each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring another win' 부분을 통해 초기 성공의 보상들이 다음 성공 확률을 높여준다는 것을 알 수 있습니다. ① 본문은 미적분(calculus)과 최적화(optimization)를 언급하며 기하학(geometry)은 언급되지 않았습니다. ② 동료의 인식을 개선(improve)시킨다고 설명합니다. ④ 노력(effort)이 아닌 재능(talent) 때문이라는 대안 설명이 제시되었습니다. ⑤ 매튜효과는 성공 그 자체가 미래의 성공 가능성을 높인다고 상정합니다.

question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [3.1점]

question: 10. 다음 글의 내용으로 보아 밑줄 친 단어의 영어 뜻풀이로 올바른 것은? [2.7점]

"You were here in September," he said. "Why are you back so soon?" "I came in September to prepare to return this month," I replied with a trembling voice, ⓒc<u>onsider</u>ing if I missed any Italian regulations. "For how long?" he asked. "One month, this time," I answered truthfully. I knew it was not against the rules to stay in Italy for three months. "Enjoy your stay," he finally said, as he ⓓ<u>stamp</u>ed my passport. Whew! options: ① ⓐmodel: to demonstrate or exemplify something for others to follow or learn from
② ⓑuneasy: making you feel physically relaxed
③ ⓒconsider: to think of someone or something in a particular way or to have a particular opinion
④ ⓓstamp: an act of putting the foot down on the ground hard
⑤ ⓔvanish: to start to exist or become available
explanation: ⓐ 'model'은 여기에서 '다른 사람들이 따르거나 배울 수 있도록 무언가를 보여주거나 본보기가 되다'는 의미로 쓰였으므로 ①이 정답입니다. ② 'uneasy'는 불안한 상태이므로 'relaxed'와는 반대입니다. ③ 'consider'는 여기서 '숙고하다, 검토하다'의 의미입니다. ④ 'stamp'는 여기에서 '도장을 찍다'의 의미이며, 발을 구르는 것이 아닙니다. ⑤ 'vanish'는 '사라지다'는 뜻으로 '존재하기 시작하다'는 반대의 뜻입니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐmodel: 다른 사람들이 따르거나 배울 수 있도록 무언가를 보여주거나 본보기가 되다
② ⓑuneasy: 신체적으로 편안함을 느끼게 만드는
③ ⓒconsider: 누군가나 무언가를 특정한 방식으로 생각하거나 특정한 의견을 갖는 것
④ ⓓstamp: 발을 땅에 세게 내딛는 행위
⑤ ⓔvanish: 존재하기 시작하거나 이용 가능해지는 것

question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]

question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [25년 3월 36번]

question: 18. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [25년 3월 35번]
passage: Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. Using one set of words to define another word is called a lexical definition. But it's important to understand the limits of dictionary definitions. More often than not, a definition in a dictionary requires readers to have a fairly robust understanding of the language already at their disposal. In other words, a dictionary functions in many cases as a cross-reference or translator between words one knows and words that one doesn't yet know. Even the most obscure words in a dictionary, say, for example, "pulchritudinous" or "kalokagathia," must be defined using words that the reader already knows and understands. Otherwise, the dictionary isn't very helpful.

② Dictionaries are designed to teach language to beginners through simple and direct word definitions.
③ The primary function of a dictionary is to translate foreign languages into one's native language.
④ Lexical definitions are the most reliable way to fully understand any word, regardless of one's vocabulary level.

② 사전은 간단하고 직접적인 단어 정의를 통해 초보자에게 언어를 가르치도록 설계되었다.
③ 사전의 주된 기능은 외국어를 모국어로 번역하는 것이다.
④ 어휘 정의는 어휘 수준에 관계없이 모든 단어를 완전히 이해하는 가장 신뢰할 수 있는 방법이다.
⑤ 사전은 단어의 의미를 배우는 데 유용하지만, 정의를 이해하려면 종종 언어에 대한 사전 지식이 필요하기 때문에 그 효과가 제한적이다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [2.9점]

passage: For years, many psychologists have held strongly to the belief that the key to addressing negative health habits is to change behavior. Ingestive habits such as smoking, drinking and various eating behaviors are the most common health concerns targeted for behavioral changes. Process-addiction behaviors (workaholism, shopaholism, and the like) fall into this category as well. Mental imagery combined with power of suggestion was taken up as the premise of behavioral medicine to help people change negative health behaviors into positive ones. Although this technique alone will not produce changes, when used alongside other behavior modification tactics and coping strategies, behavioral changes have proved effective for some people. What mental imagery does is reinforce a new desired behavior. Repeated use of images reinforces the desired behavior more strongly over time.
options: ① 부정적인 건강 습관을 개선하려면 사람의 가치관이나 태도를 먼저 바꾸는 것이 중요하다.
② 정신적인 이미지를 활용한 기법은 정신 질환자에게 효과적인 심리치료법으로 널리 사용된다.
③ 부정적 건강 행동은 환경 요인에 의해 형성되므로 행동 자체를 바꾸는 것은 근본적인 해결책이 아니다.
④ 현대 사회에서 건강 문제의 가장 흔한 원인은 과한 음주나 흡연 때문이고 이를 위한 적절한 약물 치료가 필요하다.
⑤ 건강 습관 개선에 행동 변화 접근법이 효과적이며, 심상기법은 긍정적 행동을 강화하는 보조 수단으로 사용될 수 있다.
explanation: 이 글은 부정적인 건강 습관을 해결하는 열쇠가 행동 변화에 있으며, 특히 심상기법(mental imagery)이 다른 행동 수정 전략과 함께 사용될 때 새로운 바람직한 행동을 강화하는 데 효과적이라는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 ⑤번이 글의 요지로 가장 적절합니다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Beethoven's drive to create something ⓐ<u>novel</u> is a reflection of his state of curiosity. Our brains experience a sense of reward when we create something new in the process of exploring something ⓑ<u>familiar</u>, such as a musical phrase that we've never played or heard before. When our curiosity leads to something new, the resulting reward brings us a sense of pleasure. A number of investigators have modeled how curiosity influences musical composition. In the case of Beethoven, computer modeling focused on the thirty-two piano sonatas written after age thirteen revealed that the musical patterns found in all of Beethoven's music were ⓒ<u>reduced</u> in later sonatas, while novel patterns, including patterns that were unique to a particular sonata, were ⓓ<u>expanded</u>. In other words, Beethoven's music became ⓔ<u>less</u> predictable over time as his curiosity drove the exploration of new musical ideas. Curiosity is a powerful driver of human creativity.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 글의 흐름상 인간의 뇌는 새로운 것을 탐구할 때 보상을 느낀다고 설명하고 있습니다. ⓑ가 포함된 문장의 예시에서 '한 번도 연주하거나 들어본 적 없는 음악적 악구'를 언급하고 있으므로, '친숙한(familiar)' 것을 탐구하는 과정이 아니라 '익숙하지 않은' 또는 '새로운' 것을 탐구하는 과정이어야 문맥상 적절합니다. 따라서 ⓑ가 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Emotion socialization - learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them - starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may intrude on adolescents' autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.
options: ① The roles of parents in the development of emotion regulation
② The growing influences of media and peers on emotional learning
③ Direct guidance necessary for effective emotion controlling
④ The mechanism of children copying their parents' reactions
⑤ Emotional challenges children should confront on their own
explanation: 이 글은 정서 조절(emotion regulation)의 발달에 있어서 부모가 미치는 영향과 역할에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 아동기에는 직접적인 지도가 도움이 되지만 청소년기에는 자율성을 존중하는 간접적인 지지가 필요하다는 점을 강조하며 시기에 따른 부모의 역할 변화를 다루고 있으므로 ①번이 가장 적절한 주제입니다.
options_translation: ① 정서 조절 발달에 있어서 부모의 역할
② 정서 학습에 대한 미디어와 또래의 증가하는 영향
③ 효과적인 정서 조절을 위해 필요한 직접적인 지도
④ 아이들이 부모의 반응을 모방하는 메커니즘
⑤ 아이들이 스스로 직면해야 하는 정서적 도전

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 부분이 있는 것을 모두 고른 것은?
passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem ⓐ<u>which</u> the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the ⓑ<u>maximizing</u> of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem; they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from ⓒ<u>being consumed</u> the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops ⓓ<u>to intervene</u>, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin ⓔ<u>shifting</u> to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
explanation: ⓐ 'which'는 뒤에 목적어(a specific state)가 빠진 불완전한 문장이 오는 것처럼 보이나, grower(주어) attempts(동사) to keep(목적어/준동사) the garden(keep의 목적어 생략) in a specific state 구조이므로 관계대명사가 맞습니다. 다만 엄밀히는 'which' 뒤에 keep의 목적어가 비어있는 형태입니다. ⓑ 'maximizing'은 'the maximization'이라는 명사형으로 쓰이거나, 'the maximizing of'는 어색하며 'maximization'이 적절합니다. ⓒ stop A from B(-ing) 구문에서 곤충과 동물들이 채소를 '먹는 것(consuming)'을 막는 능동의 의미가 되어야 하므로 'being consumed'는 틀렸습니다.ⓓ 'stop ~ing'는 하던 일을 멈추는 것이고 'stop to-v'는 하기 위해 멈추는 것입니다. 문맥상 개입하는 것을 멈추면 생태계가 변한다는 내용이므로 'stop intervening'이 되어야 합니다. 따라서 ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ가 어색합니다.

question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have fostered higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes.
