question: 14. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 단어들을 포함하여 손짓을 할 수 없을 때의 해로운 영향 3가지를 각각 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (한글로 작성)
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful <u>information</u>, we solve <u>problems</u> less well, and we are less able to explain our <u>thinking</u>. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
subjective_conditions: 한글로 작성
answer: (1) 덜 유용한 정보를 기억한다. (2) 문제를 잘 해결하지 못한다. (3) 우리의 생각을 잘 설명하지 못한다.
explanation: 본문 마지막 부분의 "we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking." 문장을 해석하여 작성합니다. 밑줄 친 information, problems, thinking이 포함된 구절을 찾아 우리말로 옮기면 됩니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: While intuition can be a valuable tool, it should ideally be the result of extensive effort and experience. Professionals, for instance, are able to respond swiftly and effectively because they have devoted countless hours to study and practice - their instincts are shaped by data and refined through repetition. It is this process that allows them to make rapid decisions grounded in their accumulated knowledge and real-world evidence. However, many individuals are far from being true experts, even though they often perceive themselves as such. Especially in online interactions, people tend to express strong and immediate opinions on complex global issues without having a solid understanding behind their claims. Furthermore, the rise of artificial intelligence has amplified this phenomenon: our messages are now more likely to reach those who already agree with us, strengthening our mistaken sense of authority. As a result, we are more inclined to consider others reasonable and intelligent simply because their views mirror our own.
options: ① The Hidden Power of Intuition
② When Everyone Feels Like an Expert
③ The Role of AI in Global Development
④ How to Build Expertise in the Digital Age
⑤ Social Media: A Place for Meaningful Debate
explanation: 진짜 전문가가 아닌 일반인들도 전문 지식 없이 온라인에서 강한 의견을 내며 자신의 권위를 확신하고, 남들이 동조할 때 지적으로 느낀다는(착각 속에 있다는) 글이므로 2번(When Everyone Feels Like an Expert)이 제목으로 가장 적합하다.

question: 17. 다음 <보기>에서 주어진 단어를 활용하여 빈칸 (A), (B)를 채우고, 각각의 뜻 (C), (D)를 적으시오.
passage: Technologists are always on the lookout for quantifiable metrics. Measurable inputs to a model are their lifeblood, and like a social scientist, a technologist needs to identify concrete measures, or "proxies," for assessing progress. This need for quantifiable proxies produces a bias toward measuring things that are easy to quantify. But simple metrics can take us further away from the important goals we really care about, which may require complicated metrics or be extremely difficult, or perhaps impossible, to reduce to any measure. And when we have imperfect or bad proxies, we can easily fall under the illusion that we are solving for a good end without actually making genuine progress toward a worthy solution. The problem of proxies results in technologists frequently substituting what is measurable for what is meaningful. As the saying goes, "Not everything that (A)___________ can be (B)___________, and not everything that can be (B)___________ (A)___________."<보기>count
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 단어(count)를 활용
explanation: "Not everything that counts(중요한 모든 것) can be counted(계산될 수 있는 것은 아니다), and not everything that can be counted(계산될 수 있는 모든 것) counts(중요한 것은 아니다)." count의 다의성을 활용한 격언이다.

question: 18. 다음 주어진 요약문의 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 단어를 글에서 찾아 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: We often overestimate the influence of emerging technologies, partly because older innovations have become so integrated into our daily routines that we barely notice them anymore. Consider something as simple as a baby bottle. Though it has profoundly altered the feeding experience for countless mothers and infants, it rarely appears in our narratives of technological advancement. In many ways, the baby bottle can be seen as a tool that reshaped time management - giving mothers greater flexibility in deciding when to feed their child, or even allowing others to take on the task in their place. As such, it holds significant implications for how time is organized in everyday life. Nevertheless, such practical yet subtle innovations are often left out of conversations about modern life and the fast pace of technological change.
summary_sentence: → People often forget how older tools changed daily life and _________________ new technology.
explanation: 'overestimate'는 '과대평가하다'라는 뜻으로, 지문의 첫 문장에서 우리가 새로운 기술의 영향력을 종종 과대평가한다고 언급하고 있습니다. 요약문은 "사람들은 종종 오래된 도구들이 일상 생활을 어떻게 바꾸었는지를 윺고, 새로운 기술을 과대평가한다"는 내용이 되어야 합니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: With the rapid increase in data being collected and stored in countless large databases, our ability to fully comprehend it without advanced analytical tools has been seriously outpaced. As a result, much of the data ends up in what can be described as "digital graveyards" - vast collections that are rarely accessed or utilized. In many cases, critical decisions are not based on the rich data available but are instead made according to gut feelings, simply because those making the decisions lack the proper tools to uncover the meaningful insights hidden within the overwhelming volume of information. Although expert systems and knowledge-based technologies have been introduced to tackle this issue, they often depend on human experts manually entering knowledge - a process that is not only expensive and time-consuming but also prone to errors and subjective bias. To bridge the growing gap between raw data and useful information, there is a pressing need for systematic tools that can transform these underused data stores into valuable sources of knowledge - turning digital graveyards into true gold mines.*gut feeling: 직감

② 전문가 시스템의 전통적 방식에 대한 시대적 재평가

question: 7. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by _________________________________.
options: ① relying exclusively on food self-sufficiency
② strictly limiting all food imports from other countries
③ eliminating international trade in agricultural products

Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to taking various measures to sustain the currency in question. Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.
subjective_conditions: 1. 본문 속 '이어지는 4개의 단어'로 이루어진 표현을 사용할 것

question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested, that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. ⓐ<u>Revolutionaries have always looked to the past to frame their future cause, as is amply illustrated by examples from nationalism to communism.</u> ⓑ<u>The future has often been seen as variously a recovery of a lost time, as a replication of what is established, or as a model bequeathed by a heroic age long gone.</u> ⓒ<u>The writing of history is based on understanding or explaining future outcomes that were not known to contemporaries, since the historian has the benefit of hindsight and the past is nothing more than the accumulation of futures that are now our past.</u> ⓓ<u>Historians can be influenced by hindsight bias and overestimate what they could have predicted in the past.</u> ⓔ<u>So, rather than see the hand of the past always shaping the future, perhaps it can be seen in reverse, with the past ─ in the sense of our understanding of it ─ being shaped by our orientation to the future.</u>

question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 19. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much a creative process. A conjecture is a philosophical invention, cooked up rather mystically by the mind through the mental computation we call careful contemplation. However, until the hypothesis is tested against reality, it is not yet truly knowledge; it is just information that represents speculation. Knowledge is information that has demonstrated its usefulness. It is what is left over after cycles of experimental testing have eliminated false theories. As scientists continually test their hypotheses and modify their models to account for new and surprising data, a kind of "learning loop" emerges that statisticians call Bayesian updating. Based on Bayes' Rule, developed by eighteenth-century English statistician and philosopher Thomas Bayes, Bayesian updating refers to a mathematical process whereby an accepted theory or predictive model gets increasingly accurate through the repetitive testing of competing variants of that theory.

④ 과학적 추론이 반복적 검증을 통해 지식이 되는 과정

question: 20. 윗글에서 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말을 찾아 아래 <조건>을 참고하여 한 단어로 적으시오.

question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

question: 24. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other? This is because the brain has something of a two-tier memory system at work when it comes to retrieving memories, and this gives rise to a common yet infuriating sensation: recognising someone, but not being able to remember how or why, or what their name is. This happens because the brain differentiates between familiarity and recall. To clarify, familiarity (or recognition) is when you encounter someone or something and you know you've done so before. But beyond that, you've got nothing; all you can say is this person/thing is already in your memories. Recall is when you can access the original memory of how and why you know this person; recognition is just flagging up the fact that the memory exists. The brain has several ways and means to trigger a memory, but you don't need to "activate" a memory to know it's there. You know when you try to save a file onto your computer and it says, "This file already exists"? It's a bit like that. All you know is that _____________________________________; you can't get at it yet.

② a person's face and name are unrelated
③ long-term memories are made up of synapses
④ you need to access the information when needed
⑤ both someone's name and face have been successfully stored in the long-term memory

② 사람의 얼굴과 이름은 관련이 없다
③ 장기 기억은 시낽스로 구성된다
④ 필요할 때 정밴에 접근할 필요가 있다

question: 25. 다음 주어진 글(A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: (A) Sometimes, humour can facilitate progressive social change. The history of US television sitcoms provides a clear example. ordered_passages: (B) In this way, the humour of sitcoms acted as a cost-effective means to encourage acceptance of a more pluralistic and tolerant society. However, as a pedagogic tool humour can also be used to prevent social progress and bring about intolerance! Freud explained this insight by reference to jokes.

(C) Through jokes, ideas are delivered in an enjoyable form, which encourages us to accept them more easily. Because the ideas are presented in an enjoyable form, we tend to accept them without critical questioning, sometimes absorbing prejudice against a minority. Also, we are inclined to find nothing wrong in what has given us enjoyment.

(D) Each of these issues has been addressed through humour in a way that has helped to make more progressive values more acceptable than previously. question: 26. 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. All experts are not the same, nor do they submit their work to the same scrutiny. Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims. For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were funded in part by the sugar industry. The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared. Their article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have fostered higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes. Stories such as this one fuel suspicion ─ but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. Funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since been made compulsory. This does not mean that the soda, candy, tobacco, and pharmaceutical industries, for example, no longer fund research but only (A)___________ of funding source is necessary in publication of results. What's critical is that individuals should look for such funding source and that policy makers become careful about basing public policy on limited research.
options: ① Some scientific research can be biased depending on its funding source.

question: 27. 윗글에서 빈칸(A)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말을 찾아 아래 <조건>을 참고하여 한 단어로 적으시오.

question: 28. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: ⓐ<u>beyond</u> the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in numerous discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. Indeed, an initial success may ⓑ<u>grant</u> a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further increasing her odds of scoring ⓒ<u>additional</u> wins. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally gifted. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden ⓓ<u>talent</u>. The Matthew effect posits that success alone ⓔ<u>decreases</u> the future probability of success, raising the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an underlying talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 매튜 효과(Matthew effect)는 초기 성공이 자원, 명성, 협력자 등을 끌어들여 다음 성공의 가능성을 높인다는 이론입니다. 따라서 ⓔ의 'decreases(감소시키다)'는 문맥상 'increases(증가시키다)' 또는 'boosts'와 같은 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

question: 29. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Research shows that we all engage in "gestural foreshadowing," in which ______________________________. When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
options: ① our mouths move before we think
② our gestures follow our conscious thoughts
③ our hands anticipate what we're about to say
④ gestures are mainly decorative in communication
⑤ gestures complement spoken language by helping to highlight key points
explanation: 이 글은 '몸짓 예고(gestural foreshadowing)'에 대해 설명하며, 우리의 손이 의식적인 마음보다 먼저 우리가 무엇을 말할지 '알고' 있다는 점을 강조합니다. 오류를 수정할 때 말보다 먼저 몸짓을 멈춘다는 예시와 몸짓을 하지 못하게 할 때 유창성이 떨어진다는 점 등을 통해, 몸짓이 사고의 선두에 서서 우리가 하려는 말을 미리 준비하고 예측하는 역할을 한다는 것을 알 수 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '우리의 손이 우리가 말하려는 것을 예견한다'는 의미인 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리의 입이 생각하기 전에 움직인다
② 우리의 몸짓이 우리의 의식적인 생각을 따른다
③ 우리의 손이 우리가 말하려는 것을 예측한다
④ 몸짓은 의사소통에서 주로 장식적이다
⑤ 몸짓은 핵심 사항을 강조하는 것을 도움으로써 구어(말)를 보완한다

question: 30. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain. A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. (A) It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. (B) But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol "on" instead of "off," which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze. (C) This is because it's one of only two areas of the adult brain where neurogenesis, the growth of new brain cells, is present. (D) Neurogenesis in the hippocampus isn't just important for dementia prevention; it's also important to prevent anxiety, since the growth of brain cells in this part of the brain has been shown to reduce it. (E)
insertion_sentence: The hippocampus is also a very important part of the brain as we age.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 히포캄푸스(해마)가 '나이가 들어감에 따라' 매우 중요한 부분이라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (C) 뒤의 문장에서 이것이 성인 뇌에서 새로운 뇌 세포가 자라는 '신경 발생(neurogenesis)'이 일어나는 영역이라는 이유를 설명하고 있고, 이어지는 (D) 다음 문장에서 이 신경 발생이 '치매 예방(dementia prevention)'에 중요하다는 점을 언급하고 있습니다. 치매는 노화와 밀접한 관련이 있으므로, 노화와 관련된 히포캄푸스의 중요성을 언급한 주어진 문장은 (C) 자리에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]

options: ① 한 과학자의 성공은 후세 과학자들의 성공에 지대한 영향을 미친다.

question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: The explosion of popular music in the second half of the twentieth century as well as the global circulation and dissemination of music by the creative industries propelled a new understanding of accessbility in relation to music. Suddenly, in the 1950s, anyone could pick up spoons, a couple of pans, a second-hand guitar and start a band. This led to specific genres such as skiffle, but also, more generally, reflected a much more relaxed and inclusive attitude to music making. While ordinary people had always sung and made music, the popular music movement was driven by a spirit of rebellion and freedom. This approach led to the punk movement, whose musicians even made it a condition for their music to be non-virtuosic and accessible to all in the 1970s. Groups who had been entirely excluded from music revelled in opportunities to create. This led to a sense of novelty and empowerment in and beyond the music sphere.
options: ① 20세기 후반의 대중음악은 비주류 음악 집단의 힘을 약화시켰다.

③ 대중음악과 함께 발전한 저항음악으로 인해 음악가의 창의성이 제한되었다.

explanation: 20세기 후반 대중음악의 폭발적 성장은 음악의 '접근성(accessibility)'에 대한 새로운 이해를 촉발했습니다. 1950년대 스키플 장르나 1970년대 펑크 운동처럼, 누구나 일상 도구나 중고 기타로 음악을 만들 수 있게 됨으로써 전문적이지 않아도 누구나 음악을 만들 수 있다는 포용적인 태도가 확산되었습니다. 이는 음악 창작 주체와 방식에 대한 인식 변화를 의미하므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

The remainder shifted to varieties of English, the language of the people who had suppressed them.
options: ① moves from more suppressed societies to free ones

explanation: 언어 교류에서 단어의 차용은 주로 우세한 집단 위에서 주변부나 덜 특권적인 하위 집단으로 이루어진다는(권력 관계를 반영한다는) 내용이므로 5번이 빈칸에 가장 적합하다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The governments of virtually every country on the planet attach great importance to achieving food security and a wide variety of mechanisms have been developed to realize this goal. The first issue governments face in achieving national food security is the problem of insuring that adequate amounts of food are available to the resident population. Some governments have set goals of food self-sufficiency, which means most if not all of the food available in a country comes from the domestic farming system. However, food security does not require food self-sufficiency because countries can import food items not easily produced within the country. Agricultural products are, after all, highly sensitive to climatic, soil and other conditions that tend to vary around the world. Even countries with extremely productive agricultural sectors are not fully self-sufficient in all food items. The United States, for example, depends on imports for its supply of coffee, tea, bananas and other tropical products. In general, the problem of assuring adequate food supplies is solved by __________________________________.
options: ① depending upon both domestic production and imports
② receiving an international relief to feed the population
③ raising tariff barriers on agricultural products to decrease imports
④ expanding agricultural land to be self-sufficient in food production
⑤ making an investment in developing new agricultural technologies

question: 11. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Commitment is the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life. Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby facilitating the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents.
ordered_passages: (A) Indeed, the taxi driver is willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to taking various measures to sustain the currency in question.

(B) Moreover, commitments make people willing to perform actions that they would not otherwise perform. For example, a taxi driver picks up his clients and transports them to their desired destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service.
(C) Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.
explanation: 주어진 글은 헌신(Commitment)이 인간 사회의 사회적 삶을 결합하고 행동을 예측 가능하게 한다는 일반적인 내용을 담고 있습니다. (B)에서 'Moreover'를 사용하여 헌신이 평소에는 하지 않을 행동을 하게 만든다는 추가적인 기능을 설명하며 택시 기사와 승객의 사례를 도입합니다. (A)에서는 택시 기사가 돈을 받는 이유가 중앙은행과 같은 타인들의 헌신(약속) 때문임을 구체화하며 헌신의 네트워크를 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 'Thus'를 통해 직업, 돈, 정부, 결혼 등 사회적 기관들이 헌신의 신뢰성에 의존한다는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Emotion socialization - learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them - starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development.
ordered_passages: (A) In this regard, a positive emotional family climate - reflected in emotional acceptance, warmth, and responsiveness - is also beneficial for adolescents' emotion regulation development. In contrast, parental messages that adolescents' emotional experiences are inaccurate, insignificant, or unacceptable foster emotional suppression and are associated with an increased risk of adolescent emotion regulation problems.

(B) Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations.

(C) In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.

(D) Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may intrude on adolescents' autonomy striving.
explanation: 주어진 글은 감정 사회화의 정의와 발달적 중요성을 언급합니다. (B) 청소년기에 가족 외부의 영향이 커짐에도 부모가 여전히 주요 사회화 대리인이며 모델링 역할을 한다는 내용이 이어집니다. (D) 부모의 관행이 감정적 도전에 미치는 영향을 설명하며, 어린아이에게 유익한 직접적 지도가 청소년에게는 자율성을 침해할 수 있음을 대조합니다. (C) 그 결과('In consequence') 부모의 관행이 바뀌지 않으면 청소년이 멀어질 수 있으며, 간접적인 자율적 감정 조절 지원이 필요함을 제안합니다. (A) 마지막으로 긍정적인 가족 분위기의 유익함과 부적절한 부모의 메시지가 미치는 위험성을 대조하며 논의를 마무리합니다.

question: 13. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In 1900, at the close of the first decade in which electric systems had become a practical alternative for manufacturers, less than 5 percent of the power used in factories came from electricity.
ordered_passages: (A) And the factory owners, having always supplied their own power, were loath to assign such a critical function to an outsider. They knew that a glitch in power supply would bring their operations to a halt - and that a lot of glitches might well mean bankruptcy. As the new century began, a survey found that there were already 50,000 private electric plants in operation, far surpassing the 3,600 central stations.

(B) In short order, electric power had gone from exotic to commonplace. But one thing didn't change. Factories continued to build their own power-supply systems on their own premises. Few manufacturers considered buying electricity from the small central stations. Designed to supply lighting to local homes and shops, the central stations had neither the size nor the skill to serve the needs of big factories.

(C) But the technological advances of suppliers made electric systems and electric motors ever more affordable and reliable, and the suppliers' intensive marketing programs also sped the adoption of the new technology. Further accelerating the shift was the rapid expansion in the number of skilled electrical engineers, who provided the expertise needed to install and run the new systems.
explanation: 주어진 글은 1900년 초반 공장에서 전력 사용률이 매우 낮았음을 제시합니다. (C) 'But'으로 시작하여 기술적 발전, 마케팅, 숙련된 기술자의 증가로 인해 전력 시스템 채택이 가속화되었음을 설명합니다. (B) 그 결과 전력이 흔해졌지만, 공장들이 중앙 발전소로부터 전기를 사기보다는 자체 시스템을 유지하려 했음을 지적하며 그 이유(중앙 발전소의 규모 부족)를 설명합니다. (A) 'And'를 통해 공장주들이 외부인에게 전력 공급을 맡기기 싫어했던 추가적인 심리적/경제적 이유(파산 위험)를 설명하며 사설 발전소가 중앙 발전소보다 훨씬 많았다는 조사 결과로 마무리합니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: For years, many psychologists have held strongly to the belief that the key to addressing negative health habits is to change behavior. (B) Ingestive habits such as smoking, drinking and various eating behaviors are the most common health concerns targeted for behavioral changes. (C) Process-addiction behaviors (workaholism, shopaholism, and the like) fall into this category as well. (D) Mental imagery combined with power of suggestion was taken up as the premise of behavioral medicine to help people change negative health behaviors into positive ones. (E) What mental imagery does is reinforce a new desired behavior.
insertion_sentence: Although this technique alone will not produce changes, when used alongside other behavior modification tactics and coping strategies, behavioral changes have proved effective for some people.
explanation: 이 글은 부정적인 건강 습관을 바꾸기 위해 행동을 변화시키는 것이 중요함을 설명하고 있습니다. (D)와 (E) 문장에서는 '정신적 이미지(Mental imagery)'라는 구체적인 기법을 소개하고 있으며, 주어진 문장의 'this technique'은 바로 이 정신적 이미지를 지칭합니다. (E) 다음 위치에 문장이 들어가야 정신적 이미지 기법이 단독으로는 변화를 일으키지 못할 수 있지만, 다른 전략과 결합될 때 효과적이라는 결론적인 설명이 자연스럽게 연결됩니다.

question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: There are reasons why science is not fully trusted and why healthy skepticism and critical thinking are essential. In spite of professional standards, claims of objectivity, and the peer review process, the conduct of science can be biased. All experts are not the same, nor do they submit their work to the same scrutiny. Knowing the source of funding can be important in evaluating scientific claims. (A) For example, the Harvard researchers who made claims in the late 1960s about the problems with dietary fat, leading the nation away from perceiving sugar as one of the main causes in health problems, were funded in part by the sugar industry. (B) The authors did not reveal their funding source to the New England Journal of Medicine, where their influential article appeared. (C) Stories such as this one fuel suspicion - but also lead to further safeguards in the scientific process. (D) Funding disclosures, although not required five decades ago, have since been mandated. (E) This does not mean that the soda, candy, tobacco, and pharmaceutical industries, for example, no longer fund research but only that disclosure is necessary in publication of results.
insertion_sentence: And then, the article shaped a generation of changes in eating patterns that appears to have fostered higher use of sugar, now widely implicated as a source of the rise in obesity and diabetes.
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'the article'은 (B) 문장에서 언급된 'influential article'을 가리킵니다. (B) 문장은 설탕 산업의 자금 지원을 받은 하버드 연구진이 자신들의 자금원을 밝히지 않은 채 영향력 있는 기사를 발표했음을 설명합니다. 따라서 주어진 문장은 그 기사가 식습관의 변화를 형성하여 설탕 소비를 늘리고 비만과 당뇨를 초래했다는 결과를 설명하며 (C) 앞에 위치하는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In order to bring the ever-increasing costs of home care for elderly and needy persons under control, managers of home care providers have introduced management systems. These systems specify tasks of home care workers and the time and budget available to perform these tasks. Electronic reporting systems require home care workers to report on their activities and the time spent, thus making the distribution of time and money visible and, in the perception of managers, controllable. This, in the view of managers, has contributed to the resolution of the problem. The home care workers, on the other hand, may perceive their work not as a set of separate tasks to be performed as efficiently as possible, but as a service to be provided to a client with whom they may have developed a relationship. This includes having conversations with clients and enquiring about the person's well-being. Restricted time and the requirement to report may be perceived as obstacles that make it impossible to deliver the service that is needed. If the management systems are too rigid, this may result in home care workers becoming overloaded and demotivated.
summary_sentence: Although management systems of home care services enable managers to (A)_____________ the issue of the distribution of time and money, they may be seen as (B)_____________ that keep home care workers from doing their jobs efficiently.
options: ① straighten out ...... hindrances
② aggravate ...... barriers
③ deal with ...... advantages
④ worsen ...... merits
⑤ alleviate ...... benefits
explanation: 가정 간호 관리 시스템은 관리자 입장에서 시간과 예산 배분의 문제를 해결하거나 명확히 정리(straighten out)할 수 있게 해주지만, 현장 노동자들에게는 고객과의 관계 형성 등 필수적인 서비스를 수행하는 데 있어 방해물(hindrances)로 인식될 수 있다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 해결하다(정리하다) ...... 방해물

question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In popular genres of food writing, the social dimension of food takes precedence. Although the characteristics of food hook the reader, where and with whom one is eating and what they say or do become the focus. Often the people who produce the food and their trials and joys take center stage, the pitfalls and challenges of finding and preparing food providing narrative thrust to a story that reveals a form of life. Popular food writing tends to slide into travel writing giving the reader a way to imagine the intrigue or romance of distant destinations. Thus, food ________________________________ for the unfolding of a human drama. It becomes a metaphor for ruminations about desire, adventure, memory, or romance. Although our social gatherings coalesce around food, the meaning of these gatherings does not seem to depend on flavor. explanation: 이 글은 음식 관련 글쓰기에서 음식 자체의 맛보다는 음식을 둘러싼 사회적 측면(누구와 어디서 먹는지, 인간적인 드라마 등)이 더 중시된다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 음식은 인간 드라마가 펼쳐지기 위한 '일종의 무대 설정'으로서 기능한다는 내용이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.

question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other? question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Dictionaries are relatively good resources for anyone interested in finding out what a word means. But it's important to understand the limits of dictionary definitions. More often than not, a definition in a dictionary requires readers to have a fairly robust understanding of the language already at their disposal. In other words, a dictionary functions in many cases as a cross-reference or translator between words one knows and words that one doesn't yet know. ⓐEven the most obscure words in a dictionary, say, for example, "pulchritudinous" or "kalokagathia," must be defined using words that the reader already knows and understands. ⓑDictionaries are especially useful to people who have trouble with spelling but, unfortunately, these are the very people who find them difficult and frustrating to use. ⓒOtherwise, the dictionary isn't very helpful. ⓓAnother potential problem with dictionaries is that they often simply report on the way a word is commonly used, which can nevertheless be conceptually problematic and can change significantly over time. ⓔCritical thinkers and other inquirers, in contrast, are often interested in more precise, more accurate, and often more enduring definition.
explanation: 이 글은 사전 정의가 갖는 한계점(이미 언어를 어느 정도 알고 있어야 사전 활용이 가능하다는 점 등)과 사전의 기능적 특성에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓑ는 철자에 어려움을 겪는 사람들에게 사전이 유용하지만 그들이 사용하기에 어렵다는 내용으로, 글의 핵심 소재인 '사전 정의의 의미론적 한계'와는 거리가 멉니다.

question: 20. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
passage: It's untrue that our kids can focus on two things at once - what ⓐ<u>they</u>'re doing is shifting their attention from one task to another. In this digital age, our kids wire their brains to make these shifts very quickly, but ⓑ<u>they</u> are still paying attention to one thing at a time, sequentially. Common sense tells us multitasking should increase brain activity, but Carnegie Mellon University scientists using the latest brain imaging technology find it doesn't. As a matter of fact, they discovered that multitasking actually reduces brain activity. Neither task is done as well as if each were performed individually. Fractions of a second are lost every time we make a switch, and a person's interrupted task can take 50 percent longer to finish, with 50 percent more errors. Turns out the latest brain research supports the old advice "one thing at a time." It's not that kids can't do some tasks simultaneously. But if two tasks are performed at once, one of ⓒ<u>them</u> has to be familiar. Our brains perform a familiar task on "automatic pilot" while really paying attention to the other one. That's why insurance companies consider talking on a cell phone and driving to be as dangerous as driving while drunk - it's the driving that goes on "automatic pilot" while the conversation really holds our attention. So flooding our working memory with information makes it difficult to really focus. But is this really a big deal? Yes. The brains of the multitasking generation are getting a lot of practice with fast and superficial spurts of attention at the expense of deep, creative, and focused thinking. Our kids may be living in the Information Age but ⓓ<u>their</u> brains have not been redesigned yet. When a task requires concentration, <u>there is a cognitive cost to juggling too much at the same time</u>. So the next time your kids tell you ⓔ<u>they</u> can do homework while watching TV or talking on the phone, just say, "Sorry. One thing at a time."
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 '아이들(our kids)'을 가리키는 반면, ⓒ 'them'은 문맥상 아이들이 동시에 수행하는 '두 가지 과업(two tasks)'을 가리킵니다.

question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: As a general rule, it's better if your definition corresponds as closely as possible to the way in which the term is ordinarily used in the kinds of debates to which your claims are pertinent.
ordered_passages: (A) For example, we do not have a term in ordinary language that describes a memory that is not necessarily a memory of something the person having it has experienced. Such a thing would occur, for example, if I could somehow share your memories: I would have a memory type experience, but this would not be of something that I had actually experienced.(B) To call this a memory would be misleading. explanation: 주어진 글은 정의가 일상적인 용어 사용과 일치해야 한다는 일반적인 원칙을 제시합니다. (C)에서 'however'를 통해 예외적인 상황(새로운 용어를 만들어야 할 때)을 소개하며 전환됩니다. (A)는 (C)에서 언급한 일상 용어에 없는 구분이 필요한 구체적인 사례(직접 경험하지 않은 기억)를 'For example'로 제시합니다. question: 20. 다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 괄호 안의 단어를 조건에 맞게 바르게 배열하여 요약문을 완성하시오.
passage: Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain. A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced longlasting stress. Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol "on" instead of "off," which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.

question: 22. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 표현을 작성하시오. [25년 3월 30번]

question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.3점]
passage: Great scientists are seldom one-hit wonders. Newton is a prime example: beyond the Newtonian mechanics, he developed the theory of gravitation, calculus, laws of motion, and optimization. In fact, well-known scientists are often involved in ⓐ<u>multiple</u> discoveries, a phenomenon potentially explained by the Matthew effect. Indeed, an initial success may offer a scientist legitimacy, improve peer perception, provide knowledge of how to score and win, enhance social status, and attract resources and quality collaborators, each of these payoffs further ⓑ<u>increasing</u> her odds of scoring another win. Yet, there is an appealing alternative explanation: Great scientists have multiple hits and consistently succeed in their scientific endeavors simply because they're exceptionally ⓒ<u>talented</u>. Therefore, future success again goes to those who have had success earlier, not because of advantages offered by the previous success, but because the earlier success was indicative of a hidden talent. The Matthew effect posits that success alone is ⓓ<u>irrelevant</u> to the future probability of success. But, it raises the question: Does status dictate outcomes, or does it simply reflect an ⓔ<u>underlying</u> talent or quality? In other words, is there really a Matthew effect after all?
explanation: 마태 효과(Matthew effect)는 초기 성공이 가져다주는 이점들이 후속 성공의 가능성을 높인다는 이론입니다. 따라서 마태 효과는 성공 그 자체가 미래의 성공 확률과 '관련이 있다'고 가정해야 문맥상 적절합니다. 본문에서 ⓓ의 irrelevant(무관한)는 relevant(관련된) 혹은 indicative(나타내는)와 같은 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 합니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.3점]
passage: It is important to recognize that although science is a rule-based procedure, it is very much a ⓐ<u>creative</u> process. A conjecture is a philosophical invention, cooked up rather mystically by the mind through the mental computation we call careful contemplation. However, until the hypothesis is tested against reality, it is not yet truly knowledge; it is just information that represents ⓑ<u>presupposition</u>. Knowledge is information that has ⓒ<u>demonstrated</u> its usefulness. It is what is left over after cycles of experimental testing have eliminated false theories. As scientists continually test their hypotheses and ⓓ<u>adjust</u> their models to account for new and surprising data, a kind of "learning loop" emerges that statisticians call Bayesian updating. Based on Bayes' Rule, developed by eighteenth-century English statistician and philosopher Thomas Bayes, Bayesian updating refers to a mathematical process whereby an accepted theory or predictive model gets increasingly ⓔ<u>fragile</u> through the repetitive testing of competing variants of that theory.
explanation: 베이지안 업데이트(Bayesian updating)는 반복적인 테스트를 통해 모델을 수정하고 보완해 나가는 과정입니다. 이 과정을 통해 수용된 이론이나 예측 모델은 점점 더 '취약해지는(fragile)' 것이 아니라, 더 '정교해지거나(refined)' '강력해지는(robust)' 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.

question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, we remember less useful information, we solve problems less well, and we are less able to explain our thinking. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture _________________________________.

② functions independently from speech and thought

② 언어 및 사고와는 독립적으로 기능한다
③ 우리 정신적 활동의 최첨단(최전선)에 서 있다
④ 말할 때 감정 표현을 강조하는 역할을 한다

question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The prominence of the social dimension in food writing might suggest that the flavor of food is taking a back seat, implying that _________________________________ in social settings where food is served. Flavor assists with the narrow purpose of filling the belly, and once that is accomplished it provides the backdrop for whatever social dynamics characterize the gathering. These can be understood independently of the flavor of the food on offer, the appreciation of which is understood to be personal and subjective. options: ① the focus is entirely on the food's flavor
② social interaction is prioritized over food

question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Commitment is the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life. Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuations in their desires and interests, thereby facilitating the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. Moreover, commitments make people willing to perform actions that they would not otherwise perform. For example, a taxi driver picks up his clients and transports them to their desired destination because they are committed to paying him afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a credible commitment to pay her at the end of the month. Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money as payment only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to taking various measures to sustain the currency in question. Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments. In this way, _________________________________________.
options: ① individuals' spontaneous decisions would drive economic stability
② institutions would function effectively disregarding societal norms
③ credible commitments would be maintained through scientific advancement
④ social systems would lack stability and coordination without commitments
⑤ short-term interactions would be more crucial than long-term agreements in social structures
explanation: 모든 사회 형태와 제도들이 약속/헌신(commitment)의 신뢰성에 기반을 두고 작동하므로, 약속(commitments)이 없다면 사회 시스템은 안정성과 조정 능력이 결여될 것이라는 4번 문장이 빈칸에 적절하다.

question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: If the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other? ③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem; they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.↓In a home vegetable garden, the grower continually intervenes to maintain (A)____________ production, but without intervention the ecosystem naturally shifts to a more stable state with (B)____________ yield.
options: ① peakreduced
② optimalhigher
③ constantequal
④ moderatefluctuating
⑤ predictableconsistent
explanation: 재배자가 개입하여 유지하려는 상태는 과일과 채소 생산의 극대화(maximization, 최고조 peak)이며, 만약 개입이 없으면 자연 상태인 안정된 상태로 돌아가면서 수확량은 낮아지게(lower, 감소한 reduced) 된다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 요지를 한 문장으로 작성하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말을 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: Despite the difference between the past and the future, between what has happened and what is to come, it can be suggested, that our sense of the past has always been influenced by our view of the future. Revolutionaries have always looked to the past to frame their future cause, as is amply illustrated by examples from nationalism to communism. The future has often been seen as variously a recovery of a lost time, as a replication of what is established, or as a model bequeathed by a heroic age long gone. The writing of history is based on understanding or explaining future outcomes that were not known to contemporaries, since the historian has the benefit of hindsight and the past is nothing more than the accumulation of futures that are now our past. So, rather than see the hand of the past always shaping the future, perhaps it can be seen in reverse, with the past ─ in the sense of our understanding of it ─ being shaped by our orientation to the future.↓It can be understood that the past (A)________________; rather, (B)____________________________.
subjective_conditions: <보기>에 주어진 어휘 모두 사용
필요시 어법 변형/단어 추가
answer: (A) does not shape the future(B) our perspective on the future shapes our perception of the past
explanation: 과거가 단지 미래를 형성하는 것이 아니라, 역으로 미래에 대한 우리의 시각과 방향성이 과거를 인식하는 방식을 형성한다는 요지이다.

question: 1. 다음 글을 읽고, 필자의 주장으로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: What will the next twenty-five years bring for Emotional Intelligence? Perhaps, surprisingly the advent of artificial intelligence (AI) in the work-place may bode well for emotional intelligence (EI).

(C) As AI gains momentum and replaces people in jobs at every level, predictions are8, there will be a premium placed on people who have high ability in EI. The emotional messages people send and respond to while interacting are, at this point, far beyond the ability of AI programs to mimic.

(D) In a survey, almost three out of four executives see EI as a "must-have" skill for the workplace in the future as the automatizing of routine tasks bumps up against the impossibility of creating effective AI for activities that require emotional skill.
explanation: 제시문에서 AI의 등장이 감성 지능(EI)에 좋은 징조가 될 수 있음을 언급했습니다. (C)에서 AI가 사람을 대체함에 따라 EI 능력이 높은 사람들에게 프리미엄이 붙을 것이라는 일반적 예측을 설명하고, (B)에서 AI가 감정을 다루는 능력을 갖기 어렵기 때문에 EI 관련 일자리는 안전하다고 구체화합니다. (D)에서 경영진 설문조사를 통해 미래 직장의 필수 기술로서의 EI의 중요성을 강조하고, (A)에서 의료 분야의 예시(의료적 데이터 처리는 AI가 잘하지만 감성적 영역은 인간의 영역임)를 들어 마무리하는 구조가 적절합니다.

question: 19. 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Every brand needs a development strategy. Think about the brands that you love. like Nike and McDonald's or Oprah and Dr. Wayne Dyer. These brands are constantly evolving, trying new things, expanding their market, creating new products and services, and continuing to meet the emerging needs of the marketplace. Your personal brand will continue to evolve as well. You may be asking yourself, "What is the best way to develop my brand?" The simple answer is to create a plan. Determine your strategy for how you will stay on the cutting edge of new and emerging trends in your function and industry. Hire a coach to help you improve your personal productivity and gain critical insight into your motivations and values. Work with a mentor to expand your knowledge and understanding of how to be successful in your chosen career.Brands that fail to grow and develop lose their relevance. Think about the person you knew who was once on the fast track at your company, who is either no longer with the firm or, worse yet, appears to have hit a plateau in his or her career. Assuming he or she did not make a career-limiting move, more often than not, this individual is a victim of having failed to stay relevant and embrace the advances in his or her industry. Think about the impact personal computing technology had on the first wave of executive leadership exposed to the technology. Those who embraced the technology were able to integrate it into their work styles and excel. Those who were resistant many times found few opportunities to advance their careers and in many cases were ultimately let go through early retirement for failure to stay relevant and update their skills. Don't let this be you.
options: ① The importance of creating new products for brand success
② The role of technology in personal development
③ How personal and corporate brands must evolve to remain relevant
④ The challenges of staying committed to career goals
⑤ The need for constant innovation in marketing strategies
explanation: 이 글은 브랜드(기업 및 개인 브랜드 포함)가 시장에서 도태되지 않고 유의미함을 유지하기 위해서는 끊임없이 발전하고 새로운 트렌드에 적응해야 한다는 필요성을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '개인 및 기업 브랜드가 유의미함을 유지하기 위해 어떻게 진화해야 하는가'가 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 브랜드 성공을 위한 신제품 창출의 중요성
② 개인 발전에 있어 기술의 역할
③ 개인 및 기업 브랜드가 유의미함을 유지하기 위해 어떻게 진화해야 하는가
④ 경력 목표에 전념하는 것의 어려움

question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Just as an expert in the taste and colour of wine will gain much by being aware of the chemistry that underlies those qualities, so each perspective on the body can potentially enhance the others. And yet every scientific tool, from microscopes to mathematics, and every aspect of the body, from the brain to the microorganism, requires such depth of expertise that this tends not to happen: we tend to study the human body in silos, each community sectioned from the others by its own specialised vocabulary. Research communities may be dedicated to one type of scientific tool or a specific component of the body, such as one type of cell. How different types of cell communicate with one another becomes its own specialist topic. Even simple forms of life on Earth are now rarely studied as a whole, and the human body is evidently much more complex. As long ago as 1890, The Times newspaper commented that knowledge 'had already become too vast to be manageable'. Today, nobody is an expert in the whole of anything.
options: ① Knowledge in Islands: Missing the Whole Picture
② Cell Types: The Secret Key to Modern Science
③ Dividing Lines: The Engine of Mastery
④ Expertise as a Gateway to Comprehensive Science
⑤ Only Specialists Truly Understand the Human Body
explanation: 이 글은 현대 과학의 지식이 너무나 방대해지고 전문화됨에 따라 인체를 통합적으로 연구하지 못하고 각 분야가 고립된(silos) 상태로 연구되고 있는 문제점을 지적하고 있습니다. 지식이 파편화되어 전체적인 맥락을 놓치고 있다는 내용을 가장 잘 담고 있는 제목은 ①번 '섬에 갇힌 지식: 전체 그림을 놓치다'입니다.
options_translation: ① 섬에 갇힌 지식: 전체 그림을 놓치다
② 세포 유형: 현대 과학의 비밀 열쇠
③ 구분선: 숙달의 엔진
④ 종합 과학으로 가는 관문으로서의 전문 지식
⑤ 오직 전문가만이 진정으로 인체를 이해한다

question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Statistics in the twentieth century became the systematic collection of quantitative information needed by the state. This process occurred in all the industrialised countries as a key part of their becoming modern states. Desrosières writes: "It is difficult to think simultaneously that the objects being measured do exist and that this is only a convention". Yet this is the case. Phenomena such as prices being charged and products being sold exist, but the categories and classification frameworks supporting the collection, aggregation, and organisation of official statistics are devised to serve the purposes of the state, for macroeconomic or for social policies. Theodore Porter described the use of statistics to create state authority: "Quantification is a way of making decisions without seeming to decide", characterising it as a "social technology" intended to build trust in authority.
options: ① Numbers as the State's Compass: Steering Society through Statistics
② When Statistics Act: Unbiased Measures Driving Industrial Growth
③ Quantification as an Impediment to the State's Economic Prosperity
④ The Essential Social Role of Statistics: Fostering Cohesion and Equity
⑤ Numerical Data as Purely Factual Evidence: Desrosières' Perspective
explanation: 이 글은 20세기 통계가 국가의 목적(거시 경제, 사회 정책)을 위해 체계적으로 수집되었으며, 국가 권위를 구축하고 결정을 내리는 '사회적 기술'로 활용되었음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 국가의 나침반으로서 통계를 통해 사회를 이끌어간다는 ①번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 국가의 나침반으로서의 숫자: 통계를 통해 사회를 조종하기
② 통계가 작동할 때: 산업 성장을 이끄는 편향되지 않은 척도
③ 국가 경제 번영의 장애물로서의 수량화
④ 통계의 필수적인 사회적 역할: 화합과 형평성 촉진
⑤ 순수하게 사실적인 증거로서의 수치 데이터: Desrosières의 관점

question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
passage: Conditioned Place Preference is a way of finding out what an animal wants. Researchers train an animal to associate one place with an experience such as food or a loud noise and another place with something completely different, usually where nothing happens. The two places are made obviously different to make it as easy as possible for the animal to associate each place with what happened to ⓐ<u>it</u> there. ⓑ<u>Its</u> preference for being in one place or another is measured both before and after its experiences in the two places. If there is a shift in where the animal chooses to spend its time for the reward, this suggests that it liked the experience and is trying to repeat ⓒ<u>it</u>. Conversely, it might avoid the place the stimulus appeared and start to prefer the place where ⓓ<u>it</u> did not experience it. Then this suggests that ⓔ<u>it</u> found the stimulus unpleasant. For example, an animal with cancer shows a preference for the place where it has been given morphine, a drug used to relieve pain, rather than where it has received saline, whereas a healthy one developed no such preference. This suggests that the animal with cancer wanted the morphine.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 실험 대상인 '동물(animal)'을 가리킵니다. 반면, ⓒ는 동물이 반복하려고 하는 대상인 '그 경험(the experience)'을 가리키므로 지칭하는 대상이 다릅니다.

question: 4. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 fear of isolation trumps the need to be heard가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: As a political researcher in Germany, Noelle-Neumann observed that during election campaigns, certain views seemed to get more play than others, and sometimes people muted their opinions rather than expressing them, especially if those opinions were perceived to be unpopular. This means that from an individual's perspective, avoiding social exclusion is more important than following one's own judgment. Noelle-Neumann calls this the spiral of silence. The spiral of silence occurs when individuals who perceive that their opinions are popular express them, whereas those who do not think their opinions are popular remain quiet. This process occurs in a spiral, so that one side of an issue ends up with considerable publicity and the other side with very little. In everyday life, people express their opinions in a variety of ways: they talk about them, they wear buttons, they put bumper stickers on their cars, and they post their views on social media. According to this theory, people are more apt to do these kinds of things when they perceive that others share their opinions. Ultimately, <u>fear of isolation trumps the need to be heard</u>. *trump: 이기다
options: ① People typically express insincere opinions to avoid being left out.
② Overcoming isolation requires actively listening to others' perspectives.
③ Fostering a social environment that values diverse opinions is very challenging.
④ People tend to suppress opinions because social rejection outweighs the desire to express.
⑤ The general public is inclined to embrace new and innovative opinions to gain massive publicity.
explanation: 밑줄 친 'fear of isolation trumps the need to be heard'(고립에 대한 공포가 의견을 표출하려는 욕구를 이긴다)는 것은, 사람들이 자신의 의견이 인기가 없다고 느낄 때 사회적으로 소외되는 것을 두려워하여 자신의 의견을 드러내기보다 침묵하는 현상인 '침묵의 나선' 이론을 설명하는 핵심 문장입니다. 따라서 사회적 거부(고립)에 대한 두려움이 의견 표현 욕구보다 더 크기 때문에 의견을 억제한다는 ④번이 가장 적절한 해석입니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들은 소외되는 것을 피하기 위해 보통 거짓스러운 의견을 표현한다.
② 고립을 극복하는 것은 다른 사람들의 견해를 적극적으로 경청하는 것을 필요로 한다.
③ 다양한 의견을 가치 있게 여기는 사회적 환경을 조성하는 것은 매우 힘든 일이다.
④ 사회적 거절이 표현하고자 하는 욕구보다 더 크기 때문에 사람들은 의견을 억제하는 경향이 있다.
⑤ 일반 대중은 대중적인 홍보를 얻기 위해 새롭고 혁신적인 의견을 수용하는 경향이 있다.

question: 6. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Distinguishing moths from butterflies on outward appearance is not always easy, but there are a few rules of thumb that can help. In most butterflies the antennae end with a small club-shaped swelling, whereas in moths they are usually feathery or narrow to a fine tip. Butterflies tend to rest with their wings held shut above their body, whereas moths more usually rest with the upper sides of the wings on full view. Further distinctions can be made by looking for a tiny hook that joins fore- and hindwings, (a feature only present in moths. The stereotypical differences, with moths cast as the gloomy, nocturnal cousins of colourful sun-loving butterflies are simply wrong. There are many brightly coloured moths and many which are active throughout the day. Equally, there are a few nocturnal butterflies and plenty that come clothed in shades of brown and grey. It's more sensible to think of them together; both butterflies and moths are beautiful and fascinating insects.
options: ① While butterfly antennae usually end in a small club-like tip, moth antennae are commonly feathery or sharply pointed.
② Moths and butterflies rest their wings differently, with butterflies usually holding them closed above their bodies and moths typically keeping them spread out.
③ Moths feature a little hook connecting their forewings and hindwings, which is one method to tell them apart from butterflies.
④ Contrary to common stereotypes, both moths and butterflies can vary in color, ranging from dark to bright.
⑤ Moths, the ecological cousins of butterflies, are mostly nocturnal, so they can often be distinguished from butterflies by their active hours.
explanation: 지문에서 나방은 야행성이고 나비는 대낮에 활동한다는 고정관념은 틀렸다고 했습니다. 나방 중에도 낮에 활동하는 것이 많고 나비 중에도 야행성이 있기 때문입니다. 따라서 활동 시간으로 나방과 나비를 구별할 수 있는 경우가 많다는 ⑤번은 글 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 나비의 더듬이는 보통 작은 곤봉 모양의 끝으로 끝나지만, 나방의 더듬이는 흔히 깃털 모양이거나 날카롭게 파져 있습니다.
② 나방과 나비는 날개를 쉬게 하는 방식이 다릅니다. 나비는 보통 몸의 위로 접고 있고, 나방은 활짝 펼쳐 놓습니다.
③ 나방은 앞날개와 뒷날개를 연결하는 작은 갈고리를 가지고 있으며, 이는 나비와 구별하는 한 가지 방법입니다.
④ 일반적으로는 고정관념과 다르게, 나방과 나비 모두 어두운 색부터 밝은 색까지 다양한 색상을 띨 수 있습니다.
⑤ 나비의 생태학적 사촌인 나방은 대부분 야행성이므로 활동 시간으로 나비와 구별하는 경우가 많습니다.

question: 8. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말은?
passage: Even though sea creatures live in seawater, they still need to take in water for their bodies to function properly. They just need to get rid of any extra salt it might bring with it. Salt absorbs water like a sponge. For example, if you put a tiny mountain of salt on a small plate and add some water so that it touches the salt, the salt will absorb the water and grow larger. The same principle applies to sea creatures. If the body fluids in a sea animal are saltier than the seawater it lives in, the extra salt in the animal's body will draw in seawater, which can cause the animal to swell. On the other hand, if the seawater is saltier than the animal's body fluids, the extra salt in the water will pull water out of the animal's body, causing it to dehydrate and shrink. This demonstrates that the ____________ of salt in a sea creature's body fluids and seawater is crucial for the animal to stay healthy and to ensure proper regulation of its body fluids for survival.
options: ① quality
② pressure
③ exchange
④ component
⑤ equilibrium
explanation: 지문은 삼투압 원리에 의해 바다 생물의 체액과 바닷물 사이의 염분 농도 차이가 물의 이동을 유발하여 몸이 붓거나 탈수되는 현상을 설명합니다. 생물이 건강을 유지하고 생존하기 위해 체액 조절을 적절히 하려면 염분의 '균형(equilibrium)'이 중요하다는 결론이 가장 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 품질
② 압력
③ 교환
④ 구성 요소
⑤ 평형(균형)

question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말은?
passage: Viewing time as a purchasable and consistent product cemented artificial views on time into our psyche, but every now and again we are forced to acknowledge this mistake. On twenty-six occasions in the last fifty years, a second has been added to everyone's day to adjust for the Earth wobbling and the rate of its spin changing. For instance, when El Niño, a climatic system in the Pacific, causes wind speed to change dramatically, it can slow the rotation of the Earth slightly. Indeed, the Earth's spin is generally slowing because the moon's gravity is acting as a drag, so days are getting longer by about 1.7 milliseconds per century. Such occurrences ___________________________________________. When events like this happen, a bunch of humans make the decision to add a small slice of time to your day, without your knowledge. We try to force our fixed, man-made view of time onto nature in the false hope that it will yield. It doesn't.
options: ① illustrate that the Earth's rotation does not significantly influence human conception of the universe
② make it impossible to keep the usual clock time exactly lined up with the Earth's irregular rotation time
③ encourage the concept of human-devised time to seem more valid and convincing than natural time
④ compel people to exhibit greater flexibility and yield to the official time standard
⑤ cause humans to recognize that the Earth's spin shapes our daily routine
explanation: 지문은 인간이 시간의 개념을 고정되고 인위적인 것으로 여기지만, 실제 지구의 자전 속도는 엘니뇨나 달의 중력 같은 자연적 요인에 의해 변한다는 점을 설명합니다. 이러한 자연적인 변화들(Such occurrences) 때문에 우리가 정한 일정한 시계 시간을 지구의 불규칙한 자전 속도에 정확히 맞추는 것이 불가능해지며(make it impossible to keep the usual clock time exactly lined up with the Earth's irregular rotation time), 이에 따라 인위적으로 '윤초'를 추가하는 등의 조정이 필요하게 됩니다. 따라서 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 지구의 자전이 우주에 대한 인간의 개념에 큰 영향을 미치지 않는다는 것을 보여준다
