explanation: 지문의 전체적인 내용은 물리학에서 측정 단위(피트, 미터 등)나 온도 척도(화씨, 섭씨 등)의 선택은 물리학의 법칙 자체를 바꾸지 않으며, 이러한 선택은 단지 묘사의 편의를 위한 것일 뿐 그 자체가 본질적이거나 근본적인 것은 아니라는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 척도의 선택은 '근본적인(fundamental)' 선택이 아니라 '임의적인(arbitrary)' 혹은 '비본질적인' 선택이라고 해야 문맥상 자연스럽습니다.

question: 9. According to the passage, which of the following questions cannot be answered?
passage: Even though sea creatures live in it, they still need to take in water for their bodies to function properly. They just need to get rid of any extra salt it might bring with it. Salt absorbs water like a sponge. If you put a tiny mountain of salt on a small plate, then add enough water to the side, making sure an edge touches the salt, the salt will absorb the water. Now you have a pile of wet salt. Notice that it has increased in size. The same principle applies to sea creatures. If the body fluids in a sea animal are saltier than the seawater it lives in, then the extra salt in the creature's body will absorb seawater. This can cause them to swell up. On the other hand, if the amount of salt in the seawater is higher than the amount of salt in the body fluids of a sea animal, the extra salt in the water will draw fluids out of the creature's body, causing it to dehydrate and shrink.
options: ① What unnecessary thing do sea creatures have to filter out of the water they consume?
② What common item does the passage state that salt acts like when it absorbs water?
③ What specific physiological structure do marine organisms employ to remove the excess salt they take in from the water?
④ Based on the plate experiment described, what is the visible indicator that salt successfully drew in the moisture?
⑤ If the solute level of the habitat water is elevated compared to the internal fluids of a creature, what physical change may occur in the animal's body size?
explanation: 지문에는 바다 생물이 여분의 소금을 제거해야 한다는 필요성과 삼투 현상의 원리는 설명되어 있지만, 구체적으로 '어떤 신체 구조(physiological structure)'를 사용하여 소금을 배출하는지에 대한 설명은 나와 있지 않다.
options_translation: ① 바다 생물이 섭취하는 물에서 걸러내야 하는 불필요한 것은 무엇인가?
② 본문에서 소금이 물을 흡수할 때 어떤 흔한 물건처럼 행동한다고 기술하는가?
③ 해양 생물이 물에서 섭취한 과도한 소금을 제거하기 위해 어떤 특정 생리적 구조를 사용하는가?
④ 묘사된 접시 실험에 근거하여, 소금이 습기를 성공적으로 끌어당겼다는 것을 보여주는 가시적인 지표는 무엇인가?
⑤ 서식지 물의 용질 농도가 생물의 내부 체액에 비해 높으면 생물의 몸 크기에 어떤 물리적 변화가 일어날 수 있는가?

question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We can discard or replace a scientific theory only if we have a better way of explaining the evidence that supports it. The theories of Newton and Einstein offer great examples. A vast body of evidence supports Newton's theory of gravity, but by the late nineteenth century scientists had begun to discover cases where its predictions did not perfectly match observations. These discrepancies were explained only when Einstein developed his general theory of relativity, which was able to match the observations. Still, the many successes of Newton's theory could not be ignored, and Einstein's theory would not have gained acceptance if it had not been able to explain these successes equally well. It did, and that is why we now view Einstein's theory as a broader theory of gravity than Newton's theory. Some scientists today are seeking a theory of gravity that will go beyond Einstein's. If any new theory ever gains acceptance, it will have to ______________________ as well as work in new realms where Einstein's theory does not.
options: ① focus solely on unexplored cosmic phenomena
② deny the assumptions underlying Einstein's theory
③ eliminate the need to verify Einstein's theory
④ explain the confirmed successes of Einstein's theory
⑤ ignore the astronomical observations of Einstein's theory
explanation: 지문은 새로운 과학 이론이 기존 이론을 대체하기 위해서는 기존 이론이 설명했던 성공 사례들을 똑같이 잘 설명할 수 있어야 함을 강조하고 있습니다. 아인슈타인의 이론이 뉴턴의 이론을 대체할 수 있었던 것도 뉴턴 이론의 성공을 설명할 수 있었기 때문이므로, 아인슈타인 이후의 새로운 이론 역시 아인슈타인 이론의 확인된 성공 사례들을 설명할 수 있어야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 오로지 탐구되지 않은 우주 현상에만 초점을 맞춰야 한다
② 아인슈타인 이론의 근간이 되는 가정들을 부정해야 한다
③ 아인슈타인 이론을 검증할 필요성을 없애야 한다
④ 아인슈타인 이론의 확인된 성공 사례들을 설명해야 한다
⑤ 아인슈타인 이론의 천문학적 관측 결과들을 무시해야 한다

question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Imagine pausing in the middle of a busy day, taking a moment to refresh your mind and recharge your energy. This power of a midday break is often underestimated. When you break away from routine, especially with activities designed to stimulate your brain, you prevent cognitive tiredness and enhance productivity for the rest of the day. Neurobic exercises ─ simple yet effective ─ are perfect for such breaks. They target different areas of your brain, keeping it agile and alert. These exercises create a mental oasis that refreshes and prepares you for the afternoon's challenges. This strategic pause is not just a break; _______________________. Even briefly experimenting with neurobic exercises can work wonders for your cognitive state during lunch. Start with using your non-dominant hand for routine tasks like writing or eating. This simple switch challenges your brain, activating pathwaysthat aren't typically engaged and promoting greater flexibility in thinking.
options: ① it functions only as a momentary escape from stress
② it merely postpones the tiredness you will face later on
③ it distracts you from the tasks that truly matter
④ it interrupts your workflow without offering real benefits
⑤ it acts as a meaningful investment in your mental sharpness
explanation: 이 글은 일과 중의 휴식, 특히 뇌를 자극하는 '뉴로빅 운동'을 포함한 휴식이 인지적 피로를 방지하고 생산성을 높여준다고 설명합니다. 따라서 이러한 전략적인 중단은 단순한 휴식을 넘어 정신적 예리함(mental sharpness)을 위한 의미 있는 투자가 된다는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그것은 단지 스트레스로부터의 일시적인 탈출구로만 기능한다
② 그것은 단지 당신이 나중에 직면하게 될 피로를 연기할 뿐이다
③ 그것은 정말로 중요한 업무로부터 당신의 주의를 분산시킨다
④ 그것은 실질적인 이점 제공 없이 당신의 업무 흐름을 방해한다
⑤ 그것은 당신의 정신적 예리함에 대한 의미 있는 투자 역할을 한다

question: 17. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Within liberal culture, the value of fair equality of opportunity for individuals outweighs the preservation of the family's integrity. In contrast, for Confucian culture, while seeking fair equality of opportunity for individuals is important, the family assumes a fundamental role in human flourishing, and living within a family institution is considered the essential way of life. Individuals are primarily understood as family members before they are regarded as state citizens. Therefore, for Confucians, the family possesses inherent value that should never be abandoned, even if it results in certain societal inequalities. Some cultures, like the liberal one, may choose to impose increasing restrictions on the role of families and implement more egalitarian government programs for education, healthcare, and other positive rights in society in the pursuit of fair equality of opportunity. On the other hand, other cultures, like the Confucian one, may prefer to primarily assign welfare responsibilities to the family, accepting inequalities stemming from the existence of the family as long as everyone's basic freedoms and rights are safeguarded in the state.
summary_sentence: While liberal culture (A)__________ equal opportunity even at the expense of family authority, Confucian culture treats the family as an essential institution whose intrinsic value (B)__________ certain social inequalities.
options: ① provides - eliminates
② questions - intensifies
③ prioritizes - justifies
④ discourages - tolerates
⑤ limits - acknowledges
explanation: 자유주의 문화는 가족의 권위보다 개인의 기회 균등을 우선시(prioritizes)하는 반면, 유교 문화는 가족을 필수적인 제도로 여기며 가족의 내재적 가치가 그로부터 발생하는 사회적 불평등을 정당화(justifies)하거나 수용한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 'prioritizes', (B)에는 'justifies'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 제공하다 - 제거하다
② 의문을 제기하다 - 강화하다
③ 우선순위에 두다 - 정당화하다
④ 낙담시키다 - 용인하다
⑤ 제한하다 - 인정하다

question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Waste has historically been seen as a necessary driver of the economy. Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is. directly dependent on the demand for that product. Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be wasted, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be sustained. Many strategies have been incorporated into product design and use to ensure that waste is inevitable, such as planned obsolescence, limited access to tools for repairs, and use of cheap materials. All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a replacement. Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that prioritizing the elimination of waste via repair and remanufacturing creates a different kind of demand: products as a service. Through this setup, companies simply lease out products that were once sold directly to the customer. With this transition of ownership, companies maintain profit by offering maintenance and repair services and are encouraged to develop long-lasting products.
summary_sentence: An older tactic of shortening an item's usefulness to (A)_________ repeat purchases is being replaced by a system where (B)_________ its use lets firms retain control and gain revenue through ongoing oversight.
options: ① deter - expanding
② prompt - sustaining
③ drive - diminishing
④ inhibit - prolonging
⑤ encourage - expending
explanation: 과거에는 반복 구매를 유도(prompt/drive/encourage)하기 위해 제품 수명을 단축시키는 전략을 썼으나, 최근에는 제품을 서비스로서 임대하고 그 사용을 지속(sustaining)하게 함으로써 기업이 통제권을 유지하고 수익을 창출하는 시스템으로 바뀌고 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 유도하다는 뜻의 'prompt', (B)에는 지속한다는 뜻의 'sustaining'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 저지하다 - 확장하는 것
② 유도하다 - 지속하는 것
③ 추진하다 - 감소시키는 것
④ 억제하다 - 연장하는 것
⑤ 권장하다 - 소비하는 것

question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There are numerous ways wildlife is managed, but they all imply stewardship and can be classified into two broad categories: active management and inactive management.
ordered_passages: (A) If population numbers are too low for the goal of management agencies, other active management can be incorporated, such as predator control to minimize neonatal deaths or habitat improvement to provide required cover for neonates from predators. These efforts represent active approaches to management.

(B) Active management does something to the population ─ such as increasing or decreasing its size ─ in a direct manner through strategies like translocations or hunting, respectively. Populations can also be actively managed by altering the habitat to the benefit or disadvantage of a population.

(C) Other populations may not be actively managed, like those in national parks. In such situations, management activities minimize external influences on populations and habitat, which often involves management of humans and not animals.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 야생 동물 관리의 두 가지 범주인 적극적 관리와 소극적 관리를 소개하고 있습니다. (B)에서는 적극적 관리의 정의와 예시(개체 수 조절, 서식지 변경)를 설명하며 시작합니다. (A)는 (B)에서 언급된 적극적 관리의 또 다른 예시(포식자 조절, 서식지 개선)를 상술하고 있으므로 (B) 다음에 오는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 적극적 관리를 하지 않는 경우(소극적 관리)의 예시로 국립공원을 들며 내용을 마무리하므로 정답은 (B)-(A)-(C)입니다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Just as an expert in the taste and colour of wine will gain much by being aware of the chemistry that underlies those qualities, so each perspective on the body can potentially enhance the others. And yet every scientific tool, from microscopes to mathematics, and every aspect of the body, from the brain to the microorganism, requires such depth of expertise that this tends not to happen: we tend to study the human body in silos, each community sectioned from the others by its own specialised vocabulary. Research communities may be dedicated to one type of scientific tool or a specific component of the body, such as one type of cell. How different types of cell communicate with one an other becomes its own specialist topic. Even simple forms of life on Earth are now rarely studied as a whole, and the human body is evidently much more complex. As long ago as 1890, The Times newspaper commented that knowledge 'had already become too vast to be manageable'. Today, nobody is an expert in the whole of anything.
options: ① Scientific tools have made broad study less necessary because specialization leads to faster discoveries.
② Scientific knowledge has grown so complex that research focuses on narrow areas, limiting integrated understanding of the body.
③ Modern science helps society by organizing research into separate groups of experts, each with its own specialized language.
④ Understanding the chemistry of wine is a model for how scientific knowledge replaces intuition.
⑤ The human body is simpler than assumed, but researchers complicate it by inventing specialized terminology.
explanation: 이 글은 현대 과학 지식이 너무 방대해져서 연구자들이 자신의 전문 분야에만 매몰되어(silos), 인체를 전체적으로 통합하여 이해하는 것이 어려워졌다는 점을 지적하고 있습니다. 지식이 관리하기에 너무 방대해졌고, 아무도 전체에 대한 전문가가 아니라는 내용이 핵심입니다.
options_translation: ① 전문화가 더 빠른 발견으로 이어지기 때문에 과학 도구들은 광범위한 연구의 필요성을 줄였다.
② 과학 지식이 너무 복잡해져서 연구가 좁은 분야에 집중되어 인체에 대한 통합적인 이해를 제한하고 있다.
③ 현대 과학은 연구를 각기 다른 전문 언어를 가진 별도의 전문가 집단으로 조직함으로써 사회를 돕는다.
④ 와인의 화학적 성질을 이해하는 것은 과학적 지식이 어떻게 직관을 대체하는지에 대한 모델이다.
⑤ 인체는 가정보다 단순하지만, 연구자들은 전문적인 용어를 만들어냄으로써 그것을 복잡하게 만든다.

question: 1. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 For all the logical arguments against this ceaseless upgrading, the temptation remains compelling이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Manufacturers masterfully sow seeds of doubt about the adequacy of our current devices. Suddenly, the phone that was your lifeline a year ago is now a museum piece, unable to keep pace with your digital demands. And thus, the itch to upgrade begins, often before there's a genuine need. This cycle isn't just confined to our digital companions. It spills over into almost every aspect of consumer electronics, from the self-driving car to the smart fridge. Every product seems to be on an unstoppable march towards the next version, the next generation that promises to revolutionize your life. What's fascinating, or perhaps disturbing, is the utter efficacy of this cycle in shaping our desires. It's not so much that we want the newest device; we're led to believe we need it. The distinction between want and need blurs, shifting our financial priorities in favor of staying current with trends. <u>For all the logical arguments against this ceaseless upgrading, the temptation remains compelling</u>.
options: ① Consumers consciously reject the illusion of innovation.
② The drive to upgrade is dictated solely by cognitive rationality.
③ The realization of rationality automatically eliminates consumers' impulses.
④ Rational awareness does not necessarily free us from aspiration for advancement.
⑤ Human reasoning can logically leads to the arguments between manufacturers and consumers.
explanation: 이 글은 제조업자들이 소비자들에게 현재 기기가 부족하다는 의구심을 심어주어 끊임없이 업그레이드하도록 유도하는 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. 밑줄 친 문장은 '이러한 끊임없는 업그레이드에 반대하는 모든 논리적인 주장에도 불구하고, 그 유혹은 여전히 강력하다'는 뜻입니다. 이는 소비자들이 머리로는 업그레이드가 불필요하다는 것을 알면서도(이성적 인식), 최신 제품을 갖고 싶어 하는 욕망(발전에 대한 열망)에서 벗어나지 못함을 의미하므로 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 소비자들은 혁신의 환상을 의식적으로 거부한다.
② 업그레이드하려는 동기는 전적으로 인지적 합리성에 의해 결정된다.
③ 합리성을 깨닫는 것이 자동으로 소비자의 충동을 제거한다.
④ 합리적 인식이 반드시 발전에 대한 열망으로부터 우리를 자유롭게 해주는 것은 아니다.
⑤ 인간의 추론은 논리적으로 제조업자와 소비자 사이의 논쟁으로 이어질 수 있다.

question: 2. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 past worries about automation이 의미하는 바에 해당하는 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
passage: The future of work depends on two forces: a harmful substituting force and a helpful complementing one. Many tales have a hero and a villain fighting each other for dominance, but in our story, technology plays both roles at once, displacing workers while simultaneously raising the demand for their efforts elsewhere in the economy. This interaction helps explain why <u>past worries about automation</u> were misplaced: our ancestors had predicted the wrong winner in that fight, underestimating quite how powerful the complementing force would prove to be or simply ignoring that factor altogether. It also helps to explain why economists have traditionally been dismissive of the idea of technological unemployment: there appeared to be firm limits to the substituting force, leaving lots of tasks that could not be performed by machines, and a growing demand for human beings to do them instead.
explanation: 지문에서 '자동화에 대한 과거의 걱정'은 기술의 '대체하는 힘(substituting force)'만을 고려하고 '보완하는 힘(complementing one)'을 간과하여, 기계가 인간의 일자리를 모두 빼앗아 갈 것이라고 우려했던 상황을 지칭합니다. ⓐ는 로봇이 일자리를 대체할 것이라는 걱정, ⓒ는 셀프 계산대가 캐셔를 대체하여 일자리를 잃는 구체적 사례로, 두 보기 모두 기술의 대체 작용으로 인한 부정적 걱정만을 담고 있어 정답입니다. 반면 ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 기술이 새로운 수요를 창출하거나 인간을 보완한다는 긍정적 측면(complementing force)을 포함하고 있습니다.

question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Imagine that your usually stingy friend delights in buying you a Christmas present after taking a generosity booster. How would you feel? Undoubtedly, there is something praiseworthy about the action. You'd be pleased to receive the gift. You'd say 'thank you', and mean it. But his change of heart is not entirely satisfying. According to Zagzebski, an American philosopher, he is not really generous. When we praise someone's character, we use words for various virtues: 'generous', 'kind', 'courageous', etc. A person who gives one gift isn't generous. Instead, generosity is a stable part of a person's 'moral identity', an emotional habit that is part of who you are. Thus virtues, as opposed to nontypical impulse, are the result of your personal history. They are part of who you are, as they are part of how your character was formed. Instant virtue is therefore impossible. Popping a pill cannot make you a better person.
options: ① benefits resulting from taking pills for spontaneous attitude
② virtues through one's accumulation of consistent behaviors
③ external acquisition of goodness without inner transformation
④ risks of attempting to cultivate virtues with emotional habits
⑤ temporary manifestation of virtue independent of moral development

question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When a cell divides, the genomes of its two daughters are often not quite identical to each other or to that of the parent cell. On rare occasions, the error may represent a change for the better; more probably, it will cause no significant difference in the cell's prospects. But in some cases, the error will cause serious damage; for example, by disrupting the coding sequence for a key protein. Changes due to mistakes of the first type will tend to be perpetuated, because the altered cell has an increased likelihood of reproducing itself. Changes due to mistakes of the second type - neutral changes - may be perpetuated or not: it is a matter of chance whether the altered cell or its cousins will succeed. But changes that cause serious damage lead nowhere: the cell that suffers them dies, leaving no progeny. Through endless repetition of this cycle of mutation and natural selection organisms evolve: their genetic specifications change, sometimes giving organisms new ways to exploit the environment more effectively, to survive in competition with others, and to reproduce successfully.
options: ① Why Beneficial Mutations Are Rarely Preserved
② How Harmful Mutations Drive Evolutionary Progress
③ How Cells Eliminate All Genetic Errors During Division
④ Hidden Battles Inside Cells: The Quiet Engine of Evolution
⑤ The Restoration Processes That Lead to Genetic Advancement

passage: Distinguishing moths from butterflies on outward appearance is not always easy, but there are a few rules of thumb that can help. Butterflies tend to rest with their wings held shut above their body, whereas moths almost always rest with the upper sides of the wings on full view. Further distinctions can be made by looking for a tiny hook that joins fore - and hindwings, a feature only present in moths. The stereotypical differences, with moths cast as the gloomy, nocturnal cousins of colourful sun-loving butterflies are simply wrong. There are many brightly coloured moths and many which are active throughout the day. Equally, there are a few nocturnal butterflies and plenty that come clothed in shades of brown and grey. It's more sensible to think of them together; both butterflies and moths are beautiful and fascinating insects.

passage: According to Hobbes, man is not a being who can act morally in spite of his instinct to protect his existence in the state of nature. Hence, the only place where morality and moral liberty will begin to find an application begins in a place where a sovereign power, namely the state, emerges. Hobbes thus describes the state of nature as a circumstance in which man's life is "solitary, poor, nasty, brutish and short". It means when people live without a general power to control them all, they are indeed in a state of war. In other words, Hobbes, who accepted that human beings are not social and political beings in the state of nature, believes that without the power human beings in the state of nature are "antisocial and rational based on their selfishness". Moreover, since society is not a natural phenomenon and there is no natural force bringing people together, what will bring them together as a society is not mutual affection according to Hobbes. It is, rather, mutual fear of men's present and future that assembles them, since the cause of fear is a common drive among people in the state of nature.

Soon, at some point, the amount of traffic grows too large for the "commons" to support. Traffic jams and overcrowding lessen the benefits of the common resource for everyone - the tragedy of the commons! If the new resource cannot be expanded or provided with additional space, it becomes a problem, and you cannot solve the problem on your own, in isolation from your fellow drivers or walkers or competing users. The total activity on this new resource keeps increasing, and so does individual activity; but if the dynamic of common use and overuse continues too long, both begin to fall after a peak, leading to a crash. What makes the "tragedy of commons" tragic is the crash dynamic - the destruction or degeneration of the common resource's ability to regenerate itself.
summary_sentence: Common resources initially benefit individuals but (A)__________ causes congestion, reduced value, and eventual collapse when the resource can no longer (B)__________ itself.
options: ① misuse / decrease
② overuse / sustain
③ expansion / extend
④ optimization / exploit
⑤ mismanagement / destruct
explanation: 공유 자원은 초기에는 개인들에게 이익을 주지만, 과도하게 사용(overuse)되면 혼잡과 가치 하락을 초래하며, 자원이 스스로를 유지(sustain)할 수 없게 될 때 결국 붕괴에 이르게 된다는 내용의 글입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 overuse, (B)에는 sustain이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 22. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Weber's law concerns the perception of difference between two stimuli. It suggests that we might not be able to detect a 1-mm difference when we are looking at lines 466 mm and 467 mm in length, but we may be able to detect a 1-mm difference when we are comparing a line 2 mm long with one 3 mm long. Another example of this principle is that we can detect 1 candle when it is lit in an otherwise dark room. But when 1 candle is lit in a room in which 100 candles are already burning, we may not notice the light from this candle. Therefore, the Just-noticeable difference (JND) varies as a function of the strength of the signals. For example, the JND is greater for very loud noises than it is for much more quiet sounds. When a sound is very weak, we can tell that another sound is louder, even if it is barely louder. When a sound is very loud, to tell that another sound is even louder, it has to be much louder. Thus, Weber's law means that it is harder to distinguish between two samples when those samples are larger or stronger levels of the stimuli.
summary_sentence: Weber's law states that the perception of difference between stimuli depends on their (A)__________ difference, so as the stimulus becomes stronger or larger, the just-noticeable difference (B)__________ making changes harder to detect.
options: ① proportional ... diminishes
② comparative ... stabilizes
③ absolute ... rises
④ constant ... expands
⑤ relative ... increases
explanation: 베버의 법칙(Weber's law)은 두 자극 사이의 차이를 인식하는 것이 자극의 '상대적(relative)' 차이에 달려 있음을 설명합니다. 자극이 강하거나 커질수록, 차이를 느끼기 위해 필요한 최소한의 변화량인 최소 식별 차이(JND) 또한 '증가(increases)'하게 되어 변화를 감지하기가 더 어려워진다는 것이 핵심 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 비례적인 ... 줄어든다
② 비교적인 ... 안정화된다
③ 절대적인 ... 상승한다
④ 일정한 ... 확장된다
⑤ 상대적인 ... 증가한다

question: 23. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: All human cultures mark the passing of time by the differences they observe in the world around them. Our choice of which differences to mark depends firstly on what we can observe and secondly on what is important in our lives.
ordered_passages: (A) Conversely, among the largely nomadic peoples of Arabia, for whom seasonal changes were less significant, the lunar calendar was a more sensible choice. That did not make it inevitable that Islam would use a lunar calendar and Roman Christianity a solar one.

(B) How we mark the differences - the shapes of our calendars and our rituals - depends on the connections we make between those two things. In the agricultural society of pre-modern Europe, where higher latitudes make the seasons easily observable, it was natural to monitor the solar cycle.

(C) Political and religious decisions were made from options limited by geography and lifestyle, filtered through tradition. As a result, the calendars adopted by different cultures reflect not only the environment they live in but also the values they chose to emphasize.
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 문화가 시간을 표시하는 기준이 '관찰 가능성'과 '중요도'에 달려 있다고 언급합니다. (B)에서 이를 '두 가지 요소 사이의 연결'로 받으며 농경 사회인 유럽의 사례(태양 주기)를 제시합니다. 이어지는 (A)에서 '반대로(Conversely)'를 사용하여 계절 변화가 덜 중요한 아라비아 유목민의 사례(태음력)를 대조적으로 보여줍니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 이러한 선택들이 지리, 생활 방식, 전통에 따른 결정이었음을 요약하며 결론을 맺는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 10월 36번]

question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 다음과 같이 요약하고자 한다. <조건>에 맞추어 영작하시오.
passage: Where scientific research is concerned, explanatory tales are expected to adhere closely to experimental data and to illuminate the regular and predictable features of experience. However, this paradigm sometimes conceals the fact that theories are deeply loaded with creative elements that shape the construction of research projects and the interpretations of evidence. Scientific explanations do not just relate a chronology of facts. They construct frameworks for systematically chosen data in order to provide a consistent and meaningful explanation of what is observed. Such constructions lead us to imagine specific kinds of subject matter in particular sorts of relations, and the storylines they inspire will prove more effective for analyzing some features of experience over others. When we neglect the creative contributions of such scientific imagination and treat models and interpretive explanations as straightforward facts - even worse, as facts including all of reality - we can blind ourselves to the limitations of a given model and fail to note its potential for misunderstanding a situation to which it ill applies.
summary_sentence: 과학적 설명은 자료와 해석을 형성하는 창의적 틀을 포함하며, 이러한 상상력을 무시하고 현실을 오해하는 것은 주어진 과학 모델의 한계를 간과하게 한다.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 단어 및 어구를 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것.
<보기>의 어형 변형 불가.
<보기>의 콤마(,)를 반드시 쓸 것.
본문에 있는 단어 1개만 찾아 변형 없이 추가할 것.
vocabulary_box: scientific explanations / and misunderstanding reality / shaping data and interpretations, /
overlooking limits / of given scientific models /
answer: Scientific explanations involve creative frameworks shaping data and interpretations, and ignoring this imagination and misunderstanding reality leads to overlooking limits of given scientific models.
explanation: 본문에서 과학적 설명이 단순한 사실의 연대기가 아니라 창의적 틀(creative frameworks)을 구성한다는 점을 활용하여 요약문을 작성해야 합니다. <보기>의 단어들을 조합하고, 본문에서 'creative'라는 단어를 찾아 추가하여 완성할 수 있습니다. 'Scientific explanations involve creative frameworks shaping data and interpretations, and ignoring this imagination and misunderstanding reality leads to overlooking limits of given scientific models.'로 영작하면 조건에 부합합니다.

question: 1. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 The squeaky wheel gets the grease가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: As a political researcher in Germany, Noelle-Neumann observed that during election campaigns, certain views seemed to receive more attention than others, and sometimes people kept their opinions to themselves instead of expressing them, especially if those opinions were seen as unpopular. Noelle-Neumann calls this the spiral of silence. The spiral of silence occurs when people who believe their opinions are popular express them, while those who think their opinions are not popular stay quiet to avoid standing out. This process happens in a spiral, so that one side of an issue ends up with much publicity and the other side with very little. As the proverb goes, "<u>The squeaky wheel gets the grease</u>." In everyday life, people express their opinions in various ways - they talk about them, wear buttons, put bumper stickers on their cars, and share or post their views on social media. According to this theory, people are more apt to do these things when they think others agree with them.*squeaky: 끼익하는 소리가 나는 **grease: 기름, 윤활유
options: ① People who remain silent tend to be more respected.
② People who express unpopular opinions easily attract more attention.
③ Those who remain silent and confine their opinions to themselves are considered cautious.
④ People are likely to support unpopular opinions when they feel those views reflect their true beliefs.
⑤ Those who speak up tend to be noticed and heard, while silence often leads to receiving little attention.
explanation: 이 글은 침묵의 나선 이론을 설명하며, 자신의 의견이 다수라고 생각하는 사람들은 적극적으로 목소리를 내고, 소수라고 생각하는 사람들은 소외되지 않기 위해 침묵하는 경향을 설명하고 있습니다. 'The squeaky wheel gets the grease(삐걱거리는 바퀴가 기름을 얻는다)'라는 속담은 적극적으로 불만을 표하거나 목소리를 높이는 사람이 관심을 받게 된다는 의미입니다. 따라서 5번 '목소리를 내는 사람들이 주목을 받고 경청되는 경향이 있는 반면, 침묵은 흔히 적은 관심을 받는 결과로 이어진다'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 침묵을 지키는 사람들이 더 존경받는 경향이 있다.
② 대중적이지 않은 의견을 표현하는 사람들이 쉽게 더 많은 관심을 끈다.
③ 침묵을 지키고 자신의 의견을 가두어 두는 사람들은 신중한 것으로 여겨진다.
④ 사람들은 대중적이지 않은 의견이 자신의 진정한 신념을 반영한다고 느낄 때 그것을 지지할 가능성이 높다.
⑤ 목소리를 높이는 사람들이 주목받고 경청되는 경향이 있는 반면, 침묵은 종종 거의 관심을 받지 못하는 결과로 이어진다.

question: 2. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Consider units of measurement, a type of descriptive tool commonly ⓐ<u>used</u> in physics Spatial distances can be expressed in feet, meters, or any other unit, and the fundamental physical laws ⓑ<u>continue</u> to be the same no matter which unit is chosen. From this, we conclude that physics does not favor one unit of length over another, and any unit may be selected for convenience. Furthermore, any feature ⓒ<u>which</u> depends on this choice - for example, the numerical value assigned to the separation between two points - ⓓ<u>do</u> not exist independently of the chosen unit. Similarly, temperatures can be expressed using the Fahrenheit, Celsius, or Kelvin scales, and the physical principles involved remain ⓔ<u>unchanged</u> when using different scales. Thus, the choice of scale is entirely arbitrary, and any feature that relies on this choice is naturally scale-dependent.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'any feature'(단수)이며, 'which depends on this choice'는 관계대명사절로 주어를 수식합니다. 따라서 동사인 'do'는 단수 주어에 맞춰 'does'로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Treating time as something fixed and purchasable has established an unnatural view of it in our minds, but occasionally we are reminded that this belief is not correct. Over the past fifty years, for example, twenty-six leap seconds have been added to our clocks to compensate for the Earth's wobble and its ⓐ<u>uneven</u> rotation. Climate patterns such as El Niño can significantly alter wind speeds, which, as a result, slow the planet's spin. In fact, Earth's rotation has been gradually slowing due to the moon's gravitational pull, ⓑ<u>lengthening</u> our days by about 1.7 milliseconds per century. These fluctuations disturb the ⓒ<u>unpredictable</u> harmony we expect between human-made time measurement and the more ⓓ<u>dynamic</u> cycles shaped by Earth's motion. When such gaps appear, a small group of experts quietly decides to insert an extra moment into everyone's day. Yet we continue trying to apply our ⓔ<u>strict</u>, man-made idea of time to nature, hoping it will follow our rules. It never does. As the expression goes, "You can't put nature in a box."
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 인간이 만든 고정된 시간 체계와 실제 자연(지구의 회전 등)의 불규칙한 시간 사이의 간극을 설명하고 있습니다. 문맥상 우리가 기대하는 인간의 시간 측정과 지구의 역동적 주기 사이의 조화는 '예측 가능한(predictable)' 조화여야 하는데, 이러한 변동이 그 조화를 방해한다고 하는 것이 적절합니다. 따라서 ⓒ의 'unpredictable'을 'predictable'로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 6. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Imagine pausing in the middle of a busy day, taking a moment to refresh your mind and recharge your energy. This power of a midday break is often underestimated. When you break away from routine, especially with activities designed to stimulate your brain, you prevent cognitive tiredness and enhance productivity for the rest of the day. These exercises create a mental oasis that refreshes and prepares you for the afternoon's challenges. This strategic pause is not just a break; it boosts your cognitive capabilities, ensuring your mind remains sharp and focused. Even briefly experimenting with neurobic exercises can work wonders for your cognitive state during lunch. Start with using your nondominant hand for routine tasks like writing or eating. This simple switch challenges your brain, activating pathways that aren't typically engaged and promoting greater flexibility in thinking.

② Repeating the same habits during breaks leads to no change in your brain and hurts your ability to think.
③ Incorporating neurobic exercises into midday breaks serves as a strategic pause that effectively stimulates the brain and boosts cognitive productivity.
④ Refusing to try new things during free time limits your brain power and lowers your results.
⑤ Avoiding thinking activities during breaks can weaken your mind and stop your productivity.
explanation: 이 글은 낮 휴식 시간에 뉴로비(neurobic) 운동과 같은 뇌 자극 활동을 함으로써 인지적 피로림 방지하고 생산성을 높을   수 읈음을 강조하고 읈습니다.
options_translation: ① 아무런 댄전 없이 휴식을 취하는 것은 중중력을 해치고 뇌림 게으리게 만들어준다.
② 휴식 중에 동일한 습관을 반복하는 것은 뇌에 변화림 주준 않고 생각하는 능력을 해치게 된다.
③ 낮 휴식 시간에 뉴로비 운동을 포함시키는 것은 뇌림 효과적으로 자극하고 일지적 생산성을 높이는 술략적인 중단 역할을 한다.
④ 자유 시간에 새로운 것을 시도하기림 거부하는 것은 뇌의 힘을 제한하고 결과림 낮춘다.
⑤ 휴식 중에 사고 활동을 피하는 것은 정신을 약화시킬 수 읈고 생산성을 중단시킨다.

question: 7. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 Quantification is a way of making decisions without seeming to decide가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Statistics in the twentieth century became the systematic collection of quantitative information needed by the state. This process occurred in all the industrialised countries as a key part of their becoming modern states. Desrosieres writes: "It is difficult to think simultaneously that the objects being measured really do exist and that this is only a convention". Yet this is the case. Phenomena such as prices being charged and products being sold exist, but the categories and classification frameworks supporting the collection, aggregation, and organisation of official statistics are devised to serve the purposes of the state, for macroeconomic or for social policies. Theodore Porter described the use of statistics to create state authority: "<u>Quantification is a way of making decisions without seeming to decide</u>", characterising it as a "social technology" intended to build trust in authority.
options: ① By relying on numbers, authorities can frame their choices as objective outcomes of data rather than as deliberate decisions they themselves made.
② By ignoring numbers, authorities emphasize their choices as personal judgments made through direct experience alone.
③ By following public opinion, authorities allow citizens to determine outcomes instead of setting policies themselves.
④ By using numbers only for record-keeping, authorities keep decision-making entirely separate from statistical analysis.
⑤ By using numbers only as basic facts, authorities make their decisions without connecting them to data at all.
explanation: '계량화(Quantification)'는 통계적 수치를 통해 국가의 권위를 세우고 신늰를 구축하는 도구로 설명됩니다. 밑줄 친 붽분은 선택을 직접 내리는 것처럼 바이지 않윜면서 의사결정을 하는 방박이라고 하였으므로, 수치에 의존함으로써 권위자들이 자신의 주관적인 결정이 아닌 객관적인 데이터의 결과로 포장할 수 읈음을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 수치에 의존함써, 권위자들은 자신들이 내린 의도적인 결정이 아니라 데이터의 객관적인 결과로 그들의 선택을 구성할 수 읈다.
② 수치를 무시함써, 권위자들은 직접적인 경험만을 통해 내린 개인적 판단으로 자신들의 선택을 강조한다.
③ 여론을 따림써, 권위자들은 수숐로 정책을 정하는 대신 시물들이 결과를 결정하게 한다.
④ 기록 밑관옑으로만 수치를 사옑함써, 권위자들은 의사결정을 통계 뵄석과 완전히 뵄리한다.
⑤ 수치를 기밸적인 사실로만 사옑함써, 권위자들은 데이터와 전혐 연결하준 않고 결정을 내린다.

question: 9. 다음 굀의 내옑을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 땄, 빈셸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Within liberal culture, the value of fair equality of opportunity for individuals outweighs the preservation of the family's integrity. In contrast, for Confucian culture, while seeking fair equality of opportunity for individuals is important, the family assumes a fundamental role in human flourishing, and living within a family institution is considered the essential way of life. Individuals are primarily understood as family members before they are regarded as state citizens. Therefore, for Confucians, the family possesses inherent value that should never be abandoned, even if it results in certain societal inequalities. Some cultures, like the liberal one, may choose to impose increasing restrictions on the role of families and implement more egalitarian government programs for education, healthcare, and other positive rights in society in the pursuit of fair equality of opportunity. On the other hand, other cultures, like the Confucian one, may prefer to primarily assign welfare responsibilities to the family, accepting inequalities stemming from the existence of the family as long as everyone's basic freedoms and rights are safeguarded in the state.
summary_sentence: Liberal culture seeks fair equality of opportunity by (A)___________ state involvement and limiting the role of families, whereas Confucian culture views the family as the essential basis of human flourishing, (B)___________ it primary welfare responsibilities and accepting resulting inequalities as long as basic rights are protected.
options: ① reducinggiving
② expandingassigning
③ withdrawingdesignating
explanation: 자유주의 문화는 기회의 공정한 팑등을 촔구하기 윔해 국가의 개입(정부 프로그램 실행)을 확대하고 가중의 영활을 제한하는 반면, 유교 묳화는 가중을 복지 책임의 주체로 보고 가중에 복지 책임을 부여(할당)하며 그로 인한 뵈팑등을 수용합니다. (A)에는 expanding(확대하는), (B)에는 assigning(할당하는) 또는 giving(주는)이 적절하준대, 굀 성격상 ②이 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 줄이는 - 주는
② 확대하는 - 할당하는
③ 철회하는 - 지정하는

question: 10. 윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에 들어갈 말로 가장 알맞은 것끼리 짝지어진 것은?
passage: When your hand is hanging at your side and then you lift it, opposing muscles on your upper arm shorten and lengthen - contract and relax - to bend the elbow. Biceps contract, and triceps relax. Reversing the motion, when you drop your hand back down, muscles (A)[switch / maintain] roles. Triceps contract, and biceps relax. Lift your hand or drop it, and muscle shows what it is: a system of coordination, managed by orchestrated tension. As arms and legs rotate around joints, muscles activate and deactivate, contract and relax. All physical activity is paradoxical, in this sense: Movement depends on what muscles don't do, as much as it depends on what they do. Both are necessary, each in its time - and the same is true of each side of the pairs of concepts (B)[influenced / influencing] how we talk of muscles.Start with nature versus nurture: Some people are stronger or more muscular than others; is the difference inborn, or does it depend on what people do? To the latter question: What do you do? Do you have to lift weights, or is walking enough exercise? How should you do the exercise? Should you move fast or slowly? Lift heavy weights or lighter ones? (C)[In this way / Otherwise], basic questions about muscle may sound like they have one right answer. Oppositions can polarize. But where muscle is concerned, few oppositions are true polarities. Look closely, and most prove to be paradoxes. Born and made, heavy and light, fast and slow: _______________________________________.
options: ① maintain - influenced - Otherwise
② maintain - influencing - In this way
③ switch - influencing - In this way
④ switch - influenced - Otherwise
⑤ maintain - influenced - In this way
explanation: (A) 팔을 들어 올릴 때 이두근이 수축하고 삼두근이 이완하는 반면, 팔을 내릴 때는 그 역할이 뒤바뀌므로 'switch'가 적절합니다. (B) 문맥상 '근육에 관해 말하는 방식에 영향을 미치는(능동)' 개념의 쌍을 의미하므로 현재분사인 'influencing'이 적절합니다. (C) 앞서 언급된 질문들이 구체적인 답변을 요구하는 상황을 통해 근육에 관한 질문들이 정답이 하나인 것처럼 들리는 방식을 설명하므로 'In this way(이런 식으로)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 유지하다 - 영향을 받은 - 그렇지 않으면
② 유지하다 - 영향을 미치는 - 이런 식으로
③ 바뀌다 - 영향을 미치는 - 이런 식으로
④ 바뀌다 - 영향을 받은 - 그렇지 않으면
⑤ 유지하다 - 영향을 받은 - 이런 식으로

question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There are numerous ways wildlife is managed, but they all imply stewardship and can be classified into two broad categories: active management and inactive management.
ordered_passages: (A) Active management directly influences a population by increasing or decreasing its size through strategies such as translocations or hunting. It can also involve modifying the habitat to either support or limit the population.

(B) For instance, when population numbers fall below the goals established by management agencies, additional active measures can be applied. These may include predator control to reduce neonatal death rates or habitat improvements to provide essential shelter for young animals. Such actions therefore illustrate active management strategies.

(C) However, some populations, such as those in national parks, may not be actively managed. In these cases, management focuses on minimizing external influences on both the population and its habitat, often by regulating human activity rather than directly affecting the animals.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 야생 동물 관리의 두 가지 범주(능동적 관리와 비능동적 관리)를 소개합니다. (A)에서 능동적 관리의 정의와 직접적인 개체 수 조절 방식을 설명합니다. (B)는 'For instance'를 통해 능동적 관리의 구체적인 상황(개체 수가 목표치 미달일 때의 추가 조치 등)을 예로 들어 상술합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 'However'를 사용해 앞선 능동적 관리와 대조되는 비능동적 관리의 사례(국립공원 등)를 설명하며 마무리하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Historically, palaces weren't just homes; they were carefully constructed stages designed to impress and intimidate. While stone symbolized permanence and strength, glass offered something equally powerful: visibility. The introduction of large windows in palaces allowed rulers to literally look down upon their subjects, emphasizing their elevated position. Conversely, it also allowed subjects to gaze up at their leaders, creating a sense of awe and distance. Consider the Palace of Versailles: its Hall of Mirrors, lined with reflective surfaces, not only magnified the grandeur of the space but also placed the king at the center of a dazzling display, reinforcing his absolute authority. The use of glass in palaces wasn't merely aesthetic; it was strategic. Open sightlines allowed for better surveillance and control, ensuring the safety and security of the ruling family. Courtiers and visitors were constantly aware of being observed, contributing to an atmosphere of careful obedience and respect. The very architecture dictated social behavior, with glass acting as a silent enforcer of the power dynamic.
options: ① Seeing and Being Seen: The Power of Palace Glass
② Open Sightlines Encouraged Relaxed Freedom in Palaces
③ Palace Design Aimed to Bring Leaders and People Together
④ Palace Layout Encouraged Informal, Spontaneous Behavior
⑤ Glass Architecture Weakened Royal Influence Over People
explanation: 이 글은 과거 궁전에서 유리가 단순한 미적 요소가 아니라 권력을 과시하고 통제하기 위한 전략적 도구로 사용되었음을 설명하고 있습니다. 큰 창문을 통해 통치자는 백성을 내려다보고, 백성은 통치자를 우러러보게 함으로써 권위와 거리감을 조성했으며, 열린 시야를 통해 감시와 통제를 용이하게 했다는 내용입니다. 따라서 '보고 보이는 것: 궁전 유리의 힘'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 보고 보이는 것: 궁전 유리의 힘
② 열린 시야가 궁전 내의 편안한 자유를 장려했다
③ 궁전 설계는 지도자와 국민을 하나로 모으는 것을 목표로 했다
④ 궁전 배치는 비공식적이고 자발적인 행동을 권장했다
⑤ 유리 건축은 사람들에 대한 왕실의 영향력을 약화시켰다

question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Even though sea creatures live in seawater, they still need to take in water for their bodies to function properly. They just need to ⓐ<u>eliminate</u> any extra salt it might bring. Salt absorbs water like a sponge: for example, if you place a small pile of salt on a plate and add water until it ⓑ<u>reaches</u> the salt, the salt will draw in the water and swell. The same principle ⓒ<u>happens</u> in sea creatures. If a sea animal's body fluids are saltier than the surrounding seawater, the extra salt in its body will absorb water, causing the animal to swell. Conversely, if the seawater is saltier than the animal's body fluids, the extra salt in the water will ⓓ<u>pull</u> fluids from the bodies of sea creatures, which can result in their ⓔ<u>obtaining</u> water. This is why maintaining the right balance of salt and water is essential for their survival.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 바닷물이 동물의 체액보다 더 짤 경우, 물속의 소금이 동물의 몸에서 수분을 끌어내게 됩니다. 이로 인해 해양 생물은 수분을 얻는(obtaining) 것이 아니라 오히려 몸 안의 수분을 빼앗기게 되므로, ⓔ의 'obtaining'은 문맥상 'losing'이나 'dehydrating' 같은 표현으로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 본문에서 찾아 한 단어로 쓰시오. [3.3점]
passage: Distinguishing moths from butterflies on outward appearance is not always easy, but there are a few rules of thumb that can help. In most butterflies the antennae end with a small club-shaped swelling, whereas in moths they are usually feathery or narrow to a fine tip. Butterflies tend to rest with their wings held shut above their body, whereas moths more usually rest with the upper sides of the wings on full view. Further distinctions can be made by looking for a tiny hook that joins fore and hindwings, a feature only present in moths. The stereotypical differences, with moths cast as the gloomy, nocturnal cousins of colourful sun-loving butterflies are not correct. There are many brightly coloured moths and many which are active throughout the day. Equally, there are a few nocturnal butterflies and plenty that come clothed in shades of brown and grey. It's more sensible to think of them together; both butterflies and moths are beautiful and fascinating insects.
summary_sentence: Moths and butterflies can be differentiated by distinctions such as antennae shape wing position while resting, and a tiny wing hook found in moths, but the commonly assumed colour and activity differences are _____________, so both types are best recognized as diverse and fascinating insects.
explanation: 본문에서 나방과 나비에 대한 통념적인 차이(칙칙한 밤의 사촌 vs 화려한 태양을 사랑하는 나비)가 옳지 않다고 설명하는 부분(The stereotypical differences... are not correct)이 있습니다. 따라서 '일반적으로 가정되는 색깔과 활동의 차이'는 '진부한/고정관념적인(stereotypical)'이라는 단어가 적절합니다.

question: 22. 다음 글을 읽고, 제시된 요지의 빈칸 (A)와 (B)를 <보기>의 표현을 모두 사용하여 쓰시오. [3.8점]
passage: We can discard or replace a scientific theory only if we have a better way of explaining the evidence that supports it. The theories of Newton and Einstein offer great examples. A vast body of evidence supports Newton's theory of gravity, but by the late nineteenth century scientists had begun to discover cases where its predictions did not perfectly match observations. These discrepancies were explained only when Einstein developed his general theory of relativity, which was able to match the observations. Still, the many successes of Newton's theory could not be ignored, and Einstein's theory would not have gained acceptance if it had not been able to explain these successes equally well. It did, and that is why we now view Einstein's theory as a broader theory of gravity than Newton's theory. Some scientists today are seeking a theory of gravity that will go beyond Einstein's. If any new theory ever gains acceptance, it will have to match all the successes of Einstein's theory as well as work in new realms where Einstein's theory does not.
summary_sentence: A new theory can be accepted only if it (A)_______________________ and (B)________________________.
subjective_conditions: "the existing theory"는 두 번 사용할 것
vocabulary_box: can't / explains / explain / matches /the existing theory / the success / what / of
answer: (A) matches the success of the existing theory(B) explains what the existing theory can't explain
explanation: 지문의 내용에 따르면 새로운 과학 이론이 받아들여지려면 기존 이론의 성과와 일치해야 하며(match all the successes), 기존 이론이 설명하지 못하는 새로운 영역을 설명할 수 있어야 합니다. (A) matches the success of the existing theory (기존 이론의 성공과 일치한다)(B) explains what the existing theory can't explain (기존 이론이 설명할 수 없는 것을 설명한다)

question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고, 제시된 요지의 빈칸을 <보기>의 단어를 모두 사용하여 쓰시오. [25년 10월 39번]
passage: Waste has historically been seen as a necessary driver of the economy. Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly dependent on the demand for that product. Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be wasted, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be sustained. Many strategies have been incorporated into product design and use to ensure that waste is inevitable, such as planned obsolescence, limited access to tools for repairs, and use of cheap materials. All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a replacement. Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that prioritizing the elimination of waste via repair and remanufacturing creates a different kind of demand: products as a service. Through this setup, companies simply lease out products that were once sold directly to the customer. With this transition of ownership, companies maintain profit by offering maintenance and repair services and are encouraged to develop long-lasting products.
summary_sentence: Waste was intentionally designed into products to guarantee demand, but ______________________________.
answer: service-based models let companies remain profitable while encouraging durable products

question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고, A와 B가 나눈 대화의 빈칸 ⓐ와 ⓑ에 들어갈 말을 <보기>의 표현을 모두 사용하여 차례대로 쓰시오.
passage: Experiments testify to science's embrace of ignorance. Arguably the worst thing a scientist can do is to suppose they know what will happen in a given scenario without bothering to check. The rise of the experimental philosophy coincided with the liberation of curiosity as a valuable rather than a questionable attribute. For all that experimental science today is often assumed to be supported by a philosophical framework and an approved methodology ("state your hypothesis and then test it"), the fact is that, as philosopher of science Ian Hacking says, "One can conduct an experiment simply out of curiosity to see what will happen." Indeed, in the view of Charles Darwin's son, the astronomer George Darwin, once in a while one should do a completely crazy experiment, even if it is most likely to prove fruitless. You never know until you try.A: So realizing that scientists don't know the outcome is really the starting point of experimentation,B: Exactly Scientists shouldn't just assume that ⓐ_____________________________________.A: Right. But isn't it complicated and difficult to test a hypothesis?B: It can be, but you don't always need a complex hypothesis, ⓑ_____________________________________.A: Oh, I see. So it's important to just try it first.
subjective_conditions: <보기>의 표현을 모두 사용하여 차례대로 쓰시오
대·소문자 구별하지 않음
answer: ⓐ they already know what will happenⓑ curiosity itself can motivate an experiment
explanation: 본 지문은 과학이 모르는 것을 인정하고 호기심을 바탕으로 실험을 수행하는 것에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 대화 맥락상 빈칸 (a)는 과학자들이 결과가 무엇일지 이미 알고 있다고 가정해서는 안 된다는 내용이 되어야 하므로 'they already know what will happen'이 적절하며, 빈칸 (b)는 복잡한 가설 없이도 호기심 자체가 실험을 동기부여할 수 있다는 내용이 되어야 하므로 'curiosity itself can motivate an experiment'가 적절합니다.

question: 2. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 we're led to believe we need it이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Manufacturers masterfully sow seeds of doubt about the adequacy of our current devices. Suddenly, the phone that was your lifeline a year ago is now a museum piece, unable to keep pace with your digital demands. And thus, the itch to upgrade begins, often before there's a genuine need. This cycle isn't just confined to our digital companions. It spills over into almost every aspect of consumer electronics, from the self-driving car to the smart fridge. Every product seems to be on an unstoppable march towards the next version, the next generation that promises to revolutionize your life. What's fascinating, or perhaps disturbing, is the utter efficacy of this cycle in shaping our desires. It's not so much that we want the newest device: <u>we're led to believe we need it</u>. The distinction between want and need blurs. shifting our financial priorities in favor of staying current with trends. For all the logical arguments against this ceaseless upgrading, the temptation remains compelling.
options: ① the advanced features of new products provide objective evidence of their indispensable quality
② we autonomously make purchasing decisions based on a clear understanding of our actual needs
③ the fast pace of technological advancement genuinely renders older devices functionally obsolete
④ society creates an environment where owning the latest gadgets is a prerequisite for social acceptance
⑤ external influences skillfully manipulate our perceptions, transforming desires into perceived necessities
explanation: 지문은 제조업자들이 현재 기기의 적절성에 대한 의구심을 심어주어 소비자가 실제로 필요하지 않음에도 최신 기기를 사야 한다고 믿게 만든다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 밑줄 친 부분은 '외부적 영향(제조업자)이 우리의 인식을 교묘하게 조작하여 욕망을 인지된 필요성으로 변모시킨다'는 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 신제품의 고급 기능은 그것들의 없어서는 안 될 품질에 대한 객관적인 증거를 제공한다.
② 우리는 실제 필요에 대한 명확한 이해를 바탕으로 자율적으로 구매 결정을 내린다.
③ 기술 발전의 빠른 속도는 구형 기기를 기능적으로 진정하게 쓸모없게 만든다.
④ 사회는 최신 기기를 소유하는 것이 사회적 수용의 전제 조건인 환경을 조성한다.
⑤ 외부의 영향이 우리의 인식을 숙련되게 조작하여, 욕망을 필요하다고 느껴지는 것으로 바꾼다.

question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We encounter contrary claims about the relation of literature to action. Theorists have maintained that literature encourages solitary reading and reflection as the way to engage with the world and thus counters the social and political activities that might produce social change. At best it encourages detachment or appreciation of complexity, and at worst passivity and acceptance of what is. But on the other hand, literature has historically been seen as dangerous: it promotes the questioning of authority and social arrangements. Plato banned poets from his ideal republic because they could only do harm, and novels have long been credited with making people dissatisfied with their lives and eager for something new. By promoting identification across divisions of class, gender, and race, books may promote a fellowship that discourages struggle; but they may also produce a keen sense of injustice that makes progressive struggles possible. Historically, works of literature are credited with producing change: Uncle Tom's Cabin, a best-seller in its day, helped create a revulsion against slavery that made possible the American Civil War.
options: ① Plato's Vision: The Ideal Republic and Its Poets
② The Enduring Legacy of Classic Literary Works
③ Literature: A Mirror Reflecting Our Societal Flaws
④ The Conflicting Roles of Literature in Social Action
⑤ The Role of Reading in Personal Growth and Reflection
explanation: 이 글은 문학이 사회적 행동에 미치는 상반된 두 가지 역할을 설명하고 있습니다. 한편으로는 고립된 독서와 성찰을 통해 사회 변화를 방해(수동성 조장)하지만, 다른 한편으로는 권위에 도전하고 사회 정의에 대한 감각을 일깨워 실질적인 변화를 이끌어내기도 한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 ④ '사회적 행동에서 문학의 상충하는 역할'이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Any new resource (e.g., a new airport, a new mall) always opens with people benefiting individually by sharing a common resource (e.g., the city or state budget). Soon, at some point, the amount of traffic grows too large for the "commons" to support. Traffic jams, overcrowding, and overuse lessen the benefits of the common resource for everyone - the tragedy of the commons! If the new resource cannot be expanded or provided with additional space, it becomes a problem, and you cannot solve the problem on your own, in isolation from your fellow drivers or walkers or competing users. The total activity on this new resource keeps increasing, and so does individual activity; but if the dynamic of common use and overuse continues too long, both begin to fall after a peak, leading to a crash. What makes the "tragedy of commons" tragic is the crash dynamic - the destruction or degeneration of the common resource's ability to regenerate itself.
options: ① The Faster River Cleans Itself the More It Is Polluted
② The Well That Fails When Everyone Rushes to Drink
③ A Bridge That Grows Stronger with Every Footstep
④ A Lonely Road Waiting for Travelers
⑤ Sailing Smoothly on an Endless Sea
explanation: 이 글은 새로운 공공 자원이 초기에는 혜택을 주지만, 사용자가 급증하고 과도하게 사용되면서 결국 자원의 재생 능력이 파괴되어 붕괴에 이르게 된다는 '공유지의 비극(tragedy of the commons)' 현상을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '모두가 마시기 위해 몰려들 때 마르게 되는 우물'이라는 비유적 표현이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 강물이 오염될수록 더 빨리 스스로 정화된다
② 모두가 마시러 달려갈 때 마르는 우물
③ 발걸음마다 더 튼튼해지는 다리
④ 여행객을 기다리는 외로운 길
⑤ 끝없는 바다를 부드럽게 항해하기

question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: All translators feel some pressure from the community of readers ⓐ<u>whom</u> they are doing their work for. And all translators arrive at ⓑ<u>their</u> interpretations in dialogue with other people. The English poet Alexander Pope had pretty good Greek, but when he set about translating Homer's Iliad in the early 18th century he was not on his own. He had Greek commentaries to refer to, and translations that had already ⓒ<u>been done</u> in English, Latin, and French - and of course he had dictionaries. Translators always draw on more than one source text. Even when the scene of translation consists of just one person with a pen, paper, and the book that he is translating, or even when it is just one person translating orally for another, that person's linguistic knowledge ⓓ<u>arising</u> from lots of other texts and other conversations. And then his or her idea of the translation's purpose will be ⓔ<u>influenced</u> by the expectations of the person or people it is for. In both these senses every translation is a crowd translation.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 절에서 주어는 'that person's linguistic knowledge'입니다. 주어 뒤에는 문장의 본동사가 와야 하는데 'arising'은 현재분사로 동사 역할을 할 수 없습니다. 따라서 문맥과 수 일치에 따라 술어 동사인 'arises'로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Weber's law concerns the perception of ⓐ<u>difference</u> between two stimuli. It suggests that we might not be able to ⓑ<u>detect</u> a 1-mm difference when we are looking at lines 466mm and 467mm in length, but we may be able to detect a 1-mm difference when we are comparing a line 2mm long with one 3mm long. Another example of this principle is that we can detect 1 candle when it is lit in an otherwise dark room. But when 1 candle is lit in a room in which 100 candles are already burning, we may not notice the light from this candle. Therefore, the Just-noticeable difference (JND) varies as a function of the strength of the signals. For example, the JND is ⓒ<u>greater</u> for very loud noises than it is for much more quiet sounds. When a sound is very weak, we can tell that another sound is louder, even if it is ⓓ<u>barely</u> louder. When a sound is very loud, to tell that another sound is even louder, it has to be much louder. Thus, Weber's law means that it is ⓔ<u>easier</u> to distinguish between two samples when those samples are larger or stronger levels of the stimuli.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 베버의 법칙(Weber's law)에 의하면 자극의 세기가 강할수록 그 차이를 감지하기 위해서는 더 큰 자극의 변화가 필요합니다. 따라서 소리가 매우 클 때는 훨씬 더 큰 소리가 나야 차이를 느낄 수 있으므로, 자극의 수준이 더 강할 때 두 샘플 사이를 구별하는 것은 '더 쉽다(easier)'가 아니라 '더 어렵다(harder)'가 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Conditioned Place Preference (CPP) is a way of finding out what animals want. Researchers train them to associate one place with an experience such as food or a loud noise and another place with something completely different, usually where nothing happens. The two places are made obviously different to make it as easy as possible for the animal to associate each place with what happened to it there. The animal's preference for being in one place or another is measured both before and after its experiences in the two places. If there is a shift in where the animal chooses to spend its time for the reward, this suggests that it liked the experience and is trying to repeat it. Conversely, if it now avoids the place the stimulus appeared and starts to prefer the place it did not experience it, then this suggests that it found the stimulus unpleasant. For example, mice with cancer show a preference for the place where they have been given morphine, a drug used to relieve pain, rather than where they have received saline whereas healthy mice developed no such preference. This suggests that the mice with cancer wanted the morphine.
options: ① The purpose of the CPP experiment is to identify whether an animal prefers or avoids a stimulus based on its place choice.
② In the CPP method, animals learn to associate one place with a specific experience and another place with a different setting.
③ Researchers check the animal's preference both before and after the conditioning sessions.
④ If an animal spends less time in the place paired with a stimulus, it suggests the animal liked the experience.
⑤ The mice with cancer would have visited the place where morphine was given more frequently.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 동물이 특정 자극과 연결된 장소에서 더 많은 시간을 보낼 때 그 경험을 좋아했다는 것을 의미합니다. 반대로 시간을 적게 보내거나 피한다면 그 자극을 싫어했다는 뜻이므로, ④번은 내용과 반대되는 설명입니다.
options_translation: ① CPP 실험의 목적은 장소 선택을 바탕으로 동물이 자극을 선호하는지 회피하는지 식별하는 것이다.
② CPP 방식에서 동물들은 한 장소를 특정 경험과 연결하고 다른 장소를 다른 환경과 연결하는 것을 배운다.
③ 연구자들은 조건화 과정 전후로 동물의 선호도를 확인한다.
④ 만약 동물이 자극과 짝지어진 장소에서 더 적은 시간을 보낸다면, 그것은 동물이 그 경험을 좋아했음을 암시한다.
⑤ 암에 걸린 쥐들은 모르핀이 투여된 장소를 더 자주 방문했을 것이다.

question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Based on discoveries in neuroscience, pain and pleasure are formed and processed in the same area of the brain. Our bodies constantly strive for homeostasis, which is defined as the balance of bodily functions. Without the body's effective compensatory mechanisms, which may cushion potential highs and lows, we would not be capable of surviving. Pleasure and pain _______________________; they seem to work together and are heavily reliant on one another and keep balance. If you imagine pleasure and pain as the two opposite points on a scale, you can easily understand that as one of the two points rises, the other must correspondingly fall. We've all heard the expression, "No pain, no gain." Well, according to psychiatrist Dr. Anna Lembke, there may be some truth to these words. She says that our attempts to escape being miserable are in fact making us even more miserable. This is because pain is actually an essential component of our ability to maintain a neutral state, and allowing it will in turn reset our internal scale back to balance.
options: ① function as linked reactions in the brain
② rise and fall individually in a disconnected cycle
③ work independently without affecting our balance
④ are simple emotions that require little brain activity
⑤ work as opposite forces within their respective mechanism
explanation: 지문에서 고통가 즰거움은 뇌의 같은 영역에서 처리되며, 함께 작동하고 서로 의존하며 균형을 유지한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 고통가 즰거움이 뇌 안에서 서로 연결된 반응으로 작동한다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌 서로 연결된 반응으로 기능한다
② 단절된 순환 셍에서 개별적으로 오르내리락 한다
③ 우리의 균형에 영향을 준 수 없이 독립적으로 작동한다
④ 뇌 활동을 거의 필요로 하지 않는 단ሜ한 감정이다

question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: Near the equator, many species of bird breed all year round. But in temperate and polar regions, the breeding seasons of birds are often sharply defined. They are triggered mainly by changes in day length. If all goes well, the outcome is that birds raise their young when the food supply is at its peak. Most birds are not simply reluctant to breed at other times but they are also physically incapable of doing so. This is because their reproductive system shrinks, which helps fiying birds save weight. The main exception to this rule are nomadic desert species. They can begin breeding just a few days after rainfall, ___________________________________________. Also, different species divide the breeding season up in different ways. Most seabirds raise a single brood. In warm regions, however, songbirds may raise several families in a few months. In an exceptionally good year, a pair of House Sparrows, a kind of songbird, can raise successive broods through a marathon reproductive effort.
options: ① following a strict yearly breeding calendar
② taking advantage of the sudden chance to reproduce
③ because rainfall causes their reproductive organs to swell
④ because they need to protect their nests from heavy floods
⑤ which gives them a long occasion to raise young successfully
explanation: 일반적으로 새들은 특정 번식 시기가 정해져 있지만, 유먑 사막 종은 예외적으로 비가 온 후 며칠 만에 번식을 시작할 수 있다고 합니다. 이는 갑작스러운 번식 기회를 활용하는 것이므로 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 엄격한 연간 번식 일정을 따르면서

question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 40번]
passage: There is research that supports the idea that cognitive factors influence the phenomenology of the perceived world. Delk and Fillenbaum asked participants to match the color of figures with the color of their background. Some of the figures depicted objects associated with a particular color. These included typically red objects such as an apple, lips, and a symbolic heart. Other objects were presented that are not usually associated with red, such as a mushroom or a bell. However, all the figures were made out of the same red-orange cardboard. Participants then had to match the figure to a background varying from dark to light red. They had to make the background color match the color of the figures. The researchers found that red-associated objects required more red in the background to be judged a match than did the objects that are not associated with the color red. This implies that ______________________________________.
options: ① people's color choices stay the same no matter which object they are viewing
② the background color people chose had no relation to the object they were judging
③ the figures appeared different because they were made from different materials
④ people match colors only by using careful observation, not by relying on prior knowledge
⑤ the colors we associate with certain objects can affect how we judge the actual colors we see
explanation: 이 연구에서 참가자들은 전형적으로 '빨간색'으로 연상되는 물체(사과, 입술 등)를 실제로는 같은 주황빛 빨간색 카드보드임에도 불구하고, 빨간색과 연상되지 않는 물체(버섯, 종 등)보다 더 붉은 배경색과 일치시키려 했습니다. 이는 우리가 특정 사물에 대해 가지고 있는 '색에 대한 고정관념이나 연상(인지적 요인)'이 우리가 실제 눈으로 보는 색을 판단하는 방식에 영향을 준다는 것을 보여줍니다.

② 사람들이 선택한 배경색은 판단하고 있는 대상과 아무런 관련이 없었다

question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 10월 21번]
passage: Imagine that your usually stingy friend delights in buying you a Christmas present after taking a generosity booster. How would you feel? Undoubtedly, there is something praiseworthy about the action. You'd be pleased to receive the gift. You'd say 'thank you', and mean it. But his change of heart is not entirely satisfying. According to Zagzebski, an American philosopher, he is not really generous. When we praise someone's character, we use words for various virtues: 'generous', 'kind', 'courageous', etc. (A) A person who gives one gift isn't generous. (B) Thus virtues, as opposed to nontypical impulse, are the result of your personal history. (C) They are part of who you are, as they are part of how your character was formed. (D) Instant virtue is therefore impossible. (E) Popping a pill cannot make you a better person.
insertion_sentence: True generosity grows out of a deeply rooted emotional tendency that forms a lasting element of one's moral character.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 제시된 문장은 참된 관대함이 '도덕적 인격의 지속적인 요소가 되는 깊게 뿌리 박힌 감정적 경향'에서 비롯된다는 내용입니다. (A) 뒤의 문장은 단 한 번의 선물이 관대함이 아니라고 말하며, (B) 뒤의 문장은 '따라서(Thus)'라는 연결어와 함께 미덕이 일시적 충동이 아닌 '개인적 역사의 결과'라고 결론짓고 있습니다. 제시된 문장의 '지속적인 요소(lasting element)'는 (B) 뒤의 '개인적 역사의 결과(result of your personal history)'와 논리적으로 연결되므로 (B) 자리가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 10월 31번]
passage: One factor that may hinder creativity is unawareness of the resources required in each activity in students' learning. Often students are unable to identify the resources they need to perform the task required of them. Different resources may be compulsory for specific learning tasks, and recognizing them may simplify the activity's performance. For example, it may be that students desire to conduct some experiments in their projects. There must be a prior investigation of whether the students will have access to the laboratory, equipment, and chemicals required for the experiment. It means preparation is vital for the students to succeed, and it may be about human and financial resources such as laboratory technicians, money to purchase chemicals, and equipment for their learning where applicable. Even if some of the resources required for a task may not be available, identifying them in advance may help students' creativity. It may even lead to changing the topic, finding alternative resources, and other means.
summary_sentence: Students' creativity in learning can be (A)_________ when they fail to recognize the resources required for their tasks; however, (B)_________ these resources beforehand, even if some are scarce, can encourage them to find alternative approaches and ultimately enhance their creative problem-solving.
options: ① limited evaluating
② maximized securing
③ impeded overlooking
④ obstructed identifying
⑤ facilitated providing
explanation: 지문은 학생들이 과제에 필요한 자원을 인식하지 못할 때 창의성이 방해받을 수 있다고 설명하므로 (A)에는 'obstructed(방해받는)' 또는 'limited(제한되는)'가 적절합니다. 하지만 필요한 자원을 미리 '파악(identifying)'하는 것이 창의적 문제 해결에 도움이 된다고 했으므로 (B)에는 'identifying'이 가장 적절합니다. 따라서 정답은 ④번입니다.
options_translation: ① 제한되는 - 평가하는 것
② 극대화되는 - 확보하는 것
③ 방해받는 - 간과하는 것
④ 방해받는 - 파악하는 것
⑤ 촉진되는 - 제공하는 것

question: 19. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In each round of genome copying in our body, there is still about a 70 percent chance that at least one pair of chromosomes will have an error. With each round of genome copying, errors accumulate. This is similar to alterations in medieval books. Each time a copy was made by hand, some changes were introduced accidentally; as changes stacked up, the copies may have acquired meanings at variance with the original. Similarly, genomes (A)____________________________________. To make things worse, mutations may damage genes responsible for error checking and repair of genomes, further accelerating the introduction of mutations.Most genome mutations do not have any noticeable effects. It is just ⓐ<u>like</u> changing the i for a y in "kingdom" would not distort the word's readability. But sometimes a mutation to a human gene results in, for example, an eye ⓑ<u>whose</u> iris is of two different colors. Similarly, almost everyone has birthmarks, ⓒ<u>which</u> are due to mutations that occurred as our body's cells multiplied to form skin. If mutations are changes to the genome of one particular cell, how can a patch of cells in an iris or a whole patch of skin, consisting of many individual cells, ⓓ<u>is</u> affected simultaneously? The answer lies in the cell lineage, the developmental history of a tissue from particular cells through to their ⓔ<u>fully</u> differentiated state. If the mutation occurred early on in the lineage of the developing iris, then all cells in that patch have inherited that change.
options: ① correct most errors before the next copying step
② slowly return to their original form as new errors appear
③ improve their structure through repeated copying cycles
④ spread evenly through the whole body after each mutation
⑤ become increasingly altered during repeated genome duplication
explanation: 지문 전반부에서 유전체 복제 시 발생하는 오류가 중세 서적의 필사 과정에서 발생하는 오류와 유사하며, 이러한 오류가 축적됨에 따라 원래의 의미와 달라질 수 있다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 유전체 또한 반복되는 복제 과정에서 점점 더 변형된다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다음 복제 단계 전에 대부분의 오류를 수정한다
② 새로운 오류가 나타남에 따라 천천히 원래 형태로 돌아간다
③ 반복되는 복제 주기를 통해 구조를 개선한다
④ 각 돌연변이 이후에 전신으로 고르게 퍼진다
⑤ 반복되는 유전체 복제 동안 점점 더 변형된다
