question: 21. 다음 글의 내용에 대한 설명으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Some people argue that there is a single, logically consistent concept known as reading that can be neatly set apart from everything else people do with books. Is reading really that simple? The most productive way to think about reading is as a loosely related set of behaviors that belong together owing to family resemblances, as Ludwig Wittgenstein used the phrase, without having in common a single defining trait. Consequently, efforts to distinguish reading from non-reading are destined to fail because there is no agreement on what qualifies as reading in the first place. The more one tries to figure out where the border lies between reading and not-reading, the more edge cases will be found to stretch the term's flexible boundaries. Thus, it is worth attempting to collect together these exceptional forms of reading into a single forum, one highlighting the challenges faced by anyone wishing to establish the boundaries where reading begins and ends. The attempt moves toward an understanding of reading as a spectrum that is expansive enough to accommodate the distinct reading activities.
options: ① Some observers maintain a notion of reading clearly separated from other book-related activities.
② It is most constructive to understand reading as a cluster of loosely connected practices.
③ Attempts to draw a firm line between reading and not-reading produce a concrete definition of reading.
④ More exceptional cases emerge as one tries harder to locate a precise boundary for the concept of reading.
⑤ Collecting unusual reading practices supports viewing reading as a broad, flexible spectrum.
explanation: ③번은 본문의 내용과 상반됩니다. 본문에서는 읽기와 읽기가 아닌 갓을 구뵄하려는 시도는 실패할 수밖에 없은데, 그 이유는 읽기의 경계가 유연하고 하나의 정의로 규정할 수 없기 때문이라고 설명하고 읈습니다. 따라서 확고한 경계를 그잼으로써 구체적인 정의를 만들어 낼 수 읈다는 설명은 퉀리었습니다.
options_translation: ① 일부 관찰자들은 읽기가 책과 관련된 다른 활동들과 명확히 분리된다는 개념을 유준한다.
② 읽기를 늬게 연결된 관행들의 집합으로 이해하는 갓이 가장 건설적이다.
③ 읽기와 읽기가 아닌 갓 사이에 확고한 선을 그잼으로써 읽기의 구체적인 정의를 만들어 낸다.
④ 읽기라는 개념의 정확한 경계를 찾으려 노력할수록 덄 많은 예외적인 사례들이 나타낸다.
⑤ 특이한 읽기 관행들을 모으는 갓은 읽기를 광범위하고 유연한 스팩트럼으로 바라밴는 갓을 뒷받침한다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: How people judge color is not always determined by the actual shade they see. Based on this idea, Delk and Fillenbaum designed a study in which participants were asked to match the colors of figures with their backgrounds. Some of the figures depicted objects associated with a particular color. These included typically red objects such as an apple, lips, and a symbolic heart. Other objects were presented that are not usually associated with red, such as a mushroom or a bell. However, all the figures were made out of the same red-orange cardboard. Participants then had to match the figure to a background varying from dark to light red. They had to make the background color match the color of the figures. The researchers found that red-associated objects required more red in the background to be judged a match than did the objects that are not associated with the color red. This implies that the cognitive association of objects to color influences how we perceive that color.
options: ① The researchers investigated how cognitive links to certain objects shape people's color-matching judgments.
② Every figure was cut from the same red-orange cardboard, though some depicted red-related objects.
③ Participants were asked to choose figures according to the color shown in the background.
④ As a result of the research, red-related figures required a redder background to look the same.
⑤ The study demonstrates that conceptual associations between objects and colors shape perceptual experience.
explanation: 실험 참가자들은 배경색에 따라 도형을 고르는 갓이 아니라, 제시된 도형의 색상과 일츘하도록 배경 색상을 조절하는 갓(match the colors of figures with their backgrounds) 이었습니다. 따라서 ③번은 실험 방식을 잘못 설명하고 읈습니다.
options_translation: ① 연구자들은 특정 사물에 대한 인지적 연결이 사람들의 색상 일츘 판단을 어떻게 형성하는지 젘사핈다.
② 모든 도형은 동일한 뽤갈색 카드밴드로 만들어졌지만, 일부는 뽤간색과 관련된 사물을 묘사했다.
③ 참가자들은 배경에 나타난 색상에 따라 도형을 선택하도록 요청묛었다.
④ 연구 결과, 뽤간색과 관련된 도형들은 동일하게 보이기 위해 덄 뽤간 배경을 필요로 했다.
⑤ 이 연구는 사물과 색상 사이의 개념적 결합이 지각 경험을 형성한다는 갓을 보여준다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Near the equator, many species of bird breed all year round. But in temperate and polar regions, the breeding seasons of birds are often sharply defined. They are triggered mainly by changes in day length. If all goes well, the outcome is that birds raise their young when the food supply is at its peak. Most birds are not simply reluctant to breed at other times but they are also physically incapable of doing so. This is because their reproductive system shrinks, which helps flying birds save weight. (A) The main exception to this rule are nomadic desert species. (B) These nomadic birds of the desert can launch their breeding cycle shortly following rain. (C) Also, different species divide the breeding season up in different ways. (D) Most seabirds raise a single brood, but in warm regions songbirds may raise several families in a few months. question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: All translators feel some pressure from the community of readers for whom they are doing their work. And all translators arrive at their interpretations in dialogue with other people. The English poet Alexander Pope had pretty good Greek, but when he set about translating Homer's Iliad in the early 18th century he was not on his own. He had Greek commentaries to refer to, and translations that had already been done in English, Latin, and French─and of course he had dictionaries. Translators always draw on more than one source text. Even when the scene of translation consists of just one person with a pen, paper, and the book that is being translated, or even when it is just one person translating orally for another, that person's linguistic knowledge arises from lots of other texts and other conversations. And then his or her idea of the translation's purpose will be influenced by the expectations of the person or people it is for. In both these senses every translation is a crowd translation.
summary_sentence: Because translators depend on 'numerous sources, and dialogues, as well as the expectations of their audience, every translation is __________________________.
options: ① a collaboration formed by many influences
② a task that requires careful verification
③ the result that excludes a consensus
④ anything but a collective work
⑤ inevitably an autonomous act
explanation: 이 글은 번역가가 번역을 할 때 다양한 참고 문헌, 사전, 기존의 번역본, 그리고 독자의 기대 등 다양한 요소에 의존하여 작업한다는 내용입니다. 따라쐜 모든 번역은 'crowd translation(다수가 참여한 번역)'이몰, 이는 '많은 영향력에 의해 형성된 협업' 이라고 요약할 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 많은 영향력에 의해 형성된 협업
② 제대로 된 검증을 필요로 하는 과제
③ 합의림 배제하는 결과

⑤ 필연적으로 자율적인 행위

question: 25. 다음 글의 요약문을 아래와 같이 쓸 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: Based on discoveries in neuroscience, pain and pleasure are formed and processed in the same area of the brain. Our bodies constantly strive for homeostasis, which is defined as the balance of bodily functions. Without the body's effective compensatory mechanisms, which may cushion potential highs and lows, we would not be capable of surviving. Pleasure and pain are like two sides of the same coin; they seem to work together and are heavily reliant on one another and keep balance. If you imagine pleasure and pain as the two opposite points on a scale, you can easily understand that as one of the two points rises, the other must correspondingly fall. We've all heard the expression, "No pain, no gain." Well, according to psychiatrist Dr. Anna Lembke, there may be some truth to these words. She says that our attempts to escape being miserable are in fact leaving us even worse off. This is because pain is actually an essential component of our ability to maintain a neutral state, and allowing it will in turn reset our internal scale back to balance.
summary_sentence: Pain and pleasure function as counterbalancing forces that must remain in balance for us to sustain (A)_________. According to Dr. Anna Lembke, avoiding pain indeed (B)_________ our misery because pain itself is essential for restoring our internal balance.
subjective_conditions: • 본문에 있는 단어만을 이용하먰, 필요시 변형할 것
explanation: 본문에서 신체 기능의 균형을 'homeostasis(홈메오스타시스, 항직성)'라고 정의하였으므로 (A)에는 homeostasis가 들어갑니다. 또한 Dr. Anna Lembke는 고통을 피하려는 시도가 오히눘 상태륌 'even worse off(훨씬 더 나쁘게)' 만든다고 하였으므로, worse륌 동사 형태인 worsens로 변형하여 (B)에 기입합니다. (3인칭 단수 주어 avoiding pain에 맞춰 변형)

question: 26. 다음 글의 주제문을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
passage: Weber's law concerns the perception of difference between two stimuli. It suggests that we might not be able to detect a 1mm difference when we are looking at lines 466mm and 467 mm in length, but we may be able to detect a 1mm difference when we are comparing a line 2mm long with one 3mm long. Another example of this principle is that we can detect 1 candle when it is lit in an otherwise dark room. But when 1 candle is lit in a room in which 100 candles are already burning, we may not notice the light from this candle. Therefore, the Just-noticeable difference (JND) varies as a function of the strength of the signals. For example, the JND is greater for very loud noises than it is for much more quiet sounds. When a sound is very weak, we can tell that another sound is louder, even if it is barely louder. When a sound is very loud, to tell that another sound is even louder, it has to be much louder. Thus, Weber's law means that it is harder to distinguish between two samples when those samples are larger or stronger levels of the stimuli.
subjective_conditions: • <보기>의 단어륌 모됐 한 번쌩 이용하여 배열할 것
• 주어진 단어 외 추가하지 말 것
• 비교급을 반드시 활용하먰, 이륌 위해서만 변형할 것
• 위 주서문에서 According to Weber's law을 제외한 나머지 부분, "the _______________, the _______________ it is _____________________"을 모됐 답지에 실 것
vocabulary_box: detect / the initial stimulus / strong / is
answer: the stronger the initial stimulus is, the harder it is to detect small changes
explanation: Weber의 법칙은 자극의 강도가 강할수록 차이륌 감지하기 더 어렵다는 내용입니다. 'the + 비교급, the + 비교급' 구문을 사용하여 문장을 완성하먴, "the stronger(strong의 비교급) the initial stimulus is, the harder(hard의 비교급) it is to detect small changes"가 됩니다.

question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Any new resource (e.g., a new airport, a new mall) always opens with people benefiting individually by sharing a common resource (e.g., the city or state budget). Soon, at some point, the amount of traffic grows too large for the "commons" to support. Traffic jams, overcrowding, and overuse lessen the benefits of the common resource for everyone - the tragedy of the commons! If the new resource cannot be expanded or provided with additional space, it becomes a problem, and you cannot solve the problem on your own, in isolation from your fellow drivers or walkers or competing users. The total activity on this new resource keeps increasing, and so does individual activity; but if the dynamic of common use and overuse continues too long, both begin to fall after a peak, leading to a crash. What makes the "tragedy of commons" tragic is the crash dynamic - the destruction or degeneration of the common resource's ability to regenerate itself.
options: ① Comparing Individual and Collective Activities in Public Spaces
② Traffic Jams, Overcrowding, and the Challenges of Urban Development
③ Benefits and Limitations of Knowledge and Information as Common Resources

⑤ Overuse and Mismanagement of Common Resources Leading to Collective Loss

question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Even though sea creatures live in it, they still need to take in water for their bodies to function properly. However, they must also eliminate any excess salt that comes with it. Salt absorbs water much like a sponge. For example, if you place a small pile of salt on a plate and add water so that it touches the salt, the salt will absorb the water, forming a larger, wet pile. Notice that it has increased in size. The same principle applies to sea creatures. If a sea animal's body fluids are saltier than the surrounding seawater, the extra salt in its body will draw in seawater, which can cause the animal to swell. Conversely, if the seawater contains more salt than the animal's body fluids, the excess salt in the water will pull fluids out of the animal's body, leading to dehydration and shrinkage.

question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 지칭하는 것이 다른 하나는?

question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 Hobbes의 주장과 일치하는 것은?

question: 19. 다음 글을 바탕으로 한 아래 대화문 <A>의 밑줄 친 부분이 내용상 어색한 것은?

④ Although virtues are influenced by one's background, they can be temporarily strengthened by external enhancers.
⑤ Authentic virtue can emerge only when a sequence of commendable acts accumulates within a brief interval.
explanation: 이 글은 진정한 미덕(예: 관대함)이 단 한 번의 행위나 외부적 자극(약물 등)에 의한 일시적 변화가 아니라, 오랜 시간 동안 형성된 성격의 일부이자 안정적인 '도덕적 정체성'의 결과라고 설명합니다. 따라서 도덕적으로 훌륭한 정체성은 고립된 행위가 아닌 지속적인 성격 형성의 역사에 근거한다는 ①번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 도덕적으로 존경할 만한 정체성은 고립된 관대한 행위가 아니라 지속적인 성격 형성의 역사에 바탕을 둔다.
② 도덕적 특성은 주로 내부의 충동에 의해 결정되며, 이는 때때로 친절한 행동으로 나타난다.
③ 인위적인 수단에 의한 갑작스러운 행동 변화는 도덕적인 성격의 신뢰할 수 있는 증거를 제공한다.
④ 미덕은 개인의 배경에 영향을 받지만, 외부 강화물에 의해 일시적으로 강화될 수 있다.
⑤ 진정한 미덕은 일련의 칭찬할 만한 행동이 짧은 간격 내에 축적될 때만 나타날 수 있다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.9점]
passage: There are numerous ways wildlife is managed, but they all imply stewardship and can be classified into two broad categories: active management and inactive management. Active management does something to the population - such as increasing or decreasing its size - in a direct manner through strategies like translocations or hunting, respectively. Populations can also be actively managed by altering the habitat to the benefit or disadvantage of a population. If population numbers are too low for the goal of management agencies, other active management can be incorporated, such as predator control to minimize neonatal deaths or habitat improvement to provide required cover for neonates from predators. These efforts represent active approaches to management. Other populations may not be actively managed, like those in national parks. In such situations, management activities minimize external influences on populations and habitat, which often involves management of humans and not animals.
options: ① Wildlife management encompasses a wide range of practices, all rooted in the principle of stewardship, the responsible care and oversight of natural populations.
② Active management involves direct intervention in wildlife populations to influence their size, deliberately increasing or decreasing population numbers.
③ Inactive management adopts a largely hands-on approach, employing strategies such as translocations, hunting, and habitat alteration.
④ When populations fall below management goals, agencies may use measures such as predator control or habitat improvements to support young animals.
⑤ In national parks, management focuses on regulating human activities to minimize interference, allowing natural processes and ecosystems to function naturally.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 전략적 이동(translocations), 사냥(hunting), 서식지 변경(habitat alteration) 등은 수동적 관리(inactive management)가 아니라 능동적 관리(active management)의 예시로 설명되어 있습니다. 수동적 관리는 국립공원에서와 같이 인간의 활동을 제한함으로써 외부 영향을 최소화하는 관리를 의미하므로 ③번은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 야생 동물 관리는 다양한 관행을 포함하며, 이 모든 것들은 자연 개체군에 대한 책임 있는 보살핌과 감독인 책임 관리의 원칙에 뿌리를 두고 있다.
② 능동적 관리는 개체 수의 크기에 영향을 주기 위해 야생 동물 개체군에 직접적으로 개입하며, 의도적으로 개체 수를 늘리거나 줄이는 것을 포함한다.
③ 비능동적(수동적) 관리는 이동, 사냥, 서식지 변경과 같은 전략을 사용하여 주로 실무적인 접근 방식을 채택한다.
④ 개체 수가 관리 목표 아래로 떨어지면, 기관은 어린 동물을 보호하기 위해 포식자 통제나 서식지 개선과 같은 조치를 사용할 수 있다.
⑤ 국립공원에서의 관리는 간섭을 최소화하기 위해 인간의 활동을 조절하는 데 집중하며, 자연적인 과정과 생태계가 자연스럽게 작동하도록 한다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Near the equator, many species of bird breed all year round. But in temperate and polar regions, the breeding seasons of birds are often sharply defined. They are triggered mainly by changes in day length. If all goes well, the outcome is that birds raise their young when the food supply is at its peak. Most birds are not simply reluctant to breed at other times but they are also physically incapable of doing so. This is because their reproductive system shrinks, which helps flying birds save weight. The main exception to this rule are nomadic desert species. These can initiate their breeding cycle within days of rain. It's for making the most of the sudden breeding opportunity. Also, different species divide the breeding season up in different ways. Most seabirds raise a single brood. In warm regions, however, songbirds may raise several families in a few months. In an exceptionally good year, a pair of House Sparrows, a kind of songbird, can raise successive broods through a marathon reproductive effort.
summary_sentence: Birds (A)__________ their breeding patterns with seasonal and ecological conditions, so that their young are nurtured when essential resources are (B)__________.
options: ① adapt --- constrained
② align --- plentiful
③ maintain --- sufficient
④ confuse --- depleted
⑤ manipulate --- deficient
explanation: 이 글은 새들이 먹이 공급이 정점에 달할 때 새끼를 기를 수 있도록 낮의 길이나 강우와 같은 환경 조건에 맞춰 번식 시기를 조절한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '나란히 맞추다/조정하다'라는 의미의 align이, (B)에는 '풍부한'이라는 의미의 plentiful이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 적응시키다 --- 제약된
② 맞추다(나란히 하다) --- 풍부한
③ 유지하다 --- 충분한
④ 혼동하다 --- 고갈된
⑤ 조작하다 --- 부족한

question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Statistics in the twentieth century became the systematic collection of quantitative information needed by the state. This process occurred in all the industrialised countries as a key part of their becoming modern states. Desrosières writes: "It is difficult to think simultaneously that the objects being measured really do exist and that this is only a convention". Yet this is the case. Phenomena such as prices being charged and products being sold exist, but the categories and classification frameworks supporting the collection, aggregation, and organisation of official statistics are devised to serve the purposes of the state, for macroeconomic or for social policies. Theodore Porter described the use of statistics to create state authority: "Quantification is a way of making decisions without seeming to decide", characterising it as a "social technology" intended to build trust in authority.
options: ① How Statistics Can Be Promoted at The National Level
② Statistical Data: Tools to Reinforce State Authority
③ Data Analysis Essential for Social Development?
④ Major Changes in 20th-Century Economic Trends
⑤ Why Economic Policies Tend to Lack Consistency
explanation: 이 글은 20세기 통계가 현대 국가가 되는 과정에서 국가가 필요로 하는 정보를 체계적으로 수집하는 수단으로 발전했음을 설명합니다. 통계적 수치화가 국가의 목적을 수행하고 권위에 대한 신뢰를 구축하며 의사결정을 정당화하는 '사회적 기술'로 사용되었다는 내용이므로 ② '통계 데이터: 국가 권력을 강화하기 위한 도구'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 국가적 차원에서 통계를 장려할 수 있는 방법
② 통계 데이터: 국가 권력을 강화하기 위한 도구
③ 사회 발전에 필수적인 데이터 분석?
④ 20세기 경제 트렌드의 주요 변화
⑤ 경제 정책이 일관성을 결여하는 경향이 있는 이유

question: 7. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Just as an expert in the taste and colour of wine will gain much by being aware of the chemistry that underlies those qualities, so each perspective on the body can potentially enhance the others. And yet every scientific tool, from microscopes to mathematics, and every aspect of the body, from the brain to the microorganism, requires such depth of expertise that this tends not to happen: we tend to study the human body in silos, each community sectioned from the others by its own specialised vocabulary. Research communities may be dedicated to one type of scientific tool or a specific component of the body, such as one type of cell. How different types of cell communicate with one another becomes its own specialist topic. Even simple forms of life on Earth are now rarely studied as a whole, and the human body is evidently much more complex. As long ago as 1890, The Times newspaper commented that knowledge 'had already become too vast to be manageable'. Today, nobody is an expert in the whole of anything.
options: ① 연구 공동체에서 총체적 연구보다 독립적 연구가 일반적이다.
② 화학에 대한 연구는 사람 신체 연구에 직접적인 도움이 된다.
③ 단순한 생명체는 인간보다 복잡해서 연구하기 매우 어렵다.
④ 여러 관점을 통합하면 특정 분야를 완벽하게 연구할 수 있다.
⑤ 어떤 것에 대하여 전체적으로 완전히 이해하기는 어렵다.
explanation: 지식이 너무 방대해지고 각 분야가 고도로 전문화되면서, 개별 연구 공동체들이 분절된 상태로 특정 부분만을 연구하게 되었습니다. 이로 인해 인체와 같은 복잡한 대상을 전체적인 관점에서 이해하는 것이 불가능해졌으며, 현대 사회에서 누구도 어떤 것의 전체에 대한 전문가가 될 수 없다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Historically, palaces weren't just homes; they were carefully constructed stages designed to impress and intimidate. While stone symbolized permanence and strength, glass offered something equally powerful: visibility. The introduction of large windows in palaces allowed rulers to literally look down upon their subjects, ⓐ<u>highlighting</u> their elevated position. Conversely, it also allowed subjects to gaze up at their leaders, ⓑ<u>fostering</u> a sense of awe and distance. Consider the Palace of Versailles: its Hall of Mirrors, lined with reflective surfaces, not only magnified the grandeur of the space but also placed the king at the center of a dazzling display, ⓒ<u>reinforcing</u> his absolute authority. The use of glass in palaces wasn't merely aesthetic; it was strategic. Open sightlines ⓓ<u>facilitated</u> better surveillance and control, ensuring the safety and security of the ruling family. Courtiers and visitors were constantly aware of being observed, ⓔ<u>undermining</u> an atmosphere of careful obedience and respect. The very architecture dictated social behavior, with glass acting as a silent enforcer of the power dynamic.
explanation: 궁전에서 유리창과 개방된 시야를 통해 감시와 통제가 가능해졌으며, 신하와 방문객들이 항상 관찰되고 있다는 사실을 인지하게 되었습니다. 이러한 환경은 신하들이 주의 깊게 순종하고 존경하는 분위기를 '약화시키는(undermining)' 것이 아니라 '조성'하거나 '강화'하는 역할을 해야 문맥상 적절합니다. 따라서 ⓔ의 undermining은 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Consider units of measure, one kind of descriptive device we are familiar with using in physics. Spatial distances can be given in terms of feet or meters or some other unit, and the physics will be the same regardless. We conclude from this that physics does not prefer one unit of length over any other, and we may choose any one we like for reasons of convenience. We further conclude that any feature depending on that choice, such as the particular numerical value assigned to the spatial separation between two locations, is not out there in the world apart from a choice of unit. Temperatures can likewise be given in terms of the Fahrenheit or Celsius or Kelvin scale, and nothing in the physics changes when we switch from one scale to another. We conclude that the choice of scale is a(an) ___________ choice in description, and that any feature that depends on that choice is scaledependent.
options: ① arbitrary
② international
③ objective
④ obligatory
⑤ irrational
explanation: 지문은 물리적 측정 단위(미터, 피트, 화씨, 섭씨 등)의 선택이 물리 법칙 자체를 바꾸지 않으며, 단지 편의에 따라 선택되는 것임을 설명하고 있습니다. 특정 단위를 다른 단위보다 선호하지 않고 편의에 따라 '임의로' 선택할 수 있다는 문맥이므로 'arbitrary(임의적인, 독단적인)'가 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 임의적인
② 국제적인
③ 객관적인
④ 의무적인
⑤ 비이성적인

question: 14. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Even though sea creatures live in it, they still need to take in water for their bodies to function properly. They just need to get rid of any extra salt it might bring with it. Salt absorbs water like a sponge. If you put a tiny mountain of salt on a small plate, then add enough water to the side, making sure an edge touches the salt, the salt will absorb the water. Now you have a pile of wet salt. Notice that it has increased in size. The same principle applies to sea creatures. If the body fluids in a sea animal are saltier than the seawater it lives in, then the extra salt in the creature's body will absorb seawater. This can cause them to swell up. On the other hand, if the amount of salt in the seawater is higher than the amount of salt in the body fluids of a sea animal, the extra salt in the water will draw fluids out of the creature's body, causing it to dehydrate and shrink.
options: ① How Extra Salt Harms the Bodies of Sea Animals
② Why Seawater Contains Such a High Amount of Salt
③ Do Sea Creatures Need to Drink Water to Survive?
④ Salt: The Most Valueless Thing for All Creatures
⑤ Why Salt Causes Sea Animals to Change Their Colors
explanation: 지문은 바다 생물들이 살고 있는 바닷물을 섭취해야 하지만 염분을 조절해야 하는 이유와 그 원리(삼투 현상)를 설명하고 있습니다. 첫 문장에서 바다 생물들도 제대로 기능하기 위해 물을 섭취할 필요가 있다고 명시하고 그 과정과 기제를 설명하므로, ③번 '바다 생물들은 생존을 위해 물을 마셔야 하는가?'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 여분의 소금이 어떻게 바다 동물의 몸에 해를 끼치는가
② 왜 바닷물은 그렇게 많은 양의 소금을 포함하는가

question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Distinguishing moths from butterflies on outward appearance is not always easy, but there are a few rules of thumb that can help. In most butterflies the antennae end with a small clubshaped swelling, whereas in moths they are usually feathery or narrow to a fine tip. (A) Butterflies tend to rest with their wings held shut above their body, whereas moths more usually rest with the upper sides of the wings on full view. (B) Further distinctions can be made by looking for a tiny hook that joins fore and hindwings, a feature only present in moths. (C) The stereotypical differences, with moths cast as the gloomy, nocturnal cousins of colourful sunloving butterflies are simply wrong. (D) There are many brightly coloured moths and many which are active throughout the day. (E) So, it's more sensible to think of them together; both butterflies and moths are beautiful and fascinating insects.
insertion_sentence: Equally, there are a few nocturnal butterflies and plenty that come clothed in shades of brown and grey.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 나비 중에도 야행성이 있거나 갈색/회색을 띠는 개체가 있다는 내용입니다. 글의 (D) 부분에서 나방 중에도 화려한 색을 띠거나 낮에 활동하는 개체가 많다는 예외적 사실을 언급한 뒤, '마찬가지로(Equally)' 나비 또한 전형적인 이미지(낮에 활동, 화려함)와 다른 예외가 있음을 덧붙이는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 따라서 (E) 앞에 위치하여 나비와 나방의 구분이 고정관념만큼 뚜렷하지 않음을 뒷받침하고 결론으로 이어지는 것이 적절합니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: There are numerous ways wildlife is managed, but they all imply stewardship and can be classified into two broad categories: active management and inactive management. Active management does something to the population - such as increasing or decreasing its size - in a direct manner through strategies like translocations or hunting, ⓐ<u>respectively</u>. Populations can also be actively managed by ⓑ<u>altering</u> the habitat to the benefit or disadvantage of a population. If population numbers are too low for the goal of management agencies, other active management can be incorporated, such as predator control to minimize neonatal deaths or habitat improvement ⓒ<u>to provide</u> required cover for neonates from predators. These efforts represent active approaches to management. Other populations may not be actively managed, like ⓓ<u>those</u> in national parks. In such situations, management activities minimize external influences on populations and habitat, ⓔ<u>it</u> often involves management of humans and not animals.
explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장은 앞의 완전한 절(management activities minimize...) 뒤에 콤마(,)로 연결되어 있습니다. 두 문장을 연결하려면 접속사가 필요하므로 대명사 it 대신 관계대명사 which(계속적 용법)를 사용해야 합니다. ⓐ respectively(각각)는 두 전략에 대응하여 적절하며, ⓑ altering은 전치사 by 뒤의 동명사로 적절하고, ⓒ to provide는 목적을 나타내는 부정사, ⓓ those는 앞의 복수 명사 populations를 대신하는 대명사로 어법상 옳습니다.

question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 한 단어와, (B)에 공통으로 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 변형 없이 쓰시오.
passage: As a political researcher in Germany, Noelle-Neumann observed that during election campaigns, certain views seemed to get more play than others, and sometimes people muted their opinions rather than talking about them, especially if those opinions were perceived to be unpopular. Noelle-Neumann calls this the spiral of silence. The spiral of silence occurs when individuals who perceive that their opinions are dominant express them, whereas those who think their opinions are unpopular remain quiet. This process occurs in a spiral, so that one side of an issue ends up with considerable publicity and the other side with very little. In everyday life, people express their opinions in a variety of ways: they talk about them, they wear buttons, they put bumper stickers on their cars, and they post their views on social media. According to this theory, people are more apt to do openly these kinds of things when they perceive that others share their opinions.
summary_sentence: People tend to express their opinions more (A)_________ when they believe their views are (B)_________, but they stay silent when they think their opinions aren't (B)_________, which leads to the "spiral of silence."
explanation: 이 글은 노엘-노이만(Noelle-Neumann)의 '침묵의 나선' 이론에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 사람들은 자신의 의견이 다수(dominant)이거나 남들도 공유한다고 느낄 때 의견을 공개적으로(openly) 표현하지만, 자신의 의견이 인기가 없다고 판단되면 침묵하게 된다는 내용입니다. 따라서 요약문의 (A)에는 'openly', (B)에는 'dominant'가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Buying a television is current consumption. It makes us happy today but does nothing to make us richer tomorrow. Yes, money spent on a television keeps workers employed at the television factory. But if the same money were invested, it would create jobs somewhere else, say for scientists in a laboratory or workers on a construction site, while also making us richer in the long run. Think about college as an example. Sending students to college creates jobs for professors. Using the same money to buy fancy sports cars for high school graduates would create jobs for auto workers. The crucial difference between these scenarios is that a college education makes a young person more productive for the rest of his or her life; a sports car does not. Thus, college tuition is an investment; buying a sports car is consumption.
options: ① The Political Value of Investing in Education
② The Effect of Rising TV Costs on Consumption
③ The Distinction Between Investment and Consumption
④ How Luxury Goods Influence Modern Market Behavior
⑤ The Impact of Consumer Spending on Employment Trends
explanation: 이 글은 소비(현재의 행복을 주지만 미래의 부를 늘려주지 않음)와 투자(생산성을 높여 미래를 더 풍요롭게 만듦)의 차이를 TV 구매와 대학 교육, 스포츠카 구매 등의 예시를 통해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '투자와 소비의 구분'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 교육 투자의 정치적 가치

question: 5. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
passage: The fast-growing, tremendous amount of data, collected and stored in large and numerous data repositories, has far exceeded our human ability for understanding without powerful tools. (A) As a result, data collected in large data repositories become "data tombs" - data archives that are hardly visited. (B) Important decisions are often made based not on the information-rich data stored in data repositories but rather on a decision maker's instinct. (C) That's simply because the decision maker does not have the tools to extract the valuable knowledge hidden in the vast amounts of data. (D) Efforts have been made to develop expert system and knowledge-based technologies, which typically rely on users or domain experts to manually input knowledge into knowledge bases. (E) The widening gap between data and information calls for the systematic development of tools that can turn data tombs into "golden nuggets" of knowledge.
insertion_sentence: However, this procedure is likely to cause biases and errors and is extremely costly and time consuming.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'this procedure'는 (D)에서 언급된 '사용자나 도메인 전문가가 수동으로 지식을 지식 베이스에 입력하는 기술(expert system and knowledge-based technologies)'을 가리킵니다. 이러한 수동적 방법이 편향과 오류를 일으키고 비용과 시간이 많이 든다는 단점을 제시한 후, (E)에서 그 대안으로 데이터 무덤을 지식의 금괴로 바꿀 수 있는 도구의 체계적인 개발이 필요하다는 결론으로 이어지는 것이 논리적입니다.

question: 6. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
passage: In 2006, researchers conducted a study on the motivations for helping after the September 11th terrorist attacks against the United States. (A) In the study, they found that individuals who gave money, blood, goods, or other forms of assistance because of other-focused motives - giving to reduce another's discomfort - were almost four times more likely to still be giving support one year later. (B) They also found that those whose original motivation was to reduce personal distress were much less likely to continue giving. (C) The events of September 11th emotionally affected people throughout the United States. Those who gave to reduce their own distress reduced their emotional arousal with their initial gift, discharging that emotional distress. (D) However, those who gave to reduce others' distress did not stop empathizing with victims who continued to struggle long after the attacks. (E) This finding suggests that empathy-driven compassion leads to more enduring acts of kindness than those motivated by self-relief.
insertion_sentence: This effect likely stems from differences in emotional arousal.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'This effect'는 앞 문장(B)에서 언급된, 개인의 고통을 줄이려는 동기를 가진 사람들은 도움을 지속할 가능성이 훨씬 낮다는 결과를 가리킵니다. (C) 뒤에 이어지는 문장들은 왜 그러한 차이가 발생하는지를 '정서적 각성(emotional arousal)'의 해소 여부로 설명하고 있으므로, (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: The size of a species is not accidental. It's a fine-tuned interaction between a species and the world it inhabits. Over large periods of time, size fluctuations have often signalled significant changes in the environment. In general, animals have been growing ⓐ<u>larger</u> during the past 500 million years. Marine species exhibit a remarkable increase in average body size, expanding 150-fold over this period. However, we are starting to observe ⓑ<u>alterations</u> in this tendency. Scientists have discovered that many animals are shrinking. Globally, species across all categories are exhibiting a trend of ⓒ<u>diminishment</u>, with a significant contributing factor identified being elevated temperatures. Animals living in the Italian Alps, for example, have seen temperatures ⓓ<u>rise</u> by three to four degrees Celsius since the 1980s. To ⓔ<u>seek</u> overheating, chamois goats now spend more of their days resting rather than searching for food, and as a result, in just a few decades, the new generations of chamois are 25 percent smaller.
explanation: 글의 흐름상 샤무아 염소들은 온도가 상승함에 따라 체온이 너무 높아지는 과열을 '피하기' 위해서 먹이를 찾는 대신 휴식을 취하며 시간을 보낸다는 맥락이 되어야 합니다. 따라서 '추구하다/찾다'라는 뜻의 seek는 문맥상 적절하지 않으며, avoid(피하다)와 같은 단어로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
passage: Introverted leaders ⓐ<u>do have to overcome</u> the strong cultural presumption that extroverts are more effective leaders. ⓑ<u>Although the population splits into almost equal parts</u> between introverts and extroverts, more than 96 percent of managers and executives are extroverted. In a study done in 2006, 65 percent of senior corporate executives ⓒ<u>viewed introversion as a barrier</u> to leadership. We must reexamine this stereotype, however, as it doesn't always hold true. Regent University found that a desire to be of service to others and ⓓ<u>to empower them grow</u>, which is more common among introverts than extroverts, is a key factor in becoming a leader and retaining leadership. So-called servant leadership, dating back to ancient philosophical literature, adheres to ⓔ<u>the belief which a company's goals are best achieved</u> by helping workers or customers achieve their goals. Such leaders do not seek attention but ⓕ<u>rather want to shine a light</u> on others' wins and achievements; servant leadership requires humility, but ⓖ<u>that humility ultimate pays off</u>.
options: ① 1개
② 2개
③ 3개
④ 4개
⑤ 5개
explanation:
어법상 어색한 부분은 ⓓ, ⓔ, ⓖ로 총 3개이다.
- ⓓ: empower는 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취하는 동사이므로 'to empower them to grow'가 옳다.
- ⓔ: the belief를 선행사로 하며 뒤에 완전한 절을 이끄는 동격의 접속사 'that'이 와야 한다(which는 관계대명사).
- ⓖ: 동사구 'pays off'를 수식하기 위해서는 형용사 ultimate가 아닌 부사 형태인 'ultimately'가 되어야 한다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: A young child may be puzzled when <u>①asked</u> to distinguish between the directions of right and left. But that same child may find it easy <u>②to determine</u> the directions of up and down or back and front. Scientists propose that this occurs because, although we experience three dimensions, only two had a strong influence on our evolution: the vertical dimension, with gravity <u>③defined</u> it and, in mobile species, the front/back dimension as defined by the positioning of sensory and feeding mechanisms. These influence our perception of vertical versus horizontal, far versus close, and the search for dangers from above (such as an eagle) or below (such as a snake). However, the left right axis is not as <u>④relevant in nature</u>. A bear is equally dangerous from its left or the right side, but not if it is upside down. In fact, when observing a scene containing plants, animals, and man made objects such as cars or street signs, we can only tell when left and right have been inverted if we observe <u>⑤those</u> artificial items.
explanation: 「with + 명사 + 분사」 구문에서, gravity가 수직 차원인 it을 직접 정의하는 능동 관계의 현재분사 defining이 와야 하므로 defined는 어법상 어색합니다.

question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Imagine that seven out of ten working Americans got fired tomorrow. What would they all do? It's hard to believe you'd have an economy at all if you gave pink slips to more than half the labor force.
ordered_passages: (A) Since then, wave upon wave of new occupations have arrived - appliance repair person, food chemist, photographer, web designer - each building on previous automation. Today, the vast majority of us are doing jobs that no farmer from the 1800s could have imagined.

(B) But the displaced workers did not sit idle. Instead, automation created hundreds of millions of jobs in entirely new fields. Those who once farmed were now manning the factories that manufactured farm equipment, cars, and other industrial products.

(C) But that is what the industrial revolution did to the workforce of the early 19th century. Two hundred years ago, 70 percent of American workers lived on the farm. Today automation has eliminated all but 1 percent of their jobs, replacing them with machines.
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 노동 인구의 대다수가 해고되는 가상의 경제적 위기 상황을 가정한다. (C)는 이러한 대규모 실직이 실제 19세기 산업 혁명 당시에 농업 인구 감소라는 형태로 일어났던 일임을 언급하며 구체적인 수치를 제시한다. (B)는 그렇게 농장을 떠난 노동자들이 놀고 있었던 것이 아니라 공장 노동자 등 자동화가 만들어낸 새로운 분야의 일자리를 얻게 되었음을 설명한다. 마지막으로 (A)는 그 이후로 더 다양한 새로운 직종들이 대거 등장하여 현대의 노동 시장을 형성하게 되었음을 서술하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적이다. 따라서 가장 적절한 순서는 (C)-(B)-(A)이다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control. Scientists manipulate a variable of interest, and see if there's a difference. At the same time, they attempt to control for the potential effects of all other variables. The importance of controlled experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often correlated. For example, people who take vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who don't take vitamins. As a result, if we want to study the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely observe the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to create a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world. That's just what scientific experiments do. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while _____________________.
options: ① varying all other related factors
② focusing solely on external correlations
③ observing naturally occurring conditions
④ eliminating the need for controlled conditions
⑤ maintaining the consistency of all other conditions
explanation: 실험 방법의 핵심은 관심 있는 하나의 변인만을 조작하고, 결과에 영향을 줄 수 있는 다른 모든 잠재적 변인들을 통제(control)하여 일관되게 유지하는 것입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 한 번에 하나의 특정 변인을 조작하는 동안 '다른 모든 조건의 일관성을 유지한다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.

② 오로지 외부 상관관계에만 집중하면서
③ 자연적으로 발생하는 조건들을 관찰하면서
④ 통제된 조건의 필요성을 제거하면서
⑤ 다른 모든 조건의 일관성을 유지하면서

question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)를 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
passage: When evaluating a policy, people tend to concentrate on how the policy will fix some particular problem while ignoring or downplaying other effects it may have. explanation: 지문에서 자연 세계에는 네온사인이나 화려한 단어가 없으며, 꽃들은 문자 언어나 네온사인 대신 '향기의 언어'를 사용하여 광고한다고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 꽃이 네온사인 같은 시각적 전시에 의존한다는 ②번은 본문 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 식당들은 잠재적인 고객을 끌어들이기 위해 매력적인 심상을 만드는 엄선된 단어들을 사용한다.
② 자연에서, 꽃들은 방문하는 동물들에게 그들의 제공물을 홍보하기 위해 네온사인 같은 시각적 전시에 의존한다.

question: 24. 윗글에 대한 설명이다. 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어를 <조건>에 맞게 넣어 문장을 완성한 후, 그 문장을 그대로 옮겨 적으시오. [4.0점]
passage: All of the restaurants are using carefully chosen words to evoke vivid mental images of delicious food and rich desserts in order to draw the potential customer to their particular establishment. Just like the restaurants, nature has its own dining establishments. In a fashion similar to the restaurants' financial dependence upon drawing in many customers, the restaurateurs of the natural world (i.e., flowers) must also attract potential diners to sample their offerings in order to survive and succeed. In the natural world, there are no neon signs or flashy words in which to market a potential meal to hungry animals. These restaurants that I am referring to are the world's flowers, and the potential guests are the host of organisms that visit flowers to obtain nectar and other valuable resources. Instead of using a written language or neon sign, they advertise their offerings just as effectively using the language of smell.
subjective_conditions: 각 단어는 지문에 사용된 명사로 하고, 주어진 첫 알파벳으로 시작할 것
subjective_answer_format: Like restaurants in the human world, which offer food to visitors and attract customers using language, (A)________ in nature ─ acting like those (B)________ ─ provide resources for visiting (C)________ and attract them using (D)________.정답: ___________________________________________________
answer: Like restaurants in the human world, which offer food to visitors and attract customers using language, flowers in nature ─ acting like those restaurants ─ provide resources for visiting organisms and attract them using smell.
explanation: 본문의 내용을 요약하는 문장입니다. (A) 자연계에서 식당 역할을 하는 주체는 flowers입니다. (B) 이들이 비유되는 대상은 앞의 restaurants입니다. (C) 꿀을 얻기 위해 방문하는 손님은 organisms입니다. (D) 광고를 위해 사용하는 수단은 smell입니다.

question: 25. 윗글의 흐름으로 보아, (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말을 바르게 짝지은 것은?
passage: Would you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month? Most people will opt for the larger sum in thirteen months ─ where else will you find a monthly interest rate of 10 percent. A wise choice, since the interest will compensate you generously for any risks you face by waiting the extra few weeks. Second question: Would you prefer $1,000 today cash on the table or $1,100 in a month? If you think like most people, you'll take the $1,000 right away. This is amazing. In both cases, if you hold out for just a month longer, you get $100 more. In the first case. it's simple enough. You figure: "I've already waited twelve months; what's one more?" Not in the second case. The introduction of "now" causes us to make inconsistent decisions. Science calls this phenomenon hyperbolic discounting. (A)________ a reward is, (B)________ our "emotional interest rate" rises and (C)________ we are willing to give up in exchange for it.
options: ① The further   the lower the less
② The further   the higher the more
③ The closer   the lower the less
④ The closer   the higher the more
⑤ The nearer   the lower the more
explanation: 이 글은 시간에 따른 보상의 가치 평가인 '쌍곡선 할인(hyperbolic discounting)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 사람들은 보상이 당장 눈앞에 있을 때(closer) 감정적 이자율이 급격히 높아져(higher), 미래의 더 큰 이득을 포기하더라도 당장의 보상을 얻기 위해 더 많은(more) 비용을 지불하거나 손해를 감수하는 경향이 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 closer, (B)에는 higher, (C)에는 more가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 멀수록, 낮아지고, 덜
② 멀수록, 높아지고, 더
③ 가까울수록, 낮아지고, 덜

question: 26. 윗글에 관한 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Would you rather receive $1,000 in a year or $1,100 in a year and a month? Second question: Would you prefer $1,000 today cash on the table or $1,100 in a month? If you think like most people, you'll take the $1,000 right away. This is amazing. ② Whether it's the "one year vs. thirteen months" scenario or the "now vs. one month" scenario, waiting an extra month yields an additional $100.

options_translation: ① 사람들은 1년에 1,000달러를 받는 것보다 13개월 후에 1,100달러를 받는 것을 선택할 가능성이 더 높다.

question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

(A)는 이 이론에 따르면 사람들이 비판에 관대해질 때 이러한 행동을 더 하기 쉽다는 부연 설명을 덧붙입니다. 다만, 실제 지문 맥락상 (A)의 tolerant는 원문의 의도와 다를 수 있으나 주어진 순서 조합상 (C)-(B)-(A)가 가장 논리적입니다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Waste has historically been seen as a necessary driver of the economy. Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly ⓐ<u>dependent</u> on the demand for that product. Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be wasted, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be ⓑ<u>sustained</u>. Many strategies have been incorporated into product design and use to ensure that waste is inevitable, such as planned obsolescence, limited access to tools for repairs, and use of cheap materials. All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a ⓒ<u>replacement</u>. Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that prioritizing the ⓓ<u>accumulation</u> of waste via repair and remanufacturing creates a different kind of demand: products as a service. Through this setup, companies simply lease out products that were once sold directly to the customer. With this transition of ownership, companies maintain profit by offering maintenance and repair services and are encouraged to develop ⓔ<u>long-lasting</u> products.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 수리와 재제조(remanufacturing)를 통해 제품 수명을 연장하는 것은 폐기물의 '축적(accumulation)'을 우선시하는 것이 아니라 폐기물을 '방지'하거나 '감소'시키는 행위입니다. 문맥상 ⓓ의 'accumulation'은 수리와 재제조의 목적과 상반되므로 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Viewing time as a purchasable and consistent product cemented artificial views on time into our psyche, but every now and again we are forced to acknowledge this mistake. Indeed, the Earth's spin is generally slowing because the moon's gravity is acting as a drag, so days are getting longer by about 1.7 milliseconds per century. When events like this happen, a bunch of humans make the decision to add a small slice of time to your day, without your knowledge. ⑤ the need to reconcile scientific time keeping with knowledge

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
passage: Distinguishing moths from butterflies on outward appearance is not always easy, but there are a few rules of thumb that can help. In most butterflies the antennae end with a small club-shaped swelling, whereas in moths they are usually feathery or narrow to a fine tip. Butterflies tend to rest with their wings held shut above their body, whereas moths more usually rest with the upper sides of the wings on full view. Further distinctions can be made by looking for a tiny hook that joins fore- and hindwings, a feature only present in moths. The stereotypical differences, with moths cast as the gloomy, nocturnal cousins of colourful sun-loving butterflies are simply wrong. There are many brightly coloured moths and many which are active throughout the day. Equally, there are a few nocturnal butterflies and plenty that come clothed in shades of brown and grey. It's more sensible to think of them together; both butterflies and moths are beautiful and fascinating insects.

question: 21. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]

options_translation: ① 검증 가능한 가설의 추구
② 모든 변수의 엄격한 제거

question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.3점]

question: 24. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은? [2.9점]
passage: We can discard or replace a scientific theory only if we have a better way of explaining the evidence that supports it. The theories of Newton and Einstein offer great examples. A vast body of evidence supports Newton's theory of gravity, but by the late nineteenth century scientists had begun to discover cases where its predictions did not perfectly match observations. These discrepancies were explained only when Einstein developed his general theory of relativity, which was able to match the observations. Still, the many successes of Newton's theory could not be ignored, and Einstein's theory would not have gained acceptance if it had not been able to explain these successes equally well. It did, and that is why we now view Einstein's theory as a broader theory of gravity than Newton's theory. Some scientists today are seeking a theory of gravity that will go beyond Einstein's. If any new theory ever gains acceptance, it will have to match all the successes of Einstein's theory as well as work in new realms where Einstein's theory does not.
options: ① The discrepancies in Newton's theory first appeared when scientists were searching for new theories of gravity.
② A new theory must account for all the successful predictions of its predecessor to be widely accepted.
③ Newton's theory of gravity was quickly discarded by scientists after Einstein published the general theory of relativity.
④ A scientific theory is discarded as soon as its predictions fail to perfectly match observations in any given case.
⑤ The search for a new theory of gravity beyond Einstein's is motivated solely by the need to explain Newton's remaining successes.

passage: Historically, palaces weren't just homes; they were carefully constructed stages designed to impress and intimidate. Conversely, it also allowed subjects to gaze up at their leaders, creating a sense of awe and distance. explanation: 이 글은 시장 메커니즘의 강점이 개인들이 자신의 행동을 통해 지식을 드러내게 하는 유인(incentive)을 제공한다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 정치적 협상과 달리 시장에서는 가격 변화에 따라 개인들이 즉각적으로 행동을 수정하며(예: 필요하지 않은 물건의 구매 중단, 수요 없는 물건의 판매 중단), 이를 통해 유용한 정보가 시장에 드러나게 됩니다. 따라서 시장 체계의 주요 장점은 사람들이 즉각적으로 행동을 조정하고 유용한 정보를 드러내도록 권장한다는 5번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 개인이 시장에서 공동의 가치를 공유할 때 사회적 협력과 신뢰가 강화된다.
② 시장 메커니즘의 효과는 경제적 결정에서 감정적 요인을 최소화하는 데 있다.
③ 정치적 협상은 전략적 이점을 극대화하기 위해 자신의 진정한 선호를 숨기는 것의 중요성을 보여준다.
④ 기술 혁신은 시장에서 인간의 의사 결정을 자동화된 시스템으로 대체함으로써 효율성을 가속화한다.
⑤ 시장 체계의 주요 장점은 사람들이 자신의 행동을 즉각적으로 조정하고 유용한 정보를 드러내도록 권장한다는 것이다.

question: 2. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: All human cultures mark the passing of time by the differences they observe in the world around them. Our choice of which differences to mark depends firstly on what we can observe and secondly on what is important in our lives. ⓐHow we mark the differences - the shapes of our calendars and our rituals - depends on the connections we make between those two things. ⓑIn pre-modern Europe, where seasonal variation was pronounced, the solar cycle became the natural basis for making time. ⓒBy contrast, among the largely nomadic peoples of Arabia, for whom seasonal changes was less relevant, the lunar cycle was more practical. ⓓThe lunar calendar illustrates the passage of time, showing that time can be perceived not as a straight line, but as a continuous cycle. ⓔThat did not make it inevitable that Islam would use a lunar calendar and Roman Christianity a solar one, but political and religious decisions were made from options limited by geography and lifestyle, filtered through tradition.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 인간의 문화가 주변 세계의 관찰 가능한 변화와 삶의 중요도에 따라 시간을 측정하는 방식(태양력 vs 태음력)이 달라진다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 유럽은 계절 변화가 뚜렷해 태양력을, 아라비아 유목민은 계절 변화가 적어 태음력을 사용하게 된 지리적·생활 양식적 배경을 다루고 있습니다. 그러나 ④번 문장은 태음력이 시간을 직선이 아닌 순환적인 것으로 인식하게 한다는 '시간의 개념적 성격'을 설명하고 있어, 문화적 배경에 따른 역법의 선택이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Behavioral contagion, the tendency of people ⓐ<u>to adopt the attitudes or actions of those around them</u>, shares profound parallels with viral contagion in the way both spread rapidly through exposure and proximity. For instance, just as individuals who spend time near those infected with a virus ⓑ<u>are at a higher risk of becoming infected</u>, people who associate with heavy drinkers tend to drink more themselves. However, key differences also exist between these two forms of contagion. One such distinction is that visibility ⓒ<u>fosters behavioral contagion</u> but discourages viral transmission. For example, solar panels visible from the street are more likely to inspire nearby homeowners to install their own, while we ⓓ<u>are less inclined to withdraw from others who exhibit visible symptoms of sickness</u>. Another major difference is that viral contagion is almost always harmful, whereas behavioral contagion can ⓔ<u>have both detrimental and beneficial sides</u> - for example, it can spread unhealthy habits like smoking, but also encourage eco-friendly behaviors such as installing solar panels.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 행동 전염과 바이러스 전염의 공통점과 차이점을 다루고 있습니다. 문맥상 행동 전염은 가시성(visibility)에 의해 촉진되지만, 바이러스 전염은 가시성에 의해 억제된다고 설명합니다. ⓓ가 포함된 문장의 앞부분에서 가시성이 바이러스 전염을 저해한다고 했으므로, 질병의 가시적인 증상을 보이는 사람으로부터는 '물러나지 않으려 한다(less inclined to withdraw)'가 아니라 '물러나려 한다(more inclined to withdraw / more likely to withdraw)'가 되어야 논리적으로 맞습니다.

question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Dictionary definitions are constantly revised to keep up with our changing uses and knowledge. In Roman times, "addicts" were people who were unable to pay their debts and gave themselves as slaves to their creditors. The word eventually came to be associated with drug dependency: one becomes a slave to one's addiction. The word "husband" originally referred to being a homeowner; it had nothing to do with being married. But because owning your own property made it more likely you'd find a mate, the word eventually came to mean a male who has been wed. On November 5th, 1605, Guy Fawkes tried to blow up the British Parliament. He was captured and put to death. Loyalists burned his effigy, which they nicknamed the "guy." Centuries later, the word lost its negative connotation and a musical named Guys and Dolls ran on Broadway. In American slang, bad means good, cool means great, and wicked means excellent. If you could transport yourself one hundred years into the future, you'd find yourself confused by your great-grandchildren's speech because language itself is an ever-changing reflection of human invention.
options: ① The Use of Language to Shape Society
② Changes in the Meaning of Words Over Time
③ Language as a True Reflection of Social Hierarchy
④ The Importance of Dictionary Definitions in Linguistics
⑤ The Roman Origin of Common Words: "Addicts" and "Husband"
explanation: 이 글은 시간이 흐름에 따라 단어의 의미가 어떻게 변화하는지를 다양한 사례(addicts, husband, guy, slang 등)를 통해 설명하고 있습니다. 'addicts'는 원래 채무 노예를 뜻했으나 약물 의존으로, 'husband'는 집주인에서 기혼 남성으로 의미가 변했으며, 'guy'는 부정적 의미에서 일상적인 단어로 변했습니다. 따라서 글의 제목으로는 '시간에 따른 단어 의미의 변화'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사회를 형성하기 위한 언어의 사용
② 시간에 따른 단어 의미의 변화
③ 사회적 계급의 진정한 반영으로서의 언어
④ 언어학에서 사전적 정의의 중요성
⑤ 일반적인 단어들의 로마 시대 기원: "Addicts"와 "Husband"

question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: All translators feel some pressure from the community of readers for whom they are doing their work. And all translators arrive at their interpretations in dialogue with other people. The English poet Alexander Pope had pretty good Greek, but when he set about translating Homer's Iliad in the early 18th century he was not on his own. He had Greek commentaries to refer to, and translations that had already been done in English, Latin, and French - and of course he had dictionaries. Translators always draw on more than one source text. Even when the scene of translation consists of just one person with a pen, paper, and the book that is being translated, or even when it is just one person translating orally for another, that person's linguistic knowledge arises from lots of other texts and other conversations. And then his or her idea of the translation's purpose will be influenced by the expectations of the person or people it is for. In both these senses every translation is a crowd translation.
options: ① Translation as a Collaborative Process
② The Translator's Personal Working Process
③ How Dictionaries Improve Translation Accuracy
④ The Difficulty of Translating Foreign Languages
⑤ The Changing Role of Translators in Modern Society
explanation: 이 글은 번역이 단순히 혼자 하는 작업이 아니라, 다른 텍스트, 이전의 번역본, 사전, 그리고 독자의 기대 등 다양한 외부 요소와 상호작용하며 이루어지는 과정임을 강조하고 있습니다. 필자는 이를 'crowd translation(군중 번역)'이라고 표현하며 번역의 협력적 성격을 설명하고 있으므로, 제목으로는 '협력적 과정으로서의 번역'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 협력적 과정으로서의 번역
② 번역가의 개인적인 작업 과정
③ 사전이 번역의 정확도를 높이는 방법

question: 6. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Mother cats can tell which kittens belong to them - when litters are mixed up they use their kittens' scent to distinguish them from offspring of other mothers.
ordered_passages: (A) There is uncertainty about what makes them behave in such manner, although distress vocalizations from kittens that are lost from their nest are known to be very powerful, so it might simply be difficult for the mother to ignore the urge to bring them back, even if they are not her own kittens.

(B) However, despite this ability, when faced with a selection of kittens who have wandered from the nest, her own and others that aren't hers, a mother cat doesn't appear to favor her own offspring when retrieving them.
(C) From an evolutionary perspective, this behavior makes sense. In the wild, a squeaking kitten out in the open is likely to attract predators, which is bad news for any other kittens around it.
(D) For the purpose of lowering the risk, a rapid rescue of any crying kitten would be a good strategy to prevent them from drawing unwanted attention.
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 어미 고양이가 자신의 새끼를 냄새로 구별할 수 있다는 능력을 설명합니다. (B)에서 'However, despite this ability'를 통해 자신의 새끼를 구별할 수 있음에도 불구하고 막상 데려올 때는 자신의 새끼를 편애하지 않는다는 반전 상황을 제시합니다. (A)에서는 이러한 행동의 원인에 대한 불확실성과 어미가 느끼는 본능적인 충동을 언급하고, (C)에서 'From an evolutionary perspective'를 통해 이 행동이 진화론적으로 타당함을 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (D)에서 포식자의 위험을 낮추기 위해 울고 있는 어떤 새끼든 빨리 구조하는 것이 전략적임을 결론짓습니다. 따라서 (B)-(A)-(C)-(D)가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 7. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Mirror neurons are the hardware of empathy, and so what would make more sense than to look and see which animals possess these cells? And this is exactly where modern research now stands: all researchers know so far is that apes possess mirror neurons. We still need to test to see which other species are like us in this respect. Scientists often publicly speculate that we can probably expect surprises here, too. They assume that all animals that live in herds or large groups possess similar brain mechanisms, because social units function only if individuals can see things from the perspective of others in the group and feel what they are feeling. I can see a goldfish waving its fin at us. As an animal that travels around in a tightly-knit group, it's on board with this idea - or at least swimming alongside the boat.
options: ① Mirror neurons are concerned with the ability of animals to empathize.
② All that researchers have known until now is that apes have mirror neurons.
③ Further research is needed to identify which animals, apart from apes, have mirror neurons.
④ Scientists speculate that solitary animals possess mirror neurons.
⑤ Society functions when its members understand one another's perspectives and share emotions.
explanation: 지문에서 과학자들은 무리를 지어 사는 동물들이 거울 뉴런과 같은 뇌 기제(brain mechanisms)를 가질 것으로 추정합니다. 그 이유는 사회적 단위가 타인의 관점에서 사물을 보고 그들의 감정을 느낄 수 있을 때만 기능하기 때문입니다. 따라서 혼자 생활하는(solitary) 동물이 거울 뉴런을 가질 것이라고 추측한다는 선택지 ④는 지문의 내용과 상충합니다.
options_translation: ① 거울 뉴런은 동물의 공감 능력과 관련이 있다.
② 지금까지 연구자들이 알고 있는 전부는 유인원이 거울 뉴런을 가지고 있다는 것이다.
③ 유인원 이외에 어떤 동물이 거울 뉴런을 가지고 있는지 확인하기 위해 추가 연구가 필요하다.
④ 과학자들은 홀로 생활하는 동물들이 거울 뉴런을 가지고 있다고 추측한다.
⑤ 사회는 구성원들이 서로의 관점을 이해하고 감정을 공유할 때 기능한다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Sleep is clearly about more than just resting. One curious fact is that animals that are hibernating also have periods of sleep. It comes as a surprise to most of us, but hibernation and sleep are not the same thing at all, at least not from a neurological and metabolic perspective. Hibernating is more like being anesthetized: the subject is unconscious but not actually asleep. So a hibernating animal needs to get a few hours of conventional sleep each day within the larger unconsciousness. A further surprise to most of us is that bears, the most famous of wintry sleepers, don't actually hibernate. Real hibernation involves profound unconsciousness and a dramatic fall in body temperature - often to around 32 degrees Fahrenheit. By this definition, bears don't hibernate, because their body temperature stays near normal and they are easily awakened. Their winter sleeps are more accurately called a state of torpor, which is a light, short-term rest state where the animal's body slows down gradually.
options: ① From neurological and metabolic perspectives, hibernation and sleep can be regarded as virtually indistinguishable states.
② Even while remaining in a prolonged state of unconsciousness, an animal in hibernation still needs several hours of normal sleep each day.
③ Genuine hibernation involves entering a deep state of unconsciousness accompanied by a significant drop in body temperature.
④ During a bear's winter sleep, its body temperature does not experience a substantial decline but instead is maintained close to normal levels.
⑤ The sleep that bears enter in winter is not true hibernation but is better characterized as torpor, a state in which the animal's body becomes less active over time.
explanation: 지문에서 동면(hibernation)과 수면(sleep)은 신경학적 및 대사적 관점에서 볼 때 전혀 같은 것이 아니라고 명시되어 있습니다(hibernation and sleep are not the same thing at all). 따라서 이 둘을 거의 구별할 수 없는 상태로 간주할 수 있다는 선택지 ①은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 신경학적 및 대사적 관점에서 볼 때, 동면과 수면은 사실상 구별할 수 없는 상태로 간주될 수 있다.
② 장기간의 무의식 상태에 머물면서도, 동면 중인 동물은 여전히 매일 몇 시간의 일반적인 수면이 필요하다.
③ 진짜 동면은 체온의 현저한 하락과 함께 깊은 무의식 상태에 들어가는 것을 포함한다.
④ 곰의 겨울잠 동안, 체온은 실질적인 저하를 겪지 않고 대신 정상 수준에 가깝게 유지된다.
⑤ 곰이 겨울에 들어가는 잠은 진정한 동면이 아니라 시간이 지남에 따라 동물의 몸이 덜 활발해지는 상태인 휴면(torpor)으로 더 잘 특징지어진다.

question: 9. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Theoretically, our brain would have the capacity to store all experiences throughout life, reaching the quality of a DVD. However, this theoretical capacity is offset by the energy demand associated with the process of storing and retrieving information in memory. As a result, the brain develops efficient strategies, becoming dependent on shortcuts. When we observe a face, the visual image captured by the eyes is highly variable, depending on the point of view, lighting conditions and other contextual factors. Nevertheless, we are able to recognize the face as the same, maintaining the underlying identity. The brain, rather than focusing on the details of visualization, creates and stores general patterns that allow for consistent recognition across diverse circumstances. This ability to match what we see with general visual memory patterns serves as an effective mechanism for optimizing brain performance and saving energy. The brain, being naturally against unnecessary effort, constantly seeks to simplify and generalize information to facilitate the cognitive process.
options: ① methods for undermining cognitive recall in the brain
② importance of detailed recognition in identifying faces
③ relationship between the brain's storage capacity and emotion regulation
④ how the brain optimizes its performance by simplifying incoming information
⑤ role of repetition and reinforcement in strengthening memory traces in the brain
explanation: 이 글은 뇌가 엄청난 정보를 저장할 수 있는 이론적 용량을 가지고 있지만, 에너지 효율성을 위해 정보를 단순화하고 일반화하는 효율적인 전략(지름길)을 사용한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 시각적 세부 사항에 집중하기보다 일반적인 패턴을 생성하여 에너지를 절약하고 인지 과정을 원활하게 한다는 내용이 핵심입니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 '뇌가 들어오는 정보를 단순화하여 성능을 최적화하는 방법'인 4번입니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌의 인지적 회상을 저해하는 방법들
② 얼굴 식별에서 세부적인 인식의 중요성
③ 뇌의 저장 용량과 감정 조절 사이의 관계
④ 들어오는 정보를 단순화함으로써 뇌가 성능을 최적화하는 방식
⑤ 뇌의 기억 흔적을 강화하는 데 있어 반복과 강화의 역할

question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There is research that supports the idea that cognitive factors influence the phenomenology of the perceived world. Delk and Fillenbaum asked participants to match the color of figures with the color of their background. Some of the figures depicted objects associated with a particular color. These included typically red objects such as an apple, lips, and a symbolic heart. Other objects were presented that are not usually associated with red, such as a mushroom or a bell. However, all the figures were made out of the same red-orange cardboard. Participants then had to match the figure to a background varying from dark to light red. They had to make the background color match the color of the figures. The researchers found that red-associated objects required more red in the background to be judged a match than did the objects that are not associated with the color red. This implies that __________________________________.
options: ① people generally prefer warm colors like red to cool colors
② color perception operates independently from cognitive expectations
③ participants' emotional reactions to red objects made them perceive those objects as more vivid
④ cognitive associations between objects and colors can shape our visual perception of those colors
⑤ the complexity of the figure shapes influenced color judgment, leading participants to choose stronger reds for certain shapes
explanation: 연구 결과, 사과나 입술처럼 전형적으로 붉은색과 연관된 물체일수록 참가자들은 배경색을 더 붉게 조정해야 일치한다고 느꼈습니다. 실제 물체의 색은 동일한 주황빛 빨간색 카드보드였음에도 불구하고, 물체에 대해 미리 가지고 있던 인지적 연상(사과는 빨갛다는 생각)이 실제 색상 지각에 영향을 주어 더 붉게 보이게 만든 것입니다. 따라서 '물체와 색상 사이의 인지적 연상이 해당 색상에 대한 우리의 시각적 지각을 형성할 수 있다'는 4번이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]

question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Hobbes argues that man cannot stay ⓐ<u>peaceful</u> in the state of nature, since his instinct to protect his existence prevents him from acting morally. Hence, the only place where morality and moral liberty will begin to find an application begins in a place in which a sovereign power, namely the state, emerges. Hobbes thus describes the state of nature as a circumstance ⓑ<u>where</u> man's life is "solitary, poor, nasty, brutish and short". It means when people live without a general power to control them all, they are indeed in a state of war. In other words, Hobbes, who accepted that human beings are not social and political beings in the state of nature, ⓒ<u>maintaining</u> that without the power human beings in the state of nature are "antisocial and rational based on their selfishness". Moreover, since society is not a natural phenomenon and there is no natural force ⓓ<u>bringing</u> people together, what will bring them together as a society is not mutual affection according to Hobbes. It is, rather, mutual fear of men's present and future that ⓔ<u>assembles</u> them, since the cause of fear is a common drive among people in the state of nature.
explanation: ⓒ 'maintaining'이 포함된 문장의 주어는 'Hobbes'이고, 'who accepted that human beings are not social and political beings in the state of nature'는 주어를 수식하는 관계대명사절입니다. 따라서 문장의 본동사가 필요한 자리이므로 현재분사 형태인 'maintaining'을 정동사인 'maintains' 또는 'maintained'로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The term "anchoring" was introduced by Roland Barthes who observed that text is often used next to images (his focus was on photographs) to confine meaning. Of all possible literal or implied interpretations an image could elicit, text would point the viewer towards a desired, specific direction. In advertising, as Barthes argues, the symbolic message does not guide identification but interpretation. The viewer is not asked to recognize what they see but to understand why they see it and what it means to them. By combining images with text, advertising produces symbolic meaning that is accurate and specific on the one hand, richer on the other, thus adding depth and eliminating breadth of rational and emotional interpretations. The headline or tagline of an ad directs the reader through the intended meanings of the image, so that the reader avoids some and receives others. It "remote-controls" the reader towards a meaning chosen in advance.
summary_sentence: Roland Barthes' concept of "anchoring" illustrates how textual elements (A)__________ the potential range of meanings an image may evoke. ③ (A) obliterate (B) ambiguous
④ (A) fabricate (B) spontaneous
⑤ (A) delimit (B) predetermined

passage: Although empathy is widely praised by scholars and public figures, not everyone is an empathy booster. Critics of empathy argue that empathy will not save us from interpersonal and intergroup conflict. In fact, they argue, empathy makes such conflicts worse. These critics maintain that empathy can be exhausting and lead to burnout or insensitivity to suffering. They argue that we tend to empathize strongly with our in group and resist empathizing with out groups, and even enjoy the suffering of out groups in competitive or threatening contexts. Thus, the prescription for more empathy is often inefficient in cases of conflict. Empathy, they argue, can further entrench conflict and force us into an us vs. them mentality. Finally, even when we try to empathize with others who are dissimilar from us or in unfamiliar contexts, sometimes we are unable to accurately empathize with their experiences, causing further misunderstandings and frustration. Critics of empathy argue that we should give up on empathy and employ other tools in pursuit of social harmony, e.g., rational compassion or moral emotions like fear, anger, and shame.
summary_sentence: Although empathy is widely praised, critics argue that it can be (A) __________ and even make conflict worse. Therefore, they suggest (B) __________ empathy with rational compassion or moral sentiments to pursue social harmony more steadily.

passage: Conditioned Place Preference is a way of finding out what animals want. Researchers train them to associate one place with an experience such as food or a loud noise and another place with something completely different, usually where nothing happens. The two places are made obviously different to make it as easy as possible for the animal to associate each place with what happened to it there. The animal's preference for being in one place or another is measured both before and after its experiences in the two places. If there is a shift in where the animal chooses to spend its time for the reward, this suggests that it liked the experience and is trying to repeat it. Conversely, if it now avoids the place the stimulus appeared and starts to prefer the place it did not experience it, then this suggests that it found the stimulus unpleasant. For example, mice with cancer show a preference for the place where they have been given morphine, a drug used to relieve pain, rather than where they have received saline whereas healthy mice developed no such preference. This suggests that the mice with cancer wanted the morphine.
summary_sentence: Conditioned Place Preference helps researchers infer what an animal desires by measuring its (A)__________ shift. If an animal spends more time in a chamber conditioned with a particular stimulus, it indicates that the animal regards the stimulus as (B)__________; if not, it suggests the stimulus is (C)__________.

② emotional ... disappointing ... unattractive
③ behavioral ... rewarding ... less favored

passage: Weber's law deals with how people perceive differences between two stimuli. It suggests that we might not be able to detect a 1-mm difference when we are looking at lines 466 mm and 467 mm in length, but we may be able to detect a 1-mm difference when we are comparing a line 2 mm long with one 3 mm long. Another example of this principle is that we can detect 1 candle when it is lit in an otherwise dark room. But when 1 candle is lit in a room in which 100 candles are already burning, we may not notice the light from this candle. Therefore, the Just-noticeable difference (JND) varies as a function of the strength of the signals. For example, the JND is greater for very loud noises than it is for much more quiet sounds. When a sound is very weak, we can tell that another sound is louder, even if it is barely louder. When a sound is very loud, to tell that another sound is even louder, it has to be much louder. Thus, Weber's law means that it is harder to distinguish between two samples when those samples are larger or stronger levels of the stimuli.A: What we learned today, Weber's Law, means that how much we notice the difference between two stimuli depends on the strength of the original stimulus.B: The strength of the stimulus? What exactly does that mean?A: The key is that "the stronger the original stimulus is, the greater the change needed to perceive a difference." We call this the Just-Noticeable Difference (JND).B: Can you explain it with an example?A: Sure. We can't distinguish a 1-mm difference on a long line, but we easily notice the 1-mm difference on a short line.B: I see! So, with a very loud sound, the volume has to increase a lot so that we can notice the difference, but with a quiet sound, even a slight increase is noticeable, right?A: Exactly. When a stimulus is already powerful, ________________________________. Got it?B: JND gets larger with stronger stimuli! I understand now.
subjective_conditions: • 총 9단어로 작성할 것
• <보기>에 주어진 단어를 변형하지 않고 그대로 쓸 것
• <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것
• <보기> 이외의 단어를 추가하지 말 것
answer: Differentiating two samples successfully necessitates a significantly larger change.
explanation: 베버의 법칙(Weber's law)에 따르면, 초기 자극이 강력할수록 두 자극 사이의 차이를 감지하기 위해 필요한 변화의 정도(JND)가 커집니다. 따라서 자극이 이미 강력한 상태에서는 두 샘플을 성공적으로 구별하는 데 훨씬 더 큰 변화가 필요하다는 의미이므로, 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 'Differentiating two samples successfully necessitates a significantly larger change'라고 완성하는 것이 적절합니다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 요약문을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
passage: One factor that may hinder creativity is unawareness of the resources required in each activity in students' learning. Often students are unable to identify the resources they need to perform the task required of them. Different resources may be compulsory for specific learning tasks, and recognizing them may simplify the activity's performance. For example, it may be that students desire to conduct some experiments in their projects. There must be a prior investigation of whether the students will have access to the laboratory, equipment, and chemicals required for the experiment. To succeed, students need to prepare properly, which may include arranging laboratory technicians, money for chemicals, and necessary equipment where applicable. Even if some of the resources required for a task may not be available, figuring them out at an early stage may help students' creativity. It may even lead to adjusting the topic, finding alternative resources, and other means.
summary_sentence: One factor that can interfere with students' creativity is that they are not (A)____________________ for learning. Resource preparation in learning (B)____________________: leading to changing the topic or seeking alternatives.
subjective_conditions: • (A)는 5단어로, (B)는 4단어로 작성할 것
• <보기>에 주어진 단어를 변형하지 않고 그대로 쓸 것
• <보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것
• <보기> 이외의 단어를 추가하지 말 것
answer: (A) aware of the resources needed (B) helps enhance their creativity
explanation: 지문은 학습 시 필요한 자원을 인식하지 못하는 것이 학생들의 창의성을 저해할 수 있으며, 초기 단계에서 자원을 파악하는 것이 중요하다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A)에는 학습에 '필요한 자원을 인식하지(aware of the resources needed)' 못하는 것이 창의성을 방해한다는 내용이 들어가며, (B)에는 자원의 준비가 '그들의 창의성을 향상시키는 데 도움을 준다(helps enhance their creativity)'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 요지문을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
passage: Where scientific research is concerned, explanatory tales are expected to adhere closely to experimental data and to illuminate the regular and predictable features of experience. However, this paradigm sometimes conceals the fact that theories are deeply loaded with creative elements that shape the construction of research projects and the interpretations of evidence. Scientific explanations do not just relate a chronology of facts. They construct frameworks for systematically chosen data in order to provide a consistent and meaningful explanation of what is observed. Such constructions lead us to imagine specific kinds of subject matter in particular sorts of relations, and the storylines they inspire will prove more effective for analyzing some features of experience over others. When we neglect the creative contributions of such scientific imagination and treat models and interpretive explanations as straightforward facts - even worse, as facts including all of reality - we can blind ourselves to the limitations of a given model and fail to note its potential for misunderstanding a situation to which it ill applies.
summary_sentence: Scientific explanations are ____________________________ that provide meaningful interpretations of what is seen.
subjective_conditions: 총 9단어로 쓸 것
<보기>에 주어진 단어를 변형하지 않고 그대로 쓸 것
<보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것
<보기> 이외의 단어를 추가하지 말 것
answer: not mere collections of facts but creatively constructed frameworks
explanation: 과학적 설명은 단순히 사실의 나열이 아니라, 관찰된 것을 체계적으로 해석하기 위해 창의적으로 구성된 틀이라는 내용의 글입니다. 따라서 <보기>의 단어들을 활용하여 '단순한 사실의 모음이 아니라 창의적으로 구성된 틀'이라는 의미가 되도록 'not mere collections of facts but creatively constructed frameworks'로 영작하는 것이 적절합니다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 문장을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
passage: The future of work depends on a substituting force and a complementing one. In many tales, there are a hero and a villain fighting each other for dominance, but in our story, technology embodies both characters at once; it displaces humans, yet at the same time, needs their labor ever more elsewhere in the economy. This interaction accounts for why past worries about automation were misplaced: our ancestors had named the wrong winner in that fight, underestimating quite how great the complementing force would be or simply ignoring that factor altogether. It can also account for why economists have traditionally been dismissive of the idea that people are deprived of their livelihoods by technology: there appeared to be firm limits to the substituting force, leaving a great deal of work that could not be carried out by machines and _________________________________________ instead.
subjective_conditions: 총 10단어로 쓸 것
본문의 단어 1개를 추가로 사용하되, 반드시 변형하여 문법에 맞게 쓸 것
<보기>에 주어진 단어를 변형하지 않고 그대로 쓸 것
<보기>의 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것
answer: resulting in an increasing need for humans to handle it
explanation: 이 글은 기술이 인간의 노동을 대체하기도 하지만 동시에 보완하기도 한다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 앞부분은 기계가 수행할 수 없는 많은 양의 업무가 남아 있음을 말하고 있으며, 뒤따르는 구문은 그 결과로 인해 인간이 그 일을 처리해야 할 필요성이 증가했다는 내용이 와야 합니다. <보기>의 단어들과 본문의 'needs'를 명사형인 'need'로 변형하여 조합하면 'resulting in an increasing need for humans to handle it'이 되며, 이는 총 10단어로 조건에 부합합니다.

question: 12. 다음 Manuha Island Drone Film Contest에 관한 안내문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
