question: 13. 다음 글의 각 (A)~(C)에서 문맥에 맞는 말을 골라 짝지은 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Within liberal culture, the value of fair equality of opportunity for individuals (A)[exceeds / maintains] the preservation of the family's integrity. In contrast, for Confucian culture, while seeking fair equality of opportunity for individuals is important, the family assumes a fundamental role in human flourishing, and living within a family institution is considered the essential way of life. Individuals are primarily understood as family members before they are regarded as state citizens. Therefore, for Confucians, the family possesses inherent value that should never be abandoned, even if it results in certain societal (B)[harmony / unfairness]. Some cultures, like the liberal one, may choose to impose increasing restrictions on the role of families and implement more egalitarian government programs for education, healthcare, and other positive rights in society in the pursuit of fair equality of opportunity. On the other hand, other cultures, like the Confucian one, may prefer to primarily assign welfare responsibilities to the family, (C)[accepting / correcting] inequalities stemming from the existence of the family as long as everyone's basic freedoms and rights are safeguarded in the state.
options: ① exceeds - harmony - accepting
② exceeds - unfairness - accepting
③ exceeds - unfairness - correcting
④ maintains - unfairness - correcting

explanation: 자유주의 문화에서는 개인의 기회 균등이 가족의 온전함 보존보다 우선시되므로 (A)에는 '능가하다(exceeds)'가 적절합니다. 반면 유교 문화에서는 가족이 인간 번영의 근본적 역할을 하므로, 사회적 '불공정함(unfairness)'이 발생하더라도 가족의 가치를 포기하지 않으며, 기본적인 권리가 보장되는 한 가족으로 인해 발생하는 불평등을 '수용(accepting)'하는 경향이 있습니다.

question: 14. 다음 글에서 설명한 원리를 바닷물고기와 민물고기를 예로 들어 설명하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (단, 어형 변형 없음)
passage: Even though sea creatures live in it, they still need to take in water for their bodies to function properly. They just need to get rid of any extra salt it might bring with it. Salt absorbs water like a sponge. If you put a tiny mountain of salt on a small plate, then add enough water to the side, making sure an edge touches the salt, the salt will absorb the water. Now you have a pile of wet salt. Notice that it has increased in size. The same principle applies to sea creatures. If the body fluids in a sea animal are saltier than the seawater it lives in, then the extra salt in the creature's body will absorb seawater. This can cause them to swell up. On the other hand, if the amount of salt in the seawater is higher than the amount of salt in the body fluids of a sea animal, the extra salt in the water will draw fluids out of the creature's body, causing it to dehydrate and shrink.
summary_sentence: When a sea fish is placed in freshwater, the, fish will (A)_________. That's because the body fluids inside the sea fish are saltier than the freshwater it is in. On the other hand, when a freshwater fish is placed in seawater, the fish will (B)_________ and (C)_________. This is because the seawater has a higher amount of salt than the body fluids of the freshwater fish.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오
어형 변형 없음
explanation: 본문은 염분이 수분을 흡수하는 원리를 설명하고 있습니다. 바닷물고기를 민물에 넣으면 물고기 체액의 염분이 더 높아 외부 수분을 흡수하여 (A) 부풀어 오르게(swell up) 됩니다. 반대로 민물고기를 바닷물에 넣으면 외부 바닷물의 염분이 더 높아 체내 수분을 빼앗기게 되므로 (B) 탈수되고(dehydrate) (C) 수축(shrink)하게 됩니다.

question: 15. 다음 글을 읽고, 아래 질문에 답하고자 한다. <보기>에 주어진 단어만을 모두 한 번씩만 사용하여 빈칸을 완성하시오. (단, 어형 변형 없음)
passage: Manufacturers masterfully sow seeds of doubt about the adequacy of our current devices. Suddenly, the phone that was your lifeline a year ago is now a museum piece, unable to keep pace with your digital demands. And thus, the itch to upgrade begins, often before there's a genuine need. This cycle isn't just confined to our digital companions. It spills over into almost every aspect of consumer electronics, from the self-driving car to the smart fridge. Every product seems to be on an unstoppable march towards the next version, the next generation that promises to revolutionize your life. What's fascinating, or perhaps disturbing, is the utter efficacy of this cycle in shaping our desires. It's not so much that we want the newest device; we're led to believe we need it. The distinction between want and need blurs, shifting our financial priorities in favor of staying current with trends. For all the logical arguments against this ceaseless upgrading, the temptation remains compelling.
subjective_conditions: 보기의 단어만을 모두 한 번씩만 사용
어형 변형 없음
subjective_answer_format: Q: Based on the context, what does the 'blurring' of the distinction between want and need mean for a consumer's behavior?A: It means that ______________________ even when it is actually just a want created by manufacturers.
answer: consumers are masterfully led to believe they genuinely need the newest device for their life
explanation: 이 글은 제조업자들이 소비자들에게 현재 기기가 부족하다는 의구심을 심어주어, 단순한 '욕구(want)'를 '필요(need)'로 착각하게 만든다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 소비자들이 자신의 삶을 위해 최신 기기가 진정으로 필요하다고 믿도록 능숙하게 유도된다는 내용으로 문장을 완성하는 것이 적절합니다.

question: 16. 다음 글을 읽고, 한 학생이 내용을 정리한 메모를 작성하였다. 메모의 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 각각 들어갈 말을 올바르게 짝지은 것은?
passage: Theoretically, our brain would have the capacity to store all experiences throughout life, reaching the quality of a DVD. However, this theoretical capacity is offset by the energy demand associated with the process of storing and retrieving information in memory. As a result, the brain develops efficient strategies, becoming dependent on shortcuts. When we observe a face, the visual image captured by the eyes is highly variable, depending on the point of view, lighting conditions and other contextual factors. Nevertheless, we are able to recognize the face as the same, maintaining the underlying identity. The brain, rather than focusing on the details of visualization, creates and stores general patterns that allow for consistent recognition across diverse circumstances. This ability to match what we see with general visual memory patterns serves as an effective mechanism for optimizing brain performance and saving energy. The brain, being naturally against unnecessary effort, constantly seeks to simplify and generalize information to facilitate the cognitive process.• Brain's Limitation: Although the brain has a large theoretical storage capacity, this is limited by its high (A)________ demand.• Brain's Strategy: To solve this, the brain doesn't focus on details. Instead, it creates and stores (B)________ patterns.• Example & Result: This strategy, seen in face recognition, allows the brain to optimize performance and save energy, acting as an effective (C)________
options: ① (A) capacity - (B) detailed - (C) obstacle
② (A) capacity - (B) general - (C) mechanism
③ (A) energy - (B) general - (C) obstacle
④ (A) energy - (B) general - (C) mechanism
⑤ (A) energy - (B) detailed - (C) obstacle
explanation: (A) 본문에서 뇌의 저장 능력은 정보를 저장하고 회수하는 과정과 관련된 '에너지 수요(energy demand)'에 의해 상쇄된다고 했으므로 energy가 적절합니다. (B) 뇌는 세부 사항에 집중하기보다 '일반적인 패턴(general patterns)'을 생성하고 저장한다고 했으므로 general이 적절합니다. (C) 이러한 전략은 뇌의 성능을 최적화하고 에너지를 아끼는 효과적인 '기제(mechanism)' 역할을 한다고 했으므로 mechanism이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 용량 - 세부적인 - 장애물
② 용량 - 일반적인 - 기제
③ 에너지 - 일반적인 - 장애물
④ 에너지 - 일반적인 - 기제
⑤ 에너지 - 세부적인 - 장애물

question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 simple switch의 예시로 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Imagine pausing in the middle of a busy day, taking a moment to refresh your mind and recharge your energy. This power of a midday break is often underestimated. When you break away from routine, especially with activities designed to stimulate your brain, you prevent cognitive tiredness and enhance productivity for the rest of the day. Neurobic exercises ─ simple yet effective ─ are perfect for such breaks. They target different areas of your brain, keeping it agile and alert. These exercises create a mental oasis that refreshes and prepares you for the afternoon's challenges. This strategic pause is not just a break; it boosts your cognitive capabilities, ensuring your mind remains sharp and focused. Even briefly experimenting with neurobic exercises can work wonders for your cognitive state during lunch. Start with using your non-dominant hand for routine tasks like writing or eating. This simple switch challenges your brain, activating pathways that aren't typically engaged and promoting greater flexibility in thinking.
options: ① Trying to write your own name backwards
② Taking a different route than usual to the school cafeteria
③ Learning five new, complex physics formulas during the break
④ Trying to get dressed or button a shirt with your eyes closed
⑤ Eating your lunch by holding a spoon in your non-dominant hand
explanation: 지문에서 언급된 'simple switch' 혹은 'Neurobic exercises'는 일상적인 행동(글쓰기, 식사 등)을 평소와 다른 방식(비주류 손 사용 등)으로 수행하여 뇌의 평소 사용되지 않는 부위를 자극하는 간단한 변화를 의미합니다. ①, ②, ④, ⑤는 모두 일상적인 행위에 사소한 변화를 주어 뇌를 자극하는 적절한 예시인 반면, ③번의 '복잡한 물리 공식 학습'은 단순한 방식의 변화가 아니라 고도의 인지적 에너지를 소모하는 새로운 학습 활동이므로 지문에서 말하는 'simple switch'의 예로 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 자신의 이름을 거꾸로 써보기
② 학교 식당으로 가는 평소와 다른 길 이용하기
③ 쉬는 시간 동안 5개의 새롭고 복잡한 물리 공식 학습하기
④ 눈을 감고 옷을 입거나 셔츠 단추 채우기
⑤ 평소에 사용하지 않는 손으로 숟가락을 잡고 점심 먹기

question: 18. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: To determine the mass of my bowling ball, I might put it onto a balance and compare it with a known mass, such as a number of metal cubes each weighing 1, 10, or 100 grams. Things get much more complicated if I want to know the mass of a distant star. How do I measure it? We can roughly say that measuring the mass of a star involves various theories. If we want to measure the mass of a binary star, we first determine a center of mass between the two stars, then their distance from that center which we can then use, together with a value for the period and a certain instance of Kepler's Third Law, to calculate the mass. In other words, in order to "measure" the star mass, we measure other quantities and use those values, together with certain equations, to calculate the mass. Measurement is not a simple and unmediated estimation of independently existing properties, but a determination of certain magnitudes before the background of a number of accepted theories.
options: ① The crucial role of Kepler's Third Law in calculating the mass of stars
② Various methods to enhance the accuracy of indirect measurement
③ The limitations of relying solely on equations in scientific measurement
④ The nature of scientific measurement as a theory-dependent determination
⑤ The fundamental distinction between 'measuring' properties and 'calculating' values

question: 21. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Consider units of measure, one kind of descriptive device we are familiar with using in physics. Spatial distances can be given in terms of feet or meters or some other unit, and the physics will be the same regardless. We conclude from this that physics does not prefer one unit of length over any other, and we may choose any one we like for reasons of convenience. We further conclude that any feature depending on that choice, such as the particular numerical value assigned to the spatial separation between two locations, is not out there in the world apart from a choice of unit. Temperatures can likewise be given in terms of the Fahrenheit or Celsius or Kelvin scale, and nothing in the physics changes when we switch from one scale to another. We conclude that the choice of scale is an arbitrary choice in description, and that any feature that depends on that choice is scale-dependent.

question: 22. 다음 글에서 설명한 Conditioned Place Preference에 해당하지 않는 것은?
passage: Conditioned Place Preference is a way of finding out what animals want. Researchers train them to associate one place with an experience such as food or a loud noise and another place with something completely different, usually where nothing happens. The two places are made obviously different to make it as easy as possible for the animal to associate each place with what happened to it there. The animal's preference for being in one place or another is measured both before and after its experiences in the two places. If there is a shift in where the animal chooses to spend its time for the reward, this suggests that it liked the experience and is trying to repeat it. Conversely, if it now avoids the place the stimulus appeared and starts to prefer the place it did not experience it, then this suggests that it found the stimulus unpleasant. For example, mice with cancer show a preference for the place where they have been given morphine, a drug used to relieve pain, rather than where they have received saline, whereas healthy mice developed no such preference. This suggests that the mice with cancer wanted the morphine.
options: ① Monkeys that received fruit treats only in a green room later chose to enter the green room more often than the other rooms.
② Rats exposed to a mild electric shock in one cage began avoiding that same cage even when they were allowed to move freely afterward.
③ Fish given additional oxygen in one tank later showed a strong tendency to return to that same tank whenever they have a chance to choose.
④ Mice that had been given sugar water in one section and plain water in another kept returning to the section where they had received the sugar water.
⑤ Pigeons sensed the smell of food coming from one corner and moved toward it, remaining in that corner as the smell continued to spread throughout the area.
explanation: Conditioned Place Preference(조건 장소 선호)는 특정 장소와 특정 자극(보상 또는 혐오 자극)을 결합(연상)하여, 나중에 자극이 없더라도 그 장소에 대한 선호나 회피를 보이는 학습 현상을 말합니다. 5번의 경우, 비둘기가 현재 나고 있는 음식 냄새를 따라가서 머무는 행동은 자극에 대한 직접적인 반응일 뿐, 과거의 연상 학습에 의한 장소 선호 사례로 볼 수 없습니다.
options_translation: 초록색 방에서만 과일 간식을 받은 원숭이들이 나중에 다른 방보다 초록색 방에 더 자주 들어가는 것을 선택했다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 본문에서 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오. (단, 어형 변형 없음)
passage: We encounter contrary claims about the relation of literature to action. But on the other hand, literature has historically been seen as dangerous: it promotes the questioning of authority and social  arrangements. Plato banned poets from his ideal republic because they could only do harm, and novels have long been credited with making people dissatisfied with their lives and eager for something new. By promoting identification across divisions of class, gender, and race, books may promote a fellowship that discourages struggle; but they may also produce a keen sense of injustice that makes progressive struggles possible. question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고, <조건>에 맞게 글의 주제문을 완성하시오.
passage: Waste has historically been seen as a necessary driver of the economy. Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly dependent on the demand for that product. Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be wasted, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be sustained. Many strategies have been incorporated into product design and use to ensure that waste is inevitable, such as planned obsolescence, limited access to tools for repairs, and use of cheap materials. All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a replacement. Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that prioritizing the elimination of waste via repair and remanufacturing creates a different kind of demand: products as a service. Through this setup, companies simply lease out products that were once sold directly to the customer. With this transition of ownership, companies maintain profit by offering maintenance and repair services and are encouraged to develop long-lasting products.

question: 28. 다음 글을 읽고 보인 학생의 반응으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Weber's law concerns the perception of difference between two stimuli. It suggests that we might not be able to detect a 1-mm difference when we are looking at lines 466 mm and 467 mm in length, but we may be able to detect a 1-mm difference when we are comparing a line 2 mm long with one 3 mm long. Another example of this principle is that we can detect one candle when it is lit in an otherwise dark room. But when one candle is lit in a room in which 100 candles are already burning, we may not notice the light from this candle. Therefore, the Just-noticeable difference (JND) varies as a function of the strength of the signals. For example, the JND is greater for very loud noises than it is for much more quiet sounds. When a sound is very weak, we can tell that another sound is louder, even if it is barely louder. When a sound is very loud, to tell that another sound is even louder, it has to be much louder. Thus, Weber's law means that it is harder to distinguish between two samples when those samples are larger or stronger levels of the stimuli.
options: ① If two objects are very small, I can not sense the difference at all.
② When two stimuli are weak, even a tiny difference can be detected well.
③ So, the JND changes depending on how strong the original stimulus is.
④ It is harder to notice a small difference in loud sounds than in soft sounds.
⑤ The larger or stronger the stimuli are, the harder it becomes to distinguish their differences.
explanation: 베버의 법칙에 따르면 자극의 세기가 약할수록 작은 차이도 더 잘 감지할 수 있습니다. 지문에서 2mm와 3mm의 선 차이(매우 작은 자극)는 감지할 수 있다고 언급했으므로, 물체가 매우 작을 때 차이를 전혀 느낄 수 없다는 ①번은 지문의 내용과 정반대되는 설명입니다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Consider units of measure, one kind of descriptive device we are familiar with using in physics. Spatial distances can be given in terms of feet or meters or some other unit, and the physics will be the same regardless. We conclude from this that physics does not prefer one unit of length over any other, and we may choose any one we like for reasons of convenience. We further conclude that any feature depending on that choice, such as the particular numerical value assigned to the spatial separation between two locations, is not out there in the world apart from a choice of unit. Temperatures can likewise be given in terms of the Fahrenheit or Celsius or Kelvin scale, and nothing in the physics changes when we switch from one scale to another. We conclude that the choice of scale is an arbitrary choice in description, and that any feature that depends on that choice is scale-dependent.
options: ① Different units, such as feet and meters, were developed for practical use in various scientific fields.
② Switching between unit systems often makes it possible to compare results from different experiments.
③ Units of measurement are simply tools we choose, and features that depend on them are not inherent in the physical world.
④ Temperature scales like Fahrenheit, Celsius, and Kelvin were created to make scientific communication easier.
⑤ The consistency of physical laws across different measurement systems proves that scientists should adopt a single universal standard of units to avoid confusion.
explanation: 이 글은 물리적 측정 단위(길이, 온도 등)가 물리 법칙의 본질을 바꾸지 않으며, 우리가 편의에 따라 임의로 선택한 도구일 뿐임을 설명합니다. 따라서 특정 단위에 의존하는 수치 등은 물리적 세계에 고유하게 존재하는 속성이 아니라 단위 선택에 따라 달라지는 '단위 의존적' 특성이라는 것이 주제입니다.

question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

question: 16. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Distinguishing moths from butterflies on outward appearance is not always easy, but there are a few rules of thumb that can help. In most butterflies the antennae end with a small club-shaped swelling, whereas in moths they are usually feathery or narrow to a fine tip. Butterflies tend to rest with their wings held shut above their body, whereas moths more usually rest with the upper sides of the wings on full view. Further distinctions can be made by looking for a tiny hook that joins fore- and hindwings, a feature only present in moths. The stereotypical differences, with moths cast as the gloomy, nocturnal cousins of colourful sun-loving butterflies are simply wrong. There are many brightly coloured moths and many which are active throughout the day. Equally, there are a few nocturnal butterflies and plenty that come clothed in shades of brown and grey. It's more sensible to think of them together; both butterflies and moths are beautiful and fascinating insects.

④ Butterflies usually have antennae that end in a small rounded tip.
⑤ Moths typically rest with their wings closed above their bodies.

question: 18. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Information encountered after an event can influence subsequent remembering. External information can easily integrate into a witness's memory, especially if the event was poorly encoded or the memory is from a distant event, in which case time and forgetting have degraded the original memory. With reduced information available in memory with which to confirm the validity of post-event misinformation, it is less likely that this new information will be rejected. Instead, especially when it fits the witness's current thinking and can be used to create a story that makes sense to him or her, it may be integrated as part of the original experience. This process can be explicit (i.e., the witness knows it is happening), but it is often unconscious. That is, the witness might find himself or herself thinking about the event differently without awareness. Over time, the witness may not even know the source of information that led to the (new) memory.
options: ① Distortion of Eyewitness Accounts by Prejudice
② The Process of Explicit and Implicit Memory Formation
③ The Vulnerability of Memory to Post-event information
④ The Rules Governing the Effectiveness of Retrieval Cues
⑤ Constructive Memory Theory: How to Retrieve a Stored Memory Exactly as It Is

question: 20. 다음 글을 읽고 추론한 내용으로 옳지 않은 것은?
passage: The arts and aesthetics offer emotional connection to the full range of human experience. When Lorraine Hansberry wrote her play A Raisin in the Sun, she gave us a powerful story of people struggling with racism, discrimination, and the pursuit of the American dream while also offering a touching portrait of family life.

question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 active management에 해당하지 않는 것은?
passage: There are numerous ways wildlife is managed, but they all imply stewardship and can be classified into two broad categories: <u>active management</u> and inactive management. Active management does something to the population - such as increasing or decreasing its size - in a direct manner through strategies like translocations or hunting, respectively. Populations can also be actively managed by altering the habitat to the benefit or disadvantage of a population. If population numbers are too low for the goal of management agencies, other active management can be incorporated, such as predator control to minimize neonatal deaths or habitat improvement to provide required cover for neonates from predators. These efforts represent active approaches to management. Other populations may not be actively managed, like those in national parks. In such situations, management activities minimize external influences on populations and habitat, which often involves management of humans and not animals.
options: ① Draining or lowering the water level in wetlands or ponds to destroy the sites where mosquitoes lay their eggs.
② Closing certain hiking trails or beaches within a preserve during critical breeding seasons to prevent disturbance to birthing areas.
③ Establishing a hunting season for White-tailed deer in a suburban area where the population has exceeded the land's carrying capacity.
④ Conducting intentional fires in a forest to clear the way for new, diverse plant growth that provides better foraging and nesting cover.
⑤ Moving a group of endangered wolves from a dense population area to a new, suitable region where the population is locally extinct.
explanation: 지문에서 active management(적극적 관리)는 개체군의 크기를 직접 조절하거나 서식지를 변경하는 등 생태계에 직접적인 조치를 취하는 것을 의미합니다. 반면 inactive management(비적극적 관리)는 외부 영향을 최소화하는 것으로, 주로 동물이 아닌 인간을 관리하는 활동을 포함합니다. ②번의 '특정 등산로나 해변을 폐쇄하는 것'은 인간의 활동을 제한하여 야생 동물에 대한 외부 간섭을 줄이는 것이므로 inactive management에 해당합니다.
options_translation: ① 모기가 알을 낳는 장소를 파괴하기 위해 습지나 연못의 수위를 낮추거나 물을 빼는 것
② 출산 지역에 대한 방해를 방지하기 위해 중요한 번식기 동안 보호 구역 내의 특정 하이킹 코스나 해변을 폐쇄하는 것
③ 개체수가 토지의 수용 능력을 초과한 교외 지역에서 흰꼬리사슴의 사냥 시즌을 설정하는 것
④ 더 나은 먹이 찾기와 둥지 덮개를 제공하는 새롭고 다양한 식물 성장을 위해 숲에서 의도적인 화재를 실시하는 것

question: 25. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Within liberal culture, the value of fair equality of opportunity for individuals outweighs the preservation of the family's integrity. question: 26. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: As a political researcher in Germany, Noelle-Neumann observed that during election campaigns, certain views seemed to get more play than others, and sometimes people muted their opinions rather than talking about them, especially if those opinions were perceived to be unpopular. Noelle-Neumann calls this the spiral of silence. The spiral of silence occurs when individuals who perceive that their opinions are popular express them, whereas those who do not think their opinions are popular remain quiet. This process occurs in a spiral, so that one side of an issue ends up with considerable publicity and the other side with very little. In everyday life, people express their opinions in a variety of ways: they talk about them, they wear buttons, they put bumper stickers on their cars, and they post their views on social media. According to this theory, people are more apt to do these kinds of things when they perceive that others share their opinions. The presidential election, in which polls predicted that Candidate A would win but Candidate B ultimately won, provides an example of the spiral of silence; some voters who supported Candidate B were reluctant to voice their support because they perceived their opinion to be unpopular. ② voters changing their preferred candidate
③ political researchers struggling to identify long-term voting trends
④ an increase in the overall number of people who voted in the election
⑤ why voters were more willing to express their opinions publicly than in private

question: 27. 다음 글의 흠름으로 밴아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 28. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Viewing time as a purchasable and consistent product cemented artificial views on time into our psyche, but every now and again reality reminds us that this view is flawed. On twenty-six occasions in the last fifty years, a second has been added to everyone's day. These "leap seconds" are needed because the Earth does not rotate at a perfectly ␐<u>steady</u> rate. Natural phenomena can subtly disrupt the planet's spin. El Nio - a climate pattern in the Pacific - can dramatically alter wind speeds, which in turn slows the Earth's rotation by a tiny amount. On a longer timescale, the Moon's gravity continually pulls on the Earth, acting as a ␑<u>brake</u> and lengthening the day by roughly 1.7 milliseconds every century. Whenever irregularities like this occur, human experts quietly decide to add a small slice of time to everyone's day so that our clocks stay ␒<u>aligned</u> with the planet's changing rhythm. Most people never notice, but the adjustment highlights a deeper truth: the ␓<u>rigid</u>, mechanical system of time we construct cannot fully capture the fluid, unpredictable nature of the Earth's own timing. We kecp trying to impose a fixed human framework onto a world that ␔<u>chooses</u> to stay still-and nature, unsurprisingly, does not bend to our expectations.
explanation: ␔가 포함된 문윑은 인간이 고정된 툐을 세상에 강요하려 하지만 자연은 우리의 기대에 굽히지 않고 계속해섔 변화한다는 내용이어야 합니다. 따라서 'stay still(가변히 읈다)'이 아닌 'refuses' 또는 'fails' 등의 표현이 적절합니다.

question: 2. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Imagine pausing in the middle of a busy day, taking a moment to refresh your mind and recharge your energy. This power of a midday break is often underestimated. question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When a cell divides, the genomes of its two daughters are often not quite identical to each other or to that of the parent cell. On rare occasions, the error may represent a change for the better; more probably, it will cause no significant difference in the cell's prospects. But in some cases, the error will cause serious damage; for example, by disrupting the coding sequence for a key protein. Changes due to mistakes of the first type will tend to be perpetuated, because the altered cell has an increased likelihood of reproducing itself. Changes due to mistakes of the second type - neutral changes - may be perpetuated or not: it is a matter of chance whether the altered cell or its cousins will succeed. But changes that cause serious damage lead nowhere: the cell that suffers them dies, leaving no progeny. Through endless repetition of this cycle of mutation and natural selection organisms evolve: their genetic specifications change, sometimes giving organisms new ways to exploit the environment more effectively, to survive in competition with others, and to reproduce successfully.*perpetuate: 영속시키다 **progeny: 자손
options: ① 진화는 오직 환경 압력이 생물에게 적응을 강요할 때만 일어난다.

③ 대부분의 돌연변이는 심각한 손상을 일으켜 생물이 살아남지 못하게 한다.
④ 해로운 돌연변이를 가진 세포도 종종 생존하지만 번식 능력이 다소 떨어질 뿐이다.
⑤ 유전적 돌연변이는 그 유형에 따라 자연 선택을 통해 보존되거나 제거되며, 이러한 반복된 과정이 진화를 이끈다.
explanation: 글의 마지막 부분인 'Through endless repetition of this cycle of mutation and natural selection organisms evolve'를 통해, 돌연변이와 자연 선택의 반복을 통해 생물이 진화한다는 점을 알 수 있습니다. 또한 본문은 유익한 변화, 중립적 변화, 해로운 변화 등 돌연변이의 유형에 따라 보존되거나 사라지는 과정을 설명하고 있습니다.

question: 6. 다음 광의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Statistics in the twentieth century became the systematic collection of quantitative information needed by the state. question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Consider units of measure, one kind of descriptive device we are familiar with using in physics. Spatial distances can be given in terms of feet or meters or some other unit, and the physics will be the same regardless. We conclude from this that physics does not prefer one unit of length over any other, and we may choose any one we like for reasons of convenience. We further conclude that any feature depending on that choice, such as the particular numerical value assigned to the spatial separation between two locations, is not out there in the world apart from a choice of unit. Temperatures can likewise be given in terms of the Fahrenheit or Celsius or Kelvin scale, and nothing in the physics changes when we switch from one scale to another. We conclude that _____________________________________.*arbitrary: 임의적인
options: ① all quantities are unique to their measurement system, creating a chaos
② the numbers are fixed properties of the world, independent of the units we choose
③ the scale is a choice of representation, and anything based on it is not absolute
④ the scale is only a descriptive convention, and anything that depends on it destroys our arbitrary choice
⑤ the particular numerical value assigned to a quantity is a distinct feature, unrelated to our chosen unit
explanation: 이 글은 물리학에서 사용하는 측정 단위가 단지 묘사를 위한 장치일 뿐이며, 어떤 단위를 선택하느냐에 따라 물리 법칙 자체가 변하지 않는다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 거리나 온도를 측정할 때 어떤 단위를 쓰든 물리적 실체는 같으며, 특정 단위에 따라 달라지는 수치 값은 절대적인 것이 아니라 '표현 방식의 선택'에 의한 것이라는 결론이 적절합니다. 따라서 ③ '척도는 표현의 선택이며, 그것에 기반한 어떤 것도 절대적이지 않다'가 빈칸에 가장 알맞습니다.
options_translation: ① 모든 양은 측정 시스템에 고유하여 혼란을 야기한다
② 숫자는 우리가 선택하는 단위와 무관한 세계의 고정된 속성이다
③ 척도는 표현의 선택이며, 그것에 기반한 어떤 것도 절대적이지 않다
④ 척도는 단지 묘사적인 관습일 뿐이며, 그것에 의존하는 어떤 것도 우리의 임의적인 선택을 파괴한다
⑤ 양에 할당된 특정 수치는 우리가 선택한 단위와 관련 없는 별개의 특징이다

question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Experiments testify to science's embrace of ignorance. Arguably the worst thing a scientist can do is _________________________________________. The rise of the experimental philosophy coincided with the liberation of curiosity as a valuable rather than a questionable attribute. For all that experimental science today is often assumed to be supported by a philosophical framework and an approved methodology ("state your hypothesis and then test it"), the fact is that, as philosopher of science Ian Hacking says, "One can conduct an experiment simply out of curiosity to see what will happen." Indeed, in the view of Charles Darwin's son, the astronomer George Darwin, once in a while one should do a completely crazy experiment, even if it is most likely to prove fruitless. You never know until you try.
options: ① to testify only the hypotheses that are proven to be invalid
② to rely entirely on every evidence before making any prediction
③ to refuse to predict an outcome even after careful verification
④ to assume they can control the situation without listing all principles
⑤ to take for granted that they can predict an outcome without verifying it
explanation: 이 글은 과학이 무지(ignorance)를 수용하고 호기심에 기반한 실험을 중요하게 여긴다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 실험적 과학은 단순히 어떤 일이 일어날지 보기 위해 수행될 수 있으며, 결과가 없을 것 같은 미친 실험조차도 가치가 있다고 말합니다. 따라서 과학자가 할 수 있는 최악의 행동은 검증도 해보지 않고 결과를 예측할 수 있다고 단정 짓는 태도입니다. 정답은 ⑤ '검증하지 않고 결과를 예측할 수 있다고 당연하게 여기는 것'입니다.
options_translation: ① 무효임이 입증된 가설들만 증명하는 것
② 예측을 하기 전에 모든 증거에 전적으로 의존하는 것
③ 세심한 검증 후에도 결과 예측을 거부하는 것
④ 모든 원칙을 나열하지 않고 상황을 통제할 수 있다고 가정하는 것
⑤ 검증 없이 결과를 예측할 수 있다고 당연하게 여기는 것

question: 17. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 (A)this mistake가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Viewing time as a purchasable and consistent product cemented artificial views on time into our psyche, but every now and again we are forced to acknowledge (A)<u>this mistake</u>. On twenty-six occasions in the last fifty years, a second has been added to everyone's day to adjust for the Earth wobbling and the rate of its spin changing. For instance, when El Niño, a climatic system in the Pacific, causes wind speed to change dramatically, it can slow the rotation of the Earth slightly. Indeed, the Earth's spin is generally slowing because the moon's gravity is acting as a drag, so days are getting longer by about 1.7 milliseconds per century. Such events disturb the similarity between man-made time and more flexible time based on the Earth's naturally occurring rotation. When events like this happen, a bunch of humans make the decision to add a small slice of time to your day, without your knowledge. We try to force our fixed, man-made view of time on to nature in the false hope that it will yield. It doesn't.*wobble: 흔들리다
options: ① believing that time moves faster when you are out of time.
② treating Earth's rotation as perfectly fixed and consistent.
③ thinking that only climatic system changes the man-made time.
④ assuming that man-made clocks can perfectly match the Earth' natural rhythms.
⑤ imagining that time is a purchasable commodity that can be manipulated by nature.
explanation: 이 글은 인간이 인위적으로 만든 고정된 시간 관념과 실제 지구의 자전에 기반한 유연한 시간 사이의 괴리를 설명하고 있습니다. (A)this mistake는 앞 문장에서 언급된 '시간을 구매 가능하고 일관된 제품으로 보는 것'과 맥락을 같이 하며, 인간이 만든 시계가 자연의 리듬(지구의 자전 속도 변화 등)과 완벽하게 일치할 수 있다고 믿는 착각을 의미합니다. 따라서 정답은 ④번입니다.
options_translation: ① 시간이 없을 때 시간이 더 빨리 흐른다고 믿는 것.
② 지구의 자전을 완벽하게 고정되고 일관된 것으로 취급하는 것.
③ 오직 기후 시스템만이 인위적인 시간을 바꾼다고 생각하는 것.
④ 인위적인 시계가 지구의 자연적 리듬과 완벽하게 일치할 수 있다고 가정하는 것.
⑤ 시간이 자연에 의해 조작될 수 있는 구매 가능한 상품이라고 상상하는 것.

question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Within liberal culture, the value of fair equality of opportunity for individuals outweighs the preservation of the family's integrity.
ordered_passages: (A) Therefore, for Confucians, the family possesses inherent value that should never be abandoned, even if it results in certain societal inequalities. Some cultures, like the liberal one, may choose to impose increasing restrictions on the role of families and implement more egalitarian government programs for education, healthcare, and other positive rights in society in the pursuit of fair equality of opportunity.

(B) In contrast, for Confucian culture, while seeking fair equality of opportunity for individuals is important, the family assumes a fundamental role in human flourishing, and living within a family institution is considered the essential way of life. Individuals are primarily understood as family members before they are regarded as state citizens.

(C) On the other hand, other cultures, like the Confucian one, may prefer to primarily assign welfare responsibilities to the family, accepting inequalities stemming from the existence of the family as long as everyone's basic freedoms and rights are safeguarded in the state.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 자유주의 문화에서 개인의 기회 균등이 가족의 온전함 유지보다 중요하다는 점을 언급합니다. (B)에서 'In contrast'를 통해 유교 문화에서는 가족이 인간 번영의 근본적인 역할을 하며 개인보다 가족 구성원으로서의 정체성이 우선임을 대조적으로 보여줍니다. (A)의 'Therefore'는 (B)의 내용을 결론지으며 유교 문화에서 가족의 내재적 가치를 강조하고, 다시 자유주의 문화의 특징(평등주의적 정부 프로그램)으로 화제를 전환합니다. (C)는 'On the other hand'를 통해 다시 유교 문화의 관점(복지 책임을 가족에게 부여하고 그로 인한 불평등 수용)을 설명하며 내용을 마무리합니다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
passage: Historically, palaces weren't just homes; they were carefully constructed stages designed to impress and intimidate. While stone symbolized permanence and strength, glass offered something equally powerful: visibility. The introduction of large windows in palaces allowed rulers to literally look down upon their subjects, emphasizing their elevated position. (A) Consider the Palace of Versailles: its Hall of Mirrors, lined with reflective surfaces, not only magnified the grandeur of the space but also placed the king at the center of a dazzling display, reinforcing his absolute authority. (B) The use of glass in palaces wasn't merely aesthetic; it was strategic. (C) Open sightlines allowed for better surveillance and control, ensuring the safety and security of the ruling family. (D) Courtiers and visitors were constantly aware of being observed, contributing to an atmosphere of careful obedience and respect. (E) The very architecture dictated social behavior, with glass acting as a silent enforcer of the power dynamic.
insertion_sentence: Conversely, it also allowed subjects to gaze up at their leaders, creating a sense of awe and distance.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장은 '반대로(Conversely), 그것(유리/창문)은 또한 신하들이 지도자를 우러러보게 하여 경외감과 거리감을 조성했다'는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 주어진 문장 앞의 내용은 통치자가 위에서 아래로 신하들을 내려다보는(look down upon) 시각적 우위를 설명하고 있습니다. 'Conversely'를 통해 시선의 방향이 반대인 경우(신하가 지도자를 바라봄)를 도입해야 하므로, (A) 위치가 가장 적절합니다. (A) 뒤에 이어지는 베르사유 궁전의 거울의 방 사례는 이러한 시각적 장치들이 어떻게 왕의 권위를 강화했는지에 대한 구체적인 예시입니다.

question: 24. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
passage: There are numerous ways wildlife is managed, but they all imply stewardship and can be classified into two broad categories: active management and inactive management. Active management affects the population by increasing or decreasing its size. ⓐIt involves direct manner through strategies like translocations or hunting, respectively. ⓑPopulations can also be actively managed by altering the habitat to the benefit or disadvantage of a population. ⓒIf population numbers are too low to meet the goal of management agencies, other active management can be incorporated. It includes predator control to minimize neonatal deaths or habitat improvement to provide required cover for neonates from predators. ⓓUnderestimating unborn population might even display hypothetical preferences. These efforts represent active approaches to management. ⓔHowever, in places like national parks, other populations may not be actively managed. In such situations, management activities minimize external influences on populations and habitat, which often involves management of humans and not animals.*stewardship: (재산, 조직체 등의) 관리 책임**neonatal: 갓 태어난
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 야생 동물 관리의 두 가지 범주인 적극적 관리(active management)와 비적극적 관리(inactive management)를 설명하고 있습니다. 적극적 관리는 개체 수의 크기에 직접 영향을 주거나 서식지를 변경하고, 포식자 조절이나 서식지 개선을 포함한다는 내용이 이어집니다. 하지만 ⓓ의 '태어나지 않은 개체수를 과소평가하는 것이 가설적인 선호도를 보여줄 수 있다'는 내용은 야생 동물 관리 방식의 분류 및 구체적 방법이라는 전체 흐름과 무관합니다.

question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: Even though sea creatures live in it, they still need to take in water for their bodies to function properly. They just need to get rid of any extra salt it might bring with it. Salt absorbs water like a sponge. If you put a tiny mountain of salt on a small plate, then add enough water to the side, making sure an edge touches the salt, the salt will absorb the water. Now you have a pile of wet salt. Notice that it has increased in size. The same principle applies to sea creatures. If the body fluids in a sea animal are saltier than the seawater it lives in, then the extra salt in the creature's body will absorb seawater. This can cause them to swell up. On the other hand, if the amount of salt in the seawater is higher than the amount of salt in the body fluids of a sea animal, the extra salt in the water will draw fluids out of the creature's body, causing it to dehydrate and shrink.*swell: 부풀다 **dehydrate: 수분이 빠지다
summary_sentence: Osmosis helps marine animals survive by regulating the movement of water in their bodies. When the salt (A)___________ inside their bodies is higher than in the seawater, this (B)___________ causes water to be drawn inward, making them swell. When the seawater contains more salt, the disparity pulls the fluids outward, leading to dehydration and shrinkage.*osmosis: 삼투(현상)
options: ① temperature / inequality
② density / inaccuracy
③ concentration / imbalance
④ weight / inefficiency
⑤ proportion / unpredictability
explanation: 지문은 해양 생물의 체액과 주변 바닷물의 염분 농도 차이에 따른 삼투 현상을 설명하고 있습니다. 체내의 염분 (A)농도(concentration)가 바닷물보다 높으면, 이러한 농도의 (B)불균형(imbalance)으로 인해 물이 안으로 흡수되어 몸이 부풀어 오르게 됩니다. 따라서 정답은 ③번입니다.
options_translation: ① 온도 / 불평등
② 밀도 / 부정확
③ 농도 / 불균형
④ 무게 / 비효율
⑤ 비율 / 예측 불가능

question: 29. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞추어 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: [25년 10월 23번] We can discard or replace a scientific theory only if we have a better way of explaining the evidence that supports it. The theories of Newton and Einstein offer great examples. A vast body of evidence supports Newton's theory of gravity, but by the late nineteenth century scientists had begun to discover cases where its predictions did not perfectly match observations. These discrepancies were explained only when Einstein developed his general theory of relativity, which was able to match the observations. Still, the many successes of Newton's theory could not be ignored, and (A)__________________________ if it had not been able to explain these successes equally well. It did, and that is why we now view Einstein's theory as a broader theory of gravity than Newton's theory. Some scientists today are seeking a theory of gravity that will go beyond Einstein's. If any new theory ever gains acceptance, it will have to match all the successes of Einstein's theory as well as work in new realms where Einstein's theory does not.*discrepancy: 불일치 **realm: 영역
subjective_conditions: 1. 가정법 과거완료 구문을 사용할 것
2. <보기>의 단어를 모두 사용하고 필요한 경우 단어를 추가하거나 변형할 것
vocabulary_box: have / acceptance / Einstein's theory / would / gain
answer: Einstein's theory would not have gained acceptance.
explanation: 문맥상 아인슈타인의 이론이 뉴턴 이론의 성공 사례들을 똑같이 잘 설명하지 못했더라면 수용되지 않았을 것이라는 과거 사실에 반대되는 가정을 해야 합니다. 따라서 가정법 과거완료(If + 주어 + had p.p., 주어 + 조동사과거 + have p.p.) 형식을 사용해야 합니다. 조건에 따라 'Einstein's theory would not have gained acceptance'로 작성하는 것이 올바릅니다.

question: 30. 다음 글을 읽고, (A)~(E) 중 어법상 어색한 것 2개를 골라, 밑줄 친 부분을 올바르게 다시 쓰시오.

question: 31. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: As a political researcher in Germany, Noelle-Neumann observed that during election campaigns, certain views seemed to get more play than others, and sometimes people muted their opinions rather than talking about them, especially if those opinions were perceived to be unpopular. Noelle-Neumann calls this the spiral of silence. The spiral of silence occurs when individuals who perceive that their opinions are popular express them, whereas those who do not think their opinions are popular remain quiet. This process occurs in a spiral, so that one side of an issue ends up with considerable publicity and the other side with very little. In everyday life, people express their opinions in a variety of ways: they talk about them, they wear buttons, they put bumper stickers on their cars, and they post their views on social media. According to this theory, people are more apt to do these kinds of things when they ______________________.*apt: ~하는 경향이 있는
subjective_conditions: 1. 본문에서 찾아 변형 없이 쓸 것.
2. 빈칸을 6개의 단어로 작성할 것.
answer: perceive that their opinions are popular
explanation: 글의 중반부 'The spiral of silence occurs when individuals who perceive that their opinions are popular express them' 부분에서 자신의 의견이 인기가 있다고 생각할 때 의견을 표현한다는 내용을 찾을 수 있습니다.

question: 32. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞추어 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: When you are working in healthcare, it is important to develop a solid professional relationship with your patients. By establishing realistic self-boundaries, you can protect that relationship. It is important to keep the focus on the patient. When working with patients who are seen frequently, it is easy to start to think of them as friends. With a friend, you are likely to share personal information that is not appropriate with a patient. Patients may feel that they cannot share important health-related information because you are their friend, and it would be embarrassing to share that information. Self-boundaries can also be thought of as professional boundaries. You need to treat patients with respect and keep the relationship professional. Be friendly to patients and always keep the focus on the patient.Case ADr. Smith has been seeing Mr. Johnson, a patient with chronic diabetes, for several years. Over time, they have developed a friendly rapport, often chatting about personal hobbies during appointments. One day, Mr. Johnson asks Dr. Smith for advice about a personal family matter. Dr. Smith realizes that discussing personal issues could blur professional boundaries. Instead, Dr. Smith politely redirects the conversation to Mr. Johnson's health and offers resources for professional support for his personal concerns. By maintaining professional boundaries, Dr. Smith ensures that Mr. Johnson feels safe sharing important health information without embarrassment or hesitation.

question: 16. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Near the equator, many species of bird breed all year round. But in temperate and polar regions, the breeding seasons of birds are often sharply defined. They are triggered mainly by changes in day length. If all goes well, the outcome is that birds raise their young when the food supply is at its peak. Most birds are not simply reluctant to breed at other times but they are also physically incapable of doing so. This is because their reproductive system shrinks, which helps flying birds save weight. The main exception to this rule are nomadic desert species. These can initiate their breeding cycle within days of rain. It's for making the most of the sudden breeding opportunity. Also, different species divide the breeding season up in different ways. Most seabirds raise a single brood. In warm regions, however, songbirds may raise several families in a few months. In an exceptionally good year, a pair of House Sparrows, a kind of songbird, can raise successive broods through a marathon reproductive effort.

He consulted Greek commentaries, previous translations in English, Latin, and French, and naturally, dictionaries. Translators typically rely on ⓒ<u>multiple</u> source materials. question: 22. According to the passage, which of the following best captures the concept of the -tragedy of the commons-?
passage: Any new resource (e.g., a new airport, a new shopping center) initially provides individual advantages by sharing a common resource (e.g., the city or state budget). However, after some time, the amount of traffic grows too large for the "commons" to support. Traffic jams, overcrowding, and overuse reduce the advantages that the shared resource offers to everyone - the tragedy of the commons! If the new resource cannot be expanded or provided with additional space, it becomes a problem, and you cannot solve the problem on your own, in isolation from your fellow drivers or walkers or competing users. The total activity on this new resource keeps increasing, and so does individual activity; but if the dynamic of common use and overuse continues too long, both begin to fall after a peak, leading to a crash. What makes the "tragedy of commons" tragic is the crash dynamic - the destruction or degeneration of the common resource's ability to regenerate itself.
options: ① Shared resources inevitably degrade only when external regulations are absent, not due to individual overuse.
② The collapse of a shared resource occurs immediately after it is introduced, regardless of how individuals use it.
③ The tragedy of the commons occurs because individuals deliberately avoid using shared resources to preserve them for the future.
④ The benefits of a common resource always increase as more people use it, because individual actions are independent of each other.
⑤ Individuals may initially gain from a common resource, but excessive collective use eventually diminishes both personal and societal benefits.

question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 9월 40번]
passage: The concern about how we appear to others can be seen in children, though work by the psychologist Ervin Staub suggests that the effect may ⓐ<u>vary</u> with age. In a study where children heard another child in distress, young children (kindergarten through second grade) were more likely to help the child in distress when with another child than when alone. But for older children - in fourth and sixth grade - the effect ⓑ<u>reversed</u>: they were less likely to help a child in distress when they were with a peer than when they were alone. Staub suggested that younger children might feel more comfortable acting when they have the company of a peer, whereas older children might feel more concern about being judged by their peers and fear feeling ⓒ<u>embarrassed</u> by overreacting. Older children tended to keep their feelings ⓓ<u>private</u> and did not show their distress as readily as younger children did. In other words, the older children were ⓔ<u>unintentionally</u> putting on a poker face in front of their peers.

question: 25. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [24년 10월 29번]
passage: Conditioned Place Preference is a way of finding out what animals want. Researchers train them to associate one place with an experience such as food or a loud noise and another place with something completely different, usually where nothing happens. The two places are made obviously different to make it as easy as possible for the animal to associate each place with what happened to it there. ⓐThe animal's preference for being in one place or another is measured both before and after its experiences in the two places. ⓑIf the animal fails to recognize human faces, researchers usually exclude it from further testing. ⓒIf the animal changes the place where it prefers to stay to obtain the reward, this indicates that it enjoyed the experience and wants to experience it again. ⓓConversely, if it now avoids the place the stimulus appeared and starts to prefer the place it did not experience it, then this suggests that it found the stimulus unpleasant. ⓔFor example, mice with cancer display a preference for the place where they were given morphine, a medication used to ease pain, rather than the spot where they received saline, while healthy mice showed no such preference. This suggests that the mice with cancer wanted the morphine.

passage: There are deep similarities between viral contagion and behavioral contagion. Solar panels that are visible from the street, for instance, are more likely to stimulate neighboring installations. In contrast, we try to avoid others who are visibly ill. Another important difference is that whereas viral contagion is almost always a bad thing, behavioral contagion is sometimes negative - as in the case of smoking - but sometimes positive, as in the case of solar installations.

question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Just as an expert in the taste and colour of wine will gain much by being aware of the chemistry that underlies those qualities, so each perspective on the body can potentially enhance the others. And yet every scientific tool, from microscopes to mathematics, and every aspect of the body, from the brain to the microorganism, requires such depth of expertise that this tends not to happen: we tend to study the human body in silos, each community sectioned from the others by its own specialised vocabulary. Research communities may be dedicated to one type of scientific tool or a specific component of the body, such as one type of cell. How different types of cell communicate with one another becomes its own specialist topic. question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Waste has historically been seen as a necessary driver of the economy. Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly dependent on the demand for that product. question: 25. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Conditioned Place Preference is a way of finding out what animals want. Researchers train them to associate one place with an experience such as food or a loud noise and another place with something completely different, usually where nothing happens.
ordered_passages: (A) If there is a shift in where the animal chooses to spend its time for the reward, this suggests that it liked the experience and is trying to repeat it. Conversely, if it now avoids the place the stimulus appeared and starts to prefer the place it did not experience it, then this suggests that it found the stimulus unpleasant.

(B) For example, mice with cancer show a preference for the place where they have been given morphine, a drug used to relieve pain, rather than where they have received saline whereas healthy mice developed no such preference. This suggests that the mice with cancer wanted the morphine.

(C) The two places are made obviously different to make it as easy as possible for the animal to associate each place with what happened to it there. The animal's preference for being in one place or another is measured both before and after its experiences in the two places.

question: 18. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 'The very architecture dictated social behavior'가 의미하는 바를 다음 두 가지 측면에서 구체적으로 기술하시오.
passage: Historically, palaces weren't just homes; they were carefully constructed stages designed to impress and intimidate. While stone symbolized permanence and strength, glass offered something equally powerful: visibility. The introduction of large windows in palaces allowed rulers to literally look down upon their subjects, emphasizing their elevated position. Conversely, it also allowed subjects to gaze up at their leaders, creating a sense of awe and distance. Consider the Palace of Versailles: its Hall of Mirrors, lined with reflective surfaces, not only magnified the grandeur of the space but also placed the king at the center of a dazzling display, reinforcing his absolute authority. The use of glass in palaces wasn't merely aesthetic; it was strategic. Open sightlines allowed for better surveillance and control, ensuring the safety and security of the ruling family. question: 19. 다음 글의 중심 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Consider units of measure, one kind of descriptive device we are familiar with using in physics. Spatial distances can be given in terms of feet or meters or some other unit, and the physics will be the same regardless. We conclude from this that physics does not prefer one unit of length over any other, and we may choose any one we like for reasons of convenience. We further conclude that any feature depending on that choice, such as the particular numerical value assigned to the spatial separation between two locations, is not out there in the world apart from a choice of unit. Temperatures can likewise be given in terms of the Fahrenheit or Celsius or Kelvin scale, and nothing in the physics changes when we switch from one scale to another. We conclude that the choice of scale is an arbitrary choice in description, and that any feature that depends on that choice is scale-dependent.*arbitrary: 임의적인
options: ① 특정 물리량에 대한 단위의 선택이 복잡할수록 물리학의 본질이 더욱 명확해진다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Viewing time as a purchasable and ⓐ<u>consistent</u> product cemented artificial views on time into our psyche, but every now and again we are forced to acknowledge this ⓑ<u>mistake</u>. On twenty-six occasions in the last fifty years, a second has been added to everyone's day ⓒ<u>to adjust</u> for the Earth wobbling and the rate of its spin changing. For instance, when El Nino, a climatic system in the Pacific, causes wind speed to change dramatically, it can slow the rotation of the Earth slightly. Indeed, the Earth's spin is generally slowing because the moon's gravity is acting as a drag, so days are getting longer by about 1.7 milliseconds per century. Such events ⓓ<u>consolidate</u> the similarity between man-made time and more flexible time based on the Earth's naturally occurring rotation. When events like this happen, a bunch of humans make the decision to add a small slice of time to your day, without your knowledge. We try to force our fixed, man-made view of time on to nature in the ⓔ<u>false</u> hope that it will yield. It doesn't.*wobble: 흔들리다
explanation: 지문은 인위적인 고정된 시간과 지구 자전에 기초한 유연한 시간 사이의 차이를 설명하고 있습니다. 윤초를 추가하는 등의 사건은 인위적 시간과 자연적 시간 사이의 '유사성'을 '강화(consolidate)'하는 것이 아니라, 오히려 그 둘 사이의 '차이'나 '모순'을 드러내는 것입니다. 따라서 consolidate는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 22. 다음 글에 드러난 필자('I')의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: My two girls grew up without challenges with respect to development and social interaction. My son Benjamin, however, was quite delayed. He struggled through his childhood, not fitting in with the other children and wondering what he was doing wrong at every turn. He was teased by the other children and frowned upon by a number of unsympathetic adults. But his Grade 1 teacher was a wonderful, caring person who took the time to ask why Benjamin behaved the way he did. The teacher was determined to understand Benjamin and to accept him as he was. One day he came home with a note from his teacher. He suggested I go to the school library. They were having a sale, and he thought my son would like one of the books. I couldn't go for a couple of days and was concerned I'd missed the opportunity. When I finally went to the school, his teacher told me that the sale had ended but that the library had saved the book for my little boy. I suspected the teacher had paid for it out of his own pocket. It was a story-board book with a place for a photo. On each page there was an outline of an animal and a hole so that the face in the photo appeared to be the face of the animal. Wondering if Benjamin would really be interested in the book, I brought it home. He loved it! Through that book, he saw that he could be anything he wanted to be: a cat, an octopus, a dinosaur - even a frog! Benjamin joyfully embarked on an imaginative journey through the book, and little did we know, it laid the groundwork for his future successes. And thankfully, his teacher had taken the time to observe and understand him and had discovered a way to help him reach out of his own world and join ours through a story-board book. question: 23. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Manufacturers masterfully sow seeds of doubt about the adequacy of our current devices. Suddenly, the phone that was your lifeline a year ago is now a museum piece, unable to keep pace with your digital demands. And thus, the itch to upgrade begins, often before there's a genuine need. This cycle isn't just confined to our digital companions. It spills over into almost every aspect of consumer electronics, from the self-driving car to the smart fridge. Every product seems to be on an unstoppable march towards the next version, the next generation that promises to revolutionize your life. What's fascinating, or perhaps disturbing, is the utter efficacy of this cycle in shaping our desires. It's not so much that we want the newest device; we're led to believe we need it. The distinction between want and need blurs, shifting our financial priorities in favor of staying current with trends. For all the logical arguments against this ceaseless upgrading, the temptation remains compelling.
options: ① 기업은 소비자의 필요를 충족하기 위해 꾸준히 신제품을 개발해야 한다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Imagine that your usually stingy friend delights in buying you a Christmas present after taking a generosity booster. How would you feel? Instead, generosity is a stable part of a person's 'moral identity', an emotional habit that is part of who you are. Thus virtues, as opposed to nontypical impulse, are the result of your personal history. They are part of who you are, as they are part of how your character was formed. Instant virtue is therefore impossible. Popping a pill cannot make you a better person.

question: 25. 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: What makes questioning authority so hard? The difficulties start in childhood, when parents - the first and most powerful authority figures - show children "the way things are." This is a necessary element of learning language and socialization, and certainly most things learned in early childhood are noncontroversial: the English alphabet starts with A and ends with Z, the numbers 1 through 10 come before the numbers 11 through 20, and so on. Children, however, will spontaneously question things that are quite obvious to adults and even to older kids. The word "why?" becomes a challenge, as in, "Why is the sky blue?" Answers such as "because it just is" or "because I say so" tell children that they must unquestioningly accept what authorities say "just because," and children who persist in their questioning are likely to find themselves dismissed or yelled at for "bothering" adults with "meaningless" or "unimportant" questions. But these questions are in fact perfectly reasonable. Why is the sky blue? Many adults do not themselves know the answer. And who says the sky's color needs to be called "blue," anyway? How do we know that what one person calls "blue" is the same color that another calls "blue"? The scientific answers come from physics, but those are not the answers that children are seeking. They are trying to understand the world, and ('반복되는 질문들이 스트레스가 쌓이고 시간에 쫓기는 부모들에게 아무리 짜증스러울지라도'), it is important to take them seriously to encourage kids to question authority to think for themselves.

passage: Minimal processing can be one of the best ways to keep original flavors and taste, without any need to add artificial flavoring or additives, or too much salt. passage: Sleep is clearly about more than just resting. One curious fact is that animals that are hibernating also have periods of sleep. It comes as a surprise to most of us, but hibernation and sleep are not the same thing at all, at least not from a neurological and metabolic perspective. Hibernating is more like being anesthetized: the subject is unconscious but not actually asleep. So a hibernating animal needs to get a few hours of conventional sleep each day within the larger unconsciousness. A further surprise to most of us is that bears, the most famous of wintry sleepers, don't actually hibernate. explanation: 주어진 문장은 궁전의 큰 창문이 통치자들이 백성들을 내려다볼 수 있게 하여 그들의 높은 지위를 강조했다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A) 뒤의 문장이 'Conversely(역으로/반대로)'로 시작하며 백성들이 지도자를 올려다보게 하여 경외감과 거리감을 조성했다는 내용을 서술하므로, '내려다보는 시선'과 '올려다보는 시선'의 대조를 완성하기 위해 주어진 문장은 (A) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 5. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: We can discard or replace a scientific theory only if we have a better way of explaining the evidence that supports it. (A) The theories of Newton and Einstein offer great examples. A vast body of evidence supports Newton's theory of gravity, but by the late nineteenth century scientists had begun to discover cases where its predictions did not perfectly match observations. (B) Still, the many successes of Newton's theory could not be ignored, and Einstein's theory would not have gained acceptance if it had not been able to explain these successes equally well. (C) It did, and that is why we now view Einstein's theory as a broader theory of gravity than Newton's theory. (D) Some scientists today are seeking a theory of gravity that will go beyond Einstein's. (E) If any new theory ever gains acceptance, it will have to match all the successes of Einstein's theory as well as work in new realms where Einstein's theory does not.
insertion_sentence: These discrepancies were explained only when Einstein developed his general theory of relativity, which was able to match the observations.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장은 아인슈타인의 일반 상대성 이론이 관측 결과와 일치함으로써 불일치(discrepancies)를 설명했다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 본문에서 (B) 앞 부분은 뉴턴 역학의 예측이 관측치와 완벽하게 일치하지 않는 사례들이 발견되기 시작했다는 '불일치' 상황을 제시하고 있습니다. 따라서 이 불일치가 아인슈타인에 의해 해결되었음을 알리는 주어진 문장은 (B) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When a cell divides, the genomes of its two daughters are often not quite identical to each other or to that of the parent cell. On rare occasions, the error may represent a change for the better; more probably, it will cause no significant difference in the cell's prospects. But in some cases, the error will cause serious damage; for example, by disrupting the coding sequence for a key protein. Changes due to mistakes of the first type will tend to be perpetuated, because the altered cell has an increased likelihood of reproducing itself. Changes due to mistakes of the second type - neutral changes - may be perpetuated or not: it is a matter of chance whether the altered cell or its cousins will succeed. But changes that cause serious damage lead nowhere: the cell that suffers them dies, leaving no progeny. Through endless repetition of this cycle of mutation and natural selection organisms evolve: their genetic specifications change, sometimes giving organisms new ways to exploit the environment more effectively, to survive in competition with others, and to reproduce successfully.
options: ① difficulty of changing genetic information
② necessity of damaging mutations in evolution
③ the rate of mutations that result in neutral changes
④ importance of using the environment for organisms
⑤ evolution of organisms through mutation and natural selection
explanation: 이 글은 세포 분열 과정에서 발생하는 유전적 돌연변이가 생존에 유리한 변화, 무해한 변화, 혹은 해로운 변화를 가져올 수 있으며, 이러한 돌연변이의 발생과 자연 선택의 반복적인 과정을 통해 생명체가 진화한다는 원리를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 ⑤ '돌연변이와 자연 선택을 통한 생물체의 진화'입니다.

question: 11. 다음 삼투압에 관한 글의 설명으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Because of osmotic pressure, water moves from areas of lower salt concentration to those of higher salt concentration. Here goes the process. Even though sea creatures live in it, they still need to take in water for their bodies to function properly. They just need to get rid of any extra salt it might bring with it. Salt absorbs water like a sponge. If you put a tiny mountain of salt on a small plate, then add enough water to the side, making sure an edge touches the salt, the salt will absorb the water. Now you have a pile of wet salt. Notice that it has increased in size. The same principle applies to sea creatures. If the body fluids in a sea animal are saltier than the seawater it lives in, then the extra salt in the creature's body will absorb seawater. This can cause them to swell up. On the other hand, if the amount of salt in the seawater is higher than the amount of salt in the body fluids of a marine animal, the extra salt in the water will draw fluids out of the creature's body, causing it to dehydrate and shrink.*osmotic pressure: 삼투압 **concentration: 농도
options: ① If a marine animal's body fluids are saltier than seawater, seawater will enter its body and cause swelling.
② The water on the plate will move toward the pile of salt when the water comes into contact with the salt.
③ If a sea creature's body fluids are less salty than seawater, the fluids will go out to seawater, causing the body to shrink.
④ A sea animal's body will shrink due to the loss of its fluids if its internal salt concentration is lower than that of seawater.
⑤ A marine animal's body will become dehydrated if its internal salt concentration is higher than that of seawater.
explanation: 지문에 따르면, 해양 생물의 체액 염분 농도가 바닷물보다 '낮을' 때 바닷물의 염분이 생물의 체내에서 수분을 끌어내어 탈수와 수축을 일으킵니다. ⑤번은 체내 농도가 '높을' 때 탈수가 일어난다고 설명하고 있으므로 지문의 내용과 정반대입니다.
options_translation: ① 만약 해양 동물의 체액이 바닷물보다 더 짜다면, 바닷물이 몸 안으로 들어와 부풀어 오르게 할 것이다.
② 물이 소금에 닿으면 접시 위의 물은 소금 더미 쪽으로 이동할 것이다.
