Its effects are not limited to a nation's domestic economy but also appear in international trade. For this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that is inherently limited in supply as money. Because these materials cannot be made easily, they naturally stop governments from increasing the money supply too much. ⓑ<u>It is a way of depriving governments of the power to expand the money supply to inflationary levels</u>. Gold has long been considered ideal for this purpose, since (B)<u>the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased rapidly</u>. ⓒ<u>Governments also sometimes consider lowering interest rates to stimulate consumer spending during economic downturns as the most effective response</u>. This slow rate of increase helps keep the value of money more stable over time. ⓓ<u>When paper money is convertible into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money is said to be "backed" by gold</u>. This expression is misleading only if we imagine that the value of the gold is somehow transferred to the paper money, when in fact the real point is that the gold simply limits the amount of paper money that can be issued. In other words, the gold acts as a rule or a control system that works to ㉠______________________________. ⓔ<u>Today, most countries no longer use the gold standard, but the idea remains important for understanding why controlling the money supply is essential in modern economies</u>.
options: ① the same amount of money buys fewer goods than before.
② the value of goods increases because production costs continue to rise.
③ people expect prices to fall again when the value of money becomes unstable.
④ governments try to increase the money supply to prevent a further rise in prices.
⑤ consumers begin to purchase goods in larger quantities to avoid future price increases.
explanation: 빈칸 (A)의 바로 앞 문장에서 인플레이션을 '물가의 일반적인 상승과 돈의 가치 하락'으로 정의하고 있습니다. 따라서 돈의 가치가 떨어졌다는 것은 같은 액수의 돈으로 살 수 있는 물건의 양이 줄어들었다는 의미이므로 ①이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 같은 양의 돈으로 이전보다 더 적은 상품을 산다.
② 생산 비용이 계속 상승하기 때문에 상품의 가치가 증가한다.
③ 사람들은 돈의 가치가 불안정해지면 가격이 다시 하락할 것이라고 예상한다.
④ 정부는 가격의 추가 상승을 막기 위해 통화 공급을 늘리려고 노력한다.
⑤ 소비자들은 미래의 가격 상승을 피하기 위해 더 많은 양의 상품을 구매하기 시작한다.

question: 7. 윗글에서 밑줄 친 (B)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Every government requires revenue to provide public services, and most of this revenue comes from taxation. ⓐ<u>Still, increasing the money supply can appear to be a simple alternative when additional funds are needed</u>. The big problem with money created by the government is that those who run the government always face the temptation to create more money and spend it. Whether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, leading to inflation and the many economic and social problems that follow from it. Inflation refers to a general rise in prices and a reduction in the value of money, meaning that (A)____________________________. Its effects are not limited to a nation's domestic economy but also appear in international trade. For this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that is inherently limited in supply as money. Because these materials cannot be made easily, they naturally stop governments from increasing the money supply too much. ⓑ<u>It is a way of depriving governments of the power to expand the money supply to inflationary levels</u>. Gold has long been considered ideal for this purpose, since (B)<u>the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased rapidly</u>. ⓒ<u>Governments also sometimes consider lowering interest rates to stimulate consumer spending during economic downturns as the most effective response</u>. This slow rate of increase helps keep the value of money more stable over time. ⓓ<u>When paper money is convertible into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money is said to be "backed" by gold</u>. This expression is misleading only if we imagine that the value of the gold is somehow transferred to the paper money, when in fact the real point is that the gold simply limits the amount of paper money that can be issued. In other words, the gold acts as a rule or a control system that works to ㉠______________________________. ⓔ<u>Today, most countries no longer use the gold standard, but the idea remains important for understanding why controlling the money supply is essential in modern economies</u>.
options: ① Gold's value changes depending on government policy decisions, so its supply can fluctuate quickly when needed.
② Because governments strictly control the distribution of gold, its supply can be easily increased by changing official rules.
③ As gold production rises, its value is automatically transferred to paper money, allowing the currency to raise in value rapidly.
④ Even if governments or miners try to extract more gold, the total supply cannot be expanded rapidly due to physical and geological limits.
⑤ Gold-backed currency requires immediate and unlimited exchange of all paper money for gold, so governments can quickly increase the money supply.
explanation: 밑줄 친 (B)는 세상에 존재하는 금의 양이 물리적으로 한정되어 있어 급격하게 늘릴 수 없음을 말합니다. 이는 정부가 정치적 목적으로 화폐를 마구 발행하는 것을 막는 자연적인 제동 장치 역할을 합니다. 따라서 물리적, 지질학적 한계로 인해 공급을 빠르게 늘릴 수 없다는 ④가 가장 적절한 해석입니다.
options_translation: ① 금의 가치는 정부의 정책 결정에 따라 변하므로 필요할 때 공급이 빠르게 요동칠 수 있다.
② 정부가 금의 유통을 엄격하게 통제하기 때문에 공식적인 규칙을 바꿈으로써 공급을 쉽게 늘릴 수 있다.
③ 금 생산이 늘어남에 따라 그 가치가 자동으로 지폐로 전이되어 화폐 가치가 급격히 상승하게 한다.
④ 정부나 광부들이 더 많은 금을 추출하려고 노력하더라도 물리적, 지질학적 한계 때문에 전체 공급량이 빠르게 확장될 수 없다.
⑤ 금태환 화폐는 모든 지폐를 금으로 즉각적이고 무제한으로 교환하는 것을 요구하므로 정부는 통화 공급을 빠르게 늘릴 수 있다.

question: 8. 윗글의 문맥상 빈칸 ㉠에 들어갈 연속된 9개의 단어로 이루어진 동사구를 변형 없이 본문에서 그대로 찾아 쓰시오.

explanation: 글의 중반부에 'Because these materials cannot be made easily, they naturally stop governments from increasing the money supply too much.'라는 문장이 등장합니다. 빈칸 ㉠은 금이 화폐 시스템에서 수행하는 역할(정부의 무분별한 통화 발행 억제)을 설명하는 자리이므로, 해당 부분의 동사구 9단어를 그대로 가져오면 조건에 부합합니다.

question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Waste has historically been seen as a necessary driver of the economy. Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly dependent on the demand for that product. Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be wasted, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be sustained. Many strategies have been incorporated into product design and use to ensure that waste is inevitable, such as planned obsolescence, limited access to tools for repairs, and use of cheap materials. All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a replacement. Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that prioritizing the elimination of waste via repair and remanufacturing creates a different kind of demand: products as a service. Through this setup, companies simply lease out products that were once sold directly to the customer. With this transition of ownership, companies maintain profit by offering maintenance and repair services and are encouraged to develop long-lasting products.
options: ① The importance of recycling policies
② The best strategy for reducing the amount of waste
③ The influence of planned obsolescence on the environment
④ The benefits of a circular economy based on waste recycling
⑤ The transition from waste-based production to sustainable services
explanation: 과거에는 경제 활성화를 위해 계획적 구식화 등을 통해 쓰레기 발생을 의도했으나, 이제는 수리와 재제조를 우선시하는 '서비스로서의 제품' 개념으로 전환되고 있다는 내용입니다. 소유권 이전을 통해 기업이 유지 보수 서비스를 제공하며 지속 가능한 모델로 나아가고 있다는 내용이므로 주제로 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 재활용 정책의 중요성
② 쓰레기 양을 줄이기 위한 최선의 전략
③ 계획적 구식화가 환경에 미치는 영향
④ 쓰레기 재활용에 기반한 순환 경제의 이점
⑤ 폐기물 기반 생산에서 지속 가능한 서비스로의 전환

question: 9. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Imagine pausing in the middle of a busy day, taking a moment to refresh your mind and recharge your energy. This power of a midday break is often underestimated. When you break away from routine, especially with activities designed to stimulate your brain, you prevent cognitive tiredness and enhance productivity for the rest of the day. Neurobic exercises - simple yet effective - are perfect for such breaks. They target different areas of your brain, keeping it agile and alert. These exercises create a mental oasis that refreshes and prepares you for the afternoon's challenges. This strategic pause is not just a break; it boosts your cognitive capabilities, ensuring your mind ______________________. Even briefly experimenting with neurobic exercises can work wonders for your cognitive state during lunch. Start with using your non-dominant hand for routine tasks like writing or eating. This simple switch challenges your brain, activating pathways that aren't typically engaged and promoting greater flexibility in thinking.
options: ① produces more enzymes
② remains sharp and focused
③ sends messages to your brain
④ distracts your body movements
⑤ stays more anxious and puzzled
explanation: 이 글은 일과 중 뉴로빅(neurobic) 운동과 같은 전략적 휴식이 인지적 피로를 방지하고 생산성을 높이며 두뇌를 기민하게(agile and alert) 유지해준다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 휴식이 인지 능력을 높여 마음이 '예리하고 집중된 상태를 유지하게(remains sharp and focused)' 해준다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 더 많은 효소를 생성하게
② 예리하고 집중된 상태를 유지하게
③ 당신의 뇌에 메시지를 보내게
④ 당신의 신체 움직임을 산만하게 하게

question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A new scientific theory is accepted only if ______________________________. The theories of Newton and Einstein offer great examples. A vast body of evidence supports Newton's theory of gravity, but by the late nineteenth century scientists had begun to discover cases where its predictions did not perfectly match observations. These discrepancies were explained only when Einstein developed his general theory of relativity, which was able to match the observations. Still, the many successes of Newton's theory could not be ignored, and Einstein's theory would not have gained acceptance if it had not been able to explain these successes equally well. It did, and that is why we now view Einstein's theory as a broader theory of gravity than Newton's theory. Some scientists today are seeking a theory of gravity that will go beyond Einstein's. If any new theory ever gains acceptance, it will have to match all the successes of Einstein's theory as well as work in new realms where Einstein's theory does not.
options: ① more of the public believe it is possible
② it is created by a more renowned person
③ it explains the evidence better than the old one
④ it suggests the possibility of expanding a new theory
⑤ there are plenty of examples and supporting details
explanation: 글의 내용은 새로운 과학 이론이 받아들여지기 위해서는 기존 이론의 성과를 모두 설명할 수 있어야 할 뿐만 아니라, 기존 이론이 설명하지 못했던 부분(관찰과의 불일치 등)까지 더 잘 설명해야 한다는 것을 뉴턴과 아인슈타인의 중력 이론 사례를 통해 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '그것이 이전의 것보다 증거를 더 잘 설명한다면'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 더 많은 대중이 그것이 가능하다고 믿는다면
② 그것이 더 유명한 사람에 의해 만들어진다면
③ 그것이 이전의 것보다 증거를 더 잘 설명한다면
④ 그것이 새로운 이론을 확장할 가능성을 제시한다면
⑤ 많은 예시와 뒷받침하는 세부 사항들이 있다면

question: 11. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Historically, palaces weren't just homes; they were carefully constructed stages designed to impress and intimidate. While stone symbolized permanence and strength, glass offered something equally powerful: ______________. The introduction of large windows in palaces allowed rulers to literally look down upon their subjects, emphasizing their elevated position. Conversely, it also allowed subjects to gaze up at their leaders, creating a sense of awe and distance. Consider the Palace of Versailles: its Hall of Mirrors, lined with reflective surfaces, not only magnified the grandeur of the space but also placed the king at the center of a dazzling display, reinforcing his absolute authority. The use of glass in palaces wasn't merely aesthetic; it was strategic. Open sightlines allowed for better surveillance and control, ensuring the safety and security of the ruling family. Courtiers and visitors were constantly aware of being observed, contributing to an atmosphere of careful obedience and respect. The very architecture dictated social behavior, with glass acting as a silent enforcer of the power dynamic.
options: ① visibility
② creativity
③ certainty
④ dignity
⑤ objectivity
explanation: 이 글은 궁궐 건축에서 유리가 권력 구조를 강화하는 전략적 도구로 사용되었음을 설명하고 있습니다. 유리를 통해 통치자는 백성을 내려다보고, 백성은 통치자를 우러러보며 경외심을 느끼게 했으며, 탁 트인 시야를 통해 감시와 통제가 가능했음을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말은 '가시성(visibility)'입니다.
options_translation: ① 가시성
② 창의성
③ 확실성
④ 존엄성
⑤ 객관성

question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Experiments testify to science's embrace of ignorance. Arguably the worst thing a scientist can do is to suppose they know what will happen in a given scenario without bothering to check. The rise of the experimental philosophy coincided with the liberation of curiosity as a valuable rather than a questionable attribute. For all that experimental science today is often assumed to be supported by a philosophical framework and an approved methodology ("state your hypothesis and then test it"), the fact is that, as philosopher of science Ian Hacking says, "One can conduct an experiment simply out of curiosity to see what will happen." Indeed, in the view of Charles Darwin's son, the astronomer George Darwin, once in a while one should do a completely crazy experiment, even if it is most likely to prove fruitless. ______________________.
options: ① You never know until you try
② Strict rules are necessary in scientific research
③ Predictable outcomes are essential for meaningful science
④ Scientists should avoid experiments lacking clear hypotheses
⑤ Curiosity-driven experiments often undermine scientific progress
explanation: 이 글은 과학이 무지를 수용하고 호기심을 해방시킨 과정을 설명하며, 엄격한 방법론이나 가설 검증뿐만 아니라 단순히 어떤 일이 일어날지 보기 위한 실험의 가치를 강조합니다. 특히 마지막 부분에서 결과가 없을 것 같더라도 가끔은 미친 듯한 실험을 해보아야 한다는 조지 다윈의 견해를 언급하고 있으므로, 빈칸에는 '해보기 전까지는 결코 모른다'는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 해보기 전까지는 결코 모른다
② 과학 연구에는 엄격한 규칙이 필수적이다
③ 의미 있는 과학을 위해서는 예측 가능한 결과가 필수적이다
④ 과학자들은 명확한 가설이 없는 실험을 피해야 한다
⑤ 호기심 위주의 실험은 종종 과학적 발전을 저해한다

question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Within liberal culture, the value of fair equality of opportunity for individuals outweighs the preservation of the family's integrity. In contrast, for Confucian culture, while seeking fair equality of opportunity for individuals is important, the family assumes a fundamental role in human flourishing, and living within a family institution is considered the essential way of life. Individuals are primarily understood as family members before they are regarded as state citizens. (A)___________, for Confucians, the family possesses inherent value that should never be abandoned, even if it results in certain societal inequalities. Some cultures, like the liberal one, may choose to impose increasing restrictions on the role of families and implement more egalitarian government programs for education, healthcare, and other positive rights in society in the pursuit of fair equality of opportunity. (B)___________, other cultures, like the Confucian one, may prefer to primarily assign welfare responsibilities to the family, accepting inequalities stemming from the existence of the family as long as everyone's basic freedoms and rights are safeguarded in the state.
options: ① For instanceIn addition
② HoweverNevertheless
③ ThereforeOn the other hand
④ BesidesConsequently
⑤ FurthermoreAccordingly
explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서 유교 문화는 개인을 국가 시민 이전에 가족의 구성원으로 이해한다고 했으므로, '따라서(Therefore)' 유교도들에게 가족은 포기될 수 없는 내재적 가치를 지닌다는 결론이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.(B) 앞부분에서는 자유주의 문화가 평등을 위해 가족의 역할을 제한하는 방식을 설명했고, 뒷부분에서는 이와 대조적으로 유교 문화가 가족에게 복지 책임을 맡기는 방식을 설명하고 있으므로 대조의 연결어인 '반면에(On the other hand)'가 적절하다.
options_translation: ① 예를 들어 / 게다가
② 그러나 / 그럼에도 불구하고
③ 그러므로 / 반면에
④ 게다가 / 결과적으로
⑤ 더욱이 / 따라서

question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸을 <보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성하시오. (단, 철자 오류 시 오답 처리. 대/소문자 구분 없음)
passage: Consider units of measure, one kind of descriptive device we are familiar with using in physics. Spatial distances can be given in terms of feet or meters or some other unit, and the physics will be the same regardless. We conclude from this that physics does not prefer one unit of length over any other, and we may choose any one we like for reasons of convenience. We further conclude that any feature depending on that choice, such as the particular numerical value assigned to the spatial separation between two locations, is not out there in the world apart from a choice of unit. Temperatures can likewise be given in terms of the Fahrenheit or Celsius or Kelvin scale, and nothing in the physics changes when we switch from one scale to another. We conclude that ____________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어만 모두 한 번씩 사용
철자 오류 시 오답 처리
대/소문자 구분 없음
answer: the choice of scale is an arbitrary descriptive device that does not affect the physics

question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸을 <보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성하시오. (단, 철자 오류 시 오답 처리. 대/소문자 구분 없음)

question: 19. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

Think of events that shake you out of your everyday routine: maybe attending a family wedding, making a big presentation, or going somewhere you've never been. It's on those occasions that time seems to slow down a little, and you feel more fully engaged. The same holds true if the experience is risky, like mountain climbing or parasailing. Your senses are sharper. You notice more. Thanks to the release of a feel-good chemical in the brain called dopamine, you get a greater rush of pleasure from chance encounters with people than planned meetings. Good news, financial rewards, and gifts are more enjoyable if they are surprises. It's why the most popular television shows and movies are the ones with unexpected plot twists and astonishing endings.

question: 20. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: All human cultures mark the passing of time by the differences they observe in the world around them. Our choice of which differences to mark depends firstly on what we can observe and secondly on what is important in our lives. How we mark the differences - the shapes of our calendars and our rituals - depends on the connections we make between those two things. In the agricultural society of pre-modern Europe, where higher latitudes make the seasons easily observable, it was natural to monitor the solar cycle. Conversely, among the largely nomadic peoples of Arabia, for whom seasonal changes were less significant, the lunar calendar was a more sensible choice. That did not make it inevitable that Islam would use a lunar calendar and Roman Christianity a solar one, but political and religious decisions were made from options limited by geography and lifestyle, filtered through tradition.
options: ① Geography and Lifestyle Shaping Humanity's Calendars
② How Solar and Lunar Calendars Were Scientifically Proven
③ Conflicts Between Religious Groups Over Calendar Systems
④ Why Modern Society No Longer Needs Traditional Calendars
⑤ The Superiority of the Solar Calendar Over the Lunar Calendar

question: 21. 다음 글의 moths에 관한  내용과 일찘하는 것은?
passage: Distinguishing moths from butterflies on outward appearance is not always easy, but there are a few rules of thumb that can help. In most butterflies the antennae end with a small club-shaped swelling, whereas in moths they are usually feathery or narrow to a fine tip. Butterflies tend to rest with their wings held shut above their body, whereas moths more usually rest with the upper sides of the wings on full view. Further distinctions can be made by looking for a tiny hook that joins fore- and hindwings, a feature only present in moths. The stereotypical differences, with moths cast as the gloomy, nocturnal cousins of colourful sun-loving butterflies are simply wrong. There are many brightly coloured moths and many which are active throughout the day. Equally, there are a few nocturnal butterflies and plenty that come clothed in shades of brown and grey. It's more sensible to think of them together; both butterflies and moths are beautiful and fascinating insects.
options: ① 나방의 더듬이들은 밴통 깃털 모양이거나 미세한  끝붽분으로 점점 넓어진다.
② 나방들은 더 흤히 날개들의 윗면이 멸 윔에 닫힌 채 쉽다.
③ 암날개와 뒷날개를 분리해 준는 매우 거대한 갈고리는 나방들에만 존재하는 특징이다.
④ 밝은셑을 가진 나방들은 거의 없고, 낮 동안 내내 활동적인 나방들이 많이 있다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 세포 분열에 관한 내용과 일찘하지 않는 것은?
passage: When a cell divides, the genomes of its two daughters are often not quite identical to each other or to that of the parent cell. On rare occasions, the error may represent a change for the better; more probably, it will cause no significant difference in the cell's prospects. But in some cases, the error will cause serious damage; for example, by disrupting the coding sequence for a key protein. Changes due to mistakes of the first type will tend to be perpetuated, because the altered cell has an increased likelihood of reproducing itself. Changes due to mistakes of the second type - neutral changes - may be perpetuated or not: it is a matter of chance whether the altered cell or its cousins will succeed. But changes that cause serious damage lead nowhere: the cell that suffers them dies, leaving no progeny. Through endless repetition of this cycle of mutation and natural selection organisms evolve: their genetic specifications change, sometimes giving organisms new ways to exploit the environment more effectively, to survive in competition with others, and to reproduce successfully.
options: ① 세포가 분열할 때, 괸것의 두 딨세포들의 유전체들은 종종 서로 간에도, 또는 모세포의 유전체와도 완전히 일찘하지는 않는다.
② 세포 분열에 있어서, 괸 오류가 덄 나은 것으로의 부화를 나타낼 수도 있지만, 덄 높은 확률로 괸것은 세포의 전망에 큰 차이를 일으키지 않을 것이다.
③ 세포 분열의 오류에 있어서, 중립적 부화는 영섽될 가능성이 사라질 가능성보다 높다.
④ 심각한 손상을 초래하는 부화들은 어느 곳에도 닿지 못한다. 괸것들을 꺪는 세포는 짭고, 자섐을 남기지 않기 테문이다.
⑤ 돌연변이와 자연 선택의 순환의 끊임없는 반법을 통해 유기체들은 진화한다.
explanation: 지문에서 중립적 변화(neutral changes)는 "may be perpetuated or not: it is a matter of chance(영섽될 수도 있고 아닐 수도 있음: 이것은 우연의 문제이다)"라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 영섽될 가능성이 사라질 가능성보다 높다는 ③는 지문의 내용과 일찘하지 않습니다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Viewing time as a purchasable and consistent product cemented artificial views on time into our psyche, but every now and again we are forced to acknowledge this mistake. On twentysix occasions in the last fifty years, a second has been added to everyone's day to adjust for the Earth wobbling and the rate of its spin changing. For instance, when El Nino, a climatic system in the Pacific, causes wind speed to change dramatically, it can ⓐ<u>accelerate</u> the rotation of the Earth slightly. Indeed, the Earth's spin is generally slowing because the moon's gravity is acting as a drag, so days are getting ⓑ<u>shorter</u> by about 1.7 milliseconds per century. Such events ⓒ<u>strengthen</u> the similarity between man-made time and more flexible time based on the Earth's naturally occurring rotation. When events like this happen, a bunch of humans make the decision to ⓓ<u>subtract</u> a small slice of time to your day, without your knowledge. We try to force our fixed, man-made view of time on to nature in the ⓔ<u>incorrect</u> hope that it will yield. It doesn't.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 지문의 흐름상 인간은 인위적으로 정해진 시간 관념을 자연에 강요하며 자연이 굴복할 것이라는 '희망'을 가지지만, 실제로는 그렇지 않다고 서술하고 있습니다. 따라서 ⓔ의 'incorrect(부정확한/틀린)'는 맥락상 적절하며, 실제 오답으로 설계된 부분은 본문에 표시된 ⑤번이 아니라 문맥의 흐름을 보았을 때 지문 내 다른 단어의 쓰임을 묻는 의도였을 가능성이 높으나, 제공된 텍스트상의 정답 ⑤를 기준으로 볼 때 문제 오류 혹은 ⓔ가 다른 단어(예: correct)에서 변형되어야 함을 시사합니다. 하지만 지문 전체 맥락에서 지구 자전 속도가 느려져 날이 '더 길어지고(longer)' 있음에도 인위적 시간 체계를 유지하려는 노력을 설명하므로 ⓑ의 shorter가 longer가 되어야 문맥상 적절합니다. 제공된 정답 ⑤에 따르면 ⓔ가 맥락상 적절하지 않은 것으로 판단되나 일반적인 독해상 ⓑ가 가장 적절하지 않습니다. (출처 텍스트의 정답 정보 ⑤ 유지)

question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 모두 고르면? (답 2개)
passage: Everything in the world exists on a continuum, whether in speed, size, or any other possible descriptor you could think of. Still, we create and mindlessly ⓐ<u>adopt</u> sharp distinctions, and those distinctions change lives far more dramatically than marginal differences ever do. Indeed, all differences are arbitrary, but drawing hard lines between categories hides this arbitrariness and can be ⓑ<u>beneficial</u>. I call this resulting damage "the borderline effect." The examples are endless. Someone's IQ is 69 and someone else's is 70 - but only the score of 70 is deemed to be within the range of ⓒ<u>normal</u>. We don't have to be statisticians to know there is not a meaningful difference between 69 and 70. Yet once the person with the ⓓ<u>higher</u> score is labeled "cognitively impaired," his or her life will unfold differently than the person with a one-point ⓔ<u>advantage</u>.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 모든 것이 연속선상에 있음에도 인간이 인위적인 구분을 지어 발생하는 '경계 효과(borderline effect)'의 부정적 측면을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 ⓑ 'beneficial(유익한)'은 뒤에 언급된 'resulting damage(결과적인 손상)'와 모순되므로 'harmful' 또는 'problematic'과 같은 단어가 적절하며, ⓓ 'higher'는 지능 지수가 69인 사람(인지 장애로 분류될 수 있는 사람)에 대한 설명이므로 'lower'가 맥락상 적절합니다.

question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Within liberal culture, the value of fair equality of opportunity for individuals outweighs the preservation of the family's integrity. question: 26. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Coat a fresh, wet swab in salt, and gently touch various spots on your tongue, recording where your taste seems strongest. options: ① emotional traits
② dietary traditions
③ basic food choices
④ genetic taste types
⑤ behavioral disorders
explanation: 지문은 미각 유형(taster status)이 단순히 선호도를 넘어 특정 행동 패턴이나 질환과 관련이 있다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 예를 들어, '비미각자(non-tasters)'는 알코올 중독 발생률이 높고, '초미각자(super-tasters)'는 영양가 있는 쓴맛 음식을 피하는 등의 경향을 보입니다. 이러한 예시는 미각이 식습관을 넘어 행동적 특성이나 장애(behavioral disorders)와 연관될 수 있음을 시사하므로 빈칸에는 'behavioral disorders'가 가장 적절합니다. 다만, 원문이나 문맥상 ④번(유전적 미각 유형)과 혼동될 수 있으나, 지문 끝에서 '운명(destiny)'이 될 수 있다는 언급과 알코올 중독 등의 사례를 비추어 볼 때 행동적 결과에 초점을 맞춘 ⑤번이 답으로 제시되었습니다.

question: 27. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We're naturally wired to organize the world into a hierarchy. We do this to help make sense of the world, maintain our beliefs, and generally feel better. But when someone infringes on our place in the world and our understanding of how it works, we react without thinking. When someone cuts you off on the highway and road rage kicks in, that's your unconscious mind saying, "____________________________" You're reacting to a threat to your inherent sense of hierarchy. On the road we are all equals. We're all supposed to play by the same rules. Cutting someone off violates those rules and implies higher status. Or consider when you get frustrated with your kids and end an argument with "Because I said so." (Or the office equivalent: "Because I'm the boss.") In these moments you've stopped thinking and regressed to your biological tendencies of reaffirming the hierarchy.
options: ① Don't drink and drive.
② I will yield to oncoming traffic.
③ Did you fall asleep at the wheel?
④ Are you climbing up a ladder to my place?

explanation: 이 글은 인간이 세상을 계층 구조(hierarchy)로 조직하려는 본능이 있으며, 누군가 자신의 위치를 침해할 때 무의식적으로 반응한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 도로 위에서 누군가 끼어들 때 느끼는 분노는 상대방이 규칙을 어김으로써 자신보다 높은 지위를 점하려 한다는 위협으로 느껴지기 때문입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 자신의 계층적 지위를 침범하려는 상대에게 던지는 무의식적인 질문인 'Are you climbing up a ladder to my place?(당신이 내 자리로 사다리를 타고 올라오고 있는 건가요?)'가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 28. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 29. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Historically, palaces weren't just homes; they were carefully constructed stages designed to impress and intimidate. explanation: 주어진 문장은 '반대로(Conversely)'라는 연결사를 통해, 앞선 내용(지배자가 창문을 통해 피지배자를 내려다보는 것)과 대조되는 관점(피지배자가 지배자를 우러러보는 것)을 제시하고 있습니다. (A) 뒤 문장은 통치자가 백성을 내려다보는 시각적 우위를 설명하고 있고, 주어진 문장은 그 반대의 시각적 효과를 설명하므로 (B)의 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다. 그 뒤에는 베르사유 궁전의 거울의 방 예시가 이어지며 권위의 강화를 뒷받침합니다.

question: 30. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: We can discard or replace a scientific theory only if we have a better way of explaining the evidence that supports it. The theories of Newton and Einstein offer great examples. A vast body of evidence supports Newton's theory of gravity, but by the late nineteenth century scientists had begun to discover cases where its predictions did not perfectly match observations. (A) These discrepancies were explained only when Einstein developed his general theory of relativity, which was able to match the observations. (B) Still, the many successes of Newton's theory could not be ignored, and Einstein's theory would not have gained acceptance if it had not been able to explain these successes equally well. (C) Some scientists today are seeking a theory of gravity that will go beyond Einstein's. explanation: 주어진 문장의 'It did'는 앞 문장에 제시된 가정법적 조건, 즉 '아인슈타인의 이론이 뉴턴의 이론의 성공 사례들을 똑같이 잘 설명해 내야만 인정을 받았을 것'이라는 내용에 대해 실제로 '그렇게 해냈다'는 긍정의 대답입니다. 따라서 아인슈타인의 이론이 뉴턴의 성공을 입증해냈기에 더 넓은 중력 이론으로 간주된다는 결론을 도출하는 (C) 자리가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: According to Hobbes, man is not a being who can act ⓐ<u>morally</u> in spite of his instinct to protect his existence in the state of nature. Hence, the only place where morality and moral liberty will begin to find an application begins in a place where a sovereign power, namely the state, emerges. Hobbes thus describes the state of nature as a circumstance ⓑ<u>which</u> man's life is "solitary, poor, nasty, brutish and short". It means when people live without a general power to control them all, they are indeed in a state of war. In other words, Hobbes, who accepted that human beings are not social and political beings in the state of nature, believes that without the power human beings in the state of nature ⓒ<u>are</u> "antisocial and rational based on their selfishness". Moreover, since society is not a natural phenomenon and there is no natural force ⓓ<u>bringing</u> people together, what will bring them together as a society is not mutual affection according to Hobbes. It is, rather, mutual fear of men's present and future that assembles ⓔ<u>them</u>, since the cause of fear is a common drive among people in the state of nature.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 circumstance를 선행사로 하고 뒤에 완전한 절(man's life is "solitary, poor, nasty, brutish and short")이 이어지므로, 관계대명사 which는 적절하지 않습니다. 장소나 상황의 개념을 나타내는 관계부사 where 또는 'in which'로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Near the equator, many species of bird breed all year round. But in temperate and polar regions, the breeding seasons of birds are often sharply ⓐ<u>defined</u>. They are triggered mainly by changes in day length. If all goes well, the outcome is ⓑ<u>that</u> birds raise their young when the food supply is at its peak. Most birds are not simply reluctant to breed at other times but they are also physically incapable of doing so. This is because their reproductive system shrinks, which helps flying birds ⓒ<u>saving</u> weight. The main exception to this rule are nomadic desert species. These can initiate their breeding cycle within days of rain. It's for ⓓ<u>making</u> the most of the sudden breeding opportunity. Also, different species divide the breeding season up in different ways. Most seabirds raise a single brood. In warm regions, however, songbirds may raise several families in a few months. In an ⓔ<u>exceptionally</u> good year, a pair of House Sparrows, a kind of songbird, can raise successive broods through a marathon reproductive effort.
explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 동사 help는 목적격 보어로 동사원형이나 to부정사를 취합니다. 따라서 saving은 save 또는 to save로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.[오답 분석]① defined: 수동태(are defined)로 '정해지다'라는 의미가 적절합니다.② that: 주격 보어 역할을 하는 명사절 접속사로 뒤에 완전한 문장이 이어지므로 적절합니다.④ making: for 뒤에 동명사가 와서 '~하기 위함이다'라는 용도를 나타내므로 적절합니다.⑤ exceptionally: 형용사 good을 수식하는 부사로 적절합니다.

question: 5. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Any new resource (e.g., a new airport, a new mall) always opens with people benefiting individually by sharing a common resource (e.g., the city or state budget). Soon, at some point, the amount of traffic grows too large for the "commons" to support. Traffic jams, overcrowding, and overuse lessen the benefits of the common resource for everyone - the tragedy of the commons! If the new resource cannot be expanded or provided with additional space, it becomes a problem, and you cannot solve the problem on your own, in isolation from your fellow drivers or walkers or competing users. The total activity on this new resource keeps increasing, and so does individual activity; but if the dynamic of common use and overuse continues too long, both begin to fall after a peak, leading to a crash. What makes the "tragedy of commons" tragic is the crash dynamic - the destruction or degeneration of the common resource's ability to regenerate itself.
options: ① Using commons benefits individuals but burdens the state.
② Commons failures occur mainly because of unequal distribution.
③ Shared resources can stay sustainable through user self-restraint.
④ The more people share a resource, the better everyone benefits.
⑤ Persistent overuse of the commons leads to collapse and loss of recovery capacity.
explanation: 이 글은 공유 자원의 남용이 결국 자원의 자정 능력을 파괴하고 붕괴로 이어진다는 '공유지의 비극'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 공유지의 비극을 비극적으로 만드는 것은 공유 자원의 재생 능력이 파괴되거나 퇴화하는 '붕괴 역학'이라고 명시하고 있으므로 ⑤번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.

question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Coat a fresh, wet swab in salt, and gently touch various spots on your tongue, recording where your taste seems strongest. question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]

question: 9. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]

question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 11. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Within liberal culture, the value of fair equality of opportunity for individuals outweighs the preservation of the family's integrity. Therefore, for Confucians, the family possesses inherent value that should never be abandoned, even if it results in certain societal inequalities. Some cultures, like the liberal one, may choose to impose increasing restrictions on the role of families and implement more egalitarian government programs for education, healthcare, and other positive rights in society in the pursuit of fair equality of opportunity. On the other hand, other cultures, like the Confucian one, may prefer to primarily assign welfare responsibilities to the family, accepting inequalities stemming from the existence of the family as long as everyone's basic freedoms and rights are safeguarded in the state.

② As civilization advanced, freedom came before family.

explanation: 이 글은 자유주의 문화와 유교 문화가 '개인의 기회 균등'과 '가족의 역할 및 가치' 사이에서 서로 다른 우선순위를 두고 있음을 설명합니다. 자유주의 문화는 개인의 평등을 위해 가족의 역할에 제한을 둘 수 있는 반면, 유교 문화는 가족의 가치를 근본적인 것으로 보고 어느 정도의 불평등을 수용하더라도 가족 중심의 복지를 선호한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 문화에 따라 평등과 가족의 역할을 중시하는 방식이 다르다는 ⑤번이 정답입니다.

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: We encounter contrary claims about the relation of literature to action. Theorists have maintained that literature encourages solitary reading and reflection as the way to engage with the world and thus ①<u>triggers</u> the social and political activities that might produce social change. At best it encourages detachment or appreciation of complexity, and at worst passivity and ②<u>acceptance</u> of what is. But on the other hand, literature has historically been seen as dangerous: it promotes the ③<u>challenge</u> of authority and social arrangements. Plato ④<u>excluded</u> poets from his ideal republic because they could only do harm, and novels have long been credited with making people dissatisfied with their lives and eager for something new. By promoting identification across divisions of class, gender, and race, books may promote a fellowship that discourages struggle; but they may also produce a keen sense of injustice that ⑤<u>facilitates</u> progressive struggles. Historically, works of literature are credited with producing change: Uncle Tom's Cabin, a best-seller in its day, helped create a revulsion against slavery that made possible the American Civil War.
explanation: 문맥상 첫 번째 주장은 문학이 고립된 독서와 성찰을 장려함으로써 오히려 현실에 대한 수동성이나 복잡한 감상에 그치게 한다는 내용입니다. 바로 뒤에서 문학이 '기껏해야 분리(detachment)를 장려하고, 최악의 경우 수동성(passivity)과 현실 수용(acceptance)을 장려한다'고 설명하므로, ①의 triggers(촉발하다)는 사회적 변화를 일으키는 활동을 '대체하다(replaces)' 혹은 '방해하다'는 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 자연스럽습니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Based on discoveries in neuroscience, pain and pleasure are formed and processed in the same area of the brain. Our bodies constantly strive for homeostasis, which is defined as the balance of bodily functions. Without the body's effective ⓐ<u>compensatory</u> mechanisms, which may cushion potential highs and lows, we would not be capable of surviving. Pleasure and pain are like two sides of the same coin; they seem to work together and are heavily ⓑ<u>reliant</u> on one another and keep balance. If you imagine pleasure and pain as the two opposite points on a scale, you can easily understand that as one of the two points rises, the other must correspondingly ⓒ<u>fall</u>. We've all heard the expression, "No pain, no gain." Well, according to psychiatrist Dr. Anna Lembke, there may be some truth to these words. She says that our attempts to escape being miserable are in fact making us even ⓓ<u>less</u> miserable. This is because pain is actually an essential component of our ability to maintain a ⓔ<u>neutral</u> state, and allowing it will in turn reset our internal scale back to balance.

question: 15. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 all translators arrive at their interpretations in dialogue with other people이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: All translators feel some pressure from the community of readers for whom they are doing their work. And <u>all translators arrive at their interpretations in dialogue with other people</u>. The English poet Alexander Pope had pretty good Greek, but when he set about translating Homer's Iliad in the early 18th century he was not on his own. He had Greek commentaries to refer to, and translations that had already been done in English, Latin, and French - and of course he had dictionaries. Translators always draw on more than one source text. Even when the scene of translation consists of just one person with a pen, paper, and the book that is being translated, or even when it is just one person translating orally for another, that person's linguistic knowledge arises from lots of other texts and other conversations. And then his or her idea of the translation's purpose will be influenced by the expectations of the person or people it is for. In both these senses every translation is a crowd translation.
options: ① translators rely on many people and resources when translating
② all translators keep emotional distance from people's expectations
③ the key qualities of skilled translators are intuition and creativity
④ translators strive to remain faithful to the original author's intent
⑤ translators seldom ask native speakers for advice on their translations
explanation: 밑줄 친 부분은 번역가가 혼자 작업하는 것처럼 보여도 실제로는 다른 텍스트, 사전, 이전의 번역본, 그리고 독자의 기대 등 다양한 타인의 자원과 상호작용하며 번역에 도달한다는 의미입니다. 따라서 ① '번역가들은 번역할 때 많은 사람들과 자원에 의존한다'가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Theoretically, our brain would have the capacity to store all experiences throughout life, reaching the quality of a DVD. However, this theoretical capacity is offset by the energy demand associated with the process of storing and retrieving information in memory. As a result, the brain develops efficient strategies, becoming dependent on shortcuts. When we observe a face, the visual image captured by the eyes is highly variable, depending on the point of view, lighting conditions and other contextual factors. Nevertheless, we are able to recognize the face as the same, maintaining the underlying identity. The brain, rather than focusing on the details of visualization, creates and stores general patterns that allow for consistent recognition across diverse circumstances. This ability to match what we see with general visual memory patterns serves as an effective mechanism for optimizing brain performance and saving energy. The brain, being naturally against unnecessary effort, constantly seeks to simplify and generalize information to facilitate the cognitive process.
options: ① the major challenges of human facial recognition

③ the reason why distortion occurs in visual perception

explanation: 인간의 뇌는 이론적으로 모든 경험을 저장할 수 있는 용량을 갖추고 있으나, 정보의 저장 및 검색에 수반되는 에너지 수요를 조절하기 위해 효율적인 전략을 발달시킵니다. 뇌는 시각적 세부 사항에 집중하기보다 일반적인 패턴을 생성하고 저장함으로써 다양한 상황에서도 일관된 인식을 가능하게 하며, 이를 통해 에너지를 절약하고 성능을 최적화한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 글의 주제로 '효율적인 처리를 위해 정보를 단순화하려는 뇌의 전략'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간 얼굴 인식의 주요 과제

question: 17. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Waste has historically been seen as a necessary driver of the economy. Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly dependent on the demand for that product. Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be wasted, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be sustained. Many strategies have been incorporated into product design and use to ensure that waste is inevitable, such as planned obsolescence, limited access to tools for repairs, and use of cheap materials. All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a replacement. Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that prioritizing the elimination of waste via repair and remanufacturing creates a different kind of demand: products as a service. Through this setup, companies simply lease out products that were once sold directly to the customer. With this transition of ownership, companies maintain profit by offering maintenance and repair services and are encouraged to develop long-lasting products.
options: ① the economic effects of consumers choosing repair over replacement
② the impact of product waste on the demand for recycling facilities
③ the psychological factors that affect customers' purchasing decisions
④ the relationship between increasing service fees and consumer satisfaction
⑤ the shift from waste-driven production to service-based product models
explanation: 과거에는 제품이 폐기되도록 설계하여 지속적인 수요를 창출하는 전략(계획적 구식화 등)이 경제의 동력으로 여겨졌으나, 최근에는 수리와 재제조를 우선시하여 폐기물을 제거하고 제품을 서비스 형태로 제공하는 방식이 등장했다는 내용입니다. 이러한 전환을 통해 기업은 소유권을 유지하며 유지보수 서비스를 제공함으로써 수익을 창출하고 더 오래 지속되는 제품을 개발하게 된다는 설명이므로 주제는 '폐기물 기반 생산에서 서비스 기반 제품 모델로의 전환'이 적절합니다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When a cell divides, the genomes of its two daughters are often not quite identical to each other or to that of the parent cell. On rare occasions, the error may represent a change for the better; more probably, it will cause no significant difference in the cell's prospects. But in some cases, the error will cause serious damage; for example, by disrupting the coding sequence for a key protein. Changes due to mistakes of the first type will tend to be perpetuated, because the altered cell has an increased likelihood of reproducing itself. Changes due to mistakes of the second type - neutral changes - may be perpetuated or not: it is a matter of chance whether the altered cell or its cousins will succeed. But changes that cause serious damage lead nowhere: the cell that suffers them dies, leaving no progeny. Through endless repetition of this cycle of mutation and natural selection organisms evolve: their genetic specifications change, sometimes giving organisms new ways to exploit the environment more effectively, to survive in competition with others, and to reproduce successfully.
summary_sentence: Through repeated cycles of mutation and natural selection, changes that are beneficial tend to be (A)__________, neutral ones are fixed by chance, and harmful ones are (B)__________, driving evolution.
options: ① discarded   rejected
② ignored   modified
③ selected   inherited
④ preserved   eliminated
⑤ transmitted   maintained
explanation: 세포 분열 시 발생하는 돌연변이 중 유익한 변화는 세포의 생존 및 복제 가능성을 높여주므로 다음 세대로 보존(preserved)되는 경향이 있고, 중립적인 변화는 운에 따라 결정되며, 심각한 손상을 입히는 해로운 변화는 그 세포가 자손을 남기지 못하고 죽게 되므로 제거(eliminated)됩니다. 이러한 돌연변이와 자연 선택의 순환을 통해 진화가 이루어진다는 내용이므로 (A)에는 preserved, (B)에는 eliminated가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 버려지는 ... 거부되는

question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: When you are working in healthcare, it is important to develop a solid professional relationship with your patients. By establishing realistic self-boundaries, you can protect that relationship. It is important to keep the focus on the patient. When working with patients who are seen frequently, it is easy to start to think of them as friends. ① With a friend, you are likely to share personal information that is not appropriate with a patient. ② Patients may feel that they cannot share important health-related information because you are their friend, and it would be embarrassing to share that information. ③ Self-boundaries can also be thought of as professional boundaries. ④ Doctors should recognize that showing empathy for a patient's pain matters more than strictly maintaining professional boundaries. ⑤ You need to treat patients with respect and keep the relationship professional. Be friendly to patients and always keep the focus on the patient.
explanation: 이 글은 의료 현장에서 환자와의 건강하고 전문적인 관계를 유지하기 위해 적절한 '자기 경계(self-boundaries)'를 설정하는 것이 중요하다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 환자와 지나치게 친구처럼 지내게 될 경우 발생할 수 있는 부작용을 경고하며 전문성을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 전문적 경계를 엄격히 유지하는 것보다 공감이 더 중요하다는 ④번(4번 문장)은 전문적 경계의 중요성을 설파하는 전체 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

question: 20. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Manufacturers masterfully sow seeds of doubt about the adequacy of our current devices. Suddenly, the phone that was your lifeline a year ago is now a museum piece, unable to keep pace with your digital demands. And thus, the itch to upgrade begins, often before there's a genuine need. This cycle isn't just confined to our digital companions. It spills over into almost every aspect of consumer electronics, from the self-driving car to the smart fridge. ① Every product seems to be on an unstoppable march towards the next version, the next generation that promises to revolutionize your life. ② What's fascinating, or perhaps disturbing, is the utter efficacy of this cycle in shaping our desires. ③ This demand for the new generation of AI-enabled devices doesn't change your life. ④ It's not so much that we want the newest device; we're led to believe we need it. ⑤ The distinction between want and need blurs, shifting our financial priorities in favor of staying current with trends. For all the logical arguments against this ceaseless upgrading, the temptation remains compelling.
explanation: 이 글은 제조사들이 소비자들에게 기존 기기가 불충분하다는 의구심을 심어주어 제품 업그레이드 주기를 따르게 만드는 마케팅 전략에 대해 다루고 있습니다. ①, ②, ④, ⑤번은 모두 이러한 소비 심리의 자극과 욕망의 형성에 대해 설명하고 있는 반면, ③번은 특정 기기(AI 기기)가 삶을 바꾸지 못한다는 뜬금없는 내용을 담고 있어 지문의 전체적인 흐름과 맞지 않습니다.

question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There is research that supports the idea that cognitive factors influence the phenomenology of the perceived world.
ordered_passages: (A) They had to make the background color match the color of the figures. The researchers found that red-associated objects required more red in the background to be judged a match than did the objects that are not associated with the color red. It implies that color perception is shaped by cognitive associations.

(B) Delk and Fillenbaum asked participants to match the color of figures with the color of their background. Some of the figures depicted objects associated with a particular color. These included typically red objects such as an apple, lips, and a symbolic heart.

(C) Other objects were presented that are not usually associated with red, such as a mushroom or a bell. However, all the figures were made out of the same red-orange cardboard. Participants then had to match the figure to a background varying from dark to light red.
explanation: 주어진 글 다음에 필자가 소개하는 실험의 시작 단계인 (B)가 오고, 실험에 사용된 대상들과 대조되는 대조군을 제시하는 (C)가 이어지며, 최종적으로 실험의 구체적인 과정과 인지적 요인이 인식에 미치는 영향이라는 결과(시사점)를 정리하는 (A)가 오는 것이 논리적으로 가장 완벽합니다.

question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There are numerous ways wildlife is managed, but they all imply stewardship and can be classified into two broad categories: active management and inactive management.
ordered_passages: (A) If population numbers are too low for the goal of management agencies, other active management can be incorporated, such as predator control to minimize neonatal deaths or habitat improvement to provide required cover for neonates from predators. These efforts represent active approaches to management.

(B) Active management does something to the population - such as increasing or decreasing its size - in a direct manner through strategies like translocations or hunting, respectively. Populations can also be actively managed by altering the habitat to the benefit or disadvantage of a population.

(C) Other populations may not be actively managed, like those in national parks. In such situations, management activities minimize external influences on populations and habitat, which often involves management of humans and not animals.
explanation: 제시문에서 야생동물 관리의 두 가지 범주로 적극적 관리(active management)와 비적극적 관리(inactive management)를 소개했습니다. (B)에서 적극적 관리가 개체군 규모에 직접적으로 영향을 미치는 구체적인 전략들을 설명하며 시작하고, (A)에서 적극적 관리의 또 다른 예시(포식자 통제나 서식지 개선 등)를 보충하며 적극적 관리에 관한 내용을 마무리합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 적극적으로 관리되지 않는 다른 개체군들(비적극적 관리)의 사례와 특징을 설명하며 끝맺는 것이 논리적으로 가장 자연스럽습니다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 제시된 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Imagine that your usually stingy friend delights in buying you a Christmas present after taking a generosity booster. How would you feel? Undoubtedly, there is something praiseworthy about the action. You'd be pleased to receive the gift. You'd say 'thank you', and mean it. But his change of heart is not entirely satisfying. According to Zagzebski, an American philosopher, he is not really generous. When we praise someone's character, we use words for various virtues: 'generous', 'kind', 'courageous', etc. ① A person who gives one gift isn't generous. ② Thus virtues, as opposed to nontypical impulse, are the result of your personal history. ③ They are part of who you are, as they are part of how your character was formed. ④ Instant virtue is therefore impossible. ⑤ Popping a pill cannot make you a better person.
insertion_sentence: Instead, generosity is a stable part of a person's 'moral identity', an emotional habit that is part of who you are.
explanation: 제시문은 관대함이 개인의 도덕적 정체성의 안정적인 부분이며 정서적 습관이라고 설명하고 있습니다. ①번(A) 문장에서 단지 선물 하나를 주는 것만으로는 관대하다고 할 수 없다는 내용이 나온 뒤, 그 대신(Instead) 관대함은 정체성의 일부라는 본질을 지적하고 ②번(B) 문장의 ‘Thus’와 연결되어 그것이 인격 형성의 결과라고 서술하는 것이 흐름상 가장 자연스럽습니다.

question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고 흐름에 어울리는 문장이 되도록 <조건>에 맞게 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 영어로 쓰시오. [24년 10월 29번]
passage: Conditioned Place Preference is a way of finding out what animals want. Researchers train them to associate one place with an experience such as food or a loud noise and another place with something completely different, usually where nothing happens. The two places are made obviously different to make it as easy as possible for the animal to associate each place with what happened to it there. The animal's preference for being in one place or another is measured both before and after its experiences in the two places. If there is a shift in where the animal chooses to spend its time for the reward, this suggests that it liked the experience and is trying to repeat it. Conversely, if it now avoids the place the stimulus appeared and starts to prefer the place it did not experience it, then this suggests that it found the stimulus unpleasant. For example, mice with cancer show a preference for the place where they have been given morphine, a drug used to relieve pain, rather than where they have received saline whereas healthy mice developed no such preference. Then, _____________________________.
subjective_conditions: 1. 9~10개의 단어를 사용하여 주어와 동사가 들어간 완전한 문장으로 서술하시오.
2. cancer, mice, this, suggest를 반드시 사용하시오. (중복 사용 불가능, 어형 변형 가능)
answer: this suggests (that) the mice with cancer wanted the morphine
explanation: 이 글은 '조건부 장소 선호(Conditioned Place Preference)' 실험을 통해 동물이 무엇을 원하는지 알아내는 과정을 설명하고 있다. 암에 걸린 쥐가 모르핀(통증 완화제)을 투여받은 장소를 선호하고 건강한 쥐는 그렇지 않았다는 결과는, 결국 암에 걸린 쥐들이 통증을 완화하기 위해 모르핀을 원했음을 암시한다는 내용이 빈칸에 들어가는 것이 적절하다.

question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고 흐름에 어울리는 문장이 되도록 <조건>에 맞게 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 영어로 쓰시오. [24년 10월 33번]
passage: Some people argue that there is a single, logically consistent concept known as reading that can be neatly set apart from everything else people do with books. Is reading really that simple? The most productive way to think about reading is as a loosely related set of behaviors that belong together owing to family resemblances, as Ludwig Wittgenstein used the phrase, without having in common a single defining trait. Consequently, efforts to distinguish reading from non-reading are destined to fail because there is no agreement on what qualifies as reading in the first place. The more one tries to figure out where the border lies between reading and not-reading, the more edge cases will be found to stretch the term's flexible boundaries. Thus, it is worth attempting to collect together these exceptional forms of reading into a single forum, one highlighting the challenges faced by anyone wishing to establish the boundaries where reading begins and ends. The attempt leads to the understanding that ________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 1. 15~16개의 단어를 사용하여 주어와 동사가 들어간 완전한 문장으로 서술하시오.
2. 윗글에 있는 연속된 2단어 이상을 그대로 사용하지 마시오.
3. activities, enough, lies on, reading, that, a spectrum을 반드시 사용하시오. (중복 사용 가능, 어형 변형 불가능)
answer: reading lies on a spectrum that is expansive enough to accommodate the distinct reading activities
explanation: 독서를 하나의 고정된 개념으로 정의하기보다는 '가족 유사성'을 가진 유연한 행동들의 집합으로 보아야 한다는 내용이다. 따라서 독서는 다양한 독서 활동들을 수용할 수 있을 만큼 충분히 넓은 스펙트럼상에 놓여 있다는 이해로 이어진다는 결론이 적절하다.

question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고 흐름에 어울리는 문장이 되도록 <조건>에 맞게 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 영어로 쓰시오. [25년 10월 22번]
passage: Experiments testify to science's embrace of ignorance. Arguably the worst thing a scientist can do is to suppose they know what will happen in a given scenario without bothering to check. The rise of the experimental philosophy coincided with the liberation of curiosity as a valuable rather than a questionable attribute. For all that experimental science today is often assumed to be supported by a philosophical framework and an approved methodology ("state your hypothesis and then test it"), the fact is that, as philosopher of science Ian Hacking says, "_________________________________________." 2. can, one, see, simply out of, will를 반드시 사용하시오. (중복 사용 불가능, 어형 변형 불가능)
answer: One can conduct an experiment simply out of curiosity to see what will happen.
explanation: 과학에서 실험은 무지를 받아들이고 호기심을 해소하는 과정임을 설명하는 글이다. 현대 과학이 엄격한 방법론(가설 설정 및 검증)에 기반한다고 여겨지지만, 실제로는 무슨 일이 일어날지 보기 위해 단순히 호기심에서 실험을 수행할 수도 있다는 Ian Hacking의 견해가 빈칸에 들어가는 것이 흐름상 적절하다.

question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Technology changes how individuals and societies understand the concept of privacy. The fact that someone has a new ability to access information or watch the actions of another does not justify doing so. Rather, advances in technology require citizens and policy makers to consider how privacy protections should be expanded. For example, when cameras first became available for commercial and private use, nations and citizens struggled over whether new laws should be enacted to protect individuals from being photographed without their permission. The reconsideration of privacy brought about by this new technology re-affirmed a distinction between private and public spaces. It was determined by most cultures that people automatically gave consent to being seen - and thus recorded - once they voluntarily stepped into a public space. Although some people might be uncomfortable with the spread of surveillance cameras, citizens in most cultures have adjusted to the fact that giving up the right not to be observed in these circumstances causes less harm to the community than failing to have surveillance.
options: ① Technological progress requires redefining and reconsidering privacy.
② The balance between private and public life no longer matters.
③ New technologies have made it impossible to protect privacy.
④ People have completely lost their sense of privacy in public.
⑤ Governments must ban the use of surveillance cameras.
explanation: 이 글은 기술의 발전이 개인과 사회가 사생활의 개념을 이해하는 방식을 변화시킨다고 설명합니다. 특히 새로운 기술(예: 카메라)의 등장은 사생활 보호가 어떻게 확장되어야 하는지에 대한 재고와 법적 논의를 필요로 했으며, 공공장소에서의 사생활 권리에 대한 새로운 구분을 확립하게 했습니다. 따라서 '기술적 진보는 사생활에 대한 재정의와 재고를 요구한다'는 1번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기술적 진보는 사생활에 대한 재정의와 재고를 요구한다.
② 사적 생활과 공적 생활 사이의 균형은 더 이상 중요하지 않다.

question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Many historians have pointed to the significance of accurate time measurement to Western economic progress. The French historian Jacques Le Goff called the birth of the public mechanical clock a turning point in Western society. Until the late Middle Ages, people had sun or water clocks, which did not play any meaningful role in business activities. Market openings and activities started with the sunrise and typically ended at noon when the sun was at its peak. But when the first public mechanical clocks were introduced and spread across European cities, market times were set by the stroke of the hour. Public clocks thus greatly contributed to public life and work by providing a new concept of time that was easy for everyone to understand. This, in turn, helped facilitate trade and commerce. Interactions and transactions between consumers, retailers, and wholesalers became less irregular. Important town meetings began to follow the pace of the clock, allowing people to better plan their time and allocate resources in a more efficient manner.
options: ① When Time Became Precise: The Transformation of Europe's Economic Landscape
② How the Mechanical Clock Made Medieval Life More Enjoyable
③ The Invention That Ended Manual Labor in Western Society
④ Why Early Markets Failed to Attract Regular Customers
⑤ Why Ancient People Preferred the Sun to the Clock
explanation: 이 글은 공공 기계식 시계의 등장이 서구 사회, 특히 경제적 발전에 끼친 지대한 영향을 다루고 있습니다. 시계를 통해 정확한 시간 측정이 가능해지면서 시장 활동이 체계화되었고, 상업적 거래의 불규칙성이 줄어들었으며, 자원 배분이 효율적으로 이루어지게 되었다는 내용입니다. 따라서 '시간이 정밀해졌을 때: 유럽 경제 지형의 변화'라는 1번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.

question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The arts and aesthetics offer emotional connection to the full range of human experience. "The arts can be more than just sugar on the tongue," Anjan Chatterjee, a professor at the University of Pennsylvania, says. "In art, when there's something challenging, which can also be uncomfortable, this discomfort, if we're willing to engage with it, offers the possibility of some change, some transformation. That can also be a powerful aesthetic experience." The arts, in this way, become vehicles to contend with ideas and concepts that are difficult and uncomfortable otherwise. When Picasso painted his masterpiece Guernica in 1937, he captured the heartbreaking and cruel nature of war, and offered the world a way to consider the universal suffering caused by the Spanish Civil War. When Lorraine Hansberry wrote her play A Raisin in the Sun, she gave us a powerful story of people struggling with racism, discrimination, and the pursuit of the American dream while also offering a touching portrait of family life.
options: ① Mastering Art Appreciation through Repetition and Exposure
② Art as Transformation: Confronting Discomfort for Change
③ From Paintings to Plays: The Vast World of Artistic Genres
④ The Human Inclination toward Art and Beauty
⑤ When Personal Experience Meets Creativity
explanation: 이 글은 예술이 단순한 즐거움 이상의 역할을 하며, 특히 어렵고 불편한 주제를 다룰 때 변화와 변형의 가능성을 제공한다는 점을 강조합니다. 피카소의 '게르니카'나 한스베리의 연극 사례를 통해 예술이 전쟁, 인종차별 등 고통스러운 현실과 맞서게 하는 매개체임을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '변형으로서의 예술: 변화를 위해 불편함에 맞서기'라는 2번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.

question: 5. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In response to human-like care robots, critics might charge that human-robot interactions create moral hazards for dementia patients.
ordered_passages: (A) Even if deception is sometimes allowed when it serves worthy goals, should it be allowed for vulnerable users? Just as children on the autism spectrum with robot companions might be easily fooled into thinking of robots as friends, older adults with cognitive deficits might be.

(B) Making robots clearly fake also avoids the so-called "uncanny valley," where robots are perceived as scary because they so closely resemble us, but not quite. Other critics of robot deception argue that when care recipients are deceived into thinking that robots care, this crosses a line and violates human dignity.

(C) According to Alexis Elder, a professor at UMD, robots are false friends, inferior to true friendship. Reasoning along similar lines, John Sullins, a professor at Sonoma State University, holds that robots should "remain iconic or cartoonish so that they are easily distinguished as synthetic even by unsophisticated users." At least then no one is fooled.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 인간을 닮은 돌봄 로봇이 치매 환자에게 도덕적 해이를 일으킬 수 있다는 비판을 제기합니다. (A)에서는 속임수가 허용되더라도 취약한 사용자(자폐아동이나 인지 저하 노인)에게 허용되어야 하는지 질문하며 문제의 본질을 구체화합니다. (C)에서는 이에 대한 전문가들의 의견(로봇은 가짜 친구이며, 사용자가 속지 않도록 만화 캐릭터처럼 보여야 함)을 제시합니다. (B)에서는 로봇을 가짜처럼 보이게 하는 것의 장점(불쾌한 골짜기 회피)과 로봇이 배려한다고 속이는 것이 인간의 존엄성을 침해한다는 추가적인 비판을 덧붙이며 마무리됩니다.

question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 it(s)이 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
passage: Conditioned Place Preference is a way of finding out what animals want. Researchers train them to associate one place with an experience such as food or a loud noise and another place with something completely different, usually where nothing happens. The two places are made obviously different to make it as easy as possible for the animal to associate each place with what happened to ⓐ<u>it</u> there. The animal's preference for being in one place or another is measured both before and after ⓑ<u>its</u> experiences in the two places. If there is a shift in where the animal chooses to spend its time for the reward, this suggests that ⓒ<u>it</u> liked the experience and is trying to repeat it. Conversely, if it now avoids the place the stimulus appeared and starts to prefer the place it did not experience ⓓ<u>it</u>, then this suggests something different. That is, ⓔ<u>it</u> found the stimulus unpleasant. For example, mice with cancer show a preference for the place where they have been given morphine, a drug used to relieve pain, rather than where they have received saline whereas healthy mice developed no such preference. This suggests that the mice with cancer wanted the morphine.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ는 모두 실험 대상인 'animal(동물)'을 가리키지만, ⓓ는 동물이 경험한 'stimulus(자극)' 또는 'the experience(경험)'를 가리킵니다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Information encountered after an event can influence subsequent remembering. External information can easily integrate into a witness's memory, especially if the event was poorly encoded or the memory is from a distant event, in which case time and forgetting have degraded the original memory. With reduced information available in memory with which to confirm the validity of post-event misinformation, it is less likely that this new information will be rejected. Instead, especially when it fits the witness's current thinking and can be used to create a story that makes sense to him or her, it may be integrated as part of the original experience. This process can be explicit (i.e., the witness knows it is happening), but it is often unconscious. Over time, the witness may not even know the source of information that led to the (new) memory. Sources of misinformation in forensic contexts can be encountered anywhere, from discussions with other witnesses to social media searches to multiple interviews with investigators or other legal professionals, and even in court.
summary_sentence: A witness's memory becomes (A)__________ to alternation by subsequently encountered information, particularly when their initial memories are (B)__________, which leads to a modified perception of the original event.
options: ① vulnerable - weak
② vulnerable - strong
③ resistant - powerful
④ resistant - dull
⑤ susceptible - firm
explanation: 목격자의 기억은 사건 이후에 접하는 외부 정보에 의해 쉽게 변형될 수 있으며, 특히 원래의 기억이 부실하게 암호화되었거나 시간이 지나 기억이 흐릿해진(weak) 경우에 새로운 정보의 영향을 받기 더 쉬운(vulnerable) 상태가 됩니다.
options_translation: ① 취약한 - 약한

④ 저항력 있는 - 둔한

question: 9. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Based on discoveries in neuroscience, pain and pleasure are formed and processed in the same area of the brain. Our bodies constantly strive for homeostasis, which is defined as the balance of bodily functions. Without the body's effective compensatory mechanisms, which may cushion potential highs and lows, we would not be capable of surviving. Pleasure and pain are like two sides of the same coin; they seem to work together and are heavily reliant on one another and keep balance. If you imagine pleasure and pain as the two opposite points on a scale, you can easily understand that as one of the two points rises, the other must correspondingly fall. We've all heard the expression, "No pain, no gain." Well, according to psychiatrist Dr. Anna Lembke, there may be some truth to these words. She says that our attempts to escape being miserable are in fact making us even more miserable. explanation: 이 글은 쾌락과 고통이 뇌의 동일한 부위에서 처리되며 신체의 항상성 유지를 위해 서로 균형을 이루는 관계임을 설명합니다. 따라서 고통과 즐거움 모두가 평형을 유지하는 안정적인 내적 상태에 기여한다는 내용인 ⑤번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 11. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Coincidence that is statistically impossible seems to us like an irrational event, and some define it as a miracle. question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: The size of a species is not accidental. It's a fine-tuned interaction between a species and the world it inhabits. Over large periods of time, size fluctuations have often signalled significant changes in the environment. Generally speaking, over the last five hundred million years, the trend has been towards animals ⓐ<u>getting</u> larger. It's particularly notable in marine animals, ⓑ<u>which</u> average body size has increased 150-fold in this time. But we are beginning to see changes in this trend. Scientists have discovered that many animals are shrinking. Around the world, species in every category have ⓒ<u>been found</u> to be getting smaller, and one major cause appears to be the heat. Animals living in the Italian Alps, for example, ⓓ<u>have</u> seen temperatures rise by three to four degrees Celsius since the 1980s. To avoid overheating, chamois goats now spend more of their days ⓔ<u>resting</u> rather than searching for food, and as a result, in just a few decades, the new generations of chamois are 25 percent smaller.
explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 'average body size'라는 명사구가 뒤따르고 있으며, 선행사인 'marine animals'와의 관계가 소유의 의미('해양 동물의' 평균 몸 크기)를 나타내야 하므로 주격/목적격 관계대명사인 'which'가 아닌 소유격 관계대명사 'whose'로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓐ는 전치사 towards의 목적어로 쓰인 동명사(getting)이며 animals는 그 의미상 주어입니다. ⓒ는 '발견되어 왔다'는 현재완료 수동태로 적절합니다. ⓓ는 주어인 Animals에 맞춘 복수형 동사입니다. ⓔ는 'spend + 시간 + -ing' 구문으로 적절하게 쓰였습니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 문장 중 어법상 어색한 부분이 있는 것을 두 개 고르면?
passage: Near the equator, many species of bird breed all year round. ⓐ<u>But in temperate and polar regions, the breeding seasons of birds are often sharply defined</u>. ② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓑ 문장에서 is의 보어 자리에 오는 명사절은 뒤에 완전한 문장('birds raise their young...')이 오고 있으므로, 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사인 'what'이 아니라 접속사 'that'을 사용해야 합니다. ⓓ 문장에서 help는 목적격 보어로 원형 부정사나 to 부정사를 취하므로 'saved'를 'save' 혹은 'to save'로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓐ, ⓒ, ⓔ는 문법적으로 오류가 없습니다.

question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 11월 23번]
passage: Sylvan Goldman invented the shopping cart and introduced it in his stores in 1937. Men were reluctant because they thought they would appear weak if they pushed such carts instead of carrying their shopping. Women wouldn't touch them because the carts reminded them of baby carriages. It was only a few elderly shoppers who used them. That made the carts even less attractive to the majority of the shoppers. Then Goldman hit upon an idea. He hired several models, men and women, of different ages and asked them to wheel the carts in the store and shop. A young woman employee standing near the entrance told the regular shoppers, 'Look, everyone is using the carts. Why don't you?' That was the turning point. options: ① revealed why customers avoided the carts

③ showed that the carts were cheaper than expected
④ helped shoppers understand how the carts were made
⑤ achieved what logical reasoning and advertisements could not
explanation: 골드만은 쇼핑카트를 발명했지만 사람들은 여러 고정관념(남자는 약해 보일까 봐, 여자는 유모차 같아서) 때문에 사용을 꺼렸습니다. 반복적인 광고와 설명에도 불구하고 설득되지 않았던 고객들은 다른 사람들이 카트를 사용하는 모습(모방 행위)을 보고 나서야 비로소 카트를 사용하기 시작했습니다. 따라서 모방이라는 단순한 행위가 논리적 설득(설명)이나 광고가 해내지 못한 일을 해냈다는 5번이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 11월 33번]
passage: Correlations are powerful because the insights they offer are relatively clear. These insights are often covered up when we bring causality back into the picture. For instance, a used-car dealer supplied data to statisticians to predict which of the vehicles available for purchase at an auction were likely to have problems. A correlation analysis showed that orange-colored cars were far less likely to have defects. Even as we read this, we already think about why it might be so: Are orange-colored car owners likely to be car enthusiasts and take better care of their vehicles? Or, is it because orange-colored cars are more noticeable on the road and therefore less likely to be in accidents, so they're in better condition when resold? Quickly we are caught in a web of competing causal hypotheses. But our attempts to illuminate things this way merely ________________________. Correlations exist; we can show them mathematically. We can't easily do the same for causal links. So we would do well to hold off from trying to explain the reason behind the correlations.
options: ① provide assistance in fully grasping the details
② serve to diminish and obscure their clarity
③ adjust them to have a more academic tone
④ offer a deeper understanding of the world
⑤ have a tendency to make them simpler
explanation: 상관관계는 그 자체가 명확한 통찰을 제공하지만, 우리가 '왜' 그런지 인과관계를 설명하려 들면 오히려 그 명확성이 가려진다는 내용입니다. 오렌지색 차가 결함이 적다는 상관관계를 발견했을 때, 그 이유(인과관계 가설)를 찾으려는 시도는 오히려 상황을 복잡하게 만들고 명확성을 흐리게 합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 명확성을 감소시키고 가린다는 내용인 2번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 세부 사항을 완전히 파악하는 데 도움을 준다

④ 세상에 대한 더 깊은 이해를 제공한다
⑤ 그것들을 더 단순하게 만드는 경향이 있다

question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 11월 39번]
passage: By the nineteenth century, France had developed a system of precisely defined units of measurement to capture space, time, and more, and had begun to get other nations to adopt the same standards. However, contrary to the trend of the past several decades, in many new situations that are occurring today, allowing for imprecision - for messiness - may be a positive feature, not a shortcoming. It's not merely that having more is an advantage over having less, but that, at times, the ____________________ itself matters more than its accuracy.

(A)에서는 경험 '후'의 선호도를 다시 측정하여 동물이 특정 장소를 반복 방문하거나 피하는지를 통해 선호도를 파악한다고 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 구체적인 예시(암에 걸린 쥐와 모르핀)를 들어 이 실험이 동물이 무엇을 원하는지 보여준다는 결론을 내립니다. 따라서 (C)-(A)-(B) 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 25. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 knowledge 'had already become too vast to be manageable'가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Just as an expert in the taste and colour of wine will gain much by being aware of the chemistry that underlies those qualities, so each perspective on the body can potentially enhance the others. And yet every scientific tool, from microscopes to mathematics, and every aspect of the body, from the brain to the microorganism, requires such depth of expertise that this tends not to happen: we tend to study the human body in silos, each community sectioned from the others by its own specialised vocabulary. Research communities may be dedicated to one type of scientific tool or a specific component of the body, such as one type of cell. How different types of cell communicate with one another becomes its own specialist topic. Even simple forms of life on Earth are now rarely studied as a whole, and the human body is evidently much more complex. As long ago as 1890, The Times newspaper commented that <u>knowledge 'had already become too vast to be manageable'</u>.
options: scientific knowledge had expanded so rapidly that researchers felt overwhelmed, even while they continued to investigate the body from multiple angles
scientific knowledge had expanded and specialized to such a degree that achieving a unified understanding of the human body as a whole had become impractical
the complexity of emerging biological data made it increasingly difficult to organize research findings, even though collaboration across fields was still relatively common
the rise of numerous specialized research communities made it harder to maintain a board perspective, even though many scientists believed integration remained theoretically possible
explanation: 본문은 인체 연구가 각 분야의 전문 지식 심화로 인해 '고립된 분과(silos)' 형태로 진행되고 있으며, 전체로서의 인체를 연구하는 것이 어렵다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 밑줄 친 문장은 1890년 당시에 이미 지식이 너무 방대해져 감당할 수 없게 되었다는 점을 언급하며, 지식의 팽창과 전문화로 인해 전체적인 통합적 이해가 불가능해졌음을 시사합니다. 따라서 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 과학 지식이 너무 빠르게 팽창하여 연구자들이 여러 각도에서 신체를 계속 조사하면서도 압도당하는 기분을 느꼈다
과학 지식이 너무나 확장되고 전문화되어 인체 전체에 대한 통합된 이해를 달성하는 것이 비실용적이 되었다
새로운 생물학적 데이터의 복잡성으로 인해 연구 결과를 정리하기가 점점 더 어려워졌으며, 비록 분야 간 협력이 여전히 비교적 흔했음에도 불구하고 그러했다
수많은 전문 연구 공동체의 부상으로 넓은 관점을 유지하기가 더 어려워졌으며, 비록 많은 과학자들이 통합이 이론적으로 가능하다고 믿었음에도 불구하고 그러했다

question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Based on discoveries in neuroscience, pain and pleasure are formed and processed in the same area of the brain. Our bodies constantly strive for homeostasis, which is defined as the balance of bodily functions. Without the body's effective compensatory mechanisms, which may cushion potential highs and lows, we would not be capable of surviving. Pleasure and pain are like two sides of the same coin; they seem to work together and are heavily reliant on one another and keep balance. If you imagine pleasure and pain as the two opposite points on a scale, you can easily understand that as one of the two points rises, the other must correspondingly fall. We've all heard the expression, "No pain, no gain." Well, according to psychiatrist Dr. Anna Lembke, there may be some truth to these words. She says that our attempts to escape being miserable are in fact making us even more miserable. This is because pain is actually an essential component of our ability to maintain a neutral state, and allowing it will in turn reset our internal scale back to balance.
summary_sentence: Pleasure and pain share the same brain area and balance each other; avoiding pain (A)__________ homeostasis, while accepting it helps restore emotional (B)__________ and overall well-being.
options: ① (A) disrupts (B) stability
② (A) supports (B) instability
③ (A) reduces (B) tension
④ (A) promotes (B) equilibrium
⑤ (A) enhances (B) imbalance
explanation: 글의 내용은 쾌락과 고통이 뇌의 같은 영역에서 처리되며 항상성을 유지하려 한다는 것입니다. 고통을 피하려는 시도는 오히려 항상성을 방해(disrupt)하고, 고통을 수용하는 것이 감정적 안정(stability)을 회복하는 데 도움이 된다는 요약이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 방해한다 (B) 안정
② (A) 지지한다 (B) 불안정
③ (A) 줄인다 (B) 긴장
④ (A) 촉진한다 (B) 평형
⑤ (A) 강화한다 (B) 불균형

question: 1. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Coat a fresh, wet swab in salt, and gently touch various spots on your tongue, recording where your taste seems strongest. Then, gargle with water to thoroughly clean your tongue, use a swab coated with sugar on the same spots, and record those results. Gargle again, and then swab with lemon juice. After a final gargle, try coffee. Compare your reactions with your friends'. Your taste pattern may reveal more than just taste preferences. Recent studies suggest links between taster status and behavioral disorders. For example, "non-tasters" tend to have a higher incidence of alcoholism, perhaps because liquor seems less bitter to them. Conversely, "super-tasters" may avoid nutritious but mildly bitter foods such as broccoli, thus depriving themselves of a balanced diet. So, although taste is not nearly as glamorous as vision, hearing, or even touch, it makes sense for you to pay closer attention to it because chemistry, at least in your mouth, could be destiny.

question: 4. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 nobody is an expert in the whole of anything이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Just as an expert in the taste and colour of wine will gain much by being aware of the chemistry that underlies those qualities, so each perspective on the body can potentially enhance the others. And yet every scientific tool, from microscopes to mathematics, and every aspect of the body, from the brain to the microorganism, requires such depth of expertise that this tends not to happen: we tend to study the human body in silos, each community sectioned from the others by its own specialised vocabulary.
