question: 5. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 what is owned by all is cared for by none이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.8점]
passage: Public goods are non-excludable and non-rivalrous, meaning everyone can use them without preventing others from using them. However, when people are incentivised to act in a way that reduces their benefit, the tragedy of the commons occurs. This happens when inappropriate or selfish behavior by a few diminishes the value of public goods. Public toilets are particularly prone to this problem, as people usually use a specific public toilet once over a short time. Thus, even if they dirty it, their actions are unlikely to affect them in the future. This becomes clear when comparing home and public toilets. Home toilets are generally cleaner because you will certainly use them again and are responsible for cleaning them. Acting irresponsibly only creates more trouble for yourself. Public toilets, however, are the opposite: you are not responsible for cleaning them, nor are you likely to return to the same one, given the many alternatives. Because the consequences rarely fall on the user, people are less motivated to care for public toilets, resulting in the tragedy of the commons. After all, <u>what is owned by all is cared for by none</u>.
options: ① no one feels responsible for taking care of something shared
② a resource shared by everyone receives more attention and care
③ something owned by all makes people try harder to keep it clean
④ a task can be ruined by too many people working on it collaboratively
⑤ what everyone shares is often responsibly protected by the community
explanation: 지문은 공유지(공공재)의 비극을 공중화장실의 사례를 통해 설명하고 있습니다. 개인적인 책임이 없고 결과가 본인에게 돌아오지 않을 때 사람들이 공공재를 함부로 다루는 경향을 말하므로, '모두의 소유는 누구의 관리도 받지 않는다'는 말은 공동의 것에 대해 누구도 책임감을 느끼지 않는다는 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 누구도 공유된 것을 돌보는 데 책임감을 느끼지 않는다
② 모두에 의해 공유된 자원은 더 많은 관심과 관리를 받는다
③ 모든 사람의 소유물은 사람들이 그것을 깨끗하게 유지하기 위해 더 노력하게 만든다
④ 협력적으로 일하는 너무 많은 사람들에 의해 과업이 망쳐질 수 있다
⑤ 모두가 공유하는 것은 종종 공동체에 의해 책임감 있게 보호된다

question: 6. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 every translation is a crowd translation이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: All translators feel some pressure from the community of readers for whom they are doing their work. And all translators arrive at their interpretations in dialogue with other people. The English poet Alexander Pope had pretty good Greek, but when he set about translating Homer's Iliad in the early 18th century he was not on his own. He had Greek commentaries to refer to, and translations that had already been done in English, Latin, and French - and of course he had dictionaries. Translators always draw on more than one source text. Even when the scene of translation consists of just one person with a pen, paper, and the book that is being translated, or even when it is just one person translating orally for another, that person's linguistic knowledge arises from lots of other texts and other conversations. And then his or her idea of the translation's purpose will be influenced by the expectations of the person or people it is for. In both these senses <u>every translation is a crowd translation</u>.
options: ① a translator reveals his or her opinion rather than readers' views
② translation reflects the shared knowledge of many people, not one person
③ translation is an output of the translators' own accumulated experiences
④ translation is not be conducted by several translators but by a single person
⑤ every translation exactly copies the wording and context of the original text
explanation: 번역가는 혼자 작업하는 것처럼 보일지라도 이미 존재하는 다른 텍스트들, 사전들, 그리고 독자의 기대 등 타인과의 대화 속에서 해석에 도달한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '모든 번역은 군중 번역이다'라는 말은 번역이 한 개인이 아닌 많은 사람의 공유된 지식을 반영한다는 의미입니다.

question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Both in the storage and in the copying of genetic information, random accidents and errors occur, altering the nucleotide sequence - that is, ⓐ<u>creating</u> mutations. Therefore, when a cell divides, its two daughters are often not quite identical to one another or to their parent. On rare occasions, the error may represent a change for the better; more probably, it will cause no significant difference in th cell's prospects; and in many cases, the error will cause serious damage - for example, by disrupting the coding sequence for a key protein. Changes due to mistakes of the first type will tend ⓑ<u>to be passed on</u>, because the altered cell has an increased likelihood of reproducing itself. Changes due to mistakes of the second type - selectively neutral changes - may be perpetuated or not: in the competition for limited resources, it is a matter of chance whether the ⓒ<u>altered</u> cell or its cousins will succeed. But changes that cause serious damage lead nowhere: the cell ⓓ<u>that</u> suffers them dies, leaving no progeny. Through endless repetition of this cycle of error and trial - of mutation and natural selection - organisms evolve: their genetic specification change, giving them new ways to exploit the environment more effectively, to survive in competition with others, and ⓔ<u>reproducing</u> successfully.*nucleotide: 뉴클레오티드[핵산(DNA, RNA)의 기본 단위]**perpetuate: 영속시키다 ***progeny: 자손
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장의 병렬 구조를 확인해야 합니다. 'to exploit', 'to survive', 'and (to) reproduce'로 연결되어 organisms의 진화 방향을 설명하고 있으므로, 동명사 형태인 reproducing은 적절하지 않으며 to-부정사(또는 원형부정사)인 reproduce로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 9. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A crowd-generated translation is the result of a group of people pooling their resources to convert a text, such as a historical record or a folk narrative, into a number of other languages. For the most part, this is done using an online platform that lets contributors submit translations, work together on edits, and then vote on the final version. The crowd-sourced translation is useful because it produces more reliable and genuine accounts of cultural traditions. The translator's cultural assumptions and ignorance of the context may easily creep into a literal translation. On the other hand, crowd-generated translation encourages a wide range of people to work together to produce a translation that is accurate to the source text. Increased access to cultural material is another advantage of community-based translation. With the aid of volunteers, texts may be translated into several languages, making them accessible to a larger audience. As a result, this may be especially useful for spreading awareness about and knowledge of marginalized communities, which can help to protect their languages and traditions.*creep into...: ...에 스며들다 **marginalized: 소외된
options: ① the benefits and importance of crowd-generated translation
② the advantages of professional over crowd-sourced methods
③ the limits of collaborative translation in cultural understanding
④ the drawbacks of crowd translation in foreign language learning
⑤ every translation exactly copies the wording and context of the original text
explanation: 이 글은 대중이 참여하는 번역(crowd-generated translation)이 문화적 전통의 신뢰성을 높이고, 다양한 언어로의 번역을 가능케 하여 문화 자료에 대한 접근성을 높이며, 소외된 공동체의 언어와 전통을 보호하는 데 도움을 준다는 이점과 중요성을 다루고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 대중 참여 번역의 이점과 중요성
② 대중 참여 방식보다 전문적인 방식이 갖는 장점
③ 문화적 이해에 있어서 협력 번역의 한계
④ 외국어 학습에서 대중 번역의 단점

question: 10. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Theoretically, our brain would have the capacity to store all experiences throughout life, reaching the quality of a DVD. However, this theoretical capacity is offset by the energy demand associated with the process of storing and retrieving information in memory. As a result, the brain develops efficient strategies, becoming dependent on shortcuts. When we observe a face, the visual image captured by the eyes is highly variable, depending on the point of view, lighting conditions and other contextual factors. Nevertheless, we are able to recognize the face as the same, maintaining the underlying identity. The brain, rather than focusing on the details of visualization, creates and stores general patterns that allow for consistent recognition across diverse circumstances. This ability to match what we see with general visual memory patterns serves as an effective mechanism for optimizing brain performance and saving energy. The brain, being naturally against unnecessary effort, constantly seeks to simplify and generalize information to facilitate the cognitive process.
options: ① Human's memory capacity maintains homeostasis throughout life.
② The brain stores all details of observations to preserve accurate memory.
③ The brain uses general patterns to recognize things efficiently while saving energy.
④ The brain's tendency to simplify information keeps us from identifying familiar faces.
⑤ The human visual system is shaped by internal conditions such as moods and personality.
explanation: 이 글은 뇌가 정보를 저장하고 검색하는 데 필요한 에너지 요구를 줄이기 위해 효율적인 전략을 개발한다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 뇌는 모든 세부 사항을 저장하는 대신 일반적인 패턴을 생성하여 에너지를 절약하고 성능을 최적화한다는 것이 핵심 내용입니다. 따라서 뇌가 에너지를 절약하면서 효율적으로 사물을 인식하기 위해 일반적인 패턴을 사용한다는 ③번이 요지로 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 인간의 기억 용량은 일생 동안 항상성을 유지한다.
② 뇌는 정확한 기억을 보존하기 위해 관찰의 모든 세부 사항을 저장한다.
③ 뇌는 에너지를 절약하면서 사물을 효율적으로 인식하기 위해 일반적인 패턴을 사용한다.
④ 정보를 단순화하려는 뇌의 경향은 우리가 익숙한 얼굴을 식별하는 것을 방해한다.
⑤ 인간의 시각 시스템은 기분이나 성격과 같은 내부 조건에 의해 형성된다.

question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Viewing time as a purchasable and consistent product cemented artificial views on time into our psyche, but every now and again we are forced to acknowledge this mistake. On twenty-six occasions in the last fifty years, a second has been added to everyone's day to adjust for the Earth wobbling and the rate of its spin changing. For instance, when El Nino, a climatic system in the Pacific, causes wind speed to change dramatically, it can slow the rotation of the Earth slightly. ⓐDays get longer in the summer due to Earths' 23.5° axial tilt, which causes the hemisphere tilted towards the sun to receive more direct sunlight for longer periods. ⓑIndeed, the Earth's spin is generally slowing because the moon's gravity is acting as a drag, so days are getting longer by about 1.7 milliseconds per century. ⓒSuch events disturb the similarity between man-made time and more flexible time based on the Earth's naturally occurring rotation. ⓓWhen events like this happen, a bunch of humans make the decision to add a small slice of time to your day, without your knowledge. ⓔWe try to force our fixed, man-made view of time on to nature in the false hope that it will yield: It doesn't.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글의 전체적인 흐름은 인간이 만든 고정된 시간 개념과 지구의 회전 속도 변화로 인한 실제 시간 사이의 불일치, 그리고 이를 조정하기 위해 '윤초'를 추가하는 등의 현상을 다루고 있습니다. ⓐ번 문장은 지구의 자전축 기울기로 인해 여름에 낮이 길어지는 계절적 변화를 설명하고 있는데, 이는 지구의 자전 속도 변화나 인간이 만든 시간 체계와의 오차를 다루는 본문의 맥락과는 관계가 없는 내용입니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: We encounter contrary claims about the relation of literature to action. Theorists have maintained that literature encourages solitary reading and reflection as the way to engage with the world and thus ①<u>counters</u> the social and political activities that might produce social change. At best it encourages detachment or appreciation of complexity, and at worst passivity and acceptance of what is. But on the other hand, literature has historically been seen as dangerous: it promotes the ②<u>questioning</u> of authority and social arrangements. Plato banned poets from his ideal republic because they could only do harm, and novels have long been credited with making people ③<u>satisfied</u> with their lives and eager for something new - whether life in big cities or romance or revolution. By promoting identification across divisions of class, gender, and race, books may promote a 'fellow-feeling' that may discourage struggle but may also produce forms of identification and a keen sense of injustice that make ④<u>progressive</u> struggles possible. Historically, works of literature are credited with producing change: Harriet Beecher Stowe's Uncle Tom's Cabin, a bestseller in its day, helped to stir strong ⑤<u>opposition</u> to slavery that made possible the American Civil War.
explanation:
문맥상 부적절한 어휘는 ③번 'satisfied'입니다.

지문에서 문학(소설)이 위험하다고 간주되는 이유 중 하나로, 사람들이 대도시에서의 삶, 로맨스, 혹은 혁명과 같이 '새로운 무언가를 갈망하게(eager for something new)' 만든다는 점을 들고 있습니다. 사람들이 현재의 삶에 만족하고 있다면(satisfied) 새로운 변화를 갈망할 이유가 없으므로, 소설이 사람들을 현재의 삶에 '불만족하게(dissatisfied)' 만들어 변화를 꿈꾸게 했다는 흐름이 되어야 논리적으로 적절합니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: In Hobbes's theory of state of nature and human nature, people are born in equality and have infinite freedom, as well. However, this freedom formulated by Hobbes is extremely ①<u>dangerous</u>, since Hobbesian depiction of static human nature is based on two major features attributed to human nature which are selfish and warlike. Accordingly, human beings' basic impulses of passion and pleasure to drive the human pursuit of the people, according to Hobbes, inevitably ②<u>resist</u> their selfish nature. In such a state of nature man is described by Hobbes as man's wolf or - so commonly used - as "homo homini lupus." Since there is no sovereign power in the state of nature which may prevent people's possible ③<u>aggression</u> against each other, the equality and freedom of people indeed may lead to war. In other words, since in Hobbesian description of state of nature people are not moral beings, freedom of people may lead to ④<u>immoral</u> acts in terms of infringing other people's basic natural rights. Hence, Hobbes does not define this kind of freedom in the state of nature as moral or real freedom. In other words, in the state of nature in which chaos and fear of death dominate individuals' lives, the fact that individuals are completely free is not a kind of freedom that Hobbes finds positive sense, because Hobbes calls this kind of freedom as "useless freedom." That is, in a state of unlimited freedom, individuals' behaviors are highly ⑤<u>susceptible</u> to exploitation and conflict, which can easily lead to a state of war, since selfish and warlike individuals are equal and free to seek power over one another. *formulate: 공식화하다 **infringe: 침해하다
explanation:
문맥상 부적절한 어휘는 ②번 'resist'입니다.

홉스의 이론에 따르면 인간은 본질적으로 이기적이고 호전적인 존재입니다. 따라서 인간의 기본적인 열정이나 쾌락의 충동은 필연적으로 이러한 이기적인 본성을 '따르거나(follow)', '반영하게(reflect)' 되어 있습니다. '저항하다(resist)'라는 표현은 인간의 본성이 이기적이기 때문에 만인의 투쟁 상태가 발생한다는 지문의 전체적인 논리 흐름과 상충되므로 부적절합니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [25년 10월 23번]
passage: We can discard or replace a scientific theory only if we have a better way of explaining the evidence that supports it. The theories of Newton and Einstein offer great examples. (A) A vast body of evidence supports Newton's theory of gravity, but by the late nineteenth century scientists had begun to discover cases where its predictions did not perfectly match observations. (B) Still, the many successes of Newton's theory could not be ignored, and Einstein's theory would not have gained acceptance if it had not been able to explain these successes equally well. (C) It did, and that is why we now view Einstein's theory as a broader theory of gravity than Newton's theory. (D) Some scientists today are seeking a theory of gravity that will go beyond Einstein's. (E) If any new theory ever gains acceptance, it will have to match all the successes of Einstein's theory as well as work in new realms where Einstein's theory does not.
insertion_sentence: These discrepancies were explained only when Einstein developed his general theory of relativity, which was able to match the observations.
explanation: 이 글은 과학 이론의 폐기와 대체에 대해 설명하며 뉴턴과 아인슈타인의 중력 이론을 예로 듭니다. (A) 문장에서 뉴턴 이론의 예측과 관측치가 완벽하게 일치하지 않는 사례들이 발견되기 시작했다고 언급합니다. 주어진 문장의 'These discrepancies(이러한 불일치)'는 바로 이 (A)의 내용을 지칭하며, 아인슈타인의 일반 상대성 이론이 이를 설명할 수 있었을 때 비로소 그 문제가 해결되었다는 흐름이 되어야 합니다. 따라서 (B)에 위치하는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [25년 10월 33번]
passage: Historically, palaces weren't just homes; they were carefully constructed stages designed to impress and intimidate. While stone symbolized permanence and strength, glass offered something equally powerful: visibility. The introduction of large windows in palaces allowed rulers to literally look down upon their subjects, emphasizing their elevated position. Conversely, it also allowed subjects to gaze up at their leaders, creating a sense of awe and distance. Consider the Palace of Versailles: its Hall of Mirrors, lined with reflective surfaces, not only magnified the grandeur of the space but also placed the king at the center of a dazzling display, reinforcing his absolute authority. The use of glass in palaces wasn't merely aesthetic; it was __________. Open sightlines allowed for better surveillance and control, ensuring the safety and security of the ruling family. Courtiers and visitors were constantly aware of being observed, contributing to an atmosphere of careful obedience and respect. The very architecture dictated social behavior, with glass acting as a silent enforcer of the power dynamic.
options: ① arbitrary
② illusional
③ optional
④ tactical
⑤ haphazard
explanation: 지문은 궁전 건축에서 유리가 사용된 목적이 단순한 아름다움(aesthetic)을 넘어서, 왕의 권위를 강화하고 사람들을 감시하며 사회적 행동을 규제하는 도구로 쓰였음을 설명합니다. 빈칸 뒤의 문장들에서 '감시와 통제', '안전과 보안 보장', '권력 역학의 집행자' 등의 표현이 나오므로, 유리의 사용은 치밀하게 계획된 '전략적인(tactical)' 행위였음을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 임의적인
② 환상의
③ 선택적인
④ 전략적인
⑤ 무계획적인

question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Within liberal culture, the value of fair equality of opportunity for individuals outweighs the preservation of the family's integrity. In contrast, for Confucian culture, while seeking fair equality of opportunity for individuals is important, the family assumes a fundamental role in human flourishing, and living within a family institution is considered the essential way of life. Individuals are primarily understood as family members before they are regarded as state citizens. Therefore, for Confucians, the family possesses inherent value that should never be abandoned, even if it results in certain societal inequalities. Some cultures, like the liberal one, may choose to impose increasing restrictions on the role of families and implement more egalitarian government programs for education, healthcare, and other positive rights in society in the pursuit of fair equality of opportunity. On the other hand, other cultures, like the Confucian one, may prefer to primarily assign welfare responsibilities to the family, accepting inequalities stemming from the existence of the family as long as everyone's basic freedoms and rights are safeguarded in the state.
summary_sentence: While liberal culture prioritizes individual opportunity over family (A)__________, Confucian culture upholds the family's inherent value even at the cost of (B)__________.
options: ① freedom / agreement
② cohesion / equality
③ integrity / authority
④ discontinuity / imbalance
⑤ discord / instability
explanation: 지문은 자유주의 문화와 유교 문화의 가치관 차이를 다루고 있습니다. 자유주의 문화는 가족의 통합성(integrity)이나 결속보다 개인의 기회 균등을 우선시하며, 유교 문화는 비록 사회적 불평등(inequalities)이 발생하더라도 가족의 내재적 가치를 중시합니다. 요약문에서 (A)는 가족의 결속/통합을 의미하는 cohesion(또는 본문의 integrity), (B)는 가족 보존을 위해 희생될 수 있는 가치인 equality(평등)가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자유 / 합의
② 결속 / 평등
③ 온전함 / 권위
④ 불연속성 / 불균형
⑤ 불화 / 불안정

question: 27. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하도록 아래 표를 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
passage: Distinguishing moths from butterflies on outward appearance is not always easy, but there are a few rules of thumb that can help. In most butterflies the antennae end with a small club-shaped swelling, whereas in moths they are usually feathery or narrow to a fine tip. Butterflies tend to rest with their wings held shut above their body, whereas moths more usually rest with the upper sides of the wings on full view. Further distinctions can be made by looking for a tiny hook that joins fore- and hindwings, a feature only present in moths. The stereotypical differences, with moths cast as the gloomy, nocturnal cousins of colourful sun-loving butterflies are simply wrong. There are many brightly coloured moths and many which are active throughout the day. Equally, there are a few nocturnal butterflies and plenty that come clothed in shades of brown and grey. Thus, it's more sensible to think of them together; butterflies and moths are equally beautiful and fascinating insects.
subjective_conditions: 1. (A)와 (B) 모두 상관 접속사를 활용하여 작성할 것
2. 단어 수 제한 없음
3. 위 지문 속 단어를 사용할 수 있음 (변형 가능)
4. 철자 및 어법 오류당 1점 감점 (단, 의미 전달에 오류가 없을 시 한함)
subjective_answer_format: Category: Connection between Forewings and HindwingsFeatures: It's (A)__________________ that have a tiny hook that joins forewings and hindwings.Category: ConclusionFeatures: (B)_________________________________
answer: (A) not butterflies but moths(B) Both butterflies and moths are beautiful and fascinating insects
explanation: (A) 지문에서 앞날개와 뒷날개를 연결하는 작은 갈고리(tiny hook)는 나방(moths)에게만 있는 특징이라고 하였으므로, 'not A but B(A가 아니라 B)' 상관접속사를 사용하여 나비가 아니라 나방임을 나타냅니다.(B) 지문의 마지막 결론 부분에서 나비와 나방은 똑같이 아름답고 매혹적인 곤충이라고 하였으므로, 'both A and B(A와 B 둘 다)' 상관접속사를 사용하여 작성합니다.

question: 28. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오. [24년 10월 39번]
passage: The conditioned place preference task takes advantage of the fact that objects, events, or substances that an animal finds pleasant or noxious become conditioned to the location in which the object, event, or substance is encountered. Typically, a two-compartment box is used and the measure of behavior is the time spent in the compartments. For example, if the experimenter wishes to determine whether a drug treatment is perceived as being pleasant, the animal is exposed to one of the compartments of the box while under the effects of the drug. At some later date, while undrugged, the animal is given access to the original box or to a different box. If the animal spends more time in the original "conditioned" box, that can be taken as evidence that the animal perceived the treatment as positively rewarding. If it shows a preference for the other box, it perceived the treatment as negatively rewarding.*conditioned: 조건화된 **noxious: 불쾌한
summary_sentence: A conditioned place preference task is a behavioral experiment that assesses whether an animal finds a stimulus pleasant or unpleasant based on ___________ _____________ in the location where the stimulus was experienced.
subjective_conditions: 필수 사용 단어: how
단어 수 제한: 필수 단어 포함 4~6단어
위 지문 속 단어를 사용할 수 있음 (변형 가능)
철자 및 어법 오류당 1점 감점 (단, 의미 전달에 오류가 없을 시 한함)
조건 1, 2를 어길 시 0점 처리함
explanation: 조건화된 장소 선호 과제는 동물이 특정 장소에서 보낸 '시간'을 통해 그 장소와 연관된 자극이 긍정적이었는지 부정적이었는지를 측정하는 실험입니다. 요약문은 '자극이 경험된 장소에서 [얼마나 많은 시간을 보내는지]에 기초하여'라는 의미가 되어야 하므로 'how much time it spends'가 적절합니다.

question: 30. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오. [3.0점]
passage: The spiral of silence occurs when individuals who perceive that their opinions are popular express them, whereas those who do not think their opinions are popular remain quiet. This process occurs in a spiral, so that one side of an issue ends up with considerable publicity and the other side with very little. In everyday life, people express their opinions in a variety of ways: they talk about them, they wear buttons, they put bumper stickers on their cars, and they post their views on Facebook and Twitter. According to this theory, people are more apt to do these kinds of things when they perceive that others share their opinions. The 2016 US presidential election, in which polls suggested that Hillary Clinton would win, provides an example of the spiral of silence; some voters who supported Donald Trump were reluctant to voice their support for him because they perceived that __________________. The spiral of silence, then, seems to have been a contributing factor for why the polls were mistaken: many Trump supporters kept silent about their true preferences and Trump ended up winning the election.
subjective_conditions: 1. 단어 수 제한: 4~7단어
2. 위 지문 속 단어를 사용할 수 있음 (변형 가능)
3. 철자 및 어법 오류당 1점 감점 (단, 의미 전달에 오류가 없을 시 한함)
4. 조건 1을 어길 시 0점 처리함
explanation: 지문은 '침묵의 나선 이론'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 이 이론에 따르면 사람들은 자신의 의견이 다수 의견(popular)일 때 목소리를 내고, 소수 의견이라고 느낄 때 침묵합니다. 2016년 미국 대선 사례에서 도널드 트럼프 지지자들이 자신의 지지 의사를 밝히기를 꺼린 이유는, 여론조사 결과 등을 통해 자신의 의견이 대중적이지 않다고(not popular) 느꼈기 때문입니다. 따라서 문맥과 조건에 맞춰 'their opinions were not popular'가 적절합니다.

question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: One factor that may hinder creativity is unawareness of the resources required in each activity in students' learning. Often students are unable to identify the resources they need to perform the task required of them. Different resources may be compulsory for specific learning tasks, and recognizing them may simplify the activity's performance. For example, students who desire to conduct experiments must investigate in advance whether they will have access to the laboratory, equipment, and chemicals required. Preparation is vital for students to succeed, and it may be about human and financial resources such as laboratory technicians, money to purchase chemicals, and equipment. Even if some resources are not available, identifying them in advance may help students' creativity by leading to changing the topic or finding alternative resources.
options: ① 다양한 실험 활동을 많이 경험할수록 창의성이 높아진다.
② 학습에 대한 자율성이 보장될 때 학업 성취도가 높아진다.
③ 교사의 정서적 지지와 긍정적 피드백이 학습 성과를 좌우한다.
④ 문제 해결 능력 향상을 위해 실습 중심의 프로젝트 기반 학습이 필요하다.
⑤ 학생들이 과제 수행에 필요한 자원을 미리 파악하고 준비할 때 창의성이 향상된다.
explanation: 이 글은 학생들이 학습 과제에 필요한 자원(인적, 물적 자원 등)을 미리 파악하고 준비하는 것이 창의성을 발휘하고 성공적인 과제 수행을 하는 데 필수적이라는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 ⑤번이 가장 적절한 요지입니다.

question: 6. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When a cell divides, the genomes of its two daughters are often not quite identical to each other or to that of the parent cell. On rare occasions, the error may represent a change for the better; more probably, it will cause no significant difference in the cell's prospects. But in some cases, the error will cause serious damage; for example, by disrupting the coding sequence for a key protein. Changes due to mistakes of the first type will tend to be perpetuated, because the altered cell has an increased likelihood of reproducing itself. Changes due to mistakes of the second type - neutral changes - may be perpetuated or not: it is a matter of chance whether the altered cell or its cousins will succeed. But changes that cause serious damage lead nowhere: the cell that suffers them dies, leaving no progeny. Through endless repetition of this cycle of mutation and natural selection organisms evolve: their genetic specifications change, sometimes giving organisms new ways to exploit the environment more effectively, to survive in competition with others, and to reproduce successfully.
options: ① roles of mutation in maintaining genetic stability
② how mutations influence survival and reproduction
③ why cell division increases the lifespan of organisms
④ danger of neutral errors destroying coding sequences
⑤ difficulties organisms face in adapting to climate change

question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Weber's law concerns the perception of difference between two stimuli. It suggests that we might not be able to detect a 1-mm difference when we are looking at lines 466mm and 467mm in length, but we may be able to detect a 1-mm difference when we are comparing a line 2mm long with one 3mm long. Another example of this principle is that we can detect 1 candle when it is lit in an otherwise dark room. But when 1 candle is lit in a room in which 100 candles are already burning, we may not notice the light from this candle. Therefore, the Just-noticeable difference (JND) varies as a function of the strength of the signals. For example, the JND is greater for very loud noises than it is for much more quiet sounds. When a sound is very weak, we can tell that another sound is louder, even if it is barely louder. When a sound is very loud, to tell that another sound is even louder, it has to be much louder. Thus, Weber's law means that it is harder to distinguish between two samples when those samples are larger or stronger levels of the stimuli.
options: ① How Experimental Psychology Works on a JND
② How We Perceive Change: Exploring Weber's Law
③ Just-Noticeable Differences: the Limit of Weber's Law
④ Light in the Darkness: The Candle Analogy Explained
⑤ The Threshold Puzzle: How Much Change Can We Detect
explanation: 베버의 법칙(Weber's law)에 따르면 두 자극 사이의 차이를 인식하는 최소 식별 차이(JND)는 원래 자극의 강도에 비례합니다. 즉, 자극이 강할수록 변화를 알아차리기 위해 더 큰 차이가 필요하다는 내용이므로, 제목으로는 '우리가 변화를 인식하는 방법: 베버의 법칙 탐구'가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Some people argue that there is a single, logically consistent concept known as reading that can be neatly set apart from everything else people do with books. Is reading really that simple? The most productive way to think about reading is as loosely related set of behaviors that belong together owing to family resemblances, as Ludwig Wittgenstein used the phrase, without having in common a single defining trait. Consequently, efforts to distinguish reading from nonreading are destined to fail because there is no agreement on what qualifies as reading in the first place. The more one tries to figure out where the border lies between reading and not-reading, the more edge cases will be found to stretch the term's flexible boundaries. Thus, it is worth attempting to collect together these exceptional forms of reading into a single forum, one highlighting the challenges faced by anyone wishing to establish the boundaries where reading begins and ends. The attempt moves toward an understanding of reading as a spectrum that is expansive enough to accommodate the distinct reading activities.
options: ① Reading as a Broad and Flexible Spectrum

⑤ A Correlation Between Literacy and Intensive Reading

question: 9.   다음 글에서 전체 흠름과 관계없는 문장은?

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]

question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
passage: All translators feel some pressure from the community of readers for whom they are doing their work. And all translators arrive at their interpretations in dialogue with other people. The English poet Alexander Pope had pretty good Greek, but when he set about translating Homer's lliad in the early 18th century he did not work ⓐ<u>alone</u>. He had Greek commentaries to ⓑ<u>consult</u>, and translations that had already been done in English, Latin, and French - and of course he had dictionaries. Translators always ⓒ<u>draw on</u> more than one source text. Even when the scene of translation consists of just one person with a pen, paper, and the book that is being translated, or even when it is just one person translating orally for another, that person's linguistic knowledge ⓓ<u>generates</u> lots of other texts and conversations. And then his or her idea of the translation's purpose will be influenced by the expectations of the person or people it is for. In both these senses every translation is a ⓔ<u>collective</u> translation.

question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]

question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
passage: Viewing time as a purchasable and consistent product cemented artificial views on time into our psyche, but every now and again we are forced to acknowledge this mistake. (E) We try to force our fixed, manmade view of time on to nature in the false hope that it will yield. It doesn't.
insertion_sentence: Such events disturb the similarity between manmade time and more flexible time based on the Earth's naturally occurring rotation.
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'Such events'는 (B)와 (C)에서 설명한 엘니뇨 현상이나 달의 중력으로 인해 지구 자전 속도가 변하는 현상들을 가리킵니다. 이러한 현상들이 인위적인 시간과 자연적인 시간 사이의 일치성을 방해한다는 내용 뒤에, (D)에서 '이러한 순간들(In moments like these)'에 인간들이 시간을 추가하기로 결정한다는 내용이 이어지는 것이 논리적으로 가장 적절합니다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: Just as an expert in the taste and colour of wine will gain much by being aware of the chemistry that underlies those qualities, so each perspective on the body can potentially enhance the others. And yet every scientific tool, from microscopes to mathematics, and every aspect of the body, from the brain to the microorganism, requires such depth of expertise that this tends not to happen: we tend to study the human body in silos, each community sectioned from the others by its own specialized vocabulary. Research communities may be dedicated to one type of scientific tool or a specific component of the body, such as one type of cell. How different types of cell communicate with one another becomes its own specialist topic. Even simple forms of life on Earth are now rarely studied as a whole, and the human body is evidently much more complex. As long ago as 1890, The Times newspaper commented that knowledge 'had already become too vast to be manageable'. Today, nobody is an expert in the whole of anything.
summary_sentence: Scientific study of the human body is highly specialized and (A)__________, preventing a(n) (B)__________ understanding due to the complexity and depth of expertise required in each area.
options: ① fragmented holistic
② disconnected intuitive
③ well-established synthetic
④ advanced integrated
⑤ divided instinctive
explanation: 인체에 대한 과학적 연구는 각 분야의 전문성 때문에 서로 분리된 'silos'에서 이루어지며, 지식의 방대함으로 인해 전체를 다 아는 전문가가 없다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '파편화된(fragmented)', (B)에는 '전체적인(holistic)'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 파편화된 - 전체적인
② 단절된 - 직관적인
③ 잘 확립된 - 종합적인
④ 진보된 - 통합적인
⑤ 나누어진 - 본능적인

question: 21. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: We can discard or replace a scientific theory only if we have a better way of explaining the evidence that supports it. The theories of Newton and Einstein offer great examples. A vast body of evidence supports Newton's theory of gravity, but by the late nineteenth century scientists had begun to discover cases where its predictions did not perfectly match observations. These discrepancies were explained only when Einstein developed his general theory of relativity, which was able to match the observations. Still, the many successes of Newton's theory could not be ignored, and Einstein's theory would not have gained acceptance if it had not been able to explain these successes equally well. It did, and that is why we now view Einstein's theory as a broader theory of gravity than Newton's theory. Some scientists today are seeking a theory of gravity that will go beyond Einstein's. If any new theory ever gains acceptance, it will have to match all the successes of Einstein's theory as well as work in new realms where Einstein's theory does not.
summary_sentence: Scientific theories change only when a new theory explains all the (A)___________ of the old one and accounts for additional (B)___________ evidence, as Einstein's theory did for Newton's and future theories must do for Einstein's.
options: ① achievements unexplained
② hypotheses irrelevant
③ limitations inaccurate
④ successes observable
⑤ principles empirical
explanation: 아인슈타인의 이론이 뉴턴 이론의 성공 사례들을 모두 설명함과 동시에 기존 이론으로 설명되지 않았던 불일치(discrepancies)를 해결함으로써 수용되었다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '업적/성공(achievements)', (B)에는 '설명되지 않은(unexplained)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 업적 - 설명되지 않은
② 가설 - 무관한
③ 한계 - 부정확한
④ 성공 - 관찰 가능한
⑤ 원리 - 실증적인

question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: Coat a fresh, wet swab in salt, and gently touch various spots on your tongue, recording where your taste seems strongest. Then, gargle with water to thoroughly clean your tongue, use a swab coated with sugar on the same spots, and record those results. Gargle again, and then swab with lemon juice. After a final gargle, try coffee. Compare your reactions with your friends'. Your taste pattern may reveal more than just taste preferences. Recent studies suggest that ___________________________________, showing that taste can affect life beyond food preferences. For example, "non-tasters" tend to have a higher incidence of alcoholism, perhaps because liquor seems less bitter to them. Conversely, "super-tasters" may avoid nutritious but mildly bitter foods such as broccoli, thus depriving themselves of a balanced diet. So, although taste is not nearly as glamorous as vision, hearing, or even touch, it makes sense for you to pay closer attention to it because chemistry, at least in your mouth, could be destiny.
subjective_conditions: sensitive, associate, problem을 포함할 것 (형태 변형 가능)
10단어 이내로 작성할 것
*조건 위반, 철자 오류, 문법 오류 시 각각 1점 감점함.
answer: taste sensitivity can be associated with behavioral problems
explanation: 이 글은 맛에 대한 민감도가 단순히 음식 선호도를 넘어 행동 문제(예: 알코올 중독, 불균형한 식단)와 연관될 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 예시들이 비태이스터(non-tasters)와 슈퍼테이스터(super-tasters)의 행동 특성을 설명하므로, 맛의 민감성이 행동적 문제와 결합될 수 있다는 내용이 적절합니다.

question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고 주어진 질문에 대한 답을 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
passage: Within liberal culture, the value of fair equality of opportunity for individuals outweighs the preservation of the family's integrity. In contrast, for Confucian culture, while seeking fair equality of opportunity for individuals is important, the family assumes a fundamental role in human flourishing, and living within a family institution is considered the essential way of life. Individuals are primarily understood as family members before they are regarded as state citizens. Therefore, for Confucians, the family possesses inherent value that should never be abandoned, even if it results in certain societal inequalities. Some cultures, like the liberal one, may choose to impose increasing restrictions on the role of families and implement more egalitarian government programs for education, healthcare, and other positive rights in society in the pursuit of fair equality of opportunity. On the other hand, other cultures, like the Confucian one, may prefer to primarily assign welfare responsibilities to the family, approving inequalities stemming from the existence of the family as long as everyone's basic freedoms and rights are safeguarded in the state.
subjective_conditions: (A), (B)는 각각 5단어 이내로 작성할 것
(C), (D)는 각각 2단어 이내로 작성할 것
*지문에 있는 단어를 사용해도, 사용하지 않아도 되며, 필요하면 형태를 변형할 수 있음.
*조건 위반, 철자 오류, 문법 오류 시 각각 1점 감점함.
subjective_answer_format: Q1. What are the primary values of the two perspectives in the above text?→ Liberalism prioritizes (A)_____________________ over (B)_____________________, whereas Confucianism does the opposite.Q2. In the Confucian worldview, what is the primary identity of a person?→ a (C)_____________________Q3. How does Confucian culture view the inequalities that may result from the family's existence?→ They are to be (D)___________, on condition that the state protects basic freedoms.(A) _____________________________________________________(B) _____________________________________________________(C) _____________________________________________________(D) _____________________________________________________
answer: (A) equality of opportunity(B) the role of the family(C) family member(D) accepted (또는 admitted, tolerated, approved, allowed, endured)
explanation: 본문은 자유주의 문화와 유교 문화의 가치관 차이를 다룹니다. (A)와 (B)는 자유주의가 '기회의 평등'을 '가족의 보존(가족의 역할)'보다 중시한다는 점을 나타내며, 유교는 그 반대임을 설명합니다. (C)는 유교적 관점에서 개인의 정체성은 시민이기 전에 '가족 구성원'임을 명시합니다. (D)는 가족 제도로 인해 발생하는 불평등이라도 기본적인 자유와 권리가 보장되는 한 '용인(받아들여짐)'된다는 맥락에 맞아야 합니다.

question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: Historically, palaces weren't just homes; they were carefully constructed stages designed to impress and intimidate. While stone symbolized permanence and strength, glass offered something equally powerful: visibility. The introduction of large, high windows in palaces allowed rulers to literally look down upon their subjects, emphasizing their elevated position. ________________________________________________. Consider the Palace of Versailles: its Hall of Mirrors, lined with reflective surfaces, not only magnified the grandeur of the space but also placed the king at the center of a dazzling display, reinforcing his absolute authority. The use of glass in palaces wasn't merely aesthetic: it was strategic. Open sightlines allowed for better surveillance and control, ensuring the safety and security of the ruling family. Courtiers and visitors were constantly aware of being observed, contributing to an atmosphere of careful obedience and respect. The very architecture dictated social behavior, with glass acting as a silent enforcer of the power dynamic.
subjective_conditions: (A)는 look down을 포함하여 10단어 이내로 작성할 것 (형태 변형 가능)
(B)는 create을 포함하여 7단어 이내로 작성할 것 (형태 변형 가능)

*조건 위반, 철자 오류, 문법 오류 시 각각 1점 감점함.
answer: (A) had allowed the subjects to look down on(B) would not have created
explanation: 이 문제는 지문의 내용을 바탕으로 반대되는 상황을 가정하는 문장을 완성하는 문제입니다. 지문에 따르면 궁전의 유리창은 통치자가 피지배층을 내려다보게 하여 권위를 세웠으므로, 가정법 과거완료를 사용하여 '만약 그것(유리창)이 피지배층들로 하여금 지도자들을 내려다보게 허용했더라면(실제로는 반대), 그러한 경외감과 거리감을 만들어내지 못했을 것이다'라는 의미가 되어야 합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 had allowed the subjects to look down on, (B)에는 would not have created를 쓰는 것이 적절합니다.

question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Correlations are powerful because the insights they offer are relatively clear. These insights are often covered up when we bring causality back into the picture. For instance, a used-car dealer supplied data to statisticians to predict which of the vehicles available for purchase at an auction were likely to have problems. A correlation analysis showed that orange-colored cars were far less likely to have defects. Even as we read this, we already think about why it might be so: Are orange-colored car owners likely to be car enthusiasts and take better care of their vehicles? Or, is it because orange-colored cars are more noticeable on the road and therefore less likely to be in accidents, so they're in better condition when resold? Quickly we are caught in a web of competing causal hypotheses. But our attempts to illuminate things this way only make them cloudier. Correlations exist; we can show them mathematically. We can't easily do the same for causal links. So we would do well to hold off from trying to explain the reason behind the correlations.
options: ① Identifying the probable reasons for correlations allows researchers to eliminate uncertainty.
② Causal hypotheses are essential for transforming mere correlations into scientific knowledge.
③ Mathematical analysis of data should always aim to reveal causal relationships behind patterns.
④ The more we attempt to illuminate the causes of correlations, the clearer our understanding becomes.
⑤ It is wiser to accept correlations as they are, because forcing causal explanations only makes them more confusing.
explanation: 상관관계의 배후에 있는 인과적 설명을 시도하려 하지 말고(hold off) 상관관계 자체만으로 받아들이는 것이 더 현명하다는 내용이다.

question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: For a long time, random sampling was a good shortcut. It made analysis of large data problems possible in the pre-digital era. But much as converting a digital image or song into a smaller file results in loss of data, information is lost when sampling. Having the full (or close to the full) dataset provides a lot more freedom to explore, to look at the data from different angles or to look closer at certain aspects of it. A fitting example may be the light-field camera, which captures not just a single plane of light, as with conventional cameras, but rays from the entire light field, some 11 million of them. The photographers can decide later which element of an image to focus on in the digital file. There is no need to focus at the beginning, since collecting all the information makes it possible to do that afterwards. Because rays from the entire light field are included, it is closer to all the data. As a result, the information is more "reuseable" than ordinary pictures, where the photographer has to decide what to focus on before she presses the shutter.
options: ① A Good Shortcut to Reusing Ordinary Pictures
② Why Having More Data Means More Possibilities
③ Random Sampling: The Best Method of All Time
④ The Benefits of Reducing the Size of Digital Files
⑤ How Light-Field Cameras Work in Professional Photography
explanation: 모든(혹은 거대한) 데이터세트를 가지는 것이 정보를 다각도에서 검토하고 재사용할 수 있는 자유(더 많은 가능성)를 제공한다는 내용이므로 2번 제목이 적절하다.

question: 3. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Coincidence that is statistically impossible seems to us like an irrational event, and some define it as a miracle. But, as Montaigne has said, "the origin of a miracle is in our ignorance, at the level of our knowledge of nature, and not in nature itself." ⓐGlorious miracles have been later on discovered to be obedience to the laws of nature or a technological development that was not widely known at the time. ⓑAs the German poet, Goethe, phrased it: "Things that are mysterious are not yet miracles and we simply mistake the unknown for the supernatural." ⓒMoreover, as some modern scientists have argued, it is now considered that supernatural beings directly intervene in natural events to perform miracles. ⓓThe idea of a miracle assumes an intervention of a "higher power," but such an assumption often comes from our failure to investigate the cause of an event. ⓔInstead of examining it carefully, we label it a miracle, which then becomes an excuse for those who are too lazy to think.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 초승적인 개입(기적)이라 믿었던 것이 실은 우리의 무지나 밝혀지지 않은 자연법칙일 뿐임을 주장하는 논지인데, ⓒ문장은 오히려 초자연적인 존재가 기적을 행하기 위해 개입한다고 하므로 글의 요지와 상충된다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Moral excellence, according to Aristotle, is the result of habit and repetition, though modern science would also suggest that it may have an innate, genetic component. (A) Freud suggested that we don't change our personality much after age five or thereabouts, but as in many other things, Freud was wrong. (B) Recent psychological research shows that personality traits stabilize around age thirty in both men and women, regardless of ethnicity. (C) This occurs as the human brain continues to develop, both neuroanatomically and in terms of cognitive skills, until the mid-twenties. (D) The advantage of this new understanding is that we can be a bit more optimistic than Aristotle and Freud about being able to teach moral excellence. (E)
insertion_sentence: This means that moral excellence will be broadly set early in our lives, which is why the question of how early to teach it is so important.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장은 '이것은 도덕적 탁월함이 우리 삶의 초기에 대체로 설정될 것임을 의미하며, 이것이 왜 그것을 얼마나 일찍 가르쳐야 하는지에 대한 질문이 매우 중요한가에 대한 이유이다'라는 내용입니다. 이는 첫 번째 문장에서 언급된 아리스토텔레스의 견해(습관과 반복의 결과)를 부연 설명하는 내용이므로 (A) 자리에 들어가는 것이 적절합니다. 그 뒤의 (A)부터는 프로이트의 견해와 그에 반박하는 현대 연구 결과들이 이어집니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Introverted leaders do have to overcome the strong cultural presumption that extroverts are more effective leaders. Although the population splits into almost equal parts between introverts and extroverts, more than 96 percent of managers and executives are extroverted. (A) In a study done in 2006, 65 percent of senior corporate executives viewed introversion as a barrier to leadership. (B) We must reexamine this stereotype, however, as it doesn't always hold true. question: 14. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Sylvan Goldman invented the shopping cart and introduced it in his stores in 1937. It was an excellent device that would make it easy for shoppers to buy as much as they wanted without getting tired or seeking others' help.
ordered_passages: (A) Women wouldn't touch them because the carts reminded them of baby carriages. It was only a few elderly shoppers who used them. That made the carts even less attractive to the majority of the shoppers. Then Goldman hit upon an idea. He hired several models, men and women, of different ages and asked them to wheel the carts in the store and shop.

(B) A young woman employee standing near the entrance told the regular shoppers, 'Look, everyone is using the carts. Why don't you?' That was the turning point. A few shills disguised as regular shoppers easily accomplished what logic, explanations, and advertisements failed to do. Within a few weeks shoppers readily accepted those carts.

(C) But Goldman discovered that in spite of his repeated advertisements and explanations, he could not persuade his shoppers to use the wheeled carts. Men were reluctant because they thought they would appear weak if they pushed such carts instead of carrying their shopping.
explanation: 이 글은 실반 골드먼이 쇼핑 카트를 발명한 후 이를 대중화하기 위해 겪은 과정을 설명하고 있습니다. (C)에서 발명 초기 골드먼의 광고와 설명에도 불구하고 사람들이 카트 사용을 꺼려했던 전반적인 상황이 제시됩니다. (A)에서는 남성과 여성이 각각 카트 사용을 꺼렸던 구체적인 이유(남성은 약해 보일까 봐, 여성은 유모차 같아서)를 설명하고, 이를 해결하기 위해 골드먼이 모델을 고용했다는 해결책이 나옵니다. (B)에서 모델과 직원들의 활동을 통해 사람들의 인식이 바뀌고 결국 카트가 널리 받아들여지게 되었다는 결말로 이어지는 (C)-(A)-(B) 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
passage: The size of a species is not accidental. It's a fine-tuned interaction between a species and the world it inhabits. Over large periods of time, size ⓐ<u>fluctuations</u> have often signalled significant changes in the environment. Generally speaking, over the last five hundred million years, the trend has been towards animals getting ⓑ<u>larger</u>. It's particularly notable in marine animals, whose average body size has increased 150-fold in this time. Still, we are beginning to see ⓒ<u>continuation</u> in this trend. Scientists have discovered that many animals are ⓓ<u>shrinking</u>. Around the world, species in every category have been found to be getting smaller, and one major cause appears to be the heat. Animals living in the Italian Alps, for example, have seen temperatures rise by three to four degrees Celsius since the 1980s. To avoid overheating, chamois goats now spend more of their days ⓔ<u>resting</u> rather than searching for food, and as a result, in just a few decades, the new generations of chamois are 25 percent smaller.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 글의 전반부에서는 지난 5억 년 동안 동물의 크기가 커지는 경향(larger)이 있었다고 언급하지만, 'Still(하지만)'이라는 연결어를 통해 흐름이 바뀝니다. 이후 내용에서 과학자들이 많은 동물이 작아지고(shrinking) 있다는 사실을 발견했으며 그 원인이 지구 온난화(heat) 때문이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 동물이 커지던 기존의 경향이 '지속(continuation)'되는 것이 아니라, '역전'되거나 '변화'가 나타나고 있다고 해야 문맥상 적절합니다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 Lectin에 관한 내용을 옳게 이해한 것만을 <보기>에서 모두 고른 것은?
passage: Lectins are large proteins that serve as a crucial weapon that plants use to defend themselves. The lectins in most plants bind to carbohydrates as we consume the plant. They also bind to sugar molecules found in the gut, in the brain, between nerve endings, in joints and in all bodily fluids. According to Dr. Steven Gundry, these sticky proteins can interrupt messaging between cells and cause toxic and inflammatory reactions. Brain fog is just one result of lectins interrupting communication between nerves. An upset stomach is another common symptom of lectin overload. Dr. Gundry lists a wide range of other health problems including aching joints, dementia, headaches and infertility that have been resolved in his patients once they eliminated lectins from their diets. Dr. Paul Saladino writes that the hypothesis that lectins are involved in Parkinson's disease is also gaining support, with animal studies showing that 'lectins, once eaten, may be damaging the gut and travelling to the brain, where they appear to be toxic to dopaminergic neurons'.
vocabulary_box: ⓐ Lectins are sizable proteins that plants use as a natural defense mechanism.
ⓑ Lectins attach to carbohydrates in plants but fail to interact with sugar molecules within the human body.
ⓒ Lectins can disrupt communication between cells, potentially reducing inflammatory responses in the body.
ⓓ Excessive lectin intake may cause digestive discomfort, such as an upset stomach, which is a commonly reported symptom.
ⓔ Removing lectins from one's diet not so much worsens symptoms such as headaches and infertility as helps relieve them.
ⓕ Lectins are completely harmless and unrelated to Parkinson's disease.
explanation: 지문의 내용과 보기를 대조해 보면 다음과 같습니다.ⓐ Lectins are large proteins... plants use to defend themselves와 일치하므로 옳음.ⓑ 지문에서 장, 뇌, 신경 말단 등에 있는 당 분자(sugar molecules)와 결합한다고 했으므로 상호작용하지 못한다는 내용은 틀림.ⓒ 세포 간 메시지 전달을 방해하여 염증 반응(inflammatory reactions)을 '일으킨다(cause)'고 했으므로, 줄인다는 내용은 틀림.ⓓ An upset stomach is another common symptom of lectin overload와 일치하므로 옳음.ⓔ 식단에서 렉틴을 제거했을 때 두통이나 불임 등이 해결되었다(resolved)고 했으므로, 악화시키기보다 완화시킨다는 내용은 옳음. (not so much A as B: A라기보다는 B이다)ⓕ 렉틴이 파킨슨병과 관련이 있다는 가설이 지지를 얻고 있다는 내용이 있으므로 틀림.따라서 옳은 것은 ⓐ, ⓓ, ⓔ입니다.

question: 21. 다음 글을 읽고 (A)~(F)의 각 빈칸에 알맞은 말을 <보기>에서 골라 조건에 맞게 쓰시오. [4.0점]
passage: Technology changes how individuals and societies understand the concept of privacy. The fact that someone has a new ability to access information or watch the actions of another does not justify doing so. Rather, advances in technology require citizens and policy makers to consider how privacy (A)___________ should be expanded. For example, when cameras first became available for commercial and private use, nations and citizens struggled over whether new laws should be enacted to protect (B)___________ from being photographed without their permission. The (C)___________ of privacy brought about by this new technology re-affirmed a distinction between private and public spaces. It was determined by most cultures that people automatically gave (D)___________ to being seen - and thus recorded - once they voluntarily stepped into a public space. Although some people might be uncomfortable with the (E)___________ of surveillance cameras, citizens in most cultures have adjusted to the fact that giving up the right not to be observed in these circumstances causes less (F)___________ to the community than failing to have surveillance.
subjective_conditions: (A)~(F)에 각각 하나씩 쓰되 중복되지 않게 사용할 것
형태 변화 없이 그대로 쓸 것
answer: (A): protections, (B): individuals, (C): reconsideration, (D): consent, (E): spread, (F): harm
explanation: 이 글은 기술의 발전이 사생활의 개념과 범위를 어떻게 변화시키는지 설명하고 있습니다. (A) 기술 발전으로 사생활 '보호(protections)'의 확장이 필요해졌고, (B) 허가 없이 촬영되는 '개인(individuals)'들을 보호하기 위한 법안이 논의되었습니다. (C) 이러한 기술이 가져온 사생활에 대한 '재고(reconsideration)'는 공적 공간과 사적 공간의 구분을 재확인해주었으며, (D) 공적 공간에 발을 들이는 것은 노출에 '동의(consent)'한 것으로 간주되었습니다. (E) 감시 카메라의 '확산(spread)'이 불편할 수 있으나, (F) 감시를 하지 않는 것보다 공동체에 '해(harm)'를 덜 끼친다는 결론에 도달했다는 내용입니다.

question: 22. 윗글을 읽고, (A), (B)의 각 빈칸에 알맞은 말을 <보기>에서 골라 조건에 맞게 쓰시오. [4.0점]

question: 23. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐotherwise가 글에서 의미하는 바를 조건에 맞게 쓰시오. [4.0점]

question: 11. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]

question: 13. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Statistics in the twentieth century became the systematic collection of quantitative information needed by the state. Theodore Porter described the use of statistics to create state authority as "a way of making decisions without seeming to decide", characterizing it as a "social technology" intended to build trust in authority.

question: 15. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Experiments testify to science's embrace of ignorance. Arguably the worst thing a scientist can do is to suppose they know what will happen in a given scenario without bothering to check. The rise of the experimental philosophy coincided with the liberation of curiosity as a valuable rather than a questionable attribute. For all that experimental science today is often assumed to be supported by a philosophical framework and an approved methodology ("state your hypothesis and then test it"), the fact is that, as philosopher of science Ian Hacking says, "One can conduct an experiment simply out of curiosity to see what will happen." You never know until you try.

question: 16. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Even though sea creatures live in it, they still need to take in water for their bodies to function properly. They just need to get rid of any extra salt it might bring with it. Salt absorbs water like a sponge. If you put a tiny mountain of salt on a small plate, then add enough water to the side, making sure an edge touches the salt, the salt will absorb the water. Now you have a pile of wet salt. Notice that it has increased in size. The same principle applies to sea creatures. If the body fluids in a sea animal are saltier than the seawater it lives in, then the extra salt in the creature's body will absorb seawater. This can cause them to swell up. On the other hand, if the amount of salt in the seawater is higher than the amount of salt in the body fluids of a sea animal, the extra salt in the water will draw fluids out of the creature's body, causing it to dehydrate and shrink.

options: ① converge ... evade

③ expand ... disperse
④ diffuse ... contract
⑤ intrude ... diminish
explanation: 지문에 따르면 생물의 체액 염도가 바닷물보다 높으면 물을 흡수하여 '부풀어 오르고(swell up)', 반대로 낮으면 수분을 빼앗겨 '탈수되고 쪼그라든다(dehydrate and shrink)'고 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '부풀다'라는 의미의 bloat가, (B)에는 '쪼그라들다'라는 의미의 shrivel이 적절합니다.

passage: Within liberal culture, the value of fair equality of opportunity for individuals outweighs the preservation of the family's integrity. question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Imagine pausing in the middle of a busy day, taking a moment to refresh your mind and ⓐ<u>recharge</u> your energy. This power of a midday break is often underestimated. This strategic pause is not just a break; it boosts your cognitive capabilities, ensuring your mind remains sharp and focused. Even ⓓ<u>briefly</u> experimenting with neurobic exercises can work wonders for your cognitive state during lunch. Start with using your non-dominant hand for routine tasks like writing or eating. This simple switch challenges your brain, activating pathways that aren't typically engaged and ⓔ<u>promoting</u> greater flexibility in thinking.
explanation: ⓒ 'keeping itself agile'에서 재귀대명사 'itself'는 문장의 주어인 'They(Neurobic exercises)'와 가리키는 대상이 다릅니다. 이 문맥에서 유지되는 대상은 'your brain'이므로, 단수 명사를 지칭하는 대명사 'it'으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Distinguishing moths from butterflies on outward appearance is not always easy, but there are a few rules of thumb that can help. In most butterflies the antennae end with a small club-shaped swelling, whereas in moths they are usually feathery or narrow to a fine tip. Butterflies tend to rest with their wings ⓐ<u>hold</u> shut above their body, whereas moths more usually rest with the upper sides of the wings on full view. Further distinctions can be made by looking for a tiny hook that joins fore- and hindwings, a feature only ⓑ<u>present</u> in moths. The stereotypical differences, with moths cast as the gloomy, nocturnal cousins of colourful sun-loving butterflies ⓒ<u>are</u> simply wrong. There are many brightly coloured moths and many which are active throughout the day. Equally, there are a few nocturnal butterflies and plenty ⓓ<u>that</u> come clothed in shades of brown and grey. It's more sensible to think of them together; both butterflies and moths are beautiful and ⓔ<u>fascinating</u> insects.
explanation: ⓐ 'with + 목적어 + 분사' 구문에서 목적어인 'their wings(날개)'는 '닫혀 있게 되는' 수동의 관계에 있습니다. 따라서 동사원형 'hold'가 아닌 과거분사 'held'를 사용하는 것이 어법상 옳습니다.

question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When your hand is hanging at your side and then you lift it, opposing muscles on your upper arm shorten and lengthen - contract and relax - to bend the elbow. Biceps contract, and triceps relax. Reversing the motion, when you drop your hand back down, muscles reverse roles.
ordered_passages: (A) Some people are stronger or more muscular than others; is the difference inborn, or does it depend on what people do? To the latter question: What do you do? Do you have to lift weights, or is walking enough exercise? Should you move fast or slowly? Lift heavy weights or lighter ones? Put like that, basic questions about muscle may sound like they have one right answer.

(B) Triceps contract, and biceps relax. Lift your hand or drop it, and muscle shows what it is: a system of coordination, managed by orchestrated tension. As arms and legs rotate around joints, muscles activate and deactivate, contract and relax. All physical activity is paradoxical, in this sense.

(C) Oppositions can polarize. But where muscle is concerned, few oppositions are true polarities. Look closely, and most prove to be paradoxes. Born and made, heavy and light, fast and slow: Those opposites actually require each other.

(D) That is to say, movement depends on what muscles don't do, as much as it depends on what they do. Both are necessary, each in its time - and the same is true of each side of the pairs of concepts shaping how we talk of muscles. Start with nature versus nurture:
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 팔을 굽히고 펴는 과정에서 이두근과 삼두근의 수축과 이완이라는 상반된 작용을 설명하고 있습니다. (B)에서는 삼두근이 수축하고 이두근이 이완되는 반대 상황을 설명하며 근육이 '조정 시스템'임을 정의합니다. (D)에서 근육의 작용은 하지 않는 것(이완)만큼 하는 것(수축)에도 의존한다는 역설을 언급하며 타고난 것과 길러진 것의 대립(nature versus nurture)으로 화제를 전환합니다. (A)에서는 근육의 차이가 선천적인지 후천적인지에 대한 질문들을 던지며 정답이 하나인 것처럼 들릴 수 있다고 언급합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 이러한 대립항들이 실제로는 서로를 필요로 하는 역설임을 결론지으며 글을 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 22. 다음 주어진 문장의 내용을 반대로 가정하여 영작하시오. 단, 반드시 주어진 <조건>에 맞추어 영작하시오.
passage: Because Einstein's theory was able to explain the many successes of Newton's theory equally well, it gained acceptance.
subjective_conditions: 접속사 'if'로 시작할 것
20단어 이상 ~ 25단어 이하로 영작할 것
answer: If Einstein's theory(it) had not been able to explain the many successes of Newton's theory equally well, Einstein's theory(it) would not have gained acceptance
explanation: 주어진 문장은 과거의 사실(에인슈타인의 이론이 뉴턴 이론의 성과를 잘 설명했기 때문에 수용되었다)을 나타내고 있습니다. 이를 반대로 가정하기 위해서는 '가정법 과거완료' 구문(If + 주어 + had p.p., 주어 + 조동사과거 + have p.p.)을 사용해야 합니다. 긍정은 부정으로, 부정은 긍정으로 바꾸어 영작하며 단어 수 조건을 충족시켜야 합니다.

question: 25. 다음 우리말을 영작하시오. 단, 반드시 주어진 <조건>에 맞추어 영작하시오.
passage: 유리가 권력 역학 관계의 조용한 집행자로서 역할을 하면서, 바로 그 건축물이 사회적 행동을 명령(지배)했다.

question: 8. 다음 ⓐ~ⓔ 문장 중, 어법상 올바른 것은? [2.9점]
passage: All human cultures mark the passing of time by the differences they observe in the world around them. ⓐOur choice of which differences to mark depends firstly on what we can observe and secondly on what is important in our lives. ⓑHow we mark the differences ─ the shapes of our calendars and our rituals ─ depend on the connections we make between those two things. ⓒIn the agricultural society of pre-modern Europe, which higher latitudes make the seasons easily observable, it was natural to monitor the solar cycle. ⓓConversely, among the largely nomadic peoples of Arabia, for them seasonal changes were less significant, the lunar calendar was a more sensible choice. ⓔThat did not make it inevitable which Islam would use a lunar calendar and Roman Christianity a solar one. ② ⑁

question: 14. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: According to Einstein's theory, a large mass like the Sun 'bends' space-time. Newton's theory makes no such prediction.
ordered_passages: (A) The stars around the Sun appeared to have moved from their normal positions in the night sky. The shift was much larger than Newton's theory predicted, but exactly in the positions predicted by Einstein's theory.

question: 15. 다음 글의 내용을 바탕으로 글의 의미를 제대로 이해한 학생을 있는 대로 고른 것은? [3.2점]
passage: The term "anchoring" was introduced by Roland Barthes who observed that text is often used next to images (his focus was on photographs) to confine meaning. Of all possible literal or implied interpretations an image could elicit, text would point the viewer towards a desired, specific direction.In advertising, as Barthes argues, the symbolic message does not guide identification but interpretation. The viewer is not asked to recognize what they see but to understand why they see it and what it means to them. By combining images with text, advertising produces symbolic meaning that is accurate and specific on the one hand, richer on the other, thus adding depth and eliminating breadth of rational and emotional interpretations. The headline or tagline of an ad directs the reader through the intended meanings of the image, so that the reader avoids some and receives others. It "remote-controls" the reader towards a meaning chosen in advance.
options: ① Jisoo, Yuna
② Jisoo, Hyeon
③ Minho, Hyeon
④ Jisoo, Minho, Hyeon
⑤ Jisoo, Minho, Hyeon, Yuna
explanation: Jisoo는 텍스트가 이미지 해석을 돕는다는 점을, Minho는 텍스트가 특정 의미로 안내하는 '정박(anchoring)' 효과를, Hyeon은 헤드라인이 의미를 명확하게 하면서도 해석의 다양성을 줄인다는 점을 정확히 이해하고 있습니다. 반면 Yuna는 텍스트가 대상의 이름을 명명하는 문자적 역할만 한다거나, 광고가 제한 없는 자유로운 해석을 원한다고 한 부분에서 글의 핵심 내용(의도된 의미로 유도함)과 어긋납니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: We're naturally wired to organize the world into a hierarchy. We do this to help make sense of the world, ⓐ<u>keep</u> our beliefs, and generally feel better. But when someone infringes on our place in the world and our understanding of how it works, we react without thinking. When someone cuts you off on the highway and road rage kicks in, that's your ⓑ<u>rational</u> mind saying, "Who are you to cut me off?" You're reacting to a threat to your ⓒ<u>innate</u> sense of hierarchy. On the road we are all equals. We're all supposed to play by the same rules. Cutting someone off violates those rules and implies ⓓ<u>superior</u> status. Or consider when you get frustrated with your kids and end an argument with "Because I said so." (Or the office equivalent: "Because I'm the boss.") In these moments you've stopped thinking and ⓔ<u>regressed</u> to your biological tendencies of reaffirming the hierarchy.
explanation: 도로에서 누군가 끼어들 때 발생하는 보복 운전(road rage)은 이성적인 사고가 아니라 본능적이고 감정적인 반응입니다. 따라서 rational(이성적인)은 맥락상 어색하며, primitive(원시적인)나 emotional(감정적인)과 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

question: 17. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.7점]
passage: Paradoxically, it's uncertainty that makes us feel most alive. question: 20. 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
passage: Technology changes how individuals and societies understand the concept of privacy. The fact that someone has a new ability to access information or ⓐ<u>watching</u> the actions of another does not justify doing so. Rather, advances in technology require citizens and policy makers ⓑ<u>to consider</u> how privacy protections should be expanded. The reconsideration of privacy ⓒ<u>brought</u> about by this new technology re-affirmed a distinction between private and public spaces. question: 21. 다음 글의 맥락상 밑줄 친 this crosses a line의 구체적 의미를 가장 적절히 설명한 것은?
passage: In response to human-like care robots, critics might charge that human-robot interactions create moral hazards for dementia patients. Even if deception is sometimes allowed when it serves worthy goals, should it be allowed for vulnerable users? Just as children on the autism spectrum with robot companions might be easily fooled into thinking of robots as friends, older adults with cognitive deficits might be. According to Alexis Elder, a professor at UMD, robots are false friends, inferior to true friendship. Reasoning along similar lines, John Sullins, a professor at Sonoma State University, holds that robots should "remain iconic or cartoonish so that they are easily distinguished as synthetic even by unsophisticated users." At least then no one is fooled. Making robots clearly fake also avoids the so-called "uncanny valley," where robots are perceived as scary because they so closely resemble us, but not quite. Other critics of robot deception argue that when care recipients are deceived into thinking that robots care, <u>this crosses a line</u> and violates human dignity.*dementia: 치매 **autism: 자폐성
options: ① It implies that the robot's functionality has gone beyond its programmed limits, causing unintended harm to the patient.
② It means that the cost of developing and maintaining the robots exceeds the financial benefit provided to the care recipients.
③ It refers to the moment when the robot's appearance falls into the "uncanny valley," making it scary rather than comforting.
④ It suggests that the robot has become too realistic, making it difficult for caregivers to distinguish it from actual human friends.
⑤ It refers to the action of manipulating the emotional trust of individuals with cognitive deficits by substituting manufactured engagement for genuine human presence.
explanation: 본문에서 'this crosses a line'은 돌봄 대상자가 로봇이 자신을 돌본다고(아낀다고) 믿게끔 속이는 것이 인간의 존엄성을 훼손하고 도덕적 선을 넘는 행위라는 의미입니다. 즉, 진정한 인간의 존재 대신 제작된 관계(로봇)를 대체함으로써 인지적 결함이 있는 사람들의 감정적 신뢰를 조종하는 행위를 뜻하므로 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 로봇의 기능이 프로그래밍된 한계를 벗어나 환자에게 의도치 않은 해를 끼쳤음을 암시한다.
② 로봇 개발 및 유지 비용이 돌봄 수혜자에게 제공되는 재정적 이익을 초과함을 의미한다.
③ 로봇의 외형이 '불쾌한 골짜기'에 빠져 위안을 주기보다 무섭게 느껴지는 순간을 지칭한다.
④ 로봇이 너무 사실적으로 변해 간병인들이 실제 인간 친구와 로봇을 구별하기 어렵게 되었음을 시사한다.
⑤ 진정한 인간의 존재 대신 제조된 관여를 대체함으로써 인지적 결함이 있는 개인의 정서적 신뢰를 조종하는 행위를 지칭한다.

question: 23. 윗글의 빈칸 (1)~(3)에 들어갈 내용을 (A)와 (B)에서 각각 고른 후 서로 연결하여 작성하시오.

question: 26. 다음 밑줄 친 (A), (B)의 문법적 오류를 각각 수정하고, 밑줄 전체를 바르게 작성하시오.
passage: Lectins are large proteins that serve as a crucial weapon that plants use to defend themselves. The lectins in most plants bind to carbohydrates as we consume the plant. (A)<u>They also bind to sugar molecules that found in the gut</u>, in the brain, between nerve endings, in joints and in all bodily fluids. According to Dr. Steven Gundry, these sticky proteins can interrupt messaging between cells and cause toxic and inflammatory reactions. Brain fog is just one result of lectins interrupting communication between nerves. An upset stomach is another common symptom of lectin overload. Dr. Gundry lists a wide range of other health problems including aching joints, dementia, headaches and infertility that have been resolved in his patients once they eliminated lectins from their diets. Dr. Paul Saladino writes (B)<u>that the hypothesis which lectins are involved in Parkinson's disease are also gaining support</u>, with animal studies showing that 'lectins, once eaten, may be damaging the gut and travelling to the brain, where they appear to be toxic to dopaminergic neurons'.
answer: (A): They also bind to sugar molecules found in the gut(B): that the hypothesis that lectins are involved in Parkinson's disease is also gaining support
explanation: (A) 'sugar molecules'가 장에서 발견되는 것이므로 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 'found'가 수식해야 하거나, 주격 관계대명사와 be동사가 포함된 'that are found'로 고쳐야 합니다. 원문상 'that found'는 틀린 표현입니다.(B) 'the hypothesis'와 뒤의 절은 동격의 관계이므로 관계대명사 'which'가 아닌 동격의 접속사 'that'을 써야 하며, 주어인 'the hypothesis'가 단수이므로 동사 'are'를 'is'로 일치시켜야 합니다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 내용과 가장 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Just as an expert in the taste and colour of wine will gain much by being aware of the chemistry that underlies those qualities, so each perspective on the body can potentially enhance the others. And yet every scientific tool, from microscopes to mathematics, and every aspect of the body, from the brain to the microorganism, requires such depth of expertise that this tends not to happen: we tend to study the human body in silos, each community sectioned from the others by its own specialised vocabulary. Research communities may be dedicated to one type of scientific tool or a specific component of the body, such as one type of cell. How different types of cell communicate with one another becomes its own specialist topic. Even simple forms of life on Earth are now rarely studied as a whole, and the human body is evidently much more complex. As long ago as 1890, The Times newspaper commented that knowledge 'had already become too vast to be manageable'. Today, nobody is an expert in the whole of anything.*in silos: 개별적으로 분리해서
options: ① The vast growth of knowledge has made it difficult for any single individual to master an entire field.
② The author believes that with sufficient dedication, it is still possible for researchers to become experts in the entirety of human body.
③ Different scientific perspectives on the human body can complement one another and deepen our understanding.
④ Even relatively simple organisms are no longer commonly studied as integrated wholes in modern scientific research.
⑤ Increasing specialization in scientific fields has led to fragmented research communities with limited cross-disciplinary interaction.
explanation: 지문 후반부에서 "Today, nobody is an expert in the whole of anything."라고 명시하고 있으며, 인체가 매우 복잡하고 지식이 방대하여 어느 한 분야의 전체를 마스터하는 것은 불가능하다고 하고 있으뭀로 ②번은 지문의 내용감 반대됩니다.
options_translation: ① 방대한 지식의 성장은 어떤 한 개인이 한 분야 전체를 마스터하는 것을 어렵감 만들었다.
② 저자는 충분한 헌신이 있다면 연구자들이 인체 전체에 대한 전문가가 되는 것이 여전히 가능하다고 믿다.
③ 인체에 대한 서로 다른 과학적 관점들은 서로를 밴판하고 우리의 이해를 깊감 할 수 있다.
④ 홄대 과학 연구에서 상대적으로 단순한 생물체조차 더 이상 통합된 전체로서 일반적으로 연구되준 않다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ에 관한 설명으로 문직상 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Historically, palaces weren't just homes; they were carefully constructed stages designed to impress and intimidate. While stone symbolized permanence and strength, glass offered something equally powerful: visibility. The introduction of large windows in palaces allowed rulers to literally look down upon their subjects, emphasizing their elevated position. Conversely, it also allowed subjects to gaze up at their leaders, creating a sense of awe and distance. Consider the Palace of Versailles: its Hall of Mirrors, lined with reflective surfaces, not only magnified the grandeur of the space but also placed the king at the center of a dazzling display, reinforcing his absolute authority. The use of glass in palaces wasn't merely aesthetic; it was strategic. Open sightlines allowed for better surveillance and control, ensuring the safety and security of the ruling family. Courtiers and visitors were constantly aware of being observed, contributing to an atmosphere of careful obedience and respect. The very architecture dictated social behavior, with ⓐ<u>glass</u> acting as a silent enforcer of the power dynamic.*surveillance: 감시 **courtier: 신하
options: ① It symbolized transparency in governance by allowing subjects and rulers to observe each other on equal terms.
② It enhanced the aesthetic balance of heavy stone structures by adding visual lightness and harmony.
③ It reduced the need for physical barriers in palaces by providing natural protection against potential intruders.

② 시각적 가벼움과 화합을 더함으로써 무거운 석조 구조물의 미적 균형을 향상시킴다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.3점]
passage: Waste has historically been seen as a necessary driver of the economy. Sales are tied to the amount of a product supplied, which is directly dependent on the demand for that product. Therefore, if you design the product to eventually be wasted, you can ensure that the demand for more products will be ⓐ<u>maintained</u>. Many strategies have been incorporated into product design and use to ensure that waste is ⓑ<u>inevitable</u>, such as planned obsolescence, limited access to tools for repairs, and use of cheap materials. All these strategies ensure that the consumer will have limited access to the product in use and will eventually require a ⓒ<u>replacement</u>. Those who supported the idea that waste is necessary to drive demand failed to realize that ⓓ<u>neglecting</u> the elimination of waste via repair and remanufacturing creates a different kind of demand: products as a service. Through this setup, companies simply lease out products that were once sold directly to the customer. With this ⓔ<u>transition</u> of ownership, companies maintain profit by offering maintenance and repair services and are encouraged to develop long-lasting products.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 글의 흐름상 폐기물을 없애는 것(elimination of waste)이 새로운 형태의 수요(서비스로서의 제품)를 창출한다는 내용이 이어지므로, 폐기물 제거를 '방치'하는 것이 아니라 '추구'하거나 '우선시'하는 맥락이 되어야 합니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 neglecting은 문맥상 어색합니다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Viewing time as a purchasable and consistent product cemented artificial views on time into our psyche, but every now and again we are forced to acknowledge this mistake. On twenty-six occasions in the last fifty years, a second has been added to everyone's day to adjust for the Earth wobbling and the rate of its spin changing. For instance, when El Niño, a climatic system in the Pacific, causes wind speed to change dramatically, it can slow the rotation of the Earth slightly. Indeed, the Earth's spin is generally slowing because the moon's gravity is acting as a drag, so days are getting longer by about 1.7 milliseconds per century. Such events disturb the similarity between man-made time and more flexible time based on the Earth's naturally occurring rotation. When events like this happen, a bunch of humans make the decision to add a small slice of time to your day, without your knowledge. We try to force our fixed, man-made view of time on to nature in the false hope that it will yield. It doesn't.

③ When Time Doesn't Obey the Clock
④ Earth's Spin: Controlling Time
⑤ The Pacific Climate That Controls Our Seconds

passage: All human cultures mark the passing of time by the differences they observe in the world around them. How we mark the differences ─ the shapes of our calendars and our rituals ─ depends on the connections we make between those two things. question: 15. 윗글의 공감을 비판하는 사람들의 주장에 관한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [25년 9월 30번]
passage: Although empathy is widely praised by scholars and public figures, not everyone is an empathy booster. Critics of empathy argue that empathy will not save us from interpersonal and intergroup conflict. (A)________, they argue, empathy makes such conflicts worse. These critics maintain that empathy can be exhausting and lead to burnout or insensitivity to suffering. They argue that we tend to empathize strongly with our in-group and resist empathizing with out-groups, and even enjoy the suffering of out-groups in competitive or threatening contexts. (B)________, the prescription for more empathy is often counterproductive in cases of conflict. Empathy, they argue, can further encourage conflict and force us into an us vs. them mentality. Finally, even when we try to empathize with others who are dissimilar from us or in unfamiliar contexts, sometimes we are unable to accurately empathize with their experiences, causing further misunderstandings and frustration. Critics of empathy argue that we should give up on empathy and employ other tools in pursuit of social harmony, e.g., rational compassion or moral emotions like fear, anger, and shame.
options: ① 공감은 사람 간과 집단 간 갈등으로부터 우리를 구해주지 않는다.
② 공감은 피로와 고통에 대한 무감각을 초래할 수 있다.
③ 우리는 경쟁적이거나 위협적인 상황에서 내집단의 고통을 즐기는 경향이 있다.
④ 낯선 상황에 있는 사람에게 공감하려고 노력해도, 우리는 종종 정확하게 공감하지 못한다.
⑤ 우리는 공감을 포기하고 사회적 조화를 얻기 위해 다른 도구를 이용해야 한다.
explanation: 본문은 우리가 경쟁적이거나 위협적인 상황에서 '외집단(out-groups)'의 고통을 즐기는 경향이 있다고 설명합니다. ③번은 '내집단'의 고통이라고 기술했으므로 일치하지 않습니다.

passage: A great strength of the market mechanism is that there are ⓐ<u>incentive</u>s for individuals to reveal their knowledge through their behavior. This stands in contrast to many strategic situations ─ for example, in political negotiations ─ in which it is wise not to let the other side know what one's true ⓑ<u>preference</u>s or production capacities are. If prices are not sticky ─ as many models assume ─ individuals ⓒ<u>adapt</u> their behavior instantaneously, whenever their preferences or the circumstances change. If they have motivational problems, for example, falling into ⓓ<u>denial</u> about the fact that there is no demand for their products, markets ⓔ<u>reveal</u> to them, sometimes in quite brutal ways, that they better accept this fact.
