question: 24. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Dictionary definitions are constantly revised to keep up with our changing uses and knowledge. In Roman times, "addicts" were people who were unable to pay their debts and gave themselves as slaves to their creditors.
ordered_passages: (A) Centuries later, the word lost its negative connotation and a musical named Guys and Dolls ran on Broadway. A hundred years from now, your great-grandchildren's way of speaking would likely puzzle you, since language constantly evolves as a reflection of human creativity.

(B) A further example of such semantic change appears in the history of "guy." On November 5th, 1605, Guy Fawkes tried to blow up the British Parliament. He was captured and put to death. Loyalists burned his effigy, which they nicknamed the "guy."

(C) The word eventually came to be associated with drug dependency: one becomes a slave to one's addiction. The word "husband" originally referred to being a homeowner; it had nothing to do with being married. But because owning your own property made it more likely you'd find a mate, the word eventually came to mean a male who has been wed.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 'addicts'의 로마 시대 의미를 언급한 후, (C)에서 이 단어가 어떻게 약물 의존과 연관되었는지 설명하고 'husband'의 사례를 추가합니다. (B)에서 'guy'라는 단어의 유래에 대한 또 다른 사례를 들고, 마지막으로 (A)에서 'guy'의 긍정적 변화와 언어의 지속적인 진화에 대한 결론을 내리는 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

question: 26. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Once a nail is hammered in, it is friction that holds it in place. Friction is the force that arises when two surfaces are sliding, or trying to slide, against each other. ⓐIf you try to pull apart two blocks of wood that have been nailed together, the wood fibers grip the shaft of the nail. ⓑThe nail feels a force trying to rip it apart along its length, and we call that force tension. ⓒYour experiment can now fail in one of two ways ─ either the nail stretches and splits in half because the tension force is too large for the nail, or the nail comes loose because the friction force is overcome. ⓓHowever, in such cases, it's often more practical to consider an alternative instead. ⓔThe force it would take to stretch the nail is much larger than the friction forces on the surface, so we don't have to worry too much about the former.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 못이 박혀 있을 때 작용하는 마찰력과 장력(tension)의 관계, 그리고 못이 빠지거나 부러지는 원리에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ⓓ는 '대안을 고려하는 것이 더 실용적이다'라는 내용으로, 물리적 힘의 작용 원리를 설명하는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

question: 22. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world. Simply put, the brain is not designed to sense on its own. For instance, an exposed brain would neither sense light shining on it nor feel something touching it. In fact. patients are often kept awake during brain surgery, which can help a surgeon isolate specific regions of the brain. The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle recognized this characteristic of the brain over 2000 years ago when he said, "<u>Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses</u>." This concept can be seen clearly when volunteers are blind-folded and placed in the warm water of a sensory deprivation tank. They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as incoherent thought patterns. From these experiments and others, it is apparent that we need constant input from our senses to carry out functions that give us personality and intellect.
options: ① Human intellect depends on sensory input.
② The brain can sense things independently.
③ The mind is more powerful than the senses.
④ Sensory deprivation has no effect on the brain.
⑤ Hallucinations are unrelated to sensory experience.
explanation: 밑줄 친 문장은 '감각을 통하지 않고는 마음속에 아무것도 존재하지 않는다'는 뜻으로, 모든 지적 활동이나 사고의 근원이 감각적 입력에 의존한다는 의미입니다. 지문의 마지막 문장인 '우리가 인격과 지성을 갖게 해주는 기능을 수행하기 위해 감각으로부터의 지속적인 입력이 필요하다'는 부분과 일치하므로 ①번 '인간의 지성은 감각적 입력에 의존한다'가 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 인간의 지성은 감각적 입력에 의존한다.
② 뇌는 독립적으로 사물을 감지할 수 있다.
③ 마음은 감각보다 더 강력하다.
④ 감각 차단은 뇌에 아무런 영향을 미치지 않는다.
⑤ 환각은 감각적 경험과 관련이 없다.

question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고, 한 칸에 한 단어씩 적어 요약문을 완성하고자 한다. 알맞은 단어를 찾아 빈칸을 채우시오. 단, 필요시 어형을 변화시킬 수 있음. 단어 중복 사용 불가.
passage: Those who run the government are always tempted to create more money and spend it when they hold the authority to produce money. From ancient kings to modern politicians, this tendency has repeatedly appeared over the centuries, leading to inflation and the various problems that follow from inflation, economically and socially. To avoid such problems, many countries have chosen to use some inherently limited resource like silver or gold as money. This prevents governments from expanding the money supply excessively. In particular, gold has long been considered suitable for this purpose, because its supply in the world usually cannot be increased rapidly. When the individual converts paper money into gold, then the money is said to be guaranteed by gold. This expression is misleading if it is understood to mean that the value of the gold is directly transferred to the paper money. In fact, the gold plays significant role in restricting how much paper money can be issued.
summary_sentence: To prevent (A)__________ caused by governments creating (B)__________ paper money, many countries use (C)__________ resources like gold as money in order to (D)__________ the supply of currency, because gold's supply cannot be increased rapidly.
subjective_conditions: 한 칸에 한 단어씩 적을 것
필요시 어형을 변화시킬 수 있음
단어 중복 사용 불가
explanation: 이 글은 정부가 화폐 발행 권한을 가졌을 때 화폐를 과도하게 발행하여 인플레이션을 유발하는 경향을 설명하며, 이를 방지하기 위해 금과 같이 공급이 제한된 자원을 화폐로 사용하여 화폐 공급을 제한한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 요약문의 흐름에 따라 (A) 정부가 과도한 화폐를 발행하여 발생하는 '인플레이션(inflation)', (B) 정부가 '과도한(excessive)' 지폐를 만드는 것, (C) 금과 같은 '제한된(limited)' 자원 사용, (D) 통화 공급을 '제한하기(restrict)' 위해 라는 구성이 적절합니다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 어휘의 쓰임이 옳지 않은 것은?
passage: The study of emotions and decision making has become highly significant. One important stream of research examines people with brain damage to see whether the damage in specific parts of the brain, related to a particular cognitive functions, ⓐ<u>disturbs</u> decision making. One example of this research is the work of Antonio Damasio, who finds that the damage to the emotional part of the brain actually ⓑ<u>decreases</u> the efficacy of decision making. He recognizes that good decision is a product of the cooperation work between the emotional part and the deliberative part of the brain. This contradicts the conventional economic opinion that decision making should be generated in a ⓒ<u>rational</u> fashion, and that affective decisions are considered ⓓ<u>desirable</u>. The evidence indicates that emotions actually play an a ⓔ<u>beneficial</u> role in effective decision making.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 의사결정에 있어 감정의 중요성을 다루고 있습니다. 기존의 경제학적 통념은 의사결정이 이성적인 방식으로 이루어져야 하며 감정적인 결정은 '바람직하지 않게(undesirable)' 여겨진다는 내용이 문맥상 적절합니다. 하지만 지문에서는 'desirable(바람직한)'이라고 표현했으므로 ⓓ가 잘못되었습니다. 이어지는 문장에서 감정이 실제로 유익한(beneficial) 역할을 한다고 언급하며 기존 통념과 반대되는 증거를 제시하고 있습니다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Mirror neurons are the hardware of empathy, and so what would make more sense than to look and see which animals possess these cells? And this is exactly where modern research now stands: all researchers know so far is that apes possess mirror neurons. We still need to test to see which other species are like us in this respect. Scientists often publicly speculate that we can probably expect surprises here, too. They assume that all animals that live in herds or large groups possess similar brain mechanisms, because social units function only if individuals can see things from the perspective of others in the group and feel what they are feeling. I can see a goldfish waving its fin at us. As an animal that travels around in a tightly-knit group, it's on board with this idea - or at least swimming alongside the boat.
options: ① functions of social units in animal groups
② the link between empathy and mirror neurons in animals
③ reasons apes are the only species with mirror neurons
④ examples of communication among herd-dwelling species
⑤ scientists' misunderstanding of animal brain mechanisms
explanation: 이 글은 거울 뉴런(mirror neurons)이 공감(empathy)의 하드웨어라는 점을 언급하며, 인간 외의 다른 동물들(특히 유인원 및 무리 지어 사는 동물들)이 이러한 뇌 기제를 가지고 있는지를 탐구하는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 타인의 관점에서 사물을 보고 느끼는 능력(공감)이 사회적 단위가 기능하는 필수 조건이며, 이것이 거울 뉴런과 연결되어 있음을 설명하므로 동물의 공감과 거울 뉴런 사이의 연결고리가 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 동물 집단 내 사회적 단위의 기능들
② 동물들에게서 나타나는 공감과 거울 뉴런 사이의 연관성
③ 유인원이 거울 뉴런을 가진 유일한 종인 이유들
④ 무리 지어 사는 종들 사이의 의사소통 사례들
⑤ 동물의 뇌 기제에 대한 과학자들의 오해

question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Mother cats can tell which kittens belong to them - when litters are mixed up they use their kittens' scent to ⓐ<u>discern</u> them from offspring of other mothers. Despite this, when faced with a selection of kittens who have wandered from the nest, her own and others that aren't hers, a mother cat appears to ⓑ<u>favor</u> her own offspring when retrieving them. The reason for this is uncertain, although distress vocalizations from kittens that are lost from their nest are known to be very ⓒ<u>forceful</u>, so it may just be easy for the mother to ⓓ<u>accept</u> retrieving them, regardless of whether they are hers. In the wild, a squeaking kitten out in the open is likely to attract predators, which is bad news for any other kittens around it. A rapid ⓔ<u>retrieval</u> of any crying kitten would be a good strategy to prevent them from drawing unwanted attention.
explanation: 지문의 흐름상 어미 고양이가 자기 새끼와 남의 새끼가 섞여 있을 때 자기 새끼를 '선호(favor)'하기보다는, 새끼의 울음소리가 매우 강렬하기 때문에 자기 새끼인지 여부와 상관없이 울고 있는 새끼를 데려오는 경향이 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 ②의 favor를 '구별하지 못하다' 또는 '무시하다'는 의미인 fail to discriminate 등으로 바꾸는 것이 문맥상 적절합니다.

question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers of which it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease to form, while sufficient fibers remain undamaged for the material not to crack and fall apart.
ordered_passages: (A) Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, in which case it lacks the rigidity required of a good wrapping material. So it is its ability to hold a crease while remaining stiff that makes paper uniquely suited to this purpose.

(B) Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to resist being pulled apart, but it can also be torn easily and accurately along the crease if a point of weakness - a small, initial tear - is opened up.

(C) This winning combination of mechanical properties allows it to assume the shape of any object through creasing and folding - hence the art of origami. There are very few materials as good: metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 종이의 기계적 특성(섬유질이 일부 부러지며 영구적인 주름이 형성됨)을 설명합니다. (B)의 'in this state'는 주어진 문장에서 설명한 주름이 잡힌 상태를 가리키며, 이 상태에서도 인장 강도를 유지하지만 쉽게 찢어질 수도 있다는 특징을 추가합니다. (C)에서는 이러한 특성들의 조합이 종이접기(origami)를 가능하게 하며 금속 박판과 비교하여 종이의 우수성을 언급합니다. (A)에서는 플라스틱 시트와 비교하며 뻣뻣함을 유지하면서도 주름을 유지하는 종이만의 독특한 적합성을 강조하며 결론을 짓습니다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A great strength of the market mechanism is that there are incentives for individuals to reveal their knowledge through their behavior. This stands in contrast to many strategic situations - for example, in political negotiations - in which it is wise not to let the other side know what one's true preferences or production capacities are. A perfectly competitive market that clears on the spot leaves no room for such strategies. If prices are not sticky - as many models assume - individuals adapt their behavior instantaneously, whenever their preferences or the circumstances change. They stop buying items that do not satisfy their needs and stop selling items that do not provide them with optimal gains, maybe switching to the production of other items. If they have motivational problems, for example, falling into denial about the fact that there is no demand for their products, markets reveal to them, sometimes in quite brutal ways, that they better accept this fact.
options: ① effect of fixed prices on market strategies
② benefit of markets in adjusting through signals
③ role of needs and profits in buying and selling
④ importance of hiding real goals in political talks
⑤ problem of denial when products have no demand
explanation: 이 글은 시장 메커니즘의 강점이 개인들이 자신의 지식과 선호도를 행동(구매나 판매의 중단 등)을 통해 드러내게 한다는 점에 있다고 설명합니다. 정치적 협상과 달리 시장에서는 정보를 숨길 여지가 없으며, 가격 신호를 통해 개인들이 변화하는 환경에 즉각적으로 적응하게 해준다는 것이 핵심 내용입니다. 따라서 '신호를 통한 조정에 있어서의 시장의 이점'이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 시장 전략에 미치는 고정 가격의 영향
② 신호를 통해 조정하는 데 있어 시장의 이점
③ 매매에 있어서 필요와 이익의 역할
④ 정치적 회담에서 실제 목표를 숨기는 것의 중요성
⑤ 제품에 대한 수요가 없을 때 부정(denial)의 문제

question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Although empathy is widely praised by scholars and public figures, not everyone is an empathy booster. Critics of empathy argue that empathy will not save us from interpersonal and intergroup conflict. In fact, they argue, empathy makes such conflicts worse. These critics maintain that empathy can be exhausting and lead to burnout or insensitivity to suffering. They argue that we tend to empathize strongly with our in-group and resist empathizing with out-groups, and even enjoy the suffering of out-groups in competitive or threatening contexts. Thus, the prescription for more empathy is often counterproductive in cases of conflict. Empathy, they argue, can further encourage conflict and force us into an us vs. them mentality. Finally, even when we try to empathize with others who are dissimilar from us or in unfamiliar contexts, sometimes we are unable to accurately empathize with their experiences, causing further misunderstandings and frustration. Critics of empathy argue that ____________________________________________.
options: ① we should not give up empathy but employ it as the main path to harmony
② we must extend empathy equally across groups to reduce conflict
③ we must assume empathy invariably guarantees concord in society
④ we should turn from empathy and adopt other ways for peace
⑤ we need to rely on empathy even in competitive situations
explanation: 지문은 공감(empathy)에 대한 비판적인 시각을 다루고 있습니다. 공감이 오히려 집단 간 갈등을 심화시키고, 우리와 그들이라는 이분법적 사고를 강화하며, 서로 다른 맥락에 있는 사람들에 대한 오해를 불러일으킬 수 있다고 설명합니다. 따라서 공감의 비판자들은 공감이 아닌 평화를 위한 다른 방법을 택해야 한다고 주장하는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리는 공감을 포기해서는 안 되며 그것을 화합의 주요 경로로 사용해야 한다
② 우리는 갈등을 줄이기 위해 집단 간에 공감을 동등하게 확장해야 한다
③ 우리는 공감이 변함없이 사회의 화합을 보장한다고 가정해야 한다
④ 우리는 공감에서 벗어나 평화를 위한 다른 방법들을 채택해야 한다
⑤ 우리는 경쟁적인 상황에서도 공감에 의존할 필요가 있다

question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: We're naturally wired to organize the world into a hierarchy. We do this to help make sense of the world, maintain our beliefs, and generally feel better. But when someone infringes on our place in the world and our understanding of how it works, we react without thinking. When someone cuts you off on the highway and road rage kicks in, that's your unconscious mind saying, "Who are you to cut me off?" On the road, we are all equals. We're all supposed to play by the same rules. Cutting someone off violates those rules and implies higher status. Or consider when you get frustrated with your kids and end an argument with "Because I said so." (Or the office equivalent: "Because I'm the boss.") In these moments you've stopped thinking and are ______________________________________.
options: ① ignoring any feelings about order and authority
② acting kindly to reduce tension in social situations
③ responding to rules that always keep everyone equal
④ reacting to a challenge to your built-in sense of rank
⑤ accepting that hierarchy plays no role in human behavior
explanation: 인간은 세상을 위계질서로 정리하려는 본능이 있으며, 누군가 우리의 위치나 규칙을 침해할 때 무의식적으로 반응하게 된다는 내용입니다. 고속도로에서 끼어들기를 당했을 때 화가 나거나, 자녀나 부하 직원에게 위계를 강조하며 논쟁을 끝내는 행위는 자신의 서열 의식에 대한 도전에 반응하는 것입니다.
options_translation: ① 질서와 권위에 대한 어떤 감정도 무시하고 있다
② 사회적 상황에서 긴장을 줄이기 위해 친절하게 행동하고 있다
③ 모든 사람을 항상 평등하게 유지하는 규칙에 응답하고 있다
④ 당신의 내재된 서열 의식에 대한 도전에 반응하고 있다
⑤ 계층 구조가 인간 행동에 아무런 역할을 하지 않는다는 점을 받아들이고 있다

question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Dictionary definitions are constantly revised to keep up with our changing uses and knowledge. In Roman times, "addicts" were people who were unable to pay their debts and gave themselves as slaves to their creditors. The word eventually came to be associated with drug dependency: one becomes a slave to one's addiction. The word "husband" originally referred to being a homeowner; it had nothing to do with being married. But because owning your own property made it more likely you'd find a mate, the word eventually came to mean a male who has been wed. On November 5th, 1605, Guy Fawkes tried to blow up the British Parliament. He was captured and put to death. Loyalists burned his effigy, which they nicknamed the "guy." Centuries later, the word lost its negative connotation and a musical named Guys and Dolls ran on Broadway. In American slang, bad means good, cool means great, and wicked means excellent. If you could transport yourself one hundred years into the future, you'd find yourself confused by your great-grandchildren's speech because language itself is an ever-changing reflection of human invention.
options: ① 단어의 사전적 정의는 일정하다.
② 시대와 사회에 따른 언어의 변화는 불가피하다.

question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A great strength of the market mechanism is that there are benefits for individuals to disclose their knowledge through their observable behavior. This stands in contrast to many strategic situations - for example, in political bargaining - in which it is wise not to let the other side know what one's true preferences or production capacities are. A perfectly competitive market that clears on the spot leaves no room for such strategic concealment. If prices are not sticky - as many models assume - individuals adapt their behavior instantaneously, whenever their preferences or the circumstances change. They stop buying items that do not satisfy their needs and stop selling items that do not provide them with optimal gains, maybe switching to the production of other items. If they have motivational problems, for example, falling into denial about the fact that there is no demand for their products markets reveal to them, sometimes in quite brutal ways, that they better accept this fact.

question: 19. 다음 글의 흠름으로 밴아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.1점]

question: 23. 다음 <보기>의 단어들을 어법과 문맥에 맞게 배열하여 제목을 완성하시오. (단, 주어진 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용하되, 변형하거나 단어를 추가하지 말 것)
passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers of which it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease to form, while sufficient fibers remain undamaged for the material not to crack and fall apart. Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to resist being pulled apart, but it can also be torn easily and accurately along the crease if a point of weakness - a small, initial tear - is opened up. This winning combination of mechanical properties allows it to assume the shape of any object through creasing and folding - hence the art of origami. There are very few materials as good: metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult. Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, in which case it lacks the rigidity required of a good wrapping material. So it is its ability to hold a crease while remaining stiff that makes paper uniquely suited to this purpose.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용
변형하거나 단어를 추가하지 말 것
answer: Paper's Unique Structural Attributes Enabling Folding and Rigidity
explanation: 주어진 단어들을 나열하여 글의 제목을 완성하는 문제입니다. 본문은 종이가 쉽게 접히면서도 부러지지 않고 강성(rigidity)을 유지하는 독특한 기계적·구조적 특성에 대해 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 '접힘과 강성을 가능하게 하는 종이의 독특한 구조적 속성'이라는 의미의 'Paper's Unique Structural Attributes Enabling Folding and Rigidity'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.

question: 9. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Everything in the world exists on a continuum, whether in speed, size, or any other possible descriptor you could think of. Still, we create and mindlessly adopt sharp distinctions, and those distinctions change lives far more dramatically than marginal differences ever do. Indeed, all differences are arbitrary, but drawing hard lines between categories hides this arbitrariness and can be severely damaging. I call this resulting damage "the borderline effect." The examples are endless. Someone's IQ is 69 and someone else's is 70 ─ but only the score of 70 is deemed to be within the range of normal. We don't have to be statisticians to know there is not a meaningful difference between 69 and 70. Yet once the person with the lower score is labeled "cognitively impaired." his or her life will unfold differently than the person with a one-point advantage.
options: ① 모든 차이는 연속선상에 존재하므로 뚜렷한 경계를 긋는 것은 해롭다.

③ 사람들은 연속적인 차이를 구분하기 쉽게 임의로 범주화한다.
④ 미세한 차이는 중요하지 않으며, 큰 차이만이 의미를 갖는다.
⑤ 경계선을 설정하면 개인의 잠재력을 더 잘 이해할 수 있다.
explanation: 글의 도입부에서 세상의 모든 것은 연속선상(continuum)에 존재한다고 밝히며, 그럼에도 불구하고 인위적으로 뚜렷한 경계를 나누는 행위가 가져오는 피해인 '경계 효과(borderline effect)'를 설명하고 있습니다. IQ 69와 70의 예시를 통해 실제로는 미미한 차이임에도 불구하고 경계선에 의해 '정상'과 '인지 장애'로 나뉘어 삶이 판이하게 달라지는 문제점을 지적하고 있습니다. 따라서 모든 차이는 연속적이므로 엄격한 구분을 짓는 것이 해로울 수 있다는 ①이 요지로 적절합니다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
passage: The future of work depends on two forces: a harmful substituting force and a helpful complementing one. Many tales have a hero and a villain fighting each other for dominance, but in our story, technology plays both roles at once, displacing workers while simultaneously raising the demand for their efforts elsewhere in the economy. This interaction helps explain why past worries about automation were misplaced: our ancestors had predicted the wrong winner in that fight, underestimating quite how powerful the complementing force would prove to be or simply ignoring that factor altogether. It also helps to explain why economists have traditionally been dismissive of the idea of technological unemployment: there appeared to be firm limits to the substituting force, leaving lots of tasks that could not be performed by machines, and a growing demand for human beings to do them instead.

question: 14. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Once a nail is driven into wood, its holding power comes mainly from friction. Friction is the force that resists motion when two surfaces slide or try to slide against each other. ⓐWhen two wooden boards secured with nails are forcibly pulled apart, the surrounding wood fibers tighten and compress around the nail shaft, creating a strong frictional grip that resists separation. ⓑThis frictional grip acts along the entire length of the nail, helping it stay firmly in place. ⓒWhen the applied force becomes too great, the connection fails either because the nail bends and eventually fractures under the load or because it slides out once the static friction is overcome. ⓓTo delay such failures, many nails receive a protective coating that resists rust and moisture, which helps extend their useful life and maintain structural stability in outdoor or humid environments. ⓔBecause the force required to stretch and break a nail is far greater than the frictional force at the wood-nail interface, actual nail breakage is uncommon, and the primary concern is the gradual weakening of friction over time.*fracture 파손, 부서짐

question: 16. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: All human cultures mark the passing of time by the differences they observe in the world around them. Our choice of which differences to mark depends firstly on what we can observe and secondly on what is important in our lives. How we mark the differences─the shapes of our calendars and our rituals─depends on the connections we make between those two things. In the agricultural society of premodern Europe, where higher latitudes make the seasons easily observable, it was natural to monitor the solar cycle. Conversely, among the largely nomadic peoples of Arabia, for whom seasonal changes were less significant, the lunar calendar was a more sensible choice. That did not make it inevitable that Islam would use a lunar calendar and Roman Christianity a solar one, but political and religious decisions were made from options limited by geography and lifestyle, filtered through tradition.
options: ① Why the Lunar Calendar Is Superior to the Solar Calendar
② Calendars Have Nothing to Do with Geography or Lifestyle
③ Calendars as a Record of Human Civilization's Progress
④ Geography and Lifestyle Shape the Way We Tell Time
⑤ How Religion Alone Determines the Calendar System

question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름에 따라 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 단어를 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.

question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [24년 9월 32번]
passage: The well-known American ethnologist Alfred Louis Kroeber made a rich and in-depth study of women's evening dress in the West, stretching back about three centuries and using ⓐ<u>reproductions</u> as of engravings. Having adjusted the dimensions of these plates due to their diverse origins, he was able to ⓑ<u>analyse</u> the constant elements in fashion features and to come up with a study that was neither intuitive nor approximate, but precise, mathematical and statistical. He reduced women's clothing to a ⓒ<u>certain</u> number of features: length and size of the skirt, size and depth of the neckline, height of the waistline. He demonstrated unambiguously that fashion is a profoundly regular ⓓ<u>phenomenon</u> which is not located at the level of annual variations but on the scale of history. explanation: 이 글은 패션이 역사적 차원에서 매우 규칙적이고 수학적인 주기를 가진다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 치마 길이가 50년 주기로 가장 긴 상태에서 짧은 상태로 변하고 다시 돌아오는 등 매우 정확한 주기성을 언급하고 있으므로, ⓔ의 'vague(모호한)'는 문맥상 'precise(정확한)' 또는 'regular(규칙적인)'와 같은 의미의 단어로 바뀌어야 적절합니다.

question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [23년 9월 34번]
passage: Much of human thought is designed to screen out information and to sort the rest into a manageable condition. question: 8. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. By "competence," I mean a cluster of qualities: smartness, the ability to get things done, wise decisions, etc. We stand a better chance of doing well at our life tasks if we surround ourselves with people who know what they're doing and have a lot to teach us. But the research evidence is paradoxical: In problem-solving groups, the participants who are considered the most competent and have the best ideas tend not to be the ones who are best liked. Why? One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, those who are too competent make us uncomfortable. They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman - and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison. If this were true, we might like people more if they reveal some evidence of fallibility. For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her better if, every once in a while, they screwed up.

question: 9. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.7점]
passage: As you may already know, what and how you buy can be political. To whom do you want to give your money? Which companies and corporations do you value and respect? question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Mental development consists of individuals increasingly mastering social codes and signals themselves, ⓐ<u>which</u> they can master only in social situations with the support of more competent individuals, typically adults. In this sense, mental development consists of internalizing social patterns and gradually ⓑ<u>becomes</u> a responsible actor among other responsible actors. In Denmark, the age of criminal responsibility is 15 years, which means that we then say that people have developed sufficient mental maturity ⓒ<u>to be</u> accountable for their actions at this point. And at the age of 18 people are given the right to vote and are thereby formally included in the basic democratic process. I do not know ⓓ<u>whether</u> these age boundaries are optimal, but it is clear that mental development takes place at different rates for different individuals, and depends especially on the social and family environment they have been given. Therefore, ⓔ<u>having</u> formal limits for responsibility from a specific age that apply to everyone is a somewhat questionable practice. But the question, of course, is whether it can be done any differently.
explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 mental development이며, 이 문장은 consists of (~로 구성되다)라는 동사구를 가집니다. of 뒤에 internalizing...과 becoming...이 병렬 구조를 이루어 목적어 역할을 해야 하므로, becomes를 becoming으로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 12. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage.가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: It's often said that those who can't do, teach. It would be more accurate to say that those who can do, can't teach the basics. A great deal of expert knowledge is implicit, not explicit. The further you progress toward mastery, the less conscious awareness you often have of the fundamentals. Experiments show that skilled golfers and wine aficionados have a hard time describing their putting and tasting techniques - even asking them to explain their approaches is enough to interfere with their performance, so they often stay on autopilot. When I first saw an elite diver do four and a half somersaults, I asked how he managed to spin so fast. His answer: "Just go up in a ball." Experts often have an intuitive understanding of a route, but they struggle to clearly express all the steps to take. <u>Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage</u>.*aficionado: 애호가**somersault: 공중제비

question: 15. 다음 brain에 관한 글의 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: The brain is a high-energy consumer of glucose, which is its fuel. Although the brain accounts for merely 3 percent of a person's body weight, it consumes 20 percent of the available fuel. Your brain can't store fuel, however, so it has to "pay as it goes." Since your brain is incredibly adaptive, it economizes its fuel resources. Thus, during a period of high stress, it shifts away from the analysis of the nuances of a situation to a singular and fixed focus on the stressful situation at hand. You don't sit back and speculate about the meaning of life when you are stressed. Instead, you devote all your energy to trying to figure out what action to take. Sometimes, however, this shift from the higher-thinking parts of the brain to the automatic and reflexive parts of the brain can lead you to do something too quickly, without thinking.
options: ① 포도당이라는 연료의 고에너지 소비자이다.
② 체중의 약 3%만 차지하지만, 사용할 수 있는 연료의 20%를 소비한다.
③ 포도당을 다음에 사용할 수 있도록 저장할 수 있다.
④ 적응력이 뛰어나 연료 자원을 경제적으로 사용한다.
⑤ 고차원적 사고 영역이 자동적이고 반사적인 영역으로 이동하기도 한다.
explanation: 지문 중 'Your brain can't store fuel, however(하지만 뇌는 연료를 저장할 수 없다)'라는 문장을 통해 뇌가 포도당(연료)을 저장할 수 없음을 알 수 있습니다. 따라서 3번은 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A computational algorithm that takes input data and generates some output from it doesn't really embody any notion of meaning. Certainly, such a computation does not generally have as its purpose its own survival and well-being. It does not, in general, assign value to the inputs. Compare, for example, a computer algorithm with the waggle dance of the honeybee, by which means a foraging bee conveys to others in the hive information about the source of food (such as nectar) it has located. The "dance" - a series of stylized movements on the comb - shows the bees how far away the food is and in which direction. But this input does not simply program other bees to go out and look for it. Rather, they evaluate this information, comparing it with their own knowledge of the surroundings. Some bees might not bother to make the journey, considering it not worthwhile. The input, such as it is, ______________________________________________; there is nothing prescriptive about its effects.*forage: 먹이를 찾아다니다 **comb: 벌집
options: ① is processed in the light of the organism's own internal states and history
② operates in a manner that ignores contextual and experiential factors
③ is handled in accordance with predetermined computational principles
④ is treated on the basis of instructions coming from external sources
⑤ produces meaning automatically without considering internal states
explanation: 지문은 컴퓨터 알고리즘과 생명체(꿀벌)의 정보 처리 방식의 차이를 설명합니다. 컴퓨터와 달리 생명체는 외부 정보(입력)를 자신의 지식이나 상황에 비추어 평가하며, 무조건 따르지 않습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 '규정적인(prescriptive) 것은 없다'는 말과 상응하여, 입력값이 유기체의 내부 상태와 경험에 따라 처리된다는 1번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 유기체 자체의 내부 상태와 이력에 비추어 처리된다
② 맥락적이고 경험적인 요인을 무시하는 방식으로 작동한다
③ 미리 정해진 계산 원리에 따라 처리된다
④ 외부 소스로부터 오는 지침에 근거하여 취급된다
⑤ 내부 상태를 고려하지 않고 자동으로 의미를 생성한다

question: 18. 다음 글의 (A)<u>The B-2 bomber and other "stealth" aircraft</u>의 제작 원리와 관련된 것으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: As always happens with natural selection, bats and their prey have been engaged in a life-or-death sensory arms race for millions of years. It's believed that hearing in moths arose specifically in response to the threat of being eaten by bats. (Not all insects can hear.) Over millions of years, moths have evolved the ability to detect sounds at ever higher frequencies, and, as they have, the frequencies of bats' vocalizations have risen, too. Some moth species have also evolved scales on their wings and a fur-like coat on their bodies; both act as "acoustic camouflage," by absorbing sound waves in the frequencies emitted by bats, thereby preventing those sound waves from bouncing back. (A)<u>The B-2 bomber and other "stealth" aircraft</u> have fuselages made of materials that do something similar with radar beams.
options: ① Natural selection: the process by which populations of living organisms adapt and change over generations.
② Photosynthesis: plants and some bacteria use sunlight to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugar (glucose) and oxygen.
③ Biomimetics: relating to or indicating synthetic methods which mimic biochemical processes.
④ Evolutionary Arms Race: An ongoing battle where species keep evolving new traits to outdo each other.
⑤ Acoustic resonance: the phenomenon where an object is forced to vibrate at its natural frequency by a sound wave.
explanation: 지문에서는 나방이 박쥐의 음파를 흡수하여 탐지되지 않도록 진화한 '음향 위장' 원리를 설명하고, 스텔스 폭격기가 이와 유사하게 레이더 빔을 흡수하는 재료로 만들어졌음을 언급하고 있습니다. 이는 생물학적 원리를 공학적으로 모방한 것이므로 '생체 모방 기술(Biomimetics)'과 가장 관련이 깊습니다.
options_translation: ① 자연 선택: 생물 집단이 세대를 거쳐 적응하고 변화하는 과정.
② 광합성: 식물과 일부 박테리아가 햇빛을 사용하여 이산화탄소와 물을 설탕과 산소로 바꾸는 과정.
③ 생체 모방 기술: 생화학적 과정을 모방하는 합성 방법과 관련된 것.
④ 진화적 군비 경쟁: 종들이 서로를 능가하기 위해 계속해서 새로운 형질을 진화시키는 지속적인 전투.
⑤ 음향 공명: 음파에 의해 물체가 고유 진동수로 진동하게 되는 현상.

question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The first human beings probably evolved in tropical regions where survival was possible without clothing. It is likely that they had very dark skin because light skin would have given little protection against the burning rays of the sun.
ordered_passages: (A) For instance, early hominids probably did not walk upright, but when they developed that ability, they could travel more efficiently. More important, perhaps, was their development of tool making. With tools, they could hunt other animals, so they could consume more protein and fat than their low-energy vegetarian diet would have provided.

(B) There is a debate about whether these people spread into other parts of the world or, instead, whether people developed independently in various parts of the world. Whichever the case, it is believed that in time they became capable of spreading out from Africa, eventually to most of the world. This was probably because their physical characteristics changed.

(C) Not only their bodies but also their brains would have been changed with more energy. The brain needs lots of energy to grow. As their diet expanded, hominids could physically and intellectually expand their territory.*hominid: 인류
explanation: 주어진 글은 초기 인류가 아프리카 열대 지역에서 진화했으며 강한 햇빛으로부터 보호하기 위해 어두운 피부를 가졌을 것이라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (B)에서 이러한 사람들이 세계의 다른 지역으로 퍼져 나갔는지에 대한 논쟁과 아프리카 밖으로의 확산 가능성을 언급하며, 신체적 특징의 변화를 그 원인으로 제시합니다. (A)는 그 변화의 구체적인 예로 직립 보행과 도구 제작 능력을 설명하며, 이를 통해 고단백 식단이 가능해졌음을 말합니다. (C)에서는 이러한 식단 변화가 몸뿐만 아니라 뇌의 성장(에너지 공급)을 이끌어 인류의 영토 확장을 가능케 했다는 결론으로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If cooking is as central to human identity, biology, and culture as the biological anthropologist Richard Wrangham suggests, it stands to reason that the decline of cooking in our time would have serious consequences for modern life, and so it has.
ordered_passages: (A) It has headed off many of the domestic conflicts that such a large shift in gender roles and family dynamics was bound to spark. It has relieved other pressures in the household, including longer workdays and overscheduled children, and saved us time that we can now invest in other pursuits.

(B) It has also allowed us to diversify our diets substantially, making it possible even for people with no cooking skills and little money to enjoy a whole different cuisine. All that's required is a microwave.

(C) Are they all bad? Not at all. The outsourcing of much of the work of cooking to corporations has relieved women of what has traditionally been their exclusive responsibility for feeding the family, making it easier for them to work outside the home and have careers.
explanation: 주어진 글은 요리의 감소가 현대 생활에 중대한 결과를 초래했다고 언급합니다. (C)에서 '그 결과들이 모두 나쁜가?'라는 질문을 던지며 요리 외주화(기업에 맡김)가 여성들의 전통적 부담을 덜어주었다는 긍정적인 측면을 처음 제시합니다. (A)는 그 긍정적인 효과를 이어받아 가사 갈등 완화와 시간 절약 효과를 설명합니다. (B)는 '또한(also)'을 사용하여 식단의 다양화라는 또 다른 장점을 추가하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

question: 23. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: In 2006, researchers conducted a study on the motivations for helping after the September 11th terrorist attacks against the United States. In the study, researchers found that people who gave money, blood, goods, or other forms of help out of other-focused motives - such as reducing another person's discomfort - were much more consistent in their support. ⓐIn fact, they were almost four times more likely to still be giving one year later compared with those whose original motivation was to reduce their own distress. ⓑThis distress signal is a method for people in danger to summon aid or indicate their location, using recognized visual, sound, or radio cues effectively. ⓒThis effect likely stems from differences in emotional arousal caused by the events of September 11th, which emotionally affected people throughout the United States. ⓓThose who gave to reduce their own distress reduced their emotional arousal with their initial gift, discharging that emotional distress. ⓔHowever, those who gave to reduce others' distress did not stop empathizing with victims who continued to struggle long after the attacks.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 9.11 테러 이후 도움을 주는 동기(타인 중심 vs 자기 중심)에 따른 지속성의 차이를 다루고 있습니다. ⓑ는 '구조 신호(distress signal)'에 대한 정의와 방법을 설명하고 있는데, 이는 도움을 주는 사람의 심리적 동기와 지속성에 관한 전체 맥락과 전혀 관련이 없는 내용입니다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A typical soap opera creates an abstract world, in which a highly complex web of relationships connects fictional characters that exist first only in the minds of the program's creators and are then recreated in the minds of the viewer. If you were to think about how much human psychology, law, and even everyday physics the viewer must know in order to follow and speculate about the plot, you would discover it is considerable - at least as much as the knowledge required to follow and speculate about a piece of modern mathematics, and in most cases, much more. Yet viewers follow soap operas with ease. How are they able to cope with such abstraction? Because, of course, the abstraction is built on an extremely familiar framework. The characters in a soap opera and the relationships between them are very much like the real people and relationships we experience every day. The abstraction of a soap opera is only a step removed from the real world. The mental "training" required to follow a soap opera is provided by our everyday lives.
summary_sentence: Although soap operas seem highly abstract, they are easily (A)___________ by audiences because they are built upon a(n) (B)___________ pattern of real-life human relationships.
options: ① confused ... unique
② overlooked ... unusual
③ comprehended ... ordinary
④ interpreted ... typical
⑤ grasped ... strange
explanation: 소설 속 인물들의 관계망은 복잡하고 추상적이지만, 우리가 일상에서 겪는 실제 사람들과의 관계와 매우 유사한 친숙한 틀을 바탕으로 구성되어 있다. 따라서 시청자들은 자신의 일상적인 경험을 통해 얻은 '정신적 훈련' 덕분에 이러한 추상적인 내용을 쉽게 이해(comprehended)할 수 있으며, 이는 일상적인(ordinary) 인간관계의 패턴을 따르기 때문이다.
options_translation: ① 혼란스러운 ... 독특한
② 간과되는 ... 특이한
③ 이해되는 ... 일상적인
④ 해석되는 ... 전형적인
⑤ 파악되는 ... 이상한

question: 25. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: One well-known shift took place when the accepted view - that the Earth was the center of the universe - changed to one where we understood that we are only inhabitants on one planet orbiting the Sun. (A) With each person who grasped the solar system view, it became easier for the next person to do so. (B) So it is with the notion that the world revolves around the human economy. (C) When this perspective shifts into place, it will be obvious that our economic well-being requires that we account for, and respond to, factors of ecological health. (D) Unfortunately we do not have a century or two to make the change. (E) By clarifying the nature of the old and new perspectives, and by identifying actions on which we might cooperate to move the process along, we can help accelerate the shift.
insertion_sentence: This is slowly being replaced by the view that the economy is a part of the larger system of material flows that connect all living things.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: (B) 앞 문장은 세상이 인간의 경제를 중심으로 돌아간다는 기존의 관념을 언급하고 있다. 주어진 문장의 'This'는 바로 이 관념을 지칭하며, 이것이 경제가 생태계의 일부라는 새로운 관점으로 대체되고 있음을 설명한다. (C) 뒤의 문장은 '이러한 관점이 자리를 잡을 때(When this perspective shifts into place)'라고 언급하며 주어진 문장의 '새로운 관점'을 받아 설명하고 있으므로 (C) 위치가 가장 적절하다.

question: 28. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말을 주어진 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: People seem to recognize that the arts are cultural activities that draw on (or react against) certain cultural traditions, certain shared understanding, and certain values and ideas that are characteristic of the time and place in which the art is created. In the case of science, however, opinions differ. Some scientists, like the great biologist J. B. S. Haldane, see science in a similar light - as a(n) (A)____________ activity that occurs in a particular time and place, and that needs to be understood within that context. Others, however, see science as a purely "objective" pursuit, uninfluenced by the cultural viewpoint and values of those who create it. In describing this view of science, philosopher Hugh Lacey speaks of the belief that there is an underlying order of the world which is simply there to be discovered - the world of pure "fact" stripped of any link with value. The aim of science according to this view is to represent this world of pure "fact", (B)____________ of any relationship it might bear contingently to human practices and experiences. *contingently: 혹여라도
subjective_conditions: 1. 각 빈칸에 1개의 단어로 각각 작성하시오.
2. 품사에 유의하여, 빈칸 앞뒤의 문맥에 부합하도록 작성하시오.
explanation: (A) 과학자 J.B.S. Haldane의 관점에 따르면, 과학 또한 예술처럼 특정한 시간과 장소에서 발생하는 '역사적(historical)' 활동이며 해당 맥락 내에서 이해되어야 한다는 논리적 흐름이 성립합니다. (B) 과학을 순수한 '사실'의 세계로 보는 두 번째 관점은 과학이 인간의 실천이나 경험과 상관없이 '독립적으로(independently)' 존재한다고 믿으므로, 부사적 수식어인 independently가 문맥상 정답입니다.

question: 29. 다음 글을 읽고 광고가 소비자에게 주는 이점 2개를 본문에서 찾아 주어진 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: If you drive down a busy street, you will find many competing businesses, often right next to one another. For example, in most places a consumer in search of a quick meal has many choices, and more fast-food restaurants appear all the time. These competing firms advertise heavily. The temptation is to see advertising as driving up the price of a product without any benefit to the consumer. However, this misconception doesn't account for why firms advertise. In markets where competitors sell slightly differentiated products, advertising enables firms to inform their customers about new products and services. Yes, costs rise, but consumers also gain information to help make purchasing decisions. Consumers also benefit from added variety, and we all get a product that's pretty close to our vision of a perfect good - and no other market structure delivers that outcome.
subjective_conditions: 1. 동사로 시작하는 동사구로 작성하시오.
2. 빈칸 앞뒤의 내용과 형식에 호응하도록 작성하시오.
answer:
(A) provides information to help consumers make purchasing decisions
(B) promotes variety (or adds variety for consumers)
explanation: 본문에서 광고가 소비자가 구매 결정을 하는 데 도움을 주는 정보를 제공하고, 다양한 선택지(다양성)를 가져다주는 이점을 언급하는 것이 적절하다. not only A but also B 구문의 병렬 구조에 따라 동사구 형식으로 작성하는 것이 조건에 부합한다.

question: 30. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말을 주어진 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: Sleep is clearly about more than just resting. One curious fact is that animals that are hibernating also have periods of sleep. It comes as a surprise to most of us, but hibernation and sleep are not the same thing at all, at least not from a neurological and metabolic perspective. Hibernating is more like being anesthetized: the subject is unconscious but not actually asleep. So a hibernating animal needs to get a few hours of conventional sleep each day within the larger unconsciousness. A further surprise to most of us is that bears, the most famous of wintry sleepers, don't actually hibernate. Real hibernation involves profound unconsciousness and a dramatic fall in body temperature - often to around 32 degrees Fahrenheit. By this definition, bears don't hibernate, because (A)________________________ and (B)________________________. Their winter sleeps are more accurately called a state of torpor. *anesthetize: 마취시키다 **torpor: 휴면
subjective_conditions: 1. (A)와 (B) 모두 주어와 동사가 포함된 10단어 이하의 <u>완전한</u> 문장으로 작성하시오.
2. (A)에는 'body temperature'를, (B)에는 'easily'를 반드시 포함하여 작성하시오.
3. 윗글의 단어 혹은 표현을 활용할 수 있으며, 빈칸 앞뒤의 내용과 부합하도록 작성하시오.
answer: (A) their body temperature stays near normal, (B) they are easily awakened
explanation: 곰이 생물학적 의미의 '진정한 동면(Real hibernation)'을 하는 것이 아닌 이유는 첫째, 체온이 급격히 떨어지지 않고 정상에 가깝게 유지되기 때문이며(A), 둘째, 외부 자극에 의해 쉽게 깨어날 수 있기 때문입니다(B). 조건에서 요구하는 '완전한 절(Full Clause)'의 형태를 갖추기 위해 주어와 동사를 올바르게 구성하는 것이 핵심입니다.

question: 1. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Over the last few centuries, humanity's collective prosperity has skyrocketed, as technological progress has made us far wealthier than ever before.
ordered_passages: (A) However, rising inequality, often fueled by technology, has started to put that mechanism under strain. Today, markets already provide immense rewards to some people but leave many others with very little.
(B) Almost all societies have settled upon the market mechanism for allocating that prosperity. They reward people in various ways for the work that they do and the things that they own.

(C) At present, a more radical version of this narrative appears in the form of technological unemployment, occurring in the very market we rely on most: the labor market. As the labor market starts to collapse, more and more people may be left without any share of society's prosperity.
explanation: 주어진 문장에서 기술적 진보로 인한 인류의 번영을 언급한 뒤, (B)에서 이러한 번영을 분배하기 위해 사회가 채택한 '시장 기제(market mechanism)'를 소개합니다. (A)에서 'However'를 통해 이러한 시장 기제가 불평등 심화로 인해 압박을 받기 시작했음을 대조적으로 설명하며, (C)에서 이러한 상황의 더 극단적인 형태인 '기술적 실업'과 노동 시장의 붕괴 가능성을 언급하며 마무리되는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It's often said that those who can't do, teach. It would be more accurate to say that those who can do, can't teach the basics. A great deal of expert knowledge is implicit, not explicit. The further you progress toward mastery, the less conscious awareness you often have of the fundamentals. Experiments show that skilled golfers and wine aficionados have a hard time describing their putting and tasting techniques - even asking them to explain their approaches is enough to interfere with their performance, so they often stay on autopilot. When I first saw an elite diver do four and a half somersaults, I asked how he managed to spin so fast. His answer: "Just go up in a ball." Experts often have an intuitive understanding of a route, but they struggle to clearly express all the steps to take. Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage.
options: ① The Ease with Which Professionals Teach Beginners
② Fundamentals: Can They Be Well Conveyed by Experts?
③ The Outstanding Ability of Experts to Simplify Learning
④ Why Beginners Understand the Basics Better than Experts
⑤ The Hidden Effort Behind Elite Athletes' Acquisition of Expertise

question: 6. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 부분이 포함된 것은?
passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts ⓐ<u>to keep it in a specific state</u>, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem; they remove ⓑ<u>unwanted plants growing among the vegetables</u>, ⓒ<u>perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch</u> to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. ⓓ<u>If the grower stops intervening, even for a day</u>, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, ⓔ<u>and yet yield will almost certainly be lower</u> as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.*insecticide: 살충제
explanation: ⓐ에서 'keep'의 목적어 역할을 하는 것은 관계대명사 'that'이므로, 'it'을 중복해서 쓰면 안 된다. 따라서 'to keep in a specific state'로 고쳐야 한다. 나머지 선택지들은 분사의 후치 수식, 병렬 구조, 조건의 부사절, 문맥상 적절한 연결사 및 시제 등으로 어법상 옳다.

question: 10. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 When the process is fair we believe that our outcome is deserved가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When we get an unfavorable outcome, in some ways the last thing we want to hear is that the process was fair. As outraging as the combination of an unfavorable outcome and an unfair process is, this combination also brings with it a consolation prize: the possibility of attributing the bad outcome to something other than ourselves. We may reassure ourselves by believing that our bad outcome had little to do with us and everything to do with the unfair process. If the process is fair, however, we cannot nearly as easily externalize the outcome; we got what we got "fair and square." <u>When the process is fair we believe that our outcome is deserved</u>, which is another way of saying that there must have been something about ourselves (what we did or who we are) that caused the outcome.*consolation: 위로
options: ① We believe that despite the flaws of the process, the causes of the outcome should not be externalized.
② Even if we admit the process was fair, we hesitate to see the result as stemming from ourselves.
③ Our tendency to externalize the causes of outcomes makes it difficult for us to internalize them.
④ We dispute the fairness of the process, persistently seeking the sources of its injustice.
⑤ If the process seems fair, we recognize ourselves as accountable for the result.
explanation: 과정이 감정할 때 결과를 당당히 받아들얼야 한다는 것은, 그 결과에 대한 책임이 외부가 아닌 자신에게 있음을 인정한다는 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 우리는 과정의 결함에도 뵄구하고 결과의 원인을 외부화해서는 안 된다고 믿눔다.
② 우리는 과정이 감정했음을 인정할준라도, 결과가 우리 자신에게서 비롯되었다고 밴기를 주저한다.
③ 결과의 원인을 외부화하려눔 우리의 경픔은 그것들을 내면화하기 어렲게 만든다.
④ 우리는 과정의 감정성에 의미를 제기하며 끊임없이 뵈감의 근원을 찾눔다.
⑤ 과정이 감정해 보인다면, 우리는 우리 자신이 결과에 대한 책임이 있음을 인식한다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 this view에 대한 설명으로 적절한 것만을 <보기>에서 있는 대로 고른 것은?
passage: People seem to recognize that the arts are cultural activities that draw on (or react against) certain cultural traditions, certain shared understanding, and certain values and ideas that are characteristic of the time and place in which the art is created. In the case of science, however, opinions differ. Some scientists, like the great biologist J. B. S. Haldane, see science in a similar light - as a historical activity that occurs in a particular time and place, and that needs to be understood within that context. Others, however, see science as a purely "objective" pursuit, uninfluenced by the cultural viewpoint and values of those who create it. In describing <u>this view</u> of science, philosopher Hugh Lacey speaks of the belief that there is an underlying order of the world which is simply there to be discovered - the world of pure "fact" stripped of any link with value. The aim of science according to this view is to represent this world of pure "fact", independently of any relationship it might bear contingently to human practices and experiences.*contingently: 혹여라도
vocabulary_box: ⓐ It regards science as a pursuit that involves cultural viewpoints and scientists' values.
ⓑ It claims that brilliant scientific ideas should be derived from historical legacy.
ⓒ It is supported by the belief in the world of utter fact stripped of any correlation with value.
ⓓ The scientists who possess it might aim to detect an underlying structure of fundamental reality.
ⓔ It holds that the realm of pure fact remains subject to human practices.
explanation: 본문에서 'this view'는 과학을 문화적 관점이나 가치로부터 영향을 받지 않는 순수한 '객관적' 추구로 보는 관점을 의미합니다.  Hugh Lacey는 이 관점이 가치와 단절된 순수한 '사실'의 세계, 즉 발견되기를 기다리는 세계의 근본적인 질서가 있다는 믿음에 근거한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 ⓒ(가치와의 상관관계가 제거된 전적인 사실의 세계에 대한 믿음)와 ⓓ(근본적 실재의 기저 구조를 탐지하려 함)가 적절합니다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓔ는 과학을 문화적, 역사적, 인간적 실천과 연관 짓는 첫 번째 관점에 해당하므로 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Any new or threatening situation may require us to make decisions and this requires information. So important is communication during a disaster that normal social barriers often ⓐ<u>lessen</u>. We will talk to strangers in a way we would never consider normally. Even relatively low grade ⓑ<u>disruption</u> of our life such as a fire drill or a very late train seems to give us the permission to break normal etiquette and talk to strangers. Without an authoritative source of facts, whether that is a newspaper or trusted broadcast station, rumours often ⓓ<u>fade away</u>. Rumours start because people believe their group to be in danger and so, although the rumour is not ⓔ<u>verified</u>, feel they should pass it on. For example, if a worker heard that their employer's business was doing badly and people were going to be made redundant, they would pass that information on to colleagues.*redundant: (일시) 해고된

② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ

question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: There are deep similarities between viral contagion and behavioral contagion. But there are also important points where the two types of contagion are ⓑ<u>dissimilar</u>. One is that visibility promotes behavioral contagion but inhibits the spread of infectious diseases. Solar panels that are visible from the street, for instance, are more likely to ⓒ<u>restrict</u> neighboring installations. In contrast, we try to avoid others who are ⓓ<u>evidently</u> ill. Another important difference is that whereas viral contagion is almost always a bad thing, behavioral contagion can be good or bad depending on the situation. question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Commitment is the glue holding together characteristically human forms of social life. Commitments make individuals' behavior predictable in the face of fluctuation in their preferences and ⓐ<u>inclinations</u>, thereby facilitating the planning and coordination of joint actions involving multiple agents. ⓑ<u>Likewise</u>, many people would not be willing to perform actions that they are now voluntarily engaged in. For example, a taxi driver picks up his clients and transports them to their desired destination because he is guaranteed to ⓒ<u>receive</u> payment afterwards for the service, and a construction worker performs her job every day because her employer has made a credible commitment to pay her at the end of the month. Indeed, the taxi driver and the construction worker are willing to accept money ⓓ<u>in return</u> only because a network of other agents (notably the central bank) is committed to taking various measures to ⓔ<u>sustain</u> the currency in question. Thus, social objects and institutions such as jobs, money, government, scientific collaborations and marriage depend for their origin and stability upon the credibility of commitments.
explanation: ⓑ 'Likewise(마찬가지로)'는 앞 문장과 유사하거나 같은 결의 내용을 덧붙일 때 사용됩니다. 하지만 뒤따르는 문장은 '만약 약속(commitment)이 없다면(그렇지 않다면)' 많은 사람들이 현재 자발적으로 참여하는 활동을 하지 않을 것이라는 가정의 내용을 담고 있으므로, 문맥상 'Otherwise(그렇지 않으면)'와 같은 반대 가정의 연결어가 적절합니다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We stand a better chance of doing well at our life tasks if we surround ourselves with those that know what they're doing and have a lot to teach us: that is, competent people. question: 18. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In today's information age, in many companies and on many teams, the objective is no longer error prevention and replicability. On the contrary, it's creativity, speed, and keenness. To bring profit to our company, we should ___________________________________________. A lot of little mistakes, while sometimes painful, help the organization learn quickly and are a critical part of the innovation cycle. In these situations, rules and process are no longer the best answer. A symphony isn't what you're going for. Leave the conductor and the sheet music behind. Build a jazz band instead.
options: ① suppress absurd thinking by highly valuing processes that can actually be carried out
② stick to the replicable processes, even if they lack creativity and variation
③ formulate original ideas by rejecting consistency and fostering variability
④ view both uniformity and individuality as essential qualities of variability

explanation: 이 글은 현대 정보화 시대의 창의적 기업에서는 산업 시대와 달리 '변동성을 최소화(오류 방지 및 복제 가능성)'하는 것보다 '변동성을 최대화(창의성 및 속도)'하는 것이 더 중요하다고 주장합니다. 작은 실수들을 통해 조직이 빠르게 학습하며 혁신해야 한다는 맥락이므로, 일관성을 거부하고 변동성을 길러 독창적인 아이디어를 만들어야 한다는 내용인 ③이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.

② 창의성과 변동성이 부족하더라도 복제 가능한 과정을 고수한다.

question: 19. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The research undertaken by the psychologist Ervin Staub examined ________________________________________. Staub suggested that younger children might feel more comfortable acting when they have the company of a peer, whereas older children might feel more concern about being judged by their peers and fear feeling embarrassed by overreacting. options_translation: ① 도움이 필요할 때 도움을 받는 것에 관한 연령대별 아이들의 선호도

③ 연령과 또래의 존재 여부에 따른 고통에 처한 사람들을 돕고자 하는 아이들의 의지 변화

question: 20. 다음 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: One well-known shift took place when the accepted view - that the Earth was the center of the universe - changed to one where we understood that we are only inhabitants on one planet orbiting the Sun. question: 21. 다음 글의 내용으로 알 수 있는 것만을 <보기>에서 고른 것은?
passage: If the brain has already stored someone's face and name, why do we still end up remembering one and not the other? This is because the brain has something of a two-tier memory system at work when it comes to retrieving memories, and this gives rise to a common yet infuriating sensation: recognising someone, but not being able to remember how or why, or what their name is. This happens because the brain differentiates between familiarity and recall. To clarify, familiarity (or recognition) is when you encounter someone or something and you know you've done so before. But beyond that, you've got nothing; all you can say is this person/thing is already in your memories. Recall is when you can access the original memory of how and why you know this person; recognition is just flagging up the fact that the memory exists.*retrieve: 꺼내다 **infuriating: 짜증 나는
vocabulary_box: ⓐ The brain can recognize a person's face without remembering their name.
ⓑ Recognition involves realizing you have encountered something before, even without recalling the details.
ⓒ Recall allows you to access the original memory of how and why you know someone.
ⓓ Recall is usually faster than recognition in most situations.
ⓔ Recognition occurs when you remember both a person's face and the specific circumstances in which you met them.
explanation: 지문은 뇌의 기억 시스템인 친숙함(익숙함, recognition)과 회상(recall)의 차이를 설명합니다. ⓐ 이름은 기억나지 않지만 얼굴은 알아볼 수 있다는 내용은 지문의 'recognising someone, but not being able to remember... what their name is'와 일치합니다. ⓑ 익숙함은 세부 사항 없이 전에 마주친 적이 있다는 것을 깨닫는 것이라는 내용은 지문의 'recognition is just flagging up the fact that the memory exists'와 일치합니다. ⓒ 회상은 어떻게, 왜 아는지 원래의 기억에 접근할 수 있게 한다는 내용은 지문의 'Recall is when you can access the original memory of how and why you know this person'과 일치합니다. ⓓ 회상이 익숙함보다 빠르다는 언급은 지문에 없으며, ⓔ 얼굴과 상황을 모두 기억하는 것은 회상(recall)에 해당하므로 ⓔ는 틀린 진술입니다. 따라서 옳은 것은 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ인 ①번입니다.

passage: The first human beings probably evolved in tropical regions where survival was possible without clothing. For instance, early hominids probably did not walk upright, but when they developed that ability, they could travel more efficiently. More important, perhaps, was their development of tool making. With tools, they could hunt other animals, so they could consume more protein and fat than their low-energy vegetarian diet would have provided. Not only their bodies but also their brains would have beer changed with more energy. The brain needs lots of energy to grow. question: 24. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [24년 9월 39번]
passage: Sleep is clearly about more than just resting. Studies have shown that sleep is closely connected to essential brain and body functions such as memory consolidation, metabolic regulation, and overall health maintenance. One curious fact is that animals that are hibernating also have periods of sleep. It comes as a surprise to most of us, but hibernation and sleep are not the same thing at all, at least not from a neurological and metabolic perspective. Hibernating is more like being anesthetized: the subject is unconscious but not actually asleep. So a hibernating animal needs to get a few hours of conventional sleep each day within the larger unconsciousness. A further surprise to most of us is that bears, the most famous of wintry sleepers, don't actually hibernate. Real hibernation involves profound unconsciousness and a dramatic fall in body temperature - often to around 32 degrees Fahrenheit. By this definition, bears don't hibernate, because their body temperature stays near normal and they are easily awakened. Their winter sleeps are more accurately called a state of torpor.*hibernation: 동면 **anesthetize: 마취시키다 ***torpor: 휴면

passage: A computational algorithm that takes input data and generates some output from it doesn't really embody any notion of meaning. Certainly, such a computation does not generally have as its purpose its own survival and well-being. It does not, in general, assign value to the inputs. Compare, for example, a computer algorithm with the waggle dance of the honeybee, by which means a foraging bee conveys to others in the hive information about the source of food (such as nectar) it has located. The "dance" - a series of stylized movements on the comb - shows the bees how far away the food is and in which direction. But this input does not simply program other bees to go out and look for it. Rather, they evaluate this information, comparing it with their own knowledge of the surroundings. Some bees might not bother to make the journey, considering it not worthwhile. The input, such as it is, is processed in the light of the organism's own internal states and history; there is nothing prescriptive about its effects.*forage: 먹이를 찾아다니다 **comb: 벌집

question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: Mental development consists of individuals increasingly mastering social codes and signals themselves, which they can master only in social situations with the support of more competent individuals, typically adults. In this sense, mental development consists of internalizing social patterns and gradually becoming a responsible actor among other responsible actors. In Denmark, the age of criminal responsibility is 15 years, which means that we then say that people have developed sufficient mental maturity to be accountable for their actions at this point. And at the age of 18 people are given the right to vote and are thereby formally included in the basic democratic process. I do not know whether these age boundaries are optimal, but it is clear that mental development takes place at different rates for different individuals, and depends especially on the social and family environment they have been given. question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We're naturally wired to organize the world into a hierarchy. We do this to help make sense of the world, maintain our beliefs, and generally feel better. But when someone infringes on our place in the world and our understanding of how it works, we react without thinking. When someone cuts you off on the highway and road rage kicks in, that's your unconscious mind saying, "Who are you to cut me off?" You're reacting to a threat to your inherent sense of hierarchy. On the road we are all equals. We're all supposed to play by the same rules. Cutting someone off violates those rules and implies higher status. Or consider when you get frustrated with your kids and end an argument with "Because I said so." (Or the office equivalent: "Because I'm the boss.") In these moments you've stopped thinking and regressed to your biological tendencies of reaffirming the hierarchy.
options: ① 인간관계에서는 위계와 권위보다 상호 존중과 공감을 바탕으로 한 소통이 더 중요하다.
