question: 4. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It's often said that those who can't do, teach. It would be more accurate to say that those who can do, can't teach the basics. A great deal of expert knowledge is implicit, not explicit. The further you progress toward mastery, the less conscious awareness you often have of the fundamentals. Experiments show that skilled golfers and wine aficionados have a hard time describing their putting and tasting techniques - even asking them to explain their approaches is enough to interfere with their performance, so they often stay on autopilot. When I first saw an elite diver do four and a half somersaults, I asked how he managed to spin so fast. His answer: "Just go up in a ball." Experts often have an intuitive understanding of a route, but they struggle to clearly express all the steps to take. <u>Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage</u>.
options: ① The term "brain dump" refers to a situation in which experts supposedly lose all memory of their skills and knowledge as soon as someone asks them to describe what they know or do.
② Experts often cannot clearly articulate all the steps of their techniques, so when they try to explain them, their explanations might include a mix of useful and irrelevant or confusing details.

③ Experts are able to describe every single step of their techniques perfectly, providing complete explanations without making any errors or including any information that is unnecessary or irrelevant.
④ Experts have no real understanding of the skills they perform, and whenever they are asked to explain how they do them, they can only make random guesses without any accurate knowledge or insight.

⑤ Experts supposedly perform a "brain dump" by recording every tiny detail of their techniques into a structured checklist, to help themselves or others learn and practice their skills systematically.
explanation: 이 글은 전문가들의 지식이 명시적이기보다는 암묵적인 경우가 많아, 자신의 기술을 설명할 때 오히려 수행에 방해가 되거나 명확하게 설명하는 데 어려움을 겪는다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 마지막 문장의 '그들의 브레인 덤프(기억 쏟아내기)는 부분적으로 쓰레기로 채워져 있다'는 말은 전문가들이 자신의 기술을 설명하려 할 때, 단계별 과정을 명확히 표현하지 못해 유용한 정보와 무관하거나 혼란스러운 세부 사항이 섞여 나올 수 있음을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① "브레인 덤프"라는 용어는 전문가가 자신이 알고 있거나 행하는 것을 설명해 달라는 요청을 받자마자 자신의 기술과 지식에 대한 모든 기억을 잃어버리는 상황을 의미한다.
② 전문가는 종종 자신의 기술의 모든 단계를 명확하게 설명하지 못하므로, 이를 설명하려고 할 때 그들의 설명에는 유용한 세부 사항과 무관하거나 혼란스러운 세부 사항이 섞여 있을 수 있다.
③ 전문가는 자신의 기술의 모든 단계를 완벽하게 설명할 수 있으며, 오류를 범하거나 불필요하거나 무관한 정보를 포함하지 않고 완전한 설명을 제공한다.
④ 전문가는 자신이 수행하는 기술에 대해 실질적인 이해가 없으며, 수행 방법을 설명하라는 요청을 받을 때마다 정확한 지식이나 통찰력 없이 무작위적인 추측만 할 수 있을 뿐이다.
⑤ 전문가는 자신이나 타인이 체계적으로 기술을 배우고 연습할 수 있도록 돕기 위해 자신의 기술의 모든 세세한 부분을 구조화된 체크리스트에 기록함으로써 "브레인 덤프"를 수행한다고 여겨진다.

question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In today's information age, in many companies and on many teams, the objective is no longer error prevention and replicability. On the contrary, it's creativity, speed, and keenness. In the industrial era, the goal was to minimize variation. But in creative companies today, maximizing variation is more essential. In these situations, the biggest risk isn't making a mistake or losing consistency; it's failing to attract top talent, to invent new products, or to change direction quickly when the environment shifts. Consistency and repeatability are more likely to suppress fresh thinking than to bring your company profit. A lot of little mistakes, while sometimes painful, help the organization learn quickly and are a critical part of the innovation cycle. In these situations, rules and process are no longer the best answer. A symphony isn't what you're going for. Leave the conductor and the sheet music behind. Build a jazz band instead.
options: ① Minimizing Variation through Creativity and Speed
② The Hidden Dangers of Making Mistakes in Business
③ The Essential Role of Strict Rules and Procedures in Innovation
④ Why Consistency and Repeatability Guarantee Business Profit
⑤ From Symphony to Jazz: Why Modern Companies Must Value Creativity
explanation: 오늘날의 정보 시대와 창의적인 기업에서는 과거 산업 시대의 목표였던 '오류 방지'와 '일관성'보다 '변동성 극대화', '창의성', '속도'가 더 중요해졌습니다. 필자는 지시를 따르는 오케스트라(교향곡)보다는 즉흥적이고 유연한 '재즈 밴드'와 같은 조직이 되어야 한다고 강조하고 있으므로, 현대 기업이 창의성을 중시해야 한다는 내용의 5번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 창의성과 속도를 통한 변동성 최소화
② 비즈니스에서 실수를 하는 것의 숨겨진 위험
③ 혁신에서 엄격한 규칙과 절차의 필수적인 역할
④ 일관성과 반복성이 비즈니스 수익을 보장하는 이유
⑤ 교향곡에서 재즈로: 현대 기업이 창의성을 가치 있게 여겨야 하는 이유

question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The well-known American ethnologist Alfred Louis Kroeber made a rich and in-depth study of women's evening dress in the West, stretching back about three centuries and using reproductions of engravings. Having adjusted the dimensions of these plates due to their diverse origins, he was able to analyse the constant elements in fashion features and to come up with a study that was neither intuitive nor approximate, but precise, mathematical and statistical. He reduced women's clothing to a certain number of features: length and size of the skirt, size and depth of the neckline, height of the waistline. He demonstrated unambiguously that fashion is a profoundly regular phenomenon which is not located at the level of annual variations but on the scale of history. For practically 300 years, women's dress was subject to a very precise periodic cycle: forms reach the furthest point in their variations every fifty years. If, at any one moment, skirts are at their longest, fifty years later they will be at their shortest; thus skirts become long again fifty years after being short and a hundred years after being long.
options: ① Short-Term Fluctuations in Skirt Lengths
② The Unpredictable Nature of Western Fashion
③ Recurring Patterns in the History of Women's Dress
④ The Decline of Elegance in Modern Western Fashion
⑤ The Impact of the Industrial Revolution on Clothing Styles
explanation: 인류학자 Alfred Louis Kroeber는 서구 여성의 저녁 드레스를 300년에 걸쳐 분석한 결과, 패션이 연간 변동 수준이 아니라 역사적 규모에서 매우 규칙적인 현상임을 증명했습니다. 드레스의 형태가 50년 주기로 최대치와 최소치를 오가는 정밀한 주기적 순환을 따른다는 것이 핵심 내용이므로 3번 '여성 복식사에서 반복되는 패턴'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 치마 길이의 단기적인 변동
② 서구 패션의 예측 불가능한 본질
③ 여성 복식사에서 반복되는 패턴
④ 현대 서구 패션에서 우아함의 쇠퇴
⑤ 산업 혁명이 의류 스타일에 미친 영향

question: 8. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Although empathy is widely praised by scholars and public figures, not everyone is an empathy booster. Critics of empathy argue that empathy will not save us from interpersonal and intergroup conflict. In fact, they argue, empathy makes such conflicts worse. These critics maintain that empathy can be exhausting and lead to burnout or insensitivity to suffering. They argue that we tend to empathize strongly with our in-group and resist empathizing with out-groups, and even enjoy the suffering of out-groups in competitive or threatening contexts. Thus, the prescription for more empathy is often counterproductive in cases of conflict. Empathy, they argue, can further encourage conflict and force us into an us vs. them mentality. Finally, even when we try to empathize with others who are dissimilar from us or in unfamiliar contexts, sometimes we are unable to accurately empathize with their experiences, causing further misunderstandings and frustration. Critics of empathy argue that _____________ __________________________________________.
options: ① the more empathy we promote, the fewer conflicts we will face.
② empathy always leads to mutual understanding and stronger social bonds.
③ conflicts mainly arise because people lack empathy for their in-group members.
④ alternative approaches are required instead of empathy in pursuing social harmony.
⑤ political leaders should promote more empathy as the ultimate solution to social conflicts.
explanation: 지문은 공감(empathy)에 대한 비판적인 시각을 다루고 있습니다. 공감이 오히려 내집단 편향을 강화하여 갈등을 악화시키고, 번아웃을 유발하며, 타인에 대한 오해를 불러일으킬 수 있다는 점을 지적합니다. 따라서 공감이 갈등의 해결책이 되지 못한다는 맥락에서 빈칸에는 사회적 화합을 위해 공감 대신 다른 대안적 접근이 필요하다는 4번이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 우리가 공감을 더 많이 장려할수록, 우리는 더 적은 갈등에 직면할 것이다.
② 공감은 항상 상호 이해와 더 강한 사회적 유대로 이어진다.
③ 갈등은 주로 사람들이 내집단 구성원들에 대한 공감이 부족하기 때문에 발생한다.
④ 사회적 화합을 추구하는 데 있어 공감 대신 대안적인 접근법이 요구된다.
⑤ 정치 지도자들은 사회적 갈등에 대한 궁극적인 해결책으로서 더 많은 공감을 장려해야 한다.

question: 9. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The concern about how we appear to others can be seen in children, though work by the psychologist Ervin Staub suggests that the effect may vary with age. In a study where children heard another child in distress, young children (kindergarten through second grade) were more likely to help the child in distress when with another child than when alone. But for older children - in fourth and sixth grade - the effect reversed: they were less likely to help a child in distress when they were with a peer than when they were alone. Staub suggested that younger children might feel more comfortable acting when they have the company of a peer, whereas older children might feel more concern about being judged by their peers and fear feeling embarrassed by overreacting. Staub noted that "older children seemed to discuss the distress sounds less and to react to them less openly than younger children." In other words, the older children _____________________________________________.
options: ① were less likely to comprehend others' emotional states
② tended to react more emotionally while maintaining situational awareness
③ were generally better at identifying the exact cause of someone's distress
④ were more self-conscious and tended to restrain their reactions in social contexts
⑤ demonstrated a stronger instinct to protect their peers during distressing circumstances
explanation: 실험 결과, 나이가 더 많은 아이들(4~6학년)은 혼자 있을 때보다 또래와 함께 있을 때 곤경에 처한 아이를 덜 돕는 경향을 보였습니다. 이는 타인의 시선을 의식하고 과잉 반응으로 인한 당혹감을 두려워하기 때문입니다. 따라서 나이가 많은 아이들은 사회적 맥락에서 더 자의식이 강하고 자신의 반응을 억제하는 경향이 있다는 ④번이 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 타인의 감정 상태를 덜 이해하는 경향이 있었다
② 상황 인식을 유지하면서 더 감정적으로 반응하는 경향이 있었다
③ 누군가의 고통의 정확한 원인을 식별하는 데 일반적으로 더 능숙했다
④ 더 자의식이 강했고 사회적 맥락에서 자신의 반응을 억제하는 경향이 있었다
⑤ 괴로운 상황 동안 또래를 보호하려는 더 강한 본능을 보여주었다

question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A computational algorithm that takes input data and generates some output from it doesn't really embody any notion of meaning. Certainly, such a computation does not generally have as its purpose its own survival and wellbeing. It does not, in general, assign value to the inputs. Compare, for example, a computer algorithm with the waggle dance of the honeybee, by which means a foraging bee conveys to others in the hive information about the source of food (such as nectar) it has located. The "dance" - a series of stylized movements on the comb - shows the bees how far away the food is and in which direction. But this input does not simply program other bees to go out and look for it. Rather, they evaluate this information, comparing it with their own knowledge of the surroundings. Some bees might not bother to make the journey, considering it not worthwhile. The input, such as it is, is processed in the light of ________________________; there is nothing prescriptive about its effects.
options: ① the creature's own physiological and experiential context
② the random signals from the environment around that being
③ the universal principles guiding all animal behavior
④ the computer's internal programming structure
⑤ the hive's collective behavioral instructions
explanation: 컴퓨터 알고리즘과 달리 생명체(꿀벌)는 정보를 단순히 처리하는 것이 아니라, 자신의 생존이나 가치 판단에 따라 정보를 평가합니다. 꿀벌이 춤을 보고도 먹이를 찾아가지 않는 것은 그 정보를 자신의 상황과 지식에 비추어 판단하기 때문입니다. 따라서 정보가 '생명체 자신의 생리적, 경험적 맥락'에 따라 처리된다는 ①번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 그 생물 자신의 생리적 및 경험적 맥락
② 그 존재 주변 환경으로부터의 무작위적인 신호들
③ 모든 동물의 행동을 안내하는 보편적 원칙들
④ 컴퓨터의 내부 프로그래밍 구조
⑤ 벌집의 집단적 행동 지침

question: 11. 다음 글 (A)의 내용을 종합할 때, (B)의 빈칸에 들어갈 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: (A) It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. By "competence," I mean a cluster of qualities: smartness, the ability to get things done, wise decisions, etc. We stand a better chance of doing well at our life tasks if we surround ourselves with people who know what they're doing and have a lot to teach us. But the research evidence is paradoxical: In problem-solving groups, the participants who are considered the most competent and have the best ideas tend not to be the ones who are best liked. Why? One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, those who are too competent make us uncomfortable. They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman - and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison. If this were true, we might like people more if they reveal some evidence of fallibility. For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her better if, every once in a while, they screwed up.(B) Although we tend to assume that more competent people are more likable, research shows the opposite: overly competent people may be disliked because they make others uncomfortable. Therefore, ________________________________________.
options: ① showing occasional mistakes can increase one's likability by making them seem more human
② maintaining an image of perfection is the best strategy for winning social approval
③ intellectual excellence always results in emotional distance from others
④ competence plays no meaningful role in shaping personal relationships
explanation: 지문 (A)는 너무 유능한 사람이 타인에게 불편함을 줄 수 있으며, 가끔 실수를 하는 등 '틀릴 수 있음(fallibility)'을 보여줄 때 오히려 더 호감을 얻을 수 있다는 '실수 효과(Pratfall Effect)'를 설명하고 있습니다. (B)의 요약문에서도 너무 유능한 사람이 비호감을 살 수 있다고 했으므로, 결론적으로 가끔 실수를 보여주는 것이 인간미를 더해 호감도를 높일 수 있다는 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 가끔 실수를 보여주는 것이 사람들을 더 인간적으로 보이게 함으로써 호감도를 높일 수 있다
② 완벽한 이미지를 유지하는 것이 사회적 인정을 얻기 위한 최선의 전략이다
③ 지적 탁월함은 항상 타인과의 정서적 거리를 초래한다
④ 유능함은 개인적 관계를 형성하는 데 의미 있는 역할을 하지 않는다

question: 12. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: All human cultures mark the passing of time by the differences they observe in the world around them. Our choice of which differences to mark depends firstly on what we can observe and secondly on what is important in our lives. In the agricultural society of pre-modern Europe, where higher latitudes make the seasons easily observable, it was natural to monitor the solar cycle. Conversely, among the largely nomadic peoples of Arabia, for whom seasonal changes were less significant, the lunar cycle was a more sensible choice. That did not make it inevitable that Islam would rely on a lunar system and Roman Christianity on a solar one, but (A)_______________ strongly influenced (B)_______________, which were then shaped further by political and religious decisions filtered through tradition.
options: ① religious traditions ... natural observations
② geography and lifestyle ... seasonal rituals
③ economic policies ... geographical conditions
④ cultural exchanges ... agricultural productivity
⑤ natural surrounding and daily practices ... the calender systems adopted
explanation: 지문은 인간 문화가 주변 환경을 관찰한 결과(태양력 vs 태음력)와 그들의 삶에서 중요한 것들에 따라 시간을 측정하는 방식을 선택함을 설명합니다. (A)에서는 지리적 위치나 생활 양식과 같은 자연적 환경과 일상적 관행을 의미하는 'natural surrounding and daily practices'가 적절하며, (B)에서는 그 결과로 선택된 'the calender systems adopted'(채택된 달력 체계)가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 종교적 전통 ... 자연적 관찰
② 지리와 생활 방식 ... 계절적 의식
③ 경제 정책 ... 지리적 조건
④ 문화적 교류 ... 농업 생산성
⑤ 자연 환경과 일상적 관행 ... 채택된 달력 시스템

question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Mother cats can identify their own kittens by scent - even when litters are mixed, they rely on smell to ⓐ<u>distinguish</u> their offspring from those of other mothers. However, when several kittens, both hers and others, have strayed from the nest, a mother cat doesn't seem to show a preference for retrieving her own. The reason for this behavior remains unclear. One possible explanation is the ⓑ<u>strength</u> of the kittens' distress vocalizations. These cries are powerful triggers for maternal response and may be difficult to ⓒ<u>notice</u>, regardless of whether the kitten belongs to her. In the wild, a crying kitten left exposed can attract predators, putting all nearby kittens ⓓ<u>at risk</u>. Quickly retrieving any vocalizing kitten - whether her own or not - may be an instinctive survival strategy to reduce the threat of drawing ⓔ<u>unwelcome</u> attention.
explanation: 새끼 고양이의 고통스러운 울음소리는 어미의 반응을 유발하는 강력한 자극제이므로, 자신의 새끼인지 여부와 상관없이 그 울음소리를 '무시하기(ignore/resist)' 어렵다는 맥락이 되어야 합니다. 따라서 '알아차리다(notice)'라는 단어는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 19. 윗글에서 <보기>의 설명에 해당하는 한 단어를 찾아 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: One fascinating fact is that animals that hibernate also experience periods of sleep. It may come as a surprise to many, but hibernation and sleep are not the same thing at all, especially from a neurological and metabolic perspective. Hibernation is more similar to being anesthetized, where the animal is unconscious and does not experience the typical restorative processes associated with normal sleep. During hibernation, an animal's body undergoes dramatic physiological changes to conserve energy-heart rate, respiration, and metabolism all slow down to extremely low levels. This enables them to survive for extended periods on stored body fat without eating. Real hibernation involves a dramatic drop in body temperature, often down to around 32 degrees Fahrenheit, as seen in animals like ground squirrels and bats. Bears, the most iconic of wintry sleepers, don't truly hibernate in this strictest sense. They don't fit the definition of true hibernators because their body temperature stays relatively stable, dropping only a few degrees. They can also be easily awakened during this period, while true hibernators take much longer to rouse from their deep state. Therefore, what bears experience is more accurately described as torpor.

question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 development of tool making이 인류의 신체적·지적 발달에 어떻게 영향을 주었는지 서술하시오.
passage: The first human beings probably evolved in tropical regions where survival was possible without clothing. It is likely that they had very dark skin because light skin would have given little protection against the burning rays of the sun. There is a debate about whether these people spread into other parts of the world or, instead, whether people developed independently in various parts of the world. Whichever the case, it is believed that in time they became capable of spreading out from Africa, eventually to most of the world. This was probably because their physical characteristics changed. For instance, early hominids probably did not walk upright, but when they developed that ability, they could travel more efficiently. More important, perhaps, was their <u>development of tool making</u>. With tools, they could hunt other animals, so they could consume more protein and fat than their low-energy vegetarian diet would have provided. Not only their bodies but also their brains would have been changed with more energy. The brain needs lots of energy to grow. As their diet expanded, hominids could physically and intellectually expand their territory.

④ D: Individuals who were motivated by concern for others were almost four times more likely to continue giving support one year later.
⑤ E: Those who gave in order to reduce their own distress tended to cut back on helping once their emotional discomfort had been relieved.
explanation: 본문에서 타인 중심의 동기(다른 사람의 고통을 줄이기 위한 기부)를 가진 사람들은 공격 이후 오랜 시간이 지난 후에도 어려움을 겪는 피해자들에 대한 공감을 멈추지 않았다고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 시간이 흐르면서 공감을 멈췄다고 말한 B는 글의 내용을 잘못 이해하고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① A: 미국 전역의 사람들은 9.11 테러 이후 강한 정서적 자극을 경험했습니다.
② B: 타인에 대한 걱정으로 도왔던 사람들은 시간이 지나면서 결국 피해자들에 대한 공감을 멈췄습니다.
③ C: 공감에 의해 동기부여된 기부자들은 테러 이후 오랜 시간이 지난 후에도 피해자들에 대해 계속 우려를 느꼈기 때문에 지원을 계속했습니다.
④ D: 타인에 대한 걱정으로 동기부여된 사람들은 1년 후에도 계속 지원을 제공할 가능성이 거의 4배 더 높았습니다.
⑤ E: 자신의 고통을 줄이기 위해 기부한 사람들은 정서적 불편함이 해소되자 도움을 줄이는 경향이 있었습니다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 A great deal of expert knowledge is implicit knowledge에 대한 예로 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: It's often said that those who can do, can't teach the basics. <u>A great deal of expert knowledge is implicit knowledge</u>, meaning it is stored in the body or expressed through habits and not easily verbalized, compared to explicit knowledge, which is the kind that can be clearly articulated, written down, and transferred step by step. The further you progress toward mastery, the less conscious awareness you often have of the fundamentals. Experiments show that skilled golfers and wine aficionados have a hard time describing their putting and tasting techniques - even asking them to explain their approaches is enough to interfere with their performance, so they often stay on autopilot. When I first saw an elite diver do four and a half somersaults, I asked how he managed to spin so fast. His answer: "Just go up in a ball." Experts often have an intuitive understanding of a route, but they struggle to clearly express all the steps to take.\n*aficionado: 애호가 **somersault: 공중제비
options: ① A professional golfer hardly has trouble explaining his putting stroke when asked.
② Still struggling to describe adequately, a wine expert recognizes flavors by instinct.
③ Students often apply grammar rules without being consciously aware that they are doing so.
④ A cyclist maintains balance on the road, with little ability to convey the detailed mechanics of cycling.
⑤ A pianist performs with internalized skills, relying on practice that cannot easily be broken down into words.
explanation: 밑줄 친 '암묵적 지식(implicit knowledge)'은 몸에 배어 있어 말로 설명하기 어려운 지식을 의미합니다. 본문에 따르면 숙련된 골퍼들은 자신의 기술을 설명하는 데 어려움을 겪는다고 했으므로, 설명하는 데 거의 어려움이 없다는 ①번은 적절하지 않은 예시입니다.
options_translation: ① 프로 골퍼는 질문을 받았을 때 자신의 퍼팅 스트로크를 설명하는 데 거의 어려움을 겪지 않습니다.
② 적절하게 설명하는 데 여전히 어려움을 겪으면서도, 와인 전문가는 본능적으로 맛을 인식합니다.
③ 학생들은 종종 자신이 그렇게 하고 있다는 것을 의식하지 못한 채 문법 규칙을 적용합니다.
④ 자전거 타는 사람은 자전거 타기의 세부적인 역학을 전달하는 능력이 거의 없는 상태로 도로에서 균형을 유지합니다.
⑤ 피아니스트는 말로 쉽게 분해할 수 없는 연습에 의존하며, 내재화된 기술로 연주합니다.

question: 9. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 The last thing you want to be is relaxed가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: It's remarkable that positive fantasies help us relax to such an extent that it shows up in physiological tests. If you want to unwind, you can take some deep breaths, get a massage, or go for a walk - but you can also try simply closing your eyes and fantasizing about some future outcome that you might enjoy. But what about when your objective is to make your wish a reality? <u>The last thing you want to be is relaxed</u>. You want to be energized enough to get off the couch and lose those pounds or find that job or study for that test, and you want to be motivated enough to stay engaged even when the inevitable obstacles or challenges arise. The principle of "Dream it. Wish it. Do it." does not hold true, and now we know why: in dreaming it, you undercut the energy you need to do it. You put yourself in a temporary state of complete happiness, calmness - and inactivity.*physiological: 생리학적인
options: ① You should avoid staying in a state of comfort and rest.
② You can make your energy last all day long by taking proper rest.
③ Give yourself enough time to relax before getting your task started.
④ Having an optimistic view about future outcome helps cherish your dream.
⑤ You are the last one who will be relaxed after going through all the hardship.
explanation: 이 글은 낙관적인 공상이 우리를 너무 이완시켜 목표 달성에 필요한 에너지를 약화시킨다고 설명합니다. 따라서 목표를 현실로 만들고자 할 때 '가장 원치 않는 상태가 이완된 상태(The last thing you want to be is relaxed)'라는 말은, 편안함과 휴식 상태에 머무는 것을 피해야 한다는 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 당신은 편안함과 휴식의 상태에 머무르는 것을 피해야 한다.
② 적절한 휴식을 취함으로써 에너지를 하루 종일 유지할 수 있다.
③ 업무를 시작하기 전에 스스로에게 충분한 휴식 시간을 주어라.
④ 미래의 결과에 대해 낙관적인 전망을 갖는 것은 꿈을 소중히 여기는 데 도움이 된다.
⑤ 당신은 모든 고난을 겪은 후에 마지막으로 긴장을 풀 사람이다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 의미가 같은 것을 글에서 찾아 바르게 연결한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The brain is a high-energy consumer of glucose, which is its fuel. Although the brain accounts for merely 3 percent of a person's body weight, it consumes 20 percent of the available fuel. Your brain can't store fuel, however, so it has to "pay as it goes." Since your brain is incredibly adaptive, it economizes its fuel resources. Thus, during a period of high stress, it gives more attention to a singular and fixed focus on the stressful situation at hand rather than to the analysis of the nuances of a situation. You don't sit back and speculate about the meaning of life when you are stressed. Instead, you devote all your energy to trying to figure out what action to take. Sometimes, however, this shift from (A)<u>the higher-thinking parts of the brain</u> to (B)<u>the automatic and reflexive parts of the brain</u> can lead you to do something too quickly, without thinking.*glucose: 포도당
options: ① (A) trying to figure out what action to take / (B) doing something too quickly without thinking
② (A) analysis of the nuances of a situation / (B) a singular and fixed focus on the stressful situation at hand
③ (A) doing something too quickly without thinking / (B) sitting back and speculating about the meaning of life
④ (A) sitting back and speculating about the meaning of life / (B) analysis of the nuances of a situation
⑤ (A) a singular and fixed focus on the stressful station at hand / (B) trying to figure out what action to take
explanation: 지문에서 고차원적 사고 부위(A)는 '상황의 뉘앙스를 분석하는 것(analysis of the nuances of a situation)'과 연결되며, 자동적이고 반사적인 부위(B)는 스트레스 상황에서의 '단일하고 고정된 초점(a singular and fixed focus on the stressful situation at hand)'과 연결됩니다. 스트레스 상황에서는 연료를 아끼기 위해 분석(A)보다는 당면한 문제에 대한 집중(B)으로 전환이 일어난다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① (A) 어떤 행동을 취할지 알아내려고 노력하는 것 / (B) 생각 없이 너무 빨리 무언가를 하는 것
② (A) 상황의 뉘앙스에 대한 분석 / (B) 당면한 스트레스 상황에 대한 단일하고 고정된 초점
③ (A) 생각 없이 너무 빨리 무언가를 하는 것 / (B) 가만히 앉아 삶의 의미에 대해 숙고하는 것
④ (A) 가만히 앉아 삶의 의미에 대해 숙고하는 것 / (B) 상황의 뉘앙스에 대한 분석
⑤ (A) 당면한 스트레스 상황에 대한 단일하고 고정된 초점 / (B) 어떤 행동을 취할지 알아내려고 노력하는 것

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Any new or threatening situation may require us to make decisions and this requires information. ⓐ<u>It</u> is so important to communicate during a disaster that normal social barriers are often lowered. We will talk to strangers in a way we would never consider normally. The more important an event to a particular public, the more detailed and urgent the requirement for news ⓑ<u>become</u>. Without an authoritative source of facts, whether that is a newspaper or trusted broadcast station, rumours often run riot. So ⓒ<u>spreading</u> are the rumours that they soon reach everyone. Rumours start because, ⓓ<u>believe</u> their group to be in danger, people feel they should pass it on, although the rumour is unproven. For example, if a worker heard the news ⓔ<u>that</u> their employer's business was doing badly and people were going to be made redundant, they would pass that information on to colleagues.*redundant: (일시) 해고된
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 주절의 주어는 people입니다. 사람들이 자신의 집단이 위험에 처해 있다고 '믿기 때문에' 소문이 시작되는 것이므로, 주어인 people과의 능동 관계를 나타내는 분사구문 believing이 적절합니다. (참고: ⓑ는 주어 the requirement가 단수이므로 becomes로 고쳐야 하는 오류가 중복되어 보이나, 시험지의 정답 표기 및 분사구문 파트의 명확한 문법 오류인 ⓓ를 우선합니다.)

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: As you may already know, what and how you buy can be political. To whom do you want to give your money? Which companies and corporations do you value and respect? Every time you make a purchase, carefully research the corporations that are taking our money to decide if we should consider them ⓐ<u>trustworthy</u>. Do they have a record of polluting the environment, or do they have fair-trade practices and an end-of-life plan for the products they make? Are they committed to ⓑ<u>bringing</u> about good in the world? For instance, my family has found a company ⓒ<u>producing</u> recycled, plastic-packaging-free toilet paper with a social conscience. They contribute 50 percent of their profits to the construction of toilets around the world, and we're genuinely happy to spend our money on this special toilet paper each month. In any business, the customer comes first. Remember ⓓ<u>that</u> the corporate world is built on, and that you, as a consumer, have the power to vote with your wallet. Encourage companies to embrace healthier and more sustainable practices with every purchase you choose ⓔ<u>to make</u>.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓓ의 that은 뒤에 'the corporate world is built on'이라는 불완전한 절(전치사 on의 목적어가 없음)이 이어지고 있으므로, 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what으로 바뀌어야 합니다. 문맥상 '기업 세상이 무엇을 기반으로 세워졌는지를 기억하라'는 의미가 되어야 합니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The concern about how we appear to others can be seen in children, though work by the psychologist Ervin Staub suggests that the effect may vary with age. In a study where children heard another child in distress, young children (kindergarten through second grade) were more likely to help the child in distress when with another child than when alone. But for older children - in fourth and sixth grade - the effect reversed: they were less likely to help a child in distress when they were with a peer than when they were alone. Staub suggested that younger children might feel more comfortable acting when they have the company of a peer, whereas older children might _______________ _______________________________________. Staub noted that "older children seemed to discuss the distress sounds less and to react to them less openly than younger children." In other words, the older children were deliberately putting on a poker face in front of their peers.
options: ① prefer those who stand out but are eager to help others in need
② feel proud of themselves when their friends recognize their good
③ be affected by what their peers do for other children and follow it
④ be comfortable with those who are their age rather than with older people
⑤ hold back because of the anxiety about how they are viewed by their friends
explanation: 이 글은 타인에게 어떻게 보이는지에 대한 관심이 연령에 따라 도움 행동에 미치는 영향을 설명합니다. 어린 아이들은 친구와 함께 있을 때 더 잘 돕지만, 나이가 든 아이들은 친구 앞에서 평정심을 유지하려 노력하며(poker face) 도움 행동을 덜 합니다. 이는 친구들에게 자신이 어떻게 보일지에 대한 우려 때문이므로, 빈칸에는 친구들의 시선에 대한 불안으로 인해 행동을 주저한다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 두드러지지만 어려움에 처한 다른 사람들을 돕고자 열망하는 사람들을 선호할 수 있다
② 친구들이 자신의 선행을 알아줄 때 자신을 자랑스럽게 느낄 수 있다
③ 또래들이 다른 아이들을 위해 하는 일에 영향을 받아 그것을 따를 수 있다
④ 나이 든 사람들보다 자신과 나이가 같은 사람들과 있을 때 편안함을 느낄 수 있다
⑤ 친구들에게 어떻게 보일지에 대한 불안감 때문에 (도움을) 주저할 수 있다

question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There is little doubt that we are driven by the sell-by date. Once an item is past that date it goes into the waste stream, further increasing its carbon footprint. Remember those items have already travelled hundreds of miles to reach the shelves and once they go into waste they start a new carbon mile journey. But we all make our own judgement about sell-by dates; those brought up during the Second World War are often scornful of the terrible waste they believe such caution encourages. The manufacturer of the food has a view when making or growing something that by the time the product reaches the shelves it has already been travelling for so many days and possibly many miles. The manufacturer then decides that a product can reasonably be consumed within say 90 days and 90 days minus so many days for travelling gives the sell-by date. But ___________________________________, and this explains why people differ widely in deciding whether to keep or discard food. It would seem to make sense not to buy large packs of perishable goods but non-perishable items may become cost-effective.*sell-by date: 판매 유효 기한 **scornful: 경멸하는
options: ① not everyone needs to check the sell-by date
② it's up to each person to determine where to buy food
③ the question of whether it becomes toxic lies in personal judgement
④ it is necessary for consumers to ask manufacturers to lengthen the expiration period
⑤ whether it becomes environmentally harmful is something each individual can decide
explanation: 이 글은 판매 유효 기한(sell-by date)이 제품의 폐기 여부를 결정하는 주된 요인이지만, 사람마다 그 기한을 대하는 태도가 다르다는 점을 지적합니다. 빈칸 뒤의 '이것이 사람들이 음식을 보관할지 버릴지 결정할 때 크게 다른 이유를 설명해준다'는 문장을 통해, 빈칸에는 음식이 상했는지(독성이 생겼는지) 여부가 개인의 판단에 달려 있다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 모든 사람이 판매 유효 기한을 확인할 필요는 없다
② 어디에서 음식을 살지 결정하는 것은 각 개인의 몫이다
③ 그것이 독성이 생기는지의 문제는 개인의 판단에 달려 있다
④ 소비자가 제조업체에게 유효 기간을 연장해 달라고 요청하는 것이 필요하다
⑤ 그것이 환경적으로 해로운지 여부는 각 개인이 결정할 수 있는 것이다

question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 9월 21번]
passage: In today's information age, in many companies and on many teams, the objective is no longer error prevention and replicability. On the contrary, it's creativity, speed, and keenness. In the industrial era, the goal was to minimize variation. But in creative companies today, maximizing variation is more essential. In these situations, the biggest risk isn't making a mistake or losing consistency. (A) It's failing to attract top talent, to invent new products, or to change direction quickly when the environment shifts. (B) Consistency and repeatability are more likely to suppress fresh thinking than to bring your company profit. (C) A lot of little mistakes, while sometimes painful, help the organization learn quickly and are a critical part of the innovation cycle. (D) In this situation, a rule itself is no longer the best answer. (E) Don't go for a symphony; build a jazz band instead.
insertion_sentence: They may, for instance, lead managers to overlook a novel idea simply because it does not match conventional routines.
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'They'는 (B) 문장에 언급된 'Consistency and repeatability(일관성과 반복 가능성)'를 가리킵니다. 일관성과 반복 가능성이 새로운 사고를 억제하고, 관리자들이 참신한 아이디어를 간과하게 만든다는 내용이 연결되어야 하므로 (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 9월 33번]
passage: Over the last few centuries, humanity's collective prosperity has skyrocketed, as technological progress has made us far wealthier than ever before. (A) To share out those riches, almost all societies have settled upon the market mechanism, rewarding people in various ways for the work that they do and the things that they own. (B) But rising inequality, itself often driven by technology, has started to put that mechanism under strain. (C) Today, markets already provide immense rewards to some people but leave many others with very little.And now, technological unemployment threatens to become a more radical version of the same story, taking place in the particular market we rely upon the most: the labor market. (E) As that market begins to break down, more and more people will be in danger of not receiving a share of society's prosperity at all.
insertion_sentence: Iin such a scenario, automation could accelerate the decline of certain industries and roles, forcing even competent workers into sudden job loss.
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'such a scenario'는 바로 앞 문장에서 언급된 'technological unemployment(기술적 실업)'의 상황을 구체적으로 설명하고 있습니다. 자동화가 특정 산업의 쇠퇴를 가속화하고 노동 시장을 붕괴시킨다는 흐름이 이어져야 하므로 (E) 위치가 정답입니다.

question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 38번]
passage: There are two types of contagion: viral contagion and behavioral contagion.
ordered_passages: (A) In contrast, the visible symptoms of illness such as cough or fever do not attract people. Another difference is that behavioral contagion is not always negative - as in the case of solar installations whereas viral contagion is almost always a bad thing as in the case of smoking.

(B) Proximity affects more spread of contagion in both, though. People are more likely to drink excessively when they spend more time in the company of heavy drinkers. Similarly, people in close or extended proximity to others infected by a virus are themselves more likely to become infected.

(C) They differ in that visibility encourages behavioral contagion but discourages the spread of infectious diseases. Solar panels that are visible from the stress, for instance, are more likely to stimulate neighboring installation.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 두 가지 전염(바이러스 전염과 행동 전염)을 소개한 후, (C)에서 그 둘의 차이점인 '가시성(visibility)'에 대해 언급하기 시작합니다. (A)는 (C)에서 언급한 차이점을 'In contrast'를 통해 구체화하고 또 다른 차이점을 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 'though'와 'Proximity'를 사용하여 두 전염의 공통점(근접성의 영향)을 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Much of human thought is designed to screen out information and to sort the rest into a manageable condition. The inflow of data from our senses could create an overwhelming chaos, especially given the enormous amount of information available in culture and society.
ordered_passages: (A) Out of all the sensory impressions and possible information, it is vital to find a small amount that is most relevant to our individual needs and to organize that into a usable stock of knowledge.

(B) That is, people notice only a part of the world around them. Then, only a fraction of what they notice gets processed and stored into memory. And only part of what gets committed to memory can be retrieved.

(C) Expectancies accomplish some of this work, helping to screen out information that is irrelevant to what is expected, and focusing our attention on clear contradictions. The processes of learning and memory are marked by a steady elimination of information.
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 인간의 사고가 정보를 걸러내고 관리 가능한 상태로 분류하도록 설계되어 있음을 설명합니다. (A)에서는 모든 감각적 인상 중에서 개인적 필요에 가장 관련 있는 적은 양을 찾아 지식으로 조직하는 것이 중요하다고 언급하며 주어진 글의 내용을 구체화합니다. (C)에서는 '예상(Expectancies)'이 이러한 정보 선별 작업을 수행하며, 학습과 기억의 과정이 정보의 꾸준한 제거로 특징지어진다고 설명합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서는 'That is(즉)'로 시작하며 앞서 언급된 정보 제거의 과정을 '세상의 일부만 주목하고, 그 중 일부만 기억되며, 또 그 중 일부만 회상된다'는 말로 결론짓고 있습니다. 따라서 글의 순서는 (A)-(C)-(B)가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If you drive down a busy street, you will find many competing businesses, often right next to one another. For example, in most places a consumer in search of a quick meal has many choices, and more fast-food restaurants appear all the time. These competing firms advertise heavily. The temptation is to see advertising as driving up the price of a product without any benefit to the consumer. However, this misconception doesn't account for why firms advertise. In markets where competitors sell slightly differentiated products, advertising enables firms to inform their customers about new products and services. Yes, costs rise, but consumers also gain information to help make purchasing decisions. Consumers also benefit from added variety, and we all get a product that's pretty close to our vision of a perfect good - and no other market structure delivers that outcome.
summary_sentence: While the advertisements of the competing firms (A)__________ the price of the products and services, they are useful to consumers because they provide information about a variety of products, enabling them to select those that match their (B)__________.
options: ① raise ... prices
② lower ... interests
③ reduce ... tastes
④ increase ... preferences
⑤ promote ... incomes
explanation: 본문에서 경쟁 기업들의 광고가 비용을 상승(costs rise/driving up the price)시킨다고 언급되었으므로 (A)에는 increase가 적절합니다. 하지만 광고는 소비자들에게 정보를 제공하여 자신의 선호나 완벽한 제품에 대한 비전(vision of a perfect good)에 맞는 제품을 선택할 수 있게 하므로 (B)에는 preferences(선호)가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 올리다 ... 가격
② 낮추다 ... 관심사
③ 줄이다 ... 취향
④ 증가시키다 ... 선호도
⑤ 촉진하다 ... 소득

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
passage: It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. By "competence," I mean a cluster of qualities: smartness, the ability to get things done, wise decisions, etc. We stand a better chance of doing well at our life tasks if we surround ourselves with people who know what they're doing and have a lot to teach us. But the research evidence is paradoxical: In problem-solving groups, the participants who are considered the most competent and have the best ideas tend not to be the ones who are best liked. Why? One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, those who are too competent make us uncomfortable. They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman - and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison. If this were true, we might like people more if they reveal some evidence of fallibility. For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her better if, every once in a while, they screwed up.*fallibility: 실수를 저지르기 쉬움
summary_sentence: We favor those who (A)__________ but we tend to like them more if they (B)_________________________.
subjective_conditions: ∙(A)나는 2다너로 스ᄅ것
∙(B)나는 7다너 이내로 스ᄅ것
∙어형 밴하 어ᄇ슴
answer: (A) are competent(B) reveal some evidence of fallibility / every once in a while, screw up
explanation: 본문은 우리가 유능한(competent) 사람을 좋아하지만, 너무 완벽하면 거리감을 느끼게 되므로 가끔 실수하는 모습(fallibility/screw up)을 보일 때 더 호감을 느낀다는 내용입니다. (A)에는 '유능한' 사람을 선호한다는 의미의 'are competent'가 들어가고, (B)에는 '실수의 증거를 보여주다' 혹은 '이따금 실수하다'는 의미의 본문 문구인 'reveal some evidence of fallibility' 또는 'every once in a while, screw up'이 적절합니다. 조건에 따라 (A)는 2단어, (B)는 7단어 이내로 작성해야 합니다.

question: 21. 윗글의 (A)에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 그대로 쓰시오.
passage:
The "jolt" of caffeine does wear off. Caffeine is removed from your system by an enzyme within your liver, which gradually degrades it over time. Based in large part on genetics, some people have a more efficient version of the enzyme that (A)__________ caffeine, allowing the liver to rapidly clear it from the bloodstream. These rare individuals can drink an espresso with dinner and fall fast asleep at midnight without a problem. Others, however, have a slower-acting version of the enzyme. It takes far longer for their system to eliminate the same amount of caffeine. As a result, they are very sensitive to caffeine's effects. One cup of tea or coffee in the morning will last much of the day, and should they have a second cup, even early in the afternoon, they will find it difficult to fall asleep in the evening. Aging also alters the speed of caffeine clearance: the older we are, (B)____________________, and thus (C)____________________ in later life.

*jolt: 기운을 북돋우는 것 **enzyme: 효소
explanation: 본문 앞부분에 언급된 'an enzyme ... which gradually degrades it over time'이라는 문장을 통해 효소가 카페인을 분해(degrade)한다는 점을 알 수 있습니다. 따라서 (A)가 포함된 관계대명사 절에서도 선행사인 효소(enzyme)가 카페인을 분해한다는 문맥이 되어야 하므로 'degrades'가 정답입니다.

question: 22. 위글의 (B)와 (C)에 들어갈 표현을 <조건>에 맞게 각각 문장으로 완성하시오.
passage:
The "jolt" of caffeine does wear off. Caffeine is removed from your system by an enzyme within your liver, which gradually degrades it over time. Based in large part on genetics, some people have a more efficient version of the enzyme that (A)__________ caffeine, allowing the liver to rapidly clear it from the bloodstream. Aging also alters the speed of caffeine clearance: the older we are, (B)____________________, and thus (C)____________________ in later life.

*jolt: 기운을 북돋우는 것 **enzyme: 효소
subjective_conditions: - <보기단어>의 단어만을 각각 한 번씩 모두 사용할 것

vocabulary_box: (B) it / our system / caffeine / for / take / long / the / remove / to
(C) more / caffeine's sleep-disrupting / to / become / the / sensitive / we / influence
answer:

(C): the more sensitive we become to caffeine's sleep-disrupting influence
explanation: 내용상 나이가 들수록 카페인 제거 속도가 느려지는 것을 설명해야 하므로, 'the + 비교급, the + 비교급' 구문을 사용하여 문장을 완성합니다. (B)의 경우 'A가 ~하는 데 시간이 걸린다'는 의미의 'it takes for A to do' 구조를 활용하되, 주어가 3인칭 단수인 it이므로 take를 takes로 변형합니다. (C)는 원형 그대로를 활용하여 'the more sensitive we become ~'의 어순으로 작성합니다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 요지를 작성하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 완성하시오.
passage: One well-known shift took place when the accepted view - that the Earth was the center of the universe - changed to one where we understood that we are only inhabitants on one planet orbiting the Sun. With each person who grasped the solar system view, it became easier for the next person to do so. So it is with the notion that the world revolves around the human economy. This is slowly being replaced by the view that the economy is a part of the larger system of material flows that connect all living things. When this perspective shifts into place, it will be obvious that our economic well-being requires that we account for, and respond to, factors of ecological health. Unfortunately we do not have a century or two to make the change. By clarifying the nature of the old and new perspectives, and by identifying actions on which we might cooperate to move the process along, we can help accelerate the shift.
summary_sentence: We need to (A)_______________________ and that our (B)_______________________, which shows the need for a shift in perspective.
subjective_conditions: - <보기단어>의 단어를 각각 한 번씩 모두 사용할 것
- <보기단어>에 없는 4단어를 추가하여 사용할 것
- 가목적어(it)와 진목적어(that절)가 포함된 문장이 되도록 작성할 것
- 단어의 어형 변화는 없을 것
answer: (A): make it clear that the economy is a part of ecological systems (B): economic well-being depends on the environment
explanation: 가목적어와 진목적어 문장 구조를 활용하여 (A)를 작성하면 "make it clear that the economy is a part of ecological systems"가 됩니다. 이때 보기의 단어 외에 추가된 4단어는 it, that, is, on입니다. (A)는 경제가 생태계의 일부임을 명확히 한다는 내용을 담고 있으며, (B)는 경제적 안녕이 환경에 달려 있다는(depends on) 내용을 완성하여 전체적인 요지를 형성합니다.

question: 2. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: I suspect fungi are a little more forward "thinking" than their larger partners. Among trees, each species fights other species. Let's assume the beeches native to Central Europe could emerge victorious in most forests there. (A) Would this really be an advantage? (B) What would happen if a new pathogen came along that infected most of the beeches and killed them? (C) In that case, wouldn't it be more advantageous if there were a certain number of other species around - oaks, maples, or firs - that would continue to grow and provide the shade needed for a new generation of young beeches to sprout and grow up? (D) Because fungi are also very dependent on stable conditions, they support other species underground and protect them from complete collapse to ensure that one species of tree doesn't manage to dominate. (E)
insertion_sentence: Diversity provides security for ancient forests.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)

explanation: 제시된 문장 "Diversity provides security for ancient forests(다양성은 오래된 숲에 안정성을 제공한다)"는 (C) 이전 문장에서 제기된 의문들(특정 종이 독점했을 때의 위험성)에 대한 결론이자, (C) 문장에서 설명하는 '다른 종들이 함께 자라는 것이 유리하다'는 내용을 요약하는 핵심 문장입니다. 따라서 다양성의 이점을 정리하고 그 구체적 기작(균류의 역할)이 시작되기 전인 (D) 자리가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 3. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Managers frequently try to play psychologist, to "figure out" why an employee has acted in a certain way. However, when dealing with a problem area, in particular, remember that it is not the person who is bad, but the actions exhibited on the job. Avoid making suggestions to employees about personal traits they should change; instead suggest more acceptable ways of performing. For example, instead of focusing on a person's "unreliability," a manager might focus on the fact that the employee "has been late to work seven times this month." It is difficult for employees to change (A)_______________; it is usually much easier for them to change (B)_______________.

question: 4. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: If cooking is as central to human identity, biology, and culture as the biological anthropologist Richard Wrangham suggests, it stands to reason that the decline of cooking in our time would have serious consequences for modern life, and so it has. Are they all bad? Not at all. The outsourcing of much of the work of cooking to corporations has relieved women of what has traditionally been their exclusive responsibility for feeding the family, making it easier for them to work outside the home and have careers. ① It has headed off many of the domestic conflicts that such a large shift in gender roles and family dynamics was bound to spark. ② It has relieved other pressures in the household, including longer workdays and overscheduled children, and saved us time that we can now invest in other pursuits. ③ While the investment has made some families wealthy, it has ultimately contributed to widening the gap between the rich and the poor. ④ It has also allowed us to diversify our diets substantially, making it possible even for people with no cooking skills and little money to enjoy a whole different cuisine. ⑤ All that's required is a microwave.
explanation: 이 글은 요리 업무를 기업에 아웃소싱함으로써 얻게 된 긍정적인 사회적 변화들(여성의 가사 부담 경감, 시간 확보, 식단의 다양화 등)을 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ③번 문장은 갑자기 경제적 빈부 격차의 심화라는 주제를 다루고 있으므로, 요리의 외주화라는 핵심 주제와 어울리지 않는 무관한 문장입니다.

question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 의미하는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은? [2.9점]

explanation: 어법상 어색한 부분은 ⓑ, ⓔ, ⓖ 총 3개입니다.ⓑ: 뒤에 완전한 문장이 오므로 관계대명사 which 대신 관계부사 where나 전치사+관계대명사인 in which가 적절합니다.ⓔ: 선행사 material flows가 존재하므로, 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사인 what 대신 주격 관계대명사 that이나 which가 쓰여야 합니다.ⓖ: cooperate는 자동사로 쓰이거나 'cooperate in/on' 등의 전치사를 수반합니다. 뒤에 이어지는 문장이 action을 목적어로 취하지 않으므로, 'in which' 또는 'with which'로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers of which it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease to form, while sufficient fibers remain undamaged for the material not to crack and fall apart. Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to ⓐ<u>resist</u> being pulled apart, but it can also be torn easily and accurately along the crease if a point of weakness ─ a small, initial tear ─ is opened up. This winning combination of mechanical properties ⓑ<u>allows</u> it to assume the shape of any object through creasing and folding ─ hence the art of origami. There are ⓒ<u>many</u> materials as good: metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult. Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, in which case it ⓓ<u>lacks</u> the rigidity required of a good wrapping material. So it is its ability to hold a crease while remaining stiff that makes paper uniquely ⓔ<u>suited</u> to this purpose.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 종이의 기계적 특성이 접기에 매우 적합하다는 내용의 지문입니다. 금속 박(metal foils)은 접기 조절이 어렵고, 플라스틱 시트(Plastic sheeting)는 주름을 유지하지 못하거나 강성이 부족하다고 설명하며 종이만이 가지는 독특한 장점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '종이만큼 좋은 재료가 많다'는 ⓒ many는 문맥상 '거의 없다'는 의미의 few로 고쳐야 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 저항하다
② 허용하다/가능하게 하다
③ 많은
④ 부족하다
⑤ 적합한

question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
passage: Mother cats can tell which kittens belong to them ─ when litters are mixed up they use their kittens' scent to ⓐ<u>distinguish</u> them from offspring of other mothers. Despite this, when faced with a selection of kittens who have wandered from the nest, her own and others that aren't hers, a mother cat ⓑ<u>appears</u> to favor her own offspring when retrieving them. The reason for this is uncertain, although distress vocalizations from kittens that are lost from their nest are known to be very powerful, so it may just be ⓒ<u>hard</u> for the mother to resist retrieving them, regardless of whether they are hers. In the wild, a squeaking kitten out in the open is likely to ⓓ<u>attract</u> predators, which is bad news for any other kittens around it. A rapid rescue of any crying kitten would be a ⓔ<u>good</u> strategy to prevent them from drawing unwanted attention.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 지문에 따르면 어미 고양이는 자신의 새끼와 다른 새끼를 구별할 수 있음에도 불구하고(Despite this), 둥지를 떠난 새끼들을 데려올 때는 자신의 새끼인지 여부와 상관없이 울음소리에 반응하여 데려오는 경향이 있다고 설명합니다. 따라서 자신의 새끼를 '편애하는 것처럼 보인다'는 ⓑ appears는 문맥상 '편애하지 않는 것처럼 보인다(fails to appear / does not appear)'로 수정되어야 논리적으로 자연스럽습니다.
options_translation: ① 구별하다
② ~처럼 보이다
③ 어려운
④ 유인하다/끌어들이다
⑤ 좋은

question: 9. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Many animals pursue a mixed strategy of accumulating both body fat and food, which leads one to ask, "What are the relative advantages and disadvantages of these two forms of energy storage?"
ordered_passages: (A) Maximum fat deposition increases with body mass whereas maximum food storage is not constrained by body size. This means that animals, especially small animals, can accumulate much greater energy reserves in the form of stored food than they can in the form of body fat. Further, stored food is more economical than body fat because fat contributes to body mass, and metabolic rate increases with body mass. In other words, there is a metabolic expense to maintaining fat.

(B) Excessive fat accumulations may also have a negative effect on an animal's ability to avoid predators. And, if maintaining a high body temperature is advantageous, animals might be expected to accumulate more energy in the form of a food store than as body fat. On the other hand, stored food may rot over time, may be removed by robbers, or may simply be lost. Many animals must expend energy managing and protecting their food stores.

(C) Eating food and converting it to fat avoids these types of losses and the energetic costs of managing stored food. A large accumulation of body fat adds to an animal's fasting capacity, especially large animals, permitting some animals to enter prolonged dormancy in the relative security of a hibernaculum. Thus, both fat accumulation and food storage have some decided advantages.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 체지방과 음식 저장이라는 두 가지 에너지 저장 형태의 장단점에 대해 질문을 던집니다. (A)에서는 체질량에 따른 지방 저장의 제한과 음식 저장의 경제적 이점(대사 비용)을 설명하며 시작합니다. (B)에서는 과도한 지방 축적이 포식자 회피 능력에 주는 부정적 영향과 음식 저장의 단점(부패, 도난)을 언급합니다. (C)에서는 음식을 먹어 지방으로 전환하는 것이 저장된 음식을 관리하는 비용을 피하게 해주며 동면 등의 장점이 있음을 결론지으며 마무리하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 10. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The brain is a high-energy consumer of glucose, which is its fuel.
ordered_passages: (A) Although the brain accounts for merely 3 percent of a person's body weight, it consumes 20 percent of the available fuel. Your brain can't store fuel, however, so it has to "pay as it goes." Since your brain is incredibly adaptive, it economizes its fuel resources.

(B) Instead, you devote all your energy to trying to figure out what action to take. Sometimes, however, this shift from the higher-thinking parts of the brain to the automatic and reflexive parts of the brain can lead you to do something too quickly, without thinking.

(C) Thus, during a period of high stress, it shifts away from the analysis of the nuances of a situation to a singular and fixed focus on the stressful situation at hand. You don't sit back and speculate about the meaning of life when you are stressed.
explanation: 주어진 문장에서 뇌의 연료인 포도당 소비를 언급한 후, (A)에서 뇌의 높은 에너지 소비량과 연료 저장 불가 특성, 그리고 연료 절약의 필요성을 설명합니다. (C)에서 스트레스 상황 시 뇌가 연료를 아끼기 위해 복잡한 분석 대신 당면한 상황에 집중하도록 전환한다는 내용을 연결하고, (B)에서 그 결과(대신에)로 사고 대신 행동에 에너지를 쏟으며 때로는 성급한 결정을 내리게 된다는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.8점]
passage: In 2006, researchers conducted a study on the motivations for helping after the September 11th terrorist attacks against the United States. (A) In the study, they found that individuals who gave money, blood, goods, or other forms of assistance because of other-focused motives (giving to reduce another's discomfort) were almost four times more likely to still be giving support one year later than those whose original motivation was to reduce personal distress. (B) The events of September 11th emotionally affected people throughout the United States. (C) Those who gave to reduce their own distress reduced their emotional arousal with their initial gift, discharging that emotional distress. (D) However, those who gave to reduce others' distress did not stop empathizing with victims who continued to struggle long after the attacks. (E)
insertion_sentence: This effect likely stems from differences in emotional arousal.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: (A) 뒤의 문장에서 개인적 고통을 줄이려는 동기보다 타인 중심 동기로 돕는 사람들이 더 오랫동안 도움을 지속한다는 결과(This effect)를 제시한 후, 주어진 문장에서 이 효과가 '정서적 각성의 차이'에서 기인한다고 설명하는 것이 적절합니다. 이후 (C)와 (D)에서 각각의 동기에 따른 정서적 작용의 차이를 구체적으로 설명하고 있습니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: If you drive down a busy street, you will find many competing businesses, often right next to one another. (A) For example, in most places a consumer in search of a quick meal has many choices, and more fast-food restaurants appear all the time. (B) These competing firms advertise heavily. (C) The temptation is to see advertising as driving up the price of a product without any benefit to the consumer. (D) In markets where competitors sell slightly differentiated products, advertising enables firms to inform their customers about new products and services. (E) Yes, costs rise, but consumers also gain information to help make purchasing decisions. Consumers also benefit from added variety, and we all get a product that's pretty close to our vision of a perfect good ─ and no other market structure delivers that outcome.
insertion_sentence: However, this misconception doesn't account for why firms advertise.
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'this misconception'은 (C) 문장에서 언급한 '광고를 소비자에게 아무런 이익 없이 제품 가격을 올리는 것'으로 보는 통념을 가리킵니다. (D) 문장부터는 광고가 기업이 소비자에게 정보를 제공하게 하여 소비자에게 도움이 된다는 실제 광고의 역할을 설명하기 시작하므로, 반전이 일어나는 (D) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. By "competence," I mean a cluster of qualities: smartness, the ability to get things done, wise decisions, etc. We stand a better chance of doing well at our life tasks if we surround ourselves with people who know what they're doing and have a lot to teach us. But the research evidence is paradoxical: In problem-solving groups, the participants who are considered the most competent and have the best ideas tend not to be the ones who are best liked. Why? One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, those who are too competent make us uncomfortable. They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman - and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison. If this were true, we might like people more if they ____________________________. For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her better if, every once in a while, they screwed up.
options: ① reveal some evidence of fallibility
② are deemed the most competent athlete
③ exhibit mathematical work free from fallibility
④ have something to teach us in their own field
⑤ seem unapproachable, distant and superhuman
explanation: 글의 맥락상 너무 유능한 사람은 다른 사람들에게 거리감을 느끼게 하고 불편하게 만들 수 있으므로, 가끔 실수를 하거나 완벽하지 않은 모습을 보일 때 사람들이 더 호감을 느낀다는 내용이 적절합니다. 마지막 예시의 'screwed up(실수하다)'과 상응하는 표현은 ①번 '실수할 수 있음(틀릴 수 있음)의 증거를 보여주다'입니다.
options_translation: ① 실수를 저지를 수 있다는 증거를 보여준다
② 가장 유능한 운동선수로 여겨진다
③ 오류가 없는 수학적 결과물을 보여준다
④ 자신의 분야에서 우리에게 가르쳐 줄 것이 있다
⑤ 다가가기 어렵고, 멀리 느껴지며 초인적으로 보인다

question: 16. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 낱말에 대한 의미가 올바르게 서술된 것은 모두 몇 개인가?
passage: The irony of early democracy in Europe is that it ⓐ<u>thrived(=to decrease in quality, quantity, or importance)</u> and prospered precisely because European rulers for a very long time were remarkably weak. For more than a millennium after the fall of Rome, European rulers lacked the ability to ⓑ<u>assess(=to pay no attention to)</u> what their people were producing and to ⓒ<u>levy(=to officially impose or collect a fee, or charge by an authority)</u> substantial taxes based on this. The most striking way to illustrate European weakness is to show how little revenue they ⓓ<u>collected(=to spread or give out something to a number of people or places)</u>. Europeans would eventually develop strong systems of revenue collection, but it took them an awfully long time to do so. In medieval times, and for part of the early modern era, Chinese emperors and Muslim caliphs were able to ⓔ<u>extract(=to put something into something else)</u> much more of economic production than any European ruler with the exception of small city-states.
options: ① 1개
② 2개
③ 3개
④ 4개
⑤ 5개
explanation: 각 단어의 정의를 살펴보면 다음과 같습니다.ⓐ thrive: 번창하다. 제시된 정의(=to decrease...)는 '쇠퇴하다'를 의미하므로 틀림.ⓑ assess: 평가하다/산정하다. 제시된 정의(=to pay no attention to)는 '주의를 기울이지 않다'이므로 틀림.ⓒ levy: (세금 등을) 부과하다/징수하다. 제시된 정의(=to officially impose or collect a fee...)는 정확한 정의임.ⓓ collect: 수집하다/징수하다. 제시된 정의(=to spread or give out...)는 '배포하다'이므로 틀림.ⓔ extract: 추출하다/뽑아내다. 제시된 정의(=to put something into...)는 '넣다'이므로 틀림.따라서 올바르게 서술된 것은 ⓒ 하나뿐입니다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Rebels may think they're rebels, but clever marketers influence them just like the rest of us. Saying, "Everyone is doing it" may turn some people off from an idea. These people will look for alternatives, ⓐ<u>which</u> (if cleverly planned) can be exactly what a marketer or persuader wants you to believe. If I want you ⓑ<u>to consider</u> an idea, and know you strongly reject popular opinion in favor of maintaining your independence and uniqueness, I would present the majority option first, which you would reject in favor of my actual preference. We are often ⓒ<u>trick</u> when we try to maintain a position of defiance. People use this reversal to make us "independently" ⓓ<u>choose</u> an option which suits their purposes. Some brands have taken full effect of our defiance towards the mainstream and positioned ⓔ<u>themselves</u> as rebels; which has created even stronger brand loyalty.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'We'이고, 우리가 속임수를 쓰는 것이 아니라 마케터에 의해 '속임을 당하는' 수동의 관계이므로 과거분사 형태인 'tricked'가 되어야 합니다. be동사(are) 뒤에 동사원형 trick이 올 수 없습니다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It's often said that those who can't do, teach. It would be more accurate to say that those who can do, can't teach the basics. A great deal of expert knowledge is implicit, not explicit. The further you progress toward mastery, the less conscious awareness you often have of the fundamentals. Experiments show that skilled golfers and wine aficionados have a hard time describing their putting and tasting techniques - even asking them to explain their approaches is enough to interfere with their performance, so they often stay on autopilot. When I first saw an elite diver do four and a half somersaults, I asked how he managed to spin so fast. His answer: "Just go up in a ball." Experts often have an intuitive understanding of a route, but they struggle to clearly express all the steps to take. Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage.
options: ① limits of controlled learning in sports
② superiority of expert skills over beginners
③ challenges of acquiring skills as an elite diver
④ experts' difficulty in teaching fundamentals
⑤ explicit behavioral patterns of elite performers
explanation: 이 글은 전문가가 될수록 그 지식이 암묵적(implicit)으로 변하며, 무의식적으로 행동이 수행되기 때문에 오히려 초보자나 타인에게 기초적인 단계를 명시적으로 설명하거나 가르치는 데 어려움을 겪는다는 내용을 담고 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 스포츠에서 통제된 학습의 한계
② 초보자에 대한 전문가 기술의 우월성
③ 엘리트 다이버로서 기술을 습득하는 과정의 도전
④ 전문가들이 기초를 가르칠 때 겪는 어려움
⑤ 엘리트 수행자들의 명시적인 행동 패턴

question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Everything in the world exists on a continuum, whether in speed, size, or any other possible descriptor you could think of.
ordered_passages: (A) I call this resulting damage "the borderline effect." The examples are endless. Someone's IQ is 69 and someone else's is 70 ─ but only the score of 70 is deemed to be within the range of normal. We don't have to be statisticians to know there is not a meaningful difference between 69 and 70.(B) Still, we create and mindlessly adopt sharp distinctions, and those distinctions change lives far more dramatically than marginal differences ever do. Indeed, all differences are arbitrary, but drawing hard lines between categories hides this arbitrariness and can be severely damaging.(C) Yet once the person with the lower score is labeled "cognitively impaired," his or her life will unfold differently than the person with a one-point advantage.
explanation: 주어진 문장에서 세상의 모든 것은 연속체(continuum) 상에 존재한다고 언급합니다. (B)에서는 '그럼에도 불구하고(Still)' 우리가 뚜렷한 구분을 만들고 이것이 손상을 줄 수 있다는 일반적인 문제 제기를 합니다. (A)에서 이 손상을 '경계 효과(borderline effect)'라 명명하며 구체적인 예시인 IQ 점수(69와 70)를 도입합니다. (C)에서 그 점수 차이(1점 차이)로 인해 붙여지는 '인지 장애'라는 라벨이 삶을 다르게 만든다는 구체적인 결론으로 마무리됩니다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The term "anchoring" was introduced by Roland Barthes who observed that text is often used next to images (his focus was on photographs) to confine meaning. Of all possible literal or implied interpretations an image could elicit, text would point the viewer towards a desired, specific direction. In advertising, as Barthes argues, the symbolic message does not guide identification but interpretation. The viewer is not asked to recognize what they see but to understand why they see it and what it means to them. By combining images with text, advertising produces symbolic meaning that is accurate and specific on the one hand, richer on the other, thus adding depth and eliminating breadth of rational and emotional interpretations. The headline or tagline of an ad directs the reader through the intended meanings of the image, so that the reader avoids some and receives others. It "remote-controls" the reader towards a meaning chosen in advance.
summary_sentence: Roland Barthes' concept of "anchoring" shows that (A) ___________ images with text - especially in advertising - guides viewers toward specific interpretations by (B) ___________ the range of possible meanings.
options: ① contrasting - widening
② contrasting - reducing
③ combining - narrowing
④ combining - broadening
⑤ confusing - defining
explanation: 로랑 바르트의 '정박(anchoring)' 개념은 텍스트를 이미지와 결합하여(combining), 이미지가 가질 수 있는 막연하고 다양한 해석의 가능성들을 배제하고 시청자를 의도된 특정한 방향으로 유도하며 의미의 범위를 좁히는(narrowing) 역할을 한다는 내용입니다. 특히 광고에서 이미지와 텍스트의 결합은 상징적 메시지를 더 정확하고 깊이 있게 전달하는 수단이 됩니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '결합하는 것', (B)에는 '좁히는 것'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
passage: All human cultures mark the passing of time by the differences they observe in the world around them. ① Our choice of which differences to mark depends firstly on what we can observe and secondly on what is important in our lives. ② How we mark the differences ─ the shapes of our calendars and our rituals ─ depends on the connections we make between those two things. ③ In the agricultural society of pre-modern Europe, where higher latitudes make the seasons easily observable, it was natural to monitor the solar cycle. ④ That did not make it inevitable that Islam would use a lunar calendar and Roman Christianity a solar one, but political and religious decisions were made from options limited by geography and lifestyle, filtered through tradition. ⑤
insertion_sentence: Conversely, among the largely nomadic peoples of Arabia, for whom seasonal changes were less significant, the lunar calendar was a more sensible choice.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장은 'Conversely(반대로)'로 시작하며, 계절 변화가 중요하지 않았던 아라비아 유목 민족들에게는 태음력(lunar calendar)이 더 합리적인 선택이었다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 이는 앞서 언급된 '계절 변화가 뚜렷한 농경 사회인 유럽에서 태양력을 따르는 것이 자연스러웠다'는 내용과 대조를 이룹니다. 또한 ④번 뒤의 문장에서 '이슬람(아라비아)은 태음력을, 로마 가톨릭(유럽)은 태양력을 사용하게 된 것'이 지리적 조건을 반영한 결정이었음을 설명하고 있으므로, 주어진 문장은 ④번 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Dictionary definitions are constantly revised to keep up with our changing uses and knowledge. In Roman times, "addicts" were people who were unable to pay their debts and gave themselves as slaves to their creditors. The word eventually came to be associated with drug dependency: one becomes a slave to one's addiction. The word "husband" originally referred to being a homeowner; it had nothing to do with being married. But because owning your own property made it more likely you'd find a mate, the word eventually came to mean a male who has been wed. On November 5th, 1605, Guy Fawkes tried to blow up the British Parliament. He was captured and put to death. Loyalists burned his effigy, which they nicknamed the "guy." Centuries later, the word lost its negative connotation and a musical named Guys and Dolls ran on Broadway. In American slang, bad means good, cool means great, and wicked means excellent. If you could transport yourself one hundred years into the future, you'd find yourself confused by your great-grandchildren's speech because language itself is an ever-changing reflection of human invention.
options: ① The Psychological Impact of Changing Language Usage
② The Influence of Roman Culture on English Words
③ The Decline of Proper English in Youth Slang
④ A Guide to Modern English Grammar Rules
⑤ The Evolution of Word Meanings
explanation: 이 글은 시간이 흐르며 단어의 의미가 어떻게 변화해 왔는지를 구체적인 사례(addict, husband, guy 등)를 통해 설명하고 있습니다. 언어는 인간 사회의 변화와 발명품들을 반영하는 유기체와 같아서, 단어의 정의는 과거부터 지금까지 사용법과 지식의 변화에 따라 끊임없이 개정되어 왔다는 것이 핵심 내용입니다. 따라서 '단어 의미의 진화(The Evolution of Word Meanings)'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 변화하는 언어 사용의 심리학적 영향
② 로마 문화가 영어 단어에 미친 영향
③ 청소년 슬랭에서 적절한 영어의 쇠퇴
④ 현대 영어 문법 규칙 가이드
⑤ 단어 의미의 진화

question: 23. 다음 글에서 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 밑줄 친 우리말을 영작하시오.
passage: My two girls grew up without challenges with respect to development and social interaction. My son Benjamin, however, was quite delayed. <u>그는 다른 아이들과 잘 어울리지 않고, 언제나 그가 무엇을 잘못하고 있는지(잘못했능지) 궁금해 하면서, 그의 어린 시절 동안 고생했다</u>. He was teased by the other children and frowned upon by a number of unsympathetic adults. But his Grade 1 teacher was a wonderful, caring person who took the time to ask why Benjamin behaved the way he did. The teacher was determined to understand Benjamin and to accept him as he was. One day he came home with a note from his teacher. He suggested I go to the school library. They were having a sale, and he thought my son would like one of the books. I couldn't go for a couple of days and was concerned I'd missed the opportunity. When I finally went to the school, his teacher told me that the sale had ended but that the library had saved the book for my little boy.
subjective_conditions: 분사구문을 활용하여 22단어로 작성할 것.
children / fit / struggled / his / the other / wonder / wrong / was / every turn / and / do (위의 단어를 모두 사용하되, 필요시 단어의 형태를 바꿀 것)
다음 단어는 형태를 바꾸지 말고 두 번씩 사용할 것: he
다음 전치사를 사용할 것: with / at / in / through
answer: He struggled through his childhood, not fitting in with the other children and wondering what he was doing wrong at every turn.
explanation: 주어진 우리말 '그는 ~ 고생했다'를 주절로 삼고, '잘 어울리지 않고', '궁금해 하면서' 부분을 분사구문(not fitting ..., wondering ...)으로 표현하여 영작합니다. 'through his childhood'는 어린 시절 동안, 'at every turn'은 언제나/늘 이라는 의미로 사용되었습니다.

question: 24. 다음 글에서 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 밑줄 친 우리말을 영작하시오.
passage: The concern about how we appear to others can be seen in children, though work by the psychologist Ervin Staub suggests that the effect may vary with age. In a study where children heard another child in distress, young children (kindergarten through second grade) were more likely to help the child in distress when with another child than when alone. But for older children - in fourth and sixth grade - the effect reversed: they were less likely to help a child in distress when they were with a peer than when they were alone. <u>Staub는 더 어린 아이들은 그들이 또래와 함께 있을 때 행동하는 데 더 편안함을 느낄지도 모르는 데 반해, 나이가 더 많은 아이들은 그들의 또래들에게 판단받는 것(평가받을지에 대해)을 더욱 걱정하며 과잉 반응에 의해 창피함을 느끼는 것을 두려워할지도 모른다고 말했다</u>. Staub noted that "older children seemed to discuss the distress sounds less and to react to them less openly than younger children." In other words, the older children were deliberately putting on a poker face in front of their peers.
subjective_conditions: 37단어로 작성할 것.

judged / Staub suggested / fear / comfortable / acting / be / have the company of / a peer / and / embarrass / younger / overreacting / older / they / their peers / concern (위의 단어를 모두 사용하되, 필요시 단어의 형태를 바꿀 것)
다음 단어는 형태를 바꾸지 말고 두 번씩 사용할 것: more / might / children / by
다음 단어는 세 번씩 사용할 것 (필요시 단어의 형태를 바꿀 것): feel
다음 접속사를 사용할 것: whereas / when / that
answer: Staub suggested that younger children might feel more comfortable acting when they have the company of a peer, whereas older children might feel more concern about being judged by their peers and fear feeling embarrassed by overreacting.
explanation: Staub suggested that 절 내부에 whereas를 사용하여 두 대조되는 대상을 연결합니다. 'feel more comfortable acting when they have the company of a peer' (또래와 함께 있을 때 행동하는 것에 더 편안함을 느낌)와 'feel more concern about being judged by their peers and fear feeling embarrassed by overreacting' (또래에게 판단받는 것에 더 걱정을 느끼고 과잉반응으로 창피함을 느끼는 것을 두려워함)을 구성합니다.

question: 26. 다음 괄호 안의 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 문장을 완성하시오.
passage: The first human beings probably evolved in tropical regions where survival was possible without clothing. Whichever the case, it is believed that in time they became capable of spreading out from Africa, eventually to most of the world. This was probably because their physical characteristics changed. For instance, early hominids probably did not walk upright, but when they developed that ability, they could travel more efficiently. More important, perhaps, was their development of tool making. With tools, they could hunt other animals, so (그들은 그들의 채식 식단이 제공했을 것보다 더 많은 단백질과 지방을 섭취할 수 있었다). Not only their bodies but also their brains would have been changed with more energy. question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]

question: 25. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸에 공통으로 들어갈 어휘를 본문에서 찾아 있는 그대로 쓰시오.
