question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 각각의 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 변형 없이 쓰시오.
passage: A great strength of the market mechanism is that there are incentives for individuals to reveal their knowledge through their behavior. This stands in contrast to many strategic situations ─ for example, in political negotiations ─ in which it could be disadvantageous to let the other side know what one's true preferences or production capacities are. A perfectly competitive market that clears on the spot leaves no room for such strategies. If prices are not sticky ─ as many models assume ─ individuals adapt their behavior instantaneously, whenever their preferences or the circumstances change. They stop buying items that do not satisfy their needs and stop selling items that do not provide them with optimal gains, maybe switching to the production of other items. If they have motivational problems, for example, falling into denial about the fact that there is no demand for their products, markets reveal to them that they better accept this fact.
summary_sentence: Unlike political negotiations, where it may be (A) ___________ to let the other side know what they think, market mechanisms allow them to (B) ___________ what they know through their actions.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 찾아 변형 없이 쓸 것
explanation: 서술형 답안 핵심 단어 복원: (A) disadvantageous, (B) reveal. 시장 메커니즘은 개인이 행동을 통해 자신의 지식을 드러내도록 유도하는 강점이 있습니다. 이는 자신의 진정한 선호나 능력을 상대방에게 알리는 것이 'disadvantageous(불리한)'하게 작용할 수 있는 정치적 협상 상황과 대조됩니다. 반면 시장에서는 가격과 행동의 변화를 통해 개인이 알고 있는 바를 자연스럽게 'reveal(드러내다)'하게 된다는 것이 글의 핵심입니다.

question: 7. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The future of work depends on two forces: a harmful substituting force and a helpful complementing one. Many tales have a hero and a villain fighting each other for dominance, but in our story, technology plays both roles at once, displacing workers while simultaneously raising the demand for their efforts elsewhere in the economy. This interaction helps explain why past worries about automation were misplaced: our ancestors had predicted the wrong winner in that fight, underestimating quite how powerful the complementing force would prove to be or simply ignoring that factor altogether. It also helps to explain why economists have traditionally been dismissive of the idea of technological unemployment: there appeared to be firm limits to the substituting force, leaving lots of tasks that could not be performed by machines, and a growing demand for human beings to do them instead.
options: ① the superiority of the complementing force over the substituting force in modern times
② a comparison of the impacts of technology on Western and non-Western economies
③ how economists have always correctly predicted the outcomes of technological change
④ the reasons why agricultural societies relied more on machines than on human workers
⑤ the dual role of technology in both displacing and complementing human labor
explanation: 이 글은 기술이 노동을 대체하는 해로운 힘(substituting force)과 노동을 보완하는 유익한 힘(complementing force)이라는 두 가지 역할을 동시에 수행한다고 설명합니다. 기술이 일부 일자리를 없애기도 하지만, 동시에 다른 분야에서 인간의 노동에 대한 수요를 창출한다는 것이 핵심 내용이므로, 주제는 '인간 노동을 대체하고 보완하는 기술의 이중적 역할'입니다.
options_translation: ① 현대에 대체하는 힘보다 보완하는 힘의 우월성
② 서구 경제와 비서구 경제에 미치는 기술 영향의 비교
③ 경제학자들이 항상 기술 변화의 결과를 정확하게 예측해 온 방법
④ 농경 사회가 인간 노동자보다 기계에 더 의존했던 이유
⑤ 인간 노동을 대체하고 보완하는 기술의 이중적 역할

question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A great strength of the market mechanism is that there are incentives for individuals to reveal their knowledge through their behavior. This stands in contrast to many strategic situations - for example, in political negotiations - in which it is wise not to let the other side know what one's true preferences or production capacities are. A perfectly competitive market that clears on the spot leaves no room for such strategies. If prices are not sticky - as many models assume - individuals adapt their behavior instantaneously, whenever their preferences or the circumstances change. They stop buying items that do not satisfy their needs and stop selling items that do not provide them with optimal gains, maybe switching to the production of other items. If they have motivational problems, for example, falling into denial about the fact that there is no demand for their products, markets reveal to them, sometimes in quite brutal ways, that they better accept this fact.
options: ① The Market as a Mechanism for Revealing Knowledge
② Political Strategies in Economic Decision-Making
③ The History of International Trade Agreements
④ The Evolution of Industrial Production Systems
⑤ The Psychology of Consumer Satisfaction
explanation: 이 글은 시장 메커니즘의 큰 장점이 개인들이 자신의 행동을 통해 지식을 드러내도록 하는 인센티브가 있다는 점임을 강조하고 있습니다. 정치적 협상과 같은 전략적 상황과 달리, 시장에서는 가격 변동과 소비/판매 행위를 통해 자신의 선호와 상황을 즉각적으로 드러내게 된다는 내용이 핵심이므로 '지식을 드러내는 기제로서의 시장'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 지식을 드러내는 기제로서의 시장
② 경제적 의사결정에서의 정치적 전략
③ 국제 무역 협정의 역사
④ 산업 생산 체계의 진화
⑤ 소비자 만족의 심리학

question: 9. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Dictionary definitions are constantly revised to keep up with our changing uses and knowledge. In Roman times, "addicts" were people who were unable to pay their debts and gave themselves as slaves to their creditors. The word eventually came to be associated with drug dependency: one becomes a slave to one's addiction. The word "husband" originally referred to being a homeowner; it had nothing to do with being married. But because owning your own property made it more likely you'd find a mate, the word eventually came to mean a male who has been wed. On November 5th, 1605, Guy Fawkes tried to blow up the British Parliament. He was captured and put to death. Loyalists burned his effigy, which they nicknamed the "guy." Centuries later, the word lost its negative connotation and a musical named Guys and Dolls ran on Broadway. In American slang, bad means good, cool means great, and wicked means excellent. If you could transport yourself one hundred years into the future, you'd find yourself confused by your great-grandchildren's speech because language itself is an ever-changing reflection of human invention.
options: ① The meaning of the word "addict" has shifted from debt slavery to drug dependency.
② Owning property in the past increased one's likelihood of marriage.
③ The effigy of Guy Fawkes was celebrated as a symbol of freedom.
④ Slang terms such as "bad," "cool," and "wicked" have positive meanings in American English.
⑤ Future generations' speech may sound confusing because of linguistic change.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 Guy Fawkes의 인형(effigy)을 태운 사람들은 충성파(Loyalists)였으며, 이는 그가 영국 의사당을 폭파하려다 실패한 것에 대한 부정적인 반응이었습니다. 따라서 이를 자유의 상징으로 축하했다는 설명은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① "addict"라는 단어의 의미는 부채 노예에서 약물 의존으로 바뀌었다.
② 과거에 재산을 소유하는 것은 결혼 가능성을 높여주었다.
③ 가이 포크스의 인형은 자유의 상징으로 찬양받았다.
④ "bad", "cool", "wicked"와 같은 속어들은 미국 영어에서 긍정적인 의미를 가진다.
⑤ 언어 변화 때문에 미래 세대의 말은 혼란스럽게 들릴 수 있다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
passage: All human cultures mark the passing of time by the differences they observe in the world around them. Our choice of which differences to mark depends firstly on what we can observe and secondly on what is important in our lives. How we mark the differences - the shapes of our calendars and our rituals - depends on the connections we make between those two things. In the agricultural society of pre-modern Europe, where higher latitudes make the seasons easily observable, it was natural to monitor the solar cycle. Conversely, among the largely nomadic peoples of Arabia, for whom seasonal changes were less significant, the lunar calendar was a more sensible choice. That did not make it inevitable that Islam would use a lunar calendar and Roman Christianity a solar one, but political and religious decisions were made from options limited by geography and lifestyle, filtered through tradition.
options: ① All cultures mark time in the same way regardless of geography or lifestyle.
② The nomadic peoples of Arabia relied mainly on the solar calendar since their lives depended on farming.
③ Roman Christianity adopted the lunar calendar because seasonal changes were less important in Europe.
④ In pre-modern Europe, agricultural society made it natural to observe the solar cycle because the seasons were easy to notice.
⑤ The choice of calendars in human cultures has always been completely inevitable, without influence from politics or religion.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 전근대 유럽의 농경 사회에서는 위도가 높아 계절의 변화를 쉽게 관찰할 수 있었기 때문에 태양 주기를 관찰하는 것이 자연스러웠다고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 4번 선지가 지문의 내용과 정확히 일치합니다.
options_translation: ① 모든 문화권은 지리나 생활 방식에 관계없이 동일한 방식으로 시간을 표시한다.
② 아라비아의 유목 민족들은 삶이 농사에 달려 있었기 때문에 주로 태양력에 의존했다.
③ 로마 기독교는 유럽에서 계절 변화가 덜 중요했기 때문에 태음력을 채택했다.
④ 전근대 유럽에서 농경 사회는 계절을 알아차리기 쉬웠기 때문에 태양 주기를 관찰하는 것을 자연스럽게 만들었다.
⑤ 인류 문화에서 달력의 선택은 정치나 종교의 영향 없이 항상 완전히 불가피했다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Although empathy is widely praised by scholars and public figures, not everyone is an empathy booster. Critics of empathy argue that empathy will not save us from interpersonal and intergroup conflict. In fact, they argue, empathy makes such conflicts worse. These critics maintain that empathy can be exhausting and lead to burnout, insensitivity to suffering. They argue that we tend to empathize strongly with our in-group and resist empathizing with out-groups, and even enjoy the suffering of out-groups in competitive or threatening contexts. Thus, the prescription for more empathy is often ___________________________. Empathy, they argue, can further entrench conflict and force us into an us vs. them mentality. Finally, even when we try to empathize with others who are dissimilar from us or in unfamiliar contexts, sometimes we are unable to accurately empathize with their experiences, causing further misunderstandings and frustration. Critics of empathy argue that we should give up on empathy and employ other tools in pursuit of social harmony, e.g., rational compassion or moral emotions like fear, anger, and shame.
options: ① harmful rather than helpful in conflict situations
② universally praised as the only path to peace
③ essential for building harmony across all groups
④ the ultimate solution to all social conflicts
⑤ a neutral factor that has no real impact on conflicts
explanation: 이 글은 공감의 비판자들이 주장하는 공감의 부정적인 측면을 다루고 있습니다. 비판자들은 공감이 내집단에게만 치우쳐 갈등을 심화시키고, 번아웃을 유발하며, 타인에 대한 오해를 불러일으킬 수 있다고 주장합니다. 따라서 갈등 상황에서 더 많은 공감을 처방하는 것은 종종 도움이 되기보다 해로울 수 있다는 ①번이 빈칸에 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 갈등 상황에서 도움이 되기보다는 해롭다
평화로 가는 유일한 길로서 보편적으로 찬양받는다
모든 집단 간의 조화를 구축하는 데 필수적이다
모든 사회적 갈등에 대한 궁극적인 해결책이다
갈등에 실질적인 영향을 미치지 않는 중립적인 요소이다

question: 20. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Once a nail is hammered in, it is friction that holds it in place. Friction is the force that arises when two surfaces are sliding, or trying to slide, against each other. If you try to pull apart two blocks of wood that have been nailed together, the wood fibers grip the shaft of the nail. The nail feels a force trying to rip it apart along its length, and we call that force tension. Your experiment can now fail in one of two ways - either ______________________________, or the nail comes loose because the friction force is overcome. The force it would take to stretch the nail is much larger than the friction forces on the surface, so we don't have to worry too much about the former. It's the friction with which we need to concern ourselves.
options: ① the nail is torn apart because it cannot resist the pulling force
② the friction between the surfaces becomes too strong
③ the nail becomes loose simply due to its shape
④ the nail bends instead of being stretched
⑤ the force of tension is weaken than the friction
explanation: 이 글은 못이 박혀 있을 때 작용하는 마찰력과 장력의 관계를 설명합니다. 못으로 고정된 두 나무판을 떼어내려 할 때 실험이 실패하는 두 가지 방식 중 하나는 마찰력이 극복되어 못이 빠지는 것이고, 다른 하나는 못 자체가 장력을 견디지 못하고 끊어지는 것입니다. 문맥상 빈칸에는 못이 당기는 힘을 견디지 못하고 찢어지거나 끊어지는 상황인 ①번이 들어가야 합니다.
options_translation: 못이 당기는 힘을 견디지 못해 찢어진다
표면 사이의 마찰력이 너무 강해진다
못이 단순히 모양 때문에 헐거워진다
못이 늘어나는 대신 구부러진다
장력이 마찰력보다 약해진다

question: 22. 다음 글의 (A), (B)에 각각 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Everything in the world exists on a continuum, whether in speed, size, or any other possible descriptor you could think of. (A)__________, we create and mindlessly adopt sharp distinctions, and those distinctions change lives far more dramatically than marginal differences ever do. Indeed, all differences are arbitrary, but drawing hard lines between categories hides this arbitrariness and can be severely damaging. I call this resulting damage "the borderline effect." The examples are endless. Someone's IQ is 69 and someone else's is 70 - but only the score of 70 is deemed to be within the range of normal. We don't have to be statisticians to know there is not a meaningful difference between 69 and 70. (B)__________ once the person with the lower score is labeled "cognitively impaired," his or her life will unfold differently than the person with a one-point advantage.
options: ① Therefore - Yet
② Therefore - Because
③ Still - Yet
④ Still - Because
⑤ Likewise - So
explanation: • (A): 모든 갃은 연셍체 상에 있지만, 인간은 명확한 구분을 만들어낸다는 상반된 내용을 이어주므로 '괸럼에도 불구하고(Still)'가 적절합니다.• (B): IQ 69와 70 사이에 의미 있는 차이가 없음을 알고 있지만, 'Cognitively impaired(인지 장애)'라는 라벨이 붙으면 다른 삶을 살게 된다는 역접의 괸계림 내타내므로 'Yet(하지만)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 괸러므로 - 하지만
② 괸러므로 - ~에 때문에
③ 괸럼에도 불구하고 - 하지만
④ 괸럼에도 불구하고 - ~에 때문에
⑤ 마찬가지로 - 괸래서

question: 23. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: We're naturally wired to organize the world into a hierarchy. We do this to help make sense of the world, maintain our beliefs, and generally feel better. ⓐBut when someone infringes on our place in the world and our understanding of how it works, we react without thinking. ⓑYou probably wonder why the person did that and think carefully about what you should say. ⓒWhen someone cuts you off on the highway and road rage kicks in, that's your unconscious mind saying, "Who are you to cut me off?" ⓓYou're reacting to a threat to your inherent sense of hierarchy. ⓔOn the road we are all equals. We're all supposed to play by the same rules. Cutting someone off violates those rules and implies higher status. Or consider when you get frustrated with your kids and end an argument with "Because I said so." (Or the office equivalent: "Because I'm the boss.") In these moments you've stopped thinking and regressed to your biological tendencies of reaffirming the hierarchy.
explanation: 이 글은 인간이 세상을 계층 구조로 이해하려고 하며, 괸 계층이 위협받을 때 'Thinking(사고)'없이 무의식적으로 반응한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. ⓑ번 문장은 상대방의 핉동을 의아해하며 신중하게 무엍을 말할지 생각한다는 내용이므로, 무의식적으로 반응한다는 전체적인 흐름과 맞지 않습니다.

question: 24. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: "Tactics" is a term drawn from military usage. Strategies are plans of action directing a military force when attacking another, and tactics are responses to conditions on the ground.
ordered_passages: (A) These aren't tactics to eliminate waiting; instead, these are tactics for teaching us how to learn from the seams. These tactics have the potential to reorient us in profound ways, transforming our perspectives on our wait times.

(B) In this vein, time is imposed on us by our cultures, by the technologies that have regimented time down to the nanosecond, and by its own finite nature and the fact that we're going to live only so long. In response, we must develop tactics for dealing with time and waiting.
(C) Such renewed perspectives transform waiting from a burden to a springboard toward things like creativity, social critique, or reflection on our inner state and the state of our relationships.
explanation: • 주어진 글: '전술(tactics)'의 일반적인 정의림 내림.• (B): 세상의 시간과 괸 한계에 대해 언급하며, 시간과 기다림을 다루기 윔한 시간 전술이 필요함을 제시함.• (A): 괸러한 전술들이 기다림을 없애는 갃이 아니라 기다림 셍에서 배우는 법을 가리치고, 우리의 관점을 바꾸어 준다고 설명함.• (C): (A)에서 언급한 '바붔인 관점(Such renewed perspectives)'이 기다림을 창의성이나 성찰의 발판으로 변화시켜 준다는 결과로 마무리함.

question: 25. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending.
ordered_passages: (A) Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to resist being pulled apart, but it can also be torn easily and accurately along the crease if a point of weakness 0 a small, initial tear - is opened up. This winning combination of mechanical properties allows it to assume the shape of any object through creasing and folding - hence the art of origami.

(B) The cellulose fibers of which it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease to form, while sufficient fibers remain undamaged for the material not to crack and fall apart.

(C) There are very few materials as good: metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult. Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, in which case it lacks the rigidity required of a good wrapping material. So it is its ability to hold a crease while remaining stiff that makes paper uniquely suited to this purpose.
explanation: 이 글은 종이의 기계적 특성인 접힘과 구부러짐에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. (B) 종이를 구성하는 셀룰로오스 섬유가 최대 굴곡 지점에서 부분적으로 끊어지면서 영구적인 주름이 형성되지만, 나머지 섬유들이 손상되지 않아 재료가 부서지지 않고 유지된다는 물리적 원리를 먼저 설명합니다. (A) 이어서 이러한 상태에서 종이가 인장력에는 저항하면서도 주름을 따라서는 쉽게 찢어질 수 있다는 특성을 설명하며, 이것이 종이접기(origami)를 가능하게 한다고 연결합니다. (C) 마지막으로 금속 박판이나 플라스틱과 같은 다른 재료와 비교하여, 뻣뻣함을 유지하면서도 주름을 보유할 수 있는 종이만의 독특한 강점을 강조하며 마무리하는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 하나는?
passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending. How we mark the differences - the shapes of our calendars and our rituals - depends on the ② <u>links</u> we make between those two things. In the agricultural society of pre-modern Europe, where higher latitudes make the seasons easily ③ <u>unnoticeable</u>, it was natural to monitor the solar cycle. Conversely, among the largely nomadic peoples of Arabia, for whom seasonal changes were ④ <u>insignificant</u>, the lunar calendar was a more sensible choice. That did not make it inevitable that Islam would use a lunar calendar and Roman Christianity a solar one, but political and religious decisions were made from ⑤ <u>options</u> limited by geography and lifestyle, filtered through tradition.

⑤ options

높은 위도에 위치한 근대 이전 유럽의 농경 사회에서는 계절의 변화가 매우 뚜렷하게 관찰되었기 때문에 태양 주기를 관찰하는 것이 자연스러웠습니다. 따라서 '눈에 띄지 않는'이라는 뜻의 ③번 unnoticeable은 '뚜렷한, 관찰 가능한'이라는 의미인 noticeable 혹은 observable 등으로 고쳐야 문맥상 적절합니다.

question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 지칭하는 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.7점]
passage: The future of work depends on two forces: a harmful substituting force and a helpful complementing ① <u>one</u>. Many tales have a hero and a villain fighting each other for dominance, but in our story, technology plays ② <u>both roles</u> at once, displacing workers while simultaneously raising the demand for their efforts elsewhere in the economy. This interaction helps explain why past worries about automation were misplaced: our ancestors had predicted ③ <u>the wrong winner</u> in that fight, underestimating quite how powerful the complementing force would prove to be or simply ignoring that factor altogether. ④ <u>It</u> also helps to explain why economists have traditionally been dismissive of the idea of technological unemployment: there appeared to be firm limits to the substituting force, leaving lots of tasks that could not be performed by machines, and a growing demand for human beings to do ⑤ <u>them</u> instead.

question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
passage:
We're naturally wired to organize the world into a hierarchy. We do this to help make sense of the world, maintain our beliefs, and generally feel better. But when someone infringes on our place in the world and our understanding of how it works, we react without thinking. When someone cuts you off on the highway and road rage kicks in, that's your unconscious mind saying, "Who are you to me off? "You're reacting to a threat to your ___________ sense of hierarchy. On the road we are all equals. We're all supposed to play by the same rules. Cutting someone off violates those rules and implies higher status. Or consider when you get frustrated with your kids and end an argument with "Because I said so." (Or the office equivalent: "Because I'm the boss.) In these moments you've stopped thinking and regressed to your biological tendencies of reaffirming the hierarchy.

question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. But the research evidence is paradoxical: In problem-solving groups, the participants who are considered the most competent and have the best ideas ____________________________. Why? One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, those who are too competent make us uncomfortable. They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman - and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison. If this were true, we might like people more if they reveal some evidence of fallibility. For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her better if, every once in a while, they screwed up.

question: 12. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The concern about how we appear to others can be seen in children, though work by the psychologist Ervin Staub suggests that the effect may vary with age. In a study where children heard another child in distress, young children (kindergarten through second grade) were more likely to help the child in distress when with another child than when alone. But for older children - in fourth and sixth grade - the effect reversed: they were less likely to help a child in distress when they were with a peer than when they were alone. Staub suggested that younger children might feel more comfortable acting when they have the company of a peer, whereas older children might feel more concern about being judged by their peers and fear feeling embarrassed by overreacting. Staub noted that "older children seemed to discuss the distress sounds less and to react to them less openly than younger children." In other words, the older children were deliberately putting on a poker face in front of their peers.
options: ① 다른 사람을 돕는 것과 같은 이타적인 행동은 어릴 적부터 학습되어야 한다.

③ 어린 시절 고통을 많이 느낀 아이들은 심리적으로 더 불안하고 타인의 시선을 의식한다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

It's on those occasions that time seems to slow down a little, and you feel more fully engaged. The same holds true if the experience is risky, like mountain climbing or parasailing. Your senses are sharper. You notice more. Thanks to the release of a feelgood chemical in the brain called dopamine, you get a greater rush of pleasure from chance encounters with people than planned meetings. Good news, financial rewards, and gifts are more enjoyable if they are surprises. It's why the most popular television shows and movies are the ones with unexpected plot twists and astonishing endings.

question: 20. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: The term "anchoring" was introduced by Roland Barthes who observed that text is often used next to images (his focus was on photographs) to confine meaning. Of all possible literal or implied interpretations an image could elicit, text would point the viewer towards a desired, specific direction. ⓐIn advertising, as Barthes argues, the symbolic message does not guide identification but interpretation. ⓑToday, the majority of the messages we receive about how to live a good life come not from Granny's long experience of the world, but from advertising executives hoping to sell us products. ⓒThe viewer is not asked to recognize what they see but to understand why they see it and what it means to them. ⓓBy combining images with text, advertising produces symbolic meaning that is accurate and specific on the one hand, richer on the other, thus adding depth and eliminating breadth of rational and emotional interpretations. ⓔThe headline or tagline of an ad directs the reader through the intended meanings of the image, so that the reader avoids some and receives others.*elicit: 이끌어 내다
explanation: 이 글의 핵심 주제는 광고에서 텍스트와 이미지가 결합되어 의미를 고정(anchoring)하고 특정 해석으로 유도하는 방식에 대한 것입니다. Roland Barthes의 이론을 바탕으로 텍스트가 이미지의 모호한 해석 가능성을 좁히고 상징적 의미를 전달한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 그러나 ⓑ 문장은 우리가 삶의 지혜를 얻는 출처가 조상(할머니)의 경험에서 광고 기획자로 바뀌었다는 내용으로, 글의 핵심 소재인 '텍스트와 이미지의 상호작용을 통한 의미 한정'과는 관계가 없는 진술입니다.

question: 26. 윗글의 공감 비판론자들의 주장을 두 가지 쓰시오. (제시된 내용만 우리말로 작성하시오.)
passage: Although empathy is widely praised by scholars and public figures, not everyone is an empathy booster. Critics of empathy argue that empathy will not save us from interpersonal and intergroup conflict. In fact, they argue, empathy makes such conflicts worse. These critics maintain that empathy can be exhausting and lead to burnout or insensitivity to suffering. They argue that we tend to empathize strongly with our ingroup and resist empathizing with outgroups, and even enjoy the suffering of outgroups in competitive or threatening contexts. Thus, the prescription for more empathy is often counterproductive in cases of conflict. According to critics of empathy, the solution is as follows: we should give up on empathy and employ other tools in pursuit of social harmony, e.g. <u>moral emotions like fear, anger, and shame</u>. Moral emotions are a variety of social emotions that are involved in forming and communicating moral judgments and decisions, and in motivating behavioral responses to one's own and others' moral behavior. Moral anger arises when values such as right and wrong, justice, and fairness are violated. It is not simply a personal feeling but an emotion deeply connected to moral judgment. Unlike ordinary anger, it reflects a strong concern for protecting social rules and ethical principles. In this way, moral anger emphasizes the importance of maintaining the community's order rather than serving one's own interests.
subjective_conditions: 제시된 내용만 우리말로 작성할 것
answer: (1) 우리는 내집단에 대해 더 강하게 공감하고, 외집단에 대해서는 공감을 거부하거나 그들의 고통을 즐기기도 한다.(2) 공감은 갈등을 더 악화시키고 경쟁적인 상황에서 역효과를 낼 수 있다. (또는 공감은 기진맥진하게 하여 번아웃이나 고통에 대한 무감각으로 이어질 수 있다.)
explanation: 지문 중반부에 언급된 비판론자들의 주장을 요약합니다. 1) 내집단 편향적 공감과 외집단에 대한 적대적 감정(enjoy the suffering of outgroups), 2) 공감이 갈등을 악화시키거나(makes such conflicts worse), 번아웃(burnout) 혹은 무감각(insensitivity)을 초래한다는 내용 등을 기술하면 됩니다.

question: 29. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸에 적절한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 아래 표를 완성하시오.
passage: In today's information age, in many companies and on many teams, the objective is no longer error prevention and replicability. On the contrary, it's creativity, speed, and keenness. In the industrial era, the goal was to minimize variation. But in creative companies today, maximizing variation is more essential. In these situations, the biggest risk isn't making a mistake or losing consistency; it's failing to attract top talent, to invent new products, or to change direction quickly when the environment shifts. Consistency and repeatability are more likely to suppress fresh thinking than to bring your company profit. A lot of little mistakes, while sometimes painful, help the organization learn quickly and are a critical part of the innovation cycle. In these situations, rules and process are no longer the best answer. A symphony isn't what you're going for. Leave the conductor and the sheet music behind. Build a jazz band instead.
answer: (A) industrial era(B) information age(C) error prevention(D) replicability(E) a symphony(F) a jazz band
explanation: 지문은 산업 시대(industrial era)와 정보 시대(information age)를 대조하고 있습니다. 산업 시대의 목표는 오차 방지(error prevention)와 복제 가능성(replicability)이었으며 이를 교향악단(a symphony)에 비유했습니다. 반면 정보 시대의 목표는 창의성과 속도이며, 이를 재즈 밴드(a jazz band)에 비유하고 있습니다.

question: 30. 다음 글의 제목을 아래 조건에 맞추어 작성하시오.
passage: Sleep is clearly about more than just resting. One curious fact is that animals that are hibernating also have periods of sleep. It comes as a surprise to most of us, but hibernation and sleep are not the same thing at all, at least not from a neurological and metabolic perspective. Hibernating is more like being anesthetized: the subject is unconscious but not actually asleep. So a hibernating animal needs to get a few hours of conventional sleep each day within the larger unconsciousness. A further surprise to most of us is that bears, the most famous of wintry sleepers, don't actually hibernate. Real hibernation involves profound unconsciousness and a dramatic fall in body temperature - often to around 32 degrees Fahrenheit. By this definition, bears don't hibernate, because their body temperature stays near normal and they are easily awakened. Their winter sleeps are more accurately called a state of torpor.
subjective_conditions: 1. (A), (B) 각 한 단어
2. (C) 다섯 단어 이내
answer: (A) hibernation, (B) sleep, (C) Bears don't actually hibernate
explanation: 이 글은 동면(hibernation)과 수면(sleep)이 신경학적 및 대사적 관점에서 서로 다르다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 특히 일반적인 통념과 달리 곰은 신체 온도가 크게 떨어지지 않고 쉽게 깨어날 수 있기 때문에 진정한 의미의 동면을 하는 것이 아니라는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 제목은 동면과 수면의 대조 및 곰의 실제 상태에 대한 내용으로 구성됩니다.

question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The brain is a high-energy consumer of glucose, which is its fuel. Although the brain accounts for merely 3 percent of a person's body weight, it consumes 20 percent of the available fuel. Your brain can't store fuel, however, so it has to "pay as it goes." Since your brain is incredibly adaptive, it economizes its fuel resources. Thus, during a period of high stress, it shifts away from the analysis of the nuances of a situation to a singular and fixed focus on the stressful situation at hand. You don't sit back and speculate about the meaning of life when you are stressed. Instead, you devote all your energy to trying to figure out what action to take. Sometimes, this shift from the higher thinking parts of the brain to the automatic and reflexive parts of the brain can lead you to do something too quickly, without thinking.
options: ① Why Is Our Brain Storing Fuel?
② How the Brain Analyzes Stressful Situations
③ Speculation or Survival: Which Comes First?
④ Our Brain: A Flexible Strategist of Fuel Resource
⑤ Beyond Human Needs: The Rise of Higher Thinking Skills
explanation: 글은 뇌가 많은 에너지를 사용하지만 연료를 저장할 수 없기 때문에 매우 적응력이 뛰어나고 효율적으로 연료 자원을 배분한다는 점을 강조합니다. 특히 스트레스 상황에서 사고 능력 대신 자동적인 반응으로 에너지를 전환하는 방식을 설명하므로 '연료 자원의 유연한 전략가'라는 표현이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 왜 우리 뇌는 연료를 저장하고 있는가?
② 뇌가 스트레스 상황을 분석하는 방법
③ 사색인가 생존인가: 무엇이 우선인가?
④ 우리 뇌: 연료 자원의 유연한 전략가
⑤ 인간의 필요를 넘어서: 고등 사고 기술의 부상

question: 8. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It seems natural to describe certain environmental conditions as 'extreme', 'harsh', 'benign' or 'stressful'.
ordered_passages: (A) To a cactus there is nothing extreme about the desert conditions in which cacti have evolved; nor are the icy lands of Antarctica an extreme environment for penguins. It is lazy and dangerous for the ecologist to assume that all other organisms sense the environment in the way we do.

(B) It may seem obvious when conditions are 'extreme': the midday heat of a desert, the cold of an Antarctic winter, the salinity of the Great Salt Lake. But this only means that these conditions are extreme for us, given our particular physiological characteristics and tolerances.

(C) Rather, the ecologist should try to gain a worm's-eye or plant's-eye view of the environment: to see the world as others see it. Emotive words like harsh and benign, even relativities such as hot and cold, should be used by ecologists only with care.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 환경을 '극심한' 등으로 묘사하는 것이 자연스러워 보인다고 말한 뒤, (B)에서 이러한 조건들이 사실은 '인간의 기준'에서만 극심한 것임을 설명합니다. 이어지는 (A)에서는 선인장이나 펭귄에게는 그 환경이 극심하지 않다는 구체적 예시를 들며 생태학자가 인간 중심적으로 생각하는 것의 위험성을 경고합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 '오히려(Rather)' 생태학자는 다른 생명체의 시각에서 환경을 보려 노력해야 한다는 결론을 내리는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 11. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: Mother cats can tell which kittens belong to them - when litters are mixed up they use their kittens' scent to distinguish them from offspring of other mothers. ⓐDespite this, when faced with a selection of kittens who have wandered from the nest, her own and others that aren't hers, a mother cat doesn't appear to favor her own offspring when retrieving them. ⓑThe reason for this is uncertain, although distress vocalizations from kittens that are lost from their nest are known to be very powerful, so it may just be hard for the mother to resist retrieving them, regardless of whether they are hers. ⓒThe vocalizations of human infants are also crucial in that they convey their basic needs. ⓓIn the wild, a squeaking kitten out in the open is likely to attract predators, which is bad news for any other kittens around it. ⓔA rapid rescue of any crying kitten would be a good strategy to prevent them from drawing unwanted attention.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 어미 고양이가 자신의 새끼가 아니더라도 길을 잃고 우는 새끼 고양이를 구조하는 이유가 포식자의 주의를 끌지 않기 위한 생존 전략임을 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓒ문장은 인간 영아의 발성(vocalizations)이 기본 욕구를 전달한다는 내용으로, 고양이의 종 특유의 행동 원리를 설명하는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

question: 12. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Although empathy is widely praised by scholars and public figures, not everyone is an empathy booster.
ordered_passages: (A) Critics of empathy argue that empathy will not save us from interpersonal and intergroup conflict. In fact, they argue, empathy makes such conflicts worse. These critics maintain that empathy can be exhausting and lead to burnout or insensitivity to suffering.

(B) Finally, even when we try to empathize with others who are dissimilar from us or in unfamiliar contexts, sometimes we are unable to accurately empathize with their experiences, causing further misunderstandings and frustration.

(C) They argue that we tend to empathize strongly with our in-group and resist empathizing with out-groups, and even enjoy the suffering of out-groups in competitive or threatening contexts. Thus, the prescription for more empathy is often couterproductive in cases of conflict.
explanation: 주어진 문장에서 공감을 옹호하지 않는 사람들의 존재를 언급하며 글을 시작합니다. (A)에서 공감 비판론자들의 주요 주장을 소개하며 공감이 갈등을 악화시키고 고갈을 초래할 수 있다고 설명합니다. (C)에서는 구체적으로 내집단과 외집단 사이의 공감 격차 문제를 지적하며 공감이 오히려 비생산적일 수 있음을 논합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 유사하지 않은 타인에 대한 공감의 어려움과 그로 인한 오해를 언급하며 논의를 마무리하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The traditional bank manager in the 1950s was usually a respected pillar of the community, a cautious, careful sort of person who probably went to bed early and didn't drink too much. But from the 1970s a new kind of banker appeared - loud, flashy, and arrogant. These bankers loved taking big risks. They wanted to get rich quick and blow their money on fast cars and expensive champagne. They made their money through what's called 'speculation'. Normally, people buy things because they want to use them, such as wheat to make bread and petrol to run the car. But when people speculate, they buy things even when they have no interest in using them. They might buy a load of wheat simply because they think that its price is going to rise when a drought is predicted in wheat-growing areas. If their guess is right, they later sell the wheat for a profit.
options: ① What Should Be Done to Increase Wheat Production?
② A Shortcut to Successful Investment: Be humble, Not Arrogant
③ From Cautious Minds to High Stakes: A Shift in Banking Culture
④ A Principle Preserved by Both Traditional and Modern Bankers
⑤ The Proper Mindset for Future Investment: Safety vs. Risk-Taking
explanation: 이 글은 1950년대의 전통적이고 신중한 은행가와 1970년대 이후 등장한 위험을 감수하고 투기적인 새로운 은행가 유형을 대조하며, 은행 업무의 문화적 변화와 투기의 개념을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '신중한 마음에서 고위험으로: 은행 문화의 변화'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 밀 생산량을 늘리기 위해 무엇을 해야 하는가?
② 성공적인 투자의 지름길: 거만함이 아닌 겸손함
③ 신중한 마음에서 고위험으로: 은행 문화의 변화
④ 전통적 은행가와 현대 은행가 모두에 의해 보존된 원칙
⑤ 미래 투자를 위한 적절한 사고방식: 안전 대 위험 감수

question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We're naturally wired to organize the world into a hierarchy. We do this to help make sense of the world, maintain our beliefs, and generally feel better. But when someone infringes on our place in the world and our understanding of how it works, we respond by _____________. When someone cuts you off on the highway and road rage kicks in, that's your unconscious mind saying, "Who are you to cut me off?" You're reacting to a threat to your inherent sense of hierarchy. On the road we are all equals. We're all supposed to play by the same rules. Cutting someone off violates those rules and implies higher status. Or consider when you get frustrated with your kids and end an argument with "Because I said so." (Or the office equivalent: "Because I'm the boss.") In these moments you've stopped thinking and regressed to your biological tendencies of reaffirming the hierarchy.
options: ① instinct
② strategy
③ agreement
④ negotiation
⑤ justification
explanation: 글의 후반부에서 도로 위에서의 분노(road rage)나 '내가 엄마니까(보스니까)'와 같은 반응이 생물학적 경향(biological tendencies)으로의 회귀라고 설명하고 있습니다. 이는 생각하기를 멈추고 무의식적으로 반응하는 것이므로, 빈칸에는 '본능'에 의해 반응한다는 의미의 instinct가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 본능
② 전략
③ 합의
④ 협상
⑤ 정당화

question: 15. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: The term "anchoring" was introduced by Roland Barthes who observed that text is often used next to images (his focus was on photographs) to confine meaning. Of all possible literal or implied interpretations an image could elicit, text would point the viewer towards a desired, specific direction. (A) In advertising, as Barthes argues, the symbolic message does not guide identification but interpretation. (B) The viewer is not engaged in recognizing what is presented before their eyes. (C) By combining images with text, advertising produces symbolic meaning that is accurate and specific on the one hand, richer on the other, thus adding depth and eliminating breadth of rational and emotional interpretations. (D) The headline or tagline of an ad directs the reader through the intended meanings of the image, so that the reader avoids some and receives others. (E) It "remote- controls" the reader towards a meaning chosen in advance.
insertion_sentence: Instead, they are encouraged to think about why they perceive it and what meaning it holds for them.
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'Instead'는 앞 문장의 부정적 진술에 대한 대안을 제시합니다. (B) 위치의 문장에서 시청자가 눈앞에 제시된 것을 인식(recognizing)하는 데 관여하지 않는다고 했으므로, 그 대신(Instead) 왜 그것을 지각하고 어떤 의미를 갖는지 생각하도록 장려된다는 내용이 이어지는 (C) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Many animals use both fat and food as energy reserves. Fat, stored within the body, ⓐ<u>increasing</u> with body size, while food storage is not limited by mass. Thus, small animals are able to secure larger reserves through food than fat. Moreover, food storage tend to reduce metabolic costs ⓑ<u>to conserve</u> energy more efficiently, since fat increases body weight and the added weight results in a higher metabolism. Interestingly, excessive fat can hinder an animal's speed, making it ⓒ<u>harder</u> to escape predators. In addition, if keeping warm is required, animals may prefer storing food rather than accumulating fat. However, food can spoil, be stolen, or disappear, and animals often spend energy guarding it. Fat, ⓓ<u>which</u> is not subject to these risks, is converted directly from food and allows animals to survive long periods without eating. Especially in large animals, heavy fat deposits enable hibernation in safe shelters. Therefore, both strategies - fat accumulation and food storage - ⓔ<u>offer</u> clear benefits, depending on circumstances.
explanation: ⓐ가 포함된 절의 주어는 Fat이며, stored within the body는 수식어구입니다. 접속사 while 앞까지가 하나의 완전한 절이어야 하므로 현재분사인 increasing은 본동사 역할을 할 수 없습니다. 주어가 3인칭 단수이므로 increases 또는 단수 동사 형태로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A great strength of the market mechanism is that there are incentives for individuals to reveal their knowledge through their behavior. This stands in contrast to many strategic situations - for example, in political negotiations - in which it is wise not to let the other side know what one's true preferences or production capacities are. A perfectly competitive market that clears on the spot leaves no room for such strategies. If prices are not sticky - as many models assume - individuals adapt their behavior instantaneously, whenever their preferences or the circumstances change. They stop buying items that do not satisfy their needs and stop selling items that do not provide them with optimal gains, maybe switching to the production of other items. If they have motivational problems, for example, falling into denial about the fact that there is no demand for their products, markets reveal to them, sometimes in quite brutal ways, that they better accept this fact.
summary_sentence: Unlike strategic settings such as political decision-making, a perfectly competitive market with flexible prices encourages individuals to (A)___________ their knowledge in behavior, leading them to (B)___________ quickly to altered preferences or environments.
options: ① share / resist
② conceal / yield
③ conceal / move
④ disclose / respond
⑤ disclose / object
explanation: 본문은 시장 기제의 강점이 개인들이 행동을 통해 자신의 지식을 드러내게(reveal) 한다는 점이며, 유연한 가격 체계 하에서 선호나 환경이 바뀔 때마다 즉각적으로 적응한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '드러내다'라는 의미의 disclose가, (B)에는 '대응하다/적응하다'의 의미인 respond가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 공유하다 / 저항하다
② 숨기다 / 굴복하다
③ 숨기다 / 이동하다
④ 드러내다 / 대응하다
⑤ 드러내다 / 반대하다

question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: The future of work depends on two forces: a harmful substituting force and a helpful complementing one. Many tales have a hero and a villain fighting each other for dominance, but in our story, technology plays both roles at once, ⓐ<u>replacing</u> workers while simultaneously raising the demand for their efforts elsewhere in the economy. This ⓑ<u>interaction</u> helps explain why past worries about automation were misplaced. In the past, our ancestors had predicted the wrong winner in that fight, ⓒ<u>underestimating</u> quite how powerful the complementing force would prove to be or simply ignoring that factor altogether. It also helps to explain why economists have traditionally had an ⓓ<u>objection</u> to the idea of technological unemployment. From the perspective of economists, there appeared to be firm limits to the substituting force, leaving lots of tasks that could not be performed by machines, and a ⓔ<u>shrinking</u> demand for human beings to do them instead.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 글의 흐름상 기술은 보완적인 힘을 가지고 있어 인간의 노력을 필요로 하는 다른 분야의 수요를 높인다고 했습니다. 따라서 경제학자들의 관점에서는 기계가 수행할 수 없는 업무가 많고, 그 일을 대신 할 인간에 대한 수요가 '줄어드는(shrinking)' 것이 아니라 '지속적인' 혹은 '증가하는' 수요가 있다고 보아야 문맥상 적절합니다.

question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It's conceivable that in a world where solar panels are incredibly expensive and there's an extreme collapse in the cost of launching objects to space, you might want to maximize your energy per panel by putting them above the atmosphere.
ordered_passages: (A) Try to imagine acres upon acres of glass panels in space, regularly hit by intense radiation and bits of space debris while enduring the extreme heat of constant sunlight.
(B) They'll have to be repaired and cared for either by astronauts or an army of advanced robots. Solar panels in Australia can be cleaned by a teenager with a spray bottle and a cloth.
(C) But panels are cheap, and even if we assume pretty steep drops in the cost of space launch, the numbers don't add up. This becomes especially clear when you start to think about maintenance.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 태양광 패널이 매우 비싸고 우주 발사 비용이 급격히 낮아진다면 대기권 위에 패널을 설치하는 것이 효율적일 수 있다는 가정을 제시합니다. (C)에서 하지만 실제로는 패널 가격이 저렴하며 발사 비용이 낮아지더라도 경제성이 없다는 반박을 시작하며, 유지보수 문제를 언급합니다. (A)는 우주 공간에서 패널이 처하게 될 가혹한 환경(방사능, 파편, 고열)을 묘사하며 유지보수의 어려움을 구체화합니다. (B)는 이를 수리하기 위해 우주비행사나 로봇이 필요하다는 점을 지적하며 지상에서의 관리와 대조하여 결론을 맺습니다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: "Tactics" is a term drawn from military usage. (A) Strategies are plans of action directing a military force when attacking another, and tactics are responses to conditions on the ground. (B) In this vein, time is imposed on us by our cultures, by the technologies that have regimented time down to the nanosecond, and by its own finite nature and the fact that we're going to live only so long. (C) These aren't tactics to eliminate waiting; instead, these are tactics for teaching us how to learn from the seams. (D) These tactics have the potential to reorient us in profound ways, transforming our perspectives on our wait times. question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Everything in the world exists on a continuum, whether in speed, size, or any other possible descriptor you could think of. Still, we create and mindlessly adopt sharp distinctions, and those distinctions change lives far more dramatically than marginal differences ever do. Indeed, all differences are arbitrary, but drawing hard lines between categories hides this arbitrariness and can be severely damaging. I call this resulting damage "the borderline effect." The examples are endless. Someone's IQ is 69 and someone else's is 70 - but only the score of 70 is deemed to be within the range of normal. We don't have to be statisticians to know there is not a meaningful difference between 69 and 70. Yet once the person with the lower score is labeled "cognitively impaired," his or her life will unfold differently than the person with aone-point advantage.
summary_sentence: Although all things lie along a spectrum, the tendency to impose (A)__________ boundaries between categories can lead to (B)__________ consequences.
options: ① invisible ... trivial
② flexible ... mixed
③ flexible ... complicated
④ absolute ... negligible
⑤ absolute ... destructive
explanation: 본문은 세상의 모든 것이 연속선상(spectrum)에 존재함에도 불구하고 인간이 임의로 명확한 구분(sharp distinctions)을 지으며, 이것이 삶에 큰 영향을 미치고 피해를 줄 수 있다고 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 명확하고 엄격한 경계를 의미하는 'absolute(절대적인)'가, (B)에는 그러한 구분이 초래하는 부정적인 결과인 'destructive(파괴적인)'가 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 보이지 않는 ... 사소한
② 유연한 ... 섞인
③ 유연한 ... 복잡한
④ 절대적인 ... 무시해도 될 정도의
⑤ 절대적인 ... 파괴적인

question: 27. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Once a nail is hammered in, it is friction that holds it in place. Friction is the force that arises when two surfaces are sliding, or trying to slide, against each other. (A) If you try to pull apart two blocks of wood that have been nailed together, the wood fibers grip the shaft of the nail. (B) The nail feels a force trying to rip it apart along its length, and we call that force tension. (C) The nail might stretch and split in half because the tension force is too large for the nail or the nail may become loose because the friction force is overcome. (D) The force it would take to stretch the nail is much larger than the friction forces on the surface, so we don't have to worry too much about the former. (E) It's the friction with which we need to concern ourselves.

question: 28. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers of which it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease to form, while sufficient fibers remain ⓐ<u>sound</u> for the material not to crack and fall apart. Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to ⓑ<u>withstand</u> being pulled apart, but it can also be torn accurately along the crease if a point of weakness - a small, initial tear - is opened up. This winning combination of mechanical properties ⓒ<u>enables</u> it to assume the shape of any object through creasing and folding - hence the art of origami. There are very few materials as good: plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, in which case it ⓓ<u>possesses</u> the rigidity required of a good wrapping material. So it is its ability to ⓔ<u>maintain</u> a crease while remaining stiff that makes paper uniquely suited to this purpose.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 글의 흐름상 플라스틱 시트는 매우 부드러운 경우가 아니라면 주름이 잡히지 않으며, 부드러운 경우에는 좋은 포장재로서 필요한 '강성(rigidity)'이 결여되어 있다는 맥락이 되어야 합니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 possesses(소유하다)는 lacks(결여되다)와 같은 단어로 고쳐져야 적절합니다.

question: 29. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

question: 30. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Paradoxically, it's uncertainty that makes us feel most alive. Think of events that shake you out of your everyday routine: maybe attending a family wedding, making a big presentation, or going somewhere you've never been. It's on those occasions that time seems to slow down a little, and you feel more fully engaged. The same holds true if the experience is risky, like mountain climbing or parasailing. Your senses are sharper. You notice more. Thanks to the release of a feel-good chemical in the brain called dopamine, you get a greater rush of pleasure from chance encounters with people than planned meetings. Good news, financial rewards, and gifts are more enjoyable if they are surprises. It's why the most popular television shows and movies are the ones with unexpected plot twists and astonishing endings.
summary_sentence: Our brain is wired to find (A)___________ exciting, since it triggers dopamine release and creates more (B)___________ experiences than daily routines.

② challenge ... stimulating
③ unfamiliarity ... uninspiring
④ unpredictability ... engaging

question: 13. 다음 글의 내용에 부합하는 상황이 아닌 것은?
passage: Any threatening situation may require us to make decisions and this requires information. So important is communication during a disaster that normal social barriers are often lowered. We will talk to strangers in a way we would never consider normally. Even relatively low grade disruption of our life such as a fire drill or a very late train seems to give us the permission to break normal etiquette and talk to strangers. The more important an event to a particular public, the more detailed and urgent the requirement for news becomes. Without an authoritative source of facts, whether that is a newspaper or trusted broadcast station, rumours often run riot. Rumours start because people believe their group to be in danger and so, although the rumour is unproven, feel they should pass it on. For example, if a worker heard that their employer's business was doing badly and people were going to be made redundant, they would pass that information on to colleagues.
options: ① 이상한 화학 약품 냄새가 마을에 퍼지는데 정부 기관이 아무런 발표가 없어서, 근처 공장에서 유독 물질이 유출되었다는 소문이 주민들 사이에 빠르게 퍼져나갔다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 문장이 의미하는 바를 구체적으로 정리하고자 한다. (A)는 <보기(A)>, (B)는 <보기(B)>에 주어진 단어를 올바르게 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오. (단, 어형 변형 없음)

question: 15. 다음 글을 읽고 네 명의 학생이 나눈 대화이다. 글을 제대로 이해한 학생만을 모두 고른 것은?
passage: There are deep similarities between viral contagion and behavioral contagion. question: 16. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Mental development consists of individuals increasingly mastering social codes and signals themselves, which they can master only in social situations with the support of more competent individuals, typically adults. In this sense, mental development consists of internalizing social patterns and gradually becoming a responsible actor among other responsible actors. In Denmark, the age of criminal responsibility is 15 years, which means that we then say that people have developed sufficient mental maturity to be accountable for their actions at this point. And at the age of 18 people are given the right to vote and are thereby formally included in the basic democratic process. I do not know whether these age boundaries are optimal, but it is clear that mental development takes place at different rates for different individuals, and depends especially on the social and family environment they have been given. Therefore, having formal limits for responsibility from a specific age that apply to everyone is a somewhat questionable practice. But the question, of course, is whether it can be done any differently.
options: ① 정신적 발달을 위해서는 더 유능한 개인들의 도움을 받는 사회적 상황이 필요하다.
② 덴마크에서는 18세가 되면 투표권을 부여받아 민주적 절차에 참여하게 된다.
③ 글쓴이는 덴마크의 형사 책임 연령인 15세가 최적의 기준이 될 수 없다고 생각한다.
④ 개인의 정신 발달 속도는 사회적, 가족적 환경 등 주어진 여건에 따라 달라진다.
⑤ 글쓴이는 모든 사람에게 동일한 연령 기준을 적용하는 것에 의문을 제기한다.
explanation: 본문에서 글쓴이는 이러한 연령 경계가 최적인지 알지 못한다고("I do not know whether these age boundaries are optimal") 언급했을 뿐, 15세가 최적의 기준이 될 수 없다고 단정적으로 생각한다는 내용은 없습니다. 글쓴이는 단지 모든 사람에게 동일하게 적용되는 공식적인 연령 제한 관행에 대해 의문을 제기하고 있을 뿐입니다. 따라서 ③번이 일치하지 않는 내용입니다.

question: 17. 다음 글에서 어법상 어색한 부분을 총 2개 찾아 어색한 부분만을 각각 바르게 고쳐 쓰시오. (단, 답의 순서는 무관함)
passage: The term "anchoring" was introduced by Roland Barthes who observed that text is often used next to images (his focus was on photographs) to confine meaning. Of all possible literal or implied interpretations an image could elicit, text would point the viewer towards a desired, specific direction. In advertising, as Barthes argues, the symbolic message does not guide identification but interpretation. The viewer is not asked to recognize what they see but to understand why they see it and what it means to them. By combining images with text, advertising produces symbolic meaning that is accurate and specific on the one hand, richer on the other, thus adding depth and eliminating breadth of rational and emotional interpretations. The headline or tagline of an ad directs the reader through the intended meanings of the image, so that the reader avoids some and receives others. It "remote-controls" the reader towards a meaning chosen in advance.
subjective_conditions: 답의 순서는 무관함
explanation: 롤랑 바르트의 '정묘화(anchoring)' 개념에 대한 설명으로, 텍스트가 이미지의 광범위한 해석을 제한하고 특정 방향으로 유도한다는 내용입니다. (1) 'meanings'를 수식하는 말로, '의도된 의미'라는 수동의 의미를 나타내야 하므로 과거분사 'intended'가 적절합니다. (2) 'meaning'을 수식하는 분사로, '미리 선택된 의미'라는 수동/완료의 관계이므로 과거분사 'chosen'이 적절합니다.

question: 18. 다음 글이 지적하는 '문제적 공감'의 사례로 볼 수 없는 경험은?
passage: Although empathy is widely praised by scholars and public figures, not everyone is an empathy booster. Critics of empathy argue that empathy will not save us from interpersonal and intergroup conflict. In fact, they argue, empathy makes such conflicts worse. These critics maintain that empathy can be exhausting and lead to burnout or insensitivity to suffering. They argue that we tend to empathize strongly with our in-group and resist empathizing with out-groups, and even enjoy the suffering of out-groups in competitive or threatening contexts. Thus, the prescription for more empathy is often counterproductive in cases of conflict. Empathy, they argue, can further entrench conflict and force us into an us vs. them mentality. Finally, even when we try to empathize with others who are dissimilar from us or in unfamiliar contexts, sometimes we are unable to accurately empathize with their experiences, causing further misunderstandings and frustration. Critics of empathy argue that we should give up on empathy and employ other tools in pursuit of social harmony, e.g., rational compassion or moral emotions like fear, anger, and shame.
options: ① My friends always tell me their troubles. After listening to three of them cry yesterday. I felt so emotionally drained that I just wanted to be alone and couldn't feel anything.
② I felt terrible for our school's basketball team when they lost the final game. To be honest, I was secretly happy when our biggest rival school was defeated earlier in the tournament.

③ My friend was stressed about choosing a university major that I know nothing about. Instead of offering my own opinions, I just listened carefully and asked questions to better understand his specific concerns.

④ My friend, who grew up in a very different culture, was upset about a family matter. I tried to comfort him by saying 'I totally understand what you're going through.' but it only seemed to make him more frustrated.

⑤ I felt a strong, immediate connection to the victims of the flood in my own country and wanted to donate. However, I didn't feel the same emotional pull when I read about a similar disaster in another part of the world.
explanation: 지문은 공감의 부정적인 측면(정서적 고갈, 내집단 편향, 타 집단에 대한 적대감, 문화적 차이로 인한 오해 등)을 지적하고 있습니다. ③은 상대방의 고민을 이해하기 위해 자신의 의견을 강요하지 않고 경청하며 질문하는 모습으로, 이는 지문에서 비판하는 '문제적 공감'이 아닌 바람직한 소통이나 합리적 연민의 모습에 가깝습니다.
options_translation: 친구들이 항상 나에게 그들의 고민을 말한다. 어제 그들 중 세 명이 우는 것을 듣고 난 후, 나는 정서적으로 너무 고갈되어 혼자 있고 싶었고 아무것도 느낄 수 없었다.
우리 학교 농구팀이 결승전에서 졌을 때 기분이 좋지 않았다. 솔직히 말해서, 우리 학교의 가장 큰 라이벌 학교가 토너먼트 초반에 패배했을 때 나는 남몰래 기뻤다.
내 친구는 내가 전혀 모르는 대학 전공을 선택하는 것에 대해 스트레스를 받고 있었다. 내 의견을 제시하는 대신, 나는 주의 깊게 듣고 그의 구체적인 걱정을 더 잘 이해하기 위해 질문을 했다.
매우 다른 문화권에서 자란 내 친구가 가족 문제로 속상해했다. 나는 '네가 겪고 있는 일을 완전히 이해해'라고 말하며 그를 위로하려 했지만, 그것은 그를 더 좌절하게 만드는 것처럼 보였다.
나는 우리나라의 홍수 피해자들에게 강하고 즉각적인 유대감을 느꼈고 기부하고 싶었다. 하지만 세계의 다른 지역에서 일어난 비슷한 재난에 대해 읽었을 때는 똑같은 감정적 끌림을 느끼지 못했다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The traditional bank manager in the 1950s was usually a respected pillar of the community, a cautious, careful sort of person who probably went to bed early and didn't drink too much. But from the 1970s a new kind of banker appeared - loud, flashy, and arrogant. These bankers loved taking big risks. They wanted to get rich quick and blow their money on fast cars and expensive champagne. They made their money through what's called 'speculation'. Normally, people buy things because they want to use them, such as wheat to make bread and petrol to run the car. But when people speculate, they buy things even when they have no interest in using them. They might buy a load of wheat simply because they think that its price is going to rise when a drought is predicted in wheat-growing areas. If their guess is right, __________ _____________________________.
options: ① they put the wheat back on the market to gain a financial return
② they continue to hold the wheat, expecting the price to rise even further later
③ they attempt to buy even more wheat once its market price has peaked
④ they decide to use the purchased wheat to bake bread for local townspeople
⑤ they finally earn the community's respect for their insightful economic forecasting
explanation: 이 글은 1950년대의 보수적인 은행가와 1970년대 이후의 투기적인 은행가를 대조하고 있습니다. 투기(speculation)란 물건을 직접 사용하기 위해서가 아니라 가격이 오를 것을 예상하여 시세 차익을 얻기 위해 구매하는 행위를 말합니다. 따라서 가뭄 예측으로 밀 가격이 오를 것이라는 예상이 맞을 경우, 투기꾼들은 그 밀을 다시 시장에 내놓아 경제적 이득을 얻으려 할 것입니다.
options_translation: 재정적 수익을 얻기 위해 밀을 시장에 다시 내놓는다
나중에 가격이 훨씬 더 오를 것을 예상하여 밀을 계속 보유한다
시장 가격이 정점에 이르면 밀을 훨씬 더 많이 사려고 시도한다
지역 주민들을 위해 빵을 굽는 데 구입한 밀을 사용하기로 결정한다
그들의 통찰력 있는 경제 예측으로 마침내 공동체의 존경을 얻는다

question: 20. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A great strength of the market mechanism is that there are incentives for individuals to reveal their knowledge through their behavior. This stands in contrast to many strategic situations - for example, in political negotiations - in which it is wise not to let the other side know what one's true preferences or production capacities are. A perfectly competitive market that clears on the spot leaves no room for such strategies. If prices are not sticky - as many models assume - individuals adapt their behavior instantaneously, whenever their preferences or the circumstances change. They stop buying items that do not satisfy their needs and stop selling items that do not provide them with optimal gains, maybe switching to the production of other items. If they have motivational problems, for example, falling into denial about the fact that there is no demand for their products, markets reveal to them, sometimes in quite brutal ways, that they better accept this fact.
options: ① Using Market Incentives to Control People' Preferences
② The Brutal Reality of a Perfectly Competitive Market
③ How Individuals Adapt to Everchanging Market Prices
④ How Markets Reveal Knowledge Through Individual Behavior
⑤ Why Market Communication Is Superior to Political Negotiation
explanation: 시장의 메커니즘은 개인들이 자신의 행동(구매 및 판매 중단 등)을 통해 자신이 가진 정보와 선호를 드러내도록 만든다는 내용입니다. 이는 자신의 정보를 숨기는 것이 유리한 정치적 협상과는 대조적입니다. 따라서 시장이 개인의 행동을 통해 지식을 드러낸다는 내용의 4번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 사람들의 선호를 통제하기 위해 시장 인센티브를 사용하는 것
완전 경쟁 시장의 잔인한 현실
개인이 계속 변화하는 시장 가격에 적응하는 방식
시장이 개인의 행동을 통해 지식을 드러내는 방식
시장 소통이 정치적 협상보다 우월한 이유

question: 22. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: All human cultures mark the passing of time by the differences they observe in the world around them. Our choice of which differences to mark depends firstly on what we can observe and secondly on what is important in our lives. How we mark the differences - the shapes of our calendars and our rituals - depends on the connections we make between those two things. In the agricultural society of pre-modern Europe, where higher latitudes make the seasons easily observable, it was natural to monitor the solar cycle. Conversely, among the largely nomadic peoples of Arabia, for whom seasonal changes were less significant, the lunar calendar was a more sensible choice. That did not make it inevitable that Islam would use a lunar calendar and Roman Christianity a solar one, but political and religious decisions were made from options limited by geography and lifestyle, filtered through tradition.
options: ① 사람들의 생활 방식이 다르다면 달력의 형태도 달라진다.
② 생활 방식과 생계 형태가 사람들의 제도적 선택을 좌우한다.
③ 지역의 자연환경과 계절 변화가 사람들의 시간 개념을 결정한다.
④ 관찰 가능한 자연 현상은 지역 사회가 문화를 형성하는 중요한 출발점이 된다.
⑤ 인류의 시간 구분 방식은 자연적 조건과 사회문화적 선택이 결합되어 형성된다.
explanation: 이 글은 인간이 시간을 표시하는 방식이 주변 세계에서 관찰할 수 있는 것(자연적 조건)과 우리 삶에 중요한 것(사회문화적 선택) 사이의 연결에 달려 있다고 설명합니다. 농경 사회인 유럽에서는 태양 주기를, 유목 민족인 아라비아에서는 태음력을 선택한 사례를 통해 지리적·생활 방식적 제약 내에서 정치적, 종교적 결정(전통)이 필터링되어 시간 체계가 형성됨을 보여줍니다. 따라서 정답은 ⑤번입니다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 문장을 <보기>에 주어진 단어만을 모두 한 번씩만 사용하여 완성하시오. (단, 필요시 어형 변형 가능)
passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers of which it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease to form, while sufficient fibers remain undamaged for the material not to crack and fall apart. Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to resist being pulled apart, but it can also be torn easily and accurately along the crease if a point of weakness - a small, initial tear - is opened up. This winning combination of mechanical properties allows it to assume the shape of any object through creasing and folding - hence the art of origami. There are very few materials as good: metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult. Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, in which case it lacks the rigidity required of a good wrapping material. __________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 보기의 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용
필요시 어형 변형 가능
answer: What makes paper especially suited for origami and wrapping is its ability to hold a crease while staying stiff
explanation: 이 글은 종이가 가진 기계적 특성(접히면서도 형태를 유지하고 찢어지지 않는 성질)이 종이접기와 포장에 적합하게 만든다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 마지막 문장은 종이가 다른 재료들과 달리 왜 종이접기와 포장에 특별히 적합한지를 요약하는 문장이 되어야 합니다. 'What makes paper especially suited for origami and wrapping'(종이를 종이접기와 포장에 특히 적합하게 만드는 것은)을 주어로 하고, 'is its ability to hold a crease while staying stiff'(뻣뻣함을 유지하면서 주름을 잡는 능력이다)를 보어로 구성합니다. 주어진 'suit for'는 'suited for'로 변형하여 사용합니다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The well-known American ethnologist Alfred Louis Kroeber made a rich and in-depth study of women's evening dress in the West, stretching back about three centuries and using reproductions of engravings. Having adjusted the dimensions of these plates due to their diverse origins, he was able to analyse the constant elements in fashion features and to come up with a study that was neither intuitive nor approximate, but precise, mathematical and statistical. He reduced women's clothing to a certain number of features: length and size of the skirt, size and depth of the neckline, height of the waistline. He demonstrated unambiguously that fashion is a profoundly regular phenomenon which is not located at the level of annual variations but on the scale of history. For practically 300 years, women's dress was subject to a very precise periodic cycle: forms reach the furthest point in their variations every fifty years. If, at any one moment, skirts are at their longest, fifty years later they will be at their shortest; thus skirts become long again fifty years after being short and a hundred years after being long.
options: ① Random Fashion Trends: No Rules at All
② Skirt Length: A Matter of Personal Taste?
③ Fashion and History: A Mathematical Cycle!
④ The Secret of Engravings in Western Dresses
⑤ Waistlines and Necklines: Symbols of Social Power
explanation: 인류학자 알프레드 루이스 크로버의 연구를 통해 패션이 단순한 유행의 변화가 아니라 역사적 규모에서 매우 정밀하고 주기적인 수학적 패턴(약 50년 주기)을 따른다는 것을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 패션이 역사 속에서 수학적 주기를 가진다는 내용의 ③번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 무작위한 패션 트렌드: 규칙은 전혀 없다
② 치마 길이: 개인적 취향의 문제인가?
③ 패션과 역사: 수학적인 주기!
④ 서양 의복 판화의 비밀
⑤ 허리선과 목선: 사회적 권력의 상징

question: 25. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When we get an unfavorable outcome, in some ways the last thing we want to hear is that the process was fair. As outraging as the combination of an unfavorable outcome and an unfair process is, this combination also brings with it a consolation prize: the possibility of attributing the bad outcome to something other than ourselves. We may reassure ourselves by believing that our bad outcome had little to do with us and everything to do with the unfair process. If the process is fair, however, we cannot nearly as easily externalize the outcome; we got what we got "fair and square." When the process is fair we believe that our outcome is deserved, which is another way of saying that ______________________________.
options: ① the result came from something within ourselves
② outcomes are usually beyond our personal control
③ the outcome could have changed in another process
④ luck occasionally determines whether we succeed or fail
⑤ an unfair process tends to make accepting the result feel easier
explanation: 글의 핵심은 공정한 과정에서의 불리한 결과는 외부 탓(부당한 과정)으로 돌릴 수 없기 때문에 결국 그 결과가 본인 내부의 어떤 것(실력, 노력 등)에서 기인했다고 받아들일 수밖에 없다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 과정이 공정할 때 결과가 '응당 받아야 할 것(deserved)'이라고 믿는 것은 곧 결과가 우리 내면의 무언가로부터 나왔다는 것을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 결과가 우리 내부의 무언가로부터 나왔다
② 결과는 대개 우리의 개인적 통제를 벗어난다
③ 결과는 다른 과정에서 바뀔 수도 있었다
④ 운이 때때로 우리가 성공할지 실패할지를 결정한다
⑤ 불공정한 과정은 결과를 받아들이는 것을 더 쉽게 만드는 경향이 있다

question: 26. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것만을 모두 고르면?
passage: Dictionary definitions are constantly revised to keep up with our changing uses and knowledge. ⓐ<u>In Roman times, "addicts" were people who were unable to pay their debts and gave himself as slaves to their creditors</u>. ⓑ<u>The word eventually came to be associated with drug dependency: one becomes a slave to one's addiction</u>. ⓒ<u>The word "husband" originally referred to be a homeowner; it had nothing to do with being married</u>. ⓓ<u>But because owning your own property made it more likely you'd find a mate, the word eventually came to mean a male who has been wed</u>. On November 5th, 1605, Guy Fawkes tried to blow up the British Parliament. He was captured and put to death. ⓔ<u>Loyalists burned his effigy, and they nicknamed the "guy.</u>" Centuries later, the word lost its negative connotation and a musical named Guys and Dolls ran on Broadway. If you could transport yourself one hundred years into the future, you'd find yourself confused by your great-grandchildren's speech because language itself is an ever-changing reflection of human invention.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ

question: 17. 다음 글을 읽고 추론할 수 있는 것은?

question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [25년 9월 37번]

question: 19. 다음 글에서 어법상 어색한 세 곳을 찾아 바르게 고치시오. [25년 9월 39번]
passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers of which it makes can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease to form, while sufficient fibers remain undamaged for the material not to crack and fall apart. Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to resist being pulled apart, but it can also be torn easily and accurately along the crease if a point of weakness - a small, initial tear is opened up. This winning combination of mechanical properties allows it assuming the shape of any object through creasing and folding - hence the art of origami. "There are very few materials as good: metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult." Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, in which case it lacks the rigid required of a good wrapping material. So it is its ability to hold a crease while remaining stiff that makes paper uniquely suited to this purpose.
answer: (1) makes → is made, (2) assuming → to assume, (3) rigid → rigidity
explanation: (1) '종이가 만들어진 섬유'라는 의미로 수동태인 'is made'가 되어야 합니다. (2) 'allow + 목적어 + to 부정사' 구문이므로 'to assume'으로 고쳐야 합니다. (3) 'the' 뒤에는 명사가 와야 하므로 형용사인 'rigid'를 명사형인 'rigidity'로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: All translators feel some pressure from the community of readers for whom they are doing their work. And all translators arrive at their interpretations in dialogue with other people. He had Greek commentaries to refer to, and translations that had already been done in English, Latin, and French - and of course he had dictionaries. Translators always draw on more than one source text. Even when the scene of translation consists of just one person with a pen, paper, and the book that is being translated, or even when it is just one person translating orally for another, that person's linguistic knowledge arises from lots of other texts and other conversations. And then his or her idea of the translation's purpose will be influenced by the expectations of the person or people it is for. In both these senses every translation is a crowd translation.

passage: Although empathy is widely praised by scholars and public figures, not everyone is an empathy booster. They argue that we tend to empathize strongly with our ingroup and resist empathizing with outgroups, and even enjoy the suffering of outgroups in competitive or threatening contexts. Thus, the prescription for more empathy is often inefficient in cases of conflict. Empathy, they argue, can further encourage conflict and force us into an us vs. them mentality. Finally, even when we try to empathize with others who are dissimilar from us or in unfamiliar contexts, sometimes we are unable to accurately empathize with their experiences, causing further misunderstandings and frustration. Critics of empathy argue that we should give up on empathy and employ other tools in pursuit of social harmony, e.g., rational compassion or moral emotions like fear, anger, and shame.

question: 25. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

passage: Weber's law concerns the perception of difference between two stimuli. It suggests that we might not be able to detect a 1-mm difference when we are looking at lines 466 mm and 467 mm in length, but we may be able to detect a 1-mm difference when we are comparing a line 2 mm long with one 3 mm long. Another example of this principle is that we can detect 1 candle when it is lit in an otherwise dark room. But when 1 candle is lit in a room in which 100 candles are already burning, we may not notice the light from this candle. Therefore, the Just-noticeable difference (JND) varies as a function of the strength of the signals. For example, the JND is greater for very loud noises than it is for much more quiet sounds. When a sound is very weak, we can tell that another sound is louder, even if it is barely louder. When a sound is very loud, to tell that another sound is even louder, it has to be much louder. Thus, Weber's law means that it is harder to distinguish between two samples when those samples are larger or stronger levels of the stimuli.
summary_sentence: According to Weber's law, small differences are (A)__________ to detect in weak stimuli than in strong ones, which means that (B)__________ changes are required in strong stimuli to be perceived.

③ (A) more challenging / (B) higher
④ (A) simpler / (B) smaller
⑤ (A) easier / (B) weaker
explanation: 웨버의 법칙(Weber's law)에 따르면, 자극의 강도가 약할 때는 작은 차이도 쉽게 감지할 수 있지만, 자극이 강해질수록 차이를 감지하기 위해 더 큰 변화가 필요합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 약한 자극에서 작은 차이를 감지하는 것이 강한 자극에서보다 '덜 어렵다(less difficult)'가 들어가야 하며, (B)에는 강한 자극에서는 지각되기 위해 '더 큰(greater)' 변화가 요구된다는 내용이 들어가야 합니다.

But on the other hand, literature has historically been seen as dangerous: it promotes the questioning of authority and social arrangements. explanation: 글의 흐름상 '기술(자동화)'은 노동을 대체하는 힘(substituting force)과 보완하는 힘(complementing force)을 동시에 가집니다. 밑줄 친 부분은 과거의 우려가 잘못되었다는 이유를 설명하는 문장으로, 조상들이 '보완하는 힘'을 과소평가하거나 무시한 채 기술이 노동자를 완전히 대체할 것(대체하는 힘의 승리)이라고 예상했음을 의미합니다. 따라서 ④번 '자동화가 인력을 대체할 것이라고 예상했지만, 기술은 노동을 보완하고 노동 수요를 증가시켰다'가 가장 적절한 해석입니다.

question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

passage: Many animals pursue a mixed strategy of accumulating both body fat and food, which leads one to ask, "What are the relative advantages and disadvantages of these two forms of energy storage?" question: 27. 윗글을 읽고, Gravitational lensing이 의미하는 바를 주어진 조건에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: According to Einstein's theory, a large mass like the Sun 'bends' space-time. Newton's theory makes no such prediction. This bending of space-time leads to phenomena such as 'gravitational lensing' where the light of distant stars appears to be in different locations when they pass by a large mass like the Sun. We don't normally see this lensing because stars aren't visible during the day when the Sun is out, but a solar eclipse in 1919 allowed scientists to observe what the Sun's gravity was doing to the light from distant stars. The stars around the Sun appeared to have moved from their normal positions in the night sky. The shift was much larger than Newton's theory predicted, but exactly in the positions predicted by Einstein's theory.*solar eclipse: 일식
subjective_conditions: 1. 본문에서 찾아서 그대로 쓸 것.
2. 종속절까지 그대로, 완전한 문장을 쓸 것.
subjective_answer_format: → Gravitational lensing is the phenomenon where ______________________________________________. [2.9자ᄆᄃ]
answer: the light of distant stars appears to be in different locations when they pass by a large mass like the Sun.
explanation: 본문의 세 번째 문장 '...phenomena such as 'gravitational lensing' where the light of distant stars appears to be in different locations when they pass by a large mass like the Sun.'에서 해당 현상을 설명하는 관계부사절 내용을 그대로 가져와 완성합니다.

question: 29. 다음 글을 읽고, 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 조건에 맞추어 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: Paradoxically, ___________________________________. Think of events that shake you out of your everyday routine: maybe attending a family wedding, making a big presentation, or going somewhere you've never been. Your senses are sharper. You notice more. Thanks to the release of a feel-good chemical in the brain called dopamine, you get a greater rush of pleasure from chance encounters with people than planned meetings. Good news, financial rewards, and gifts are more enjoyable if they are surprises. It's why the most popular television shows and movies are the ones with unexpected plot twists and astonishing endings.
subjective_conditions: It으로 시작하는 강조 구문을 사용할 것

vocabulary_box: feel / make / us / is / that / uncertainty / it / most / alive
answer: It is uncertainty that makes us feel most alive.

question: 31. 다음 글을 읽고, (A)~(E) 중 어법상 어색한 것 2개를 골라, 밑줄 친 부분을 올바르게 다시 쓰시오.

question: 32. 다음 글을 읽고, 적절한 주제를 주어진 조건에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: "Tactics" is a term drawn from military usage. Strategies are plans of action directing a military force when attacking another, and tactics are responses to conditions on the ground. In response, we must develop tactics for dealing with time and waiting. These aren't tactics to eliminate waiting; instead, these are tactics for teaching us how to learn from the seams. question: 1. 다음 글을 읽고 밑줄 친 어휘가 가진 영영 뜻으로 바르지 않게 설명된 것은? [2.9점]
passage: It's ⓐ<u>conceivable</u> that in a world where solar panels are incredibly expensive and there's an extreme collapse in the cost of launching objects to space, you might want to maximize your energy per panel by putting them above the ⓑ<u>atmosphere</u>. But panels are cheap, and even if we assume pretty steep drops in the cost of space launch, the numbers don't add up. This becomes especially clear when you start to think about ⓒ<u>maintenance</u>. options: ① ⓐconceivable: possible to imagine or believe; able to be thought of as a possibility.
② ⓑatmosphere: the mixture of gases that surrounds a planet; the feeling, mood, or tone of a place or situation.
③ ⓒmaintenance: the continuous process of enhancing something by making it more advanced than before.
④ ⓓradiation: energy that comes from a source and travels through space or a material as waves or particles, especially light, heat, or nuclear energy.

options_translation: ⓐconceivable: 상상하거나 믿는 것이 가능한; 가능성으로 생각될 수 있는.
ⓑatmosphere: 행성을 둘러싼 가스의 혼합물; 장소나 상황의 느낌, 분위기 또는 어조.
ⓒmaintenance: 이전보다 더 발전되게 함으로써 무언가를 향상시키는 지속적인 과정.
ⓓradiation: 원천으로부터 나와 파동이나 입자의 형태로 우주나 물질을 통해 이동하는 에너지, 특히 빛, 열, 또는 핵 에너지.
ⓔdebris: 부서지거나 파괴되거나 버려진 것의 흩어진 조각들.

question: 25. 다음 글에 있는 문법적인 오류 두 곳을 찾아 바르게 고치고 그 이유를 설명하시오.
passage: Everything in the world exists on a continuum, whether in speed, size, or any other possible descriptor you could think of. Still, we create and mindlessly adopt sharp distinctions, and those distinctions change lives far more dramatically than marginal differences ever do. Indeed, all differences are arbitrary, but drawing hard lines between categories hide this arbitrariness and can be severely damaging. I call this resulting damage "the borderline effect." The examples are endless. Someone's IQ is 69 and someone else's is 70 - but only the score of 70 is deemed to be within the range of normal. We don't have to be statisticians to know there is not a meaningful difference between 69 and 70. Yet once the person with the lower score is labeled "cognitively impaired," his or her life will unfold differently with the person with a one-point advantage.
answer: (1) hide → hides / 수정이유: 주어가 동명사구인 drawing hard lines between categories이므로 단수 취급하여야 한다.(2) differently with → differently than or differently from / 수정이유: differently는 비교 부사이며, 전치사로 with를 사용하지 않는다.
explanation: (1) 문장의 주어는 'drawing hard lines between categories'라는 동명사구입니다. 동명사구 주어는 단수 취급하므로 동사 hide를 단수형인 hides로 고쳐야 합니다. (2) 'differently'는 비교의 대상을 나타낼 때 전치사 from이나 than을 사용합니다. 'with'는 ~와 함께라는 의미로 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: The Net differs from most of the mass media it replaces in an obvious and very important way: it's bidirectional. ④ The Net has been only confined to commercial transactions rather than personal interactions.

explanation: 지문 후반부에서 인터넷은 사업뿐만 아니라 개인과 개인을 연결하며, 수백만 명의 사람들이 자신의 디지털 창작물을 공유하고 다른 사람의 작업에 참여하는 개인적 방송 매체로 쓰인다고 설명합니다. 따라서 인터넷이 상업적 거래에만 국한되었다는 ④번은 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 인터넷의 양방향성은 전통적인 대중 매체와 비교하여 그 유용성을 향상시켰다.

④ 인터넷은 개인적인 상호작용보다는 오직 상업적인 거래에만 국한되어 왔다.
