question: 17. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 this route가 의미하는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: As the old joke goes: "Software, free. User manual, $10,000." But it's no joke. A couple of high-profile companies make their living selling instruction and paid support for free software. The copy of code, being merebits, is free. The lines of free code become valuable to you only through support and guidance. A lot of medical and genetic information will go <u>this route</u> in the coming decades. Right now getting a full copy of all your DNA is very expensive ($10,000), but soon it won't be. The price is dropping so fast, it will be $100 soon, and then the next year insurance companies will offer to sequence you for free. When a copy of your sequence costs nothing, the interpretation of what it means, what you can do about it, and how to use it - the manual for your genes - will be expensive. *sequence: (유전자) 배열 순서를 밝히다
options: ① having insurance companies cover the cost of DNA sequencing
② providing free access to records but charging for data protection
③ making genetic data free but having interpretation cost a lot
④ facing legal and ethical issues with genetic research
⑤ reducing the price of DNA sequencing technology
explanation: 글의 앞부분에서 소프트웨어 코드는 무료이지만 매뉴얼과 지원이 유료인 모델을 언급합니다. 의료 및 유전 정보가 '이 경로(this route)'를 갈 것이라는 말은, 유전자 정보(데이터)는 곧 저렴하거나 무료가 되겠지만, 그것을 해석하고 활용하는 방법(매뉴얼)은 유료가 될 것임을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 보험 회사가 DNA 서열 분석 비용을 지불하게 하는 것
② 기록에 대한 무료 접근을 제공하지만 데이터 보호에 비용을 청구하는 것
③ 유전 데이터를 무료로 만들되 해석에 많은 비용이 들게 하는 것
④ 유전 연구와 관련된 법적 및 윤리적 문제에 직면하는 것
⑤ DNA 서열 분석 기술의 가격을 낮추는 것

question: 18. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 pay as it goes가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The brain is a high-energy consumer of glucose, which is its fuel. Although the brain accounts for merely 3 percent of a person's body weight, it consumes 20 percent of the available fuel. Your brain can't store fuel, however, so it has to "<u>pay as it goes</u>." Since your brain is incredibly adaptive, it economizes its fuel resources. Thus, during a period of high stress, it shifts away from the analysis of the nuances of a situation to a singular and fixed focus on the stressful situation at hand. You don't sit back and speculate about the meaning of life when you are stressed. Instead, you devote all your energy to trying to figure out what action to take. Sometimes, however, this shift from the higher-thinking parts of the brain to the automatic and reflexive parts of the brain can lead you to do something too quickly, without thinking. *glucose: 포도당
options: ① It must store energy for future use.
② It has to use fuel immediately as needed.
③ It can reduce its energy demand in the long run.
④ It consumes less fuel compared to other body organs.
⑤ It wastes a large amount of energy when under stress.
explanation: 뇌는 연료(포도당)를 저장할 수 없기 때문에 그때그때 즉각적으로 지불(에너지 사용)을 해야 한다는 뜻입니다. 문맥상 에너지를 미리 비축해두지 못하고 필요한 순간마다 즉시 연료를 사용해야 함을 나타냅니다.
options_translation: ① 미래의 사용을 위해 에너지를 저장해야 한다.
② 필요할 때 연료를 즉시 사용해야 한다.
③ 장기적으로 에너지 수요를 줄일 수 있다.
④ 다른 신체 기관에 비해 연료를 적게 소모한다.
⑤ 스트레스를 받을 때 많은 양의 에너지를 낭비한다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 부분이 지칭하는 것으로 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: The irony of early democracy in Europe is that ⓐ<u>it</u> thrived and prospered precisely because European rulers for a very long time were remarkably weak. The clearest way to understand this weakness is by looking at how little revenue ⓒ<u>they</u> managed to collect. Eventually, Europeans did succeed in creating stronger systems of taxation, but ⓓ<u>this achievement</u> came only after a very long time. Unlike rulers in Asia and the Middle East, European rulers did not have strong governments that could manage large amounts of resources. ⓔ<u>They</u> often depended on the cooperation of local nobles and towns, which limited their power even further. Meanwhile, during the same period, Chinese emperors and Muslim caliphs extracted a far greater share of economic output than most European monarchs, except in a few wealthy city-states.

question: 20. 윗글을 읽고 나눈 대화 중 본문의 내용과 관련이 없는 것은?
passage: As you may already know, what and how you buy can be political. To whom do you want to give your money? Which companies and corporations do you value and respect? Be ⓐ<u>mindful</u> about every purchase by carefully researching the corporations that are taking our money to decide if they deserve our support. Do they have a record of polluting the environment, or do they have fair-trade practices and an end-of-life plan for the products they make? Are they ⓑ<u>committed</u> to bringing about good in the world? For instance, my family has found a company producing recycled, plastic-packaging-free toilet paper with a ⓒ<u>social conscience</u>. They contribute 50 percent of their ⓓ<u>profits</u> to the construction of toilets around the world, and we're genuinely happy to spend our money on this special toilet paper each month. Remember that the corporate world is built on consumers, so as a consumer you have the power to vote with your ⓔ<u>wallet</u> and encourage companies to embrace healthier and more sustainable practices with every purchase you choose to make.
options: ① A: Did you know that the way we spend money can actually be political?   B: Yeah, I've heard that. It's like every purchase is a kind of vote for the companies we support, right?

② A: Exactly. That's why it matters which companies we give our money to-some care about the planet, while others just exploit it.   B: True. For example, I always check if a brand has fair-trade practices or if they use eco-friendly packaging.
③ A: So, after reading the passage, I learned about that toilet paper company.   B: Yeah, me too. But I thought all they do is plant trees whenever someone buys their products.

④ A: The point is, as consumers, we have the power to push corporations to change.   B: Right. If enough people are mindful about what they buy, companies will be forced to adopt healthier and more sustainable practices.
⑤ A: It might take some effort to research, but I think it's worth it.   B: Definitely. Every choice we make adds up, so in the long run, our spending really can make a difference.
explanation: 본문에서 예로 든 화장지 회사는 수익의 50%를 전 세계 화장실 건설에 기부한다고 언급되어 있습니다. ③번 대화에서 '나무를 심는 것뿐이라고 생각했다'는 내용은 본문의 사실과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① A: 돈을 쓰는 방식이 실제로 정치적일 수 있다는 거 알았니? B: 응, 들어봤어. 모든 구매가 우리가 지지하는 기업에 대한 일종의 투표 같은 거지, 맞지?
② A: 맞아. 그래서 우리가 누구에게 돈을 주느냐가 중요해. 어떤 기업은 지구를 아끼지만, 다른 기업은 그냥 착취하거든. B: 사실이야. 예를 들어, 나는 항상 브랜드가 공정 거래 관행을 따르는지나 친환경 포장재를 사용하는지 확인해.
③ A: 그래서 지문을 읽고 나서 그 화장지 회사에 대해 알게 됐어. B: 응, 나도 그래. 하지만 난 그들이 누군가 제품을 살 때마다 나무를 심는 것뿐이라고 생각했어.
④ A: 핵심은 소비자로서 우리가 기업들이 변하도록 압박할 힘이 있다는 거야. B: 맞아. 충분한 사람들이 자신이 사는 것에 주의를 기울인다면, 기업들은 더 건강하고 지속 가능한 관행을 채택할 수밖에 없을 거야.
⑤ A: 조사하는 데 노력이 좀 들 수도 있겠지만, 그럴 가치가 있다고 생각해. B: 분명히 그래. 우리가 내리는 모든 선택이 쌓여서, 결국 장기적으로 우리의 소비는 정말로 차이를 만들 수 있어.

question: 22. 다음 글의 전개 과정에 비추어 볼 때, 사건들을 나열한 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The passport control line was short and the inspectors looked relaxed; except the inspector at my window. He seemed to want to model the seriousness of the task at hand for the other inspectors. Maybe that's why I felt uneasy when he studied my passport more carefully than I expected. "You were here in September," he said. "Why are you back so soon?" "I came in September to prepare to return this month," I replied with a trembling voice, considering if I missed any Italian regulations. "For how long?" he asked. "One month, this time," I answered truthfully. I knew it was not against the rules to stay in Italy for three months. "Enjoy your stay," he finally said, as he stamped my passport. Whew! As I walked away, the burden I had carried, even though I did nothing wrong, vanished into the air. My shoulders, once weighed down, now stretched out with comfort.
ordered_passages: ⓐ The inspector stamped the passport.
ⓑ The inspector asked why the narrator returned so soon.
ⓒ The narrator's anxiety disappeared, and relief took its place.
ⓓ The narrator answered that this stay would last for one month.
ⓔ The narrator wondered if any Italian regulations had been missed.
explanation: 글의 흐름은 다음과 같습니다. (ⓑ) 입국 심사관이 왜 이렇게 빨리 돌아왔는지 묻고, (ⓔ) 화자는 이탈리아 규정을 어긴 것이 있는지 걱정하며, (ⓓ) 이번에는 한 달 동안 머물 것이라고 대답합니다. (ⓐ) 심사관이 여권에 도장을 찍어주고, (ⓒ) 화자의 불안감이 사라지며 안도감이 찾아옵니다. 따라서 적절한 순서는 ⓑ-ⓔ-ⓓ-ⓐ-ⓒ입니다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The well-known American ethnologist Alfred Louis Kroeber made a rich and in-depth study of women's evening dress in the West, stretching back about three centuries and using reproductions of engravings. Having adjusted the dimensions of these plates due to their diverse origins, he was able to analyse the constant elements in fashion features and to come up with a study that was neither intuitive nor approximate, but precise, mathematical and statistical. He reduced women's clothing to a certain number of features: length and size of the skirt, size and depth of the neckline, height of the waistline. He demonstrated unambiguously that fashion is a profoundly regular phenomenon which is not located at the level of annual variations but on the scale of history. For practically 300 years, women's dress was subject to a very precise periodic cycle: forms reach the furthest point in their variations every fifty years. If, at any one moment, skirts are at their longest, fifty years later they will be at their shortest; thus skirts become long again fifty years after being short and a hundred years after being long.*engraving: 판화 **dimension: 크기
options: ① Fashion as a Historical Phenomenon, Not a Passing
② The Random Shifts of Fashion without Any Clear Pattern
③ Why Evening Dresses Became Shorter in Modern Times
④ The Rise and Fall of Women's Dress Through the Ages
⑤ The Historical Rhythms of Changes in Women's Clothing
explanation: 이 글은 Alfred Louis Kroeber의 연구를 인용하여 여성의 패션이 단순한 연간 변화가 아니라 역사적 규모에서 수학적이고 통계적으로 예측 가능한 주기적인 리듬(50년 주기)을 가지고 변화한다는 것을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '여성 의복 변화의 역사적 리듬'인 ⑤번이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 일시적인 것이 아닌 역사적 현상으로서의 패션
② 명확한 패턴 없는 패션의 무작위적 변화
③ 현대에 이브닝드레스가 짧아진 이유
④ 시대를 통한 여성 의복의 흥망성쇠
⑤ 여성 의복 변화의 역사적 리듬

question: 24. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Many things spark envy: ownership, status, health, youth, talent, popularity, beauty. It is often confused with jealousy because the physical reactions are identical. The difference: the subject of envy is a thing (status, money, health etc.). The subject of jealousy is the behaviour of a third person. Envy needs two people. Jealousy, on the other hand, requires three: Peter is jealous of Sam because the beautiful girl next door rings him instead. ______________________________________. Paradoxically, with envy we direct resentments toward those who are most similar to us in age, career and residence. We don't envy businesspeople from the century before last. We don't envy millionaires on the other side of the globe. As a writer, I don't envy musicians, managers or dentists, but other writers. As a CEO you envy other, bigger CEOs. As a supermodel you envy more successful supermodels. Aristotle knew this: 'Potters envy potters.
options: ① Envy and jealousy are thus distinguished mainly by the number of people involved.
② This shows that envy arises mainly when others' advantages seem unattainable.
③ Therefore, envy is less about possessions and more about the fear of losing affection.
④ These emotional reactions are usually stronger toward strangers than toward those close to us.
⑤ This difference in numbers proves that envy and jealousy are essentially the same emotion.
explanation: 지문 앞부분에서 시기와 질투의 차이점을 설명하며, 시기는 두 명(envy needs two people)이 필요하고 질투는 세 명(jealousy requires three)이 필요하다고 언급합니다. 빈칸은 이 설명을 요약하는 문장이 들어가야 하므로, 인원수에 의해 두 감정이 구분된다는 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 시기와 질투는 따라서 주로 관련된 사람들의 수에 의해 구별된다.
② 이것은 시기가 주로 타인의 이점이 도달 불가능해 보일 때 발생함을 보여준다.
③ 그러므로, 시기는 소유에 관한 것이라기보다 애정을 잃는 것에 대한 두려움에 관한 것이다.
④ 이러한 정서적 반응은 보통 가까운 사람들보다 낯선 사람들에게 더 강하게 나타난다.
⑤ 이러한 숫자의 차이는 시기와 질투가 본질적으로 같은 감정임을 증명한다.

question: 25. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The first human beings probably evolved in tropical regions where survival was possible without clothing. It is likely that they had very dark skin because light skin would have given little protection against the burning rays of the sun. There is a debate about whether these people spread into other parts of the world or, instead, whether people developed independently in various parts of the world. Whichever the case, it is believed that in time they became capable of spreading out from Africa, eventually to most of the world. This was probably because their physical characteristics changed. For instance, early hominids probably did not walk upright, but when they developed that ability, they could travel more efficiently. More important, perhaps, was their development of tool making. With tools, they could hunt other animals, so they could consume more protein and fat than their low-energy vegetarian diet would have provided. Not only their bodies but also their brains would have been changed with more energy. The brain needs lots of energy to grow. As their diet expanded, hominids could physically and intellectually expand their territory. This demonstrates how ______________________ _________________________.*hominid: 인류
options: ① diverse climates fostered the rapid development of human intelligence
② dietary shifts profoundly influenced both physical evolution and territorial expansion
③ the need for clothing directly spurred the invention of advanced tools
④ early hominids initially relied solely on vegetarian diets for survival

④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓓ의 'increase'는 주어 'staying with it'이 동명사구로 단수 취급되므로 수 일치에 따라 'increases'가 되어야 적절합니다.

question: 5. 윗글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: If we've invested in something that hasn't repaid us - be it money in a failing venture, or time in an unhappy relationship - we find ⓐ<u>it</u> very difficult to walk away. This is the sunk cost fallacy. Our instinct is ⓑ<u>to continue</u> investing money or time as we hope that our investment will prove to be worthwhile in the end. Giving up would mean ⓒ<u>acknowledging</u> that we've wasted something we can't get back, and that thought is so painful that we prefer to avoid it if we can. The problem, of course, is that if something really is a bad bet, then staying with it simply ⓓ<u>increase</u> the amount we lose. Rather than walk away from a bad five-year relationship, for example, we turn it into a bad 10-year relationship; rather than accept that we've lost a thousand dollars, we lay down another thousand and lose that too. In the end, by ⓔ<u>delaying</u> the pain of admitting our problem, we only add to it. Sometimes we just have to cut our losses.
summary_sentence: The sunk cost fallacy compels us to persist in unprofitable investments or detrimental relationships to (A)__________ acknowledging past losses, yet this invariably (B)__________ our total harm.
options: ① face ... aggravates
② evade ... worsens
③ resist ... relieves
④ confront ... diminishes
⑤ address ... wears off
explanation: 매몰 비용 오류(sunk cost fallacy)는 우리가 과거의 손실을 인정하는 것을 피하기(evade) 위해 수익성 없는 일에 계속 집착하게 만들지만, 이는 결과적으로 피해를 악화(worsens)시킨다는 내용이므로 ②번이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 직면하다 ... 악화시키다
② 피하다 ... 악화시키다
③ 저항하다 ... 완화시키다
④ 맞서다 ... 감소시키다
⑤ 다루다 ... 사라지다

question: 7. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
passage: When we realize we've said something in error and we pause to go back to correct it, we stop gesturing a couple of hundred milliseconds before we stop speaking. Such sequences suggest the startling notion that our hands "know" what we're going to say before our conscious minds do, and in fact this is often the case. Gesture can mentally prime a word so that the right term comes to our lips. When people are prevented from gesturing, they talk less fluently; their speech becomes halting because their hands are no longer able to supply them with the next word, and the next. Not being able to gesture has other deleterious effects: without gesture to help our mental processes along, _______________________________________. Far from tagging along as speech's clumsy companion, gesture represents the leading edge of our thought.
options: ① we recall fewer important facts
② we articulate our ideas with ease
③ we struggle more to explicate our reasoning
④ we become less effective at solving problems
⑤ our ability to recall important information declines
explanation: 지문은 제스처가 사고를 돕고 단어를 떠올리게 하는 중요한 역할을 한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 제스처를 하지 못하면 사고 능력이 저하되거나 말을 잘 못하게 된다는 내용이 빈칸에 와야 합니다. ② '우리는 아이디어를 쉽게 명확하게 표현한다'는 제스처의 부재로 인한 부정적 효과(deleterious effects)와 반대되는 내용이므로 적절하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 우리는 중요한 사실을 덜 기억한다
② 우리는 아이디어를 쉽게 명확하게 표현한다
③ 우리는 추론을 설명하는 데 더 큰 어려움을 겪는다
④ 우리는 문제 해결에 덜 효과적이게 된다
⑤ 중요한 정보를 회상하는 능력이 감소한다

question: 1. 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The transition from an oral culture, in which knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were used, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. Wood suffers from splitting and is susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is limited. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, solved these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex - or, as we call it now, the book - that the material reached its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a dominant form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, won out as the guardian of the written word is a remarkable materials story.
options: ① To show how the development of writing materials enabled the spread of literate culture
② To trace how limitations of earlier writing media hindered the progress of literacy
③ To argue that oral culture was superior to literate culture in preserving knowledge
④ To emphasize the practical advantages of scrolls over the codex in knowledge storage
⑤ To highlight the cultural competition between Chinese and Roman innovations
explanation: 이 글은 지식의 전승이 구두 문화에서 문자 문화로 전환되는 과정에서 필기 재료의 발전(점토판, 나무 등에서 종이와 코덱스로의 발전)이 문자 문화의 확산을 어떻게 가능하게 했는지를 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 글의 목적은 필기 재료의 발전이 문자 문화의 확산을 가능하게 한 과정을 보여주는 것입니다.
options_translation: ① 필기 재료의 발전이 어떻게 문자 문화의 확산을 가능하게 했는지 보여주기 위해
② 초기 필기 매체의 한계가 어떻게 식자율의 진보를 방해했는지 추적하기 위해
③ 지식을 보존하는 데 있어 구두 문화가 문자 문화보다 우월했음을 주장하기 위해
④ 지식 저장에 있어 두루마리가 코덱스보다 갖는 실용적 이점을 강조하기 위해
⑤ 중국과 로마의 혁신 사이의 문화적 경쟁을 강조하기 위해

question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The term migration is often portrayed in the media and even in academic writing as a crisis or a serious issue. The reality, however, is more complex, and many migrants are simply seeking greater economic opportunity. Certainly, migration can lead to social and economic challenges. Yet it can also provide solutions to preexisting problems. For example, out-migration generally redistributes workers from places of labor surplus to areas where there is greater demand or more opportunity. Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to bear affliction in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin. Studies examining the long-term consequences of migration, such as remittances and upward mobility across generations, generally reveal beneficial outcomes for both the places migrants leave and the destinations they move to.
options: ① The economic risks associated with the mass movement of labor include long-term strains on national infrastructure.
② Generational cycles of poverty are often reinforced through migration from marginalized regions to overcrowded urban centers.
③ Population changes caused by migration can destabilize the local communities that receive migrants and weaken social cohesion.
④ Migration continues to be viewed as a global threat that contributes to social instability and economic strain in vulnerable regions.
⑤ The public and academic perception of migration needs to move beyond seeing it only as a crisis to reflect its complex and generally beneficial nature.
explanation: 글의 전반부에서 이주는 대개 위기나 심각한 문제로 묘사되지만, 실제로는 더 복잡하며 경제적 기회 제공, 노동력 재분배 등 긍정적인 측면이 많다는 것을 설명합니다. 따라서 이주를 단순히 위기로만 보는 시각에서 벗어나 복합적이고 유익한 본질을 반영해야 한다는 내용이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 노동의 대규모 이동과 관련된 경제적 위험에는 국가 기간 시설에 대한 장기적인 압박이 포함된다.
② 빈곤의 세대적 순환은 소외된 지역에서 과밀화된 도시 중심으로의 이주를 통해 흔히 강화된다.
③ 이주로 인한 인구 변화는 이주민을 받아들이는 지역 사회를 불안정하게 만들고 사회적 응집력을 약화시킬 수 있다.
④ 이주는 취약 지역의 사회적 불안정과 경제적 압박에 기여하는 세계적인 위협으로 계속 간주되고 있다.
⑤ 이주에 대한 대중과 학계의 인식은 그것을 오직 위기로만 보는 것에서 벗어나 그것의 복잡하고 일반적으로 유익한 본질을 반영할 필요가 있다.

question: 3. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world. Simply put, the brain is not designed to sense on its own. For instance, an exposed brain would neither sense light shining on it nor feel something touching it. In fact, patients are often kept awake during brain surgery, which can help a surgeon isolate specific regions of the brain. The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle recognized this characteristic of the brain over 2,000 years ago when he said, "Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses." This concept can be seen clearly when volunteers are blind-folded and placed in the warm water of a sensory deprivation tank. They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as incoherent thought patterns. From these experiments and others, it is apparent that we need constant input from our senses to carry out functions that give us personality and intellect.
options: ① The absence of external stimuli primarily affects emotional stability rather than intellectual functioning.
② The role of ancient philosophy in shaping modern neuroscience remains underappreciated in contemporary research.
③ Advances in neurosurgical techniques have minimized the necessity for sensory input in maintaining higher cognitive processes.
④ Hallucinations experienced in sensory deprivation experiments indicate that the brain possesses its own intrinsic sensory mechanisms.
⑤ Sensory organs serve as indispensable mediators for cognitive and perceptual experiences, without which the brain cannot generate coherent thought or awareness of reality.
explanation: 뇌는 스스로 감각할 수 없으며 외부 세계와 소통하기 위해 감각 기관이 필수적이라는 것이 글의 핵심입니다. 감각 박탈 실험 등을 통해 감각의 끊임없는 유입이 지적 능력과 성격을 유지하는 데 필수적임을 강조하고 있으므로 5번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 외부 자극의 부재는 지적 기능보다는 주로 정서적 안정에 영향을 미친다.
② 현대 신경과학을 형성하는 데 있어 고대 철학의 역할은 현대 연구에서 여전히 저평가되고 있다.
③ 신경 외과 기술의 발전은 고차원적 인지 과정을 유지하는 데 있어 감각 입력의 필요성을 최소화했다.
④ 감각 박탈 실험에서 경험한 환각은 뇌가 자체적인 내재적 감각 기제를 가지고 있음을 나타낸다.
⑤ 감각 기관은 인지 및 지각 경험을 위한 필수적인 매개체 역할을 하며, 그것 없이는 뇌가 일관된 사고나 현실에 대한 인식을 생성할 수 없다.

question: 4. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 they often stay on autopilot이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It's often said that those who can't do, teach. It would be more accurate to say that those who can do, can't teach the basics. A great deal of expert knowledge is implicit, not explicit. The further you progress toward mastery, the less conscious awareness you often have of the fundamentals. Experiments show that skilled golfers and wine aficionados have a hard time describing their putting and tasting techniques - even asking them to explain their approaches is enough to interfere with their performance, so <u>they often stay on autopilot</u>. When I first saw an elite diver do four and a half somersaults, I asked how he managed to spin so fast. His answer: "Just go up in a ball." Experts often have an intuitive understanding of a route, but they struggle to clearly express all the steps to take. Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage.
options: ① experts refine their techniques, ensuring that even the smallest details are carefully analyzed
② experts exert considerable deliberate effort to transform their exceptional knowledge into automatized competence
③ the further experts move from mastery, the more the underlying fundamentals tend to surface in conscious awareness
④ experts execute their skills through automatic and intuitive processes, bypassing the need for deliberate, step-by-step conscious reasoning
⑤ experts' cognitive processes often operate with automaticity, enabling them to instruct learners effectively with minimal conscious intervention
explanation: 이 지문은 전문가들이 숙련될수록 기초적인 지식이나 기술이 명시적이기보다는 암묵적으로 변하여, 이를 의식적으로 설명하려 할 때 오히려 수행에 방해가 된다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 'they often stay on autopilot'은 전문가들이 자신의 기술을 수행할 때 세세한 단계를 의식적으로 생각하기보다 자동적이고 직관적인 프로세스에 의존한다는 의미입니다. 따라서 '전문가들은 정교하고 단계적인 의식적 추론의 필요성을 우회하여 자동적이고 직관적인 과정을 통해 기술을 실행한다'는 4번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 전문가들은 아주 작은 세부 사항까지도 주의 깊게 분석되도록 보장하면서 자신의 기술을 다듬는다
② 전문가들은 자신들의 뛰어난 지식을 자동화된 능력으로 바꾸기 위해 상당한 의도적인 노력을 기울인다
③ 전문가들이 숙련도에서 멀어질수록, 그 근저에 있는 기초들이 의식적 인식 속으로 더 많이 떠오르는 경향이 있다
④ 전문가들은 정교하고 단계적인 의식적 추론의 필요성을 건너뛰고 자동적이고 직관적인 과정을 통해 기술을 실행한다
⑤ 전문가들의 인지 과정은 종종 자동성으로 작동하여, 최소한의 의식적 개입만으로 학습자들을 효과적으로 가르칠 수 있게 한다

question: 5. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 the assumptions of conventional economics가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The study of emotions and decision making has become increasingly important, using insights from neuroscience. A well-known example is the work of Antonio Damasio, who discovered that when the emotional part of the brain is damaged, the effectiveness of decision making actually declines. Good decisions are a product of the emotional part of the brain working in conjunction with the deliberative part. This contradicts <u>the assumptions of conventional economics</u>, and there emotions play a negative role in the decision-making process. Here it is assumed that decision making can be modeled as being generated in a stoic, unemotional fashion, and that's why decisions tend to be optimal. But the evidence suggests that emotions actually play an important and, often, a positive role in decision making. The brain's emotional part working in relation with its deliberative part enhances the effectiveness of decision making, which counters the ideas about emotions in the decision-making process of traditional economics.
options: ① the theories that decisions influenced by emotion may sometimes produce optimal and generally exceptional outcomes
② the notions that sustained rational deliberation in complex decisions fundamentally depends on emotional engagement
③ the convictions that effective decision making arises from the collaboration between emotional and rational brain systems
④ the views that emotions inevitably distort reasoning and must always be included from the decision-making process
⑤ the beliefs that decision quality is maximized when outcomes are derived through dispassionate analysis, independent of emotional input
explanation: 이 지문은 전통적인 경제학(conventional economics)이 의사결정을 감정이 배제된 이성적이고 냉철한 과정으로 보며, 감정을 의사결정에 부정적인 영향을 미치는 요소로 간주한다고 설명합니다. 반면 신경과학적 연구는 감정이 이성적인 부분과 함께 작용할 때 의사결정의 효율성이 높아진다는 것을 보여줌으로써 전통 경제학의 가정을 반박합니다. 따라서 '전통적인 경제학의 가정'은 감정적 입력과는 무관하게 냉정한 분석을 통해 결과가 도출될 때 결정의 질이 극대화된다는 믿음을 의미하므로 5번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 감정에 영향을 받은 결정이 때때로 최적의 그리고 일반적으로 뛰어난 결과를 낼 수 있다는 이론들
② 복잡한 결정에서의 지속적인 합리적 숙고가 근본적으로 감정적 참여에 달려 있다는 개념들
③ 효과적인 의사결정이 감정적 뇌 체계와 합리적 뇌 체계 사이의 협력에서 발생한다는 확신들
④ 감정이 필연적으로 추론을 왜곡하며 의사결정 과정에서 항상 포함되어야 한다는 견해들
⑤ 감정적 입력과는 독립적으로, 냉정한 분석을 통해 결과가 도출될 때 결정의 질이 극대화된다는 믿음들

question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [25년 6월 33번]
passage: For countless generations, newly hatched sea turtles have instinctively crawled toward the brightest light they can see. For millions of years, this strategy made perfect sense: the shimmering glow on a dark horizon came from the moon and stars reflecting off the ocean's surface, guiding the hatchlings safely back to the sea. The trouble began when humans began illuminating the coastlines with glowing resorts, streetlights, and beachfront homes. Suddenly, the brightest lights no longer marked the ocean's edge but instead lured the tiny turtles inland - straight toward roads and danger. Does this mean the hatchlings are behaving irrationally? In the modern world, yes. But in truth, they are simply following decision-making instincts shaped by an environment that no longer exists. What was once a reliable survival cue has been sabotaged by artificial lights, leaving the turtles' ancient navigation system fatally misled.
options: ① When Tradition Meets Technology: The Unexpected Harmony of Old Turtle and AI
② Guided by the Wrong Lights: The Perils of Ancient Instincts in a Modern World
③ Instinct in the Age of Illumination: A Journey Beyond Rational Thought
④ From Moonlight to Headlights: How Humanity Preserves Its Environment
⑤ The Ocean's Edge: A Frontier of Dreams and Discoveries
explanation: 이 글은 바다거봁 새기들이 가장 밝은 빛을 따라가는 고대의 방식이, 인과적인 조명이 많은 현대 세계에서는 위험한 결과를 초래한다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 따라서 '잘못된 빛에 의해 인댄됨: 현대 세계에서 고대 밸능이 갖는 위험성'이라는 제목이 가장 적절합다.
options_translation: ① 전통이 기술을 별났 땀: 눙은 거봁과 AI의 예상치 못한 접화
② 잘못된 빛에 의해 인댄됨: 현대 세계에서 고대 밸능이 갖는 위험성
③ 조명의 시대의 밸능: 합리적 사고를 넘어선 여정
④ 달빛에서 전조등까지: 인류가 환경을 보존하는 방법
⑤ 바다의 가장자리: 꿈과 발견의 경계

question: 7. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 21번]
passage: In today's information age, in many companies and on many teams, the objective is no longer error prevention and replicability. On the contrary, it's creativity, speed, and keenness. In the industrial era, the predominant objective was the systematic reduction of variability. But in creative companies today, maximizing variation is more essential. Under such conditions, the most significant hazard does not stem from error or inconsistency, but from an organization's inability to recruit exceptional talent, generate novel innovations, or promptly reorient itself in response to environmental shifts. Consistency and repeatability are more likely to hold back fresh thinking than to bring your company profit. A lot of little mistakes, while sometimes painful, help the organization learn quickly and are a critical part of the innovation cycle. In these situations, rules and processes are no longer the best answer. A symphony isn't what you're going for. Leave the conductor and the sheet music behind. Build a jazz band instead.
options: ① Many Mistakes as the Fuel for Innovation
② Talent and Innovation over Error Prevention
③ Consistency as the Key Driver of Creative Success
④ The Industrial Age: Lessons for Today's Creative Firms
⑤ Changes from Symphony to Jazz: Rethinking Rules in the Age of Creativity

question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [25년 6월 29번]
passage: In art, there are several ways to create the feeling of depth on a flat surface. question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Over the last few centuries, humanity's collective prosperity has soared, as technological progress has made us far ⓐ<u>wealthier</u> than ever before. To share out that wealth, almost all societies have settled upon the market mechanism, ⓑ<u>paving</u> people in various ways for the work that they do and the things that they own. But ⓒ<u>declining</u> disparity, itself often driven by technology, has begun to stretch that mechanism to the limit. Today, markets already provide immense rewards to some people but leave many others with ⓓ<u>scarcely</u> anything. And now, technological unemployment threatens to become a more radical version of the same story, taking place in the particular market we rely upon the most: the labor market. As that market begins to break down, more and more people will be ⓔ<u>vulnerable</u> to being left out of society's prosperity entirely.
explanation: 문맥상 기술 발전으로 인해 시장 매커니즘이 한계에 다다르고, 일부에게만 막대한 보상이 돌아가며 많은 이들이 소외되는 상황을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 불평등이 '감소하는(declining)' 것이 아니라, '증가하는(increasing/rising)' 또는 '커지는(widening)' 불평등이 시장 매커니즘을 한계로 몰아넣고 있다는 내용이 되어야 적절합니다.ⓐ 기술 발전으로 인류가 더 '부유해진(wealthier)' 것은 문맥상 자연스럽습니다.ⓑ 시장 매커니즘이 사람들에게 보상을 '지급하는(paying)' 것(오타로 보이나 원문 문맥상 보상하는 의미)은 적절합니다.ⓓ 시장이 일부에게만 보상을 주고 다른 이들에게는 '거의 아무것도(scarcely anything)' 남겨주지 않는다는 표현은 적절합니다.ⓔ 노동 시장의 붕괴로 사람들이 소외에 '취약해질(vulnerable)' 것이라는 표현은 적절합니다.

question: 12. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A reason for a conclusion is very unlikely to consist in a single claim. No matter how we might state it in shorthand, it is, analytically, a complex interaction of many ideas and implications. The reason must be broken down into a chain of more precise premises. For example, the claim that 'university education should be free for all Australians' might be supported by the reason that 'the economy benefits from a well-educated Australian population'. But is our analysis of the situation clearly expressed in just one statement? Hardly. The conclusion is about universities and free education, while the reason introduces some new ideas: economic benefit and a well-educated population. While the link between these two ideas and the conclusion might seem obvious, the purpose of reasoning is _________________ _____________________________.
options: ① to prevent assuming the 'obvious' by thoroughly examining how the ideas in the original reason are related
② to show how different ideas, while seemingly related, must be carefully distinguished to support a conclusion
③ to confirm the 'obvious' and thereby eliminate the need for detailed analysis
④ to reduce every claim and reason into a single, simplified statement
⑤ to prove that whatever appears obvious must necessarily be true
explanation: 글의 요지는 결론에 대한 근거가 단일한 주장이 아니라 여러 아이디어의 복잡한 상호작용이므로, 이를 더 정밀한 전제들로 세분화해야 한다는 것입니다. 빈칸 앞부분에서 근거와 결론 사이의 연결이 '명백해(obvious)' 보일지 모르지만, 추론의 진짜 목적은 이러한 아이디어들이 어떻게 연관되어 있는지 철저히 검토함으로써 '명백한 것'을 당연하게 가정해버리는 것을 방지하는 것이라는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 원래 근거 속의 아이디어들이 어떻게 관련되어 있는지 철저히 조사함으로써 '명백한 것'을 가정하는 것을 방지하는 것
② 겉보기에 관련 있어 보이는 서로 다른 아이디어들이 결론을 뒷받침하기 위해 어떻게 신중하게 구별되어야 하는지 보여주는 것
③ '명백한 것'을 확인하고 그로 인해 상세한 분석의 필요성을 없애는 것
④ 모든 주장과 근거를 하나의 단순화된 진술로 줄이는 것
⑤ 명백해 보이는 것은 무엇이든 반드시 사실임을 증명하는 것

question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절할 것은?
passage: It might seem natural to assume that the more capable someone is, the more we would like them. options: ① individuals with exceptional skills are celebrated for both their competence and their unmatched ability to form close social bonds

explanation: 지문은 능력이 뛰어난 사람이 반드시 더 호감을 사는 것은 아니라는 '놀라운 반전'을 설명하고 있습니다. 너무 완벽해 보이는 사람은 타인에게 위축감을 주거나 거리감을 느끼게 할 수 있으며, 오히려 인간적인 실수(human side)를 보여줄 때 더 호감을 얻는다는 내용입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '능력 있고 기여도가 높은 사람이 집단 내에서 가장 사회적으로 선호되는 것은 아니다'라는 내용이 적절합니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장을 고른 것은?
passage: Sleep clearly serves purposes beyond simple rest. Interestingly, even animals that hibernate experience periods of sleep. question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The first human beings probably evolved in tropical regions where survival was possible without clothing. It is likely that they had very dark skin because light skin would have given little protection against the burning rays of the sun.
ordered_passages: (A) With tools, they could hunt other animals, so they could consume more protein and fat than their low-energy vegetarian diet would have provided. explanation: 주어진 글에서는 인류의 기원과 피부색의 특징에 대한 내용이 나옵니다. 그다음으로는 인류가 전 세계로 퍼져 나간 과정과 신체적 특성의 변화를 언급한 (B)가 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다. (B)의 마지막 부분에서 언급된 신체적 특성 변화의 구체적인 예시(직립보행)와 도구 제작의 발전을 다룬 (C)가 뒤를 잇고, 마지막으로 도구 사용을 통해 단백질과 지방 섭취가 늘어나 뇌가 성장하고 지적 성장을 이루었다는 내용의 (A)가 오는 것이 논리적으로 가장 적절합니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A computational algorithm that takes input data and generates some output from it doesn't really embody any notion of meaning. Certainly, such a computation does not generally have as its purpose its own survival and well-being. It does not, in general, assign value to the inputs. Compare, for example, a computer algorithm with the waggle dance of the honeybee, by which means a foraging bee conveys to others in the hive information about the source of food (such as nectar) it has located. The "dance" - a series of stylized movements on the comb - shows the bees how far away the food is and in which direction. But this input does not simply program other bees to go out and look for it. Rather, they evaluate this information, comparing it with their own knowledge of the surroundings. Some bees might not bother to make the journey, considering it not worthwhile. The input, such as it is, is processed in the light of the organism's own internal states and history; there is nothing prescriptive about its effects.
summary_sentence: Unlike computational algorithms, living organisms such as honeybees (A)___________ information in the context of their own experiences and internal states, engaging in (B)__________________________.
options: ① evaluate ... automatic responses
② manipulate ... assigning meaning or value
③ interpret ... evaluation-based decision making
④ suppress ... a dynamic and self-directed process
⑤ program ... a process that compels following prescribed conduct
explanation: 컴퓨터 알고리즘은 입력 데이터에 의미를 부여하거나 가치를 할당하지 않지만, 꿀벌과 같은 생명체는 정보를 자신의 경험과 내부 상태에 비추어 평가하고 해석합니다. 꿀벌은 춤을 통해 얻은 정보를 단순히 따르는 것이 아니라, 자신의 지식과 대조하여 갈만한 가치가 있는지 판단하므로 (A)에는 'interpret(해석하다)'가, (B)에는 'evaluation-based decision making(평가 기반의 의사 결정)'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 평가하다 ... 자동적인 반응
② 조작하다 ... 의미나 가치를 할당하는 것
③ 해석하다 ... 평가 기반의 의사 결정
④ 억제하다 ... 역동적이고 자기 주도적인 과정
⑤ 프로그램하다 ... 규정된 행위를 따르도록 강요하는 과정

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Employees who are simply given a free trip to Paris feel satisfied, and the same goes for those given a free trip to Hawaii. But when they are asked to choose between the two destinations, they feel less satisfied regardless of which option they take. Why might choice be so disruptive? The reason is that choice forces us to make comparisons and acknowledge relative disadvantages. People who choose Paris complain that it doesn't have the ocean and those who choose Hawaii regret that it doesn't have the museums. Psychologist Barry Schwartz calls this the 'tyranny of choice' because rather than providing freedom, it actually constrains our decision-making. He argues that wider choice increases unhappiness because we worry that we are going to make the wrong decision and so we get stressed about trying to process all the comparisons in an effort to get it right. This both increases our fear of making the wrong choice and raises expectations that we should be able to get the best choice. Having made the choice, we then start to regret, wondering whether it was the right one.
summary_sentence: Barry Schwartz explains that having more choices, rather than giving us (A)___________, often results in (B)___________ because it makes people compare options, feel stressed, and regret their decisions.
options: ① liberty ... discontent
② autonomy ... satisfaction
③ convenience ... instability
④ relief ... confidence
⑤ opportunity ... fairness
explanation: 본문은 선택지가 많아질수록 비교와 상대적 단점 인식을 강요받아 오히려 결정이 힘들어지고 불행해진다는 '선택의 폭정'을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 더 많은 선택지가 우리에게 자유를 주기보다는 불만족을 결과로 가져온다는 내용이 되어야 하므로 (A)에는 'liberty(자유)', (B)에는 'discontent(불만족)'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 자유 ... 불만족
② 자율성 ... 만족
③ 편리함 ... 불안정
④ 안도 ... 자신감
⑤ 기회 ... 공정함

question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분을 <조건>에 맞게 <보기>에 주어진 단어를 활용하여 작성하시오.
passage: One well-known shift took place when the accepted view - that the Earth was the center of the universe-changed to one where we understood that we are only inhabitants on one planet orbiting the Sun. With each person who grasped the solar system view, it became easier for the next person to do so. So it is with the notion that the world revolves around the human economy. This is slowly being replaced by the view that the economy is a part of the larger system of material flows that connect all living things. When this perspective shifts into place, it will be obvious that our economic well-being requires that we account for, and respond to, factors of ecological health. Unfortunately we do not have a century or two to make the change. <u>오래된 관점과 새로운 관점의 본질을 명확히 하고, 그 과정을 진전시키기 위해 협력할지도 모를 행동을 밝힘으로써</u>, we can help accelerate the shift.

<보기>의 '/'안에 연결된 단어들은 분리하지 마시오.
<보기>의 단어와 어구만을 <u>모두</u>, <u>한 번씩</u>만 사용하시오.
vocabulary_box: of the old and new perspectives, / the nature / clarify / and / actions / we might cooperate /
to move the process along / by / on
answer: By clarifying the nature of the old and new perspectives, and identifying actions on which we might cooperate to move the process along
explanation: 이 문장은 '~함으로써'에 해당하는 전치사 'By' 뒤에 동명사 병렬 구조(clarifying and identifying)를 사용하여 작성해야 합니다. '오래된 관점과 새로운 관점의 본질을 명확히 함으로써(By clarifying the nature of the old and new perspectives)'와 '그 과정을 진전시키기 위해 협력할지도 모를 행동을 밝힘으로써(and identifying actions on which we might cooperate to move the process along)'를 결합합니다. 여기서 'on which'는 'cooperate on actions'의 구조에서 기인한 관계대명사절입니다.

question: 23. 윗글에서 다음 빈칸 (B)와 (C)에 각각 들어갈 한 단어를 찾아 쓰시오. (필요한 경우 변형 가능)
passage: Low oil prices are a good thing, because it means lower energy costs of production for the majority of industries, not least the automobile and the logistics industries. Firms directly benefit from the decrease in their costs of production and provision of services. This (A)___________________________________. Conversely, a sudden rise in oil prices due to a shrink in oil production is never good news, even though it definitely gives a big boost to the energy sector. A look through the history of oil price fluctuations proves this notion, as this has been the subject of much economic research. Following an oil price jump of 10 per cent due to a contraction in supply, an economy (as typified by the US economy) typically sees its output (GDP) slowed by close to 1 percentage point. For a $15 trillion economy, that is a loss of $150 billion in potential wealth or economic growth. Conversely, there has never been much concern with oil price decreases following an excess in its supply.
subjective_conditions: 필요한 경우 변형 가능
subjective_answer_format: Aspect | Oil Price Decrease | Oil Price Increase--- | --- | ---Supply | → (B)____________ supply | → (C)____________ in supplyCause | More oil supply → Prices fall | Less oil supply → Prices riseIndustry Impact | Most industries benefit | Energy sector profitsMacro Effect | Aggregate supply rises | GDP growth slows(B) ________________________(C) ________________________
explanation: 지문에서 유가 하락의 원인을 'excess in its supply(공급 과잉)'로 설명하고 있으므로 (B)에는 'excessive'가 적절합니다. 또한 유가 상승의 원인을 'shrink in oil production' 또는 'contraction in supply(공급 수축)'로 설명하고 있으므로 (C)에는 'contraction'이 적절합니다.

question: 25. 다음 <A>를 대화문 <B>로 표현한 것이다. <B>의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <보기>의 단어를 활용하여 <조건>에 맞게 서술하시오.
passage: <A> The concern about how we appear to others can be seen in children, though work by the psychologist Ervin Staub suggests that the effect may vary with age. In a study where children heard another child in distress, young children (kindergarten through second grade) were more likely to help the child in distress when with another child than when alone. But for older children - in fourth and sixth grade - the effect reversed: they were less likely to help a child in distress when they were with a peer than when they were alone. Staub suggested that younger children might feel more comfortable acting when they have the company of a peer, whereas older children might feel more concern about being judged by their peers and fear feeling embarrassed by overreacting. question: 16. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers of which it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease to form, while sufficient fibers remain undamaged for the material not to crack and fall apart. Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to resist being pulled apart, but it can also be torn easily and accurately along the crease if a point of weakness - a small, initial tear - is opened up. This winning combination of mechanical properties allows it to assume the shape of any object through creasing and folding - hence the art of origami. There are very few materials as good: metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult. Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, in which case it lacks the rigidity required of a good wrapping material. So it is its ability to hold a crease while remaining stiff that makes paper uniquely suited to this purpose.
options: ① 공기그래류로스 사튜느느내가 생기느느 뱨바테서 뱨바ᄐ서그로 브러지르 스 으따.

question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Mother cats can tell which kittens belong to them - when litters are mixed up they use their kittens' scent to distinguish them from offspring of other mothers.
ordered_passages: (A) In the wild, a squeaking kitten out in the open is likely to attract predators, which is bad news for any other kittens around it. A rapid rescue of any crying kitten would be a good strategy to prevent them from drawing unwanted attention.(B) Despite this, when faced with a selection of kittens who have wandered from the nest, her own and others that aren't hers, a mother cat doesn't appear to favor her own offspring when retrieving them.(C) The reason for this is uncertain, although distress vocalizations from kittens that are lost from their nest are known to be very powerful, so it may just be hard for the mother to resist retrieving them, regardless of whether they are hers.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 어미 고양이가 냄새를 통해 자신의 새끼를 구별할 수 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (B)의 'Despite this(이에도 불구하고)'는 앞의 구별 능력에도 불구하고 실제 상황에서는 자신의 새끼를 편애하지 않는다는 반전의 내용을 연결하므로 첫 번째에 옵니다. (C)에서는 이러한 현상에 대한 이유(The reason for this)가 불확실하지만 울음소리가 강력한 영향을 미친다는 점을 언급하며, 마지막으로 (A)에서 야생의 관점에서 울음소리가 포식자를 끌어들일 수 있기에 일단 구조하는 것이 좋은 전략이라는 보충 설명을 덧붙이는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 18. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 단어를 각각 쓰시오. (단, 이 지문에 나오지 않은 단어를 쓰고 어법에 맞게 쓸 것)
passage: The term "(A)__________" was introduced by Roland Barthes who observed that text is often used next to images (his focus was on photographs) to ⓐ<u>refine</u> meaning. Of all possible literal or implied interpretations an image could elicit, text would point the viewer towards a desired, specific direction. In advertising, as Barthes argues, the symbolic message does not guide identification but ⓑ<u>interpretation</u>. The viewer is not asked to recognize what they see but to ⓒ<u>understand</u> why they see it and what it means to them. By combining images with text, advertising produces symbolic meaning that is accurate and specific on the one hand, richer on the other, thus adding depth and ⓓ<u>eliminating</u> breadth of rational and emotional interpretations. The headline or tagline of an ad directs the reader through the ⓔ<u>intended</u> meanings of the image, so that the reader avoids some and receives others. It "(B)__________" the reader towards a meaning chosen in advance.
subjective_conditions: 단, 이 지문에 나오지 않은 단어를 쓰고 어법에 맞게 쓸 것
explanation: (A) 롤랑 바르트가 제안한 개념으로 이미지가 가질 수 있는 수많은 의미 중 하나를 텍스트가 고정시키는 역할을 '정박(anchorage)' 혹은 '정박 효과(anchoring effect)'라고 합니다. (B) 문맥상 텍스트가 독자를 미리 선택된 의미로 '원격 조정'하거나 '전달'한다는 의미가 들어가야 하므로 remote-controls 혹은 relays가 적절합니다.

question: 19. 윗글의 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 문맥상 어색한 것은?

question: 20. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A great strength of the market mechanism is that there are incentives for individuals to reveal their knowledge through their behavior. This stands in contrast to many strategic situations - for example, in political negotiations - in which it is wise not to let the other side know what one's true preferences or production capacities are. A perfectly competitive market that clears on the spot leaves no room for such strategies. If prices are not sticky - as many models assume - individuals adapt their behavior instantaneously, whenever their preferences or the circumstances change. They stop buying items that do not satisfy their needs and stop selling items that do not provide them with optimal gains, maybe switching to the production of other items. If they have motivational problems, for example, falling into denial about the fact that there is no demand for their products, markets reveal to them, sometimes in quite brutal ways, that they better accept this fact.
options: ① The strategic advantages of political negotiation over market competition
② The role of information and knowledge in political negotiations
③ The function of the market as an efficient mechanism for revealing information
④ The psychological difficulties individuals face when their products fail
⑤ The various models that assume flexible prices in competitive markets
explanation: 본문은 시장 기제의 가장 큰 장점이 개인들이 자신의 행동을 통해 지식을 드러내게 만드는 인센티브를 제공한다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 정치 협상과 달리 시장에서는 가격과 행동을 통해 즉각적으로 선호도와 정보가 공개된다는 점을 강조하므로 '정보를 드러내는 효율적인 기제로서의 시장의 기능'이 주제로 가장 적합합니다.

② 정치 협상에서 정보와 지식의 역할
③ 정보를 드러내기 위한 효율적인 기제로서의 시장의 기능
④ 제품이 실패했을 때 개인이 직면하는 심리적 어려움

question: 21. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: One well-known shift took place when the accepted view - that the Earth was the center of the universe - changed to one where we understood that we are only inhabitants on one planet orbiting the Sun. With each person who grasped the solar system view, it became easier for the next person to do so. So it is with the notion that the world revolves around the human economy. This is slowly being replaced by the view that the economy is a part of the larger system of material flows that connect all living things. When this perspective shifts into place, it will be obvious that our economic well-being requires that we account for, and respond to, factors of ecological health. Unfortunately we do not have a century or two to make the change. By clarifying the nature of the old and new perspectives, and by identifying actions on which we might cooperate to move the process along, we can help accelerate the shift.
options: ① Economic development should proceed within limits that do not harm the health of the ecosystem.
② A new perspective should be communicated gradually rather than being imposed on everyone at once.
③ Investment in scientific research and technological development is urgently needed to solve environmental problems.
④ We must move beyond human economy-centric thinking and recognize and respond to our interconnectedness with the ecosystem.
⑤ For economic development, environmental protection policies must be established with a long-term perspective.
explanation: 이 글은 과거 지구가 우주의 중심이라는 생각이 지구가 태양 주위를 도는 행성 중 하나라는 생각으로 바뀐 것처럼, 세상이 인간의 경제를 중심으로 돌아간다는 생각도 경제가 생태계라는 더 큰 시스템의 일부라는 생각으로 바뀌어야 한다고 주장합니다. 필자는 이러한 인식의 변화를 가속화하여 생태적 건강 요인에 반응하고 책임을 져야 한다고 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 ④번 '인간 경제 중심의 사고에서 벗어나 생태계와의 상호 연결성을 인식하고 그에 대응해야 한다'가 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 경제 발전은 생태계의 건강을 해치지 않는 범위 내에서 진행되어야 한다.
② 새로운 관점은 모든 사람에게 한꺼번에 강요되기보다는 점진적으로 전달되어야 한다.
③ 환경 문제 해결을 위해 과학 연구와 기술 개발에 대한 투자가 절실히 필요하다.
④ 우리는 인간 경제 중심의 사고에서 벗어나 생태계와의 상호 연결성을 인식하고 대응해야 한다.
⑤ 경제 발전을 위해 장기적인 관점에서 환경 보호 정책이 수립되어야 한다.

question: 22. 다음 글을 읽고, 우리말 '그들이 어떻게 느끼는지와 상관없이 걱정하며 행동하는 것을 거부한다면' 의미가 되도록 주어진 단어들을 바르게 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.
passage: Merely convincing your children that worry is senseless and that they would be more content if they didn't worry isn't going to stop them from worrying. For some reason, young people seem to believe that worry is a fact of life over which they have little or no control. Consequently, they don't even try to stop. Therefore, you need to convince them that worry, like guilt and fear, is nothing more than an emotion, and like all emotions, is subject to the power of the will. Tell them that they can eliminate worry from their lives by simply refusing to attend to it. Explain to them that '<u>그들이 어떻게 느끼는지와 상관없이 걱정하며 행동하는 것을 거부한다면</u>', they will eventually stop feeling worried and will begin to experience the contentment that accompanies a worry-free life.
vocabulary_box: act / feel / how / if / of / refuse / regardless / they / they / to / worried
answer: if they refuse to act worried regardless of how they feel
explanation: 주어진 우리말을 영어로 옮길 때, 조건절 '~한다면'을 위해 'if'를 사용하고, 주어 'they', 동사 'refuse to'를 연결합니다. '걱정하며 행동하다'는 'act worried'로 표현하며, '~와 상관없이'는 'regardless of', '그들이 어떻게 느끼는지'는 의문사절 'how they feel'로 구성합니다.

question: 23. 다음 글을 읽고, 윗글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Merely convincing your children that worry is senseless and that they would be more content if they didn't worry isn't going to stop them from worrying. For some reason, young people seem to believe that worry is a fact of life over which they have little or no control. Consequently, they don't even try to stop. Therefore, you need to convince them that worry, like guilt and fear, is nothing more than an emotion, and like all emotions, is subject to the power of the will. Tell them that they can eliminate worry from their lives by simply refusing to attend to it. Explain to them that '<u>그들이 어떻게 느끼는지와 상관없이 걱정하며 행동하는 것을 거부한다면</u>', they will eventually stop feeling worried and will begin to experience the contentment that accompanies a worry-free life.
options: ① Worry is an unavoidable part of life, and one should not attempt to overcome it through futile efforts.
② Emotions are responsive to the power of will, so young people should make a deliberate effort to overcome worry.
③ Worry can lead to negative emotions such as guilt and fear.
④ Parents should provide practical help to their children so they can confront and overcome their worries.
⑤ Emotional support from those around is essential to experience the contentment of a worry-free life.
explanation: 이 글은 걱정이 통제할 수 없는 삶의 사실이 아니라, 의지의 힘에 종속되는 감정일 뿐이라는 점을 강조합니다. 따라서 걱정에 주목하기를 거부하고 의도적으로 행동을 바꿈으로써 걱정을 없앨 수 있다는 것이 핵심입니다. 이에 가장 부합하는 요지는 ②번 '감정은 의지의 힘에 반응하므로, 젊은이들은 걱정을 극복하기 위해 의도적인 노력을 기울여야 한다'입니다.
options_translation: ① 걱정은 삶의 피할 수 없는 부분이며, 헛된 노력을 통해 이를 극복하려 해서는 안 된다.
② 감정은 의지의 힘에 반응하므로, 젊은이들은 걱정을 극복하기 위해 의도적인 노력을 기울여야 한다.
③ 걱정은 죄책감이나 두려움과 같은 부정적인 감정으로 이어질 수 있다.
④ 부모는 자녀가 걱정에 맞서고 극복할 수 있도록 실질적인 도움을 주어야 한다.
⑤ 걱정 없는 삶의 만족감을 경험하기 위해서는 주변 사람들의 정서적 지지가 필수적이다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Imagine that seven out of ten working Americans got fired tomorrow. What would they all do? It's hard to believe you'd have an economy at all if you gave pink slips to more than half the labor force. But that is what the industrial revolution did to the workforce of the early 19th century. Two hundred years ago, 70 percent of American workers lived on the farm. Today automation has eliminated all but 1 percent of their jobs, replacing them with machines. But the displaced workers did not sit idle. Instead, automation created hundreds of millions of jobs in entirely new fields. Those who once farmed were now manning the factories that manufactured farm equipment, cars, and other industrial products. Since then, wave upon wave of new occupations have arrived - appliance repair person, food chemist, photographer, web designer - each building on previous automation. Today, the vast majority of us are doing jobs that no farmer from the 1800s could have imagined.
options: ① Large-scale job losses severly damage the economy as a whole, leading to the collapse of the economic system.
② The development of new technologies eliminates existing jobs but has created even more new occupations.
③ The shift from an agrarian to an industrial society was an inevitable process for increasing productivity.
④ Unemployment caused by automation can be an opportunity to broaden humanity's range of job choices.
⑤ Innovation in occupational education systems is urgently needed to prepare for the unpredictable future labor market.
explanation: 이 글은 과거 산업 혁명기부터 현재까지 자동화와 기술 발전이 기존의 일자리를 없앴지만, 동시에 이전에는 상상할 수 없었던 수많은 새로운 직업군을 창출해 왔음을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '새로운 기술의 발전이 기존 일자리를 없애지만 더 많은 새로운 직업을 창출해 왔다'는 2번이 글의 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 대규모의 일자리 손실은 경제 전체에 심각한 피해를 입혀 경제 시스템의 붕괴를 초래한다.
② 새로운 기술의 개발은 기존의 일자리를 없애지만 훨씬 더 많은 새로운 직업을 창출했다.
③ 농경 사회에서 산업 사회로의 전환은 생산성을 높이기 위한 필연적인 과정이었다.
④ 자동화로 인한 실업은 인류의 직업 선택 범위를 넓히는 기회가 될 수 있다.
⑤ 예측할 수 없는 미래 노동 시장에 대비하기 위해 직업 교육 시스템의 혁신이 시급하다.

question: 25. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When we get an unfavorable outcome, in some ways the last thing we want to hear is that the process was fair. As outraging as the combination of an unfavorable outcome and an unfair process is, this combination also brings with it a consolation prize: the possibility of attributing the bad outcome to something other than ourselves. We may reassure ourselves by believing that our bad outcome had little to do with us and everything to do with the unfair process. If the process is fair, however, we cannot nearly as easily externalize the outcome; we got what we got "fair and square." When the process is fair we believe that our outcome is deserved, which is another way of saying that there must have been something about ourselves (what we did or who we are) that caused the outcome.
options: ① problems of social inequality caused by unjust processes
② why objective assessment is challenging in subjective contexts
③ strategies for self-reassurance in the face of disappointing results
④ psychological impact of process fairness on accepting unfavorable outcomes
⑤ issues related to externalizing an unfavorable outcome in the workplace
explanation: 이 글은 불리한 결과를 얻었을 때 과정이 공정하면 그 결과를 외부 탓으로 돌리기 어려워져서 결국 자기 자신(자신의 능력이나 행동)의 탓으로 받아들여야 하는 심리적 상황을 설명하고 있습니다. 즉, 불리한 결과를 수용하는 데 있어 과정의 공정성이 미치는 심리적 영향을 다루고 있으므로 4번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 부당한 과정으로 인해 발생하는 사회적 불평등의 문제들
② 주관적인 맥락에서 객관적인 평가가 어려운 이유
③ 실망스러운 결과에 직면했을 때 자기 위안을 위한 전략들
④ 불리한 결과를 수용함에 있어 과정의 공정성이 미치는 심리적 영향
⑤ 직장에서 불리한 결과를 외부화하는 것과 관련된 문제들

question: 26. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: We have biases that support our biases! If we're partial to one option - perhaps because it's more memorable, or framed to minimize loss, or seemingly consistent with a promising pattern - we tend to search for information that will justify choosing that option. On the one hand, it's sensible to make choices that we can defend with data and a list of reasons. On the other hand, if we're not careful, we're likely to conduct an imbalanced analysis, falling prey to a cluster of errors collectively known as "confirmation biases." For example, nearly all companies include classic "tell me about yourself" job interviews as part of the hiring process, and many rely on these interviews alone to evaluate applicants. But it turns out that traditional interviews are actually one of the least useful tools for predicting an employee's future success. This is because interviewers often subconsciously make up their minds about interviewees based on their first few moments of interaction and spend the rest of the interview cherry-picking evidence and phrasing their questions to confirm that initial impression: "I see here you left a good position at your previous job. You must be pretty ambitious, right?" versus "You must not have been very committed, huh?" This means that interviewers can be prone to neglecting significant information that would clearly indicate whether this candidate was actually the best person to hire. More structured approaches, like obtaining samples of a candidate's work or asking how he would respond to difficult hypothetical situations, are dramatically better at assessing future success, with a nearly threefold advantage over traditional interviews.
options: ① Confirmation bias leads us to seek information that justifies our favored options.
② Many companies rely solely on traditional interviews to evaluate applicants as part of their hiring process.
③ Traditional interviews are considered one of the most effective tools for predicting an employee's future success.
④ Interviewers often form judgments about applicants based on initial impressions and hten seek evidence to support these impressions.
⑤ Structured assessment methods, such as work samples, offer a significantly better prediction of future success than traditional interviews.
explanation: 지문에서 전통적인 면접(traditional interviews)은 직원의 미래 성공을 예측하는 데 있어 '가장 유용하지 않은 도구 중 하나(one of the least useful tools)'라고 언급되어 있습니다. 따라서 ③번의 '가장 효과적인 도구 중 하나로 간주된다'는 설명은 본문의 내용과 정반대입니다.
options_translation: ① 확증 편향은 우리가 선호하는 선택지를 정당화하는 정보를 찾게 만든다.
② 많은 기업들이 채용 과정의 일부로 지원자를 평가하기 위해 전통적인 면접에만 의존한다.
③ 전통적인 면접은 직원의 미래 성공을 예측하는 가장 효과적인 도구 중 하나로 간주된다.
④ 면접관들은 종종 초기 인상에 근거하여 지원자에 대한 판단을 형성하고 이러한 인상을 뒷받침할 증거를 찾는다.
⑤ 작업 샘플과 같은 구조화된 평가 방법은 전통적인 면접보다 미래의 성공에 대해 상당히 더 나은 예측을 제공한다.

question: 27. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Mental development consists of individuals increasingly ①<u>mastering</u> social codes and signals themselves, which they can master only in social situations with the support of more competent individuals, typically adults. In this sense, mental development consists of internalizing social patterns and gradually becoming a responsible actor among other responsible actors. In Denmark, the age of criminal responsibility is 15 years, ②<u>which</u> means that we then say that people have developed sufficient mental maturity to be accountable for their actions at this point. And at the age of 18 people are given the right to vote and are thereby formally included in the basic democratic process. I do not know ③<u>whether</u> these age boundaries are optimal, but it is clear that mental development takes place at different rates for different individuals, and depends especially on the social and family environment they ④<u>have given</u>. Therefore, having formal limits for responsibility from a specific age that apply to everyone ⑤<u>is</u> a somewhat questionable practice. But the question, of course, is whether it can be done any differently.
explanation: ④번이 포함된 절은 'the social and family environment (관계대명사 생략) they have been given'으로, 그들이 '제공받은' 홀경이띀 수동의 의미가 되어야 합니다. 따라서 have given을 현재완료 수동형인 have been given으로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 28. 윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 30. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 be both at some point가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Financial markets do more than take capital from the rich and lend it to everyone else. They enable each of us to smooth consumption over our lifetimes, which is a fancy way of saying that we don't have to spend income at the same time we earn it. Shakespeare may have admonished us to be neither borrowers nor lenders; the fact is that most of us will <u>be both at some point</u>. If we lived in an agrarian society, we would have to eat our crops reasonably soon after the harvest or find some way to store them. Financial markets are a more sophisticated way of managing the harvest. We can spend income now that we have not yet earned - as by borrowing for college or a home - or we can earn income now and spend it later, as by saving for retirement. The important point is that earning income has been divorced from spending it, allowing us much more flexibility in life.
options: ① conduct earning and spending simultaneously
② go through cycles of prosperity and adversity economically
③ inevitably act as both a borrower and a lender throughout their lives
④ cultivate economic foresight for an unpredictable future
⑤ maintain a balance between borrowing and lending to ensure stability
explanation: 이 글은 금융 시장이 소득의 획득과 소비 시점을 분리해주는 역할을 함으로써 인생의 유연성을 제공한다고 설명합니다. 셰익스피어는 빌리지도 빌려주지도 말라고 했으나, 실제로는 우리가 대학이나 주택 마련을 위해 돈을 빌리기도 하고(borrower), 은퇴를 위해 저축하여 나중에 쓰기도 하므로(lender) 인생의 어느 시점에서는 두 역할을 모두 하게 된다는 의미입니다. 따라서 ③ '평생 동안 필연적으로 대출자와 대출해주는 사람 모두로서 행동한다'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 수입과 지출을 동시에 수행한다
② 경제적으로 번영과 역경의 주기를 겪는다
③ 평생 동안 불가피하게 빌리는 사람과 빌려주는 사람 모두의 역할을 한다

question: 31. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The first human beings probably evolved in tropical regions where survival was possible without clothing. It is likely that they had very dark skin because light skin would have given little protection against the burning rays of the sun. There is a debate about whether these people spread into other parts of the world or, instead, whether people developed independently in various parts of the world. Whichever the case, it is believed that in time they became capable of spreading out from Africa, eventually to most of the world. This was probably because their physical characteristics changed. For instance, early hominids probably did not walk upright, but when they developed that ability, they could travel more efficiently. More important, perhaps, was their development of tool making. With tools, they could hunt other animals, so they could consume more protein and fat than their low-energy vegetarian diet would have provided. Not only their bodies but also their brains would have been changed with more energy. The brain needs lots of energy to grow. As their diet expanded, hominids could (A)____________________________.
options: ① shorten their traveling distances
② develop more complex languages
③ rely less on physical strength for survival
④ develop more advanced communication methods
⑤ increase their range of influence, physically and intellectually
explanation: 인류의 진화 과정에서 직립 보행을 통해 더 효율적으로 이동할 수 있게 되었고, 도구 제작을 통해 육류를 섭취함으로써 더 많은 에너지를 얻게 되었습니다. 이러한 에너지 공급은 뇌의 성장을 가능하게 했으며, 결과적으로 인류는 아프리카에서 벗어나 전 세계로 퍼져나갈 수 있었습니다. 즉, 식단의 확장과 그에 따른 뇌의 성장은 인류가 신체적, 지적 영향력을 확장하는 결과를 가져왔으므로 ⑤가 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 이동 거리를 단축하다
② 더 복잡한 언어를 개발하다
③ 생존을 위해 신체적 힘에 덜 의존하다
④ 더 진보된 의사소통 방법을 개발하다
⑤ 신체적으로나 지적으로 그들의 영향력 범위를 넓히다

question: 32. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: On Saturday morning, Todd and his 5-year-old daughter Ava walked out of the store with the groceries they had just purchased. As they pushed their grocery cart through the parking lot, they saw a red car pulling into the space next to their pick-up truck. A young man named Greg was driving. "That's a cool car," Ava said to her dad. He agreed and looked at Greg, who finished parking and opened his door. As Todd finished loading his groceries, Greg's door remained open. Todd noticed Greg didn't get out of his car. But he was pulling something from his car. He put a metal frame on the ground beside his door. Remaining in the driver's seat, he then reached back into his car to grab something else. Todd realized what he was doing and considered whether he should try to help him. After a moment, he decided to approach Greg. By this time, Greg had already pulled one thin wheel out of his car and attached it to the frame. He was now pulling a second wheel out when he looked up and saw Todd standing near him. Todd said, "Hi there! Have a great weekend!" Greg seemed a bit surprised, but replied by wishing him a great weekend too. Then Greg added, "Thanks for letting me have my independence." "Of course," Todd said. After Todd and Ava climbed into their truck, Ava became curious. So she asked why he didn't offer to help the man with his wheelchair. Todd said, "Why do you insist on brushing your teeth without my help?" She answered, "Because I know how to!" He said, "And the man knows how to put together his wheelchair." Ava understood that sometimes the best way to help someone is to (A)_______________________.
options: ① recognize their capabilities and respect their autonomy
② anticipate their needs before they become apparent
③ prioritize efficiency in completing tasks for others
④ offer assistance only when explicitly asked for it
⑤ encourage their dependency on external help
explanation: 본문의 마지막 대화에서 아버지는 딸에게 스스로 양치를 하는 이유를 물으며, 휠체어를 조립하는 남성 또한 스스로 할 수 있는 능력이 있음을 가르쳐 줍니다. 따라서 누군가를 돕는 최선의 방법은 그들의 능력을 인정하고 자율성을 존중하는 것이라는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그들의 능력을 인정하고 그들의 자율성을 존중하는 것
② 필요가 명확해지기 전에 그들의 필요를 예상하는 것
③ 타인을 위한 과업 완수에 있어 효율성을 우선시하는 것
④ 명시적으로 요청받았을 때만 도움을 제안하는 것
⑤ 외부의 도움에 대한 그들의 의존성을 장려하는 것

question: 33. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: People seem to recognize that the arts are cultural activities that draw on (or react against) certain cultural traditions, certain shared understanding, and certain values and ideas that are characteristic of the time and place in which the art is created.
ordered_passages: (A) In the case of science, however, opinions differ. Some scientists, like the great biologist J. B. S. Haldane, see science in a similar light - as a historical activity that occurs in a particular time and place, and that needs to be understood within that context.

(B) In describing this view of science, philosopher Hugh Lacey speaks of the belief that there is an underlying order of the world which is simply there to be discovered - the world of pure "fact" stripped of any link with value. The aim of science according to this view is to represent this world of pure "fact", independently of any relationship it might bear contingently to human practices and experiences.
(C) Others, however, see science as a purely "objective" pursuit, uninfluenced by the cultural viewpoint and values of those who create it.
explanation: 예술이 문화적 맥락에 기반한다는 것에는 이견이 없으나 과학에 대해서는 의견이 갈린다는 내용입니다. (A)에서 과학 또한 예술처럼 역사적/문화적 맥락에서 이해되어야 한다는 J.B.S. Haldane의 견해를 먼저 제시합니다. (C)에서 'Others'를 통해 과학이 가치와 무관한 객관적 추구라고 보는 대조적인 견해를 소개합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 철학자 Hugh Lacey의 말을 인용하여 (C)에서 언급된 과학의 객관적 견해(순수한 사실의 세계)를 구체적으로 설명하는 흐름이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 34. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: In today's information age, in many companies and on many teams, the objective is no longer error prevention and replicability. On the contrary, it's creativity, speed, and keenness. In the industrial era, the goal was to minimize variation. (A) But in creative companies today, maximizing variation is more essential. (B) In these situations, the biggest risk isn't making a mistake or losing consistency; it's failing to attract top talent, to invent new products, or to change direction quickly when the environment shifts. (C) Consistency and repeatability are more likely to suppress fresh thinking than to bring your company profit. (D) A lot of little mistakes, while sometimes painful, help the organization learn quickly and are a critical part of the innovation cycle. (E) A symphony isn't what you're going for. Leave the conductor and the sheet music behind. Build a jazz band instead.
insertion_sentence: In these situations, rules and process are no longer the best answer.
explanation: 글의 전반부는 현대 창의적 기업에서는 실수 방지보다 변동성 극대화와 혁신이 중요함을 설명합니다. 주어진 문장의 'In these situations'는 창의성이 강조되고 실수가 혁신의 일부가 되는 상황을 가리킵니다. (E) 뒤에 이어지는 문장들은 지휘자와 악보(규칙과 절차)를 버리고 재즈 밴드처럼 행동하라고 조언하는데, 이는 규칙과 절차가 더 이상 최선의 답이 아니라는 주어진 문장의 결론과 자연스럽게 연결되어 비유적 결론으로 이어집니다.

question: 35. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: On our little world, light travels, for all practical purposes, instantaneously. If a lightbulb is glowing, then of course it's physically where we see it, shining away. We reach out our hand and touch it: It's there all right, and unpleasantly hot. If the filament fails, then the light goes out. We don't see it in the same place, glowing, illuminating the room years after the bulb breaks and it's removed from its socket. The very notion seems nonsensical. But if we're far enough away, an entire sun can go out and we'll continue to see it shining brightly; we won't learn of its death, it may be, for ages to come - in fact, for how long it takes light, which travels fast but not infinitely fast, to cross the intervening vastness. The immense distances to the stars and the galaxies mean that we see everything in space in the past.
summary_sentence: While light appears to travel almost (A)__________ on Earth, the (B)__________ speed of light, combined with the vast distances of the universe, means we observe everything in space as it appeared in the past.
options: ① promptly / finite
② gradually / infinite
③ irregularly / variable
④ immediately / immense
⑤ unpredictably / predictable
explanation: 지구상에서 빛은 즉각적으로(instantaneously) 전달되는 것처럼 보이지만, 실제로는 유한한(finite) 속도를 가지고 있습니다. 우주의 거대한 거리 때문에 우리가 보는 별빛은 과거의 모습이 됩니다. (A)에는 instantaneously와 유사한 promptly 또는 immediately가 적절하며, (B)에는 빛의 속도가 '무한하지 않다(not infinitely fast)'는 본문의 내용을 반영하는 finite가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 즉각적으로 / 유한한
② 점진적으로 / 무한한
③ 불규칙적으로 / 가변적인
④ 즉시 / 거대한
⑤ 예측 불가능하게 / 예측 가능한

question: 36. 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. 윗글의 밑줄 친 this가 의미하는 것을 지문에서 찾아 영어로 구체적으로 쓰시오. [24년 6월 36번]
passage: Brains are expensive in terms of energy. Twenty percent of the calories we consume are used to (A)[power / powering] the brain. So brains try to operate in the most energy-efficient way possible, and that means (B)[processing / to process] only the minimum amount of information from our senses that we need (C)[to navigate / navigate] the world. Neuroscientists weren't the first to discover that fixing your gaze on something is no guarantee of seeing it. Magicians figured this out long ago. By directing your attention, they perform tricks with their hands in full view. Their actions should give away the game, but they can rest (D)[assured / assuring] that your brain processes only small bits of the visual scene. This all helps to explain the prevalence of traffic accidents (E)[in which / which] drivers hit pedestrians in plain view, or collide with cars directly in front of them. In many of these cases, the eyes are pointed in the right direction, but the brain isn't seeing what's really out there.
answer: fixing your gaze on something is no guarantee of actually seeing it
explanation: 지문에서 'Magicians figured this out long ago'의 바로 앞 문장에 언급된 '무언가에 시선을 고정하는 것이 그것을 보는 것을 보장하지 않는다는 사실'을 의미합니다. 지문 내의 'fixing your gaze on something is no guarantee of seeing it' 부분을 찾아 쓰면 됩니다.

question: 37. 다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. 윗글의 (A)~(E)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것을 찾아 쓰시오. [24년 6월 36번]
passage: Brains are expensive in terms of energy. Twenty percent of the calories we consume are used to (A)[power / powering] the brain. So brains try to operate in the most energy-efficient way possible, and that means (B)[processing / to process] only the minimum amount of information from our senses that we need (C)[to navigate / navigate] the world. Neuroscientists weren't the first to discover that fixing your gaze on something is no guarantee of seeing it. Magicians figured this out long ago. By directing your attention, they perform tricks with their hands in full view. Their actions should give away the game, but they can rest (D)[assured / assuring] that your brain processes only small bits of the visual scene. This all helps to explain the prevalence of traffic accidents (E)[in which / which] drivers hit pedestrians in plain view, or collide with cars directly in front of them. In many of these cases, the eyes are pointed in the right direction, but the brain isn't seeing what's really out there.
answer: (A) power(B) processing(C) to navigate(D) assured(E) in which
explanation: (A) be used to 동사원형 (~하기 위해 사용되다): power가 적절합니다.(B) mean의 목적어로 동명사 processing이 와서 '~하는 것을 의미하다'가 됩니다.(C) need의 목적어인 명사구 뒤에서 수식하거나 목적을 나타내는 to부정사 to navigate가 적절합니다.(D) rest assured (안심해도 좋다/확신해도 좋다)라는 관용적 표현으로 과거분사 형태가 쓰입니다.(E) 뒤에 완전한 문장이 이어지므로 전치사+관계대명사인 in which가 적절합니다.

question: 38. 다음 글을 읽고 제목을 만들 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 적절한 표현을 지문에서 찾아 한 단어의 영어로 각각 쓰시오. [24년 6월 40번]
passage: Many things spark envy : ownership, status, health, youth, talent, popularity, beauty. It is often confused with jealousy because the physical reactions are identical. The difference: the subject of envy is a thing (status, money, health etc.). The subject of jealousy is the behaviour of a third person. Envy needs two people. Jealousy, on the other hand, requires three: Peter is jealous of Sam because the beautiful girl next door rings him instead. Paradoxically, with envy we direct resentments toward those who are most similar to us in age, career and residence. We don't envy businesspeople from the century before last. We don't envy millionaires on the other side of the globe. As a writer, I don't envy musicians, managers or dentists, but other writers. As a CEO you envy other, bigger CEOs. As a supermodel you envy more successful supermodels. Aristotle knew this: 'Potters envy potters.'
summary_sentence: Paradoxical (A)__________: An Emotion Directed at Those Most (B)__________ to Us
subjective_conditions: 지문에서 찾아 한 단어의 영어로 쓸 것
explanation: 본문은 질투(jealousy)와 구별되는 '부러움(envy)'의 특성에 대해 설명하며, 특히 우리와 가장 '유사한(similar)' 사람들을 향해 부러움을 느낀다는 역설적인 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 핵심 소재인 Envy, (B)에는 부러움의 대상을 나타내는 similar가 적합합니다.

question: 다음 광을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. [24년 9월 22번]28. 윗광의 빈칸 (A)에 됔어갈 뤐로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Any new or threatening situation may ⓐ<u>require</u> us to make decisions and this requires information. So important is communication during a disaster that normal social barriers are often ⓑ<u>reinforced</u>. We will talk to strangers in a way we would never consider normally. Without an ⓓ<u>authoritative</u> source of facts, whether that is a newspaper or trusted broadcast station, rumours (A)__________. options: ① lose their credibility

explanation: 광의 문맥사 재난 상황이나 위협적인 상황에서 권위 읈는 정바원이 없을 경우 근거 없는 소문이 겉잡을 수 없이 퍼지가 쉽다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 신뢰성을 잃다

question: 다음 광을 읽고 물음에 답하시오. [24년 9월 22번]29. 윗광의 묜줄 친 바분 중 문맥사 낱뤐의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
