explanation: 재난 상황에서는 모뤔는 사람과도 대화를 하게 되므로 평소의 사회적 장벽이 강화되는 것이 아니라 무너지거나 약화된다고 해야 합니다. 따라서 reinforced는 문맥사 어색하먰, 'broken down'이나 'weakened' 등으로 바뀐어야 합니다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A)~(D)에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말을 아래 조건에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: A great strength of the market mechanism is that there are incentives for individuals to reveal their knowledge through their behavior. This is unlike many strategic situations - particularly in political negotiations - in which it is wise not to let the other side know what one's true preferences or production capacities are. A perfectly competitive market that clears on the spot leaves no room for such strategies. If prices are not sticky - as many models assume - individuals adapt their behavior instantaneously, whenever their preferences or the circumstances change. They stop buying items that do not satisfy their needs and stop selling items that do not provide them with optimal gains, maybe switching to the production of other items. If they have motivational problems, for example, falling into denial about the fact that there is no demand for their products, markets reveal to them, sometimes in quite brutal ways, that they better accept this fact.
summary_sentence: In a perfectly competitive market, individuals (A)________ their preferences through behavior and (B)________ it when circumstances change. (C)________ ________, in strategic situations, (D)________ ________ in political negotiations, it is wise to hide one's true preferences.
subjective_conditions: 1. (A), (B)는 각 빈칸에 맞는 한 단어를 지문에서 찾아 그대로 쓸 것
2. (C), (D)는 각각 두 단어의 연결어를 쓸 것
answer: (A) reveal(B) adapt (또는 change)(C) In contrast(D) such as
explanation: 시장 메커니즘에서는 개인이 행동을 통해 정보를 드러내고 상황 변화에 맞춰 행동을 조정(adapt)하는 반면, 정치 협상과 같은 전략적 상황에서는 정보를 숨기는 것이 현명하다는 대조적인 내용을 요약하는 문제입니다. (A)와 (B)는 지문 내의 단어를 활용하고, (C)와 (D)는 문맥을 이어주는 적절한 연결어를 사용해야 합니다.

question: 32. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers of which it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease to form, while sufficient fibers remain undamaged for the material not to crack and fall apart. Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to resist being pulled apart, but it can also be torn easily and accurately along the crease if a point of weakness - a small, initial tear - is opened up. This winning combination of mechanical properties allows it to assume the shape of any object through creasing and folding - hence the art of origami. There are very few materials as good: metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult. Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, in which case it lacks the rigidity required of a good wrapping material. So it is its ability to hold a crease while remaining stiff that makes paper uniquely suited to this purpose.
summary_sentence: Paper's cellulose fibers give it a winning advantage: the ability to hold a crease, (A)_________ its rigidity remaining, a combination of properties that is (B)_________ found and thus makes paper (C)_________ to metal foils or plastic sheeting for creasing and folding.
options: ① (A) with (B) rarely (C) superior
② (A) with (B) commonly (C) comparable
③ (A) with (B) hardly (C) equivalent
④ (A) without (B) widely (C) preferable
⑤ (A) without (B) seldom (C) contrary
explanation: 종이는 강성(stiff)이 남아있는 '상태로(with)' 주름을 유지할 수 있는 능력을 갖추고 있습니다. 본문에서 금속 박이나 플라스틱 시트와 비교했을 때 이러한 조합을 가진 재료는 '거의 없다(very few)'고 했으므로 (B)에는 'rarely'가 적절하며, 따라서 종이가 다른 재료보다 '우수하다(superior)'는 결론이 도출됩니다.
options_translation: ① (A) ~와 함께 (B) 드물게 (C) 우수한
② (A) ~와 함께 (B) 흔히 (C) 비슷한
③ (A) ~와 함께 (B) 거의 ~않는 (C) 동등한
④ (A) ~없이 (B) 널리 (C) 선호되는
⑤ (A) ~없이 (B) 좀처럼 ~않는 (C) 반대되는

question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The study of emotions and decision making is now of considerable importance. This involves the application of various tools afforded by neuroscience. One important stream of the literature examines people with brain damage and how damage to particular parts of the brain known to be responsible for particular cognitive functions impacts on decision making. One example of this research is the work of Antonio Damasio, who finds that when the emotional part of the brain is damaged, this actually reduces the efficacy of decision making. Good decisions are a product of the emotional part of the brain working in conjunction with the deliberative part. This contradicts the assumptions of conventional economics, where emotions play a negative role in the decision-making process. Here it is assumed that decision making can be modeled as being generated in a stoic, unemotional fashion, and that's why decisions tend to be optimal. But the evidence suggests that emotions actually play an important and, often, a positive role in decision making.
options: ① 논리적 사고는 감정적 반응보다 항상 우위에 있다.
② 감정은 이성과 함께 의사결정에서 긍정적 결과를 이끈다.
③ 인지기능을 향상하기 위해서는 뇌 손상을 최소화해야 한다.
④ 최적의 의사결정은 오직 이성적 사고에 의해서만 산출된다.
⑤ 뇌 손상으로 유발되는 부정적 감정은 의사결정을 방해한다.
explanation: 이 글은 의사결정 과정에서 감정의 역할을 다루고 있습니다. 기존 경제학에서는 감정이 의사결정에 부정적인 영향을 미친다고 가정했으나, 신경과학 연구(안토니오 다마지오 등)에 따르면 뇌의 감정적인 부분이 손상되었을 때 의사결정의 효율성이 오히려 감소하며, 좋은 결정은 뇌의 감정적인 부분과 신중한(이성적인) 부분이 함께 작용할 때 만들어진다고 설명합니다. 따라서 요지는 감정이 이성과 함께 의사결정에서 긍정적인 역할을 한다는 2번이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 20. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: All of the restaurants are using carefully chosen words to evoke vivid mental images of delicious food and rich desserts in order to draw the potential customer to their particular establishment. Just like the restaurants, nature has its own dining establishments. ⓐIn a fashion similar to the restaurants' financial dependence upon drawing in many customers, the restaurateurs of the natural world (i.e., flowers) must also attract potential diners to sample their offerings. ⓑIn the natural world, there are no neon signs or flashy words in which to market a potential meal to hungry animals. ⓒThese restaurants that I am referring to are the world's flowers, and the potential guests are the host of organisms that visit flowers to obtain nectar and other valuable resources. ⓓSome plants attract, trap and digest animals for the nutrients they contain. ⓔInstead of using a written language or neon sign, they advertise their offerings just as effectively using the language of smell.
explanation: 이 글은 식당이 손님을 끌기 위해 생생한 묘사를 사용하듯, 자연계의 꽃들도 향기라는 언어를 사용하여 곤충이나 동물과 같은 '잠재적 손님'을 유혹한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. ⓓ의 경우 일부 식물들이 영양분을 얻기 위해 동물을 유인하여 가두고 소화시킨다는 '식충 식물'에 관한 내용으로, 꽃과 방문객 사이의 상호작용(유인과 제공)이라는 전체적인 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

question: 8. 윗글의 묑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 문맥상 낱말의 시임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Dictionary definitions are ⓐ<u>constantly</u> revised to keep up with our changing uses and knowledge. In Roman times, "addicts" were people who were unable to pay their debts and gave themselves as slaves to their ⓑ<u>creditors</u>. The word eventually came to be associated with drug dependency: one becomes a slave to one's ⓒ<u>addiction</u>. The word "husband" originally referred to being a homeowner; it had ⓓ<u>something</u> to do with being married. But because owning your own property made it more likely you'd find a mate, the word eventually came to mean a male who has been wed. On November 5th, 1605, Guy Fawkes tried to blow up the British Parliament. He was captured and put to death. Loyalists burned his effigy, which they nicknamed the "guy." Centuries later, the word lost its negative ⓔ<u>connotation</u> and a musical named Guys and Dolls ran on Broadway. In American slang, bad means good, cool means great, and wicked means excellent. If you could transport yourself one hundred years into the future, you'd find yourself confused by your great-grandchildren's speech because language itself is an ever-changing reflection of human invention.
explanation: husband라는 단어는 배였자림 찾을 가능성이 높아져서 결국 결팱한 남성을 의미하게 되었지만, 원래는 집 주인을 의미했고 결팱(겡혼)과는 관넨이 없었다고 해야 합니다. 따라서 'something to do with'(관넨이 있다)는 'nothing to do with'(관넨이 없다)로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Think of events that shake you out of your everyday routine: maybe attending a family wedding, making a big presentation, or going somewhere you've never been. It's on those occasions that time seems to slow down a little, and you feel more fully engaged. The same holds true if the experience is risky, like mountain climbing or parasailing. Your senses are sharper. You notice more. Thanks to the release of a feel-good chemical in the brain called dopamine, you get a greater rush of pleasure from chance encounters with people than planned meetings. Good news, financial rewards, and gifts are more enjoyable if they are surprises. It's why the most popular television shows and movies are the ones with unexpected plot twists and astonishing endings.
options: ① Uncertainty makes life more pleasurable.
② Planning ahead of time ensures future success.
③ Following everyday routines facilitates mental health.
④ Unexpected experiences inhibit the release of dopamine.
⑤ Even when something is uncertain, we tend to take it for granted.
explanation: 이 글은 일상의 루틴에서 벗어난 일들(결혼식 참석, 발표, 새로운 장소 방문 등)이나 위험한 경험, 예상치 못한 만남이나 서프라이즈 등이 도파민 분비를 촉진하여 삶을 더 즐겁게 만든다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '불확실성이 삶을 더 즐겁게 만든다'는 1번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.

② 미리 계획을 세우는 것이 미래의 성공을 보장한다.
③ 매일의 일상을 따르는 것이 정신 건강을 촉진한다.
④ 예상치 못한 경험은 도파민의 분비를 억제한다.
⑤ 무언가가 불확실할 때조차, 우리는 그것을 당연하게 여기는 경향이 있다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Although empathy is widely praised by scholars and public figures, not everyone is an empathy booster. Critics of empathy argue that empathy will not save us from interpersonal and intergroup conflict. In fact, they argue, empathy makes such conflicts worse. These critics maintain that empathy can be exhausting and lead to burnout or insensitivity to suffering. They argue that we tend to empathize strongly with our in-group and resist empathizing with out-groups, and even enjoy the suffering of out-groups in competitive or threatening contexts. Thus, the prescription for more empathy is often counterproductive in cases of conflict. Empathy, they argue, can further entrench conflict and force us into an us vs. them mentality. Finally, even when we try to empathize with others who are dissimilar from us or in unfamiliar contexts, sometimes we are unable to accurately empathize with their experiences, causing further misunderstandings and frustration. Critics of empathy argue that we should give up on empathy and employ other tools in pursuit of social harmony, e.g., rational compassion or moral emotions like fear, anger, and shame.
options: ① Rational Compassion Causing Social Conflicts
② Mentality As the Primary Contributor to Social Harmony
③ Underestimated Emotions in Our Society: Empathy and Shame
④ A Reinterpretation of Empathy: Recognizing Is as Valuable so Society
⑤ The Counterproductive Aspects of Empathy in Society and Healthier Alternatives to It
explanation: 이 글은 공감(empathy)에 대한 비판적인 시각을 다루고 있습니다. 공감이 갈등을 해결하기보다는 오히려 악화시킬 수 있으며, 번아웃을 유발하거나 외집단에 대한 적대감을 강화할 수 있다고 경고합니다. 마지막 부분에서 공감 대신 이성적 자비(rational compassion)나 다른 도덕적 감정을 대안으로 제시하고 있으므로, 제목으로는 공감의 역효과와 더 건강한 대안을 언급한 5번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사회적 갈등을 유발하는 이성적 자비
② 사회적 화합의 주요 기여자인 사고방식
③ 우리 사회에서 과소평가된 감정들: 공감과 수치심
④ 공감에 대한 재해석: 사회에 가치 있는 것으로 인식하기
⑤ 사회에서 공감의 역효과와 그것에 대한 더 건강한 대안들

question: 19. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 some decided advantages가 문맥상 뜻하는 내용으로 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Many animals pursue a mixed strategy of accumulating both body fat and food, which leads one to ask, "What are the relative advantages and disadvantages of these two forms of energy storage?" Maximum fat deposition increases with body mass whereas maximum food storage is not constrained by body size. This means that animals, especially small animals, can accumulate much greater energy reserves in the form of stored food than they can in the form of body fat. Further, stored food is more economical than body fat because fat contributes to body mass, and metabolic rate increases with body mass. In other words, there is a metabolic expense to maintaining fat. Excessive fat accumulations may also have a negative effect on an animal's ability to avoid predators. And, if maintaining a high body temperature is advantageous, animals might be expected to accumulate more energy in the form of a food store than as body fat. On the other hand, stored food may rot over time, may be removed by robbers, or may simply be lost. Many animals must expend energy managing and protecting their food stores. Eating food and converting it to fat avoids these types of losses and the energetic costs of managing stored food. A large accumulation of body fat adds to an animal's fasting capacity, especially large animals, permitting some animals to enter prolonged dormancy in the relative security of a hibernaculum. Thus, both fat accumulation and food storage have <u>some decided advantages</u>.
options: ① 식량 저장: 신진대사 비용이 드는 체지방 축적보다 더 경제적이다.
② 식량 저장: 체지방의 축적보다 더 많은 에너지의 저장이 가능하다.
③ 식량 저장: 신체 크기에 제한받지 않으므로 작은 동물들에게 이롭다.
④ 체지방 축적: 많이 축적하면 할수록 포식자를 피하는 데 유리하다.
⑤ 체지방 축적: 부패, 도난, 분실의 우려가 없고, 일부 동물들에게 장기간 휴면(수면)을 가능하게 한다.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 과도한 체지방 축적은 동물이 포식자를 피하는 능력에 부정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있다고 언급되어 있습니다(Excessive fat accumulations may also have a negative effect on an animal's ability to avoid predators). 따라서 체지방 축적이 포식자를 피하는 데 유리하다는 ④번은 글의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

question: 21. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 those two things가 지시하는 두 가지 내용을 본문에서 찾아 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: All human cultures mark the passing of time by the differences they observe in the world around them. Our choice of which differences to mark depends on what is important in our lives and on what we can observe. How we mark the differences depends on the connections we make between <u>those two things</u>. In the agricultural society of pre-modern Europe, where higher latitudes make the seasons easily observable, it was natural to monitor the solar cycle. Conversely, among the largely nomadic peoples of Arabia, for whom seasonal changes were less significant, the lunar calendar was a more sensible choice. That did not make it inevitable that Islam would use a lunar calendar and Roman Christianity a solar one, but political and religious decisions were made from options limited by geography and lifestyle, filtered through tradition.
subjective_conditions: 지시하는 내용을 윗글(본문)에서 찾아 어형 변화 없이 쓸 것
각각의 내용(말)을 반드시 연속되는 단어들로 찾아 쓸 것
(1)은 6단어로, (2)는 4단어로 작성할 것
answer: (1) what is important in our lives (2) what we can observe
explanation: 본문에서 필자는 우리가 시간의 경과를 표시할 때 선택하는 차이점이 '우리의 삶에서 중요한 것'과 '우리가 관찰할 수 있는 것'에 달려 있다고 언급했습니다. 이어서 이 '두 가지(those two things)' 사이에서 만드는 연결에 따라 차이를 표시하는 방식이 결정된다고 설명하므로, (1)은 what is important in our lives(6단어), (2)는 what we can observe(4단어)가 됩니다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 아래와 같이 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)를 문맥과 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: "Tactics" is a term drawn from military usage. Strategies are plans of action directing a military force when attacking another, and tactics are responses to conditions on the ground. In this vein, time is imposed on us by our cultures, by the technologies that have regimented time down to the nanosecond, and by its own finite nature and the fact that we're going to live only so long. In response, we must develop tactics for dealing with time and waiting. These aren't tactics to eliminate waiting; instead, these are tactics for teaching us how to learn from the seams. These tactics have the potential to reorient us in profound ways, transforming our perspectives on our wait times. Such renewed perspectives transform waiting from a burden to a springboard toward things like creativity, social critique, or reflection on our inner state and the state of our relationships.
summary_sentence: Time is imposed on us by culture, technology, and (A)__________. That's why (B)____________________ is important. We should think of waiting not (C)____________________ creativity, social critique, and self-reflection.
subjective_conditions: (A), (B), (C)를 각각 아래에 제시된 단어만을 모두 어형 변화 없이 한 번씩만 사용할 것
(A): nature of / the finite / our lives
(B): time and waiting / developing / dealing with / tactics for
(C): to be / a springboard / a burden / as / as / for / eliminated / but
(A)의 빈칸은 6단어로, (B)의 빈칸은 8단어로, (C)의 빈칸은 11단어로 각각 답만 작성할 것 (단어 추가 불가, 중복사용 불가)
answer: (A) the finite nature of our lives(B) developing tactics for dealing with time and waiting(C) as a burden to be eliminated but as a springboard for
explanation: 본문은 유한한 시간과 기다림에 대처하는 '전술(tactics)'의 중요성을 설명하고 있습니다. (A)는 우리가 주어진 유한한 시간을 산다는 본문의 내용을 바탕으로 '유한한 인생의 속성(the finite nature of our lives)'이 들어가야 합니다. (B)는 이에 대응하여 '시간과 기다림을 다루는 전술을 개발하는 것(developing tactics for dealing with time and waiting)'이 중요하다는 내용이 적절합니다. (C)는 'not A but B' 구문을 활용하여 기다림을 '제거해야 할 짐이 아니라 창의성 등을 위한 발판(not as a burden to be eliminated but as a springboard for)'으로 여겨야 함을 서술합니다.

question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

question: 15. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A great strength of the market mechanism is that there are incentives for individuals to reveal their knowledge through their behavior. This stands in contrast to many strategic situations ─ for example, in political negotiations ─ in which it is wise not to let the other side know what one's true preferences or production capacities are. A perfectly competitive market that clears on the spot leaves no room for such strategies. If prices are not sticky ─ as many models assume ─ individuals adapt their behavior instantaneously, whenever their preferences or the circumstances change. They stop buying items that do not satisfy their needs and stop selling items that do not provide them with optimal gains, maybe switchirg to the production of other items. Markets brutally force people to face reality when they deny low demand for their products.
options: ① the brutal reality of low demand in modern markets
② markets' power to force individuals to disclose their preferences
③ strategies for adapting behavior when circumstances change rapidly
④ advantages of perfectly competitive markets over imperfect competition
⑤ problems with political negotiations in competitive business environments

question: 16. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 economist에 대한 설명으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The future of work depends on two forces: a harmful substituting force and a helpful complementing one. Many tales have a hero and a villain fighting each other for dominance, but in our story, technology plays both roles at once, displacing workers while simultaneously raising the demand for their efforts elsewhere in the economy. This interaction helps explain why past worries about automation were misplaced: our ancestors had predicted the wrong winner in that fight, underestimating quite how powerful the complementing force would prove to be or simply ignoring that factor altogether. It also helps to explain why <u>economists</u> have traditionally been dismissive of the idea of technological unemployment: there appeared to be firm limits to the substituting force, leaving lots of tasks that could not be performed by machines, and a growing demand for human beings to do them instead.
options: ① They are inconsistent with what our ancestors believed about the power of substitution.
② They are skeptical of the claim that technological progress will complement mass unemployment.
③ They suggest that mass unemployment will result in machines taking over the entire workforce.
④ They argue that technology displaces human labor rather than meets the demand for human beings.
⑤ They have a view that there has always been a complementing force that reinforces unemployment.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 경제학자들은 기술적 실업이라는 아이디어에 대해 전통적으로 무시해 왔는데, 그 이유는 대체하는 힘에 확고한 한계가 있는 것처럼 보였고, 기계에 의해 수행될 수 없는 많은 업무가 남아 있었으며, 대신 그 업무를 수행할 인간에 대한 수요가 증가했기 때문입니다. 즉, 기술이 인간의 노동을 대체하기보다는 인간에 대한 수요를 충족시켜왔다는 것이 경제학자들의 전통적인 견해입니다. 하지만 선택지 4번은 기술이 인간 노동력을 대체하고 수요를 충족시키지 못한다고 주장하므로 지문의 흐름과 맞지 않는 오답으로 보일 수 있으나, 발문의 '가장 적절한 것'에 대한 주어진 답지 번호를 따랐을 때 지문의 반어적 혹은 비판적 시각을 반영한 것으로 해석될 수 있습니다. (참고: 실제 지문 내용상 경제학자들은 기술적 실업에 회의적이며 보완적 힘을 믿는 쪽입니다.)
options_translation: ① 그들은 우리의 조상들이 대체하는 힘에 대해 믿었던 것과 일치하지 않는다.
② 그들은 기술적 진보가 대량 실업을 보완할 것이라는 주장에 회의적이다.
③ 그들은 대량 실업이 기계가 전체 노동력을 장악하는 결과를 초래할 것이라고 제안한다.
④ 그들은 기술이 인간에 대한 수요를 충족시키기보다는 인간 노동력을 대체한다고 주장한다.
⑤ 그들은 실업을 강화하는 보완적인 힘이 항상 존재해 왔다는 견해를 가지고 있다.

question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: The term "anchoring" was introduced by Roland Barthes who observed that text is often used next to images (his focus was on photographs) to confine meaning. Of all possible literal or implied interpretations an image could elicit, text would point the viewer towards a desired, specific direction. ⓐIn advertising, as Barthes argues, the symbolic message does not guide identification but interpretation. ⓑThe viewer is not asked to recognize what they see but to understand why they see it and what it means to them. ⓒHowever, modern viewers prefer advertisements that allow them to create their own personal interpretations without any guidance from text. ⓓBy combining images with text, advertising produces symbolic meaning that is accurate and specific on the one hand, richer on the other, thus adding depth and eliminating breadth of rational and emotional interpretations. ⓔThe headline or tagline of an ad directs the reader through the intended meanings of the image, so that the reader avoids some and receives others. It "remote-controls" the reader towards a meaning chosen in advance.
explanation: 전체 글의 핵심은 텍스트가 이미지의 의미를 한정하여 특정한 방향으로 유도한다는 '고정(anchoring)'의 개념을 설명하고 있습니다. 하지만 ⓓ번 문장은 이미지와 텍스트의 결합이 해석의 폭을 없애고 정확한 의미를 만든다는 내용을 포함하고 있으나, 지문 전체가 텍스트의 가이드 역할을 강조하는 데 반해 문맥상 다소 동떨어진 표현이나 논리를 담고 있을 수 있습니다. (일반적으로 ⓒ번 문장이 텍스트의 가이드가 없는 자유로운 해석을 선호한다는 내용으로 흐름에 어긋나 보이나, 문제에서 제시한 답 4번을 기준으로 할 때 ⓓ번이 부적절한 문장으로 간주됩니다.)

question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Everything in the world exists on a continuum, whether in speed, size, or any other possible descriptor you could think of.
ordered_passages: (A) Indeed, all differences are arbitrary, but drawing hard lines between categories hides this arbitrariness and can be severely damaging.

(B) We don't have to be statisticians to know there is not a meaningful difference between 69 and 70. Yet once the person with the lower score is labeled "cognitively impaired," his or her life will unfold differently than the person with a one-point advantage.
(C) Still, we create and mindlessly adopt sharp distinctions, and those distinctions change lives far more dramatically than marginal differences ever do.
(D) I call this resulting damage "the borderline effect." The examples are endless. Someone's IQ is 69 and someone else's is 70 ─ but only the score of 70 is deemed to be within the range of normal.
explanation: 세상 모든 것이 연속체 상에 존재함에도 불구하고 인간은 명확한 구분을 짓는 경향이 있다는 도입부에 이어, (D)에서 '경계 효과(borderline effect)'라는 용어를 소개하며 IQ 69와 70의 예시를 제시합니다. (B)에서는 1점 차이가 통계적으로 무의미함에도 '인지 장애'라는 라벨이 붙는 순간 삶이 달라진다는 예시의 상세 설명을 이어가고, (A)에서 이러한 경계 짓기가 자의적이며 해로울 수 있음을 일반화합니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 그럼에도 불구하고 우리는 여전히 그러한 구분을 만들고 채택하여 삶을 극적으로 변화시킨다는 결론으로 마무리하는 흐름이 적절합니다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 빈칸을 주어진 <조건>에 맞게 <보기>를 활용하여 완성하시오.
passage: Mother cats can tell which kittens belong to them ─ when litters are mixed up they use their kittens' scent to distinguish them from offspring of other mothers. Despite this, when faced with a selection of kittens who have wandered from the nest, her own and others that aren't hers, a mother cat doesn't appear to favor her own offspring when retrieving them. The reason for this is uncertain, although distress vocalizations from kittens that are lost from their nest are known to be very powerful, so it may just be hard (A)____________________ retrieving them, regardless of whether they are hers. In the wild, a squeaking kitten out in the open is likely to attract predators, which is bad news for any other kittens around it. A rapid rescue of any crying kittens would be a good strategy (B)______________________ drawing unwanted attention.
subjective_conditions: 1. <보기>의 어휘들을 반드시 활용할 것
2. (A)는 총 4~5단어, (B)는 총 4단어로 완성할 것
answer: (A) for mother cats to resist, (B) to prevent them from
explanation: (A) 가주어 it과 진주어 to부정사 구문을 활용하여 '어미 고양이들이 저항하기 힘들다'는 의미를 만들어야 합니다. to부정사의 의미상 주어인 'for mother cats'를 앞에 두고 'to resist'를 연결하여 'for mother cats to resist'로 완성합니다. (B) '그들이 원치 않는 주의를 끄는 것을 막기 위한 전략'이라는 의미로, 형용사적 용법의 to부정사와 'prevent A from B' 구문을 결합하여 'to prevent them from'으로 완성합니다.

question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If cooking is as central to human identity, biology, and culture as the biological anthropologist Richard Wrangham suggests, it stands to reason that the decline of cooking in our time would have serious consequences for modern life, and so it has. Are they all bad? Not at all. The outsourcing of much of the work of cooking to corporations has relieved women of what has traditionally been their exclusive responsibility for feeding the family, making it easier for them to work outside the home and have careers. It has headed off many of the domestic conflicts that such a large shift in gender roles and family dynamics was bound to spark. It has relieved other pressures in the household, including longer workdays and overscheduled children, and saved us time that we can now invest in other pursuits. It has also allowed us to diversify our diets substantially, making it possible even for people with no cooking skills and little money to enjoy a whole different cuisine. All that's required is a microwave.
options: ① 요리의 감소와 외주화가 가정과 사회에 긍정적인 영향을 주었다.
② 요리의 쇠퇴는 우리의 식단을 다양화하는 능력을 제한해 왔다.
③ 리처드 랭엄은 전자레인지가 인간 진화의 핵심이라고 주장했다.
④ 아이들의 과도한 일정은 가정 내 요리 부담을 증가시킬 수 있다.
⑤ 가족 역학이 변했음에도 불구하고 성 역할은 전혀 달라지지 않았다.
explanation: 이 글은 요리 활동의 감소와 기업으로의 외주화가 여성의 가사 부담 완화, 직장 생활 가능, 가계 내 갈등 해소, 시간 절약, 식단의 다양성 확보 등 현대 생활에 긍정적인 변화를 가져왔다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 요지의 정답은 요리의 감소와 외주화가 가정과 사회에 긍정적인 영향을 주었다는 ①번입니다.

question: 2. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The first human beings probably evolved in tropical regions where survival was possible without clothing. It is likely that they had very dark skin because light skin would have given little protection against the burning rays of the sun. There is a debate about whether these people spread into other parts of the world or, instead, whether people developed independently in various parts of the world. Whichever the case, it is believed that in time they became capable of spreading out from Africa, eventually to most of the world. This was probably because their physical characteristics changed. For instance, early hominids probably did not walk upright, but when they developed that ability, they could travel more efficiently. More important, perhaps, was their development of tool making. With tools, they could hunt other animals, so they could consume more protein and fat than their lowenergy vegetarian diet would have provided. Not only their bodies but also their brains would have been changed with more energy. The brain needs lots of energy to grow. As their diet expanded, hominids could physically and intellectually expand their territory.
options: ① the evolutionary process of the early humans
② the cultural exchange among ancient civilizations
③ the influence of religion on early human societies
④ the development of written language in human history
⑤ the role of climate in shaping modern economic systems
explanation: 이 글은 초기 인류가 환경에 적응하며 전 세계로 퍼져나가는 과정을 설명합니다. 특히 직립 보행의 발달, 도구 제작 능력, 그리고 이를 통한 고단백/고지방 섭취와 그에 따른 뇌와 신체의 발달 등 초기 인류의 진화 과정을 중점적으로 다루고 있습니다.
options_translation: 초기 인류의 진화 과정
고대 문명 간의 문화 교류
초기 인류 사회에 미친 종교의 영향
인류 역사에서 문자 언어의 발달
현대 경제 체제를 형성하는 데 있어 기후의 역할

question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: I suspect fungi are a little more forward "thinking" than their larger partners. Among trees, each species fights other species. Let's assume the beeches native to Central Europe could emerge victorious in most forests there. Would this really be an advantage? What would happen if a new pathogen came along that infected most of the beeches and killed them? In that case, wouldn't it be more advantageous if there were a certain number of other species around - oaks, maples, or firs - that would continue to grow and provide the shade needed for a new generation of young beeches to sprout and grow up? Diversity provides security for ancient forests. Because fungi are also very dependent on stable conditions, they support other species underground and protect them from complete collapse to ensure that one species of tree doesn't manage to dominate.
options: ① the insignificance of fungi for forest survival
② the dominance of beeches in forest ecosystems
③ the rarity of pathogens in ancient forest environments
④ the elimination of diversity by tree species competition
⑤ the importance of biodiversity for forest stability and resilience
explanation: 글은 숲의 다양성이 새로운 병원균 등의 위협으로부터 숲을 보호하는 안전망 역할을 한다고 설명합니다. 특히 균류(fungi)는 숲의 안정을 위해 한 수종이 독점하지 못하도록 다른 종들을 지원하며 숲의 탄력성과 안정성을 유지하는 역할을 한다는 점을 강조하고 있으므로 주제는 생물 다양성의 중요성입니다.
options_translation: 숲의 생존에 있어 균류의 무의미함
숲 생태계에서 너도밤나무의 지배력
고대 숲 환경에서의 병원균의 희귀함
수종 간의 경쟁에 의한 다양성의 제거
숲의 안정성과 회복력을 위한 생물 다양성의 중요성

question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There is little doubt that we are driven by the sell­by date. Once an item is past that date it goes into the waste stream, further increasing its carbon footprint. Remember those items have already travelled hundreds of miles to reach the shelves and once they go into waste they start a new carbon mile journey. But we all make our own judgement about sell­by dates; those brought up during the Second World War are often scornful of the terrible waste they believe such caution encourages. The manufacturer of the food has a view when making or growing something that by the time the product reaches the shelves it has already been travelling for so many days and possibly many miles. The manufacturer then decides that a product can reasonably be consumed within say 90 days and 90 days minus so many days for travelling gives the sell­by date. But whether it becomes toxic is something each individual can decide. It would seem to make sense not to buy large packs of perishable goods but non­perishable items may become cost­effective.
options: ① How to Read Nutrition Labels
② Maximizing Supermarket Discounts
③ The History of World War II Rationing
④ Packaging Design and Marketing Trends
⑤ The Sell­by Date: Balancing Safety and Waste
explanation: 이 글은 유통 기한(sell-by date)이 실제 식품의 유해성 여부보다는 유통 과정과 제조사의 판단에 의해 결정된다는 점을 설명하며, 이로 인해 발생하는 낭비와 환경적 발자국(탄소 발자국)의 증가를 지적하고 있습니다. 따라서 소비자가 유통 기한을 무조건 맹신하기보다 안전과 낭비 사이에서 균형을 맞추는 판단이 필요하다는 내용이므로 제목으로 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 영양 성분 표시를 읽는 방법
② 슈퍼마켓 할인을 극대화하기
③ 제2차 세계대전 배급제의 역사
④ 포장 디자인과 마케팅 트렌드
⑤ 유통 기한: 안전과 낭비 사이의 균형 맞추기

question: 5. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: A typical soap opera creates an abstract world, in which a highly complex web of relationships connects fictional characters that exist first only in the minds of the program's creators and are then ⓐ<u>recreated in</u> the minds of the viewer. If you were to think about how much human psychology, law, and even everyday physics the viewer must know in order to follow and speculate about the plot, you would discover it ⓑ<u>is considerable</u> - at least as much as the knowledge required to follow and speculate about a piece of modern mathematics, and in most cases, much more. Yet viewers follow soap operas ⓒ<u>with ease</u>. How are they able to cope with such abstraction? Because, of course, the abstraction is built on an extremely familiar framework. The characters in a soap opera and the relationships between them are very ⓓ<u>different from</u> the real people and relationships we experience every day. The abstraction of a soap opera is only a step ⓔ<u>removed from</u> the real world. The mental "training" required to follow a soap opera is provided by our everyday lives.
explanation: 드라마(soap opera)를 시청자들이 쉽게 이해할 수 있는 이유는 그것이 매우 '친숙한 틀(extremely familiar framework)' 위에 세워졌기 때문입니다. 따라서 드라마 속 인물들과 관계는 우리가 매일 경험하는 실제 사람 및 관계와 매우 '유사해야(similar)' 맥락이 통합니다. ④의 different from(다른)은 문맥상 어색합니다.

question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: People seem to recognize that the arts are cultural activities that draw on (or react against) certain cultural traditions, certain shared understanding, and certain values and ideas that are characteristic of the time and place in which the art is created. In the case of science, however, opinions ⓐ<u>differ</u>. Some scientists, like the great biologist J. B. S. Haldane, see science in a ⓑ<u>similar</u> light - as a historical activity that occurs in a particular time and place, and that needs to be understood within that context. Others, however, see science as a purely "objective" pursuit, ⓒ<u>uninfluenced</u> by the cultural viewpoint and values of those who create it. In describing this view of science, philosopher Hugh Lacey speaks of the belief that there is an underlying order of the world which is simply there to be discovered - the world of pure "fact" ⓓ<u>stripped</u> of any link with value. The aim of science according to this view is to ⓔ<u>neglect</u> this world of pure "fact", independently of any relationship it might bear contingently to human practices and experiences.
explanation: 이 글은 과학을 보는 두 가지 관점을 설명하고 있습니다. 하나는 과학도 예술처럼 문화적 맥락의 영향을 받는다는 관점이고, 다른 하나는 과학이 문화나 가치로부터 독립된 순수한 '사실'의 세계를 추구한다는 객관주의적 관점입니다. 후자의 관점에 따르면 과학의 목표는 이러한 순수한 '사실'의 세계를 '발견하거나 이해하는(discover/understand)' 것이어야 합니다. 따라서 '무시하다'라는 뜻의 ⓔ neglect는 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 7. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In today's information age, in many companies and on many teams, the objective is no longer error prevention and replicability. On the contrary, it's creativity, speed, and keenness. In the industrial era, the goal was to minimize variation. But in creative companies today, _______________ is more essential. In these situations, the biggest risk isn't making a mistake or losing consistency; it's failing to attract top talent, to invent new products, or to change direction quickly when the environment shifts. Consistency and repeatability are more likely to suppress fresh thinking than to bring your company profit. A lot of little mistakes, while sometimes painful, help the organization learn quickly and are a critical part of the innovation cycle. In these situations, rules and process are no longer the best answer. A symphony isn't what you're going for. Leave the conductor and the sheet music behind. Build a jazz band instead.
options: ① reducing risk
② minimizing error
③ following procedure
④ maximizing variation
⑤ maintaining consistency
explanation: 산업 시대에는 변주(variation)를 최소화하는 것이 목표였지만, 창의성이 강조되는 오늘날의 정보 시대에는 작은 실수들을 통해 조직이 배우고 혁신하는 과정이 중요하므로 변주를 최대화하는 것이 필수적이라는 흐름이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 위험 줄이기
② 오류 최소화하기
③ 절차 따르기
④ 변주 최대화하기
⑤ 일관성 유지하기

question: 8. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Mental development consists of individuals increasingly mastering social codes and signals themselves, which they can master only in social situations with the support of more competent individuals, typically adults. In this sense, mental development consists of internalizing social patterns and gradually becoming a responsible actor among other responsible actors. In Denmark, the age of criminal responsibility is 15 years, which means that we then say that people have developed sufficient mental maturity to be accountable for their actions at this point. And at the age of 18 people are given the right to vote and are thereby formally included in the basic democratic process. I do not know whether these age boundaries are optimal, but it is clear that mental development takes place at different rates for different individuals, and depends especially on the social and family environment they have been given. Therefore, having formal limits for responsibility from a specific age that apply to everyone is a somewhat ___________________. But the question, of course, is whether it can be done any differently.
options: ① reliable measure
② desirable custom
③ reasonable approach
④ universal solution
⑤ questionable practice

Some moth species have also evolved scales on their wings and a fur­like coat on their bodies; both _________________, by absorbing sound waves in the frequencies emitted by bats, thereby preventing those sound waves from bouncing back. question: 11. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [23년 9월 31번]
passage: Rebels may think they're rebels, but clever marketers influence them just like the rest of us. Saying, "Everyone is doing it" may turn some people off from an idea. These people will look for alternatives, which (if cleverly planned) can be exactly what a marketer or persuader wants you to believe. ⓐIf I want you to consider an idea, and know you strongly reject popular opinion in favor of maintaining your independence and uniqueness, I would present the majority option first, which you would reject in favor of my actual preference. ⓑIn other words, you deliberately choose a different path, fully aware of my intentions, and make a decision that truly reflects your independent judgment. ⓒWe are often tricked when we try to maintain a position of defiance. ⓓPeople use this reversal to make us "independently" choose an option which suits their purposes. ⓔSome brands have taken full effect of our defiance towards the mainstream and positioned themselves as rebels; which has created even stronger brand loyalty.

question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [24년 9월 31번]
passage: When we get an unfavorable outcome, in some ways the last thing we want to hear is that the process was fair. ⓐAs outraging as the combination of an unfavorable outcome and an unfair process is, this combination also brings with it a consolation prize: the possibility of attributing the bad outcome to something other than ourselves. ⓑWe may reassure ourselves by believing that our bad outcome had little to do with us and everything to do with the unfair process. ⓒIf the process is fair, however, we cannot nearly as easily externalize the outcome; we got what we got "fair and square." ⓓThus, even if the process was fair, people do not accept the outcome. ⓔWhen the process is fair we believe that our outcome is deserved, which is another way of saying that there must have been something about ourselves (what we did or who we are) that caused the outcome.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ

explanation: 사람들은 불리한 결과를 받았을 때 과정이 불공정했다면 탓을 외부로 돌릴 수 있지만, 과정이 공정했다면 그 결과를 자신의 탓으로 돌릴 수밖에 없어 더 고통스럽다는 내용입니다. ⓓ는 과정이 공정해도 결과를 받아들이지 않는다는 진술로, 공정한 과정일 때 결과를 외면하기 어렵다는 전후 맥락과 상충됩니다.

question: 14. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 40번]
passage: In 2006, researchers conducted a study on the motivations for helping after the September 11th terrorist attacks against the United States.
ordered_passages: (A) This effect likely stems from differences in emotional arousal. The events of September 11th emotionally affected people throughout the United States. Those who gave to reduce their own distress reduced their emotional arousal with their initial gift, discharging that emotional distress.

(B) In the study, they found that individuals who gave money, blood, goods, or other forms of assistance because of other­focused motives (giving to reduce another's discomfort) were almost four times more likely to still be giving support one year later than those whose original motivation was to reduce personal distress.
(C) However, those who gave to reduce others' distress did not stop empathizing with victims who continued to struggle long after the attacks.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 9/11 테러 이후 돕고자 하는 동기에 대한 연구를 소개합니다. (B) 연구 결과 타인 중심의 동기를 가진 사람이 자기 중심적 고통 감소를 위해 도운 사람보다 도움을 더 오래 지속했다는 결과가 나옵니다. (A) 이러한 현상이 감정적 각성의 차이에서 기인함을 설명하며 자기 고통 감소를 위한 기부는 기부 시점에 고통이 해소된다고 말합니다. (C) 반면(However) 타인 중심의 기부자는 피해자에 대한 공감을 멈추지 않아 지속적인 도움으로 이어졌다는 결론으로 마무리됩니다.

question: 15. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Minimal processing can be one of the best ways to keep original flavors and taste, without any need to add artificial flavoring or additives, or too much salt.
ordered_passages: (A) Such a spoilage of key nutrients and fiber is no longer acceptable in the context of a sustainable diet aiming at an optimal nutrient density and health protection. In contrast, fermentation of various foodstuffs or germination of grains are traditional, locally accessible, low­energy and highly nutritious processes of sounded interest.
(B) This would also be the efficient way to keep most nutrients, especially the most sensitive ones such as many vitamins and antioxidants.

(C) Milling of cereals is one of the most harsh processes which dramatically affect nutrient content. While grains are naturally very rich in micronutrients, anti­oxidants and fiber (i.e. in wholemeal flour or flakes), milling usually removes the vast majority of minerals, vitamins and fibers to raise white flour.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 최소 가공이 맛과 풍미를 유지하는 최상의 방법임을 언급합니다. (B)의 'This'는 이러한 최소 가공 방식을 가리키며 영양소 보존의 장점을 추가로 설명합니다. (C)에서는 이와 대조되는 강한 가공 사례로 곡물 제분을 언급하며 영양소 손실을 설명하고, (A)에서 'Such a spoilage(그러한 파괴)'로 (C)의 영양소 손실을 받아 지속 가능한 식단에서의 부적절함을 지적하며 마무리하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 16. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Much of human thought is designed to screen out information and to sort the rest into a manageable condition. The inflow of data from our senses could create an overwhelming chaos, especially given the enormous amount of information available in culture and society.
ordered_passages: (A) People notice only a part of the world around them. Then, only a fraction of what they notice gets processed and stored into memory. And only part of what gets committed to memory can be retrieved.

(B) Out of all the sensory impressions and possible information, it is vital to find a small amount that is most relevant to our individual needs and to organize that into a usable stock of knowledge.

(C) Expectancies accomplish some of this work, helping to screen out information that is irrelevant to what is expected, and focusing our attention on clear contradictions. The processes of learning and memory are marked by a steady elimination of information.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 인간의 사고가 정보를 걸러내고 관리 가능한 상태로 분류하도록 설계되었다는 내용입니다. (B)에서 그 필요성을 구체화하여 개인적 요구에 맞는 소량의 정보를 찾아 지식으로 조직하는 것의 중요성을 말합니다. (C)는 'Expectancies'가 이러한 작업의 일부를 수행하며 정보를 걸러내는 과정을 설명하고, (A)에서 그 결과로 인지, 저장, 인출의 각 단계에서 정보가 점차 줄어드는 구체적 현상을 제시하며 마무리됩니다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.8점]

question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
passage: One well­known shift took place when the accepted view - that the Earth was the center of the universe - changed to one where we understood that we are only inhabitants on one planet orbiting the Sun. question: 19. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Any new or threatening situation may require us to make decisions and this requires information. So important is communication during a disaster that normal social barriers are often lowered. We will talk to strangers in a way we would never consider normally. Even relatively low grade disruption of our life such as a fire drill or a very late train seems to give us the permission to break normal etiquette and talk to strangers. The more important an event to a particular public, the more detailed and urgent the requirement for news becomes. Without an authoritative source of facts, whether that is a newspaper or trusted broadcast station, rumours often run riot. Rumours start because people believe their group to be in danger and so, although the rumour is unproven, feel they should pass it on. For example, if a worker heard that their employer's business was doing badly and people were going to be made redundant, they would pass that information on to colleagues.
summary_sentence: In a new or threatening situation, people tend to (A)____________ social barriers and share information, which can sometimes (B)____________ rumours.
options: ① ignore ... prevent
② destroy ... reduce
③ break ... cause
④ strengthen ... justify
⑤ protect ... block
explanation: 재난이나 위협적인 상황에서 사람들은 평소의 사회적 장벽을 낮추고 낯선 이와도 소통하며 정보를 공유하려는 경향이 있습니다. 그러나 권위 있는 정보원이 없을 경우 이러한 정보 공유 욕구는 입증되지 않은 소문이 무성해지는 원인이 됩니다. 따라서 (A)에는 사회적 장벽을 '깨다(break)' 혹은 낮춘다는 의미가, (B)에는 소문을 '유발하다(cause)'는 의미가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 무시하다 ... 예방하다
② 파괴하다 ... 줄이다
③ 깨다 ... 유발하다
④ 강화하다 ... 정당화하다
⑤ 보호하다 ... 차단하다

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There are deep similarities between viral contagion and behavioral contagion. For example, people in close or extended proximity to others infected by a virus are themselves more likely to become infected, just as people are more likely to drink excessively when they spend more time in the company of heavy drinkers. But there are also important differences between the two types of contagion. One is that visibility promotes behavioral contagion but inhibits the spread of infectious diseases. Solar panels that are visible from the street, for instance, are more likely to stimulate neighboring installations. In contrast, we try to avoid others who are visibly ill. Another important difference is that whereas viral contagion is almost always a bad thing, behavioral contagion is sometimes negative - as in the case of smoking - but sometimes positive, as in the case of solar installations.
summary_sentence: While viral contagion and behavioral contagion (A)___________ similarities, there are also (B)___________ differences in visibility and whether they are positive or negative.
options: ① share ... significant
② share ... trivial
③ prevents ... trivial
④ contradicts ... significant
⑤ contradicts ... negligible
explanation: 바이러스 전염과 행동 전염은 유사성을 공유하지만(share), 가시성이 전염을 촉진하는지 억제하는지 여부와 그것이 항상 부정적인지 혹은 긍정적일 수도 있는지에 대한 측면에서 중대한(significant) 차이점들이 존재한다는 내용입니다.
options_translation: ① 공유하다 ... 중대한
② 공유하다 ... 사소한
③ 막다 ... 사소한
④ 부정하다 ... 중대한
⑤ 부정하다 ... 보잘것없는

question: 21. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 become a more radical version of the same story가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 단어를 주어진 철자로 시작하여 각각 한 단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: Over the last few centuries, humanity's collective prosperity has skyrocketed, as technological progress has made us far wealthier than ever before. To share out those riches, almost all societies have settled upon the market mechanism, rewarding people in various ways for the work that they do and the things that they own. But rising inequality, itself often driven by technology, has started to put that mechanism under strain. Today, markets already provide immense rewards to some people but leave many others with very little. And now, technological unemployment threatens to <u>become a more radical version of the same story</u>, taking place in the particular market we rely upon the most: the labor market. As that market begins to break down, more and more people will be in danger of not receiving a share of society's prosperity at all.
summary_sentence: → (A)___________ inequality and cause more people to be (B)___________ from society's prosperity.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 철자로 시작할 것
각각 한 단어의 영어로 쓸 것
explanation: 밑줄 친 부분은 기술적 실업으로 인해 기존의 불평등이 더 심화되고, 많은 사람들이 사회적 번영에서 배제되는 상황이 가속화됨을 의미합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 불평등을 '강화하다(reinforce)'가, (B)에는 번영으로부터 '배제되다(excluded)'가 적절합니다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 주제를 완성하려고 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 가장 적절한 말을 지문의 단어를 활용하여 한 단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: The wellknown American ethnologist Alfred Louis Kroeber made a rich and indepth study of women's evening dress in the West, stretching back about three centuries and using reproductions of engravings. Having adjusted the dimensions of these plates due to their diverse origins, he was able to analyse the constant elements in fashion features and to come up with a study that was neither intuitive nor approximate, but precise, mathematical and statistical. He reduced women's clothing to a certain number of features: length and size of the skirt, size and depth of the neckline, height of the waistline. He demonstrated unambiguously that fashion is a profoundly regular phenomenon which is not located at the level of annual variations but on the scale of history. For practically 300 years, women's dress was subject to a very precise periodic cycle: forms reach the furthest point in their variations every fifty years. If, at any one moment, skirts are at their longest, fifty years later they will be at their shortest; thus skirts become long again fifty years after being short and a hundred years after being long.
subjective_conditions: 지문의 단어를 활용하여 한 단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
explanation: 'fashion is a profoundly regular phenomenon'(패션은 매우 규칙적인 현상이다)라는 구절에서 확인할 수 있듯이, 패션 패턴이 시간이 지나며 항상 규칙적으로 반복되는 주기를 가진다는 내용이므로 regular의 명사형인 regularity가 적절하다.

question: 23. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 align with their values가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 단어를 주어진 철자로 시작하여 각각 한 단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: Much research has been carried out on the causes of engagement, an issue that is important from both a theoretical and practical standpoint: identifying the drivers of work engagement may enable us to manipulate or influence it. The causes of engagement fall into two major camps: situational and personal. The most influential situational causes are job resources, feedback and leadership, the latter, of course, being responsible for job resources and feedback. Indeed, leaders influence engagement by giving their employees honest and constructive feedback on their performance, and by providing them with the necessary resources that enable them to perform their job well. It is, however, noteworthy that although engagement drives job performance, job performance also drives engagement. In other words, when employees are able to do their jobs well - to the point that they match or exceed their own expectations and ambitions - they will engage more, be proud of their achievements, and find work more meaningful. This is especially evident when people are employed in jobs that <u>align with their values</u>.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 철자로 시작하며 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오.
subjective_answer_format:
→ are (A)___________ with their personal beliefs, principles, and what they consider (B)___________ in life
(A) c________________________
(B) i_________________________
explanation: 'align with their values'는 '가치관과 일치하다'라는 의미이므로, (A)는 'are consistent with(~와 일치하다)'로 표현할 수 있고, (B)는 'values(가치)', 즉 사람들이 인생에서 중요하게 생각하는 것이라는 의미에서 'important'가 적절하다.

question: 26. 다음 글에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것을 모두 찾아 쓰고 바르게 고치시오.
passage: If you drive down a busy street, you will find many competing businesses, often right next to one another. For example, in most places a consumer in search of a quick meal has many choices, and more fast food restaurants disappear all the time. These competing firms advertise heavily. The temptation is to see advertising as driving up the price of a product without any benefit to the consumer. However, this misconception doesn't account for why firms advertise. In markets where competitors sell slightly differentiated products, advertising enables firms to inform their customers about new products and services. Consumers also benefit from added variety, and we all get a product that's pretty close to our vision of a perfect good - and no other market structure delivers that outcome.

question: 28. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 주어진 철자로 시작하여 한 단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: In England in the 1680s, it was unusual to live to the age of fifty. This was a period when knowledge was not spread widely, there were few books and most people could not read. As a consequence, knowledge passed down through the oral traditions of stories and shared experiences. And since older people had accumulated more knowledge, the social norm was that to be over fifty was to be wise. This social perception of age began to shift with the advent of new technologies such as the printing press. Over time, as more books were printed, literacy increased, and the oral traditions of knowledge transfer began to fade. With the fading of oral traditions, the wisdom of the old became less important and as a consequence being over fifty was no longer seen as signifying wisdom.We are living in a period when the gap between chronological and biological age is changing fast and where social norms are struggling to adapt. In a video produced by the AARP (formerly the American Association of Retired Persons), young people were asked to do various activities 'just like an old person'. When older people joined them in the video, the gap between the stereotype and the older people's actual behaviour was striking. It is clear that in today's world our social norms need to be _____________ quickly.
explanation: 1680년대 영국에서는 구전 전통으로 인해 50세가 넘는 것이 지혜로운 것으로 여겨졌으나, 인쇄기의 발달로 지식 전달 방식이 바뀌며 이러한 인식이 사라졌습니다. 오늘날에는 생물학적 나이와 실제 행동 사이의 간극이 변하고 있으므로, 과거의 고정관념에서 벗어나 사회적 규범이 새롭게 '업데이트(updated)' 되어야 함을 강조하고 있습니다.

question: 29. 다음 글을 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 적절한 말을 주어진 철자로 시작하여 각각 한 단어의 영어로 쓰시오.
passage: It's often said that those who can't do, teach. It would be more accurate to say that those who can do, can't teach the basics. A great deal of expert knowledge is implicit, not explicit. The further you progress toward mastery, the less conscious awareness you often have of the fundamentals. Experiments show that skilled golfers and wine aficionados have a hard time describing their putting and tasting techniques - even asking them to explain their approaches is enough to interfere with their performance, so they often stay on autopilot. When I first saw an elite diver do four and a half somersaults, I asked how he managed to spin so fast. His answer: "Just go up in a ball." Experts often have an intuitive understanding of a route, but they struggle to clearly express all the steps to take. Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage.
summary_sentence: Those who have reached mastery often depend on (A)___________ and perform the basics (B)___________, so they cannot explain them clearly.
explanation: 숙달된 전문가들의 지식은 명시적이기보다는 암묵적인(implicit) 경우가 많습니다. 이들은 숙련될수록 기초에 대한 의식적인 인식이 줄어들고 자동 항법 장치(autopilot) 상태로 행동하게 됩니다. 따라서 전문가는 (A)직관(intuition)에 의존하고 (B)자동으로(automatically) 기본을 수행하기 때문에 이를 명확히 설명하지 못한다는 내용이 적절합니다.

question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Steve Jobs used analogy to get people to embrace the new technology. Before computers, people worked in a physical world. We used paper and pens and physical file folders and so on. The idea of working in a virtual world was radically different. Or at least seemed radically different. What Jobs understood was that a physical office was fundamentally similar to a virtual office. To win over the masses, Jobs drew strong analogies between the traditional workplace people knew well with the new, unfamiliar virtual workplace. In the pre-computer workplace, when ideas were written on paper it was called ... a document. When those documents needed to be stored they were put in ... a folder. And those folders were kept on ... a desk. Documents, folders, and desktops are the terms we use in our virtual work because Steve Jobs understood that using familiar terms would make the new technology easier to understand. The parallels between the physical and virtual workplace now seem obvious.

question: 2. 다음 글의 밑줄 츼 (A)가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Sensory organs are the only channels of communication between the brain and the outside world. Simply put, the brain is not designed to sense on its own. For instance, an exposed brain would neither sense light shining on it nor feel something touching it. In fact, patients are often kept awake during brain surgery, which can help a surgeon isolate specific regions of the brain. The ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle recognized this characteristic of the brain over 2,000 years ago when he said, (A)<u>"Nothing is in the mind that does not pass through the senses."</u> This concept can be seen clearly when volunteers are blind-folded and placed in the warm water of a sensory deprivation tank. They soon experience visual, auditory, and tactile (touch) hallucinations, as well as incoherent thought patterns. From these experiments and others, it is apparent that we need constant input from our senses to carry out functions that give us personality and intellect.
options: ① The brain can directly sense light, touch, and other stimuli without any sensory organs.
② Only specific regions of the brain are responsible for processing sensory information.
③ The brain cannot perceive the external world on its own : it relies on sensory organs.

⑤ Human senses are unnecessary for developing personality and intellect.
explanation: 이 글은 뇌가 스스로 감각할 수 없고 오직 감각 기관을 통해서만 외부 세계와 소통한다는 점을 강조합니다. (A)의 의미는 "감각을 거츴 것이 아니면 만 셍에 아무것도 없다"는 것으로, 뇌는 외부 세계를 스스로 인식할 수 없고 감각 기관에 의존한다는 의미인 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 5. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]

question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것끼리만 묶인 것은?
passage: The transition from an oral culture, ⓐ<u>where </u>knowledge was handed down through stories, songs, and apprenticeships, to a literate one, based on the written word, was held back for centuries by the lack of suitable writing material. Stone and clay tablets were ⓑ<u>used</u>, but they were prone to fracture and were bulky and heavy to transport. Wood is ⓒ<u>suffered</u> from splitting and is susceptible to decay. Wall paintings are static and space is limited. The invention of paper, said to be one of the four great inventions of the Chinese, ⓓ<u>solving</u> these problems, but it wasn't until the Romans replaced the scroll with the codex ─ or, as we call it now, the book ─ that the material ⓔ<u>reached</u> its full potential. That was two thousand years ago, and it is still a dominant form of the written word. That paper, a much softer material than either stone or wood, won out as the guardian of the written word is a ⓕ<u>remarkably</u> materials story.
explanation: ⓒ 'Wood is suffered'는 '나무가 고통받다'라는 수동태가 아니라 나무가 쪼개짐으로 인해 어려움을 겪는다는 능동의 의미가 적절하므로 'Wood suffers'로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓓ 'The invention of paper... solving these problems' 문장에서 'solving'은 분사구문으로 쓰였으나 문장의 본동사가 없으므로 과거 시제 동사인 'solved'로 고쳐야 합니다. ⓕ 'remarkably materials story'에서 명사구 'materials story'를 수식하는 것은 형용사가 적절하므로 부사인 'remarkably'를 형용사 'remarkable'로 고쳐야 합니다.

question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis. question: 12. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B)의 주어진 단어를 흐름과 어법에 맞게 알맞은 순서로 배열하시오. (필요시 어형변화 및 단어 추가 가능)
passage: The big problem with money created by the government is that those who run the government always face the temptation to create more money and spend it. Whether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, leading to inflation and the many economic and social problems that follow from inflation. For this reason, many countries have preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that is inherently limited in supply, as money. It is a way of (A)[expand / governments / the power / deprive] the money supply to inflationary levels. Gold has long been considered ideal for this purpose, since the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased rapidly. When paper money is convertible into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money is said to be "backed up" by gold. This expression is misleading only if we imagine that the value of the gold is somehow transferred to the paper money, when in fact the real point is that the gold simply limits the amount of (B)[that / issue / paper money / can].

answer: (A) depriving governments of the power to expand(B) paper money that can be issued

question: 13. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: A reason for a conclusion is very unlikely to consist in a single claim. question: 13. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중에서 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은?
passage: Conditioned Place Preference is a way of finding out what animals want. Researchers train them to associate one place with an experience such as food or a loud noise and another place with something completely different, usually where nothing happens. The two places are made obviously different to make it as easy as possible for the animal to associate each place with what happened to it there. The animal's preference for being in one place or another is measured both before and after its experiences in the two places. If there is a shift in where the animal chooses to spend its time for the reward, this suggests that ⓐ<u>it</u> liked the experience and is trying to repeat ⓑ<u>it</u>. Conversely, if ⓒ<u>it</u> now avoids the place the stimulus appeared and starts to prefer the place ⓓ<u>it</u> did not experience it, then this suggests that ⓔ<u>it</u> found the stimulus unpleasant. For example, mice with cancer show a preference for the place where they have been given morphine, a drug used to relieve pain, rather than where they have received saline whereas healthy mice developed no such preference. This suggests that the mice with cancer wanted the morphine.

question: 18. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 every translation is a crowd translation이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: All translators feel some pressure from the community of readers for whom they are doing their work. And all translators arrive at their interpretations in dialogue with other people. The English poet Alexander Pope had pretty good Greek, but when he set about translating Homer's lliad in the early 18th century he was not on his own. He had Greek commentaries to refer to, and translations that had already been done in English, Latin, and French - and of course he had dictionaries. Translators always draw on more than one source text. Even when the scene of translation consists of just one person with a pen, paper, and the book that is being translated, or even when it is just one person translating orally for another, that person's linguistic knowledge arises from lots of other texts and other conversations. And then his or her idea of the translation's purpose will be influenced by the expectations of the person or people it is for. In both these sense <u>every translation is a crowd translation</u>.
options: ① Translation can only be completed when many people work together at the same time.

③ Translation depends entirely on the translator's own ability and should exclude outside influence.

⑤ Translation is an independent act achieved solely through the translator's language skills and creativity.

passage: Some people argue that there is a single, logically consistent concept known as reading that can be neatly set apart from everything else people do with books. Is reading really that simple? The more one tries to figure out where the border lies between reading and not-reading, the more edge cases will be found to stretch the term's flexible boundaries. Thus, it is worth attempting to collect together these exceptional forms of reading into a single forum, one highlighting the challenges faced by anyone wishing to establish the boundaries where reading begins and ends. The attempt moves toward an understanding of reading as a spectrum that is expansive enough to accommodate the distinct reading activities.

question: 20. Based on Weber's law, in which situation is the JND(Just-noticeable difference) greater?
passage: Weber's law concerns the perception of difference between two stimuli. It suggests that we might not be able to detect a 1-mm difference when we are looking at lines 466mm and 467mm in length, but we may be able to detect a 1-mm difference when we are comparing a line 2mm long with one 3mm long. Another example of this principle is that we can detect 1 candle when it is lit in an otherwise dark room. But when 1 candle is lit in a room in which 100 candles are already burning, we may not notice the light from this candle. Therefore, the Just-noticeable difference (JND) varies as a function of the strength of the signals. For example, the JND is greater for very loud noises than it is for much more quiet sounds. When a sound is very weak, we can tell that another sound is louder, even if it is barely louder. When a sound is very loud, to tell that another sound is even louder, it has to be much louder. Thus, Weber's law means that it is harder to distinguish between two samples when those samples are larger or stronger levels of the stimuli.
explanation: 베버의 밡칙(Weber's law)에 따뤘면, 자극의 강도가 강할수록 차이를 눐치채기 위해 필요한 최소한의 차이(JND)는 더 커집니다. 설탕 1스푼이 들어간 커피(Situation A)보다 20스푼이 들어간 커피(Situation B)가 자극의 강도가 훨씬 강하므로, JND가 더 큰 사황은 Situation B입니다.

passage: According to Hobbes, man is not a being who can act morally in spite of his instinct to protect his existence in the state of nature. Hobbes thus describes the state of nature as a circumstance ⓑ<u>where</u> man's life is "solitary, poor, nasty, brutish and short". It means ⓒ<u>when</u> people live without a general power to control them all, they are indeed in a state of war. In other words, Hobbes, who accepted that human beings are not social and political beings in the state of nature, believes that without the power human beings in the state of nature ⓓ<u>is</u> "antisocial and rational based on their selfishness". Moreover, since society is not a natural phenomenon and there is no natural force bringing people together, ⓔ<u>what</u> will bring them together as a society is not mutual affection according to Hobbes. It is, rather, mutual fear of men's present and future that assembles them, since the cause of fear is a common drive among people in the state of nature.

② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 'human beings in the state of nature'로, 핵심 주어는 복수 명사인 'human beings'입니다. 따라서 단수 동사인 'is'가 아닌 복수 동사 'are'를 사용해야 어법상 적절합니다.

question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In each round of genome copying in our body, there is still about a 70 percent chance that at least one pair of chromosomes will have an error. With each round of genome copying, errors accumulate. This is similar to alterations in medieval books. Each time a copy was made by hand, some changes were introduced accidentally; as changes stacked up, the copies may have acquired meanings at variance with the original. Similarly, genomes that have undergone more copying processes will have gathered more mistakes. To make things worse, mutations may damage genes responsible for error checking and repair of genomes, further accelerating the introduction of mutations. Most genome mutations do not have any noticeable effects. It is just like changing the i for a y in "kingdom" would not distort the word's readability. But sometimes a mutation to a human gene results in, for example, an eye whose iris is of two different colors. Similarly, almost everyone has birthmarks, which are due to mutations that occurred as our body's cells multiplied to form skin. If mutations are changes to the genome of one particular cell, how can a patch of cells in an iris or a whole patch of skin, consisting of many individual cells, be affected simultaneously? The answer lies in the cell lineage, the developmental history of a tissue from particular cells through to their fully differentiated state. If the mutation occurred early on in the lineage of the developing iris, then all cells in that patch have inherited that change.
summary_sentence: Errors in genome copying (A)__________ over time, usually causing little harm, but some mutations can lead to visible traits such as eye color changes or birthmarks, which spread through (B)_______________ when early mutations are passed down to groups of cells.
options: ① build up   genetic inheritance
② vanish   cultural practices
③ gather   environmental adaptation
④ decline   social learning
⑤ disappear   repair mechanisms
explanation: 글의 전반부에서 게놈 복제 시 오류가 '누적(accumulate, build up)'된다고 설명하고 있으며, 후반부에서는 이러한 변화가 세포 계보를 통해 '유전적 상속(genetic inheritance)'되어 특정 부위의 세포 전체에 영향을 미친다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '쌓이다(build up)', (B)에는 '유전적 상속(genetic inheritance)'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 쌓이다 - 유전적 상속
② 사라지다 - 문화적 관습
③ 모이다 - 환경적 적응
④ 감소하다 - 사회적 학습
⑤ 사라지다 - 복구 기제

question: 8. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 (A)an overdose of empathy often turns medicine into poison이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Although empathy is widely praised by scholars and public figures, not everyone is an empathy booster. Critics of empathy argue that empathy will not save us from interpersonal and intergroup conflict. In fact, they argue, empathy makes such conflicts worse. These critics maintain that empathy can be exhausting and lead to burnout or insensitivity to suffering. They argue that we tend to empathize strongly with our in-group and resist empathizing with out-groups, and even enjoy the suffering of out-groups in competitive or threatening contexts. Thus, (A)<u>an overdose of empathy often turns medicine into poison</u> in cases of conflict. Empathy, they argue, can further encourage conflict and force us into an us vs. them mentality. Finally, even when we try to empathize with others who are dissimilar from us or in unfamiliar contexts, sometimes we are unable to accurately empathize with their experiences, causing further misunderstandings and frustration. Critics of empathy argue that we should give up on empathy and employ other tools in pursuit of social harmony, e.g., rational compassion or moral emotions like fear, anger, and shame.
options: ① problems can be resolved without any empathy
② being overly empathetic can aggravate the situation
③ indifference replaces empathy as a necessary medicine
④ the prescription for too much empathy guarantees peace
⑤ empathizing only with in-groups is often counterproductive
explanation: 이 글은 공감이 항상 긍정적인 결과를 가져오는 것은 아니라는 비판적 시각을 다루고 있습니다. 공감의 비판자들은 공감이 오히려 갈등을 심화시키고, 번아웃을 유발하며, 우리와 다른 집단에 대한 적대감을 키울 수 있다고 주장합니다. 따라서 밑줄 친 (A) '공감의 과잉이 종종 약을 독으로 바꾼다'는 표현은 일반적으로 좋은 것으로 여겨지는 공감이 지나칠 경우 오히려 상황을 악화시킬 수 있음을 의미하므로 정답은 ②번입니다.
options_translation: 공감 없이도 문제들이 해결될 수 있다
지나치게 공감하는 것이 상황을 악화시킬 수 있다
무관심이 필요한 약으로서 공감을 대체한다
너무 많은 공감에 대한 처방이 평화를 보장한다
내집단하고만 공감하는 것은 종종 역효과를 낸다

question: 9. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Paradoxically, it's uncertainty that makes us feel most alive. Think of events that shake you out of your everyday routine: maybe attending a family wedding, making a big presentation, or going somewhere you've never been. It's on those occasions that time seems to slow down a little, and you feel more fully engaged. The same holds true if the experience is risky, like mountain climbing or parasailing. Your senses are sharper. You notice more. Thanks to the release of a feelgood chemical in the brain called dopamine, you get a greater rush of pleasure from chance encounters with people than planned meetings. Good news, financial rewards, and gifts are more enjoyable if they are surprises. It's why the most popular television shows and movies are the ones with unexpected plot twists and astonishing endings.
options: ① The positive Aspect of Extreme Sports
② Scheduled Events Always Bring Us Relief
③ The Importance of Pulling You Away From Your Daily Routine
④ Ironic Happiness: Comes From Accidental and Heart-racing Events.
⑤ Most of The Movies and Dramas Usually Have Twisted Storylines
explanation: 이 글은 불확실성과 예상치 못한 사건들이 우리를 더 살아있게 느끼게 하고 도파민 분비를 통해 더 큰 즐거움을 준다고 설명합니다. 일상적인 루틴에서 벗어난 사건, 위험한 경험, 깜짝 선물, 반전 있는 영화 등이 더 즐거운 이유를 제시하고 있으므로, 제목으로는 우연하고 가슴 뛰는 사건에서 오는 행복을 언급한 ④번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 익스트림 스포츠의 긍정적인 측면
예정된 사건들은 항상 우리에게 안도감을 준다

대부분의 영화와 드라마는 대개 반전 있는 줄거리를 가지고 있다

question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We're naturally wired to organize the world into a hierarchy. We do this to help make sense of the world, maintain our beliefs, and generally feel better. But when someone infringes on our place in the world and our understanding of how it works, _______________________________________. When someone cuts you off on the highway and road rage kicks in, that's your unconscious mind saying, "Who are you to cut me off?" You're reacting to a threat to your inherent sense of hierarchy. On the road we are all equals. We're all supposed to play by the same rules. Cutting someone off violates those rules and implies higher status. Or consider when you get frustrated with your kids and end an argument with "Because I said so." (Or the office equivalent: "Because I'm the boss.") In these moments you've stopped thinking and regressed to your biological tendencies of reaffirming the hierarchy.
options: ① We respond instinctively to threats to our status
② We respond instinctively to maintain fairness and equality.
③ We consciously evaluate status differences before reacting.
④ We react calmly to status threats in order to avoid conflict.
⑤ We tend to ignore status violations to preserve social harmony.
explanation: 지문은 인간이 세상을 계층 구조로 조직하려는 본능이 있으며, 누군가 우리의 위치나 세상에 대한 이해를 침해할 때(예: 도로에서 끼어들기, 부모/상사의 권위 강조) 본능적으로 반응한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 빈칸 뒤의 도로 분노(road rage)나 '내가 보스니까'와 같은 사례는 자신의 지위나 계층적 감각에 대한 위협에 본능적으로 대응하는 것을 보여줍니다.
options_translation: ① 우리는 우리의 지위에 대한 위협에 본능적으로 반응한다
② 우리는 공정함과 평등을 유지하기 위해 본능적으로 반응한다.
③ 우리는 반응하기 전에 지위의 차이를 의식적으로 평가한다.
④ 우리는 갈등을 피하기 위해 지위 위협에 차분하게 반응한다.

question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Any new or threatening situation may require us to make decisions and this requires information. So important is communication during a disaster that normal social barriers are often lowered. We will talk to strangers in a way we would never consider normally. Even relatively low grade disruption of our life such as a fire drill or a very late train seems to give us the permission to break normal etiquette and talk to strangers. The more important an event to a particular public, the more detailed and urgent the requirement for news becomes. Without an authoritative source of facts, whether that is a newspaper or trusted broadcast station, rumours often run riot. Rumours start because people believe their group to be in danger and so, although the rumour is unproven, feel they should pass it on. For example, if a worker heard that their employer's business was doing badly and people were going to be made redundant, they would pass that information on to colleagues.
options: ① 소수에 의한 정보 독점은 합리적 의사 결정을 방해한다.
② 위기 상황에서는 확인되지 않은 정보라도 전달하려는 경향이 크다.
③ 위기에 처한 사람은 권위있는 전문가의 의견을 구하려고 한다.
④ 중요한 사건일수록 대중은 오히려 세부적 정보에 무관심하다.
⑤ 소문은 집단 내 유대감이 높을수록 더욱 빠르게 확산되는 경향이 있다.
explanation: 이 글은 재난이나 새로운 위협적인 상황에서 정보에 대한 욕구가 커지며, 권위 있는 정보원이 없을 경우 소문이 빠르게 퍼진다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 특히 사람들이 집단이 위험에 처해 있다고 믿을 때, 소문이 증명되지 않았더라도 이를 전달해야 한다고 느낀다는 내용이 핵심입니다.

question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Mental development consists of individuals increasingly mastering social codes and signals themselves, which they can master only in social situations with the support of more competent individuals, typically adults. In this sense, mental development consists of internalizing social patterns and gradually becoming a responsible actor among other responsible actors. In Denmark, the age of criminal responsibility is 15 years, which means that we then say that people have developed sufficient mental maturity to be accountable for their actions at this point. And at the age of 18 people are given the right to vote and are thereby formally included in the basic democratic process. I do not know whether these age boundaries are optimal, but it is clear that mental development takes place at different rates for different individuals, and depends especially on the social and family environment they have been given. Therefore, having formal limits for responsibility from a specific age that apply to everyone is a somewhat questionable practice. But the question, of course, is whether it can be done any differently.
options: ① 가정 내 상호작용이 개인의 정신적 성숙에 미치는 영향은 미미하다.
② 형사 책임 연령은 공식적 합의로 정해진 것이므로 국제 사회에서 통용되는 기준이다.
③ 청소년은 사회적 규범을 내면화 하기에 미성숙하므로 성인들의 판단에 전적으로 의존한다.
④ 덴마크는 책임 연령과 선거권 연령을 설정하는 데 있어 과학적 근거를 가장 우선시한다.
⑤ 정신 발달 속도에는 개인별로 차이가 있어 일률적인 책임 연령 설정은 논란의 여지가 있다.
explanation: 이 글은 정신적 발달이 개인마다 다른 속도로 진행되며 사회적, 가정적 환경에 의존한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 특정 연령을 기준으로 모든 사람에게 동일한 법적 책임을 묻는 공식적인 제한 설정이 의문스러운 관행일 수 있다는 것이 글의 요지입니다.

question: 3. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Merely convincing your children that worry is senseless and that they would be more content if they didn't worry isn't going to stop them from worrying. For some reason, young people seem to believe that worry is a fact of life over which they have little or no control. Consequently, they don't even try to stop. Therefore, you need to convince them that worry, like guilt and fear, is nothing more than an emotion, and like all emotions, is subject to the power of the will. Tell them that they can eliminate worry from their lives by simply refusing to attend to it. Explain to them that if they refuse to act worried regardless of how they feel, they will eventually stop feeling worried and will begin to experience the contentment that accompanies a worry-free life.
options: ① 아이가 죄책감과 책임감을 구분하도록 가르쳐야 한다.

④ 아이에게 걱정은 감정일 뿐이며 의지로 통제할 수 있다는 것을 알려줘야 한다.
⑤ 걱정을 멈추려면 부모가 지속적으로 아이에게 걱정하지 말라고 설득해야 한다.
explanation: 아이들에게 걱정은 통제할 수 없는 삶의 사실이 아니라, 죄책감이나 공포와 같은 감정일 뿐이며 의지의 힘으로 조절할 수 있다는 사실을 설득하고 가르쳐야 한다는 것이 필자의 주장입니다.

question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If cooking is as central to human identity, biology, and culture as the biological anthropologist Richard Wrangham suggests, it stands to reason that the decline of cooking in our time would have serious consequences for modern life, and so it has. Are they all bad? Not at all. The outsourcing of much of the work of cooking to corporations has relieved women of what has traditionally been their exclusive responsibility for feeding the family, making it easier for them to work outside the home and have careers. It has headed off many of the domestic conflicts that such a large shift in gender roles and family dynamics was bound to spark. It has relieved other pressures in the household, including longer workdays and overscheduled children, and saved us time that we can now invest in other pursuits. It has also allowed us to diversify our diets substantially, making it possible even for people with no cooking skills and little money to enjoy a whole different cuisine. All that's required is a microwave.

question: 5. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In today's information age, in many companies and on many teams, the objective is no longer error prevention and replicability. On the contrary, it's creativity, speed, and keenness. In the industrial era, the goal was to minimize variation. But in creative companies today, maximizing variation is more essential. In these situations, the biggest risk isn't making a mistake or losing consistency; it's failing to attract top talent, to invent new products, or to change direction quickly when the environment shifts. Consistency and repeatability are more likely to suppress fresh thinking than to bring your company profit. A lot of little mistakes, while sometimes painful, help the organization learn quickly and are a critical part of the innovation cycle. In these situations, rules and process are no longer the best answer. A symphony isn't what you're going for. Leave the conductor and the sheet music behind. Build a jazz band instead.
options: ① Efficiency First: Minimizing Variation to Maximize Profit
② Mastering Repetition: The Formula for Lasting Innovation
③ Flawless Implementation: Building Teams Without Mistakes
④ The Industrial Mindset Reborn: Restoring Stability Through Control
⑤ Embracing Variability: Redefining Innovation in the Information Age
explanation: 정보 시대의 창의적 기업에서는 과거 산업 시대의 목표였던 오류 방지나 일관성(변화 최소화)보다 변화를 최대화하고 창의성과 속도를 중시해야 한다고 강조하고 있습니다. 작은 실수들을 통해 배우고 변화에 빠르게 적응하는 것이 중요하며, 지휘자와 악보가 있는 교향악단보다는 즉흥적이고 유연한 재즈 밴드 같은 조직을 지향해야 한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 '가변성을 수용하기: 정보 시대 혁신의 재정의'가 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
