question: 6. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Over the last few centuries, humanity's collective prosperity has skyrocketed, as technological progress has made us far wealthier than ever before. To share out those riches, almost all societies have settled upon the market mechanism, rewarding people in various ways for the work that they do and the things that they own. But rising inequality, itself often driven by technology, has started to put that mechanism under strain. Today, markets already provide immense rewards to some people but leave many others with very little. And now, technological unemployment threatens to become a more radical version of the same story, taking place in the particular market we rely upon the most: the labor market. As that market begins to break down, more and more people will be in danger of not receiving a share of society's prosperity at all.
options: ① Are the Principles of the Market System Truly Adverse to the Equitable Redistribution of Wealth?
② The Paradox of the Intense Competition in the Free Market: Working Hard, Getting Nothing at All
③ The Dark Side of Technological Advance: How It Pushes the Market System to Face Rising Inequality and Labor Crisis
④ Fundamental Requisites of Labor Market Reforms to Address Unequal Sharing of Humanity's Collective Prosperity
⑤ Why Fairness of Market System Is Challenged by the Gap between Technological Progress and Social Recognition on It
explanation: 기술 발전이 인류의 번영을 가져왔지만, 동시에 불평등을 심화시키고 시장 메커니즘(분배 방식)에 부담을 주고 있다는 내용입니다. 특히 노동 시장에서 기술적 실업이 발생하면서 사람들이 사회적 번영의 몫을 분배받지 못할 위험에 처해 있음을 지적하고 있습니다. 따라서 '기술 발전의 어두운 면: 그것이 어떻게 시장 시스템이 심화되는 불평등과 노동 위기에 직면하게 만드는가'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 시장 시스템의 원칙이 진정으로 부의 공평한 재분배에 적대적인가?
② 자유 시장에서의 치열한 경쟁의 역설: 열심히 일하지만 아무것도 얻지 못함
③ 기술 발전의 어두운 면: 그것이 어떻게 시장 시스템이 심화되는 불평등과 노동 위기에 직면하게 만드는가
④ 인류 공동 번영의 불평등한 공유를 해결하기 위한 노동 시장 개혁의 근본적 필수 조건들
⑤ 왜 시장 시스템의 공정성이 기술 발전과 그에 대한 사회적 인식 사이의 격차에 의해 도전받는가

question: 7. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 34번]
passage: It's often said that those who can't do, teach. It would be more accurate to say that those who can do, can't teach the basics. A great deal of expert knowledge is not explicit. The further you progress toward mastery, the less conscious awareness you often have of the fundamentals. Experiments show that skilled golfers and wine aficionados have a hard time describing their putting and tasting techniques - even asking them to explain their approaches is enough to interfere with their performance, so they often stay on autopilot. When I first saw an elite diver do four and a half somersaults, I asked how he managed to spin so fast. His answer: "Just go up in a ball." Experts often have an intuitive understanding of a route, but they struggle to clearly express all the steps to take. <u>Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage</u>.
options: ① Experts often give messy explanations made up of quite irrelevant or ambiguous bits
② Experts have little difficulty improvising coherent and convincing solutions to complex problems
③ Experts get used to applying technical knowledge by using sophisticated terms excessively
④ Experts make a clear distinction between difficult tasks and simple procedures by thoroughly applying solid basics
⑤ Experts tend to be exclusive about their knowledge, which lead them to deliberately provide inaccurate information
explanation: 이 글은 전문가들이 숙련도에 도달할수록 기초적인 원리에 대한 의식적인 인식이 낮아져서 이를 타인에게 설명하는 데 어려움을 겪는다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 전문가들은 직관적으로는 이해하고 있지만, 이를 언어로 설명하려 할 때 오히려 수행에 방해를 받거나 "공처럼 몸을 말아라"와 같이 아주 단순하거나 모호한 답변을 내놓게 됩니다. 따라서 밑줄 친 부분은 전문가들이 지식을 쏟아낼 때(brain dump) 그 설명이 상당히 관련 없거나 모호한 정보들로 구성되어 엉망인 경우가 많다는 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 전문가들은 흔히 꽤 무관하거나 모호한 조각들로 이루어진 엉망인 설명을 한다.
② 전문가들은 복잡한 문제에 대해 일관성 있고 설득력 있는 해결책을 즉석에서 만드는 데 어려움이 거의 없다.
③ 전문가들은 세련된 용어를 과도하게 사용하여 전문 지식을 적용하는 데 익숙해진다.
④ 전문가들은 탄탄한 기초를 철저히 적용함으로써 어려운 과업과 단순한 절차를 명확히 구분한다.
⑤ 전문가들은 자신의 지식에 대해 독점적인 경향이 있으며, 이는 그들이 의도적으로 부정확한 정보를 제공하도록 이끈다.

question: 8. What does the underlined expression 'this misconception' refer to in the passage? [23년 9월 36번]
passage: If you drive down a busy street, you will find many competing businesses, often right next to one another. For example, in most places a consumer in search of a quick meal has many choices, and more fast-food restaurants appear all the time. These competing firms advertise heavily. The temptation is to see advertising as driving up the price of a product without any benefit to the consumer. However, <u>this misconception</u> doesn't account for why firms advertise. In markets where competitors sell slightly differentiated products, advertising enables firms to inform their customers about new products and services. Yes, costs rise, but consumers also gain information to help make purchasing decisions. Consumers also benefit from added variety, and we all get a product that's pretty close to our vision of a perfect good - and no other market structure delivers that outcome.
options: ① The view that advertising functions solely as a cost burden, raising product prices without providing any compensating benefit to consumers.
② The assumption that advertising should be dismissed as irrelevant since consumers already have sufficient knowledge of market options.
③ The belief that advertising is justified because it conveys information that allows consumers to compare slightly differentiated products more effectively.
④ The perspective that advertising is valuable because it expands consumer choice and moves markets closer to individual preferences for an ideal good.
⑤ The claim that advertising primarily operates as a signaling device in markets of nearly identical goods, ensuring consumers recognize product similarity.
explanation: 지문에서 'this misconception'이 가리키는 것은 바로 앞 문장의 내용입니다. 앞 문장에서는 광고를 '소비자에게 아무런 혜택을 주지 않으면서 제품의 가격을 올리기만 하는 것'으로 보는 유혹이 있다고 언급했습니다. 따라서 이 오해는 광고가 보상적인 혜택 없이 비용 부담으로만 작용하여 가격을 인상시킨다는 견해를 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 광고가 소비자에게 어떠한 보상적 혜택도 제공하지 않으면서 제품 가격을 높이는 비용 부담으로만 기능한다는 견해.
② 소비자가 이미 시장 선택지에 대해 충분한 지식을 가지고 있으므로 광고는 무관한 것으로 치부되어야 한다는 가정.
③ 광고가 소비자로 하여금 약간 차별화된 제품들을 더 효과적으로 비교할 수 있게 해주는 정보를 전달하기 때문에 정당화된다는 믿음.
④ 광고가 소비자 선택을 확대하고 시장을 이상적인 상품에 대한 개인적 선호에 더 가깝게 이동시키기 때문에 가치 있다는 관점.
⑤ 광고가 거의 동일한 상품의 시장에서 주로 신호 장치로 작동하여 소비자가 제품의 유사성을 인식하도록 보장한다는 주장.

question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [24년 9월 39번]
passage: Sleep is clearly about more than just resting. One curious fact is that animals which are hibernating also ⓐ<u>have</u> periods of sleep. It comes as a surprise to most of us, but hibernation and sleep are not the same thing at all, at least not from a neurological and metabolic perspective. Hibernating is more like ⓑ<u>being</u> anesthetized: the subject is unconscious but not actually asleep. So a hibernating animal is required ⓒ<u>to get</u> a few hours of conventional sleep each day within the larger unconsciousness. A further surprise to most of us is ⓓ<u>what</u> bears, the most famous of wintry sleepers, don't actually hibernate. Real hibernation involve profound unconsciousness and a dramatic fall in body temperature - often to around 32 degrees Fahrenheit. By this definition, bears don't hibernate, because their body temperature stays near normal and they are easily awakened. Their winter sleeps are more ⓔ<u>accurately</u> called a state of torpor.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓓ가 포함된 문장에서 'A further surprise to most of us is' 뒤에 나오는 절은 보어 역할을 하는 명사절입니다. 뒤따르는 문장 'bears ... don't actually hibernate'는 주어(bears)와 동사(don't hibernate)를 모두 갖춘 완전한 문장이므로, 관계대명사 what이 아니라 접속사 that이 쓰여야 적절합니다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [23년 9월 32번]
passage: A typical soap opera creates an abstract world, ⓐ<u>in which</u> a highly complex web of relationships connects fictional characters that exist first only in the minds of the program's creators and are then recreated in the minds of the viewer. If you were to think about how much human psychology, law, and even everyday physics the viewer must know in order to follow and speculate about the plot, you would discover it is considerable - at least as much as the knowledge needed to follow and speculate about a piece of modern mathematics, and in most cases, ⓑ<u>even</u> more. Yet viewers follow soap operas with ⓒ<u>ease</u>. How are they able to cope with such abstraction? Because, of course, the abstraction is built on an ⓓ<u>extreme</u> familiar framework. The characters in a soap opera and the relationships between them ⓔ<u>are</u> very much like the real people and relationships we experience every day. The abstraction of a soap opera is only a step removed from the real world. The mental "training" necessary to follow a soap opera is provided by our everyday lives.
explanation: ④번의 extreme은 들에 오는 형옕사 familiar를 수식해야 하므로 부사인 extremely로 바꿔야 합니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [24년 9월 23번]
passage: People seem to recognize that the arts are cultural activities ⓐ<u>which</u> draw on (or react against) certain cultural traditions, certain shared understanding, and certain values and ideas that are characteristic of the time and place where the art is created. In the case of science, however, opinions differ. Some scientists, like the great biologist J. B. S. Haldane, see science in a similar light - as a historical activity that occurs in a particular time and place, and that ⓑ<u>needs</u> to be understood within that context. Others, however, see science as a purely "objective" pursuit, uninfluenced by the cultural viewpoint and values of those who create ⓒ<u>it</u>. In describing this view of science, philosopher Hugh Lacey speaks of the belief that there is an underlying order of the world that is simply there ⓓ<u>to discover</u> - the world of pure "fact" stripped of any link with value. The aim of science according to this view is ⓔ<u>representing</u> this world of pure "fact", independently of any relationship it might bear contingently to human practices and experiences.
explanation: ④번의 to discover는 문맥상 '발견되기 위해 그곳에 있는 세상'을 의미하며, 세상의 질서가 발견되는 수동적 관계이므로 to be discovered로 쓰이거나, 혹은 discover의 목적어가 암시된 상태에서 유취해야 하는데, 이 문유적 표현에서 세상의 질서가 발견되기림 기다리고 있다는 의미로서 to be discovered가 적절합니다. 또한 5번의 represents는 to represent로 바꿔 쓸 수 있으며 보어주는 것이라눠 의미로 큰 문제가 없지만, 원문은 to represent이며 문법적으로는 ④번이 명확히 수동의 의미를 갖지 못하여 툠린 것으로 간주됩니다.

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [23년 9월 24번]
passage: As you may already know, what and how you buy can be ⓐ<u>political</u>. To whom do you want to give your money? Which companies and corporations do you value and respect? Be mindful about every purchase by carefully researching the corporations that are taking our money to decide if they ⓑ<u>deserve</u> our support. Do they have a record of polluting the environment, or do they have fair-trade practices and an end-of-life plan for the products they make? Are they committed to bringing about good in the world? For instance, my family has found a company producing recycled, plastic-packaging-free toilet paper with a social conscience. They contribute 50 percent of their profits to the construction of toilets around the world, and we're genuinely happy to spend our money on this special toilet paper each month. Remember that the corporate world is built on consumers, so as a consumer you have the power to vote with your wallet and encourage companies to ⓒ<u>avoid</u> healthier and more sustainable practices with every purchase you choose to make. But before you even decide which companies win your ⓓ<u>approval</u>, it is wise tó ask yourself whether you truly need to buy something new at all. A great motto is "First buy at home." There's no better place to shop than your own cupboards and closets. Shop for your next meal in your very own fridge and pantry - it saves money and prevents food waste. Rather than heading out to the mall to buy another outfit, see what you can create from your own closet and drawers. You just may surprise yourself, and at the same time reduce unnecessary production and waste. Whether you choose to favor ⓔ<u>ethical</u> companies or reduce consumption altogether, every decision you make is a powerful vote for more sustainable world.
explanation: ③번의 avoid(피하다)는 문맥상 소비자가 지갑으로 투표하여 기업이 더 건강하고 지석 가능한 관행을 '받아들이도록' 장려한다는 내용이 어울리므로 embrace 또는 adopt 등의 단어가 적절합니다.

question: 13. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In 2006, researchers conducted a study on the motivations for helping after the September 11th terrorist attacks against the United States. In the study, they found that individuals who gave money, blood, goods, or other forms of assistance because of other-focused motives (giving to reduce another's discomfort) were almost four times more likely to still be giving support one year later than those whose original motivation was to reduce personal distress. This effect can ________________________________. The events of September 11th emotionally affected people throughout the United States. Those who gave to reduce their own distress reduced their emotional arousal with their initial gift, discharging that emotional distress. However, those who gave to reduce others' distress did not stop empathizing with victims who continued to struggle long after the attacks.
options: ① be explained by differences in regulation of emotional arousal
② be linked to the rapid emotional recovery of most victims
③ highlight that personal distress guarantees long-term support
④ show that military attack had a stronger impact than empathy
⑤ prove that giving material aid is more effective than emotional support
explanation: 이 글은 9/11 테러 이후 도움을 주는 동기에 따른 지속성을 분석하고 있습니다. 자신의 괴로움을 줄이기 위해 도움을 준 사람들은 초기 지원으로 감정적 해소를 느끼며 도움을 중단했지만, 타인 중심의 동기(타인의 고통을 줄이기 위해)로 도움을 준 사람들은 계속해서 피해자들과 공감하며 1년 후에도 지원을 이어갈 가능성이 4배 더 높았습니다. 따라서 이러한 차이는 '감정적 각성의 조절 차이'로 설명될 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 감정적 각성의 조절 차이로 설명될 수 있다
② 대부분 피해자들의 빠른 감정적 회복과 연결될 수 있다
③ 개인적 고통이 장기적인 지원을 보장한다는 것을 강조한다
④ 군사적 공격이 공감보다 더 강한 영향을 미쳤음을 보여준다
⑤ 물질적 원조를 주는 것이 감정적 지원보다 더 효과적임을 증명한다

question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There is little doubt that we are driven by the sell-by date. Once an item is past that date it goes into the waste stream, further increasing its carbon footprint. Remember those items have already travelled hundreds of miles to reach the shelves and once they go into waste they start a new carbon mile journey But we all ________________________________; those brought up during the Second World War are often scornful of the terrible waste they believe such caution encourages. The manufacturer of the food has a view when making or growing something that by the time the product reaches the shelves it has already been travelling for so many days and possibly many miles. The manufacturer then decides that a product can reasonably be consumed within say 90 days and 90 days minus so many days for travelling gives the sell-by date. But whether it becomes toxic is something each individual can decide. It would seem to make sense not to buy large packs of perishable goods but non-perishable items may become cost-effective.
options: ① believe sell-by dates should be abolished
② strictly obey the sell-by dates without question
③ determine individually how to treat sell-by dates
④ deliberately alter the sell-by dates for convenience
⑤ treat sell-by dates as warnings of immediate danger
explanation: 판매 유효 기간(sell-by date)이 탄소 발자국을 늘리고 낭비를 초래할 수 있다는 점을 지적하며, 세대나 개인에 따라 이 날짜를 대하는 방식이 다름을 설명합니다. 특히 2차 세계대전 당시 사람들은 이러한 주의가 초래하는 낭비를 경멸한다는 예시를 통해, 빈칸에는 '판매 유효 기간을 어떻게 다룰지 개별적으로 결정한다'는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 판매 유효 기간이 폐지되어야 한다고 믿는다
② 질문 없이 엄격하게 판매 유효 기간을 준수한다

⑤ 판매 유효 기간을 즉각적인 위험에 대한 경고로 취급한다

question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: I suspect that fungi may be somewhat more forward-looking than their larger plant partners, because they seem to _________________________________. Among trees, different species often compete with one another for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Suppose the beeches native to Central Europe were able to prevail over most other species in their forests. At first, this might look like an advantage, since beeches could occupy more space and secure more resources. But what if a new pathogen appeared, infected the beeches, and wiped most of them out? In that case, wouldn't it be wiser if other species - such as oaks, maples, or firs - remained to keep growing and to provide the shade and protection needed for a new generation of beeches to sprout and thrive? This shows that diversity is what provides stability for ancient forests. Because fungi also rely on stable conditions, they quietly support other species underground, supplying them with nutrients and protection, and making sure that no single species comes to dominate.
options: ① focus on their own rapid growth and reproduction
② promote the long-term balance of the forest ecosystem
③ survive without depending on the stability of the forest
④ compete with trees for sunlight and nutrients underground
⑤ make forests more vulnerable to sudden environmental changes
explanation: 균류가 식물 파트너보다 더 앞을 내다본다는 추측의 근거는 그들이 숲의 안정성을 위해 다양성을 유지하려 하기 때문입니다. 특정 종이 지배하면 질병 등에 의해 숲 전체가 붕괴될 수 있으므로, 균류는 지하에서 영양분을 공급하고 보호하며 단일 종이 지배하지 못하게 함으로써 '산림 생태계의 장기적인 균형을 증진'합니다.
options_translation: ① 그들 자신의 빠른 성장과 번식에 집중한다
② 산림 생태계의 장기적인 균형을 증진한다
③ 숲의 안정성에 의존하지 않고 생존한다
④ 햇빛과 영양분을 두고 지하에서 나무와 경쟁한다
⑤ 숲을 갑작스러운 환경 변화에 더 취약하게 만든다

question: 16. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Rebels may think they're rebels, but clever marketers influence them just like the rest of us. Saying, "Everyone is doing it" may turn some people off from an idea. These people will look for alternatives, which (if cleverly planned) can be exactly what a marketer or persuader wants you to believe. If I want you to consider an idea, and know you strongly reject popular opinion in favor of maintaining your independence and uniqueness, I would present the majority option first, which you would not accept in favor of my actual preference. We are often tricked when we try to maintain a position of defiance. People use this reversal to make us independently choose an option which suits their purposes. Some brands have taken full effect of our defiance towards the mainstream and positioned themselves as rebels; which has created even stronger brand loyalty. In this way, the desire to be free from outside influence becomes another tool in the hands of advertisers. True autonomy in choice is far harder to achieve than most people imagine. Ultimately, marketing goes beyond the mere transaction of goods, actively _________________________.
options: ① encouraging conformity to mainstream consumption patterns
② cultivating and maintaining temporary consumer trends and fashions
③ exaggerating and distorting the perceived value of ordinary products
④ appealing to and exploiting consumers' impulsive shopping desire
⑤ constructing and redefining the very identities and cultural frameworks of consumers
explanation: 반항적인 소비자들은 자신이 주체적이라고 생각하지만, 마케터들은 그들의 반항심을 이용하여 마케터가 의도한 선택을 하도록 유도합니다. 즉, 주류에 반대하려는 욕구가 오히려 광고주들의 도구가 되며, 이는 마케팅이 단순히 상품 거래를 넘어 소비자의 정체성과 문화적 틀을 형성하고 재정의한다는 것을 의미합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '소비자들의 바로 그 정체성과 문화적 틀을 구축하고 재정의한다'는 내용이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 주류 소비 패턴에 대한 순응을 장려한다
② 일시적인 소비자 트렌드와 유행을 경작하고 유지한다
③ 일반적인 제품의 지각된 가치를 과장하고 왜곡한다
④ 소비자의 충동적인 쇼핑 욕구에 호소하고 이를 이용한다
⑤ 소비자들의 바로 그 정체성과 문화적 틀을 구축하고 재정의한다

question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Like an assembly line of a clothing factory, a computational algorithm that takes input data and generates some output from it doesn't really embody any notion of meaning. Certainly, such a computation does not generally have as its purpose its own survival and well-being. It does not, in general, assign value to the inputs. Regarding the cases of living organisms, interestingly, they _________________________________. Compare, for example, a computer algorithm with the waggle dance of the honeybee, by which means a foraging bee conveys to others in the hive information about the source of food (such as nectar) it has located. The "dance" - a series of stylized movements on the comb - shows the bees how far away the food is and in which direction. But this input does not simply program other bees to go out and look for it. Rather, they evaluate this information, comparing it with their own knowledge of the surroundings. Some bees might not bother to make the journey, considering it not worthwhile. The input, such as it is, is processed in the light of the organism's own internal states and history; there is nothing prescriptive about its effects.
options: ① figure out an identical meaning collectively by considering multiple components
② autonomously weigh whether to respond, taking into account various pieces of information
③ respond with a mechanistic reaction rather than attempting to grasp certain meanings from situation
④ identify inputs according to decisive criteria, thereby deriving corresponding meanings in a predefined manner
⑤ assess the given situations based on its environmental contexts, while disregarding internal value judgement
explanation: 컴퓨터 알고리즘은 입력 데이터에 대해 의미를 부여하거나 생존을 목적으로 하지 않지만, 생명체는 다릅니다. 꿀벌의 사례처럼 생명체는 외부 정보(입력)를 자신의 내부 상태, 주변 지식, 과거 경험 등과 대조하여 평가합니다. 즉, 단순히 프로그래밍된 대로 행동하는 것이 아니라 정보를 바탕으로 대응 여부를 자율적으로 판단합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '다양한 정보를 고려하여 대응할지 여부를 자율적으로 가늠한다'는 내용이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 여러 구성 요소를 고려하여 집단적으로 동일한 의미를 파악한다
② 다양한 정보를 고려하여 대응할지 여부를 자율적으로 가늠한다
③ 상황에서 어떤 의미를 파악하려고 시도하기보다는 기계적인 반응으로 응답한다
④ 결정적인 기준에 따라 입력을 식별함으로써 미리 정의된 방식으로 상응하는 의미를 도출한다
⑤ 내부의 가치 판단을 무시하면서 환경적 맥락에 기초하여 주어진 상황을 평가한다

question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.7점]
passage: As always happens with natural selection, bats and their prey have been engaged in a life-or-death sensory arms race for millions of years. ⓐIt's believed that hearing in moths arose specifically in response to the threat of being eaten by bats. (Not all insects can hear.) ⓑOver millions of years, moths have evolved the ability to detect sounds at ever higher frequencies, and, as they have, the frequencies of bats' vocalizations have risen, too. ⓒSome moth species have also evolved scales on their wings and a fur-like coat on their bodies; both act as "acoustic camouflage," by absorbing sound waves in the frequencies emitted by bats, thereby preventing those sound waves from bouncing back. ⓓMoths also serve an important role in the pollination of many plants, which makes them essential for supporting various ecosystems. ⓔThe B-2 bomber and other "stealth" aircraft have fuselages made of materials that do something similar with radar beams.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 박쥐와 나방 사이의 진화적 생존 경쟁(군비 확장 경쟁)에 관한 내용입니다. 나방은 박쥐의 소리를 듣거나 음파를 흡수하는 '음향 위장' 기술을 발달시켰고, 박쥐는 이에 맞춰 더 높은 주파수를 사용하게 되었다는 것이 주된 내용입니다. 하지만 ⓓ는 나방이 식물의 수분을 돕는 생태학적 역할에 대해 설명하고 있으므로, 박쥐와 나방의 생존 경쟁이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
passage: Minimal processing can be one of the best ways to keep original flavors and taste, without any need to add artificial flavoring or additives, or too much salt. This would also be the efficient way to keep most nutrients, especially the most sensitive ones such as many vitamins and anti-oxidants. ⓐMilling of cereals is one of the most harsh processes which dramatically affect nutrient content. ⓑWhile grains are naturally very rich in micronutrients, anti-oxidants and fiber (i.e. in wholemeal flour or flakes), milling usually removes the vast majority of minerals, vitamins and fibers to raise white flour. ⓒAs such, milling has been considered a key factor in facilitating the transportation and storage of food resources, ultimately contributing to the improvement of food security and nutritional status. ⓓSuch a spoilage of key nutrients and fiber is, thus, no longer acceptable in the context of a sustainable diet aiming at an optimal nutrient density and health protection. ⓔIn contrast, fermentation of various foodstuffs or germination of grains are traditional, locally accessible, low-energy and highly nutritious processes of sounded interest.
explanation: 이 글은 최소 가공(minimal processing)의 이점과 곡물 제분(milling)이 영양소를 파괴한다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 ③번 문장은 제분이 식품 자원의 수송과 저장을 용이하게 하여 식량 안보와 영양 상태 개선에 기여해 왔다는 내용으로, 가공의 부정적 영향(영양소 손실)이라는 전체 흐름과 상반되는 내용입니다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.9점]
passage: The earliest humans are thought to have evolved in tropical regions where survival was possible without clothing. It is likely that they had very dark skin because light skin would have given little protection against the burning rays of the sun. (A) There is an ongoing debate over whether humans gradually spread into other parts of the world or, instead, whether they developed independently in different regions. (B) Whichever the case, it is widely believed that in time they became capable of spreading out from Africa, eventually to most of the world. (C) This was probably made possible by changes in their physical characteristics. (D) For instance, early hominids were probably unable to walk fully upright, but once they developed that ability, they could travel more efficiently. (E) This dietary shift brought about changes not only in their bodies but also in their brains, since the brain requires a great deal of energy to grow. As their diet expanded, hominids were able to physically and intellectually expand their territory.
insertion_sentence: More important, perhaps, was their development of tool-making skills; they could hunt other animals with tools, and thereby consume more protein and fat than their low-energy vegetarian diet would have provided.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 도구 제작 기술의 발달과 그로 인한 식단 변화(더 많은 단백질과 지방 섭취)에 대해 언급하고 있습니다. (E) 바로 뒤 문장에서 'This dietary shift(이러한 식단의 변화)'라고 지칭하고 있으므로, 식단 변화에 대한 구체적 내용이 포함된 주어진 문장은 (E) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Much research has been carried out on the causes of engagement, an issue that is important from both a theoretical and practical standpoint: identifying the drivers of work engagement may enable us to manipulate or influence it.
ordered_passages: (A) To better understand this issue, we can classify the factors affecting engagement into two categories: situational and personal. Among the situational drivers, leadership, job resources, and feedback hold the greatest influence, with leadership largely governing the latter two.

(C) Indeed, leaders influence engagement by giving their employees honest and constructive feedback on their performance, and by providing them with the necessary resources that enable them to perform their job well. Importantly, while engagement enhances job performance, performance itself also strengthens engagement.

(B) In other words, when employees are able to do their jobs well - to the point that they match or exceed their own expectations and ambitions - they will engage more, be proud of their achievements, and find work more meaningful. This is especially evident when people are employed in jobs that align with their values.
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 업무 몰입(engagement)의 동인을 식별하는 것의 중요성을 언급합니다. (A)에서는 이 문제를 이해하기 위해 요인을 상황적 요인과 개인적 요인으로 분류하며 상황적 요인으로 리더십, 자원, 피드백을 제시합니다. (C)에서는 (A)의 마지막 부분에서 언급한 리더십이 어떻게 피드백과 자원을 통해 영향을 주는지 부연하며, 몰입과 성과의 상관관계를 설명합니다. (B)에서는 'In other words'를 통해 (C)의 마지막 내용(성과가 몰입을 강화함)을 풀어서 설명하며 결론을 맺습니다.

question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 38번]
passage: Behavioral contagion refers to the spread of ideas and behaviors in a manner similar to infectious diseases; for instance, individuals are more likely to engage in excessive drinking when surrounded by heavy drinkers, a pattern that mirrors the transmission of viruses through close interpersonal contact.
ordered_passages: (A) Together, these features underline the importance of carefully designed policies. Considering that visibility and social proximity can substantially reinforce the spread of positive behaviors, governments as well as researchers should implement actions to promote such dynamics. Yet again, the fact that harmful behaviors spread through the very same channels suggests that targeted regulations and interventions need to be pursued simultaneously.

(B) Solar panels that are readily observable from the street, for example, often encourage neighboring households to adopt similar installations, thereby amplifying sustainable practices. Another more insightful and quite interesting difference is that whereas viral contagion is almost invariably harmful, behavioral contagion can be either negative or positive, as illustrated by the examples like drinking and solar panel.

(C) Despite this similarity, there are crucial distinctions between behavioral and viral contagion, which carry significant theoretical and political implications. One key difference concerns the role of visibility. While visibility generally constrains the spread of infectious disease - as people tend to avoid others who are visibly ill - it naturally facilitates behavioral contagion, instead.
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 행동 전염(behavioral contagion)을 소개하며 그것이 바이러스의 전염과 유사하다는 점을 설명합니다. (C)에서 'Despite this similarity'를 통해 앞선 내용과 연결되며, 바이러스 전염과 행동 전염의 차이점인 '가시성(visibility)'을 설명합니다. (B)에서는 가시성의 예시로 태양광 패널을 언급하며 행동 전염은 긍정적일 수도 부정적일 수도 있다는 또 다른 차이점을 제시합니다. (A)에서 'Together, these features'를 통해 앞선 차이점들을 종합하며 정책적 함의를 도출하므로 정답은 (C)-(B)-(A)입니다.

question: 23. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 35번]
passage: The development of early democracy was hardly unique to Europe, since assemblies in Greece, tribal gatherings among the Germanic peoples, and councils in medieval city-states all resembled forms of shared decision-making found in other regions of the world. Yet Europe was different in crucial ways, especially when compared with other regions such as China and the Middle East.
ordered_passages: (A) The irony of early democracy in Europe is that it prospered precisely because European rulers for a very long time were remarkably weak. For more than a millennium after the fall of Rome, they lacked the capacity to measure what their people were producing or to levy substantial taxes based on it.

(B) The most striking evidence of this weakness is how little revenue they could collect, especially when compared with Chinese emperors and Muslim caliphs who extracted far greater shares of economic production during the same era, with the exception of a few European city-states.

(C) Unlike in those regions, early democracy in Europe survived and even thrived rather than being completely replaced by absolute rule. Europeans were also distinctive because they eventually managed to expand the practice of early democracy to societies covering large territories, and over time this tradition evolved step by step into modern democracy.
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 유럽의 초기 민주주의가 다른 지역들과 유사했으나 결정적인 차이가 있었다고 언급합니다. (C)에서 'Unlike in those regions'를 통해 중국과 중동 같은 지역들과 달리 유럽의 민주주의가 살아남아 발전했다는 점을 설명합니다. (A)에서 유럽 민주주의가 번영한 역설적인 이유로 통치자들의 '약함'을 언급하며, (B)에서 'this weakness'라는 지시어를 통해 통치자들이 세금을 걷는 능력이 부족했다는 구체적인 증거를 제시하며 중국/이슬람 통치자들과 비교합니다. 따라서 정답은 (C)-(A)-(B)입니다.

question: 24. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The concern about how we appear to others can be seen in children, though work by the psychologist Ervin Staub suggests that the effect may vary with age.
ordered_passages: (A) They were less likely to react to a third party who appeared to be in trouble when they were with their peers than when alone. The clear difference between the two groups attracted the interest of Staub and his colleagues. Therefore, Staub sought to clarify, through further research, the factors with which older children were preoccupied, and the underlying mechanisms leading to the foregoing outcomes.

(B) In a study where children heard another child in distress, young children (kindergarten through second grade) were more likely to help a child in distress when they were with another child than when they were alone. In the meantime, for older children such as sixth graders, interestingly, the effect reversed.

(C) Staub noted their behavior through the concepts of the 'bystander effect' and 'social anxiety.' In situations where peers were present, they either became more passive, expecting that others would help even if they themselves did not, or feared that their behavior would be seen as an exaggerated reaction, being judged negatively by their peers, which caused them to adopt a social mask of 'indifference.'
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 타인에게 어떻게 보이는지에 대한 관심이 아이들에게서 나타나며 연령에 따라 다르다는 점을 언급합니다. (B)에서 구체적인 연구 사례를 들어 어린아이들(유치원~2학년)은 혼자일 때보다 다른 아이와 함께 있을 때 더 잘 돕는 반면, 고학년(6학년)은 그 효과가 역전된다고 설명합니다. (A)에서 이 역전된 효과(혼자일 때보다 또래와 있을 때 덜 반응함)를 구체화하며 Staub이 그 이유를 규명하고자 했음을 밝힙니다. 마지막으로 (C)에서 '방관자 효과'와 '사회적 불안'이라는 개념을 통해 그들이 또래의 부정적 평가를 두려워하여 '무관심'의 가면을 쓰게 된다는 결론을 도출하므로 정답은 (B)-(A)-(C)입니다.

question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The brain is a high-energy consumer of glucose, which is its fuel. Although the brain accounts for merely 3 percent of a person's body weight, it consumes 20 percent of the available fuel. Your brain can't store fuel, however, so it has to "pay as it goes." Since your brain is incredibly adaptive, it economizes its fuel resources. Thus, during a period of high stress, it shifts away from the analysis of the nuances of a situation to a singular and fixed focus on the stressful situation at hand. You don't sit back and speculate about the meaning of life when you are stressed. Instead, you devote all your energy to trying to figure out what action to take. Sometimes, however, this shift from the higher-thinking parts of the brain to the automatic and reflexive parts of the brain can lead you to do something too quickly, without thinking.
summary_sentence: When you are stressed, your brain's remarkable adaptability enables temporary (A)___________ of higher cognition, reallocating limited energy toward (B)___________ immediate threats.
options: ① expansion / ignoring
② suspension / handling
③ suppression / abandoning
④ stimulation / mitigating
⑤ activation / facilitating
explanation: 지문에 따르면 뇌는 스트레스 상황에서 연료를 절약하기 위해 고차원적인 분석(higher cognition)에서 벗어나 당면한 스트레스 상황에 집중하게 됩니다. 이는 고차원 인지 능력이 일시적으로 '중단(suspension)' 또는 억제되는 것을 의미하며, 제한된 에너지를 즉각적인 위협을 '처리(handling)'하는 데 재배분하는 과정입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 suspension, (B)에는 handling이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 확장 / 무시하기
② 중단 / 처리하기
③ 억제 / 포기하기
④ 자극 / 완화하기
⑤ 활성화 / 용이하게 하기

question: 26. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The "jolt" of caffeine does wear' off. Caffeine is removed from your system by an enzyme within your liver, which gradually degrades it over time. Based in large part on genetics, some people have a more efficient version of the enzyme that degrades caffeine, allowing the liver to rapidly clear it from the bloodstream. These rare individuals can drink an espresso with dinner and fall fast asleep at midnight without a problem. Others, however, have a slower-acting version of the enzyme. It takes far longer for their system to eliminate the same amount of caffeine. As a result, they are very sensitive to caffeine's effects. One cup of tea or coffee in the morning will last much of the day, and should they have a second cup, even early in the afternoon, they will find it difficult to fall asleep in the evening. Aging also alters the speed of caffeine clearance: the older we are, the longer it takes our brain and body to remove caffeine, and thus the more sensitive we become in later life to caffeine's sleep-disrupting influence.
summary_sentence: Caffeine affects people (A)___________ because genetic variations in liver enzymes and the aging process determine how quickly it is metabolized, which in turn influences their (B)___________ to its impact on sleep.
options: ① differently / sensitivity
② identically / immunity
③ universally / stability
④ periodically / vulnerability
⑤ comparably / endurance
explanation: 글의 요지는 유전적 요인(간 효소의 효율성 차이)과 노화 과정에 따라 카페인이 분해되는 속도가 다르다는 것입니다. 따라서 카페인은 사람들에게 '다르게(differently)' 영향을 미치며, 이는 카페인이 수면에 미치는 영향에 대한 '민감도(sensitivity)'에 영향을 줍니다. 그러므로 (A) differently, (B) sensitivity가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 다르게 / 민감도
② 동일하게 / 면역력
③ 보편적으로 / 안정성
④ 주기적으로 / 취약성
⑤ 비교적 / 인내력

question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 this phenomenon에 대해 정확하게 이해하지 못한 사람은?
passage: We collect stamps, coins, vintage cars even when they serve no practical purpose. The post office doesn't accept the old stamps, the banks don't take old coins, and the vintage cars are no longer allowed on the road. These are all side issues; the attraction is that they are in short supply. In one study, students were asked to arrange ten posters in order of attractiveness - with the agreement that afterward they could keep one poster as a reward for their participation. Five minutes later, they were told that the poster with the third highest rating was no longer available. Then they were asked to judge all ten from scratch. The poster that was no longer available was suddenly classified as the most beautiful. In psychology, <u>this phenomenon</u> is called reactance: when we are deprived of an option, we suddenly deem it more attractive.
options: ① A: When our school banned smartphones during class, I suddenly wanted to use mine more than ever.
② B: The restaurant became incredibly appealing to me the moment I heard it was fully booked for months.
③ C: My desire to read that book intensified significantly after the library informed me it was permanently removed from their collection.
④ D: I found myself desperately wanting to attend the party once my parents explicitly didn't allow me to go.
⑤ E: The chess club seemed like an excellent choice because my successful older brother recommended it for developing strategic thinking.
explanation: 밑줄 친 'this phenomenon'은 '심리적 저항(reactance)'으로, 선택권이 박탈되거나 공급이 부족해질 때 그것을 더 매력적으로 느끼는 현상을 의미합니다. ⑤번은 형의 추천이라는 외부적 요인에 의해 매력을 느끼는 상황이므로, 박탈이나 희소성에 의한 매력 증대인 심리적 저항과는 거리가 멉니다.
options_translation: ① A: 우리 학교가 수업 시간에 스마트폰을 금지했을 때, 나는 갑자기 내 스마트폰을 그 어느 때보다 더 사용하고 싶어졌다.
② B: 그 식당이 몇 달 동안 예약이 꽉 찼다는 소식을 들은 순간 그곳은 나에게 믿을 수 없을 정도로 매력적으로 느껴졌다.
③ C: 도서관에서 그 책이 소장 목록에서 영구적으로 제거되었다는 통보를 받은 후 그 책을 읽고 싶은 욕구가 상당히 강해졌다.
④ D: 부모님이 명시적으로 파티에 가는 것을 허락하지 않으시자 나는 필사적으로 파티에 가고 싶어졌다.
⑤ E: 성공한 우리 형이 전략적 사고 발달을 위해 추천해 주었기 때문에 체스 클럽은 탁월한 선택처럼 보였다.

question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: If we've invested in something that hasn't repaid us - be it money in a failing venture, or time in an unhappy relationship - we find it very difficult to walk away. This is the sunk cost fallacy. Our instinct is to continue investing money or time as we hope that our investment will prove to be worthwhile in the end. Giving up would mean acknowledging that we've wasted something we can't get back, and that thought is so painful that we prefer to avoid it if we can. The problem, of course, is that if something really is a bad bet, then staying with it simply increases the amount we lose. For example, ___________________________________________________; rather than accept that we've lost a thousand dollars, we lay down another thousand and lose that too. In the end, by delaying the pain of admitting our problem, we only add to it. Sometimes we just have to cut our losses.
options: ① we keep buying more shares of a stock as its value declines, thinking that our initial investment makes it worth continuing
② we abandon unprofitable ventures early to minimize losses and redirect resources toward more promising opportunities
③ we diversify our investment portfolio to reduce risk exposure and avoid putting all resources into a single failing project
④ we seek professional financial advice before making any additional investments in under-performing assets
⑤ we set strict budget limits and stick to predetermined loss cutoff regardless of emotional attachment to investments
explanation: 이 글은 매몰 비용의 오류(sunk cost fallacy)에 대해 다루고 있습니다. 이미 투자한 돈이나 시간이 아까워 실패할 것이 뻔한 일에 계속 투자하는 상황을 예로 들어야 하므로, 주식 가치가 하락함에도 불구하고 초기 투자가 아까워 계속 주식을 더 사는 상황을 묘사한 ①번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 가치가 하락하고 있는 주식의 주식을 초기 투자가 계속할 가치가 있다고 생각하며 계속 더 매수한다
② 손실을 최소화하고 자원을 더 유망한 기회로 돌리기 위해 수익성이 없는 벤처를 조기에 포기한다
③ 리스크 노출을 줄이고 단일 실패 프로젝트에 모든 자원을 쏟아붓는 것을 피하기 위해 투자 포트폴리오를 다각화한다
④ 실적이 저조한 자산에 추가 투자를 하기 전에 전문적인 금융 조언을 구한다
⑤ 투자에 대한 감정적 애착에 상관없이 엄격한 예산 한도를 설정하고 사전에 결정된 손실 차단 지점을 고수한다

question: 15. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Coincidence that is statistically impossible seems to us like an irrational event, and some define it as a miracle. But, as Montaigne has said, "the origin of a miracle is in our ignorance, at the level of our knowledge of nature, and not in nature itself." Glorious miracles have been later on discovered to be obedience to the laws of nature or a technological development that was not widely known at the time. As the German poet, Goethe, phrased it: "Things that are mysterious are not yet miracles." The miracle assumes the intervention of a "higher power" in its occurrence that is beyond human capability to grasp. Yet there are methodical and simple ways to "cause a miracle" without divine revelation and inspiration. Instead of checking it out, investigating and finding the source of the event, we define it as a miracle. The miracle, then, is the excuse of those who are too lazy to think.
options: ① Great Thinkers' Views on Supernatural Phenomena
② The Mysterious Power of Miracles in Human History
③ How Science and Miracles Coexist in Modern Society
④ The Divine Nature of Miracles: Beyond Human Understanding
⑤ The Reality of Miracles: Illusions Created by Ignorance and Laziness
explanation: 이 글은 기적이라고 여겨지는 현상들이 사실은 자연 법칙에 대한 무지나 기술 발전에 대한 이해 부족에서 비롯된 것이며, 더 깊이 생각하고 조사하기를 게을리하는 사람들의 핑계일 뿐이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 '기적의 실체: 무지와 나태함이 만들어낸 환상'이라는 의미의 ⑤번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 초자연적 현상에 대한 위대한 사상가들의 견해
② 인류 역사에서 기적의 신비로운 힘
③ 현대 사회에서 과학과 기적이 공존하는 방식
④ 기적의 신성한 본질: 인간의 이해를 넘어서는 것
⑤ 기적의 실체: 무지와 나태함이 만들어낸 환상

question: 16. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Rebels may think they're rebels, but clever marketers influence them just like the rest of us. Saying, "Everyone is doing it" may turn some people off from an idea. These people will look for ⓐ<u>options</u>, which (if cleverly planned) can be exactly what a marketer or persuader wants you to believe. If I want you to consider an idea, and know you strongly reject popular opinion in favor of maintaining your independence and uniqueness, I would present the majority option first, which you would ⓑ<u>adopt</u> in favor of my actual preference. We are often tricked when we try to maintain a position of ⓒ<u>opposition</u>. People use this reversal to make us "independently" choose an option which ⓓ<u>matches</u> their purposes. Some brands have taken full ⓔ<u>advantage</u> of our defiance towards the mainstream and positioned themselves as rebels; which has created even stronger brand loyalty.
explanation: 이 글은 마케터들이 '반항아' 성향을 가진 사람들을 어떻게 심리적으로 조종하는지에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 반항적인 사람들은 다수의 의견을 거부하고 독립성을 유지하려 합니다. 따라서 마케터는 그들이 실제로 선택하게 만들고 싶은 옵션(자신의 진짜 선호)이 아니라, 대다수가 선택하는 옵션(the majority option)을 먼저 제시합니다. 그러면 반항적인 사람들은 독립성을 지키기 위해 그 다수의 옵션을 '채택(adopt)'하는 것이 아니라 '거부(reject)'하고, 마케터가 의도한 다른 대안을 선택하게 됩니다. 따라서 ⓑ의 adopt는 reject와 같은 단어로 바뀌어야 문맥상 적절합니다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [3.1점]
passage: As always happens with natural selection, bats and their prey have been engaged in a life-or-death sensory arms race for millions of years. It's believed that hearing in moths arose specifically in response to the threat of being eaten by bats. (Not all insects can hear.) Over millions of years, moths have evolved the ability to detect sounds at ever higher frequencies, and, as they have, the frequencies of bats' vocalizations have risen, too. Some moth species have also evolved scales on their wings and a fur-like coat on their bodies; both act as "acoustic camouflage," by absorbing sound waves in the frequencies emitted by bats, thereby preventing those sound waves from bouncing back. The B-2 bomber and other "stealth" aircraft have fuselages made of materials that do something similar with radar beams.
options: ① 박쥐와 먹이 동물들 사이의 감각적 군비경쟁은 자연 선택에 의해 수백만 년간 지속되어왔다.
② 곤충 중 일부만 청각 능력을 가지고 있지만, 나방의 청각은 박쥐의 위협에 대응하여 발달했다.
③ 나방이 고주파 탐지 능력을 향상시키자 박쥐의 발성 주파수도 함께 상승했다.
④ 모든 나방 종들이 날개의 비늘과 몸의 털을 통해 박쥐의 음파를 흡수하는 음향 위장 전략을 사용한다.
⑤ 스텔스 항공기 동체는 레이더 빔에 대해 나방의 음향 위장과 유사한 원리를 사용한다.
explanation: 지문의 하단부에서 'Some moth species have also evolved scales on their wings...'라고 언급되어 있습니다. 즉, 모든 나방 종이 아니라 '일부(Some)' 나방 종들이 날개의 비늘과 털을 이용한 음향 위장 전략을 진화시킨 것이므로, ④번의 '모든 나방 종들'이라는 설명은 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

question: 18. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.0점]
passage: It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. By "competence," I mean a cluster of qualities: smartness, the ability to get things done, wise decisions, etc. (A) We stand a better chance of doing well at our life tasks if we surround ourselves with people who know what they're doing and have a lot to teach us. (B) But the research evidence is paradoxical: In problem-solving groups, the participants who are considered the most competent and have the best ideas tend not to be the ones who are best liked. Why? (C) They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman - and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison. (D) If this were true, we might like people more if they reveal some evidence of fallibility. (E) For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her better if, every once in a while, they screwed up.
insertion_sentence: One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, those who are too competent make us uncomfortable.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: (B) 뒤의 질문인 "Why?"에 대한 직접적인 대답으로 주어진 문장이 가장 적절합니다. 유능한 사람이 왜 인기가 없는지에 대한 '한 가지 가능성(One possibility)'으로 너무 유능한 사람은 우리를 불편하게 만든다는 점을 제시하고, (C)에서 그 불편함의 구체적인 이유(다가가기 힘들고, 비교되어 우리가 초라해 보임)를 설명하는 구조가 자연스럽습니다.

question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
passage: In order to bring the ever-increasing costs of home care for elderly and needy persons under control, managers of home care providers have introduced management systems. ⓐThese systems specify tasks of home care workers and the time and budget available to perform these tasks. ⓑElectronic reporting systems require home care workers to report on their activities and the time spent, thus making the distribution of time and money visible and, in the perception of managers, controllable. ⓒStudies have shown that countries with universal healthcare systems tend to invest more in preventive care services, which can reduce long-term healthcare costs significantly. ⓓThe home care workers, on the other hand, may perceive their work not as a set of separate tasks to be performed as efficiently as possible, but as a service to be provided to a client with whom they may have developed a relationship. ⓔIf the management systems are too rigid, this may result in home care workers becoming overloaded and demotivated.
explanation: 이 글은 노인 재가 복지(home care) 비용 조절을 위해 도입된 관리 시스템과 그에 대한 관리자 및 노동자들의 서로 다른 인식을 다루고 있습니다. ⓐ, ⓑ는 시스템의 특징과 관리자의 관점을, ⓓ, ⓔ는 노동자들의 관점과 시스템의 부작용을 설명합니다. 반면 ⓒ는 보편적 의료 시스템을 가진 국가들이 예방 진료 서비스에 투자한다는 내용으로, 재가 복지 관리 시스템에 관한 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

question: 20. 다음 중 어법상 옳지 않은 문장은?
passage: When you drive down a busy street, you will find many competing businesses, often located right next to one another. For example, in most places a consumer in search of a quick meal has many choices, and more fast-food restaurants appear all the time. ⓐThese competing firms advertise heavily. ⓑThe temptation is to see advertising as driving up the price of a product without any benefit to the consumer. ⓒHowever, this misconception doesn't account for why firms advertise. ⓓIn markets where competitors sell slightly differentiated products, advertising enables firms to inform their customers about new products and services. ⓔYes, costs rise, but consumers also gain information helped them make purchasing decisions. Consumers also benefit from added variety, and we all get a product that's pretty close to our vision of a perfect good - and no other market structure delivers that outcome.
explanation: ⓔ에서 'helped'는 'information'을 수식하는 분사구의 역할을 해야 하는데, 정보가 소비자들을 돕는(능동) 관계이므로 현재분사인 'helping'으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다. 또는 'that helped them'과 같이 주격 관계대명사를 포함한 절로 써야 합니다.

question: 21. 다음 글을 읽고 아래 표의 빈칸에 들어갈 적절한 표현을 본문에서 그대로 찾아 쓰시오.
passage: Financial markets do more than take capital from the rich and lend it to everyone else. They enable each of us to smooth consumption over our lifetimes, which is a fancy way of saying that we don't have to spend income at the same time we earn it. Shakespeare may have admonished us to be neither borrowers nor lenders; the fact is that most of us will be both at some point. If we lived in an agrarian society, we would have to eat our crops reasonably soon after the harvest or find some way to store them, giving us only limited options. Financial markets are a more sophisticated way of managing the harvest. We can spend income now that we have not yet earned - as by borrowing for college or a home - or we can earn income now and spend it later, as by saving for retirement. The important point is that earning income has been divorced from spending it, allowing us much more flexibility in life.
subjective_conditions: 본문에서 그대로 찾아 쓸 것
vocabulary_box: Timing of earning and (A)__________ | Income is spent at the same time as we (B)__________ it. | Earning income has been (C)__________ from the act of using it.
Result | (D)__________ options are available. | There is much more flexibility in life.
explanation: 본문의 내용을 바탕으로 농경 사회와 금융 시장의 특징을 비교하는 표입니다. (A)와 (B)는 'we don't have to spend income at the same time we earn it'을 통해 소득 창출과 소비(spending) 시점이 농경 사회에서는 동일(earn)하다는 것을 알 수 있습니다. (C)는 'earning income has been divorced from spending it'에서 금융 시장을 통해 소득과 소비가 분리(divorced)되었음을 알 수 있고, (D)는 'giving us only limited options'를 통해 농경 사회의 제한된(Limited) 선택권을 설명할 수 있습니다.

question: 22. 다음 글을 읽고 아래 요약문의 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 적절한 단어를 지문에서 찾아 그대로 쓰시오.
passage: Buying a television is current consumption. It makes us happy today but does nothing to make us richer tomorrow. Yes, money spent on a television keeps workers employed at the television factory. But if the same money were invested, it would create jobs somewhere else, say for scientists in a laboratory or workers on a construction site, while also making us richer in the long run. Think about college as an example. Sending students to college creates jobs for professors. Using the same money to buy fancy sports cars for high school graduates would create jobs for auto workers. The crucial difference between these scenarios is that a college education makes a young person more productive for the rest of his or her life; a sports car does not. Thus, college tuition is an investment; buying a sports car is consumption.
summary_sentence: (A)____________ provides immediate satisfaction but offers no future benefit, whereas (B)____________ makes people more (C)____________ and creates long-term wealth.
subjective_conditions: 지문에서 찾아 그대로 쓸 것
explanation: 지문은 소비와 투자의 차이를 설명하고 있습니다. TV 구매나 스포츠카 구매와 같은 소비(Consumption)는 현재의 만족을 주지만 미래의 부를 만들지 못합니다. 반면, 대학 교육과 같은 투자(investment)는 사람을 더 생산적(productive)으로 만들어 장기적인 부를 창출합니다.

question: 1. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 they가 가리키는 대상이 다른 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The traditional bank manager in the 1950s was usually a respected pillar of the community, a cautious, careful sort of person who probably went to bed early and didn't drink too much. But from the 1970s a new kind of banker appeared - loud, flashy, and arrogant. These bankers loved taking big risks. ⓐ<u>They</u> wanted to get rich quick and blow their money on fast cars and expensive champagne. ⓑ<u>They</u> made their money through what's called 'speculation'. Normally, people buy things because ⓒ<u>they</u> want to use them, such as wheat to make bread and petrol to run the car. But when these bankers speculate, they buy things even when they have no interest in using them. ⓓ<u>They</u> might buy a load of wheat simply because they think that its price is going to rise when a drought is predicted in wheat - growing areas. If their guess is right, ⓔ<u>they</u> later sell the wheat for a profit.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 문맥상 1970년대 이후 등장한 새로운 유형의 은행가들(these bankers)을 가리키지만, ⓒ는 문장의 맥락상 일반적인 사람들(people)을 가리킵니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ

question: 2. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Paradoxically, it's uncertainty ⓐ<u>that</u> makes us feel most alive. Think of events that ⓑ<u>shake</u> you out of your everyday routine: maybe attending a family wedding, making a big presentation, or going somewhere you've never been. It's on those occasions that time ⓒ<u>is seemed</u> to slow down a little, and you feel more fully engaged. The same holds true if the experience is risky, like mountain climbing or parasailing. Your senses are sharper. You notice more. Thanks to the release of a feel-good chemical in the brain ⓓ<u>called</u> dopamine, you get a greater rush of pleasure from chance encounters with people than planned meetings. Food news, financial rewards, and gifts are more enjoyable if they are surprises. It's why the most popular television shows and movies are the ⓔ<u>ones</u> with unexpected plot twists and astonishing endings.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓒ 'seem'은 자동사로 수동태로 쓸 수 없습니다. 따라서 'is seemed'는 틀린 표현이며, 'seems'로 고쳐야 합니다. 'It is ~ that' 강조 구문 내에서 주어인 time에 맞춰 단수 동사 형태를 취해야 합니다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: According to Einstein' s theory, a large mass like the Sun 'bends' space-time. Newton's theory makes no such prediction. This bending of space-time leads to phenomena such as 'gravitational lensing' where the light of distant stars appears to be in different locations when they pass by a large mass like the Sun. We don't normally see this lensing because stars aren't visible during the day when the Sun is out, but a solar eclipse in 1919 allowed scientists to observe what the Sun's gravity was doing to the light from distant stars. The stars around the Sun appeared to have moved from their normal positions in the night sky. The shift was much larger than Newton's theory predicted, but exactly in the positions predicted by Einstein's theory.
options: ① 아인슈타인의 이론에 따르면, 거대한 질량은 시공간을 휘게 한다.
② 뉴턴의 이론은 태양이 시공간을 휘게 한다는 예측을 하지 않는다.
③ 중력 렌즈 효과는 별빛이 태양 근처를 지날 때 원래 위치에서 벗어나 보이는 것이다.
④ 1919년 일식 때 과학자들은 태양의 중력이 별빛에 미치는 영향을 관찰할 수 있었다.
⑤ 1919년 일식에서 별빛의 이동은 뉴턴 이론이 예측한 값과 거의 일치했다.
explanation: 지문 마지막 문장에 따르면 별빛의 이동(The shift)은 뉴턴의 이론이 예측한 것보다 훨씬 컸으며(much larger), 아인슈타인의 이론이 예측한 위치와 정확히 일치했다고 서술되어 있습니다. 따라서 뉴턴 이론의 예측값과 거의 일치했다는 5번은 내용과 다릅니다.

question: 10. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Mirror neurons are the hardware of empathy, and so what would make more sense than to look and see which animals possess these cells? And this is exactly where modern research now stands: all researchers know so far is that apes possess mirror neurons. We still need to test to see which other species are like us in this respect. Scientists often publicly speculate that we can probably expect surprises here, too. They assume that all animals that live in herds or large groups _________________________, because social units function only if individuals can see things from the perspective of others in the group and feel what they are feeling. I can see a goldfish waving its fin at us. As an animal that travels around in a tightly-knit group, it's on board with this idea - or at least swimming alongside the boat.
options: ① tend to become emotional
② possess similar brain mechanisms
③ use effective ways to escape from danger
④ learn survival skills with the help of humans
⑤ interact with animals that have mirror neurons
explanation: 거울 뉴런(mirror neurons)은 공감의 하드웨어이며, 사회적 단위가 기능하기 위해서는 타인의 관점에서 보고 느끼는 능력이 필요하다고 설명합니다. 따라서 무리 생활을 하는 동물들은 거울 뉴런과 같은 '유사한 뇌 기제(similar brain mechanisms)'를 가지고 있을 것이라고 추론하는 것이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 감정적이 되는 경향이 있다
② 유사한 뇌 기제를 소유하고 있다
③ 위험에서 탈출하는 효과적인 방법을 사용한다
④ 인간의 도움으로 생존 기술을 배운다
⑤ 거울 뉴런을 가진 동물들과 상호작용한다

question: 11. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The future of work depends on two forces: a harmful substituting force and a helpful complementing one. Many tales have a hero and a villain fighting each other for dominance, but in our story, technology plays both roles at once, displacing workers while simultaneously raising the demand for their efforts elsewhere in the economy. This interaction helps explain why past worries about automation were ______________: our ancestors had predicted the wrong winner in that fight, underestimating quite how powerful the complementing force would prove to be or simply ignoring that factor altogether. It also helps to explain why economists have traditionally been dismissive of the idea of technological unemplloyment: there appeared to be firm limits to the substituting force, leaving lots of tasks that could not be performed by machines, and a growing demand for human beings to do them instead.
options: ① understood
② misplaced
③ helpful
④ controlled
⑤ relevant
explanation: 지문은 기술이 노동자를 대체하는 힘(substituting force)과 보완하는 힘(complementing force)을 동시에 가지고 있다고 설명합니다. 과거에 자동화에 대해 가졌던 우려가 틀렸던 이유(조상들이 보완하는 힘의 위력을 과소평가하여 잘못된 승자를 예측함)를 설명하는 맥락이므로, 그 우려가 '부적절했다' 혹은 '잘못 놓였다'는 의미인 misplaced가 빈칸에 가장 적합합니다.
options_translation: ① 이해된
② 부적절한(잘못된 위치에 놓인)
③ 도움이 되는
④ 통제된
⑤ 관련 있는

question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Mother cats can tell which kittens belong to them - when litters are mixed up they use their kittens' scent to distinguish them from offspring of other mothers.
ordered_passages: (A) In the wild, a squeaking kitten out in the open is likely to attract predators, which is bad news for any other kittens around it. A rapid rescue of any crying kitten would be a good strategy to prevent them from drawing unwanted attention.(B) Despite this, when faced with a selection of kittens who have wandered from the nest, her own and others that aren't hers, a mother cat doesn't appear to favor her own offspring when retrieving them.(C) The reason for this is uncertain, although distress vocalizations from kittens that are lost from their nest are known to be very powerful, so it may just be hard for the mother to resist retrieving them, regardless of whether they are hers.

(B) Despite this, when faced with a selection of kittens who have wandered from the nest, her own and others that aren't hers, a mother cat doesn't appear to favor her own offspring when retrieving them.

(C) The reason for this is uncertain, although distress vocalizations from kittens that are lost from their nest are known to be very powerful, so it may just be hard for the mother to resist retrieving them, regardless of whether they are hers.
explanation: 주어진 글에서는 어미 고양이가 냄새를 통해 자신의 새끼를 구별할 수 있다는 능력을 설명합니다. (B)에서는 'Despite this(이것에도 불구하고)'를 사용하여, 구별 능력이 있음에도 불구하고 둥지를 벗어난 새끼들을 다시 데려올 때는 자신의 새끼를 편애하지 않는다는 반전된 사실을 제시합니다. (C)에서는 이러한 행동의 이유가 불확실하지만, 새끼의 울음소리가 매우 강력하여 저항하기 힘들기 때문일 수 있다는 가설을 제시합니다. 마지막으로 (A)에서는 야생에서 울고 있는 새끼가 포식자를 유인할 수 있으므로, 모든 새끼를 빠르게 구조하는 것이 전략적으로 유리하다는 구체적인 진화적 이유를 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

question: 22. 다음 빈칸을 <보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성하시오. (단, 철자 오류 시 오답 처리. 대/소문자 구분 없음. 필요할 경우 쉼표 넣기)
passage: A great strength of the market mechanism is that _____________________________________________. This stands in contrast to many strategic situations - for example, in political negotiations - in which it is wise not to let the other side know what one's true preferences or production capacities are. A perfectly competitive market that clears on the spot leaves no room for such strategies. If prices are not sticky - as many models assume - individuals adapt their behavior instantaneously, whenever their preferences or the circumstances change. They stop buying items that do not satisfy their needs and stop selling items that do not provide them with optimal gains, maybe switching to the production of other items. If they have motivational problems, for example, falling into denial about the fact that there is no demand for their products, markets reveal to them, sometimes in quite brutal ways, that they better accept this fact.
subjective_conditions: 철자 오류 시 오답 처리
대/소문자 구분 없음
필요할 경우 쉼표 넣기
answer: there are incentives for individuals to reveal their knowledge through their behavior
explanation: 지문은 정치적 협상 등과 달리 시장 메커니즘에서는 자신의 진짜 선호나 정보를 숨길 필요 없이, 행동을 통해 자신의 지식을 드러내게 하는 유인이 있다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 'there are incentives for individuals to reveal their knowledge through their behavior' (개인이 자신의 행동을 통해 지식을 드러내게 하는 유인이 있다)로 완성하는 것이 문맥상 가장 적절합니다.

question: 25. 다음 빈칸을 <보기>에 주어진 단어만 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성하시오. (단, 철자 오류 시 오답 처리. 대/소문자 구분 없음. 필요할 경우 쉼표 넣기)
passage: Although empathy is widely praised by scholars and public figures, not everyone is an empathy booster. Critics of empathy argue that empathy will not save us from interpersonal and intergroup conflict. In fact, they argue, empathy makes such conflicts worse. These critics maintain that empathy can be exhausting and lead to burnout or insensitivity to suffering. They argue that we tend to empathize strongly with our in-group and resist empathizing with out-groups, and even enjoy the suffering of out-groups in competitive or threatening contexts. Thus, the prescription for more empathy is often counterproductive in cases of conflict. Empathy, they argue, can further encourage conflict and force us into an us vs. them mentality. Finally, even when we ________________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어만 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성
철자 오류 시 오답 처리
대/소문자 구분 없음
필요할 경우 쉼표 넣기
answer: try to empathize with people who are different from us, we may fail to understand their experiences, causing further frustration
explanation: 이 글은 공감의 부정적인 측면과 한계에 대해 논하고 있습니다. 빈칸은 마지막 결론 부분으로, 우리와 다른 사람들에게 공감하려 노력할 때조차 그들의 경험을 이해하지 못해 더 큰 좌절을 초래할 수 있다는 내용이 적절합니다. 'even when we try to empathize with people(우리가 사람들과 공감하려 노력할 때조차)'를 'who are different from us(우리와 다른)'가 수식하고, 주절인 'we may fail to understand their experiences(우리는 그들의 경험을 이해하는 데 실패할 수 있다)' 뒤에 분사구문 'causing further frustration(더 큰 좌절을 야기하며)'을 연결합니다.

question: 1. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Minimal processing can be one of the best ways to keep original flavors and taste, without any need to add artificial flavoring or additives, or too much salt. This would also be the efficient way to keep most nutrients, especially the most sensitive ones such as many vitamins and anti-oxidants. Milling of cereals is one of the most harsh processes which dramatically affect nutrient content. While grains are naturally very rich in micronutrients, anti-oxidants and fiber (i.e. in wholemeal flour or flakes), milling usually removes the vast majority of minerals, vitamins and fibers to raise white flour. Such a spoilage of key nutrients and fiber is no longer acceptable in the context of a sustainable diet aiming at an optimal nutrient density and health protection.
options: ① Milling: Basic Condition for Sustainable Diets
② Why Consumers Prefer Highly Processed Foods
③ How to Intensify Grains Nutritious and Delicious
④ Minimal Processing: Path to Flavor and Nutrition
⑤ Artificial Flavorings: A New Breakthrough in Taste
explanation: 이 글은 최소한의 가공(minimal processing)이 인공 감미료나 첨가물 없이 본래의 맛을 유지하고 비타민, 항산화제와 같은 영양소를 보존하는 가장 좋은 방법이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 반면 곡물의 제분(milling) 과정은 영양소를 파괴하여 지속 가능한 식단에 부합하지 않는다고 지적합니다. 따라서 글의 제목으로는 최소 가공이 맛과 영양으로 가는 길임을 나타내는 4번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 제분: 지속 가능한 식단을 위한 기본 조건
② 소비자들이 고도로 가공된 식품을 선호하는 이유
③ 곡물의 영양과 맛을 강화하는 방법
④ 최소 가공: 맛과 영양으로 가는 길
⑤ 인공 감미료: 맛의 새로운 돌파구

question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The term "anchoring" was introduced by Roland Barthes who observed that text is often used next to images (his focus was on photographs) to confine meaning. Of all possible literal or implied interpretations an image could elicit, text would point the viewer towards a desired, specific direction. In advertising, as Barthes argues, the symbolic message does not guide identification but interpretation. The viewer is not asked to recognize what they see but to understand why they see it and what it means to them. By combining images with text, advertising produces symbolic meaning that is accurate and specific on the one hand, richer on the other, thus adding depth and eliminating breadth of rational and emotional interpretations. The headline or tagline of an ad directs the reader through the intended meanings of the image, so that the reader avoids some and receives others. It "remote-controls" the reader towards a meaning chosen in advance.
options: ① The Side Effects of Combining Text and Images
② How to Use Emotional Effects in Advertising
③ The Reasons Headlines Can Mislead Readers
④ Text: Guide to Interpretation of Images
⑤ Pictures: Powerful Tools for Creativity
explanation: 이 글은 롤랑 바르트의 '고정(anchoring)' 개념을 통해 텍스트가 이미지와 함께 사용되어 그 의미를 특정한 방향으로 한정하고 안내하는 역할을 한다는 것을 설명합니다. 광고에서 텍스트(헤드라인 등)는 독자가 이미지를 미리 의도된 의미로 해석하도록 '원격 조정'한다는 내용이 핵심입니다. 따라서 이미지 해석의 가이드로서의 텍스트를 언급한 4번이 정답입니다.
options_translation: ① 텍스트와 이미지를 결합할 때의 부작용
② 광고에서 감정적 효과를 사용하는 방법
③ 헤드라인이 독자를 오도할 수 있는 이유
④ 텍스트: 이미지 해석의 가이드
⑤ 사진: 창의성을 위한 강력한 도구

question: 3. 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In today's information age, in many companies and on many teams, the objective is no longer error prevention and replicability. On the contrary, it's creativity, speed, and keenness. In the industrial era, the goal was to minimize variation. But in creative companies today, maximizing variation is more essential. In these situations, the biggest risk isn't making a mistake or losing consistency; it's failing to attract top talent, to invent new products, or to change direction quickly when the environment shifts. Consistency and repeatability are more likely to suppress fresh thinking than to bring your company profit. A lot of little mistakes, while sometimes painful, help the organization learn quickly and are a critical part of the innovation cycle. In these situations, rules and process are no longer the best answer. A symphony isn't what you're going for. Leave the conductor and the sheet music behind. Build a jazz band instead.
options: ① Companies should minimize variation and prevent errors.
② Prioritizing outcomes over the process helps promote creativity.
③ Strict rules and repeated processes lead to higher profits for modern organizations.
④ The greatest threat to firms is losing consistency rather than missing talent or new ideas.
⑤ In today's creative work, embracing variation and tolerating small mistakes fuel innovation.
explanation: 필자는 현대 정보화 시대의 창의적인 기업에서는 과거 산업 시대의 목표였던 '오차 최소화'나 '일관성 유지'보다 '변화의 극대화'와 '창의성'이 더 중요하다고 강조합니다. 작은 실수들은 조직이 빠르게 배우는 데 도움을 주며 혁신 주기의 필수적인 부분이라고 주장하므로, 5번이 필자의 주장으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기업은 변동을 최소화하고 실수를 방지해야 한다.
② 과정보다 결과를 우선시하는 것이 창의성 증진에 도움이 된다.
③ 엄격한 규칙과 반복된 공정은 현대 조직에 더 높은 수익을 가져다준다.
④ 기업에 가장 큰 위협은 인재나 새로운 아이디어를 놓치는 것보다 일관성을 잃는 것이다.
⑤ 오늘날의 창의적인 업무에서, 변동을 수용하고 작은 실수를 용인하는 것이 혁신의 동력이 된다.

question: 4. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Any new or threatening situation may require us to make decisions and this requires information. So important is communication during a disaster that normal social barriers are often lowered. We will talk to strangers in a way we would never consider normally. Even relatively low grade disruption of our life such as a fire drill or a very late train seems to give us the permission to break normal etiquette and talk to strangers. The more important an event to a particular public, the more detailed and urgent the requirement for news becomes. Without an authoritative source of facts, whether that is a newspaper or trusted broadcast station, rumours often run riot. Rumours start because people believe their group to be in danger and so, although the rumour is unproven, feel they should pass it on. For example, if a worker heard that their employer's business was doing badly and people were going to be made redundant, they would pass that information on to colleagues.
options: ① People are unwilling to share their true feeling.
② People tend to trust their gut during emergencies.
③ Drills not only enhance safety but also prevent chaos.
④ Rumors make people more anxious and suspicious of others.
⑤ Crises break down social barriers and accelerate the spread of gossip.
explanation: 이 글은 재난이나 새로운 위협 상황에서 정보에 대한 욕구가 커짐에 따라 평상시의 사회적 장벽이 낮아지고, 권위 있는 정보원이 없을 때 근거 없는 소문(가십)이 빠르게 퍼진다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 위기 상황이 사회적 장벽을 허물고 소문의 확산을 가속화한다는 5번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 사람들은 자신의 진실된 감정을 공유하기를 꺼린다.
② 사람들은 비상 상황에서 자신의 직감을 믿는 경향이 있다.
③ 훈련은 안전을 강화할 뿐만 아니라 혼란도 방지한다.
④ 루머는 사람들을 더 불안하게 만들고 타인을 의심하게 만든다.
⑤ 위기는 사회적 장벽을 허물고 소문의 확산을 가속화한다.

question: 5. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Everything in the world exists on a continuum, whether in speed, size, or any other possible descriptor you could think of. Still, we create and mindlessly adopt sharp distinctions, and those distinctions change lives far more dramatically than marginal differences ever do. Indeed, all differences are arbitrary, but drawing hard lines between categories hides this arbitrariness and can be severely damaging. I call this resulting damage "the borderline effect." The examples are endless. Someone's IQ is 69 and someone else's is 70 - but only the score of 70 is deemed to be within the range of normal. We don't have to be statisticians to know there is not a meaningful difference between 69 and 70. Yet once the person with the lower score is labeled "cognitively impaired," his or her life will unfold differently than the person with a onepoint advantage.
options: ① Human traits that must be respected exist in clear categories.
② The best way to evaluate people is by drawing strict boundaries between groups.
③ Arbitrary distinctions on a continuum can distort reality and cause serious harm.
④ Statistical differences always provide the most accurate picture of human abilities.
⑤ People with higher IQ scores always live happier lives than those with lower scores.
explanation: 세상의 모든 것은 연속선상에 존재함에도 불구하고 인간은 자의적인 구분을 만들어내며, 이러한 '경계 효과(borderline effect)'가 실제로는 근소한 차이임에도 불구하고 한 사람의 인생을 크게 바꿀 정도로 해로운 영향을 끼칠 수 있다는 내용입니다.

question: 7. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The future of work depends on two forces: a harmful substituting force and a helpful complementing one. question: 8. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 we got what we got "fair and square."가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: When we get an unfavorable outcome, in some ways the last thing we want to hear is that the process was fair. As outraging as the combination of an unfavorable outcome and an unfair process is, this combination also brings with it a consolation prize: the possibility of attributing the bad outcome to something other than ourselves. We may reassure ourselves by believing that our bad outcome had little to do with us and everything to do with the unfair process. If the process is fair, however, we cannot nearly as easily externalize the outcome; <u>we got what we got "fair and square."</u> When the process is fair we believe that our outcome is deserved, which is another way of saying that there must have been something about ourselves (what we did or who we are) that caused the outcome.
options: ① We valued the process over the outcome.
② The result stemmed from external factors.
③ Fate decided the result regardless of our efforts.
④ The unfair process kept us from moving forward.
⑤ We couldn't blame the process; the result was on us.
explanation: 글의 핵심은 공정한 과정에서의 불리한 결과는 외부(과정의 불공정함)의 탓으로 돌릴 수 없으며, 결국 결과의 원인이 자신에게 있다는 점을 인정해야 한다는 것입니다. 따라서 '정정당당하게 얻은 결과'라는 말은 과정을 탓할 수 없으며 그 결과에 대한 책임이 자신에게 있다는 ⑤번의 의미와 가장 일맥상통합니다.

② 결과는 외부 요인에서 비롯되었다.
③ 우리의 노력과 상관없이 운명이 결과를 결정했다.
④ 불공정한 과정이 우리가 앞으로 나아가는 것을 막았다.
⑤ 우리는 과정을 비난할 수 없었다; 그 결과는 우리 책임이었다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend ⓐ<u>themselves</u> to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers of ⓑ<u>them</u> it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease to form, while sufficient fibers remain undamaged for the material not to crack and fall apart. Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to resist being pulled apart, but it can also be torn easily and accurately along the crease if a point of weakness - a small, initial tear - ⓒ<u>is opened up</u>. This winning combination of mechanical properties allows it to assume the shape of any object through creasing and folding - hence the art of origami. There are very few materials as good: metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult. Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, ⓓ<u>in which case</u> it lacks the rigidity required of a good wrapping material. So it is its ability to hold a crease while ⓔ<u>remaining</u> stiff that makes paper uniquely suited to this purpose.
explanation: ⓑ번 'them'이 포함된 문장은 '종이가 만들어진 셀룰로오스 섬유'를 뜻하며, 'the cellulose fibers [of which] it is made' 형태가 되어야 합니다. be made of (~로 만들어지다)에서 of의 목적어 역할을 하면서 문장을 연결하는 관계대명사 which가 필요합니다. 단순 대명사인 them은 문장을 연결할 수 없으므로 'of which'로 수정해야 합니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Although empathy is widely praised by scholars and public figures, not everyone is an empathy booster. Critics of empathy argue that empathy will not save us from interpersonal and intergroup conflict. In fact, they argue, empathy makes such conflicts worse. These critics maintain that empathy can be exhausting and lead to burnout or ⓐ<u>insensitivity</u> to suffering. They argue that we tend to empathize strongly with our ingroup and resist empathizing with outgroups, and even ⓑ<u>enjoy</u> the suffering of outgroups in competitive or threatening contexts. Thus, the prescription for more empathy is often counterproductive in cases of conflict. Empathy, they argue, can further ⓒ<u>discourage</u> conflict and force us into an us vs. them mentality. Finally, even when we try to empathize with others who are ⓓ<u>dissimilar</u> from us or in unfamiliar contexts, sometimes we are unable to accurately empathize with their experiences, causing further misunderstandings. Critics of empathy argue that we should ⓔ<u>give up on</u> empathy and employ other tools in pursuit of social harmony, e.g., rational compassion or moral emotions like fear, anger, and shame.

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Mother cats can tell which kittens belong to them - when litters are mixed up they use their kittens' scent to ⓐ<u>distinguish</u> them from offspring of other mothers. question: 14. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We're naturally wired to organize the world into a hierarchy. We do this to help make sense of the world, maintain our beliefs, and generally feel better. question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 36번]
passage: It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. question: 18. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: A great strength of the market mechanism is that there are incentives for individuals to reveal their knowledge through their behavior. This stands in contrast to many strategic situations - for example, in political negotiations - in which it is wise not to let the other side know what one's true preferences or production capacities are. ①A perfectly competitive market that clears on the spot leaves no room for such strategies. ②If prices are not sticky - as many models assume - individuals adapt their behavior instantaneously, whenever their preferences or the circumstances change. ③They stop buying items that do not satisfy their needs and stop selling items that do not provide them with optimal gains, maybe switching to the production of other items. ④Accordingly, individuals will delay adjusting their behavior until the market stabilizes. ⑤If they have motivational problems, for example, falling into denial about the fact that there is no demand for their products, markets reveal to them, sometimes in quite brutal ways, that they better accept this fact.
explanation: 마케스 메가니스하고 경재가 혀바라게 이뢔어지나는 시장에사는 개인달이 자기네의 서노도나 상황 변해가 즈가ᄀ저괘로 반응댜어사 나타나나는데, 대부분의 내용은 시장의 혀바ᄅ한 그가ᄀ저ᄀ 바능을 설먕하나 ④반은 개인달이 시장이 안정댤 태까지 해ᄂ동 조정을 지연시길 거시라고 하여 글의 흐르ᄆ가 마ᄌ지 안스바니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Sleep is clearly about more than just resting. One curious fact is that animals that are hibernating also have periods of sleep. It comes as a surprise to most of us, but hibernation and sleep are not the same thing at all, at least not from a neurological and metabolic perspective. (A) Hibernating is more like being anesthetized: the subject is unconscious but not actually asleep. (B) So a hibernating animal needs to get a few hours of conventional sleep each day within the larger unconsciousness. (C) A further surprise to most of us is that bears, the most famous of wintry sleepers, don't actually hibernate. (D) Real hibernation involves profound unconsciousness and a dramatic fall in body temperature - often to around 32 degrees Fahrenheit. (E) Their winter sleeps are more accurately called a state of torpor.
insertion_sentence: By this definition, bears don't hibernate, because their body temperature stays near normal and they are easily awakened.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 만장은 '이 정으ᅵ에 타르면, 고ᄆ은 동면하지 아느는데, 그 이유나는 그달의 테온이 자ᄀ상 상태라 유지댜고 쉬파게 깨나기 태문ᅵ다'라는 내용ᅵ므로, 'Real hibernation'의 정으ᅵ라른 설먕하나 (D) 다으ᄆ타가 오는 거시 저절하며, (E) 자리가 가장 저절하게 연결다는데 (E) 문장의 Their winter sleeps가 고ᄆ의 겨울자ᄆ을 가리키기 태문ᅵ다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Mental development consists of individuals increasingly mastering social codes and signals themselves, which they can master only in social situations with the support of more competent individuals, typically adults. (A) In this sense, mental development consists of internalizing social patterns and gradually becoming a responsible actor among other responsible actors. (D) Therefore, having formal limits for responsibility from a specific age that apply to everyone is a somewhat questionable practice. (E) But the question, of course, is whether it can be done any differently.
insertion_sentence: I do not know whether these age boundaries are optimal, but it is clear that mental development takes place at different rates for different individuals, and depends especially on the social and family environment they have been given.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
