In describing this view of science, philosopher Hugh Lacey speaks of the belief that there is an underlying order of the world which is simply there to be discovered - the world of pure "fact" stripped of any link with value. The aim of science according to this view is to ____________________, independently of any relationship it might bear contingently to human practices and experiences.
options: ① explain cultural values and ideas
② portray nature as value-free reality
③ minimize cultural bias in its findings
④ discover historical traditions of society
⑤ harmonize science with human practices
explanation: 본문은 과학을 보는 두 가지 관점을 대조하고 있습니다. 첫 번째는 과학을 특정 시대와 장소의 맥락에서 이해해야 하는 역사적 활동으로 보는 관점이고, 두 번째는 과학을 문화적 관점이나 가치와 무관한 순수하고 객관적인 추구로 보는 관점입니다. 빈칸은 두 번째 관점에 대한 설명으로, 필로소퍼 휴 레이시의 말을 빌려 과학이 가치와 분리된 순수한 '사실'의 세계를 발견하는 것을 목표로 한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 자연을 가치가 배제된(value-free) 현실로 묘사한다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 문화적 가치와 아이디어를 설명하다
② 자연을 가치가 없는 현실로 묘사하다
③ 연구 결과에서 문화적 편향을 최소화하다
④ 사회의 역사적 전통을 발견하다
⑤ 과학을 인간의 관습과 조화시키다

question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [24년 9월 33번]
passage: Over the last few centuries, humanity's collective prosperity has skyrocketed, as technological progress has made us far wealthier than ever before. (A) To share out those riches, almost all societies have settled upon the market mechanism, rewarding people in various ways for the work that they do and the things that they own. (B) Today, markets already provide immense rewards to some people but leave many others with very little. (C) And now, technological unemployment threatens to become a more radical version of the same story, taking place in the particular market we rely upon the most: the labor market. (D) As that market begins to break down, more and more people will be in danger of not receiving a share of society's prosperity at all. (E)
insertion_sentence: But rising inequality, itself often driven by technology, has started to put that mechanism under strain.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'that mechanism'은 (A)에서 언급된 'the market mechanism'을 지칭합니다. (A)에서는 사회가 부를 나누기 위해 시장 기제를 정착시켰다고 설명하고 있으며, 주어진 문장은 기술에 의한 불평등 심화가 그 기제(시장 기제)를 긴장 상태에 빠뜨리기 시작했다는 전환을 보여줍니다. 이어지는 (B) 이후의 내용은 시장이 일부에게는 막대한 보상을 주지만 다른 이들에게는 거의 주지 않는 불평등의 현실과 기술적 실업 문제를 다루고 있으므로, (B) 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [23년 9월 32번]
passage: There is little doubt that we are driven by the sell-by date. Once an item is past that date it goes into the waste stream, further increasing its carbon footprint.
ordered_passages: (A) The manufacturer then decides that a product can reasonably be consumed within say 90 days and 90 days minus so many days for travelling gives the sell-by date. But whether it becomes toxic is something each individual can decide.(B) Those brought up during the Second World War are often scornful of the terrible waste they believe such caution encourages. The manufacturer of the food has a view when making or growing something that by the time the product reaches the shelves it has already been travelling for so many days and possibly many miles.(C) Remember those items have already travelled hundreds of miles to reach the shelves and once they go into waste they start a new carbon mile journey. But we all make our own judgement about sell-by dates.
explanation: 주어진 글에서 판매 유통기한(sell-by date)이 지나면 폐기물이 되어 탄소 발자국을 늘린다는 점을 언급했습니다. (C)는 폐기 시 새로운 탄소 여정이 시작된다는 점을 다시 상기시키며, 우리가 유통기한에 대해 각자 판단을 내린다는 내용을 도입합니다. (B)에서는 유통기한에 민감한 주의가 낭비를 초래한다고 생각하는 세대(2차 세계대전 세대)를 언급하고, 제조사의 관점에서 이동 기간을 고려하기 시작한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (A)는 (B)의 제조사 관점을 이어받아 유통기한이 어떻게 결정되는지 설명하고, 개별적인 판단의 중요성을 다시 강조하며 마무리됩니다.

question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 35번]
passage: Minimal processing can be one of the best ways to keep original flavors and taste, without any need to add artificial flavoring or additives, or too much salt. This would also be the efficient way to keep most nutrients, especially the most sensitive ones such as many vitamins and anti-oxidants.
ordered_passages: (A) The loss of essential nutrients and fiber like this is now considered unacceptable when pursuing a sustainable diet focused on maximizing nutrient density and safeguarding health.(B) However, milling of cereals is one of the most harsh processes which dramatically affect nutrient content. While grains are naturally very rich in micronutrients, anti-oxidants and fiber, milling usually removes the vast majority of minerals, vitamins and fibers to raise white flour.(C) On the other hand, fermentation of various foodstuffs or germination of grains are traditional, locally accessible, low-energy and highly nutritious processes of sounded interest.
explanation: 주어진 글은 최소한의 가공(minimal processing)의 장점(영양소 보존 등)을 설명합니다. (B)는 'However'를 통해 대조를 이루며 곡물 제분(milling)과 같은 가혹한 가공 과정이 영양소를 심각하게 파괴한다는 점을 설명합니다. (A)는 (B)에서 언급한 이러한(like this) 필수 영양소와 섬유질의 손실이 건강을 중시하는 식단에서는 받아들여질 수 없다고 강조합니다. 마지막으로 (C)는 'On the other hand'를 통해 발효나 발아와 같이 전통적이고 영양가가 높은 가공 방식을 다시 긍정적인 측면에서 소개하며 마무리됩니다.

question: 22. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
passage: Much of human thought is designed to screen out information and to sort the rest into a manageable condition. The inflow of data from our senses could create an overwhelming chaos, especially given the enormous amount of information available in culture and society. ⓐOut of all the sensory impressions and possible information, it is vital to find a small amount that is most relevant to our individual needs and to organize that into a usable stock of knowledge. ⓑExpectancies accomplish some of this work, helping to screen out information that is irrelevant to what is expected, and focusing our attention on clear contradictions. ⓒThe processes of learning and memory are facilitated when information comes into us as it is rather than being manipulated. ⓓPeople notice only a part of the world around them and then, only a fraction of what they notice gets processed and stored into memory. ⓔAnd only part of what gets committed to memory can be retrieved.
explanation: 이 글의 주제는 인간의 사고가 방대한 정보 중 필요한 것만 걸러내고 관리 가능한 상태로 정리한다는 내용입니다. ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 정보를 선별하고(screen out) 조직하는 과정에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 반면, ⓒ는 정보가 조작되지 않고 있는 그대로 들어올 때 학습과 기억이 촉진된다는 내용으로, 정보의 선별과 처리 과정이라는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: Any new or threatening situation may require us to make decisions and this requires information. So important is communication during a disaster that normal social barriers are often lowered. We will talk to strangers in a way we would never consider normally. Even relatively low grade disruption of our life such as a fire drill or a very late train seems to give us the permission to break normal etiquette and talk to strangers. The more important an event to a particular public, the more detailed and urgent the requirement for news becomes. Without an authoritative source of facts, whether that is a newspaper or trusted broadcast station, rumours often run riot. Rumours start because people believe their group to be in danger and so, although the rumour is unproven, feel they should pass it on. For example, if a worker heard that their employer's business was doing badly and people were going to be made redundant, they would pass that information on to colleagues.
summary_sentence: While the need for communication (A)__________ barriers in crises, lack of reliable information often allows rumors to spread (B)__________ among people.
options: ① breaks down / uncontrollably
② reduces / carefully
③ intensifies / desperately
④ elevates / unmanageably
⑤ tears down / systematically
explanation: 글의 앞부분에서 위기 상황이나 재난 시에는 평상시의 사회적 장벽이 낮아지거나 허물어져(breaks down) 낯선 사람과도 소통하게 된다고 언급하고 있습니다. 글의 뒷부분에서는 신뢰할 수 있는 정보원이 없을 때 근거 없는 소문이 걷잡을 수 없이(uncontrollably) 퍼지게 된다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 (A)에는 '무너뜨리다', (B)에는 '통제할 수 없이'라는 의미의 단어가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 허물다 / 통제할 수 없이
② 줄이다 / 조심스럽게
③ 강화하다 / 필사적으로
④ 높이다 / 감당할 수 없게
⑤ 허물다 / 체계적으로

question: 24. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: One well-known shift took place when the accepted view - that the Earth was the center of the universe - changed to one where we understood that we are only inhabitants on one planet orbiting the Sun. With each person who grasped the solar system view, it became easier for the next person to do so. So it is with the notion that the world revolves around the human economy. This is slowly being replaced by the view that the economy is a part of the larger system of material flows that connect all living things. When this perspective shifts into place, it will be obvious that our economic well-being requires that we account for, and respond to, factors of ecological health. Unfortunately we do not have a century or two to make the change. By clarifying the nature of the old and new perspectives, and by identifying actions on which we might cooperate to move the process along, we can help accelerate the shift.
summary_sentence: A growing number of people are moving from a worldview centered on (A)__________ to one that prioritizes (B)__________ as essential for long-term survival.
options: ① planetary centrality / ecological diversity
② human-centered economy / environmental responsibility
③ population expansion / sustainable development
④ economic centrality / market efficiency
⑤ material consumption / ecological health
explanation: 본문은 세상이 인간 경제(human economy)를 중심으로 돌아간다는 관점에서, 경제가 모든 생물을 연결하는 거대한 물질적 흐름(생태계)의 일부라는 관점으로 변화하고 있음을 설명합니다. 이러한 변화는 우리의 경제적 안녕이 생태학적 건강(ecological health) 요소에 대응할 것을 요구한다는 점을 시사합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 인간 중심의 경제, (B)에는 환경적 책임(혹은 생태적 건강)에 대한 우선순위가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다. 선택지 5번의 ecological health도 적절해 보이나 (A)의 material consumption이 지문의 핵심인 '인간 중심적 경제 관념'을 충분히 대변하지 못하므로, (A)에 human-centered economy를 포함한 2번이 가장 정답에 가깝습니다.
options_translation: ① 행성 중심성 / 생태적 다양성
② 인간 중심 경제 / 환경적 책임
③ 인구 확장 / 지속 가능한 발전
④ 경제적 중심성 / 시장 효율성
⑤ 물질적 소비 / 생태적 건강

question: 25. 다음 글의 요지를 한 문장으로 작성하고자 할 때 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 작성하시오.
passage: When we get an unfavorable outcome, in some ways the last thing we want to hear is that the process was fair. As outraging as the combination of an unfavorable outcome and an unfair process is, this combination also brings with it a consolation prize: the possibility of attributing the bad outcome to something other than ourselves. We may reassure ourselves by believing that our bad outcome had little to do with us and everything to do with the unfair process. If the process is fair, however, we cannot nearly as easily externalize the outcome; we got what we got "fair and square." When the process is fair we believe that our outcome is deserved, which is another way of saying that there must have been something about ourselves (what we did or who we are) that caused the outcome.
subjective_conditions: ·<보기>의 단어를 형태 변형 없이 모두 한 번씩 포함할 것
·14단어의 한 문장으로 작성할 것
vocabulary_box: people / anything / feel / blame / about / but / because / worse / themselves / cannot
subjective_answer_format: 정답: When the process is fair, ______________________
answer: people feel worse about an unfavorable outcome because they cannot blame anything but themselves
explanation: 이 글은 결과가 공정할 때 사람들이 불리한 결과에 대해 더 나쁘게 느낀다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 그 이유는 과정이 공정했으므로 자신 외에는 탓할 대상이 없기 때문입니다. 따라서 <보기>의 단어들을 조합하여 '사람들은 자신 외에는 아무것도 탓할 수 없기 때문에 불리한 결과에 대해 더 기분이 나쁘다'는 의미의 문장을 완성해야 합니다.

question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 작성하시오.
passage: It's remarkable that positive fantasies help us relax to such an extent that it shows up in physiological tests. If you want to unwind, you can take some deep breaths, get a massage, or go for a walk - but you can also try simply closing your eyes and fantasizing about some future outcome that you might enjoy. But what about when your objective is to make your wish a reality? The last thing you want to be is relaxed. You want to be energized enough to get off the couch and lose those pounds or find that job or study for that test, and you want to be motivated enough to stay engaged even when the inevitable obstacles or challenges arise. The principle of "Dream it. Wish it. Do it." does not hold true, and now we know why: in dreaming it, you undercut the energy you need to do it. You put yourself in a temporary state of complete happiness, calmness - and inactivity.
subjective_conditions: ·<보기>의 단어를 형태 변형 없이 모두 한 번씩 포함할 것
·12단어로 작성할 것
vocabulary_box: your wish / the power / necessary / which / weaken / come true / for
subjective_answer_format: Q: What is the reason positive fantasies are not helpful when your aim is to make your desire realized?A: It is because when you fantasize about your future outcome that you might enjoy, you __________ ____________.정답: ___________________________________________________
answer: weaken the power which is necessary for making your wish come true
explanation: 낙관적인 상상이 목표 달성에 도움이 되지 않는 이유는 그것이 행동에 필요한 에너지를 약화시키기 때문입니다. <보기>의 표현들을 사용하여 '당신의 소망을 이루기 위해 필요한 힘을 약화시킨다'는 내용을 12단어로 구성해야 합니다.

question: 27. 다음 글을 읽고 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 영어로 작성하시오.
passage: I suspect fungi are a little more forward "thinking" than their larger partners. Among trees, each species fights other species. Let's assume the beeches native to Central Europe could emerge victorious in most forests there. Would this really be an advantage? What would happen if a new pathogen came along that infected most of the beeches and killed them? In that case, wouldn't it be more advantageous if there were a certain number of other species around - oaks, maples, or firs - that would continue to grow and provide the shade needed for a new generation of young beeches to sprout and grow up? Diversity provides security for ancient forests. Because fungi are also very dependent on stable conditions, they support other species underground and protect them from complete collapse to ensure that one species of tree doesn't manage to dominate.
subjective_conditions: ·<보기>의 단어를 모두 포함하되, 필요할 경우 형태를 변형하여 사용할 것
·12단어의 한 문장으로 작성할 것
vocabulary_box: they / can / depend on / exist / that / ensure / when
subjective_answer_format: Q: Why do fungi support diversity?A: Fungi support diversity because ___________________.정답: ___________________________________________________
answer: the stability(security) that they depend on can exist when diversity is ensured
explanation: 곰팡이가 다양성을 지지하는 이유는 곰팡이가 의존하는 안정적 조건이 다양성이 확보될 때 존재할 수 있기 때문입니다. <보기>의 단어들을 변형 및 조합하여 '그들이 의존하는 안정성이 다양성이 보장될 때 존재할 수 있다'는 의미의 12단어 문장을 완성합니다.

question: 9. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Any new or threatening situation may require us to make decisions and this requires information. So important is communication during a disaster that normal social barriers are often lowered. We will talk to strangers in a way we would never consider normally. Even relatively low grade disruption of our life such as a fire drill or a very late train seems to give us the permission to break normal etiquette and talk to strangers. The more important an event to a particular public, the more detailed and urgent the requirement for news becomes. Without an authoritative source of facts, whether that is a newspaper or trusted broadcast station, rumours often run riot. Rumours start because people believe their group to be in danger and so, although the rumour is unproven, feel they should pass it on. For example, if a worker heard that their employer's business was doing badly and people were going to be made redundant, they would pass that information on to colleagues.
options: ① In disasters, people may talk to strangers more freely than usual.
② Even a late train can make people break ordinary etiquette.
③ Even when no reliable facts are available, rumours can still spread widely.
④ Rumours spread only when the information is completely verified.
⑤ A worker may share news of possible layoffs with colleagues.
explanation: 지문에서 루머는 입증되지 않았음에도 불구하고(although the rumour is unproven) 사람들이 위험을 느끼면 전달하기 때문에 발생한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 정보가 완전히 검증되었을 때만 루머가 퍼진다는 4번 선택지는 본문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 재난 상황에서 사람들은 평소보다 더 자유롭게 낯선 사람과 대화할 수 있다.
② 기차 연착조차도 사람들이 평상시의 예의를 깨게 만들 수 있다.
③ 신뢰할 만한 사실이 없을 때조차도 루머는 널리 퍼질 수 있다.
④ 루머는 정보가 완전히 검증되었을 때만 퍼진다.
⑤ 근로자는 가능한 해고 소식을 동료들과 공유할 수 있다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. By "competence," I mean a cluster of qualities: smartness, the ability to get things done, wise decisions, etc. We stand a better chance of doing well at our life tasks if we surround ourselves with people who know what they're doing and have a lot to teach us. But the research evidence is paradoxical: In problem-solving groups, the participants who are considered the most competent and have the best ideas tend not to be the ones who are best liked. Why? One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, those who are too competent make us uncomfortable. They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman ─ and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison. If this were true, we might like people more if they reveal some evidence of fallibility. For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her better if, every once in a while, they screwed up.
options: ① The Paradox of Competence and Likeability
② The Subtle Disadvantage of Human Fallibility
③ How to Improve Your Decision-Making Skills
④ Why Group Work Always Produces the Best Ideas
⑤ The Importance of Surrounding Yourself with Smart Friends
explanation: 지문은 유능한 사람을 좋아할 것 같지만 실제로는 너무 완벽한 사람보다 실수(fallibility)를 보여주는 사람에게 더 호감을 느낀다는 역설적인 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 '유능함과 호감도의 역설'이 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 유능함과 호감도의 역설
② 인간의 불완전함의 미묘한 단점
③ 의사결정 능력을 향상시키는 방법
④ 왜 그룹 작업이 항상 최고의 아이디어를 만들어내는가
⑤ 똑똑한 친구들을 곁에 두는 것의 중요성

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: When we get an unfavorable outcome, in some ways the last thing we want to hear is that the process was fair. As outraging as the combination of an unfavorable outcome and an unfair process is, this combination also brings with it a ①<u>comfort</u>: the possibility of attributing the bad outcome to something other than ourselves. We may ②<u>soothe</u> ourselves by believing that our bad outcome had little to do with us. We think it had everything to do with the ③<u>reasonable</u> process. If the process is fair, however, we cannot nearly as easily externalize the outcome; we got what we got "fair and square." When the process is fair, we believe that our outcome is ④<u>deserved</u>. This is another way of saying that there must have been ⑤<u>something</u> about ourselves (what we did or who we are) that caused the outcome.
explanation: 결과가 좋지 않을 때 과정이 불공정하다면 그 탓을 외부로 돌릴 수 있어 위안이 되지만, 과정이 공정하다면 결과를 외부 탓으로 돌릴 수 없다는 맥락입니다. ③번 문맥은 과정이 불공정해서 나쁜 결과가 자신과 상관없다고 믿으며 위안을 얻는 상황이므로, '합리적인(reasonable)'이 아니라 '불공정한(unfair)' 과정이 되어야 적절합니다.

question: 12. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: The well-known American ethnologist Alfred Louis Kroeber made a rich and in-depth study of women's evening dress in the West, stretching back about three centuries and using reproductions of engravings. ⓐAfter adjusting the dimensions of these plates because of their diverse origins, he was able to analyse the constant elements in fashion features and produce a study that was not intuitive or approximate but precise, mathematical, and statistical. ⓑHe reduced women's clothing to a certain number of features: length and size of the skirt, size and depth of the neckline, height of the waistline. ⓒAt the same time, this also illustrates how women's growing participation in the labor market led them to prefer more practical clothing styles for everyday life. ⓓHe demonstrated unambiguously that fashion is a profoundly regular phenomenon, not at the level of annual variations but on the scale of history, as shown by the fact that for practically 300 years women's dress was subject to a very precise periodic cycle with forms reaching the furthest point in their variations every fifty years. ⓔIf, at any one moment, skirts are at their longest, fifty years later they will be at their shortest; thus skirts become long again fifty years after being short and a hundred years after being long.
explanation: 이 글은 알프레드 루이 크뢰버의 연구를 통해 패션이 역사적 차원에서 매우 정밀하고 주기적인 주기를 따르는 규칙적인 현상임을 설명하고 있습니다. 반면, ③(ⓒ)번 문장은 여성의 노동 시장 참여와 실용적인 의복 스타일의 선호에 대해 언급하고 있어 패션의 주기적 변화라는 핵심 논지에서 벗어납니다.

question: 15. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Over the last few centuries, humanity's collective prosperity has skyrocketed, as technological progress has made us far wealthier than ever before. In order to distribute those riches, nearly all societies have turned to the market system, which rewards people in different ways for their labor and possessions. However, growing inequality, often fueled by technology, has begun to weaken that very system. Today, markets already provide immense rewards to some people but leave many others with very little. At present, technological unemployment poses the threat of becoming an even more extreme version of the same problem in the labor market we depend on most, and as that market collapses, more and more people risk losing any share of society's prosperity.
options: ① Prosperity always removes inequality.
② Markets collapse mainly because societies abandon the continuous development of technologies.
③ Technological progress increases prosperity but also causes inequality threatening the market system.
④ Some people firmly insist that technology guarantees prosperity for all members of society regardless of circumstances.
⑤ Technology enriches societies in many ways and steadily reduces inequality and unemployment, supporting the stability of the market system.
explanation: 이 글은 기술 진보가 인류의 번영을 가져왔으나, 기술로 인한 불평등 심화와 실업 위협이 시장 시스템을 약화시키고 번영의 혜택을 잃게 만들 수 있다는 점을 지적하고 있습니다. 따라서 기술 발전이 번영을 늘리지만 동시에 시장 시스템을 위협하는 불평등을 초래한다는 ③번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 번영은 항상 불평등을 제거한다.
② 시장은 주로 사회가 기술의 지속적인 발전을 포기하기 때문에 붕괴한다.
③ 기술적 진보는 번영을 증가시키지만 시장 시스템을 위협하는 불평등도 야기한다.
④ 일부 사람들은 상황에 관계없이 기술이 사회의 모든 구성원에게 번영을 보장한다고 굳게 주장한다.
⑤ 기술은 여러 면에서 사회를 풍요롭게 하고 불평등과 실업을 꾸준히 감소시켜 시장 시스템의 안정을 지원한다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In today's information age, in many companies and on many teams, the objective is no longer error prevention and replicability. On the contrary, it's creativity, speed, and keenness. In the industrial era, the goal was to minimize variation. But in creative companies today, maximizing variation is more essential. In these situations, the biggest risk isn't making a mistake or losing consistency; it's failing to attract top talent, to invent new products, or to change direction quickly when the environment shifts. Consistency and repeatability are more likely to suppress fresh thinking than to bring your company profit. A lot of little mistakes, while sometimes painful, help the organization learn quickly and are a critical part of the innovation cycle. In these situations, rules and process are no longer the best answer. A symphony isn't what you're going for. Leave the conductor and the sheet music behind. Build a jazz band instead.
options: ① the seriousness of talent loss in companies
② the importance of creativity and adaptability in the Information Age
③ a comparison between business leadership and the role of a musical conductor
④ the shift from creativity to consistency in modern corporate management
⑤ the potential advantages of maintaining consistency and repeatability in management systems
explanation: 이 글은 정보화 시대의 기업 환경에서 과거 산업 시대의 목표였던 오류 방지와 일관성 대신 창의성, 속도, 변화에 대한 적응력이 더 중요해졌음을 강조하고 있습니다. 지휘자가 있는 교향악단보다는 자유로운 재즈 밴드와 같은 조직 문화를 지향하라는 비유를 통해 창의성과 유연성의 중요성을 역설하고 있으므로 주제는 ②번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기업 내 인재 손실의 심각성
② 정보화 시대에서 창의성과 적응력의 중요성
③ 비즈니스 리더십과 음악 지휘자 역할 간의 비교
④ 현대 기업 경영에서 창의성에서 일관성으로의 전환
⑤ 경영 시스템에서 일관성과 반복성을 유지할 때의 잠재적 이점

question: 17. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 adding depth and eliminating breath of rational and emotional interpretations가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The term "anchoring" was introduced by Roland Barthes who observed that text is often used next to images (his focus was on photographs) to confine meaning. Of all possible literal or implied interpretations an image could elicit, text would point the viewer towards a desired, specific direction. In advertising, as Barthes argues, the symbolic message does not guide identification but interpretation. The viewer is not asked to recognize what they see but to understand why they see it and what it means to them. By combining images with text, advertising produces symbolic meaning that is accurate and specific on the one hand, richer on the other, thus <u>adding depth and eliminating breadth of rational and emotional interpretations</u>. The headline or tagline of an ad directs the reader through the intended meanings of the image, so that the reader avoids some and receives others. It "remotecontrols" the reader towards a meaning chosen in advance.
options: ① oversimplifying the image and losing depth and precision
② giving richer meaning but limiting interpretive freedom
③ removing emotional meanings and keeping only rational ones
④ making the image more confusing and increasing possible interpretations
⑤ enriching the image but still allowing many free interpretations
explanation: 글의 맥락에 따르면 텍스트는 이미지의 의미를 한정하고 관객을 특정 방향으로 안내하는 '고정(anchoring)' 역할을 합니다. 따라서 텍스트를 통해 광고는 더 풍부하고 구체적인 상징적 의미를 부여하지만(adding depth), 동시에 독자가 가질 수 있는 다양한 해석의 폭을 제한하고 미리 정해진 의미로 유도한다(eliminating breadth)는 것을 의미합니다. 그러므로 정답은 ②번입니다.
options_translation: ① 이미지를 과도하게 단순화하고 깊이와 정밀함을 잃는 것
② 더 풍부한 의미를 제공하지만 해석의 자유를 제한하는 것
③ 감정적인 의미를 제거하고 이성적인 의미만 유지하는 것
④ 이미지를 더 혼란스럽게 만들고 가능한 해석을 늘리는 것
⑤ 이미지를 풍부하게 만들지만 여전히 많은 자유로운 해석을 허용하는 것

question: 18. 다음 글에서 밑줄로서 친 Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It's often said that those who can't do, teach. It would be more accurate to say that those who can do, can't teach the basics. A great deal of expert knowledge is implicit, not explicit. The further you progress toward mastery, the less conscious awareness you often have of the fundamentals. Experiments show that skilled golfers and wine aficionados have a hard time describing their putting and tasting echniques ─ even asking them to explain their approaches is enough to interfere with their performance, so they often stay on autopilot. When I first saw an elite diver do four and a half somersaults, I asked how he managed to spin so fast. His answer: "Just go up in a ball." Experts often have an intuitive understanding of a route, but they struggle to clearly express all the steps to take. <u>Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage</u>.
options: ① Experts deliberately hide the basics from beginners.
② Experts' explanations are entirely full of wrong information.
③ Non-experts are not as good as experts at explaining the basics.
④ Experts always organize their ideas logically and present them clearly.
⑤ Experts' explanations cannot clearly cover the basics because they are vague or incomplete.
explanation: 글에 따르면 전문가는 특정 분야의 숙달도가 높아질수록 기초적인 부분에 대한 의식적인 인식이 줄어들며, 지식의 많은 부분이 암묵적인 상태가 됩니다. 이로 인해 전문가들은 자신이 하는 방식에 대해 직관적으로는 알지만 그것을 초보자에게 명확한 단계로 설명하는 데 어려움을 겪습니다. 따라서 밑줄 친 부분은 전문가의 머릿속에 든 정보를 쏟아냈을 때 기초적인 설명 부분은 모호하거나 불완전하여 실질적인 도움이 되지 않을 수 있음을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 전문가들은 초보자들에게 의도적으로 기초를 숨긴다.
② 전문가들의 설명은 전적으로 잘못된 정보로 가득 차 있다.
③ 비전문가들은 기초를 설명하는 데 있어 전문가만큼 뛰어나지 않다.
④ 전문가들은 항상 자신의 생각을 논리적으로 정리하고 명확하게 제시한다.
⑤ 전문가들의 설명은 모호하거나 불완전하기 때문에 기초를 명확하게 다룰 수 없다.

question: 20. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: People seem to recognize that the arts are cultural activities that draw on (or react against) certain cultural traditions, certain shared understanding, and certain values and ideas that are characteristic of the time and place in which the art is created. In the case of science, however, opinions differ. Some scientists, like the great biologist J. B. S. Haldane, see science in a similar light ─ as a historical activity that occurs in a particular time and place, and that needs to be understood within that context. Others, however, see science as a(an) ________________________, uninfluenced by the cultural viewpoint and values of those who create it. In describing this view of science, philosopher Hugh Lacey speaks of the belief that there is an underlying order of the world which is simply there to be discovered ─ the world of pure "fact" stripped of any link with value. The aim of science according to this view is to represent this world of pure "fact", independently of any relationship it might bear contingently to human practices and experiences.
options: ① value-free pursuit of truth
② socially conditioned belief
③ tradition reacting to cultural influences
④ ethical responsibility in scientific practice
⑤ subjective interpretation of facts
explanation: 과학을 문화적 맥락에서 이해해야 한다는 견해와 달리, 다른 이들은 과학을 창조자의 문화적 관점이나 가치에 영향을 받지 않는 것으로 봅니다. 빈칸 뒤의 '순수한 사실의 세계', '가치와의 연결이 제거된' 등의 설명을 통해 과학이 가치와 무관하게 진리를 추구하는 활동으로 간주됨을 알 수 있습니다.
options_translation: ① 가치 중립적인 진리 추구
② 사회적으로 제약된 신념
③ 문화적 영향에 반응하는 전통
④ 과학적 관행에서의 윤리적 책임
⑤ 사실에 대한 주관적 해석

question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Mental development consists of individuals increasingly mastering social codes and signals themselves, which they can master only in social situations with the support of more competent individuals, typically adults. (A) On this basis, mental development consists of adopting social patterns and step by step becoming a reliable actor among other reliable actors. (B) In Denmark, people reach the age of criminal responsibility at 15, which indicates that they are then regarded as mentally mature enough to be held accountable for their actions. (C) At 18, they are granted the right to vote and are thus officially included in the core democratic process. (D) Therefore, having formal limits for responsibility from a specific age that apply to everyone is a somewhat questionable practice. (E) But the question, of course, is whether it can be done any differently.
insertion_sentence: I am not certain that these age limits are ideal, but it is evident that mental development varies from person to person and is strongly influenced by the social and family environment provided to them.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 연령 제한이 이상적인지 확신할 수 없으며, 정신적 발달은 개인마다 다르고 환경의 영향을 받는다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. (C) 앞까지는 덴마크의 법적 연령 사례를 설명하고 있고, (D) 뒤의 문장은 특정 연령을 일괄 적용하는 것이 의심스러운 관행이라는 결론을 내리고 있습니다. 따라서 법적 연령의 일괄 적용에 대한 의구심을 제기하는 근거가 되는 주어진 문장은 (D) 위치에 들어가는 것이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: The concern about how we appear to others can be seen in children, though work by the psychologist Ervin Staub suggests that the effect may vary with age. (A) In a study where children heard another child in distress, young children (kindergarten through second grade) were more likely to help the child in distress when with another child than when alone. (B) Staub suggested that younger children might feel more comfortable acting when they have the company of a peer. (C) Older children, however, might feel more concern about being judged by their peers and fear feeling embarrassed by overreacting. (D) Staub noted that "older children seemed to discuss the distress sounds less and to react to them less openly than younger children." (E) In other words, the older children were deliberately putting on a poker face in front of their peers.
insertion_sentence: But for older children ─ in fourth and sixth grade ─ the effect reversed: they were less likely to help a child in distress when they were with a peer than when they were alone.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 4학년과 6학년의 더 나이가 많은 아이들에게서는 효과가 반대로 나타나 혼자 있을 때보다 또래와 함께 있을 때 곤경에 처한 아이를 덜 돕는 경향이 있다는 내용입니다. (B) 앞까지는 어린 아이들(유치원생~2학년)이 또래와 함께 있을 때 더 잘 돕는다는 내용이 나오고, (B) 위치에 주어진 문장이 들어가 '반전된 효과'를 소개한 뒤, (C)부터 그 이유(타인의 시선을 의식하고 창피함을 느낌)를 설명하는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 24. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Minimal processing can be one of the best ways to keep original flavors and taste, without any need to add artificial flavoring or additives, or too much salt. This would also be the efficient way ⓐ<u>in which</u> most nutrients, especially the most sensitive ones such as many vitamins and antioxidants, are kept. Milling of cereals is one of the most harsh processes which dramatically ⓑ<u>affect</u> nutrient content. Being naturally very rich in micronutrients, anti-oxidants and fiber (i.e. in wholemeal flour or flakes), milling usually removes the vast majority of minerals, vitamins and fibers ⓒ<u>raise</u> white flour. Such a spoilage of key nutrients and fiber ⓓ<u>is</u> no longer acceptable in the context of a sustainable diet aiming at an optimal nutrient density and health protection. In contrast, fermentation of various foodstuffs or germination of grains are traditional, locally accessible, low-energy, and highly nutritious processes, and many people continue to practice ⓔ<u>them</u> in their communities.
explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장에서 milling이 주어, removes가 동사, the vast majority...가 목적어인 완전한 절이므로, raise는 목적어를 설명하는 분사 구문이 되어야 합니다. 흰 밀가루를 '만들어내면서/남기면서'라는 능동의 의미가 적절하므로 raising 또는 '만들어진'의 의미인 resulting in 등으로 수정되어야 합니다. 원문 문맥상으로는 'producing' 혹은 분사 형태가 와야 할 자리에서 동사 원형인 raise가 쓰인 것은 문법적으로 틀립니다.

question: 25. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The first human beings probably evolved in tropical regions where survival was possible without clothing. It is likely that they had very dark skin because light skin would have given little protection against the burning rays of the sun. There is a debate about whether these people spread into other parts of the world or, instead, whether people developed independently in various parts of the world.
ordered_passages: (A) For example, early hominids were likely not upright walkers at first, but once they gained this skill, their movement became more efficient. Even more significant was their invention of tools. By using tools, they were able to hunt animals, which gave them access to greater amounts of protein and fat than their former plant-based, low-energy diet could offer.

(B) Whichever the case, it is believed that in time they became capable of spreading out from Africa, eventually to most of the world. This was probably because their physical characteristics changed.

(C) With an increase in available energy, both their bodies and brains underwent changes. Since brain growth requires a large amount of energy, the improved diet allowed hominids to extend their range both physically and mentally.
explanation: 제시문에서 인류의 기원과 전파에 대한 논쟁을 언급합니다. (B)에서 'Whichever the case(어떤 경우든)'를 통해 제시문의 두 가지 가능성을 모두 받으며 아프리카를 벗어나 전파된 원인으로 신체적 특성의 변화를 듭니다. (A)는 신체적 변화의 예시(직립 보행)와 도구 사용을 통한 식이 변화(단백질 섭취 증가)를 설명합니다. (C)는 (A)의 마지막 부분인 식이 변화로 인한 '에너지 증가'를 받아 신체와 뇌의 변화를 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다.

question: 26. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Sleep is clearly about more than just resting. One curious fact is that animals that are hibernating also have periods of sleep.
ordered_passages: (A) By this definition, bears don't hibernate, because their body temperature stays near normal and they are easily awakened. Their winter sleeps are more accurately called a state of torpor.

(B) So a hibernating animal needs to get a few hours of conventional sleep each day within the larger unconsciousness. A further surprise to most of us is that bears, the most famous of wintry sleepers, don't actually hibernate. Real hibernation involves profound unconsciousness and a dramatic fall in body temperature ─ often to around 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

(C) It comes as a surprise to most of us, but hibernation and sleep are not the same thing at all, at least not from a neurological and metabolic perspective. Hibernating is more like being anesthetized: the subject is unconscious but not actually asleep.
explanation: 수면은 단순히 휴식 그 이상의 것이며 동면 중인 동물도 수면의 기간을 갖는다는 제시문 다음에, 동면과 수면은 신경학적 및 대사적 측면에서 완전히 다르며 동면은 마취 상태에 가깝다는 (C)의 설명이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽습니다. 그 후 동면 중에도 전형적인 수면이 필요하다는 사실과 함께, 곰의 사례를 들어 진정한 동면의 정의(체온의 하락 등)를 설명하는 (B)가 오고, 마지막으로 그 정의에 따라 곰의 상태를 '동면(torpor)'으로 규정하는 (A)로 마무리하는 것이 논리적입니다. 따라서 정답은 ⑤번입니다.

question: 27. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: One well-known shift took place when the accepted view ─ that the Earth was the center of the universe ─ changed to one where we understood that we are only inhabitants on one planet orbiting the Sun. With each person who grasped the solar system view, it became easier for the next person to do so. So it is with the notion that the world revolves around the human economy. This is slowly being replaced by the view that the economy is a part of the larger system of material flows that connect all living things. When this perspective shifts into place, it will be obvious that our economic well-being requires that we account for, and respond to, factors of ecological health. Unfortunately we do not have a century or two to make the change. By clarifying the nature of the old and new perspectives, and by identifying actions on which we might cooperate to move the process along, we can help accelerate the shift.
summary_sentence: Just as the belief that the universe centered on Earth (A)_________ to the idea that Earth circles the Sun, our economic view is also changing, with the human-centered economy now seen as part of the larger natural flows that (B)_________ all life.
options: ① (A) shifted - (B) sustain
② (A) started - (B) exhaust
③ (A) remained - (B) maintain
④ (A) stopped - (B) preserve
⑤ (A) collapsed - (B) consume
explanation: 지구가 우주의 중심이라는 믿음이 지구가 태양 주위를 돈다는 생각으로 변화한 것처럼, 경제 관념 또한 인간 중심적인 시각에서 벗어나 모든 생명을 지탱하는 더 큰 자연적 흐름의 일부로 변화하고 있다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 ‘변화했다’는 의미의 shifted가, (B)에는 모든 생명을 ‘지탱하다/유지하다’라는 의미의 sustain이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 변화했다 - 지탱하다
② 시작했다 - 고갈시키다
③ 남아있다 - 관리하다
④ 멈추었다 - 보존하다
⑤ 붕괴되었다 - 소비하다

question: 2. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Technological unemployment occurs when developments in technology and working practices cause some workers to lose their jobs. Specifically, when labour-saving machines are introduced into the productive process, a firm can get rid of workers and produce the same amount of goods as before. As a result, some workers can lose their job. Nevertheless, technological change doesn't have to increase overall unemployment, even though some types of workers may temporarily lose their jobs. For instance, in 1800, the majority of British workers were employed in agriculture. Labour-saving technology meant that food could be produced with fewer workers and so some agricultural laborers lost their jobs as farms used more machines. At the same time, however, as jobs were lost in agriculture, new jobs were created in producing machines. In the same way, advances in computers and robots meant that firms could produce manufactured goods with fewer workers. Consequently, the increased productivity in manufactured goods meant that the relative cost fell, and therefore more opportunities for people to work in the service sector emerged.
options: ① Technological progress takes away some jobs, and because it does not create enough new ones, it finally causes more unemployment.
② Technological advancement creates new jobs, but it increases business costs, so overall profits may decline even though unemployment falls.
③ Technological advancement takes away some positions, but by generating new ones throughout the economy, it prevents unemployment from rising.
④ Technological innovation often drives economic growth by creating new industries, but at the same time, it can widen inequality as certain workers are left behind.
⑤ Technological progress increases efficiency and reduces some traditional workplace dangers, but it also creates new kinds of industrial accidents that did not exist before.
explanation: 기술의 발달로 인해 특정 분야의 노동자들이 일자리를 잃는 '기술적 실업'이 발생할 수 있지만, 이것이 반드시 전체적인 실업의 증가로 이어지지는 않는다는 것이 글의 핵심입니다. 기술 혁신은 과거 농업 분야에서 일자리가 줄어든 대신 기계 제조 분야에서 새 일자리가 생겨난 것처럼, 한 분야의 인력 수요를 줄이는 동시에 다른 분야(예: 서비스 부문)에서 새로운 일자리를 창출하기 때문입니다. 따라서 기술 발달이 일부 직책을 없애지만 경제 전반에서 새로운 일자리를 만들어 실업 증가를 막는다는 ③번이 요지로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 기술적 진보는 일부 일자리를 앗아가고, 충분한 새 일자리를 만들어내지 못하기 때문에 결국 더 많은 실업을 야기한다.
② 기술적 발달은 새로운 일자리를 만들어내지만, 기업 비용을 증가시키므로 실업은 감소하더라도 전반적으로는 이익이 감소할 수 있다.
③ 기술적 발달은 일부 직책을 앗아가지만, 경제 전반에 걸쳐 새로운 일자리를 창출함으로써 실업의 증가를 막는다.
④ 기술 혁신은 새로운 산업을 창출하여 경제 성장을 주도하는 경우가 많지만, 동시에 따라잡지 못하는 일부 노동자들이 소외되며 불평등을 악화시킬 수 있다.
⑤ 기술적 진보는 효율을 높이고 일부 전통적인 직장에서의 위험을 제거하지만, 이전에는 없었던 새로운 분야의 산업 재해를 만들어내기도 한다.

question: 6. 다음 밑줄 친 "remote-controls" the reader가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The term "anchoring" was introduced by Roland Barthes who observed that text is often used next to images (his focus was on photographs) to confine meaning. Of all possible literal or implied interpretations an image could elicit, text would point the viewer towards a desired, specific direction. In advertising, as Barthes argues, the symbolic message does not guide identification but interpretation. The viewer is not asked to recognize what they see but to understand why they see it and what it means to them. By combining images with text, advertising produces symbolic meaning that is accurate and specific on the one hand, richer on the other, thus adding depth and eliminating breadth of rational and emotional interpretations. The headline or tagline of an ad directs the reader through the intended meanings of the image, so that the reader avoids some and receives others. It <u>"remote-controls" the reader</u> towards a meaning chosen in advance.
options: ① guides or manipulates the viewer's interpretation
② diminishes the impact of the intended message
③ helps the reader create alternative meanings
④ gives the reader interpretive freedom
⑤ misleads the advertiser's intention
explanation: 본문은 이미지와 함께 쓰이는 텍스트(광고의 헤드라인 등)가 이미지의 의미를 한정하고 독자가 제작자가 의도한 방향으로만 이미지를 해석하도록 유도한다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 독자를 '원격 조정(remote-controls)'한다는 것은 시청자의 해석을 특정한 방향으로 안내하거나 조종한다는 의미입니다.
options_translation: ① 시청자의 해석을 유도하거나 조종한다
② 의도된 메시지의 영향력을 감소시킨다
③ 독자가 대안적인 의미를 창조하도록 돕는다
④ 독자에게 해석의 자유를 부여한다
⑤ 광고주의 의도를 오도한다

question: 7. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [24년 9월 40번]
passage: The concern about how we appear to others can be seen in children, though work by the psychologist Ervin Staub suggests that the effect may vary with age. In a study where children heard another child in distress, young children (kindergarten through second grade) were more likely to help the child in distress when with another child than when alone. But for older children - in fourth and sixth grade - the effect reversed: they were less likely to help a child in distress when they were with a peer than when they were alone. Staub suggested that younger children might feel more comfortable acting when they have the company of a peer, whereas older children might feel more concern about being judged by their peers and fear feeling embarrassed by overreacting. Staub noted that "older children seemed to discuss the distress sounds less and to react to them less openly than younger children." In other words, the older children were deliberately putting on a poker face in front of their peers.
options: ① emotional reactions to distressful situations
② children's tendency to be indifferent to their elders
③ the impact of peer judgment on children's prosocial actions
④ reasons of helping others at any age regardless of social evaluation
⑤ the possibility of alleviating social anxiety through emotional resilience
explanation: 이 글은 심리학자 Ervin Staub의 연구를 인용하여, 아이들이 남에게 어떻게 보이는지에 대한 걱정이 연령에 따라 달라짐을 보여줍니다. 특히 어린 아이들은 또래와 함께 있을 때 더 많이 돕는 경향이 있는 반면, 나이가 든 아이들은 또래의 평가를 의식하여 오히려 덜 돕게 된다는 점을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 주제는 '아이들의 친사회적 행동에 미치는 또래 판단의 영향'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 고통스러운 상황에 대한 감정적 반응
② 아이들이 어른들에게 무관심해지는 경향
③ 아이들의 친사회적 행동에 미치는 또래 판단의 영향
④ 사회적 평가와 상관없이 어떤 연령에서든 타인을 돕는 이유
⑤ 정서적 회복탄력성을 통한 사회적 불안 완화의 가능성

question: 8. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [25년 9월 29번]
passage: All human cultures mark the passing of time by the differences they observe in the world around them. Our choice of which differences to mark depends firstly on what we can observe and secondly on what is important in our lives. How we mark the differences ─ the shapes of our calendars and our rituals ─ depends on the connections we make between those two things. In the agricultural society of pre-modern Europe, where higher latitudes make the seasons easily observable, it was natural to monitor the solar cycle. Conversely, among the largely nomadic peoples of Arabia, for whom seasonal changes were less significant, the lunar calendar was a more sensible choice. That did not make it inevitable that Islam would use a lunar calendar and Roman Christianity a solar one, but political and religious decisions were made from options limited by geography and lifestyle, filtered through tradition.
options: ① Why Islam Did Not Worship the Moon
② How Modern Science Understands Time
③ The Politics of Astronomy in Medieval Europe
④ Nomads and Farmers: A Conflict of Civilizations
⑤ From Sun to Moon: How Societies Mark the Passage of Time
explanation: 이 글은 모든 인류 문화가 주변 세계에서 관찰되는 변화를 통해 시간의 흐름을 표시하며, 그 방식(태양력 또는 태음력 등)은 지리적 조건과 생활 양식에 따라 결정된다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로는 '태양에서 달까지: 사회가 시간의 경과를 표시하는 방법'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 이슬람교가 달을 숭배하지 않은 이유
② 현대 과학이 시간을 이해하는 방식
③ 중세 유럽 천문학의 정치학
④ 유목민과 농경민: 문명의 충돌
⑤ 태양에서 달까지: 사회가 시간의 흐름을 표시하는 방법

question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [25년 9월 39번]
passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend ⓐ<u>themselves</u> to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers of which it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease ⓑ<u>to form</u>, while sufficient fibers remain undamaged for the material not to crack and fall apart. Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to resist being pulled apart, but it can also be torn easily and accurately along the crease if a point of weakness ─ a small, initial tear ─ is opened up. This winning combination of mechanical properties makes ⓒ<u>them</u> possible to assume the shape of any object through creasing and folding ─ hence the art of origami. There are very few materials as good: metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult. Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, ⓓ<u>in which</u> case it lacks the rigidity required of a good wrapping material. So it is its ability to hold a crease while remaining stiff that makes paper uniquely ⓔ<u>suited</u> to this purpose.
explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 문장은 'makes + 목적어 + 목적격 보어' 구조를 가지고 있습니다. 여기서 'to assume the shape...'라는 목적어 부분이 길기 때문에 가목적어 'it'을 사용해야 합니다. 따라서 'them'이 아니라 'it'으로 고쳐야 어법상 적절합니다. ⓐ는 mechanical properties를 가리키는 재귀대명사로 적절하며, ⓑ는 allow의 목적격 보어로 to부정사가 쓰였고, ⓓ는 전치사+관계대명사(in which case)로 문맥상 적합하며, ⓔ는 paper가 purpose에 적합하게 '된' 수동의 의미이므로 분사 형태가 맞습니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The future of work depends on two forces: a harmful substituting force and a helpful complementing one. Many tales have a hero and a villain fighting each other for dominance, but in our story, technology plays both roles at once, (A)[replacing / allocating] workers while simultaneously raising the demand for their efforts elsewhere in the economy. This interaction helps explain why past worries about automation were (B)[plausible / implausible]: our ancestors had predicted the wrong winner in that fight, underestimating quite how powerful the complementing force would prove to be or simply ignoring that factor altogether. It also helps to explain why economists have traditionally been dismissive of the idea of technological unemployment: there appeared to be firm limits to the (C)[complementing / substituting] force, leaving lots of tasks that could not be performed by machines, and a growing demand for human beings to do them instead.
options: ① replacing - plausible - complementing
② allocating - plausible - complementing
③ replacing - implausible - complementing
④ allocating - implausible - substituting
⑤ replacing - implausible - substituting
explanation: (A) 기술이 노동자를 대체하면서(replacing) 동시에 다른 곳에서 수요를 높인다는 문맥이 적절합니다. (B) 조상들이 보완하는 힘을 과소평가하여 틀린 예측을 했으므로, 과거 자동화에 대한 우려가 근거가 없었음(implausible)을 설명해 줍니다. (C) 경제학자들이 기술적 실업에 대해 부정적이었던 이유는 대체하는(substituting) 힘에 한계가 있어 인간이 할 일이 여전히 많다고 보았기 때문입니다.
options_translation: ① 대체하는 - 타당한 - 보완하는
② 할당하는 - 타당한 - 보완하는
③ 대체하는 - 타당하지 않은 - 보완하는
④ 할당하는 - 타당하지 않은 - 대체하는
⑤ 대체하는 - 타당하지 않은 - 대체하는

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
passage: Any new or threatening situation may require us to make decisions and this requires information. So important is communication during a disaster that normal social barriers are often ⓐ<u>lowered</u>. We will talk to strangers in a way we would never consider normally. Even relatively low grade disruption of our life such as a fire drill or a very late train seems to give us the permission to ⓑ<u>break</u> normal etiquette and talk to strangers. The more important an event to a particular public, the ⓒ<u>more</u> detailed and urgent the requirement for news becomes. Without an authoritative source of facts, whether that is a newspaper or trusted broadcast station, rumours often run riot. Rumours ⓓ<u>stop</u> because people believe their group to be in danger and so, although the rumour is unproven, feel they should pass it on. For example, if a worker heard that their employer's business was doing badly and people were going to be made ⓔ<u>redundant</u>, they would pass that information on to colleagues.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 재난 상황이나 위협적인 상황에서 사람들은 집단이 위험에 처해 있다고 믿기 때문에 근거 없는 소문이라도 전달해야 한다고 느낍니다. 따라서 루머가 '멈춘다(stop)'는 표현은 문맥상 어색하며, 루머가 '발생한다' 혹은 '퍼진다(arise/spread)' 등의 표현이 적절합니다.

question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We're naturally wired to organize the world into a(n) ____________. We do this to help make sense of the world, maintain our beliefs, and generally feel better. But when someone infringes on our place in the world and our understanding of how it works, we react without thinking. When someone cuts you off on the highway and road rage kicks in, that's your unconscious mind saying, "Who are you to cut me off?" You're reacting to a threat to your inherent sense of power structure. On the road we are all equals. We're all supposed to play by the same rules. Cutting someone off violates those rules and implies higher status. Or consider when you get frustrated with your kids and end an argument with "Because I said so." (Or the office equivalent: "Because I'm the boss.") In these moments you've stopped thinking and regressed to your biological tendencies of reaffirming the system of ranks.
options: ① hierarchy
② balance
③ network
④ equity
⑤ circle
explanation: 글 마지막 문장에서 'reaffirming the system of ranks(계급 시스템을 재확인하는 것)'가 언급되고, 고속도로에서의 끼어들기가 'higher status(더 높은 지위)'를 나타내는 것이라고 한 것으로 보아 인간은 세상을 위계질서(hierarchy)로 조직하려는 본능이 있다는 내용이므로 ① hierarchy(위계질서)가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 위계질서 (위계 조직)
② 균형
③ 네트워크
④ 형평성
⑤ 원 (순환)

question: 17. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. By "competence," I mean a cluster of qualities: smartness, the ability to get things done, wise decisions, etc. We stand a better chance of doing well at our life tasks if we surround ourselves with people who know what they're doing and have a lot to teach us. But the research evidence is paradoxical: In problem-solving groups, the participants who are considered the most competent and have the best ideas tend not to be the ones who are best liked. Why? One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, those who are too competent make us uncomfortable. They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman - and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison. If this were true, we might like people more if they reveal ___________________________. For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her better if, every once in a while, they screwed up.
options: ① some evidence of fallibility
② their superiority in every aspect
③ unknown secrets of their popularity
④ their friends' weaknesses and faults
⑤ the capacity for further achievements
explanation: 너무 유능한 사람들은 우리를 불편하게 만들거나 비교되어 기분 나쁘게 만들 수 있다는 내용입니다. 마지막 예시에서 뛰어난 친구가 가끔 '실수할 때(screwed up)' 그 사람을 더 좋아할 수 있다고 했으므로, 빈칸에는 '실수할 수 있음(fallibility)의 증거'를 드러낼 때 사람들이 더 좋아하게 된다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 실수할 수 있다는 어떠한 증거
② 모든 면에서의 우월함
③ 그들 인기의 알려지지 않은 비밀
④ 그들 친구들의 약점과 결점
⑤ 추가적인 성취를 위한 능력

question: 19. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Paradoxically, it's uncertainty that makes us feel most alive. Think of events that shake you out of your everyday routine: maybe attending a family wedding, making a big presentation, or going somewhere you've never been. It's on those occasions that time seems to slow down a little, and you feel more fully engaged. The same holds true if the experience is risky, like mountain climbing or parasailing. Your senses are sharper. You notice more. Thanks to the release of a feel-good chemical in the brain called dopamine, you get a greater rush of pleasure from chance encounters with people than planned meetings. Good news, financial rewards, and gifts are more enjoyable if they are surprises. It's why the most popular television shows and movies are the ones _____________________________.
options: ① that tell us exactly what we have expected
② with unexpected plot twists and astonishing endings
③ accurately portraying genuine human emotions in detail
④ illustrating the power of tranquility in this very noisy world
⑤ widely recognized with good reviews and commercial success
explanation: 이 글은 불확실성과 예상치 못한 상황이 우리를 더 활기차게 만들고 즐거움을 준다는 내용입니다. 일상적인 루틴을 벗어난 사건이나 우연한 만남, 서프라이즈 선물이 더 큰 즐거움을 주는 것과 마찬가지로, 가장 인기 있는 TV 쇼나 영화도 관객이 예상하지 못한 반전이나 놀라운 결말을 포함하고 있어야 한다는 논리가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: 우리가 기대했던 것을 정확히 말해주는 것들
예상치 못한 반전과 놀라운 결말을 가진 것들
진정한 인간의 감정을 상세하고 정확하게 묘사하는 것들
매우 시끄러운 세상에서 평온함의 힘을 보여주는 것들
좋은 평판과 상업적 성공으로 널리 인정받는 것들

question: 20. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: "Tactics" is a term drawn from military usage. Strategies are plans of action directing a military force when attacking another, and tactics are responses to conditions on the ground. In this vein, time is imposed on us by our cultures, by the technologies that have regimented time down to the nanosecond, and by its own finite nature and the fact that we're going to live only so long. ␖In response, we must develop tactics for dealing with time and waiting. ␗These aren't tactics to eliminate waiting; instead, these are tactics for teaching us how to learn from the seams. ␘These tactics have the potential to reorient us in profound ways, transforming our perspectives on our wait times. ␙Wasting wait times often leads to emotional and psychological distress including guilt. ␚Such renewed perspectives transform waiting from a burden to a springboard toward things like creativity, social critique, or reflection on our inner state and the state of our relationships.
explanation: 이 글은 시간에 대한 문화를 받아들이고, 기다림의 시간을 단순한 낭비가 아닌 배움과 성찰의 기회로 바꾸는 '전술(tactics)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. ␙(d) 문장은 기다림의 시간을 낭비하는 것이 정서적 고통과 죄책감을 유발한다는 부정적인 측면을 언급하고 있어, 기다림을 긍정적인 도약대로 삼자는 글의 전반적인 흐름과 관계가 없습니다.

question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: People seem to recognize that the arts are cultural activities that draw on (or react against) certain cultural traditions, certain shared understanding, and certain values and ideas that are characteristic of the time and place in which the art is created.
ordered_passages: (A) In describing this view of science, philosopher Hugh Lacey speaks of the belief that there is an underlying order of the world which is simply there to be discovered - the world of pure "fact" stripped of any link with value. The aim of science according to this view is to represent this world of pure "fact", independently of any relationship it might bear contingently to human practices and experiences.(B) In the case of science, however, opinions differ. Some scientists, like the great biologist J. B. S. Haldane, see science in a similar light - as a historical activity that occurs in a particular time and place, and that needs to be understood within that context.(C) Others, however, see science as a purely "objective" pursuit, uninfluenced by the cultural viewpoint and values of those who create it.
explanation: 주어진 글은 예술이 문화적 맥락에 기반함을 설명합니다. (B)에서는 과학에 대해 언급하며, 예술처럼 맥락 속에서 이해해야 한다는 과학자들의 의견을 제시합니다. (C)에서 'Others(다른 이들)'를 통해 과학을 순수하게 객관적인 추구로 보는 상반된 시각을 소개하며, (A)에서 이러한 객관적 과학관(this view of science)을 구체화하여 가치와 분리된 '사실'의 세계를 묘사하는 철학자의 설명을 덧붙이는 흐름이 가장 자연스럽습니다.

question: 26. 다음 밑줄 친 Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage가 글에서 의미하는 바를 한 문장으로 쓰고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: It's often said that those who can't do, teach. It would be more accurate to say that those who can do, can't teach the basics. A great deal of expert knowledge is implicit, not explicit. The further you progress toward mastery, the less conscious awareness you often have of the fundamentals. Experiments show that skilled golfers and wine aficionados have a hard time describing their putting and tasting techniques - even asking them to explain their approaches is enough to interfere with their performance, so they often stay on autopilot. When I first saw an elite diver do four and a half somersaults, I asked how he managed to spin so fast. His answer: "Just go up in a ball." Experts often have an intuitive understanding of a route, but they struggle to clearly express all the steps to take. <u>Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage</u>.
summary_sentence: "<u>Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage</u>" (metaphorically) means when experts try to (A)___________ their skills, despite their deep knowledge, their descriptions are often incomplete or inaccurate because their expertise is rooted in (B)___________ rather than in conscious awareness.
subjective_conditions: • (A), (B) 각각 한 단어로 쓸 것
• 위 지문에 있는 단어를 사용할 수 있음 (필요시 변형 가능)
• 철자 및 어법 오류 당 1점 감점 (의미 전달에 오류가 없을 시 한함)
explanation: 이 글은 전문가들이 자신의 기술을 말로 설명하는 데 어려움을 겪는 이유를 다루고 있습니다. 전문가들의 지식은 암묵적(implicit)이고 직관적(intuitive)이어서, 이를 의식적으로 설명하려고 하면 부정확하거나 불완전할 수 있다는 내용입니다. 요약문의 (A)에는 기술을 '설명하다'라는 의미의 describe나 explain이 적절하며, (B)에는 숙련도가 '직관'에 뿌리를 두고 있다는 의미의 intuition이 적절합니다.

question: 27. 다음 밑줄 친 부분을 글에서 의미하는 바와 같게 다시 쓰려고 한다. 아래 (A)와 같은 뜻이 되도록 (B)의 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: Mirror neurons are the hardware of empathy, and so what would make more sense than to look and see which animals possess these cells? And this is exactly where modern research now stands: all researchers know so far is that apes possess mirror neurons. We still need to test to see which other species are like us in this respect. Scientists often publicly speculate that we can probably expect surprises here, too. They assume that all animals that live in herds or large groups possess similar brain mechanisms, because social units function only if individuals can <u>see things from the perspective of others in the group and feel what they are feeling</u>. I can see a goldfish waving its fin at us. As an animal that travels around in a tightly-knit group, it's on board with this idea ─ or at least swimming alongside the boat.
subjective_conditions: • 위 지문에 있는 단어만을 이용하되, 필요시 변형 가능 (단, mirror neurons는 사용하지 말 것)
• 세 단어로 작성할 것
• 철자 및 어법 오류 당 1점 감점 (의미 전달에 오류가 없을 시 한함)
explanation: 밑줄 친 'see things from the perspective of others in the group and feel what they are feeling(집단 내 타인의 관점에서 상황을 보고 그들이 느끼는 것을 느끼다)'은 지문의 핵심 소재인 '공감(empathy)'의 구체적인 정의입니다. 따라서 이를 동사 형태인 'empathize(공감하다)'를 활용하여 '타인에게 공감하다'라는 의미인 'empathize with others'로 바꾸어 쓸 수 있습니다.

question: 4. 다음 밑줄 친 a consolation prize가 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: When we get an unfavorable outcome, in some ways the last thing we want to hear is that the process was fair. As outraging as the combination of an unfavorable outcome and an unfair process is, this combination also brings with it <u>a consolation prize</u>: the possibility of attributing the bad outcome to something other than ourselves. We may reassure ourselves by believing that our bad outcome had little to do with us and everything to do with the unfair process. If the process is fair, however, we cannot nearly as easily externalize the outcome; we got what we got "fair and square." When the process is fair we believe that our outcome is deserved, which is another way of saying that there must have been something about ourselves (what we did or who we are) that caused the outcome.
options: ① a financial compensation given to those who fail
② a recognition of one's effort despite the final result
③ a moral lesson that teaches us how to accept failure
④ a psychological relief we gain from blaming the process
⑤ an official apology from those responsible for the process
explanation: 이 글은 결과가 좋지 않을 때 과정이 불공정하다면 오히려 그 불행한 결과를 자신이 아닌 외부의 탓(불공정한 과정)으로 돌릴 수 있다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 'a consolation prize(위안이 되는 상)'는 나쁜 결과의 원인을 내가 아닌 공정하지 못한 과정 탓으로 돌림으로써 얻게 되는 심리적 안도감을 의미합니다.
options_translation: ① 실패한 사람들에게 주어지는 금전적 보상
② 최종 결과에도 불구하고 누군가의 노력을 인정해 주는 것
③ 실패를 받아들이는 방법을 가르쳐 주는 도덕적 교훈
④ 과정을 탓함으로써 얻게 되는 심리적 안도감
⑤ 공정하지 못한 과정에 책임이 있는 사람들로부터의 공식적인 사과

question: 5. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Mirror neurons are the hardware of empathy, and so what would make more sense than to look and see which animals possess these cells? And this is exactly where modern research now stands: all researchers know so far is that apes possess mirror neurons. We still need to test to see which other species are like us in this respect. Scientists often publicly speculate that we can probably expect surprises here, too. They assume that all animals that live in herds or large groups possess similar brain mechanisms, because social units function only if individuals can see things from the perspective of others in the group and feel what they are feeling. I can see a goldfish waving its fin at us. As an animal that travels around in a tightly-knit group, it's on board with this idea ─ or at least swimming alongside the boat.
options: ① 공감 능력은 학습을 통해서 발달한다.
② 집단생활은 인지 능력이 뛰어난 동물의 특성이다.
③ 대부분의 동물은 선천적으로 공감 능력을 지니고 있다.
④ 거울 뉴런은 시각 정보를 처리하여 인지 기능을 수행한다.
⑤ 공감 관련 신경세포는 집단생활을 하는 동물 전반에 존재할 수 있다.
explanation: 거울 뉴런(mirror neurons)은 공감의 하드웨어이며, 연구자들은 유인원뿐만 아니라 무리 지어 생활하는 모든 동물이 다른 개체의 관점을 이해하고 느끼는 능력이 필요하므로 비슷한 뇌 기제(거울 뉴런)를 가지고 있을 것이라고 가정한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 요지는 ⑤번입니다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: In today's information age, in many companies and on many teams, the objective is no longer error prevention and replicability. On the contrary, it's creativity, speed, and keenness. In the industrial era, the goal was to minimize variation. But in creative companies today, maximizing variation is more essential. In these situations, the biggest risk isn't making a mistake or losing consistency; it's failing to attract top talent, to invent new products, or to change direction quickly when the environment shifts. Consistency and repeatability are more likely to suppress fresh thinking than to bring your company profit. A lot of little mistakes, while sometimes painful, help the organization learn quickly and are a critical part of the innovation cycle. In these situations, rules and process are no longer the best answer. In order to thrive in a changing environment, choose speed and fresh thinking instead of error prevention, and _______________________________.
options: ① treat predictability as the ultimate goal
② value individual adaptability over regidity
③ choose conformity at the cost of creativity
④ get rid of a culture that emphasizes loyalty
⑤ highlight hierarchy as the source of strength
explanation: 오늘날의 정보화 시대와 창의적인 기업 환경에서는 오류 방지나 일관성보다는 창의성, 속도, 신선한 사고가 중요하다고 강조하고 있습니다. 일관성과 반복성은 새로운 사고를 억제할 수 있으므로, 변화하는 환경에서 번성하기 위해서는 오류 방지 대신 속도와 신선한 사고를 택하고, 경직성(rigidity)보다는 개인의 적응성(adaptability)을 가치 있게 여겨야 한다는 흐름이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 예측 가능성을 궁극적인 목표로 대우하라
② 경직성보다 개인의 적응성을 가치 있게 여겨라
③ 창의성을 희생하면서 순응을 선택하라
④ 충성심을 강조하는 문화를 없애라
⑤ 계층 구조를 힘의 원천으로 강조하라

question: 9. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The traditional bank manager in the 1950s was usually a respected pillar of the community, a cautious, careful sort of person who probably went to bed early and didn't drink too much. But from the 1970s a new kind of banker appeared ─ loud, flashy, and arrogant. These bankers loved taking big risks. They wanted to get rich quick and blow their money on fast cars and expensive champagne. They made their money through what's called 'speculation'. Normally, people buy things because they want to use them, such as wheat to make bread and petrol to run the car. But when people speculate, they buy things even when they have no interest in using them. They might buy a load of wheat ________________________________ when a drought is predicted in wheat-growing areas. If their guess is right, they later sell the wheat for a profit.
options: ① to fulfill an immediate personal need
② because they anticipate a rise in price
③ because they believe it has no risk involved
④ as a long-term investment for production purposes
⑤ to ensure sufficient wheat supply for use in emergency
explanation: 지문은 '투기(speculation)'에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 투기하는 사람들은 실제 사용 목적이 아니라, 가격이 오를 것을 예상하여 물건을 삽니다. 밀 재배 지역에 가뭄이 예상될 때 밀을 대량으로 사는 이유는 가격 상승을 예상하기 때문이며, 나중에 이익을 남기고 팔기 위함입니다.
options_translation: ① 즉각적인 개인적 필요를 충족시키기 위해
② 가격 상승을 예상하기 때문에
③ 위험이 전혀 관련되어 있지 않다고 믿기 때문에
④ 생산 목적을 위한 장기 투자로서
⑤ 비상시 사용을 위한 충분한 밀 공급을 확보하기 위해

question: 10. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We're naturally wired to organize the world into a hierarchy. We do this to help make sense of the world, maintain our beliefs, and generally feel better. But when someone infringes on our place in the world and our understanding of how it works, we react without thinking. When someone cuts you off on the highway and road rage kicks in, that's your unconscious mind saying, "Who are you to cut me off?" You're reacting to a threat to your inherent sense of hierarchy. On the road we are all equals. We're all supposed to play by the same rules. Cutting someone off violates those rules and implies higher status. Or consider when you get frustrated with your kids and end an argument with "Because I said so." (Or the office equivalent: "Because I'm the boss.") In these moments you've stopped thinking and ______________________________________.
options: ① ignored the social rules that govern hierarchy
② relied on deliberate strategies for promoting equality
③ returned to innate impulses for maintaining the hierarchy
④ regressed to conscious decisions for challenging the hierarchy
⑤ reacted based on conscious thought rather than instinctive drives
explanation: 인간은 세상을 위계질서로 조직하려는 타고난 성향이 있습니다. 누군가 도로에서 끼어들거나 자녀에게 '내가 그렇게 말했으니까'라고 권위를 내세우는 상황은, 평등해야 할 규칙이 깨지거나 자신의 지위가 위협받을 때 무의식적으로 반응하는 것입니다. 이러한 순간에는 사고를 멈추고 위계질서를 유지하려는 타고난 충동으로 돌아가게 됩니다.
options_translation: ① 위계질서를 지배하는 사회적 규칙을 무시했다
② 평등을 증진하기 위한 계획적인 전략에 의존했다
③ 위계질서를 유지하려는 타고난 충동으로 돌아갔다
④ 위계질서에 도전하기 위한 의식적인 결정으로 퇴행했다
