question: 12. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It would seem obvious that the more competent someone is, the more we will like that person. By "competence," I mean a cluster of qualities: smartness, the ability to get things done, wise decisions, etc. We stand a better chance of doing well at our life tasks if we surround ourselves with people who know what they're doing and have a lot to teach us. But the research evidence is paradoxical: In problem-solving groups, the participants who are considered the most competent and have the best ideas tend not to be the ones who are best liked. Why? One possibility is that, although we like to be around competent people, those who are too competent make us uncomfortable. They may seem unapproachable, distant, superhuman - and make us look bad (and feel worse) by comparison. If this were true, we might like people more if they reveal some evidence of fallibility. For example, if your friend is a brilliant mathematician, superb athlete, and gourmet cook, you might like him or her better if, every once in a while, they screwed up.
options: ① universal preference for high competence
② emotional intelligence as sole popularity factor
③ superiority of group harmony over competence
④ the irony of ability and popularity in human relationships
⑤ competence in its modern sense, which includes social skills
explanation: 이 글은 유능한 사람을 좋아할 것 같다는 일반적인 통념과 달리, 실제로는 너무 유능한 사람이 타인에게 불편함을 주어 덜 선호될 수 있다는 역설적인 연구 결과를 설명하고 있습니다. 사람들은 완벽해 보이는 사람보다 때로는 실수(fallibility)를 보여주는 사람에게 더 호감을 느낀다는 내용을 담고 있으므로, 인간관계에서 능력과 인기 사이의 아이러니를 다룬 ④번이 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 높은 유능함에 대한 보편적인 선호
② 인기 요인으로서의 유일한 정서적 지능
③ 유능함보다 집단 조화의 우월성
④ 인간관계에서 능력과 인기의 아이러니
⑤ 사회적 기술을 포함하는 현대적 의미의 유능함

question: 13. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Once a nail is hammered in, it is friction that holds it in place. Friction is the force that arises when two surfaces are sliding, or trying to slide, against each other. If you try to pull apart two blocks of wood that have been nailed together, the wood fibers grip the shaft of the nail. The nail feels a force trying to rip it apart along its length, and we call that force tension. Your experiment can now fail in one of two ways ─ either the nail stretches and splits in half because the tension force is too large for the nail, or the nail comes loose because the friction force is overcome. The force it would take to stretch the nail is much larger than the friction forces on the surface, so we don't have to worry too much about the former. It's the friction with which we need to concern ourselves.
options: ① How Forces Work on a Nailed Connection
② What Happens When a Nail Splits in Half?
③ Why Friction Alone Cannot Explain a Nail's Strength
④ Durability of Nails: Secrets of Long-Lasting Strength
⑤ Tension: The Main Factor in Determining the Strength of Materials
explanation: 이 글은 못이 박혔을 때 작용하는 두 가지 주요 힘인 마찰력(friction)과 인장력(tension)에 대해 설명하고 있습니다. 특히 못이 제자리에 있도록 유지하는 것은 마찰력이며, 못이 빠지거나 끊어지는 원리를 물리적 힘의 관점에서 다루고 있으므로 '못으로 연결된 부분에 힘이 작용하는 방식'을 의미하는 ①번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 못으로 연결된 부분에 힘이 작용하는 방식
② 못이 반으로 쪼개질 때 어떤 일이 일어나는가?
③ 왜 마찰력만으로는 못의 강도를 설명할 수 없는가?
④ 못의 내구성: 오래 지속되는 강도의 비밀
⑤ 인장력: 재료의 강도를 결정하는 주요 요인

question: 14. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Any new or threatening situation may require us to make decisions and this requires information. So important is communication during a disaster that normal social barriers are often lowered. We will talk to strangers in a way we would never consider normally. Even relatively low grade disruption of our life such as a fire drill or a very late train seems to give us the permission to break normal etiquette and talk to strangers. The more important an event to a particular public, the more detailed and urgent the requirement for news becomes. Without an authoritative source of facts, whether that is a newspaper or trusted broadcast station, rumours often run riot. Rumours start because people believe their group to be in danger and so, although the rumour is unproven, feel they should pass it on. For example, if a worker heard that their employer's business was doing badly and people were going to be made redundant, they would pass that information on to colleagues.
options: ① Lessons Learned from Historical Rumors
② The Role of Social Media in Spreading Panic
③ Economic Impacts of Disaster Communication
④ Workplace Dynamics Under Stressful Conditions
⑤ Crisis Conversations: How Emergencies Reshape Social Norms
explanation: 이 글은 위협적인 상황이나 재난 상황에서 정보에 대한 요구가 높아짐에 따라 평소의 사회적 장벽이 낮아지고 낯선 사람과도 대화를 나누게 되는 현상을 설명하고 있습니다. 또한 권위 있는 정보원이 없을 때 루머가 확산되는 방식도 다루고 있습니다. 즉, 비상 상황이 어떻게 사회적 규범(에티켓, 장벽 등)을 재구성하고 대화를 유도하는지를 다루고 있으므로 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 역사적 루머로부터 얻은 교훈
② 공포를 확산시키는 데 있어서 소셜 미디어의 역할
③ 재난 의사소통의 경제적 영향
④ 스트레스 상황에서의 직장 내 역학 관계
⑤ 위기 상황의 대화: 비상 사태가 사회적 규범을 재구성하는 방식

question: 16. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Mental development consists of individuals increasingly mastering social codes and signals themselves, which they can master only in social situations with the support of more competent individuals, typically adults. (A) In this sense, mental development consists of internalizing social patterns and gradually becoming a responsible actor among other responsible actors. (B) In Denmark, the age of criminal responsibility is 15 years, which means that we then say that people have developed sufficient mental maturity to be accountable for their actions at this point. (C) And at the age of 18 people are given the right to vote and are thereby formally included in the basic democratic process. (D) I do not know whether these age boundaries are optimal. (E) Therefore, having formal limits for responsibility from a specific age that apply to everyone is a somewhat questionable practice. But the question, of course, is whether it can be done any differently.
insertion_sentence: It treats, however, that mental development takes place at different rates for different individuals, and depends especially on the social and family environment they have been given.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 정신적 발달이 개인마다 다른 속도로 일어나며 환경에 의존한다는 점을 명시하고 있습니다. (D)까지는 덴마크의 법적 연령 기준을 설명하고 있고, (E) 뒤에서 '모든 사람에게 적용되는 특정 연령의 공식적 제한을 두는 것이 의문스러운 관행이다'라고 결론짓는 논리적 근거가 바로 개인별 발달 속도의 차이입니다. 따라서 (E)에 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The future of work depends on two forces: a harmful substituting force and a helpful complementing one. Many tales have a hero and a villain fighting each other for dominance, but in our story, technology plays both roles at once, displacing workers while simultaneously raising the demand for their efforts elsewhere in the economy. This interaction helps explain why past worries about automation were misplaced: our ancestors had predicted the wrong winner in that fight, underestimating quite how powerful the complementing force would prove to be or simply ignoring that factor altogether. It also helps to explain why economists have traditionally been dismissive of the idea of technological unemployment: there appeared to be firm limits to the substituting force, leaving lots of tasks that could not be performed by machines, and a growing demand for human beings to do them instead.
summary_sentence: Technology has both replaced and complemented workers, but historically the complementary role has (A)___________, helping to (B)___________ fears that technological progress will lead to job loss.
options: ① dominated / disprove
② prevailed / prove
③ led / prove
④ yielded / disprove
⑤ surrendered / disregard
explanation: 지문은 기술이 노동을 대체하기도 하지만 보완하기도 하며, 역사적으로 보완하는 힘이 매우 강력했기 때문에 자동화에 대한 과거의 우려가 잘못된 것(misplaced)이었다고 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 보완적 역할이 우세했다는 의미의 dominated가 적절하며, (B)에는 기술 진보가 실업을 유발한다는 공포가 틀렸음을 입증(disprove)했다는 내용이 와야 합니다.
options_translation: ① 지배했다 / 틀렸음을 입증하다
② 우세했다 / 증명하다
③ 이끌었다 / 증명하다
④ 굴복했다 / 틀렸음을 입증하다
⑤ 항복했다 / 무시하다

question: 18. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Over the last few centuries, humanity's collective prosperity has skyrocketed, as technological progress has made us far wealthier than ever before. To share out those riches, almost all societies have settled upon the market mechanism, rewarding people in various ways for the work that they do and the things that they own. But rising inequality, itself often driven by technology, has started to put that mechanism under strain. Today, markets already provide immense rewards to some people but leave many others with very little. And now, technological unemployment threatens to become a more radical version of the same story, taking place in the particular market we rely upon the most: the labor market. As that market begins to break down, more and more people will be in danger of not receiving a share of society's prosperity at all.
summary_sentence: While technological progress has increased wealth, it has also widened (A)___________, and with technological unemployment threatening the labor market, many people are likely to (B)___________ from society's prosperity despite markets traditionally distributing rewards.
options: ① stability ...... be excluded
② imbalance ...... benefit
③ poverty ...... learn
④ disparity ...... be left out
⑤ conflict ...... be protected
explanation: 이 글은 기술 발전이 인류의 번영을 가져왔으나, 기술로 인해 발생하는 불평등이 기존의 시장 분배 메커니즘을 위협하고 있음을 설명합니다. 특히 노동 시장의 기술적 실업 문제로 인해 많은 사람들이 사회적 번영의 혜택을 받지 못할 위험에 처해 있다고 말합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 기술 발전에 따른 불평등의 심화를 의미하는 'disparity(격차)', (B)에는 번영에서 소외되는 상황을 의미하는 'be left out(소외되다)'이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 안정성 ...... 제외되다
② 불균형 ...... 혜택을 입다
③ 가난 ...... 배우다
④ 격차 ...... 소외되다
⑤ 갈등 ...... 보호받다

question: 19. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: People usually think of the arts as cultural activities that are shaped by certain traditions, common ideas, and shared values of the time and place where the art appears. But when it comes to science, people disagree. ⓐSome scientists, like the famous biologist J. B. S. Haldane, believe that science should also be seen this way: as a historical activity that takes place in a specific context and must be understood within it. ⓑThat's why modern science often relies on independent institutions to guarantee the objectivity of its findings. ⓒOthers, however, argue that science is a purely "objective" activity, not influenced by the culture or values of the scientists. ⓓPhilosopher Hugh Lacey describes this second view by saying that many believe there is an order in the world that simply exists to be discovered separate from human values. ⓔAccording to this view, the goal of science is to represent these pure facts, without considering any connection they may have to human life or experience.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 과학이 예술처럼 특정 문화적 맥락의 영향을 받는지, 아니면 완전히 객관적인 활동인지에 대한 두 가지 상반된 관점을 설명하고 있습니다. ⓐ는 과학이 역사적 맥락 내에서 이해되어야 한다는 관점을, ⓒ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 과학이 객관적이고 가치 중립적인 활동이라는 관점을 설명합니다. 반면 ⓑ는 현대 과학이 객관성을 보장하기 위해 독립적인 기관에 의존한다는 내용으로, 과학의 속성에 대한 본질적인 관점 차이를 다루는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

question: 20. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The first human beings probably evolved in tropical regions where survival was possible without clothing.
ordered_passages: (A) Not just their bodies, but their brains also would have evolved with an increased energy consumption. The brain needs lots of energy to grow. As their diet expanded, hominids could physically and intellectually expand their territory.

(B) They probably had very dark skin because lighter skin would have offered little protection against the sun's intense rays. There is a debate about whether these people spread into other parts of the world or, instead, whether people developed independently in various parts of the world. Whichever the case, it is believed that in time they became capable of spreading out from Africa, eventually to most of the world.

(C) It is likely that their physical characteristics changed. For instance, early hominids probably did not walk upright, but when they developed that ability, they could travel more efficiently. More important, perhaps, was their development of tool making. With tools, they could hunt other animals, so they could consume more protein and fat than their low-energy vegetarian diet would have provided.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 초기 인류가 옷 없이 생존 가능한 열대 지역에서 진화했음을 언급합니다. (B)는 그들의 신체적 특징(어두운 피부)과 아프리카에서 전 세계로 퍼져나갔을 가능성을 설명하여 주어진 문장에 바로 이어집니다. (C)는 이동 능력의 향상(직립 보행)과 도구 제작을 통한 식단 변화를 다루며 (B)의 '확산' 가능성을 뒷받침합니다. (A)는 식단 확장 결과 뇌가 진화하고 영토를 확장하게 되었다는 내용으로, (C)의 도구 제작 및 식단 변화(단백질 섭취 증가)에 이어지는 결과이므로 (B)-(C)-(A) 순서가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 21. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Einstein suggested that a huge mass like the Sun causes space-time to bend, an idea not addressed in Newton's system. This bending explains the effect called gravitational lensing, where light coming from distant stars seems to be displaced when it passes close to a massive body.
ordered_passages: (A) Yet, the solar eclipse of 1919 gave scientists a rare chance to observe it directly. At that moment, the stars near the Sun appeared to be shifted from their normal night-sky positions.
(B) Usually, this bending of starlight goes unnoticed during the daytime, since the intense brightness of the Sun completely blocks the faint light emitted by distant stars.
(C) The displacement was far greater than Newton's theory predicted, but it coincided exactly with Einstein's calculations, giving clear evidence for his revolutionary idea.
explanation: 아인슈타인의 시공간 굴절 이론(중력 렌즈 효과)이 제시된 도입글 뒤에, (B) 평상시 낮에는 태양 빛 때문에 이 굴절 현상을 관찰할 수 없다는 일반적인 상황이 옵니다. (A) 그러나 1919년 일식이 이를 직접 관찰할 기회를 제공했고 태양 주변 별들의 위치가 어긋나 보였다는 관찰 사례가 이어집니다. (C) 마지막으로 이 어긋남이 뉴턴의 예측보다 컸으나 아인슈타인의 계산과 일치하여 그의 이론에 증거를 제공했다는 결론으로 마무리됩니다. 따라서 정답은 (B)-(A)-(C)입니다.

question: 22. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Everything in the world exists on a continuum, whether in speed, size, or any other possible descriptor you could think of. Still, we create and mindlessly adopt sharp distinctions, and those distinctions change lives far more dramatically than ⓐ<u>slight</u> differences ever do. Indeed, all differences are arbitrary, but drawing ⓑ<u>firm</u> boundaries between categories hides this arbitrariness and can be severely damaging. I call this ⓒ<u>consequent</u> damage "the borderline effect." The examples are endless. Someone's IQ is 69 and someone else's is 70 ─ but only the score of 70 is deemed to be ⓓ<u>beyond</u> the range of normal. We don't have to be statisticians to know there is not a meaningful difference between 69 and 70. Yet once the person with the ⓔ<u>lesser</u> score is labeled "cognitively impaired," his or her life will unfold differently than the person with a one-point advantage.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 문맥상 IQ 69인 사람은 '인지적 장애'로 분류되고 70인 사람은 '정상' 범위에 있는 것으로 간주된다는 내용입니다. 따라서 ⓓ의 beyond(범위를 넘어서는, 벗어난)는 70이 정상 범위 '안에' 있다는 맥락에 맞지 않습니다. within(안에) 혹은 at the threshold of(문턱에)와 같은 표현이 적절합니다.

question: 23. 다음 글의 내용을 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: All human cultures mark the passing of time by the differences they observe in the world around them. Our choice of which differences to mark depends firstly on what we can observe and secondly on what is important in our lives. How we mark the differences ─ the shapes of our calendars and our rituals ─ depends on the connections we make between those two things. In the agricultural society of pre-modern Europe, where higher latitudes make the seasons easily observable, it was natural to monitor the solar cycle. Conversely, among the largely nomadic peoples of Arabia, for whom seasonal changes were less significant, the lunar calendar was a more sensible choice. That did not make it inevitable that Islam would use a lunar calendar and Roman Christianity a solar one, but political and religious decisions were made from options limited by geography and lifestyle, filtered through tradition.
summary_sentence: Human calendars and rituals are shaped by (A)__________ of natural cycles and the (B)__________ each culture places on life needs.
subjective_conditions: (A), (B) 모두 지문에 있는 단어를 활용할 것 (형태 변형 가능)
(A), (B) 각각 1단어로 작성할 것
※ 조건 위반, 철자 오류, 문법 오류 시 각각 1점 감점함.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 인간의 달력과 의례는 자연 주기에서 관찰되는 것(observe)과 삶에서 중요한 것(important/significant)에 따라 결정됩니다. 요약문의 빈칸 (A)는 전치사 by 뒤에 명사형이 와야 하므로 observe의 명사형인 observation이 적절하며, (B) 역시 정관사 the 뒤에 명사형이 와야 하므로 importance 또는 significance가 적절합니다.

question: 24. 다음 글을 읽고 anchoring의 정의를 완성하되, 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말을 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: The term "anchoring" was introduced by Roland Barthes who observed that text is often used next to images (his focus was on photographs) to confine meaning. Of all possible literal or implied interpretations an image could elicit, text would point the viewer towards a desired, specific direction. In advertising, as Barthes argues, the symbolic message does not guide identification but interpretation. The viewer is not asked to recognize what they see but to understand why they see it and what it means to them. By combining images with text, advertising produces symbolic meaning that is accurate and specific on the one hand, richer on the other, thus adding depth and eliminating breadth of rational and emotional interpretations. The headline or tagline of an ad directs the reader through the intended meanings of the image, so that the reader avoids some and receives others. It "remote-controls" the reader towards a meaning chosen in advance.
summary_sentence: Anchoring is a technique where text guides the viewer to a specific (A)__________ of an image, fixing its (B)__________ by precisely defining the symbolic message and (C)__________ other interpretations.
subjective_conditions: (A)~(C): 각각 한 단어로 답하시오.
지문에 있는 단어를 사용해도, 사용하지 않아도 되며, 필요하다면 형태를 변형할 수 있음.
※ 조건 위반, 철자 오류, 문법 오류 시 각각 1점 감점함.
answer: (A) interpretation (또는 understanding / meaning)(B) meaning (또는 message)(C) limiting (또는 restriction / narrowing / controlling)
explanation: 이 글은 롤랑 바르트가 제시한 'anchoring(정박)' 개념을 설명하고 있습니다. 텍스트가 이미지 옆에 쓰여 이미지의 모호한 의미를 특정한 방향으로 고정(confine)하고 제한한다는 내용입니다. 따라서 (A)에는 이미지가 끌어낼 수 있는 여러 가지 '해석(interpretation)' 중 하나로 유도한다는 내용이, (B)에는 이미지의 '의미(meaning)'를 고정한다는 내용이, (C)에는 다른 해석들을 '제한(limiting)'하거나 배제한다는 내용이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.

question: 25. 다음 글의 요지를 <조건>에 맞게 쓰시오.
passage: Paradoxically, it's uncertainty that makes us feel most alive. Think of events that shake you out of your everyday routine: maybe attending a family wedding, making a big presentation, or going somewhere you've never been. It's on those occasions that time seems to slow down a little, and you feel more fully engaged. The same holds true if the experience is risky, like mountain climbing or parasailing. Your senses are sharper. You notice more. Thanks to the release of a feel-good chemical in the brain called dopamine, you get a greater rush of pleasure from chance encounters with people than planned meetings. Good news, financial rewards, and gifts are more enjoyable if they are surprises. It's why the most popular television shows and movies are the ones with unexpected plot twists and astonishing endings.
subjective_conditions: life, and, make를 사용할 것 (형태 변형 불가)
지문에 있는 단어만 사용할 것 (형태 변형 가능)
10단어 이내의 문장으로 작성할 것
※ 조건 위반, 철자 오류, 문법 오류 시 각각 1점 감점함.
answer: Uncertainty and surprises make our life more enjoyable.
explanation: 지문은 불확실성(uncertainty)과 예기치 못한 놀라움(surprises)이 우리를 더 살아있게 느끼게 하고 즐거움을 준다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 도파민의 분비와 관련하여 계획된 만남보다 우연한 만남이, 예상 가능한 결말보다 반전이 있는 이야기가 더 즐겁다는 사례를 제시합니다. 조건에 맞춰 10단어 이내로 작성하면 '불확실성과 놀라움이 우리의 삶을 더 즐겁게 만든다'는 문장이 적절합니다. (다른 정답 후보: Unexpected occasions make our life more enjoyable.)

question: 3. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The brain is a high-energy consumer of glucose, which is its fuel. Although the brain accounts for merely 3 percent of a person's body weight, it consumes 20 percent of the available fuel. Your brain can't store fuel, however, so it has to "pay as it goes." Since your brain is incredibly adaptive, it economizes its fuel resources. Thus, during a period of high stress, it shifts away from the analysis of the nuances of a situation to a singular and fixed focus on the stressful situation at hand. You don't sit back and speculate about the meaning of life when you are stressed. Instead, you devote all your energy to trying to figure out what action to take. Sometimes, however, this shift from the higher-thinking parts of the brain to the automatic and reflexive parts of the brain can lead you to do something too quickly, without thinking.*glucose: 포도당
options: ① the brain's adaptability in using energy depending on the situation
② the brain's ability to process information at an amazing speed
③ the brain's limited capacity in analyzing difficult situations
④ brain superiority in terms of quantity rather than quality
⑤ problems with brain functions for overcoming stress
explanation: 뇌는 에너지를 많이 소모하며 저장이 불가능하기 때문에 상황에 따라 에너지를 효율적으로 사용하는 적응력을 발휘합니다. 특히 스트레스 상황에서는 정밀한 분석보다는 당면한 문제에 집중하도록 에너지 자원을 이동시킨다는 내용이 핵심입니다.

question: 4. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The "jolt" of caffeine does wear off. Caffeine is removed from your system by an enzyme within your liver, which gradually degrades it over time. Based in large part on genetics, some people have a more efficient version of the enzyme that degrades caffeine, allowing the liver to rapidly clear it from the bloodstream. These rare individuals can drink an espresso with dinner and fall fast asleep at midnight without a problem. Others, however, have a slower-acting version of the enzyme. It takes far longer for their system to eliminate the same amount of caffeine. As a result, they are very sensitive to caffeine's effects. One cup of tea or coffee in the morning will last much of the day, and should they have a second cup, even early in the afternoon, they will find it difficult to fall asleep in the evening. Aging also alters the speed of caffeine clearance: the older we are, the longer it takes our brain and body to remove caffeine, and thus the more sensitive we become in later life to caffeine's sleep-disrupting influence.*jolt: 충격 **enzyme: 효소
options: ① Caffeine Sensitivity: The Role of Genetics and Age
② How Does Your Body Eliminate Caffeine?
③ Why Caffeine Interferes with Sleep
④ The Advantages of Fast Caffeine Metabolism
⑤ Caffeine Clearance: Not a Genetic and Age-Related Process
explanation: 이 글은 카페인이 간의 효소에 의해 제거되는 과정을 설명하면서, 유전적 요인에 따라 효소의 효율성이 달라져 카페인 민감도가 사람마다 다름을 설명합니다. 또한 노화가 진행됨에 따라 카페인 제거 속도가 느려져 수면 방해 효과에 더 민감해진다는 점을 언급하고 있습니다. 따라서 제목으로 '카페인 민감도: 유전과 연령의 역할'이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 카페인 민감도: 유전과 연령의 역할
② 신체는 어떻게 카페인을 제거하는가?
③ 왜 카페인은 수면을 방해하는가
④ 빠른 카페인 대사의 장점

question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Architects might say a machine can never design an innovative or impressive building because a computer cannot be "creative." Yet consider the Elbphilharmonie, new concert hall in Hamburg, ①<u>which</u> contains a remarkably beautiful auditorium composed of ten thousand interlocking acoustic panels. It is the type of space that instinctively leads one ②<u>to think</u> that only a human ─ and a human with a remarkably refined creative sensibility, at that ─ could design something so aesthetically impressive. Yet the auditorium, in fact, ③<u>designed</u> algorithmically, using a technique known as "parametric design." The architects supplied the system with a set of criteria, and it produced a range of possible designs for the architects to choose from. Similar software ④<u>has been employed</u> to create lightweight bicycle frames, sturdier chairs, and much more. Are these systems operating "creatively"? No, they are using lots of processing power to blindly generate varied possible designs, ⑤<u>functioning</u> in a very different way from a human being.*aesthetically: 미적으로 **sturdy: 튼튼한, 견고한
explanation: ③ designed → was designed: 문장의 주어인 the auditorium에 걸리는 동사 자리이며, 강당은 설계되는 대상이므로 수동태(was designed)가 적절하다.

question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: If cooking is as central to human identity, biology, and culture as the biological anthropologist Richard Wrangham suggests, it stands to reason that the decrease of cooking in our time ①<u>would have</u> severe results for modern life, and so it has. Are they all bad? Not at all. The outsourcing of much of the work of cooking to corporations has relieved women of what has conventionally been their sole duty for feeding the family, making it ②<u>simpler</u> for them to work beyond the home and have careers. It has headed off many of the domestic conflicts that such a large shift in gender roles and family dynamics ③<u>was</u> bound to spark. It has relieved other stresses in the household, including longer workdays and over-scheduled children, and ④<u>spared</u> us time that we can now invest in other endeavors. It has also enabled us to broaden our diets considerably, making it possible even for people with no cooking talents and little funds ⑤<u>savoring</u> a whole different cuisine. All that's needed is a microwave.
explanation: ⑤ savoring → to savor: 앞의 구조가 making it possible(가목적어 it)이므로, 'even for people...'은 의미상의 주어이고, 그 뒤는 진목적어가 와야 하는 자리이므로 to부정사 형태인 to savor가 와야 한다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: A typical soap opera generates an abstract world, where a highly complex web of relationships connects fictional characters that exist first only in the minds of the program's creators and are then ①<u>reimagined</u> in the minds of the viewer. If you were to think about how much human psychology, law, and even everyday physics the viewer must know in order to follow and speculate about the plot, you would discover it is ②<u>significant</u> ─ at least as much as the knowledge required to follow and speculate about a piece of modern mathematics, and in most cases, much more. Yet viewers follow soap operas ③<u>easily</u>. How are they able to cope with such abstraction? Because, of course, the abstraction is built on an extremely ④<u>recognizable</u> framework. The characters in a soap opera and the relationships between them are ⑤<u>unlike</u> the real people and relationships we experience every day. The abstraction of a soap opera is only a step removed from the real world. The mental "training" required to follow a soap opera is provided by our everyday lives.*soap opera: 드라마, 연속극
options: ① reimagined (재상상되는)
② significant (상당한/중요한)
③ easily (쉽게)
④ recognizable (인식 가능한)
⑤ unlike (~와 다른)
explanation: 드라마의 세계가 고도의 추상성을 띠고 있음에도 시청자들이 쉽게 이해하는 이유는, 드라마 속 인물과 관계가 우리가 매일 겪는 실제 사람과 관계와 '매우 닮았기(very much like)' 때문입니다. 바로 다음 문장에서 드라마의 추상성은 실제 세계에서 겨우 한 걸음 떨어져 있을 뿐이라고 설명하고 있으므로, '다르다'는 의미의 ⑤ unlike는 문맥상 적절하지 않으며 '유사하다'는 의미의 어휘로 고쳐야 합니다.
options_translation: ① reimagined (재상상되는)
② significant (상당한/중요한)
③ easily (쉽게)
④ recognizable (인식 가능한)

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: If you drive down a busy street, you will find many competing businesses, often right next to one another. For example, in most places a consumer in search of a quick meal has many choices, and more fast-food restaurants ①<u>appear</u> all the time. These competing firms advertise heavily. The temptation is to perceive advertising as ②<u>increasing</u> a product's price without any benefit to the consumer. Yet, this ③<u>understanding</u> doesn't account for why companies advertise. In markets where competitors sell slightly differentiated products, advertising enables firms to inform their customers about new products and services. Yes, costs ④<u>rise</u>, but consumers also gain information to help make purchasing decisions. Consumers also benefit from ⑤<u>additional</u> diversity, and we all get a product that's pretty close to our vision of a perfect good-and no other market structure delivers that outcome.
options: ① appear (나타나다)
② increasing (높이는)
③ understanding (이해/관점)
④ rise (오르다)
⑤ additional (추가적인)
explanation: 앞 문장에서 광고를 소비자에게 혜택 없이 제품의 가격만 높이는 부정적인 것으로 간주하기 쉽다고 말했습니다. 따라서 이러한 '관점' 내지는 '오해'는 기업이 광고를 하는 실제 이유를 설명하지 못한다는 흐름이 되어야 합니다. 문맥상 단순한 이해(understanding)보다는 오해(misconception) 혹은 비판적인 견해(view) 등의 어휘가 쓰이는 것이 더 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① appear (나타나다)

question: 15. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: There is little doubt that we are driven by the sell-by date. Once an item is past that date it goes into the waste stream, further increasing its carbon footprint. Remember those items have already travelled hundreds of miles to reach the shelves and once they go into waste they start a new carbon mile journey. But we all _______________________________; those raised during the Second World War are frequently dismissive of the dreadful waste they believe such caution fosters. The manufacturer of the food has a view when making or growing something that by the time the product reaches the shelves it has already been travelling for so many days and possibly many miles. The manufacturer then decides that a product can reasonably be consumed within say 90 days and 90 days minus so many days for travelling gives the sell-by date. But whether it becomes toxic is something each individual can decide. It would seem to make sense not to buy large packs of perishable goods but non-perishable items may become cost-effective.*sell-by date: 판매 유효 기한
options: ① essentially keep exact sell-by dates
② believe sell-by dates of non-perishable items
③ agree with sell-by dates of travelled products
④ make our own assessment about sell-by dates
⑤ question the quality and expiration dates of items
explanation: 이 글은 판매 유효 기한(sell-by date)이 실제 유독성 여부보다는 제조사의 유통 과정을 고려한 계산에 가깝다는 점을 설명합니다. 빈칸 문장 이후에 2차 세계 대전 세대는 유통 기한에 회의적이라는 예시와 각 개인이 독성 여부를 결정할 수 있다는 내용이 이어지므로, 빈칸에는 사람들이 유통 기한에 대해 독자적인 판단을 내린다는 내용이 적절합니다.
options_translation: 본질적으로 정확한 판매 유효 기한을 준수한다
비부패성 품목의 판매 유효 기한을 믿는다
이동 과정을 거친 제품의 판매 유효 기한에 동의한다
판매 유효 기한에 대해 우리 자신의 평가를 내린다

question: 16. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?
passage: It's remarkable that positive fantasies help us relax to such an extent that it shows up in physiological tests. ⓐIf you want to unwind, you can take some deen breaths, get a massage, or go for a walk─but you can also try simply closing your eyes and fantasizing about some future outcome that you might enjoy. ⓑBut when your objective is to make your wish a reality, the last thing you want to be is relaxed. ⓒYou want to be energized enough to get off the couch and lose those pounds or find that job or study for that test, and you want to be motivated enough to stay engaged even when the inevitable obstacles or challenges arise. We could use the power of positive fantasy to visualize our success and make our goals a reality. ⓓThe principle of "Dream it. Wish it. Do it." does not hold true, and now we know why: in dreaming it, you undercut the energy you need to do it. You put yourself in a temporary state of complete happiness, calmness─and inactivity.
explanation: 이 글은 긍정적인 환상이 휴식에는 도움이 되지만, 실제로 목표를 달성하는 데 필요한 에너지와 동기를 감소시킨다는 점을 주장하고 있습니다. 따라서 긍정적 환상의 힘을 사용해 목표를 현실로 만들 수 있다는 문장은 글의 핵심 논지와 상반되는 무관한 문장입니다.

question: 17. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: Rebels may think they're rebels, but clever marketers influence them just like the rest of us. (A) Saying, "Everyone is doing it" may turn some people off from an idea. (B) These people will look for alternatives, which (if cleverly planned) can be exactly what a marketer or persuader wants you to believe. options: ① (A)

④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장의 'this inversion(이러한 반전/역전)'은 앞선 문장에서 설명한 '독립성을 유지하려는 사람들에게 표준적인 옵션을 먼저 제시하여 이를 거부하게 하고 진짜 원하는 선택지를 택하게 만드는 기법'을 가리킵니다. 이러한 기법을 활용하여 우리가 독립적으로 선택한다고 착각하게 만든다는 내용 뒤에, 브랜드들이 이러한 반항심을 이용해 스스로를 반항아로 포지셔닝하여 브랜드 충성도를 높였다는 예시가 나오는 것이 흐름상 가장 적절하므로 (E) 위치가 정답입니다.

question: 22. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Much of human thought is designed to screen out information and to sort the rest into a manageable condition. The inflow of data from our senses could create an overwhelming chaos, especially given the enormous amount of information available in culture and society.
ordered_passages: (A) Expectancies accomplish some of this work, helping to screen out information that is irrelevant to what is expected, and focusing our attention on clear contradictions. The processes of learning and memory are marked by a steady elimination of information.

(B) The processes mean people notice only a part of the world around them. Then, only a fraction of what they notice gets processed and stored into memory. And only part of what gets committed to memory can be retrieved.

Finally, even when we try to empathize with others who are dissimilar from us or in unfamiliar contexts, sometimes we are unable to accurately empathize with their experiences, causing further misunderstandings and frustration. question: 29. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The future of work depends on two forces: a harmful substituting force and a helpful complementing one. Many tales have a hero and a villain fighting each other for dominance, but in our story, technology plays both roles at once, displacing workers while simultaneously raising the demand for their efforts elsewhere in the economy. This interaction helps explain why past worries about automation were misplaced: our ancestors had predicted the wrong winner in that fight, underestimating quite how powerful the complementing force would prove to be or simply ignoring that factor altogether. It also helps to explain why economists have traditionally been dismissive of the idea of technological unemployment: there appeared to be firm limits to the substituting force, leaving lots of tasks that could not be performed by machines, and a growing demand for human beings to do them instead.
summary_sentence: Technological change both displaces and (A)__________ workers, which explains why fears of automation- driven unemployment have historically been (B)__________.
options: ① ignores ... emphasized
② complements ... validated
③ supplements ... overstated
④ undermines ... amplified
⑤ supports ... justified
explanation: 이 글은 기술이 노동자를 대체하는 힘(substituting force)과 보완하는 힘(complementing one)을 동시에 가지고 있음을 설명합니다. 과거의 자동화로 인한 실업 공포가 잘못된 것(misplaced)이었던 이유는 보완하는 힘의 위력을 과소평가했기 때문입니다. 따라서 기술 변화는 노동자를 대체하기도 하지만 (A) 보완/보충(supplements)하며, 이로 인해 자동화로 인한 실업 공포는 역사적으로 (B) 과장(overstated)되었다고 보는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 무시하다 ... 강조된
② 보완하다 ... 입증된

question: 6. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The "jolt" of caffeine does wear off. Caffeine is removed from your system by an enzyme within your liver, which gradually degrades it over time. Based in large part on genetics, some people have a more efficient version of the enzyme that degrades caffeine, allowing the liver to rapidly clear it from the bloodstream. These rare individuals can drink an espresso with dinner and fall fast asleep at midnight without a problem. (A)____________, others have a slower-acting version of the enzyme. It takes far longer for their system to eliminate the same amount of caffeine. (B)____________, they are very sensitive to caffeine's effects. One cup of tea or coffee in the morning will last much of the day, and should they have a second cup, even early in the afternoon, they will find it difficult to fall asleep in the evening. (C)____________, aging alters the speed of caffeine clearance: the older we are, the longer it takes our brain and body to remove caffeine, and thus the more sensitive we become in later life to caffeine's sleep-disrupting influence.

options_translation: ① (A) 반대로, (B) 결과적으로, (C) 그럼에도 불구하고
② (A) 더욱이, (B) 오히려, (C) 한편
③ (A) 대조적으로, (B) 따라서, (C) 게다가
④ (A) 반대로, (B) 무엇보다도, (C) 대신에

question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Rebels may think they're rebels, but clever marketers influence them just like the rest of us. Saying, "Everyone is doing it" may turn some people off from an idea. These people will look for alternatives, which (if cleverly planned) can be exactly ⓐ<u>what</u> a marketer or persuader wants you to believe. Say I want you to consider an idea, ⓑ<u>knowing</u> that you strongly reject popular opinion in favor of maintaining your independence and uniqueness. I would then present the majority option first, ⓒ<u>which</u> you would reject in favor of my actual preference. We are often tricked when we try to maintain a position of defiance. People use this reversal to make us "independently" ⓓ<u>choose</u> an option which suits their purposes. Some brands have taken full effect of our defiance towards the mainstream and positioned ⓔ<u>them</u> as rebels; which has created even stronger brand loyalty.
explanation: ⓔ가 포함된 문장의 주어는 Some brands이며, 목적어 또한 구랜드 자신들을 반항아로 설정한다는 의미이므로 재귀대명사 'themselves'를 쌨야 합니다.

question: 13. 윗글을 읽고 정리한 Keywords의 내용 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 옳은 것만을 있는 대로 고른 것은?
passage: Victorian England is characterised by the full development of the Industrial Revolution. England became the first industrial nation in the world and, by 1850, the first nation to have more people employed in industry than in agriculture. Expanding trade coincided with the growth of the Empire and brought great wealth to Britain, but this wealth was not evenly distributed. Many enterprising individuals (the 'self-made men') rose from humble origins to positions of wealth and influence, but large sections of the working class were forced into the overcrowded slums of large cities where they worked long hours for low wages in unhealthy conditions. The manufacturing towns of the north of England provided some of the worst examples and inspired such socially conscious novels as Kingsley's Alton Locke, Gaskell's Mary Barton, and Dickens's Hard Times. In the south there was London, already the largest city in the world, showing all the crime, evil, and misery which result from overpopulation and unplanned growth.
explanation:
각 어휘의 정의와 유의어 적절성을 판단하는 문제입니다.
- ⓐ Wealth(부): 'Lacking'(결핍)이 아니라 'Abundance'(풍요) 등의 의미가 되어야 하므로 틀렸으며, 유의어 ⓑ fortune(재산, 행운)은 적절합니다.
- ⓒ Enterprising(진취적인): 'Showing initiative and desire'(진취성과 욕구를 보여주는)라는 정의와 유의어 ⓓ ambitious(야심 있는)는 모두 지문의 문맥과 부합합니다.
- ⓔ Overpopulation(과잉 인구): 슬럼가(slum)의 정의가 인구 과잉의 정의로 쓰였으므로 부적절하며, 유의어인 ⓕ depopulation은 '인구 감소'를 뜻하므로 틀렸습니다.
따라서 옳은 것만 묶은 것은 ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓓ로 정답은 ②번입니다.

question: 15. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: The brain is a high-energy consumer of glucose, which is the fuel of the brain. Although the brain occupies merely 3 percent of a person's body weight, it consumes 20 percent of the available fuel. Your brain is not capable of ⓐ<u>reserving</u> fuel, however, so it has to "pay as it goes." Since your brain is incredibly adaptive, it makes ⓑ<u>efficient</u> use of fuel resources. In ordinary times, your brain may carefully analyze tiny details, ⓒ<u>weighing</u> subtle differences and hidden implications before making a decision. In contrast, under stressful conditions, your brain abandons such meticulous analysis and shifts to a rapid, survival-oriented focus on the immediate action. This indicates that during a period of high stress, the brain concentrates not so much on ⓓ<u>scrutinizing</u> the nuances of a situation as on a stressful situation at hand. You don't speculate the meaning of life when you are stressed. Instead, you devote all your energy to trying to figure out what action to take. Sometimes, however, this shift from the higher-thinking parts of the brain to the ⓔ<u>reflective</u> parts of the brain can lead you to do something too quickly, without thinking.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: 이 글은 스트레스 상황에서 뇌가 고도의 분석적이고 세심한 사고 과정(higher-thinking)에서 즉각적이고 생존 지향적인 빠른 행동 중심으로 전환된다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 이러한 전환이 생각 없이 너무 빨리 무언가를 하게 만든다고 설명하고 있으므로, '성찰적인(reflective)' 부분이 아니라 '반응적인(reactive)' 또는 '자동적인' 부분으로의 이동이 적절합니다. 따라서 ⓔ가 문맥상 적절하지 않습니다.

question: 16. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Architects might say a machine can never design an innovative or impressive building because a computer cannot be "creative." Yet consider the Elbphilharmonie, a new concert hall in Hamburg, which contains a remarkably beautiful auditorium composed of ten thousand interlocking acoustic panels. It is the sort of space that makes one instinctively think that only a human being ─ and a human with a remarkably refined creative sensibility, at that ─ could design something so aesthetically impressive. Yet the auditorium was, in fact, designed algorithmically, using a technique known as "parametric design." The architects gave the system a set of criteria, and it generated a set of possible designs for the architects to choose from. Similar software has been used to design lightweight bicycle frames and sturdier chairs, among much else. Are these systems behaving "creatively"? No, they are using lots of processing power to blindly generate varied possible designs, working in a very different way from a human being.
summary_sentence: While (A)______________ authentic human creativity, algorithmic design systems exemplify how computational processes can yield architecturally and aesthetically impressive outcomes through processes fundamentally (B)______________ those of human creative endeavors.
options: ① lacking - distinct from
② featuring - irreconcilable with
③ devoid of - dismissive of
④ equipped with - consistent with
⑤ overwhelmed by - in harmony with
explanation: 본문은 알고리즘 설계 시스템이 인간과 같은 창의성을 가지고 있지는 않지만, 인간의 창의적 방식과는 매우 다른(distinct from) 연산 과정을 통해 미적으로 훌륭한 건축물을 만들어낼 수 있음을 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 인간의 창의성이 없다는 의미의 'lacking'이, (B)에는 인간의 방식과는 다르다는 의미의 'distinct from'이 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 결여된 - ~와 별개인

question: 17. 다음 글의 내용을 옳게 이해하지 못한 것은?
passage: The development of early democracy was not unique to Europe. The assemblies of classical Greece, the gatherings of the Germanic tribes, and the councils of medieval city-states all bear certain strong resemblances to collective governance as it occurred in other world regions. But Europe was different in several crucial ways. Unlike what happened in China and the Middle East, early democracy continued to survive and thrive in Europe rather than being fully replaced by autocratic and bureaucratic rule. This is a first development we need to consider. Europeans were also different because they eventually succeeded in expanding the practice of early democracy to societies covering large territories. Finally, early democracy in Europe then evolved, through a series of steps, into modern democracy. The irony of early democracy in Europe is that it thrived and prospered precisely because European rulers for a very long time were remarkably weak. For more than a millennium after the fall of Rome, European rulers lacked the ability to assess what their people were producing and to levy substantial taxes based on this. The most striking way to illustrate European weakness is to show how little revenue they collected. Europeans would eventually develop strong systems of revenue collection, but it took them an awfully long time to do so. In medieval times, and for part of the early modern era, Chinese emperors and Muslim caliphs were able to extract much more of economic production than any European ruler.*autocratic: 독재적인 *bureaucratic: 관료적인
options: ① The emergence of democratic systems in various regions, such as Greece and the Germanic tribes, shows that early democracy was not exclusive to Europe.
② Europe differed from other regions in that early democratic practices persisted there, making the survival of democracy a key distinguishing feature.
③ Europeans were unable to extend democratic practices beyond local areas even though their democracy evolved into modern forms.
④ The prolonged weakness of European rulers, reflected in their inability to accurately assess production or impose substantial taxes, contributed to the success of early democracy in Europe.
⑤ Europeans took a long time to develop effective tax systems, during which Chinese and Middle Eastern rulers collected much more economic output than their European counterparts.
explanation: 지문에서 유럽인들은 초기 민주주의 관행을 넓은 영토를 포함하는 사회로 확장하는 데 결국 성공했다고 언급하고 있습니다(succeeded in expanding the practice of early democracy to societies covering large territories). 따라서 지역적인 범위를 넘어 확장하지 못했다는 3번 선택지는 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.

question: 18. 다음 글을 읽고 추론할 수 있는 비유적 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

question: 20. 다음 글의 내용을 읽고 옳게 이해한 것만을 <보기>에서 모두 고른 것은?
passage: If cooking is as central to human identity, biology, and culture as the biological anthropologist Richard Wrangham suggests, it stands to reason that the decline of cooking in our time would have serious consequences for modern life, and so it has. Are they all bad? Not at all. The outsourcing of much of the work of cooking to corporations has relieved women of what has traditionally been their exclusive responsibility for feeding the family, making it easier for them to work outside the home and have careers. It has headed off many of the domestic conflicts that such a large shift in gender roles and family dynamics was bound to spark. It has relieved other pressures in the household, including longer workdays and overscheduled children, and saved us time that we can now invest in other pursuits. It has also allowed us to diversify our diets substantially, making it possible even for people with no cooking skills and little money to enjoy a whole different cuisine. All that's required is a microwave.
explanation: 글의 내용을 분석하면:ⓐ 요리의 감소는 현대 생활에 심각한 영향을 미쳤으므로 틀림.ⓑ 요리를 기업에 맡김(외주화)으로써 여성의 전통적인 의무가 경감되었으므로 맞음.ⓒ 요리의 외주화는 많은 가사 갈등(domestic conflicts)을 방지했으므로 맞음.ⓓ 성 역할의 변화가 갈등을 일으킬 뻔했으나 요리의 외주화가 이를 막아준 것이지, 갈등이 전혀 없었다는 것은 아님.ⓔ 요리의 감소는 오히려 식단을 실질적으로 다양화(diversify)하게 해 주었으므로(marginal하게 표준화했다는 내용은 틀림).따라서 옳은 것은 ⓑ, ⓒ입니다.

question: 24. 다음 <보기>의 단어들을 조건에 맞게 사용하여 요약문을 완성하시오.
passage: There is little doubt that we are driven by the sell-by date. Once an item is past that date it goes into the waste stream, further increasing its carbon footprint and contributing to unnecessary food waste, even though it has already traveled long distances to reach the shelves. The manufacturer of the food has a view when making or growing something that by the time the product reaches the shelves it has already been travelling for so many days and possibly many miles. Manufacturers therefore set this date by estimating how long a product can reasonably be consumed, subtracting the time spent in transport. However, whether food past that date is actually unsafe is not always clear, and ultimately, the decision to consume such food is left to personal judgment. Such judgment often translates into everyday choices about how we shop and store our food. For example, it would seem to make sense not to buy large packs of perishable goods but non-perishable items may become cost-effective.
summary_sentence: → Although the sell-by date greatly effects carbon footprints and food waste, _______________________________________________________.
subjective_conditions: <보기>에 제시된 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용할 것
필요시 어형을 변화시킬 것
<보기>에 제시된 단어 이외의 추가 단어 없음
vocabulary_box: depend on / eat / past / the sell-by date /
answer: whether or not food past the sell-by date should be eaten depends on individual judgment
explanation: 이 글은 유통기한(sell-by date)이 환경적 영향과 식품 낭비에 기여함에도 불구하고, 실제 유통기한이 지난 식품의 안전성은 명확하지 않으며 결국 섭취 여부는 개인의 판단에 달려 있다는 내용을 담고 있습니다. 요약문은 '비록 유통기한이 탄소 발자국과 식품 낭비에 큰 영향을 미치지만, 유통기한이 지난 음식을 먹을지 여부는 개인의 판단에 달려 있다'는 구조로 완성되어야 합니다. 주어부인 'whether or not food past the sell-by date'가 절의 형태이므로 동사인 'depend on'은 3인칭 단수형인 'depends on'으로 변형해야 하며, 'should be' 뒤에는 수동태를 구성하는 'eaten'이 적절합니다.

question: 12. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 the numbers don't add up이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It's conceivable that in a world where solar panels are incredibly expensive and there's an extreme collapse in the cost of launching objects to space, you might want to maximize your energy per panel by putting them above the atmosphere. But panels are cheap, and even if we assume pretty steep drops in the cost of space launch, <u>the numbers don't add up</u>. This becomes especially clear when you start to think about maintenance. Try to imagine acres upon acres of glass panels in space, regularly hit by intense radiation and bits of space debris while enduring the extreme heat of constant sunlight. They'll have to be repaired and cared for either by astronauts or an army of advanced robots. Solar panels in Australia can be cleaned by a teenager with a spray bottle and a cloth.

explanation: 필자는 우주에 태양광 패널을 설치하는 것이 발사 비용과 유지보수의 어려움(우주 파편, 방사선 등)을 고려할 때 현실적이지 않다고 주장하고 있습니다. 따라서 'the numbers don't add up(수치가 맞지 않는다)'은 경제적, 기술적 효율성을 따져보았을 때 우주 태양광 발전이 비현실적이라는 ②번의 의미를 가집니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [25년 9월 30번]
passage: Although empathy is widely praised by scholars and public figures, not everyone is an empathy booster. Critics of empathy argue that empathy will not save us from interpersonal and intergroup conflict. In fact, they argue, empathy makes such conflicts worse. These critics maintain that empathy can be exhausting and lead to burnout or insensitivity to suffering. They argue that we tend to empathize strongly with in-group and refuse to empathize with out-groups, and even enjoy the suffering of out-groups in competitive or threatening contexts. Thus, the prescription for more empathy is often inefficient in cases of conflict. Empathy, they argue, can further encourage conflict and force us into an us vs. them mentality. Finally, even when we try to empathize with others who are dissimilar from us or in unfamiliar contexts, sometimes we are unable to accurately empathize with their experiences, causing further misunderstandings and frustration. Critics of empathy argue that we should give up on empathy and employ other tools in pursuit of social harmony, e.g., rational compassion or moral emotions like fear, anger, and shame.
summary_sentence: Critics argue that empathy can (A)___________ conflict by causing in-group bias, emotional exhaustion, and misunderstanding, suggesting that rational compassion or moral emotions may be more (B)___________.
options: ① mitigate  efficient solutions
② identify  inefficient choices
③ restrain  promising emotions
④ aggravate  effective alternatives
⑤ worsen  counterproductive substitutes

question: 14. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [25년 9월 32번]

question: 16. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The term "anchoring" was introduced by Roland Barthes who observed that text is often used next to images (his focus was on photographs) to confine meaning. Of all possible literal or implied interpretations an image could elicit, text would point the viewer towards a desired, specific direction. In advertising, as Barthes argues, the symbolic message does not guide identification but interpretation. The viewer is not asked to recognize what they see but to understand why they see it and what it means to them. By combining images with text, advertising produces symbolic meaning that is accurate and specific on the one hand, richer on the other, thus adding depth and eliminating breadth of rational and emotional interpretations. The headline or tagline of an ad directs the reader through the intended meanings of the image, so that the reader avoids some and receives others. It "remote-controls" the reader towards a meaning chosen in advance.
options: ① the need for images to bear more specific and richer symbolic messages
② the role of text in guiding image interpretation toward specific meanings
③ the impact of advertising with text on the increase in product sales

⑤ considerations in selecting images for advertisements
explanation: 이 글은 롤랑 바르트의 '고정(anchoring)' 개념을 설명하며, 텍스트가 이미지 옆에 쓰일 때 이미지의 다양한 해석 가능성을 제한하고 관람객을 의도된 특정한 방향으로 안내하는 역할을 한다고 설명하고 있습니다. 특히 광고에서 헤드라인이나 태그라인이 이미지의 의미를 미리 선택된 방향으로 '원격 조정'한다는 내용이 핵심이므로, 주제는 '이미지 해석을 특정 의미로 안내하는 텍스트의 역할'입니다.
options_translation: ① 이미지들이 더 구체적이고 풍부한 상징적 메시지를 지녀야 할 필요성
② 이미지 해석을 특정 의미로 안내하는 텍스트의 역할
③ 텍스트가 포함된 광고가 제품 판매 증가에 미치는 영향

question: 17. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Mother cats can tell which kittens belong to them - when litters are mixed up they use their kittens' scent to distinguish them from offspring of other mothers. question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Many animals pursue a mixed strategy of accumulating both body fat and food, which leads one to ask, "What are the relative advantages and disadvantages of these two forms of energy storage?"
ordered_passages: (A) Maximum fat deposition increases with body mass whereas maximum food storage is not constrained by body size. This means animals, especially small animals, can accumulate much greater energy reserves in the form of stored food than they can in the form of body fat. Further, stored food is more economical than body fat because fat contributes to body mass, and metabolic rate increases with body mass.(B) Many animals must expend energy managing and protecting their food stores. Eating food and converting it to fat avoids these types of losses and the energetic costs of managing stored food. A large accumulation of body fat adds to an animal's fasting capacity, especially large animals, permitting some animals to enter prolonged dormancy in the relative security of a hibernaculum.(C) Excessive fat accumulations may also have a negative effect on an animal's ability to avoid predators. And, if maintaining a high body temperature is advantageous, animals might be expected to accumulate more energy in the form of a food store than as body fat. On the other hand, stored food may rot over time, may be removed by robbers, or may simply be lost.
explanation: 주어진 글은 체지방과 음식 저장이라는 두 가지 에너지 저장 형태의 장단점에 대해 질문을 던집니다. (A)에서는 몸의 크기에 따른 두 저장 방식의 한계(작은 동물은 음식 저장이 유리)와 경제성을 언급하며 비교를 시작합니다. (C)에서는 체지방의 단점(포식자 회피 방해)과 대조적으로 음식 저장의 단점(부패, 도난 가능성)을 나열합니다. 마지막으로 (B)에서는 (C)에서 언급된 음식 저장의 단점(관리 비용)을 극복하는 대안으로서의 체지방 축적의 장점(단식 능력, 동면 가능성)을 설명하며 마무리하는 것이 논리적으로 가장 자연스럽습니다.

question: 19. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: All human cultures mark the passing of time by the differences they observe in the world around them. question: 20. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers ⓐ<u>which</u> it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease to form, while sufficient fibers remain undamaged for the material not to crack and fall apart. Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to resist ⓑ<u>being</u> pulled apart, but it can also be torn easily and accurately along the crease if a point of weakness - a small, initial tear - is opened up. This winning combination of mechanical properties ⓒ<u>allows</u> it to assume the shape of any object through creasing and folding - hence the art of origami. There are very few materials as good: metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult. Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, in which case it lacks the rigidity ⓓ<u>required</u> of a good wrapping material. So it is its ability to hold a crease while remaining stiff that makes paper ⓔ<u>uniquely</u> suited to this purpose.

⑤ ⓔ

question: 22. 다음 우리말을 영작하시오. 단, 반드시 주어진 2가지 <조건>에 맞추어 영작하시오.
passage: Many tales have a hero and a villain fighting each other for dominance, but in our story, technology plays both roles at once, displacing workers while simultaneously raising the demand for their efforts elsewhere in the economy. It also helps to explain why economists have traditionally been dismissive of the idea of technological unemployment: there appeared to be firm limits to the substituting force, leaving lots of tasks that could not be performed by machines, and a growing demand for human beings to do them instead.

passage: The word "migration" is almost always reported in the popular media and even in scientific literature as a problem or a crisis. For example, migrants are assumed to overcrowd cities, clog up labor markets, and increase poverty. The other questionable assumption is that most migration is involuntary - people fleeing natural or man-made disasters. However, the reality is more complex, and many migrants are simply seeking greater economic opportunity. Of course migration can and does create social and economic problems. However, migration can also be a solution for many preexisting problems. For example, out-migration generally redistributes workers from places of labor surplus to areas where there is greater demand or more opportunity. Migration is generally selective of persons who are younger, healthier, more flexible, and more willing to endure hardship in hopes of a better life relative to their prospects in their places of origin. Most research that examines long-term outcomes of migration, including remittances and intergenerational mobility, finds positive "long-term" effects on places of origin and destination.

⑤ ⓔshare: a part of something that has been divided into parts and given to different people
explanation: ⓒunemployment는 '실업(일자리가 없는 상태)'을 의미합니다. ③번의 설명인 '어려운 상황, 불운, 비극'은 'adversity'나 'misfortune'에 대한 설명에 가깝습니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ번영: 대개 많은 돈을 벌어 성공한 상태

question: 1. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Any new or threatening situation may require us to make decisions and this requires information. So important is communication during a disaster that normal social barriers are often lowered. We will talk to strangers in a way we would never consider normally. Even relatively low grade disruption of our life such as a fire drill or a very late train seems to give us the permission to break normal etiquette and talk to strangers. The more important an event to a particular public, the more detailed and urgent the requirement for news becomes. Without an authoritative source of facts, whether that is a newspaper or trusted broadcast station, rumours often run riot. Rumours start because people believe their group to be in danger and so, although the rumour is unproven, feel they should pass it on. For example, _____________________________________.
options: ① if someone heard that their neighbor had adopted a new dog, they would share the news with neighbors
② if a parent heard that the local school might be closing due to budget cuts, they would contact the school to complain
③ if a shopper noticed that their favorite brand of cereal was missing from the shelf, they would post it on their Instagram
④ if a student heard a rumour that a new principal was coming to their school, they would spread it among their classmates
⑤ if a passenger at an airport overheard that flights were being cancelled due to an incoming storm, they would share that information with other travellers
explanation: 이 글은 재난이나 위협적인 상황에서 정보에 대한 욕구가 커지고 평소의 사회적 장벽이 낮아져 낯선 사람과도 소통하게 된다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. ⑤번 선택지는 공항에서 폭풍으로 인해 항공편이 취소될 것이라는 위협적이고 중요한 정보를 들었을 때 다른 여행객들과 그 정보를 공유한다는 내용이므로, 글의 문맥(재난/위협 상황에서의 정보 공유 및 소통)에 가장 적절한 예시입니다.
options_translation: ① 만약 누군가 이웃이 새 강아지를 입양했다는 소식을 듣는다면, 그들은 그 소식을 이웃들과 공유할 것이다.
② 만약 학부모가 지역 학교가 예산 삭감으로 폐교될 수도 있다는 소식을 듣는다면, 그들은 항의하기 위해 학교에 연락할 것이다.
③ 만약 쇼핑객이 자신이 좋아하는 시리얼 브랜드가 선반에서 사라진 것을 발견하면, 그들은 그것을 인스타그램에 게시할 것이다.
④ 만약 학생이 학교에 새 교장 선생님이 부임한다는 소문을 듣는다면, 그들은 그것을 반 친구들 사이에 퍼뜨릴 것이다.
⑤ 만약 공항의 승객이 다가오는 폭풍으로 인해 항공편이 취소되고 있다는 말을 우연히 듣는다면, 그들은 그 정보를 다른 여행객들과 공유할 것이다.

question: 2. 윗글의 오늘날의 조직이 추구해야 할 목표와 관련 있는 것은?
passage: In today's information age, in many companies and on many teams, the objective is no longer error prevention and replicability. On the contrary, it's creativity, speed, and keenness. In the industrial era, the goal was to minimize variation. But in creative companies today, maximizing variation is more essential. In these situations, the biggest risk isn't making a mistake or losing consistency; it's failing to attract top talent, to invent new products, or to change direction quickly when the environment shifts. Consistency and repeatability are more likely to suppress fresh thinking than to bring your company profit. A lot of little mistakes, while sometimes painful, help the organization learn quickly and are a critical part of the innovation cycle. In these situations, rules and process are no longer the best answer. A symphony isn't what you're going for. Leave the conductor and the sheet music behind. Build a jazz band instead.
options: ① sticking to the same routine
② following the standard playbook
③ aiming for error-free performance
④ bringing in high-performing individuals
⑤ improving the ability to reproduce the same results
explanation: 지문은 오늘날의 창의적인 기업들이 실수를 방지하거나 일관성을 유지하는 것보다 창의성, 속도, 변화에 대한 대응, 인재 확보를 더 중요하게 여긴다고 설명합니다. ④번 '뛰어난 성과를 내는 개인들을 데려오는 것'은 지문의 'attract top talent'와 일치하는 목표입니다.
options_translation: ① 똑같은 일상을 고수하는 것
② 표준 플레이북(지침서)을 따르는 것
③ 오류 없는 성과를 목표로 하는 것
④ 높은 성과를 내는 개인들을 영입하는 것
⑤ 동일한 결과를 재생산하는 능력을 향상시키는 것

question: 3. 윗글의 요지를 <보기>의 단어만을 모두 한 번씩 사용하여 완성하시오.

question: 4. 윗글의 흐름을 도식화한 것이다. 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: One well-known shift took place when the accepted view - that the Earth was the center of the universe - changed to one where we understood that we are only inhabitants on one planet orbiting the Sun. With each person who grasped the solar system view, it became easier for the next person to do so. So it is with the notion that the world revolves around the human economy. This is slowly being replaced by the view that the economy is a part of the larger system of material flows that connect all living things. When this perspective shifts into place, it will be obvious that our economic well-being requires that we account for, and respond to, factors of ecological health. Unfortunately we do not have a century or two to make the change. By clarifying the nature of the old and new perspectives, and by identifying actions on which we might cooperate to move the process along, we can help accelerate the shift.
options: ① urgent protectionindividual
② systematic ignorancesupportive
③ recent adjustmentcompetitive
④ major explanationindependent
⑤ current considerationcollaborative
explanation: (A) 지문에서 지구가 중심이라는 관점에서 태양 중심 관점으로의 변화를 언급한 뒤, 현재 일어나는 경제 관점의 변화를 설명하고 있으므로 current(현재의)가 적절합니다. (B) 경제적 안녕은 생태적 건강 요소를 고려(account for)해야 한다는 내용이므로 consideration(고려)이 적절합니다. (C) 마지막 문장에서 변화를 가속화하기 위해 협력할 수 있는(cooperate) 조치를 식별해야 한다고 했으므로 collaborative(협력적인)가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 긴급한 - 보호 - 개인적인
② 체계적인 - 무지 - 지원적인
③ 최근의 - 조정 - 경쟁적인
④ 주요한 - 설명 - 독립적인
⑤ 현재의 - 고려 - 협력적인

question: 6. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It's often said that those who can't do, teach. It would be more accurate to say that those who can do, can't teach the basics. A great deal of expert knowledge is implicit, not explicit. The further you progress toward mastery, the less conscious awareness you often have of the fundamentals. Experiments show that skilled golfers and wine aficionados have a hard time describing their putting and tasting techniques - even asking them to explain their approaches is enough to interfere with their performance, so they often stay on autopilot. When I first saw an elite diver do four and a half somersaults, I asked how he managed to spin so fast. His answer: "Just go up in a ball." Experts often have an intuitive understanding of a route, but they struggle to clearly express all the steps to take. <u>Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage</u>.
options: ① Experts have a lot of knowledge but not all of it is useful.
② Experts like to show their knowledge indirectly and ambiguously.
③ Experts deliberately confuse others by giving vague explanations.
④ Experts acquire their knowledge intuitively rather than through explicit instruction.
⑤ Experts often know things intuitively but they can't always put them into clear words.
explanation: 글의 핵심은 전문가들이 기술을 습득할수록 그 지식이 암묵적(implicit)으로 변해버려 기초적인 원리나 과정에 대한 의식적인 인식이 줄어든다는 것입니다. 따라서 그들에게 설명을 요청하면 명확하게 설명하지 못하거나 엉뚱한(쓰레기 같은) 설명이 나올 수 있다는 맥락이므로, '전문가들은 직관적으로 알지만 항상 명확한 말로 표현할 수 있는 것은 아니다'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 전문가들은 많은 지식을 가지고 있지만 그것이 모두 유용한 것은 아니다.
② 전문가들은 그들의 지식을 간접적이고 모호하게 보여주는 것을 좋아한다.
③ 전문가들은 모호한 설명을 제공함으로써 의도적으로 다른 사람들을 혼란스럽게 한다.
④ 전문가들은 명시적인 교육보다는 직관을 통해 지식을 습득한다.
⑤ 전문가들은 종종 직관적으로 알고 있지만 항상 그것을 명확한 말로 표현할 수 있는 것은 아니다.

question: 7. 윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Historians, or to be more accurate, ethnologist have studied this creative aspect of fashion. The well-known American ethnologist Kroeber made a rich and in-depth study of women's evening dress in the West, stretching back about three centuries and using reproductions of engravings. Having adjusted the dimensions of these plates due to their diverse origins, he was able to analyse the constant elements in fashion features and to come up with a study that was neither intuitive nor approximate, but precise, mathematical and statistical. He reduced women's clothing to a certain number of features: length and size of the skirt, size and depth of the neckline, height of the waistline. He demonstrated unambiguously that fashion is a profoundly regular phenomenon which is not located at the level of annual variations but on the scale of history. For practically 300 years, women's dress was subject to a very precise periodic cycle: forms reach the furthest point in their variations every fifty years. If, at any one moment, skirts are at their longest, fifty years later they will be at their shortest; thus skirts become long again fifty years after being short and a hundred years after being long. Kroeber also showed regular connections between, for example, the variations in the length of the skirt and the width of the neckline; certain features are linked in the __________ of fashion.
options: ① rhythm
② progress
③ similarity
④ irregularity
⑤ consistency
explanation: 글에서 패션이 매우 정확한 주기적인 사이클(periodic cycle)을 따르며, 일정한 시간 간격으로 변화가 반복된다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 이러한 규칙적이고 반복적인 변화를 가장 잘 나타내는 단어는 'rhythm(리듬)'입니다.
options_translation: ① 리듬
② 진보
③ 유사성
④ 불규칙성
⑤ 일관성

question: 8. 윗글의 내용을 바탕으로 다음 문장의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 연도를 숫자로 각각 쓰시오.

question: 9. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: Free play is nature's means of teaching children that they are not helpless. In play, away from adults, children really do have control and can practice asserting it. In free play, children learn to make their own decisions, solve their own problems, create and follow rules, and get along with others as equals rather than as obedient or rebellious subordinates. In active outdoor play, children deliberately dose themselves with moderate amounts of fear and they thereby learn how to control not only their bodies, but also their fear. In social play children learn how to negotiate with others, how to please others, and how to manage and overcome the anger that can arise from conflicts. None of these lessons can be taught through verbal means; they can be learned only through experience, which free play provides.
options: ① Free play provides experiences that cannot be fully replaced by verbal instruction.
② Through active outdoor play, children learn to manage both their physical abilities and emotional responses.
③ In free play, children acquire obedience to adults by following rules set by grown-ups.
④ Free play allows children to make independent decisions and solve their own problems.
⑤ Social play helps children practice negotiation, cooperation, and conflict management with peers.
explanation: 이 글은 자유 놀이를 통해 아이들이 스스로 통제력을 기르고 문제를 해결하며 사회적 기술을 습득한다고 설명합니다. 지문에 따르면 아이들은 자유 놀이에서 '순종적이거나 반항적인 하급자로서가 아니라 동등한 존재로(as equals rather than as obedient or rebellious subordinates)' 타인과 어울리는 법을 배우며 스스로 규칙을 만든다고 했으므로, 어른들이 정한 규칙을 따르며 복종을 배운다는 ③번은 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않습니다.
options_translation: ① 자유 놀이는 언어적 교육에 의해 완전히 대체될 수 없는 경험을 제공한다.
② 활발한 야외 놀이를 통해, 아이들은 신체적 능력과 정서적 반응을 모두 관리하는 법을 배운다.
③ 자유 놀이에서, 아이들은 성인들에 의해 세워진 규칙을 따름으로써 성인들에 대한 복종을 습득한다.
④ 자유 놀이는 아이들이 독립적인 결정을 내리고 그들 자신의 문제를 해결하도록 허용한다.
⑤ 사회적 놀이는 아이들이 또래와 협상, 협력, 그리고 갈등 관리를 연습하도록 돕는다.

question: 10. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
passage: Mirror neurons are the hardware of empathy, and so what would make more sense than to look and see which animals possess these cells? And this is exactly ⓐ<u>where</u> modern research now stands: all researchers know so far is that apes possess mirror neurons. We still need to test to see which other species are like us in this respect. Scientists often publicly speculate ⓑ<u>what</u> we can probably expect surprises here, too. They assume that all animals that live in herds or large groups ⓒ<u>possess</u> similar brain mechanisms, because social units function only if individuals can see things from the perspective of others in the group and feel ⓓ<u>what</u> they are feeling. I can see a goldfish waving its fin at us. As an animal that ⓔ<u>travels</u> around in a tightly knit group, it's on board with this idea - or at least swimming alongside the boat.
explanation: ⓑ가 포함된 문장에서 speculate의 목적어 역할을 하는 절 'we can probably expect surprises here, too'는 주어, 동사, 목적어를 모두 갖춘 완전한 문장입니다. 따라서 불완전한 절을 이끄는 관계대명사나 의문사 what이 아니라, 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 that이 쓰여야 합니다.

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: The fundamental nature of the experimental method is manipulation and control. Scientists ⓐ<u>manipulate</u> a variable of interest, and see if there's a difference. At the same time, they attempt to control for the potential effects of all other variables. The importance of ⓑ<u>controlled</u> experiments in identifying the underlying causes of events cannot be overstated. In the real-uncontrolled-world, variables are often ⓒ<u>correlated</u>. For example, people who take vitamin supplements may have different eating and exercise habits than people who don't take vitamins. As a result, if we want to study the health effects of vitamins, we can't merely observe the real world, since any of these factors (the vitamins, diet, or exercise) may affect health. Rather, we have to ⓓ<u>create</u> a situation that doesn't actually occur in the real world. That's just what scientific experiments do. They try to separate the naturally occurring relationship in the world by manipulating one specific variable at a time, while holding everything else ⓔ<u>constant</u>.

explanation: 이 글은 문화마다 시간을 기록하는 방식(달력)이 주변 세계에서 관찰하는 차이점, 관찰 가능한 것, 그리고 삶에서 중요한 것에 따라 달라진다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다. 농경 사회였던 전근대 유럽은 태양 주기를 관찰했고, 유목 생활을 하던 아라비아 사람들은 음력을 선택했다는 예시를 통해 지리적 여건, 생활 방식, 전통 등이 달력의 뿌리가 됨을 강조하고 있습니다. 따라서 '문화, 관찰, 그리고 생활 방식: 달력의 뿌리'가 가장 적절한 제목입니다.
options_translation: ① 문명 간 의식을 수행하는 다양한 방법들

③ 고대 달력과 의식에 대한 오해들
