⑤ 문화, 관찰, 그리고 생활 방식: 달력의 뿌리

question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The traditional bank manager in the 1950s was usually a respected pillar of the community, a cautious, careful sort of person who probably went to bed early and didn't drink too much. (A)__________ from the 1970s a new kind of banker appeared - loud, flashy, and arrogant. These bankers loved taking big risks. They wanted to get rich quick and blow their money on fast cars and expensive champagne. They made their money through what's called 'speculation'. Normally, people buy things because they want to use them, such as wheat to make bread and petrol to run the car. (B)__________ when people speculate, they buy things even when they have no interest in using them. They might buy a load of wheat simply because they think that its price is going to rise when a drought is predicted in wheat-growing areas. If their guess is right, they later sell the wheat for a profit.
options: ① However  Yet
② Moreover  Thus
③ In contrast  In addition
④ Nevertheless  Accordingly
⑤ Furthermore  In other words
explanation: (A) 앞 문장에서는 1950년대의 신중하고 조심스러운 은행가를 묘사하고 있고, 뒷 문장에서는 1970년대의 화려하고 오만한 새로운 유형의 은행가를 묘사하므로 역접의 연결어 'However'가 적절합니다. (B) 앞 문장에서는 보통 사람들이 물건을 사용하기 위해 구매한다고 설명하지만, 뒷 문장에서는 투기하는 사람들이 사용할 목적이 없어도 물건을 구매한다고 설명하며 대조를 이루므로 'Yet' 혹은 'But'의 의미를 가진 연결어가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 그러나 - 하지만
② 더욱이 - 따라서
③ 대조적으로 - 게다가
④ 그럼에도 불구하고 - 그에 따라
⑤ 뿐만 아니라 - 다시 말해서

question: 22. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers of which it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease to form, while sufficient fibers remain undamaged for the material not to crack and fall apart. Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to resist being pulled apart, but it can also be torn easily and accurately along the crease if a point of weakness - a small, initial tear - is opened up. This winning combination of mechanical properties allows it to assume the shape of any object through creasing and folding - hence the art of origami. There are very few materials as good: metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult. Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, in which case it lacks the rigidity required of a good wrapping material. So paper proves to be superior to other materials like plastic sheeting because it successfully balances foldability with _________________.
options: ① low durability
② aesthetic appeal
③ moderate rigidity
④ thermal resistance
⑤ complete transparency
explanation: 이 글은 종이가 접힘과 굽힘에 적합한 기계적 성질을 가지고 있음을 설명합니다. 종이는 접힌 자국을 유지할 수 있으면서도 찢어지지 않고 버티는 힘을 동시에 가지고 있습니다. 마지막 문장에서 플라스틱 시트와 비교하는데, 플라스틱은 너무 부드러우면 포장재에 필요한 '강성(rigidity)'이 부족하여 접힌 자국을 유지하지 못한다고 언급합니다. 따라서 종이가 다른 재료보다 뛰어난 이유는 접을 수 있는 성질(foldability)과 '적당한 강성(moderate rigidity)'의 균형을 잘 맞추기 때문입니다.
options_translation: ① 낮은 내구성
② 미적 매력
③ 적당한 단단함(강성)
④ 내열성
⑤ 완전한 투명성

question: 23. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.2점]
passage: The future of work depends on two forces: a harmful substituting force and a helpful complementing one. Many tales have a hero and a villain fighting each other for dominance, but in our story, technology plays both roles at once, displacing workers while simultaneously raising the demand for their efforts elsewhere in the economy. This interaction helps explain why past worries about automation were misplaced: our ancestors had predicted the wrong winner in that fight, underestimating quite how powerful the complementing force would prove to be or simply ignoring that factor altogether. It also helps to explain why economists have traditionally been dismissive of the idea of technological unemployment: there appeared to be firm limits to the substituting force, leaving lots of tasks that could not be performed by machines, and a growing demand for human beings to do them instead.
options: ① A Double-Edge Sword of Technology Nowadays
② Forced Dominance between Interpersonal Relationships
③ Precise Foresight of Ancestors in Estimating Technology
④ Negative Subconscious Awareness on Applied Technology
⑤ Burden of Workers' Adaptation to Brand-new Technology
explanation: 지문은 기술이 일자리를 대체하는 해로운 힘(substituting force)과 새로운 수요를 창출하여 보완하는 유익한 힘(complementing force)이라는 두 가지 역할을 동시에 수행한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 기술의 이러한 양면성을 나타내는 '오늘날 기술의 양날의 검'이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 오늘날 기술의 양날의 검
② 대인 관계 사이의 강제적인 지배
③ 기술 평가에 있어 조상들의 정확한 예견
④ 응용 기술에 대한 부정적인 잠재의식적 인식
⑤ 신기술에 대한 노동자들의 적응 부담

question: 24. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.1점]
passage: Although empathy is widely praised by scholars and public figures, not everyone is an empathy booster. Critics of empathy argue that empathy will not save us from interpersonal and intergroup conflict. In fact, they argue, empathy makes such conflicts worse. These critics maintain that empathy can be exhausting and lead to burnout, insensitivity to suffering, or worse. They argue that we tend to empathize strongly with our in-group and resist empathizing with out-groups, and even enjoy the suffering of out-groups in competitive or threatening contexts. Thus, the prescription for more empathy is often counterproductive in cases of conflict. Empathy, they argue, can further entrench conflict and force us into an us vs. them mentality. Finally, even when we try to empathize with others who are dissimilar from us or in unfamiliar contexts, sometimes we are unable to accurately empathize with their experiences, causing further misunderstandings and frustration. Critics of empathy argue that we should give up on empathy and employ other tools in pursuit of social harmony, e.g., rational compassion or moral emotions like fear, anger, and shame.
options: ① conflict is responsible for human empathy
② empathy is to blame for intensified conflict
③ empathy leads to the positive social change
④ out-group friendship ends up leading to moral hazard
⑤ one with emphatic manner suffers from social criticism
explanation: 본문은 공감이 대인 관계나 집단 간의 갈등을 해결해주기보다는 오히려 심화시킨다는 비판론자들의 주장을 다루고 있습니다. 공감이 내집단 편향을 강화하고 외집단에 대한 적대감을 유발할 수 있다는 내용이 핵심이므로, '공감이 심화된 갈등의 원인이다'라는 선택지가 주제로 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 갈등은 인간 공감의 원인이다
② 공감은 격화된 갈등의 원인이다
③ 공감은 긍정적인 사회 변화를 이끈다
④ 외집단과의 우정은 결국 도덕적 해이로 이어진다
⑤ 공감하는 태도를 가진 사람은 사회적 비판으로 고통받는다

question: 25. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은? [3.3점]
passage: Paradoxically, it's uncertainty that makes us feel most alive. Think of events that shake you out of your everyday routine: maybe attending a family wedding, making a big presentation, or going somewhere you've never been. It's on those occasions that time seems to slow down a little, and you feel more fully engaged. The same holds true if the experience is risky, like mountain climbing or parasailing. Your senses are sharper. You notice more. Thanks to the release of a feel-good chemical in the brain called dopamine, you get a greater rush of pleasure from chance encounters with people than planned meetings. Good news, financial rewards, and gifts are more enjoyable if they are surprises. It's why the most popular television shows and movies are the ones with unexpected plot twists and astonishing endings.
summary_sentence: According to the passage, our brains are wired to perceive (A)__________ events as more (B)__________, partly due to the release of dopamine.
options: ① routine   tiring
② unexpected   rewarding
③ social   meaningful
④ difficult   memorable
⑤ planned   efficient
explanation: 지문은 불확실성과 예상치 못한 사건(unexpected events)이 우리를 더 살아있게 느끼게 하고, 도파민 분비 덕분에 계획된 일보다 더 큰 즐거움과 보상감(rewarding)을 준다고 설명합니다. 따라서 (A)에는 'unexpected', (B)에는 'rewarding'이 들어가는 것이 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 일상적인 - 피곤한
② 예상치 못한 - 보람 있는(수익이 되는)
③ 사회적인 - 의미 있는
④ 어려운 - 기억에 남는
⑤ 계획된 - 효율적인

question: 26. 다음 글을 읽고 밑줄 친 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 주어진 조건에 맞게 정답 속 빈칸을 적절한 단어로 채우시오.
passage: Collin's dad had a 15-year-old car, which was the same age as Collin. He decided that it was finally time to replace it with a newer model. Yesterday evening at dinner, he shared his plan to buy a new car with his family. Excited by the news, Collin became determined to contribute to his dad's big purchase. Over the past several years, Collin had saved his allowance money. He felt that this was the perfect opportunity to do something special for his dad. Before heading to bed, Collin put an envelope on the kitchen table. This morning, when his dad came into the kitchen, he noticed the envelope and asked his wife about it. She explained that Collin had left it there last night. Collin's dad opened the envelope and saw a thick stack of money. "There's $1,000 in here!" he exclaimed, after counting it. His wife smiled and said, "Collin wanted to help you pay for the new car." Collin's dad went to the car dealership right away and purchased a car that was only one year old. He picked a red car because that was Collin's favorite color. When he got back home in the evening, he showed it to Collin with a warm hug. He said, <u>"만약 어제 네가 나에게 그 돈을 주지 않았다면, 나는 오늘 이 멋진 차를 살 수 없었을거야."</u>
subjective_conditions: 'give'와 'buy'를 반드시 포함시킬 것
(필요한 경우, 단어의 형태를 바꾸어도 됨)
subjective_answer_format: If you __________ __________ __________ me the money yesterday, I __________ __________ __________ this awesome car today.
answer: had not given, could not buy
explanation: 이 문제는 과거의 사실과 반대되는 상황을 가정하여 현재의 결과에 미치는 영향을 표현하는 혼합 가정법(Mixed Conditionals) 문장을 완성하는 문제입니다. 조건절(If-clause)은 과거 사실('어제 돈을 주지 않은 것')에 대한 반대 가정이므로 'had + p.p.' 형태인 'had not given'을 사용해야 하며, 주절은 현재 사실('오늘 차를 살 수 있는 것')에 대한 반대 가정이므로 '조동사 과거형 + 동사원형'인 'could not buy'를 사용하는 것이 적절합니다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
passage: "Tactics" is a term drawn from military usage. (A) Strategies are plans of action directing a military force when attacking another, and tactics are responses to conditions on the ground. (B) In this vein, time is imposed on us by our cultures, by the technologies that have regimented time down to the nanosecond, and by its own finite nature and the fact that we're going to live only so long. (C) In response, we must develop tactics for dealing with time and waiting. These aren't tactics to eliminate waiting; instead, these are tactics for teaching us how to learn from the seams. (D) Such renewed perspectives transform waiting from a burden to a springboard toward things like creativity, social critique, or reflection on our inner state and the state of our relationships. (E)
insertion_sentence: These tactics have the potential to reorient us in profound ways, transforming our perspectives on our wait times.
options: ① (A)
② (B)
③ (C)
④ (D)
⑤ (E)
explanation: 주어진 문장은 '이러한 전술들(These tactics)'이 우리의 관점을 변화시킬 잠재력을 가지고 있다는 내용입니다. (D) 앞 문장에서 기다림의 틈새로부터 배우는 방법을 가르쳐주는 전술(tactics)이 언급되었습니다. 따라서 주어진 문장이 (D)에 위치해야 그 뒤에 나오는 '그러한 새로워진 관점들(Such renewed perspectives)'이 가리키는 대상이 명확해집니다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The future of work depends on two forces: a harmful substituting force and a helpful complementing one. Many tales have a hero and a villain fighting each other for dominance, but in our story, technology plays both roles at once, ________________________________________. This interaction helps explain why past worries about automation were misplaced: our ancestors had predicted the wrong winner in that fight, underestimating quite how powerful the complementing force would prove to be or simply ignoring that factor altogether. It also helps to explain why economists have traditionally been dismissive of the idea of technological unemployment: there appeared to be firm limits to the substituting force, leaving lots of tasks that could not be performed by machines, and a growing demand for human beings to do them instead.

explanation: 이 글은 기술이 일자리를 대체하는 '해로운 대체력(substituting force)'과 일자리를 보완하는 '도움이 되는 보완력(complementing one)'이라는 두 가지 역할을 동시에 수행한다고 설명합니다. 빈칸은 이 두 가지 역할을 모두 수행한다는 점을 설명해야 합니다. ⑤번 '일자리를 뺏어가지만 다른 곳에서 인간에 대한 수요를 늘린다'는 내용이 대체와 보완이라는 두 측면을 가장 잘 요약하고 있습니다.

question: 23. 다음 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 알맞게 짝지어진 것은? [25년 9월 30번]

question: 24. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [25년 9월 33번]
passage: Dictionary definitions are constantly revised to keep up with our changing uses and knowledge. In Roman times, "addicts" were people who were unable to pay their debts and gave themselves as slaves to their creditors. The word eventually came to be associated with drug dependency: one becomes a slave to one's addiction. The word "husband" originally referred to being a homeowner; it had nothing to do with being married. But because owning your own property made it more likely you'd find a mate, the word eventually came to mean a male who has been wed. On November 5th, 1605, Guy Fawkes tried to blow up the British Parliament. He was captured and put to death. Loyalists burned his effigy, which they nicknamed the "guy." Centuries later, the word lost its negative connotation and a musical named Guys and Dolls ran on Broadway. In American slang, bad means good, cool means great, and wicked means excellent. If you could transport yourself one hundred years into the future, you'd find yourself confused by your great-grandchildren's speech because language itself is an ever-changing reflection of human invention.
options: ① 사전적인 정의는 변화하는 용례에 따라 수정된다.
② 'addicts'는 채권자의 노예가 된 사람들이었다.
③ 'husband'는 주택을 소유하여 기혼 상태를 나타낸 단어였다.
④ 'guy'는 시간이 지나 함축되어 있던 부정적 의미를 잃었다.
⑤ 언어는 인간이 만들어 내는 계속해서 변화하는 반영물이다.

question: 25. 다음 밑줄 친 우리말에 알맞게 빈칸 (A)~(C)를 채우시오. 단, (A)와 (B)에 주어진 단어는 반드시 활용하여 작성하시오.

question: 23. 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은? [2.7점]
passage: All human cultures mark the passing of time by the differences they observe in the world around them. question: 27. 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The term "anchoring" was introduced by Roland Barthes, who noted that text next to images (especially photographs) confines meaning. Of all possible interpretations an image could elicit, text points the viewer toward a desired, specific direction. In advertising, the symbolic message does not guide identification but interpretation. The viewer is asked not simply to recognize what they see, but to understand why they see it and what it means. By combining images with text, ads produce symbolic meaning that is accurate and specific, adding depth while limiting breadth of rational and emotional interpretations. A headline or tagline directs the reader through intended meanings of the image, "remote-controlling" interpretation toward a meaning chosen in advance. For example, a puppy alone may elicit countless feelings, but with a headline "This one will die in the streets" and an end line "Adopt a stray pet," the viewer is guided toward the intended meaning: the need to protect stray animals. Thus, anchoring _______________________________________.

② reduces ambiguity and secures intended comprehension

question: 28. 다음 글을 읽고 작성한 분석표의 빈칸 (A)~(C)에 들어갈 적절한 말을 아래 조건을 참고하여 각각 한 단어로 적으시오.

question: 29. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 적절한 곳은?

question: 11. 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We're naturally wired to organize the world into a hierarchy. We do this to help make sense of the world, maintain our beliefs, and generally feel better. But when someone infringes on our place in the world and our understanding of how it works, we react without thinking. When someone cuts you off on the highway and road rage kicks in, that's your unconscious mind saying, "<u>Who are you to cut me off?</u>" You're reacting to a threat to your inherent sense of hierarchy. On the road we are all equals. We're all supposed to play by the same rules. Cutting someone off violates those rules and implies higher status. Or consider when you get frustrated with your kids and end an argument with "Because I said so." (Or the office equivalent: "Because I'm the boss.") In these moments you've stopped thinking and regressed to your biological tendencies of reaffirming the hierarchy.

② an attempt to establish one's own dominance on the road
③ a biological tendency to react emotionally to unexpected events

passage: Once a nail is hammered in, it is friction that holds it in place. Friction is the force that arises when two surfaces are sliding, or trying to slide, against each other. explanation: 이 지문은 인간 문화가 주변 세계에서 관찰되는 변화를 통해 시간을 표시하는 방식을 설명합니다. ② 지문의 첫 문장에서 모든 문화는 '주변 세계에서 관찰하는 차이점'을 통해 시간의 흐름을 표시한다고 답할 수 있습니다. ④ 지문 중반부에서 유럽 농경 사회는 고위도 지역의 특성상 계절 변화를 관찰하기 쉬웠기 때문에 태양 주기를 모니터링하는 것이 자연스러웠다고 설명하므로 답할 수 있습니다. ⑤ 지문 후반부에서 이슬람이 태음력을 사용하는 것이 '불가피한(inevitable)' 것은 아니었으며, 지리적/생활 방식의 한계 내에서 정치적, 종교적 결정이 내려진 것이라고 언급하므로 답할 수 있습니다. ①(정확성 비교)과 ③(태음력의 구체적 일수)은 지문에 언급되지 않았습니다.
options_translation: ① 태양력과 태음력 중 어느 쪽이 더 정확한가?
② 모든 인간 문화는 시간을 측정하기 위해 무엇을 사용하는가?
③ 태음력에는 며칠이 있는가?
④ 왜 유럽의 농경 사회는 태양 주기를 따랐는가?
⑤ 이슬람이 태음력을 사용하는 것은 확실(필연적)했는가?

question: 10. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Paradoxically, it's uncertainty that makes us feel most alive. Think of events that shake you out of your everyday routine: maybe attending a family wedding, making a big presentation, or going somewhere you've never been. It's on those occasions that time seems to slow down a little, and you feel more fully engaged. The same holds true if the experience is risky, like mountain climbing or parasailing. Your senses are sharper. You notice more. Thanks to the release of a feel-good chemical in the brain called dopamine, you get a greater rush of pleasure from chance encounters with people than planned meetings. Good news, financial rewards, and gifts are more enjoyable if they are surprises. It's why the most popular television shows and movies are the ones with unexpected plot twists and astonishing endings.
summary_sentence: Uncertainty makes us feel most alive, and this becomes stronger in (A)___________ experiences and (B)___________ moments.
options: ① boring - unexpected
② repeated - planned
③ meaningless - calm
④ ordinary - expected
⑤ new - surprising
explanation: 지문은 불확실성과 일상에서 벗어난 경험이 우리를 더 활기차게 만든다고 설명합니다. 가보지 않은 곳에 가는 것과 같은 새로운 경험(A: new)과 계획된 만남보다 우연한 만남, 그리고 깜짝 선물이나 반전 있는 결말과 같은 놀라운 순간(B: surprising)에서 즐거움과 생동감이 더 커진다는 내용입니다. 따라서 ⑤번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 지루한 - 예상치 못한
② 반복되는 - 계획된
③ 의미 없는 - 차분한
④ 평범한 - 예상된
⑤ 새로운 - 놀라운

question: 12. 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
passage: A great strength of the market mechanism is that there are incentives for individuals to reveal their knowledge through their behavior. This stands in contrast to many strategic situations - for example, in political negotiations - in which it is wise not to let the other side know what one's true preferences or production capacities are. A perfectly competitive market that clears on the spot leaves no room for such strategies. If prices are not sticky - as many models assume - individuals adapt their behavior instantaneously, whenever their preferences or the circumstances change. They stop buying items that do not satisfy their needs and stop selling items that do not provide them with optimal gains, maybe switching to the production of other items. If they have motivational problems, for example, falling into denial about the fact that there is no demand for their products, markets reveal to them, sometimes in quite brutal ways, that ________________________________.
options: ① In markets, people reveal their knowledge and preferences through their actions.
② A perfectly competitive market that clears instantly allows no room for strategic hiding.
③ When preferences or conditions change, people adjust their behavior immediately in a flexible market.
④ The market mechanism protects producers from losing demand for their products.
⑤ Markets can be harsh in showing people the reality of demand and supply.
explanation: 지문에 따르면 시장은 제품에 대한 수요가 없다는 사실을 부인하는 생산자들에게 때로는 잔인한 방식으로 그 현실(수요 없음)을 드러낸다고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 시장 기커니즘이 생산자들을 제품 수요 상실로부터 보호한다는 ④번은 지문의 내용과 정반대입니다.
options_translation: ① 시장에서 사람들은 행동을 통해 자신의 지식과 선호도를 드러낸다.
② 즉각적으로 결제되는 완전 경쟁 시장은 전략적 은닉의 여지를 허용하지 않는다.
③ 선호나 조건이 변할 때, 사람들은 유연한 시장에서 즉각적으로 행동을 조정한다.
④ 시장 메커니즘은 생산자들이 제품에 대한 수요를 잃는 것으로부터 보호한다.
⑤ 시장은 사람들에게 수요와 공급의 현실을 보여주는 데 있어 가혹할 수 있다.

options_translation: ① 그들이 이 현실을 직면할 수밖에 없다

question: 14. 윗글의 일부를 다음과 같이 쓰고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: We're naturally wired to organize the world into a hierarchy. We do this to help make sense of the world, maintain our beliefs, and generally feel better. But when someone infringes on our place in the world and our understanding of how it works, we react without thinking. When someone cuts you off on the highway and road rage kicks in, that's your unconscious mind saying, "Who are you to cut me off?" You're reacting to a threat to your inherent sense of hierarchy. On the road we are all equals. We're all supposed to play by the same rules. Cutting someone off violates those rules and implies higher status. Or consider when you get frustrated with your kids and end an argument with "Because I said so." (Or the office equivalent: "Because I'm the boss.") In these moments you've stopped thinking and regressed to your biological tendencies of reaffirming the hierarchy.
summary_sentence: Hierarchical frameworks provide a sense of order and predictability, allow people to locate themselves in relation to others, and support the maintenance of deeply held beliefs about fairness, authority, and personal identity. When an individual's position within this hierarchy is perceived to be undermined, their reactions often are expected that _______________ _________________________________________.
options: ① embody personal value-laden ways of understanding the world
② enforce the conscious thought of the complexity of social life
③ concern involuntary outbreaks outweighing the conscious mind
④ gut feelings are gradually replaced with more legitimate ones
⑤ aimed at modifying the hierarchical order with reasoned engagement
explanation: 지문은 위계질서에 대한 위협이 느껴질 때 인간이 '생각하지 않고 반응(react without thinking)'하며 '무의식적인 마음(unconscious mind)'이 작동하여 '생물학적 성향으로 퇴행(regressed to biological tendencies)'한다고 설명합니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 '의식적인 마음보다 더 비중이 큰 무의식적인(비자발적인) 폭발과 관련이 있다'는 내용의 ③번이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 세상을 이해하는 개인의 가치가 가득 담긴 방식을 구체화한다
② 사회 생활의 복잡성에 대한 의식적인 사고를 강요한다
③ 의식적인 마음보다 더 비중이 큰 비자발적인 폭발과 관련이 있다
④ 직감이 점차 더 타당한 것으로 대체된다
⑤ 이성적인 관여를 통해 위계 질서를 수정하는 것을 목표로 한다

question: 15. 윗글의 일부를 다음과 같이 쓰고자 한다. 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

options: ① threatening

question: 17. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓗ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 총개수는?
passage: Once a nail is hammered in, it is friction that holds it in place. The (A)___________ of the nail is primarily governed by frictional forces. Friction is the force that arises ⓐ<u>when</u> two surfaces are sliding, or trying to slide. against each other. If you try to pull apart two blocks of wood that ⓑ<u>has been nailed</u> together, the wood fibers grip the shaft of the nail, ⓒ<u>producing</u> friction that holds it in place. The nail feels a force trying to rip ⓓ<u>itself</u> apart along its length, and we call that force tension. Your experiment can now fail in one of two ways - ⓔ<u>either</u> the nail stretches and splits in half because the tension force is too large for the nail, or the nail comes loose because the friction force is ⓕ<u>overcome</u>. The force it would take ⓖ<u>to stretch</u> the nail is much larger than the friction forces on the surface, so we don't have to worry too much about the former. It's the friction ⓗ<u>with which</u> we need to concern ourselves. The main factor that determines whether a nail holds or fails is (B)___________.
options: ① 1개
② 2개
③ 3개
④ 4개
⑤ 5개
explanation: 어법상 어색한 것은 ⓑ와 ⓓ 총 2개입니다.ⓑ: 선행사가 'two blocks of wood'로 복수이므로 동사는 단수형 has가 아닌 복수형 'have been nailed'가 되어야 합니다.ⓓ: 분사구 'trying to rip'의 의미상 주어는 a force입니다. 힘이 못을 찢으려 하는 상황이므로 목적어는 주어와 일치하지 않으므로 재귀대명사 itself가 아닌 'it'을 써야 합니다.

question: 18. 윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

options: ① (A) retention ... (B) the nail's own strength

question: 22. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: The term "anchoring" was introduced by Roland Barthes who observed that text is often used next to images (his focus was on photographs) to confine meaning. Of all possible literal or implied interpretations an image could elicit, text would point the viewer towards a desired, specific direction. In advertising, as Barthes argues, the symbolic message does not guide identification but interpretation. The viewer is not asked to recognize what they see but to understand why they see it and what it means to them. By combining images with text, advertising produces symbolic meaning that is accurate and specific on the one hand, richer on the other, thus adding depth and eliminating breadth of rational and emotional interpretations. The headline or tagline of an ad directs the reader through the intended meanings of the image, so that the reader avoids some and receives others. It "remote-controls" the reader towards a meaning chosen in advance.
options: ① graphical symbols that convey meanings through its visual parallel to a physical object
② circumstances that render illustrations uniquely chosen in advertising industry
③ sophisticated advertising strategies that liberate the viewers from intended interpretations
④ the function of inscription when placed alongside images, particularly photographs
⑤ literary properties that depict a variety of interpretations visual representations generate
explanation: 이 글은 Roland Barthes가 도입한 'anchoring(고정)'이라는 개념을 설명하며, 텍스트가 이미지(특히 사진)와 함께 사용될 때 이미지의 모호한 해석 가능성을 제한하고 특정한 방향으로 관객의 해석을 유도한다는 점을 강조합니다. 따라서 주제로 가장 적절한 것은 이미지 옆에 배치된 명문(텍스트)의 기능인 ④번입니다.
options_translation: ① 물리적 대상과의 시각적 평행을 통해 의미를 전달하는 그래픽 기호
② 광고 산업에서 삽화가 독특하게 선택되게 만드는 상황들
③ 시청자를 의도된 해석으로부터 해방시키는 정교한 광고 전략
④ 이미지, 특히 사진과 함께 배치될 때 비문의 기능
⑤ 시각적 표현이 생성하는 다양한 해석을 묘사하는 문학적 속성

question: 23. 윗글의 밑줄 친 '비록 많은 사람들이 공감을 칭찬하지만, 일부 비평가들은 동의하지 않는다.'라는 의미가 되도록 보기에 주어진 단어만을 사용하여 영작하시오. (단, 필요시 어형을 변형할 것)
passage: <u>비록 많은 사람들이 공감을 칭찬하지만, 일부 비평가들은 동의하지 않는다</u>. They say empathy cannot prevent conflicts between people or groups and may even make them worse. Empathy can be tiring, cause burnout, or make people less sensitive to suffering. People tend to empathize more with their own group and less with outsiders, and sometimes even enjoy the suffering of out-groups in competitive situations. Therefore, encouraging more empathy can be (A)______________. Even when we try to understand people who are different from us, we may fail, which can cause misunderstandings and frustration. Critics suggest that instead of relying on empathy, we should use other tools, such as rational compassion or moral emotions like fear, anger, and shame, to improve social harmony.
subjective_conditions: 필요시 어형을 변형할 것
answer: Although many people praise empathy, some critics disagree.
explanation: '비록 ~이지만'의 양보 절을 이끄는 접속사 although를 사용하여 문장을 구성합니다. '공감을 칭찬하다'에서 empathy가 praise의 목적어로 쓰이며, '동의하지 않는다'는 disagree 또는 do not agree로 표현할 수 있는데 보기의 agree를 활용하여 disagree로 변형해야 합니다.

question: 24. 윗글의 문맥상 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 수 있는 적절한 표현을 1개의 영단어로 쓰시오.
passage: <u>비록 많은 사람들이 공감을 칭찬하지만, 일부 비평가들은 동의하지 않는다</u>. They say empathy cannot prevent conflicts between people or groups and may even make them worse. Critics suggest that instead of relying on empathy, we should use other tools, such as rational compassion or moral emotions like fear, anger, and shame, to improve social harmony.

explanation: 글의 맥락상 공감이 갈등을 악화시키거나 피로를 유발하고, 자기 집단에만 편향될 수 있다는 비판적 시각을 서술하고 있습니다. 따라서 공감을 장려하는 것이 결과적으로 효과가 없거나 비효율적일 수 있다는 의미의 'inefficient'가 적절합니다. (원문 문맥상 counterproductive 등도 가능하나 제시된 정답은 inefficient입니다.)

question: 26. 윗글에 관한 내용을 다음과 같이 쓰고자 한다. 주어진 단어들만 활용하여(모든 단어 1번만 사용할 것) 문장의 의미가 완성되도록 영작하시오. (단, 필요시 어형을 변형할 것) [5.0점]
passage: The traditional bank manager in the 1950s was usually a respected pillar of the community, a cautious, careful sort of person who probably went to bed early and didn't drink too much. But from the 1970s a new kind of banker appeared - loud, flashy, and arrogant. These bankers loved taking big risks. They wanted to get rich quick and blow their money on fast cars and expensive champagne. They made their money through what's called 'speculation'. Normally, people buy things because they want to use them, such as wheat to make bread and petrol to run the car. But when people speculate, they buy things even when they have no interest in using them. They might buy a load of wheat simply because they think that its price is going to rise when a drought is predicted in wheat-growing areas. If their guess is right, they later sell the wheat for a profit. However, incorrect projections may result in significant financial loss.
subjective_conditions: 주어진 단어들만 활용하여(모든 단어 1번만 사용할 것) 문장의 의미가 완성되도록 영작
필요시 어형을 변형할 것
subjective_answer_format: → The bankers of the 1950s were typically regarded as respected pillars of the community, characterized by caution and a disciplined lifestyle, and led stable and steady lives by __________________________________________________.
answer: abiding by standards that were considered reasonable by most people
explanation: 1950년대 은행가들은 대다수의 사람들에 의해 합리적이라고 여겨지는 기준을 준수하며 안정적인 삶을 살았다는 내용이 되도록 영작해야 합니다. 'by' 뒤에 수단이나 방법을 나타내는 동명사구 'abiding by standards'를 배치하고, 그 뒤에 관계대명사 'that'을 사용하여 'were considered reasonable by most people'이 'standards'를 수식하게 구성합니다.

question: 27. 윗글의 내용을 다음과 같이 쓰고자 한다. 문맥상 내용에 맞게 요약문의 빈칸 (A)~(C)를 주어진 <보기>의 단어들에서 각각 1개씩만 선택하여 문장을 완성하시오. [3.0점]
passage: The traditional bank manager in the 1950s was usually a respected pillar of the community, a cautious, careful sort of person who probably went to bed early and didn't drink too much. But from the 1970s a new kind of banker appeared - loud, flashy, and arrogant. These bankers loved taking big risks. They wanted to get rich quick and blow their money on fast cars and expensive champagne. They made their money through what's called 'speculation'. Normally, people buy things because they want to use them, such as wheat to make bread and petrol to run the car. But when people speculate, they buy things even when they have no interest in using them. They might buy a load of wheat simply because they think that its price is going to rise when a drought is predicted in wheat-growing areas. If their guess is right, they later sell the wheat for a profit. However, incorrect projections may result in significant financial loss.
summary_sentence: Beginning in the 1970s, bankers (A)__________ a tendency for high-risk financial activities, driven by the pursuit of rapid wealth accumulation and luxury-oriented consumption. Their earnings were mainly generated through a practice known as speculation. Unlike traditional purchasing, which is motivated by (B)__________ consumption, speculative behavior involves acquiring assets without any immediate intention of direct use. For example, a speculator might purchase a large quantity of wheat in anticipation of a price increase following a predicted drought in wheat-producing regions. explanation: (A) 1970년대 은행가들이 고위험 금융 활동에 대한 경향을 '보여주었다(demonstrate)'는 의미가 적절합니다.(B) 전통적인 구매는 실제 사용 목적, 즉 '필요에 기반한(needs-based)' 소비에 의해 동기부여됩니다.(C) 잘못된 추측의 결과로 경제적 손실을 입어 '경제적으로 지급 능력이 있는 상태를 유지하는 것(staying afloat)'에 어려움을 겪을 수 있습니다.

question: 28. 윗글에서 언급된 금속 호일의 특징을 우리말로 쓰시오. [2.0점]
passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers of which it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease to form, while sufficient fibers remain undamaged for the material not to crack and fall apart. Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to resist being pulled apart, but it can also be torn easily and accurately along the crease if a point of weakness - a small, initial tear - is opened up. This winning combination of mechanical properties allows it to (A)__________ the shape of any object through creasing and folding - hence the art of origami. There are very few materials as good: metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult. Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, in which case it lacks the rigidity required of a good wrapping material. So it is its ability to hold a crease while remaining stiff that makes paper uniquely suited to this purpose. This combination (B)__________ both its functional uses in packaging and folding practices like origami.
answer: 주름을 유지할 수 읈지만, 주름의 통서가 다소 어렵다.
explanation: 방문 본문 중 "metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult." 문윙에 근거하여, 금속 호일은 주름을 유지할 수는 읈지만 궼 주름을 제어(통제)하는 감은 다소 어렵다는 특징을 서술합니다.

question: 2. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The future of work depends on two forces: a harmful substituting force and a helpful complementing one. Many tales have a hero and a villain fighting each other for dominance, but in our story, technology plays both roles at once, displacing workers while simultaneously raising the demand for their efforts elsewhere in the economy. This interaction helps explain why past worries about automation were misplaced: our ancestors had predicted the wrong winner in that fight, underestimating quite how powerful the complementing force would prove to be or simply ignoring that factor altogether. It also helps to explain why economists have traditionally been dismissive of the idea of technological unemployment: there appeared to be firm limits to the substituting force, leaving lots of tasks that could not be performed by machines, and a growing demand for human beings to do them instead.
options: ① Why Creativity is Key to Winning in the Automated Age
② Artificial Intelligence Dilemma: Threat or Opportunity?
③ Bridging the Gap: Ensuring Equal Tech Access for All
④ Is Technology Only Detrimental to Employment?
⑤ The Dark Side of Technological Advancement
explanation: 이 글은 기술이 노동을 대체하는 해로운 힘(substituting force)뿐만 아니라 노동의 수요를 높이는 유익한 보완적 힘(complementing force)을 동시에 가지고 있음을 설명하고 있습니다. 과거의 자동화에 대한 우려가 잘못되었으며 기술적 실업에 대한 경제학자들의 전통적인 낙관론의 배경을 다루고 있으므로, '기술이 고용에 해롭기만 한가?'라는 질문을 던지는 4번이 제목으로 가장 적절합니다.

question: 3. 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: Mirror neurons are the hardware of empathy, and so what would make more sense than to look and see which animals possess these cells? And this is exactly where modern research now stands: all researchers know so far is that apes possess mirror neurons. We still need to test to see which other species are like us in this respect. Scientists often publicly speculate that we can probably expect surprises here, too. They assume that all animals that live in herds or large groups possess similar brain mechanisms, because social units function only if individuals can see things from the perspective of others in the group and feel what they are feeling. question: 4. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Minimal processing can be one of the best ways to keep original flavors and taste, without any need to add artificial flavoring or additives, or too much salt. This would also be the efficient way to keep most nutrients, especially the most sensitive ones such as many vitamins and anti-oxidants. question: 5. 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Our biological tendencies are hardwired within us. Those tendencies often served our prehistoric ancestors well, but they tend to get in our way today. These timeless behaviors have been described and discussed by philosophers and scientists from Aristotle and the Stoics to Daniel Kahneman and Jonathan Haidt. For instance, we're naturally wired to organize the world into a hierarchy. We do this to help make sense of the world, maintain our beliefs, and generally feel better. But when someone infringes on our place in the world and our understanding of how it works, we react without thinking. When someone cuts you off on the highway and road rage kicks in, that's your unconscious mind saying, "Who are you to cut me off?" You're reacting to a threat to your inherent sense of hierarchy. On the road we are all equals. We're all supposed to play by the same rules. Cutting someone off violates those rules and implies higher status. Or consider when you get frustrated with your kids and end an argument with "Because I said so." (Or the office equivalent: "Because I'm the boss.") In these moments you've stopped thinking and regressed to your biological tendencies of reaffirming the hierarchy.
options: ① turning ordinary moments into extraordinary success
② human instincts to classify the world hierarchically
③ how hierarchical structure influences information
④ safety tips for handling road rage drivers
⑤ ways to ensure social order and stability
explanation: 글의 중심 내용은 인간이 세상을 계층 구조로 조직하려는 타고난 생물학적 경향성을 가지고 있다는 것입니다. 도로에서의 난폭 운전(road rage)이나 부모/상사의 권위적인 태도 등을 예로 들어, 자신의 서열이나 지위가 침해받는다고 느낄 때 무의식적으로 계층을 확인하려 반응하게 된다는 점을 설명하고 있습니다.

③ 계층 구조가 정보에 미치는 영향

question: 6. 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: One way to get your children to stop worrying is by refusing to discuss their worries with them or to feel sorry for them. Instead of expressing appreciation for their worries or sympathizing over how miserable they are making themselves, point out the futility of worrying over situations that are out of their hands. Ask them what they hope to accomplish by worrying. Ask them, (A)__________, if they think worrying is going to improve their health, cure their acne, keep someone they care about from being injured, or improve the quality of their world in any way. Then, without expressing sympathy for them, point out the fact that they could be making much better use of their time and energy by engaging in constructive activities or by simply having fun instead of making themselves sick with worry. However, merely convincing your children that worry is senseless and that they would be more content if they didn't worry isn't going to stop them from worrying. For some reason, young people seem to believe that worry is a fact of life over which they have little or no control. Consequently, they don't even try to stop. (B)__________, you need to convince them that worry, like guilt and fear, is nothing more than an emotion, and like all emotions, is subject to the power of the will.
options: ① (A) for example - (B) Thus
② (A) however - (B) For instance
③ (A) nonetheless - (B) Likewise

explanation: (A)의 앞 문장에서 걱정을 통해 무엇을 성취하고 싶은지 물으라고 했고, 빈칸 뒤에는 건강 향상, 여드름 치유 등 구체적인 예시 항목들이 나오므로 예시를 나타내는 'for example'이 적절합니다. (B)의 앞부분에서는 아이들이 걱정을 조절할 수 없는 것으로 믿고 멈추려 하지 않는다는 원인/상황을 설명하고 있으며, 빈칸 뒤에는 그러므로 걱정이 의지의 힘에 달려 있다는 것을 확신시켜야 한다는 결론이 이어지므로 인과관계를 나타내는 'Thus'가 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 예를 들어 - 따라서
② 하지만 - 예를 들어
③ 그럼에도 불구하고 - 마찬가지로
④ 예를 들어 - 대조적으로

question: 7. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 가리키는 대상이 나머지 넷과 다른 것은? [2.9점]
passage: A paper whose title starts intriguingly with 'Are You My Mummy?' describes the fascinating results of an odour memory study in kittens. The study does show that a mother cat has her own individual odour that must be consistent enough despite changes in her reproductive state over time for her kittens to remember her scent ten months after ⓐ<u>they</u> last saw or smelled her. Mother cats can tell which kittens belong to them, too - when litters are mixed up ⓑ<u>they</u> use their kittens' scent to distinguish them from offspring of other mothers. Despite this, when faced with a selection of kittens who have wandered from the nest, her own and others that aren't hers, a mother cat doesn't appear to favour her own offspring when retrieving them. The reason for this is uncertain, although distress vocalizations from kittens that are lost from ⓒ<u>their</u> nest are known to be very powerful. Thus, it may just be hard for the mother to resist retrieving them, regardless of whether ⓓ<u>they</u> are hers. In the wild, a squeaking kitten out in the open is likely to attract predators, which is bad news for any other kittens around it. A rapid rescue of any crying kitten would be a good strategy to prevent ⓔ<u>they</u> from drawing unwanted attention.
options: ① ⓐ
② ⓑ
③ ⓒ
④ ⓓ
⑤ ⓔ
explanation: ⓐ, ⓒ, ⓓ, ⓔ는 모두 '새끼 고양이들(kittens)'을 가리키는 반면, ⓑ는 새끼 고양이들의 냄새를 이용해 자신의 새끼를 구별하는 주체인 '어미 고양이들(Mother cats)'을 가리킵니다.
options_translation: ① ⓐ (새끼 고양이들)
② ⓑ (어미 고양이들)
③ ⓒ (새끼 고양이들)

question: 8. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.8점]
passage: Looking at the seams ⓐ<u>allows</u> us to see how things are put together. Waiting forces time to be visible, as loosely stitched and seemingly inefficient. We are able to see the cultural assumptions around ⓑ<u>what</u> our society assumes to be good or wasteful uses of time. As we begin noticing these times, we can see the work they do in a society, both good and bad. By making us students of the seams, wait times can teach us about the forces in life that have shaped our assumptions about time, efficiency, and productivity. Once we study these things in our lives, we can start developing tactics for dealing with our wait times. "Tactics" is a term drawn from military force when ⓒ<u>attacked</u> another, and tactics are responses to conditions on the ground. In this vein, time is imposed on us by our cultures, by the technologies that have regimented time down to the nanosecond, and by ⓓ<u>its</u> own finite nature and the fact that we're going to live only so long. In response, we must develop tactics for dealing with time and waiting. These aren't tactics to eliminate waiting; instead, these are tactics for teaching us how ⓔ<u>to learn</u> from the seams.
explanation: ⓒ가 포함된 부사절에서 주어인 military force가 다른 대상을 '공격하는' 능동의 관계이므로 과거분사인 attacked를 현재분사인 attacking으로 고쳐야 합니다. (when attacking another 또는 when it attacks another)

question: 9. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 어색한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: What makes questioning authority so hard? The difficulties start in childhood, when parents - the first and most powerful authority figures - show children "the way things are." This is a necessary element of learning language and socialization, and certainly most things ⓐ<u>learned</u> in early childhood are noncontroversial: the English alphabet starts with A and ends with Z, the numbers 1 through 10 come before the numbers 11 through 20, and so on. Children, however, will ⓑ<u>spontaneously</u> question things that are quite obvious to adults and even to older kids. The word "why?" becomes a challenge, as in, "Why is the sky blue?" Answers such as "because it just is" or "because I say so" tell children that they must unquestioningly accept what authorities say "just because," and children who persist in their questioning are likely to find ⓒ<u>them</u> dismissed or yelled at for "bothering" adults with "meaningless" or "unimportant" questions. But these questions are in fact perfectly reasonable. Why is the sky blue? Many adults do not themselves know the answer. And who says the sky's color needs to be called "blue," anyway? How do we know that what one person calls "blue" is the same color ⓓ<u>that</u> another calls "blue"? The scientific answers come from physics, but those are not the answers that children are seeking. They are trying to understand the world, and no matter how irritating the repeated questions may become to stressed and time-pressed parents, it is important to take them seriously to make kids ⓔ<u>question</u> authority to think for themselves.
explanation: ⓒ는 문장의 주어인 'children who persist in their questioning' 자신을 가리키므로 목적어 자리에 대명사 them 대신 재귀대명사인 themselves를 써야 합니다. (find themselves dismissed: 자신들이 묵살당하는 것을 알게 되다)

question: 11. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.1점]
passage: A computational algorithm that takes input data and generates some output from it doesn't really ⓐ<u>embody</u> any notion of meaning. Certainly, such a computation does not generally have as its purpose its own survival and well-being. It does not, in general, assign value to the inputs. Compare, for example, a computer algorithm with the waggle dance of the honeybee, by which means a foraging bee ⓑ<u>delivers</u> to others in the hive information about the source of food (such as nectar) it has located. The "dance" - a series of stylized movements on the comb - shows the bees how far away the food is and in which direction. But this input does not simply program other bees to go out and look for it. Rather, they ⓒ<u>weigh</u> this information, comparing it with their own knowledge of the surroundings. Some bees might not bother to make the journey, considering it ⓓ<u>invaluable</u>. The input, such as it is, is processed in the light of the organism's own internal states and history; there is nothing ⓔ<u>fixed</u> about its effects.
explanation: ⓓ번의 invaluable은 '매우 귀중한'이라는 뜻임에 반해, 문맥상 볺리가 머기를 찾아 나설 가치가 없다고 판단하여 여정을 하지 않는다는 내용이므로 'worthless'(가치 없는)와 같은 단어가 적절합니다.

question: 12. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3.2점]
passage: Paper's mechanical properties lend themselves to folding and bending. The cellulose fibers of which it is made can be partially snapped in the area of maximum bend, allowing a permanent crease to form, while sufficient fibers remain ⓐ<u>intact</u> for the material not to crack and fall apart. Indeed, in this state it pretty much maintains its ability to resist being pulled apart, but it can also be torn ⓑ<u>easily</u> along the crease if a point of weakness - a small, initial tear - is opened up. This ⓒ<u>successful</u> combination of mechanical properties allows it to assume the shape of any object through creasing and folding - hence the art of origami. There are very ⓓ<u>few</u> materials as good: metal foils can hold a crease, but control of the crease is somewhat more difficult. Plastic sheeting doesn't tend to hold a crease at all, unless it is very soft, in which case it lacks the rigidity required of a good wrapping material. So it is its ability to hold a crease while remaining stiff that makes paper uniquely ⓔ<u>unsuitable</u> for this purpose.
explanation: 종이가 접힌 상태를 유지하면서도 강성을 유지하는 특성 땄문에 포장 재료로서 매우 적합하다는 내용이 뒤따라야 합니다. 따라서 ⓔ번의 unsuitable(부적합한)은 suitable(적합한) 또는 perfect로 바꾸어야 합니다.

question: 13. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: When we get an unfavorable outcome, in some ways the last thing we want to hear is that the process was fair. As outraging as the combination of an unfavorable outcome and an unfair process is, this combination also brings with it a ①<u>consolation</u> prize: the possibility of attributing the bad outcome to something other than ourselves. We may reassure ourselves by believing that our bad outcome had little to do with us and ②<u>nothing</u> to do with the unfair process. If the process is fair, however, we cannot nearly as easily internalize the outcome; we got what we got "fair and square." When the process is fair we believe that our outcome is ③<u>well-earned</u>, which is another way of saying that there must have been something about ourselves (what we did or who we are) that caused the outcome. When we are on the receiving end of a bad outcome we may have ④<u>different</u> types of negative feelings depending upon whether we see the accompanying process as fair or unfair. On the one hand, if we see the accompanying process as fair, we feel bad about ourselves. On the other hand, if we see the accompanying process as unfair, we feel ⑤<u>resentful</u> toward the decision maker.
explanation: 결과가 바라지 않는 것이라도 과정이 불공정하면 사람은 그 결과를 자신이 아닌 과정의 부정함으로 돌릴 수 있으므로 위안을 얻는다는 내용입니다. 따라서 나쁜 결과가 자신과는 관련이 없고, 불공정한 과정과는 ‘모든’ 관련이 있다고 믿어야 자기합리화가 가능하므로 ②번의 nothing은 everything 등으로 바뀌어야 맥락상 적절합니다.

question: 14. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: In today's information age, in many companies and on many teams, the objective is no longer error prevention and replicability. On the contrary, it's creativity, speed, and agility. In the industrial era, the goal was to minimize variation. But in creative companies today, maximizing variation is more ①<u>vital</u>. In these situations, the biggest risk isn't making a mistake or losing consistency; it's failing to attract top talent, to invent new products, or to change direction quickly when the environment shifts. Consistency and repeatability are more likely to ②<u>squash</u> fresh thinking than to bring your company profit. A lot of little mistakes, while sometimes painful, help the organization learn quickly and are a ③<u>critical</u> part of the innovation cycle. In these situations, rules and process are the ④<u>best</u> answer. A symphony isn't what you're going for. Leave the conductor and the sheet music behind. Build a jazz band instead. Jazz emphasizes individual ⑤<u>spontaneity</u>. The musicians know the overall structure of the song but have the freedom to improvise, riffing off one another, creating incredible music.
explanation: 글의 흐름상 창의성과 민첩함을 강조하는 상황에서는 규칙과 과정은 창의적이거나 새로운 생각을 억압하는 요인이 되므로, 결정적인 답이 될 수 없습니다. 따라서 best는 문맥상 어색하며, last 혹은 wrong 등으로 바뀌어야 합니다.

question: 15. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: It's often said that those who can't do, teach. It would be more accurate to say that those who can do, can't teach the basics. A great deal of expert knowledge is implicit, not explicit. The further you progress toward mastery, the less conscious awareness you often have of the fundamentals. Experiments show that skilled golfers and wine aficionados have a hard time describing their putting and tasting techniques - even asking them to explain their approaches is enough to interfere with their performance, so they often stay on autopilot. When I first saw an elite diver do four and a half somersaults, I asked how he managed to spin so fast. His answer: "Just go up in a ball." Experts often have an intuitive understanding of a route, but they _______________________________. Their brain dump is partially filled with garbage.
options: ① engage only particular regions of their brains
② struggle to express their emotions coherently
③ rely on conscious reasoning rather than on gut
④ find it challenging to articulate sequences involved
⑤ consider mastering specialized knowledge time-consuming
explanation: 전문가들은 자신의 기술이나 과정을 무의식적으로 수행하기 때문에, 그 과정을 말하거나 설명하는 데 어려움을 겪는다는 내용입니다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ④번 ‘개입된 순서를 말하기 어려워한다’가 들어가는 것이 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 뇌의 특정 영역만을 사용한다
② 자신의 감정을 일관성 있게 표현하는 데 어려움을 겪는다
③ 직관보다는 의식적인 추론에 의존하는 경향이 있으며
④ 개입된 순서를 명확히 말하기 어려워하는 경향이 있으며
⑤ 전문 지식을 습득하는 것이 시간이 많이 걸리는 것이라고 생각하는 경향이 있으며

question: 16. 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Dictionary definitions are constantly revised to ____________________________. In Roman times, "addicts" were people who were unable to pay their debts and gave themselves as slaves to their creditors. The word eventually came to be associated with drug dependency: one becomes a slave to one's addiction. The word "husband" originally referred to being a homeowner; it had nothing to do with being married. But because owning your own property made it more likely you'd find a mate, the word eventually came to mean a male who has been wed. On November 5th, 1605, Guy Fawkes tried to blow up the British Parliament. He was captured and put to death. Loyalists burned his effigy, which they nicknamed the "guy." Centuries later, the word lost its negative connotation and a musical named Guys and Dolls ran on Broadway. In American slang, bad means good, cool means great, and wicked means excellent. If you could transport yourself one hundred years into the future, you'd find yourself confused by your great-grandchildren's speech because language itself is an ever-changing reflection of human invention.
options: ① stay relevant in representing current language usage
② provide people with advice on enhancing speech skills
③ document notable technology terms in the digital age
④ eliminate language that implies moral judgment
⑤ give a variety of examples of connotation
explanation: 이 글은 시대의 변화에 따라 단어의 의미가 변해온 사례들(addict, husband, guy, slang 등)을 나열하며, 언어는 인간 발명의 끊임없이 변하는 반영물이라고 설명하고 있습니다. 따라서 사전 정의가 끊임없이 수정되는 이유는 '현재의 언어 사용을 나타내는 데 있어 적절함을 유지하기 위해서'가 가장 적절합니다.
options_translation: ① 현재의 언어 사용을 나타내는 데 있어 적절함을 유지하기 위해
② 사람들에게 언어 능력을 향상시키는 조언을 제공하기 위해
③ 디지털 시대의 주목할 만한 기술 용어들을 기록하기 위해
④ 도덕적 판단을 암시하는 언어를 제거하기 위해
⑤ 함축의 다양한 사례들을 제시하기 위해

question: 17. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Everything in the world exists on a continuum, whether in speed, size, or any other possible descriptor you could think of.
ordered_passages: (A) This rigid approach to categorizing differences has implications in many areas of life. An athlete misses earning a medal by a few milliseconds. A patient barely meets the threshold for a diagnosis. A law student fails the bar exam by one question. Are these people truly substantially different from the medalist, the healthy patient just below the threshold, or the attorney who just barely passes the bar exam?

(B) Someone's IQ is 69 and someone else's is 70 - but only the score of 70 is deemed to be within the range of normal. We don't have to be statisticians to know there is not a meaningful difference between 69 and 70. Yet once the person with the lower score is labeled "cognitively impaired," his or her life will unfold differently than the person with a one-point advantage.

(C) Still, we create and mindlessly adopt sharp distinctions, and those distinctions change lives far more dramatically than marginal differences ever do. Indeed, all differences are arbitrary, but drawing hard lines between categories hides this arbitrariness and can be severely damaging. I call this resulting damage "the borderline effect." The examples are endless.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 세상 모든 것이 연속체 상에 존재한다고 말합니다. (C)는 그럼에도 불구하고 우리가 분명한 구분을 만들어내며, 이것이 '경계 효과(borderline effect)'라는 피해를 준다는 점을 언급하며 예시가 끝이 없다고 끝맺습니다. (B)는 IQ 69와 70의 구체적인 예시를 통해 경계 효과가 삶에 미치는 영향을 설명합니다. (A)는 '이러한 엄격한 접근 방식(This rigid approach)'이라는 표현으로 앞선 (B)의 내용을 요약하며 운동선수, 환자, 법학도 등의 추가적인 예시를 제시하는 것이 자연스럽습니다.

question: 18. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
passage: Many animals pursue a mixed strategy of accumulating both body fat and food, which leads one to ask, "What are the relative advantages and disadvantages of these two forms of energy storage?"
ordered_passages: (A) In other words, there is a metabolic expense to maintaining fat. Excessive fat accumulations may also have a negative effect on an animal's ability to avoid predators. And, if maintaining a high body temperature is advantageous, animals might be expected to accumulate more energy in the form of a food store than as body fat. On the other hand, stored food may rot over time, may be removed by robbers, or may simply be lost.

(B) Many animals must expend energy managing and protecting their food stores. Eating food and converting it to fat avoids these types of losses and the energetic costs of managing stored food. A large accumulation of body fat adds to an animal's fasting capacity, especially large animals, permitting some animals to enter prolonged dormancy in the relative security of a hibernaculum. Thus, both fat accumulation and food storage have some decided advantages.

(C) Maximum fat deposition increases with body mass whereas maximum food storage is not constrained by body size. This means that animals, especially small animals, can accumulate much greater energy reserves in the form of stored food than they can in the form of body fat. Further, stored food is more economical than body fat because fat contributes to body mass, and metabolic rate increases with body mass.
explanation: 주어진 글은 체지방과 음식 저장의 장단점에 대한 질문을 던집니다. (C)는 신체 크기에 따른 저장 용량의 제한과 대사율 측면에서의 경제성을 비교하며 음식 저장이 체지방보다 더 많은 에너지를 비축할 수 있고 경제적임을 설명합니다. (A)는 (C)의 마지막 내용을 '다시 말해서(In other words)'로 부연하며 지방 유지의 대사적 비용과 포식자 회피의 어려움을 언급한 뒤, 음식 저장의 단점(부패, 도난)을 '반면에(On the other hand)'로 제시합니다. (B)는 음식 저장의 관리 비용을 언급하며 다시 체지방의 장점(단식 능력, 동면 가능)을 설명하고 두 방식 모두 확실한 장점이 있다는 결론으로 마무리합니다.

question: 19. 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [2.9점]
passage: The first human beings probably evolved in tropical regions where survival was possible without clothing.
ordered_passages: (A) For instance, early hominids probably did not walk upright, but when they developed that ability, they could travel more efficiently. More important, perhaps, was their development of tool making. With tools, they could hunt other animals, so they could consume more protein and fat than their low-energy vegetarian diet would have provided. Not only their bodies but also their brains would have been changed with more energy. As their diet expanded, hominids could physically and intellectually expand their territory.

(B) It is likely that they had very dark skin because light skin would have given little protection against the burning rays of the sun. There is a debate about whether these people spread into other parts of the world or, instead, whether people developed independently in various parts of the world. Whichever the case, it is believed that in time they became capable of spreading out from Africa, eventually to most of the world. This was probably because their physical characteristics changed.

(C) Although all early hominids were probably dark-skinned, as they moved, that changed. In the most northern of the territories into which they expanded, the sun was very weak, especially in the long winters, and was often hidden by clouds or fog. Dark skin, which had been an advantage in warm, sunny climates, became a disadvantage because the sun's rays, by penetrating human skin, help produce vitamin D, which is an essential element in nutrition. Populations that remained in these colder regions for very long periods of time seem gradually, through gene mutations and the process of natural selection, to have developed much lighter shades of skin.
explanation: 주어진 문장은 초기 인류가 의복 없이 살 수 있는 열대 지역에서 진화했다는 내용입니다. (B)에서 그들의 신체적 특징인 어두운 피부색과 아프리카 밖으로 퍼져 나갔을 가능성을 언급하며 연결됩니다. (A)는 도구 제작과 식단 변화를 통해 영토를 확장한 구체적인 사례를 설명하며, (C)에서 추운 지역으로 이동하며 비타민 D 합성을 위해 어두운 피부가 밝게 변하게 된 진화적 과정을 설명하는 순서가 가장 자연스럽습니다.

question: 20. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [2.8점]
passage: There are deep similarities between viral contagion and behavioral contagion. (A) For example, people in close or extended proximity to others infected by a virus are themselves more likely to become infected, just as people are more likely to drink excessively when they spend more time in the company of heavy drinkers. (B) But there are also important differences between the two types of contagion. (C) One is that visibility promotes behavioral contagion but inhibits the spread of infectious diseases. (D) Solar panels that are visible from the street, for instance, are more likely to stimulate neighboring installations. (E) Another important difference is that whereas viral contagion is almost always a bad thing, behavioral contagion is sometimes negative - as in the case of smoking - but sometimes positive, as in the case of solar installations.
insertion_sentence: In contrast, we try to avoid others who are visibly ill.
explanation: 글의 흐름상 (C)에서 가시성이 행동 전염은 촉진하지만 질병 확산은 억제한다는 핵심 차이점을 제시했습니다. (D)는 행동 전염이 가시성에 의해 촉진되는 사례(태양광 패널)를 보여줍니다. 주어진 문장은 그와 대조적으로(In contrast) 가시성이 질병 확산을 어떻게 억제하는지(아픈 사람을 피함)를 설명하므로, 새로운 차이점을 설명하기 시작하는 (E) 바로 앞 위치가 가장 적절합니다.

question: 21. 다음 글의 흐름으로 보아 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3.2점]
passage: People seem to recognize that the arts are cultural activities that draw on (or react against) certain cultural traditions, certain shared understanding, and certain values and ideas that are characteristic of the time and place in which the art is created. (A) In the case of science, however, opinions differ. (B) Some scientists, like the great biologist J. B. S. Haldane, see science in a similar light - as a historical activity that occurs in a particular time and place, and that needs to be understood within that context. (C) In describing this view of science, philosopher Hugh Lacey speaks of the belief that there is an underlying order of the world which is simply there to be discovered - the world of pure "fact" stripped of any link with value. (D) The aim of science according to this view is to represent this world of pure "fact", independently of any relationship it might bear contingently to human practices and experiences. (E) Such representations are assumed in theories which, in order to be faithful to the object of inquiry, must deploy only categories without evaluative content or implications.
insertion_sentence: Others, however, see science as a purely "objective" pursuit, uninfluenced by the cultural viewpoint and values of those who create it.
explanation: 이 글은 과학을 바라보는 두 가지 상반된 관점을 다룹니다. (B)에서 과학을 역사적/문맥적 활동으로 보는 일부 과학자들의 관점을 소개한 후, 주어진 문장의 'Others, however'를 통해 과학을 순수하게 객관적인 추구로 보는 대조적인 관점을 도입해야 합니다. 따라서 (C)의 위치가 가장 적절하며, (C) 이후의 문장들은 이 '객관적 추구'라는 관점(가치와 분리된 사실의 세계)에 대해 상세히 부연 설명하고 있습니다.

question: 22. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
passage: The traditional bank manager in the 1950s was usually a respected pillar of the community, a cautious, careful sort of person who probably went to bed early and didn't drink too much. But from the 1970s a new kind of banker appeared - loud, flashy, and arrogant. These bankers loved taking big risks. They wanted to get rich quick and blow their money on fast cars and expensive champagne. They made their money through what's called 'speculation'. ⓐWhether they're acquiring a small family-run business or a more complex corporate operation, careful planning and expert legal guidance were key to protecting their investment. ⓑThey might buy a load of wheat simply because they think that its price is going to rise when a drought is predicted in wheat-growing areas. ⓒIf their guess is right, they later sell the wheat for a profit. ⓓSpeculation has gone for centuries, but from the 1970s onwards it really took off. ⓔBanks had whole teams of people whose job was to trade in pretty much anything in order to make money.
explanation: 이 글은 1970년대 이후 등장한 새로운 유형의 은행가들이 '투기(speculation)'를 통해 돈을 벌기 시작했다는 내용을 다루고 있습니다. ⓐ번 문장은 소규모 가족 사업이나 복잡한 기업 운영을 인수할 때 신중한 계획과 법적 지도가 투자 보호의 핵심이라는 내용으로, 공격적인 위험을 감수하며 투기를 일삼는 새로운 은행가들의 성향을 설명하는 전체 흐름에서 벗어납니다.

question: 23. 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계없는 문장은? [2.9점]
passage: It's conceivable that in a world where solar panels are incredibly expensive and there's an extreme collapse in the cost of launching objects to space, you might want to maximize your energy per panel by putting them above the atmosphere. question: 1. 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

③ Using familiar analogies is effective when introducing new concepts to people.

explanation: 스티브 잡스가 가상 세계의 개념을 대중에게 이해시키기 위해 기존의 물리적 사무실에서 사용하던 친숙한 용어들(문서, 폴더, 데스크톱)을 비유로 사용했다는 내용입니다. 따라서 새로운 개념을 소개할 때 친숙한 비유를 사용하는 것이 효과적이라는 ③번이 글의 요지로 가장 적절합니다.

③ 새로운 개념을 사람들에게 소개할 때 친숙한 비유를 사용하는 것이 효과적이다.

question: 2. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

question: 3. 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
passage: Because people tend to adapt, interrupting positive things with negative ones can actually increase enjoyment. Take commercials. Most people hate them, so ⓐ<u>removing</u> them should make shows or other entertainment less enjoyable. But the opposite is true. Shows are actually more enjoyable when they're broken up by annoying commercials. Because these less enjoyable moments break up adaptation to the ⓑ<u>positive</u> experience of the show. Think about eating chocolate chips. The first chip is delicious: sweet, melt-in-your-mouth goodness. The second chip is also pretty good. But by the fourth, fifth, or tenth chip in ⓒ<u>succession</u>, the sense of delight progressively decreases. We adapt. Interspersing positive experiences with less positive ones, however, can ⓓ<u>inhibit</u> adaptation. Eating a Brussels sprout between chocolate chips or viewing commercials between parts of TV shows disrupts the process. ④ ⓓ

explanation: 글 전체의 논지는 긍정적인 경험 사이에 부정적인(덜 즐거운) 경험을 끼워 넣는 것이 즐거움을 유지해 준다는 것입니다. 광고를 싫어하므로 광고를 제거하면 즐거움이 '증가'해야 하는 것이 일반적인 생각인데, 본문은 '반대가 사실이다(the opposite is true)'라고 말하며 광고가 있을 때 더 즐겁다고 설명합니다. 따라서 ⓐ 'removing(제거하는)'을 'including(포함하는)' 등으로 생각했을 때 일반적인 기대와 반대되는 상황이 되거나, 혹은 '제거하는 것이 즐겁게 만들어야 하는데(make it more enjoyable), 실제로는 광고가 있는 것이 더 즐겁다'는 흐름이 되어야 하므로 ⓐ의 위치에서 '제거하는 것'이 쇼를 '덜' 즐겁게 만든다는 논리는 어색합니다. 문맥상 '광고를 제거하는 것이 쇼를 더 즐겁게 만들 것 같지만, 실제로는 광고가 있는 것이 더 즐겁다'는 흐름이 되어야 하므로 ⓐ 'removing'은 적절해 보일 수 있으나, 뒤의 'less enjoyable'과 결합하여 '제거하는 것이 덜 즐겁게 만든다'는 문장은 논리적 모순입니다. 즉, 광고를 '포함하는 것(including)'이 쇼를 덜 즐겁게 만들 것 같지만 실제로는 광고가 있을 때 더 즐겁다는 흐름이 자연스럽습니다.
